verses.text: And because it is believed that he is to arrive at so great a pitch of empty glory, and he will be permitted to do so great things, both against all men and against the Saints of God, that then some weak ones shall indeed think that God cares not for human affairs, the Psalmist interposing a diapsalma, adds as it were the voice of men groaning and asking why judgment is deferred.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:1
verses.text: Psalm X  "Why, O Lord," saith he, "hast Thou withdrawn afar off?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:2
verses.text: Then he who thus inquired, as if all on a sudden he understood, or as if he asked, though he knew, that he might teach, adds, "Thou despisest in due seasons, in tribulations:" that is, Thou despisest seasonably, and causest tribulations to inflame men's minds with longing for Thy coming.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:3
verses.text: For that fountain of life is sweeter to them that have much thirst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:4
verses.text: Therefore he hints the reason of the delay, saying, "Whilst the ungodly vaunteth himself, the poor man is inflamed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:5
verses.text: Wondrous it is and true with what earnestness of good hope the little ones are inflamed unto an upright living by comparison with sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:6
verses.text: In which mystery it comes to pass, that even heresies are permitted to exist; not that heretics themselves wish this, but because Divine Providence worketh this result from their sins, which both maketh and ordaineth the light; but ordereth only the darkness, that by comparison therewith the light may be more pleasant, as by comparison with heretics the discovery of truth is more sweet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:7
verses.text: For so, by this comparison, the approved, who are known to God, are made manifest among men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:8
verses.text: "They are taken in their thoughts, which they think:" that is, their evil thoughts become chains to them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:9
verses.text: But how become they chains? "For the sinner is praised," saith he, "in the desires of his soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:10
verses.text: The tongues of flatterers bind souls in sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:11
verses.text: For there is pleasure in doing those things, in which not only is no reprover feared, but even an approver heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:12
verses.text: "And he that does unrighteous deeds is blessed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:13
verses.text: Hence "are they taken in their thoughts, which they think".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:14
verses.text: "The sinner hath angered the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:15
verses.text: Let no one congratulate the man that prospers in his way, to whose sins no avenger is nigh, and an approver is by.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:16
verses.text: This is the greater anger of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:17
verses.text: For the sinner hath angered the Lord, that he should suffer these things, that is, should not suffer the scourging of correction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:18
verses.text: "The sinner hath angered the Lord: according to the multitude of His anger He will not search it out".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:19
verses.text: Great is His anger, when He searcheth not out, when He as it were forgetteth and marketh not sin, and by fraud and wickedness man attains to riches and honours: which will especially be the case in that Antichrist, who will seem to man blessed to that degree, that he will even be thought God But how great this anger of God is, we are taught by what follows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:20
verses.text: "God is not in his sight, his ways are polluted in all time".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:21
verses.text: He that knows what in the soul gives joy and gladness, knows how great an ill it is to be abandoned by the light of truth: since a great ill do men reckon the blindness of their bodily eyes, whereby this light is withdrawn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:22
verses.text: How great then the punishment he endures, who through the prosperous issue of his sins is brought to that pass, that God is not in his sight, and that his ways are polluted in all time, that is, his thoughts and counsels are unclean! "Thy judgments are taken away from his face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:23
verses.text: For the mind conscious of evil, whilst it seems to itself to suffer no punishment, believes that God doth not judge, and so are God's judgments taken away from its face; while this very thing is great condemnation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:24
verses.text: "And he shall have dominion over all his enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:25
verses.text: For so is it delivered, that he will overcome all kings, and alone obtain the kingdom; since too according to the Apostle, who preaches concerning him, "He shall sit in the temple of God, exalting himself above all that is worshipped and that is called God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:26
verses.text: And seeing that being delivered over to the lust of his own heart, and predestinated to extreme condemnation, he is to come, by wicked arts, to that vain and empty height and rule; therefore it follows, "For he hath said in his heart, I shall not move from generation to generation without evil" : that is, my fame and my name will not pass from this generation to the generation of posterity, unless by evil arts I acquire so lofty a principality, that posterity cannot be silent concerning it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:27
verses.text: For a mind abandoned and void of good arts, and estranged from the light of righteousness, by bad arts devises a passage for itself to a fame so lasting, as is celebrated even in posterity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:28
verses.text: And they that cannot be known for good, desire that men should speak of them even for ill, provided that their name spread far and wide.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:29
verses.text: And this I think is here meant, "I shall not move from generation to generation without evil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:30
verses.text: There is too another interpretation, if a mind vain and full of error supposes that it cannot come from the mortal generation to the generation of eternity, but by bad arts: which indeed was also reported of Simon, when he thought that he would gain heaven by wicked arts, and pass from the human generation to the generation divine by magic Where then is the wonder, if that man of sin too, who is to fill up all the wickedness and ungodliness, which all false prophets have begun, and to do such "great signs; that, if it were possible, he should deceive the very elect," shall say in his heart, "I shall not move from generation to generation without evil"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:31
verses.text: "Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness and deceit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:32
verses.text: For it is a great curse to seek heaven by such abominable arts, and to get together such earnings for acquiring the eternal seat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:33
verses.text: But of this cursing his mouth is full.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:34
verses.text: For this desire shall not take effect, but within his mouth only will avail to destroy him, who dared promise himself such things with bitterness and deceit, that is, with anger and insidiousness, whereby he is to bring over the multitude to his side.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:35
verses.text: "Under his tongue is toil and grief".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:36
verses.text: Nothing is more toilsome than unrighteousness and ungodliness: upon which toil follows grief; for that the toil is not only without fruit, but even unto destruction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:37
verses.text: Which toil and grief refer to that which he hath said in his heart, "I shall not be moved from generation to generation without evil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:38
verses.text: And therefore, "under his tongue," not on his tongue, because he will devise these things in silence, and to men will speak other things, that he may appear good and just, and a son of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:39
verses.text: "He lieth in ambush with the rich".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:40
verses.text: What rich, but those whom he will load with this world's gifts? And he is therefore said to lie in ambush with them, because he will display their false happiness to deceive men; who, when with a perverted will they desire to be such as they, and seek not the good things eternal, will fall into his snares.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:41
verses.text: "That in the dark he may kill the innocent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:42
verses.text: "In the dark,"  I suppose, is said, where it is not easily understood what should be sought, or what avoided.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:43
verses.text: Now to kill the innocent, is of an innocent to make one guilty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:44
verses.text: "His eyes look against the poor," for he is chiefly to persecute the righteous, of whom it is said, "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:45
verses.text: "He lieth in wait in a secret place, as a lion in his den".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:46
verses.text: By a lion in a den, he means one in whom both violence and deceit will work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:47
verses.text: For the first persecution of the Church was violent, when by proscriptions, by torments, by murders, the Christians were compelled to sacrifice: another persecution is crafty, which is now conducted by heretics of any kind and false brethren: there remains a third, which is to come by Antichrist, than which there is nothing more perilous; for it will be at once violent and crafty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:48
verses.text: Violence he will exert in empire, craft in miracles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:49
verses.text: To the violence, the word "lion" refers; to craft, the words "in his den".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:50
verses.text: And these are again repeated with a change of order.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:51
verses.text: "He lieth in wait," he says, "that he may catch the poor;" this hath reference to craft: but what follows, "To catch the poor whilst he draweth him," is put to the score of violence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:52
verses.text: For "draweth" means, he bringeth him to himself by violence, by whatever tortures he can.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:53
verses.text: Again, the two which follow are the same.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:54
verses.text: "In his snare he will humble him," is craft.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:55
verses.text: "He shall decline and fall, whilst he shall have domination over the poor," is violence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:56
verses.text: For a "snare" naturally points to "lying in wait:" but domination most openly conveys the idea of terror.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:57
verses.text: And well does he say, "He will humble him in his snare".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:58
verses.text: For when he shall begin to do those signs, the more wonderful they shall appear to men, the more those Saints that shall be then will be despised, and, as it were, set at nought: he, whom they shall resist by righteousness and innocence, shall seem to overcome by the marvels that he does.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:59
verses.text: But "he shall decline and fall, whilst he shall have domination over the poor;" that is, whilst he shall inflict whatsoever punishments he will upon the servants of God that resist him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:60
verses.text: But how shall he decline, and fall? "For he hath said in his heart, God hath forgotten; He turneth away His face, that He see not unto the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:61
verses.text: This is declining, and the most wretched fall, while the mind of a man prospers as it were in its iniquities, and thinks that it is spared; when it is being blinded, and kept for an extreme and timely vengeance: of which the Psalmist now speaks: "Arise, O Lord God, let Thine hand be exalted" : that is, let Thy power be made manifest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:62
verses.text: Now he had said above, "Arise, O Lord, let not man prevail, let the heathen be judged in Thy sight:" that is, in secret, where God alone seeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:63
verses.text: This comes to pass when the ungodly have arrived at what seems great happiness to men: over whom is placed a lawgiver, such as they had deserved to have, of whom it is said, "Place a lawgiver over them, O Lord, let the heathen know that they are men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:64
verses.text: But now after that hidden punishment and vengeance it is said, "Arise, O Lord God, let Thine hand be exalted;" not of course in secret, but now in glory most manifest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:65
verses.text: "That Thou forget not the poor unto the end;" that is, as the ungodly think, who say, "God hath forgotten, He turneth away His face, that He should not see unto the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:66
verses.text: Now they deny that God seeth unto the end, who say that He careth not for things human and earthly, for the earth is as it were the end of things; in that it is the last element, in which men labour in most orderly sort, but they cannot see the order of their labours, which specially belongs to the hidden things of the Son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:67
verses.text: The Church then labouring in such times, like a ship in great waves and tempests, awaketh the Lord as if He were sleeping, that He should command the winds, and calm should be restored He says therefore, "Arise, O Lord God, let Thine hand be exalted, that Thou forget not the poor unto the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:68
verses.text: Accordingly understanding now the manifest judgment, and in exultation at it, they say, "Wherefore hath the ungodly angered God?" ; that is, what hath it profited him to do so great evil? "For he said in his heart, He will not require it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:69
verses.text: Then follows, "For Thou seest toil and considerest anger, to deliver them into Thine hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:70
verses.text: This sentence looks for distinct explanation, wherein if there shall be error it becomes obscure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:71
verses.text: For thus has the ungodly said in his heart, God will not require it, as though God regarded toil and anger, to deliver them into His hands; that is, as though He feared toil and anger, and for this reason would spare them, lest their punishment be too burdensome to Him, or lest He should be disturbed by the storm of anger: as men generally act, excusing themselves of vengeance, to avoid toil or anger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:72
verses.text: "The poor hath been left unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:73
verses.text: For therefore is he poor, that is, hath despised all the temporal goods of this world, that Thou only mayest be his hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:74
verses.text: "Thou wilt be a helper to the orphan," that is, to him to whom his father this world, by whom he was born after the flesh, dies, and who can already say, "The world hath been crucified unto me, and I unto the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:75
verses.text: For of such orphans God becomes the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:76
verses.text: The Lord teaches us in truth that His disciples do become orphans, to whom He saith, "Call no man father on earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:77
verses.text: Of which He first Himself gave an example in saying, "Who is my mother, and who my brethren?" Whence some most mischievous heretics would assert that He had no mother; and they do not see that it follows from this, if they pay attention to these words, that neither had His disciples fathers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:78
verses.text: For as He said, "Who is my mother?" so He taught them, when He said, "Call no man your father on earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:79
verses.text: "Break the arm of the sinner and of the malicious" ; of him, namely, of whom it was said above, "He shall have dominion over all his enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:80
verses.text: He called his power then, his arm; to which Christ's power is opposed, of which it is said, "Arise, O Lord God, let Thine hand be exalted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:81
verses.text: His fault shall be required, and he shall not be found because of it;" that is he shall be judged for his sins, and himself shall perish because of his sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:82
verses.text: After this, what wonder if there follow, "The Lord shall reign for ever and world without end; ye heathen shall perish out of His earth"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:83
verses.text: He uses heathen for sinners and ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:84
verses.text: "The Lord hath heard the longing of the poor" : that longing wherewith they were burning, when in the straits and tribulations of this world they desired the day of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:85
verses.text: "Thine ear hath heard the preparation of their heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:86
verses.text: This is the preparation of the heart, of which it is sung in another Psalm, "My heart is prepared, O God, my heart is prepared:" of which the Apostle says, "But if we hope for what we see not, we do with patience wait for it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:87
verses.text: Now, by the ear of God, we ought, according to a general rule of interpretation, to understand not a bodily member, but the power whereby He heareth; and so (not to repeat this often) by whatever members of His are mentioned, which in us are visible and bodily, must be understood powers of operation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:88
verses.text: For we must not suppose it anything bodily, in that the Lord God hears not the sound of the voice, but the preparation of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:89
verses.text: "To judge for the orphan and the humble" : that is, not for him who is conformed to this world, nor for the proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:90
verses.text: For it is one thing to judge the orphan, another to judge for the orphan.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:91
verses.text: He judges the orphan even, who condemns him; but he judges for the orphan, who delivers sentence for him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:92
verses.text: "That man add not further to magnify himself upon earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:93
verses.text: For they are men, of whom it was said, "Place a lawgiver over them, O Lord: let the heathen know that they are men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:94
verses.text: But he too, who in this same passage is understood to be placed over them, will be man, of whom it is now said, "That man add not further to magnify himself upon earth:" namely, when the Son of Man shall come to judge for the orphan, who hath put off from himself the old man, and thus, as it were, buried his father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:95
verses.text: After the hidden things then of the Son, of which, in this Psalm, many things have been said, will come the manifest things of the Son, of which a little has been now said at the end of the same Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:96
verses.text: But the title is given from the former, which here occupy the larger portion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:97
verses.text: Indeed, the very day of the Lord's advent may be rightly numbered among the hidden things of the Son, although the very presence of the Lord itself will be manifest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:98
verses.text: For of that day it is said, that no man knoweth it, neither angels, nor powers, nor the Son of man What then so hidden, as that which is said to be hidden even to the Judge Himself, not as regards knowledge, but disclosure? But concerning the hidden things of the Son, even if any one would not wish to understand the Son of God, but of David himself, to whose name the whole Psalter is attributed, for the Psalms we know are called the Psalms of David, let him give ear to those words in which it is said to the Lord, "Have mercy on us, O Son of David:"  and so even in this manner let him understand the same Lord Christ, concerning whose hidden things is the inscription of this Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:99
verses.text: For so likewise is it said by the Angel: "God shall give unto Him the throne of His father David".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:100
verses.text: Nor to this understanding of it is the sentence opposed in which the same Lord asks of the Jews, "If Christ be the Son of David, how then doth he in spirit call Him Lord, saying, The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit Thou on my right hand, until I put Thine enemies under Thy feet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:101
verses.text: For it was said to the unskilled, who although they looked for Christ's coming, yet expected Him as man, not as the Power and Wisdom of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:102
verses.text: He teacheth then, in that place, the most true and pure faith, that He is both the Lord of king David, in that He is the Word in the beginning, God with God, by which all things were made; and Son, in that He was made to him of the seed of David according to the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 10:103
verses.text: For He doth not say, Christ is not David's Son, but if ye already hold that He is his Son, learn how He is his Lord: and do not hold in respect of Christ that He is the Son of Man, for so is He David's Son; and leave out that He is the Son of God, for so is He David's Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:1
verses.text: Psalm XI  To the end, a psalm of David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:2
verses.text: This title does not require a fresh consideration: for the meaning of, "to the end," has already been sufficiently handled Let us then look to the text itself of the Psalm, which to me appears to be sung against the heretics, who, by rehearsing and exaggerating the sins of many in the Church, as if either all or the majority among themselves were righteous, strive to turn and snatch us away from the breasts of the one True Mother Church: affirming that Christ is with them, and warning us as if with piety and earnestness, that by passing over to them we may go over to Christ, whom they falsely declare they have.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:3
verses.text: Now it is known that in prophecy Christ, among the many names in which notice of Him is conveyed in allegory, is also called a mountain We must accordingly answer these people, and say, "I trust in the Lord: how say ye to my soul, Remove into the mountains as a sparrow?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:4
verses.text: I keep to one mountain wherein I trust, how say ye that I should pass over to you, as if there were many Christs? Or if through pride you say that you are mountains, I had indeed need to be a sparrow winged with the powers and commandments of God: but these very things hinder my flying to these mountains, and placing my trust in proud men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:5
verses.text: I have a house where I may rest, in that I trust in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:6
verses.text: For even "the sparrow hath found her a house,"  and, "The Lord hath become a refuge to the poor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:7
verses.text: Let us say then with all confidence, lest while we seek Christ among heretics we lose Him, "In the Lord I trust: how say ye to my soul, Remove into the mountains as a sparrow?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:8
verses.text: "For, lo, sinners have bent the bow, they have prepared their arrows in the quiver, that they may in the obscure moon shoot at the upright in heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:9
verses.text: These be the terrors of those who threaten us as touching sinners, that we may pass over to them as the righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:10
verses.text: "Lo," they say, "the sinners have bent the bow:" the Scriptures, I suppose, by carnal interpretation of which they emit envenomed sentences from them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:11
verses.text: "They have prepared their arrows in the quiver:" the same words, that is, which they will shoot out on the authority of Scripture, they have prepared in the secret place of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:12
verses.text: "That they may in the obscure moon shoot at the upright in heart:" that when they see, from the Church's light being obscured by the multitude of the unlearned and the carnal, that they cannot be convicted, they may corrupt good manners by evil communications But against all these terrors we must say, "In the Lord I trust".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:13
verses.text: Now I remember that I promised to consider in this Psalm with what suitableness the moon signifies the Church There are two probable opinions concerning the moon: but of these which is the true, I suppose it either impossible or very difficult for a man to decide.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:14
verses.text: For when we ask whence the moon has her light, some say that it is her own, but that of her globe half is bright, and half dark: and when she revolves in her own orbit, that part wherein she is bright gradually turns towards the earth, so as that it may be seen by us; and that therefore at first her appearance is as if she were horned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:15
verses.text: According to this opinion the moon in allegory signifies the Church, because in its spiritual part the Church is bright, but in its carnal part is dark: and sometimes the spiritual part is seen by good works, but sometimes it lies hid in the conscience, and is known to God alone, since in the body alone is it seen by men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:16
verses.text: But according to the other opinion also the moon is understood to be the Church, because she has no light of her own, but is lighted by the only-begotten Son of God, who in many places of holy Scripture is allegorically called the Sun Whom certain heretics being ignorant of, and not able to discern Him, endeavour to turn away the minds of the simple to this corporeal and visible sun, which is the common light of the flesh of men and flies, and some they do pervert, who as long as they cannot behold with the mind the inner light of truth, will not be content with the simple Catholic faith; which is the only safety to babes, and by which milk alone they can arrive in assured strength at the firm support of more solid food.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:17
verses.text: Whichever then of these two opinions be the true, the moon in allegory is fitly understood as the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:18
verses.text: Or if in such difficulties as these, troublesome rather than edifying, there be either no satisfaction or no leisure to exercise the mind, or if the mind itself be not capable of it, it is sufficient to regard the moon with ordinary eyes, and not to seek out obscure causes, but with all men to perceive her increasings and fulnesses and wanings; and if she wanes to the end that she may be renewed, even to this rude multitude she sets forth the image of the Church, in which the resurrection of the dead is believed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:19
verses.text: Next we must enquire, what in this Psalm is meant by "the obscure moon," in which sinners have prepared to shoot at the upright in heart? For not in one way only may the moon be said to be obscure: for when her monthly course is finished, and when her brightness is interrupted by a cloud, and when she is eclipsed at the full, the moon may be called obscure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:20
verses.text: It may then be understood first of the persecutors of the Martyrs, for that they wished in the obscure moon to shoot at the upright in heart; whether it be yet in the time of the Church's youth, because she had not yet shone forth in greatness on the earth, and conquered the darkness of heathen superstitions; or by the tongues of blasphemers and such as defame the Christian name, when the earth was as it were beclouded, the moon, that is, the Church, could not be clearly seen; or when by the slaughter of the Martyrs themselves and so great effusion of blood, as by that eclipse and obscuration, wherein the moon seems to exhibit a bloody face, the weak were deterred from the Christian name; in which terror sinners shot out words crafty and sacrilegious to pervert even the upright in heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:21
verses.text: And secondly, it can be understood of these sinners, whom the Church contains, because at that time, taking the opportunity of this moon's obscurity, they committed many crimes, which are now tauntingly objected to us by the heretics, whereas their founders are said to have been guilty of them But howsoever that be which was done in the obscure moon, now that the Catholic name is spread and celebrated throughout the whole world, what concern of mine is it to be disturbed by things unknown? For "in the Lord I trust;" nor do I listen to them that say to my soul, "Remove into the mountains as a sparrow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:22
verses.text: For, lo, sinners have bent the bow, that they may in the obscure moon shoot at the upright in heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:23
verses.text: Or if the moon seem even  now obscure to them, because they would make it uncertain which is the Catholic Church, and they strive to convict her by the sins of those many carnal men whom she contains; what concern is this to him, who says in truth, "In the Lord I trust"? By which word every one shows that he is himself wheat, and endures the chaff with patience unto the time of winnowing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:24
verses.text: "In the Lord," therefore, "I trust".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:25
verses.text: Let them fear who trust in man, and cannot deny that they are of man's party, by whose grey hairs they swear; and when in conversation it is demanded of them, of what communion they are, unless they say that they are of his party, they cannot be recognised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:26
verses.text: Or perhaps you will say that it is written, "Ye shall know them by their works"? I see indeed marvellous works the daily violences of the Circumcelliones, with the bishops and presbyters for their leaders, flying about in every direction, and calling their terrible clubs "Israels;" which men now living daily see and feel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:27
verses.text: But for the times of Macarius, respecting which they raise an invidious cry, most men have not seen them, and no one sees them now: and any Catholic who saw them could say, if he wished to be a servant of God, "In the Lord I trust".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:28
verses.text: Let the Catholic soul then say, "In the Lord I trust; how say ye to my soul, Remove into the mountains as a sparrow? For, lo, the sinners have bent the bow, they have prepared their arrows in the quiver, that they may in the obscure moon shoot at the upright in heart:" and from them let her turn her speech to the Lord and say, "For they have destroyed what Thou hast perfected".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:29
verses.text: And this let her say not against these only, but against all heretics.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:30
verses.text: For they have all, as far as in them lies, destroyed the praise which God hath perfected out of the mouth of babes and sucklings, when they disturb the little ones with vain and scrupulous questions, and suffer them not to be nourished with the milk of faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:31
verses.text: As if then it were said to this soul, why do they say to you, "Remove into the mountains as a sparrow;" why do they frighten you with sinners, who "have bent the bow, to shoot in the obscure moon at the upright in heart"? She answers, Therefore it is they frighten me, "because they have destroyed what Thou hast perfected".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:32
verses.text: Where but in their conventicles, where they nourish not with milk, but kill with poison the babes and ignorant of the interior light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:33
verses.text: "But what hath the Just done?" If Macarius, if Caecilianus, offend you, what hath Christ done to you, who said, "My peace I give unto you, My peace I leave with you;" which ye with your abominable dissensions have violated? What hath Christ done to you? who with such exceeding patience endured His betrayer, as to give to him, as to the other Apostles, the first Eucharist consecrated with His own hands, and blessed with His own mouth What hath Christ done to you? who sent this same betrayer, whom He called a devil, who before betraying the Lord could not show good faith even to the Lord's purse, with the other disciples to preach the kingdom of heaven; that He might show that the gifts of God come to those that with faith receive them, though he, through whom they receive them, be such as Judas was.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:34
verses.text: "The Lord is in His holy temple" , yea in such wise as the Apostle saith, "For the temple of God is holy, which" temple "ye are".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:35
verses.text: "Now if any man shall violate the temple of God, him shall God destroy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:36
verses.text: He violateth the temple of God, who violateth unity: for he "holdeth not the head, from which the whole body fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplieth according to the working after the measure of every part maketh increase of the body to the edifying of itself in love".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:37
verses.text: The Lord is in this His holy temple; which consisteth of His many members, fulfilling each his own separate duties, by love built up into one building.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:38
verses.text: Which temple he violateth, who for the sake of his own pre-eminence separateth himself from the Catholic society.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:39
verses.text: "The Lord is in His holy temple; the Lord, His seat is in heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:40
verses.text: If you take heaven to be the just man, as you take the earth to be the sinner, to whom it was said, "Earth thou art, and unto earth shalt thou go;" the words, "The Lord is in His holy temple" you will understand to be repeated, whilst it is said, "The Lord, His seat is in heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:41
verses.text: "His eyes look upon the poor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:42
verses.text: His to Whom the poor man hath been left, and Who hath been made a refuge to the poor And therefore all the seditions and tumults within these nets, until they be drawn to shore, concerning which heretics upbraid us to their own ruin and our correction, are caused by those men, who will not be Christ's poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:43
verses.text: But do they turn away God's eyes from such as would be so? "For His eyes look upon the poor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:44
verses.text: Is it to be feared lest, in the crowd of the rich, He may not be able to see the few poor, whom He brings up in safe keeping in the bosom of the Catholic Church? "His eyelids question the sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:45
verses.text: Here by that rule I would wish to take "the sons of men" of those that from old men have been regenerated by faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:46
verses.text: For these, by certain obscure passages of Scripture, as it were the closed eyes of God, are exercised that they may seek: and again, by certain clear passages, as it were the open eyes of God, are enlightened that they may rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:47
verses.text: And this frequent closing and opening in the holy Books are as it were the eyelids of God; which question, that is, which try the "sons of men;" who are neither wearied with the obscurity of the matter, but exercised; nor puffed up by knowledge, but confirmed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:48
verses.text: "The Lord questioneth the righteous and ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:49
verses.text: Why then do we fear lest the ungodly should be any hurt to us, if so be they do with insincere heart share the sacraments with us, seeing that He "questioneth the righteous and the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:50
verses.text: "But whoso loveth iniquity, hateth his own soul:" that is, not him who believeth God, and putteth not his hope in man, but only his own soul doth the lover of iniquity hurt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:51
verses.text: "He shall rain snares upon the sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:52
verses.text: If by clouds are understood prophets generally, whether good or bad, who are also called false prophets: false prophets are so ordered by the Lord God, that by them He may rain snares upon sinners For no one, but the sinner, falls into a following of them, whether by way of preparation for the last punishment, if he shall choose to persevere in sin; or to dissuade from pride, if in time he shall come to seek God with a more sincere intent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:53
verses.text: But if by clouds are understood good and true prophets only; by these too it is clear that God raineth snares upon sinners, although by them He watereth also the godly unto fruitfulness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:54
verses.text: "To some," saith the Apostle, "we are the savour of life unto life; to some the savour of death unto death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:55
verses.text: For not prophets only, but all who with the word of God water souls, may be called clouds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:56
verses.text: Who when they are understood amiss, God raineth snares upon sinners; but when they are understood aright, He maketh the hearts of the godly and believing fruitful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:57
verses.text: As, for instance, the passage, "and they two shall be in one flesh," if one interpret it with an eye to lust, He raineth a snare upon the sinner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:58
verses.text: But if you understand it, as he who says, "But I speak concerning Christ and the Church," He raineth a shower on the fertile soil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:59
verses.text: Now both are effected by the same cloud, that is, holy Scripture.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:60
verses.text: Again the Lord says, "Not that which goeth into your mouth defileth you, but that which cometh out".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:61
verses.text: The sinner hears this, and makes ready his palate for gluttony: the righteous hears it, and is guarded against the superstitious distinction in meats.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:62
verses.text: Here then also out of the same cloud of Scripture, according to the several desert of each, upon the sinner the rain of snares, upon the righteous the rain of fruitfulness, is poured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:63
verses.text: "Fire and brimstone and the blast of the tempest is the portion of their cup".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:64
verses.text: This is their punishment and end, by whom the name of God is blasphemed; that first they should be wasted by the fire of their own lusts, then by the ill savour of their evil deeds cast off from the company of the blessed, at last carried away and overwhelmed suffer penalties unspeakable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:65
verses.text: For this is the portion of their cup: as of the righteous, "Thy cup inebriating how excellent is it! for they shall be inebriated with the richness of Thine house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:66
verses.text: Now I suppose a cup is mentioned for this reason, that we should not suppose that anything is done by God's providence, even in the very punishments of sinners, beyond moderation and measure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:67
verses.text: And therefore as if he were giving a reason why this should be, he added, "For the Lord is righteous, and hath loved righteousnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:68
verses.text: The plural not without meaning, but only because he speaks of men, is as that righteousnesses be understood to be used for righteous men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:69
verses.text: For in many righteous men there seem, so to say, to be righteousnesses, whereas there is one only righteousness of God whereof they all participate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:70
verses.text: Like as when one face looks upon many mirrors, what in it is one only, is by those many mirrors reflected manifoldly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:71
verses.text: Wherefore he recurs to the singular, saying, "His face hath seen equity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:72
verses.text: Perhaps, "His face hath seen equity," is as if it were said, Equity hath been seen in His face, that is, in knowledge of Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:73
verses.text: For God's face is the power by which He is made known to them that are worthy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:74
verses.text: Or at least, "His face hath seen equity," because He doth not allow Himself to be known by the evil, but by the good; and this is equity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:75
verses.text: But if any one would understand the moon of the synagogue, let him refer the Psalm to the Lord's passion, and of the Jews say, "For they have destroyed what Thou hast perfected;" and of the Lord Himself, "But what hath the Just done?" whom they accused as the destroyer of the Law: whose precepts, by their corrupt living, and by despising them, and by setting up their own, they had destroyed, so that the Lord Himself may speak as Man, as He is wont, saying, "In the Lord I trust; how say ye to my soul, Remove into the mountains as a sparrow?" by reason, that is, of the fear of those who desire to apprehend and crucify Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:76
verses.text: Since the interpretation is not unreasonable of sinners wishing to "shoot at the upright in heart," that is, those who believed in Christ, "in the obscure moon," that is, the Synagogue filled with sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:77
verses.text: To this too the words, "The Lord is in His holy temple; the Lord, His seat is in heaven," are suitable; that is, the Word in Man, or the very Son of Man who is in heaven "His eyes look upon the poor;" either on to Him whom He assumed as God, or for whom He suffered as Man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:78
verses.text: "His eyelids question the sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:79
verses.text: The closing and opening of the eyes, which is probably meant by the word eyelids, we may take to be His death and resurrection, whereby He tried the sons of men His disciples, terrified at His passion, and gladdened by the resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:80
verses.text: "The Lord questioneth the righteous and ungodly," even now from out of Heaven governing the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:81
verses.text: "But whoso loveth iniquity, hateth his own soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:82
verses.text: Why it is so, what follows teaches us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 11:83
verses.text: For "He shall rain snares upon the sinners:" which is to be taken according to the exposition above given, and so on with all the rest to the end of the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:1
verses.text: Psalm XII  To the end, for the eighth, a psalm of David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:2
verses.text: It has been said on the sixth Psalm, that "the eighth" may be taken as the day of judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:3
verses.text: "For the eighth" may also be taken "for the eternal age;" for that after the time present, which is a cycle of seven days, it shall be given to the Saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:4
verses.text: "Save me, O Lord, for the holy hath failed;" that is, is not found: as we speak when we say, Corn fails, or, Money fails.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:5
verses.text: "For the truths have been minished from among the sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:6
verses.text: The truth is one, whereby holy souls are enlightened: but forasmuch as there are many souls, there may be said in them to be many truths: as in mirrors there are seen many reflections from one face.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:7
verses.text: "He hath talked vanity each man to his neighbour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:8
verses.text: By neighbour we must understand every man: for that there is no one with whom we should work evil; "and the love of our neighbour worketh no evil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:9
verses.text: "Deceitful lips, with a heart and a heart they have spoken evil things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:10
verses.text: The repetition, "with a heart and a heart," signifies a double heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:11
verses.text: "May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:12
verses.text: He says "all," that no one may suppose himself excepted: as the Apostle says, "Upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and of the Greek".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:13
verses.text: "The tongue speaking great things:" the proud tongue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:14
verses.text: "Who have said, We will magnify our tongue, our lips are our own, who is Lord over us?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:15
verses.text: Proud hypocrites are meant, putting confidence in their speech to deceive men, and not submitting themselves to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:16
verses.text: "Because of the wretchedness of the needy and the sighing of the poor, now I will arise, saith the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:17
verses.text: For so the Lord Himself in the Gospel pitied His people, because they had no ruler, when they could well obey.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:18
verses.text: Whence too it is said in the Gospel, "The harvest is plenteous, but the labourers are few".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:19
verses.text: But this must be taken as spoken in the person of God the Father, who, because of the needy and the poor, that is, who in need and poverty were lacking spiritual good things, vouchsafed to send His own Son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:20
verses.text: From thence begins His sermon on the mount to Matthew, where He says, "Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:21
verses.text: "I will place in salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:22
verses.text: He does not say what He would place: but, "in salvation," must be understood as, in Christ; according to that, "For mine eyes have seen Thy salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:23
verses.text: And hence He is understood to have placed in Him what appertains to the taking away the wretchedness of the needy, and the comforting the sighing of the poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:24
verses.text: "I will deal confidently in Him:" according to that in the Gospel, "For He taught them as one having authority, and not as their scribes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:25
verses.text: "The words of the Lord" are "pure words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:26
verses.text: This is in the person of the Prophet himself, "The words of the Lord" are "pure words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:27
verses.text: He says "pure," without the alloy of pretence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:28
verses.text: For many preach the truth impurely; for they sell it for the bribe of the advantages of this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:29
verses.text: Of such the Apostle says, that they declared Christ not purely.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:30
verses.text: "Silver tried by the fire for the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:31
verses.text: These words of the Lord by means of tribulations approved to sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:32
verses.text: "Purified seven times:" by the fear of God, by godliness, by knowledge, by might, by counsel, by understanding, by wisdom For seven steps also of beatitude there are, which the Lord goes over, according to Matthew, in the same sermon which He spake on the Mount, "Blessed" are "the poor in spirit, blessed the meek, blessed they that mourn, blessed they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness, blessed the merciful, blessed the pure in heart, blessed the peacemakers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:33
verses.text: Of which seven sentences, it may be observed how all that long sermon was spoken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:34
verses.text: For the eighth where it is said, "Blessed" are "they which suffer persecution for righteousness' sake," denotes the fire itself, whereby the silver is proved seven times.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:35
verses.text: And at the termination of this sermon it is said, "For He taught them as one having authority, and not as their scribes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:36
verses.text: Which refers to that which is said in this Psalm, "I deal confidently in Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:37
verses.text: "Thou, O Lord, shalt preserve us, and keep us from this generation to eternity" : here as needy and poor, there as wealthy and rich.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:38
verses.text: "The ungodly walk in a circle round about" : that is, in the desire of things temporal, which revolves as a wheel in a repeated circle of seven days; and therefore they do not arrive at the eighth, that is, at eternity, for which this Psalm is entitled So too it is said by Solomon, "For the wise king is the winnower of the ungodly, and he bringeth on them the wheel of the wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:39
verses.text: —After Thine height Thou hast multiplied the sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:40
verses.text: For there is in temporal things too a multiplication, which turns away from the unity of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:41
verses.text: Hence "the corruptible body weigheth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle presseth down the mind that museth upon many things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 12:42
verses.text: But the righteous are multiplied "after the height of God," when "they shall go from strength to strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:1
verses.text: Psalm XII  Unto the end, a psalm of David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:2
verses.text: "For Christ is the end of the law to every one that believeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:3
verses.text: "How long, O Lord, wilt Thou forget me unto the end?"  that is, put me off as to spiritually understanding Christ, who is the Wisdom of God, and the true end of all the aim of the soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:4
verses.text: "How long dost Thou turn away Thy face from me?" As God doth not forget, so neither doth He turn His face away: but Scripture speaks after our manner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:5
verses.text: Now God is said to turn away His face, when He doth not give to the soul, which as yet hath not the pure eye of the mind, the knowledge of Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:6
verses.text: "How long shall I place counsel in my soul?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:7
verses.text: There is no need of counsel but in adversity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:8
verses.text: Therefore "How long shall I place counsel in my soul?" is as if it were said, How long shall I be in adversity? Or at least it is an answer, so that the meaning is this, So long, O Lord, wilt Thou forget me to the end, and so long turn away Thy face from me, until I shall place counsel in mine own soul: so that except a man place counsel in his own soul to work mercy perfectly, God will not direct him to the end, nor give him that full knowledge of Himself, which is "face to face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:9
verses.text: "Sorrow in my heart through the day?" How long shall I have, is understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:10
verses.text: And "through the day" signifies continuance, so that day is taken for time: from which as each one longs to be free, he has sorrow in his heart, making entreaty to rise to things eternal, and not endure man's day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:11
verses.text: "How long shall mine enemy be exalted over me?" either the devil, or carnal habit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:12
verses.text: "Look on me, and hear me, O Lord my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:13
verses.text: "Look on me," refers to what was said, "How long" dost "Thou turn away Thy face from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:14
verses.text: "Hear," refers to what was said, "How long wilt Thou forget me to the end? Lighten mine eyes, that I sleep not in death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:15
verses.text: The eyes of the heart must be understood, that they be not closed by the pleasurable eclipse of sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:16
verses.text: "Lest at any time mine enemy say, I have prevailed against him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:17
verses.text: The devil's mockery is to be feared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:18
verses.text: "They that trouble me will exult, if I be moved;" the devil and his angels; who exulted not over that righteous man, Job, when they troubled him; because he was not moved, that is, did not draw back from the stedfastness of his faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:19
verses.text: "But I have hoped in Thy mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:20
verses.text: Because this very thing, that a man be not moved, and that he abide fixed in the Lord, he should not attribute to self: lest when he glories that he hath not been moved, he be moved by this very pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:21
verses.text: "My heart shall exult in Thy salvation;" in Christ, in the Wisdom of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:22
verses.text: "I will sing to the Lord who hath given me good things;" spiritual good things, not belonging to man's day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:23
verses.text: "And I will chant to the name of the Lord most high" ; that is, I give thanks with joy, and in most due order employ my body, which is the song of the spiritual soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 13:24
verses.text: But if any distinction is to be marked here, "I will sing" with the heart, "I will chant" with my works; "to the Lord," that which He alone seeth, but "to the name of the Lord," that which is known among men, which is serviceable not for Him, but for us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:1
verses.text: Psalm XIV  To the end, a psalm of David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:2
verses.text: What "to the end" means, must not be too often repeated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:3
verses.text: "For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth;" as the Apostle saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:4
verses.text: We believe on Him, when we begin to enter on the good road: we shall see Him, when we shall get to the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:5
verses.text: And therefore is He the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:6
verses.text: "The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:7
verses.text: For not even have certain sacrilegious and abominable philosophers, who entertain perverse and false notions of God, dared to say, "There is no God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:8
verses.text: Therefore it is, hath said "in his heart;" for that no one dares to say it, even if he has dared to think it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:9
verses.text: "They are corrupt, and become abominable in their affections:" that is, whilst they love this world and love not God; these are the affections which corrupt the soul, and so blind it, that the fool can even say, "in his heart, There is no God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:10
verses.text: For as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:11
verses.text: "There is none that doeth goodness, no not up to one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:12
verses.text: "Up to one," can be understood either with that one, so that no man be understood: or besides one, that the Lord Christ may be excepted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:13
verses.text: As we say, This field is up to the sea; we do not of course reckon the sea together with the field.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:14
verses.text: And this is the better interpretation, so that none be understood to have done goodness up to Christ; for that no man can do goodness, except He shall have shown it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:15
verses.text: And that is true; for until a man know the one God, he cannot do goodness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:16
verses.text: "The Lord from heaven looked out upon the sons of men, to see if there be one understanding, or seeking after God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:17
verses.text: It may be interpreted, upon the Jews; as he may have given them the more honourable name of the sons of men, by reason of their worship of the One God, in comparison with the Gentiles; of whom I suppose it was said above, "The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:18
verses.text: Now the Lord looks out, that He may see, by His holy souls: which is the meaning of, "from heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:19
verses.text: For by Himself nothing is hid from Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:20
verses.text: "All have gone out of the way, they have together become useless:" that is, the Jews have become as the Gentiles, who were spoken of above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:21
verses.text: "There is none that doeth good, no not up to one" , must be interpreted as above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:22
verses.text: "Their throat is an open sepulchre".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:23
verses.text: Either the voracity of the ever open palate is signified: or allegorically those who slay, and as it were devour those they have slain, into whom they instil the disorder of their own conversation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:24
verses.text: Like to which with the contrary meaning is that which was said to Peter, "Kill and eat;" that he should convert the Gentiles to his own faith and good conversation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:25
verses.text: "With their tongues they have dealt craftily".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:26
verses.text: Flattery is the companion of the greedy and of all bad men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:27
verses.text: "The poison of asps is under their lips".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:28
verses.text: By "poison," he means deceit; and "of asps," because they will not hear the precepts of the law, as asps "will not hear the voice of the charmer;" which is said more clearly in another Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:29
verses.text: "Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness:" this is, "the poison of asps".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:30
verses.text: "Their feet are swift to shed blood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:31
verses.text: He here shows forth the habit of ill doing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:32
verses.text: "Destruction and unhappiness" are "in their ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:33
verses.text: For all the ways of evil men are full of toil and misery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:34
verses.text: Hence the Lord cries out, "Come unto Me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:35
verses.text: Take My yoke upon you, and learn of Me, for I am meek and lowly in heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:36
verses.text: For My yoke is easy and My burden light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:37
verses.text: "And the way of peace have they not known:" that way, namely, which the Lord, as I said, mentions, in the easy yoke and light burden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:38
verses.text: "There is no fear of God before their eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:39
verses.text: These do not say, "There is no God;" but yet they do not fear God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:40
verses.text: "Shall not all, who work iniquity, know?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:41
verses.text: He threatens the judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:42
verses.text: "Who devour My people as the food of bread:" that is, daily.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:43
verses.text: For the food of bread is daily food.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:44
verses.text: Now they devour the people, who serve their own ends out of them, not referring their ministry to the glory of God, and the salvation of those over whom they are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:45
verses.text: "They have not called upon the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:46
verses.text: For he doth not really call upon Him, who longs for such things as are displeasing to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:47
verses.text: "There they trembled for fear, where no fear was" : that is, for the loss of things temporal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:48
verses.text: For they said, "If we let Him thus alone, all men will believe on Him; and the Romans will come, and take away both our place and nation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:49
verses.text: They feared to lose an earthly kingdom, where no fear was; and they lost the kingdom of heaven, which they ought to have feared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:50
verses.text: And this must be understood of all temporal goods, the loss of which when men fear, they come not to things eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:51
verses.text: "For God is in the just generation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:52
verses.text: It refers to what went before, so that the sense is, "shall not all they that work iniquity know that the Lord is in the just generation;" that is, He is not in them who love the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:53
verses.text: For it is unjust to leave the Maker of the worlds, and "serve the creature more than the Creator".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:54
verses.text: Ye have shamed the counsel of the poor, for the Lord is his hope" : that is, ye have despised the humble coming of the Son of God, because ye saw not in Him the pomp of the world: that they, whom he was calling, should put their hope in God alone, not in the things that pass away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:55
verses.text: "Who will give salvation to Israel out of Sion?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:56
verses.text: Who but He whose humiliation ye have despised? is understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:57
verses.text: For He will come in glory to the judgment of the quick and the dead, and the kingdom of the just: that, forasmuch as in that humble coming "blindness hath happened in part unto Israel, that the fulness of the Gentiles might enter in," in that other should happen what follows, "and so all Israel should be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:58
verses.text: For the Apostle too takes that testimony of Isaiah, where it is said, "There shall come out of Sion He who shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob:" for the Jews, as it is here, "Who shall give salvation to Israel out of Sion?" "When the Lord shall turn away the captivity of His people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 14:59
verses.text: It is a repetition, as is usual: for I suppose, "Israel shall be glad," is the same as, "Jacob shall rejoice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:1
verses.text: Psalm XV  A psalm of David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:2
verses.text: Touching this title there is no question.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:3
verses.text: "O Lord who shall sojourn in Thy tabernacle?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:4
verses.text: Although tabernacle be sometimes used even for an everlasting habitation: yet when tabernacle is taken in its proper meaning, it is a thing of war.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:5
verses.text: Hence soldiers are called tent-fellows, as having their tents together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:6
verses.text: This sense is assisted by the words, "Who shall sojourn?" For we war with the devil for a time, and then we need a tabernacle wherein we may refresh ourselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:7
verses.text: Which specially points out the faith of the temporal Dispensation, which was wrought for us in time through the Incarnation of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:8
verses.text: "And who shall rest in Thy holy mountain?" Here perhaps he signifies at once the eternal habitation itself,  that we should understand by "mountain" the supereminence of the love of Christ in life eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:9
verses.text: "He who walketh without stain, and worketh righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:10
verses.text: Here he has laid down the proposition; in what follows he sets it forth in detail.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:11
verses.text: "Who speaketh the truth in his heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:12
verses.text: For some have truth on their lips, and not in their heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:13
verses.text: As if one should deceitfully point out a road, knowing that there were robbers there, and should say, If you go this way, you will be safe from robbers; and it should turn out that in fact there were no robbers found there: he has spoken the truth, but not in his heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:14
verses.text: For he supposed it to be otherwise, and spoke the truth in ignorance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:15
verses.text: Therefore it is not enough to speak the truth, unless it be so also in heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:16
verses.text: "Who hath practised no deceit in his tongue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:17
verses.text: Deceit is practised with the tongue, when one thing is professed with the mouth, another concealed in the breast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:18
verses.text: "Nor done evil to his neighbour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:19
verses.text: It is well known that by "neighbour," every man should be understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:20
verses.text: "And hath not entertained slander against his neighbour," that is, hath not readily or rashly given credence to an accuser.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:21
verses.text: "The malicious one hath been brought to nought in his sight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:22
verses.text: This is perfection, that the malicious one have no force against a man; and that this be "in his sight;" that is, that he know most surely that the malicious is not, save when the mind turns itself away from the eternal and immutable form of her own Creator to the form of the creature, which was made out of nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:23
verses.text: "But those that fear the Lord, He glorifieth:" the Lord Himself, that is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:24
verses.text: Now "the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:25
verses.text: As then the things above belong to the perfect, so what he is now going to say belongs to beginners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:26
verses.text: "Who sweareth unto his neighbour, and deceiveth him not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:27
verses.text: "Who hath not given his money upon usury, and hath not taken rewards against the innocent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:28
verses.text: These are no great things: but he who is not able to do even this, much less able is he to speak the truth in his heart, and to practise no deceit in his tongue, but as the truth is in the heart, so to profess and have it in his mouth, "yea, yea; nay, nay;"  and to do no evil to his neighbour, that is, to any man; and to entertain no slander against his neighbour: all which are the virtues of the perfect, in whose sight the malicious one hath been brought to nought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:29
verses.text: Yet he concludes even these lesser things thus, "Whoso doeth these things shall not be moved for ever:" that is, he shall attain unto those greater things, wherein is great and unshaken stability.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:30
verses.text: For even the very tenses are, perhaps not without cause, so varied, as that in the conclusion above the past tense should be used, but in this the future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 15:31
verses.text: For there it was said, "The malicious one hath been brought to nought in his sight:" but here, "shall not be moved for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:1
verses.text: Psalm XVI  The inscription of the title, of David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:2
verses.text: Our King in this Psalm speaks in the character of the human nature He assumed, of whom the royal title at the time of His passion was eminently set forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:3
verses.text: Now He saith as follows; "Preserve me, O Lord, for in Thee have I hoped" : "I have said to the Lord, Thou art my God, for Thou requirest not my goods" : for with my goods Thou dost not look to be made blessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:4
verses.text: "To the saints who are on His earth" : to the saints who have placed their hope in the land of the living, the citizens of the heavenly Jerusalem, whose spiritual conversation is, by the anchor of hope, fixed in that country, which is rightly called God's earth; although as yet in this earth too they be conversant in the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:5
verses.text: "He hath wonderfully fulfilled all My wishes in them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:6
verses.text: To those saints then He hath wonderfully fulfilled all My wishes in their advancement, whereby they have perceived, how both the humanity of My divinity hath profited them that I might die, and the divinity of the humanity that I might rise again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:7
verses.text: "Their infirmities have been multiplied" : their infirmities have been multiplied not for their destruction, but that they might long for the Physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:8
verses.text: "Afterwards they made haste".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:9
verses.text: Accordingly after infirmities multiplied they made haste, that they might be healed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:10
verses.text: "I will not gather together their assemblies by blood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:11
verses.text: For their assemblies shall not be carnal, nor will I gather them together as one propitiated by the blood of cattle "Nor will I be mindful of their names within My lips".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:12
verses.text: But by a spiritual change what they have been shall be forgotten; nor by Me shall they be any more called either sinners, or enemies, or men; but righteous, and My brethren, and sons of God through My peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:13
verses.text: "The Lord is the portion of Mine inheritance, and of My cup".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:14
verses.text: For together with Me they shall possess the inheritance, the Lord Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:15
verses.text: Let others choose for themselves portions, earthly and temporal, to enjoy: the portion of the Saints is the Lord eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:16
verses.text: Let others drink of deadly pleasures, the portion of My cup is the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:17
verses.text: In that I say, "Mine," I include the Church: for where the Head is, there is the body also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:18
verses.text: For into the inheritance will I gather together their assemblies, and by the inebriation of the cup I will forget their old names.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:19
verses.text: "Thou art He who will restore to Me My inheritance:" that to these too, whom I free, may be known "the glory wherein I was with Thee before the world was made".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:20
verses.text: For Thou wilt not restore to Me that which I never lost, but Thou wilt restore to these, who have lost it, the knowledge of that glory: in whom because I am, Thou wilt restore to Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:21
verses.text: "The lines have fallen to me in glorious places".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:22
verses.text: The boundaries of my possession have fallen in Thy glory as it were by lot, like as God is the possession of the Priests and Levites "For Mine inheritance is glorious to Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:23
verses.text: "For Mine inheritance is glorious," not to all, but to them that see; in whom because I am, "it is to Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:24
verses.text: "I will bless the Lord, who hath given Me understanding" : whereby this inheritance may be seen and possessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:25
verses.text: "Yea moreover too even unto night my reins have chastened Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:26
verses.text: Yea besides understanding, even unto death, My inferior part, the assumption of flesh, hath instructed Me, that I might experience the darkness of mortality, which that understanding hath not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:27
verses.text: "I foresaw the Lord in My sight always".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:28
verses.text: But coming into things that pass away, I removed not Mine eye from Him who abideth ever, foreseeing this, that to Him I should return after passing through the things temporal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:29
verses.text: "For He is on My right hand, that I should not be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:30
verses.text: For He favoureth Me, that I should abide fixedly in Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:31
verses.text: "Wherefore My heart was glad, and My tongue exulted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:32
verses.text: Wherefore both in My thoughts is gladness, and in my words exultation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:33
verses.text: "Moreover too My flesh shall rest in hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:34
verses.text: Moreover too My flesh shall not fail unto destruction, but shall sleep in hope of the resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:35
verses.text: "For Thou wilt not leave My soul in hell".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:36
verses.text: For Thou wilt neither give My soul for a possession to those parts below.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:37
verses.text: "Neither wilt Thou grant Thine Holy One to see corruption".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:38
verses.text: Neither wilt Thou suffer that sanctified body, whereby others are to be also sanctified, to see corruption.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:39
verses.text: "Thou hast made known to Me the paths of life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:40
verses.text: Thou hast made known through Me the paths of humiliation, that men might return to life, from whence they fell through pride; in whom because I am, "Thou hast made known to Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:41
verses.text: "Thou wilt fill Me with joy with Thy countenance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:42
verses.text: Thou wilt fill them with joy, that they should seek nothing further, when they shall see Thee "face to face;" in whom because I am, "Thou wilt fill Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:43
verses.text: "Pleasure is at Thy right hand even to the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 16:44
verses.text: Pleasure is in Thy favour and mercy in this life's journey, leading on even to the end of the glory of Thy countenance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:1
verses.text: Psalm XVII  A prayer of David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:2
verses.text: This prayer must be assigned to the Person of the Lord, with the addition of the Church, which is His body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:3
verses.text: "Hear My righteousness, O God, consider My supplication".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:4
verses.text: "Hearken unto My prayer, not in deceitful lips:" not going forth to Thee in deceitful lips.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:5
verses.text: "Let My judgment from Thy countenance go forth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:6
verses.text: From the enlightening of the knowledge of Thee, let Me judge truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:7
verses.text: Or at least, let My judgment go forth, not in deceitful lips, from Thy countenance, that is, that I may not in judging utter aught else than I understand in Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:8
verses.text: "Let Mine eyes see equity:" the eyes, of course, of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:9
verses.text: "Thou hast proved and visited Mine heart in the night-season".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:10
verses.text: For this Mine heart hath been proved by the visitation of tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:11
verses.text: "Thou hast examined Me by fire, and iniquity hath not been found in Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:12
verses.text: Now not night only, in that it is wont to disturb, but fire also, in that it burns, is this tribulation to be called; whereby when I was examined I was found righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:13
verses.text: "That My mouth may not speak the works of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:14
verses.text: That nothing may proceed out of My mouth, but what relates to Thy glory and praise; not to the works of men, which they do beside Thy will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:15
verses.text: "Because of the words of Thy lips".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:16
verses.text: Because of the words of Thy peace, or of Thy prophets.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:17
verses.text: "I have kept hard ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:18
verses.text: I have kept the toilsome ways of human mortality and suffering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:19
verses.text: "To perfect My steps in Thy paths".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:20
verses.text: That the love of the Church might be perfected in the strait ways, whereby she arrives at Thy rest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:21
verses.text: "That My footsteps be not moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:22
verses.text: That the signs of My way, which, like footsteps, have been imprinted on the Sacraments and Apostolical writings, be not moved, that they may mark them who would follow Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:23
verses.text: Or at least, that I may still abide fixedly in eternity, after that I have accomplished the hard ways, and have finished My steps in the straits of Thy paths.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:24
