verses.text: "I have cried out, for Thou hast heard Me, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:25
verses.text: With a free and strong effort have I directed My prayers unto Thee: for that I might have this power, Thou hast heard Me when praying more weakly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:26
verses.text: "Incline Thine ear to Me, and hear My words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:27
verses.text: Let not Thy hearing forsake My humiliation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:28
verses.text: "Make Thy mercies marvellous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:29
verses.text: Let not Thy mercies be disesteemed, lest they be loved too little.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:30
verses.text: "Who savest them that hope in Thee from such as resist Thy right hand:" from such as resist the favour, whereby Thou favourest Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:31
verses.text: "Keep Me, O Lord, as the apple of Thine eye" : which seems very little and minute: yet by it is the sight of the eye directed, whereby the light is distinguished from the darkness; as by Christ's humanity, the divinity of the Judgment distinguishing between the righteous and sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:32
verses.text: "In the covering of Thy wings protect Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:33
verses.text: In the defence of Thy love and mercy protect Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:34
verses.text: "From the face of the ungodly who have troubled Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:35
verses.text: "Mine enemies have compassed about My soul;" "they have shut up their own fat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:36
verses.text: They have been covered with their own gross joy, after that their desire hath been satiated with wickedness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:37
verses.text: "Their mouth hath spoken pride".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:38
verses.text: And therefore their mouth spoke pride, in saying, "Hail, King of the Jews," and other like words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:39
verses.text: "Casting Me forth they have now compassed Me about".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:40
verses.text: Casting Me forth outside the city, they have now compassed Me about on the Cross.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:41
verses.text: "Their eyes they have determined to turn down on the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:42
verses.text: The bent of their heart they have determined to turn down on these earthly things: deeming Him, who was slain, to endure a mighty evil, and themselves, that slew Him, none.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:43
verses.text: "As a lion ready for prey, have they taken Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:44
verses.text: They have taken Me, like that adversary who "walketh about, seeking whom he may devour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:45
verses.text: "And as a lion's whelp dwelling in secret places".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:46
verses.text: And as his whelp, the people to whom it was said, "Ye are of your father the devil:" meditating on the snares, whereby they might circumvent and destroy the just One.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:47
verses.text: "Arise, O Lord, prevent them, and cast them down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:48
verses.text: Arise, O Lord, Thou whom they suppose to be asleep, and regardless of men's iniquities; be they blinded before by their own malice, that vengeance may prevent their deed; and so cast them down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:49
verses.text: "Deliver My soul from the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:50
verses.text: Deliver My soul, by restoring Me after the death, which the ungodly have inflicted on Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:51
verses.text: "Thy weapon: from the enemies of Thine hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:52
verses.text: For My soul is Thy weapon, which Thy hand, that is, Thy eternal Power, hath taken to subdue thereby the kingdoms of iniquity, and divide the righteous from the ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:53
verses.text: This weapon then "deliver from the enemies of Thine hand," that is, of Thy Power, that is, from Mine enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:54
verses.text: "Destroy them, O Lord, from off the earth, scatter them in their life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:55
verses.text: O Lord, destroy them from off the earth, which they inhabit, scatter them throughout the world in this life, which only they think their life, who despair of life eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:56
verses.text: "And by Thy hidden things their belly hath been filled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:57
verses.text: Now not only this visible punishment shall overtake them, but also their memory hath been filled with sins, which as darkness are hidden from the light of Thy truth, that they should forget God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:58
verses.text: "They have been filled with swine's flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:59
verses.text: They have been filled with uncleanness, treading under foot the pearls of God's words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:60
verses.text: "And they have left the rest to their babes:" crying out, "This sin be upon us and upon our children".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:61
verses.text: "But I shall appear in Thy righteousness in Thy sight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:62
verses.text: But I, Who have not appeared to them that, with their filthy and darkened heart, cannot see the light of wisdom, "I shall appear in Thy righteousness in Thy sight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:63
verses.text: "I shall be satiated, when Thy glory shall be manifested".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:64
verses.text: And when they have been satiated with their uncleanness, that they could not know Me, I shall be satiated, when Thy glory shall be manifested, in them that know Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:65
verses.text: In that verse indeed where it is said, "filled with swine's flesh," some copies have, "filled with children:" for from the ambiguity of the Greek a double interpretation has resulted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 17:66
verses.text: Now by "children" we understand works; and as by good children, good works, so by evil, evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:1
verses.text: Psalm XVIII  To the end, for the servant of the Lord, David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:2
verses.text: That is, for the strong of hand, Christ in His Manhood "The words of this song which he spoke to the Lord on the day when the Lord delivered him out of the hands of his enemies, and of the hand of Saul; and he said, On the day when the Lord delivered him out of the hands of his enemies and of the hand of Saul:" namely, the king of the Jews, whom they had demanded for themselves For as "David" is said to be by interpretation, strong of hand; so "Saul" is said to be demanding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:3
verses.text: Now it is well known, how that People demanded for themselves a king, and received him for their king, not according to the will of God, but according to their own will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:4
verses.text: Christ, then, and the Church, that is, whole Christ, the Head and the Body, saith here, "I will love Thee, O Lord, My strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:5
verses.text: I will love Thee, O Lord, by whom I am strong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:6
verses.text: "O Lord, My stay, and My refuge, and My deliverer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:7
verses.text: O Lord, who hast stayed Me, because I sought refuge with Thee: and I sought refuge, because Thou hast delivered Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:8
verses.text: "My God is My helper; and I will hope in Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:9
verses.text: My God, who hast first afforded me the help of Thy call, that I might be able to hope in Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:10
verses.text: "My defender, and the horn of My salvation, and My redeemer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:11
verses.text: My defender, because I have not leant upon Myself, lifting up as it were the horn of pride against Thee; but have found Thee a horn indeed, that is, the sure height of salvation: and that I might find it, Thou redeemedst Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:12
verses.text: "With praise will I call upon the Lord, and I shall be safe from Mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:13
verses.text: Seeking not My own but the Lord's glory, I will call upon Him, and there shall be no means whereby the errors of ungodliness can hurt Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:14
verses.text: "The pains of death," that is, of the flesh, have "compassed Me about.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:15
verses.text: And the overflowings of ungodliness have troubled Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:16
verses.text: Ungodly troubles stirred up for a time, like torrents of rain which will soon subside, have come on to trouble Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:17
verses.text: "The pains of hell compassed Me about".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:18
verses.text: Among those that compassed Me about to destroy Me, were pains of envy, which work death, and lead on to the hell of sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:19
verses.text: "The snares of death prevented Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:20
verses.text: They prevented Me, so that they wished to hurt Me first, which shall afterwards be recompensed unto them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:21
verses.text: Now they seize unto destruction such men as they have evilly persuaded by the boast of righteousness: in the name but not in the reality of which they glory against the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:22
verses.text: "And in Mine oppression I called upon the Lord, and cried unto My God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:23
verses.text: And He heard My voice from His holy temple".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:24
verses.text: He heard from My heart, wherein He dwelleth, My voice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:25
verses.text: "And My cry in His sight entered into His ears;" and My cry, which I utter, not in the ears of men, but inwardly before Him Himself, "entered into His ears".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:26
verses.text: "And the earth was moved and trembled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:27
verses.text: When the Son of Man was thus glorified, sinners were moved and trembled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:28
verses.text: "And the foundations of the mountains were troubled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:29
verses.text: And the hopes of the proud, which were in this life, were troubled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:30
verses.text: "And were moved, for God was wroth with them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:31
verses.text: That is, that the hope of temporal goods might have now no more establishment in the hearts of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:32
verses.text: "There went up smoke in His wrath".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:33
verses.text: The tearful supplication of penitents went up, when they came to know God's threatenings against the ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:34
verses.text: "And fire burneth from His face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:35
verses.text: And the ardour of love after repentance burns by the knowledge of Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:36
verses.text: "Coals were kindled from Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:37
verses.text: They, who were already dead, abandoned by the fire of good desire and the light of righteousness, and who remained in coldness and darkness, re-enkindled and enlightened, have come to life again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:38
verses.text: "And He bowed the heaven, and came down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:39
verses.text: And He humbled the just One, that He might descend to men's infirmity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:40
verses.text: "And darkness under His feet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:41
verses.text: And the ungodly, who savour of things earthly, in the darkness of their own malice, knew not Him: for the earth under His feet is as it were His footstool.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:42
verses.text: "And He mounted above the cherubim, and did fly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:43
verses.text: And He was exalted above the fulness of knowledge, that no man should come to Him but by love: for "love is the fulfilling of the law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:44
verses.text: And full soon He showed to His lovers that He is incomprehensible, lest they should suppose that He is comprehended by corporeal imaginations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:45
verses.text: "He flew above the wings of the winds".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:46
verses.text: But that swiftness, whereby He showed Himself to be incomprehensible, is above the powers of souls, whereon as upon wings they raise themselves from earthly fears into the air of liberty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:47
verses.text: "And hath made darkness His hiding place".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:48
verses.text: And hath settled the obscurity of the Sacraments, and the hidden hope in the heart of believers, where He may lie hid, and not abandon them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:49
verses.text: In this darkness too, wherein "we yet walk by faith, and not by sight," as long as "we hope for what we see not, and with patience wait for it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:50
verses.text: "Round about Him is His tabernacle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:51
verses.text: Yet they that believe Him turn to Him and encircle Him; for that He is in the midst of them, since He is equally the friend of all, in whom as in a tabernacle He at this time dwells.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:52
verses.text: "Dark water in clouds of air".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:53
verses.text: Nor let any one on this account, if he understand the Scripture, imagine that he is already in that light, which will be when we shall have come out of faith into sight: for in the prophets and in all the preachers of the word of God there is obscure teaching.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:54
verses.text: "In respect of the brightness in His sight" : in comparison with the brightness, which is in the sight of His manifestation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:55
verses.text: "His clouds have passed over".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:56
verses.text: The preachers of His word are not now bounded by the confines of Judaea, but have passed over to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:57
verses.text: "Hail and coals of fire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:58
verses.text: Reproofs are figured, whereby, as by hail, the hard hearts are bruised: but if a cultivated and genial soil, that is, a godly mind, receive them, the hail's hardness dissolves into water, that is, the terror of the lightning-charged, and as it were frozen, reproof dissolves into satisfying doctrine; and hearts kindled by the fire of love revive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:59
verses.text: All these things in His clouds have passed over to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:60
verses.text: "And the Lord hath thundered from heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:61
verses.text: And in confidence of the Gospel the Lord hath sounded forth from the heart of the just One.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:62
verses.text: "And the Highest gave His voice;" that we might entertain it, and in the depth of human things, might hear things heavenly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:63
verses.text: "And He sent out His arrows, and scattered them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:64
verses.text: And He sent out Evangelists traversing straight paths on the wings of strength, not in their own power, but His by whom they were sent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:65
verses.text: And "He scattered them," to whom they were sent, that to some of them they should be "the savour of life unto life, to others the savour of death unto death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:66
verses.text: "And He multiplied lightnings, and troubled them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:67
verses.text: And He multiplied miracles, and troubled them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:68
verses.text: "And the fountains of water were seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:69
verses.text: And the fountains of water springing up into everlasting life," which were made in the preachers, were seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:70
verses.text: "And the foundations of the round world were revealed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:71
verses.text: And the Prophets, who were not understood, and upon whom was to be built the world of believers in the Lord, were revealed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:72
verses.text: "At Thy chiding, O Lord:" crying out, "The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:73
verses.text: "At the blasting of the breath of Thy displeasure;" saying, "Except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:74
verses.text: "He hath sent down from on high, and hath fetched Me : by calling out of the Gentiles for an inheritance "a glorious Church, not having spot, or wrinkle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:75
verses.text: "He hath taken Me out of the multitude of waters".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:76
verses.text: He hath taken Me out of the multitude of peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:77
verses.text: "He hath delivered Me from My strongest enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:78
verses.text: He hath delivered Me from Mine enemies, who prevailed to the afflicting and overturning of this temporal life of Mine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:79
verses.text: "And from them which hate Me; for they are too strong for Me:" as long as I am under them knowing not God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:80
verses.text: "They have prevented Me in the day of My affliction".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:81
verses.text: They have first injured Me, in the time when I am bearing a mortal and toilsome body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:82
verses.text: "And the Lord hath become My stay".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:83
verses.text: And since the stay of earthly pleasure was disturbed and torn up by the bitterness of misery, the Lord hath become My stay.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:84
verses.text: "And hath brought Me forth into a broad place".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:85
verses.text: And since I was enduring the straits of the flesh, He brought Me forth into the spiritual breadth of faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:86
verses.text: "He hath delivered Me, because He desired Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:87
verses.text: Before that I desired Him, He delivered Me from My most powerful enemies (who were envious of Me when I once desired Him), and from them that hated Me, because I do desire Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:88
verses.text: "And the Lord shall reward Me according to My righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:89
verses.text: And the Lord shall reward Me according to the righteousness of My good will, who first showed mercy, before that I had the good will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:90
verses.text: "And according to the cleanness of My hands He will recompense Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:91
verses.text: And according to the cleanness of My deeds He will recompense Me, who hath given Me to do well by bringing Me forth into the broad place of faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:92
verses.text: "Because I have kept the ways of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:93
verses.text: That the breadth of good works, that are by faith, and the long-suffering of perseverance should follow after.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:94
verses.text: "Nor have I walked impiously apart from My God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:95
verses.text: "For all His judgments are in My sight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:96
verses.text: "For" with persevering contemplation I weigh "all His judgments," that is, the rewards of the righteous, and the punishments of the ungodly, and the scourges of such as are to be chastened, and the trials of such as are to be proved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:97
verses.text: "And I have not cast out His righteousness from Me:" as they do that faint under their burden of them, and return to their own vomit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:98
verses.text: "And I shall be undefiled with Him, and I shall keep Myself from Mine iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:99
verses.text: "And the Lord shall reward Me according to My righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:100
verses.text: Accordingly not only for the breadth of faith, which worketh by love; but also for the length of perseverance, will the Lord reward Me according to My righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:101
verses.text: "And according to the cleanness of My hands in the sight of His eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:102
verses.text: Not as men see, but "in the sight of His eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:103
verses.text: For "the things that are seen are temporal; but the things that are not seen are eternal:" whereto the height of hope appertains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:104
verses.text: "With the holy Thou shalt be holy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:105
verses.text: There is a hidden depth also, wherein Thou art known to be holy with the holy, for that Thou makest holy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:106
verses.text: "And with the harmless Thou shalt be harmless".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:107
verses.text: For Thou harmest no man, but each one is bound by the bands of his own sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:108
verses.text: "And with the chosen Thou shalt be chosen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:109
verses.text: And by him whom Thou choosest, Thou art chosen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:110
verses.text: "And with the froward Thou shalt be froward".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:111
verses.text: And with the froward Thou seemest froward: for they say, "The way of the Lord is not right:" and their way is not right.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:112
verses.text: "For Thou wilt make whole the humble people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:113
verses.text: Now this seems froward to the froward, that Thou wilt make them whole that confess their sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:114
verses.text: "And Thou wilt humble the eyes of the proud".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:115
verses.text: But them that are "ignorant of God's righteousness, and seek to establish their own," Thou wilt humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:116
verses.text: "For thou wilt light My candle, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:117
verses.text: For our light is not from ourselves; but "Thou wilt light my candle, O Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:118
verses.text: O my God, Thou wilt enlighten my darkness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:119
verses.text: For we through our sins are darkness; but "Thou, O my God, wilt enlighten my darkness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:120
verses.text: "For by Thee shall I be delivered from temptation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:121
verses.text: For not by myself, but by Thee, shall I be delivered from temptation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:122
verses.text: "And in my God shall I leap over the wall".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:123
verses.text: And not in myself, but in my God shall I leap over the wall, which sin has raised between men and the heavenly Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:124
verses.text: "My God, His way is undefiled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:125
verses.text: My God cometh not unto men, except they shall have purified the way of faith, whereby He may come to them; for that "His way is undefiled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:126
verses.text: "The words of the Lord have been proved by fire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:127
verses.text: The words of the Lord are tried by the fire of tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:128
verses.text: "He is the Protector of them that hope in Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:129
verses.text: And all that hope not in themselves, but in Him, are not consumed by that same tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:130
verses.text: For hope followeth faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:131
verses.text: "For who is God, but the Lord?"  whom we serve.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:132
verses.text: "And who God, but our God?" And who is God, but the Lord? whom after good service we sons shall possess as the hoped-for inheritance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:133
verses.text: "God, who hath girded me with strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:134
verses.text: God, who hath girded me that I might be strong, lest the loosely flowing folds of desire hinder my deeds and steps.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:135
verses.text: "And hath made my way undefiled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:136
verses.text: And hath made the way of love, whereby I may come to Him, undefiled, as the way of faith is undefiled, whereby He comes to me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:137
verses.text: "Who hath made my feet perfect like harts' feet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:138
verses.text: Who hath made my love perfect to surmount the thorny and dark entanglements of this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:139
verses.text: "And will set me up on high".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:140
verses.text: And will fix my aim on the heavenly habitation, that "I may be filled with all the fulness of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:141
verses.text: "Who teacheth my hands for battle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:142
verses.text: Who teacheth me to work for the overthrow of mine enemies, who strive to shut the kingdom of heaven against us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:143
verses.text: "And Thou hast made mine arms as a bow of steel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:144
verses.text: And Thou hast made my earnest striving after good works unwearied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:145
verses.text: "And Thou hast given me the defence of my salvation, and Thy right hand hath held me up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:146
verses.text: And the favour of Thy grace hath held me up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:147
verses.text: "And Thy discipline hath directed me to the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:148
verses.text: And Thy correction, not suffering me to wander from the way, hath directed me that whatsoever I do, I refer to that end, whereby I may cleave to Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:149
verses.text: "And this Thy discipline, it shall teach me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:150
verses.text: And that same correction of Thine shall teach me to attain to that, whereunto it hath directed me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:151
verses.text: "Thou hast enlarged my steps under me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:152
verses.text: Nor shall the straits of the flesh hinder me; for Thou hast enlarged my love, working in gladness even with these mortal things and members which are under me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:153
verses.text: "And my footsteps have not been weakened".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:154
verses.text: And either my goings, or the marks which I have imprinted for the imitation of those that follow, have not been weakened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:155
verses.text: "I will follow up mine enemies, and seize them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:156
verses.text: I will follow up my carnal affections, and will not be seized by them, but will seize them, so that they may be consumed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:157
verses.text: "And I will not turn, till they fail".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:158
verses.text: And from this purpose I will not turn myself to rest, till they fail who make a tumult about me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:159
verses.text: "I will break them, and they shall not be able to stand" : and they shall not hold out against me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:160
verses.text: "They shall fall under my feet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:161
verses.text: When they are cast down, I will place before me the loves whereby I walk for evermore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:162
verses.text: "And Thou hast girded me with strength to the war".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:163
verses.text: And the loose desires of my flesh hast Thou bound up with strength, that in such a fight I may not be encumbered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:164
verses.text: "Thou hast supplanted under me them that rose up against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:165
verses.text: Thou hast caused them to be deceived, who followed upon me, that they should be brought under me, who desired to be over me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:166
verses.text: "And thou hast given mine enemies the back to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:167
verses.text: And thou hast turned mine enemies, and hast made them to be a back to me, that is, to follow me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:168
verses.text: "And Thou hast destroyed them that hate me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:169
verses.text: But such other of them as have persisted in hatred, Thou hast destroyed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:170
verses.text: "They have cried out, and there was none to save them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:171
verses.text: For who can save them, whom Thou wouldest not save? "To the Lord, and He did not hear them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:172
verses.text: Nor did they cry out to any chance one, but to the Lord: and He did not judge them worthy of being heard, who depart not from their wickedness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:173
verses.text: "And I will beat them as small as dust before the face of the wind".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:174
verses.text: And I will beat them small; for dry they are, receiving not the shower of God's mercy; that borne aloft and puffed up with pride they may be hurried along from firm and unshaken hope, and as it were from the earth's solidity and stability.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:175
verses.text: "As the clay of the streets I will destroy them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:176
verses.text: In their wanton and loose course along the broad ways of perdition, which many walk, will I destroy them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:177
verses.text: "Thou wilt deliver Me from the contradictions of the people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:178
verses.text: Thou wilt deliver Me from the contradictions of them who said, "If we send Him away, all the world will go after Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:179
verses.text: "Thou shalt make Me the head of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:180
verses.text: A people whom I have not known have served Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:181
verses.text: The people of the Gentiles, whom in bodily presence I have not visited, have served Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:182
verses.text: "At the hearing of the ear they have obeyed Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:183
verses.text: They have not seen Me with the eye: but, receiving my preachers, at the hearing of the ear they have obeyed Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:184
verses.text: "The strange children have lied unto Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:185
verses.text: Children, not to be called Mine, but rather strange children, to whom it is rightly said, "Ye are of your father the devil," have lied unto Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:186
verses.text: "The strange children have waxen old".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:187
verses.text: The strange children, to whom for their renovation I brought the new Testament, have remained in the old man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:188
verses.text: "And they have halted from their own paths".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:189
verses.text: And like those that are weak in one foot, for holding the old they have rejected the new Testament, they have become halt, even in their old Law, rather following their own traditions, than God's.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:190
verses.text: For they brought frivolous charges of unwashen hands, because such were the paths, which themselves had made and worn by long use, in wandering from the ways of God's commands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:191
verses.text: "The Lord liveth, and blessed be my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:192
verses.text: "But to be carnally minded is death:" for "the Lord liveth, and blessed be my God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:193
verses.text: And let the God of my salvation be exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:194
verses.text: And let me not think after an earthly fashion of the God of my salvation; nor look from Him for this earthly salvation, but that on high.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:195
verses.text: "O God, who givest Me vengeance, and subduest the people under Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:196
verses.text: O God, who avengest Me by subduing the people under Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:197
verses.text: "My Deliverer from My angry enemies:" the Jews crying out, "Crucify Him, Crucify Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:198
verses.text: "From them that rise up against Me Thou wilt exalt Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:199
verses.text: From the Jews that rise up against Me in My passion, Thou wilt exalt Me in My resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:200
verses.text: "From the unjust man Thou wilt deliver Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:201
verses.text: From their unjust rule Thou wilt deliver Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:202
verses.text: "For this cause will I confess to Thee among the Gentiles, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:203
verses.text: For this cause shall the Gentiles confess to Thee through Me, O Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:204
verses.text: "And I will sing unto Thy Name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:205
verses.text: And Thou shalt be more widely known by My good deeds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:206
verses.text: "Magnifying the salvation of His King".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:207
verses.text: God, who magnifieth, so as to make wonderful, the salvation, which His Son giveth to believers "And showing mercy to His Christ:" God, who showeth mercy to His Christ: "To David and to His seed for evermore:" to the Deliverer Himself strong of hand, who hath overcome this world; and to them whom, as belie vers in the Gospel, He hath begotten for evermore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:208
verses.text: What things soever are spoken in this Psalm which cannot apply to the Lord Himself personally, that is to the Head of the Church, must be referred to the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 18:209
verses.text: For whole Christ speaks here, in whom are all His members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:1
verses.text: Psalm XIX  To the end, a psalm of David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:2
verses.text: It is a well-known title; nor does the Lord Jesus Christ say what follows, but it is said of Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:3
verses.text: "The heavens tell out the glory of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:4
verses.text: The righteous Evangelists, in whom, as in the heavens, God dwelleth, set forth the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ, or the glory wherewith the Son glorified the Father upon earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:5
verses.text: "And the firmament showeth forth the works of His hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:6
verses.text: And the firmament showeth forth the deeds of the Lord's power, that now made heaven by the assurance of the Holy Ghost, which before was earth by fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:7
verses.text: "Day unto day uttereth word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:8
verses.text: To the spiritual the Spirit giveth out the fulness of the unchangeable Wisdom of God, the Word which in the beginning is God with God "And night unto night announceth knowledge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:9
verses.text: And to the fleshly, as to those afar off, the mortality of the flesh, by conveying faith, announceth future knowledge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:10
verses.text: "There is no speech nor language, in which their voices are not heard".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:11
verses.text: In which the voices of the Evangelists have not been heard, seeing that the Gospel was preached in every tongue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:12
verses.text: "Their sound is gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:13
verses.text: "In the sun hath He set His tabernacle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:14
verses.text: Now that He might war against the powers of temporal error, the Lord, being about to send not peace but a sword on earth, in time, or in manifestation, set so to say His military dwelling, that is, the dispensation of His incarnation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:15
verses.text: "And He as a bridegroom coming forth out of His chamber".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:16
verses.text: And He, coming forth out of the Virgin's womb, where God was united to man's nature as a bridegroom to a bride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:17
verses.text: "Rejoiced as a giant to run His way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:18
verses.text: Rejoiced as One exceeding strong, and surpassing all other men in power incomparable, not to inhabit, but to run His way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:19
verses.text: For, "He stood not in the way of sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:20
verses.text: "His going forth is from the highest heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:21
verses.text: From the Father is His going forth, not that in time, but from everlasting, whereby He was born of the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:22
verses.text: "And His meeting is even to the height of heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:23
verses.text: And in the fulness of the Godhead He meets even to an equality with the Father "And there is none that may hide himself from His heat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:24
verses.text: But whereas, "the Word was even made flesh, and dwelt in us," assuming our mortality, He permitted no man to excuse himself from the shadow of death; for the heat of the Word penetrated even it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:25
verses.text: "The law of the Lord is undefiled, converting souls".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:26
verses.text: The law of the Lord, therefore, is Himself who came to fulfil the law, not to destroy it; an undefiled law, "Who did no sin, neither was guile found in His mouth," not oppressing souls with the yoke of bondage, but converting them to imitate Him in liberty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:27
verses.text: "The testimony of the Lord is sure, giving wisdom to babes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:28
verses.text: "The testimony of the Lord is sure;" for, "no man knoweth the Father save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal Him," which things have been hidden from the wise and revealed to babes; for, "God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace to the humble".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:29
verses.text: "The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:30
verses.text: All the statutes of the Lord are right in Him who taught not what He did not; that they who should imitate Him might rejoice in heart, in those things which they should do freely with love, not slavishly with fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:31
verses.text: "The commandment of the Lord is lucid, enlightening the eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:32
verses.text: "The commandment of the Lord is lucid," with no veil of carnal observances, enlightening the sight of the inner man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:33
verses.text: "The fear of the Lord is chaste, enduring for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:34
verses.text: "The fear of the Lord;" not that distressing fear under the law, dreading exceedingly the withdrawal of temporal goods, by the love of which the soul commits fornication; but that chaste fear wherewith the Church, the more ardently she loves her Spouse, the more carefully does she take heed of offending Him, and therefore, "perfect love casteth" not "out" this "fear," but it endureth for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:35
verses.text: "The judgments of the Lord are true, justified together".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:36
verses.text: The judgments of Him, who "judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son," are justified in truth unchangeably.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:37
verses.text: For neither in His threatenings nor His promises doth God deceive any man, nor can any withdraw either from the ungodly His punishment, or from the godly His reward.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:38
verses.text: "To be desired more than gold, and much precious stone".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:39
verses.text: Whether it be "gold and stone itself much," or "much precious," or "much to be desired;" still, the judgments of God are to be desired more than the pomp of this world; by desire of which it is brought to pass that the judgments of God are not desired, but feared, or despised, or not believed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:40
verses.text: But if any be himself gold and precious stone, that he may not be consumed by fire, but received into the treasury of God, more than himself does he desire the judgments of God, whose will he preferreth to his own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:41
verses.text: "And sweeter than honey and the honey comb".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:42
verses.text: And whether one be even now honey, who, disenthralled already from the chains of this life, is awaiting the day when he may come up to God's feast; or whether he be yet as the honey comb, wrapped about with this life as it were with wax, not mixed and become one with it, but filling it, needing some pressure of God's hand, not oppressing but expressing it, whereby from life temporal it may be strained out into life eternal: to such an one the judgments of God are sweeter than he himself is to himself, for that they are "sweeter than honey and the honey comb".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:43
verses.text: "For Thy servant keepeth them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:44
verses.text: For to him who keepeth them not the day of the Lord is bitter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:45
verses.text: "In keeping them there is great reward".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:46
verses.text: Not in any external benefit, but in the thing itself, that God's judgments are kept, is there great reward; great because one rejoiceth therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:47
verses.text: "Who understandeth sins?" (ver.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:48
verses.text: ) But what sort of sweetness can there be in sins, where there is no understanding? For who can understand sins, which close the very eye, to which truth is pleasant, to which the judgments of God are desirable and sweet? yea, as darkness closes the eye, so do sins the mind, and suffer it not to see either the light, or itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:49
verses.text: "Cleanse me, O Lord, from my secret faults".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:50
verses.text: From the lusts which lie hid in me, cleanse me, O Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:51
verses.text: "And from the" faults "of others preserve Thy servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:52
verses.text: Let me not be led astray by others.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:53
verses.text: For he is not a prey to the faults of others, who is cleansed from his own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:54
verses.text: Preserve therefore from the lusts of others, not the proud man, and him who would be his own master, but, Thy servant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:55
verses.text: "If they get not the dominion over me, then shall I be undefiled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:56
verses.text: If neither my own secret sins, nor those of others, get the dominion over me, then shall I be undefiled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:57
verses.text: For there is no third source of sin, but one's own secret sin, by which the devil fell, and another's sin, by which man is seduced, so as by consenting to make it his own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:58
verses.text: "And I shall be cleansed from the great offence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:59
verses.text: What but pride? for there is none greater than apostasy from God, which is "the beginning of the pride of man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:60
verses.text: And he shall indeed be undefiled, who is free from this offence also; for this is the last to them who are returning to God, which was the first as they departed from Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:61
verses.text: "And the words of my mouth shall be pleasing, and the meditation of my heart is always in Thy sight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:62
verses.text: The meditation of my heart is not after the vain glory of pleasing men, for now there is pride no more, but in Thy sight alway, who regardest a pure conscience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:63
verses.text: "O Lord, my Helper, and my Redeemer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 19:64
verses.text: O Lord, my Helper, in my approach to Thee; for Thou art my Redeemer, that I might set out unto Thee: lest any attributing to his own wisdom his conversion to Thee, or to his own strength his attaining to Thee, should be rather driven back by Thee, who resistest the proud; for he is not cleansed from the great offence, nor pleasing in Thy sight, who redeemest us that we may be converted, and helpest us that we may attain unto Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:1
verses.text: Psalm XX  To the end, a psalm of David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:2
verses.text: This is a well-known title; and it is not Christ who speaks; but the prophet speaks to Christ, under the form of wishing, foretelling things to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:3
verses.text: "The Lord hear Thee in the day of trouble".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:4
verses.text: The Lord hear Thee in the day in which Thou saidst, "Father glorify Thy Son".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:5
verses.text: "The name of the God of Jacob protect Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:6
verses.text: For to Thee belongeth the younger people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:7
verses.text: Since "the elder shall serve the younger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:8
verses.text: "Send Thee help from the Holy, and from Sion defend Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:9
verses.text: Making for Thee a sanctified Body, the Church, from watching safe, which waiteth when Thou shalt come from the wedding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:10
verses.text: "Be mindful of all Thy sacrifice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:11
verses.text: Make us mindful of all Thy injuries and despiteful treatment, which Thou hast borne for us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:12
verses.text: "And be Thy whole burnt offering made fat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:13
verses.text: And turn the cross, whereon Thou wast wholly offered up to God, into the joy of the resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:14
verses.text: "Diapsalma".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:15
verses.text: The Lord render to Thee according to Thine Heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:16
verses.text: The Lord render to Thee, not according to their heart, who thought by persecution they could destroy Thee; but according to Thine Heart, wherein Thou knewest what profit Thy passion would have "And fulfil all Thy counsel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:17
verses.text: "And fulfil all Thy counsel," not only that whereby Thou didst lay down Thy life for Thy friends, that the corrupted grain might rise again to more abundance; but that also whereby "blindness in part hath happened unto Israel, that the fulness of the Gentiles might enter in, and so all Israel might be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:18
verses.text: "We will exult in Thy salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:19
verses.text: We will exult in that death will in no wise hurt Thee; for so Thou wilt also show that it cannot hurt us either.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:20
verses.text: "And in the name of the Lord our God will we be magnified".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:21
verses.text: And the confession of Thy name shall not only not destroy us, but shall even magnify us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:22
verses.text: "The Lord fulfil all Thy petitions".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:23
verses.text: The Lord fulfil not only the petitions which Thou madest on earth, but those also whereby Thou intercedest for us in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:24
verses.text: "Now have I known that the Lord hath saved his Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:25
verses.text: Now hath it been shown to me in prophecy, that the Lord will raise up His Christ again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:26
verses.text: "He will hear Him from His holy heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:27
verses.text: He will hear Him not from earth only, where He prayed to be glorified; but from heaven also, where interceding for us at the Right Hand of the Father, He hath from thence shed abroad the Holy Spirit on them that believe on Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:28
verses.text: "In strength is the safety of His right hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:29
verses.text: Our strength is in the safety of His favour, when even out of tribulation He giveth help, that "when we are weak, then we may be strong".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:30
verses.text: "For vain is" that "safety of man," which comes not of His right hand but of His left: for thereby are they lifted up to great pride, whosoever in their sins have secured a temporal safety.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:31
verses.text: "Some in chariots, and some in horses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:32
verses.text: Some are drawn away by the ever moving succession of temporal goods; and some are preferred to proud honours, and in them exult: "But we will exult in the name of the Lord our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:33
verses.text: But we, fixing our hope on things eternal, and not seeking our own glory, will exult in the name of the Lord our God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:34
verses.text: "They have been bound, and fallen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:35
verses.text: And therefore were they bound by the lust of temporal things, fearing to spare the Lord, lest they should lose their place by "the Romans:" and rushing violently on the stone of offence and rock of stumbling, they fell from the heavenly hope: to whom the blindness in part of Israel hath happened, being ignorant of God's righteousness, and wishing to establish their own "But we are risen, and stand upright".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:36
verses.text: But we, that the Gentile people might enter in, out of the stones raised up as children to Abraham, who followed not after righteousness, have attained to it, and are risen; and not by our own strength, but being justified by faith, we stand upright.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:37
verses.text: "O Lord, save the King:" that He, who in His Passion hath shown us an example of conflict, should also offer up our sacrifices, the Priest raised from the dead, and established in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:38
verses.text: "And hear us in the day when we shall call on Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 20:39
verses.text: And as He now offereth for us, "hear us in the day when we shall call on Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:1
verses.text: Psalm XXI  To the end, a psalm of David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:2
verses.text: The title is a familiar one; the Psalm is of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:3
verses.text: "O Lord, the King shall rejoice in Thy strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:4
verses.text: O Lord, in Thy strength, whereby the Word was made flesh, the Man Christ Jesus shall rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:5
verses.text: "And shall exult exceedingly in Thy salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:6
verses.text: And in that, whereby Thou quickenest all things, shall exult exceedingly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:7
verses.text: "Thou hast given Him the desire of His soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:8
verses.text: He desired to eat the Passover, and to lay down His life when He would, and again when He would to take it; and Thou hast given it to Him "And hast not deprived Him of the good pleasure of His lips".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:9
verses.text: "My peace," saith He, "I leave with you:" and it was done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:10
verses.text: "For Thou hast presented Him with the blessings of sweetness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:11
verses.text: Because He had first quaffed the blessing of Thy sweetness, the gall of our sins did not hurt Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:12
verses.text: "Diapsalma.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:13
verses.text: Thou hast set a crown of precious stone on His Head".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:14
verses.text: At the beginning of His discoursing precious stones were brought, and compassed Him about; His disciples, from whom the commencement of His preaching should be made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:15
verses.text: "He asked life; and Thou gavest Him:" He asked a resurrection, saying, "Father, glorify Thy Son;" and Thou gavest it Him, "Length of days for ever and ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:16
verses.text: The prolonged ages of this world which the Church was to have, and after them an eternity, world without end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:17
verses.text: "His glory is great in Thy salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:18
verses.text: Great indeed is His glory in the salvation, whereby Thou hast raised Him up again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:19
verses.text: "Glory and great honour shalt Thou lay upon Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:20
verses.text: But Thou shalt yet add unto Him glory and great honour, when Thou shalt place Him in heaven at Thy right hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:21
verses.text: "For Thou shalt give Him blessing for ever and ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:22
verses.text: This is the blessing which Thou shalt give Him for ever and ever: "Thou shalt make Him glad in joy together with Thy countenance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:23
verses.text: According to His manhood, Thou shalt make Him glad together with Thy countenance, which He lifted up to Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:24
verses.text: "For the King hopeth in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:25
verses.text: For the King is not proud, but humble in heart, he hopeth in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:26
verses.text: "And in the mercy of the Most Highest He shall not be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:27
verses.text: And in the mercy of the Most Highest His obedience even unto the death of the Cross shall not disturb His humility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:28
verses.text: "Let Thy hand be found by all Thine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:29
verses.text: Be Thy power, O King, when Thou comest to judgment, found by all Thine enemies; who in Thy humiliation discerned it not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:30
verses.text: "Let Thy right hand find out all that hate Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:31
verses.text: Let the glory, wherein Thou reignest at the right hand of the Father, find out for punishment in the day of judgment all that hate Thee; for that now they have not found it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:32
verses.text: "Thou shalt make them like a fiery oven:" Thou shalt make them on fire within, by the consciousness of their ungodliness: "In the time of Thy countenance:" in the time of Thy manifestation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:33
verses.text: "The Lord shall trouble them in His wrath, and the fire shall devour them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:34
verses.text: And then, being troubled by the vengeance of the Lord, after the accusation of their conscience, they shall be given up to eternal fire, to be devoured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:35
verses.text: "Their fruit shalt Thou destroy out of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:36
verses.text: Their fruit, because it is earthly, shalt Thou destroy out of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:37
verses.text: "And their seed from the sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:38
verses.text: And their works; or, whomsoever they have seduced, Thou shalt not reckon among the sons of men, whom Thou hast called into the everlasting inheritance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:39
verses.text: "Because they turned evils against Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:40
verses.text: Now this punishment shall be recompensed to them, because the evils which they supposed to hang over them by Thy reign, they turned against Thee to Thy death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:41
verses.text: "They imagined a device, which they were not able to establish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:42
verses.text: They imagined a device, saying, "It is expedient that one die for all:" which they were not able to establish, not knowing what they said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:43
verses.text: "For Thou shalt set them low".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:44
verses.text: For Thou shalt rank them among those from whom in degradation and contempt Thou wilt turn away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:45
verses.text: "In Thy leavings Thou shalt make ready their countenance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:46
verses.text: And in these things that Thou leavest, that is, in the desires of an earthly kingdom, Thou shalt make ready their shamelessness for Thy passion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:47
verses.text: "Be Thou exalted, O Lord, in Thy strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:48
verses.text: Be Thou, Lord, whom in humiliation they did not discern, exalted in Thy strength, which they thought weakness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:49
verses.text: "We will sing and praise Thy power".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 21:50
verses.text: In heart and in deed we will celebrate and make known Thy marvels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:1
verses.text: Psalm XXII  To the end, for the taking up of the morning, a psalm of David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:2
verses.text: "To the end," for His own resurrection, the Lord Jesus Christ Himself speaketh For in the morning on the first day of the week was His resurrection, whereby He was taken up, into eternal life, "Over whom death shall have no more dominion ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:3
verses.text: Now what follows is spoken in the person of The Crucified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:4
verses.text: For from the head of this Psalm are the words, which He cried out, whilst hanging on the Cross, sustaining also the person of the old man, whose mortality He bare.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:5
verses.text: For our old man was nailed together with Him to the Cross.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:6
verses.text: "O God, my God, look upon me, why hast Thou forsaken me far from my salvation?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:7
verses.text: Far removed from my salvation: for "salvation is far from sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:8
verses.text: "The words of my sins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:9
verses.text: For these are not the words of righteousness, but of my sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:10
verses.text: For it is the old man nailed to the Cross that speaks, ignorant even of the reason why God hath forsaken him: or else it may be thus, The words of my sins are far from my salvation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:11
verses.text: "My God, I will cry unto Thee in the daytime, and Thou wilt not hear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:12
verses.text: My God, I will cry unto Thee in the prosperous circumstances of this life, that they be not changed; and Thou wilt not hear, because I shall cry unto Thee in the words of my sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:13
verses.text: "And in the night-season, and not to my folly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:14
verses.text: And so in the adversities of this life will I cry to Thee for prosperity; and in like manner Thou wilt not hear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:15
verses.text: And this Thou doest not to my folly, but rather that I may have wisdom to know what Thou wouldest have me cry for, not with the words of sins out of longing for life temporal, but with the words of turning to Thee for life eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:16
verses.text: "But Thou dwellest in the holy place, O Thou praise of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:17
verses.text: But Thou dwellest in the holy place, and therefore wilt not hear the unclean words of sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:18
verses.text: The "praise" of him that seeth Thee; not of him who hath sought his own praise in tasting of the forbidden fruit, that on the opening of his bodily eyes he should endeavour to hide himself from Thy sight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:19
verses.text: "Our Fathers hoped in Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:20
verses.text: All the righteous, namely, who sought not their own praise, but Thine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:21
verses.text: "They hoped in Thee, and Thou deliveredst them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:22
verses.text: "They cried unto Thee, and were saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:23
verses.text: They cried unto Thee, not in the words of sins, from which salvation is far; and therefore were they saved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:24
verses.text: "They hoped in Thee, and were not confounded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:25
verses.text: "They hoped in Thee," and their hope did not deceive them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:26
verses.text: For they placed it not in themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:27
verses.text: "But I am a worm, and no man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:28
verses.text: But I, speaking now not in the person of Adam, but I in My own person, Jesus Christ, was born without human generation in the flesh, that I might be as man beyond men; that so at least human pride might deign to imitate My humility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:29
verses.text: "The scorn of men, and outcast of the people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:30
verses.text: In which humility I was made the scorn of men, so as that it should be said, as a reproachful railing, "Be thou His disciple:" and that the people despise Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:31
verses.text: "All that saw Me laughed Me to scorn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:32
verses.text: All that saw Me derided Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:33
verses.text: "And spake with the lips, and shook the head".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:34
verses.text: And they spoke, not with the heart, but with the lips.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:35
verses.text: For they shook their head in derision, saying, "He trusted in the Lord, let Him deliver Him:" "let Him save Him, since He desireth Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:36
verses.text: These were their words; but they were spoken "with the lips".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:37
verses.text: "Since Thou art He who drew Me out of the womb".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:38
verses.text: Since Thou art He who drew Me, not only out of that Virgin womb (for this is the law of all men's birth, that they be drawn out of the womb), but also out of the womb of the Jewish nation; by the darkness whereof he is covered, and not yet born into the light of Christ, whosoever places his salvation in the carnal observance of the Sabbath, and of circumcision, and the like.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:39
verses.text: "My hope from My mother's breasts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:40
verses.text: "My hope," O God, not from the time when I began to be fed by the milk of the Virgin's breasts; for it was even before; but from the breasts of the Synagogue, as I have said, out of the womb, Thou hast drawn Me, that I should not suck in the customs of the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:41
verses.text: "I have been strengthened in Thee from the womb".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:42
verses.text: It is the womb of the Synagogue, which did not carry Me, but threw Me out: but I fell not, for Thou heldest me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:43
verses.text: "From My mother's womb Thou art My God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:44
verses.text: "From My mother's womb: My mother's womb did not cause that, as a babe, I should be forgetful of Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:45
verses.text: "Thou art My God," "depart not from Me; for trouble is hard at hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:46
verses.text: Thou art, therefore, My God, depart not from Me; for trouble is nigh unto Me; for it is in My body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:47
verses.text: "For there is none to help".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:48
verses.text: For who helpeth, if Thou helpest not?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:49
verses.text: "Many calves came about Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:50
verses.text: The multitude of the wanton populace came about Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:51
verses.text: "Fat bulls closed Me in".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:52
verses.text: And their leaders, glad at My oppression, "closed Me in".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:53
verses.text: "They opened their mouth upon Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:54
verses.text: They opened their mouth upon Me, not out of Thy Scripture, but of their own lusts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:55
verses.text: "As a ravening and roaring lion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:56
verses.text: As a lion, whose ravening is, that I was taken and led; and whose roaring, "Crucify, Crucify".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:57
verses.text: "I was poured out like water, and all My bones were scattered".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:58
verses.text: "I was poured out like water," when My persecutors fell: and through fear, the stays of My body, that is, the Church, My disciples were scattered from Me "My heart became as melting wax, in the midst of my belly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:59
verses.text: My wisdom, which was written of Me in the sacred books, was, as if hard and shut up, not understood: but after that the fire of My Passion was applied, it was, as if melted, manifested, and entertained in the memory of My Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:60
verses.text: "My strength dried up as a potsherd".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:61
verses.text: My strength dried up by My Passion; not as hay, but a potsherd, which is made stronger by fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:62
verses.text: "And My tongue cleaved to My jaws".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:63
verses.text: And they, through whom I was soon to speak, kept My precepts in their hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:64
verses.text: "And Thou broughtest Me down to the dust of death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:65
verses.text: And to the ungodly appointed to death, whom the wind casteth forth as dust from the face of the earth,  Thou broughtest Me down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:66
verses.text: "For many dogs came about Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:67
verses.text: For many came about Me barking, not for truth, but for custom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:68
verses.text: "The council of the malignant came about Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:69
verses.text: The council of the malignant besieged Me "They pierced My hands and feet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:70
verses.text: They pierced with nails My hands and feet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:71
verses.text: "They numbered distinctly all My bones".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:72
verses.text: They numbered distinctly all My bones, while extended on the wood of the Cross.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:73
verses.text: "Yea, these same regarded, and beheld Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:74
verses.text: Yea, these same, that is, unchanged, regarded and beheld Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:75
verses.text: "They divided My garments for themselves, and cast the lot upon My vesture".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:76
verses.text: "But Thou, O Lord, withhold not Thy help far from Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:77
verses.text: But Thou, O Lord, raise Me up again, not as the rest of men, at the end of the world, but immediately.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:78
verses.text: "Look to My defence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:79
verses.text: "Look," that they in no wise hurt Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:80
verses.text: "Deliver My soul from the sword".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:81
verses.text: "Deliver My soul" from the tongue of dissension.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:82
verses.text: "And My only One from the hand of the dog".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:83
verses.text: And from the power of the people, barking after their custom, deliver My Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:84
verses.text: "Save Me from the lion's mouth:" save Me from the mouth of the kingdom of this world: "and my humility from the horns of the unicorns".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:85
verses.text: And from the loftiness of the proud, exalting themselves to special pre-eminence, and enduring no partakers, save My humility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:86
verses.text: "I will declare Thy name to My brethren".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:87
verses.text: I will declare Thy name to the humble, and to My Brethren that love one another as they have been beloved by Me "In the midst of the Church will I sing of Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:88
verses.text: In the midst of the Church will I with rejoicing preach Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:89
verses.text: "Ye that fear the Lord, praise Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:90
verses.text: "Ye that fear the Lord," seek not your own praise, but "praise Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:91
verses.text: "All ye seed of Jacob, magnify Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:92
verses.text: All ye seed of him whom the elder shall serve, magnify Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:93
verses.text: "Let all the seed of Israel fear Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:94
verses.text: Let all who have been born to a new life, and restored to the vision of God "fear Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:95
verses.text: "Since He hath not despised, nor disregarded the prayer of the poor man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:96
verses.text: Since He hath not despised the prayer, not of him who, crying unto God in the words of sins was loath to overpass a vain life, but the prayer of the poor man, not swollen up with transitory pomps.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:97
verses.text: "Nor hath He turned away His face from Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:98
verses.text: As from him who said, I will cry unto Thee, but Thou wilt not hear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:99
verses.text: "And when I cried unto Him He heard Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:100
verses.text: "With Thee is My praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:101
verses.text: For I seek not Mine own praise, for Thou art My praise, who dwellest in the holy place; and, praise of Israel, Thou hearest The Holy One now beseeching Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:102
verses.text: "In the great Church I will confess Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:103
verses.text: In the Church of the whole world "I will confess Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:104
verses.text: "I will offer My vows in the sight of them that fear Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:105
verses.text: I will offer the sacraments of My Body and Blood in the sight of them that fear Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:106
verses.text: "The poor shall eat, and be filled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:107
verses.text: The humble and the despisers of the world shall eat, and imitate Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:108
verses.text: For so they will neither desire this world's abundance, nor fear its want.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:109
verses.text: "And they shall praise the Lord, who seek Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:110
verses.text: For the praise of the Lord is the pouring out of that fulness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:111
verses.text: "Their hearts shall live for ever and ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:112
verses.text: For that food is the food of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:113
verses.text: "All the borders of the earth shall remember themselves, and be turned to the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:114
verses.text: They shall remember themselves: for, by the Gentiles, born in death and bent on outward things, God had been forgotten; and then shall all the borders of the earth be turned to the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:115
verses.text: "And all the kindreds of the nations shall worship in His sight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:116
verses.text: And all the kindreds of the nations shall worship in their own consciences.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:117
verses.text: "For the kingdom is the Lord's, and He shall rule over the nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:118
verses.text: For the kingdom is the Lord's, not proud men's: and He shall rule over the nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:119
verses.text: "All the rich of the earth have eaten, and worshipped".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:120
verses.text: The rich of the earth too have eaten the Body of their Lord's humiliation, and though they have not, as the poor, been filled even to imitation, yet they have worshipped.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:121
verses.text: "In His sight shall fall all that descend to earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:122
verses.text: For He alone seeth how all they fall, who abandoning a heavenly conversation, make choice, on earth, to appear happy to men, who see not their fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:123
verses.text: "And My Soul shall live to Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:124
verses.text: And My Soul, which in the contempt of this world seems to men as it were to die, shall live, not to itself, but to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:125
verses.text: "And My seed shall serve Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:126
verses.text: And My deeds, or they who through Me believe on Him, shall serve Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:127
verses.text: "The generation to come shall be declared to the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:128
verses.text: The generation of the New Testament shall be declared to the honour of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:129
verses.text: "And the heavens shall declare His righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:130
verses.text: And the Evangelists shall declare His righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:131
verses.text: "To a people that shall be born, whom the Lord hath made".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 22:132
verses.text: To a people that shall be born to the Lord through faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:1
verses.text: Psalm XXIII  A psalm of David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:2
verses.text: The Church speaks to Christ: "The Lord feedeth me, and I shall lack nothing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:3
verses.text: The Lord Jesus Christ is my Shepherd, "and I shall lack nothing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:4
verses.text: "In a place of pasture there hath He placed me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:5
verses.text: In a place of fresh pasture, leading me to faith, there hath He placed me to be nourished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:6
verses.text: "By the water of refreshing hath He brought me up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:7
verses.text: By the water of baptism, whereby they are refreshed who have lost health and strength, hath He brought me up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:8
verses.text: "He hath converted my soul: He hath led me forth in the paths of righteousness, for His Name's sake".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:9
verses.text: He hath brought me forth in the narrow ways, wherein few walk, of His righteousness; not for my merit's sake, but for His Name's sake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:10
verses.text: "Yea, though I walk in the midst of the shadow of death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:11
verses.text: Yea, though I walk in the midst of this life, which is the shadow of death "I will fear no evil, for Thou art with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:12
verses.text: I will fear no evil, for Thou dwellest in my heart by faith: and Thou art now with me, that after the shadow of death I too may be with Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:13
verses.text: "Thy rod and Thy staff, they have comforted me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:14
verses.text: Thy discipline, like a rod for a flock of sheep, and like a staff for children of some size, and growing out of the natural into spiritual life, they have not been grievous to me; rather have they comforted me: because Thou art mindful of me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:15
verses.text: "Thou hast prepared a table in my sight, against them that trouble me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:16
verses.text: Now after the rod, whereby, whilst a little one, and living the natural life, I was brought up among the flock in the pastures; after that rod, I say, when I began to be under the staff, Thou hast prepared a table in my sight, that I should no more be fed as a babe with milk, but being older should take meat, strengthened against them that trouble me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:17
verses.text: "Thou hast fattened my head with oil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:18
verses.text: Thou hast gladdened my mind with spiritual joy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:19
verses.text: "And Thy inebriating cup, how excellent is it!" And Thy cup yielding forgetfulness of former vain delights, how excellent is it!.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:20
verses.text: "And Thy mercy shall follow me all the days of my life:" that is, as long as I live in this mortal life, not Thine, but mine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:21
verses.text: "That I may dwell in the house of the Lord for length of days".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 23:22
verses.text: Now Thy mercy shall follow me not here only, but also that I may dwell in the house of the Lord for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:1
verses.text: Psalm XXIV  A psalm of David himself, on the first day of the week.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:2
