verses.text: A Psalm of David himself, touching the glorifying and resurrection of the Lord, which took place early in the morning on the first day of the week, which is now called the Lord's Day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:3
verses.text: "The earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof, the compass of the world, and all they that dwell therein" ; when the Lord, being glorified, is announced for the believing of all nations; and the whole compass of the world becomes His Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:4
verses.text: "He hath founded it above the seas".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:5
verses.text: He hath most firmly established it above all the waves of this world, that they should be subdued by it, and should not hurt it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:6
verses.text: "And hath prepared it above the rivers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:7
verses.text: The rivers flow into the sea, and men of lust lapse into the world: these also the Church, which, when worldly lusts have been conquered by the grace of God, hath been prepared by love for the reception of immortality, subdues.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:8
verses.text: "Who shall ascend into the mount of the Lord?" Who shall ascend to the height of the righteousness of the Lord? "Or who shall stand in His holy place?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:9
verses.text: Or who shall abide in that place, whither He shall ascend, founded above the seas, and prepared above the rivers?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:10
verses.text: "The innocent of hand, and the pure in heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:11
verses.text: Who then shall ascend thither, and abide there, but the guiltless in deed, and pure in thought? "Who hath not received his soul in vain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:12
verses.text: Who hath not reckoned his soul among things that pass away, but feeling it to be immortal, hath longed for an eternity stedfast and unchangeable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:13
verses.text: "And hath not sworn in deceit to his neighbour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:14
verses.text: And therefore without deceit, as things eternal are simple and undeceiving, hath so behaved himself to his neighbour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:15
verses.text: "This man shall receive blessing from the Lord, and mercy from the God of his salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:16
verses.text: "This is the generation of them that seek the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:17
verses.text: For thus are they born that seek Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:18
verses.text: "Of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob Diapsalma".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:19
verses.text: Now they seek the face of God, who gave the pre-eminence to the younger born.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:20
verses.text: "Take away your gates, ye princes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:21
verses.text: All ye, that seek rule among men, remove, that they hinder not, the entrances which ye have made, of desire and fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:22
verses.text: "And be ye lift up, ye everlasting gates".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:23
verses.text: And be ye lift up, ye entrances of eternal life, of renunciation of the world, and conversion to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:24
verses.text: "And the King of glory shall come in".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:25
verses.text: And the King, in whom we may glory without pride, shall come in: who having overcome the gates of death, and having opened for Himself the heavenly places, fulfilled that which He said, "Be of good cheer, for I have overcome the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:26
verses.text: "Who is this King of glory?" Mortal nature is awe-struck in wonder, and asks, "Who is this King of glory?" "The Lord strong and mighty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:27
verses.text: He whom thou didst deem weak and overwhelmed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:28
verses.text: "The Lord mighty in battle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:29
verses.text: Handle the scars, and thou wilt find them made whole, and human weakness restored to immortality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:30
verses.text: The glorifying of the Lord, which was owing to earth, where It warred with death, hath been paid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:31
verses.text: "Take away your gates, ye princes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:32
verses.text: Let us go hence straightway into heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:33
verses.text: Again, let the Prophet's trumpet cry aloud, "Take away too, ye princes of the air, the gates, which ye have in the minds of men who 'worship the host of heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:34
verses.text: '" "And be ye lift up, ye everlasting gates".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:35
verses.text: And be ye lift up, ye doors of everlasting righteousness, of love, and chastity, through which the soul loveth the One True God, and goeth not a-whoring with the many that are called gods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:36
verses.text: "And the King of glory shall come in".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:37
verses.text: "And the King of glory shall come in," that He may at the right hand of the Father intercede for us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:38
verses.text: "Who is this King of glory?" What! dost thou too, prince of the power of this air, marvel and ask, "Who is this King of glory?" "The Lord of powers, He is the King of glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:39
verses.text: Yea, His Body now quickened, He who was tempted marches above thee; He who was tempted by the angel, the deceiver, goes above all angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 24:40
verses.text: Let none of you put himself before us and stop our way, that he may be worshipped as a god by us: neither principality, nor angel, nor power, separateth us from the love of Christ It is good to trust in the Lord, rather than to trust in a prince; that he who glorieth, should glory in the Lord These indeed are powers in the administration of this world, but "the Lord of powers, He is the King of glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:1
verses.text: Psalm XXV  To the end, a psalm of David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:2
verses.text: Christ speaks, but in the person of the Church: for what is said has reference rather to the Christian People turned unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:3
verses.text: "Unto Thee, O Lord, have I lift up my soul" : with spiritual longing have I lift up the soul, that was trodden down on the earth with carnal longings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:4
verses.text: "O my God, in Thee I trust, I shall not be ashamed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:5
verses.text: O my God, from trusting in myself I was brought even to this weakness of the flesh; and I who on abandoning God wished to be as God, fearing death from the smallest insect, was in derision ashamed for my pride; now, therefore, "in Thee I trust, I shall not be ashamed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:6
verses.text: "And let not my enemies mock me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:7
verses.text: And let them not mock me, who by ensnaring me with serpent-like and secret suggestions, and prompting me with "Well done, well done," have brought me down to this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:8
verses.text: "For all that wait upon Thee shall not be confounded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:9
verses.text: "Let them be confounded who do vain things unrighteously".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:10
verses.text: Let them be confounded who act unrighteously for the acquiring things that pass away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:11
verses.text: "Make Thy ways, O Lord, known to me, and teach me Thy paths" : not those which are broad, and lead the many to destruction; but Thy paths, narrow, and known to few, teach Thou me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:12
verses.text: "In Thy truth guide me:" avoiding error.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:13
verses.text: "And teach me:" for by myself I know nothing, but falsehood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:14
verses.text: "For Thou art the God of my salvation; and for Thee have I waited all the day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:15
verses.text: For dismissed by Thee from Paradise, and having taken my journey into a far country, I cannot by myself return, unless Thou meetest the wanderer: for my return hath throughout the whole tract of this world's time waited for Thy mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:16
verses.text: "Remember Thy compassions, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:17
verses.text: Remember the works of Thy mercy, O Lord; for men deem of Thee as though Thou hadst forgotten.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:18
verses.text: "And that Thy mercies are from eternity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:19
verses.text: And remember this, that Thy mercies are from eternity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:20
verses.text: For Thou never wast without them, who hast subjected even sinful man to vanity indeed, but in hope; and not deprived him of so many and great consolations of Thy creation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:21
verses.text: "Remember not the offences of my youth and of my ignorance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:22
verses.text: The offences of my presumptuous boldness and of my ignorance reserve not for vengeance, but let them be as if forgotten by Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:23
verses.text: "According to Thy mercy, be mindful of me, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:24
verses.text: Be mindful indeed of me, not according to the anger of which I am worthy, but according to Thy mercy which is worthy of Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:25
verses.text: "For Thy goodness, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:26
verses.text: Not for my deservings, but for Thy goodness, O Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:27
verses.text: "Gracious and upright is the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:28
verses.text: The Lord is gracious, since even sinners and the ungodly He so pitied, as to forgive all that is past; but the Lord is upright too, who after the mercy of vocation and pardon, which is of grace without merit, will require merits meet for the last judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:29
verses.text: "Wherefore He will establish a law for them that fail in the way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:30
verses.text: For He hath first bestowed mercy to bring them into the way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:31
verses.text: "He will guide the meek in judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:32
verses.text: He will guide the meek, and will not confound in the judgment those that follow His will, and do not, in withstanding It, prefer their own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:33
verses.text: "The gentle He will teach His ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:34
verses.text: He will teach His ways, not to those that desire to run before, as if they were better able to rule themselves; but to those who do not exalt the neck, nor lift the heel, when the easy yoke and the light burden is laid upon them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:35
verses.text: "All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:36
verses.text: And what ways will He teach them, but mercy wherein He is placable, and truth wherein He is incorrupt? Whereof He hath exhibited the one in forgiving sins, the other in judging deserts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:37
verses.text: And therefore "all the ways of the Lord" are the two advents of the Son of God, the one in mercy, the other in judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:38
verses.text: He then attaineth unto Him holding on His ways, who seeing himself freed by no deserts of his own, lays pride aside, and henceforward bewares of the severity of His trial, having experienced the clemency of His help.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:39
verses.text: "To them that seek His testament and His testimonies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:40
verses.text: For they understand the Lord as merciful at His first advent, and as the Judge at His second, who in meekness and gentleness seek His testament, when with His Own Blood He redeemed us to a new life; and in the Prophets and Evangelists, His testimonies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:41
verses.text: "For Thy Name's sake, O Lord, Thou wilt be favourable to my sin; for it is manifold".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:42
verses.text: Thou hast not only forgiven my sins, which I committed before I believed; but also to my sin, which is manifold, since even in the way there is no lack of stumbling, Thou wilt be made favourable by the sacrifice of a troubled spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:43
verses.text: "Who is the man that feareth the Lord?" from which fear he begins to come to wisdom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:44
verses.text: "He shall establish a law for him in the way, which he hath chosen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:45
verses.text: He shall establish a law for him in the way, which in his freedom he has taken, that he may not sin now with impunity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:46
verses.text: "His soul shall dwell in good, and his seed shall, by inheritance, possess the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:47
verses.text: And his work shall possess the stable inheritance of a renewed body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:48
verses.text: "The Lord is the stay of them that fear Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:49
verses.text: Fear seems to belong to the weak, but the Lord is the stay of them that fear Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:50
verses.text: And the Name of the Lord, which hath been glorified throughout the whole world, is a stay to them that fear Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:51
verses.text: "And His testament, that it may be manifested unto them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:52
verses.text: And He maketh His testament to be manifested unto them, for the Gentiles and the bounds of the earth are Christ's inheritance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:53
verses.text: "Mine eyes are ever unto the Lord; for He shall pluck my feet out of the snare".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:54
verses.text: Nor would I fear the dangers of earth, while I look not upon the earth: for He upon whom I look, will pluck my feet out of the snare.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:55
verses.text: "Look upon me, and have mercy upon me; for I am single and poor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:56
verses.text: For I am a single people, keeping the lowliness of Thy single Church, which no schisms or heresies possess.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:57
verses.text: "The tribulations of my heart have been multiplied".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:58
verses.text: The tribulations of my heart have been multiplied by the abounding of iniquity and the waxing cold of love "O bring Thou me out of my necessities".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:59
verses.text: Since I must needs bear this, that by enduring unto the end I may be saved, bring Thou me out of my necessities.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:60
verses.text: "See my humility and my travail".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:61
verses.text: See my humility, whereby I never, in the boast of righteousness, break off from unity; and my travail, wherein I bear with the unruly ones that are mingled with me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:62
verses.text: "And forgive all my sins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:63
verses.text: And, propitiated by these sacrifices, forgive all my sins, not those only of youth and my ignorance before I believed, but those also which, living now by faith, I commit through infirmity, or the darkness of this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:64
verses.text: "Consider mine enemies, how they are multiplied".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:65
verses.text: For not only without, but even within, in the Church's very communion, they are not wanting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:66
verses.text: "And with an unrighteous hate they hate me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:67
verses.text: And they hate me who love them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:68
verses.text: "Keep my soul, and deliver me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:69
verses.text: Keep my soul, that I turn not aside to imitate them; and draw me out from the confusion wherein they are mingled with me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:70
verses.text: "Let me not be confounded, for I have put my trust in Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:71
verses.text: Let me not be confounded, if haply they rise up against me: for not in myself, but in Thee have I put my trust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:72
verses.text: "The innocent and the upright have cleaved to me, for I have waited for Thee, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:73
verses.text: The innocent and the upright, not in bodily presence only, as the evil, are mingled with me, but in the agreement of the heart in the same innocence and uprightness cleave to me: for I have not fallen away to imitate the evil; but I have waited for Thee, expecting the winnowing of Thy last harvest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:74
verses.text: "Redeem Israel, O God, out of all his troubles".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 25:75
verses.text: "Redeem Thy people, O God," whom Thou hast prepared to see Thee, out of his troubles, not those only which he bears without, but those also which he bears within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:1
verses.text: Psalm XXVI  Of David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:2
verses.text: It may be attributed to David himself, not the Mediator, the Man Christ Jesus, but the whole Church now perfectly established in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:3
verses.text: "Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:4
verses.text: Judge me, O Lord, for, after the mercy which Thou first showedst me, I have some desert of my innocence, the way whereof I have kept.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:5
verses.text: "And trusting in the Lord I shall not be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:6
verses.text: And yet not even so trusting in myself, but in the Lord, I shall abide in Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:7
verses.text: "Prove me, O Lord, and try me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:8
verses.text: Lest, however, any of my secret sins should be hid from me, prove me, O Lord, and try me, making me known, not to Thee from whom nothing is hid, but to myself, and to men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:9
verses.text: "Burn my reins and my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:10
verses.text: Apply a remedial purgation, as it were fire, to my pleasures and thoughts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:11
verses.text: "For Thy mercy is before mine eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:12
verses.text: For, that I be not consumed by that fire, not my merits, but Thy mercy, whereby Thou hast brought me on to such a life, is before my eyes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:13
verses.text: "And I have been pleasing in Thy truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:14
verses.text: And since my own falsehood hath been displeasing to me, but Thy truth pleasing, I have myself been pleasing also with it and in it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:15
verses.text: "I have not sat with the council of vanity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:16
verses.text: I have not chosen to give my heart to them who endeavour to provide, what is impossible, how they may be blessed in the enjoyment of things transitory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:17
verses.text: "And I will not enter in with them that work wickedly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:18
verses.text: And since this is the very cause of all wickedness, therefore I will not have my conscience hid, with them that work wickedly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:19
verses.text: "I have hated the congregation of evil doers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:20
verses.text: But to arrive at this council of vanity, congregations of evil doers are formed, which I have hated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:21
verses.text: "And I will not sit with the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:22
verses.text: And, therefore, with such a council, with the ungodly, I will not sit, that is, I will not place my consent "And I will not sit with the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:23
verses.text: "I will wash mine hands amid the innocent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:24
verses.text: I will make clean my works among the innocent: among the innocent will I wash mine hands, with which I shall embrace Thy glorious gifts "And I will compass Thy altar, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:25
verses.text: "That I may hear the voice of Thy praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:26
verses.text: That I may learn how to praise Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:27
verses.text: "And that I may declare all Thy wondrous works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:28
verses.text: And after I have learnt, I may set forth all Thy wondrous works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:29
verses.text: "O Lord, I have loved the beauty of Thy house:" of Thy Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:30
verses.text: "And the place of the habitation of Thy glory" : where Thou dwellest, and art glorified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:31
verses.text: "Destroy not my soul with the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:32
verses.text: Destroy not then, together with them that hate Thee, my soul, which hath loved the beauty of Thy house.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:33
verses.text: "And my life with the men of blood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:34
verses.text: And with them that hate their neighbour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:35
verses.text: For Thy house is beautified with the two commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:36
verses.text: "In whose hands is wickedness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:37
verses.text: Destroy me not then with the ungodly and the men of blood, whose works are wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:38
verses.text: "Their right hand is full of gifts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:39
verses.text: And that which was given them to obtain eternal salvation, they have converted into the receiving this world's gifts, "supposing that godliness is a trade".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:40
verses.text: "But I have walked in mine innocence: deliver me, and have mercy on me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:41
verses.text: Let so great a price of my Lord's Blood avail for my complete deliverance: and in the dangers of this life let not Thy mercy leave me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:42
verses.text: "My foot hath stood in uprightness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:43
verses.text: My Love hath not withdrawn from Thy righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:44
verses.text: "In the Churches I will bless Thee, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 26:45
verses.text: I will not hide Thy blessing, O Lord, from those whom Thou hast called; for next to the love of Thee I join the love of my neighbour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:1
verses.text: Psalm XXVII  Of David himself, before he was anointed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:2
verses.text: Christ's young soldier speaketh, on his coming to the faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:3
verses.text: "The Lord is my light, and my salvation: whom shall I fear?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:4
verses.text: The Lord will give me both knowledge of Himself, and salvation: who shall take me from Him? "The Lord is the Protector of my life: of whom shall I be afraid?" The Lord will repel all the assaults and snares of mine enemy: of no man shall I be afraid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:5
verses.text: "Whilst the guilty approach unto me to eat up my flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:6
verses.text: Whilst the guilty come near to recognise and insult me, that they may exalt themselves above me in my change for the better; that with their reviling tooth they may consume not me, but rather my fleshly desires.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:7
verses.text: "Mine enemies who trouble me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:8
verses.text: Not they only who trouble me, blaming me with a friendly intent, and wishing to recall me from my purpose, but mine enemies also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:9
verses.text: "They became weak, and fell".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:10
verses.text: Whilst then they do this with the desire of defending their own opinion, they became weak to believe better things, and began to hate the word of salvation, whereby I do what displeases them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:11
verses.text: "If camps stand together against me, my heart will not fear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:12
verses.text: But if the multitude of gain-sayers conspire to stand together against me, my heart will not fear, so as to go over to their side.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:13
verses.text: "If war rise up against me, in this will I trust".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:14
verses.text: If the persecution of this world arise against me, in this petition, which I am pondering, will I place my hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:15
verses.text: "One have I asked of the Lord, this will I require".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:16
verses.text: For one petition have I asked the Lord, this will I require.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:17
verses.text: "That I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:18
verses.text: That as long as I am in this life, no adversities may exclude me from the number of them who hold the unity and the truth of the Lord's faith throughout the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:19
verses.text: "That I may contemplate the delight of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:20
verses.text: With this end, namely, that persevering in the faith, the delightsome vision may appear to me, which I may contemplate face to face.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:21
verses.text: "And I shall be protected, His temple".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:22
verses.text: And death being swallowed up in victory, I shall be clothed with immortality, being made His temple.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:23
verses.text: "For He hath hidden me in His tabernacle in the day of my evils".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:24
verses.text: For He hath hidden me in the dispensation of His Incarnate Word in the time of temptations, to which my mortal life is exposed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:25
verses.text: "He hath protected me in the secret place of His tabernacle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:26
verses.text: He hath protected me, with the heart believing unto righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:27
verses.text: "On a rock hath He exalted me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:28
verses.text: And that what I believed might be made manifest for salvation, He hath made my confession to be conspicuous in His own strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:29
verses.text: "And now, lo! He hath exalted mine head above mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:30
verses.text: What doth He reserve for me at the last, when even now the body is dead because of sin, lo! I feel that my mind serves the law of God, and is not led captive under the rebellious law of sin? "I have gone about, and have sacrificed in His tabernacle the sacrifice of rejoicing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:31
verses.text: I have considered the circuit of the world, believing on Christ; and in that for us God was humbled in time, I have praised Him with rejoicing: for with such sacrifice He is well pleased.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:32
verses.text: "I will sing and give praises to the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:33
verses.text: In heart and in deed I will be glad in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:34
verses.text: "Hear my voice, O Lord, wherewith I have cried unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:35
verses.text: Hear, Lord, my interior voice, which with a strong intention I have addressed to Thy ears.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:36
verses.text: "Have mercy upon me, and hear me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:37
verses.text: Have mercy upon me, and hear me therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:38
verses.text: "My heart hath said to Thee, I have sought Thy countenance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:39
verses.text: For I have not exhibited myself to men; but in secret, where Thou alone hearest, my heart hath said to Thee; I have not sought from Thee aught without Thee as a reward, but Thy countenance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:40
verses.text: "Thy countenance, O Lord, will I seek".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:41
verses.text: In thus search will I perseveringly persist: for not aught that is common, but Thy countenance, O Lord, will I seek, that I may love Thee freely, since nothing more precious do I find.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:42
verses.text: "Turn not away Thy face from me" : that I may find what I seek.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:43
verses.text: "Turn not aside in anger from Thy servant:" lest, while seeking Thee, I fall in with somewhat else.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:44
verses.text: For what is more grievous than this punishment to one who loveth and seeketh the truth of Thy countenance? "Be Thou my Helper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:45
verses.text: How shall I find it, if Thou help me not? "Leave me not, neither despise me, O God my Saviour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:46
verses.text: Scorn not that a mortal dares to seek the Eternal; for Thou, God, dost heal the wound of my sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:47
verses.text: "For my father and my mother have left me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:48
verses.text: For the kingdom of this world and the city of this world, of which I was born in time and mortality, have left me seeking Thee, and despising what they promised, since they could not give what I seek.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:49
verses.text: "But the Lord took me up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:50
verses.text: But the Lord, who can give me Himself, took me up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:51
verses.text: "Appoint me a law, O Lord, in Thy way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:52
verses.text: For me then who am setting out toward Thee, and commenting so great a profession, of arriving at wisdom, from fear, appoint, O Lord, a law in Thy way, lest in my wandering Thy rule abandon me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:53
verses.text: "And direct me in the right path because of mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:54
verses.text: And direct me in the right way of its straits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:55
verses.text: For it is not enough to begin, since enemies cease not until the end is attained.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:56
verses.text: "Deliver me not up unto the souls of them that trouble me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:57
verses.text: Suffer not them that trouble me to be satiated with my evils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:58
verses.text: "For unrighteous witnesses have risen up against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:59
verses.text: For there have risen up against me they that speak falsely of me, to remove and call me back from Thee, as if I seek glory of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:60
verses.text: "And iniquity hath lied unto itself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:61
verses.text: Therefore iniquity hath been pleased with its own lie.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:62
verses.text: For me it hath not moved, to whom because of this there hath been promised a greater reward in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:63
verses.text: "I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:64
verses.text: And since my Lord hath first suffered these things, if I too despise the tongues of the dying ("for the mouth that lieth slayeth the soul"), I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living, where there is no place for falsity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:65
verses.text: "Wait on the Lord, quit thyself like a man: and let thy heart be strong, yea wait on the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:66
verses.text: But when shall this be? It is arduous for a mortal, it is slow to a lover: but listen to the voice, that deceiveth not, of him that saith, "Wait on the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:67
verses.text: Endure the burning of the reins manfully, and the burning of the heart stoutly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:68
verses.text: Think not that what thou dost not as yet receive is denied thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 27:69
verses.text: That thou faint not in despair, see how it is said, "Wait on the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:1
verses.text: Psalm XXVIII  Of David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:2
verses.text: It is the Voice of the Mediator Himself, strong of hand in the conflict of the Passion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:3
verses.text: Now what He seems to wish for against His enemies, is not the wish of malevolence, but the declaration of their punishment; as in the Gospel, with the cities, in which though He had performed miracles, yet they had not believed on Him, He doth not wish in any evil will what He saith, but predicteth what is impending over them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:4
verses.text: "Unto Thee, O Lord, have I cried; My God, be not silent from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:5
verses.text: Unto Thee, O Lord, have I cried; My God, separate not the unity of Thy Word from that which as Man I am.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:6
verses.text: "Lest at any time Thou be silent from me: and I shall be like them that go down into the pit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:7
verses.text: For from this, that the Eternity of Thy Word ceaseth not to unite Itself to Me, it comes that I am not such a man as the rest of men, who are born into the deep misery of this world: where, as if Thou art silent, Thy Word is not recognised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:8
verses.text: "Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication, whist I pray unto Thee, whilst I hold up my hands to Thy holy temple".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:9
verses.text: Whilst I am crucified for their salvation, who on believing become Thy holy temple.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:10
verses.text: "Draw not My Soul away with sinners, and destroy me not with them that work iniquity, with them that speak peace with their neighbours".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:11
verses.text: With them that say unto Me, "We know that Thou art a Master come from God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:12
verses.text: "But evil in their hearts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:13
verses.text: But they speak evil in their hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:14
verses.text: "Give unto them according to their works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:15
verses.text: Give unto them according to their works, for this is just.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:16
verses.text: "And according to the malice of their affections".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:17
verses.text: For aiming at evil, they cannot discover good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:18
verses.text: "According to the works of their hands give Thou unto them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:19
verses.text: Although what they have done may avail for salvation to others, yet give Thou unto them according to the works of their wills.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:20
verses.text: "Pay them their recompense".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:21
verses.text: Because, for the truth which they heard, they wished to recompense deceit; let their own deceit deceive them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:22
verses.text: "For they have not had understanding in the works of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:23
verses.text: And whence is it clear that this hath befallen them? From this forsooth, "for they have not had understanding in the works of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:24
verses.text: This very thing, in truth, hath been, even now, their recompense, that in Him whom they tempted with malicious intent as a Man, they should not recognise God, with what design the Father sent Him in the Flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:25
verses.text: "And the works of His hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:26
verses.text: Nor be moved by those visible works, which are laid out before their very eyes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:27
verses.text: "Thou shalt destroy them, and not build them up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:28
verses.text: Let them do Me no hurt, nay, nor again in their endeavour to raise engines against My Church, let them aught avail.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:29
verses.text: "Blessed be the Lord, for He hath heard the voice of My prayer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:30
verses.text: "The Lord My Helper and My Protector".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:31
verses.text: The Lord helping Me in so great sufferings, and protecting Me with immortality in My resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:32
verses.text: "In Him hath My Heart trusted, and I have been helped".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:33
verses.text: "And My Flesh hath flourished again:" that is, and My Flesh hath risen again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:34
verses.text: "And of my will I will confess unto Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:35
verses.text: Wherefore, the fear of death being now destroyed, not by the necessity of fear under the Law, but with a free will with the Law, shall they who believe on Me, confess unto Him; and because I am in them, I will confess.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:36
verses.text: "The Lord is the strength of His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:37
verses.text: Not that people "ignorant of the righteousness of God, and willing to establish their own".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:38
verses.text: For they thought not themselves strong in themselves: for the Lord is the strength of His people, struggling in this life's difficulties with the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:39
verses.text: "And the protector of the salvation of His Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:40
verses.text: That, having saved them by His Christ after the strength of war, He may protect them at the last with the immortality of peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:41
verses.text: "Save Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:42
verses.text: I intercede therefore, after My Flesh hath flourished again, because Thou hast said, "Desire of Me, and I will give Thee the heathen for Thine inheritance;" "Save Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance:" for "all Mine are Thine".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:43
verses.text: "And rule them, and set them up even for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 28:44
verses.text: And rule them in this temporal life, and raise them from hence into life eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:1
verses.text: Psalm XXIX  A psalm of David himself, of the consummation of the tabernacle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:2
verses.text: A Psalm of the Mediator Himself, strong of hand, of the perfection of the Church in this world, where she wars in time against the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:3
verses.text: The Prophet speaks, "Bring unto the Lord, O ye Sons of God, bring unto the Lord the young of rams".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:4
verses.text: Bring unto the Lord yourselves, whom the Apostles, the leaders of the flocks, have begotten by the Gospel "Bring unto the Lord glory and honour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:5
verses.text: By your works let the Lord be glorified and honoured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:6
verses.text: "Bring unto the Lord glory to His name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:7
verses.text: Let Him be made known gloriously throughout the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:8
verses.text: "Worship the Lord in His holy court".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:9
verses.text: Worship the Lord in your heart enlarged and sanctified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:10
verses.text: For ye are His regal holy habitation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:11
verses.text: "The Voice of the Lord is upon the waters".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:12
verses.text: The Voice of Christ is upon the peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:13
verses.text: "The God of majesty hath thundered".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:14
verses.text: The God of majesty, from the cloud of the flesh, hath awfully preached repentance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:15
verses.text: "The Lord is upon many waters".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:16
verses.text: The Lord Jesus Himself, after that He sent forth His Voice upon the peoples, and struck them with awe, converted them to Himself, and dwelt in them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:17
verses.text: "The Voice of the Lord is in power".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:18
verses.text: The Voice of the Lord now in them themselves, making them powerful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:19
verses.text: "The Voice of the Lord is in great might".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:20
verses.text: The Voice of the Lord working great things in them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:21
verses.text: "The Voice of the Lord breaking the cedars".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:22
verses.text: The Voice of the Lord humbling the proud in brokenness of heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:23
verses.text: "The Lord shall break the cedars of Libanus".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:24
verses.text: The Lord by repentance shall break them that are lifted on high by the splendour of earthly nobility, when to confound them He shall have "chosen the base things of this world," in the which to display His Divinity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:25
verses.text: "And shall bruise them as the calf of Libanus".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:26
verses.text: And when their proud exaltation hath been cut off, He will lay them low after the imitation of His Own humility, who like a calf was led to slaughter by the nobility of this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:27
verses.text: "For the kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers agreed together against the Lord, and against His Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:28
verses.text: "And the Beloved is as the young of the unicorns".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:29
verses.text: For even He the Beloved, and the Only One of the Father, "emptied Himself" of His glory; and was made man, like a child of the Jews, that were "ignorant of God's righteousness," and proudly boasting of their own righteousness as peculiarly theirs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:30
verses.text: "The Voice of the Lord cutting short the flame of fire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:31
verses.text: The Voice of the Lord, without any harm to Himself, passing through all the excited ardour of them that persecute Him, or dividing the furious rage of His persecutors, so that some should say, "Is not this haply the very Christ;" others, "Nay; but He deceiveth the people:" and so cutting short their mad tumult, as to pass some over into His love, and leave others in their malice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:32
verses.text: "The Voice of the Lord moving the wilderness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:33
verses.text: The Voice of the Lord moving to the faith the Gentiles once "without hope, and without God in the world;" where no prophet, no preacher of God's word, as it were, no man had dwelt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:34
verses.text: "And the Lord will move the desert of Cades".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:35
verses.text: And then the Lord will cause the holy word of His Scriptures to be fully known, which was abandoned by the Jews who understood it not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:36
verses.text: "The Voice of the Lord perfecting the stags".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:37
verses.text: For the Voice of the Lord hath first perfected them that overcame and repelled the envenomed tongues "And will reveal the woods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:38
verses.text: And then will He reveal to them the darknesses of the Divine books, and the shadowy depths of the mysteries, where they feed with freedom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:39
verses.text: "And in His temple doth every man speak of His glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:40
verses.text: And in His Church all born again to an eternal hope praise God, each for His own gift, which He hath received from the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:41
verses.text: "The Lord inhabiteth the deluge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:42
verses.text: The Lord therefore first inhabiteth the deluge of this world in His Saints, kept safely in the Church, as in the ark.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:43
verses.text: "And the Lord shall sit a King for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:44
verses.text: And afterward He will sit reigning in them for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:45
verses.text: "The Lord will give strength to His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:46
verses.text: For the Lord will give strength to His people fighting against the storms and whirlwinds of this world, for peace in this world He hath not promised them "The Lord will bless His people in peace".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 29:47
verses.text: And the same Lord will bless His people, affording them peace in Himself; for, saith He, "My peace I give unto you, My peace I leave with you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:1
verses.text: Psalm XXX  To the end, the psalm of the canticle of the dedication of the house, of David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:2
verses.text: To the end, a Psalm of the joy of the Resurrection, and the change, the renewing of the body to an  immortal state, and not only of the Lord, but also of the whole Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:3
verses.text: For in the former Psalm the tabernacle was finished, wherein we dwell in the time of war: but now the house is dedicated, which will abide in peace everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:4
verses.text: It is then whole Christ who speaketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:5
verses.text: "I will exalt Thee, O Lord, for Thou hast taken Me up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:6
verses.text: I will praise Thy high Majesty, O Lord, for Thou hast taken Me up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:7
verses.text: "Thou hast not made Mine enemies to rejoice over Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:8
verses.text: And those, who have so often endeavoured to oppress Me with various persecutions throughout the world, Thou hast not made to rejoice over Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:9
verses.text: "O Lord, My God, I have cried unto Thee, and Thou hast healed Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:10
verses.text: O Lord, My God, I have cried unto Thee, and I no longer bear about a body enfeebled and sick by mortality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:11
verses.text: "O Lord, Thou hast brought back My Soul from hell, and Thou hast saved Me from them that go down into the pit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:12
verses.text: Thou hast saved Me from the condition of profound darkness, and the lowest slough of corruptible flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:13
verses.text: "Sing to the Lord, O ye saints of His".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:14
verses.text: The prophet seeing these future things, rejoiceth, and saith, "Sing to the Lord, O ye saints of His.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:15
verses.text: And make confession of the remembrance of His holiness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:16
verses.text: And make confession to Him, that He hath not forgotten the sanctification, wherewith He hath sanctified you, although all this intermediate period belong to your desires.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:17
verses.text: "For in His indignation is wrath".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:18
verses.text: For He hath avenged against you the first sin, for which you have paid by death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:19
verses.text: "And life in His will".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:20
verses.text: And life eternal, whereunto you could not return by any strength of your own, hath He given, because He so would.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:21
verses.text: "In the evening weeping will tarry".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:22
verses.text: Evening began, when the light of wisdom withdrew from sinful man, when he was condemned to death: from this evening weeping will tarry, as long as God's people are, amid labours and temptations, awaiting the day of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:23
verses.text: "And exultation in the morning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:24
verses.text: Even to the morning, when there will be the exultation of the resurrection, which hath shone forth by anticipation in the morning resurrection of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:25
verses.text: "But I said in my abundance, I shall not be moved for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:26
verses.text: But I, that people which was speaking from the first, said in mine abundance, suffering now no more any want, "I shall not be moved for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:27
verses.text: "O Lord, in Thy will Thou hast afforded strength unto my beauty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:28
verses.text: But that this my abundance, O Lord, is not of myself, but that in Thy will Thou hast afforded strength unto my beauty, I have learnt from this, "Thou turnedst away Thy Face from me, and I became troubled;" for Thou hast sometimes turned away Thy Face from the sinner, and I became troubled, when the illumination of Thy knowledge withdrew from me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:29
verses.text: "Unto Thee, O Lord, will I cry, and unto my God will I pray".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:30
verses.text: And bringing to mind that time of my trouble and misery, and as it were established therein, I hear the voice of Thy First-Begotten, my Head, about to die for me, and saying "Unto Thee, O Lord, will I cry, and unto My God will I pray".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:31
verses.text: "What profit" is there in the shedding of My blood, whilst I go down to corruption? "Shall dust confess unto Thee?" For if I shall not rise immediately, and My body shall become corrupt, "shall dust confess unto Thee?" that is, the crowd of the ungodly, whom I shall justify by My resurrection? "Or declare Thy truth?" Or for the salvation of the rest declare Thy truth?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:32
verses.text: "The Lord hath heard, and had mercy on Me, the Lord hath become My helper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:33
verses.text: Nor did "He suffer His holy One to see corruption".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:34
verses.text: "Thou hast turned My mourning into joy to Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:35
verses.text: Whom I, the Church, having received, the First-Begotten from the dead, now in the dedication of Thine house, say, "Thou hast turned my mourning into joy to me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:36
verses.text: Thou hast put off my sackcloth, and girded me with gladness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:37
verses.text: Thou hast torn off the veil of my sins, the sadness of my mortality; and hast girded me with the first robe, with immortal gladness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:38
verses.text: "That my glory should sing unto Thee, and I should not be pricked".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:39
verses.text: That now, not my humiliation, but my glory should not lament, but should sing unto Thee, for that now out of humiliation Thou hast exalted me; and that I should not be pricked with the consciousness of sin, with the fear of death, with the fear of judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:40
verses.text: "O Lord, my God, I will confess unto Thee for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 30:41
verses.text: And this is my glory, O Lord, my God, that I should confess unto Thee for ever, that I have nothing of myself, but that all my good is of Thee, who art "God, All in all".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:1
verses.text: Psalm XXXI  To the end, a psalm of David himself, an ecstasy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:2
verses.text: To the end a Psalm of David Himself, the Mediator strong of hand in persecutions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:3
verses.text: For the word ecstasy, which is added to the title, signifies a tran sport of the mind, which is produced either by a panic, or by some revelation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:4
verses.text: But in this Psalm the panic of the people of God troubled by the persecution of all the heathen, and by the failing of faith throughout the world, is principally seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:5
verses.text: But first the Mediator Himself speaks: then the People redeemed by His Blood gives thanks: at last in trouble it speaks at length, which is what belongs to the ecstasy; but the Person of the Prophet himself is twice interposed, near the end, and at the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:6
verses.text: "In Thee, O Lord, have I trusted, let Me not be put to confusion for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:7
verses.text: In Thee, O Lord, have I trusted, let Me never be confounded, whilst they shall insult Me as one like other men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:8
verses.text: "In Thy righteousness rescue Me, and deliver Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:9
verses.text: And in Thy righteousness rescue Me from the pit of death, and deliver Me out of their company.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:10
verses.text: "Bend down Thine ear unto Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:11
verses.text: Hear Me in My humiliation, nigh at hand unto Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:12
verses.text: "Make haste to deliver Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:13
verses.text: Defer not to the end of the world, as with all who believe on Me, My separation from sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:14
verses.text: "Be unto Me a God who protecteth Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:15
verses.text: Be unto Me God, and Protector.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:16
verses.text: "And a house of refuge, that Thou mayest save Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:17
verses.text: And as a house, wherein taking refuge I may be saved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:18
verses.text: "For Thou art My strength, and My refuge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:19
verses.text: For Thou art unto Me My strength to bear My persecutors, and My refuge to escape them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:20
verses.text: "And for Thy Name's sake Thou shalt be My guide, and shalt nourish Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:21
verses.text: And that by Me Thou mayest be known to all the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:22
verses.text: I will in all things follow Thy will; and, by assembling, by degrees, Saints unto Me, Thou shalt fulfil My body, and My perfect stature.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:23
verses.text: "Thou shalt bring Me out of this trap, which they have hidden for Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:24
verses.text: Thou shalt bring Me out of these snares, which they have hidden for Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:25
verses.text: "For Thou art My Protector".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:26
verses.text: "Into Thy hands I commend My Spirit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:27
verses.text: To Thy power I commend My Spirit, soon to receive It back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:28
verses.text: "Thou hast redeemed Me, O Lord God of truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:29
verses.text: Let the people too, redeemed by the Passion of their Lord, and joyful in the glorifying of their Head, say, "Thou hast redeemed me, O Lord God of truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:30
verses.text: "Thou hatest them that hold to vanity uselessly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:31
verses.text: Thou hatest them that hold to the false happiness of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:32
verses.text: "But I have trusted in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:33
verses.text: "I will be glad, and rejoice in Thy mercy:" which doth not deceive me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:34
verses.text: "For Thou hast regarded My humiliation:" wherein Thou hast subjected me to vanity in hope "Thou hast saved my soul from necessities".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:35
verses.text: Thou hast saved my soul from the necessities of fear, that with a free love it may serve Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:36
verses.text: "And hast not shut me up into the hands of the enemy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:37
verses.text: And hast not shut me up, that I should have no opening for recovering unto liberty, and be given over for ever into the power of the devil, ensnaring me with the desire of this life, and terrifying me with death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:38
verses.text: "Thou hast set my feet in a large room".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:39
verses.text: The resurrection of my Lord being known, and mine own being promised me, my love, having been brought out of the straits of fear, walks abroad in continuance, into the expanse of liberty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:40
verses.text: "Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am troubled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:41
verses.text: But what is this unlooked-for cruelty of the persecutors, striking such dread into me? "Have mercy on me, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:42
verses.text: For I am now no more alarmed for death, but for torments and tortures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:43
verses.text: "Mine eye hath been disordered by anger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:44
verses.text: I had mine eye upon Thee, that Thou shouldest not abandon me: Thou art angry, and hast disordered it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:45
verses.text: "My soul, and my belly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:46
verses.text: By the same anger my soul hath been disturbed, and my memory, whereby I retained what my God hath suffered for me, and what He hath promised me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:47
verses.text: "For my life hath failed in pain" (ver ).

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:48
verses.text: For my life is to confess Thee, but it failed in pain, when the enemy had said, Let them be tortured until they deny Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:49
verses.text: "And my years in groanings".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:50
verses.text: The time that I pass in this world is not taken away from me by death, but abides, and is spent in groanings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:51
verses.text: "My strength hath been weakened by want".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:52
verses.text: I want the health of this body, and racking pains come on me: I want the dissolution of the body, and death forbears to come: and in this want my confidence hath been weakened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:53
verses.text: "And my bones have been disturbed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:54
verses.text: And my stedfastness hath been disturbed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:55
verses.text: "I have been made a reproach above all mine enemies" (ver ).

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:56
verses.text: All the wicked are my enemies; and nevertheless they for their wickednesses are tortured only till they confess: I then have overpassed their reproach, I, whose confession death doth not follow, but racking pains follow upon it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:57
verses.text: "And to my neighbours too much".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:58
verses.text: This hath seemed too much to them, who were already drawing near to know Thee, and to hold the faith that I hold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:59
verses.text: "And a fear to mine acquaintance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:60
verses.text: And into my very acquaintance I struck fear by the example of my dreadful tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:61
verses.text: "They that did see me, fled without from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:62
verses.text: Because they did not understand my inward and invisible hope, they fled from me into things outward and visible.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:63
verses.text: "I have been forgotten, as one dead from the heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:64
verses.text: And they have forgotten me, as if I were dead from their hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:65
verses.text: "I have become as a lost vessel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:66
verses.text: I have seemed to myself to be lost to all the Lord's service, living in this world, and gaining none, when all were afraid to join themselves unto me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:67
verses.text: "For I have heard the rebuking of many dwelling by in a circuit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:68
verses.text: For I have heard many rebuking me, in the pilgrimage of this world near me, following the circuit of time, and refusing to return with me to the eternal country.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:69
verses.text: "Whilst they were assembling themselves together against me, they conspired that they might take my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:70
verses.text: That my soul, which should by death easily escape from their power, might consent unto them, they imagined a device, whereby they would not suffer me even to die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:71
verses.text: "But I have hoped in Thee, O Lord; I have said, Thou art my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:72
verses.text: For Thou hast not changed, that Thou shouldest not save, Who dost correct.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:73
verses.text: "In Thy hands" are "my lots".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:74
verses.text: In Thy power are my lots.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:75
verses.text: For I see no desert for which out of the universal ungodliness of the human race Thou hast elected me particularly to salvation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:76
verses.text: And though there be with Thee some just and secret order in my election, yet I, from whom this is hid, have attained by lot unto my Lord's vesture "Deliver me from the hands of mine enemies, and from them that persecute me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:77
verses.text: "Make Thy Face to shine upon Thy servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:78
verses.text: Make it known to men, who do not think that I belong unto Thee, that Thy Face is bent upon me, and that I serve Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:79
verses.text: "Save me in Thy mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:80
verses.text: "O Lord, let me not be confounded, for I have called upon Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:81
verses.text: O Lord, let me not be put to shame by those who insult me, for that I have called upon Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:82
verses.text: "Let the ungodly be ashamed, and be brought down to hell".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:83
verses.text: Let them rather who call upon stones be ashamed, and made to dwell with darkness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:84
verses.text: "Let the deceitful lips be made dumb".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:85
verses.text: In making known to the peoples Thy mysteries wrought in me, strike with dumb amazement the lips of them that invent falsehood of me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:86
verses.text: "Which speak iniquity against the Righteous, in pride and contempt".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:87
verses.text: Which speak iniquity against Christ, in their pride and contempt of Him as a crucified man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:88
verses.text: "How great" is "the multitude of Thy sweetness, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:89
verses.text: Here the Prophet exclaims, having sight of all this, and admiring how manifoldly plenteous is Thy sweetness, O Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:90
verses.text: "Which Thou hast hid for them that fear Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:91
verses.text: Even those, whom Thou correctest, Thou lovest much: but lest they should go on negligently from relaxed security, Thou hidest from them the sweetness of Thy love, for whom it is profitable to fear Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:92
verses.text: "Thou hast perfected it for them that hope in Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:93
verses.text: But Thou hast perfected this sweetness for them that hope in Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:94
verses.text: For Thou dost not withdraw from them what they look for perseveringly even unto the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:95
verses.text: "In sight of the sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:96
verses.text: For it does not escape the notice of the sons of men, who now live no more after Adam, but after the Son of Man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:97
verses.text: "Thou wilt hide them in the hidden place of Thy Countenance:" which seat Thou shalt preserve for everlasting in the hidden place of the knowledge of Thee for them that hope in Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:98
verses.text: "From the troubling of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:99
verses.text: So that now they suffer no more trouble from men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:100
verses.text: "Thou wilt protect them in Thy tabernacle from the contradiction of tongues".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:101
verses.text: But here meanwhile whilst evil tongues murmur against them, saying, Who hath come thence? Thou wilt protect them in the tabernacle, that of faith in those things, which the Lord wrought and endured for us in time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:102
verses.text: "Blessed be the Lord; for He hath made His mercy marvellous, in the city of compassing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:103
verses.text: Blessed be the Lord, for after the correction of the sharpest persecutions He hath made His mercy marvellous to all throughout the world, in the circuit of human society.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:104
verses.text: "I said in my ecstasy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:105
verses.text: Whence that people again speaking saith, I said in my fear, when the heathen were raging horribly against me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:106
verses.text: "I have been cast forth from the sight of Thine eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:107
verses.text: For if Thou hadst regard to me, Thou wouldest not suffer me to endure these things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:108
verses.text: "Therefore Thou heardest, O Lord, the voice of my prayer, when I cried unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:109
verses.text: Therefore putting a limit to correction, and showing that I have part in Thy care, Thou heardest, O Lord, the voice of my prayer, when I raised it high out of tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:110
verses.text: "Love the Lord, all ye His saints".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:111
verses.text: The Prophet again exhorts, having sight of these things, and saith, "Love the Lord, all ye His saints; for the Lord will require truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:112
verses.text: Since "if the righteous shall scarcely be saved, where shall the sinner and the ungodly appear?" "And He will repay them that do exceeding proudly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:113
verses.text: And He will repay them who even when conquered are not converted, because they are very proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:114
verses.text: "Quit you like men, and let your heart be strengthened" : working good without fainting, that ye may reap in due season.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 31:115
verses.text: "All ye who trust in the Lord:" that is, ye who duly fear and worship Him, trust ye in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:1
verses.text: Psalm XXXII  To David himself; for understanding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:2
verses.text: To David himself; for understanding; by which it is understood that not by the merits of works, but by the grace of God, man is delivered, confessing his sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:3
verses.text: "Blessed are they whose unrighteousness is forgiven, and whose sins are covered" : and whose sins are buried in oblivion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:4
verses.text: "Blessed is the man to whom the Lord hath not imputed sin, nor is there guile in his mouth" : nor has he in his mouth boastings of righteousness, when his conscience is full of sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:5
verses.text: "Because I kept silence, my bones waxed old:" because I made not with my mouth "confession unto salvation," all firmness in me has grown old in infirmity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:6
verses.text: "Through my roaring all the day long" : when I was ungodly and a blasphemer, crying against God, as though defending and excusing my sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:7
verses.text: "Because day and night Thy Hand was heavy upon me:" because, through the continual punishment of Thy scourges, "I was turned in misery, while a thorn was fixed through me" : I was made miserable by knowing my misery, being pricked with an evil conscience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:8
verses.text: "I acknowledged my sin, and my unrighteousness have I not hid:" that is, my unrighteousness have I not concealed "I said, I will confess against myself my unrighteousness to the Lord:" I said, I will confess, not against God (as in my ungodly crying, when I kept silence), but against myself, my unrighteousness to the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:9
verses.text: "And Thou forgavest the iniquity of my heart" ; hearing the word of confession in the heart, before it was uttered with the voice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:10
verses.text: "For this shall every one that is holy pray unto Thee in an acceptable time:" for this wickedness of heart shall every one that is righteous pray unto Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:11
verses.text: For not by their own merits will they be holy, but by that acceptable time, that is, at His coming, who redeemed us from sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:12
verses.text: "Nevertheless in the flood of great waters they shall not come nigh him" : nevertheless, let none think, when the end has come suddenly, as in the days of Noah, that there remaineth a place of confession, whereby he may draw nigh unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:13
verses.text: "Thou art my refuge from the pressures, which have compassed me about:" Thou art my refuge from the pressure of my sins, which hath compassed my heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:14
verses.text: "O Thou, my Rejoicing, deliver me from them that compass me about" : in Thee is my joy: deliver me from the sorrow which my sins bring upon me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:15
verses.text: Diapsalma.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:16
verses.text: The answer of God: "I will give thee understanding, and will set thee in the way in which thou shalt go;" I will give thee understanding after confession, that thou depart not from the way in which thou shouldest go; lest thou wish to be in thine own power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:17
verses.text: "I will fix Mine Eyes upon thee" ; so will make sure upon thee My Love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:18
verses.text: "Be not ye like unto horse or mule, which have no understanding:" and therefore would govern themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:19
verses.text: But saith the Prophet, "Hold in their jaws with bit and bridle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:20
verses.text: Do Thou then, O God, unto them "that will not come nigh Thee" , what man doth to horse and mule, that by scourges Thou make them to bear Thy rule.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:21
verses.text: "Many are the scourges of the sinner:" much is he scourged, who, confessing not his sins to God, would be his own ruler.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:22
verses.text: "But he that trusteth in the Lord, mercy compasseth him about" ; but he that trusteth in the Lord, and submitteth himself to His rule, mercy shall compass him about.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:23
verses.text: "Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye righteous:" be glad, and rejoice, ye righteous, not in yourselves, but in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 32:24
verses.text: "And glory, all ye that are right in heart" : and glory in Him, all ye who understand that it is right to be subject unto Him, that so ye may be placed above all things beside.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:1
verses.text: Psalm XXXIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:2
verses.text: "Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous:" rejoice, O ye righteous, not in yourselves, for that is not safe; but in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:3
verses.text: "For praise is comely to the upright" : these praise the Lord, who submit themselves unto the Lord; for else they are distorted and perverse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:4
verses.text: "Praise the Lord with harp:" praise the Lord, presenting unto Him your bodies a living sacrifice "Sing unto Him with the psaltery for ten strings" : let your members be servants to the love of God, and of your neighbour, in which are kept both the three and the seven commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:5
verses.text: "Sing unto Him a new song:" sing unto Him a song of the grace of faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:6
verses.text: "Sing skilfully unto Him with jubilation" : sing skillfully unto Him with rejoicing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:7
verses.text: "For the Word of the Lord is right:" for the Word of the Lord is right, to make you that which of yourselves ye cannot be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:8
verses.text: "And all His works are done in faith" : lest any think that by the merit of works he hath arrived at faith, when in faith are done all the works which God Himself loveth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:9
verses.text: "He loveth Mercy and Judgment:" for He loveth Mercy, which now He showeth first; and Judgment, wherewith He exacteth that which He hath first shown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:10
verses.text: "The earth is full of the Mercy of the Lord" : throughout the whole world are sins forgiven unto men by the Mercy of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:11
verses.text: "By the Word of the Lord were the heavens made firm:" for not by themselves, but by the Word of the Lord were the righteous made strong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:12
verses.text: "And all the strength of them by the Breath of His Mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:13
verses.text: And all their faith by His Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:14
verses.text: "He gathereth the waters of the sea together as into a bottle:" He gathered the people of the world together, to confession of mortified sin, lest through pride they flow too freely.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:15
verses.text: "He layeth up the deep in storehouses" : and keepeth in them His secrets for riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:16
verses.text: "Let all the earth fear the Lord:" let every sinner fear, that so he may cease to sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:17
verses.text: "Let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of Him" : not of the terrors of men, or of any creature, but of Him let them stand in awe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:18
verses.text: "For He spake, and they were made:" for no other one made those things which are to fear; but He spake, and they were made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:19
verses.text: "He commanded, and they were created" : He commanded by His Word, and they were created.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:20
verses.text: "The Lord bringeth the counsel of the heathen to nought;" of them that seek not His Kingdom, but kingdoms of their own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:21
verses.text: "He maketh the devices of the people of none effect:" of them that covet earthly happiness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:22
verses.text: "And reproveth the counsels of princes" : of them that seek to rule over such peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:23
verses.text: "But the counsel of the Lord standeth for ever;" but the counsel of the Lord, whereby He maketh none blessed but him that submitteth unto Himself, standeth for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:24
verses.text: The thoughts of His Heart to all generations" : the thoughts of His Wisdom are not mutable, but endure to all generations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:25
verses.text: "Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord:" one nation is blessed, belonging to the heavenly city, which hath not chosen save the Lord for their God: "And the people whom He hath chosen for His own inheritance" : and which not of itself, but by the gift of God, hath been chosen, that He by possessing it may not suffer it to be uncared for and miserable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:26
verses.text: "The Lord looketh from Heaven; He beholdeth all the sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:27
verses.text: From the souls of the righteous, the Lord looketh mercifully upon all who would rise to newness of life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:28
verses.text: "From His prepared habitation:" from His habitation of assumed Humanity, which He prepared for Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:29
verses.text: "He looketh upon all the inhabitants of the earth" : He looketh mercifully upon all who live in the flesh, that He may be over them in ruling them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:30
verses.text: "He fashioneth their hearts singly:" He giveth spiritually to their hearts their proper gifts, so that neither the whole body may be eye, nor the whole hearing; but that one in this manner, another in that manner, may be incorporated with Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:31
verses.text: "He understandeth all their works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:32
verses.text: Before Him are all their works understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:33
verses.text: "A king shall not be saved by much strength:" he shall not be saved who ruleth his own flesh, if he presume much upon his own strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:34
verses.text: "Neither shall a giant be saved by much strength" : nor shall he be saved whoever warreth against the habit of his own lust, or against the devil and his angels, if he trust much to his own might.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:35
verses.text: "A horse is a deceitful thing for safety:" he is deceived, who thinketh either that through men he gaineth salvation received among men, or that by the impetuosity of his own courage he is defended from destruction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:36
verses.text: "In the abundance of his strength shall he not be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:37
verses.text: "Behold, the Eyes of the Lord are upon them that fear Him:" because if thou seek salvation, behold, the love of the Lord is upon them that fear Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:38
