verses.text: "Upon them that hope in His mercy" : that hope not in their own strength, but in His mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:39
verses.text: "To deliver their souls from death, and to keep them alive in famine".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:40
verses.text: To give them the nourishment of the Word, and of Everlasting Truth, which they lost while presuming on their own strength, and therefore have not even their own strength, from lack of righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:41
verses.text: "My soul shall be patient for the Lord:" that hereafter it may be filled with dainties incorruptible, meanwhile, whilst here it remaineth, my soul shall be patient for the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:42
verses.text: "For He is our Helper and Defender" : our Helper He is, while we endeavour after Him; and our Defender, while we resist the adversary.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:43
verses.text: "For our heart shall rejoice in Him:" for not in ourselves, wherein without Him there is great need; but in Himself shall our heart rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:44
verses.text: "And we have trusted in His holy Name" ; and therefore have we trusted that we shall come to God, because unto us absent hath He sent, through faith, His own Name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 33:45
verses.text: "Let Thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, according as we have hoped in Thee" : let Thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us; for hope confoundeth not, because we have hoped in Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:1
verses.text: Psalm XXXIV  A psalm of David, when he changed his countenance before Abimelech, and he sent him away, and he departed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:2
verses.text: Because there was there a sacrifice after the order of Aaron, and afterwards He of His Own Body and Blood appointed a sacrifice after the order of Melchizedek; He changed then His Countenance in the Priesthood, and sent away the kingdom of the Jews, and came to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:3
verses.text: What then is, "He affected"? He was full of affection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:4
verses.text: For what is so full of affection as the Mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, who, seeing our infirmity, that He might deliver us from everlasting death, underwent temporal death with such great injury and contumely? "And He drummed:" because a drum is not made, except when a skin is extended on wood; and David drummed, to signify that Christ should be crucified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:5
verses.text: But, "He drummed upon the doors of the city:" what are "the doors of the city," but our hearts which we had closed against Christ, who by the drum of His Cross hath opened the hearts of mortal men? "And was carried in His Own Hands:" how "carried in His Own Hands"? Because when He commended His Own Body and Blood, He took into His Hands that which the faithful know; and in a manner carried Himself, when He said, "This is My Body".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:6
verses.text: "And He fell down at the doors of the gate;" that is, He humbled Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:7
verses.text: For this it is, to fall down even at the very beginning of our faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:8
verses.text: For the door of the gate is the beginning of faith; whence beginneth the Church, and arriveth at last even unto sight: that as it believeth those things which it seeth not, it may deserve to enjoy them, when it shall have begun to see face to face.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:9
verses.text: So is the title of the Psalm; briefly we have heard it; let us now hear the very words of Him that affecteth, and drummeth upon the doors of the city.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:10
verses.text: "I will bless the Lord at all times; His praise shall be ever in my mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:11
verses.text: So speaketh Christ, so also let a Christian speak; for a Christian is in the Body of Christ; and therefore was Christ made Man, that that Christian might be enabled to be an Angel, who saith, "I will bless the Lord at all times".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:12
verses.text: When shall I "bless the Lord"? When He blesseth thee? When the goods of this world abound? When thou hast great abundance of corn, oil, and wine, of gold and silver, of servants and cattle; when this mortal health remaineth unwounded and sound; when all that are born to thee grow up, nothing is withdrawn by immature death, happiness wholly reigneth in thy house, and all things overflow around thee; then shalt thou bless the Lord? No; but "at all times".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:13
verses.text: Therefore both then, and when according to the time, or according to the scourges of our Lord God, these things are troubled, are taken away, are seldom born to thee, and born pass away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:14
verses.text: For these things come to pass, and thence followeth penury, need, labour, pain, and temptation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:15
verses.text: But thou, who hast sung, "I will bless the Lord at all times: His praise shall be ever in my mouth," both when He giveth them, bless; and when He taketh them away, bless.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:16
verses.text: For it is He that giveth, it is He that taketh away: but Himself from him that blesseth Him He taketh not away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:17
verses.text: But who is it that blesseth the Lord at all times, except the humble in heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:18
verses.text: For very humility taught our Lord in His Own Body and Blood: because when He commendeth His Own Body and Blood, He commendeth His Humility, in that which is written in this history, in that seeming madness of David, which we have passed by, "And his spittle ran down over his beard".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:19
verses.text: When the Apostle was read, Ye heard the same spittle, but running down over the beard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:20
verses.text: One saith perhaps, What spittle have we heard? Was it not read but now, where the Apostle saith, "The Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom?" But now it was read, "But we preach," saith he, "Christ crucified" (for then He drummed), "unto the Jews a stumbling block, and unto the Greeks foolishness; but unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the Power of God, and the Wisdom of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:21
verses.text: Because the Foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the Weakness of God is stronger than men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:22
verses.text: For spittle signifieth foolishness; spittle signifieth weakness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:23
verses.text: But if the Foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the Weakness of God is stronger than men; let not the spittle as it were offend thee, but observe that it runneth down over the beard: for as by the spittle, weakness; so by the beard, strength is signified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:24
verses.text: He covered then His Strength by the body of His Weakness, and that which without was weak, appeared as it were in spittle; but within His Divine Strength was covered as a beard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:25
verses.text: Therefore humility is commended unto us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:26
verses.text: Be humble if thou wouldest bless the Lord at all times, and that His praise should be ever in thy mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:27
verses.text: But wherefore doth man bless the Lord at all times? Because he is humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:28
verses.text: What is it to be humble? To take not praise unto himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:29
verses.text: Who would himself be praised, is proud: who is not proud, is humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:30
verses.text: Wouldest thou not then be proud? That thou mayest be humble, say what is here written; "In the Lord shall my soul be praised: the humble shall hear thereof and be glad".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:31
verses.text: Those then who will not be praised in the Lord, are not humble, but fierce, rough, lifted up, proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:32
verses.text: Gentle cattle would the Lord have; be thou the Lord's jumentum; that is, be thou humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:33
verses.text: He sitteth upon thee, He ruleth thee: fear not lest thou stumble, and fall headlong: that indeed is thy infirmity; but consider Who sitteth upon thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:34
verses.text: Thou art an ass's colt, but thou carriest Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:35
verses.text: For even He on an ass's colt came into the city; and that beast was gentle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:36
verses.text: "Be not ye as the horse or as the mule, which have no understanding".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:37
verses.text: For horse and mule sometimes lift up their neck, and by their own fierceness throw off their rider.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:38
verses.text: They are tamed with the bit, with bridle, with stripes, until they learn to submit, and to carry their master.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:39
verses.text: But thou, before thy jaws are bruised with the bridle, be humble, and carry thy Lord: wish not praise for thyself, but praised be He who sitteth upon thee, and say thou, "In the Lord shall my soul be praised; the humble shall hear thereof, and be glad".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:40
verses.text: Now followeth, "O magnify the Lord with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:41
verses.text: Who is this that exhorteth us, that we should magnify the Lord with him? Whoever, Brethren, is in the body of Christ, ought for this to labour, that the Lord may be magnified with him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:42
verses.text: For he loveth the Lord, whoever he is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:43
verses.text: And how doth he love Him? So as not to envy his fellow-lover.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:44
verses.text: Let them blush who so love God as to envy others.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:45
verses.text: Abandoned men love a charioteer, and whoever loveth a charioteer or hunter, wisheth the whole people to love with him, and exhorteth, saying, Love with me this pantomime, love with me this or that shame.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:46
verses.text: He calleth among the people that shame may be loved with him; and doth not a Christian call in the Church, that the Truth of God may be loved with him? Stir up then love in yourselves, Brethren; and call to every one of yours, and say, "O magnify the Lord with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:47
verses.text: Let there be in you that fervour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:48
verses.text: Wherefore are these things recited and explained? If ye love God, bring quickly to the love of God all who are joined unto you, and all who are in your house; if the Body of Christ is loved by you, that is, if the unity of the Church, bring them quickly to enjoy, and say, "O magnify the Lord with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:49
verses.text: "And let us exalt His Name together".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:50
verses.text: What is, "let us exalt His Name together"? That is, in one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:51
verses.text: For many copies so have it, "O magnify the Lord with me; and let us exalt His Name in one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:52
verses.text: Whether it be said, "together," or "in one," it is the same thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:53
verses.text: Therefore bring quickly whom ye can, by exhorting, by transporting, by beseeching, by disputing, by rendering a reason, with meekness, with gentleness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:54
verses.text: Bring them quickly unto love; that if they magnify the Lord, they may magnify Him in one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:55
verses.text: "I sought the Lord, and He heard me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:56
verses.text: Where heard the Lord? Within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:57
verses.text: Where giveth He? Within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:58
verses.text: There thou prayest, there thou art heard, there thou art blessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:59
verses.text: Thou hast prayed, thou art heard, thou art blessed; and he knoweth not who standeth by thee: it is all carried on in secret, as the Lord saith in the Gospel, "Enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:60
verses.text: When therefore thou enterest into thy chamber, thou enterest into thy heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:61
verses.text: Blessed are they who rejoice when they enter into their heart, and find therein nought of evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:62
verses.text: "I sought the Lord, and He heard me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:63
verses.text: Who then are not heard, seek not the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:64
verses.text: Attend, Holy Brethren; he said not, I sought gold from the Lord, and He heard me; I sought from the Lord long life, and He heard me; I sought from the Lord this or that, and He heard me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:65
verses.text: It is one thing to seek anything from the Lord, another to seek the Lord Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:66
verses.text: "I sought" (saith he) "the Lord, and He heard me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:67
verses.text: But thou, when thou prayest, saying, Kill that my enemy, seekest not the Lord, but, as it were, makest thyself a judge over thy enemy, and makest thy God an executioner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:68
verses.text: How knowest thou that he is not better than thou, whose death thou seekest? In that very thing haply he is, that he seeketh not thine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:69
verses.text: Therefore seek not from the Lord anything without, but seek the Lord Himself, and He will hear thee, and while thou yet speakest, He will say, "Lo, here I am".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:70
verses.text: I have said who was the exhorter, namely, that lover who would not alone embrace what he loveth, and saith, "Approach unto Him, and be ye lightened".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:71
verses.text: For he saith what he himself proved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:72
verses.text: For some spiritual person in the Body of Christ, or even our Lord Jesus Christ Himself according to the flesh, the Head exhorting His Own Members, saith; what? "Approach unto Him, and be ye lightened".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:73
verses.text: Or rather some spiritual Christian inviteth us to approach to our Lord Jesus Christ Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:74
verses.text: But let us approach to Him and be lightened; not as the Jews approached to Him, that they might be darkened; for they approached to Him that they might crucify Him: let us approach to Him that we may receive His Body and Blood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:75
verses.text: They by Him crucified were darkened; we by eating and drinking The Crucified are lightened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:76
verses.text: "Approach unto Him, and be ye lightened".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:77
verses.text: Lo, this is said to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:78
verses.text: Christ was crucified amid the Jews raging and seeing; the Gentiles were absent; lo, they have approached who were in darkness, and they who saw not are lightened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:79
verses.text: Whereby approach the Gentiles? By following with faith, by longing with the heart, by running with charity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:80
verses.text: Thy feet are thy charity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:81
verses.text: Have two feet, be not lame.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:82
verses.text: What are thy two feet? The two commandments of love, of thy God, and of thy Neighbour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:83
verses.text: With these feet run thou unto God, approach unto Him, for He hath both exhorted thee to run, and hath Himself shed His Own Light, as he hath magnificently and divinely continued "And your faces shall not be ashamed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:84
verses.text: "Approach" (saith he) "unto Him, and be ye lightened; and your faces shall not be ashamed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:85
verses.text: No face shall be ashamed but of the proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:86
verses.text: Wherefore? Because he would be lifted up, and when he hath suffered insult, or ignominy, or mischance in this world, or any affliction, he is ashamed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:87
verses.text: But fear not thou, approach unto Him, and thou shalt not be ashamed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:88
verses.text: As the Prophet testifieth, "The poor man cried, and the Lord heard him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:89
verses.text: He teacheth thee how thou mayest be heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:90
verses.text: Therefore art thou not heard, because thou art rich.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:91
verses.text: Lest haply thou say, thou criedst and wast not heard, hear wherefore; "The poor man cried, and the Lord heard him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:92
verses.text: As poor cry thou, and the Lord heareth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:93
verses.text: And how shall I cry as poor? By not, if thou hast aught, presuming therefrom upon thy own strength: by understanding that thou art needy; by understanding that so long art thou poor, as thou hast not Him who maketh thee rich.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:94
verses.text: But how did the Lord hear him? "And saved him out of all his troubles".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:95
verses.text: And how saveth He men out of all their troubles? "The Angel of the Lord shall send round about them that fear Him, and shall deliver them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:96
verses.text: So it is written, brethren, not as some bad copies have it, "The Lord shall send His Angel round about them that fear Him, and He shall deliver them:" but thus, "The Angel of the Lord shall send round about them that fear Him, and shall deliver them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:97
verses.text: Whom called He here the Angel of the Lord, who shall send round about them that fear Him, and shall deliver them? Our Lord Jesus Christ Himself is called in Prophecy, the Angel of the great Counsel, the Messenger of the great Counsel; so the Prophets called Him Even He then, the Angel of the great Counsel, that is, the Messenger, shall send unto them that fear the Lord, and shall deliver them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:98
verses.text: Fear not then lest thou be hid: wheresoever thou hast feared the Lord, there doth that Angel know thee, who shall send to succour thee, and shall deliver thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:99
verses.text: Now will He speak openly of the same Sacrament, whereby  He was carried in His Own Hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:100
verses.text: "O taste and see that the Lord is good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:101
verses.text: Doth not the Psalm now open itself, and show thee that seeming insanity and constant madness, the same insanity and sober inebriety of that David, who in a figure showed I know not what, when in the person of king Achis they said to him, How is it?  When the Lord said, "Except a man eat My Flesh and drink My Blood, he shall have no life in him"? And they in whom reigned Achis, that is, error and ignorance, said; what said they? "How can this man give us his flesh to eat?" If thou art ignorant, "Taste and see that the Lord is good:" but if thou understandest not, thou art king Achis: David shall change His Countenance and shall depart from thee, and shall quit thee, and shall depart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:102
verses.text: "Blessed is the man that trusteth in Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:103
verses.text: Why needeth this to be explained at length? Whoever trusteth not in the Lord, is miserable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:104
verses.text: Who is there that trusteth not in the Lord? He that trusteth in himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:105
verses.text: "O fear the Lord, all ye His saints, for there is no want to them that fear Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:106
verses.text: For many therefore will not fear God the Lord, lest they suffer hunger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:107
verses.text: It is said to them, Defraud not; and they say, Whence can I feed myself? No art can be without imposture; no business can be without fraud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:108
verses.text: But fraud God punisheth: fear God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:109
verses.text: But if I should fear God, I shall not have whence to live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:110
verses.text: "O fear the Lord, all ye His saints, for there is no want to them that fear Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:111
verses.text: He promiseth plenty to him that trembleth, and doubteth, lest haply if he should fear God, he should lose things superfluous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:112
verses.text: The Lord fed thee despising Him, and will He desert thee fearing Him? Attend, and say not, Such an one is rich, and I am poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:113
verses.text: I fear the Lord, he by not fearing how much has he gained, and I by fearing am bare! See what follows; "The rich do lack and suffer hunger, but they that seek the Lord shall not want any good thing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:114
verses.text: If thou receive it according to the letter, He seemeth to deceive thee, for thou seest that many rich men that are wicked die in their riches, and are not made poor while they live; thou seest them grow old, and come even to the end of life amid great abundance and riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:115
verses.text: Thou seest their funeral pomp celebrated with great profusion, the man himself brought rich even to the sepulchre, having expired in beds of ivory, his family weeping around; and thou sayest in thy mind, if haply thou knowest some both sins and crimes done by him: I know what things that man hath done; lo, he hath grown old, he hath died in his bed, his friends follow him to the grave, his funeral is celebrated with all this pomp; I know what he hath done; the Scripture has deceived me, and has spoken falsely, where I hear and sing; "The rich do lack and suffer hunger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:116
verses.text: When was this man in need? when did he suffer hunger? "But they that seek the Lord shall not want any good thing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:117
verses.text: Daily I rise up to Church, daily I bend the knee, daily I seek the Lord, and have nothing good: this man sought not the Lord, and he hath died in the midst of all these good things! Thus thinking, the snare of offence choketh him; for he seeketh mortal food on the earth, and seeketh not a true reward in heaven, and so he putteth his head into the devil's noose, his jaws are tied close, and the devil holdeth him fast unto evil doing, that so he may imitate the evil men, whom he seeth to die in such plenty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:118
verses.text: Therefore understand it not so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:119
verses.text: When thou art filled with spiritual riches, canst thou be poor? And was he therefore rich, because he had a bed of ivory; and art thou poor who hast the chamber of thy heart filled with such jewelry of virtues, justice, truth, charity, faith, endurance? Unfold thy riches, if thou hast them, and compare them with the riches of the rich.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:120
verses.text: But such an one has found in the market mules of great value, and has bought them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:121
verses.text: If thou couldest find faith to be sold, how much wouldest thou give for that, which God willeth that thou shouldest have gratis, and thou art ungrateful? Those rich then lack, they lack, and what is heavier, they lack bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:122
verses.text: For He hath said, "I am the Living Bread which came down from Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:123
verses.text: And again, "Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:124
verses.text: "But they that seek the Lord shall not want any good thing:" but what manner of good, I have already said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:125
verses.text: "Come, ye children, hearken unto me: I will teach you the fear of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:126
verses.text: Ye think, brethren, that I say this: think that David saith it; think that an Apostle saith it; nay think that our Lord Jesus Christ Himself saith it; "Come, ye children, hearken unto Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:127
verses.text: Let us hearken unto Him together: hearken ye unto Him through us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:128
verses.text: For He would teach us; He the Humble, He that drummeth, He that affecteth, would teach us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:129
verses.text: "What man is he that desireth life, and loveth to see good days?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:130
verses.text: He asketh a question.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:131
verses.text: Doth not every one among you answer, I? Is there any man among you that loveth not life, that is, that desireth not life, and loveth not to see good days? Do ye not daily thus murmur, and thus speak; How long shall we suffer these things? Daily are they worse and worse: in our fathers' time were days more joyful, were days better.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:132
verses.text: O if thou couldest ask those same, thy fathers, in like manner would they murmur to thee of their own days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:133
verses.text: Our fathers were happy, miserable are we, evil days have we: such an one ruled over us, we thought that after his death might some refreshing be given to us; worse things have come: O God, show unto us good days! "What man is he that desireth life, and loveth to see good days?" Let him not seek here good days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:134
verses.text: A good thing he seeketh, but not in its right place doth he seek it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:135
verses.text: As, if thou shouldest seek some righteous man in a country, wherein he lived not, it would be said to thee, A good man thou seekest, a great man thou seekest, seek him still, but not here; in vain thou seekest him here, thou wilt never find him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:136
verses.text: Good days thou seekest, together let us seek them, seek not here.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:137
verses.text: Read the Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:138
verses.text: Let not a Christian then murmur, let him see whose steps he followeth: but if he loveth good days, let him hearken unto Him teaching and saying, "Come, ye children, hearken unto Me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:139
verses.text: What wouldest thou? Life and good days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:140
verses.text: Hear, and do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:141
verses.text: "Keep thy tongue from evil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:142
verses.text: This do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:143
verses.text: I will not, saith a miserable man, I will not keep my tongue from evil, and yet I desire life and good days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:144
verses.text: If a workman of thine should say to thee, I indeed lay waste this vineyard, yet I require of thee my reward; thou broughtest me to the vineyard to lop and prune it, I cut away all the useful wood, I will cut short also the very trunks of the vines, that thou have thereon nothing to gather, and when I have done this, thou shalt repay to me my labour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:145
verses.text: Wouldest thou not call him mad? Wouldest thou not drive him from thy house or ever he put his hand to the knife? Such are those men who would both do evil, and swear falsely, and speak blasphemy against God, and murmur, and defraud, and be drunken, and dispute, and commit adultery, and use charms, and consult diviners, and withal see good days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:146
verses.text: To such it is said, thou canst not doing ill seek a good reward.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:147
verses.text: If thou art unjust, shall God also be unjust? What shall I do, then? What desirest thou? Life I desire, good days I desire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:148
verses.text: "Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips that they speak no guile," that is, defraud not any, lie not to any.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:149
verses.text: But what is, "Depart from evil"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:150
verses.text: It is little that thou injure none, murder none, steal not, commit not adultery, do no wrong, speak no false witness; "Depart from evil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:151
verses.text: When thou hast departed, thou sayest, Now I am safe, I have done all, I shall have life, I shall see good days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:152
verses.text: Not only saith he, "Depart from evil," but also, "and do good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:153
verses.text: It is nothing that thou spoil not: clothe the naked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:154
verses.text: If thou hast not spoiled, thou hast declined from evil; but thou wilt not do good, except thou receive the stranger into thine house.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:155
verses.text: So then depart from evil, as to do good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:156
verses.text: "Seek peace, and ensue it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:157
verses.text: He hath not said, Thou shalt have peace here; seek it, and ensue it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:158
verses.text: Whither shall I ensue it? Whither it hath gone before.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:159
verses.text: For the Lord is our peace, hath risen again, and hath ascended into Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:160
verses.text: "Seek peace, and ensue it;" because when thou also hast risen, this mortal shall be changed, and thou shalt embrace peace there where no man shall trouble thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:161
verses.text: For there is perfect peace, where thou wilt not hunger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:162
verses.text: "The Eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous:" fear not then; labour; the eyes of the Lord are upon thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:163
verses.text: "And His Ears are open unto their prayers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:164
verses.text: What wouldest thou more? If an householder in a great house should not hearken to a servant murmuring, he would complain, and say, What hardship do we here suffer, and none heareth us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:165
verses.text: Canst thou say this of God, What hardships I suffer, and none heareth me? If He heard me, haply, sayest thou, He would take away my tribulation: I cry unto Him, and yet have tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:166
verses.text: Only do thou hold fast His ways, and when thou art in tribulation, He heareth thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:167
verses.text: But He is a Physician, and still hast thou something of putrefaction; thou criest out, but still He cutteth, and taketh not away His Hand, until He hath cut as much as pleaseth Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:168
verses.text: For that Physician is cruel who heareth a man, and spareth his wound and putrefaction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:169
verses.text: How do mothers rub their children in the baths for their health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:170
verses.text: Do not the little ones cry out in their hands? Are they then cruel because they spare not, nor hearken unto their tears? Are they not full of affection? And yet the children cry out, and are not spared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:171
verses.text: So our God also is full of charity, but therefore seemeth He not to hear, that He may spare and heal us for everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:172
verses.text: Haply say the wicked, I securely do evil, because the Eyes of the Lord are not upon me: God attendeth to the righteous, me He seeth not, and whatever I do, I do securely.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:173
verses.text: Immediately added the Holy Spirit, seeing the thoughts of men, and said, "But the Face of the Lord is against them that do evil; to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:174
verses.text: "The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them, and delivered them out of all their troubles".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:175
verses.text: Righteous were the Three Children; out of the furnace cried they unto the Lord, and in His praises their flames cooled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:176
verses.text: The flame could not approach nor hurt the innocent and righteous Children praising God, and He delivered them out of the fire Some one saith, Lo, truly righteous were those who were heard, as it is written, "The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them, and delivered them out of all their troubles:" but I have cried, and He delivereth me not; either I am not righteous, or I do not the things which He commandeth me, or haply He seeth me not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:177
verses.text: Fear not: only do what He commandeth; and if He deliver thee not bodily, He will deliver thee spiritually.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:178
verses.text: For He who took out of the fire the Three Children, did He take out of the fire the Maccabees? Did not the first sing hymns in the flames, these last in the flames expire? The God of the Three Children, was not He the God also of the Maccabees? The one He delivered, the other He delivered not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:179
verses.text: Nay, He delivered both: but the Three Children He so delivered, that even the carnal were confounded; but the Maccabees therefore He delivered not so, that those who persecuted them should go into greater torments, while they thought that they had overcome God's Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:180
verses.text: He delivered Peter, when the Angel came unto him being in prison, and said, "Arise, and go forth," and suddenly his chains were loosed, and he followed the Angel, and He delivered him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:181
verses.text: Had Peter lost righteousness when He delivered him not from the cross? Did He not deliver him then? Even then He delivered him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:182
verses.text: Did his long life make him unrighteous? Haply He heard him more at last than at first, when truly He delivered him out of all his troubles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:183
verses.text: For when He first delivered him, how many things did he suffer afterwards! For thither He sent him at last, where he could have suffered no evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:184
verses.text: "The Lord is nigh unto them that have broken their heart; and saveth such as be lowly in spirit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:185
verses.text: God is High: let a Christian be lowly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:186
verses.text: If he would that the Most High God draw nigh unto him, let him be lowly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:187
verses.text: A great mystery, Brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:188
verses.text: God is above all: thou raisest thyself, and touchest not Him: thou humblest thyself, and He descendeth unto thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:189
verses.text: "Many are the troubles of the righteous" : doth He say, "Therefore let Christians be righteous, therefore let them hear My Word, that they may suffer no tribulation? He promiseth not this; but saith, "Many are the troubles of the righteous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:190
verses.text: Rather, if they be unrighteous they have fewer troubles, if righteous they have many.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:191
verses.text: But after few tribulations, or none, these shall come to tribulation everlasting, whence they shall never be delivered: but the righteous after many tribulations shall come to peace everlasting, where they shall never suffer any evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:192
verses.text: "Many are the tribulations of the righteous: but the Lord delivereth him out of all".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:193
verses.text: "The Lord keepeth all their bones: not one of them shall be broken" : this also, Brethren, let us not receive carnally.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:194
verses.text: Bones are the firm supports of the faithful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:195
verses.text: For as in flesh our bones give firmness, so in the heart of a Christian it is faith that gives firmness The patience then which is in faith, is as the bones of the inner man: this is that which cannot be broken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:196
verses.text: "The Lord keepeth all their bones: not one of them shall be broken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:197
verses.text: If of our Lord God Jesus Christ he had said this, "The Lord keepeth all the bones of His Son; not one of them shall be broken;" as is prefigured of Him also in another place, when the lamb was spoken of that should be slain, and it was said of it, "Neither shall ye break a bone thereof:"  then was it fulfilled in the Lord, because when He hung upon the Cross, He expired before they came to the Cross, and found His Body lifeless already, and would not break His legs, that it might be fulfilled which was written But He gave this promise to other Christians also, "The Lord keepeth all their bones; not one of them shall be broken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:198
verses.text: Therefore, Brethren, if we see any Saint suffer tribulation, and haply either by a Physician so cut, or by some persecutor so mangled, that his bones be broken; let us not say, This man was not righteous, for this hath the Lord promised to His righteous, of whom He said, "The Lord keepeth all their bones; not one of them shall be broken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:199
verses.text: Wouldest thou see that He spoke of other bones, those which we called the firm supports of faith, that is, patience and endurance in all tribulations? For these are the bones which are not broken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:200
verses.text: Hear, and see ye in the very Passion of our Lord, what I say.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:201
verses.text: The Lord was in the middle Crucified; near Him were two thieves: the one mocked, the other believed: the one was condemned, the other justified: the one had his punishment both in this world, and that which shall be, but unto the other said the Lord, "Verily I say unto thee, To-day shalt thou be with Me in Paradise;" and yet those who came brake not the bones of the Lord, but of the thieves they brake: as much were broken the bones of the thief who blasphemed, as of the thief who believed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:202
verses.text: Where then is that which is spoken, "The Lord keepeth all their bones; not one of them shall be broken"? Lo, unto whom He said, "To-day shalt thou be with Me in Paradise," could He keep all his bones? The Lord answereth thee: Yea, I kept them: for the firm support of his faith could not be broken by those blows whereby his legs were broken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:203
verses.text: "The death of sinners is the worst".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:204
verses.text: Attend, Brethren, for the sake of those things which I said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:205
verses.text: Truly Great is the Lord, and His Mercy, truly Great is He who gave to us to eat His Body, wherein He suffered such great things, and His Blood to drink.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:206
verses.text: How regardeth He them that think evil and say, "Such an one died ill, by beasts was he devoured: he was not a righteous man, therefore he perished ill; for else would he not have perished".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:207
verses.text: Is he then righteous who dieth in his own house and in his own bed? This then (sayest thou) it is whereat I wonder; because I know the sins and the crimes of this same man, and yet he died well; in his own house, within his own doors, with no injury of travel, with none even in mature age.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:208
verses.text: Hearken, "The death of sinners is worst".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:209
verses.text: What seemeth to thee a good death, is worst if thou couldest see within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:210
verses.text: Thou seest him outwardly lying on his bed, dost thou see him inwardly carried to hell? Hearken, Brethren, and learn from the Gospel what is the "worst death" of sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:211
verses.text: Were there not two in that age, a rich man who was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day; another a poor man who lay at his door full of sores, and the dogs came and licked his sores, and he desired to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man's table? Now it came to pass that the poor man died (righteous was that poor man), and was carried by Angels into Abraham's bosom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:212
verses.text: He who saw his body lying at the rich man's door, and no man to bury it, what haply said he? So die he who is my enemy; and whoever persecutes me, so may I see him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:213
verses.text: His body is accursed with spitting, his wounds stink; and yet in Abraham's bosom he resteth If we are Christians, let us believe: if we believe not, Brethren, let none feign himself a Christian.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:214
verses.text: Faith bringeth us to the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:215
verses.text: As the Lord spake these things, so are they.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:216
verses.text: Doth indeed an astrologer speak unto thee, and it is true, and doth Christ speak, and it is false? But by what sort of death died the rich man? What sort of death must it not be in purple and fine linen, how sumptuous, how pompous! What funeral ceremonies were there! In what spices was that body buried! And yet when he was in hell, being in torments, from the finger of that despised poor man he desired one drop of water to be poured upon his burning tongue, and obtained it not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:217
verses.text: Learn then what meaneth, "The death of sinners is worst;" and ask not beds covered with costly garments, and to have the flesh wrapped in many rich things, friends exhibiting a show of lamentation, a household beating their breasts, a crowd of attendants going before and following when the body is carried out, marble and gilded memorials.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:218
verses.text: For if ye ask those things, they answer you what is false, that of many not light sinners, but altogether wicked, the death is best, who have deserved to be so lamented, so embalmed, so covered, so carried out, so entombed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:219
verses.text: But ask the Gospel, and it will show to your faith the soul of the rich man burning in torments, which was nothing profited by all those honours and obsequies, which to his dead body the vanity of the living did afford.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:220
verses.text: But because there are many kinds of sinners, and not to be a sinner is difficult, or perhaps in this life impossible, he added immediately, of what kind of sinners the death is worst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:221
verses.text: "And they that hate the righteous one" (saith he) "shall perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:222
verses.text: What righteous one, but "Him that justifieth the ungodly"? Whom, but our Lord Jesus Christ, who is also "the propitiation for our sins"? Who then hate Him, have the worst death; because they die in their sins, who are not through Him reconciled to our God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:223
verses.text: "For the Lord redeemeth the souls of His servants".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:224
verses.text: But according to the soul is death to be understood either the worst or best, not according to bodily either dishonour, or honours which men see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 34:225
verses.text: "And none of them which trust in Him shall perish" ; this is the manner of human righteousness, that mortal life, however advanced, because without sin it cannot be, in this perisheth not, while it trusteth in Him, in whom is remission of sins, Amen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:1
verses.text: Psalm XXXV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:2
verses.text: The title of it causeth us no delay, for it is both brief, and to be understood not difficult, espe cially to those nursed in the Church of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:3
verses.text: For so it is, "To David himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:4
verses.text: The Psa lm then is to David himself: now David is interpreted, Strong in hand, or Desirable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:5
verses.text: The Psalm then is to the Strong in hand, and Desirable, to Him who for us hath overcome death, who unto us hath promised life: for in this is He Strong in hand, that He hath overcome death for us; in this is He Desirable, that He hath promised unto us life eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:6
verses.text: For what stronger than that Hand which touched the bier, and he that was dead rose up? What stronger than that Hand which overcame the world, not armed with steel, but pierced with wood? Or what more desirable than He, whom not having seen, the  Martyrs wished even to die, that they might be worthy to come unto Him? Therefore is the Psalm unto Him: to Him let our heart, to Him our tongue sing worthily: if yet Himself shall deign to give somewhat to sing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:7
verses.text: "Judge Thou, O Lord" (saith he), "them that hurt me, and fight Thou against them that fight against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:8
verses.text: "If God be for us, who can be against us?" And whereby doth God this for us? "Take hold" (saith he) "of arms and shield, and rise up to my help".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:9
verses.text: A great spectacle is it, to see God armed for thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:10
verses.text: And what is His Shield, what are His Arms? "Lord," in another place saith the man who here also speaketh, "as with the shield of Thy good-will hast Thou compassed us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:11
verses.text: But His Arms, wherewith He may not only us defend, but also strike His enemies, if we have well profited, shall we ourselves be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:12
verses.text: For as we from Him have this, that we be armed, so is He armed from us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:13
verses.text: But He is armed from those whom He hath made, we are armed with those things which we have received from Him who made us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:14
verses.text: These our arms the Apostle in a certain place calleth, "The shield of Faith, the helmet of Salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:15
verses.text: He hath armed us with such arms as ye have heard, arms admirable, and unconquered, insuperable and shining; spiritual truly and invisible, because we have to fight also against invisible enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:16
verses.text: If thou seest thine enemy, let thine arms be seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:17
verses.text: We are armed with faith in those things which we see not, and we overthrow enemies whom we see not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:18
verses.text: "Pour forth the weapon, and stop the way against them that persecute me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:19
verses.text: Who are they that persecute thee? Haply thy neighbour, or he whom thou hast offended, or to whom thou hast done wrong, or who would take away what is thine, or against whom thou preachest the truth, or whose sin thou rebukest, or whom living ill by thy well living thou offendest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:20
verses.text: There are indeed even these enemies to us, and they persecute us: but other enemies we are taught to know, those against whom we fight invisibly, of whom the Apostle warneth us, saying, "We wrestle not against flesh and blood," that is, against men; not against those whom ye see, but against those whom ye see not; "against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the world, of this darkness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:21
verses.text: "The whole world lieth in wickedness;" therefore the Apostle explained of what world they were rulers, he said, "of this darkness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:22
verses.text: The rulers of this world, I say, are the rulers of this darkness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:23
verses.text: And what follows? "Let them be confounded and put to shame, that seek after my soul" : for to this end they  seek after it, to destroy it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:24
verses.text: For I would that they would seek it for good! for in another Psalm he blameth this in men, that there was none who would seek after his soul: "Refuge failed me: there was none that would seek after my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:25
verses.text: Who is this that saith, "There was none that would seek after my soul"? Is it haply He, of whom so long before it was predicted, "They pierced My Hands and My Feet, they numbered all My Bones, they stared and looked upon Me, they have parted My Garments among them, and cast lots for My Vesture"? Now all these things were done before their eyes, and there was none who would seek after His Soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:26
verses.text: Many have been confounded to their health: many, put to shame, have passed over from the persecution of Christ to the society of His members with devoted piety; and this would not have been, had they not been confounded and put to shame.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:27
verses.text: Therefore he wished well to them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:28
verses.text: Let them not go before, but follow; let them not give counsel, but take it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:29
verses.text: For Peter would go before the Lord, when the Lord spake of His future Passion: he would to Him as it were give counsel for His health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:30
verses.text: The sick man to the Saviour give counsel for His health! And what said he to the Lord, affirming that His future Passion? "Be it far from Thee, Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:31
verses.text: Be gracious to Thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:32
verses.text: This shall not be to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:33
verses.text: He would go before that the Lord might follow; and what said He? "Get thee behind Me, Satan".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:34
verses.text: By going before thou art Satan, by following thou wilt be a disciple.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:35
verses.text: The same then is said to these also, "Let them be turned back and brought to confusion that think evil against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:36
verses.text: For when they have begun to follow after, now they will not think evil against me, but desire my good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:37
verses.text: What of others? For all are not so conquered as to be converted and believe: many continue in obstinacy, many preserve in heart the spirit of going before, and if they exert it not, yet they labour with it, and finding opportunity bring it forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:38
verses.text: Of such, what followeth? "Let them be as dust before the wind".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:39
verses.text: "Not so are the ungodly, not so; but as the dust which the wind driveth away from the face of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:40
verses.text: The wind is temptation; the dust are the ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:41
verses.text: When temptation cometh, the dust is raised, it neither standeth nor resisteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:42
verses.text: "Let them be as dust before the wind, and let the Angel of the Lord trouble them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:43
verses.text: "Let their way be darkness and slipping".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:44
verses.text: A horrible way! Darkness alone who feareth not? A slippery way alone who avoids not? In a dark and slippery way how shalt thou go? where set foot? These two ills are the great punishments of men: darkness, ignorance; a slippery way, luxury.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:45
verses.text: "And let the Angel of the Lord persecute them;" that they be not able to stand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:46
verses.text: For any one in a dark and slippery way, when he seeth that if he move his foot he will fall, and there is no light before his feet, haply resolveth to wait until light come; but here is the Angel of the Lord persecuting them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:47
verses.text: These things he predicted would come upon them, not as though he wished them to happen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:48
verses.text: Although the Prophet in the Spirit of God so speaketh these things, even as God doth the same, with sure judgment, with a judgment good, righteous, holy, tranquil; not moved with wrath, not with bitter jealousy, not with desire of wreaking enmities, but of punishing wickedness with righteousness; nevertheless, it is a prophecy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:49
verses.text: But wherefore these so great evils? By what desert? Hear by what desert.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:50
verses.text: "For without cause have they hid for me the corruption of their trap".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:51
verses.text: For Him that is our Head, observe, the Jews did this: they hid the corruption of their trap.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:52
verses.text: For whom hid they their trap? For Him who saw the hearts of those that hid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:53
verses.text: But yet was He among them like one ignorant, as though He were deceived, whereas they were in that deceived, that they thought Him to be deceived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:54
verses.text: For therefore was He as though deceived, living among them, because we among such as they were so to live, as to be without doubt deceived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:55
verses.text: He saw His betrayer, and chose him the more to a necessary work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:56
verses.text: By his evil He wrought a great good: and yet among the twelve was he chosen, lest even the small number of twelve should be without one evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:57
verses.text: This was an example of patience to us, because it was necessary that we should live among the evil: it was necessary that we should endure the evil, either knowing them or knowing them not: an example of patience He gave thee lest thou shouldest fail, when thou hast begun to live among the evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:58
verses.text: And because that School of Christ in the twelve failed not, how much more ought we to be firm, when in the great Church is fulfilled what was predicted of the mixture of the evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:59
verses.text: But yet what is to be done? "Without a cause have they hid for me the corruption of their trap".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:60
verses.text: What meaneth, "Without a cause"? I have done them no evil, I have hurt them not at all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:61
verses.text: "Vainly have they reviled my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:62
verses.text: What is, "Vainly"? Speaking falsely, proving nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:63
verses.text: "Let a trap come upon them which they know not of".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:64
verses.text: A magnificent retribution, nothing more just! They have hidden a trap that I might know not: let a trap come upon them which they know not of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:65
verses.text: For I know of their trap.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:66
verses.text: But what trap is coming upon them? That which they know not of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:67
verses.text: Let us hear, lest haply he speak of that.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:68
verses.text: "Let a trap come upon them, which they know not of".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:69
verses.text: Perhaps that is one which they hid for him, that another which shall come upon themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:70
verses.text: Not so: but what? "The wicked shall be holden with the cords of his own sins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:71
verses.text: Thereby are they deceived, whereby they would deceive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:72
verses.text: Thence shall come mischief to them, whence they endeavoured mischief.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:73
verses.text: For it follows, "And let the net which they have hidden catch themselves, and let them fall into their own trap".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:74
verses.text: As if any one should prepare a cup of poison for another, and forgetting should drink it up himself: or as if one should dig a pit, that his enemy might fall thereinto in the darkness and himself forgetting what he had dug, should first walk that way, and fall into it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:75
verses.text: This then for the wicked that would hurt me: what for me? "But my soul shall rejoice in the Lord" ; as in Him from whom it hath heard, "I am thy salvation;" as not seeking other riches from without; as not seeking to abound in pleasures and good things of earth; but loving freely the true Spouse, not from Him wishing to receive aught that may delight, but Him alone proposing to itself, by whom it may be delighted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:76
verses.text: For what better than God will be given unto me? God loveth me: God loveth thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:77
verses.text: See He hath proposed to thee, Ask what thou wilt If the emperor should say to thee, Ask what thou wilt, what commands, what dignities, wouldest thou burst forth with! What great things wouldest thou propose to thyself, both to receive and to bestow! When God saith unto thee, Ask what thou wilt, what wilt thou ask? empty thy mind, exert thy avarice, stretch forward as far as possible, and enlarge thy desire: it is not any one, but Almighty God that said, Ask what thou wilt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:78
verses.text: If of possessions thou art a lover, thou wilt desire the whole earth, that all who are born may be thy husbandmen, or thy slaves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:79
verses.text: And what when thou hast possessed the whole earth? Thou wilt ask the sea, in which yet thou canst not live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:80
verses.text: In this greediness the fishes will have the better of thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:81
verses.text: But perhaps thou wilt possess the islands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:82
verses.text: Pass over these also; ask the air although thou canst not fly; stretch thy desire even unto the heavens, call thine own the sun, the moon, and the stars, because He who made all said, Ask what thou wilt: yet nothing wilt thou find more precious, nothing wilt thou find better, than Himself who made all things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:83
verses.text: Him seek, who made all things, and in Him and from Him shalt thou have all things which He made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:84
verses.text: All things are precious, because all are beautiful; but what more beautiful than He? Strong are they; but what stronger than He? And nothing would He give thee rather than Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:85
verses.text: If aught better thou hast found, ask it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:86
verses.text: If thou ask aught else, thou wilt do wrong to Him, and harm to thyself, by preferring to Him that which He made, when He would give to thee Himself who made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:87
verses.text: "But my soul shall be joyful in the Lord; it shall rejoice in His salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:88
verses.text: The salvation of God is Christ: "For mine eyes have seen Thy salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:89
verses.text: "All my bones shall say, Lord, who is like unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:90
verses.text: Who can speak anything worthily of these words? I think them only to be pronounced, not to be expounded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:91
verses.text: Why seekest thou this or that? What is like unto thy Lord? Him hast thou before thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:92
verses.text: "The unrighteous have declared unto me delights, but not after Thy law, O Lord!" Persecutors have been who have said, Worship Saturn, worship Mercury.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:93
verses.text: I worship not idols (saith he): "Lord, who is like unto Thee? They have eyes, and see not; ears have they, but they hear not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:94
verses.text: "Lord, who is like unto Thee," who hast made the eye to see, the ear to hear? But I (saith he) worship not idols, for them a workman made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:95
verses.text: Worship a tree or mountain; did a workman make them also? Here too, Lord, who is like unto Thee? Earthly things are shown unto me; Thou art Creator of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:96
verses.text: And from these haply they turn to the higher creation, and say to me, Worship the Moon, worship this Sun, who with his light, as a great lamp in the Heavens, maketh the day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:97
verses.text: Here also I plainly say, "Lord, who is like unto Thee?" The Moon and the Stars Thou hast made, the Sun to rule the day hast Thou kindled, the Heavens hast Thou framed together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:98
verses.text: There are many invisible things better.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:99
verses.text: But haply here also it is said to me, Worship Angels, adore Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:100
verses.text: And here also will I say, "Lord, who is like unto Thee?" Even the Angels Thou hast created.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:101
verses.text: The Angels are nothing, but by seeing Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:102
verses.text: It is better with them to possess Thee, than by worshipping them to fall from Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:103
verses.text: O Body of Christ, Holy Church, let all thy bones say, "Lord, who is like unto thee?" And if the flesh under persecution hath fallen away, let the bones say, "Lord, who is like unto Thee?" For of the righteous it is said, "The Lord keepeth all their bones; not one of them shall be broken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:104
verses.text: Of how many righteous have the bones under persecution been broken? Finally, "The just shall live by faith," and "Christ justifieth the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:105
verses.text: But how justifieth He any except believing and confessing? "For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:106
verses.text: Therefore also that thief, although from His theft led to the judge, and from the judge to the cross, yet on the very cross was justified: with his heart he believed, with his mouth he confessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:107
verses.text: For neither to a man unrighteous and not already justified, would the Lord have said, "To-day shalt thou be with Me in Paradise," and yet his bones were broken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:108
verses.text: For when they came to take down the bodies, by reason of the approaching Sabbath, the Lord was found already dead, and His Bones were not broken But of those that yet lived, that they might be taken down, the legs were broken, that so from this pain having died, they might be buried.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:109
verses.text: Were then of the one thief, who persisted in his ungodliness on the cross, the bones broken, and not also of the other who with his heart believed, and with his mouth made confession unto salvation? Where then is that which was said, "The Lord keepeth all his bones; not one of them shall be broken;" except that in the Body of the Lord the name of bones is given to all the righteous, the firm in heart, the strong, yielding to no persecutions, no temptations, so as to consent unto evil?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:110
verses.text: "Which deliverest the poor from him that is too strong for him; yea, the poor and needy from him that spoileth him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:111
verses.text: Who that deliverest, but He who is Strong in hand? Even that David shall deliver the poor from him that is too strong for him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:112
verses.text: For the devil was too strong for thee, and held thee, because he conquered thee, when thou consentedst unto him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:113
verses.text: But what hath the Strong in hand done? "No man entereth into a strong man's house, to spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:114
verses.text: By His own Power, most Holy, most Magnificent, hath He bound the devil by pouring forth the weapon to stop the way against him, that He may deliver the poor and needy, to whom there was no helper For who is thy helper but the Lord to whom thou sayest, "O Lord, My Strength, and My Redeemer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:115
verses.text: If thou wilt presume of thy own strength, thereby wilt thou fall, whereof thou hast presumed: if of another's, he would lord it over thee, not succour thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:116
verses.text: He then alone is to be sought Who hath redeemed them, and made them free, and hath given His Blood to purchase them, and of His servants hath made them His Brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:117
verses.text: Let then our Head say, "False witnesses did rise up, they laid to My charge things that I knew not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:118
verses.text: But let us say to our Head, Lord, what knewest Thou not? Didst Thou indeed know not anything? Didst Thou not know the hearts of them that charged Thee? Didst Thou not foresee their deceits? Didst Thou not give Thyself into their hands knowingly? Hadst Thou not come that Thou mightest suffer by them? What then knewest Thou not? He knew not sin, and thereby He knew not sin, not by not judging, but by not committing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:119
verses.text: There are phrases of this kind also in daily use, as when thou sayest of any one, He knoweth not to stand, that is, he doth not stand; and, He knoweth not to do good, because he doth not good; and, He knoweth not to do ill, because he doth not ill.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:120
verses.text: What knew not Christ so much, as to blaspheme? Thereof was He called in question by His persecutors, and because He spake truth, He was judged to have spoken blasphemy But by whom? By them of whom it followeth, "They rewarded Me evil for good, and barrenness to My Soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:121
verses.text: I gave unto them fruitfulness, they rewarded Me barrenness; I gave life, they death; I honour, they dishonour; I medicine, they wounds; and in all these which they rewarded Me, was truly barrenness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:122
verses.text: This barrenness in the tree He cursed, when seeking fruit He found none Leaves there were, and fruit there was not: words there were, and deeds there were not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:123
verses.text: See of words abundance, and of deeds barrenness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:124
verses.text: "Thou that preachest a man should not steal, stealest: thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, committest adultery".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:125
verses.text: Such were they who charged Christ with things that He knew not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:126
verses.text: "But I, when they troubled me, clothed myself with sackcloth, and humbled my soul with fasting, and my prayer shall return into mine own bosom" Brethren, if for some little space with pious curiosity we lift the veil, and search with the intent eye of the heart the inner part of this Scripture, we find that even this the Lord did.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:127
verses.text: Sackcloth, haply He calleth His mortal flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:128
verses.text: Wherefore Sackcloth? For the likeness of sinful flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:129
verses.text: For the Apostle saith, "God sent His Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, that through sin He might condemn sin in the flesh:" that is, He clothed His Own Son with sackcloth, that through sackcloth He might condemn the goats.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:130
verses.text: Not that there was sin, I say not in the Word of God, but not even in that Holy Soul and Mind of a Man, which the Word and Wisdom of God had so joined to Himself as to be One Person.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:131
verses.text: Nay, nor even in His very Body was any sin, but the likeness of sinful flesh there was in the Lord; because death is not but by sin, and surely that Body was mortal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:132
verses.text: For had It not been mortal, It had not died; had It not died, It had not risen again; had It not risen again, It had not showed us an example of eternal life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:133
verses.text: So then death, which is caused by sin, is called sin; as we say the Greek tongue, the Latin tongue, meaning not the very member of flesh, but that which is done by the member of flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:134
verses.text: For the tongue in our members is one among others, as the eyes, nose, ears, and the rest: but the Greek tongue is Greek words, not that the tongue is words, but that words are by the tongue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:135
verses.text: So then the sin of the Lord is that which was caused by sin; because He assumed flesh, of the same lump which had deserved death by sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:136
verses.text: For to speak more briefly, Mary who was of Adam died for sin, Adam died for sin, and the Flesh of the Lord which was of Mary died to put away sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:137
verses.text: With this sackcloth the Lord clothed Himself, and therefore was He not known, because He lay hid under sackcloth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:138
verses.text: "When they," saith He, "troubled Me, I clothed Myself with sackcloth:" that is, they raged, I lay hid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:139
verses.text: For had He not willed to lie hid neither could He have died, since in one moment of time one drop only of His Power, if indeed it is to be called a drop, He put forth, when they wished to seize Him, and at His one question, "Whom seek ye?" they all went back and fell to the ground Such power could He not have humbled in passion, if He had not lain hid under sackcloth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:140
verses.text: Again, if we have understood the sackcloth, how understand we the fasting? Wished Christ to eat, when He sought fruit on the tree, and if He had found, would He have eaten? Wished Christ to drink, when He said to the woman of Samaria, "Give Me to drink"? when He said on the Cross, "I thirst"? For what hungered, for what thirsted Christ, but our good works? Because in them that crucified and persecuted Him He had found no good works, He fasted; for they rewarded barrenness to His soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:141
verses.text: For what a fast was His, who found barely one thief, whom on the Cross He might taste! For the Apostles had fled, and had hidden themselves in the multitude.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:142
verses.text: And even Peter, who even to the death of his Lord had promised to persevere, had now thrice denied Him, had now wept, and still lay hid in the multitude, still feared lest He should be known.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:143
verses.text: Lastly, having seen Him dead, all of them despaired of their own safety and despairing He found them, after His resurrection, and when He spake with them, found them grieving and mourning, no longer hoping anything.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:144
verses.text: In great fasting had the Lord remained, had He not refreshed them that He might feed on them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:145
verses.text: For He refreshed them, He comforted them, He confirmed them, and into His Own Body converted them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:146
verses.text: In this manner then was our Lord also in fasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:147
verses.text: "And My prayer shall return into Mine Own Bosom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:148
verses.text: In the bosom of this verse is plainly a great depth, and may the Lord grant that it be fathomable by us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:149
verses.text: For in the "bosom" a secret is understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:150
verses.text: And we ourselves, Brethren, are here well admonished to pray within our own bosom, where God seeth, where God heareth, where no human eye penetrateth, where none seeth but He who succoureth; where Susanna prayed, and her voice, though it was not heard by men, yet by God was heardWe read also that in the mount Jesus prayed alone, we read that He passed the night in prayer, even at the time of His Passion What then? "And My prayer shall return into Mine Own Bosom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:151
verses.text: I know not what better to understand concerning the Lord: take meanwhile what now occurs; perhaps something better will occur hereafter, either to me or to some better: "My prayer shall return into Mine Own Bosom:" this I understand to be said, because in His Own Bosom He had the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:152
verses.text: "For God was in Christ reconciling the world unto Himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:153
verses.text: In Himself He had Him to whom He prayed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:154
verses.text: He was not far from Him, for Himself had said, "I am in the Father, and the Father in Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:155
verses.text: But because prayer rather belongeth to very Man (for according as Christ is the Word, He prayeth not, but heareth prayer; and seeketh not to be succoured for Himself, but with the Father succoureth all): what is, "My prayer shall return into Mine Own Bosom," but in Me My Manhood invoketh in Me My Godhead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:156
verses.text: "As a Neighbour, as our Brother, so I pleased Him: as one mourning and sorrowful, so I humbled myself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:157
verses.text: Now looketh He back to His Own Body: let us now look to this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:158
verses.text: When we rejoice in prayer, when our mind is calmed, not by the world's prosperity, but by the light of Truth: (who perceiveth this light, knoweth what I say, and he seeth and acknowledgeth what is said, "As a Neighbour, as our Brother, so I pleased Him"): even then our soul pleaseth God, not placed afar off, for, "In Him," saith one, "we live and move and have our being,"  but as a Brother, as a Neighbour, as a Friend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:159
verses.text: But if it be not such that it can so rejoice, so shine, so approach, so cleave unto Him, and seeth itself far off thence, then let it do what followeth, "As one mourning and sorrowful, so I humbled Myself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:160
verses.text: As our Brother, so I pleased Him," said He, drawing near; "As one mourning and sorrowful, so I humbled Myself," said He, removed and set afar off.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:161
verses.text: Did not Peter draw near, when he said, "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the Living God"? And yet the same man became afar off by saying, "Be it far from Thee, Lord; this shall not be unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:162
verses.text: Lastly, what said He, his Neighbour, as it were, to him drawing near? "Blessed art thou, Simon, Barjona".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:163
verses.text: To him afar off, as it were, and unlike, what said He? "Get thee behind Me, Satan".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:164
verses.text: To him drawing near, "Flesh and blood," saith He, "hath not revealed it unto thee, but My Father, which is in Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:165
verses.text: His Light is shed over thee, in His Light thou shinest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:166
verses.text: But when having become afar off, he spake against the Lord's Passion, which should be for our Salvation, "Thou savourest not," said He, "the things that be of God, but those that be of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:167
verses.text: One rightly placing together both of these saith in a certain Psalm, "I said in my ecstasy, I am cast off from before Thine Eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:168
verses.text: In my ecstasy, would he not have said, had he not drawn near; for ecstasy is the transporting of the mind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:169
verses.text: He poured over himself his own soul, and drew near unto God; and through some cloud and weight of the flesh being again cast down to earth, and recollecting where he had been, and seeing where he was, he said, "I am cast off from before Thine Eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:170
verses.text: This then, "As a Neighbour, as our Brother, so I pleased Him," may He grant to be done in us; but when that is not, let even this be done, "As one mourning and sorrowful, so I humbled myself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:171
verses.text: "And against Me they rejoiced, and gathered themselves together" , against Me only: they rejoicing, I sorrowful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:172
verses.text: But we heard just now in the Gospel, "Blessed are they that mourn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:173
verses.text: If they are blessed that mourn, miserable are they that laugh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:174
verses.text: "Against Me they rejoiced, and gathered themselves together: scourges were gathered together against Me, and they knew not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:175
verses.text: Because they laid to My charge things that I knew not, they also knew not Whom they charged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:176
verses.text: "They tempted Me, and mocked Me with mocking".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:177
verses.text: That is, they derided Me, they insulted Me; this of the Head, this of the Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:178
