verses.text: Consider, Brethren, the glory of the Church which now is; remember its past dishonours, remember how once were Christians everywhere put to flight, and wherever found, mocked, beaten, slain, exposed to beasts, burned, men rejoicing against them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:179
verses.text: As it was to the Head, so it is also to the Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:180
verses.text: For as it was to the Lord on the Cross, so has it been to His Body in all that persecution which was made but now: nor even now cease the persecutions of the same.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:181
verses.text: Wherever men find a Christian, they are wont to insult, to persecute, to deride him, to call him dull, senseless, of no spirit, of no knowledge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:182
verses.text: Do they what they will, Christ is in Heaven: do they what they will, He hath honoured His punishment, already hath He fixed His Cross in the foreheads of all; the ungodly is permitted to insult, to rage he is not permitted; but yet from that which the tongue uttereth, is understood what he beareth in his heart: "They gnashed upon Me with their teeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:183
verses.text: "Lord, when wilt Thou look on? Rescue My Soul from their deceits, My Darling from the lions".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:184
verses.text: For to us the time is slow; and in our person is this said, "When wilt Thou look on?" that is, when shall we see vengeance upon those who insult us? When shall the Judge, overcome by weariness, hear the widow? But our Judge, not from weariness, but from love, delayeth our salvation; from reason, not from need; not that He could not even now succour us, but that the number of us all may be filled up even to the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:185
verses.text: And yet out of our desire, what do we say? "Lord, when wilt Thou look on? Rescue My Soul from their deceits, My Darling from the lions:" that is, My Church from raging powers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:186
verses.text: Lastly, wouldest thou know what is that Darling? Read the words following: "I will confess unto Thee, O Lord, in the great Congregation; in a weighty people will I praise Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:187
verses.text: Truly saith He, "I will confess unto Thee:" for confession is made in all the multitude, but not in all is God praised: the whole multitude heareth our confession, but not in all the multitude is the praise of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:188
verses.text: For in all the whole multitude, that is, in the Church which is spread abroad in the whole world, is chaff, and wheat: the chaff flieth, the wheat remaineth; therefore, "in a weighty people will I praise Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:189
verses.text: In a weighty people, which the wind of temptation carries not away, in such is God praised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:190
verses.text: For in the chaff He is ever blasphemed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:191
verses.text: "Let not them that are Mine enemies wrongfully rejoice over Me:" for they rejoice over Me because of My chaff.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:192
verses.text: "Who hate Me without a cause;" that is, whom I never hurt; "winking with their eyes" : that is, pretending hypocrites, "For they spake indeed peace to Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:193
verses.text: What is, "winking with their eyes"? Declaring by their looks, what they carry not in their heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:194
verses.text: And who are these "winking with their eyes"? "For they spake indeed peace to Me; and with wrath devised craftily".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:195
verses.text: "Yea they opened their mouth wide against Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:196
verses.text: First winking with their eyes, those lions sought to ravish and devour; first fawning they spake peace, and then with wrath devised craftily.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:197
verses.text: What peace spake they? "Master, we know that Thou acceptest not man's person, and teachest the way of God in truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:198
verses.text: Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar, or not?" They spake indeed peace unto Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:199
verses.text: What then? Didst not Thou know them, and deceived they Thee, winking with their eyes? Truly He knew them; therefore said He, "Why tempt ye Me, ye hypocrites?" Afterward, "they opened their mouth wide against Me," crying, "Crucify Him, Crucify Him! and said, Aha, Aha, our eyes have seen it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:200
verses.text: This, when they insulted Him, "Aha, Aha, Prophesy unto us, Thou Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:201
verses.text: As their peace was pretended when they tempted Him concerning the money, so now insulting was their praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:202
verses.text: "They said, Aha, Aha, our eyes have seen it" : that is, Thy deeds, Thy miracles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:203
verses.text: This Man is the Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:204
verses.text: "If He be the Christ, let Him come down from the Cross, and we will believe Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:205
verses.text: He saved others, Himself He cannot save".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:206
verses.text: "Our eyes have seen it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:207
verses.text: This is all whereof He boasted Himself, when "He called Himself the Son of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:208
verses.text: But the Lord was hanging patient upon the Cross: His power had He not lost, but He showed His patience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:209
verses.text: For what great thing was it for Him to come down from the Cross, who could afterward rise again from the sepulchre? But He seems to have yielded to His insulters; and this, beloved, that having risen again He should show Himself to His own, and not to them, and this is a great mystery; for His resurrection signified the New Life, but the New Life is known to His friends, not to His enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:210
verses.text: "This Thou hast seen, O Lord; keep not silence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:211
verses.text: What is, "keep not silence"? Judge Thou.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:212
verses.text: For of judgment is it said in a certain place, "I have kept silence; shall I keep silence for ever?" And of the delaying of judgment it is said to the sinner, "These things hast thou done, and I kept silence;" "Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:213
verses.text: How keepeth He silence, who speaketh by the Prophets, who speaketh with His own mouth in the Gospel, who speaketh by the Evangelists, who speaketh by us, when we speak the truth? What then? He keepeth silence from judgment, not from precept, not from doctrine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:214
verses.text: But this His judgment the Prophet in a manner invoketh, and predicteth: "Thou hast seen, O Lord: keep not silence;" that is, Thou wilt not keep silence, needs must that Thou wilt judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:215
verses.text: "O Lord, be not far from Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:216
verses.text: Until Thy judgment come, be not far from Me, as Thou hast promised, "Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:217
verses.text: "Arise, Lord, and attend to My judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:218
verses.text: To what judgment? That Thou art in tribulation; that Thou art tormented with labours and pains? Do not even many wicked men suffer the same? To what judgment? Therefore art Thou righteous, because Thou sufferest these things? No: but what? "To My judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:219
verses.text: What followeth? "Attend to My judgment; even to My cause, My God, and My Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:220
verses.text: Not to My punishment, but to My cause: not to that which the robber hath in common with Me, but to that whereof is said, "Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:221
verses.text: For this cause is distinguished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:222
verses.text: For punishment is equal to good and bad.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:223
verses.text: Therefore Martyrs, not the punishment, but the cause maketh, for if punishment made Martyrs, all the mines would be full of Martyrs, every chain would drag Martyrs, all that are executed with the sword would be crowned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:224
verses.text: Therefore let the cause be distinguished; let none say, because I suffer, I am righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:225
verses.text: Because He who first suffered, suffered for righteousness' sake, therefore He added a great exception, "Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:226
verses.text: For many having a good cause do persecution, and many having a bad cause suffer persecution.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:227
verses.text: For if persecution could not be done rightly, it had not been said in a certain Psalm, "Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him did I persecute".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:228
verses.text: Let none then say, I suffer persecution: let him not sift the punishment, but prove the cause: lest if he prove not the cause, he be numbered with the ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:229
verses.text: Therefore how watchfully, how excellently hath This Man recommended Himself, "O Lord, attend to My judgment," not to My punishments; "even to My cause, My God, and My Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:230
verses.text: "Judge me, O Lord, according to My righteousness" ; that is, attend to My cause.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:231
verses.text: Not according to My punishment, but "according to My righteousness, O Lord, My God," that is, according to this judge Thou Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:232
verses.text: "And let them not rejoice over Me;" that is, Mine enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:233
verses.text: "Let them not say in their heart, Aha, aha, so would we have it" ; that is, We have done what we could, we have slain him, we have taken him away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:234
verses.text: "Let them not say:" show them that they have done nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:235
verses.text: "Let them not say, We have swallowed him up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:236
verses.text: Whence say those Martyrs, "If the Lord had not been on our side, then they had swallowed us up quick".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:237
verses.text: What is, "had swallowed us up"? Had passed into their own body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:238
verses.text: For that thou swallowest up, which thou passest into thy own body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:239
verses.text: The world would swallow thee up; swallow thou the world, pass it into thy own body: kill and eat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:240
verses.text: As it was said to Peter, "Kill and eat;" do thou kill in them what they are, make them what thou art.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:241
verses.text: But if they on the other hand persuade thee to ungodliness, thou art swallowed up by them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:242
verses.text: Not when they persecute thee art thou swallowed up by them, but when they persuade thee to be what they are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:243
verses.text: "Let them not say, We have swallowed him up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:244
verses.text: Do thou swallow up the body of Pagans.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:245
verses.text: Why the body of Pagans? It would swallow thee up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:246
verses.text: Do thou to it, what it would to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:247
verses.text: Therefore perhaps that calf, being ground to powder, was cast into the water and given to the children of Israel to drink, that so the body of ungodliness might be swallowed up by Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:248
verses.text: "Let them be ashamed and brought to confusion together that rejoice at mine hurt: let them be clothed with shame and dishonour" ; so that we may swallow up them ashamed and brought to confusion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:249
verses.text: "Who speak evil against me:" let them be ashamed, let them be brought to confusion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:250
verses.text: What sayest thou now, the Head with the Members? "Let them shout for joy and be glad that favour My righteous cause:" who cleave to My Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:251
verses.text: Yea, let them say "continually, Let the Lord be magnified, which hath pleasure in the prosperity of His servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:252
verses.text: "And my tongue shall speak of Thy righteousness, and of Thy praise all the day long".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:253
verses.text: And whose tongue endureth to speak the praise of God all the day long? See now I have made a discourse something longer; ye are wearied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:254
verses.text: Who endureth to praise God all the day long? I will suggest a remedy, whereby thou mayest praise God all the day long if thou wilt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:255
verses.text: Whatever thou dost, do well, and thou hast praised God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:256
verses.text: When thou singest an hymn, thou praisest God, but what doth thy tongue, unless thy heart also praise Him? Hast thou ceased from singing hymns, and departed, that thou mayest refresh thyself? Be not drunken, and thou hast praised God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:257
verses.text: Dost thou go away to sleep? Rise not to do evil, and thou hast praised God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:258
verses.text: Dost thou transact business? Do no wrong, and thou hast praised God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:259
verses.text: Dost thou till thy field? Raise not strife, and thou hast praised God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 35:260
verses.text: In the innocency of thy works prepare thyself to praise God all the day long.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:1
verses.text: Psalm XXXVI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:2
verses.text: "The ungodly hath said in himself that he will sin: there is no fear of God before his eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:3
verses.text: Not of one man, but of a race of ungodly men he speaketh, who fight against their own selves, by not understanding, that so they may live well; not because they cannot, but because they will not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:4
verses.text: For it is one thing, when one endeavours to understand some thing, and through infirmity of flesh cannot; as saith the Scripture in a certain place, "For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthly tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things;" but another when the human heart acts mischievously against itself, so that what it could understand, if it had but good will thereto, it understandeth not, not because it is difficult, but because the will is contrary.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:5
verses.text: But so it is when men love their own sins, and hate God's Commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:6
verses.text: For the Word of God is thy adversary, if thou be a friend to thy ungodliness; but if thou art an adversary to thy ungodliness, the Word of God is thy friend, as well as the adversary of thy ungodliness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:7
verses.text: "For he hath wrought deceitfully in His sight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:8
verses.text: In whose sight? In His, whose fear was not before the eyes of him that did work deceitfully.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:9
verses.text: "To find out his iniquity, and hate it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:10
verses.text: He wrought so as not to find it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:11
verses.text: For there are men who as it were endeavour to seek out their iniquity, and fear to find it; because if they should find it, it is said to them, Depart from it: this thou didst before thou knewest; thou didst iniquity being in ignorance; God giveth pardon: now thou hast discovered it, forsake it, that to thy ignorance pardon may easily be given; and that with a clear face thou mayest say to God, "Remember not the sins of my youth, and of my ignorance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:12
verses.text: Thus he seeketh it, thus he feareth lest he find it; for he seeketh it deceitfully.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:13
verses.text: When saith a man, I knew not that it was sin? When he hath seen that it is sin, and ceaseth to do the sin, which he did only because he was ignorant: such an one in truth would know his sin, to find it out, and hate it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:14
verses.text: But now many "work deceitfully to find out their iniquity:" they work not from their heart to find it out and hate it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:15
verses.text: But because in the very search after iniquity, there is deceit, in the finding it there will be defence of it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:16
verses.text: For when one hath found his iniquity, lo now it is manifest to him that it is iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:17
verses.text: Do it not, thou sayest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:18
verses.text: And he who wrought deceitfully to find it out, now he hath found, hateth it not; for what saith he? How many do this! Who is there that doth it not? And will God destroy them all? Or at least he saith this: if God would not these things to be done, would men live who commit the same? Seest thou that thou didst work deceitfully to find out thy iniquity? For if not deceitfully but sincerely thou hadst wrought, thou wouldest now have found it out, and hated it; now thou hast found it out, and thou defendest it; therefore thou didst work deceitfully, when thou soughtest it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:19
verses.text: "The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit: he would not understand, that he might do good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:20
verses.text: Ye see that he attributeth that to the will: for there are men who would understand and cannot, and there are men who would not understand, and therefore understand not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:21
verses.text: "He would not understand, that he might do good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:22
verses.text: "He hath meditated iniquity on his bed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:23
verses.text: What said He, "On his bed?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:24
verses.text: "The ungodly hath said in himself, that he will sin:" what above he said, in himself, that here he said, "On his bed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:25
verses.text: Our bed is our heart: there we suffer the tossing of an evil conscience; and there we rest when our conscience is good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:26
verses.text: Whoso loveth the bed of his heart, let him do some good therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:27
verses.text: There is our bed, where the Lord Jesus Christ commands us to pray.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:28
verses.text: "Enter into thy chamber, and shut thy door".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:29
verses.text: What is, "Shut thy door?" Expect not from God such things as are without, but such as are within; "and thy Father which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:30
verses.text: Who is he that shutteth not the door? He who asketh much from God such things, and in such wise directeth all his prayers, that he may receive the goods that are of this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:31
verses.text: Thy door is open, the multitude seeth when thou prayest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:32
verses.text: What is it to shut thy door? To ask that of God, which God alone knoweth how He giveth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:33
verses.text: What is that for which thou prayest, when thou hast shut the door? What "eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, or hath entered into the heart of man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:34
verses.text: And haply it hath not entered into thy very bed, that is, into thy heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:35
verses.text: But God knoweth what He will give: but when shall it be? When the Lord shall be revealed, when the Judge shall appear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:36
verses.text: "He hath set himself in every way that is not good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:37
verses.text: What is, "he hath set himself"? He hath sinned perseveringly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:38
verses.text: Whence also of a certain pious and good man it is said, "He hath not stood in the way of sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:39
verses.text: As this "hath not stood," so that "hath set himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:40
verses.text: "But wickedness hath he not hated".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:41
verses.text: There is the end, there the fruit: if a man cannot but have wickedness, let him at least hate it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:42
verses.text: For when thou hatest it, it scarcely occurs to thee to do any wickedness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:43
verses.text: For sin is in our mortal body, but what saith the Apostle? "Let not sin reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:44
verses.text: When beginneth it not to be therein? When that shall be fulfilled in us which he saith, "When this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:45
verses.text: Before this come to pass, there is a delighting in sin in the body, but greater is the delighting and the pleasure in the Word of Wisdom, in the Commandment of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:46
verses.text: Overcome sin and the lust thereof.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:47
verses.text: Sin and iniquity do thou hate, that thou mayest join thyself to God, who hateth it as well as thou.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:48
verses.text: Now being joined in mind unto the Law of God, in mind thou servest the Law of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:49
verses.text: And if in the flesh thou therefore servest the law of sin, because there are in thee certain carnal delightings, then will there be none when thou shalt no longer fight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:50
verses.text: It is one thing not to fight, and to be in true and lasting peace; another to fight and overcome; another to fight and to be overcome; another not to fight at all, but to be carried away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:51
verses.text: "Thy mercy, O Lord, is in the heavens, and Thy truth reacheth even unto the clouds".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:52
verses.text: I know not what Mercy of Him he meaneth, which is in the heavens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:53
verses.text: For the Mercy of the Lord is also in the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:54
verses.text: Thou hast it written, "The earth is full of the Mercy of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:55
verses.text: Of what Mercy then speaketh He, when He saith, "Thy Mercy, O Lord, is in the heavens"? The gifts of God are partly temporal and earthly, partly eternal and heavenly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:56
verses.text: Whoso for this worshippeth God, that he may receive those temporal and earthly goods, which are open to all, is still as it were like the brutes: he enjoyeth indeed the Mercy of God, but not that which is excepted, which shall not be given, save only to the righteous, to the holy, to the good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:57
verses.text: What are the gifts which abound to all? "He maketh His sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:58
verses.text: Who hath not this Mercy of God, first that he hath being, that he is distinguished from the brutes, that he is a rational animal, so as to understand God; secondly, that he enjoys this light, this air, rain, fruits, diversity of seasons, and all the earthly comforts, health of body, the affection of friends, the safety of his family? All these are good, and they are God's gifts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:59
verses.text: But this man rightly understood what mercy he should pray for from God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:60
verses.text: "Thy Mercy, O Lord, is in the Heavens; and Thy Truth reacheth even to the clouds".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:61
verses.text: That is, the Mercy which Thou givest to Thy Saints, is Heavenly, not earthly; is Eternal, not temporal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:62
verses.text: And how couldest Thou declare it unto men? Because "Thy Truth reacheth even unto the clouds".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:63
verses.text: For who could know the Heavenly Mercy of God, unless God should declare it unto men? How did He declare it? By sending His truth even unto the clouds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:64
verses.text: What are the clouds? The Preachers of the Word of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:65
verses.text: Truth reached even to the clouds: therefore unto us could be declared the Mercy of God, which is in Heaven and not in earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:66
verses.text: And truly, Brethren, the clouds are the Preachers of the Word of Truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:67
verses.text: When God threateneth through His Preachers, He thunders through the clouds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:68
verses.text: When God worketh miracles through His Preachers, He lightneth through the clouds, He terrifieth through the clouds, and watereth by the rain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:69
verses.text: Those Preachers, then, by whom is preached the Gospel of God, are the clouds of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:70
verses.text: Let us then hope for Mercy, but for that which is in the Heavens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:71
verses.text: "Thy Righteousness is like the mountains of God: Thy Judgments are a great deep".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:72
verses.text: Who are the mountains of God? Those who are called clouds, the same are also the mountains of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:73
verses.text: The great Preachers are the mountains of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:74
verses.text: And as when the sun riseth, he first clothes the mountains with light, and thence the light descends to the lowest parts of the earth: so our Lord Jesus Christ, when He came, first irradiated the height of the Apostles, first enlightened the mountains, and so His Light descended to the valley of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:75
verses.text: And therefore saith He in a certain Psalm, "I lifted up mine eyes unto the mountains, from whence cometh my help".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:76
verses.text: But think not that the mountains themselves will give thee help: for they receive what they may give, give not of their own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:77
verses.text: And if thou remain in the mountains, thy hope will not be strong: but in Him who enlighteneth the mountains, ought to be thy hope and presumption.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:78
verses.text: Thy help indeed will come to thee through the mountains, because the Scriptures are administered to thee through the mountains, through the great Preachers of the Truth: but fix not thy hope in them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:79
verses.text: Hear what He saith next following: "I lifted up mine eyes unto the mountains, from whence cometh my help".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:80
verses.text: What then? Do the mountains give thee help? No; hear what follows, "My help cometh from the Lord, which made Heaven and earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:81
verses.text: Through the mountains cometh help, but not from the mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:82
verses.text: From whom then? "From the Lord, which made Heaven and earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:83
verses.text: "Thy Judgments are like the great abyss".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:84
verses.text: The abyss he calleth the depth of sin, whither every one cometh by despising God; as in a certain place it is said, "God gave them over to their own hearts' lusts, to do the things which are not convenient".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:85
verses.text: Because then they were proud and ungrateful, they were held worthy to be delivered up to the lusts of their own hearts, and became a great abyss, so that they not only sinned, but also worked craftily, lest they should understand their iniquity, and hate it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:86
verses.text: That is the depth of wickedness, to be unwilling to find it out and to hate it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:87
verses.text: But how one cometh to that depth, see; "Thy Judgments are the great abyss".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:88
verses.text: As the mountains are by the Righteousness of God,  who through His Grace become great: so also through His Judgments come they unto the depth, who sink lowest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:89
verses.text: By this then let the mountains delight thee, by this turn away from the abyss, and turn thyself unto that, of which it is said, "My help cometh from the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:90
verses.text: But whereby? "I have lifted up mine eyes unto the mountains".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:91
verses.text: What meaneth this? I will speak plainly In the Church of God thou findest an abyss, thou findest also mountains; thou findest there but few good, because the mountains are few, the abyss broad; that is, thou findest many living ill after the wrath of God, because they have so worked that they are delivered up to the lusts of their own heart; so now they defend their sins and confess them not; but say, Why? What have I done? Such an one did this, and such an one did that.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:92
verses.text: Now will they even defend what the Divine Word reproves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:93
verses.text: This is the abyss.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:94
verses.text: Therefore in a certain place saith the Scripture (hear this abyss), "The sinner when he cometh unto the depth of sin despiseth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:95
verses.text: See, "Thy Judgments are like the great abyss".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:96
verses.text: But yet not art thou a mountain; not yet art thou in the abyss; fly from the abyss, tend towards the mountains; but yet remain not on the mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:97
verses.text: "For thy help cometh from the Lord, which made Heaven and earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:98
verses.text: Because he said, Thy Mercy is in the Heavens, that it may be known to be also on earth, he said, "O Lord, Thou savest man and beast, as Thy Mercy is multiplied, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:99
verses.text: Great is Thy Mercy, and manifold is Thy Mercy, O God; and that showest Thou both to man and beast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:100
verses.text: For from whom is the saving of men? From God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:101
verses.text: Is not the saving of beasts also from God? For He who made man, made also beasts; He who made both, saveth both; but the saving of beasts is temporal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:102
verses.text: But there are who as a great thing ask this of God, which He hath given to beasts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:103
verses.text: "Thy Mercy, O God, is multiplied," so that not only unto men, but unto beasts also is given the same saving which is given to men, a carnal and temporal saving.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:104
verses.text: Have not men then somewhat reserved with God, which beasts deserve not, and whereunto beasts arrive not? They have evidently.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:105
verses.text: And where is that which they have.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:106
verses.text: "The children of men put their trust under the shadow of Thy wings".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:107
verses.text: Attend, my Beloved, to this most pleasant sentence; "Thou savest man and beast".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:108
verses.text: First, he spake of "man and beast," then of "the children of men;" as though "men" were one, "the children of men" other.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:109
verses.text: Sometimes in Scripture children of men is said generally of all men, sometimes in some proper manner, with some proper signification, so that not all men are understood; chiefly when there is a distinction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:110
verses.text: For not without reason is it here put; "O Lord, Thou savest man and beast: but the children of men;" as though setting aside the first, he keepeth separate the children of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:111
verses.text: Separate from whom? Not only from beasts, but also from men, who seek from God the saving of beasts, and desire this as a great thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:112
verses.text: Who then are the children of men? Those who put their trust under the shadow of His wings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:113
verses.text: For those men together with beasts rejoice in possession, but the children of men rejoice in hope: those follow after present goods with beasts, these hope for future goods with Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:114
verses.text: "They shall be satiated with the fulness of Thy House".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:115
verses.text: He promiseth us some great thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:116
verses.text: He would speak it, and He speaketh it not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:117
verses.text: Can He not, or do not we receive it? I dare, my Brethren, to say, even of holy tongues and hearts, by which Truth is declared to us, that it can neither be spoken, which they declared, nor even thought of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:118
verses.text: For it is a great thing, and ineffable; and even they saw through a glass darkly, as saith the Apostle, "For now we see through a glass darkly; but then face to face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:119
verses.text: Lo, they who saw through a glass darkly, thus burst forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:120
verses.text: What then shall we be, when we shall see face to face? That with which they travailed in heart, and could not with their tongue bring forth, that men might receive it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:121
verses.text: For what necessity was there that he should say, "They shall be satiated with the fulness of Thy House"? He sought a word whereby to express from human things what he would say; and because he saw that men drowning themselves in drunkenness receive indeed wine without measure, but lose their senses, he saw what to say; for when shall have been received that ineffable joy, then shall be lost in a manner the human soul, it shall bec ome Divine, and be satiated with the fulness of God's House.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:122
verses.text: Wherefore also in another Psalm it is said, "Thy cup inebriating, how excellent is it!" With this cup were the Martyrs satiated when going to their passion, they knew not their own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:123
verses.text: What so inebriated as not to know a wife weeping, not children, not parents? They knew them not, they thought not that they were before their eyes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:124
verses.text: Wonder not: they were inebriated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:125
verses.text: Wherewith were they so? Lo, they had received a cup wherewith they were satiated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:126
verses.text: Wherefore he also gives thanks to God, saying, "What shall I render unto the Lord for all His benefits towards me? I will take the cup of Salvation, and call upon the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:127
verses.text: Therefore, Brethren of men, let us be children and let us trust under the shadow of His wings and be satiated with the fulness of His House.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:128
verses.text: As I could, I have spoken; and as far as I can I see; and how far I see, I cannot speak "And of the torrent of Thy Pleasure shalt Thou give them to drink".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:129
verses.text: A torrent we call water coming with a flood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:130
verses.text: There will be a flood of God's Mercy to overflow and inebriate those who now put their trust under the shadow of His wings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:131
verses.text: What is that Pleasure? As it were a torrent inebriating the thirsty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:132
verses.text: Let him then who thirsts now, lay up hope: whoso thirsts now, let him have hope; when inebriated, he shall have possession: before he have possession, let him thirst in hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:133
verses.text: "Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:134
verses.text: With what fountain then wilt thou be overflowed, and whence runneth such a torrent of His Pleasure? "For with Thee," saith he, "is the fountain of Life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:135
verses.text: What is the fountain of Life, but Christ? He came to thee in the flesh, that He might bedew thy thirsty lips: He will satisfy thee trusting, who bedewed thee thirsting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:136
verses.text: "For with Thee is the fountain of Life; in Thy Light shall we see light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:137
verses.text: Here a fountain is one thing, light another: there not so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:138
verses.text: For that which is the Fountain, the same is also Light: and whatever thou wilt thou callest It, for It is not what thou callest It: for thou canst not find a fit name: for It remaineth not in one name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:139
verses.text: If thou shouldest say, that It is Light only, it would be said to thee, Then without cause am I told to hunger and thirst, for who is there that eateth light? It is said to me plainly, directly, "Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:140
verses.text: If It is Light, my eyes must I prepare.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:141
verses.text: Prepare also lips; for That which is Light is also a Fountain: a Fountain, because It satisfieth the thirsty: Light, because It enlighteneth the blind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:142
verses.text: Here sometimes, light is in one place, a fountain in another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:143
verses.text: For sometimes fountains run even in darkness; and sometimes in the desert thou sufferest the sun, findest no fountain: here then can these two be separated: there thou shalt not be wearied, for there is a Fountain; there thou shalt not be darkened, for there is Light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:144
verses.text: "Show forth Thy Mercy unto them that know Thee; Thy Righteousness to them that are of a right heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:145
verses.text: As I have said, Those are of a right heart who follow in this life the Will of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:146
verses.text: The will of God is sometimes that thou shouldest be whole, sometimes that thou shouldest be sick.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:147
verses.text: If when thou art whole God's Will be sweet, and when thou art sick God's Will be bitter; thou art not of a right heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:148
verses.text: Wherefore? Because thou wilt not make right thy will according to God's Will, but wilt bend God's Will to thine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:149
verses.text: That is right, but thou art crooked: thy will must be made right to That, not That made crooked to thee; and thou wilt have a right heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:150
verses.text: It is well with thee in this world; be God blessed, who comforteth thee: it goeth hardly with thee in this world; be God blessed, because He chasteneth and proveth thee; and so wilt thou be of a right heart, saying, "I will bless the Lord at all times: His Praise shall be ever in my mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:151
verses.text: "Let not the foot of pride come against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:152
verses.text: But now he said, The children of men shall put their trust under the shadow of Thy wings: they shall be satiated with the fulness of Thy House.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:153
verses.text: When one hath begun to be plentifully overflowed with that Fountain, let him take heed lest he grow proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:154
verses.text: For the same was not wanting to Adam, the first man: but the foot of pride came against him, and the hand of the sinner removed him, that is, the proud hand of the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:155
verses.text: As he who seduced him, said of himself, "I will sit in the sides of the north;" so he persuaded him, by saying, "Taste, and ye shall be as gods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:156
verses.text: By pride then have we so fallen as to arrive at this mortality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:157
verses.text: And because pride had wounded us, humility maketh us whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:158
verses.text: God came humbly, that from such great wound of pride He might heal man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:159
verses.text: He came, for "The Word was made Flesh, and dwelt among us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:160
verses.text: He was taken by the Jews; He was reviled of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:161
verses.text: Ye heard when the Gospel was read, what they said, and to Whom they said, "Thou hast a devil:" and He said not, Ye have a devil, for ye are still in your sins, and the devil possesseth your hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:162
verses.text: He said not this, which if He had said, He had said truly: but it was not meet that He should say it, lest He should seem not to preach Truth, but to retort evil speaking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:163
verses.text: He let go what He heard as though He heard it not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:164
verses.text: For a Physician was He, and to cure the madman had He come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:165
verses.text: As a Physician careth not what he may hear from the madman; but how the madman may recover and become sane; nor even if he receive a blow from the madman, careth he; but while he to him giveth new wounds, he cureth his old fever: so also the Lord came to the sick man, to the madman came He, that whatever He might hear, whatever He might suffer, He should despise; by this very thing teaching us humility, that being taught by humility, we might be healed from pride: from which he here prayeth to be delivered, saying, "Let not the foot of pride come against me; neither let the hand of the sinner remove me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:166
verses.text: For if the foot of pride come, the hand of the sinner removeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:167
verses.text: What is the hand of the sinner? The working of him that adviseth ill.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:168
verses.text: Hast thou become proud? Quickly he corrupteth thee who adviseth ill.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:169
verses.text: Humbly fix thyself in God, and care not much what is said to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:170
verses.text: Hence is that which is elsewhere spoken, "From my secret sins cleanse Thou me; and from others' sins also keep Thy servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:171
verses.text: What is, "From my secret sins"? "Let not the foot of pride come against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:172
verses.text: What is, "From other men's sins also keep Thy servant"? "Let not the hand of the wicked remove me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:173
verses.text: Keep that which is within, and thou shalt not fear from without.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:174
verses.text: But wherefore so greatly fearest thou this? Because it is said, "Thereby have fallen all that work iniquity" ; so that they have come into that abyss of which it is said, "Thy judgments are like the great abyss:" so that they have come even to that deep wherein sinners who despise have fallen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:175
verses.text: "Have fallen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:176
verses.text: Whereby did they first fall? By the foot of pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:177
verses.text: Hear the foot of pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:178
verses.text: "When they knew God, they glorified Him not as God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:179
verses.text: Therefore came against them the foot of pride, whereby they came into the depth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:180
verses.text: "God gave them over to their own hearts' lusts, to do those things which are not convenient".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:181
verses.text: The root of sin, and the head of sin feared he who said, "Let not the foot of pride come against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:182
verses.text: Wherefore said he, "the foot"? Because by walking proudly man deserted God, and departed from Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:183
verses.text: His foot, called he his affection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:184
verses.text: "Let not the foot of pride come against me: let not the hand of the wicked remove me:" that is, let not the works of the wicked remove me from Thee, that I should wish to imitate them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:185
verses.text: But wherefore said he this against pride, "Thereby have fallen all that work iniquity"? Because those who now are ungodly, have fallen by pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:186
verses.text: Therefore when the Lord would caution His Church, He said, "It shall watch thy head, and thou shalt watch his heel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:187
verses.text: The serpent watcheth when the foot of pride may come against thee, when thou mayest fall, that he may cast thee down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:188
verses.text: But watch thou his head: the beginning of all sin is pride "Thereby have fallen all that work iniquity: they are driven out, and are not able to stand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:189
verses.text: He first, who in the Truth stood not, then, through him, they whom God sent out of Paradise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:190
verses.text: Whence he, the humble, who said that he was not worthy to unloose His shoe's latchet, is not driven out, but standeth and heareth Him, and rejoiceth greatly because of the Bridegroom's voice; not because of his own, lest the foot of pride come against him, and he be driven out, and be not able to stand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 36:191
verses.text: Contents   Part  Part  Part.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:1
verses.text: Psalm XXXVII  On the first part of the psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:2
verses.text: With terror do they hear of the coming of the last day, who will not be secure by living well: and who fain would live ill, long.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:3
verses.text: But it was for useful purposes that God willed that day to remain unknown; that the heart may be ever ready to expect that of which it knows it is to come, but knows not when it is to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:4
verses.text: Seeing, however, that our Lord Jesus Christ was sent to us to be our "Master," He said, that "of the day not even the Son of Man knew," because it was not part of His office as our Master that through Him it should become known to us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:5
verses.text: For indeed the Father knoweth nothing that the Son knoweth not; since that is the Very Knowledge of the Father Itself, which is His Wisdom; now His Son, His Word, is "His Wisdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:6
verses.text: But because it was not for our good to know that, which however was known to Him who came indeed to teach us, though not to teach us that which it was not good for us to know, He not only, as a Master, taught us something, but also, as a Master, left something untaught.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:7
verses.text: For, as a Master, He knew how both to teach us what was good for us, and not to teach us what was injurious.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:8
verses.text: Now thus, according to a certain form of speech, the Son is said not to know what He does not teach: that is, in the same way that we are daily in the habit of speaking, He is said not to know what He causes us not to know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:9
verses.text: This it is that disturbs you who are a Christian; that you see men of bad lives prospering, and surrounded with abundance of things like these; you see them sound in health, distinguished with proud honours; you see their family unvisited by misfortune; the happiness of their relatives, the obsequious attendance of their dependants, their most commanding influence, their life uninterrupted by any sad event; you see their characters most profligate, their external resources most affluent; and your heart says that there is no Divine judgment; that all things are carried to and fro by accidents, and blown about in disorderly and irregular motions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:10
verses.text: For if God, thou sayest, regarded human affairs, would his iniquity flourish, and my innocence suffer? Every sickness of the soul hath in Scripture its proper remedy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:11
verses.text: Let him then whose  sickness is of that kind that he says in his heart things like these, let him drink this Psalm by way of potion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:12
verses.text: "Be not envious because of evil-doers, neither be envious against the workers of iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:13
verses.text: "For they shall soon wither like the grass, and shall fade like the herbs of the meadow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:14
verses.text: That which to thee seemeth long, is "soon" in the sight of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:15
verses.text: Conform thou thyself to God; and it will be "soon" to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:16
verses.text: That which he here calls "grass," that we understand by the "herbs of the meadow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:17
verses.text: They are some worthless things, occupying the surface only of the ground, they have no depth of root.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:18
verses.text: In the winter then they are green; but when the summer sun shall begin to scorch, they will wither away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:19
verses.text: For now it is the season of winter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:20
verses.text: Thy glory doth not as yet appear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:21
verses.text: But if thy love hath but a deep root, like that of many trees during winter, the frost passes away, the summer (that is, the Day of Judgment) will come; then will the greenness of the grass wither away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:22
verses.text: Then will the glory of the trees appear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:23
verses.text: "For ye" (saith the Apostle) "are dead," even as trees seem to be in winter, as it were dead, as it were withered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:24
verses.text: What is our hope then, if we are dead? The root is within; where our root is, there is our life also, for there our love is fixed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:25
verses.text: "And your life is hid with Christ in God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:26
verses.text: When shall he wither who is thus rooted? But when will our spring be? When our summer? When will the honour of foliage clothe us around, and the fulness of fruit make us rich? When shall this come to pass? Hear what follows: "When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with Him in glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:27
verses.text: And what then shall we do now? "Be not envious because of the evil-doers, neither be envious against the workers of iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:28
verses.text: For they shall soon wither like the grass, and fade like the herb of the meadow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:29
verses.text: What shouldest thou do then? "Trust in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:30
verses.text: For they too trust, but not "in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:31
verses.text: Their hope is perishable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:32
verses.text: Their hope is short-lived, frail, fleeting, transitory, baseless.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:33
verses.text: "Trust thou in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:34
verses.text: "Behold," thou sayest, "I do trust; what am I to do?"  "And do good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:35
verses.text: Do not do that evil which thou beholdest in those men, who are prosperous in wickedness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:36
verses.text: "Do good, and dwell in the land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:37
verses.text: Lest haply thou shouldest be doing good without "dwelling in the land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:38
verses.text: For it is the Church that is the Lord's land.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:39
verses.text: It is her whom He, the Father, the tiller of it, waters and cultivates.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:40
verses.text: For there are many that, as it were, do good works, but yet, in that they do not "dwell in the land," they do not belong to the husbandman.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:41
verses.text: Therefore do thou thy good, not outside of the land, but do thou "dwell in the land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:42
verses.text: And what shall I have?  "And thou shalt be fed in its riches".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:43
verses.text: What are the riches of that land? Her riches are her Lord! Her riches are her God! He it is to whom it is said, "The Lord is the portion of mine inheritance, and of my cup".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:44
verses.text: In a late discourse we suggested to you, dearly beloved, that God is our possession, and that we are at the same time God's possession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:45
verses.text: Hear how that He is Himself the riches of that land.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:46
verses.text: "Delight thyself in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:47
verses.text: As if thou hadst put the question, and hadst said "Show me the riches of that land, in which thou biddest me dwell," he says, "Delight thyself in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:48
verses.text: "And He shall give thee the desires of thine heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:49
verses.text: Understand in their proper signification, "the desires of thine heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:50
verses.text: Distinguish the "desires of thine heart" from the desires of thy flesh; distinguish as much as thou canst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:51
verses.text: It is not without a meaning that it is said in a certain Psalm, "God is" (the strength) "of mine heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:52
verses.text: For there it says in what follows: "And God is my portion for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:53
verses.text: For instance: One labours under bodily blindness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:54
verses.text: He asks that he may receive his sight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:55
verses.text: Let him ask it; for God does that too, and gives those blessings also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:56
verses.text: But these things are asked for even by the wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:57
verses.text: This is a desire of the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:58
verses.text: One is sick, and prays to be made sound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:59
verses.text: From the point of death he is restored to health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:60
verses.text: That too is a desire of the flesh, as are all of such a kind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:61
verses.text: What is "the desire of the heart"? As the desire of the flesh is to wish to have one's eyesight restored, to enable him, that is, to see that light, which can be seen by such eyes; so "the desire of the heart" relates to a different sort of light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:62
verses.text: For, "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:63
verses.text: Delight thou thyself in the Lord; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:64
verses.text: "Behold" (you say), "I do long after it, I do ask for it, I do desire it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:65
verses.text: Shall I then accomplish it?" No.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:66
verses.text: Who shall then? "Reveal thy way unto the Lord: trust also in Him, and He shall bring it to pass".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:67
verses.text: Mention to Him what thou sufferest, mention to Him what thou dost desire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:68
verses.text: For what is it that thou sufferest? "The flesh lusteth against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:69
verses.text: What is it then that thou dost desire? "Wretched man that I am! Who shall deliver me from the body of this death?" And because it is He "Himself" that "will bring it to pass," when thou shalt have "revealed thy ways unto Him;" hear what follows: "The grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:70
verses.text: What is it then that He is to bring to pass, since it is said, "Reveal thy way unto Him, and He will bring it to pass"? What will He bring to pass?  "And He shall bring forth thy righteousness as the light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:71
verses.text: For now, "thy righteousness" is hid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:72
verses.text: Now it is a thing of faith; not yet of sight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:73
verses.text: You believe something that you may do it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:74
verses.text: You do not yet see that in which you believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:75
verses.text: But when thou shalt begin to see that, which thou didst believe before, "thy righteousness will be brought forth to the light," because it is thy faith that was thy righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:76
verses.text: For "the just lives by faith".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:77
verses.text: "And He shall bring forth thy judgment as the noon-day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:78
verses.text: That is to say, "as the clear light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:79
verses.text: It was too little to say, "as the light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:80
verses.text: For we call it "light" already, even when it but dawns: we call it light even while the sun is rising.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:81
verses.text: But never is the light brighter than at mid-day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:82
verses.text: Therefore He will not only "bring forth thy righteousness as the light," but "thy judgment shall be as the noon-day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:83
verses.text: For now dost thou make thy "judgment" to follow Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:84
verses.text: This is thy purpose: this is thy choice: this is thy "judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:85
verses.text: "What should I do then?" Hear what thou shouldest do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:86
verses.text: "Submit thee to the Lord, and entreat Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:87
verses.text: Be this thy life, to obey His commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:88
verses.text: For this is to submit thee to Him; and to entreat Him until He give thee what He hath promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:89
verses.text: Let good works "continue;" let prayer "continue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:90
verses.text: For "men ought always to pray, and not to faint".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:91
verses.text: Wherein dost thou show that thou art "submitted to Him"? In doing what He hath commanded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:92
verses.text: But haply thou dost not receive thy wages as yet, because as yet thou art not able.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:93
verses.text: For He is already able to give them; but thou art not already able to receive them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:94
verses.text: Exercise thou thyself in works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:95
verses.text: Labour in the vineyard; at the close of the day crave thy wages.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:96
verses.text: "Faithful is He" who brought thee into the vineyard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:97
verses.text: "Submit thee to the Lord, and entreat Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:98
verses.text: "See! I do so; I do 'submit to the Lord, and I do entreat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:99
verses.text: ' But what do you think? That neighbour of mine is a wicked man, living a bad life, and prosperous! His thefts, adulteries, robberies, are known to me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:100
verses.text: Lifted up above every one, proud, and raised on high by wickedness, he deigns not to notice me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:101
verses.text: In these circumstances, how shall I hold out with patience?" This is a sickness; drink, by way of remedy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:102
verses.text: "Fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:103
verses.text: He prospereth, but it is "in his way:" thou sufferest, but it is in God's way! His portion is prosperity on his way, misery on arriving at its end: yours, toil on the road, happiness in its termination.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:104
verses.text: "The Lord knoweth the way of the righteous; and the way of the ungodly shall perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:105
verses.text: Thou walkest those ways which "the Lord knoweth," and if thou dost suffer toil in them, they do not deceive thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:106
verses.text: The "way of the ungodly" is but a transitory happiness; at the end of the way the happiness is at an end also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:107
verses.text: Why? Because that way is "the broad road;" its termination leads to the pit of hell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:108
verses.text: Now, thy way is narrow; and "few there be" that enter in through it: but into how ample a field it comes at the last, thou oughtest to consider.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:109
verses.text: "Fret not thyself at him who prospereth in his way; because of the man who bringeth wicked devices to pass".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:110
verses.text: "Cease from anger, and forsake wrath".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:111
verses.text: Wherefore art thou wroth? Wherefore is it that, through that passion and indignation, thou dost blaspheme, or almost blaspheme? Against "the man who bringeth wicked devices to pass, cease from anger, and forsake wrath".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:112
verses.text: Knowest thou not whither that wrath tempts thee on? Thou art on the point of saying unto God, that He is unjust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:113
verses.text: It tends to that.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:114
verses.text: "Look! why is that man prosperous, and this man in adversity?" Consider what thought it begets: stifle the wicked notion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:115
verses.text: "Cease from anger, and forsake wrath:" so that now returning to thy senses, thou mayest say, "Mine eye is disturbed because of wrath".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:116
verses.text: What eye is that, but the eye of faith? To the eye of thy faith I appeal Thou didst believe in Christ: why didst thou believe? What did He promise thee? If it was the happiness of this world that Christ promised thee, then murmur against Christ; yes! murmur against Him, when thou seest the wicked flourishing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:117
verses.text: What of happiness did He promise? What, save in the Resurrection of the Dead? But what in this life? That which was His portion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:118
verses.text: His portion, I say! Dost thou, servant and disciple, disdain what thy Lord, what thy Master bore?  "For evil-doers shall be cut off".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:119
verses.text: "But I see their prosperity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:120
verses.text: Believe Him who saith, "they shall be cut off;" Him who seeth better than thou, since His eye anger cannot cloud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:121
verses.text: "For evil-doers shall be cut off.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:122
verses.text: But those that wait upon the Lord,"—not upon any one that can deceive them; but verily on Him who is the Truth itself,—"But those that wait upon the Lord, they shall inherit the land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:123
verses.text: What "land," but that Jerusalem, with the love of which whosoever is inflamed, shall come to peace at the last.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:124
verses.text: "But how long is the sinner to flourish? How long shall I have to endure?" Thou art impatient; that which seems long to thee, will soon come to pass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:125
verses.text: It is infirmity makes that seem long, which is really short, as is found in the case of the longings of sick men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:126
verses.text: Nothing seems so long as the mixing of the potion for him when athirst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:127
verses.text: For all that his attendants are making all speed, lest haply the patient be angry; "When will it be done? (he cries).

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:128
verses.text: When will it be drest? When will it be served?" Those who are waiting upon you are making haste, but your infirmity fancies that long which is being done with expedition.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:129
verses.text: Behold ye, therefore, our Physician complying with the infirmity of the patient, saying, "How long shall I have to endure? How long will it be?"  "Yet a little while, and the sinner shall not be".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:130
verses.text: Is it certainly among sinners, and because of the sinner, that thou murmurest? "A little while, and he shall not be".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:131
verses.text: Lest haply because I said, "They that wait upon the Lord, they shall inherit the land," thou shouldest think that waiting to be of very long duration.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:132
verses.text: Wait "a little while," thou shalt receive without end what thou waitest for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:133
verses.text: A little while, a moderate space.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:134
verses.text: Review the years from Adam's time up to this day; run through the Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:135
verses.text: It is almost yesterday that he fell from Paradise! So many ages have been measured out, and unrolled Where now are the past ages? Even so, however, shall the few which remain, pass away also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:136
verses.text: Hadst thou been living throughout all that time, since Adam was banished from Paradise up to this present day, thou wouldest certainly see that the life, which had thus flown away, had not been of long duration.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:137
verses.text: But how long is the duration of each individual's life? Add any number of years you please: prolong old age to its longest duration: what is it? Is it not but a morning breeze? Be it so, however, that the Day of Judgment is far off, when the reward of the righteous and of the unrighteous is to come: your last day at all events cannot be far off.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:138
verses.text: Make thyself ready against this! For such as thou shall have departed from this life, shalt thou be restored to the other.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:139
verses.text: At the close of that short life, you will not yet be, where the Saints shall be, to whom it shall be said, "Come, ye blessed of My Father: inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the beginning of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:140
verses.text: You will not yet be there? Who does not know that? But you may already be there, where that beggar, once "covered with sores," was seen at a distance, at rest, by that proud and unfruitful "rich man" in the midst of his torments Surely hid in that rest thou waitest in security for the Day of Judgment, when thou art to receive again a body, to be changed so as to be made equal to an Angel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:141
verses.text: How long then is that for which we are impatient, and are saying, "When will it come? Will it tarry long?" This our sons will say hereafter, and our sons' sons will say too; and, though each one of these in succession will say this same thing, that "little while" that is yet to be, passes away, as all that is already past hath passed away already! O thou sick one! "Yet a little while, and the sinner shall not be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:142
verses.text: Yea, thou shalt diligently consider his place, and thou shalt not find him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:143
verses.text: "But the meek shall inherit the land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:144
verses.text: That land is the one of which we have often spoken, the holy Jerusalem, which is to be released from these her pilgrimages, and to live for ever with God, and on God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:145
verses.text: Therefore, "They shall inherit the land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:146
verses.text: What shall be their delight? "And they shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:147
verses.text: Let the ungodly man delight himself here in the multitude of his gold, in the multitude of his silver, in the multitude of his slaves, in the multitude, lastly, of his baths, his roses, his intoxicating wines, his most sumptuous and luxurious banquets.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:148
verses.text: Is this the power thou enviest? Is this the glory that delights thee? Would not his fate be worthy to be deplored, even if he were to be so for ever? What shall be thy delights? "And they shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:149
verses.text: Peace shall be thy gold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:150
verses.text: Peace shall be thy silver.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:151
verses.text: Peace shall be thy lands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:152
verses.text: Peace shall be thy life, thy God Peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:153
verses.text: Peace shall be to thee whatsoever thou dost desire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:154
verses.text: On the Second Part of the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:155
verses.text: Then follow these words: "The wicked plotteth against the just, and gnasheth upon him with his teeth" : "But the Lord shall laugh at him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:156
verses.text: At whom? Surely at the sinner, "gnashing upon" the other "with his teeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:157
verses.text: But wherefore shall the Lord "laugh at him"? "For He foreseeth that his day is coming".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:158
verses.text: He seems indeed full of wrath, while, ignorant of the morrow that is in store for him, he is threatening the just.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:159
verses.text: But the Lord beholds and "foresees his day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:160
verses.text: "What day?" That in which "He will render to every man according to his works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:161
verses.text: For he is "treasuring up unto himself wrath against the day of wrath, and revelation of the just judgment of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:162
verses.text: But it is the Lord that foresees it; thou dost not foresee it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:163
verses.text: It hath been revealed to thee by Him who foresees it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:164
verses.text: Thou didst not know of the "day of the unrighteous," in which he is to suffer punishment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:165
verses.text: But He who knows it hath revealed it to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:166
verses.text: It is a main part of knowledge to join thyself to Him who hath knowledge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:167
verses.text: He hath the eyes of knowledge: have thou the eyes of a believing mind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:168
verses.text: That which God "sees," be thou willing to believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:169
verses.text: For the day of the unjust, which God foresees, will come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:170
verses.text: What day is that? The day for all vengeance! For it is necessary that vengeance should be taken upon the ungodly, that vengeance be taken upon the unjust, whether he turn, or whether he turn not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:171
verses.text: For if he shall turn from his ways, that very thing, that his "injustice is come to an end," is the infliction of vengeance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:172
verses.text: "The wicked have drawn out the sword, and have bent their bow, to cast down the poor and needy, and to slay such as be of upright heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:173
verses.text: "Their weapon shall enter into their own heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:174
verses.text: It is an easy thing for his weapon, that is, his sword, to reach thy body, even as the sword of the persecutors reached the body of the Martyrs, but when the body had been smitten, "the heart" remained unhurt; but his heart who "drew out the sword against" the body of the just did not clearly remain unhurt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:175
verses.text: This is attested by this very Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:176
verses.text: It saith, Their weapon, that is, "Their sword shall," not go into their body, but, "their weapon shall go into their own heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:177
verses.text: They would fain have slain him in the body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:178
verses.text: Let them die the death of the soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:179
verses.text: For those whose bodies they sought to kill, the Lord hath freed from anxiety, saying, "Fear not them who kill the body, but cannot kill the soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:180
verses.text: "And their bows shall be broken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:181
verses.text: What is meant by, "And their bows shall be broken"? Their plots shall be frustrated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:182
verses.text: For above He had said, "The wicked have drawn out the sword and bent their bows".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:183
verses.text: By the "drawing out of the sword" he would have understood open hostility; but by the" bending of the bow," secret conspiracies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:184
verses.text: See! His sword destroys himself, and his laying of snares is frustrated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:185
verses.text: What is meant by frustrated? That it does no mischief to the righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:186
verses.text: How then, for instance (you ask), did it do no mischief to the man, whom it thus stripped of his goods, whom it reduced to straitened circumstances by taking away his possessions? He has still cause to sing, "A little that a righteous man hath, is better than great riches of the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:187
verses.text: "For the arms of the wicked shall be broken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:188
verses.text: Now by "their arms" is meant their power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:189
verses.text: What will he do in hell? Will it be what the rich man had to do, he who was wont "to fare sumptuously" in the upper world, and in hell "was tormented"? Therefore their arms shall be broken; "but the Lord upholdeth the righteous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:190
verses.text: How does He "uphold" them? What saith He unto them? Even what is said in another Psalm, "Wait on the Lord, be of good courage; and let thine heart be strengthened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:191
verses.text: Wait, I say, on the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:192
verses.text: What is meant by this, "Wait on the Lord"? Thou sufferest but for a time; thou shalt rest for ever: thy trouble is short; thy happiness is to be everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:193
verses.text: It is but for "a little while" thou art to sorrow; thy joy shall have no end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:194
verses.text: But in the midst of trouble does thy "foot" begin to "slip"? The example even of Christ's sufferings is set before thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:195
verses.text: Consider what He endured for thee, in whom no cause was found why He should endure it? How great soever be thy sufferings, thou wilt not come to those insults, those scourgings, to that robe of shame, to that crown of thorns, and last of all to that Cross, which He endured; because that is now removed from the number of human punishments For though under the ancients criminals were crucified, in the present day no one is crucified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:196
verses.text: It was honoured, and it came to an end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:197
verses.text: It came to an end as a punishment; it is continued in glory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:198
verses.text: It hath removed from the place of execution to the foreheads of Emperors.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:199
verses.text: He who hath invested His very sufferings with such honour, what doth He reserve for His faithful servants?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:200
verses.text: But observe whether that was fulfilled in his case which the Psalm now speaks of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:201
verses.text: "The Lord strengtheneth the righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:202
verses.text: —Not only so" (saith that same Paul, whilst suffering many evils), "but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience, and patience experience; and experience hope; but hope maketh not ashamed, because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost, which is given unto us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:203
verses.text: Justly is it said by him, now righteous, now "strengthened".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:204
verses.text: As therefore those who persecuted him did no harm to him, when now "strengthened," so neither did he himself do any harm to those whom he persecuted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:205
