verses.text: "But the Lord," he saith, "strengtheneth the righteous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:206
verses.text: Therefore "the Lord does strengthen the righteous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:207
verses.text: In what way does He strengthen them? "The Lord knoweth the ways of the spotless ones".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:208
verses.text: When they suffer ills, they are believed to be walking ill ways by those who are ignorant, by those who have not knowledge to discern "the ways of the spotless ones".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:209
verses.text: He who "knoweth those ways," knoweth by  what way to lead His own, "them that are gentle," in the right way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:210
verses.text: Whence in another Psalm he said, "The meek shall He guide in judgment; them that are gentle will He teach His way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:211
verses.text: How, think you, was that beggar, who lay covered with sores before the rich man's door, spurned by the passers by! How did they, probably, close their nostrils and spit at him! The Lord, however, knew how to reserve Paradise for him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:212
verses.text: How did they, on the other hand, desire for themselves the life of him who was "clad in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day!" But the Lord, who foresaw that man's "day coming," knew the torments, the torments without end, that were in store for him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:213
verses.text: Therefore "The Lord knoweth the ways of the upright".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:214
verses.text: "And their inheritance shall be for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:215
verses.text: This we hold by faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:216
verses.text: Doth the Lord too know it by faith? The Lord knoweth those things with as clear a manifestation, as we cannot speak of even when we shall be made equal to the Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:217
verses.text: For the things that shall be manifest to us, shall not be equally manifest to us as they are now to Him, who is incapable of change.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:218
verses.text: Yet even of us ourselves what is said? "Beloved, now are we the sons of God: and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when He shall appear, we shall be like Him, for we shall see Him as He is".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:219
verses.text: There is therefore surely some blissful vision reserved for us; and if it can be now in some measure conceived, "darkly and through a glass," yet cannot we in any way express in language the ravishing beauty of that bliss, which God reserves for them that fear Him, which He consummates in those that hope in Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:220
verses.text: It is for that destination that our hearts are being disciplined in all the troubles and trials of this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:221
verses.text: Wonder not that it is in trouble that thou art disciplined for it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:222
verses.text: It is for something glorious that thou art being disciplined.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:223
verses.text: Whence comes that speech of the now strengthened righteous man: "The sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared to the glory which shall be revealed in us"? What is that promised glory to be, but to be made equal to the Angels and to see God? How great a benefit doth he bestow on the blind man, who makes his eyes sound so as to be able to see the light of this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:224
verses.text: What reward then shall we give unto that Physician who restores soundness to our inward eyes, to enable them to see a certain eternal Light, which is Himself?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:225
verses.text: "They shall not be ashamed in the evil time".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:226
verses.text: In the day of trouble, in the day of distress, they shall not be "ashamed," as he is ashamed whose hope deceives him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:227
verses.text: Who is the man that is "ashamed"? He who saith, "I have not found that which I was in hopes of".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:228
verses.text: Nor undeservedly either; for thou didst hope it from thyself or from man, thy friend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:229
verses.text: But "cursed is he that putteth his trust in man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:230
verses.text: Thou art ashamed, because thy hope hath deceived thee; thy hope that was set on a lie.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:231
verses.text: For "every man is a liar".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:232
verses.text: But if thou dost place thy hopes on thy God, thou art not made "ashamed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:233
verses.text: For He in whom thou hast put thy trust, cannot be deceived Whence also the man whom we mentioned just above, the now "strengthened" righteous man, when fallen on an evil time, on the day of tribulation, what saith he to show that he was not "ashamed"? "We glory in tribulation; knowing that tribulation worketh patience, and patience experience, and experience hope; but hope maketh not ashamed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:234
verses.text: Whence is it that hope "maketh not ashamed"? Because it is placed on God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:235
verses.text: Therefore follows immediately, "Because the love of God is spread in our hearts by the Holy Spirit, which is given unto us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:236
verses.text: The Holy Spirit hath been given to us already: how should He deceive us, of whom we possess such an "earnest" already? "They shall not be ashamed in the evil time, and in the days of famine they shall be satisfied".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:237
verses.text: "For the wicked shall perish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:238
verses.text: But the enemies of the Lord, when they shall begin to glory, and to be lifted up, immediately shall consume away utterly, even as the smoke".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:239
verses.text: Recognise from the comparison itself the thing which he intimates.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:240
verses.text: Smoke, breaking forth from the place where fire has been, rises up on high, and by the very act of rising up, it swells into a large volume: but the larger that volume is, the more unsubstantial does it become; for from that very largeness of volume, which has no foundation or consistency, but is merely loose, shifting and evanescent, it passes into air, and dissolves; so that you perceive its very largeness to have been fatal to it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:241
verses.text: For the higher it ascends, the farther it is extended, the wider the circumference which it spreads itself over, the thinner, and the more rare and wasting and evanescent does it become.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:242
verses.text: "But the enemies of the Lord, when they shall begin to glory, and to be lifted up, immediately shall consume away utterly even as the smoke".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:243
verses.text: Of such as these was it said, "As Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the Truth; men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:244
verses.text: But how is it that they resist the Truth, except by the vain inflation of their swelling pride, while they raise themselves up on high, as if great and righteous persons, though on the point of passing away into empty air? But what saith he of them? As if speaking of smoke, he says, "They shall proceed no farther, for their folly shall be manifest unto all men, even as theirs also was".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:245
verses.text: "The wicked borroweth, and payeth not again".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:246
verses.text: He receiveth, and will not repay.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:247
verses.text: What is it he will not repay? Thanksgiving.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:248
verses.text: For what is it that God would have of thee, what doth He require of thee, except that He may do thee good? And how great are the benefits which the sinner hath received, and which he will not repay! He hath received the gift of being; he hath received the gift of being a man; and of a being highly distinguished above the brutes; he hath received the form of a body, and the distinction of the senses in the body, eyes for seeing, ears for hearing, the nostrils for smelling, the palate for tasting, the hands for touching, and the feet for walking; and even the very health and soundness of the body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:249
verses.text: But up to this point we have these things in common even with the brute; he hath received yet more than this; a mind capable of understanding, capable of Truth, capable of distinguishing right from wrong; capable of seeking after, of longing for, its Creator, of praising Him, and fixing itself upon Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:250
verses.text: All this the wicked man hath received as well as others; but by not living well, he fails to repay that which he owes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:251
verses.text: Thus it is, "the wicked borroweth, and payeth not again:" he will not requite Him from whom he hath received; he will not return thanks; nay, he will even render evil for good, blasphemies, murmuring against God, indignation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:252
verses.text: Thus it is that he "borroweth, and payeth not again; but the righteous showeth mercy, and lendeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:253
verses.text: The one therefore hath nothing; the other hath.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:254
verses.text: See, on the one side, destitution: see, on the other, wealth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:255
verses.text: The one receiveth and "payeth not again:" the "other showeth mercy, and lendeth:" and he hath more than enough.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:256
verses.text: What if he is poor? Even so he is rich; do you but look at his riches with the eyes of Religion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:257
verses.text: For thou lookest at the empty chest; but dost not look at the conscience, that is full of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:258
verses.text: "For such as shall bless Him shall inherit the land" , that is, they shall possess that righteous One: the only One who both is truly righteous, and maketh righteous: who both was poor in this world, and brought great riches to it, wherewith to make those rich whom He found poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:259
verses.text: For it is He who hath enriched the hearts of the poor with the Holy Spirit; and having emptied out their souls by confession of sins, hath filled them with the richness of righteousness: He who was able to enrich the fisherman, who, by forsaking his nets, spurned what he possessed already, but sought to draw up what he possessed not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:260
verses.text: For "God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:261
verses.text: And it was not by an orator that He gained to Himself the fisherman; but by the fisherman that He gained to Himself the orator; by the fisherman that He gained the Senator; by the fisherman that He gained the Emperor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:262
verses.text: For "such as shall bless Him shall inherit the land;" they shall be fellow-heirs with Him, in that "land of the living," of which it is said in another Psalm, "Thou art my hope, my portion in the land of the living".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:263
verses.text: Observe what follows: "The steps of a good man are ordered by the Lord; and he delighteth in His way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:264
verses.text: That man may himself "delight in the Lord's way," his steps are ordered by the Lord Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:265
verses.text: For if the Lord did not order the steps of man, so crooked are they naturally, that they would always be going through crooked paths, and by pursuing crooked ways, would be unable to return again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:266
verses.text: He however came, and called us, and redeemed us, and shed His blood; He hath given this ransom; He hath done this good, and suffered these evils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:267
verses.text: Consider Him in what He hath done, He is God! Consider Him in what He hath suffered, He is Man! Who is that God-Man? Hadst not thou, O man, forsaken God, God would not have been made Man for thee! For that was too little for thee to requite, or for Him to bestow, that He had made thee man; unless He Himself should become Man for thee also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:268
verses.text: For it is He Himself that hath "ordered our steps;" that we should "delight in His way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:269
verses.text: Now if man were to be through the whole of his life in toil, and in sufferings, in pain, in tortures, in prison, in scourgings, in hunger, and in thirst, every day and every hour through the whole length of life, to the period of old age, yet the whole life of man is but a few days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:270
verses.text: That labour being over, there is to come the Eternal Kingdom; there is to come happiness without end; there is to come equality with the Angels; there is to come Christ's inheritance, and Christ, our "joint Heir," is to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:271
verses.text: How great is the labour, for which thou receivest so great a recompense? The Veterans who serve in the wars, and move in the midst of wounds for so many years, enter upon the military service from their youth, and quit it in old age: and to obtain a few days of repose in their old age, when age itself begins to weigh down those whom the wars do not break down, how great hardships do they endure; what marches, what frosts, what burning suns; what privations, what wounds, and what dangers! And while suffering all these things, they fix their thoughts on nothing but those few days of repose in old age, at which they know not whether they will ever arrive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:272
verses.text: Thus it is, the "steps of a good man are ordered by the Lord, and he delighteth in His way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:273
verses.text: This is the point with which I commenced.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:274
verses.text: If thou dost "delight in the way" of Christ, and art truly a Christian (for he is a Christian indeed who does not despise the way of Christ, but "delighteth in" following Christ's "way" through His sufferings), do not thou go by any other way than that by which He Himself hath also gone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:275
verses.text: It appears painful, but it is the very way of safety; another perhaps is delightful, but it is full of robbers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:276
verses.text: "And he delighteth in His way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:277
verses.text: "Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down; for the Lord upholdeth his hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:278
verses.text: See what it is "to delight in" Christ's "way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:279
verses.text: Should it happen that he suffers some tribulation; some forfeiture of honour, some affliction, some loss, some contumely, or all those other accidents incident to mankind frequently in this life, he sets the Lord before him, what kind of trials He endured! and, "though he fall he shall not be utterly cast down, for the Lord upholdeth his hand," because He has suffered before him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:280
verses.text: For what shouldest thou fear, O man, whose steps are ordered so, that thou shouldest "delight in the way of the Lord"? What shouldest thou fear? Pain? Christ was scourged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:281
verses.text: Shouldest thou fear contumelies? He was reproached with, "Thou hast a devil," who was Himself casting out the devils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:282
verses.text: Haply thou fearest faction, and the conspiracy of the wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:283
verses.text: Conspiracy was made against Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:284
verses.text: Thou canst not make clear the purity of thy conscience in some accusation, and sufferest wrong and violence, because false witnesses are listened to against thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:285
verses.text: False witness was borne against Him first, not only before His death, but also after His resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:286
verses.text: On the Third Part of the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:287
verses.text: "I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:288
verses.text: If it is spoken but in the person of one single individual, how long is the whole life of one man? And what is there wonderful in the circumstance, that a single man, fixed in some one part of the earth, should not, throughout the whole space of his life, being so short as man's life is, have ever seen "the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread," although he may have advanced from youth to age.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:289
verses.text: It is not anything worthy of marvel; for it might have happened, that before his lifetime there should have been some "righteous man seeking bread;" it might have happened, that there had been some one in some other part of the earth not where he himself was.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:290
verses.text: Hear too another thing, which makes an impression upon us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:291
verses.text: Any single one among you (look you) who has now grown old, may perhaps, when, looking back upon the past course of his life, he turns over in his thoughts the persons whom he has known, not find any instance of a righteous man begging bread, or of his seed begging bread, suggest itself to him; but nevertheless he turns to the inspired Scriptures, and finds that righteous Abraham was straitened, and suffered hunger in his own country, and left that land for another; he finds too that the son of the very same man, Isaac, removed to other countries in search of bread, for the same cause of hunger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:292
verses.text: And how will it be true to say, "I have never seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread"? And if he finds this true in the duration of his own life, he finds it is otherwise in the inspired writings, which are more trustworthy than human life is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:293
verses.text: What are we to do then? Let us be seconded by your pious attention, so that we may discern the purpose of God in these verses of the Psalm, what it is He would have us understand by them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:294
verses.text: For there is a fear, lest any unstable person, not capable of understanding the Scriptures spiritually, should appeal to human instances, and should observe the virtuous servants of God to be sometimes in some necessity, and in want, so as to be compelled to beg bread: should particularly call to mind the Apostle Paul, who says, "In hunger and thirst; in cold and nakedness;" and should stumble thereat, saying to himself, "Is that certainly true which I have been singing? Is that certainly true, which I have been sounding forth in so devout a voice, standing in church? 'I have never seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:295
verses.text: '" Lest he should say in his heart, "Scripture deceives us;" and all his limbs should be paralyzed to good works: and when those limbs within him, those limbs of the inner man, shall have been paralyzed (which is the more fearful paralysis), he should henceforth leave off from good works, and say to himself, "Wherefore do I do good works? Wherefore do I break my bread to the hungry, and clothe the naked, and take home to mine house him who hath no shelter, putting faith in that which is written? 'I have never seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread;' whereas I see so many persons who live virtuously, yet for the most part suffering from hunger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:296
verses.text: But if perhaps I am in error in thinking the man who is living well, and the man who is living ill, to be both of them living well, and if God knows him to be otherwise; that is, knows him, whom I think just, to be unjust, what am I to make of Abraham's case, who is commended by Scripture itself as a righteous person? What am I to make of the Apostle Paul, who says, 'Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:297
verses.text: ' What? that I should myself be in evils such as he endured, 'In hunger and thirst, in cold and nakedness'?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:298
verses.text: Whilst therefore he thus thinks, and whilst his limbs are paralyzed to the power of good works, can we, my brethren, as it were, lift up the sick of the palsy; and, as it were, "lay open the roof" of this Scripture, and let him down before the Lord For you observe that it is obscure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:299
verses.text: If obscure therefore, it is covered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:300
verses.text: And I behold a certain patient paralytic in mind, and I see this roof, and am convinced that Christ is concealed beneath the roof.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:301
verses.text: Let me, as far as I am able, do that which was praised in those who opened the roof, and let down the sick of the palsy before Christ; that He might say unto him, "Son, be of good cheer, thy sins be forgiven thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:302
verses.text: For it was so that He made the inner man whole of his palsy, by loosing his sins, by binding fast his faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:303
verses.text: But who is "the righteous" man, who "hath never been seen forsaken, nor his seed begging bread"? If you understand what is meant by "bread," you understand who is meant by him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:304
verses.text: For the "bread" is the Word of God, which never departs from the righteous man's mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:305
verses.text: See now if "holy meditation doth 'keep thee'" in the rumination of this bread, then "hast thou never seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:306
verses.text: "He is always merciful, and lendeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:307
verses.text: "Foeneratur" is used in Latin indeed, both for him who lendeth, and for him who borroweth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:308
verses.text: But in this passage the meaning is more plain, if we express it by "foenerat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:309
verses.text: What matters it to us, what the grammarians please to rule? It were better for us to be guilty of a barbarism, so that ye understand, than that in our propriety of speech ye be left unprovided.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:310
verses.text: Therefore, that "righteous man is all day merciful, and (foenerat) lendeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:311
verses.text: Let not the lenders of money on usury, however, rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:312
verses.text: For we find it is a particular kind of lender that is spoken of, as it was a particular kind of bread; that we may, in all passages, "remove the roof," and find our way to Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:313
verses.text: I would not have you be lenders of money on usury; and I would not have you be such for this reason, because God would not have you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:314
verses.text: Whence does it appear that God would not have it so? It is said in another place, "He that putteth not out his money to usury".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:315
verses.text: And how detestable, odious, and execrable a thing it is, I believe that even usurers themselves know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:316
verses.text: Again, on the other hand, I myself, nay rather our God Himself bids thee be an usurer, and says to thee, "Lend unto God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:317
verses.text: If thou lendest to man, hast thou hope? and shalt thou not have hope, if thou lendest to God? If thou hast lent thy money on usury to man, that is, if thou hast given the loan of thy money to one, from whom thou dost expect to receive something more than thou hast given, not in money only, but anything, whether it be wheat, or wine, or oil, or whatever else you please, if you expect to receive more than you have given, you are an usurer, and in this particular are not deserving of praise, but of censure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:318
verses.text: "What then," you say, "am I to do, that I may 'lend' profitably?" Consider what the usurer does.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:319
verses.text: He undoubtedly desires to give a less sum, and to receive a larger; do thou this also; give thou a little, receive much.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:320
verses.text: See how thy principal grows, and increases! Give "things temporal," receive "things eternal:" give earth, receive heaven! And perhaps thou wouldest say, "To whom shall I give them?" The self-same Lord, who bade thee not lend on usury, comes forward as the Person to whom thou shouldest lend on usury! Hear from Scripture in what way thou mayest "lend unto the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:321
verses.text: "He that hath pity on the poor, lendeth unto the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:322
verses.text: For the Lord wanteth not aught of thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:323
verses.text: But thou hast one who needs somewhat of thee: thou extendest it to him; he receives it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:324
verses.text: For the poor hath nothing to return to thee, and yet he would himself fain requite thee, and finds nothing wherewith to do it: all that remains in his power is the good-will that desires to pray for thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:325
verses.text: Now when the poor man prays for thee, he, as it were, says unto God, "Lord, I have borrowed this; be Thou surety for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:326
verses.text: Then, though you have no bond on the poor man to compel his repayment, yet you have on a sponsible security.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:327
verses.text: See, God from His own Scriptures saith unto thee; "Give it, and fear not; I repay it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:328
verses.text: It is to Me thou givest it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:329
verses.text: In what way do those who make themselves sureties for others, express themselves? What is it that they say? "I repay it: I take it upon myself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:330
verses.text: It is to me you are giving it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:331
verses.text: Do we then suppose that God also says this, "I take it on Myself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:332
verses.text: It is unto me thou givest it"? Assuredly, if Christ be God, of which there is no doubt, He hath Himself said, "I was an hungred, and ye gave Me meat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:333
verses.text: And when they said unto Him, "When saw we Thee hungry?" that He might show Himself to be the Surety for the poor, that He answers for all His members, that He is the Head, they the members, and that when the members receive, the Head receiveth also; He says, "Inasmuch as ye have done it to one of the least of these that belong to Me, ye have done it unto Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:334
verses.text: Come, thou covetous usurer, consider what thou hast given; consider what thou art to receive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:335
verses.text: Hadst thou given a small sum of money, and he to whom thou hadst given it were to give thee for that small sum a great villa, worth incomparably more money than thou hadst given, how great thanks wouldest thou render, with how great joy wouldest thou be transported! Hear what possession He to whom thou hast been lending bestows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:336
verses.text: "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive" —What? The same that they have given? God forbid! What you gave were earthly things, which, if you had not given them, would have become corrupted on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:337
verses.text: For what could you have made of them, if you had not given them? That which on earth would have been lost, has been preserved in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:338
verses.text: Therefore what we are to receive is that which hath been preserved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:339
verses.text: It is thy desert that hath been preserved, thy desert hath been made thy treasure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:340
verses.text: For consider what it is that thou art to receive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:341
verses.text: Receive—"the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:342
verses.text: On the other hand, what shall be their sentence, who would not "lend"? "Go ye into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:343
verses.text: And what is the kingdom which we receive called? Consider what follows: "And these shall go into everlasting burning; but the righteous into life eternal".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:344
verses.text: Make interest for this; purchase this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:345
verses.text: Give your money on usury to earn this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:346
verses.text: You have Christ throned in heaven, begging on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:347
verses.text: We have discovered in what way the righteous lendeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:348
verses.text: "He is alway merciful, and lendeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:349
verses.text: "And his seed is blessed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:350
verses.text: Here too let not any carnal notion suggest itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:351
verses.text: We see many of the sons of the righteous dying of hunger; in what sense then will his seed be blessed? His seed is that which remains of him afterwards; that wherewith he soweth here, and will hereafter reap.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:352
verses.text: For the Apostle says, "Let us not be weary in well-doing; for in due season we shall reap if we faint not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:353
verses.text: As we have therefore time," he says, "let us do good unto all men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:354
verses.text: This is that "seed" of thine which shall "be blessed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:355
verses.text: You commit it to the earth, and gather ever so much more; and dost thou lose it in committing it to Christ? See it expressly termed "seed" by the Apostle, when he was speaking of alms.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:356
verses.text: For this he saith; "He which soweth sparingly, shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth in blessings, shall also reap in blessings".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:357
verses.text: Observe therefore what follows, and be not slothful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:358
verses.text: "Depart from evil, and do good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:359
verses.text: Do not think it to be enough for thee to do, if thou dost not strip the man who is already clothed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:360
verses.text: For in not stripping the man who is already clothed, thou hast indeed "departed from evil:" but do not be barren, and wither.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:361
verses.text: So choose not to strip the man who is clothed already, as to clothe the naked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:362
verses.text: For this is to "depart from evil, and to do good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:363
verses.text: And you will say, "What advantage am I to derive from it?" He to whom thou lendest has already assured thee of what He will give thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:364
verses.text: He will give thee everlasting life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:365
verses.text: Give to Him, and fear not! Hear too what follows: "Depart from evil, and do good, and dwell for evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:366
verses.text: And think not when thou givest that no one sees thee, or that God forsakes thee, when haply after thou hast given to the poor, and some loss, or some sorrow for the property thou hast lost, should follow, and thou shouldest say to thyself, "What hath it profited me to have done good works? I believe God doth not love the men who do good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:367
verses.text: Whence comes that buzz, that subdued murmur among you, except that those expressions are very common? Each one of you at this present moment recognises these expressions, either in his own lips, or on those of his friend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:368
verses.text: May God destroy them; may He root out the thorns from His field; may He plant "the good seed," and "the tree bearing fruit"! For wherefore art thou afflicted, O man, that thou hast given some things away to the poor, and hast lost certain other things? Seest thou not that it is what thou hast not given, that thou hast lost? Wherefore dost thou not attend to the voice of thy God? Where is thy faith? wherefore is it so fast asleep? Wake it up in thy heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:369
verses.text: Consider what the Lord Himself said unto thee, while exhorting thee to good works of this kind: "Provide yourselves bags which wax not old; a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:370
verses.text: Call this to mind therefore when you are lamenting over a loss.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:371
verses.text: Wherefore dost thou lament, thou fool of little mind, or rather of unsound mind? Wherefore didst thou lose it, except that thou didst not lend it to Me? Wherefore didst thou lose it? Who has carried it off? Thou wilt answer, "A thief".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:372
verses.text: Was it not this, that I forewarned thee of? that thou shouldest not lay it up where the thief could approach? If then he who has lost anything, grieves, let him grieve for this, that he did not lay it up there, whence it could not be lost.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:373
verses.text: "For the Lord loveth judgment, and forsaketh not His Saints".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:374
verses.text: When the Saints suffer affliction, think not that God doth not judge, or doth not judge righteously.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:375
verses.text: Will He, who warns thee to judge righteously, Himself judge unrighteously? He "loveth judgment, and forsaketh not His Saints".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:376
verses.text: But (think) how the "life" of the Saints is "hid with Him," in such a manner, that who now suffer trouble on earth, like trees in the winter-time, having no fruit and leaves, when He, like a newly-risen sun, shall have appeared, that which before was living in their root, will show itself forth in fruits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:377
verses.text: He does then "love judgment, and doth not forsake His Saints".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:378
verses.text: "But the unrighteous shall be punished; the seed of the wicked shall be cut off".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:379
verses.text: Just as the "seed of the" other "shall be blessed," so shall the "seed of the wicked be cut off".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:380
verses.text: For the "seed" of the wicked is the works of the wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:381
verses.text: For again, on the other hand, we find the son of the wicked man flourish in the world, and sometimes become righteous, and flourish in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:382
verses.text: Be careful therefore how thou takest it; that thou mayest remove the covering, and make thy way to Christ Do not take the text in a carnal sense; for thou wilt be deceived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:383
verses.text: But "the seed of the wicked"—all the works of the wicked—"will be cut off:" they shall have no fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:384
verses.text: For they are effective indeed for a short time; afterwards they shall seek for them, and shall not find the reward of that which they have wrought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:385
verses.text: For it is the expression of those who lose what they have wrought, that text which says, "What hath pride profited us, or what good hath riches with our vaunting brought us? All those things are passed away like a shadow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:386
verses.text: "The seed of the wicked," then, "shall be cut off".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:387
verses.text: "The righteous shall inherit the land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:388
verses.text: Here again let not covetousness steal on thee, nor promise thee some great estate; hope not to find there, what you are commanded to despise in this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:389
verses.text: That "land" in the text, is a certain "land of the living," the kingdom of the Saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:390
verses.text: Whence it is said: "Thou art my hope, my portion in the land of the living".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:391
verses.text: For if thy life too is the same life as that there spoken of, think what sort of "land" thou art about to inherit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:392
verses.text: That is "the land of the living;" this the land of those who are about to die: to receive again, when dead, those whom it nourished when living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:393
verses.text: Such then as is that land, such shall the life itself be also: if the life be for ever, "the land" also is to be thine "for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:394
verses.text: And how is "the land" to be thine "for ever"?  "And they shall dwell therein" (it says) "for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:395
verses.text: It must therefore be another land, where "they are to dwell therein for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:396
verses.text: For of this land (of this earth) it is said, "Heaven and earth shall pass away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:397
verses.text: "The mouth of the righteous speaketh wisdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:398
verses.text: See here is that "bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:399
verses.text: Observe with what satisfaction this righteous man feedeth upon it; how he turns wisdom over and over in his mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:400
verses.text: "And his tongue talketh of judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:401
verses.text: "The law of his God is in his heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:402
verses.text: Lest haply thou shouldest think him to have that on his lips, which he hath not in his heart, lest thou shouldest reckon him among those of whom it is said, "This people honour Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:403
verses.text: And of what use is this to him?  "And none of his steps shall slide".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:404
verses.text: The "word of God in the heart" frees from the snare; the "word of God in the heart" delivers from the evil way; "the word of God in the heart" delivers from "the slippery place".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:405
verses.text: He is with thee, Whose word departeth not from thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:406
verses.text: Now what evil doth he suffer, whom God keepeth? Thou settest a watchman in thy vineyard, and feelest secure from thieves; and that watchman may sleep, and may himself fall, and may admit a thief.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:407
verses.text: But "He who keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:408
verses.text: "The law of his God is in his heart, and none of his steps shall slide".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:409
verses.text: Let him therefore live free from fear; let him live free from fear even in the midst of the wicked; free from fear even in the midst of the ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:410
verses.text: For what evil can the ungodly or unrighteous man do to the righteous? Lo! see what follows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:411
verses.text: "The wicked watcheth the righteous, and seeketh to slay him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:412
verses.text: For he says, what it was foretold in the book of Wisdom that he should say, "He is grievous unto us, even to behold; for his life is not like other men's".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:413
verses.text: Therefore he "seeks to slay him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:414
verses.text: What? Doth the Lord, who keepeth him, who dwelleth with him, who departeth not from his lips, from his heart, doth He forsake him? What then becomes of what was said before: "And He forsaketh not His Saints"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:415
verses.text: "The wicked therefore watcheth the righteous, and seeketh to slay him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:416
verses.text: But the Lord will not leave him in his hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:417
verses.text: Wherefore then did He leave the Martyrs in the hands of the ungodly? Wherefore did they do unto them "whatsoever they would"? Some they slew with the sword; some they crucified; some they delivered to the beasts; some they burnt by fire; others they led about in chains, till wasted out by a long protracted decay.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:418
verses.text: Assuredly "the Lord forsaketh not His Saints".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:419
verses.text: He will not "leave him in his hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:420
verses.text: Lastly, wherefore did He leave His own Son in "the hands of the ungodly"? Here also, if thou wouldest have all the limbs of thy inner man made strong, remove the covering of the roof, and find thy way to the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:421
verses.text: Hear what another Scripture, foreseeing our Lord's future suffering at the hands of the ungodly, saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:422
verses.text: What saith it? "The earth is given into the hands of the wicked".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:423
verses.text: What is meant by "earth" being "given into the hands of the ungodly"? The delivering of the flesh into the hands of the persecutors.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:424
verses.text: But God did not leave "His righteous One" there: from the flesh, which was taken captive, He leads forth the soul unconquered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:425
verses.text: "The Lord will not leave him in his hand, nor condemn him when there shall be judgment for him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:426
verses.text: Some copies have it, "and when He shall judge him, there shall be judgment for him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:427
verses.text: "For him," however, means when sentence is passed upon him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:428
verses.text: For we can express ourselves so as to say to a person, "Judge for me," i-e: "hear my cause".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:429
verses.text: When therefore God shall begin to hear the cause of His righteous servant, since "we must all" be presented "before the tribunal of Christ," and stand before it to receive every one "the things he hath done in this body," whether good or evil, when therefore he shall have come to that Judgment, He will not condemn him; though he may seem to be condemned in this present life by man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:430
verses.text: Even though the Proconsul may have passed sentence on Cyprian, yet the earthly seat of judgment is one thing, the heavenly tribunal is another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:431
verses.text: From the inferior tribunal he receives sentence of death; from the superior one a crown, "Nor will He condemn him when there shall be judgment for him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:432
verses.text: "Wait on the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:433
verses.text: And while I am waiting upon Him, what am I to do?—"and keep His ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:434
verses.text: And if I keep them, what am I to receive? "And He shall exalt thee to inherit the land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:435
verses.text: "What land"? Once more let not any estate suggest itself to your mind:—the land of which it is said, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:436
verses.text: What of those who have troubled us, in the midst of whom we have groaned, whose scandals we have patiently endured, for whom, while they were raging against us, we have prayed in vain? What will become of them? What follows? "When the wicked are cut off, thou shall see it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:437
verses.text: "I have seen the ungodly lifted up on high, and rising above the cedars of Libanus".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:438
verses.text: And suppose him to be "lifted up on high;" suppose him to be towering above the "rest;" what follows?  "I passed by, and, lo, he was not! I sought him, and his place could nowhere be found!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:439
verses.text: Why was he "no more, and his place nowhere to be found"? Because thou hast "passed by".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:440
verses.text: But if thou art yet carnally-minded, and that earthly prosperity appears to thee to be true happiness, thou hast not yet "passed by" him; thou art either his fellow, or thou art below him; go on, and pass him; and when thou hast made progress, and hast passed by him, thou observest him by the eye of faith; thou seest his end, thou sayest to thyself, "Lo! he who so swelled before, is not!" just as if it were some smoke that thou wert passing near to.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:441
verses.text: For this too was said above in this very Psalm, "They shall consume and fade away as the smoke".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:442
verses.text: "Keep innocency" ; keep it even as thou usedst to keep thy purse, when thou wert covetous; even as thou usedst to hold fast that purse, that it might not be snatched from thy grasp by the thief, even so "keep innocency," lest that be snatched from thy grasp by the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:443
verses.text: Be that thy sure inheritance, of which the rich and the poor may both be sure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:444
verses.text: "Keep innocency".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:445
verses.text: What doth it profit thee to gain gold, and to lose innocence?  "Keep innocency, and take heed unto the thing which is right".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:446
verses.text: Keep thou thine eyes "right," that thou mayest see "the thing which is right;" not perverted, wherewith thou lookest upon the wicked; not distorted, so that God should appear to thee distorted and wrong, in that He favours the wicked, and afflicts the faithful with persecutions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:447
verses.text: Dost thou not observe how distorted thy vision is? Set right thine eyes, and "behold the thing that is right".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:448
verses.text: What "thing that is right"? Take no heed of things present.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:449
verses.text: And what wilt thou see?  "For there is a remainder for the man that maketh peace".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:450
verses.text: What is meant by "there is a remainder"? When thou art dead, thou shalt not be dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:451
verses.text: This is the meaning of "there is a remainder".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:452
verses.text: He will still have something remaining to him, even after this life, that is to say, that "seed," which "shall be blessed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:453
verses.text: Whence our Lord saith, "He that believeth on Me, though he die, yet shall he live;"—"seeing there is a remainder for the man that maketh peace".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:454
verses.text: "But the transgressors shall be destroyed in the self-same thing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:455
verses.text: What is meant by, "in the self-same thing"? It means for ever: or all together in one and the same destruction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:456
verses.text: "The remainder of the wicked shall be cut off".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:457
verses.text: Now there is "(a remainder) for the man that maketh peace:" they therefore who are not peace-makers are ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:458
verses.text: For, "Blessed are the peace-makers: for they shall be called the children of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:459
verses.text: "But the salvation of the righteous is of the Lord, and He is their strength in the time of trouble".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:460
verses.text: "And the Lord shall help them, and deliver them; He shall deliver them from the sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 37:461
verses.text: At present therefore let the righteous bear with the sinner; let the wheat bear with the tares; let the grain bear with the chaff: for the time of separation will come, and the good seed shall be set apart from that which is to be consumed with fire The one will be consigned to the garner, the other to "everlasting burning;" for it was for this reason that the just and the unjust were at the first together; that the one should lay a stumbling-block, that the other should be proved; that afterwards the one should be condemned, the other receive a crown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:1
verses.text: Psalm XXXVIII  A psalm to David himself, on the remembrance of the Sabbath.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:2
verses.text: What doth this recollection of the Sabbath mean? What is this Sabbath? For it is w ith groaning that he "calls it to recollection".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:3
verses.text: You have both heard already when the Psalm was read, and you will now hear it when we shall go over it, how great is his groaning, his mourning, his tears, his misery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:4
verses.text: But happy he who is wretched after this manner! Whence the Lord also in the Gospel called some who mourn blessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:5
verses.text: "How should he be blessed if he is a mourner? How blessed, if he is miserable?" Nay rather, he would be miserable, if he were not a mourner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:6
verses.text: Such an one then let us understand here too, calling the Sabbath to remembrance (viz.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:7
verses.text: ), some mourner or other: and would that we were ourselves that "some one or other"! For there is here some person sorrowing, groaning, mourning, calling the Sabbath to remembrance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:8
verses.text: The Sabbath is rest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:9
verses.text: Doubtless he was in some disquietude, who with groaning was calling the Sabbath to remembrance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:10
verses.text: "O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine indignation; neither chasten me in Thy hot displeasure".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:11
verses.text: For it will be that some shall be chastened in God's "hot displeasure," and rebuked in His "indignation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:12
verses.text: And haply not all who are "rebuked" will be "chastened;" yet are there some that are to be saved in the chastening So it is to be indeed, because it is called "chastening," but yet it shall be "so as by fire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:13
verses.text: But there are to be some who will be "rebuked," and will not be "corrected".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:14
verses.text: For he will at all events "rebuke" those to whom He will say, "I was an hungred, and ye gave me no meat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:15
verses.text: "Neither chasten me in Thy hot displeasure;" so that Thou mayest cleanse me in this life, and make me such, that I may after that stand in no need of the cleansing fire, for those "who are to be saved, yet so as by fire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:16
verses.text: Why? Why, but because they "build upon the foundation, wood, stubble, and hay".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:17
verses.text: Now they should build on it, "gold, silver, and precious stones;" and should have nothing to fear from either fire: not only that which is to consume the ungodly for ever, but also that which is to purge those who are to escape through the fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:18
verses.text: For it is said, "he himself shall be saved, yet so as by fire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:19
verses.text: And because it is said, "he shall be saved," that fire is thought lightly of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:20
verses.text: For all that, though we should be "saved by fire," yet will that fire be more grievous than anything that man can suffer in this life whatsoever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:21
verses.text: Now on what ground does this person pray that he may not be "rebuked in indignation, nor chastened in hot displeasure"? (He speaks) as if he would say unto God, "Since the things which I already suffer are many in number, I pray Thee let them suffice;" and he begins to enumerate them, by way of satisfying God; offering what he suffers now, that he may not have to suffer worse evils hereafter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:22
verses.text: "For Thine arrows stick fast in me, and Thy hand presseth me sore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:23
verses.text: "There is no soundness in my flesh, from the face of Thine anger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:24
verses.text: He has now begun telling these evils, which he is suffering here: and yet even this already was from the wrath of the Lord, because it was of the vengeance of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:25
verses.text: "Of what vengeance?" That which He took upon Adam.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:26
verses.text: For think not that punishment was not inflicted upon him, or that God had said to no purpose, "Thou shalt surely die;" or that we suffer anything in this life, except from that death which we earned by the original sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:27
verses.text: Whence then do His "arrows stick fast in" him? The very punishment, the very vengeance, and haply the pains both of mind and of body, which it is necessary for us to suffer here, these he describes by these self-same "arrows".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:28
verses.text: For of these arrows holy Job also made mention, and said that the arrows of the Lord stuck fast in him, whilst he was labouring under those pains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:29
verses.text: We are used, however, to call God's words also arrows; but could he grieve that he should be struck by these? The words of God are arrows, as it were, that inflame love, not pain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:30
verses.text: We may then understand the "arrows sticking fast," thus: Thy words are fixed fast in my heart; and by those words themselves is it come to pass, that I "called the Sabbath to remembrance:" and that very remembrance of the Sabbath, and the non-possession of it at present, prevents me from rejoicing at present; and causes me to acknowledge that there "is neither health in my very flesh," neither ought it to be so called when I compare this sort of soundness to that soundness which I am to possess in the everlasting rest; where "this corruptible shall put on incorruption, and this mortal shall put on immortality,"  and see that in comparison with that soundness this present kind is but sickness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:31
verses.text: "Neither is there any rest in my bones, from the face of my sin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:32
verses.text: It is commonly enquired, of what person this is the speech; and some understand it to be Christ's, on account of some things which are here said of the Passion of Christ; to which we shall shortly come; and which we ourselves shall acknowledge to be spoken of His Passion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:33
verses.text: But how could He who had no sin, say, "There is no rest in my bones, from the face of my sin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:34
verses.text: For if we were to say that they are not the words of Christ, those words, "My God, My God, why hast Thou forsaken Me?" will also not be the words of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:35
verses.text: For there too you have, "My God, My God, why hast Thou forsaken Me?" "The words of mine offences are far from my health".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:36
verses.text: Just as here you have, "from the face of my sins," so there also you have, "the words of my offences".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:37
verses.text: And if Christ is, for a ll that, without "sin," and without "offences," we begin to think those words  in the Psalm also not to be His.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:38
verses.text: And it is exceedingly harsh and inconsistent that that Psalm should not relate to Christ, where we have His Passion as clearly laid open as if it were being read to us out of the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:39
verses.text: For there we have, "They parted My garments among th em, and cast lots upon My vesture".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:40
verses.text: Why should I mention that the first verse of that Psalm was pronounced by the Lord Himself while hanging on the Cross, with His own mouth, saying, "My God, My God, why hast  Thou forsaken Me?" What did He mean to be inferred from it, but that the whole of that Psalm relates to Him, seeing He Himself, the Head of His Body, pronounced it in His own Person? Now when it goes on to say, "the words of mine offences," it is beyond a doubt that they are the words of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:41
verses.text: Whence then come "the sins," but from the Body, which is the Church? Because both the Head and the Body of Christ are speaking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:42
verses.text: Why do they speak as if one person only? Because "they twain," as He hath said, "shall be one flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:43
verses.text: "This" (says the Apostle) "is a great mystery; but I speak concerning Christ and the Church".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:44
verses.text: For why should He not say, "my sins," who said, "I was an hungred, and ye gave Me no meat; I was thirsty, and ye gave Me no drink; I was a stranger, and ye took Me not in.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:45
verses.text: I was sick and in prison, and ye visited Me not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:46
verses.text: Assuredly the Lord was not in prison.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:47
verses.text: Why should He not say this, to whom when it was said, "When saw we Thee a hungred, and athirst, or in prison; and did not minister unto Thee?" He replied, that He spake thus in the person of His Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:48
verses.text: "Inasmuch as ye did it not unto one of the least of Mine, ye did it not unto Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:49
verses.text: Why should He not say, "from the face of my sins," who said to Saul, "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou Me," who, however, being in Heaven, now suffered from no persecutors? But just as, in that passage, the Head spake for the Body, so here too the Head speaks the words of the Body; whilst you hear at the same time the accents of the Head Itself also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:50
verses.text: Yet do not either, when you hear the voice of the Body, separate the Head from it; nor the Body, when you hear the voice of the Head: because "they are no more twain, but one flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:51
verses.text: "There is no soundness in my flesh from the face of thine anger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:52
verses.text: But perhaps God is unjustly angry with thee, O Adam; unjustly angry with thee, O son of man; because now brought to acknowledge that thy punishment, now that thou art a man that hath been placed in Christ's Body, thou hast said, "There is no soundness in my flesh from the face of Thine anger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:53
verses.text: Declare the justice of God's anger: lest thou shouldest seem to be excusing thyself, and accusing Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:54
verses.text: Go on to tell whence the "anger" of the Lord proceeds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:55
verses.text: "There is no soundness in my flesh from the face of Thine anger; neither is there any rest in my bones".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:56
verses.text: He repeats what he said before, "There is no soundness in my flesh;" for, "There is no rest in my bones," is equivalent to this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:57
verses.text: He does not however repeat "from the face of Thine anger;" but states the cause of the anger of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:58
verses.text: "There is no rest in my bones from the face of my sins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:59
verses.text: "For mine iniquities have lifted up my head; and are like a heavy burden too heavy for me to bear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:60
verses.text: Here too he has placed the cause first, and the effect afterwards.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:61
verses.text: What consequence followed, and from what cause, he has told us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:62
verses.text: "Mine iniquities have lift up mine head".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:63
verses.text: For no one is proud but the unrighteous man, whose head is lifted up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:64
verses.text: He is "lifted up," whose "head is lifted up on high" against God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:65
verses.text: You heard when the lesson of the Book of Ecclesiasticus was read: "The beginning of pride is when a man departeth from God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:66
verses.text: He who was the first to refuse to listen to the Commandment, "his head iniquity lifted up" against God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:67
verses.text: And because his iniquities have lifted up his head, what hath God done unto him? They are "like a heavy burden, too heavy for me to bear"! It is the part of levity to lift up the head, just as if he who lifts up his head had nothing to carry.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:68
verses.text: Since therefore that which admits of being lifted up is light, it receives a weight by which it may be weighed down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:69
verses.text: For "his mischief returns upon his own head, and his violent dealing comes down upon his own pate".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:70
verses.text: "They are like a heavy burden, too heavy for me to bear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:71
verses.text: "My wounds stink and are corrupt".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:72
verses.text: Now he who has wounds is not perfectly sound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:73
verses.text: Add to this, that the wounds "stink and are corrupt".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:74
verses.text: Wherefore do they "stink"? Because they are "corrupt:" now in what way this is explained in reference to human life, who doth not understand? Let a man but have his soul's sense of smelling sound, he perceives how foully sins stink.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:75
verses.text: The contrary to which stink of sin, is that savour of which the Apostle says, "We are the sweet savour of Christ unto God, in every place, unto them which be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:76
verses.text: But whence is this, except from hope? Whence is this, but from our "calling the Sabbath to remembrance"? For it is a different thing that we mourn over in this life, from that which we anticipate in the other.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:77
verses.text: That which we mourn over is stench, that which we reckon upon is fragrance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:78
verses.text: Were there not therefore such a perfume as that to invite us, we should never call the Sabbath to remembrance But since, by the Spirit, we have such a perfume, as to say to our Betrothed, "Because of the savour of Thy good ointments we will run after Thee;" we turn our senses away from our own unsavourinesses, and turning ourselves to Him, we gain some little breathing-time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:79
verses.text: But indeed, unless our evil deeds also did smell rank in our nostrils, we should never confess with those groans, "My wounds stink and are corrupt".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:80
verses.text: And wherefore? "from the face of my foolishness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:81
verses.text: From the same cause that he said before, "from the face of my sins;" from that same cause he now says, "from the face of my foolishness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:82
verses.text: "I am troubled, I am bowed down even unto the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:83
verses.text: Wherefore was he "bowed down"? Because he had been "lifted up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:84
verses.text: If thou art "humble, thou shalt be exalted;" if thou exaltest thyself, thou shalt be "bowed down;" for God will be at no loss to find a weight wherewith to bow thee down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:85
verses.text: Let him groan on these things; that he may receive the other; let him "call the Sabbath to remembrance," that he may deserve to arrive at it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:86
verses.text: For that which the Jews used to celebrate was but a sign.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:87
verses.text: Of what thing was it the sign? Of that which he calls to remembrance, who saith, "I am troubled, and am bowed down even unto the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:88
verses.text: What is meant by even "unto the end"? Even to death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:89
verses.text: "I go mourning all the day long".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:90
verses.text: "All day long," that is, "without intermission".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:91
verses.text: By "all the day long," he means, "all my life long".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:92
verses.text: But from what time hath he known it? From the time that he began to "call the Sabbath to remembrance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:93
verses.text: For so long as he "calls to remembrance" what he no longer possesses, wouldest thou not have him "go mourning"? "All the day long have I gone mourning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:94
verses.text: "For my soul is filled with illusions, and there is no soundness in my flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:95
verses.text: Where there is the whole man, there there is soul and flesh both.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:96
verses.text: The "soul is filled with illusions;" the flesh hath "no soundness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:97
verses.text: What does there remain that can give joy? Is it not meet that one should "go mourning"? "All the day long have I gone mourning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:98
verses.text: Let mourning be our portion, until our soul be divested of its illusions; and our body be clothed with soundness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:99
verses.text: For true soundness is no other than immortality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:100
verses.text: How great however are the soul's illusions, were I even to attempt to express, when would the time suffice me? For whose soul is not subject to them? There is a brief particular that I will remind you of, to show how our soul is filled with illusions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:101
verses.text: The presence of those illusions sometimes scarcely permits us to pray.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:102
verses.text: We know not how to think of material objects without images, and such as we do not wish, rush in upon the mind; and we wish to go from this one to that, and to quit that for another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:103
verses.text: And sometimes you wish to return to that which you were thinking of before, and to quit that which you are now thinking of; and a fresh one presents itself to you; you wish to call up again what you had forgotten; and it does not occur to you; and another comes instead which you would not have wished for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:104
verses.text: Where meanwhile was the one that you had forgotten? For why did it afterwards occur to you, when it had ceased to be sought after; whereas, while it was being sought for, innumerable others, which were not desired, presented themselves instead of it? I have stated a fact briefly; I have thrown out a kind of hint or suggestion to you, brethren, taking up which, you may yourselves suggest the rest to yourselves, and discover what it is to mourn over the "illusions" of our "soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:105
verses.text: He hath received therefore the punishment of illusion; he hath forfeited Truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:106
verses.text: For just as illusion is the soul's punishment, so is Truth its reward.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:107
verses.text: But when we were set in the midst of these illusions, the Truth Itself came to us, and found us overwhelmed by illusions, took upon Itself our flesh, or rather took flesh from us; that is, from the human race.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:108
verses.text: He manifested himself to the eyes of the Flesh, that He might "by faith" heal those to whom He was going to reveal the Truth hereafter, that Truth might be manifested to the now healed eye.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:109
verses.text: For He is Himself "the Truth," which He promised unto us at that time, when His Flesh was to be seen by the eye, that the foundation might be laid of that Faith, of which the Truth was to be the reward.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:110
verses.text: For it was not Himself that Christ showed forth on earth; but it was His Flesh that He showed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:111
verses.text: For had He showed Himself, the Jews would have seen and known Him; but had they "known Him, they would never have crucified the Lord of Glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:112
verses.text: But perhaps His disciples saw Him, when they said unto Him, "Show us the Father, and it sufficeth us;" and He, to show that it was not Himself that had been seen by them, added: "Have I been so long with you, and have ye not known Me, Philip? He that seeth Me, seeth the Father also".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:113
verses.text: If then they saw Christ, wherefore did they yet seek for the Father? For if it were Christ whom they saw, they would have seen the Father also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:114
verses.text: They did not therefore yet see Christ, who desired that the Father should be shown unto them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:115
verses.text: To prove that they did not yet see Him, hear that, in another place, He promised it by way of reward, saying, "He who loveth Me, keepeth My commandments; and whoso loveth Me, shall be loved of My Father; and I will love Him and" (as if it were said to Him, "what wilt Thou give unto him, as Thou lovest him?" He saith), "I will manifest Myself unto him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:116
verses.text: If then He promises this by way of a reward unto them that love Him, it is manifest that the vision of the Truth, promised to us, is of such a nature, that, when we have seen it, we shall no longer say, "My soul is filled with illusions".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:117
verses.text: "I am become feeble, and am bowed down greatly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:118
verses.text: He who calls to mind the transcendent height of the Sabbath, sees how "greatly" he is himself "bowed down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:119
verses.text: For he who cannot conc eive what is that height of rest, sees not where he is at present.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:120
verses.text: Therefore another Psalm hath said, "I said in my trance, I am cast out of the sight of Thine eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:121
verses.text: For his mind being taken up thither, he beheld something sublime; and was not yet entirely there, where what he beheld was; and a kind of flash, as it were, if one may so speak, of the Eternal Light having glanced upon him, when he perceived that he was not yet arrived at this, which he was able after a sort to understand, he saw where he himself was, and how he was cramped and "bowed down" by human infirmities.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:122
verses.text: And he says, "I said in my trance, I am cast out of the sight of Thine eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:123
verses.text: Such is that certain something which I saw in my trance, that thence I perceive how far off I am, who am not already there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:124
verses.text: He was already there who said that he was "caught up into the third Heaven, and there heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:125
verses.text: But he was recalled to us, in order that, as requiring to be made perfect, he might first mourn his infirmity, and afterwards be clothed with might.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:126
verses.text: Yet encouraged for the ministration of his office by having seen somewhat of those things, he goes on saying, "I heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:127
verses.text: Now then what use is it for you to ask, either of me or of any one, the "things which it is not lawful for man to utter".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:128
verses.text: If it was not lawful for him to utter them, to whom is it lawful to hear them? Let us however lament and groan in Confession; let us own where we are; let us "call the Sabbath to remembrance," and wait with patience for what He has promised, who hath, in His own Person also, showed forth an example of patience to us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:129
verses.text: "I am become feeble, and bowed down greatly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:130
verses.text: "I have roared with the groaning of my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:131
verses.text: You observe the servants of God generally interceding with groaning; and the reason of it is asked, and there is nothing apparent, but the groaning of some servant of God, if indeed it does find its way at all to the ears of a person placed near him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:132
verses.text: For there is a secret groaning, which is not heard by man: yet if the thought of some strong desire has taken so strong hold of the heart, that the wound of the inner man finds expression in some uttered exclamation, the reason of it is asked; and a man says to himself, "Perhaps this is the cause of his groaning;" and, "Perhaps this or that hath befallen him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:133
verses.text: Who can determine, but He in whose Eyes and Ears he groaned? Therefore he says, "I roared with the groaning of mine heart;" because if men ever hear a man's groanings, they for the most part hear but the groaning of the flesh; they do not hear him who groans "with the groaning of his heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:134
verses.text: Some one hath carried off his goods; he "roareth," but not "with the groaning of his heart:" another because he has buried his son, another his wife; another because his vineyard has been injured by a hailstorm; another because his cask has turned sour; another because some one hath stolen his beast; another because he has suffered some loss; another because he fears some man who is his enemy: all these "roar" with the "groaning of the flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:135
verses.text: The servant of God, however, because he "roareth" from the recollection of the Sabbath, where the Kingdom of God is, which flesh and blood shall not possess, says, "I have roared with the groaning of my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:136
verses.text: And who observed and noticed the cause of his groaning? "All my desire is before Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:137
verses.text: For it is not before men who cannot see the heart, but it is before Thee that all my desire is open! Let your desire be before Him; and "the Father, who seeth in secret, shall reward thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:138
verses.text: For it is thy heart's desire that is thy prayer; and if thy desire continues uninterrupted, thy prayer continueth also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:139
verses.text: For not without a meaning did the Apostle say, "Pray without ceasing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:140
verses.text: Are we to be "without ceasing" bending the knee, prostrating the body, or lifting up our hands, that he says, "Pray without ceasing"? Or if it is in this sense that we say that we "pray," this, I believe, we cannot do "without ceasing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:141
verses.text: There is another inward kind of prayer without ceasing, which is the desire of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:142
verses.text: Whatever else you are doing, if you do but long for that Sabbath, you do not cease to pray.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:143
verses.text: If you would never cease to pray, never cease to long after it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:144
verses.text: The continuance of thy longing is the continuance of thy prayer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:145
verses.text: You will be ceasing to speak, if you cease to long for it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:146
verses.text: Who are those who have ceased to speak? They of whom it is said, "Because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:147
verses.text: The freezing of charity is the silence of the heart; the burning of charity is the cry of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:148
verses.text: If love continues still you are still lifting up your voice; if you are always lifting up your voice, you are always longing after something; if always longing for something absent, you are calling "the Sabbath rest to remembrance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:149
verses.text: And it is important you should understand too before whom the "roaring of thine heart" is open.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:150
verses.text: Now then consider what sort of desires those should be, that are before the eyes of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:151
verses.text: Should it be the desire for the death of our enemy? a thing which men flatter themselves they lawfully wish for? For sometimes we pray for what we ought not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:152
verses.text: Let us consider what they flatter themselves they pray for lawfully! For they pray that some person may die, and his inheritance come to them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:153
