verses.text: But let those too, who pray for the death of their enemies, hear the Lord saying, "Pray for your enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:154
verses.text: Let them not pray for this, that their enemies may die; but rather pray for this, that they may be reclaimed; then will their enemies be dead; for from the time that they are reclaimed, henceforth they will be enemies no longer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:155
verses.text: "And all my desire is before Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:156
verses.text: What if we suppose that our desire is before Him, and that yet that very "groaning" is not before Him? How can that be, since our desire itself finds its expression in "groaning"? Therefore follows, "And my groaning is not hid from Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:157
verses.text: From Thee indeed it is not hid; but from many men it is hid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:158
verses.text: The servant of God sometimes seems to be saying in humility, "And my groaning is not hid from Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:159
verses.text: Sometimes also he seems to smile.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:160
verses.text: Is then that longing dead in his heart? If however there is the desire within, there is the "groaning" also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:161
verses.text: It does not always find its way to the ears of man; but it never ceases to sound in the ears of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:162
verses.text: "My heart is troubled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:163
verses.text: Wherefore is it troubled? "And my courage hath failed me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:164
verses.text: Generally something comes upon us on a sudden; the "heart is troubled;" the earth quakes; thunder is sent from Heaven; a formidable attack is made upon us, or a horrible sound heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:165
verses.text: Perhaps a lion is seen on the road; the "heart is troubled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:166
verses.text: Perhaps robbers lie in wait for us; the "heart is troubled:" we are filled with a panic fear; from every quarter something excites anxiety.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:167
verses.text: Wherefore? Because "my courage hath failed me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:168
verses.text: For what would be feared, did that courage still remain unmoved? Whatever bad tidings were brought, whatever threatened us, whatever sound was heard, whatever were to fall, whatever appeared horrible, would inspire no terror.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:169
verses.text: But whence that trouble? "My courage faileth me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:170
verses.text: Wherefore hath my courage failed me? "The light of mine eyes also is gone from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:171
verses.text: Thus Adam also could not see "the light of his eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:172
verses.text: For the "light of his eyes" was God Himself, whom when he had offended, he fled to the shade, and hid himself among the trees of Paradise He shrunk in alarm from the face of God: and sought the shelter of the trees; thenceforth among the trees he had no more "the light of his eyes," at which he had been wont to rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:173
verses.text: "My lovers;" why should I henceforth speak of my enemies? "My lovers and my neighbours drew nigh, and stood over against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:174
verses.text: Understand this that he saith, "Stood over against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:175
verses.text: For if they stood over against me, they fell against themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:176
verses.text: "My lovers and my neighbours drew nigh and stood over against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:177
verses.text: Let us now recognise the words of the Head speaking; now let our Head in His Passion begin to dawn upon us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:178
verses.text: Yet again when the Head begins to speak, do not sever the Body from it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:179
verses.text: If the Head would not separate itself from the words of the Body, should the Body dare to separate itself from the sufferings of the Head? Do thou suffer in Christ's suffering: for Christ, as it were, sinned in thy infirmity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:180
verses.text: For just now He spoke of thy sins, as if speaking in His own Person, and called them His own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:181
verses.text: To those who wished to be near His exaltation, yet thought not of His humility, He answered and said to them, "Can ye drink of the cup that I shall drink of?" Those sufferings of the Lord then are our sufferings also: and were each individual to serve God well, to keep faith truly, to render to each their dues, and to conduct himself honestly among men, I should like to see if he does not suffer even that which Christ here details in the account of His Passion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:182
verses.text: "My lovers and my neighbours drew nigh, and stood over against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:183
verses.text: "And my neighbours stood afar off".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:184
verses.text: Who were the "neighbours" that drew nigh, and who were those who stood afar off? The Jews were "neighbours" because "near kinsmen," they drew near even when they crucified Him: the Apostles also were His "neighbours;" and they also "stood afar off," that they might not have to suffer with Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:185
verses.text: This may also be understood thus: "My friends," that is, those who feigned themselves "My friends:" for they feigned themselves His friends, when they said, "We know that Thou teachest the way of God in truth;" when they wished to try Him, whether tribute ought to be paid to Caesar; when He convinced them out of their own mouth, they wished to seem to be His friends.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:186
verses.text: "But He needed not that any should testify of man, for He Himself knew what was in man;" so that when they spoke unto Him words of friendship, He answered them, "Why tempt ye Me, ye hypocrites?" "My friends and my neighbours" then "drew near and stood over against me, and my neighbours stood afar off".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:187
verses.text: You understand what I said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:188
verses.text: I called those neighbours who "drew nigh," and at the same time "stood afar off".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:189
verses.text: For they "drew nigh" in the body, but "stood afar off" in their heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:190
verses.text: Who were in the body so near to Him as those who lifted Him on the Cross? Who in heart so as those who blasphemed Him? Hear this sort of distance described by the Prophet Isaiah; observe this nearness and distance at one and the same time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:191
verses.text: "This people honours Me with their lips:" behold, with their body they draw near; "but their heart is far from Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:192
verses.text: The same persons are at the same time "near" and "afar off" also: with their lips they are near, in heart afar off.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:193
verses.text: However, because the Apostles also stood afar off, through fear, we understand it more simply and properly of them; so that we mean by it, that some drew near, and others stood afar off; since even Peter, who had followed more boldly than the rest, was still so far off, that being questioned and alarmed, he thrice denied the Lord, with whom he had promised to "be ready to die".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:194
verses.text: Who afterwards that, from being afar off, he might be made to draw nigh, heard after the resurrection the question, "Lovest thou Me?" and said, "I love Thee;" and by so saying was brought "nigh," even as by denying Him, he had become "far off;" till with the threefold confession of love, he had put away from him his threefold denial.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:195
verses.text: "And my neighbours stood afar off".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:196
verses.text: "They also that sought after my soul were preparing violence against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:197
verses.text: It is now plain who "sought after His soul;" viz.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:198
verses.text: those who had not His soul, in that they were not in His Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:199
verses.text: They who were "seeking after His soul," were far removed from His soul; but they were "seeking it" to destroy it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:200
verses.text: For His soul may be "sought after" in a right way also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:201
verses.text: For in another passage  He finds fault with some persons, saying, "There is no man to care for My soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:202
verses.text: He finds fault with some for not seeking after His soul; and again, with others for seeking after it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:203
verses.text: Who is he that seeketh after His soul in the right way? He who imitates His sufferings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:204
verses.text: Who are they that sought after His soul in the wrong way? Even those who "prepared violence against Him," and crucified Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:205
verses.text: He goes on: "Those who sought after My faults had spoken vanity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:206
verses.text: What is, "sought after My faults"? They sought after many things, and found them not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:207
verses.text: Perhaps He may have meant this: "They sought for criminal charges against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:208
verses.text: For they sought for somewhat to say against Him, and "they found not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:209
verses.text: For they were seeking to find evil things to say of "the Good;" crimes of the Innocent; When would they find such things in Him, who had no sin? But because they had to seek for sins in Him who had no sin, it remained for them to invent that which they could not find.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:210
verses.text: Therefore, "those who sought after My faults have spoken vanity," i-e:, untruth, "and imagined deceit all the day long;" that is, they meditated treachery without intermission.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:211
verses.text: You know how atrocious false-witness was borne against the Lord, before He suffered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:212
verses.text: You know how atrocious false-witness was borne against Him, even after His resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:213
verses.text: For those soldiers who watched His sepulchre of whom Isaiah spake, "I will appoint the wicked for His burial" (for they were wicked men, and would not speak the truth, and being bribed they disseminated a lie), consider what "vanity" they spake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:214
verses.text: They also were examined, and they said, "While we slept, His disciples came and stole Him away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:215
verses.text: This it is, "to speak vanity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:216
verses.text: For if they were sleeping, how could they know what had been done?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:217
verses.text: He saith then, "But I as a deaf man heard not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:218
verses.text: He who replied not to what He heard, did, as it were, not hear them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:219
verses.text: "But I as a deaf man heard not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:220
verses.text: And I was as a dumb man that openeth not his mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:221
verses.text: And he repeats the same things again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:222
verses.text: "And I became as a man that heareth not, and in whose mouth are no reproofs".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:223
verses.text: As if He had nothing to say unto them, as if He had nothing wherewith to reproach them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:224
verses.text: Had He not already reproached them for many things? Had He not said many things, and also said, "Woe unto you, Scribes and Pharisees," and many things besides? Yet when He suffered, He said none of these things; not that He had not what to say, but He waited for them to fulfil all things, and that all the prophecies might be fulfilled of Him, of whom it had been said, "And as a sheep before her shearer is dumb, so openeth He not His mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:225
verses.text: It behoved Him to be silent in His Passion, though not hereafter to be silent in Judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:226
verses.text: For He had come to be judged, then, who was hereafter coming to judge; and who was for this reason to come with great power to judge, that He had been judged in great humility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:227
verses.text: "For in Thee, O Lord, do I hope; Thou wilt hear, O Lord, my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:228
verses.text: As if it were said to Him, "Wherefore openedst thou not thy mouth? Wherefore didst Thou not say, 'Refrain'? Wherefore didst Thou not rebuke the unrighteous, while hanging on the Cross?" He goes on and says, "For in Thee, O Lord, do I hope; Thou, O Lord my God, wilt hear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:229
verses.text: He warns you what to do, should tribulation haply befall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:230
verses.text: For you seek to defend yourself, and perhaps your defence is not listened to by any one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:231
verses.text: Then are you confounded, as if you had lost your cause; because you have none to defend or to bear testimony in your favour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:232
verses.text: "Keep" but your "innocence" within, where no one can pervert thy cause.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:233
verses.text: False-witness has prevailed against you before men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:234
verses.text: Will it then prevail before God, where your cause has to be pleaded? When God shall be Judge, there shall be no other witness than your own conscience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:235
verses.text: In the presence of a just judge, and of your own conscience, fear nothing but your own cause.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:236
verses.text: If you have not a bad cause, you will have no accuser to dread; no false-witness to confute, nor witness to the truth to look for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:237
verses.text: Do but bring into court a good conscience, that you may say, "For in Thee, O Lord, do I hope; Thou, O Lord my God, wilt hear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:238
verses.text: "For I said, Let not mine enemies ever rejoice over me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:239
verses.text: And when my feet slip, they magnify themselves against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:240
verses.text: Again He returns to the infirmity of His Body: and again the Head takes heed of Its "feet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:241
verses.text: The Head is not in such a manner in Heaven, as to forsake what It has on earth; He evidently sees and observes us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:242
verses.text: For sometimes, as is the way of this life, our feet are "turned aside," and they slip by falling into some sin; there the tongues of the enemy rise up with the bitterest malignity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:243
verses.text: From this then we discern what they really had in view, even while they kept silence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:244
verses.text: Then they speak with an unsparing harshness; rejoicing to have discovered what they ought to have grieved for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:245
verses.text: "And I said, Lest at any time my adversaries should rejoice over me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:246
verses.text: I said this indeed; and yet it was perhaps for my correction that Thou hast caused them to "magnify themselves against me, when my feet slipped;" that is to say, when I stumbled, they were elated, and said many things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:247
verses.text: For pity, not insult, was due from them to the weak; even as the Apostle speaks: "Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual restore such an one in the spirit of meekness;" and he combines the reason why: "considering thyself also, lest thou also be tempted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:248
verses.text: Not such as these were the persons of whom He speaks: "And when my feet slipped, they rejoiced greatly against me;" but they were such as those of whom He says elsewhere: "They that hate me will rejoice if I fall".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:249
verses.text: "For I am prepared for the scourges".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:250
verses.text: Quite a magnificent expression; as if He were saying, "It was even for this that I was born; that I might suffer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:251
verses.text: For He was not to be born, but from Adam, to whom the scourge is due.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:252
verses.text: But sinners are in this life sometimes not scourged at all, or are scourged less than their deserts: because the wickedness of their heart is given over as already desperate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:253
verses.text: Those, however, for whom eternal life is prepared, must needs be scourged in this life: for that sentence is true: "My son, faint not under the chastening of the Lord, neither be weary when thou art rebuked of Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:254
verses.text: "For whom the Lord loveth He chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom He receiveth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:255
verses.text: Let not mine enemies therefore insult over me; let "them not magnify themselves;" and if my Father scourgeth me, "I am prepared for the scourge;" because there is an inheritance in store for me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:256
verses.text: Thou wilt not submit to the scourge: the inheritance is not bestowed upon thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:257
verses.text: For "every son" must needs be scourged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:258
verses.text: So true it is that "every son" is scourged, that He spared not even Him who had no sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:259
verses.text: For "I am prepared for the scourges".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:260
verses.text: "And my sorrow is continually before me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:261
verses.text: What "sorrow" is that? Perhaps, a sorrow for my scourge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:262
verses.text: And, in good truth, my brethren, in good truth, let me say unto you, men do mourn for their scourges, not for the causes on account of which they are scourged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:263
verses.text: Not such was the person here.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:264
verses.text: Listen, my brethren: If any person suffers any loss, he is more ready to say, "I did not deserve to suffer it," than to consider why he suffered it, mourning the loss of money, not mourning over that of righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:265
verses.text: If thou hast sinned, mourn for the loss of thy inward treasure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:266
verses.text: Thou hast nothing in thy house, but perhaps thou art still more empty in heart; but if thine heart is full of its Good, even thy God, why dost thou not say, "The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away; as it pleased the Lord was it done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:267
verses.text: Blessed be the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:268
verses.text: Whence then was it that He was grieving? Was it for the "scourging" wherewith He was scourged? God forbid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:269
verses.text: "And my sorrow" (says He) "is continually before me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:270
verses.text: And as if we were to say, "What sorrow? whence comes that sorrow?" he says: "For I declare mine iniquity; and I will have a care for my sin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:271
verses.text: See here the reason for the sorrow! It is not a sorrow occasioned by the scourge; not one for the remedy, not for the wound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:272
verses.text: For the scourge is a remedy against sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:273
verses.text: Hear, brethren; We are Christians, and yet if any one's son dies, he mourns for him but does not mourn for him if he sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:274
verses.text: It is then, when he sees him sinning, that he ought to make mourning for him, to lament over him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:275
verses.text: It is then he should restrain him, and give him a rule to live by; should impose a discipline upon him: or if he has done so, and the other has not taken heed, then was the time when he ought to have been mourned over; then he was more fatally dead whilst living in luxury, than when, by death, he brought his luxury to its close: at that time, when he was doing such things in thine house, he was not only "dead, but he stank also".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:276
verses.text: These things were worthy to be lamented, the others were such as might well be endured; those, I say, were tolerable, these worthy to be mourned over.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:277
verses.text: They were to be mourned over in the same way that you have heard this person mourn over them: "For I declare mine iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:278
verses.text: I will have a care for my sin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:279
verses.text: Be not free from anxiety when you have confessed your sin, as if always able to confess thy sin, and to commit it again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:280
verses.text: Do thou "declare thine iniquity in such a manner, as to have a care for thy sin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:281
verses.text: What is meant by "having a care of thy sin"? To have a care of thy wound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:282
verses.text: If you were to say, "I will have a care of my wound," what would be meant by it, but I will do my endeavour to have it healed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:283
verses.text: For this is "to have a care for one's sin," to be ever struggling, ever endeavouring, ever exerting one's self, earnestly and zealously, to heal one's wound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:284
verses.text: Behold! thou art from day to day mourning over thy sins; but perhaps thy tears indeed flow, but thy hands are unemployed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:285
verses.text: Do alms, redeem thy sins, let the poor rejoice of thy bounty, that thou also mayest rejoice of the Grace of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:286
verses.text: He is in want; so art thou in want also: he is in want at thy hands; so art thou also in want at God's hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:287
verses.text: Dost thou despise one who needs thy aid; and shall God not despise thee when thou needest His? Do thou therefore supply the needs of him who is in want of thine aid; that God may supply thy needs within This is the meaning of, "I will have a care for my sin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:288
verses.text: I will do all that ought to be done, to blot out and to heal my sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:289
verses.text: "And I will have a care for my sin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:290
verses.text: "But mine enemies live".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:291
verses.text: They are well off: they rejoice in worldly prosperity, while I am suffering, and "roaring with the groaning of my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:292
verses.text: In what way do His enemies "live, " in that He hath said of them already, that they have "spoken vanity"? Hear in another Psalm also: "Whose sons are as young plants; firmly rooted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:293
verses.text: But above He had said, "Whose mouth speaketh vanity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:294
verses.text: Their daughters polished after the similitude of a temple: their garners full bursting forth more and more; their cattle fat, their sheep fruitful, multiplying in their streets; no hedge falling into ruin; no cry in their streets".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:295
verses.text: "Mine enemies" then "live".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:296
verses.text: This is their life; this life they praise; this they set their hearts upon: this they hold fast to their own ruin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:297
verses.text: For what follows? They pronounce "the people that is in such a case" blessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:298
verses.text: But what sayest thou, who "hast a care for thy sin"? What sayest thou, who "confessest thine iniquity"? He says, "Blessed is the people whose God is the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:299
verses.text: "But mine enemies live, and are strengthened against me, and they that hate me wrongfully are multiplied".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:300
verses.text: What is "hate me wrongfully"? They hate me, who wish their good, whereas were they simply requiting evil for evil, they would not be righteous; were they not to requite with good the good done to them, they would be ungrateful: they, however, who "hate wrongfully," actually return evil for good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:301
verses.text: Such were the Jews; Christ came unto them with good things; they requited Him evil for good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:302
verses.text: Beware, brethren, of this evil; it soon steals upon us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:303
verses.text: Let no one of you think himself to be far removed from the danger, because we said, "Such were the Jews".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:304
verses.text: Should a brother, wishing your good, rebuke you, and you hate him, you are like them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:305
verses.text: And observe, how easily, how soon it is produced; and avoid an evil so great, a sin so easily committed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:306
verses.text: "They also that render evil for good, were speaking evil of me, because I have pursued the thing that is just".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:307
verses.text: Therefore was it that I was requited evil for good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:308
verses.text: What is meant by "pursued after the thing that is just"? Not forsaken it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:309
verses.text: That you might not always understand persecutio in a bad sense, He means by persecutus pursued after, thoroughly followed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:310
verses.text: "Because I have followed the thing that is just".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:311
verses.text: Hear also our Head crying with a lamentable voice in His Passion: "And they cast Me forth, Thy Darling, even as a dead man in abomination".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:312
verses.text: Was it not enough that He was "dead"? wherefore "in abomination" also? Because He was crucified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:313
verses.text: For this death of the Cross was a great abomination in their eyes, as they did not perceive that it was spoken in prophecy, "Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:314
verses.text: For He did not Himself bring death; but He found it here, propagated from the curse of the first man; and this same death of ours, which had originated in sin, He had taken upon Himself, and hung on the Tree.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:315
verses.text: Lest therefore some persons should think (as some of the Heretics think), that our Lord Jesus Christ had only a false body of flesh; and that the death by which He made satisfaction on the Cross was not a real death, the Prophet notices this, and says, "Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:316
verses.text: He shows then that the Son of God died a true death, the death which was due to mortal flesh: lest if He were not "accursed," you should think that He had not truly died.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:317
verses.text: But since that death was not an illusion, but had descended from that original stock, which had been derived from the curse, when He said, "Ye shall surely die:" and since a true death assuredly extended even to Him, that a true life might extend itself to us, the curse of death also did extend to Him, that the blessing of life might extend even unto us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:318
verses.text: "And they cast Me forth, Thy Darling, even as a dead man in abomination".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:319
verses.text: "Forsake me not, O Lord; O my God, depart not from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:320
verses.text: Let us speak in Him, let us speak through Him (for He Himself intercedeth for us), and let us say, "Forsake me not, O Lord my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:321
verses.text: And yet He had said, "My God! My God! why hast Thou forsaken Me?" and He now says, "O My God, depart not from Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:322
verses.text: If He does not forsake the body, did He forsake the Head? Whose words then are these but the First Man's? To show then that He carried about Him a true body of flesh derived from him, He says, "My God, My God why hast Thou forsaken Me?" God had not forsaken Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:323
verses.text: If He does not forsake Thee, who believest in Him, could the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost, One God, forsake Christ? But He had transferred to Himself the person of the First Man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:324
verses.text: We know by the words of an Apostle, that "our old man is crucified with Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:325
verses.text: We should not, however, be divested of our old nature, had He not been crucified "in weakness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:326
verses.text: For it was to this end that He came that we may be renewed in Him, because it is by aspiration after Him, and by following the example of His suffering, that we are renewed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:327
verses.text: Therefore that was the cry of infirmity; that cry, I mean, in which it was said, "Why hast Thou forsaken Me?" Thence was it said in that passage above, "the words of mine offences".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:328
verses.text: As if He were saying, These words are transferred to My Person from that of the sinner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:329
verses.text: "Depart not from me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:330
verses.text: Make haste to help me, Lord of my salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:331
verses.text: This is that very "salvation," Brethren, concerning which, as the Apostle Peter saith, "Prophets have enquired diligently," and though they have enquired diligently, yet have not found it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:332
verses.text: But they searched into it, and foretold of it; while we have come and have found what they sought for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:333
verses.text: And see, we ourselves too have not as yet received it; and after us shall others also be born, and shall find, what they also shall not receive, and shall pass away, that we may, all of us together, receive the "penny of salvation in the end of the day," with the Prophets, the Patriarchs, and the Apostles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:334
verses.text: For you know that the hired servants, or labourers, were taken into the vineyard at different times; yet did they all receive their wages on an equal footing Apostles, then, and Prophets, and Martyrs, and ourselves also, and those who will follow us to the end of the world, it is in the End itself that we are to receive everlasting salvation; that beholding the face of God, and contemplating His Glory, we may praise Him for ever, free from imperfection, free from any punishment of iniquity, free from every perversion of sin: praising Him; and no longer longing after Him, but now clinging to Him for whom we used to long to the very end, and in whom we did rejoice, in hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:335
verses.text: For we shall be in that City, where God is our Bliss, God is our Light, God is our Bread, God is our Life; whatever good thing of ours there is, at being absent from which we now grieve, we shall find in Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:336
verses.text: In Him will be that "rest," which when we "call to remembrance" now, we cannot choose but grieve.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 38:337
verses.text: For that is the "Sabbath" which we "call to remembrance;" in the recollection of which, so great things have been said already; and so great things ought to be said by us also, and ought never to cease being said by us, not with our lips indeed, but in our heart: for therefore do our lips cease to speak, that we may cry out with our hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:1
verses.text: Psalm XXXIX.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:2
verses.text: The title of this Psal m, which we have just chanted and proposed to discuss, is, "On the end, for Idithun, a Psalm for David himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:3
verses.text: Here then we must look for, and must attend to, the words of a certain person who is called Idithun; and if each one of ourselves may be Idithun, in that which he sings he recognises himself, and hears himself speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:4
verses.text: For thou mayest see who was called Idithun, according to the ancient descent of man; let us, however, understand what this name is translated, and seek to comprehend the Truth in the translation of the word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:5
verses.text: According therefore to what we have been able to discover by enquiry in those names which have been translated from the Hebrew tongue into the Latin, by those who study the sacred writings, Idithun being translated is "over-leaping them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:6
verses.text: Who then is this person "over-leaping them"? or who those whom he hath "over-leaped"?For there are some persons, yet clinging to the earth, yet bowed down to the ground, yet setting their hearts on what is below, yet placing their hopes in things that pass away, whom he who is called "over-leaping them" hath "over-leaped".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:7
verses.text: You know that some of the Psalms are entitled, "Songs of Degrees;" and in the Greek it is obvious enough what the word ‡ναβαθμῶν means.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:8
verses.text: For ‡ναβαθμοὶ are degrees (or steps) of them that ascend, not of them that descend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:9
verses.text: The Latin, not being able to express it strictly, expresses it by the general term; and in that it called them "steps," left it undetermined, whether they were "steps" of persons ascending or descending.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:10
verses.text: But because there is no "speech or language where their voices are not heard among them," the earlier language explains the one which comes after it: and what was ambiguous in one is made certain in another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:11
verses.text: Just then as there the singer is some one who is "ascending," so here is it some one who is "over-leaping".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:12
verses.text: Let this Idithun come still to us, let him "over-leap" those whose delight is in things below, and take delight in these things, and let him rejoice in the Word of the Lord; in the delight of the law of the Most High.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:13
verses.text: "I said, I will take heed to my ways, that I sin not with my tongue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:14
verses.text: For it is not without reason that the tongue is set in a moist place, but because it is so prone to slip Perceiving therefore how hard it was for a man to be under the necessity of speaking, and not to say something that he will wish unsaid, and filled with disgust at these sins, he seeks to avoid the like.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:15
verses.text: To this difficulty is he exposed who is seeking to "leap beyond".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:16
verses.text: Although I have "leaped beyond" the pleasures of earth, although the fleeting passions for things temporal ensnare me not, though now I despise these things below, and am rising up to better things than these, yet in these very better things the satisfaction of knowledge in the sight of God is enough for me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:17
verses.text: Of what use is it for me to speak what is to be laid hold of, and to give a handle to cavillers? Therefore, "I said, I will take heed to my ways, that I sin not with my tongue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:18
verses.text: I keep my mouth with a bridle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:19
verses.text: Wherefore is this? Is it on account of the religious, the thoughtful, the faithful, the holy ones? God forbid! These persons hear in such a manner, as to praise what they approve; but as for what they disapprove, perhaps, among much that they praise they rather excuse than cavil at it; on account of what persons then dost thou "take heed to thy ways," and place a guard on thy lips "that thou mayest not sin with thy tongue"? Hear: it is, "While the wicked standeth over against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:20
verses.text: It is not "by me" that he takes up his station, but "against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:21
verses.text: Why?Even the Lord Himself says, "I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:22
verses.text: And the Apostle, "I could not speak unto you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:23
verses.text: Yet not as to persons to be despaired of, but as to those who still required to be nourished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:24
verses.text: For he goes on to say, "As babes in Christ, I have fed you with milk, and not with meat; for hitherto ye were not able".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:25
verses.text: Well, tell it unto us even now.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:26
verses.text: "Neither yet now are ye able".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:27
verses.text: Be not therefore impatient to hear that which as yet thou art not capable of; but grow that thou mayest be "able to bear it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:28
verses.text: It is thus we address the little one, who yet requires to be fed with kindly milk in the bosom of Mother Church, and to be rendered meet for the "strong meat" of the Lord's Table.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:29
verses.text: But what can I say even of that kind to the sinner, who "taketh his stand against me," who either thinks or pretends himself capable of what he "cannot bear;" so that when I say anything unto him, and he has failed to comprehend it, he should not suppose that it was not he that had failed to comprehend, but I who had broken down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:30
verses.text: Therefore because of this sinner, who "taketh up his stand against me, I keep my mouth as it were with a bridle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:31
verses.text: "I became deaf, and was humbled, I held my peace from good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:32
verses.text: For this person, who is "leaping beyond," suffers some difficulty in a certain stage to which he hath already attained; and he desires to advance beyond, even from thence, to avoid this difficulty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:33
verses.text: I was afraid of committing a sin; so that I spoke not; that I imposed on myself the necessity of silence: for I had spoken thus, "I will take heed to my ways, that I may not sin with my tongue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:34
verses.text: Whilst I was too much afraid of saying anything wrong, I kept silence from all that is good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:35
verses.text: For whence could I say good things, except that I heard them? "It is Thou that shalt make me to hear of joy and gladness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:36
verses.text: And the "friend of the bridegroom standeth and heareth Him, and rejoiceth on account of the bridegroom's voice," not his own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:37
verses.text: That he may speak true things, he hears what he is to say.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:38
verses.text: For it is he that "speaketh a lie," that "speaketh of his own".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:39
verses.text: When therefore I had "put a bridle," as it were, "on my lips;" and constrained myself to silence, because I saw that everywhere speech was dangerous, then, says he, that came to pass upon me, which I did not wish, "I became deaf, and was humbled;" not humbled myself, but was humbled; "and I held my peace even from good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:40
verses.text: Whilst afraid of saying any evil, I began to refrain from speaking what is good: and I condemned my determination; for "I was holding my peace even from what is good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:41
verses.text: "And my sorrow was stirred up again".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:42
verses.text: Inasmuch as I had found in silence a kind of respite from a certain "sorrow," that had been inflicted upon me by those who cavilled at my words, and found fault with me: and that sorrow that was caused by the cavillers, had ceased indeed; but when "I held my peace even from good, my sorrow was stirred up again".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:43
verses.text: I began to be more grieved at having refrained from saying what I ought to have said, than I had before been grieved by having said what I ought not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:44
verses.text: "And my sorrow was stirred up again".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:45
verses.text: "And while I was musing, the fire burned".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:46
verses.text: I reflected on the words of my Lord, "Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou oughtest to have put My money to the exchangers, and I at My coming should receive it again with usury".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:47
verses.text: And that which follows may God avert from those who are His stewards! Bind him hand and foot, and let him be cast into outer darkness; the servant, who was not a waster of his master's goods, so as to destroy them, but was slothful in laying them out to improve them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:48
verses.text: What ought they to expect, who have wasted them in luxury, if they are condemned who through slothfulness have kept them? "As I was musing, the fire burned".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:49
verses.text: And as he was in this state of wavering suspense, between speaking and holding his peace, between those who are prepared to cavil and those who are anxious to be instructed,in this state of suspense, he prays for a better place, a place different from this his present stewardship, in which man is in such difficulty and in such danger, and sighing after a certain "end," when he was not to be subject to these things, when the Lord is to say to the faithful dispenser, "Enter thou into the joy of thy Lord," he says, "Then spake I with my tongue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:50
verses.text: In this fluctuation, in the midst of these dangers and these difficulties, because, that in consequence of the abundance of offences "the love of many is waxing cold," although the law of the Lord inspires delight, in this fluctuation then, (I say), "then spake I with my tongue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:51
verses.text: To whom? not to the hearer whom I would fain instruct; but to Him who heareth and taketh heed also, by whom I would fain be instructed myself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:52
verses.text: "I spake with my tongue" to Him, from whom I inwardly hear whatever I hear that is good or true.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:53
verses.text: —What saidst thou?  "Lord, make me to know mine end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:54
verses.text: For some things I have passed by already; and I have arrived at a certain point, and that to which I have arrived is better than that from which I have advanced to this; but yet there remains a point, which has to be left behind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:55
verses.text: For we are not to remain here, where there are trials, offences, where we have to bear with persons who listen to us and cavil at us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:56
verses.text: "Make me to know mine end;" the end, from which I am still removed, not the course which is already before me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:57
verses.text: The "end" he speaks of, is that which the Apostle fixed his eye upon, in his course; and made confession of his own infirmity, perceiving in himself a different state of things from that which he looked for elsewhere.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:58
verses.text: For he says, "Not that I have already attained, or am already perfect.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:59
verses.text: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:60
verses.text: And that you might not say, "If the Apostle hath not apprehended, have I apprehended? If the Apostle is not perfect, am I perfect?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:61
verses.text: "And the number of my days, what it is".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:62
verses.text: I ask of "the number of my days, what it is".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:63
verses.text: I can speak of "number" without number, and understand "number without number," in the same sense as "years without years" may be spoken of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:64
verses.text: For where there are years, there is a sort of "number" at all events, also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:65
verses.text: But yet, "Thou art the same, and Thy years shall not fail".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:66
verses.text: "Make me to know the number of my days;" but "to know what it is".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:67
verses.text: What then? that number in which thou art, think you that it "is" not? Assuredly, if I weigh the matter well, it has no being; if I linger behind, it has a sort of being; if I rise above it, it has none.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:68
verses.text: If, shaking off the trammels of these things, I contemplate things above, if I compare things that pass away with those that endure, I see what has a true being, and what rather seems to be, than really is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:69
verses.text: Should I say that these days of mine "are;" and shall I rashly apply this word so full of meaning to this course of things passing away? To such a degree have I my own self almost ceased to "be, failing" as I am in my weakness, that He escaped from my memory, who said, "I AM HE THAT IS".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:70
verses.text: Hath then any number of days any existence? In truth it hath, and it is "number without end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:71
verses.text: Everything is swept on by a series of moments, fleeting by, one after the other; there is a torrent of existences ever flowing on and on; a "torrent," of which He "drank in the way," who hath now "lift up His Head".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:72
verses.text: These days then have no true being; they are gone almost before they arrive; and when they are come, they cannot continue; they press upon one another, they follow the one the other, and cannot check themselves in their course.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:73
verses.text: Of the past nothing is called back again; what is yet to be, is expected as something to pass away again: it is not as yet possessed, whilst as yet it is not arrived; it cannot be kept when once it has arrived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:74
verses.text: He asks then concerning "the number of his days, which is;" not that which is "not:" and (which confounds me by a still greater and more perplexing difficulty) at once "is," and "is not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:75
verses.text: We can neither say that "is," which does not continue; nor that it "is not," when it has come and is passing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:76
verses.text: It is that absolute "IS," that true "IS," that "IS" in the true sense of the word, that I long for; that "IS;" which "is" in that "Jerusalem" which is "the Bride" of my Lord; where there will not be death, there will not be failing; there will be a day that passeth not away, but continueth: which has neither a yesterday to precede it, nor a to-morrow pressing close upon it This "number of my days, which is," this (I say), "make Thou me to know".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:77
verses.text: "That I may know what is wanting to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:78
verses.text: For while I am struggling here, "this" is wanting unto me: and so long as it is wanting unto me, I do not call myself perfect.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:79
verses.text: So long as I have not received it, I say, "not that I have already attained, either am already perfect; but I am pressing towards the prize of God's high calling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:80
verses.text: This let me receive as the prize of my running the race! There will be a certain resting-place, to terminate my course; and in that resting-place there will be a Country, and no pilgrimage, no dissension, no temptation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:81
verses.text: Make me then to know "this number of my days, which is, that I may know what is wanting unto me;" because I am not there yet; lest I should be made proud of what I already am, that "I may be found in Him, not having mine own righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:82
verses.text: "Behold, thou hast made my days old".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:83
verses.text: For these days are "waxing old".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:84
verses.text: I long for new days "that never shall wax old," that I may say, "Old things have passed away; behold, things are become new".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:85
verses.text: Already new in hope; then in reality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:86
verses.text: For though, in hope and in faith, made new already, how much do we even now do after our old nature! For we are not so completely "clothed upon" with Christ, as not to bear about with us anything derived from Adam.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:87
verses.text: Observe that Adam is "waxing old" within us, and Christ is being "renewed" in us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:88
verses.text: "Though our outward man is perishing, yet is our inward man being renewed day by day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:89
verses.text: Therefore, while we fix our thoughts on sin, on mortality, on time, that is hastening by, on sorrow, and toil, and labour, on stages of life following each other in succession, and continuing not, passing on insensibly from infancy even to old age; whilst, I say, we fix our eyes on these things, let us see here "the old man," the "day that is waxing old;" the Song that is out of date; the Old Testament; when however we turn to the inner man, to those things that are to be renewed in place of these which are to be changed, let us find the "new man," the "new day," the "new song," the "New Testament;" and that "newness," let us so love, as to have no fears of its "waxing old".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:90
verses.text: This man, therefore, who is hasting forward to those things which are new, and "reaching forward to those things which are before," says, "Lord, make me to know mine end, and the number of my days, which really is, that I may know what is wanting unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:91
verses.text: See he still drags with him Adam; and even so he is hasting unto Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:92
verses.text: "Behold," saith he, "thou hast made my days old".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:93
verses.text: It is those days that are derived from Adam, those days, I say, that thou hast made old.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:94
verses.text: They are waxing old day by day: and so waxing old, as to be at some day or other consumed also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:95
verses.text: "And my substance is as nothing before Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:96
verses.text: "Before Thee, O Lord, my substance is as nothing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:97
verses.text: "Before Thee;" who seest this; and I too, when I see it, see it only when "before Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:98
verses.text: When "before men" I see it not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:99
verses.text: For what shall I say? What words shall I use to show, that which I now am is nothing in comparison of That which truly "IS"? But it is within that it is said; it is within that it is felt, so far as it is felt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:100
verses.text: "Before Thee, O Lord," where Thine eyes are; and not where the eyes of men are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:101
verses.text: And where Thine eyes are, what is the state of things? "That which I am is as nothing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:102
verses.text: "But, verily, every man living is altogether vanity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:103
verses.text: "But, verily".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:104
verses.text: For what was he saying above? Behold, I have already "leaped beyond" all mortal things, and despised things below, have trampled under foot the things of earth, have soared upwards to the delights of the law of the Lord, I have been afloat in the dispensation of the Lord, have yearned for that "End" which Itself is to know no end, have yearned for the number of my days that truly "is," because the number of days like these hath no real being.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:105
verses.text: Behold, I am already such a one as this; I have already overleaped so much; I am longing for those things which abide.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:106
verses.text: "But verily," in the state in which I am here, so long as I am here, so long as I am in this world, so long as I bear mortal flesh, so long as the life of man on earth is a trial, so long as I sigh among causes of offence, as long as while I "stand" I am in "fear lest I fall," as long as both my good and my ill hangs in uncertainty, "every man living is altogether vanity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:107
verses.text: "Albeit man walketh in the Image".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:108
verses.text: In what "Image," save that of Him who said, "Let Us make man in Our Image, after Our Likeness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:109
verses.text: "Albeit man walks in the Image".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:110
verses.text: For the reason he says "albeit," is, that this is some great thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:111
verses.text: And this "albeit" is followed by "nevertheless," that the "albeit" which you have already heard, should relate to what is beyond the sun; but this "nevertheless," which is to follow, to what is "under the sun," and that the one should relate to the Truth, the other to "vanity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:112
verses.text: "Albeit," then, "that man walketh in the Image, nevertheless he is disquieted in vain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:113
verses.text: Hear the cause of his "disquieting," and see if it be not a vain one; that thou mayest trample it under foot, that thou mayest "leap beyond it," and mayest dwell on high, where that "vanity" is not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:114
verses.text: What "vanity" is that? "He heapeth up riches, and knoweth not for whom he may be gathering them together".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:115
verses.text: O infatuated vanity! "Blessed is the man that maketh the Lord his trust, and hath not respected vanities, nor lying deceits".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:116
verses.text: To you indeed, O covetous man, to you I seem to be out of my senses, these words appear to you to be "old wives' tales".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:117
verses.text: For you, a man of great judgment, and of great prudence, to be sure, are daily devising methods of acquiring money, by traffic, by agriculture, by eloquence perhaps, by making yourself learned in the law, by warfare, perhaps you even add that of usury.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:118
verses.text: Like a shrewd man as you are, you leave nothing untried, whereby you may pile coin on coin; and may store it up more carefully in a place of secrecy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:119
verses.text: You plunder others; you guard against the plunderer; you are afraid lest you should yourself suffer the wrong, that you yourself do; and even what you do suffer, does not correct you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:120
verses.text: Examine your own heart, and that prudence of yours, which leads you to deride me, to think me out of my senses for saying these things: and tell me now, "You are heaping up treasures; for whom are you gathering them together?" I see what you would tell me; as if what you would say had not occurred to the person described here; you will say, I am keeping them for my children? This is the voice of parental affection; the excuse of injustice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:121
verses.text: "I am keeping them" (you say) "for my children".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:122
verses.text: So then you are keeping them for your children, are you? Did not Idithun then know this? Assuredly he did; but he reckoned it one of the things of the "old days," that have waxed old, and therefore he despised it: because he was hastening on to the new "days".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:123
verses.text: For He, "by whom all things were made," hath built "mansions" for all of us: thither He would have that which we have go before us; that we may not lose it on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:124
verses.text: When, however, you have kept them on earth, tell me for whom you are to "gather them together"? You have children: add one more to their number; and give something to Christ also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:125
verses.text: "He is disquieted in vain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:126
verses.text: "And now".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:127
verses.text: "And now," saith this Idithun,—looking back on a certain "vain" show, and looking up to a certain Truth, standing midway where he has something beyond him, and something also behind him, having below him the place from which he took his spring, having above him that toward which he has stretched forth;—"And now," when I have "over-leaped" some things, when I have trampled many things under foot, when I am no longer captivated by things temporal; even now, I am not perfect, "I have not yet apprehended".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:128
verses.text: "For it is by hope that we are saved; but hope that is seen is not hope; for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for? But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:129
verses.text: Therefore he says: "And now what wait I for? Is it not for the Lord?" He is my expectation, who hath given me all those things, that I might despise them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:130
verses.text: He will give unto me Himself also, even He who is above all, and "by whom all things were made," and by whom I was made amongst all; even He, the Lord, is my Expectation! You see Idithun, brethren, you see in what way he waiteth for Him! Let no man therefore call himself perfect here; he deceives and imposes upon himself; he is beguiling himself, he cannot have perfection here, and what avails it that he should lose humility?  "And my substance is ever before Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:131
verses.text: Already advancing, already tending towards Him, and to some extent already beginning to "be," still (he says) "my substance is ever before Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:132
verses.text: Now that other substance is also before men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:133
verses.text: You have gold, silver, slaves, estates, trees, cattle, servants.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:134
verses.text: These things are visible even to men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:135
verses.text: There is a certain "substance that is ever before Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:136
verses.text: "Deliver me from all my transgressions".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:137
verses.text: I have "over-leaped" a great deal of ground, a very great deal of ground already; but, "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the Truth is not in us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:138
verses.text: I have "over-leaped" a great deal: but still do I "beat my breast," and say, "Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:139
verses.text: Thou therefore art "my expectation!" my "End".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:140
verses.text: For "Christ is the end of the Law unto righteousness, unto every man that believeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:141
verses.text: From all mine offences: not only from those, that I may not relapse into those which I have already "over-leaped;" but from all, without exception, of those on account of which I now beat my breast, and say, "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:142
verses.text: "Deliver me from all mine offences:" me being thus minded, and holding fast what the Apostle said, "As many of us as be perfect, let us be thus minded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:143
verses.text: For at the time that he said that he was not "already perfect," he then immediately goes on and says, "As many of us as be perfect, let us be thus minded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:144
verses.text: Art thou then, O Apostle, not perfect, and are we perfect? But hath it escaped you, that he did just now call himself "perfect"? For he does not say, "As many of you as are perfect, be ye thus minded;" but "As many of us as be perfect, let us be thus minded;" after having said a little before, "Not that I have already attained; either am already perfect".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:145
verses.text: In no other way then can you be perfect in this life, than by knowing that you cannot be perfect in this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:146
verses.text: This then will be your perfection, so to have "over-leaped" some things, as to have still some point to which you are hastening on: so as to have something remaining, to which you will have to leap on, when everything else has been passed by.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:147
verses.text: It is such faith as this that is secure; for whoever thinks that he has already attained, is "exalting himself," so as to be "abased" hereafter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:148
verses.text: "Thou hast made me the reproach of the foolish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:149
verses.text: Thou hast so willed it, that I should live among those, and preach the Truth among those, who love vanity; and I cannot but be a laughing-stock to them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:150
verses.text: "For we have been made a spectacle unto this world, and unto angels, and unto men:" to angels who praise, to men who censure, us; or rather to angels, some of whom praise, some of whom are censuring us: and to men also, some of whom are praising, and some censuring us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:151
verses.text: Both the one and the other are arms to us: the one "on the right hand," the other "on the left:" arms however they are both of them; both of these kinds of arms, both those "on the right hand," and those "on the left;" both those who praise, and those who censure; both those who pay us honour, and those who heap dishonour upon us; with both these kinds I contend against the devil; with both of these I smite him; I defeat him with prosperity, if I be not corrupted by it; by adversity, if I am not broken in spirit by it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:152
verses.text: "I became dumb; and I opened not my mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:153
verses.text: But it was to guard against "the foolish man," that "I became dumb, and opened not my mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:154
verses.text: For to whom should I tell what is going on within me? "For I will hear what the Lord God will speak in me; for He will speak peace unto His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:155
verses.text: But "There is no peace," saith the Lord, "to the wicked".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:156
verses.text: "I was dumb, and opened not my mouth; because it is Thou that madest me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:157
verses.text: Was this the reason that thou openedst not thy mouth, "because God made thee"? That is strange; for did not God make thy mouth, that thou shouldest speak? "He that planted the ear, doth He not hear? He that formed the eye, doth He not see?" God hath given thee a mouth to speak with; and dost thou say, "I was dumb, and opened not my mouth, because Thou madest me"? Or does the clause, "Because Thou madest me," belong to the verse that follows? "Remove Thy stroke away from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:158
verses.text: Because it is "Thou that hast made me," let it not be Thy pleasure to destroy me utterly; scourge, so that I may be made better, not so that I faint; beat me, so that I may be beaten out to a greater length and breadth, not so that I may be ground to powder.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:159
verses.text: "By the heaviness of Thy hand I fainted in corrections".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:160
verses.text: That is, I "fainted" while Thou wast correcting me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:161
verses.text: And what is meant by "correcting" me? except what follows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:162
verses.text: "Thou with rebukes hast chastened man for iniquity; Thou hast made my life to consume away like a spider".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:163
verses.text: There is much that is discerned by this Idithun; by every one who discerns as he does; who overleaps as he does.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:164
verses.text: For he says, that he has fainted in God's corrections; and would fain have the stroke removed away from him, "because it is He who made him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:165
verses.text: Let Him renew me, who also made me; let Him who created me, create me anew.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:166
verses.text: But yet, Brethren, do we suppose that there was no cause for his fainting, so that he wishes to be "renewed," to be "created anew"? It is "for iniquity," saith he, "that Thou hast chastened man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:167
verses.text: All this, my having fainted, my being weak, my "crying out of the deep," all of this is because of "iniquity;" and in this Thou hast not condemned, but hast "chastened" me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:168
verses.text: "Thou hast chastened man for sin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:169
verses.text: Hear this more plainly from another Psalm: "It is good for me that Thou hast afflicted me, that I might learn Thy righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:170
verses.text: I have been "afflicted," and at the same time "it is good for me;" it is at once a punishment, and an act of favour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:171
verses.text: What hath He in store for us after punishment is over, who inflicts punishment itself by way of favour? For He it is of whom it was said, "I was brought low, and He made me whole:" and, "It is good for me that Thou hast afflicted me, that I might learn Thy righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:172
verses.text: "Thou chastenest man for iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:173
verses.text: And that which is written, "Thou formest my grief in teaching me," could only be said unto God by one who was "leaping beyond" his fellows; "Thou formest my grief in teaching me;" Thou makest, that is to say, a lesson for me out of my sorrow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:174
verses.text: It is Thou that formest that very grief itself; Thou dost not leave it unformed, but formest it; and that grief, that has been inflicted by Thee, when formed, will be a lesson unto me, that I may be set free by Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:175
verses.text: For the word finges is used in the sense of "forming," as it were moulding, my grief; not in the sense of "feigning" it; in the same way that fingit is applied to the artist, in the same sense that figulus is derived from fingere.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:176
verses.text: Thou therefore "hast chastened man for iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:177
verses.text: I see myself in afflictions; I see myself under punishment; and I see no unrighteousness in Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:178
verses.text: If I therefore am under punishment, and if there is no unrighteousness with Thee, it remains that Thou must have been "chastening man for iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:179
verses.text: And by what means hast Thou "chastened" him? Tell us, O Idithun, the manner of thy chastening; tell us in what way thou hast been "chastened".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:180
verses.text: "And Thou hast made my life consume like a spider".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:181
verses.text: This is the chastening! What consumes away sooner than the spider? I speak of the creature itself; though what can be more liable to "consume away" than the spider's webs? Observe too how liable to decay is the creature itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:182
verses.text: Do but set your finger lightly upon it, and it is a ruin: there is nothing at all more easily destroyed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:183
verses.text: To such a state hast Thou brought my life, by chastening me "because of iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:184
verses.text: When chastening makes us weak, there is a kind of strength that would be a fault.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:185
verses.text: It was by a kind of strength that man offended, so as to require to be corrected by weakness: for it was by a certain "pride" that he offended; so as to require to be chastened by humility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:186
verses.text: All proud persons call themselves strong men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:187
verses.text: Therefore have many "come from the East and the West," and have attained "to sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:188
verses.text: Wherefore was it that they so attained? Because they would not be strong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:189
verses.text: What is meant by "would not be strong"? They were afraid to presume of their own merits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:190
verses.text: They did not "go about to establish their own righteousness," that they might "submit themselves to the righteousness of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:191
verses.text: Behold! you are mortal; and you bear about you a body of flesh that is corrupting away: "And ye shall fall like one of the princes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:192
verses.text: Ye shall die like men," and shall fall like the devil What good does the remedial discipline of mortality do you? The devil is proud, as not having a mortal body, as being an angel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:193
verses.text: But as for you, who have received a mortal body, and to whom even this does no good, so as to humble you by so great weakness, you shall "fall like one of the princes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:194
verses.text: This then is the first grace of God's gift, to bring us to the confession of our infirmity, that whatever good we can do, whatever ability we have, we may be that in Him; that "He that glorieth, may glory in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:195
verses.text: "When I am weak," saith he, "then am I strong".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:196
verses.text: "But surely every man living disquieteth himself in vain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:197
verses.text: He returns to what he mentioned a little before.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:198
verses.text: Although he be improving here, yet for all that, "every man living disquieteth himself in vain;" forasmuch as he lives in a state of uncertainty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:199
verses.text: For who has any assurance even of his own goodness? "He is disquieted in vain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:200
verses.text: Let him "cast upon the Lord the burden" of his care; let him cast upon Him whatever causes him anxiety.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:201
verses.text: "Let Him sustain thee;" let Him keep thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:202
verses.text: For on this earth what is there that is certain, except death? Consider the whole sum of all the good or the ill of this life, either those belonging to righteousness, or those belonging to unrighteousness; what is there that is certain here, except death? Have you been advancing in goodness? You know what you are to-day; what you will be to-morrow, you know not! Are you a sinner? you know what you are to-day; what you will be to-morrow, you know not! You hope for wealth; it is uncertain whether it will fall to your lot.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:203
verses.text: You hope to have a wife; it is uncertain whether you will obtain one, or what sort of one you will obtain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:204
verses.text: You hope for sons: it is uncertain whether they will be born to you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:205
verses.text: Are they born? it is uncertain whether they will live: if they live, it is uncertain whether they will grow up in virtue, or whether they will fall away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:206
verses.text: Whichever way you turn, all is uncertain, death alone is certain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:207
verses.text: Art thou poor? It is uncertain whether thou wilt grow rich.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:208
verses.text: Art thou unlearned? It is uncertain whether thou wilt become learned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:209
verses.text: Art thou in feeble health, it is uncertain whether thou wilt regain thy strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:210
verses.text: Art thou born? It is certain that thou wilt die: and in this certainty of death itself, the day of thy death is uncertain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:211
verses.text: Amidst these uncertainties, where death alone is certain, while even of that the hour is uncertain, and while it alone is studiously guarded against, though at the same time it is in no way to be escaped, "every man living disquieteth himself in vain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:212
verses.text: "Hear my prayer, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:213
verses.text: Whereof shall I rejoice? Whereof should I groan? I rejoice on account of what is past, I groan longing for these which are not yet come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:214
verses.text: "Hear my prayer, and give ear unto my cry.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:215
verses.text: Hold not Thy peace at my tears".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:216
verses.text: For do I now no longer weep, because I have already "passed by," have "left behind" so great things as these? "Do I not weep much the more?" For, "He that increaseth knowledge, increaseth sorrow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:217
verses.text: The more I long for what is not here, do I not so much the more groan for it until it comes? do I not so much the more weep until it comes?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:218
verses.text: "For I am a sojourner with Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:219
verses.text: But with whom am I a "sojourner"? When I was with the devil, I was a "sojourner;" but then I had a bad host and entertainer; now, however, I am with Thee; but I am a "sojourner" still.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:220
verses.text: What is meant by a sojourner? I am a "sojourner" in the place from which I am to remove; not in the place where I am to dwell for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:221
verses.text: The place where I am to abide for ever, should be rather called my home.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:222
verses.text: In the place from which I am to remove I am a "sojourner;" but yet it is with my God that I am a sojourner, with whom I am hereafter to abide, when I have reached my home.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:223
verses.text: But what home is that to which you are to remove from this estate of a sojourner? Recognise that home, of which the Apostle speaks, "We have an habitation of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the Heavens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:224
verses.text: If this house is eternal in the Heavens, when we have come to it, we shall not be sojourners any more.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:225
verses.text: For how should you be a sojourner in an eternal home? But here, where the Master of the house is some day to say to you, "Remove," while you yourself know not when He will say it, be thou in readiness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:226
verses.text: And by longing for your eternal home, you will be keeping yourself in readiness for it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:227
verses.text: And be not angry with Him, because He gives thee notice to remove, when He Himself pleases.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:228
verses.text: For He made no covenant with thee, nor did He bind Himself by any engagement; nor didst thou enter upon the tenancy of this house on a certain stipulation for a definite term: thou art to quit, when it is its Master's pleasure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:229
verses.text: For therefore is it that you now dwell there free of charge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:230
verses.text: "For I am a sojourner with Thee, and a stranger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:231
verses.text: Therefore it is there is my country: it is there is my home.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:232
verses.text: "I am a sojourner with Thee, and a stranger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:233
verses.text: Here too is understood "with Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:234
verses.text: For many are strangers with the devil: but they who have already believed and are faithful, are, it is true, "strangers" as yet, because they have not yet come to that country and to that home: but still they are strangers with God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:235
verses.text: For so long as we are in the body, we are strangers from the Lord, and we desire, whether we are strangers, or abiding here, "we may be accepted with Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:236
verses.text: I am a "sojourner with Thee; and a stranger, as all my fathers were".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:237
verses.text: If then I am as all my fathers were, shall I say that I will not remove, when they have removed? Am I to lodge here on other terms, than those on which they lodged here also?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:238
verses.text: "Grant me some remission, that I may be refreshed before I go hence".
