verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:239
verses.text: Consider well, Idithun, consider what knots those are which thou wouldest have "loosed" unto thee, that thou mightest be "refreshed before thou goest hence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:240
verses.text: For thou hast certain fever-heats from which thou wouldest fain be refreshed, and thou sayest, "that I may be refreshed," and "grant me a remission".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:241
verses.text: What should He remit, or loosen unto thee, save that difficulty under which, and in consequence of which, thou sayest, "Forgive us our debts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:242
verses.text: Grant me a remission before I go hence, and be no more".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:243
verses.text: Set me free from my sins, "before I go hence," that I may not go hence with my sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:244
verses.text: Remit them unto me, that I may be set at rest in my conscience, that it may be disburthened of its feverish anxiety, the anxiety with which "I am sorry for my sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:245
verses.text: Grant me a remission, that I may be refreshed" (before everything else), "before I go hence, and be no more".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:246
verses.text: For if thou grantest me not a "remission, that I may be refreshed," I shall "go and be no more".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:247
verses.text: "Before I go" thither, where if I go, I shall thenceforth "be no more.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:248
verses.text: Grant me a remission, that I may be refreshed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:249
verses.text: A question has suggested itself, how he will be no more.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:250
verses.text: What is meant then by "shall be no more," unless Idithun is alluding to what is true "being," and what is not true "being".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:251
verses.text: For he was beholding with the mind, with which he could do so, with the "mind's eye," by which he was able to behold it, that end, which he had desired to have shown unto him, saying, "Lord, make me to know mine end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:252
verses.text: He was beholding "the number of his days, which truly is;" and he observed that all that is below, in comparison of that true being, has no true being.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:253
verses.text: For those things are permanent; these are subject to change; mortal, and frail, and the eternal suffering, though full of corruption, is for this very reason not to be ended, that it may ever be being ended without end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:254
verses.text: He alluded therefore to that realm of bliss, to the happy country, to the happy home, where the Saints are partakers of eternal Life, and of Truth unchangeable; and he feared to "go" where that is not, where there is no true being; longing to be there, where "Being" in the highest sense is! It is on account of this contrast then, while standing midway between them, he says, "Grant me a remission, that I may be refreshed before I go hence and be no more".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:255
verses.text: For if Thou "grantest me not a remission" of my sins, I shall go from Thee unto all eternity! And from whom shall I go to all eternity? From Him who said, I Am HE that Am: from Him who said, "Say unto the children of Israel, I Am hath sent me unto you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 39:256
verses.text: He then who goes from Him, in the contrary direction, goes to non-existence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:1
verses.text: Psalm XL.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:2
verses.text: Of all those things which our Lord Jesus Christ has foretold, we know part to have been already accomplished, part we hope will be accomplished hereafter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:3
verses.text: All of them, however, will be fulfilled, because He is "the Truth" who speaks them, and requires of us to be as "faithful," as He Himself speaks them faithfully.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:4
verses.text: Let us say then what this Psalm says.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:5
verses.text: "I waited patiently for the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:6
verses.text: I waited patiently for the promise of no mere mortal who can both deceive and be himself deceived: I waited for the consolation of no mere mortal, who may be consumed by sorrow of his own, before he gives me comfort.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:7
verses.text: Should a brother mortal attempt to comfort me, when he himself is in sorrow likewise? Let us mourn in company; let us weep together, let us "wait patiently" together, let us join our prayers together also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:8
verses.text: Whom did I wait for but for the Lord? The Lord, who though He puts off the fulfilment of His promises, yet never recalls them? He will make it good; assuredly He will make it good, because He has made many of His promises good already: and of God's truth we ought to have no fears, even if as yet He had made none of them good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:9
verses.text: Lo! let us henceforth think thus, "He has promised us everything; He has not as yet given us possession of anything; He is a sponsible Promiser; a faithful Paymaster: do you but show yourself a dutiful exactor of what is promised; and if you be "weak," if you be one of the little ones, claim the promise of His mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:10
verses.text: Do you not see tender lambs striking their dams' teats with their heads, in order that they may get their fill of milk?"And He took heed unto me, and heard my cry".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:11
verses.text: He took heed to it, and He heard it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:12
verses.text: See thou hast not waited in vain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:13
verses.text: His eyes are over thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:14
verses.text: His ears turned towards thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:15
verses.text: For, "the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears are open unto their cry".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:16
verses.text: What then? Did He not see thee, when thou usedst to do evil and to blaspheme Him? What then becomes of what is said in that very Psalm, "The face of the Lord is upon them that do evil"? But for what end? "that He may cut off the remembrance of them from the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:17
verses.text: Therefore, even when thou wert wicked, He "took heed of thee;" but He "took no heed to thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:18
verses.text: So then to him who "waited patiently for the Lord," it was not enough to say, "He took heed of me, He says, "He took heed to me;" that is, He took heed by comforting me, that He might do me good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:19
verses.text: What was it that He took heed to? "and He heard my cry".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:20
verses.text: And what hath He accomplished for thee? What hath He done for thee? "He brought me up also out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:21
verses.text: He hath given us great blessings already: and still He is our debtor; but let him who hath this part of the debt repaid already, believe that the rest will be also, seeing that he ought to have believed even before he received anything.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:22
verses.text: Our Lord has employed facts themselves to persuade us, that He is a faithful promiser, a liberal giver.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:23
verses.text: What then has He already done? "He has brought me out of a horrible pit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:24
verses.text: What horrible pit is that? It is the depth of iniquity, from the lusts of the flesh, for this is meant by "the miry clay".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:25
verses.text: Whence hath He brought thee out? Out of a certain deep, out of which thou criedst out in another Psalm, "Out of the deep have I called unto Thee, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:26
verses.text: And those who are already "crying out of the deep," are not absolutely in the lowest deep: the very act of crying is already lifting them up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:27
verses.text: There are some deeper in the deep, who do not even perceive themselves to be in the deep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:28
verses.text: Such are those who are proud despisers, not pious entreaters for pardon; not tearful criers for mercy: but such as Scripture thus describes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:29
verses.text: "The sinner when he comes into the depth of evil despiseth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:30
verses.text: For he is deeper in the deep, who is not satisfied with being a sinner, unless instead of confessing he even defends his sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:31
verses.text: But he who has already "cried out of the deep," hath already lifted up his head in order that he might "cry out of the deep," has been heard already, and has been "brought out of the horrible pit, and out of the mire and clay".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:32
verses.text: He already has faith, which he had not before; he has hope, which he was before without; he now walks in Christ, who before used to go astray in the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:33
verses.text: For on that account it is that he says, "He hath set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:34
verses.text: Now "that Rock was Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:35
verses.text: Supposing that we are "upon the rock," and that our "goings are ordered," still it is necessary that we continue to walk; that we advance to something farther.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:36
verses.text: For what did the Apostle Paul say when now upon the Rock, when his "goings had now been established"? "Not as though I had already attained, either were already perfect: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:37
verses.text: What then has been done for thee, if thou hast not apprehended? On what account dost thou return thanks, saying, "But I have obtained mercy"? Because his goings are now established, because he now walks on the Rock?Therefore, when he was saying, "I press forward toward the prize of my high calling," because "his feet were now set on the Rock," and "his goings were ordered," because he was now walking on the right way, he had something to return thanks for; something to ask for still; returning thanks for what he had received already, while he was claiming that which still remained due.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:38
verses.text: For what things already received was he giving thanks? For the remission of sins, for the illumination of faith; for the strong support of hope, for the fire of charity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:39
verses.text: But in what respects had he still a claim of debt on the Lord? "Henceforth," he says, "there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:40
verses.text: There is therefore something due me still.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:41
verses.text: What is it that is due? "A crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, shall give me at that day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:42
verses.text: He was at first a loving Father to "bring him forth from the horrible pit;" to forgive his sins, to rescue him from "the mire and clay;" hereafter he will be a "righteous Judge," requiting to him walking rightly, what He promised; to him (I say), unto whom He had at the first granted that power to walk rightly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:43
verses.text: He then as a "righteous Judge" will repay; but whom will he repay? "He that endureth unto the end, the same shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:44
verses.text: "And He hath put a new song in my mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:45
verses.text: What new song is this? "Even a hymn unto our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:46
verses.text: Perhaps you used to sing hymns to strange gods; old hymns, because they were uttered by the "old man," not by the "new man;" let the "new man" be formed, and let him sing a "new song;" being himself made "new," let him love those "new" things by which he is himself made new.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:47
verses.text: For what is more Ancient than God, who is before all things, and is without end and without beginning? He becomes "new" to thee, when thou returnest to Him; because it was by departing from Him, that thou hadst become old; and hadst said, "I have waxed old because of all mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:48
verses.text: We therefore utter "a hymn unto our God;" and the hymn itself sets us free.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:49
verses.text: "For I will call upon the Lord to praise Him, and I will be safe from all mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:50
verses.text: For a hymn is a song of praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:51
verses.text: Call on God to "praise" Him, not to find fault with Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:52
verses.text: If haply any one asks, what person is speaking in this Psalm? I would say briefly, "It is Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:53
verses.text: But as ye know, brethren, and as we must say frequently, Christ sometimes speaks in His own Person, in the Person of our Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:54
verses.text: For He Himself is "the Saviour of the Body".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:55
verses.text: He is our Head; the Son of God, who was born of the Virgin, suffered for us, "rose again for our justification," sitteth "at the right hand of God," to "make intercession for us:" who is also to recompense to the evil and to the good, in the judgment, all the evil and the good that they have done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:56
verses.text: He deigned to be come our Head; to become "the Head of the Body," by taking of us that flesh in which He should die for us; that flesh which He also raised up again for our sakes, that in that flesh He might place before us an instance of the resurrection; that we might learn to hope for that of which we heretofore despaired, and might henceforth have our feet upon the rock, and might walk in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:57
verses.text: He then sometimes speaks in the name of our Head; sometimes also He speaks of us who are His members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:58
verses.text: For both when He said, "I was an hungred, and ye gave Me meat," He spoke on behalf of His members, not of Himself: and when He said, "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou Me?" the Head was crying on behalf of its members: and yet He did not say, "Why dost thou persecute My members?" but, "Why persecutest thou Me?" If He suffers in us, then shall we also be crowned in Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:59
verses.text: Such is the love of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:60
verses.text: What is there can be compared to this? This is the thing on account of which "He hath put a hymn in our mouth," and this He speaks on behalf of His members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:61
verses.text: "The just shall see, and shall fear, and shall trust in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:62
verses.text: "The just shall see".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:63
verses.text: Who are the just? The faithful; because it is "by faith that the just shall live".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:64
verses.text: For there is in the Church this order, some go before, others follow; and those who go before make themselves "an example" to those who follow; and those who follow imitate those who go before.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:65
verses.text: But do those then follow no one, who exhibit themselves as an ensample to them that come after? If they follow no one at all, they will fall into error.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:66
verses.text: These persons then must themselves also follow some one, that is, Christ Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:67
verses.text: "The just," therefore, "shall see, and shall fear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:68
verses.text: They see a narrow way on the one hand; on the other side, "a broad road:" on this side they see few, on the other many.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:69
verses.text: But thou art a just man; count them not, but weigh them; bring "a just balance," not a "deceitful" one: because thou art called just.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:70
verses.text: "The just shall see, and fear," applies to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:71
verses.text: Count not therefore the multitudes of men that are filling the "broad ways," that are to fill the circus tomorrow; celebrating with shouts the City's Anniversary,  while they defile the City itself by evil living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:72
verses.text: Look not at them; they are many in number; and who can count them? But there are a few travelling along the narrow road.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:73
verses.text: Bring forth the balance, I say.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:74
verses.text: Weigh them; see what a quantity of chaff you lift up on the one side, against a few grains of corn on the other.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:75
verses.text: Let this be done by "the just," the "believers," who are to follow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:76
verses.text: And what shall they who precede do? Let them not be proud, let them not "exalt themselves;" let them not deceive those who follow them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:77
verses.text: How may they deceive those who follow them? By promising them salvation in themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:78
verses.text: What then ought those who follow to do? "The just shall see, and fear: and shall trust in the Lord;" not in those who go before them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:79
verses.text: But indeed they fix their eyes on those who go before them, and follow and imitate them; but they do so, because they consider from Whom they have received the grace to go before them; and because they trust in Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:80
verses.text: Although therefore they make these their models, they place their trust in Him from whom the others have received the grace whereby they are such as they are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:81
verses.text: "The just shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:82
verses.text: Just as in another Psalm, "I lift up mine eyes unto the hills," we understand by hills, all distinguished and great spiritual persons in the Church; great in solidity, not by swollen inflation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:83
verses.text: By these it is that all Scripture hath been dispensed unto us; they are the Prophets, they are the Evangelists; they are sound Doctors: to these "I lift up mine eyes, from whence shall come my help".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:84
verses.text: And lest you should think of mere human help, he goes on to say, "My help cometh from the Lord, which made heaven and earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:85
verses.text: The just shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:86
verses.text: "Blessed is that man that maketh the name of the Lord his trust, and hath not respected vanities or lying madnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:87
verses.text: Behold the way by which thou wouldest fain have gone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:88
verses.text: Behold the "multitude that fill the Broad way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:89
verses.text: It is not without reason "that" road leads to the amphitheatre.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:90
verses.text: It is not without reason it leads to Death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:91
verses.text: The "broad way" leads unto death, its breadth delights for time: its end is straitness to all eternity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:92
verses.text: Aye; but the multitudes murmur; the multitudes are rejoicing together; the multitudes are hastening along; the multitudes are flocking together! Do not thou imitate them; do not turn aside after them: they are "vanities, and lying madnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:93
verses.text: Let the Lord thy God be thy hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:94
verses.text: Hope for nothing else from the Lord thy God; but let the Lord thy God Himself be thine hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:95
verses.text: For many persons hope to obtain from God's hands riches, and many perishable and transitory honours; and, in short, anything else they hope to obtain at God's hands, except only God Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:96
verses.text: But do thou seek after thy God Himself: nay, indeed, despising all things else, make thy way unto Him! Forget other things, remember Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:97
verses.text: Leave other things behind, and "press forward" unto Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:98
verses.text: Surely it is He Himself, who set thee right, when turned away from the right path; who, now that thou art set in the right path, guides thee aright, who guides thee to thy destination.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:99
verses.text: Let Him then be thy hope, who both guides thee, and guides thee to thy destination.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:100
verses.text: Whither does worldly covetousness lead thee? And to what point does it conduct thee at the last? Thou didst at first desire a farm; then thou wouldest possess an estate; thou wouldest shut out thy neighbours; having shut them out, thou didst set thy heart on the possessions of other neighbours; and didst extend thy covetous desires till thou hadst reached the shore: arriving at the shore, thou covetest the islands: having made the earth thine own, thou wouldest haply seize upon heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:101
verses.text: Leave thou all thy loves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:102
verses.text: He who made heaven and earth is more beautiful than all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:103
verses.text: "Blessed is the man that maketh the name of the Lord his hope, and who hath not regarded vanities and lying madnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:104
verses.text: For whence is it that "madness" is called "lying"? Insanity is a lying thing, even as it is sanity that sees the Truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:105
verses.text: For what thou seest as good things, thou art deceived; thou art not in thy sound senses: a violent fever has driven thee to frenzy: that which thou art in love with is not a reality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:106
verses.text: Thou applaudest the charioteer; thou cheerest the charioteer; thou art madly in love with the charioteer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:107
verses.text: It is "vanity;" it is "a lying madness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:108
verses.text: "It is 'not'" (he cries).

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:109
verses.text: "Nothing can be better; nothing more delightful".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:110
verses.text: What can I do for one in a state of high fever? Pray ye for such persons, if you have any feelings of compassion in you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:111
verses.text: For the physician himself also in a desperate case generally turns to those in the house, who stand around weeping; who are hanging on his lips to hear his opinion of the patient who is sick and in danger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:112
verses.text: The physician stands in a state of doubt: he sees not any good to promise; he fears to pronounce evil, lest he should excite alarm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:113
verses.text: He devises a thoroughly modest sentence: "The good God can do all things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:114
verses.text: Pray ye for him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:115
verses.text: Which then of these madmen shall I check? Which of them will listen to me? Which of them would not call us miserable? Because they suppose us to have lost great and various pleasures, of which they are madly fond, in that we are not as madly in love with them as they are: and they do not see that they are "lying" pleasures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:116
verses.text: "And hath not respected vanities, and lying madnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:117
verses.text: "Such a one has won," he cries; "he harnessed such and such a horse," he proclaims aloud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:118
verses.text: He would fain be a kind of diviner; he aspires to the honours of divination by abandoning the fountain of Divinity; and he frequently pronounces an opinion, and is frequently mistaken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:119
verses.text: Why is this? Even because they are "lying madnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:120
verses.text: But why is it that what they say sometimes comes true? That they may lead astray the foolish ones; that by loving the semblance of truth there, they may fall into the snare of falsehood: let them be left behind, let them be "given over," let them be "cut off".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:121
verses.text: If they were members of us, they must be mortified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:122
verses.text: "Mortify," he says, "your members which are upon the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:123
verses.text: Let our God be our hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:124
verses.text: He who made all things, is better than all! He who made what is beautiful, is more beautiful than all that is such.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:125
verses.text: He who made whatever is mighty, is Himself mightier.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:126
verses.text: He who made whatever is great, is Himself greater.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:127
verses.text: He will be unto you everything that you love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:128
verses.text: Learn in the creature to love the Creator; and in the work Him who made it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:129
verses.text: Let not that which has been made by Him detain thine affections, so that thou shouldest lose Him by whom thou thyself wert made also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:130
verses.text: "Blessed," then, "is the man that maketh the Name of the Lord his trust, and hath not respected vanities and lying madnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:131
verses.text: We will give him other sights in exchange for such sights as these.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:132
verses.text: And what sights shall we present to the Christian, whom we would fa in divert from those sights? I thank the Lord our God; He in the following verse of the Psalm hath shown us what sights we ought to present and offer to spectators who would fain have sights to see? Let us now suppose him to be weaned from the circus, the theatre, the amphitheatre; let him be looking after, let him by all means be looking after, some sight to see; we do not leave him without a spectacle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:133
verses.text: What then shall we give in exchange for those? Hear what follows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:134
verses.text: "Many, O Lord my God, are the wonderful works which Thou hast made".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:135
verses.text: He used to gaze at the "wonderful works" of man; let him now contemplate the wonderful works of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:136
verses.text: "Many are the wonderful works" that God "has made".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:137
verses.text: Why are they become vile in his eyes? He praises the charioteer guiding four horses; running all of them without fault and without stumbling.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:138
verses.text: Perhaps the Lord has not made such "wonderful works" in things spiritual.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:139
verses.text: Let him control lust, let him control cowardice, let him control injustice, let him control imprudence, I mean, the passions which falling into excess produce those vices; let him control these and bring them into subjection, and let him hold the reins, and not suffer himself to be carried away; let him guide them the way he himself would have them go; let him not be forced away whither he would not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:140
verses.text: He used to applaud the charioteer, he himself shall be applauded for his own charioteering; he used to call out that the charioteer should be invested with a dress of honour; he shall himself be clothed with immortality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:141
verses.text: These are the spectacles, these the sights that God exhibits to us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:142
verses.text: He cries out of heaven, "My eyes are upon you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:143
verses.text: Strive, and 'I will' assist you; triumph, and I will crown you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:144
verses.text: "And in Thy thought there is none that is like unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:145
verses.text: Now then look at the actor! For the man hath by dint of great pains learnt to walk upon a rope; and hanging there he holds thee hanging in suspense.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:146
verses.text: Turn to Him who exhibits spectacles far more wonderful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:147
verses.text: This man hath learned to walk upon the rope; but hath he caused another to walk on the sea? Forget now thy theatre; behold our Peter; not a walker on the rope, but, so to speak, a walker on the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:148
verses.text: And do thou also walk on other waters (though not on those on which Peter walked, to symbolize a certain truth), for this world is a sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:149
verses.text: It hath a deleterious bitterness; it hath the waves of tribulations, the tempests of temptations; it hath men in it who, like fish, delight in their own ruin, and prey upon each other; walk thou here, set thou thy foot on this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:150
verses.text: Thou wouldest see sights; be thyself a "spectacle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:151
verses.text: That thy spirit may not sink, look on Him who goes before thee, and says, "We have been made a spectacle unto this world, and unto angels, and unto men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:152
verses.text: Tread thou on the waters; suffer not thyself to be drowned in the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:153
verses.text: Thou wilt not go there, thou wilt not "tread it under foot," unless it be His bidding, who was Himself the first to walk upon the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:154
verses.text: For it was thus that Peter spoke.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:155
verses.text: "If Thou art, bid me come unto Thee on the waters".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:156
verses.text: And because "He was," He heard him when praying; He granted his wish to him when expressing his desire; He raised him up when sinking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:157
verses.text: These are the "wonderful works" that the "Lord hath made".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:158
verses.text: Look on them; let faith be the eye of him who would behold them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:159
verses.text: And do thou also likewise; for although the winds alarm thee, though the waves rage against thee, and though human frailty may have inspired thee with some doubt of thy salvation, thou hast it in thy power to "cry out," thou mayest say "Lord, I perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:160
verses.text: He who bids thee walk there, suffers thee not to perish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:161
verses.text: For in that thou now walkest "on the Rock," thou fearest not even on the sea! If thou art without "the Rock," thou must sink in the sea; for the Rock on which thou must walk is such an one as is not sunk in the sea,.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:162
verses.text: Observe then the "wonderful works" of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:163
verses.text: "I have declared, and have spoken; they are multiplied beyond number".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:164
verses.text: There is "a number," there are some over and above the number.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:165
verses.text: There is a fixed number that belongs to that heavenly Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:166
verses.text: For "the Lord knoweth them that are His;" the Christians that fear Him, the Christians that believe, the Christians that keep the commandments, that walk in God's ways, that keep themselves from sins; that if they fall confess: they belong to "the number".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:167
verses.text: But are they the only ones? There are also some "beyond the number".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:168
verses.text: For even if they be but a few (a few in comparison of the numbers of the larger majority), with how great numbers are our Churches filled, crowded up to the very walls; to what a degree do they annoy each other by the pressure, and almost choke each other by their overflowing numbers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:169
verses.text: Again, out of these very same persons, when there is a public spectacle, there are numbers flocking to the amphitheatre; these are over and above "the number".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:170
verses.text: But it is for this reason that we say this, that they may be in "the number".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:171
verses.text: Not being present, they do not hear this from us; but when ye have gone from hence, let them hear it from you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:172
verses.text: "I have declared," he says, "and have spoken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:173
verses.text: It is Christ who speaks.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:174
verses.text: "He hath declared it," in His own Person, as our Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:175
verses.text: He hath Himself declared it by His members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:176
verses.text: He Himself hath sent those who should "declare" it; He Himself hath sent the Apostles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:177
verses.text: "Their sound is gone out into all lands, and their words unto the ends of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:178
verses.text: How great the number of believers that are gathered together; how great the multitudes that flock together; many of them truly converted, many but in appearance: and those who are truly converted are the minority; those who are so but in appearance are the majority: because "they are multiplied beyond the number".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:179
verses.text: These are the "wonderful works" of God; these are the "thoughts" of God, to which "no man's thoughts are like;" that the lover of sight-seeing may be weaned from curiosity: and with us may seek after those more excellent, those more profitable things, in which, when he shall have attained unto them, he will rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:180
verses.text: "Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire" , saith the Psalm to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:181
verses.text: For the men of old time, when as yet the true Sacrifice, which is known to the faithful, was foreshown in figures, used to celebrate rites that were figures of the reality that was to be hereafter; many of them understanding their meaning; but more of them in ignorance of it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:182
verses.text: For the Prophets and the holy Patriarchs understood what they were celebrating; but the rest of the "stiff-necked people" were so carnal, that what was done by them was but to symbolize the things that were to come afterwards; and it came to pass, when that first sacrifice was abolished; when the burnt-offerings of "rams, of goats, and of calves," and of other victims, had been abolished, "God did not desire them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:183
verses.text: Why did God not desire them? And why did He at the first desire them? Because all those things were, as it were, the words of a person making a promise; and the expressions conveying a promise, when the thing that they promise is come, are no longer uttered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:184
verses.text: Those sacrifices then, as being but expressions of a promise, have been abrogated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:185
verses.text: What is that which has been given as its fulfilment? That "Body;" which ye know; which ye do not all of you know; which, of you who do know it, I pray God all may not know it unto condemnation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:186
verses.text: Observe the time when it was said; for the person is Christ our Lord, speaking at one time for His members, at another in His own person.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:187
verses.text: "Sacrifice and offering," said He, "Thou didst not desire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:188
verses.text: What then? Are we left at this present time without a sacrifice? God forbid!  "But a Body hast Thou perfected for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:189
verses.text: It was for this reason that Thou didst not desire the others; that Thou mightest "perfect" this; before Thou "perfectedst" this, Thou didst desire the others.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:190
verses.text: The fulfilment of the promise has done away with the words that express the promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:191
verses.text: For if they still hold out a promise, that which was promised is not yet fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:192
verses.text: This was promised by certain signs; the signs that convey the promise are done away; because the Substance that was promised is come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:193
verses.text: We are in this "Body".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:194
verses.text: We are partakers of this "Body".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:195
verses.text: We know that which we ourselves receive; and ye who know it not yet, will know it bye and bye; and when ye come to know it, I pray ye may not receive it unto condemnation "For he that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh damnation unto himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:196
verses.text: "A Body" hath been "perfected" for us; let us be made perfect in the Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:197
verses.text: "Burnt-offerings also for sin hast Thou not required".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:198
verses.text: "Then said I, Lo, I come!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:199
verses.text: It is time that what "was promised should come;" because the signs, by means of which they were promised, have been put away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:200
verses.text: And indeed, Brethren, observe these put away; those fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:201
verses.text: Let the Jewish nation at this time show me their priest, if they can! Where are their sacrifices? They are brought to an end;  they are put away now.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:202
verses.text: Should we at that time have rejected them? We do reject them now; because, if you chose to celebrate them now, it were unseasonable; unfitting at the time; incongruous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:203
verses.text: You are still making promises; I have already received! There has remained to them a certain thing for them to celebrate; that they might not remain altogether without a sign.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:204
verses.text: In such a case then are they; like Cain with his mark.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:205
verses.text: The sacrifices, however, which used to be performed there, have been put away; and that which remained unto them for a sign like that of Cain, hath by this time been fulfilled; and they know it not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:206
verses.text: They slay the Lamb; they eat the unleavened bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:207
verses.text: "Christ has been sacrificed for us, as our Passover".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:208
verses.text: Lo, in the sacrifice of Christ, I recognise the Lamb that was slain! What of the unleavened bread? "Therefore," says he, "let us keep the feast; not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of wickedness" (he shows what is meant by "old;" it is "stale" flour; it is sour), "but in the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:209
verses.text: They have continued in the shade; they cannot abide the Sun of Glory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:210
verses.text: We are already in the light of day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:211
verses.text: We have "the Body" of Christ, we have the Blood of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:212
verses.text: If we have a new life, let us "sing a new song, even a hymn unto our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:213
verses.text: "Burnt offerings for sin Thou didst not desire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:214
verses.text: Then said I, Lo, I come!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:215
verses.text: "In the head of the Book it is written of me, that I should fulfil Thy will: O my God, I am willing, and Thy Law is within my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:216
verses.text: Behold! He turns His regards to His members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:217
verses.text: Behold! He hath Himself "fulfilled the will" of the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:218
verses.text: But in what "beginning of a Book" is it written of Him? Perhaps in the beginning of this Book of Psalms.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:219
verses.text: For why should we seek far for it, or examine into other books for it? Behold! It is written in the beginning of this Book of Psalms! "His will is in the Law of the Lord;" that is, "'O my God, I am willing,' and 'Thy Law is within my heart;'" that is the same as, "And in His Law doth he meditate day and night".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:220
verses.text: "I have well declared Thy righteousness in the great congregation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:221
verses.text: He now addresses His members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:222
verses.text: He is exhorting them to do what He has already done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:223
verses.text: He has "declared;" let us declare also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:224
verses.text: He has suffered; let us "suffer with Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:225
verses.text: He has been glorified; we shall be "glorified with Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:226
verses.text: "I have declared Thy righteousness in the great congregation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:227
verses.text: How great an one is that? In all the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:228
verses.text: How great is it? Even among all nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:229
verses.text: Why among all nations? Because He is "the Seed of Abraham, in whom all nations shall be blessed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:230
verses.text: Why among all nations? "Because their sound hath gone forth into all lands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:231
verses.text: "Lo! I will not refrain my lips, O Lord, and that Thou knowest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:232
verses.text: My lips speak; I will not "refrain" them from speaking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:233
verses.text: My lips indeed sound audibly in the ears of men; but "Thou knowest" mine heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:234
verses.text: "I will not refrain my lips, O Lord; that Thou knowest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:235
verses.text: It is one thing that man heareth; another that God "knoweth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:236
verses.text: That the "declaring" of it should not be confined to the lips alone, and that it might not be said of us, "Whatsoever things they say unto you, do; but do not after their works;" or lest it should be said to the people, "praising God with their lips, but not with their heart," "This people honoureth Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me;" do thou make audible confession with thy lips; draw nigh with thine heart also "For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:237
verses.text: In case like unto which that thief was found, who, hanging on the Cross with the Lord, did on the Cross acknowledge the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:238
verses.text: Others had refused to acknowledge Him while working miracles; this man acknowledged Him when hanging on the Cross.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:239
verses.text: That thief had every other member pierced through; his hands were fastened by the nails; his feet were pierced also; his whole body was fastened to the tree; the body was not disengaged in its other members; the heart and the tongue were disengaged; "with the heart" he "believed; with the tongue" he made "confession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:240
verses.text: "Remember me, O Lord," he said, "when Thou comest into Thy kingdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:241
verses.text: He hoped for the coming of his salvation at a time far remote; he was content to receive it after a long delay; his hope rested on an object far remote.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:242
verses.text: The day, however, was not postponed! The answer was, "This day shalt thou be with Me in Paradise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:243
verses.text: Paradise hath happy trees! This day hast thou been with Me on "the Tree" of the Cross.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:244
verses.text: This day shalt thou be with Me on "the Tree" of Salvation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:245
verses.text: "I have not hid my righteousness within my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:246
verses.text: What is meant by "my righteousness"? My faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:247
verses.text: For, "the just shall live by faith".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:248
verses.text: As suppose the persecutor under threat of punishment, as they were once allowed to do, puts you to the question, "What art thou? Pagan or Christian?" "A Christian".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:249
verses.text: That is his "righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:250
verses.text: He believeth; he "lives by faith".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:251
verses.text: He doth not "hide his righteousness within his heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:252
verses.text: He has not said in his heart, "I do indeed believe in Christ; but I will not tell what I believe to this persecutor, who is raging against me, and threatening me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:253
verses.text: My God knoweth that inwardly, within my heart, I do believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:254
verses.text: He knoweth that I renounce Him not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:255
verses.text: Lo! you say that you have this inwardly within your heart! What have you upon your lips? "I am not a Christian".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:256
verses.text: Your lips bear witness against your heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:257
verses.text: "I have not hid my righteousness within my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:258
verses.text: "I have declared Thy Truth and Thy Salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:259
verses.text: I have declared Thy Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:260
verses.text: This is the meaning of, "I have declared Thy Truth and Thy Salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:261
verses.text: How is "Thy Truth" Christ? "I am the Truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:262
verses.text: How is Christ "His Salvation"? Simeon recognised the infant in His Mother's hands in the Temple, and said, "For mine eyes have seen Thy Salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:263
verses.text: The old man recognised the little child; the old man having himself "become a little child" in that infant, having been renewed by faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:264
verses.text: For he had received an oracle from God; and it said this, "The Lord had said unto him, that he was not to depart out of this life, until he had seen the "Salvation of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:265
verses.text: This "Salvation of God" it is a good thing to have shown unto men; but let them cry, "Show us Thy mercy, O Lord, and grant us Thy Salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:266
verses.text: "I have not concealed Thy mercy and Thy Truth from the great congregation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:267
verses.text: Let us be there; let us also be numbered among the members of this Body: let us not keep back "the mercy" of the Lord, and "the Truth" of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:268
verses.text: Wouldest thou hear what "the mercy of the Lord" is? Depart from thy sins; He will forgive thy sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:269
verses.text: Wouldest thou hear what "the truth" of the Lord is? Hold fast righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:270
verses.text: Thy righteousness shall receive a crown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:271
verses.text: For mercy is announced to you now; "Truth" is to be shown unto thee hereafter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:272
verses.text: For God is not merciful in such a way as not to be just, nor just in such a way as not to be merciful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:273
verses.text: Does that mercy seem to thee an inconsiderable one? He will not impute unto thee all thy former sins: thou hast lived ill up to this present day; thou art still living; this day live well; then thou wilt not "conceal" this "mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:274
verses.text: If this is meant by "mercy," what is meant by "truth"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:275
verses.text: "Remove not Thou Thy mercies far from me, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:276
verses.text: He is turning his attention to the wounded members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:277
verses.text: Because I have not "concealed Thy mercy and Thy Truth from the great congregation," from the Unity of the Universal Church, look Thou on Thy afflicted members, look on those who are guilty of sins of omission, and on those who are guilty of sins of commission: and withhold not Thou Thy mercies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:278
verses.text: "Thy mercy and Thy Truth have continually preserved me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:279
verses.text: I should not dare to turn from my evil way, were I not assured of remission; I could not endure so as to persevere, if I were not assured of the fulfilment of Thy promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:280
verses.text: "Innumerable evils have compassed me about".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:281
verses.text: Who can number sins? Who can count his own sins, and those of others? A burden under which he was groaning, who said, "Cleanse Thou me from my secret faults; and from the faults of others, spare Thou Thy servant, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:282
verses.text: Our own are too little; those "of others" are added to the burden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:283
verses.text: I fear for myself; I fear for a virtuous brother, I have to bear with a wicked brother; and under such burthen what shall we be, if God's mercy were to fail? "But Thou, Lord, remove not afar off".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:284
verses.text: Be Thou near unto us! To whom is the Lord near? "Even" unto them that "are of a broken heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:285
verses.text: He is far from the proud: He is near to the humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:286
verses.text: "For though the Lord is high, yet hath He respect unto the lowly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:287
verses.text: But let not those that are proud think themselves to be unobserved: for the things that are high, He "beholdeth afar off".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:288
verses.text: He "beheld afar off" the Pharisee, who boasted himself; He was near at hand to succour the Publican, who made confession The one extolled his own merits, and concealed his wounds; the other boasted not of his merits, but laid bare his wounds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:289
verses.text: He came to the Physician; he knew that he was sick, and that he required to be made whole; he "dared not lift up his eyes to Heaven: he smote upon his breast".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:290
verses.text: He spared not himself, that God might spare him; he acknowledged himself guilty, that God might "ignore" the charge against him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:291
verses.text: He punished himself, that God might free him from punishment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:292
verses.text: "Mine iniquities have taken hold upon me, so that I could not see".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:293
verses.text: There is a something for us "to see;" what prevents us so that we see it not? Is it not iniquity? From beholding this light your eye is prevented perhaps by some humour penetrating into it; perhaps by smoke, or dust, or by something else that has been thrown into it: and you have not been able to raise your wounded eye to contemplate this light of day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:294
verses.text: What then? Will you be able to lift up your wounded heart unto God? Must it not be first healed, in order that thou mayest see? Do you not show your pride, when you say, "First let me see, and then I will believe"? Who is there who says this? For who that would fain see, says, "Let me see, and then I will believe"? I am about to manifest the Light unto thee; or rather the Light Itself would fain manifest Itself to thee! To whom? It cannot manifest Itself to the blind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:295
verses.text: He does not see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:296
verses.text: Whence is it that he seeth not? It is that the eye is clogged by the multitude of sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:297
verses.text: "They are more than the hairs of my head".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:298
verses.text: He subjects the number of the "hairs of his head" to calculation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:299
verses.text: Who is there can calculate the number of the hairs of his head? Much less can he tell the number of his sins, which exceed the number of the hairs of his head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:300
verses.text: They seem to be minute; but they are many in number.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:301
verses.text: You have guarded against great ones; you do not now commit adultery, or murder; you do not plunder the property of others; you do not blaspheme; and do not bear false witness; those are the weightier kind of sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:302
verses.text: You have guarded against great sins, what are you doing about your smaller ones? You have cast off the weight; beware lest the sand overwhelm you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:303
verses.text: "And my heart hath forsaken me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:304
verses.text: What wonder if thine heart is forsaken by thy God, when it is even "forsaken" by itself? What is meant by "faileth me," "forsaketh me"? Is not capable of knowing itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:305
verses.text: He means this: "My heart hath forsaken me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:306
verses.text: I would fain see God with mine heart, and cannot from the multitude of my sins: that is not enough; mine heart does not even know itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:307
verses.text: For no one thoroughly knows himself: let no one presume upon his own state.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:308
verses.text: Was Peter able to comprehend with his own heart the state of his own heart, who said, "I will be with Thee even unto death"? There was a false presumption in the heart; there was lurking in that heart at the same time a real fear: and the heart was not able to comprehend the state of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:309
verses.text: Its state was unknown to the sick heart itself: it was manifest to the physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:310
verses.text: That which was foretold of him was fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:311
verses.text: God knew that in him which he knew not in himself: because his heart had forsaken him, his heart was unknown to his heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:312
verses.text: "Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:313
verses.text: As if he were saying, "'If Thou wilt, Thou canst make me clean.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:314
verses.text: ' Be pleased to deliver me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:315
verses.text: O Lord, look upon me to help me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:316
verses.text: Look, that is, on the penitent members, members that lie in pain, members that are writhing under the instruments of the surgeon; but still in hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:317
verses.text: "Let them be ashamed and confounded together that seek after my soul to destroy it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:318
verses.text: For in a certain passage he makes an accusation, and says, "I looked upon my right hand, and beheld; and there was no man who sought after my soul;" that is, there was no man to imitate Mine example.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:319
verses.text: Christ in His Passion is the Speaker.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:320
verses.text: "I looked on my right hand," that is, not on the ungodly Jews, but on Mine own right hand, the Apostles,—"and there was no man who sought after My soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:321
verses.text: So thoroughly was there no man to "seek after My soul," that he who had presumed on his own strength, "denied My soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:322
verses.text: But because a man's soul is sought after in two ways, either in order that you may enjoy his society; or that you may persecute him; therefore he here speaks of others, whom he would have "confounded and ashamed," who are "seeking after his soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:323
verses.text: But lest you should understand it in the same way as when he complains of some who did not "seek after his soul," He adds, "to destroy it;" that is, they seek after my soul in order to my death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:324
verses.text: "Let them be turned backward and put to shame that wish me evil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:325
verses.text: "Turned backwards".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:326
verses.text: Let us not take this in a bad sense.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:327
verses.text: He wishes them well; and it is His voice, who said from the Cross, "Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:328
verses.text: Wherefore then doth he say to them, that they should return "backwards"? Because they who before were proud, so that they fell, are now become humble, so that they may rise again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:329
verses.text: For when they are before, they are wishing to take precedence of their Lord; to be better than He; but if they go behind Him, they acknowledge Him to be better than they; they acknowledge that He ought to go before; that He should precede, they follow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:330
verses.text: Thence He thus rebukes Peter giving Him evil counsel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:331
verses.text: For the Lord, when about to suffer for our salvation, also foretold what was to happen concerning that Passion itself; and Peter says, "Be it far from Thee," "God forbid it!" "This shall not be!" He would fain have gone before his Lord; would have given counsel to his Master! But the Lord, that He might make him not go before Him, but follow after Him, says, "Get thee behind, Satan!" It is for this reason He said "Satan," because thou art seeking to go before Him, whom thou oughtest to follow; but if thou art behind, if thou follow Him, thou wilt henceforth not be "Satan".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:332
verses.text: What then? "Upon this Rock I will build My Church".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:333
verses.text: "Let them speedily bear away their own confusion, that say unto me, Well done! Well done!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:334
verses.text: They praise you without reason.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:335
verses.text: "A great man! A good man! A man of education and of learning; but why a Christian?" They praise those things in you which you should wish not to be praised; they find fault with that at which you rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:336
verses.text: But if perhaps you say, "What is it you praise in me, O man? That I am a virtuous man? A just man? If you think this, Christ made me this; praise Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:337
verses.text: But the other says, "Be it far from you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:338
verses.text: Do yourself no wrong! You yourself made yourself such".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:339
verses.text: "Let them be confounded who say unto me, Well done! Well done!" And what follows?  "Let all those that seek Thee, O Lord, rejoice and be glad".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:340
verses.text: Those who "seek" not me, but "Thee;" who say not to me, "Well done! Well done!" but see me "glory in Thee," if I have anything whereof to glory; for "he who glories, let him glory in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:341
verses.text: "Let all those who seek Thee, Lord, rejoice and be glad".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:342
verses.text: "And say continually, the Lord be magnified".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:343
verses.text: For even if the sinner becometh righteous, thou shouldest give the glory to "Him who justifieth the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:344
verses.text: Whether therefore it be a sinner, let Him be praised who calls him to forgiveness; or one already walking in the way of righteousness, let Him be praised who calls him to receive the crown! Let the Name of the Lord be magnified continually by "such as love Thy salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:345
verses.text: "But I".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:346
verses.text: I for whom they were seeking evil, I whose "life they were seeking, that they might take it away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:347
verses.text: But turn thee to another description of persons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:348
verses.text: But I to whom they said, "Well done! Well done!" "I am poor and needy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:349
verses.text: There is nothing in me that may be praised as mine own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:350
verses.text: Let Him rend my sackcloth in sunder, and cover me with His robe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:351
verses.text: For, "Now I live, not I myself; but Christ liveth in me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:352
verses.text: If it is Christ that "liveth in thee," and all that thou hast is Christ's, and all that thou art to have hereafter is Christ's also; what art thou in thyself? "I am poor and needy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:353
verses.text: Now I am not rich, because I am not proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:354
verses.text: He was rich who said, "Lord, I thank Thee that I am not as other men are;" but the publican was poor, who said, "Lord, be merciful to me a sinner!" The one was belching from his fulness; the other from want was crying piteously, "I am poor and needy!" And what wouldest thou do, O poor and needy man? Beg at God's door; "Knock, and it shall be opened unto thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:355
verses.text: —"As for me, I am poor and needy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:356
verses.text: Yet the Lord careth for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:357
verses.text: —"Cast thy care upon the Lord, and He shall bring it to pass".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:358
verses.text: What canst thou effect for thyself by taking care what canst thou provide for thyself? Let Him who made thee "care for thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:359
verses.text: He who cared for thee before thou wert, how shall He fail to have a care of thee, now that thou art what He would have thee be? For now thou art a believer, now thou art walking in the "way of righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:360
verses.text: Shall not He have a care for thee, who "maketh His sun rise on the good and on the evil, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust"?  "Thou art my Help, and my Deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:361
verses.text: He is calling upon God, imploring Him, fearing lest he should fall away: "Make no tarrying".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:362
verses.text: What is meant by "make no tarrying"? We lately read concerning the days of tribulation: "Unless those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:363
verses.text: The members of Christ—the Body of Christ extended everywhere—are asking of God, as one single person, one single poor man, and beggar! For He too was poor, who "though He was rich, yet became poor, that ye through His poverty might be made rich".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:364
verses.text: It is He that maketh rich those who are the true poor; and maketh poor those who are falsely rich.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:365
verses.text: He crieth unto Him; "From the end of the earth I cried unto Thee, when my heart was in heaviness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:366
verses.text: There will come days of tribulations, and of greater tribulations; they will come even as the Scripture speaks: and as days advance, so are tribulations increased also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 40:367
verses.text: Let no one promise himself what the Gospel doth not promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:1
verses.text: Psalm XLI  To the people, on the Feast of the Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:2
verses.text: The solemn day of the Martyrs hath dawned; therefore to the glory of the Passion of Christ, the Captain of Martyrs, who spared not Himself, ordering His soldiers to the fight; but first fought, first conquered, that their fighting He might encourage by His examp le, and aid with His majesty, and crown with His promise: let us hear somewhat from this Psalm pertaining to His Passion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:3
verses.text: I commend unto you oftentimes, nor grieve I to repeat, what for you is useful to retain, that our Lord Jesus Christ speaketh often of Himself, that is, in His own Person, which is our Head; often in the person of His Body, which are we and His Church; but so that the words sound as from the mouth of one, that we may understand the Head and the Body to consist together in the unity of integrity, and not be separated the one from the other; as in that marriage whereof it is said, "They two shall be one flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:4
verses.text: If then we acknowledge two in one flesh, let us acknowledge two in one voice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:5
verses.text: First, that which responding to the reader we have sung, though it be from the middle of the Psalm, from that I will take the beginning of this Sermon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:6
verses.text: "Mine enemies speak evil of Me, When He shall die, then shall His Name perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:7
verses.text: This is the Person of our Lord Jesus Christ: but see if herein are not understood the members also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:8
verses.text: This was spoken also when our Lord Himself walked in the flesh here on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:9
verses.text: When they saw the people go after Him, they said, "When He shall die, then shall His Name perish;" that is, when we have slain Him, then shall His Name be no more in the earth, nor shall He seduce any, being dead; but by that very slaying of Him shall men understand, that He was but a man whom they followed, that there was in Him no hope of salvation, and shall desert His Name, and it shall no more be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:10
verses.text: He died, and His Name perished not, but His Name was sown as seed: He died, but He was a grain, which dying, the corn immediately sprang up When glorified then was our Lord Jesus Christ, began they much more, and much more numerously to trust in Him; then began His members to hear what the Head had heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:11
verses.text: Now then our Lord Jesus Christ being in heaven set down, and Himself in us labouring on earth, still spake His enemies, "When He shall die, then shall His Name perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:12
verses.text: For hence stirred up the devil persecutions in the Church to destroy the Name of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:13
verses.text: Unless haply ye think, brethren, that those Pagans, when they raged against Christians, said not this among themselves, "to blot out the Name of Christ from the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:14
verses.text: That Christ might die again, not in the Head, but in His Body, were slain also the Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:15
verses.text: To the multiplying of the Church availed the Holy Blood poured forth, to help Its seminating came also the death of the Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:16
verses.text: "Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His Saints".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:17
verses.text: More and more were the Christians multiplied, nor was it fulfilled which spake the enemies, "When He shall die, then shall His Name perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:18
verses.text: Even now also is it spoken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:19
verses.text: Down sit the Pagans, and compute them the years, they hear their fanatics saying, A time shall come when Christians shall be none, and those idols must be worshipped as before they were worshipped: still say they, "When He shall die, then shall His Name perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:20
verses.text: Twice conquered, now the third time be wise! Christ died, His Name has not perished: the Martyrs died, multiplied more is the Church, groweth through all nations the Name of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:21
verses.text: He who foretold of His own Death, and of His Resurrection, He who foretold of His Martyrs' death, and of their crown, He Himself foretold of His Church things yet to come, if truth He spake twice, has He the third time lied? Vain then is what ye believe against Him; better is it that ye believe in Him, that ye may "understand upon the needy and poor One;" that "though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, that ye through His poverty might be rich".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:22
verses.text: "Blessed is he that understandeth upon the needy and poor One: in the evil day shall the Lord deliver him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:23
verses.text: For the evil day will come: will thou, nill thou, come it will: the Day of Judgment will come upon thee, an evil day if thou "understand not the needy and poor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:24
verses.text: For what now thou wilt not believe, shall be made manifest in the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:25
verses.text: But neither shalt thou escape, when it shall be made manifest, because thou believest not, when it is kept secret.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:26
verses.text: Invited art thou, what thou seest not to believe, lest when thou see, thou be put to the blush.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:27
verses.text: "Understand then upon the needy and poor One," that is, Christ: understand in Him the hidden riches, whom poor thou seest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:28
verses.text: "In Him are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:29
verses.text: For thereby in the evil day shall He deliver thee, in that He is God: but in that He is man, and that which in Him is human hath raised to life, and changed for the better, He hath lifted (thee) to heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:30
verses.text: But He who is God, who would have one person in man and with man, could neither decrease nor increase, neither die nor rise again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:31
verses.text: He died out of man's infirmity, but God dieth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:32
verses.text: But as we rightly say, Such a man died, though his soul dieth not; so we rightly say, Christ died, though His Divinity dieth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:33
verses.text: Wherefore died? Because needy and poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:34
verses.text: Let not His death offend thee, and avert thee from beholding His Divinity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:35
verses.text: "Blessed is he that understandeth upon the needy and poor One".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:36
verses.text: Consider also the poor, the needy, the hungry and thirsty, the naked, the sick, the prisoners; understand also upon such poor, for if upon such thou understand, thou understandest upon Him who said, "I was an hungred, I was thirsty, I was a stranger, naked, sick, in prison;" so in the evil day shall the Lord deliver thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:37
verses.text: "And deliver him not into the hand of his enemy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:38
verses.text: The enemy is the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:39
verses.text: Let none think of a man his enemy, when he hears these words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:40
verses.text: Haply one thought of his neighbour, of him who had a suit with him in court, of him who would take from him his own possession, of him who would force him to sell to him his house.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:41
verses.text: Think not this; but that enemy think of, of whom said the Lord, "an enemy hath done this".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:42
verses.text: For He it is who suggests that for things earthly he be worshipped, for overthrow the Christian Name this enemy cannot.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:43
verses.text: For he hath seen himself conquered by the fame and praises of Christ, he hath seen, whereas he slew Christ's Martyrs, that they are crowned, he triumphed over.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:44
verses.text: He hath begun to be unable to persuade men that Christ is nought; and because by reviling Christ, he now with difficulty deceives, by lauding Christ, he endeavours to deceive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:45
verses.text: Before this what said he? Whom worship ye? A Jew, dead, crucified, a man of no moment, who could not even from himself drive away death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:46
verses.text: When after His Name he saw running the whole human race, saw that in the Name of the Crucified temples are thrown down, idols are broken, sacrifices abolished; and that all these things predicted in the Prophets are considered by men, by men with wonder astonished, and closing now their hearts against the reviling of Christ; he clothes himself with praise of Christ, and begins to deter from the faith in another manner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:47
verses.text: Great is the law of Christ, powerful is that law, divine, ineffable! but who fulfilleth it? In the name of our Saviour, "tread upon the lion and the dragon".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:48
verses.text: By reviling openly roared the lion; by lauding craftily lurks the dragon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:49
verses.text: Let them come to the faith, who doubted; and not say, Who fulfilleth it? If on their own strength they presume, they will not fulfil it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:50
verses.text: Presuming on the grace of God let them believe, presuming (on it) let them come; to be aided come, not to be judged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:51
verses.text: So live all the faithful in the Name of Christ, each one in his degree fulfilling the commands of Christ, whether married, or celibates and virgins, they live as much as God granteth them to live; neither presume they in their own strength, but know that in Him they ought to glory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:52
verses.text: "The Lord help him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:53
verses.text: But when? Haply in heaven, haply in the life eternal, that so it remain to worship the devil for earthly needs, for the necessities of this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:54
verses.text: Far be it! Thou hast "promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:55
verses.text: He came unto thee on earth, by Whom were made heaven and earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:56
verses.text: Consider then what He saith, "The Lord help him, on his bed of pain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:57
verses.text: The bed of pain is the infirmity of the flesh; lest thou shouldest say, I cannot hold, and carry, and tie up my flesh; thou art aided that thou mayest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:58
verses.text: The Lord help thee on thy bed of pain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:59
verses.text: Thy bed did carry thee, thou carriedst not thy bed, but wast a paralytic inwardly; He cometh who saith to thee, "Take up thy bed, and go thy way into thy house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:60
verses.text: "The Lord help him on his bed of pain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:61
verses.text: Then to the Lord Himself He turneth, as though it were asked, Why then, since the Lord helpeth us, suffer we such great ills in this life, such great scandals, such great labours, such disquiet from the flesh and the world? He turneth to God, and as though explaining to us the counsel of His healing, He saith, "Thou hast turned all his bed in his infirmity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:62
verses.text: By the bed is understood anything earthly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:63
verses.text: Every soul that is infirm in this life seeketh for itself somewhat whereon to rest, because intensity of labour, and of the soul extended toward God, it can hardly endure perpetually, somewhat it seeketh on earth whereon to rest, and in a manner with a kind of pausing to recline, as are those things which innocent ones love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:64
verses.text: The innocent man resteth in his house, his family, his wife, his children; in his poverty, his little farm, his orchard planted with his own hand, in some building fabricated with his own study; in these rest the innocent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:65
verses.text: But yet God willing us not to have love but of life eternal, even with these, though innocent delights, mixeth bitterness, that even in these we may suffer tribulation, and so He turneth all our bed in our infirmity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:66
verses.text: "Thou hast turned all his bed in his infirmity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:67
verses.text: Let him not then complain, when in these things which he hath innocently, he suffereth some tribulations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 41:68
