verses.text: "The King has greatly desired thy beauty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:302
verses.text: And the daughters of Tyre shall worship with gifts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:303
verses.text: With what gifts? Even so would this King be approached, and would have His treasuries filled: and it is He Himself who has given us that wherewith they may be filled, and may be filled by you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:304
verses.text: Let them come (He says) and "worship Him with gifts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:305
verses.text: What is meant by "with gifts"?"Give alms, and all things are clean unto you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:306
verses.text: Come with gifts to Him that saith, "I will have mercy rather than sacrifice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:307
verses.text: To that Temple that existed aforetime as a shadow of that which was to come, they used to come with bulls, and rams, and goats, with every different kind of animal for sacrifice: that with that blood one thing should be done, and another be typified by it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:308
verses.text: Now that very blood, which all these things used to figure, hath come: the King Himself hath come, and He Himself would have your "gifts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:309
verses.text: What gifts? Alms.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:310
verses.text: For He Himself will judge hereafter, and will Himself hereafter account "gifts" to certain persons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:311
verses.text: "Come" (He says), "ye blessed of My Father".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:312
verses.text: Why? "I was an hungred, and ye gave Me meat," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:313
verses.text: These are the gifts with which the daughters of Tyre worship the King; for when they said, "When saw we Thee?" He who is at once above and below (whence those "ascending" and "descending" are spoken of ), said, "Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of Mine, ye have done it unto Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:314
verses.text: "The rich among the people shall entreat Thy face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:315
verses.text: Both they who shall entreat that face, and He whose face they will entreat, are all collectively but one Bride, but one Queen, mother and children belonging all together unto Christ, belonging unto their Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:316
verses.text: "All the glory of her, the King's daughter, is from within".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:317
verses.text: Not only is her robe, outwardly, "of gold, and of divers colours;" but He who loved her beauty, knew her to be also beautiful within What are those inward charms? Those of conscience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:318
verses.text: It is there Christ sees; it is there Christ loves her: it is there He addresses her, there punishes, there crowns.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:319
verses.text: Let then thine alms be done in secret; for "all the glory of her, the King's daughter, is from within".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:320
verses.text: "With fringes of gold, clothed with divers colours".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:321
verses.text: Her beauty is from within; yet in the "fringes of gold" is the diversity of languages: the beauty of doctrine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:322
verses.text: What do these avail, if them be not that beauty "from within"? "The virgins shall be brought unto the King after her".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:323
verses.text: It has been fulfilled indeed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:324
verses.text: The Church has believed; the Church has been formed throughout all nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:325
verses.text: And to what a degree do virgins now seek to find favour in the eyes of that King! Whence are they moved to do so? Even because the Church preceded them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:326
verses.text: "The virgins shall be brought unto the King after her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:327
verses.text: Her near kinswomen  shall be brought unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:328
verses.text: For they that are brought unto Him are not strangers, but her "near kinswomen," that belong to her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:329
verses.text: And because he had said, "unto the King," he says, turning the discourse to Him, "her near kinswomen shall be brought unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:330
verses.text: "With gladness and rejoicing shall they be brought and shall be led into the Temple of the King".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:331
verses.text: The "Temple of the King" is the Church itself: it is the Church itself that enters into "the Temple of the King".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:332
verses.text: Whereof is that Temple constructed? Of the men who enter the Temple? Who but God's "faithful" ones are its "living stones"? "They shall be led into the Temple of the King".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:333
verses.text: For there are virgins without the Temple of the King, the nuns among the heretics: they are virgins, it is true; but what will that profit them, unless they be led into the "Temple of the King"? The "Temple of the King" is in unity: the "Temple of the King" is not ruinous, is not rent asunder, is not divided.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:334
verses.text: The cement of those living stones is "charity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:335
verses.text: "Instead of thy fathers, children are born to thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:336
verses.text: Nothing can be more manifest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:337
verses.text: Now consider the "Temple of the King" itself, for it is on its behalf he speaks, on account of the unity of the body that is spread throughout all the world: for those very persons who have chosen to be virgins, cannot find favour with the King unless they be led into the Temple of the King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:338
verses.text: "Instead of thy fathers, are thy children born to thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:339
verses.text: It was the Apostles begat thee: they were "sent:" they were the preachers: they are "the fathers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:340
verses.text: But was it possible for them to be with us in the body for ever? Although one of them said, "I desire to depart, and to be with Christ, which is far better: to abide in the flesh is necessary for your sakes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:341
verses.text: It is true he said this, but how long was it possible for him to remain here? Could it be till this present time, could it be to all futurity? Is the Church then left desolate by their departure? God forbid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:342
verses.text: "Instead of thy fathers, children have been born to thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:343
verses.text: What is that? The Apostles were sent to thee as "fathers," instead of the Apostles sons have been born to thee: there have been appointed Bishops.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:344
verses.text: For in the present day, whence do the Bishops, throughout all the world, derive their origin? The Church itself calls them fathers; the Church itself brought them forth, and placed them on the thrones of "the fathers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:345
verses.text: Think not thyself abandoned then, because thou seest not Peter, nor seest Paul: seest not those through whom thou wert born.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:346
verses.text: Out of thine own offspring has a body of "fathers" been raised up to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:347
verses.text: "Instead of thy fathers, have children been born to thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:348
verses.text: Observe how widely diffused is the "Temple of the King," that "the virgins that are not led to the Temple of the King," may know that they have nothing to do with that marriage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:349
verses.text: "Thou shalt make them princes over all the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:350
verses.text: This is the Universal Church: her children have been made "princes over all the earth:" her children have been appointed instead of the "fathers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:351
verses.text: Let those who are cut off own the truth of this, let them come to the One Body: let them be led into the Temple of the King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:352
verses.text: God hath established His Temple everywhere: hath laid everywhere "the foundations of the Prophets and Apostles".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:353
verses.text: The Church has brought "forth sons;" has made them "instead of her fathers" to be "princes over all the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:354
verses.text: "They shall be mindful of thy name in every generation and generation; therefore shall the peoples confess unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:355
verses.text: What does it profit then to "confess" indeed and yet to confess out of "the Temple"? What does it profit to pray, and yet not to pray on the Mount? "I cried," says he, "unto the Lord with my voice: and He heard me out of His holy hill".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:356
verses.text: Out of what "hill"? Out of that of which it is said, "A city set upon a hill cannot be hid".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:357
verses.text: Of what "hill"? Out of that hill which Daniel saw "grow out of a small stone, and break all the kingdoms of the earth; and cover all the face of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:358
verses.text: There let him pray, who hopes to receive: there let him ask, who would have his prayer heard: there let him confess, who wishes to be pardoned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:359
verses.text: "Therefore shall the peoples confess unto thee for ever, world without end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:360
verses.text: For in that eternal life it is true indeed there will no longer be the mourning over sins: but yet in the praises of God by that everlasting City which is above, there will not be wanting a perpetual  confession of the greatness of that happiness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 45:361
verses.text: For to that City itself, to which another Psalm sings, "Glorious things are spoken of thee, O City of God," to her who is the very Bride of Christ, the very Queen, a "King's daughter, and a King's consort;"the peoples shall for this very cause confess even to herself; the hearts of all, now enlightened by perfect charity, being laid bare, and made manifest, that she may know the whole of herself most completely, who here is, in many parts of her, unknown to herself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:1
verses.text: Psalm XLVI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:2
verses.text: It is called, "A Psalm, to the end, for the sons of Korah, for things secret".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:3
verses.text: Secret is it then; but He Himself, who in the place of Calvary was crucified, ye know, hath rent the veil, that the secrets of the temple might be discovered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:4
verses.text: Furthermore since the Cross of our Lord was a key, whereby things closed might be opened; let us trust that He will be with us, that these secrets may be revealed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:5
verses.text: What is said, "To the end," always ought to be understood of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:6
verses.text: For "Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:7
verses.text: But The End He is called, not because He consumeth, but because He perfecteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:8
verses.text: For ended call we the food which is eaten, and ended the coat which is woven, the former to consumption, the latter to perfection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:9
verses.text: Because then we have not where to go farther when we have come to Christ, Himself is called the end of our course.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:10
verses.text: Nor ought we to think, that when we have come to Him, we ought to strive any further to come also to the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:11
verses.text: For this thought Philip also, when he said to Him, "Lord, show us the Father, and it sufficeth us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:12
verses.text: When he said, "It sufficeth us," he sought the end of satisfaction and perfection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:13
verses.text: Then said He, "Have I been so long time with you, and hast thou not known Me, Philip: he that hath seen Me, hath seen the Father".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:14
verses.text: In Him then have we the Father, because He is in the Father, and the Father in Him, and He and His Father are One.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:15
verses.text: "Our God is a refuge and strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:16
verses.text: There are some refuges wherein is no strength, whereto when any fleeth, he is more weakened than strengthened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:17
verses.text: Thou fleest, for example, to some one greater in the world, that thou mayest make thyself a powerful friend; this seemeth to thee a refuge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:18
verses.text: Yet so great are this world's uncertainties, and so frequent grow the ruins of the powerful day by day, that when to such refuge thou art come, thou beginnest to fear more than ever therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:19
verses.text: Our refuge is not such, but our refuge is strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:20
verses.text: When thither we have fled, we shall be firm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:21
verses.text: "A helper in tribulations, which find us out too much".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:22
verses.text: Tribulations are many, and in every tribulation unto God must we flee; whether it be a tribulation in our estate, or in our body's health, or about the peril of those dearest to us, or any other thing necessary to the sustaining of this life, refuge ought there to be none at all to a Christian man, other than his Saviour, other than his God, to whom when he has fled, he is strong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:23
verses.text: For he will not in himself be strong, nor will he to himself be strength, but He will be his strength, who has become his refuge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:24
verses.text: But, dearly beloved, among all tribulations of the human soul is no greater tribulation than the consciousness of sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:25
verses.text: For if there be no wound herein, and that be sound within man which is called conscience, wherever else he may suffer tribulation, thither will he flee, and there find God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:26
verses.text: Ye see, dearly beloved, when trees are cut down and proved by the carpenters, sometimes in the surface they seem as though injured and rotten; but the carpenter looks into the inner marrow as it were of the tree, and if within he find the wood sound, he promises that it will last in a building; nor will he be very anxious about the injured surface, when that which is within he declares sound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:27
verses.text: Furthermore, to man anything more inward than conscience is not found; what then profits it, if what is without is sound, and the  marrow of conscience has become rotton? These are close and vehement overmuch, and as this Psalm saith, too great tribulations; yet even in these the Lord hath become a helper by forgiving sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:28
verses.text: For the consciences of the ungodly hateth nothing save indulgence; for if one saith he hath great tribulations, being a confessed debtor to the treasury, when he beholdeth the narrowness of his estate, and seeth that he cannot be solvent; if on account of the distrainers every year hanging over him, he saith that he suffereth great tribulations, and doth not breathe freely except in hope of indulgence, and that in things earthly; how much more the debtor of penalties out of the abundance of sins: when shall he pay what he owes out of his evil conscience, when if he pay, he perisheth? For to pay this debt, is to undergo the penalties.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:29
verses.text: Remaineth then that of His indulgence, we may be secure, yet so that, indulgence received, we return not again to contract debts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:30
verses.text: Now then, such security received, what say they? "Therefore will not we fear, when the earth shall be confounded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:31
verses.text: Just before anxious, suddenly secure; out of too great tribulations set in great tranquillity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:32
verses.text: For in them Christ was sleeping, therefore were they tossed: Christ awoke (as but now we heard out of the Gospel), He commanded the winds, and they were still Since Christ is in each man's heart by faith, it is signified to us, that his heart as a ship in this world's tempest is tossed, who forgetteth his faith: as though Christ sleeping it is tossed, but Christ awaking cometh tranquillity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:33
verses.text: Nay, the Lord Himself, what said He? "Where is your faith?" Christ aroused, aroused up faith, that what had been done in the ship, might be done in their hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:34
verses.text: "A helper in tribulations, which found us out too much".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:35
verses.text: He caused that therein should be great tranquillity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:36
verses.text: See what tranquillity: "Therefore will not we fear when the earth shall be confounded, and the mountains shall be carried into the heart of the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:37
verses.text: Then we shall find not fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:38
verses.text: Let us seek mountains carried, and if we can find, it is manifest that this is our security.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:39
verses.text: The Lord truly said to His disciples, "If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say to this mountain, Be Thou removed, and be Thou cast into the sea, and it shall be done".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:40
verses.text: Haply "to this mountain," He said of Himself; for He is called a Mountain: "It shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord shall be manifest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:41
verses.text: But this Mountain is placed above other mountains; because the Apostles also are mountains, supporting this Mountain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:42
verses.text: Therefore followeth, "In the last days the Mountain of the Lord shall be manifest, established in the top of the mountains".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:43
verses.text: Therefore passeth It the tops of all mountains, and on the top of all mountains is It placed; because the mountains are preaching The Mountain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:44
verses.text: But the sea signifieth this world, in comparison of which sea, like earth seemed the nation of the Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:45
verses.text: For it was not covered over with the bitterness of idolatry, but, like dry land, was surrounded with the bitterness of the Gentiles as with sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:46
verses.text: It was to be, that the earth be confounded, that is, that nation of the Jews; and that the mountains be carried into the heart of the sea, that is, first that great Mountain established in the top of the mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:47
verses.text: For He deserted the nation of the Jews, and came among the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:48
verses.text: He was carried from the earth into the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:49
verses.text: Who carrying Him? The Apostles, to whom He had said, "If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say to this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea, and it shall be done:" that is, through your most faithful preaching it shall come to pass, that this mountain, that is, I Myself, be preached among the Gentiles, be glorified among the Gentiles, be acknowledged among the Gentiles, and that be fulfilled which was predicted of Me, "A people whom I have not known shall serve Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:50
verses.text: "The waters thereof roared, and were troubled" : when the Gospel was preached, "What is this? He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods:" this the Athenians; but the Ephesians, with what tumult would they have slain the Apostles, when in the theatre, for their goddess Diana, they made such an uproar, as to be shouting, "Great is Diana of the Ephesians!" Amidst which waves and roaring of the sea, feared not they who to that refuge had fled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:51
verses.text: Nay, the Apostle Paul would enter in to the theatre, and was kept back by the disciples, because it was necessary that he should still abide in the flesh for their sakes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:52
verses.text: But yet, "the waters thereof roared, and were troubled: the mountains shook at the mightiness thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:53
verses.text: Whose might? The sea's? or rather God's, of whom was said, "refuge and strength, a helper in tribulations, which have found us out too much?" For shaken were the mountains, that is, the powers of this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:54
verses.text: For one thing are the mountains of God, another the mountains of the world: the mountains of the world, they whose head is the devil, the mountains of God, they whose Head is Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:55
verses.text: But by these mountains were shaken those mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:56
verses.text: Then gave they their voices against Christians, when the mountains were shaken, the waters roaring; for the mountains were shaken, and there was made a great earthquake, with quaking of the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:57
verses.text: But against whom this? Against the City founded upon a rock.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:58
verses.text: The waters roar, the mountains shake, the Gospel being preached.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:59
verses.text: What then, the City of God? Hear what followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:60
verses.text: "The streams of the river make glad the City of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:61
verses.text: When the mountains shake, when the sea rages, God deserteth not His City, by the streams of the river.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:62
verses.text: What are these streams of the river? That overflowing of the Holy Spirit, of which the Lord said, "If any man thirst, let him come unto Me, and drink.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:63
verses.text: He that believeth on Me, out of his bosom shall flow rivers of living water".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:64
verses.text: These rivers then flowed out of the bosom of Paul, Peter, John, the other Apostles, the other faithful Evangelists.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:65
verses.text: Since these rivers flowed from one river, many "streams of the river make glad the City of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:66
verses.text: For that ye might know this to be said of the Holy Spirit, in the same Gospel next said the Evangelist, "But this spake He of the Spirit, which they that were to believe on Him should receive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:67
verses.text: For the Holy Ghost was not yet given, because that Jesus was not yet glorified".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:68
verses.text: Jesus being glorified after His Resurrection, glorified after His Ascension, on the day of Pentecost came the Holy Spirit, and filled the believers, who spake with tongues, and began to preach the Gospel to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:69
verses.text: Hence was the City of God made glad, while the sea was troubled by the roaring of its waters, while the mountains were confounded, asking what they should do, how drive out the new doctrine, how root out the race of Christians from the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:70
verses.text: Against whom? Against the streams of the river making glad the City of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:71
verses.text: For thereby showed He of what river He spake; that He signified the Holy Spirit, by "the streams of the river make glad the City of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:72
verses.text: And what follows? "The Most High hath sanctified His tabernacle:" since then there followeth the mention of Sanctification, it is manifest that these streams of the river are to be understood of the Holy Spirit, by whom is sanctified every godly soul believing in Christ, that it may be made a citizen of the City of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:73
verses.text: "God is in the midst of her: she shall not be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:74
verses.text: Let the sea rage, the mountains shake; "God is in the midst of her: she shall not be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:75
verses.text: What is, "in the midst of her"? That God stands in any one place, and they surround Him who believe in Him? Then is God circumscribed by place; and broad that which surroundeth, narrow that which is surrounded? God forbid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:76
verses.text: No such thing imagine of God, who is contained in no place, whose seat is the conscience of the godly: and so is God's seat in the hearts of men, that if man fall from God, God in Himself abideth, not falleth like one not finding where to be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:77
verses.text: For rather doth He lift up thee, that thou mayest be in Him, than so lean upon thee, as if thou withdraw thyself, to fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:78
verses.text: Himself if He withdraw, fall wilt thou: thyself if thou withdraw, fall will not He.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:79
verses.text: What then is, "God is in the midst of her"? It signifieth that God is equal to all, and accepteth not persons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:80
verses.text: For as that which is in the middle has equal distances to all the boundaries, so God is said to be in the middle, because He consulteth equally for all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:81
verses.text: "God is in the midst of her: she shall not be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:82
verses.text: Wherefore shall she not be moved? Because God is in the midst of her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:83
verses.text: He is "the Helper in tribulations that have found us out too much.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:84
verses.text: God shall help her with His Countenance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:85
verses.text: What is, "with His Countenance"? With manifestation of Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:86
verses.text: How manifests God Himself, so as that we see His Countenance? I have already told you; ye have learned God's Presence; we have learned it through His works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:87
verses.text: When from Him we receive any help so that we cannot at all doubt that it was granted to us by the Lord, then God's Countenance is with us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:88
verses.text: "The heathen are troubled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:89
verses.text: And how troubled? why troubled? To cast down the City of God, in the midst whereof is God? To overthrow the tabernacle sanctified, which God helpeth with His Countenance? No: with a wholesome trouble are the heathen now troubled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:90
verses.text: For what followeth? "And the kingdoms are bowed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:91
verses.text: Bowed, saith He, are the kingdoms; not now erected that they may rage, but bowed that they may adore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:92
verses.text: When were the kingdoms bowed? When that came to pass which was predicted in another Psalm, "All kings shall fall down before Him, all nations shall serve Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:93
verses.text: What cause made the kingdoms to bow? Hear the cause.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:94
verses.text: "The Most High gave His Voice, and the earth was moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:95
verses.text: The fanatics of idolatry, like frogs in the marshes, clamoured, the more tumultuously, the more sordidly, in filth and mire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:96
verses.text: And what is the brawling of frogs to the thunder of the clouds? For out of them "the Most High gave His Voice, and the earth was moved:" He thundered out of His clouds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:97
verses.text: And what are His clouds? His Apostles, His preachers, by whom He thundered in precepts, lightened in miracles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:98
verses.text: The same are clouds who are also mountains: mountains for their height and firmness, clouds for their rain and fruitfulness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:99
verses.text: For these clouds watered the earth, of which it was said, "The Most High gave His Voice, and the earth was moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:100
verses.text: For it is of those clouds that He threateneth a certain barren vineyard, whence the mountains were carried into the heart of the sea; "I will command," saith He, "the clouds that they rain no rain upon it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:101
verses.text: This was fulfilled in that which I have mentioned, when the mountains were carried into the heart of the sea; when it was said, "It was necessary that the word of God should have been spoken first to you; but seeing ye put it from you, we turn to the Gentiles;" then was fulfilled, "I will command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:102
verses.text: The nation of the Jews hath just so remained as a fleece dry upon the ground.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:103
verses.text: For this, ye know, happened in a certain miracle, the ground was dry, the fleece only was wet, yet rain in the fleece appeared not So also the mystery of the New Testament appeared not in the nation of the Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:104
verses.text: What there was the fleece, is here the veil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:105
verses.text: For in the fleece was veiled the mystery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:106
verses.text: But on the ground, in all the nations open lieth Christ's Gospel; the rain is manifest, the Grace of Christ is bare, for it is not covered with a veil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:107
verses.text: But that the rain might come out of it, the fleece was pressed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:108
verses.text: For by pressure they from themselves excluded Christ, and the Lord now from His clouds raineth on the ground, the fleece hath remained dry.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:109
verses.text: But of them then "the Most High gave His Voice," out of those clouds; by which Voice the kingdoms were bowed and worshipped.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:110
verses.text: "The Lord of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our taker up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:111
verses.text: Not any man, not any power, not, in short, Angel, or any creature either earthly or heavenly, but "the Lord of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our taker up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:112
verses.text: He who sent Angels, came after Angels, came that Angels might serve Him, came that men He might make equal to Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:113
verses.text: Mighty Grace! If God be for us, who can be against us? "The Lord of Hosts is with us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:114
verses.text: What Lord of Hosts is with us? "If" (I say) "God be for us, who can be against us? He that spared not His own Son, but delivered Him up for us all; how hath He not with Him also freely given us all things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:115
verses.text: Therefore be we secure, in tranquillity of heart nourish we a good conscience with the Bread of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:116
verses.text: "The Lord of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our taker up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:117
verses.text: However great be thy infirmity, see who taketh thee up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:118
verses.text: One is sick, a physician is called to him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:119
verses.text: His own taken-up, the Physician calleth the sick man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:120
verses.text: Who hath taken him up? Even He.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:121
verses.text: A great hope of salvation; a great Physician hath taken him up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:122
verses.text: What Physician?  Every Physician save He is man: every Physician who cometh to a sick man, another day can be made sick, beside Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:123
verses.text: "The God of Jacob is our taker up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:124
verses.text: Make thyself altogether as a little child, such as are taken up by their parents.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:125
verses.text: For those not taken up, are exposed; those taken up are nursed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:126
verses.text: Thinkest thou God hath so taken thee up, as when an infant thy mother took thee up? Not so, but to eternity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:127
verses.text: For thy voice is in that Psalm, "My father and my mother forsake me, but the Lord hath taken me up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:128
verses.text: "Come and see the works of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:129
verses.text: Now of this taking up, what hath the Lord done? Consider the whole world, come and see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:130
verses.text: For if thou comest not, thou seest not; if thou seest not, thou believest not; if thou believest not, thou standest afar off: if thou believest thou comest, if thou believest thou seest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:131
verses.text: For how came we to that mountain? Not on foot? Is it by ship? Is it on the wing? Is it on horses? For all that pertain to space and place, be not concerned, trouble not thyself, He cometh to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:132
verses.text: For out of a small stone He hath grown, and become a great mountain, so that He hath filled all the face of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:133
verses.text: Why then wouldest thou by land come to Him, who filleth all lands? Lo, He hath already come: watch thou.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:134
verses.text: By growing He waketh even sleepers; if yet there is not in them so deep sleep, as that they be hardened even against the mountain coming; but they hear, "Awake, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:135
verses.text: For it was a great thing for the Jews to see the stone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:136
verses.text: For the stone was yet small: and small they deservedly despised it, and despising they stumbled, and stumbling they were broken; remains that they be ground to powder.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:137
verses.text: For so was it said of the stone, "Whosoever shall fall upon that stone shall be broken; but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:138
verses.text: It is one thing to be broken, another to be ground to powder.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:139
verses.text: To be broken is less than to be ground to powder: but none grindeth He coming exalted, save whom He brake lying low.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:140
verses.text: For now before His coming He lay low before the Jews, and they stumbled at Him, and were broken; hereafter shall He come in His Judgment, glorious and exalted, great and powerful, not weak to be judged, but strong to judge, and grind to powder those who were broken stumbling at Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:141
verses.text: For "A stone of stumbling and a rock of offence," is He to them that believe not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:142
verses.text: Therefore, brethren, no wonder if the Jews acknowledged not Him, whom as a small stone lying before their feet they despised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:143
verses.text: They are to be wondered at, who even now so great a mountain will not acknowledge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:144
verses.text: The Jews at a small stone by not seeing stumbled; the heretics stumble at a mountain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:145
verses.text: For now that stone hath grown, now say we unto them, Lo, now is fulfilled the prophecy of Daniel, "The stone that was small became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:146
verses.text: Wherefore stumble ye at Him, and go not rather up to Him? Who is so blind as to stumble at a mountain? Came He to thee that thou shouldest have whereat to stumble, and not have whereto to go up? "Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:147
verses.text: Isaiah saith this: "Come ye, and let us go up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:148
verses.text: What is, "Come ye, and let us go up"? "Come ye," is, Believe ye.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:149
verses.text: "Let us go up," is, Let us profit But they will neither come, nor go up, nor believe, nor profit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:150
verses.text: They bark against the mountain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:151
verses.text: Even now by so often stumbling on Him they are broken, and will not go up, choosing always to stumble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:152
verses.text: Say we to them, "Come ye, and see the works of the Lord:" what "prodigies He hath set forth through the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:153
verses.text: Prodigies are called, because they portend something, those signs of miracles which were done when the world believed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:154
verses.text: And what thereafter came to pass, and what did they portend?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:155
verses.text: "He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:156
verses.text: This not yet see we fulfilled: yet are there wars, wars among nations for sovereignty; among sects, among Jews, Pagans, Christians, heretics, are wars, frequent wars, some for the truth, some for falsehood contending.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:157
verses.text: Not yet then is this fulfilled, "He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth;" but haply it shall be fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:158
verses.text: Or is it now also fulfilled? In some it is fulfilled; in the wheat it is fulfilled, in the tares it is not yet fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:159
verses.text: What is this then, "He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth"? Wars He calleth whereby it is warred against God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:160
verses.text: But who warreth against God? Ungodliness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:161
verses.text: And what to God can ungodliness do? Nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:162
verses.text: What doth an earthen vessel dashed against the rock, however vehemently dashed? With so much greater harm to itself it cometh, with how much the greater force it cometh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:163
verses.text: These wars were great, frequent were they.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:164
verses.text: Against God fought ungodliness, and earthen vessels were dashed in pieces, even men by presuming on themselves, by too much prevailing by their own strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:165
verses.text: This is that, the shield whereof Job also named concerning one ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:166
verses.text: "He runneth against God, upon the stiff neck of his shield".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:167
verses.text: What is, "upon the stiff neck of his shield"? Presuming too much upon his own protection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:168
verses.text: Were they such who said, "God is our refuge and strength, a Helper in tribulations which have found us out too much"? or in another Psalm, "For I will not trust in my bow, neither shall my sword save me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:169
verses.text: When one learneth that in himself he is nothing, and help in himself has none, arms in him are broken in pieces, wars are made to cease.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:170
verses.text: Such wars then destroyed that Voice of the Most High out of His holy clouds, whereby the earth was moved, and the kingdoms were bowed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:171
verses.text: These wars hath He made to cease unto the end of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:172
verses.text: "He shall break the bow, and dash in pieces the arms, and burn the shield with fire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:173
verses.text: Bow, arms, shield, fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:174
verses.text: The bow is plots; arms, public warfare; shields, vain presuming of self-protection: the fire wherewith they are burned, is that whereof the Lord said, "I am come to send fire on the earth;" of which fire saith the Psalm, "There is nothing hid from the heat thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:175
verses.text: This fire burning, no arms of ungodliness shall remain in us, needs must all be broken, dashed in pieces, burned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:176
verses.text: Remain thou unharmed, not having any help of thine own; and the more weak thou art, having no arms thine own, the more He taketh thee up, of whom it is said, "The God of Jacob is our taker up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:177
verses.text: But when God taketh us up, doth He send us away unarmed? He armeth us, but with other arms, arms Evangelical, arms of truth, continence, salvation, faith, hope, charity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:178
verses.text: These arms shall we have, but not of ourselves: but the arms which of ourselves we had, are burnt up: yet if by that fire of the Holy Spirit we are kindled, whereof it is said, "He shall burn the shields with fire;" thee, who didst wish to be powerful in thyself, hath God made weak, that He may make thee strong in Him, because in thyself thou wast made weak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:179
verses.text: What then followeth? "Be still".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:180
verses.text: To what purpose? "And see that I am God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:181
verses.text: That is, Not ye, but I am God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:182
verses.text: I created, I create anew; I formed, I form anew; I made, I make anew.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:183
verses.text: If thou couldest not make thyself, how canst thou make thyself anew? This seeth not the contentious tumult of man's soul; to which contentious tumult is it said, "Be still".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:184
verses.text: That is, restrain your souls from contradiction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:185
verses.text: Do not argue, and, as it were, arm against God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:186
verses.text: Else yet live thy arms, not yet burned up with fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:187
verses.text: But if they are burned, "Be still;" because ye have not wherewith to fight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:188
verses.text: But if ye be still in yourselves, and from Me seek all, who before presumed on yourselves, then shall ye "see that I am God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:189
verses.text: "I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:190
verses.text: Just before I said, by the name of earth is signified the nation of the Jews, by the name of sea the other nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:191
verses.text: The mountains were carried into the heart of the sea; the nations are troubled, the kingdoms are bowed; the Most High gave His Voice, and the earth was moved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:192
verses.text: "The Lord of Hosts is with us, the God of Jacob is our taker up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:193
verses.text: Miracles are done among the heathen, full filled is the faith of the heathen; burned are the arms of human presumption.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:194
verses.text: Still are they, in tranquillity of heart, to acknowledge God the Author of all their gifts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:195
verses.text: And after this glorifying, doth He yet desert the people of the Jews? of which saith the Apostle, "I say unto you, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened unto Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:196
verses.text: That is, until the mountains be carried hither, the clouds rain here, the Lord here bows the kingdoms with His thunder, "until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:197
verses.text: And what thereafter? "And so all Israel shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 46:198
verses.text: Therefore, here too observing the same order, "I will be exalted" (saith He) "among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth;" that is, both in the sea, and in the earth, that now might all say what followeth: "the God of Jacob is our taker up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:1
verses.text: Psalm XLVII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:2
verses.text: The title of the Psalm goeth thus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:3
verses.text: "To the end: for the sons of Korah: a Psalm of David himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:4
verses.text: These sons of Korah have the title also of some other Psalms, and indicate a sweet mystery, insinuate a great Sacrament: wherein let us willingly understand ourselves, and let us acknowledge in the title us who hear, and read, and as in a glass set before us behold who we are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:5
verses.text: The sons of Korah, who are they?Haply the sons of the Bridegroom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:6
verses.text: For the Bridegroom was crucified in the place of Calvary.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:7
verses.text: Recollect the Gospel, where they crucified the Lord, and ye will find Him crucified in the place of Calvary.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:8
verses.text: Furthermore, they who deride His Cross, by devils, as by beasts, are devoured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:9
verses.text: For this also a certain Scripture signified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:10
verses.text: When God's Prophet Elisha was going up, children called after him mocking, "Go up thou bald head, Go up thou bald head:" but he, not so much in cruelty as in mystery, made those children to be devoured by bears out of the wood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:11
verses.text: If those children had not been devoured, would they have lived even till now? Or could they not, being born mortal, have been taken off by a fever? But so in them had no mystery been shown, whereby posterity might be put in fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:12
verses.text: Let none then mock the Cross of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:13
verses.text: The Jews were possessed by devils, and devoured; for in the place of Calvary, crucifying Christ, and lifting on the Cross, they said as it were with childish sense, not understanding what they said, "Go up, thou bald head".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:14
verses.text: For what is, "Go up"? "Crucify Him, Crucify Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:15
verses.text: For childhood is set before us to imitate humility, and childhood is set before us to beware of foolishness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:16
verses.text: To imitate humility, childhood was set before us by the Lord, when He called children to Him, and because they were kept from Him, He said, "Suffer them to come unto Me, for of such is the Kingdom of Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 47:17
verses.text: The example of childhood is set before us to beware of foolishness by the Apostle, "Brethren, be not children in understanding:" and again he proposeth it to imitate, "Howbeit in ma.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:1
verses.text: lice be ye children, that in understanding ye may be men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:2
verses.text: "For the sons of Korah" the Psalm is sung; for Christians then is it sung.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:3
verses.text: Let us hear it as sons of the Bridegroom, whom senseless children crucified in the place of Calvary.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:4
verses.text: For they earned to be devoured by beasts; we to be crowned by Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:5
verses.text: For we acknowledge the humility of our Lord, and of it are not ashamed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:6
verses.text: We are not ashamed of Him called in mystery "the bald" (Calvus), from the place of Calvary.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:7
verses.text: For on the very Cross whereon He was insulted, He permitted not our forehead to be bald; for with His own Cross He marked it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:8
verses.text: Finally, that ye may know that these things are said to us, see what is said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:9
verses.text: "O clap your hands, all ye nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:10
verses.text: Were the people of the Jews all the nations? No, but blindness in part is happened to Israel, that senseless children might cry, "Calve," "Calve;" and so the Lord might be crucified in the place of Calvary, that by His Blood shed He might redeem the Gentiles, and that might be fulfilled which saith the Apostle, "Blindness in part is happened unto Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:11
verses.text: Let them insult, then, the vain, and foolish, and senseless, and say, "Calve," "Calve;" but ye redeemed by His Blood which was shed in the place of Calvary, say, "O clap your hands, all ye nations;" because to you hath come down the Grace of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:12
verses.text: "O clap your hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:13
verses.text: What is "O clap"? Rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:14
verses.text: But wherefore with the hands? Because with good works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:15
verses.text: Do not rejoice with the mouth while idle with the hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:16
verses.text: If ye rejoice, "clap your hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:17
verses.text: The hands of the nations let Him see, who joys hath deigned to give them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:18
verses.text: What is, the hands of the nations? The acts of them doing good works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:19
verses.text: "O clap your hands, all ye nations: shout unto God with the voice of triumph".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:20
verses.text: Both with voice and with hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:21
verses.text: If with the voice only it is not well, because the hands are slow; if only with the hands it is not well, because the tongue is mute.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:22
verses.text: Agree together must the hands and tongue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:23
verses.text: Let this confess, these work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:24
verses.text: "Shout unto God with the voice of triumph".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:25
verses.text: "For the Lord Most High is terrible".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:26
verses.text: The Most High in descending made like one ludicrous, by ascending into Heaven is made terrible.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:27
verses.text: "A great King over all the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:28
verses.text: Not only over the Jews; for over them also He is King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:29
verses.text: For of them also the Apostles believed and of them many thousands of men sold their goods, and laid the price at the Apostles' feet, and in them was fulfilled what in the title of the Cross was written, "The King of the Jews".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:30
verses.text: For He is King also of the Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:31
verses.text: But "of the Jews" is little "O clap your hands, all ye nations: for God is the King of all the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:32
verses.text: For it sufficeth not Him to have under Him one nation: therefore such great price gave He out of His side, as to buy the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:33
verses.text: "He hath subdued the people under us, and the nations under our feet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:34
verses.text: Which subdued, and to whom? Who are they that speak? Haply Jews? Surely, if Apostles; surely, if Saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:35
verses.text: For under these God hath subdued the people and the nations, that to-day are they honoured among the nations, who by their own citizens earned to be slain: as their Lord was slain by His citizens, and is honoured among the nations; was crucified by His own, is adored by aliens, but those by a price made His own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:36
verses.text: For therefore bought He us, that aliens from Him we might not be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:37
verses.text: Thinkest thou then these are the words of Apostles, "He hath subdued the people under us, and the nations under our feet"? I know not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:38
verses.text: Strange that Apostles should speak so proudly, as to rejoice that the nations were put under their feet, that is, Christians under the feet of Apostles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:39
verses.text: For they rejoice that we are with them under the feet of Him who died for us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:40
verses.text: For under Paul's feet ran they, who would be of Paul, to whom He said, "Was Paul crucified for you?" What then here, what are we to understand? "He hath subdued the people under us, and the nations under our feet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:41
verses.text: All pertaining to Christ's inheritance are among "all the nations," and all not pertaining to Christ's inheritance are among "all the nations:" and ye see so exalted in Christ's Name is Christ's Church, that all not yet believing in Christ lie under the feet of Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:42
verses.text: For what numbers now run to the Church; not yet being Christians, they ask aid of the Church; to be succoured by us temporally they are willing, though eternally to reign with us as yet they are unwilling.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:43
verses.text: When all seek aid of the Church, even they who are not yet in the Church, hath He not "subdued the people under us, and the nations under our feet"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:44
verses.text: "He hath chosen an inheritance for us, the excellency of Jacob, whom He loved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:45
verses.text: A certain beauty of Jacob He hath chosen for our inheritance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:46
verses.text: Esau and Jacob were two brothers; in their mother's womb both struggled, and by this struggle their mother's bowels were shaken; and while they two were yet therein, the younger was elected and preferred to the elder, and it was said, "Two peoples are in thy womb, and the elder shall serve the younger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:47
verses.text: Among all nations is the elder, among all nations the younger; but the younger is in good Christians, elect, godly, faithful; the elder in the proud, unworthy, sinful, stubborn, defending rather than confessing their sins: as was also the very people of the Jews, "being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:48
verses.text: But for that it is said, "The elder shall serve the younger;" it is manifest that under the godly are subdued the ungodly, under the humble are subdued the proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:49
verses.text: Esau was born first, and Jacob was born last; but he who was last born, was preferred to the first-born, who through gluttony lost his birthright.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:50
verses.text: So thou hast it written, He longed for the pottage, and his brother said to him, If thou wilt that I give it thee, give me thy birthright.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:51
verses.text: He loved more that which carnally he desired, than that which spiritually by being born first he had earned: and he laid aside his birthright, that he might eat lentils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:52
verses.text: But lentils we find to be the food of the Egyptians, for there it abounds in Egypt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:53
verses.text: Whence is so magnified the lentil of Alexandria, that it comes even to our country, as if here grew no lentil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:54
verses.text: Therefore by desiring Egyptian food he lost his birthright.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:55
verses.text: So also the people of the Jews, of whom it is said, "in their hearts they turned back again into Egypt".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:56
verses.text: They desired in a manner the lentil, and lost their birthright.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:57
verses.text: "God is gone up with jubilation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:58
verses.text: Even He our God, the Lord Christ, is gone up with jubilation; "the Lord with the sound of a trumpet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:59
verses.text: "Is gone up:" whither, save where we know? Whither the Jews followed Him not, even with their eyes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:60
verses.text: For exalted on the Cross they mocked Him, ascending into Heaven they did not see Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:61
verses.text: "God hath gone up with jubilation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:62
verses.text: What is jubilation, but admiration of joy which cannot be expressed in words? As the disciples in joy admired, seeing Him go into Heaven, whom they had mourned dead; truly for the joy, words sufficed not: remained to jubilate what none could express.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:63
verses.text: There was also the voice of the trumpet, the voice of Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:64
verses.text: For it is said, "Lift up thy voice like a trumpet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:65
verses.text: Angels preached the ascension of the Lord: they saw the Disciples, their Lord ascending, tarrying, admiring, confounded, nothing speaking, but in heart jubilant: and now was the sound of the trumpet in the clear voice of the Angels, "Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into Heaven? this is Jesus".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:66
verses.text: As if they knew not that it was the same Jesus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:67
verses.text: Had they not just before seen Him before them? Had they not heard Him speaking with them? Nay, they not only saw the figure of Him present, but handled also His limbs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:68
verses.text: Of themselves then knew they not, that it was the same Jesus? But they being by very admiration, from joy of jubilation, as it were transported in mind, the Angels said, "that same is Jesus".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:69
verses.text: As though they said, If ye believe Him, this is that same Jesus, whom crucified, your feet stumbled, whom dead and buried, ye thought your hope lost.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:70
verses.text: Lo, this is the same Jesus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:71
verses.text: He hath gone up before you, "He shall so come in like manner as ye have seen Him go into Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:72
verses.text: His Body is removed indeed from your eyes, but God is not separated from your hearts: see Him going up, believe on Him absent, hope for Him coming; but yet through His secret Mercy, feel Him present.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:73
verses.text: For He who ascended into Heaven that He might be removed from your eyes, promised unto you, saying, "Lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:74
verses.text: Justly then the Apostle so addressed us, "The Lord is at hand; be careful for nothing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:75
verses.text: Christ sitteth above the Heavens; the Heavens are far off, He who there sitteth is near.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:76
verses.text: "Sing praises to our God, sing praises".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:77
verses.text: Whom as Man mocked they, who from God were alienated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:78
verses.text: "Sing praises to our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:79
verses.text: For He is not Man only, but God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:80
verses.text: Man of the seed of David, God the Lord of David, of the Jews having flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:81
verses.text: "Whose" (saith the Apostle) "are the fathers, of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:82
verses.text: Of the Jews then is Christ, but according to the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:83
verses.text: But who is this Christ who is of the Jews according to the flesh? "Who is over all, God blessed for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:84
verses.text: God before the flesh, God in the flesh, God with the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:85
verses.text: Nor only God before the flesh, but God before the earth whence flesh was made; nor only God before the earth whereof flesh was made, but even God before the Heaven which was first made; God before the day which was first made; God before Angels; the same Christ is God: for "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:86
verses.text: "For God is the King of all the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:87
verses.text: What? And before was He not God of all the earth? Is He not God of both heaven and earth, since by Him surely were all things made? Who can say that He is not his God? But not all men acknowledged Him their God; and where He was acknowledged, there only, so to say, He was God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:88
verses.text: "In Judah is God known".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:89
verses.text: Not yet was it said to the sons of Korah, "O clap your hands, all ye nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:90
verses.text: For that God known in Judah, is King of all the earth: now by all He is acknowledged, for that is fulfilled which Isaiah saith, "He is thy God who hath delivered thee, the God of the whole earth shall He be called".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:91
verses.text: "Sing ye praises with understanding".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:92
verses.text: He teacheth us and warneth us to sing praises with understanding, not to seek the sound of the ear, but the light of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:93
verses.text: The Gentiles, whence ye were called that ye might be Christians, adored gods made with hands, and sang praises to them, but not with understanding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:94
verses.text: If they had sung with understanding, they had not adored stones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:95
verses.text: When a man sensible sang to a stone insensible, did he sing with understanding? But now, brethren, we see not with our eyes Whom we adore, and yet correctly we adore Much more is God commended to us, that with our eyes we see Him not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:96
verses.text: If with our eyes we saw Him, haply we might despise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:97
verses.text: For even Christ seen, the Jews despised; unseen, the Gentiles adored.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:98
verses.text: "God shall reign over all nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:99
verses.text: Who reigned over one nation, "shall reign" (saith He) "over all nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:100
verses.text: When this was said, God reigned over one nation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:101
verses.text: It was a prophecy, the thing was not yet shown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:102
verses.text: Thanks be to God, we now see fulfilled what before was prophesied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:103
verses.text: A written promise God sent unto us before the time, the time fulfilled He hath repaid us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:104
verses.text: "God shall reign over all nations," is a promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:105
verses.text: "God sitteth upon His Holy Seat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:106
verses.text: What then was promised to come, now being fulfilled, is acknowledged and held.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:107
verses.text: "God sitteth upon His Holy Seat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:108
verses.text: What is His Holy Seat? Haply saith one, The Heavens, and he understandeth well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:109
verses.text: For Christ hath gone up, as we know, with the Body, wherein He was crucified, and sitteth at the right hand of the Father; thence we expect Him to come to judge the quick and the dead "God sitteth upon His Holy Seat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:110
verses.text: The Heavens are His Holy Seat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:111
verses.text: Wilt thou also be His Seat? think not that thou canst not be; prepare for Him a place in thy heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:112
verses.text: He cometh, and willingly sitteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:113
verses.text: The same Christ is surely "the Power of God, and the Wisdom of God:" and what saith the Scripture of Wisdom Herself? The soul of the righteous is the seat of Wisdom If then the soul of the righteous is the seat of Wisdom, be thy soul righteous, and thou shalt be a royal seat of Wisdom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:114
verses.text: And truly, brethren, all men who live well, who act well, converse in godly charity, doth not God sit in them, and Himself command? Thy soul obeyeth God sitting in it, and itself commandeth the members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:115
verses.text: For thy soul commandeth thy members, that so may move the foot, the hand, the eye, the ear, and itself commandeth the members as its servants, but yet itself serveth its Lord sitting within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:116
verses.text: It cannot well rule its inferior, unless its superior it have not disdained to serve.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:117
verses.text: "The princes of the peoples are gathered together unto the God of Abraham".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:118
verses.text: The God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob True it is, God said this, and thereupon the Jews prided themselves, and said, "We are Abraham's children;" priding themselves in their father's name, carrying his flesh, not holding his faith; by seed cleaving to Him, in manners degenerating.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:119
verses.text: But the Lord, what said He to them so priding themselves? "If ye are Abraham's children, do the works of Abraham".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:120
verses.text: Again"The princes of the peoples:" the princes of the nations: not the princes of one people, but the princes of all people have "gathered together unto the God of Abraham".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:121
verses.text: Of these princes was that Centurion too, of whom but now when the Gospel was read ye heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:122
verses.text: For he was a Centurion having honour and power among men, he was a prince among the princes of the peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:123
verses.text: Christ coming to him, he sent his friends to meet Him, nay unto Christ truly passing over to him he sent his friends, and asked that He would heal his servant who was dangerously sick.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:124
verses.text: And when the Lord would come, he sent to Him this message: "I am not worthy that Thou shouldest enter under my roof, but say in a word only, and my servant shall be healed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:125
verses.text: "For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:126
verses.text: See how he kept his rank! first he mentioned that he was under another, and afterwards that another was under him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:127
verses.text: I am under authority, and I am in authority; both under some I am, and over some I am.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:128
verses.text: As though he said, If I being set under authority command those who are under me, Thou who art set under no man's authority, canst not Thou command Thy creature, since all things were made by Thee, and without Thee was nothing made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:129
verses.text: "Say," then, said he, "in a word, and my servant shall be healed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:130
verses.text: For I am not worthy that Thou shouldest enter under my roof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:131
verses.text: Admiring at his faith, Jesus reprobates the Jews' misbelief.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:132
verses.text: For sound to themselves they seemed, whereas they were dangerously sick, when their Physician not knowing they slew.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:133
verses.text: Therefore when He reprobated, and repudiated their pride what said he? "I say unto you, that many shall come from the east and west," not belonging to the kindred of Israel: many shall come to whom He said, "O clap your hands, all ye nations;" "and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:134
verses.text: Abraham begat them not of his own flesh; yet shall they come and sit down with him in the kingdom of heaven, and be his sons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:135
verses.text: Whereby his sons? Not as born of his flesh, but by following his faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:136
verses.text: "But the children of the kingdom," that is, the Jews, "shall be cast into outer darkness, there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:137
verses.text: They shall be condemned to outer darkness who are born of the flesh of Abraham, and they shall sit down with him in the kingdom of heaven, who have imitated Abraham's faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:138
verses.text: And what they who belonged to the God of Abraham? "For the mighty gods of the earth are greatly lifted up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:139
verses.text: They who were gods, the people of God, the vineyard of God, whereof it is said, "Judge betwixt Me and My vineyard," shall go into outer darkness, shall not sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, are not gathered unto the God of Abraham.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:140
verses.text: Wherefore? "For the mighty gods of the earth;" they who were mighty gods of the earth, presuming upon earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:141
verses.text: What earth? Themselves; for every man is earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:142
verses.text: For to man was it said, "Dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:143
verses.text: But man ought to presume upon God, and thence to hope for help, not from himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:144
verses.text: For the earth raineth not upon itself, nor shineth for itself; but as the earth from heaven expecteth rain and light, so man from God ought to expect mercy and truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:145
verses.text: They then, "the mighty gods of the earth, were greatly lifted up," that is, greatly prided themselves: they thought no physician necessary for themselves, and therefore remained in their sickness, and by their sickness were brought down even to death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 48:146
verses.text: The natural branches were broken off that the humble wild olive tree might be grafted in Hold we fast then, brethren, humility, charity, godliness: since we are called, on their proving reprobate, even by their example let us fear to pride ourselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:1
verses.text: Psalm XLVIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:2
verses.text: The title of this Psalm is, "A song of praise, to the sons of Korah, on the second day of the week".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:3
verses.text: Concerning this what the Lord deigneth to grant receive ye like sons of the firmament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:4
verses.text: For on the second day of the week, that is, the day after the first which we call the Lord's day, which also is called the second week-day, was made the firmament of HeavenThe second day of the week then we ought not to understand but of the Church of Christ: but the Church of Christ in the Saints, the Church of Christ in those who are written in Heaven, the Church of Christ in those who to this world's temptations yield not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:5
verses.text: For they are worthy of the name of "firmament".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:6
verses.text: The Church of Christ, then, in those who are strong, of whom saith the Apostle, "We that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak,"  is called the firmament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:7
verses.text: Of this it is sung in this Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:8
verses.text: Let us hear, acknowledge, associate, glory, reign.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:9
verses.text: For Her called firmament, hear also in the Apostolic Epistles, "the pillar and firmament of the truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:10
verses.text: "Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:11
verses.text: That is, "in the city of our God, in His holy mountain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:12
verses.text: This is the city set upon an hill, which cannot be hid: this is the candle which is not hidden under a bushel, to all known, to all proclaimed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:13
verses.text: Yet are not all men citizens thereof, but they in whom "great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:14
verses.text: What then is that city: let us see whether perhaps, since it is said, "In the city of our God, in His holy mountain," we ought not to enquire for this mountain where also we may be heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:15
verses.text: What then is that mountain, brethren? One is it with great care to be enquired for, with great solicitude investigated, with labour also to be occupied and ascended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:16
verses.text: But if in any part of the earth it is, what shall we do? Shall we go abroad out of our own country, that to that mountain we may arrive? Nay, then we are abroad, when in it we are not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:17
verses.text: For that is our city, if we are members of the King, who is the head of the same city.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:18
verses.text: For there was a certain corner-stone contemptible, whereat the Jews stumbled, cut out of a certain mountain without hands, that is, coming of the kingdom of the Jews without hands, because human operation went not with Mary of whom was born Christ But if that stone, when the Jews stumbled thereat, had remained there, thou hadst not had whither to ascend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:19
verses.text: But what was done? What saith the prophecy of Daniel? What but that the stone grew, and became a great mountain? How great? So that it filled the whole face of the earth By growing, then, and by filling the whole face of the earth, that mountain came to us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:20
verses.text: Why then seek we the mountain as though absent, and not as being present ascend to it; that in us the Lord may be "great, and greatly to be praised"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:21
verses.text: Further,when he had said, "in the city of our God, in His holy mountain," what added he? "Spreading abroad the joys of the whole earth, the mountains of Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:22
verses.text: Sion is one mountain, why then "mountains"? Is it that to Sion belonged also those which came from the other side, so as to meet together on the Corner Stone, and become two walls, as it were two mountains, one of the circumcision, the other of the uncircumcision; one of the Jews, the other of the Gentiles: no longer adverse, although diverse, because from different sides, now in the corner not even diverse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:23
verses.text: "For He is our peace, who hath made both one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:24
verses.text: The same Corner Stone "which the builders rejected, is become the Head Stone of the corner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:25
verses.text: The mountain hath joined in itself two mountains; one house there is, and two houses; two, because coming from different sides; one, because of the Corner Stone, wherein both are joined together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:26
verses.text: Hear also this, "the mountains of Sion: the sides of the North are the city of the great King".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:27
verses.text: See the Gentiles; "the sides of the North:" the sides of the North are joined to the city of the great King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:28
verses.text: The North is wont to be contrary to Sion: Sion forsooth is in the South, the North over against the South.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:29
verses.text: Who is the North, but He who said, "I will sit in the sides of the North, I will be like the Most High"? The devil had held dominion over the ungodly, and possessed the nations serving images, adoring demons; and all whatsoever there was of human kind anywhere throughout the world, by cleaving to Him, had become North.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:30
verses.text: But since He who binds the strong man, taketh away his goods, and maketh them His own goods; men delivered from infidelity and superstition of devils, believing in Christ, are fitted on to that city, have met in the corner that wall that cometh from the circumcision, and that was made the city of the great King, which had been the sides of the North.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:31
verses.text: Therefore also in another Scripture is it said, "Out of the North come clouds of golden colour: great is the glory and honour of the Almighty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:32
verses.text: For great is the glory of the physician, when from being despaired of the sick recovers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:33
verses.text: "Out of the North come clouds," and not black clouds, not dark clouds, not lowering, but "of golden colour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:34
verses.text: Whence but by grace illumined through Christ? See, "the sides of the North are the city of the great King".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:35
verses.text: Let the Psalm then follow, and say, "God shall be known in her houses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:36
