verses.text: Now in her "houses," because of the mountains, because of the two walls, because of the two sons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:37
verses.text: "God shall be known in her houses," but he commendeth grace, therefore he added, "when He shall take her up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:38
verses.text: For what would that city have been, unless He had taken her up? Would it not immediately have fallen, unless it had such foundation? For "other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:39
verses.text: Let none then glory in his own merits; but "he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:40
verses.text: The Lord then hath taken up this city, and is known therein, that is, His grace is known in that city: for whatever that city hath, which glorieth in the Lord, it hath not of itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:41
verses.text: For because of this it is said, "What hast thou that thou didst not receive?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:42
verses.text: "For, lo, the kings of the earth are gathered together".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:43
verses.text: Behold now those sides of the North, see how they come, see how they say, "Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord: and He will teach us His way, and we will walk in it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:44
verses.text: "And have come together in one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:45
verses.text: In what one, but that "corner-stone"? "They saw it, and so they marvelled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:46
verses.text: After their marvelling at the miracles and glory of Christ, what followed? "They were troubled, they were moved" , "trembling took hold upon them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:47
verses.text: Whence took trembling hold upon them, but from the consciousness of sins? Let them run then, king after a king; kings, let them acknowledge the King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:48
verses.text: Therefore saith He elsewhere, "Yet have I been set by Him a King upon His holy hill of Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:49
verses.text: A King then was heard of, set up in Sion, to Him were delivered possessions even to the uttermost parts of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:50
verses.text: Kings behoved to fear lest they should lose the kingdom, lest the kingdom be taken from them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:51
verses.text: As wretched Herod feared, and for the Child slew the children But fearing to lose his kingdom, he deserved not to know the King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:52
verses.text: Would that he too had adored the King with the Magi: not by ill-seeking the kingdom, slain the Innocents, and perished guilty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:53
verses.text: For as concerning him, he destroyed the Innocents: but as for Christ, even a Child, the children dying for Him did He crown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:54
verses.text: Therefore behoved kings to fear when it was said, "Yet have I been set a King by Him upon His holy hill of Sion," and inheritance to the uttermost parts of the earth shall He give Him, who set Him up King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:55
verses.text: Thence also this is said to them, "Understand now therefore, O ye kings; be instructed, ye judges of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:56
verses.text: Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice unto Him with trembling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:57
verses.text: And what did they? "There pains as of a woman in travail".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:58
verses.text: What are the pains "as of a woman in travail," but the pangs of a penitent? See the same conception of pain and travail: "Of Thy fear" (saith Isaiah) "we have conceived, we have travailed of the Spirit of salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:59
verses.text: So then the kings conceived from the fear of Christ, that by travailing they brought forth salvation by believing on Him whom they had feared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:60
verses.text: "There pains as of a woman in travail:" when of travail thou hearest, expect a birth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:61
verses.text: The old man travaileth, but the new man is born.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:62
verses.text: "With a strong wind Thou shalt break the ships of Tarshish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:63
verses.text: Briefly understood, this is, Thou shalt overthrow the pride of the nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:64
verses.text: But where in this history is mentioned the overthrowing of the pride of the nations? Because of "the ships of Tarshish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:65
verses.text: Learned men have enquired for Tarshish a city, that is, what city was signified by this name: and to some it has seemed that Cilicia is called Tarshish, because its metropolis is called Tarsus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:66
verses.text: Of which city was the Apostle Paul, being born in Tarsus of Cilicia But some have understood by it Carthage, being haply sometimes so named, or in some language so signified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:67
verses.text: For in the Prophet Isaiah it is thus found: "Howl, ye ships of Carthage".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:68
verses.text: But in Ezekiel by some interpreters the word is translated Carthage, by some Tarshish: and from this diversity it can be understood that the same which was called Carthage, is called Tharsus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:69
verses.text: But it is manifest, that in the beginning of its reign Carthage flourished with ships, and so flourished, that among other nations they excelled in trafficking and navigation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:70
verses.text: For when Dido, flying from her brother, escaped to the parts of Africa, where she built Carthage, the ships which had been prepared for commerce in his country she had taken with her for her flight, the princes of the country consenting to it; and the same ships also when Carthage was built failed not in traffic.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:71
verses.text: And hence that city became too proud, so that justly by its ships may be understood the pride of the nations, presuming on things uncertain, as on the breath of the winds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:72
verses.text: Now let none presume on full sails, and on the seeming fair state of this life, as of the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:73
verses.text: Be our foundation in Sion: there ought we to be stablished, not to be "carried about with every wind of doctrine".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:74
verses.text: Whoso then by the uncertain things of this life had been puffed up, let them be overthrown, and be all the pride of the nations subjected to Christ, who shall "with a strong wind break all the ships of Tarshish:" not of any city, but of "Tarshish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:75
verses.text: How "with a strong wind"? With very strong fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:76
verses.text: For so all pride feared Him that shall judge, as on Him humble to believe, lest Him exalted it should fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:77
verses.text: "As we have heard, so have we seen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:78
verses.text: Blessed Church! at one time thou hast heard, at another time thou hast seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:79
verses.text: She heard in promises, seeth in performance: heard in Prophecy, seeth in the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:80
verses.text: For all things which are now fulfilled were before prophesied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:81
verses.text: Lift up thine eyes then, and stretch them over the world; see now His "inheritance even to the uttermost parts of the earth:"  see now is fulfilled what was said, "All kings shall fall down before Him: all nations shall serve Him:" see fulfilled what was said, "Be Thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, and Thy glory above all the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:82
verses.text: See Him whose feet and hands were pierced with nails, whose bones hanging on the tree were counted, upon whose vesture lots were cast: see reigning whom they saw hanging; see sitting in Heaven whom they despised walking on earth: see thus fulfilled, "All the ends of the earth shall remember, and turn to the Lord, and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:83
verses.text: Seeing all this, exclaim with joy, "As we have heard, so have we seen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:84
verses.text: Justly the Church herself is so called out of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:85
verses.text: They to whom the Prophets were not sent, first heard and understood the Prophets: they who first heard not, afterwards hearing marvelled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:86
verses.text: They remained behind to whom they were sent, carrying the books, understanding not the truth: having the tables of the Testament, and not holding the inheritance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:87
verses.text: But we,"As we have heard, so have we seen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:88
verses.text: And where hearest thou? where seest thou? "In the city of the Lord of Hosts, in the city of our God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:89
verses.text: God hath founded it for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:90
verses.text: Let not heretics insult, divided into parties, let them not exalt themselves who say, "Lo, here is Christ, or lo, there".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:91
verses.text: Whoso saith, "Lo, here is Christ, or lo, there," inviteth to parties.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:92
verses.text: Unity God promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:93
verses.text: The kings are gathered together in one, not dissipated through schisms.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:94
verses.text: But haply that city which hath held the world, shall sometime be overthrown? Far be the thought! "God hath founded it for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:95
verses.text: If then God hath founded it for ever, why fearest thou lest the firmament should fall?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:96
verses.text: "We have received Thy mercy, O God, in the midst of Thy people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:97
verses.text: Who have received, and where received? Hath not the same Thy people received Thy mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:98
verses.text: If Thy people hath received Thy mercy, how then, "in the midst of Thy people"? As if they who received were one party, they in the midst of whom they received another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:99
verses.text: A great mystery, but yet well known.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:100
verses.text: When hence also, that is, out of these verses, hath been extracted and brought forth what ye know; it will be not ruder, but sweeter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:101
verses.text: Now forsooth all are reckoned the people of God, who carry His Sacraments, but not all belong to His Mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:102
verses.text: All forsooth receiving the Sacrament of the Baptism of Christ, are called Christians, but not all live worthily of that Sacrament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:103
verses.text: There are some of whom saith the Apostle, "Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:104
verses.text: Yet on account of this form of godliness they are named among God's people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:105
verses.text: As to the floor, until the corn is threshed, belongs not the wheat only, but the chaff.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:106
verses.text: But will it also belong to the garner? In the midst then of an evil people is a good people, which hath received the Mercy of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:107
verses.text: He liveth worthily of the Mercy of God who heareth, and holdeth, and doeth what the Apostle saith, "We beseech you that ye receive not the Grace of God in vain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:108
verses.text: Whoso then receiveth not the Grace of God in vain, the same receiveth not only the Sacrament, but also the Mercy of God as well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:109
verses.text: So those who have the Sacraments, and have not good manners, are both said to be of God, and not of God; are both said to be His, and to be strangers: His because of His own Sacraments, strangers because of their own vice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:110
verses.text: So also strange daughters: daughters, because of the form of godliness; strange, because of their loss of virtue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:111
verses.text: Be the lily there; let it receive the Mercy of God: hold fast the root of a good flower, be not ungrateful for soft rain coming from heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:112
verses.text: Be thorns ungrateful, let them grow by the showers: for the fire they grow, not for the garner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:113
verses.text: In the midst of Thy people not receiving Thy mercy, we have received Thy mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:114
verses.text: For "He came unto His own, and His own received Him not," yet, in the midst of them, "as many as received Him, to them gave He power to become the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:115
verses.text: For when he had said, "We have received Thy mercy in the midst of Thy people," he signified that there is a people not receiving the mercy of God, in the midst of whom some do receive the mercy of God: and then lest it should occur to men that there are so few, as to be nearly none, how did He console them in the words following? "According to Thy Name, O God, so is Thy praise unto the ends of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:116
verses.text: What is this? That is, as Thou art known through all the earth, so Thou art also praised through all the earth, nor are there wanting who now praise Thee through all the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:117
verses.text: But they praise Thee who live well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:118
verses.text: For, "According to Thy Name, O God, so is Thy praise," not in a part, but "unto the ends of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:119
verses.text: "Thy right hand is full of righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:120
verses.text: That is, many are they also who shall stand at Thy right hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:121
verses.text: Not only shall they be many who shall stand at Thy left hand, but there also shall be a full heap set at Thy right hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:122
verses.text: "Let mount Zion rejoice, and the daughters of Judah be glad, because of Thy judgments, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:123
verses.text: O mount Zion, O daughters of Judah, ye labour now among tares, among chaff, among thorns ye labour: yet be glad because of God's judgments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:124
verses.text: God erreth not in judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:125
verses.text: Live ye separate, though separate ye were not born; not vainly hath a voice gone forth from your mouth and heart, "Destroy not my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloody men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:126
verses.text: He shall winnow with such art, carrying in His hand a fan, that not one grain of wheat shall fall into the heap of chaff prepared to be burned, nor one beard of chaff pass to the heap to be laid up in the garner Be glad, O ye daughters of Judaea, because of the judgments of God that erreth not, and do not yet judge rashly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:127
verses.text: To you let it belong to collect, to Him let it belong to separate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:128
verses.text: But think not that the "daughters of Judah" are Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:129
verses.text: Judah is confession; all the sons of confession are all the sons of Judah.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:130
verses.text: For "salvation is of the Jews," is nothing else than that Christ is of the Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:131
verses.text: This saith also the Apostle, "He is not a Jew which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh: but he is a Jew which is one inwardly, and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter, whose praise is not of men, but of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:132
verses.text: Be such a Jew; glory in the circumcision of the heart, though thou hast not the circumcision of the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:133
verses.text: Let the daughters of Judah be glad, because of Thy judgments, O Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:134
verses.text: "Walk about Zion, and embrace her".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:135
verses.text: Be it said to them who live ill, in the midst of whom is the people, which hath received the mercy of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:136
verses.text: In the midst of you is a people living well, "Walk about Zion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:137
verses.text: But how? "embrace her".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:138
verses.text: Not with scandals, but with love go round about her: that so those who live well in the midst of you ye may imitate, and by imitation of them, be incorporate with Christ, whose members they are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:139
verses.text: "Walk about Zion, go round about her: speak in the towers thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:140
verses.text: In the height of her bulwarks, set forth the praises thereof.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:141
verses.text: "Set your hearts upon her might".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:142
verses.text: Not that ye may have the form of godliness, deny the power thereof, but, "upon her might set your hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:143
verses.text: Speak ye in her towers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:144
verses.text: What is the might of this city? Whoso would understand the might of this city, let him understand the force of love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:145
verses.text: That is a virtue which none conquereth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:146
verses.text: Love's flame no waves of the world, no streams of temptation, extinguish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:147
verses.text: Of this it is said, "Love is strong as death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:148
verses.text: For as when death cometh, it cannot be resisted; by whatever arts, whatever medicines, you meet it; the violence of death can none avoid who is born mortal; so against the violence of love can the world do nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:149
verses.text: For from the contrary the similitude is made of death; for as death is most violent to take away, so love is most violent to save.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:150
verses.text: Through love many have died to the world, to live to God; by this love inflamed, the martyrs, not pretenders, not puffed up by vain-glory, not such as they of whom it is written, "Though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing," but men whom truly a love of Christ and of the truth led on to this passion; what to them were the temptations of the tormentors? Greater violence had the eyes of their weeping friends, than the persecutions of enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:151
verses.text: For how many were held by their children, that they might not suffer? to how many did their wives fall upon their knees, that they might not be left widows? How many have their parents forbidden to die; as we know and read in the Passion of the Blessed Perpetua! All this was done; but tears, however great, and with whatever force flowing, when did they extinguish the ardour of love? This is the might of Sion, to whom elsewhere it is said, "Peace be within thy walls, and prosperity within thy palaces".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:152
verses.text: What here understand we, "Set your hearts upon her might, and distribute her houses"? That is, distinguish house from house.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:153
verses.text: Do not confound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:154
verses.text: For there is a house having the form of godliness, and not having godliness; but there is a house having both form and godliness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:155
verses.text: Distribute, confound not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:156
verses.text: But then ye distribute and confound not, when ye "set your hearts upon her might;" that is, when through love ye are made spiritual.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:157
verses.text: Then ye will not judge rashly, then ye will see that the evil harms not the good as long as we are in this floor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:158
verses.text: "Distribute her houses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:159
verses.text: There can be also another understanding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:160
verses.text: The two houses, one coming of the circumcision, one of the uncircumcision, it is commanded the Apostles to distribute.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:161
verses.text: For when Saul was called, and made the Apostle Paul, agreeing in unity with his fellow Apostles, he so with thorn determined, that they should go to the circumcision, he to the uncircumcision.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:162
verses.text: By that dispensation of their Apostleship, they distributed the houses of the city of the great King; and meeting in the corner, divided the Gospel in dispensation, in love united it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:163
verses.text: And truly this is rather to be understood; for it followeth and showeth that it is here said to the preachers, "distribute her houses: that ye may tell it to the generation following:" that is, that even to us, who were to come after them, their dispensation of the Gospel should reach: For not for those only they laboured, with whom they lived in the earth; nor the Lord for those Apostles only to whom He deigned to show Himself alive after His Resurrection, but for us also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:164
verses.text: For to them He spake, and signified us when He spake, "Lo, I am with you alway, even to the end of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:165
verses.text: Were they then to be here alway, even to the end of the world? Also He said, "Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on Me through their word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:166
verses.text: Therefore He considereth us, because He suffered on account of us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:167
verses.text: Justly then it is said, "That ye may tell it to the generation following".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:168
verses.text: Tell what? "For this is God, even our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:169
verses.text: The earth was seen, the earth's Creator was not seen; the flesh was held, God in the flesh was not acknowledged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:170
verses.text: For the flesh was held by those from whom had been taken the same flesh, for of the seed of Abraham was the Virgin Mary.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:171
verses.text: At the flesh they stayed, the Divinity they did not understand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:172
verses.text: O Apostles, O mighty city, preach thou on the towers, and say, "This is God, even our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:173
verses.text: So, even so as He was despised, as He lay a stone before the feet of the stumbling, that He might humble the hearts of the confessing; even so, "This is God, even our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:174
verses.text: Certainly He was seen, as was said, "Afterward did He show Himself upon earth, and conversed with men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:175
verses.text: "This is God, even our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:176
verses.text: He is also Man, and who is there will know Him? "This is God, even our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:177
verses.text: But haply for a time as the false gods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:178
verses.text: For because they can be called gods, but cannot be so, for a time they are even called so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:179
verses.text: For what saith the Prophet, or what warneth He to be said to them? This shall ye say to them, "The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth, even they shall perish from the earth, and from those that are under the heavens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:180
verses.text: He is not such a god: for our God is above all gods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:181
verses.text: Above all what gods? "For all the gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:182
verses.text: The same then is our God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:183
verses.text: "This is God, even our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:184
verses.text: For how long? "For ever and ever: He shall rule us for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:185
verses.text: If He is our God, He is also our King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:186
verses.text: He protecteth us, being our God, lest we die; He ruleth us, being our King, lest we fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:187
verses.text: But by ruling us He doth not break us; for whom He ruleth not, He breaketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:188
verses.text: "Thou shalt rule them," saith He, "with a rod of iron, and dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:189
verses.text: But there are whom He ruleth not; these He spareth not, as a potter's vessel dashing them in pieces.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:190
verses.text: By Him then let us wish to be ruled and delivered, "for He is our God for ever and ever, and He shall rule us for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 49:191
verses.text: Contents   Part  Part.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:1
verses.text: Psalm XLIX  The First Part.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:2
verses.text: "Hear ye these things, all ye nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:3
verses.text: Not then you only who are here.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:4
verses.text: For of what power is our voice so to cry out, as that all nations may hear? For Our Lord Jesus Christ hath proclaimed it through the Apostles, hath proclaimed it in so many tongues that He sent; and we see this Psalm, which before was only repeated in one nation, in the Synagogue of the Jews, now repeated throughout the whole world, throughout all Churches; and that fulfilled which is here spoken of, "Hear ye these words, all ye nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:5
verses.text: Of whom ye are: "With ears ponder, all ye that dwell in the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:6
verses.text: This He seemeth to have repeated a second time, lest to have said "hear," before, were too little.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:7
verses.text: What I say, he saith, "hear, with ears ponder," that is, hear not cursorily.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:8
verses.text: What is, "with ears ponder"? It is what the Lord said, "he that hath ears to hear, let him hear:"  for as all who were in His presence must have had ears, what ears did He require save those of the h eart, when He said, "he that hath ears to hear, let him hear"? The same ears also this Psalm doth smite.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:9
verses.text: "With ears ponder, all ye that dwell in the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:10
verses.text: Perhaps there is here some distinction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:11
verses.text: We ought not indeed to narrow our view, but there is no harm in explaining even this view of the sense.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:12
verses.text: Perhaps there is some difference between the saying, "all nations," and the saying, "all ye that dwell in the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:13
verses.text: For perchance he would have us understand the expression, "dwell in," with a further meaning, so as to take all nations for all the wicked, but the dwellers of the world all the just.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:14
verses.text: For he doth inhabit who is not held fast: but he that is occupied is inhabited, and doth not inhabit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:15
verses.text: Just as he doth possess whatever he hath, who is master of his property: but a master is one who is not held in the meshes of covetousness: while he that is held fast by covetousness is the possessed, and not the possessor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:16
verses.text: Therefore let even the ungodly hear: "Hear ye this, all ye nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:17
verses.text: Let the just also hear, who have not heard to no purpose, and who rather rule the world than are ruled by the world: "with ears ponder, all ye that dwell in the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:18
verses.text: And again he saith, "both all ye earthborn, and sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:19
verses.text: The expression "earthborn" he doth refer to sinners; the expression "sons of men" to the faithful and righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:20
verses.text: Ye see then that this distinction is observed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:21
verses.text: Who are the "earthborn"? The children of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:22
verses.text: Who are the children of the earth? They who desire earthly inheritances.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:23
verses.text: Who are the "sons of men"? They who appertain to the Son of Man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:24
verses.text: We have already before explained this distinction to your Sanctity,  and have concluded that Adam was a man, but not the son of man; that Christ was the Son of Man, but was God also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:25
verses.text: For whosoever pertain to Adam, are "earthborn:" whosoever pertain to Christ, are "sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:26
verses.text: Nevertheless, let all hear, I withhold my discourse from no one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:27
verses.text: If one is "earthborn," let him hear, because of the judgment: another is a "son of man," let him hear for the kingdom's sake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:28
verses.text: "The rich and poor together".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:29
verses.text: Again, the same words are repeated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:30
verses.text: The expression "rich" refers to the "earthborn;" but the word "poor" to the "sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:31
verses.text: By the "rich" understand the proud, by the "poor" the humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:32
verses.text: He saith in another Psalm, "The poor shall eat and be satisfied".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:33
verses.text: How hath he commended the poor? "The poor shall eat and be satisfied".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:34
verses.text: What eat they? That Food which the faithful know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:35
verses.text: How shall they be satisfied? By imitating the Passion of their Lord, and not without cause receiving their recompense.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:36
verses.text: "The poor shall eat and be satisfied, and they shall praise the Lord who seek Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:37
verses.text: What of the rich? Even they eat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:38
verses.text: But how eat they? "All the rich upon the earth have eaten and worshipped".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:39
verses.text: He said not, "Have eaten and are satisfied;" but, "have eaten and worshipped".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:40
verses.text: They worship God indeed, but they will not display brotherly humaneness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:41
verses.text: These eat and worship; those eat and are filled: yet both eat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:42
verses.text: Of the eater what he eateth is required: let him not be forbidden by the distributor to eat, but let him be admonished to fear him who doth require his account.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:43
verses.text: Let these words then be heard by sinners and righteous, nations, and those who inhabit the world, "earthborn and sons of men, the rich and the poor together:" not divided, not separated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:44
verses.text: That is for the time of the harvest to do, the hand of the winnower will effect that Now together let rich and poor hear, let goats and sheep feed in the same pasture, until He come who shall separate the one on His right hand, the other on His left Let them all hear together the teacher, lest separated from one another they hear the voice of the Judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:45
verses.text: And what is it they are now to hear? "My mouth shall speak of wisdom, and the meditation of my heart understanding".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:46
verses.text: And this repetition is perhaps made, lest perchance if he had said only "my mouth," thou shouldest suppose that one spake to thee who had understanding but in his lips.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:47
verses.text: For many have understanding in their lips, but have not in their heart, of whom the Scripture saith, "This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:48
verses.text: What saith he then who speaketh to thee? when he hath said, "My mouth shall speak of wisdom," in order that thou mayest know that what is poured forth from the mouth floweth from the bottom of the heart, he hath added, "And the meditation of my heart of understanding".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:49
verses.text: "I will incline mine ear to the parable, I will show my proposition upon the harp".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:50
verses.text: And why "to a parable"? Because "now we see through a glass darkly," as saith the Apostle; "whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:51
verses.text: For our vision is not yet that face to face, where there are no longer parables, where there no longer are riddles and comparisons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:52
verses.text: Whatever now we understand we behold through riddles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:53
verses.text: A riddle is a dark parable which it is hard to understand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:54
verses.text: Howsoever a man may cultivate his heart and apply himself to apprehend mysteries, so long as we see through the corruption of this flesh, we see but in part.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:55
verses.text: But as He was seen by those who believed, and by those who crucified Him, when He was judged; so will He be seen, when He shall have begun to be judge, both by those whom He shall condemn, and by those whom He shall crown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:56
verses.text: But that vision of divinity, which He hath promised to them that love Him, when He saith, "He that loveth Me shall be loved of My Father, and he that loveth Me keepeth My commandments, and I will love him, and will manifest Myself to him:" this the ungodly shall not see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:57
verses.text: This manifestation is in a certain way familiar: He keepeth it for His own, He will not show it to the ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:58
verses.text: Of what sort is the vision itself? Of what sort is Christ? Equal to the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:59
verses.text: Of what sort is Christ? "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:60
verses.text: For this vision we sigh now, and groan so long as we sojourn here; to this vision we shall be brought home at the last, this vision now we see but darkly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:61
verses.text: If then we see now darkly, let us "incline our ear to the parable," and then let us "show our proposition upon the harp:" let us hear what we say, do what we enjoin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:62
verses.text: And what hath he said? "And wherefore shall I fear in the evil day? The iniquity of my heel shall compass me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:63
verses.text: He beginneth something obscurely.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:64
verses.text: Therefore he ought the rather to fear if the iniquity of his heel shall compass him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:65
verses.text: Nay, for let not man fear, he saith, who hath not power to escape.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:66
verses.text: For example, he who feareth death, what shall he do to escape death? Let him tell me how he is to escape what Adam oweth, he who is born of Adam.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:67
verses.text: But let him consider that he is born of Adam, and hath followed Christ, and ought to pay what Adam oweth, and obtain what Christ hath promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:68
verses.text: Therefore, he who feareth death can no wise escape: but he who feareth the damnation which the ungodly shall hear, "Go ye into everlasting fire," hath an escape.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:69
verses.text: Let him not fear then.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:70
verses.text: For why should he fear? Will the iniquity of his heel compass him? If then he avoid "the iniquity of his heel," and walk in the ways of God, he shall not come to the evil day: the evil day, the last day, shall not be evil to him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:71
verses.text: Now while they live, let them take heed to themselves, let them put away iniquity from their heel: let them walk in that way, let them walk in the way of which He saith Himself, "I am the way, the truth, and the life:" and let them not fear in the evil day, for He giveth them safety who became "The Way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:72
verses.text: Therefore let them avoid the iniquity of their heel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:73
verses.text: With the heel a man slippeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:74
verses.text: Let your Love observe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:75
verses.text: What was said by God to the Serpent? "She shall mark thy head, and thou shalt mark her heel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:76
verses.text: The devil marketh thy heel, in order that when thou slippest he may overthrow thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:77
verses.text: He marketh thy heel, do thou mark his head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:78
verses.text: What is his head? The beginning of an evil suggestion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:79
verses.text: When he beginneth to suggest evil thoughts, then do thou thrust him away before pleasure ariseth, and consent followeth; and so shalt thou avoid his head, and he shall not grasp thy heel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:80
verses.text: But wherefore said He this to Eve? Because through the flesh man doth slip.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:81
verses.text: Our flesh is an Eve within us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:82
verses.text: "He that loveth his wife," he saith, "loveth himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:83
verses.text: What meaneth "himself"? He continueth, and saith, "For no man ever yet hath hated his own flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:84
verses.text: Because then the devil would make us slip through the flesh, just as he made that man Adam to slip, through Eve; Eve is bidden to mark the head of the devil, because the devil marketh her heel "If then the iniquity of our heel shall compass us, why fear we in the evil day," since being converted to Christ we are able not to do iniquity; and there will be nothing to compass us, and we shall joy and not sorrow in the last day?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:85
verses.text: But who are they whom the "iniquity of their heel shall compass"? "They who trust in their virtue, and in the abundance of their riches do glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:86
verses.text: Therefore such sins will I avoid, and the "iniquity of my heel" shall never compass me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:87
verses.text: What is avoiding such sins? Let us not trust in our own virtue, let us not glory in the abundance of our own riches, but let us glory in Him who hath promised to us, being humble, exaltation, and hath threatened condemnation to men exalted; and then iniquity of our heel shall never compass us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:88
verses.text: There are some who rely on their friends, others rely on their virtue, others on their riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:89
verses.text: This is the presumption of mankind which relieth not on God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:90
verses.text: He hath spoken of virtue, he hath spoken of riches, he speaketh of friends.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:91
verses.text: "Brother redeemeth not, shall man redeem?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:92
verses.text: Dost thou expect that man shall redeem thee from the wrath to come? If brother redeem thee not, shall man redeem thee? Who is the brother, who if He hath not redeemed thee, no man will redeem? It is He who said after His resurrection, "Go, tell My brethren".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:93
verses.text: Our Brother He hath willed to be: and when we say to God, "Our Father," this is manifested in us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:94
verses.text: For he that saith to God, "Our Father;" saith to Christ, "Brother".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:95
verses.text: Therefore let him that hath God for his Father and Christ for his Brother, not fear in the evil day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:96
verses.text: "For the iniquity of his heel shall not compass him;" for he relieth not on his virtue, nor glorieth in the abundance of his riches, nor vaunteth himself of his powerful friends.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:97
verses.text: Let him rely on Him who died for him, that he might not die eternally: who for his sake was humbled, in order that he might be exalted; who sought him ungodly, in order that He might be sought by him faithful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:98
verses.text: Therefore if He redeem not, shall man redeem? Shall any man redeem, if the Son of man redeem not? If Christ redeem not, shall Adam redeem? "Brother redeemeth not, shall man redeem?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:99
verses.text: "He shall not give to God his propitiation, and the price of the redemption of his soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:100
verses.text: He trusteth in his virtue, and in the abundance of his riches doth glory, who "shall not give to God his propitiation:" that is, satisfaction whereby he may prevail with God for his sins: "nor the price of the redemption of his soul," who relieth on his virtue, and on his friends, and on his riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:101
verses.text: But who are they that give the price of the redemption of their souls? They to whom the Lord saith, "Make to yourselves friends of the Mammon of unrighteousness, that they may receive you into everlasting habitations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:102
verses.text: They give the price of the redemption of their soul who cease not to do almsdeeds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:103
verses.text: So those whom the Apostle chargeth by Timothy he would not have to be proud, lest they should glory in the abundance of their riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:104
verses.text: Lastly, what they possessed he would not have to grow old in their hands: but that something should be made of it to be for the price of the redemption of their souls.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:105
verses.text: For he saith, "Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not high-minded: nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:106
verses.text: And as if they had said, "What shall we then make of our riches?" he continueth, "Let them be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate," and they will not lose that.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:107
verses.text: How know we? Hear what followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:108
verses.text: "Let them lay up for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on the true life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:109
verses.text: So shall they give the price of the redemption of their soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:110
verses.text: And our Lord counselleth this: "Make for yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where thief approacheth not, neither moth corrupteth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:111
verses.text: God would not have thee lose thy wealth, but He hath given thee counsel to change the place thereof.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:112
verses.text: Let your love understand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:113
verses.text: Suppose thy friend were just now to enter thy house, and find thou hadst placed thy store of grain in a damp place, and he knew the natural proneness of grain to decay, which thou perchance knewest not, he would give thee counsel of this sort, saying, "Brother, thou art losing what with great toil thou hast gathered, thou hast placed it in a damp place, in a few days this grain will decay".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:114
verses.text: "And what am I to do, brother? "Raise it into a higher place".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:115
verses.text: Thou wouldest hearken to thy friend suggesting that thou shouldest raise grain from a lower to a higher chamber, and dost thou not hearken to Christ charging thee to lift thy treasure from earth to heaven, where not what thou keepest in store may be paid to thee, but that thou mayest keep in store earth, mayest receive heaven, mayest keep in store things mortal, mayest receive things everlasting, that while thou lendest Christ to receive at thy hands but a small loan upon earth, He may repay thee a great recompense in Heaven? Nevertheless, they whom "the iniquity of their heel shall compass," because they trust in their virtue, and in the abundance of their riches do glory, and rely on human friends who are able to help them in nothing, "shall not give to God their propitiation, and the price of the redemption of their souls".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:116
verses.text: And what hath he said of such a man? "Yea, he hath laboured for ever, and shall live till the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:117
verses.text: His labour shall be without end, his life shall have an end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:118
verses.text: Wherefore saith he, "He shall live till the end"? Because such men think life to be nought but daily enjoyments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:119
verses.text: So when many poor and needy men of our times, unstable, and not looking to what God doth promise them for their labours, see rich men in daily feastings, in the splendour and glitter of gold and of silver, they say what? "These are the only people; they really live!" This is a saying, be it said no longer: we both warn you, and it remains to warn you, that it be said by fewer persons than it would be said, if we had not warned you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:120
verses.text: For we do not presume to say that we so say these words, as that it be not said, but that it be said by fewer persons: for it will be said even unto the end of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:121
verses.text: It is too little that he saith, "he liveth;" he addeth and saith, he thundereth, thinkest thou that he alone liveth? Let him live! his life will be ended: because he giveth not the price of the redemption of his soul, his life will end, his labour will not end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:122
verses.text: "He laboured for ever, and shall live till the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:123
verses.text: How shall he live till the end? As he lived that was "clothed with purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day," who, being proud and puffed up, spurned the man full of sores lying before his gate, whose sores the dogs licked, and who longed for the crumbs which fell from his table.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:124
verses.text: What did those riches profit him? Both changed places: the one was borne from the rich man's gate into Abraham's bosom, the other from his rich feasts was cast into the fire; the one was in peace, the other burned; the one was sated, the other thirsted; the one had laboured till the end, but he lived for ever; the other had lived till the end, but he laboured for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:125
verses.text: And what did it profit the rich man, who asked, while lying in torments in hell, that a drop of water should be poured upon his tongue from the finger of Lazarus, saying, "For I am burning here in this flame," and it was not granted to him? One longed for the drop from the finger, as the other had for the crumbs from the rich man's table; but the labour of the one is ended, and the life of the other is ended: the labour of this is for ever, the life of that is for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:126
verses.text: We who labour perchance here on the earth, have not our life here: and shall not be so placed hereafter, for our life shall be Christ for ever: while they who "will" have their life here, shall labour for ever and live till the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:127
verses.text: "For he shall not see death, though he shall have seen wise men dying".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:128
verses.text: The man who laboured for ever and shall live till the end, "shall not see death, though he shall have seen wise men dying".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:129
verses.text: What is this? He shall not comprehend what death is, whenever he shall have seen wise men dying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:130
verses.text: For he saith to himself, "this fellow, for all he was wise and dwelled with wisdom and worshipped God with piety, is he not dead? Therefore I will enjoy myself while I live; for if they that are wise in other respects, could do anything, they would not have died".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:131
verses.text: Just as the Jews saw Christ hanging on the Cross and despised Him, saying, "If this Man were the Son of God, He would come down from the Cross:" not seeing what death is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:132
verses.text: If they had seen what death is; if they had seen, I say He died for a time, that He might live again for ever: they lived for a time, that they might die for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:133
verses.text: But because they saw Him dying, they saw not death, that is to say, they understood not what was very death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:134
verses.text: What say they even in Wisdom? "Let us condemn Him with a most shameful death, for by His own sayings He shall be respected;" for if he is indeed the Son of God, He will deliver Him from the hands of His adversaries: He will not suffer His Son to die, if He is truly His Son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:135
verses.text: But when they saw themselves insulting Him upon the Cross, and Him not descending from the Cross, they said, He was indeed but a Man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:136
verses.text: Thus was it spoken: and surely He could have come down from the Cross, He that could rise again from the tomb: but He taught us to bear with those who insult us; He taught us to be patient of the tongues of men, to drink now the cup of bitterness, and afterwards to receive everlasting salvation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:137
verses.text: "The imprudent and unwise shall perish together".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:138
verses.text: Who is "the imprudent"? He that looketh not out for himself for the future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:139
verses.text: Who is "the unwise"? He that perceiveth not in what evil case he is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:140
verses.text: But do thou perceive in what evil case thou art now, and look out that thou be in a good case for the future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:141
verses.text: By perceiving in what evil case thou art, thou wilt not be unwise: by looking out for thyself for the future, thou wilt not be imprudent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:142
verses.text: Who is he that looketh out for himself? That servant to whom his master gave what he should expend, and afterwards said to him, "Thou canst not be my steward, give an account of thy stewardship;" and who answered, "What shall I do? I cannot dig, to beg I am ashamed;" had, nevertheless, by even his master's goods made to himself friends, who might receive him when he was put out of his stewardship.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:143
verses.text: Now he cheated his master in order that he might get to himself friends to receive him: fear not thou lest thou be cheating, the Lord Himself exhorteth thee to do so: He saith Himself to thee, "Make to thyself friends of the mammon of unrighteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:144
verses.text: Perhaps what thou hast got, thou hast gotten of unrighteousness: or perhaps this very thing is unrighteousness, that thou hast and another hath not, thou aboundest and another needeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:145
verses.text: Of this mammon of unrighteousness, of these riches which the unrighteous call riches, make to thyself friends, and thou shalt be prudent: thou art gaining for thyself, and art not cheating.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:146
verses.text: For now thou seemest to lose it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:147
verses.text: Wilt thou lose it if thou place it in a treasury? For boys, my brethren, no sooner find some money, wherewith to buy something, than they put it in a money-box, which they open not until afterwards: do they, because they see not what they have got, on that account lose it? Fear not: boys put in a money-box, and are secure: dost thou place it in the hand of Christ, and fear? Be prudent, and provide for thyself against the future in Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:148
verses.text: Be therefore prudent, copy the ant, as saith the Scripture: "Store in summer, lest thou hunger in winter;" the winter is the last day, the day of tribulation; the winter is the day of offences and of bitterness: gather what may be there for thee for the future: but if thou doest not so, thou wilt perish both imprudent and unwise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:149
verses.text: But that rich man too died, and a like funeral was made for him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:150
verses.text: See to what men have brought themselves: they regard not what a wicked life he led while he lived, but what pomp followed him when he died! O happy he, whom so many lament! But the other lived in such sort, that few lament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:151
verses.text: For all ought to lament a man living so sadly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:152
verses.text: But there is the funeral train; he is received in a costly tomb, he is wound in costly robes, he is buried in perfumes and spices.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:153
verses.text: Secondly, what a monument he hath! How marbled! Doth he live in that same monument? He is therein dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:154
verses.text: Men deeming these to be good things, have strayed from God, and have not sought the true good things, and have been deceived with the false.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:155
verses.text: To this end see what followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:156
verses.text: He who gave not the price of the redemption of his soul, who understood not death, because he saw wise men dying, he became imprudent and unwise, in order that he might die with them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:157
verses.text: And how shall they perish, who "shall leave their riches to aliens"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:158
verses.text: But do those same aliens indeed serve them who are called their own? Hear in what they serve them, observe how they are ridiculed: why hath he said, "to strangers"? Because they can do them no good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:159
verses.text: Nevertheless, wherein do they seem to themselves to do good? "And their tombs shall be their house for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:160
verses.text: Now because these tombs are erected, the tombs are a house.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:161
verses.text: For often thou hearest a rich man saying, I have a house of marble which I must quit, and I think not for myself of an eternal house, where I shall alway be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:162
verses.text: When he thinketh to make for himself a monument of marble or of sculpture, he is deeming as it were of an eternal house: as if therein this rich man would abide! If he would abide there, he would not burn in hell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:163
verses.text: We must consider that the place where the spirit of an evil doer abideth, is not where the mortal body is laid: but "their tombs shall be their house for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:164
verses.text: Their dwelling places are from generation to generation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:165
verses.text: "Dwelling places" are wherein they abode for a season: "house" is wherein they will abide as it were for ever, that is to say, their tombs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:166
verses.text: Thus they leave their dwelling places, where they abode while they lived, to their families, and they pass as it were to everlasting houses, to their tombs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:167
verses.text: What profit to them are "their dwelling places, from generation to generation"? Now suppose a generation and generation are sons, grandsons there will be, and great grandsons; what do their dwelling places, what do they profit them? What? Hear: "they shall invoke their names in their lands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:168
verses.text: What is this? They shall take bread and wine to their tombs, and there they shall invoke the names of the dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:169
verses.text: Dost thou consider how loudly was invoked the name of the rich man after his death, when men drank them drunk at his monument, and there came down not one drop upon his own burning tongue? Men minister to their own belly, not to the ghosts of their friends.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:170
verses.text: The souls of the dead nothing doth reach, but what they have done of themselves while alive: but if they have done nought of themselves while alive, nothing doth reach them dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:171
verses.text: But what do the survivors? They will but "invoke their names in their lands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:172
verses.text: "And man though he was in honour perceived not, he was compared to the beasts without sense, and was made like to them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:173
verses.text: They ought, on the contrary, to have made ready for themselves an eternal house in good works, to have made ready for themselves everlasting life, to have sent before them expenditure, to have followed their works, to have ministered to a needy companion, to have given to him with whom they were walking, not to have despised Christ covered with sores before their gate, who hath said, "Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these My brethren, ye have done it unto Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:174
verses.text: However, "man being in honour hath not understood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:175
verses.text: What is, "being in honour"? Being made after the image and likeness of God, man is preferred to beasts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:176
verses.text: For God hath not so made man as He made a beast: but God hath made man for beasts to minister to: is it to his strength then, and not to his understanding? Nay.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:177
verses.text: But he "understood not;" and he who was made after the image of God, "is compared to the beasts without sense, and is made like unto them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:178
verses.text: Whence it is said elsewhere, "Be ye not like to horse and mule, in which there is no understanding".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:179
verses.text: "This their own way is an offence to them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:180
verses.text: Be it an offence to them, not to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:181
verses.text: But when will it be so to thee too? If thou thinkest such men to be blessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:182
verses.text: If thou perceivest that they be not blessed, their own way will be an offence to themselves; not to Christ, not to His Body, not to His members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:183
verses.text: "And afterwards they shall bless with their mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:184
verses.text: What meaneth, "Afterwards they shall bless with their mouth"? Though they have become such, that they seek nothing but temporal goods, yet they become hypocrites: and when they bless God, with lips they bless, and not with heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:185
verses.text: Christians like these, when to them eternal life is commended, and they are told, that in the name of Christ they ought to be despisers of riches, do make grimaces in their hearts: and if they dare not do it with open face, lest they blush, or lest they should be rebuked by men, yet they do it in heart, and scorn; and there remaineth in their mouth blessing, and in their heart cursing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:186
verses.text: The Second Part.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:187
verses.text: "Like sheep laid in hell, death is their shepherd".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:188
verses.text: Whose? Of those whose way is a stumbling-block to themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:189
verses.text: Whose? Of those who mind only things present, while they think not of things future: of those who think not of any life, but of that which must be called death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:190
verses.text: Not without cause, then, like sheep in hell, have they death to their shepherd.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:191
verses.text: What meaneth, "they have death to their shepherd"? For is death either some thing or some power? Yea, death is either the separation of the soul from the body, or a separation of the soul from God, and that indeed which men fear is the separation of the soul from the body: but the real death, which men do not fear, is the separation of the soul from God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:192
verses.text: And ofttimes when men fear that which doth separate the soul from the body, they fall into that wherein the soul is separated from God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:193
verses.text: This then is death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:194
verses.text: But how is "death their shepherd"? If Christ is life, the devil is death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:195
verses.text: But we read in many places in Scripture, how that Christ is life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:196
verses.text: But the devil is death, not because he is himself death, but because through him is death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:197
verses.text: For whether that (death) wherein Adam fell was given man to drink by the persuasion of him: or whether that wherein the soul is separated from the body, still they have him for the author thereof, who first falling through pride envied him who stood, and overthrew him who stood with an invisible death, in order that he might have to pay the visible death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:198
verses.text: They who belong to him have death to their shepherd: but we who think of future immortality, and not without reason do wear the sign of the Cross of Christ on the forehead, have no shepherd but life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:199
verses.text: Of unbelievers death is the shepherd, of believers life is the shepherd.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:200
verses.text: If then in hell are the sheep, whose shepherd is death, in heaven are the sheep, whose shepherd is life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:201
verses.text: What then? Are we now in heaven? In heaven we are by faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:202
verses.text: For if not in heaven, where is the "Lift up your heart"? If not in heaven, whence with the Apostle Paul, "For our conversation is in heaven"? In body we walk on earth, in heart we dwell in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:203
verses.text: We dwell there, if thither we send anything which holdeth us there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:204
verses.text: For no one dwelleth in heart, save where thought is: but there his thought is, where his treasure is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:205
verses.text: He hath treasured on earth, his heart doth not withdraw from earth: he hath treasured in heaven, his heart from heaven doth not come down: for the Lord saith plainly, "Where thy treasure is, there will thy heart be also".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:206
verses.text: They, then, whose shepherd is death, seem to flourish for a time, and the righteous to labour: but why? Because it is yet night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:207
verses.text: What meaneth, it is night? The merits of the righteous appear not, and the felicity of the unrighteous hath, as it were, a name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:208
verses.text: So long as it is winter, grass appeareth more verdant than a tree.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:209
verses.text: For grass flourisheth through the winter, a tree is as it were dry through the winter: when in summer time the sun hath come forth with greater heat, the tree, which seemed dry through the winter, is bursting with leaves, and putteth forth fruits, but the grass withereth: thou wilt see the honour of the tree, the grass is dried.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:210
verses.text: So also now the righteous labour, before that summer cometh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:211
verses.text: There is life in the root, it doth not yet appear in the branches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:212
verses.text: But our root is love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:213
verses.text: And what saith the Apostle? That we ought to have our root above, in order that life may be our shepherd, because our dwelling ought not to quit heaven, because in this earth we ought to walk as if dead; so that living above, below we may be dead; not so as that being dead above, we may live below.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:214
verses.text: Our labour shall appear in the morning, and there shall be fruit in the morning: so that they that now labour shall hereafter reign, and they that now boast them and are proud, shall hereafter be brought under.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:215
verses.text: For what followeth? "Like sheep laid in hell, death is their shepherd; and the righteous shall reign over them in the morning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:216
verses.text: Endure thou the night, yearn for the morning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:217
verses.text: Think not because the night hath life, the morning too hath not life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:218
verses.text: Doth then he that sleepeth live, and he that riseth live not? Is not he that sleepeth more like death? And who are they that sleep? They whom the Apostle Paul rouseth, if they choose but to awake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:219
verses.text: For to certain he saith, "Awake, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:220
verses.text: They then that are lightened by Christ watch now, but the fruit of their watchings appeareth not yet: in the morning it shall appear, that is, when doubtful things of this world shall have passed away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:221
verses.text: For these are very night: for do they not appear to thee like darkness?But they on whom men have trampled, and who were ridiculed for believing, shall hear from Life Itself, whom they have for shepherd, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive the kingdom which was prepared for you from the foundation of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:222
verses.text: Therefore the righteous "shall reign over them," not now, but "in the morning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:223
verses.text: Let no one say, Wherefore am I a Christian? I rule no one, I would rule the wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:224
verses.text: Be not in haste, thou shalt reign, but "in the morning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:225
verses.text: "And the help of them shall grow old in hell from their glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:226
verses.text: Now they have glory, in hell they shall grow old.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:227
verses.text: What is "the help of them"? Help from money, help from friends, help from their own might.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:228
verses.text: But when a man shall be dead, "in that day shall perish all his thoughts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:229
verses.text: How great glory he seemed to have among men, while he lived, so great oldness and decay of punishments shall he have, when he shall be dead in hell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:230
verses.text: "Nevertheless, God shall redeem my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:231
verses.text: Behold the voice of one hoping in the future: "Nevertheless, God shall redeem my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:232
verses.text: Perhaps it is the voice of one still wishing to be relieved from oppression.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:233
verses.text: Some one is in prison, he saith, "God shall redeem my soul:" some one is in bond, "God shall redeem my soul:" some one is suffering peril by sea, is being tossed by waves and raging tempests, what saith he? "God shall redeem my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:234
verses.text: They would be delivered for the sake of this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:235
verses.text: Not such is the voice of this man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:236
verses.text: Hear what followeth: "God shall redeem my soul from the hand of hell, when He shall have received me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:237
verses.text: He is speaking of this redemption, which Christ now showeth in Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:238
verses.text: For He hath descended into hell, and hath ascended into heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:239
verses.text: What we have seen in the Head we have found in the Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:240
verses.text: For what we have believed in the Head, they that have seen, have themselves told us, and by themselves we have seen: "For we are" all "one body".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:241
verses.text: But are they better that hear, we worse to whom it hath been told? Not so saith The Life Itself, Our Shepherd Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:242
verses.text: For He rebuketh a certain disciple of His, doubting and desiring to handle His scars, and when he had handled the scars and had cried out, saying, "My Lord and my God," seeing His disciple doubting, and looking to the whole world about to believe, "Because thou hast seen Me," He saith, "thou hast believed: blessed are they that see not, and believe".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:243
verses.text: "But God shall redeem my soul from the land of hell, when He hath received me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:244
verses.text: Here then what? Labour, oppression, tribulation, temptation: expect nothing else.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:245
verses.text: Where joy? In future hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:246
verses.text: Perchance thy heart saith, Wretch that I am, I suppose to no purpose I have believed, God doth not regard things human.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:247
verses.text: God therefore doth awaken us: and He saith what? "Fear not, though a man have become rich".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:248
verses.text: For why didst thou fear, because a man hath become rich? Thou didst fear that thou hadst believed to no purpose, that perchance thou shouldest have lost the labour for thy faith, and the hope of thy conversion: because perchance there hath come in thy way gain with guilt, and thou couldest have been rich, if thou hadst seized upon that same gain with the guilt, and neededst not have laboured; and thou, remembering what God hath threatened, hast refrained from guilt, and hast contemned the gain: thou seest another man that hath made gain by guilt, and hath suffered no harm; and thou fearest to be good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:249
verses.text: "Fear not," saith the Spirit of God to thee, "though a man shall have become rich".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:250
verses.text: Wouldest thou not have eyes but for things present? Things future He hath promised, who hath risen again; peace in this world, and repose in this life, He hath not promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:251
verses.text: Every man doth seek repose; a good thing he is seeking, but not in the proper region thereof he is seeking it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:252
verses.text: There is no peace in this life; in Heaven hath been promised that which on earth we are seeking: in the world to come hath been promised that which in this world we are seeking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:253
verses.text: "Fear not, though a man be made rich, and though the glory of his house be multiplied".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:254
verses.text: Wherefore "fear not"? "For when he shall die, he shall not receive anything".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:255
verses.text: Thou seest him living, consider him dying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:256
verses.text: Thou markest what he hath here, mark what he taketh with him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:257
verses.text: What doth he take with him? He hath store of gold, he hath store of silver, numerous estates, slaves: he dieth, these remain, he knoweth not for whom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:258
verses.text: For though he leaveth them for whom he will, he keepeth them not for whom he will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:259
verses.text: For many have gained even what was not left them, and many have lost what was left them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:260
verses.text: All these things then remain, and he taketh with him what? Perhaps some one saith, He taketh that with him in which he is wound, and that which is expended upon him for a costly and marble tomb, to erect a monument, this he taketh with him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:261
verses.text: I say, not even this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:262
verses.text: For these things are presented to him without his feeling them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:263
verses.text: If thou deckest a man sleeping and not awake, he hath the decorations with him on the couch: perhaps the decorations are resting upon the body of him as he lieth, and perhaps he seeth himself in tatters during sleep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:264
verses.text: What he feeleth is more to him than what he feeleth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:265
verses.text: Though even this when he shall have awaked will not be: yet to him sleeping, that which he saw in sleep was more than that which he felt not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:266
verses.text: Why then, brethren, should men say to themselves, Let money be spent at my death: why do I leave my heirs rich? Many things will they have of mine, let me too have something of my own for my body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:267
verses.text: What shall a dead body have? what shall rotting flesh have? what shall flesh not feeling have? If that rich man had anything, whose tongue was dry, then man hath something of his own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:268
verses.text: My brethren, do we read in the Gospel, that this rich man appeared in the fire with all-silken and fine-linen coverings? Was he of such sort in hell as he was in feastings at table? When he thirsted and desired a drop, all those things were not there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:269
verses.text: Therefore man carrieth not with him anything, nor doth the dead take with him that which the burial taketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:270
verses.text: For where feeling is, there is the man; where is no feeling, the man is not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:271
verses.text: There lieth fallen the vessel which contained the man, the house which held the man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:272
verses.text: The body let us call the house, the spirit let us call the inhabitant of the house.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:273
verses.text: The spirit is tormented in hell: what doth it profit him, that the body lieth in spices and perfumes, wound in costly linens? just as if the master of the house should be sent into banishment, and thou shouldest garnish the walls of his house.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:274
verses.text: He in banishment is in need, and doth faint with hunger, he scarce findeth to himself one hovel where he may snatch a sleep, and thou sayest, "Happy is he, for his house hath been garnished".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:275
verses.text: Who would not judge that thou wast either jesting or wast mad? Thou dost garnish the body, the spirit is tormented.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:276
verses.text: Give something to the spirit, and ye have given something to the dead man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:277
verses.text: But what wilt thou give him, when he desired one drop, and received not? For the man scorned to send before him anything.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:278
verses.text: Wherefore scorned? "because this their way is a stumbling-block to them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:279
verses.text: He minded not any but the present life, he thought not but how he might be buried, wound in costly vestments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:280
verses.text: His soul was taken from him, as the Lord saith: "Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be taken from thee, an d whose shall those things be which thou hast provided?" And that is fulfilled which this Psalm saith: "Fear not, though a man be made rich, and though the glory of his house be multiplied: for when he shall die he shall not receive anything, nor shall his glory descend together with him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:281
verses.text: Let your love observe: "For his soul shall be blessed in his life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:282
verses.text: As long as he lived he did well for himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:283
verses.text: This all men say, but say falsely.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:284
verses.text: It is a blessing from the mind of the blesser, not from the truth itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:285
verses.text: For what sayest thou? Because he ate and drank, because he did what he chose, because he feasted sumptuously, therefore he did well with himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:286
verses.text: I say, he did ill for himself.
