verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:287
verses.text: Not I say, but Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:288
verses.text: He did ill for himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:289
verses.text: For that rich man, when he feasted sumptuously every day, was supposed to do well with himself: but when he began to burn in hell, then that which was supposed to be well was found to be ill.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:290
verses.text: For what he had eaten with men above, he digested in hell beneath.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:291
verses.text: Unrighteousness I mean, brethren, on which he used to feast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:292
verses.text: He used to eat costly banquets with the mouth of flesh, with his heart's mouth he used to eat unrighteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:293
verses.text: What he ate with his heart's mouth with men above, this he digested amid those punishments in the places beneath.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:294
verses.text: And verily he had eaten for a time, he digested ill for everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:295
verses.text: Is then unrighteousness eaten? perhaps some one saith: what is it that he saith? Unrighteousness eaten? It is not I that say: hear the Scripture: "As a sour grape is vexation to the teeth, and smoke to the eyes, so is unrighteousness to them that use it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:296
verses.text: For he that shall have eaten unrighteousness, that is, he that shall have had unrighteousness wilfully, shall not be able to eat righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:297
verses.text: For righteousness is bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:298
verses.text: Who is bread? "I am the living bread which came down from heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:299
verses.text: Himself is the bread of our heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:300
verses.text: Is then even righteousness eaten? If it were not eaten, the Lord would not have said, "Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:301
verses.text: Therefore "since his soul shall be blessed in life," in life it "shall" be blessed, in death it shall be tormented.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:302
verses.text: "He shall confess to Thee, when Thou shalt have done him good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:303
verses.text: Be not of such sort, brethren: see ye how that to this end we say these words, to this end we sing, to this end we treat, to this end toil—do not these things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:304
verses.text: Your business doth prove you: sometimes in your business ye hear the truth, and ye blaspheme.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:305
verses.text: The Church ye blaspheme.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:306
verses.text: Wherefore? Because ye are Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:307
verses.text: "If so it be, I betake myself to Donatus's party: I will be a heathen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:308
verses.text: Wherefore? Because thou hast eaten bread, and the teeth are in pain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:309
verses.text: When thou sawest the bread itself, thou didst praise; thou beginnest to eat, and the teeth are in pain; that is, when thou wast hearing the Word of God thou didst praise: when it is said to thee, "Do this," thou blasphemest: do not so ill: say this, "The bread is good, but I cannot eat it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:310
verses.text: But now if thou seest with the eyes, thou praisest: when thou beginnest to close the teeth thou sayest, "Bad is this bread, and like him that made it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:311
verses.text: So it cometh to pass that thou confessest to God, when God doeth thee good and thou liest when thou singest, "I will alway bless God, His praise is ever in my mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:312
verses.text: How alway? If alway gain, alway He is blessed: if sometime there is loss, He is not blessed, but blasphemed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:313
verses.text: Forsooth thou blessest alway, forsooth His praise is ever in thy mouth! Thou wilt be such as just now he describeth: "He will confess to Thee, when Thou shalt have done him good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:314
verses.text: "He shall enter even unto the generations of his fathers" : that is, he shall imitate his fathers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:315
verses.text: For the unrighteous, that now are, have brothers, have fathers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:316
verses.text: Unrighteous men of old, are the fathers of the present; and they that are now unrighteous, are the fathers of unrighteous posterity: just as the fathers of the righteous, the righteous of old, are the fathers of the righteous that now are; and they that now are, are the fathers of them that are to be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:317
verses.text: The Holy Spirit hath willed to show that righteousness is not evil when men murmur against her: but these men have their father from the beginning, even to the generation of their fathers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:318
verses.text: Two men Adam begat, and in one was unrighteousness, in one was righteousness: unrighteousness in Cain, righteousness in Abel Unrighteousness seemed to prevail over righteousness, because Cain unrighteous slew Abel righteous in the night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:319
verses.text: Is it so in the morning? Nay, "but the righteous shall reign over them in the morning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:320
verses.text: The morning shall come, and it shall be seen where Abel is, and where Cain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:321
verses.text: So all men who are after Cain, and so all who are after Abel, even unto the end of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:322
verses.text: "He shall enter even unto the generations of his fathers: even to eternity he shall not see light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:323
verses.text: Because even when he was here, he was in darkness, taking pleasure in false goods, and not loving real goods: even so he shall go hence into hell: from the darkness of his dreams the darkness of torments shall receive him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:324
verses.text: Therefore, "even to eternity he shall not see light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:325
verses.text: But wherefore this? What he hath written in the middle of the Psalm, the same also he hath writ at the end: "Man, though he was in honour, understood not, was compared to the beasts without sense, and was made like to them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:326
verses.text: But ye, brethren, consider that ye be men made after the image and likeness of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:327
verses.text: The image of God is within, is not in the body; is not in these ears which ye see, and eyes, and nostrils, and palate, and hands, and feet; but is made nevertheless: wherein is the intellect, wherein is the mind, wherein the power of discovering truth, wherein is faith, wherein is your hope, wherein your charity, there God hath His Image: there at least ye perceive and see that these things pass away; for so he hath said in another Psalm, "Though man walketh in an image, yet he is disquieted in vain: he heapeth up treasures, and knoweth not for whom he shall gather them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:328
verses.text: Be not disquieted, for of whatsoever kind these things be, they are transitory, if ye are men who being in honour understand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 50:329
verses.text: For if being men in honour ye understand not, ye are compared to the beasts without sense, and are made like to them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:1
verses.text: Psalm L.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:2
verses.text: How much availeth the Word of God to us for the correction of our life, both regarding His rewards to be expected, and His punishments to be feared, let each one measure in himself; and let him put his conscience without deceit before His eyes, and not flatter himself in a danger so great: for ye see that even our Lord God Himself doth flatter no one: though He comforteth us by promising His blessings, and by strengthening our hope; yet them that live ill and despise His word He assuredly spareth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:3
verses.text: Let each one examine himself, while it is time, and let him see where he is, and either persevere in good, or be changed from evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:4
verses.text: For as he saith in this Psalm, not any man whatever nor any angel whatever, but, "The Lord, the God of gods, hath spoken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:5
verses.text: But in speaking, He hath done what? "He hath called the earth from the rising of the sun unto the going down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:6
verses.text: He that "hath called the world from the rising of the sun unto the going down," is Our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, "the Word made Flesh," in order that He might dwell in us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:7
verses.text: Our Lord Jesus Christ then is the "God of gods;" because by Himself were all things made, and without Himself was nothing made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:8
verses.text: The Word of God, if He is God, is truly the God of gods; but whether He be God the Gospel answereth, "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:9
verses.text: And if all things were made by Himself, as He saith in the sequel, then if any were made gods, by Himself were they made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:10
verses.text: For the one God was not made, and He is Himself alone truly God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:11
verses.text: But Himself the only God, Father and Son and Holy Ghost, is one God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:12
verses.text: But then who are those gods, or where are they, of whom God is the true God? Another Psalm saith, "God hath stood in the synagogue of gods, but in the midst He judgeth gods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:13
verses.text: As yet we know not whether perchance any gods be congregated in heaven, and in their  congregation, for this is "in the synagogue," God hath stood to judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:14
verses.text: See in the same Psalm those to whom he saith, "I have said, Ye are gods, and children of the Highest all; but ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:15
verses.text: It is evident then, that He hath called men gods, that are deified of His Grace, not born of His Substance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:16
verses.text: For He doth justify, who is just through His own self, and not of another; and He doth deify who is God through Himself, not by the partaking of another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:17
verses.text: But He that justifieth doth Himself deify, in that by justifying He doth make sons of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:18
verses.text: "For He hath given them power to become the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:19
verses.text: If we have been made sons of God, we have also been made gods: but this is the effect of Grace adopting, not of nature generating.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:20
verses.text: For the only Son of God, God, and one God with the Father, Our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, was in the beginning the Word, and the Word with God, the Word God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:21
verses.text: The rest that are made gods, are made by His own Grace, are not born of His Substance, that they should be the same as He, but that by favour they should come to Him, and be fellow-heirs with Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:22
verses.text: For so great is the love in Him the Heir, that He hath willed to have fellow-heirs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:23
verses.text: What covetous man would will this, to have fellow-heirs? But even one that is found so to will, will share with them the inheritance, the sharer having less himself, than if he had possessed alone: but the inheritance wherein we are fellow-heirs of Christ, is not lessened by multitude of possessors, nor is it made narrower by the number of fellow-heirs: but is as great for many as it is for few, as great for individuals as for all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:24
verses.text: "See," saith the Apostle, "what love God hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called, and be, the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:25
verses.text: And in another place, "Dearly beloved, we are the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:26
verses.text: We are therefore in hope, not yet in substance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:27
verses.text: "But we know," he saith, "that when He shall have appeared, we shall be like Him, for we shall see Him as He is".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:28
verses.text: The Only Son is like Him by birth, we like by seeing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:29
verses.text: For we are not like in such sort as He, who is the same as He is by whom He was begotten: for we are like, not equal: He, because equal, is therefore like.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:30
verses.text: We have heard who are the gods that being made are justified, because they are called the sons of God:  and who are the gods that are not Gods, to whom the God of gods is terrible? For another Psalm saith, "He is terrible over all gods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:31
verses.text: And as if thou shouldest enquire, what gods? He saith, "For all the gods of the nations are devils".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:32
verses.text: To the gods of the nations, to the devils, terrible: to the gods made by Himself, to sons, lovely.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:33
verses.text: Furthermore, I find both of them confessing the Majesty of God, both the devils confessed Christ, and the faithful confessed Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:34
verses.text: "Thou art Christ, the Son of the living God," said Peter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:35
verses.text: "We know who Thou art, Thou art the Son of God," said the devils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:36
verses.text: A like confession I hear, but like love I find not; nay even here love, there fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:37
verses.text: To whom therefore He is lovely, the same are sons; to whom He is terrible, are not sons; to whom He is lovely, the same He hath made gods; those to whom He is terrible He doth prove not to be gods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:38
verses.text: For these are made gods, those are reputed gods; these Truth maketh gods, those error doth so account.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:39
verses.text: "The God," therefore, "of gods, the Lord hath spoken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:40
verses.text: Hath spoken many ways.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:41
verses.text: By Angels He hath Himself spoken, by Prophets He hath Himself spoken, by His own mouth He hath Himself spoken, by His faithful He doth Himself speak, by our lowliness, when we say anything true, He doth Himself speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:42
verses.text: See then, by speaking diversely, many ways, by many vessels, by many instruments, yet He doth Himself sound everywhere, by touching, moulding, inspiring: see what He hath done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:43
verses.text: For "He hath spoken, and hath called the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:44
verses.text: What world? Africa, perhaps! for the sake of those that say, the Church of Christ is the portion of Donatus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:45
verses.text: Africa indeed alone He hath not called, but even Africa He hath not severed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:46
verses.text: For He that "hath called the world from the rising of the sun unto the going down," leaving out no parts that He hath not called, in His calling hath found Africa.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:47
verses.text: Let it rejoice therefore in unity, not pride itself in division.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:48
verses.text: We say well, that the voice of the God of gods hath come even into Africa, hath not stayed in Africa.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:49
verses.text: For "He hath called the world from the rising of the sun unto the going down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:50
verses.text: There is no place where may lurk the conspiracies of heretics, they have no place wherein they may hide themselves under the shadow of falsehood; for "there is none that can hide himself from the heat thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:51
verses.text: He that hath called the world, hath called even the whole world: He that hath called the world, hath called as much as He hath formed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:52
verses.text: Why do false christs and false prophets rise up against me? why is it that they strive to ensnare me with captious words, saying, "Lo! here is Christ, Lo! He is there!" I hear not them that point out portions: the God of gods hath pointed out the whole: "He" that "hath called the world from the rising of the sun unto the going down," hath redeemed the whole; but hath condemned them that lay false claim to portions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:53
verses.text: But we have heard the world called from the rising of the sun unto the going down: whence doth He begin to call, who hath called?  This thing also hear ye: "Out of Sion is the semblance of His beauty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:54
verses.text: Evidently the Psalm doth agree with the Gospel, which saith, "Throughout all nations, beginning at Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:55
verses.text: Hear, "Throughout all nations:" He hath called the world from the rising of the sun unto the going down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:56
verses.text: Hear, "Beginning at Jerusalem:" "Out of Sion is the semblance of His beauty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:57
verses.text: Therefore, "He hath called the world from the rising of the sun unto the going down," agreeth with the words of the Lord, who saith, "It behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day; and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His Name throughout all nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:58
verses.text: For all nations are from the rising of the sun unto the going down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:59
verses.text: But that, "Out of Sion is the semblance of His beauty," that thence beginneth the beauty of His Gospel, that thence He began to be preached, being "beautiful in form beyond the sons of men," agreeth with the words of the Lord, who saith, "Beginning at Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:60
verses.text: New things are in tune with old, old things with new: the two Seraphim say to one another, "Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of Sabaoth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:61
verses.text: The two Testaments are both in tune, and the two Testaments have one voice: let the voice of the Testaments in tune be heard, not that of pretenders disinherited.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:62
verses.text: This thing then hath the God of gods done, "He hath called the world from the rising of the sun unto the going down, His semblance going before out of Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:63
verses.text: For in that place were His disciples, who received the Holy Ghost sent from heaven on the fiftieth day after His resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:64
verses.text: Thence the Gospel, thence the preaching, thence the whole world filled, and that in the Grace of Faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:65
verses.text: For when the Lord Himself had come, because He came to suffer, He came hidden: and though He was strong in Himself, He appeared in the flesh weak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:66
verses.text: For He must needs appear in order that He might not be perceived; be despised, in order that He might be slain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:67
verses.text: There was semblance of glory in divinity, but it lay concealed in flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:68
verses.text: "For if they had known, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:69
verses.text: So then He walked hidden among the Jews, among His enemies, doing marvels, suffering ills, until He was hanged on the tree, and the Jews seeing Him hanging both despised Him the more, and before the Cross wagging their heads they said, "If He be the Son of God, let Him come down from the Cross".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:70
verses.text: Hidden then was the God of gods, and He gave forth words more out of compassion for us than out of His own majesty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:71
verses.text: For whence, unless assumed from us, were those words, "My God, My God, why hast Thou forsaken me?" But when hath the Father forsaken the Son, or the Son the Father? Are not Father and Son one God? Whence then, "My God, My God, why hast Thou forsaken Me," save that in the Flesh of infirmity there was acknowledged the voice of a sinner? For as He took upon Him the likeness of the flesh of sin, why should He not take upon Him the voice of sin? Hidden then was the God of gods, both when He walked among men, and when He hungered, and when He thirsted, and when fatigued He sat, and when with wearied body He slept, and when taken, and when scourged, and when standing before the judge, and when He made answer to him in his pride, "Thou couldest have no power against Me, except it had been given thee from above;" and while led as a victim "before His shearer He opened not His mouth," and while crucified, and while buried, He was always hidden God of gods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:72
verses.text: What took place after He rose again? The disciples marvelled, and at first believed not, until they touched and handled But flesh had risen, because flesh had been dead: Divinity which could not die, even still lay hid in the flesh of Him rising.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:73
verses.text: Form could be seen, limbs held, scars handled: the Word by whom all things were made, who doth see? who doth hold? who doth handle? And yet "the Word was made flesh, and dwelled among us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:74
verses.text: And Thomas, that was holding Man, understood God as he was able.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:75
verses.text: For when he had handled the scars, he cried out, "My Lord, and my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:76
verses.text: Yet the Lord was showing that form, and that flesh, which they had seen upon the Cross, which had been laid in the sepulchre.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:77
verses.text: He stayed with them forty days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:78
verses.text: But what was said to Thomas handling? "Because thou hast seen, thou hast believed; blessed are they that see not, and believe".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:79
verses.text: We are foretold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:80
verses.text: That world called from the rising of the sun unto the going down seeth not, and believeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:81
verses.text: Hidden then is the God of gods, both to those among whom He walked, and to those by whom He was crucified, and to those before whose eyes He rose, and to us who believe on Him in heaven sitting, whom we have not seen on earth walking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:82
verses.text: But even if we were to see, should we not see that which the Jews saw and crucified? It is more, that not seeing we believe Christ to be God, than that they seeing deemed Him only to be man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:83
verses.text: They in a word by thinking evil slew, we by believing well are made alive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:84
verses.text: What then, brethren? This God of gods, both then hidden, and now hidden, shall He ever be hidden? Evidently not: hear what followeth: "God shall come manifest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:85
verses.text: He that came hidden, shall come manifest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:86
verses.text: Hidden He came to be judged, manifest He shall come to judge: hidden He came that He might stand before a judge, manifest He shall come that He may be judge even of judges: "He shall come manifest, and shall not be silent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:87
verses.text: But why? Is He now silent? And whence are all the words that we say? whence those precepts? whence those warnings? whence that trumpet of terror? He is not silent, and is silent: is not silent from warning, is silent from avenging: is not silent from precept, is silent from judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:88
verses.text: For He suffereth sinners daily doing evil things, not caring for God, not in their conscience, not in heaven, not in earth: all these things escape Him not, and universally He doth admonish all; and whenever He chastiseth any on earth, it is admonition, not yet condemnation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:89
verses.text: He is silent then from judgment, He is hidden in heaven, as yet He intercedeth for us: He is long-suffering to sinners, not putting forth His wrath, but awaiting penitence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:90
verses.text: He saith in another place: "I have held my peace, shall I always hold my peace?" When then He shall not hold His peace, "God shall come manifest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:91
verses.text: What God? "Our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:92
verses.text: And the God Himself, who is our God: for he is not God, who is not our God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:93
verses.text: For the gods of the nations are devils: the God of Christians is very God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:94
verses.text: Himself shall come, but "manifest," not still to be mocked, not still to be buffeted and scourged: He shall come, but "manifest," not still to be smitten with a reed upon the head, not still to be crucified, slain, buried: for all these things God being hidden hath willed to suffer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:95
verses.text: "He shall come manifest, and shall not be silent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:96
verses.text: But that He shall come to judgment, the following words teach.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:97
verses.text: "Fire shall go before Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:98
verses.text: Do we fear? Be we changed, and we shall not fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:99
verses.text: Let chaff fear the fire: what doth it to gold? What thou mayest do is now in thy power, so thou mayest not experience, for want of being corrected, that which is to come even against thy will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:100
verses.text: For if we might so bring it about, brethren, that the day of judgment should not come; I think that even then it were not for us to live ill.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:101
verses.text: If the fire of the day of judgment were not to come, and over sinners there impended only separation from the face of God, in whatever affluence of delights they might be, not seeing Him by whom they were created, and separated from that sweetness of His ineffable countenance, in whatever eternity and impunity of sin, they ought to bemoan themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:102
verses.text: But what shall I say, or to whom shall I say? This is a punishment to lovers, not to despisers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:103
verses.text: They that have begun to feel in any degree the sweetness of wisdom and truth, know what I say, how great a punishment it is to be only separated from the face of God: but they that have not tasted that sweetness, if not yet they yearn for the face of God, let them fear even fire; let punishments terrify those, whom rewards win not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:104
verses.text: Of no value to thee is what God promiseth, tremble at what He threateneth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:105
verses.text: The sweetness of His presence shall come; thou art not changed, thou art not awakened, thou sighest not, thou longest not: thou embracest thy sins and the delights of thy flesh, thou art heaping stubble to thyself, the fire will come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:106
verses.text: "Fire shall burn in His presence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:107
verses.text: This fire will not be like thy hearth-fire, into which nevertheless, if thou art compelled to thrust thy hand, thou wilt do whatsoever he would have thee who doth threaten this alternative.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:108
verses.text: If he say to thee, "write against the life of thy father, write against the lives of thy children, for if thou do not, I thrust thy hand into thy fire:" thou wilt do it in order that thy hand be not burned, in order that thy member be not burned for a time, though it is not to be ever in pain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:109
verses.text: Thine enemy threateneth then but so light an evil, and thou doest evil; God threateneth eternal evil, and doest thou not good? To do evil not even menaces should compel thee: from doing good not even menaces should deter thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:110
verses.text: But by the menaces of God, by menaces of everlasting fire, thou art dissuaded from evil, invited to good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:111
verses.text: Wherefore doth it grieve thee, except because thou believest not? Let each one then examine his heart, and see what faith doth hold there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:112
verses.text: If we believe a judgment to come, brethren, let us live well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:113
verses.text: Now is time of mercy, then will be time of judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:114
verses.text: No one will say, "Call me back to my former years".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:115
verses.text: Even then men will repent, but will repent in vain: now let there be repentance, while there is fruit of repentance; now let there be applied to the roots of the tree a basket of dung, sorrow of heart, and tears; lest He come and pluck up by the roots.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:116
verses.text: For when He shall have plucked up, then the fire is to be looked for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:117
verses.text: Now, even if the branches have been broken, they can again be grafted in: then, "every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit, shall be cut down, and shall be cast into the fire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:118
verses.text: "Fire shall burn in His presence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:119
verses.text: "And a mighty tempest round about Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:120
verses.text: "A mighty tempest," in order to winnow so great a floor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:121
verses.text: In this tempest shall be that winnowing whereby from the saints shall be put away everything impure, from the faithful every unreality; from godly men and them that fear the Word of God, every scorner and every proud man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:122
verses.text: For now a sort of mixture doth lie there, from the rising of the sun unto the going down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:123
verses.text: Let us see then how He will do that is to come, what He will do with that tempest which "shall be a mighty tempest round about Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:124
verses.text: Doubtless this tempest is to make a sort of separation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:125
verses.text: It is that separation which they waited not for, who brake the nets, before they came to land But in this separation there is made a sort of distinction between good men and bad men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:126
verses.text: There be some that now follow Christ with lightened shoulders without the load of the world's cares, who have not heard in vain, "If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell all that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow Me;" to which sort is said, "Ye shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:127
verses.text: Some then shall be judging with the Lord: but others to be judged, but to be placed on the right hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:128
verses.text: For that there will be certain judging with the Lord, we have most evident testimony, which I have but now quoted: "Ye shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:129
verses.text: But what the Lord did after His resurrection, signified what is to be to us after our resurrection, in that number of the kingdom of heaven, where shall be no bad man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:130
verses.text: Lastly, those seven thousand of whom reply was made to Elias, "I have left me seven thousand men that have not bowed knees before Baal," far exceed that number of fishes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:131
verses.text: Therefore the hundred and fifty-three fishes doth not alone express just such a number of saints, but Scripture doth express the whole number of saints and righteous men by so great a number for a particular reason; to wit, in order that in those hundred and fifty-three all may be understood that pertain to the resurrection to eternal life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:132
verses.text: For the Law hath ten commandments: but the Spirit of Grace, through which alone the Law is fulfilled, is called sevenfold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:133
verses.text: The number then must be examined, what mean ten and seven: ten in commandments, seven in the grace of the Holy Spirit: by which grace the commandments are fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:134
verses.text: Ten then and seven contain all that pertain to the resurrection, to the right hand, to the kingdom of heaven, to life eternal, that is, they that fulfil the Law by the Grace of the Spirit, not as it were by their own work or their own merit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:135
verses.text: But ten and seven, if thou countest from one unto seventeen, by adding all the numbers by steps, so that to one thou mayest add two, add three, add four, that they may become ten, by adding five that they may become fifteen, by adding six that they may become twenty-one, by adding seven that they may become twenty-eight, by adding eight that they may become thirty-six, by adding nine that they may become forty-five, by adding ten that they may become fifty-five, by adding eleven that they may become sixty-six, by adding twelve that they may become seventy-eight, by adding thirteen that they may become ninety-one, by adding fourteen that they may become one hundred and five, by adding fifteen that they may become one hundred and twenty, by adding sixteen that they may become one hundred and thirty-six, by adding seventeen, make up one hundred and fifty-three, thou wilt find a vast number of all saints to belong to this number of a few fishes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:136
verses.text: In like manner then as in five virgins, countless virgins; as in five brethren of him that was tormented in hell, thousands of the people of the Jews; as in the number of one hundred and fifty-three fishes, thousands of thousands of saints: so in twelve thrones, not twelve men, but great is the number of the perfect.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:137
verses.text: But I see what is next required of us; in like manner as in the case of the five virgins, a reason was given why many should belong to five, and why to those five many Jews, and why to a hundred and fifty-three many perfect—to show why and how to the twelve thrones not twelve men, but many belong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:138
verses.text: What mean the twelve thrones, which signify all men everywhere that have been enabled to be so perfect as they must be perfect, to whom it is said, "Ye shall sit over the twelve tribes of Israel"? And why do all men everywhere belong to the number twelve? Because the very "everywhere" which we say, we say of the whole world: but the compass of lands is contained in four particular quarters, East, West, South, and North: from all these quarters they being called in the Trinity and made perfect in the faith and precept of the Trinity,—seeing that three times four are twelve, ye perceive wherefore the saints belong to the whole world; they that shall sit upon twelve thrones to judge the twelve tribes of Israel, since the twelve tribes of Israel, also, are the twelve tribes of the whole of Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:139
verses.text: For like as they that are to judge are from the whole world, so also they that are to be judged are from the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:140
verses.text: The Apostle Paul of himself, when he was reproving believing laymen, because they referred not their causes to the Church, but dragged them with whom they had matters before the public, said, "Know ye not that we shall judge Angels?"  See after what sort He hath made Himself judge: not only himself, but also all that judge aright in the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:141
verses.text: Since then it is evident, that many are to judge with the Lord, but that others are to be judged, not however on equality, but according to their deserts; He will come with all His Angels, when before Him shall be gathered all nations, and among all the Angels are to be reckoned those that have been made so perfect, that sitting upon twelve thrones they judge the twelve tribes of Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:142
verses.text: For men are called Angels: the Apostle saith of himself, "As an angel of God ye received me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:143
verses.text: Of John Baptist it is said, "Behold, I send My Angel before Thy face, that shall prepare Thy way before Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:144
verses.text: Therefore, coming with all Angels, together with Him He shall have the Saints also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:145
verses.text: For plainly saith Isaias also, "He shall come to judgment with the elders of the people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:146
verses.text: Those "elders of the people," then, those but now named Angels, those thousands of many men made perfect coming from the whole world, are called Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:147
verses.text: But the others are called earth, yet fruitful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:148
verses.text: Which is the earth that is fruitful? That which is to be set on the right hand, unto which it shall be said, "I was an hungred, and ye gave Me to eat:" truly fruitful earth in which the Apostle doth joy, when they sent to him to supply his necessities: "Not because I ask a gift," he saith, "but I require fruit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:149
verses.text: And he giveth thanks, saying, "Because at length ye have budded forth again to be thoughtful for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:150
verses.text: He saith, "Ye have budded forth again," as to trees which had withered away with a kind of barrenness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:151
verses.text: Therefore the Lord coming to judgment (that we may now hear the Psalm, brethren), He will do what? "He will call the heaven from above".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:152
verses.text: The heaven, all the Saints, those made perfect that shall judge, them He shall call from above, to be sitters with Him to judge the twelve tribes of Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:153
verses.text: For how shall "He call the heaven from above," when the heaven is always above? But those that He here calleth heaven, the same elsewhere He calleth heavens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:154
verses.text: What heavens? That tell out the glory of God: for, "The heavens tell out the glory of God:" whereof is said, "Into all the earth their sound hath gone forth, and into the ends of the world their words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:155
verses.text: For see the Lord severing in judgment: "He shall call the heaven from above and the earth, to sever His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:156
verses.text: From whom but from evil men? Of whom here afterwards no mention is made, now as it were condemned to punishment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:157
verses.text: See these good men, and distinguish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:158
verses.text: "He shall call the heaven from above, and the earth, to sever His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:159
verses.text: He calleth the earth also, not however to be associated, but to be dissociated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:160
verses.text: For at first He called them together, "when the God of gods spake and called the world from the rising of the sun unto the going down," He had not yet severed: those servants had been sent to bid to the marriage, who had gathered good and bad.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:161
verses.text: But when the God of gods shall come manifest and shall not keep silence, He shall so call the "heaven from above" that it may judge with Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:162
verses.text: For what the heaven is, the heavens themselves are; just as what the earth is, the lands themselves, just as what the Church is, the Churches themselves: "He shall call the heaven from above, and the earth, to sever His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:163
verses.text: Now with the heaven He severeth the earth, that is, the heaven with Him doth sever the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:164
verses.text: How doth He sever the earth? In such sort that He setteth on the right hand some, others on the left.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:165
verses.text: But to the earth severed, He saith what? "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive the kingdom which was prepared for you from the beginning of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:166
verses.text: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me to eat," and so forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:167
verses.text: But they say, "When saw we Thee an hungred?" And He, "Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of Mine, ye have done it unto Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:168
verses.text: "He shall call therefore the heaven from above, and the earth, to sever His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:169
verses.text: "Gather to Him His righteous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:170
verses.text: The voice divine and prophetic, seeing future things as if present doth exhort the Angels gathering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:171
verses.text: For He shall send His Angels, and before Him shall be gathered all nations Gather to Him His righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:172
verses.text: What righteous men save those that live of faith and do works of mercy? For those works are works of righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:173
verses.text: Thou hast the Gospel: "Beware of doing your righteousness before men to be seen of them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:174
verses.text: And as if it were inquired, What righteousness? "When therefore thou doest alms," He saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:175
verses.text: Therefore alms He hath signified to be works of righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:176
verses.text: Those very persons gather for His righteous: gather those that have had compassion on the "needy," that have considered the needy and poor: gather them, "The Lord preserve them, and make them to live;" "Gather to Him His righteous: who order His covenant above sacrifices:" that is, who think of His promises above those things which they work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:177
verses.text: For those things are sacrifices, God saying, "I will have mercy more than sacrifice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:178
verses.text: "Who keep His covenant more than sacrifice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:179
verses.text: "And the Heaven shall declare His righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:180
verses.text: Truly this righteousness of God to us the "heavens have declared," the Evangelists have foretold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:181
verses.text: Through them we have heard that some will be on the right hand, to whom the Householder saith, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:182
verses.text: Receive what? "A kingdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:183
verses.text: In return for what thing? "I was an hungred, and ye gave Me to eat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:184
verses.text: What so valueless, what so earthly, as to break bread to the hungry? At so much is valued the kingdom of heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:185
verses.text: "Break thy bread to the hungry, and the needy without covering bring into thy house; if thou seest one naked, clothe him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:186
verses.text: If thou hast not the means of breaking bread, hast not house into which thou mayest bring, hast not garment wherewith thou mayest cover: give a cup of cold water, cast two mites into the treasury As much the widow doth buy with two mites, as Peter buyeth, by leaving the nets, as Zacchaeus buyeth by giving half his goods Of so much worth is all that thou hast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:187
verses.text: "The heavens shall declare His righteousness, for God is Judge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:188
verses.text: Truly judge not confounding but severing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:189
verses.text: For "the Lord knoweth them that are His".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:190
verses.text: Even if grains lie hid in the chaff, they are known to the husbandman.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:191
verses.text: Let no one fear that he is a grain even among the chaff; the eyes of our winnower are not deceived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:192
verses.text: Fear not lest that tempest, which shall be round about Him, should confound thee with chaff.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:193
verses.text: Certainly mighty will be the tempest; yet not one grain will it sweep from the side of the corn to the chaff: because not any rustic with three-pronged fork, but God, Three in One, is Judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:194
verses.text: And the heavens shall declare His righteousness: for God is Judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:195
verses.text: Let heavens go, let the heavens tell, into every land let their sound go out, and unto the ends of the world their words: and let that body say, "From the ends of the world unto Thee have I cried, when my heart was in heaviness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:196
verses.text: For now mingled it groaneth, divided it shall rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:197
verses.text: Let it cry then and say, "Destroy not my soul with ungodly men, and with men of blood my life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:198
verses.text: He destroyeth not together, because God is Judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:199
verses.text: Let it cry to Him and say, "Judge me, O Lord, and sever my cause from the nation unholy:" let it say, He shall do it: there shall be gathered to Him His righteous ones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:200
verses.text: He hath called the earth that He may sever His people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:201
verses.text: "Hear, my people, and I will speak to thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:202
verses.text: He shall come and shall not keep silence; see how that even now, if ye hear, He is not silent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:203
verses.text: Hear, my people, and I will speak to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:204
verses.text: For if thou hearest not, I will not speak to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:205
verses.text: "Hear, and I will speak to thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:206
verses.text: For if thou hearest not, even though I shall speak, it will not be to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:207
verses.text: When then shall I speak to thee? If thou hearest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:208
verses.text: When hearest thou? If thou art my people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:209
verses.text: For, "Hear, my people:" thou hearest not if thou art an alien people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:210
verses.text: "Hear, my people, and I will speak to thee: Israel, and I will testify to thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:211
verses.text: For "Thy God," is properly said to that man whom God doth keep more as one of His family, as though in His household, as though in His peculiar: "Thy God am I".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:212
verses.text: What wilt thou more? Requirest thou a reward from God, so that God may give thee something; so that what He hath given thee may be thine own? Behold God Himself, who shall give, is thine own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:213
verses.text: What richer than He? Gifts thou wast desiring, thou hast the Giver Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:214
verses.text: "God, thy God, I am".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:215
verses.text: What He requireth of man, let us see; what tribute our God, our Emperor and our King doth enjoin us; since He hath willed to be our King, and hath willed us to be His province? Let us hear His injunctions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:216
verses.text: Let not a poor man tremble beneath the injunction of God: what God enjoineth to be given to Himself, He doth Himself first give that enjoineth: be ye only devoted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:217
verses.text: God doth not exact what He hath not given, and to all men hath given what He doth exact.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:218
verses.text: For what doth He exact? Let us hear now: "I will not reprove thee because of thy sacrifices".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:219
verses.text: I will not say to thee, Wherefore hast thou not slain for me a fat bull? why hast thou not selected the best he-goat from thy flock? Wherefore doth that ram amble among thy sheep, and is not laid upon mine altar? I will not say, Examine thy fields and thy pen and thy walls, seeking what thou mayest give Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:220
verses.text: "I will not reprove thee because of thy sacrifices".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:221
verses.text: What then: Dost Thou not accept my sacrifices? "But thy holocausts are always in My sight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:222
verses.text: Certain holocausts concerning which it is said in another Psalm, "If Thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would surely have given, with holocausts Thou wilt not be delighted:"  and again he turneth himself, "Sacrifice to God is a troubled spirit, a heart broken and humbled God doth not despise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:223
verses.text: Which be then holocausts that He despiseth not? Which holocausts that are always in His sight? "Kindly, O Lord," he saith, "deal in Thy good will with Sion, and be the walls of Jerusalem builded, then shalt Thou accept the sacrifice of righteousness, oblations, and holocausts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:224
verses.text: He saith that certain holocausts God will accept.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:225
verses.text: But what is a holocaust? A whole consumed with fire: causis is burning, holon is whole: but a "holocaust" is a whole consumed with fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:226
verses.text: There is a certain fire of most burning love: be the mind inflamed with love, let the same love hurry off the limbs to its use, let it not allow them to serve cupidity, in order that we may wholly glow with fire of divine love that will offer to God a holocaust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:227
verses.text: Such "holocausts of thine are in My sight always".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:228
verses.text: As yet that Israel perchance doth not understand what are the holocausts thereof which He hath in His sight always, and is still thinking of oxen, of sheep, of he-goats: let it not so think: "I will not accept calves of thy house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:229
verses.text: Holocausts I named; at once in mind and thought to earthly flocks thou wast running, therefrom thou wast selecting for Me some fat thing: "I will not accept calves of thy house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:230
verses.text: He is foretelling the New Testament, wherein all those sacrifices have ceased.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:231
verses.text: For they were then foretelling a certain Sacrifice which was to be, with the Blood whereof we should be cleansed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:232
verses.text: "I will not accept calves of thy house, nor he-goats of thy flocks".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:233
verses.text: "For mine are all the beasts of the wood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:234
verses.text: Why should I ask of thee what I have made? Is it more thine, to whom I have given it to possess, than Mine, who have made it? "For mine are all the beasts of the wood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:235
verses.text: But perchance that Israel saith, The beasts are God's, those wild beasts which I enclose not in my pen, which I bind not to my stall; but this ox and sheep and he-goat—these are mine own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:236
verses.text: "Cattle on the mountain, and oxen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:237
verses.text: Mine are those which thou possessest not, Mine are these which thou possessest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:238
verses.text: For if thou art My servant, the whole of thy property is Mine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:239
verses.text: For it cannot be, that is the property of the master which the servant hath gotten to himself, and yet that not be the property of the Master which the Master Himself hath created for the servant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:240
verses.text: Therefore Mine are the beasts of the wood which thou hast not taken; Mine are also the cattle on the mountains which are thine, and the oxen which are at thy stall: all are Mine own, for I have created them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:241
verses.text: "I know all the winged creatures of heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:242
verses.text: How doth He know? He hath weighed them, hath counted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:243
verses.text: Which of us knoweth all the winged creatures of heaven? But even though to some man God give knowledge of all the winged creatures of heaven, He doth not Himself know in the same manner as He giveth man to know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:244
verses.text: One thing is God's knowledge, another man's: in like manner as there is one possession of God's, another of man's: that is, God's possessing is one thing, man's another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:245
verses.text: For what thou possessest thou hast not wholly in thy power, or else thy ox, so long as it liveth, is in thy power; so as that it either die not, or be not to be fed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:246
verses.text: With whom there is the highest power, there is highest and most secret cognition.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:247
verses.text: Let us ascribe this to God, while praising God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:248
verses.text: Let us not dare to say, How knoweth God? Do not, I pray you, brethren, of me expect this, that I should unfold to you, how God doth know: this only I say, He doth not so know as a man, He doth not so know as an Angel: and how He knoweth I dare not say, because also I cannot ken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:249
verses.text: One thing, nevertheless, I ken, that even before all the winged creatures of heaven were, God knew that which He was to create.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:250
verses.text: What is that knowledge? O man, thou beginnest to see, after that thou hadst been formed, after that thou hadst received sense of seeing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:251
verses.text: These fowls sprung of the water at the word of God, saying, "Let the waters bring forth fowls".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:252
verses.text: Whereby did God know the things which He commanded the water to bear forth? Now surely He knew what He had created, and before He created He knew.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:253
verses.text: So great then is the knowledge of God, so that with Himself they were in a certain ineffable manner before they were created: and of thee doth He expect to receive what He had, before He created? "I know all the winged creatures of heaven," which thou to Me canst not give.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:254
verses.text: The things which thou wast about to slay for Me, I know all: not because I made I know, but in order that I might make.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:255
verses.text: "And the beauty of the field is with Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:256
verses.text: The fairness of the field, the abundance of all things engendering upon earth, "is with Me," He saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:257
verses.text: How with Him? Were they so, even before they were made? Yea, for with Him were all things to come, and with Him are all things by-gone: things to come in such sort, that there be not withdrawn from Him all things by-gone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:258
verses.text: With Him are all things by a certain cognition of the ineffable wisdom of God residing in the Word, and the Word Himself is all things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:259
verses.text: Is not the beauty of the field in a manner with Him, inasmuch as He is everywhere, and Himself hath said, "Heaven and earth I fill"? What with Him is not, of whom it is said, "If I shall have ascended into heaven, Thou art there; and if I shall have descended into hell, Thou art present"? With Him is the whole: but it is not so with Him as that He doth suffer any contamination from those things which He hath created, or any want of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:260
verses.text: For with thee, perchance, is a pillar near which thou art standing, and when thou art weary, thou leanest against it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:261
verses.text: Thou needest that which is with thee, God needeth not the field which is which Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:262
verses.text: With Him is field, with Him beauty of earth, with Him beauty of heaven, with Him all winged creatures, because He is Himself everywhere.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:263
verses.text: And wherefore are all things near Him? Because even before that all things were, or were created, to Him were known all things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:264
verses.text: Who can explain, who expound that which is said to Him in another Psalm, "For my goods Thou needest not"? He hath said that He needeth not from us any necessary thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:265
verses.text: "If I shall be hungry, I will not tell thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:266
verses.text: He that keepeth Israel shall neither hunger nor thirst, nor be weary, nor fall asleep But, lo! according to thy carnality I speak: because thou wilt suffer hunger when thou hast not eaten, perhaps thou thinkest even God doth hunger that He may eat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:267
verses.text: Even though He shall be hungry, He telleth not thee: all things are before Him, whence He will He taketh what is needful for Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:268
verses.text: These words are said to convince little understanding; not that God hath declared His hunger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:269
verses.text: Though for our sake this God of gods deigned even to hunger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:270
verses.text: He came to hunger, and to fill; He came to thirst, and give drink; He came to be clothed with mortality, and to clothe with immortality; He came poor, to make rich.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:271
verses.text: For He lost not His riches by taking to Him our poverty, for, "In him are all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hidden".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:272
verses.text: "If I shall be hungry, I will not tell thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:273
verses.text: For Mine is the whole world, and the fulness thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:274
verses.text: Do not then labour to find what to give Me, without whom I have what I will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:275
verses.text: Why then dost still think of thy flocks? "Shall I eat the flesh of bulls, or shall I drink the blood of he-goats?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:276
verses.text: Ye have heard what of us He requireth not, who willeth to enjoin us somewhat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:277
verses.text: If of such things ye were thinking, now withdraw your thoughts from such things: think not to offer God any such thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:278
verses.text: If thou hast a fat bull, kill for the poor: let them eat the flesh of bulls, though they shall not drink the blood of he-goats.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:279
verses.text: Which, when thou shalt have done, He will account it to thee, that hath said, "If I shall be hungry, I will not tell thee:" and He shall say to thee, "I was hungry, and thou gavest Me to eat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:280
verses.text: "Shall I eat the flesh of bulls, or shall I drink the blood of he-goats?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:281
verses.text: Say then, Lord our God, what dost Thou enjoin thy people, Thy Israel? "Immolate to God the sacrifice of praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:282
verses.text: Let us also say to Him, "In me, O God, are thy vows, which I will render of prose to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:283
verses.text: I had feared lest Thou mightest enjoin something which would be out of my power, which I was counting to be in my pen, and but now perchance it had been taken away by a thief.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:284
verses.text: What dost Thou enjoin me? "Immolate to God the sacrifice of praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:285
verses.text: Let me revert to myself, wherein I may find what I may immolate: let me revert to myself; in myself may I find immolation of praise: be Thy altar my conscience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:286
verses.text: We are without anxiety, we go not into Arabia in quest of frankincense: not any bags of covetous dealer do we sift: God requireth of us the sacrifice of praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:287
verses.text: Zacchaeus had the sacrifice of praise in his patrimony; the widow had it in her bag; some poor host or other hath had it in his jar: another neither in patrimony, nor in bag, nor in jar, hath had anything, had it wholly in his heart: salvation was to the house of Zacchaeus; and more this poor widow cast in than those rich men: this man, that doth offer a cup of cold water, shall not lose his reward: but there is even "peace on earth to men of good will".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:288
verses.text: "Immolate to God the sacrifice of praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:289
verses.text: O sacrifice gratuitous, by grace given! I have not indeed bought this to offer, but Thou hast given: for not even this should I have had.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:290
verses.text: And this is the immolation of the sacrifice of praise, to render thanks to Him from whom thou hast whatever of good thou hast, and by whose mercy is forgiven thee whatsoever of evil of thine thou hast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:291
verses.text: "Immolate to God the sacrifice of praise: and render to the Highest thy prayers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:292
verses.text: With this odour the Lord is well pleased.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:293
verses.text: "And call thou upon Me in the day of thy tribulation: and I will draw thee forth, and thou shalt glorify Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:294
verses.text: For thou oughtest not to rely on thy powers, all thy aids are deceitful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:295
verses.text: "Upon Me call thou in the day of tribulation: I will draw thee forth, and thou shalt glorify Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:296
verses.text: For to this end I have allowed the day of tribulation to come to thee: because perchance if thou wast not troubled, thou wouldest not call on Me: but when thou art troubled, thou callest on Me; when thou callest upon Me, I will draw thee forth; when I shall draw thee forth, thou shalt glorify Me, that thou mayest no more depart from Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:297
verses.text: A certain man had grown dull and cold in fervour of prayer, and said, "Tribulation and grief I found, and on the Name of the Lord I called".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:298
verses.text: He found tribulation as it were some profitable thing; he had rotted in the slough of his sins; now he had continued without feeling, he found tribulation to be a sort of caustic and cutting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:299
verses.text: "I found," he saith, "tribulation and grief, and on the Name of the Lord I called".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:300
verses.text: And truly, brethren, tribulations are known to all men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:301
verses.text: Behold those afflictions that abound in mankind; one afflicted with loss bewaileth; another smitten with bereavement mourneth; another exiled from country grieveth and desireth to return, deeming sojourning intolerable; another's vineyard is hailed upon, he observeth his labours and all his toil spent in vain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:302
verses.text: When can a human being not be made sad? An enemy he findeth in a friend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:303
verses.text: What greater misery in mankind? These things all men do deplore and grieve at, and these are tribulations: in all these they call upon the Lord, and they do rightly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:304
verses.text: Let them call upon God, He is able either to teach how it must be borne, or to heal it when borne.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:305
verses.text: He knoweth how not to suffer us to be tried above that we are able to bear Let us ca ll upon God even in those tribulations: but these tribulations do find us; as in another Psalm is written, "Helper in tribulations which have found us too much:" there is a certain tribulation which we ought to find.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:306
verses.text: Let such tribulations find us: there is a certain tribulation which we ought to seek and to find.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:307
verses.text: What is that? The above-named felicity in this world, abundance of temporal things: that is not indeed tribulation, these are the solaces of our tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:308
verses.text: Of what tribulation? Of our sojourning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:309
verses.text: For the very fact that we are not yet with God, the very fact that we are living amid trials and difficulties, that we cannot be without fear, is tribulation: for there is not that peace which is promised us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:310
verses.text: He that shall not have found this tribulation in his sojourning, doth not think of going home to his father-land.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:311
verses.text: This is tribulation, brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:312
verses.text: Surely now we do good works, when we deal bread to the hungry, home to the stranger, and the like: tribulation even this is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:313
verses.text: For we find pitiful objects upon whom we show pity; and the pitiful case of pitiful objects maketh us compassionate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:314
verses.text: How much better now would it be with thee in that place, where thou findest no hungry man whom thou mayest feed, where thou findest no stranger whom thou mayest take in, no naked man whom thou mayest cover, no sick man whom thou mayest visit, no litigant whom thou mayest set at one! For all things in that place are most high, are true, are holy, are everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:315
verses.text: Our bread in that place is righteousness, our drink there is wisdom, our garment there is immortality, our house is everlasting in the heavens, our stedfastness is immortality: doth sickness come over? Doth weariness weigh down to sleep? No death, no litigation: there peace, quiet, joy, righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:316
verses.text: No enemy hath entrance, no friend falleth away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:317
verses.text: What is the quiet there? If we think and observe where we are, and where He that cannot lie hath promised that we are to be, from His very promise we find in what tribulation we are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:318
verses.text: This tribulation none findeth, but he that shall have sought it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:319
verses.text: Thou art whole, see if thou art miserable; for it is easy for him that is sick to find himself miserable: when thou art whole, see if thou art miserable; that thou art not yet with God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:320
verses.text: "Tribulation and grief I found, and on the Name of the Lord I called".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:321
verses.text: "Immolate," therefore, "to God the sacrifice of praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:322
verses.text: Praise Him promising, praise Him calling, praise Him exhorting, praise Him helping: and understand in what tribulation thou art placed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:323
verses.text: Call upon (Him), thou shalt be drawn forth, thou shalt glorify, shalt abide.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:324
verses.text: But see what followeth, my brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:325
verses.text: For now some one or other, because God had said to him, "Immolate to God the sacrifice of praise," and had enjoined in a manner this tribute, did meditate to himself and said, I will rise daily, I will proceed to Church, I will say one hymn at matins, another at vespers, a third or fourth in my house, daily I do sacrifice the sacrifice of praise, and immolate to my God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:326
verses.text: Well thou doest indeed, if thou doest this: but take heed, lest now thou be careless, because now thou doest this: and perchance thy tongue bless God, and thy life curse God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:327
verses.text: O my people, saith to thee the God of gods, the Lord that spake, "calling the earth from the rising of the sun unto the setting," though yet thou art placed amid the tares, "Immolate the sacrifice of praise to thy God, and render to Him thy prayers:" but take heed lest thou live ill, and chant well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:328
verses.text: Wherefore this? For, "Unto the sinner, saith God, why dost thou tell out My judgments, and takest My Covenant in thy mouth?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:329
verses.text: Ye see, brethren, with what trembling we say these words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:330
verses.text: We take the Covenant of God in our mouth, and we say these words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:331
verses.text: We take the Covenant of God in our mouth, and we preach to you the instruction and judgment of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:332
verses.text: And what saith God to the sinner? "Why dost thou?" Doth He then forbid preachers that be sinners? And where is that, "What they say do, but what they do, do not"? Where is that, "Whether in truth or on occasion Christ be preached"? But these words were said, lest they should fear that hear, from whomsoever it be that they hear: not that they should be without care that speak good words, and do evil deeds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:333
verses.text: Now therefore, brethren, ye are without care: if ye hear good words ye hear God, through whomsoever it be that ye may hear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:334
verses.text: But God would not dismiss without reproof them that speak: lest with their speaking alone, without care for themselves they should slumber in evil life, and say to themselves, "For God will not consign us to perdition, through whose mouth He has willed that so many good words should be spoken to His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:335
verses.text: Nay, but hear what thou speakest, whoever thou art that speakest: and thou that writ be heard thyself, first hear thyself; and speak what a certain man doth speak in another Psalm, "I will hear what in me speaketh the Lord God, for He shall speak peace to His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:336
verses.text: What am I then, that hear not what in me He speaketh, and will that other hear what through me He speaketh? I will hear first, will hear, and chiefly I will hear what speaketh in me the Lord God, for He shall speak peace to His people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:337
verses.text: Let me hear, and "chasten my body, and to servitude subject it, lest perchance to others preaching, myself be found a cast-away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:338
verses.text: "Why dost thou tell out my judgments?" Wherefore to thee what profiteth not thee? He admonisheth him to hear: not to lay down preaching, but to take up obedience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:339
verses.text: "But thou, why dost thou take My Covenant in they mouth?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:340
verses.text: "But thou hatest instruction".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:341
verses.text: Thou hatest discipline.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:342
verses.text: When I spare, thou singest and praisest: when I chasten, thou murmurest: as though, when I spare, I am thy God: and, when I chasten, I am not thy God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:343
verses.text: "I rebuke and chasten those whom I love".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:344
verses.text: "But thou hatest instruction: and hast thrown My sayings behind thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:345
verses.text: The words that are said through thee, thou throwest behind thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:346
verses.text: "And thou hast thrown My sayings behind thee:" to a place where they may not be seen by thee, but may load thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:347
verses.text: "And thou hast thrown My sayings behind thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:348
verses.text: "If thou sawest a thief, thou didst consent unto him, and with adulterers thou didst make thy portion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:349
verses.text: Lest perchance thou shouldest say, I have not committed theft, I have not committed adultery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:350
verses.text: What if he pleased thee that hath committed? Hast thou not with the very pleasing consented? Hast thou not by approval made thy portion with him that hath committed? For this is, brethren, to consent with a thief, and to make with an adulterer thy portion: for even if thou committest not, and approvest what is committed, thou art an accessory in the deed: for "the sinner is praised in the longings of his soul, and he that doeth iniquity shall be blessed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:351
verses.text: Thou doest not evil things, thou praisest evil-doers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:352
verses.text: For is this a small evil? "Thou didst make thy portion with adulterers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:353
verses.text: "Thy mouth hath abounded in malice, and thy tongue hath embraced deceit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:354
verses.text: Of the malevolence and deceit, brethren, of certain men he speaketh, who by adulation, though they know what they hear to be evil, yet lest they offend those from whom they hear, not only by not reproving but by holding their peace do consent Too little is it, that they do not say, Thou hast done evil: but they even say, Thou hast done even well: and they know it to be evil: but their mouth aboundeth in malice, and their tongue embraceth deceit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:355
verses.text: Deceit is a sort of guile in words, of uttering one thing, thinking another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:356
verses.text: He saith not, thy tongue hath committed deceit or perpetrated deceit, but in order to point out to thee a kind of pleasure taken in the very evil doing, He hath said, "Hath embraced".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:357
verses.text: It is too little that thou doest it, thou art delighted too; thou praisest openly, thou laughest to thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:358
verses.text: Thou dost push to destruction a man heedlessly putting forth his faults, and knowing not whether they be faults: thou that knowest it to be a fault, sayest not, "Whither art thou rushing?" If thou wert to see him heedlessly walk in the dark, where thou knewest a well to be, and wert to hold thy peace, of what sort wouldest thou be? wouldest thou not be set down for an enemy of his life?  And yet if he were to fall into a well, not in soul but in body he would die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:359
verses.text: He doth fall headlong into his vices, he doth expose before thee his evil doings: thou knowest them to be evil, and praisest and laughest to thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:360
verses.text: Oh that at length he were to be turned to God at whom thou laughest, and whom thou wouldest not reprove, and that he were to say, "Let them be confounded that say to me, Well, well".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:361
verses.text: "Sitting against thy brother thou didst detract".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:362
verses.text: And this "sitting" doth belong to that whereof he hath spoken above in, "hath embraced".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:363
verses.text: For he that doeth anything while standing or passing along, doth it not with pleasure: but if he for this purpose sitteth, how much leisure doth he seek out to do it! That very evil detraction thou wast making with diligence, thou wast making sitting; thou wouldest thereon be wholly engaged; thou wast embracing thy evil, thou wast kissing thy craftiness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:364
verses.text: "And against thy mother's son thou didst lay a stumbling-block".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:365
verses.text: Who is "mother's son"? Is it not brother? He would repeat then the same that he had said above, "thy brother".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:366
verses.text: Hath he intimated that any distinction must be perceived by us? Evidently, brethren, I think a distinction must be made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:367
verses.text: Brother against brother doth detract, for example's sake, as though for instance one strong, and now a doctor and scholar of some weight, doth detract from his brother, one perchance that is teaching well and walking well: but another is weak, against him he layeth a stumbling-block by detracting from the former.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:368
verses.text: For when the good are detracted from by those that seem to be of some weight and to be learned, the weak fall upon the stumbling-block, who as yet know not how to judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:369
verses.text: Therefore this weak one is called "mother's son," not yet father's, still needing milk, and hanging on the breast.
