verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:370
verses.text: He is borne as yet in the bosom of his mother the Church, he is not strong enough to draw near to the solid food of his Father's table, but from the mother's breast he draweth sustenance, unskilled in judging, inasmuch as yet he is animal and carnal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:371
verses.text: "For the spiritual man judgeth all things," but "the animal man perceiveth not those things which are of the Spirit of God; for they are foolishness to him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:372
verses.text: To such men saith the Apostle, "I could not speak unto you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal, as to babes in Christ I gave you milk to drink, not meat; for ye were not able, but not even now are ye able".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:373
verses.text: A mother I have been to you: as is said in another place, "I became a babe among you, even as a nurse cherishing her own children".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:374
verses.text: Not a nurse nursing children of others, but a nurse cherishing her own children.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:375
verses.text: For there are mothers who when they have borne give to nurses: they that have borne cherish not their children, because they have given them to be nursed; but those that cherish, cherish not their own, but those of others: but he himself had borne, he was himself cherishing, to no nurse did commit what he had borne; for he had said, "Of whom I travail again until Christ be formed in you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:376
verses.text: He did cherish them, and gave milk.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:377
verses.text: But there were some as it were learned and spiritual men who detracted from Paul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:378
verses.text: "His letters indeed, say they, are weighty and powerful; but the presence of his body weak, and speech contemptible:" he saith himself in his Epistle, that certain his detractors had said these words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:379
verses.text: They were sitting, and were detracting against their brother, and against that their mother's son, to be fed with milk, they were laying a stumbling-block.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:380
verses.text: "And against thy mother's son thou didst lay a stumbling-block".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:381
verses.text: "These things hast thou done, and I held my tongue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:382
verses.text: Therefore the Lord our God shall come, and shall not keep silence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:383
verses.text: Now, "These things hast thou done, and I held my tongue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:384
verses.text: What is, "I held my tongue"? From vengeance I have desisted, my severity I have deferred, patience to thee I have prolonged, thy repentance I have long looked for"Thou hast imagined iniquity, that I shall be like unto thee;" Thou hast imagined that I shall be like unto thee, while thou wilt not be like unto Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:385
verses.text: For, "Be ye," he saith, "perfect, even as your Father, which is in the heavens, who maketh His sun to rise on the good and evil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:386
verses.text: Him thou wouldest not copy, who giveth good things even to evil men, insomuch that sitting thou dost detract even from good men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:387
verses.text: "I will reprove thee," when "God manifest shall come, our God, and shall not keep silence," "I will reprove thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:388
verses.text: And what to thee shall I do in reproving thee? what to thee shall I do? Now thyself thou seest not, I will make thee see thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:389
verses.text: Because if thou shouldest see thyself, and shouldest displease thyself, thou wouldest please Me: but because not seeing thyself thou hast pleased thyself, thou wilt displease both Me and thyself; Me when thou shalt be judged; thyself when thou shalt burn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:390
verses.text: But what to thee shall I do? He saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:391
verses.text: "I will set thee before thy face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:392
verses.text: For why wouldest thou escape thyself? At thy back thou art to thyself, thou seest not thyself: I make thee see thyself: what behind thy back thou hast put, before thy face will I put; thou shalt see thy uncleanness, not that thou mayest amend, but that thou mayest blush.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:393
verses.text: But, "understand these things, ye that forget God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:394
verses.text: See how He crieth, and keepeth not silence, spareth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:395
verses.text: Thou hadst forgotten the Lord, didst not think of thy evil life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:396
verses.text: Perceive how thou hast forgotten the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:397
verses.text: "Lest at length He seize like a lion, and there be none to deliver".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:398
verses.text: What is "like a lion"? Like a brave one, like a mighty one, like him whom none can withstand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:399
verses.text: To this he made reference when he said, "Lion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:400
verses.text: For it is used for praise, it is used also for showing evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:401
verses.text: The devil hath been called lion: "Your adversary," He saith, "like a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom He may devour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:402
verses.text: May it not be that whereas he hath been called lion because of savage fierceness, Christ hath been called Lion for wondrous mightiness? And where is that, "The Lion hath prevailed of the tribe of Judah?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:403
verses.text: "Sacrifice of praise shall glorify Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:404
verses.text: How shall "sacrifice of praise glorify Me"? Assuredly sacrifice of praise doth no wise profit evil men, because they take Thy Covenant in their mouth, and do damnable things that displease Thine eyes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:405
verses.text: Straightway, he saith, even to them this I say, "Sacrifice of praise shall glorify Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:406
verses.text: For if thou livest ill and speakest good words, not yet dost thou praise: but again, if, when thou beginnest to live well, to thy merits thou dost ascribe thy living well, not yet dost thou praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:407
verses.text: Therefore the Publican went down justified, rather than that Pharisee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:408
verses.text: Therefore hear ye that live well, hear ye that live ill: "Sacrifice of praise shall glorify Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:409
verses.text: No one offereth Me this sacrifice, and is evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:410
verses.text: I say not, Let there not offer Me this any one that is evil; but no one doth offer Me this, that is evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:411
verses.text: For he that praiseth, is good: because if he praiseth, he doth also live well, because if he praiseth, not only with tongue he praiseth, but life also with tongue doth agree.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:412
verses.text: "And there is the way whereby I will show him the salvation of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:413
verses.text: In sacrifice of praise "is the way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:414
verses.text: What is "the salvation of God"? Christ Jesus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:415
verses.text: And how in sacrifice of praise to us is shown Christ? Because Christ with grace came to us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:416
verses.text: These words saith the Apostle: "But I live, now not I, but Christ liveth in me: but that in flesh I live, in faith I live of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave Himself for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:417
verses.text: Acknowledge then sinners, that there would not need physician, if they were whole For Christ died for the ungodly When then they acknowledge their ungodlinesses, and first copy that Publican, saying, "Lord, be merciful to me a sinner:" show wounds, beseech Physician: and because they praise not themselves, but blame themselves,—"So that he that glorieth, not in himself but in the Lord may glory,"—they acknowledge the cause of the coming of Christ, because for this end He came, that He might save sinners: for "Jesus Christ came," he saith, "into this world to save sinners; of whom I am chief".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:418
verses.text: Further, those Jews, boasting of their work, thus the same Apostle doth rebuke, in saying, that they to grace belonged not, who to their merits and their works thought that reward was owing He therefore that knoweth himself to belong to grace, doth know what is Christ and what is Christ's because he needeth grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 51:419
verses.text: If grace it is called, gratis it is given; if gratis it is given, not any merits of time have preceded that it should be given.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:1
verses.text: Psalm LI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:2
verses.text: Neither must this multitude's throng be defrauded, nor their infirmity burthened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:3
verses.text: Silence we ask, and quiet, in order that our voice, after yesterday's labour, be able with some little vigour to last out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:4
verses.text: It must be believed, that your love hath met together in greater numbers to-day for nothing else, but that ye may pray for those whom an alien and perverse inclination doth keep away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:5
verses.text: For we are speaking neither of heathens nor of Jews, but of Christians: nor of those that are yet Catechumens, but of many that are even baptized, from the Laver of whom ye do no wise differ, and yet to their heart ye are unlike.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:6
verses.text: For to-day how many brethren of ours we think of, and deplore their going unto vanities and lying insanities, to the neglect of that to which they have been called.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:7
verses.text: Who, if in the very circus from any cause they chance to be startled, do immediately cross themselves, and stand bearing It on the forehead, in the very place, from whence they had withdrawn, if they had borne It in heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:8
verses.text: God's mercy must be implored, that He may give understanding for condemning these t hings, inclination to flee them, and mercy to forgive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:9
verses.text: Opportunately, then, of Penitence a Psalm to-day has been chanted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:10
verses.text: Speak we even with the absent: there will be to them for our voice your memory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:11
verses.text: Neglect not the wounded and feeble, but that ye may more easily make whole, whole ye ought to abide.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:12
verses.text: Correct by reproving, comfort by addressing, set an example by living well, He will be with them that hath been with you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:13
verses.text: For now that ye have overpassed these dangers, the fountain of God's mercy is not closed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:14
verses.text: Where ye have come they will come; where ye have passed they will pass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:15
verses.text: A grievous thing it is indeed, and exceeding perilous, nay ruinous, and for certain a deadly thing, that witting they sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:16
verses.text: For in one way to these vanities doth he run that despiseth the voice of Christ; in another way, he that k noweth from what he is fleeing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:17
verses.text: But that not even of such men we ought to despair, this Psalm doth show.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:18
verses.text: For there is written over it the title thereof, "A Psalm of David himself, when there came to him Nathan the prophet, when he went in unto Bersabee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:19
verses.text: Bersabee was a woman, wife of another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:20
verses.text: With grief indeed we speak, and with trembling; but yet God would not have to be hushed what He hath willed to be written.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:21
verses.text: I will say then not what I will, but what I am obliged; I will say not as one exhorting to imitation, but as one instructing you to fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:22
verses.text: Captivated with this woman's beauty, the wife of another, the king and prophet David, from whose seed accordi ng to the flesh the Lord was to come, committed adultery with her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:23
verses.text: This thing in this Psalm is not read, but in the title thereof it appeareth; but in the book of Kings it is more fully read.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:24
verses.text: Both Scriptures are canonical, to both without any doubt by Christians credit must be given.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:25
verses.text: The sin was committed, and was written down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:26
verses.text: Moreover her husband in war he caused to be killed: and after this deed there was sent to him Nathan the prophet; sent by the Lord, to reprove him for so great an outrage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:27
verses.text: What men should beware of, we have said; but what if they shall have fallen they should imitate, let us hear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:28
verses.text: For many men will to fall with David, and will not to rise with David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:29
verses.text: Not then for falling is the example set forth, but if thou shalt have fallen for rising again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:30
verses.text: Take heed lest thou fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:31
verses.text: Not the delight of the younger be the lapse of the elder, but be the fall of the elder the dread of the younger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:32
verses.text: For this it was set forth, for this was written, for this in the Church often read and chanted: let them hear that have not fallen, lest they fall; let them hear that have fallen, that they may rise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:33
verses.text: So great a man's sin is not hushed, is proclaimed in the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:34
verses.text: There men hear that are ill hearers, and seek for themselves countenance for sinning: they look out for means whereby they may defend what they have made ready to commit, not how they may beware of what they have not committed, and they say to themselves, If David, why not I too? Thence that soul is more unrighteous, which, forasmuch as it hath done it because David did, therefore hath done worse than David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:35
verses.text: I will say this very thing, if I shall be able, more plainly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:36
verses.text: David had set forth to himself none for a precedent as thou hast: he had fallen by lapse of concupiscence, not by the countenance of holiness: thou dost set before thine eyes as it were a holy man, in order that thou mayest sin: thou dost not copy his holiness, but dost copy his fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:37
verses.text: Thou dost love that in David, which in himself David hated: thou makest thee ready to sin, thou inclinest to sin: in order that thou mayest sin thou consultest the book of God: the Scriptures of God for this thou hearest, that thou mayest do what displeaseth God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:38
verses.text: This did not David; he was reproved by a Prophet, he stumbled not over a Prophet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:39
verses.text: But others hearing to their health, by the fall of a strong man measure their weakness: and desiring to avoid what God condemneth, from careless looking do restrain their eyes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:40
verses.text: Them they fix not upon the beauty of another's flesh, nor make themselves careless with perverse simpleness; they say not, "With good intent I have observed, of kindness I have observed, of charity I have long looked".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:41
verses.text: For they set before themselves the fall of David, and they see that this great man for this purpose hath fallen, in order that little men may not be willing to look on that whereby they may fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:42
verses.text: For they restrain their eyes from wantonness, not readily do they join themselves in company, they do not mingle with strange women, they raise not complying eyes to strange balconies, to strange terraces.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:43
verses.text: For from afar David saw her with whom he was captivated Woman afar, lust near.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:44
verses.text: What he saw was elsewhere, in himself that whereby he fell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:45
verses.text: This weakness of the flesh must be therefore minded, the words of the Apostle recollected, "Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:46
verses.text: He hath not said, let there not be; but, "let there not reign".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:47
verses.text: There is sin in thee, when thou takest pleasure; there reigneth, if thou shalt have consented.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:48
verses.text: Carnal pleasure, especially if proceeding unto unlawful and strange objects, is to be bridled, not let loose: by government to be tamed, not to be set up for government.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:49
verses.text: Look and be without care, if thou hast nothing whereby thou mayest be moved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:50
verses.text: But thou makest answer, "I contain with strong resolution".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:51
verses.text: Art thou any wise stronger than David?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:52
verses.text: He admonisheth, moreover, by such an example, that no one ought to lift himself up in prosperous circumstances.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:53
verses.text: For many fear adverse circumstances, fear not prosperous circumstances.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:54
verses.text: Prosperity is more perilous to soul than adversity to body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:55
verses.text: First, prosperity doth corrupt, in order that adversity may find something to break.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:56
verses.text: My brethren, stricter watch must be kept against felicity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:57
verses.text: Wherefore, see ye after what manner the saying of God amid our own felicity doth take from us security: "Serve ye," He saith, "the Lord in fear, and exult unto Him with trembling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:58
verses.text: In exultation, in order that we may render thanks; in trembling, lest we fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:59
verses.text: This sin did not David, when he was suffering Saul for persecutor When holy David was suffering Saul his enemy, when he was being vexed by his persecutions, when he was fleeing through divers places, in order that he might not fall into his hands, he lusted not for her that was another's, he slew not husband after committing adultery with wife.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:60
verses.text: He was in the infirmity of his tribulation so much the more intimate with God as he seemed more miserable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:61
verses.text: Something useful is tribulation; useful the surgeon's lancet rather than the devil's temptation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:62
verses.text: He became secure when his enemies were overthrown, pressure was removed, swelling grew out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:63
verses.text: This example therefore doth avail to this end, that we should fear felicity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:64
verses.text: "Tribulation," he saith, "and grief I found, and on the name of the Lord I called".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:65
verses.text: But it was done; I would say these words to those that have not done the like, in order that they should watch to keep their uncorruptness, and that while they take heed how a great one has fallen, they that be small should fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:66
verses.text: But if any that hath already fallen  heareth these words, and that hath in his conscience any evil thing; to the words of this Psalm let him advert; let him heed the greatness of the wound, but not despair of the majesty of the Physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:67
verses.text: Sin with despair is certain death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:68
verses.text: Let no one therefore say, If already any evil thing I have done, already I am to be condemned: God pardoneth not such evil things, why add I not sins to sins? I will enjoy this word in pleasure, in wantonness, in wicked cupidity: now hope of amendm ent having been lost, let me have even what I see, if I cannot have what I believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:69
verses.text: This Psalm then, while it maketh heedful those that have not believed, so doth not will them that have fallen to be despaired of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:70
verses.text: Whoever thou art that hast sinned, and hesitatest to exercise penitence for thy sin, despairing of thy salvation, hear David groaning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:71
verses.text: To thee Nathan the prophet hath not been sent, David himself hath been sent to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:72
verses.text: Hear him crying, and with him cry: hear him groaning, and with him groan; hear him weeping, and mingle tears; hear him amended, and with him rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:73
verses.text: If from thee sin could not be excluded, be not hope of pardon excluded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:74
verses.text: There was sent to that man Nathan the prophet, observe the king's humility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:75
verses.text: He rejected not the words of him giving admonition, he said not, Darest thou speak to me, a king? An exalted king heard a prophet, let His humble people hear Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:76
verses.text: Hear therefore these words, and say thou with him: "Have pity upon me, O God, after Thy great mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:77
verses.text: He that imploreth great mercy, confesseth great misery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:78
verses.text: Let them seek a little mercy of Thee, that have sinned in ignorance: "Have pity," he saith, "upon me, after Thy great mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:79
verses.text: Relieve a deep wound after Thy great healing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:80
verses.text: Deep is what I have, but in the Almighty I take refuge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:81
verses.text: Of my own so deadly wound I should despair, unless I could find so great a Physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:82
verses.text: "Have pity upon me, O God, after Thy great mercy: and after the multitude of Thy pities, blot out my iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:83
verses.text: What he saith, "Blot out my iniquity," is this, "Have pity upon me, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:84
verses.text: And what he saith, "After the multitude of Thy pities," is this, "After Thy great mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:85
verses.text: Because great is the mercy, many are the mercies; and of Thy great mercy, many are Thy pitying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:86
verses.text: Thou dost regard mockers to amend them, dost regard ignorant men to teach them, dost regard men confessing to pardon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:87
verses.text: Did he this in ignorance? A certain man had done some, aye many evil things he had done; "Mercy," he saith, "I obtained, because ignorant I did it in unbelief".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:88
verses.text: This David could not say, "Ignorant I did it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:89
verses.text: For he was not ignorant how very evil a thing was the touching of another's wife, and how very evil a thing was the killing of the husband, who knew not of it, and was not even angered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:90
verses.text: They obtain therefore the mercy of the Lord that have in ignorance done it; and they that have knowing done it, obtain not any mercy it may chance, but "great mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:91
verses.text: "More and more wash me from mine unrighteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:92
verses.text: What is, "More and more wash"? One much stained.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:93
verses.text: More and more wash the sins of one knowing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:94
verses.text: Thou that hast washed off the sins of one ignorant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:95
verses.text: Not even thus is it to be despaired of Thy mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:96
verses.text: "And from my delinquency purge Thou me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:97
verses.text: According to the manner in which He is physician, offer a recompense.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:98
verses.text: He is God, offer sacrifice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:99
verses.text: What wilt thou give that thou mayest be purged? For see upon whom thou callest; upon a Just One thou callest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:100
verses.text: He hateth sins, if He is just; He taketh vengeance upon sins, if He is just; thou wilt not be able to take away from the Lord God His justice: entreat mercy, but observe the justice: there is mercy to pardon the sinner, there is justice to punish the sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:101
verses.text: What then? Thou askest mercy; shall sin unpunished abide? Let David answer, let those that have fallen answer, answer with David, and say, No, Lord, no sin of mine shall be unpunished; I know the justice of Him whose mercy I ask: it shall not be unpunished, but for this reason I will not that Thou punish me, because I punish my sin: for this reason I beg that Thou pardon, because I acknowledge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:102
verses.text: "For mine iniquity I acknowledge, and my delinquency is before me ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:103
verses.text: I have not put behind my back what I have done, I look not at others, forgetful of myself, I pretend not to pull out a straw from my brother's eye, when there is a beam in my eye; my sin is before me, not behind me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:104
verses.text: For it was behind me when to me was sent the Prophet, and set before me the parable of the poor man's sheep For saith Nathan the Prophet to David, "There was a certain rich man having very many sheep; but a poor man his neighbour had one little ewe sheep, which in his bosom and of his own food he was feeding: there came a stranger to the rich man, nothing from his flock he took, for the lithe ewe sheep of the poor man his neighbour he lusted; her he slew for the stranger: what doth he deserve?" But the other being angry doth pronounce sentence: then the king, evidently knowing not wherein he had been taken, declared the rich man deserving of death, and that the sheep be restored fourfold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:105
verses.text: Most sternly and most justly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:106
verses.text: But his sin was not yet before him, behind his back was what he had done: his own iniquity he did not yet acknowledge, and therefore another's he did not pardon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:107
verses.text: But the Prophet, being for this purpose sent, took from his back the sin, and before his eyes placed it, so that he might see that sentence so stern to have been pronounced against himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:108
verses.text: For cutting and healing his heart's wound, he made a lancet of his tongue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:109
verses.text: "Against Thee alone have I sinned, and before Thee an evil thing have I done".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:110
verses.text: What is this? For before men was not another's wife debauched and husband slain? Did not all men know what David had done? What is, "Against Thee alone have I sinned, and before Thee an evil thing have I done".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:111
verses.text: Because Thou alone art without sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:112
verses.text: He is a just punisher that hath nothing in Him to be punished; He is a just reprover that hath nothing in Him to be reproved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:113
verses.text: "That thou mayest be justified in Thy sayings, and conquer when Thou art judged".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:114
verses.text: To whom he speaketh, brethren, to whom he speaketh, is difficult to understand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:115
verses.text: To God surely he speaketh, and it is evident that God the Father is not judged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:116
verses.text: What is, "And conquer when Thou art judged"? He seeth the future Judge to be judged, one just by sinners to be judged, and therein conquering, because in Him was nothing to be judged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:117
verses.text: For alone among men could truly say the God-Man, "If ye have found in Me sin, say".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:118
verses.text: But perchance there was what escaped men, and they found not what was really there, but was not manifest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:119
verses.text: In another place He saith, "Behold there cometh the Prince of the world," being an acute observer of all sins; "Behold," He saith, "there cometh the Prince of this world," with death afflicting sinners, presiding over death: for, "By the malice of the devil death came into the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:120
verses.text: "Behold," He saith, "there cometh the Prince of the world:"—He said these words close upon His Passion:—"and in Me he shall find nothing," nothing of sin, nothing worthy of death, nothing worthy of condemnation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:121
verses.text: And as if it were said to Him, Why then dost Thou die? He continueth and saith, "But that all men may know that I do the will of My Father; arise, let us go hence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:122
verses.text: I suffer, He saith, undeserving, for men deserving, in order that them I may make deserving of My Life, for whom I undeservedly suffer their death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:123
verses.text: To Him then, having no sin, saith on the present occasion the Prophet David, "Against Thee only have I sinned, and before Thee an evil thing have I done, that Thou mayest be justified in Thy sayings, and conquer when Thou art judged".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:124
verses.text: For Thou overcomest all men, all judges; and he that deemeth himself just, before Thee is unjust: Thou alone justly judgest, having been unjustly judged, That hast power to lay down Thy life, and hast power again to take it Thou conquerest, then, when Thou art judged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:125
verses.text: All men Thou overcomest, because Thou art more than men, and by Thee were men made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:126
verses.text: "For, behold, in iniquities I was conceived".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:127
verses.text: As though he were saying, They are conquered that have done what thou, David, hast done: for this is not a little evil and little sin, to wit, adultery and man-slaying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:128
verses.text: What of them that from the day that they were born of their mother's womb, have done no such thing? even to them dost thou ascribe some sins, in order that He may conquer all men when He beginneth to be judged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:129
verses.text: David hath taken upon him the person of mankind, and hath heeded the bonds of all men, hath considered the offspring of death, hath adverted to the origin of iniquity, and he saith, "For, behold, in iniquities I was conceived".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:130
verses.text: Was David born of adultery; being born of Jesse, a righteous man, and his own wife? What is it that he saith himself to have been in iniquity conceived, except that iniquity is drawn from Adam? Even the very bond of death, with iniquity itself is engrained? No man is born without bringing punishment, bringing desert of punishment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:131
verses.text: A Prophet saith also in another place, "No one is clean in Thy sight, not even an infant, whose life is of one day upon earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:132
verses.text: For we know both by the Baptism of Christ that sins are loosed, and that the Baptism of Christ availeth the remission of sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:133
verses.text: If infants are every way innocent, why do mothers run with them when sick to the Church? What by that Baptism, what by that remission is put away? An innocent one I see that rather weeps than is angry.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:134
verses.text: What doth Baptism wash off? what doth that Grace loose? There is loosed the offspring of sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:135
verses.text: For if that infant could speak to thee, it would say, and if it had the understanding which David had, it would answer thee, Why heedest thou me, an infant? Thou dost not indeed see my actions: but I in iniquity have been conceived, "And in sins hath my mother nourished me in the womb".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:136
verses.text: Apart from this bond of mortal concupiscence was Christ born without a male, of a virgin conceiving by the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:137
verses.text: He cannot be said to have been conceived in iniquity, it cannot be said, In sins His mother nourished Him in the womb, to whom was said, "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the Virtue of the Highest shall overshadow thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:138
verses.text: It is not therefore because it is sin to have to do with wives that men are conceived in iniquity, and in sins nourished in the womb by their mother; but because that which is made is surely made of flesh deserving punishment For the punishment of the flesh is death, and surely there is in it liability to death itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:139
verses.text: Whence the Apostle spoke not of the body as if to die, but as if dead: "The body indeed is dead," he saith, "because of sin, but the Spirit is life because of righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:140
verses.text: How then without bond of sin is born that which is conceived and sown of a body dead because of sin? This chaste operation in a married person hath not sin, but the origin of sin draweth with it condign punishment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:141
verses.text: For there is no husband that, because he is an husband, is not subject to death, or that is subject to death for any other reason but because of sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:142
verses.text: For even the Lord was subject to death, but not on account of sin: He took upon Him our punishment, and so looseth our guilt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:143
verses.text: With reason then, "In Adam all die, but in Christ shall all be made alive".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:144
verses.text: For, "Through one man," saith the Apostle, "sin hath entered into this world, and through sin death, and so hath passed unto all men, in that all have sinned".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:145
verses.text: Definite is the sentence: "In Adam," he saith, "all have sinned".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:146
verses.text: Alone then could such an infant be innocent, as hath not been born of the work of Adam.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:147
verses.text: "For, behold, truth Thou hast loved: uncertain and hidden things of Thy wisdom, Thou hast manifested to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:148
verses.text: That is, Thou hast not left unpunished even the sins of those whom Thou dost pardon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:149
verses.text: "Truth Thou hast loved:" so mercy Thou hast granted first, as that Thou shouldest also preserve truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:150
verses.text: Thou pardonest one confessing, pardonest, but only if he punisheth himself: so there are preserved mercy and truth: mercy because man is set free; truth, because sin is punished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:151
verses.text: "Uncertain and hidden things of Thy wisdom Thou hast manifested to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:152
verses.text: What "hidden things"? What "uncertain things"? Because God pardoneth even such.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:153
verses.text: Nothing is so hidden, nothing so uncertain For this uncertainty the Ninevites repented, for they said, though after the threatenings of the Prophet, though after that cry, "Three days and Nineve shall be overthrown:" they said to themselves, Mercy must be implored; they said in this sort reasoning among themselves, "Who knoweth whether God may turn for the better His sentence, and have pity?" It was "uncertain," when it is said, "Who knoweth?" on an uncertainty they did repent, certain mercy they earned: they prostrated them in tears, in fastings, in sackcloth and ashes they prostrated them, groaned, wept, God spared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:154
verses.text: Nineve stood: was Nineve overthrown? One way indeed it seemeth to men, and another way it seemed to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:155
verses.text: But I think that it was fulfilled that the Prophet had foretold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:156
verses.text: Regard what Nineve was, and see how it was overthrown; overthrown in evil, builded in good; just as Saul the persecutor was overthrown, Paul the preacher builded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:157
verses.text: Who would not say that this city, in which we now are, was happily overthrown, if all those madmen, leaving their triflings, were to run together to the Church with contrite heart, and were to call upon God's mercy for their past doings? Should we not say, Where is that Carthage? Because there is not what there was, it is overthrown: but if there is what there was not, it is builded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:158
verses.text: So is said to Jeremiah, "Behold, I will give to thee to root up, to dig under, to overthrow, to destroy," and again, "to build, and to plant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:159
verses.text: Thence is that voice of the Lord, "I will smite and I will heal".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:160
verses.text: He smiteth the rottenness of the deed, He healeth the pain of the wound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:161
verses.text: Physicians do thus when they cut; they smite and heal; they arm themselves in order to strike, they carry steel, and come to cure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:162
verses.text: But because great were the sins of the Ninevites, they said, "Who knoweth?" This uncertainty had God disclosed to His servant David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:163
verses.text: For when he had said, before the Prophet standing and convicting him, "I have sinned:" straightway he heard from the Prophet, that is, from the Spirit of God which was in the Prophet, "Thy sin is put away from thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:164
verses.text: "Uncertain and hidden things" of His wisdom He manifested to him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:165
verses.text: "Thou shalt sprinkle me," he saith, "with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:166
verses.text: Hyssop we know to be a herb humble but healing: to the rock it is said to adhere with roots.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:167
verses.text: Thence in a mystery the similitude of cleansing the heart has been taken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:168
verses.text: Do thou also take hold, with the root of thy love, on thy Rock: be humble in thy humble God, in order that thou mayest be exalted in thy glorified God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:169
verses.text: Thou shalt be sprinkled with hyssop, the humility of Christ shall cleanse thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:170
verses.text: Despise not the herb, attend to the efficacy of the medicine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:171
verses.text: Something further I will say, which we are wont to hear from physicians, or to experience in sick persons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:172
verses.text: Hyssop, they say, is proper for purging the lungs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:173
verses.text: In the lung is wont to be noted pride: for there is inflation, there breathing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:174
verses.text: It was said of Saul the persecutor as of Saul the proud, that he was going to bind Christians, breathing slaughter: he was breathing out slaughter, breathing out blood, his lung not yet cleansed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:175
verses.text: Hear also in this place one humbled, because with hyssop purged: "Thou shalt wash me," that is, shalt cleanse me: "and above snow I shall be whitened".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:176
verses.text: "Although," he saith, "your sins shall have been like scarlet, like snow I will whiten".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:177
verses.text: Out of such men Christ doth present to Himself a vesture without spot and wrinkle Further, His vesture on the mount, which shone forth like whitened snow, signified the Church cleansed from every spot of sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:178
verses.text: But where is humility from hyssop? Hear what followeth: "To my hearing Thou shall give exultation and gladness, and bones humbled shall exult".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:179
verses.text: I will rejoice in hearing Thee, not in speaking against Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:180
verses.text: Thou hast sinned, why defendest thou thyself? Thou wilt speak: suffer thou; hear, yield to divine words, lest thou be put to confusion, and be still more wounded: sin hath been committed, be it not defended: to confession let it come, not to defence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:181
verses.text: Thou engagest thyself as defender of thy sin, thou art conquered: no innocent patron hast thou engaged, thy defence is not profitable to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:182
verses.text: For who art thou that defendest thyself? Thou art meet to accuse thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:183
verses.text: Say not, either, "I have done nothing;" or, "What great thing have I done?" or, "Other men as well have done".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:184
verses.text: If in doing sin thou sayest thou hast done nothing, thou wilt be nothing, thou wilt receive nothing: God is ready to give indulgence, thou closest the door against thyself: He is ready to give, do not oppose the bar of defence, but open the bosom of confession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:185
verses.text: "To my hearing Thou shalt give exultation and gladness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:186
verses.text: "Turn Thou away Thy face from my sins, and all mine iniquities blot out".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:187
verses.text: For now bones humbled exult, now with hyssop cleansed, humble I have become.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:188
verses.text: "Turn Thou away Thy face," not from me, but "from my sins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:189
verses.text: For in another place praying he saith, "Turn not away Thy face from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:190
verses.text: He that would not that God's face be turned away from himself, would that God's face be turned away from his sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:191
verses.text: For to sin, when God turneth not Himself away, he adverteth: if he adverteth, he animadverteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:192
verses.text: "And all mine iniquities blot out".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:193
verses.text: He is busied with that capital sin: he reckoneth on more, he would have all his iniquities to be blotted out: he relieth on the Physician's hand, on that "great mercy," upon which he hath called in the beginning of the Psalm: "All mine iniquities blot out".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:194
verses.text: God turneth away His face, and so blotteth out; by "turning away" His face, sins He blotteth out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:195
verses.text: By "turning towards," He writeth them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:196
verses.text: Thou hast heard of Him blotting out by turning away, hear of Him by turning towards, doing what? "But the countenance of the Lord is upon men doing evil things, that He may destroy from the earth the remembrance of them:" He shall destroy the remembrance of them, not by "blotting out their sins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:197
verses.text: But here he doth ask what? "Turn away Thy face from my sins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:198
verses.text: Well he asketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:199
verses.text: For he himself doth not turn away his face from his own sins, saying, "For my sin I acknowledge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:200
verses.text: With reason thou askest and well askest, that God turn away from thy sin, if thou from thence dost not turn away thy face: but if thou settest thy sin at thy back, God doth there set His face.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:201
verses.text: Do thou turn sin before thy face, if thou wilt that God thence turn away His face; and then safely thou askest, and He heareth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:202
verses.text: "A clean heart create in me, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:203
verses.text: "Create"—he meant to say, "as it were begin something new".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:204
verses.text: But, because repentant he was praying (that had committed some sin, which before he had committed, he was more innocent), after what manner he hath said "create" he showeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:205
verses.text: "And a right spirit renew in my inner parts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:206
verses.text: By my doing, he saith, the uprightness of my spirit hath been made old and bowed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:207
verses.text: For he saith in another Psalm, "They have bowed my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:208
verses.text: And when a man doth make himself stoop unto earthly lusts, he is "bowed" in a manner, but when he is made erect for things above, upright is his heart made, in order that God may be good to him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:209
verses.text: For, "How good is the God of Israel to the upright of heart!" Moreover, brethren, listen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:210
verses.text: Sometimes God in this world chastiseth for his sin him that He pardoneth in the world to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:211
verses.text: For even to David himself, to whom it had been already said by the Prophet, "Thy sin is put away," there happened certain things which God had threatened for that very sin For his son Abessalom against him waged bloody war, and many ways humbled his father He was walking in grief, in the tribulation of his humiliation, so resigned to God, that, ascribing to Him all that was just, he confessed that he was suffering nothing undeservedly, having now an heart upright, to which God was not displeasing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:212
verses.text: A slanderous person and one throwing in his teeth harsh curses he patiently heard, one of the soldiers on the opposite side, that were with his unnatural son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:213
verses.text: And when he was heaping curses upon the king, one of the companions of David, enraged, would have gone and smitten him; but he is kept back by David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:214
verses.text: And he is kept back how? For that he said, God sent him to curse me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:215
verses.text: Acknowledging his guilt he embraced his penance, seeking glory not his own, praising the Lord in that good which he had, praising the Lord in that which he was suffering, "blessing the Lord alway, ever His praise was in his mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:216
verses.text: Such are all the upright in heart: not those crooked persons who think themselves upright and God crooked: who when they do any evil thing, rejoice; when they suffer any evil thing, blaspheme; nay, if set in tribulation and scourging, they say from their distorted heart, "O God, what have I done to Thee?" Truly it is because they have done nothing to God, for they have done all to themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:217
verses.text: "And an upright spirit, renew in my inner parts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:218
verses.text: "Cast me not forth from Thy face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:219
verses.text: Turn away Thy face from my sins: and "cast me not forth from Thy face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:220
verses.text: Whose face he feareth, upon the face of the Same he calleth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:221
verses.text: "And Thy Holy Spirit take not away from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:222
verses.text: For in one confessing there is the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:223
verses.text: Even now, to the gift of the Holy Spirit it belongeth, that what thou hast done displeaseth thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:224
verses.text: The unclean spirit sins do please; the Holy One they displease.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:225
verses.text: Though then thou still implore pardon, yet thou art joined to God on the other part, because the evil thing that thou hast committed displeaseth thee: for the same thing displeaseth both thee and Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:226
verses.text: Now, to assail thy fever, ye are two, thou and the Physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:227
verses.text: For the reason that there cannot be confession of sin and punishment of sin in a man of himself: when one is angry with himself, and is displeasing to himself, then it is not without the gift of the Holy Spirit, nor doth he say, Thy Holy Spirit give to me, but, "Take not away from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:228
verses.text: "Give back to me the exultation of Thy salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:229
verses.text: "Give back" what I had; what by sinning I had lost: to wit, of Thy Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:230
verses.text: For who without Him can be made whole? Because even before that He was Son of Mary, "In the beginning He was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God;" and so, by the holy fathers a future dispensation of flesh taken upon Him, was looked for; as is believed by us to have been done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:231
verses.text: Times are changed, not faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:232
verses.text: "And with Principal Spirit confirm me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:233
verses.text: Some have here understood the Trinity in God, Itself God; the dispensation of Flesh being excepted therefrom: since it is written, "God is a Spirit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:234
verses.text: For that which is not body, and yet is, seemeth to exist in such sort as that it is spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:235
verses.text: Therefore some understand here the Trinity spoken of: "In upright Spirit," the Son; in "Holy Spirit," Holy Ghost; in "Principal Spirit," Father It is not any heretical opinion, therefore, whether this be so, or whether "upright Spirit" He would have to be taken of man himself (when He saith, "An upright spirit renew in my inner parts"), which I have bowed and distorted by sinning, so that in that case the Holy Spirit be Himself the Principal Spirit: which also he would not have to be taken away from him, and thereby would have himself to be confirmed therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:236
verses.text: But see what he annexeth: "With Principal Spirit," he saith, "confirm Thou me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:237
verses.text: Wherein "confirm"? Because Thou hast pardoned me, because I am secure, that what Thou hast forgiven is not to be ascribed, on this being made secure and with this grace confirmed, therefore I am not ungrateful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:238
verses.text: But I shall do what? "I would teach unrighteous men Thy ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:239
verses.text: Being myself of the unrighteous (that is, one that was myself an unrighteous man, now no longer unrighteous; the Holy Spirit not having been taken away from me, and I being confirmed with Principal Spirit).

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:240
verses.text: "I would teach unrighteous men Thy ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:241
verses.text: What ways wilt thou teach unrighteous men? "And ungodly men to Thee shall be converted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:242
verses.text: If David's sin is counted for ungodliness, let not ungodly men despair of themselves, forasmuch as God hath spared an ungodly man; but let them take heed that to Him they be converted, that His ways they learn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:243
verses.text: But if David's deed is not counted for ungodliness, but this is properly call ungodliness, namely, to apostatize from God, not to worship one God, or never to have worshipped, or to have forsaken, Him whom one did worship, then what he saith hath the force of superabundance, "And ungodly men shall to Thee be converted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:244
verses.text: So full art thou of the fatness of mercy, that for those converted to Thee, not only sinners of any sort, but even ungodly, there is no cause for despair.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:245
verses.text: Wherefore? That believing on Him that justifieth an ungodly man, their faith may be counted for righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:246
verses.text: "Deliver me from bloods, O God, God of my health".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:247
verses.text: The Latin translator hath expressed, though by a word not Latin, yet an accuracy from the Greek For we all know that in Latin, sanguines (bloods) are not spoken of, nor yet sanguina (bloods in the neuter), nevertheless because the Greek translator hath thus used the plural number, not without reason, but because he found this in the original language the Hebrew, a godly translator hath preferred to use a word not Latin, rather than one not exact.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:248
verses.text: Wherefore then hath he said in the plural number, "From bloods"? In many bloods, as in the origin of the sinful flesh, many sins he would have to be understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:249
verses.text: The Apostle having regard to the very sins which come of the corruption of flesh and blood, saith, "Flesh and blood shall not possess the kingdom of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:250
verses.text: For doubtless, after the true faith of the same Apostle, that flesh shall rise again and shall itself gain incorruption, as He saith Himself, "This corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal put on immortality".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:251
verses.text: Because then this corruption is of sin, by the name thereof sins are called.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:252
verses.text: In like manner as both that morsel of flesh and member which playeth in the mouth when we articulate words is called a tongue, and that is called a tongue which by the tongue is made, so we call one tongue the Greek, another the Latin; for the flesh is not diverse, but the sound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:253
verses.text: In the same manner, then, as the speech which is made by the tongue is called a tongue; so also the iniquity which is made by blood is called blood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:254
verses.text: Heeding, then, his many iniquities, as in the expression above, "And all my iniquities blot out," and ascribing them to the corruption of flesh and blood, "Free me," he saith, "from bloods:" that is, free me from iniquities, cleanse me from all corruption.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:255
verses.text: Not yet is the substance, but certain hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:256
verses.text: "And my tongue shall exult of Thy righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:257
verses.text: "O Lord, my lips Thou shalt open, and my mouth shall tell of Thy praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:258
verses.text: "Thy praise," because I have been created: "Thy praise," because sinning I have not been forsaken: "Thy praise," because I have been admonished to confess: "Thy praise," because in order that I might be secured I have been cleansed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:259
verses.text: "Because if Thou hadst willed sacrifice, I would have given it surely".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:260
verses.text: David was living at that time when sacrifices of victim animals were offered to God, and he saw these times that were to be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:261
verses.text: Do we not perceive ourselves in these words? Those sacrifices were figurative, foretelling the One Saving Sacrifice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:262
verses.text: Not even we have been left without a Sacrifice to offer to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:263
verses.text: For hear what he saith, having a concern for his sin, and wishing the evil thing which he hath done to be forgiven him: "If Thou hadst willed," he saith, "sacrifice, I would have given it surely.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:264
verses.text: With holocausts Thou wilt not be delighted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:265
verses.text: Nothing shall we therefore offer? So shall we come to God? And whence shall we propitiate Him? Offer; certainly in thyself thou hast what thou mayest offer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:266
verses.text: Do not from without fetch frankincense, but say, "In me are, O God, Thy vows, which I will render of praise to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:267
verses.text: Do not from without seek cattle to slay, thou hast in thyself what thou mayest kill.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:268
verses.text: "Sacrifice to God is a spirit troubled, a heart contrite and humbled God despiseth not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:269
verses.text: Utterly he despiseth bull, he-goat, ram: now is not the time that these should be offered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:270
verses.text: They were offered when they indicated something, when they promised something; when the things promised come, the promises are taken away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:271
verses.text: "A heart contrite and humbled God despiseth not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:272
verses.text: Ye know that God is high: if thou shalt have made thyself high, He will be from thee; if thou shalt have humbled thyself, He will draw near to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:273
verses.text: See who this is: David as one man was seeming to implore; see ye here our image and the type of the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:274
verses.text: "Deal kindly, O Lord, in Thy good will with Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:275
verses.text: With this Sion deal kindly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:276
verses.text: What is Sion? A city holy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:277
verses.text: What is a city holy? That which cannot be hidden, being upon a mountain established.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:278
verses.text: Sion in prospect, because it hath prospect of something which it hopeth for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:279
verses.text: For Sion is interpreted "prospect," and Jerusalem, "vision of peace".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:280
verses.text: Ye perceive then yourselves to be in Sion and in Jerusalem, if being sure ye look for hope that is to be, and if ye have peace with God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:281
verses.text: "And be the walls of Jerusalem builded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:282
verses.text: "Deal kindly, O Lord, in Thy good will with Sion, and be the walls of Jerusalem builded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:283
verses.text: For not to herself let Sion ascribe her merits: do Thou with her deal kindly, "Be the walls of Jerusalem builded:" be the battlements of our immortality laid, in faith and hope and charity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:284
verses.text: "Then Thou shalt accept the sacrifice of righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:285
verses.text: But now sacrifice for iniquity, to wit, a spirit troubled, and a heart humbled; then the sacrifice of righteousness, praises alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:286
verses.text: For, "Blessed they that dwell in Thy house, for ever and ever they shall praise Thee:" for this is the sacrifice of righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:287
verses.text: "Oblations and holocausts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:288
verses.text: What are "holocausts"? A whole victim by fire consumed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:289
verses.text: When a whole beast was laid upon the altar with fire to be consumed, it was called a holocaust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:290
verses.text: May divine fire take us up whole, and that fervour catch us whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:291
verses.text: What fervour? "Neither is there that hideth himself from the heat thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:292
verses.text: What fervour? That whereof speaketh the Apostle: "In spirit fervent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:293
verses.text: Be not merely our soul taken up by that divine fire of wisdom, but also our body; that it may earn their immortality; so be it lifted up for a holocaust, that death be swallowed into victory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:294
verses.text: "Oblations and holocausts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:295
verses.text: "Then shall they lay upon thine altar calves".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 52:296
verses.text: Whence "calves"? What shall He therein choose? Will it be the innocence of the new age, or necks freed from the yoke of the law?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:1
verses.text: Psalm LII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:2
verses.text: The title of the Psalm hath: "At the end, understanding of David, when there came Doeg the Edomite and told Saul, David hath come into the house of Abimelech:" whereas we read that he had come into the house of Achimelech.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:3
verses.text: And it may chance that we do not unreasonably suppose, that because of the similarity of a name and the difference of one syllable, or rather of one letter, the titles have been varied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:4
verses.text: In the manuscripts, however, of the Psalms, when we looked into them, rather Abimelech we have found than Achimelech.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:5
verses.text: And since in another place thou hast a most evident Psalm, intimating not a dissimilarity of name, but an utterly different name; when, for instance, David changed his face before King Achish, not be fore king Abimelech, and he sent him away, and he departed: and yet the title of the Psalm is thus written, "When he changed his countenance in the presence of Abimelech"—the very change of name maketh us the rather intent upon a mystery, lest thou shouldest pursue the quasi-facts of history, and despise the sacred veilings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:6
verses.text: Observe ye two kinds of men; the one of men labouring, the other of those among whom they labour: the one of men thinking of earth, the other of heaven: the one of men weighing down their heart unto the deep, the other of men with Angels their heart conjoining: the one trusting in earthly things, wherein this world aboundeth, the other confiding in heavenly things, which God, who lieth not, hath promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:7
verses.text: But mingled are these kinds of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:8
verses.text: We see now the citizen of Jerusalem, citizen of the kingdom of heaven, have some office upon earth: to wit, one weareth purple, is a Magistrate, is aedile, is Proconsul, is Emperor, doth direct the earthly republic: but he hath his heart above, if he is a Christian, if he is a believer, if he is godly, if he is despising those things wherein he is, and trusteth in that wherein he is not yet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:9
verses.text: Of which kind was that holy woman Esther, who, though she was wife of a king, incurred the danger of interceding for her countrymen: and when she was praying before God, where she could not lie, in her prayer said, that her royal ornaments were to her but as the cloth of a menstruous woman Despair we not then of the citizens of the kingdom of heaven, when we see them engaged in any of Babylon's matters, doing something earthly in republic earthly: nor again let us forthwith congratulate all men that we see doing matters heavenly; because even the sons of pestilence sit sometimes in the seat of Moses, of whom is said, "What things they say, do ye: but what things they do, do not: for they say, and do not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:10
verses.text: Those, amid earthly things, lift up heart unto heaven, these, amid heavenly words, trail heart upon earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:11
verses.text: But there will come time of winnowing, when both are to be severed with greatest diligence, in order that no grain may pass over unto the heap of chaff that is to be burned, that not one single straw may pass over to the mass that is to be stored in the barn So long as then now it is mingled, hear we thence our voice, that is, voice of the citizens of the kingdom of heaven (for to this we ought to aspire, to bear with evil men here, rather than be borne with by good men): and let us conjoin ourselves to this voice, both with ear and with tongue, and with heart and work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:12
verses.text: Which if we shall have done, we are here speaking in those things which we hear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:13
verses.text: Let us therefore speak first of the evil body of kingdom earthly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:14
verses.text: "Why doth he glory in malice that is mighty?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:15
verses.text: Observe, my brethren, the glorying of malignity, the glorying of evil men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:16
verses.text: Where is glorying? "Why doth he glory in malice that is mighty?" That is, he that in malice is mighty, why doth he glory? There is need that a man be mighty, but in goodness, not in malice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:17
verses.text: Is it any great thing to glory in malice? To build a house doth belong to few men, any ignorant man you please can pull down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:18
verses.text: To sow wheat, to dress the crop, to wait until it ripen, and in that fruit on which one has laboured to rejoice, doth belong to few men: with one spark any man you please can burn all the crop.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:19
verses.text: To breed an infant, when born to feed him, to educate, to bring him on to youth's estate, is a great task: to kill him in one moment of time any one you please is able.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:20
verses.text: Therefore those things which are done for destruction, are most easily done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:21
verses.text: "He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord:" he that glorieth, let him glory in goodness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:22
verses.text: Thou gloriest, because thou art mighty in evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:23
verses.text: What art thou about to do, O mighty man, what art thou about to do, boasting thyself much? Thou art about to kill a man: this thing also a scorpion, this also one fever, this also a poisonous fungus can do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:24
verses.text: To this is thy mightiness reduced, that it be made equal to a poisonous fungus? This therefore do the good citizens of Jerusalem, who not in malice but in goodness glory: firstly, that not in themselves, but in the Lord they glory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:25
verses.text: Secondly, that those things which make for edification they earnestly do, and do such things as are strong to abide: but things which make for destruction they may do, for the discipline of men advancing, not for the oppression of the innocent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:26
verses.text: To this mightiness then that earthly body being compared, why may it not hear out of these words, "Why doth he glory in malice that is mighty?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:27
verses.text: "In iniquity the whole day upon injustice hath thy tongue thought" : that is, in the whole of time, without weariness, without intermission, without cessation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:28
verses.text: And when thou doest not, thou thinkest; so that when anything of evil is away from thy hands, from thy heart it is not away; either thou doest an evil thing, or while thou canst not do, thou sayest an evil thing, that is, thou evil-speakest: or when not even this thou canst do, thou willest and thinkest an evil thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:29
verses.text: "The whole day," then, that is, without intermission.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:30
verses.text: We expect punishment to this man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:31
verses.text: Is he to himself a small punishment? Thou threatenest him: thou, when thou threatenest him, wilt send him whither? Unto evil? Send him away unto himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:32
verses.text: In order that thou mayest vent much rage, thou art going to give him into the power of beasts: unto himself he is worse than beasts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:33
verses.text: For a beast can mangle his body: of himself he cannot leave his heart whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:34
verses.text: Within, against himself he doth rage of himself, and dost thou from without seek for stripes? Nay, pray God for him, that he may be set free from himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:35
verses.text: Nevertheless in this Psalm, my brethren, there is not a prayer for evil men, or again st evil men, but a prophecy of what is to result to evil men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:36
verses.text: Think not therefore that the Psalm of ill-will saith anything: for it is said in the spirit of prophecy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:37
verses.text: There followeth then what? All thy might and all thy thought of iniquity all the day, and meditation of malignity in thy tongue without intermission, hath performed what, done what? "As with a sharp razor thou hast done deceit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:38
verses.text: See what do evil men to Saints, they scrape their hair.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:39
verses.text: What is it that I have said? If there be such citizens of Jerusalem, that hear the voice of their Lord, of their King, saying, "Fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul:" that hear the voice which but now from the Gospel hath been read, "What doth it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and of himself make wreck:" they despise all present good things, and above all life itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:40
verses.text: And what is Doeg's razor to do to a man on this earth meditating on the kingdom of heaven, and about to be in the kingdom of heaven, having with him God, and about to abide with God? What is that razor to do? Hair it is to scrape, it is to make a man bald.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:41
verses.text: And this belongeth to Christ, who in the Place of a Skull was crucified It maketh also the son of Core, which is interpreted baldness For this hair signifieth a superfluity of things temporal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:42
verses.text: Which hairs indeed are not made by God superfluously on the body of men, but for a sort of ornament: yet because without feeling they are cut off, they that cleave to the Lord with their heart, so have these earthly things as they have hair.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:43
verses.text: But sometimes even something of good with "hair" is wrought, when thou breakest bread to the hungry, the poor without roof thou bringest into thy house; if thou shalt have seen one naked, thou coverest him: lastly, the Martyrs themselves also imitating the Lord, blood for the Church shedding, hearing that voice, "As Christ laid down His life for us, so also ought we also to lay down for the brethren," in a certain way with their hair did good to us, that is, with those things which that razor can lop off or scrape.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:44
verses.text: But that therefore even with the very hair some good can be done, even that woman a sinner intimated, who, when she had wept over the feet of the Lord, with her hair wiped what with tears she wetted Signifying what? That when thou shalt have pitied any one, thou oughtest to relieve him also if thou canst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:45
verses.text: For when thou hast pity, thou sheddest as it were tears: when thou relievest, thou wipest with hair.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:46
verses.text: And if this to any one, how much more to the feet of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:47
verses.text: The feet of the Lord are what? The holy Evangelists, whereof is said, "How beautiful are the feet of them that tell of peace, that tell of good things!" Therefore like a razor let Doeg whet his tongue, let him whet deceit as much as he may: he will take away superfluous temporal things; will he necessary things everlasting?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:48
verses.text: "Thou hast loved malice above benignity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:49
verses.text: Before thee was benignity; herself thou shouldest have loved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:50
verses.text: For thou wast not going to expend anything, nor wast thou going to fetch something to love by a distant voyage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:51
verses.text: Benignity is before thee, iniquity before thee: compare and choose.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:52
verses.text: But perchance thou hast an eye wherewith thou seest malignity, and hast no eye wherewith thou seest benignity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:53
verses.text: Woe to the iniquitous heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:54
verses.text: What is worse, it doth turn away itself, that it may not see what it is able to see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:55
verses.text: For what of such hath been said in another place? "He would not understand that he might do good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:56
verses.text: For it is not said, he could not: but "he would not," he saith, "understand that he might do good," he closed his eyes from present light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:57
verses.text: And what followeth? "Of iniquity he hath meditated in his bed;" that is, in the inner secrecy of his heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:58
verses.text: Some reproach of this kind is heaped upon this Doeg the Edomite, a malignant body, a motion of earth, not abiding, not heavenly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:59
verses.text: "Thou hast loved malignity above benignity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:60
verses.text: For wilt thou know how an evil man doth see both, and the former he doth rather choose, from the other doth turn himself away? Wherefore doth he cry out when he suffereth anything unjustly? Wherefore doth he then exaggerate as much as he can the iniquity, and praise benignity, censuring him that hath wrought in him malignity above benignity? Be he then a rule to himself for seeing: out of himself he shall be judged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:61
verses.text: Moreover, if he do what is written, "Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself;"  and, "Whatsoever good things ye will that men should do unto you, these also do ye do unto them:" at home he hath means of knowing, because what on himself he will not have to be done, he ought not to do to another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:62
verses.text: "Thou hast loved malice above benignity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:63
verses.text: Iniquitously, inordinately, perversely thou wouldest raise water above oil: the water will be sunk, the oil will remain above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:64
verses.text: Thou wouldest under darkness place a light: the darkness will be put to flight, the light will remain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:65
verses.text: Above heaven thou wouldest place earth, by its weight the earth will fall into its place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:66
verses.text: Thou therefore wilt be sunk by loving malice above benignity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:67
verses.text: For never will malice overcome benignity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:68
verses.text: "Thou hast loved malice above benignity: iniquity more than to speak of equity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:69
verses.text: Before thee is equity, before thee is iniquity: one tongue thou hast, whither thou wilt thou turnest it: wherefore then rather to iniquity and not to equity? Food of bitterness dost thou not give to thy belly, and food of iniquity dost thou give to thy malignant tongue? As thou choosest whereon to live, so choose what thou mayest speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:70
verses.text: Thou preferrest iniquity to equity, and preferrest malice to benignity; thou indeed preferrest, but above what can ever be but benignity and equity? But thou, by placing thyself in a manner upon those things which it is necessary should go beneath, wilt not make them to be above good things, but thou with them wilt be sunk unto evil things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:71
verses.text: Because of this there followeth in the Psalm, "Thou hast loved all words of sinking under".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:72
verses.text: Rescue therefore thyself, if thou canst, from sinking under.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:73
verses.text: From shipwreck thou art fleeing, and dost embrace lead! If thou wilt not sink, catch at a plank, be borne on wood, let the Cross carry thee through.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:74
verses.text: But now because thou art a Doeg the Edomite, a "motion," and "of earth," thou doest what? "Thou hast loved all words of sinking-under, a tongue deceitful".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:75
verses.text: This hath preceded, words of sinking-under have followed a tongue deceitful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:76
verses.text: What is a tongue deceitful? A minister of guile is a tongue deceitful, of men bearing one thing in heart, another thing from mouth bringing forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:77
verses.text: But in these is overthrowing, in these sinking under.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:78
verses.text: "Wherefore God shall destroy thee at the end" : though now thou seemest to flourish like grass in the field before the heat of the sun.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:79
