verses.text: For, "All flesh is grass, and the brightness of man as the bloom of grass: the grass hath withered, and the bloom hath fallen down: but the word of the Lord abideth for everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:80
verses.text: Behold that to which thou mayest bind thyself, to what "abideth for everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:81
verses.text: For if to grass, and to the bloom of grass, thou shalt have bound thyself, since the grass shall wither, and the bloom shall fall down, "God shall destroy thee at the end:" and if not now, certainly at the end He shall destroy, when that winnowing shall have come, and the heap of chaff from the solid grain shall have been separated Is not the solid grain for the barns, and the chaff for the fire? Shall not the whole of that Doeg stand at the left hand, when the Lord is to say, "Go ye into fire everlasting, which hath been prepared for the devil and his angels"? Therefore "God shall destroy at the end: shall pluck thee out, and shall remove thee from thy dwelling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:82
verses.text: Now then this Doeg the Edomite is in a dwelling: "But a servant abideth not in the house for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:83
verses.text: Even he worketh something of good, even if not with his doings, at least with the words of God, so that in the Church, when he "seeketh his own," he would say, at least, those things which are of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:84
verses.text: "But He shall remove thee from thy dwelling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:85
verses.text: "Verily, verily, I say unto you, they have received their reward".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:86
verses.text: "And thy root from the land of the living".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:87
verses.text: Therefore in the land of the living we ought to have root.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:88
verses.text: Be our root there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:89
verses.text: Out of sight is the root: fruits may be seen, root cannot be seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:90
verses.text: Our root is our love, our fruits are our works: it is needful that thy works proceed from love, then is thy root in the land of the living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:91
verses.text: Then shall be rooted up that Doeg, nor any wise shall he be able there to abide, because neither more deeply there hath he fixed a root: but it shall be with him in like manner as it is with those seeds on the rock, which even if a root they throw out, yet, because moisture they have not, with the risen sun forthwith do wither.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:92
verses.text: But, on the other hand, they that fix a root more deeply, hear from the Apostle what? "I bow my knees for you to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye may be in love rooted and grounded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:93
verses.text: And because there now is root, "That ye may be able," he saith, "to comprehend what is the height, and breadth, and length, and depth: to know also the supereminent knowledge of the love of Christ, that ye may be filled unto all the fulness of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:94
verses.text: Of such fruits so great a root is worthy, being so single, so budding, for buddings so deeply grounded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:95
verses.text: But truly this man's root shall be rooted up from the land of the living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:96
verses.text: "And the just shall see, and shall fear; and over him they shall laugh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:97
verses.text: Shall fear when? Shall laugh when? Let us therefore understand, and make a distinction between those two times of fearing and laughing, which have their several uses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:98
verses.text: For so long as we are in this world, not yet must we laugh, lest hereafter we mourn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:99
verses.text: We have read what is reserved at the end for this Doeg, we have read and because we understand and believe, we see but fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:100
verses.text: This, therefore, hath been said, "The just shall see, and shall fear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:101
verses.text: So long as we see what will result at the end to evil men, wherefore do we fear? Because the Apostle hath said, "In fear and trembling work out your own salvation:" because it hath been said in a Psalm, "Serve the Lord in fear, and exult unto Him with trembling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:102
verses.text: Wherefore "with fear"? "Wherefore let him that thinketh himself to stand, see that he fall not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:103
verses.text: Wherefore "with trembling"? Because he saith in another place: "Brethren, if a man shall have been overtaken in any delinquency, ye that are spiritual instruct such sort in the spirit of gentleness; heeding thyself, lest thou also be tempted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:104
verses.text: Therefore, the just that are now, that live of faith, so see this Doeg, what to him is to result, that nevertheless they fear also for themselves: for what they are to-day, they know; what to-morrow they are to be, they know not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:105
verses.text: Now, therefore, "The just shall see, and they shall fear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:106
verses.text: But when shall they laugh? When iniquity shall have passed over; when it shall have flown over; as now to a great degree hath flown over the time uncertain; when shall have been put to flight the darkness of this world, wherein now we walk not but by the lamp of the Scriptures, and therefore fear as though in night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:107
verses.text: For we walk by prophecy; whereof saith the Apostle Peter, "We have a more sure prophetic word, to which giving heed ye do well, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day shine, and the day-star arise in your hearts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:108
verses.text: So long then as by a lamp we walk, it is needful that with fear we should live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:109
verses.text: But when shall have come our day, that is, the manifestation of Christ, whereof the same Apostle saith, "When Christ shall have appeared, your life, then ye also shall appear with Himself in glory," then the just shall laugh at that Doeg.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:110
verses.text: But what shall they then say that shall laugh? "And over him they shall laugh; and shall say, Behold a man that hath not set God for his helper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:111
verses.text: See ye the body earthly! "As much as thou shalt have, so great shalt thou be," is a proverb of covetous men, of grasping men, of men oppressing the innocent, of men seizing upon other men's goods, of men denying things entrusted to their care.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:112
verses.text: Of what sort is this proverb? "As much as thou shalt have, so great shalt thou be;" that is, as much as thou shalt have had of money, as much as thou shalt have gotten, by so much the more mighty shalt thou be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:113
verses.text: "Behold a man that hath not set God for his helper, but hath trusted in the multitude of his riches".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:114
verses.text: Let not a poor man, one perchance that is evil, say, I am not of this body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:115
verses.text: For he hath heard the Prophet saying, "He hath trusted in the multitude of his riches:" forthwith if he is poor, he heedeth his rags, he hath observed near him perchance a rich man among the people of God more richly apparelled, and he saith in his heart, Of this man he speaketh; doth he speak of me? Do not thence except thyself, do not separate thyself, unless thou shalt have seen and feared, in order that thou mayest hereafter laugh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:116
verses.text: For what doth it profit thee, if thou dost want means, and thou burnest with cupidity? When our Lord Jesus Christ to that rich man that was grieved, and that was departing from Him, had said, "Go, sell all that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven, and come follow Me:" and great hopelessness for rich men foretold, so that He said, more easily could a camel pass through the eye of a needle, than a rich man enter into the kingdom of Heaven, were not forthwith the disciples grieved, saying with themselves, "Who shall be able to be saved?" Therefore when they were saying, "Who shall be able to be saved?" did they think of the few rich men, did there escape them so great a multitude of poor men? Could they not say to themselves, If it is hard, aye an impossible thing, that rich men should enter into the kingdom of heaven, as it is impossible that a camel should enter through the eye of a needle, let all poor men enter into the kingdom of heaven, be the rich alone shut out? For how few are the rich men? But of poor men are thousands innumerable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:117
verses.text: For not the coats are we to look upon in the kingdom of heaven; but for every one's garment shall be reckoned the effulgence of righteousness: there shall be therefore poor men equal to Angels of God, clothed with the stoles of immortality, they shall shine as the sun in the kingdom of their Father: what reason is there for us about a few rich men to be concerned, or distressed? This thought not the Apostles; but when the Lord had spoken this, "It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of heaven:" they saying to themselves, "Who shall be able to be saved," meant what? Not means, but desires; for they saw even poor men themselves, even if not having money, yet to have covetousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:118
verses.text: And that ye may know, that not money in a rich man, but covetousness is condemned, attend to what I say; Thou observest that rich man standing near thee, and perchance in him is money, and is not covetousness; in thee is not money, and is covetousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:119
verses.text: A poor man full of sores, full of woe, licked by dogs, having no help, having no morsel, not having perchance a mere garment, was borne by the Angels unto Abraham's bosom Ho! being a poor man, art thou glad now; for are even sores by thee to be desired? Is not thy patrimony soundness? There is not in this Lazarus the merit of poverty, but that of godliness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:120
verses.text: For thou seest who was borne up, thou seest not whither he was borne up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:121
verses.text: Who was borne up by Angels? A poor man, full of woe, full of sores.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:122
verses.text: Whither was he borne up? Unto Abraham's bosom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:123
verses.text: Read the Scriptures, and thou shall find Abraham to have been a rich man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:124
verses.text: In order that thou mayest know, that not riches are blamed; Abraham had much gold, silver, cattle, household, was a rich man, and unto his bosom Lazarus, a poor man, was borne up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:125
verses.text: Unto bosom of rich man, poor man: are not rather both unto God rich men, both in cupidity poor men?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:126
verses.text: Therefore that man having been condemned that "hath trusted in the multitude of his riches, and hath prevailed in his vanity:" for what more vain, than he that thinketh coin more to avail than God? Therefore that man having been condemned that said, blessed of the people to whom these things are: thou that sayest, "Blessed the people of whom is the Lord their own God," dost think of thyself what? dost hope for thyself what? "But I;" now at length hear that body: "But I am like an olive, fruit-bearing in the house of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:127
verses.text: Not one man speaketh, but that olive fruit-bearing, whence have been pruned the proud branches, and the humble wild olive graffed in "Like an olive, fruit-bearing in the house of God, I have trusted in the mercy of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:128
verses.text: He did what? "In the multitude of his riches:" therefore his root shall be plucked out from the land of the living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:129
verses.text: "But I," because "like an olive, fruit-bearing in the house of God," the root whereof is nourished, is not rooted out, "have trusted in the mercy of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:130
verses.text: But perchance now? For even herein men err sometimes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:131
verses.text: God indeed they worship, and are not now like to that Doeg: but though on God they rely, it is for temporal things nevertheless; so that they say to themselves, I worship my God, who will make me rich upon earth, who to me will give sons, who to me will give a wife.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:132
verses.text: Such things indeed giveth none but God, but God would not have Himself for the sake of such things to be loved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:133
verses.text: For to this end oftentimes those things He giveth even to evil men, in order that some other thing good men of Him may learn to seek.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:134
verses.text: In what manner then sayest thou, "I have trusted in the mercy of God"? Perchance for obtaining temporal things? Nay but, "For everlasting and world without end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:135
verses.text: The expression, "For everlasting," he willed to repeat by adding, "world without end," in order that by there repeating he might affirm how rooted he was in the love of the kingdom of heaven, and in the hope of everlasting felicity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:136
verses.text: "I will confess to Thee for ever, because Thou hast done".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:137
verses.text: "Hast done what?" Doeg Thou hast condemned, David Thou hast crowned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:138
verses.text: "I will confess to Thee for ever, because Thou hast done".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:139
verses.text: Great confession, "Because thou hast done"! "Hast done" what? except these very things which above have been spoken of, that like an olive fruit-bearing in the house of God, I should trust in the mercy of God for everlasting and world without end? Thou hast done: an ungodly man cannot justify himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:140
verses.text: But who is He that justifieth? "Believing," he saith, "on Him" that justifieth "the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:141
verses.text: "For what hast thou which thou hast not received? But if thou hast received, why dost thou glory as if thou hast not received, as if of thyself thou hast?" Be it far from me that I should so glory, saith he, that is opposed against Doeg, that beareth with Doeg upon earth, until he remove from his dwelling, and be rooted up from the land of the living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:142
verses.text: I glory not as if I have not received, but in God I glory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:143
verses.text: "And I will confess to Thee because Thou hast done," that is, because Thou hast done not according to my merits, but according to Thy mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:144
verses.text: But I have done what? If thou recollectest, "Before, I was a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:145
verses.text: But thou, what hast thou done? "But mercy I have obtained, because ignorant I did it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:146
verses.text: "I will confess to Thee for ever, because Thou hast done".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:147
verses.text: "And I will look for Thy name, for it is pleasant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:148
verses.text: Bitter is the world, but Thy name is pleasant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:149
verses.text: Even if certain sweet things are in the world, yet with bitterness they are digested.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:150
verses.text: Thy name is preferred, not only for greatness but also for pleasantness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:151
verses.text: "For unjust men have told to me their delights, but it is not as Thy law, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:152
verses.text: For if there were nothing sweet to the Martyrs, they would not have suffered with equanimity so great bitterness of tribulations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:153
verses.text: Their bitterness by any one was experienced, their sweetness easily could no one taste.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:154
verses.text: The name of God therefore is pleasant to men loving God above all pleasantnesses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:155
verses.text: "I will look for Thy name, for it is pleasant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:156
verses.text: And to what dost Thou prove that it is pleasant? Give me a palate to which it is pleasant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:157
verses.text: Praise honey as much as thou art able, exaggerate the sweetness thereof with what words thou shalt have the power: a man knowing not what honey is, unless h e shall have tasted, what thou sayest knoweth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:158
verses.text: Therefore the rather to the proof the Psalm inviting thee saith what? "Taste and see that sweet is the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:159
verses.text: Taste thou wilt not, and thou sayest, Is it pleasant? What is pleasant? If thou hast tasted, in thy fruit be it found, not in words alone, as it were only in leaves, lest by the curse of the Lord, to wither like that fig-tree thou shouldest deserve.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:160
verses.text: "Taste," he saith, "and see, that sweet is the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:161
verses.text: Taste and see: then ye shall see, if ye shall have tasted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:162
verses.text: But to a man not tasting, how provest thou? By praising the pleasantness of the name of God, whatsoever things thou shalt have said are words: something else is taste.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:163
verses.text: The words of His praise there hear even the ungodly, but none taste how sweet it is, but the Saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:164
verses.text: Further, a man discerning the sweetness of the name of God, and wishing to unfold and wishing to show the same, and not finding persons to whom he may unfold it; for to the Saints there is no need that he show it, because they even of themselves taste and know, but the ungodly cannot discern what they will not taste: doth, I say, what, because of the sweetness of the name of God? He hath borne him forthwith away from the crowds of the ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:165
verses.text: "And I will look," he saith, "for Thy name, for it is pleasant, in the sight of Thy Saints".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:166
verses.text: Pleasant is Thy name, but not in the sight of the ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 53:167
verses.text: I know how sweet a thing it is, but it is to them that have tasted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:1
verses.text: Psalm LIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:2
verses.text: Of this Psalm we undertake to treat with you, as far as the Lord supplieth us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:3
verses.text: A brother biddeth us that we may have the will, and prayeth that we may have the power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:4
verses.text: If anything in haste perchance I shall have passed over, He that even to us deigneth to give what we shall be enabled to say, will supply it in you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:5
verses.text: The title of it is: "At the end, for Maeleth, understanding to David himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:6
verses.text: "For Maeleth," as we find in interpretations of Hebrew names, seemeth to say, For one travailing, or in pain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:7
verses.text: But who there is in this world that travaileth and is in pain, the faithful acknowledge, because thereof they are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:8
verses.text: Christ here travaileth, Christ here is in pain: the Head is above, the members below.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:9
verses.text: For one not travailing nor in pain would not say, "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" Him, with whom when persecuting He was travailing, being converted, He made to travail.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:10
verses.text: For he also was himself afterwards enlightened, and grafted on those members which he used to persecute; being pregnant with the same love, he said, "My little children, of whom again I travail, until Christ be formed in you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:11
verses.text: For the members therefore of Christ, for His Body which is the Ch urch, for that same One Man, that is, for that very unity, whereof the Head is above, this Psalm is sung.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:12
verses.text: Who are they, then, amid whom we travail and groan, if in the Body of Christ we are, if under Him, the Head, we live, if amongst His members we are counted? Who they are, hear ye.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:13
verses.text: "The unwise man hath said in his heart, There is no God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:14
verses.text: Such sort is it of men amid whom is pained and groaneth the Body of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:15
verses.text: If such is this sort of men, of not many do we travail; as far as seemeth to occur to our thoughts, very few there are; and a difficult thing it is to meet with a man that saith in his heart, "There is no God;" nevertheless, so few there are, that, fearing amid the many to say this, in their heart they say it, for that with mouth to say it they dare not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:16
verses.text: Not much then is that which we are bid to endure, hardly is it found: uncommon is that sort of men that say in their heart, "There is no God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:17
verses.text: But, if it be examined in another sense, is not that found to be in more men, which we supposed to be in men few and uncommon, and almost in none? Let them come forth into the midst that live evil lives, let us look into the doings of profligate, daring, and wicked men, of whom there is a great multitude; who foster day by day their sins, who, their acts having been changed into habit, have even lost sense of shame: this is so great a multitude of men, that the Body of Christ, set amid them, scarce dareth to censure that which it is not constrained to commit, and deemeth it a great matter for itself that the integrity of innocence be preserved in not doing that which now, by habit, either it doth not dare to blame, or if it shall have dared, there breaketh out the censure and recrimination of them that live evil lives, more readily than the free voice of them that live good lives.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:18
verses.text: And those men are such as say in their heart, "There is no God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:19
verses.text: Such men I am confuting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:20
verses.text: Whence confuting? That their doings please God, they judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:21
verses.text: He doth not therefore affirm, "some say," but "The unwise man hath said in his heart, There is no God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:22
verses.text: Which men do so far believe there is a God, that the same God they judge with what they do to be pleased.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:23
verses.text: But if thou being wise dost perceive, how "the unwise man hath said in his heart, There is no God," if thou give heed, if thou understand, if thou examine; he that thinketh that evil doings please God, Him he doth not think to be God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:24
verses.text: For if God is, He is just; if He is just, injustice displeaseth Him, iniquity displeaseth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:25
verses.text: But thou, when thou thinkest that iniquity pleaseth Him, dost deny God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:26
verses.text: For if God is one Whom iniquity displeaseth, but God seemeth not to thee to be one whom iniquity displeaseth, and there is no God but one whom iniquity displeaseth, then when thou sayest in thy heart, God doth countenance my iniquities, thou sayest nothing else than, "There is no God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:27
verses.text: Let us advert also to that sense, which concerning Christ our Lord Himself, our Head Himself, doth present itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:28
verses.text: For when Himself in form of a servant appeared on earth, they that crucified Him said, "He is not God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:29
verses.text: Because Son of God He was, truly God He was.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:30
verses.text: But they that are corrupted and have become abominable said what? "He is not God:" let us slay Him, "He is not God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:31
verses.text: Thou hast the voice of these very men in the book of Wisdom For after there had gone before the verse, "The unwise man hath said in his heart, There is no God;" as if reasons were required why the unwise man could say this, he hath subjoined, "Corrupted they are, and abominable have become in their iniquities".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:32
verses.text: Hear ye those corrupted men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:33
verses.text: "For they have said with themselves, not rightly thinking:" corruption beginneth with evil belief, thence it proceedeth to depraved morals, thence to the most flagrant iniquities, these are the grades.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:34
verses.text: But what with themselves said they, thinking not rightly? "A small thing and with tediousness is our life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:35
verses.text: From this evil belief followeth that which also the Apostle hath spoken of, "Let us eat and drink, for to-morrow we shall die".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:36
verses.text: But in the former passage more diffusely luxury itself is described: "Let us crown us with roses, before they be withered; in every place let us leave the tokens of our gladness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:37
verses.text: After the more diffuse description of that luxury, what followeth? "Let us slay the poor just man:" this is therefore saying, "He is not God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:38
verses.text: Soft words they seemed but now to say: "Let us crown us with roses, before they be withered".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:39
verses.text: What more delicate, what more soft? Wouldest thou expect, out of this softness, Crosses, swords? Wonder not, soft are even the roots of brambles; if any one handle them, he is not pricked: but that wherewith thou shalt be pricked from thence hath birth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:40
verses.text: "Corrupted," therefore, are those men, "and abominable have become in their iniquities".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:41
verses.text: They say, "If Son of God He is, let Him come down from the Cross".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:42
verses.text: Behold them openly saying, "He is not God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:43
verses.text: "The Lord from Heaven hath looked forth upon the sons of men, that He might see if there is one understanding and seeking after God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:44
verses.text: What is this? "Corrupted they are," all these that say, "There is no God"? And what? Did it escape God, that they were become such? Or indeed to us would their inward thought be opened, except by Him it were told? If then He understood, if then He knew, what is this which hath been said, "that He might see"? For the words are of one inquiring, of one not knowing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:45
verses.text: "God from Heaven hath looked forth," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:46
verses.text: And as though He had found what He sought by looking upon, and by looking down from Heaven, He giveth sentence: "All men have gone aside, together useless they have become: there is not one that doeth good, not so much as one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:47
verses.text: Two questions arise somewhat difficult: for if God looketh out from Heaven, in order that He may see if there is one understanding or seeking after God; there stealeth upon an unwise man the thought, that God knoweth not all things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:48
verses.text: This is one question: what is the other? If there is not one that doeth good, is not so much as one; who is he that travaileth amid bad men? The former question then is solved as followeth: ofttimes the Scripture speaketh in such manner, that what by the gift of God a creature doth, God is said to do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:49
verses.text: For hence has been said the following also, "For the Spirit searcheth all things, even the depth of God;" not because He that knoweth all things searcheth, but because to thee hath been given the Spirit, which maketh thee also to search: and that which by His own gift thou doest, He is said to do; because without Him thou wouldest not do it: therefore God is said to do, when thou doest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:50
verses.text: And because this by the gift of God thou doest, God from heaven is "looking forth upon the sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:51
verses.text: The former question then, according to our measure, thus hath been solved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:52
verses.text: What is that which looking forth we acknowledge? What is that which looking forth God acknowledgeth? What (because here He giveth it) doth He acknowledge? Hear what it is; that "All have gone aside, together useless they have become: there is not one that doeth good, there is not so much as one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:53
verses.text: What then is that other question, but the same whereof a little before I have made mention? If, "There is not one that doeth good, is not so much as one," no one remaineth to groan amid evil men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:54
verses.text: Stay, saith the Lord, do not hastily give judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:55
verses.text: I have given to men to do well; but of Me, He saith, not of themselves: for of themselves evil they are: sons of men they are, when they do evil; when well, My sons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:56
verses.text: For this thing God doth, out of sons of men He maketh sons of God: because out of Son of God He hath made Son of Man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:57
verses.text: See what this participation is: there hath been promised to us a participation of Divinity: He lieth that hath promised, if He is not first made partaker of mortality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:58
verses.text: For the Son of God hath been made partaker of mortality, in order that mortal man may be made partaker of divinity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:59
verses.text: He that hath promised that His good is to be shared with thee, first with thee hath shared thy evil: He that to thee hath promised divinity, showeth in thee love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:60
verses.text: Therefore take away that men are sons of God, there remaineth that they are sons of men: "There is none that doeth good, is not so much as one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:61
verses.text: "Shall not all know that work iniquity, that devour My people for the food of bread"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:62
verses.text: There is therefore here a people of God that is being devoured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:63
verses.text: Nay, "There is not one that doeth good, there is not so much as one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:64
verses.text: We reply by the rule above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:65
verses.text: But this people that is devoured, this people that suffereth evil men, this that groaneth and travaileth amid evil men, now out of sons of men have been made sons of God: therefore are they devoured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:66
verses.text: For, "The counsel of the needy man thou hast confounded, because the Lord is his hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:67
verses.text: For ofttimes, in order that the people of God may be devoured, this very thing in it is despised, that it is the people of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:68
verses.text: I will pillage, he saith, and despoil; if he is a Christian, what will he do to me?But what followeth? "I will convince thee, and will set thee before thy face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:69
verses.text: Thou wilt not now know so as thou shouldest be displeasing to thyself, thou shalt know so as thou mayest mourn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:70
verses.text: For God cannot but show to the unrighteous their iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:71
verses.text: If He is not to show, who will they be that are to say, "What hath profited us pride, and what hath boasting of riches bestowed upon us?" For then shall they know, that now will not know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:72
verses.text: "Shall not all know?" etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:73
verses.text: Why hath He added, "for the food of bread"? As it were as bread, they eat My people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:74
verses.text: For all other things which we eat, we can eat now these, now those; not always this vegetable, not always this flesh, not always these apples: but always bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:75
verses.text: What is then, "Devour My people for the food of bread"? Without intermission, without cessation they devour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:76
verses.text: "On God they have not called".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:77
verses.text: He is comforting the man that groaneth, and chiefly by an admonition, lest by imitating evil men, who ofttimes prosper, they delight in evil doing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:78
verses.text: There is kept for thee that which to thee hath been promised: their hope is present, thine is future, but theirs is transient, thine sure; theirs false, thine true.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:79
verses.text: For they "upon God have not called".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:80
verses.text: Do not daily such men ask of God? They do "not" ask of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:81
verses.text: Give heed, if I am able to say this by the aid of God Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:82
verses.text: God gratuitously will have Himself to be worshipped, gratuitously will have Himself to be loved, that is chastely to be loved; not Himself to be loved for the reason that He giveth anything besides Himself, but because He giveth Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:83
verses.text: He then that calleth upon God in order that He may be made rich, on God doth not call: for upon that He calleth which to himself he willeth to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:84
verses.text: But now thou wouldest have coffer full, and conscience void: God filleth not coffer, but breast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:85
verses.text: What do outward riches profit thee, if inward need presseth thee? Therefore those men that for the sake of worldly comforts, that for the sake of earthly good things, that for the sake of present life and earthly felicity, call upon God, do not call upon God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:86
verses.text: For this reason what followeth concerning them? "There have they feared with fear, where there was no fear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:87
verses.text: For is there fear, if a man lose riches? There is no fear there, and yet in that case men are afraid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:88
verses.text: But if a man lose wisdom, truly there is fear, and in that case he is not afraid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:89
verses.text: Thou hast feared to give back money, and hast willed to lose fidelity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:90
verses.text: The Martyrs took not away property of other persons, but even their own they despised that they might not lose fidelity: and it was too little to lose money, when they were proscribed; they took also their life when they suffered: they lost life, in order that unto everlasting life they might find it Therefore there they feared, where they ought to have been afraid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:91
verses.text: But they that of Christ have said, "He is not God," have there feared where was no fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:92
verses.text: For they said, "If we shall have let Him go, there will come the Romans, and will take away from us both place and kingdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:93
verses.text: O folly and imprudence saying in its heart, "He is not God"! Thou hast feared to lose earth, thou hast lost Heaven: thou hast feared lest there should come the Romans, and take away from thee place and kingdom! Could they take away from thee God? What then remaineth? what but that thou confess, that thou hast willed to keep, and by keeping ill hast lost? For thou hast lost both place and nation by slaying Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:94
verses.text: For ye did will rather to slay Christ, than to lose place; and ye have lost place, and nation, and Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:95
verses.text: In fearing, they have slain Christ: but wherefore this? "For God hath scattered the bones of them that please men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:96
verses.text: Willing to please men, they feared to lose their place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:97
verses.text: But Christ Himself, of whom they said, "He is not God," willed rather to displease such men, as they were: sons of men, not sons of God, He willed rather to displease.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:98
verses.text: Thence were scattered their bones, His bones no one hath broken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:99
verses.text: "They were confounded, for God hath despised them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:100
verses.text: In very deed, brethren, as far as regardeth them, great confusion hath come to them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:101
verses.text: In the place where they crucified the Lord, whom for this cause they crucified, that they might not lose both place and nation, the Jews are not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:102
verses.text: "God," therefore, "hath despised them:" and yet in despising He warned them to be converted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:103
verses.text: Let them now confess Christ, and say, He is God, of whom they said, "He is not God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:104
verses.text: Let them return to the inheritance of their fathers, to the inheritance of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, let them possess with these very persons life eternal: though they have lost life temporal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:105
verses.text: Wherefore this? Because out of sons of men have been made sons of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:106
verses.text: For so long as they remain, and will not, there is not one that doeth good, there is not so much as one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:107
verses.text: "They were confounded, for God hath despised them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:108
verses.text: And as though to these very persons He were turned, He saith, "Who shall give out of Sion salvation to Israel?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:109
verses.text: O ye fools, ye revile, insult, buffet, besmear with spittings, with thorns ye crown, upon the Cross ye lift up; whom? "Who shall give out of Sion salvation to Israel?" Shall not That Same of whom ye have said, "He is not God"? "In God's turning away the captivity of His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:110
verses.text: For there turneth away the captivity of His people, no one but He that hath willed to be a captive in your own hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:111
verses.text: But what men shall understand this thing? "Jacob shall exult, and Israel shall rejoice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 54:112
verses.text: "Israel;" the true Jacob, and the true Israel, that younger, to whom the elder was servant,  shall himself exult, for he shall himself understand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:1
verses.text: Psalm LIV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:2
verses.text: The title  of this Psalm hath fruit in the prolixity thereof, if it be unde rstood: and because the Psalm is short, let us make up our not having to tarry over the Psalm by tarrying over the title.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:3
verses.text: For upon this dependeth every verse which is sung.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:4
verses.text: If any one, therefore, observe that which on the front of the house is fixed, secure he will enter; and, when he shall have entered, he will not err.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:5
verses.text: For this on the post itself is prominently marked, namely, in what manner within he may not be in error.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:6
verses.text: The title thereof standeth thus: "At the end, in hymns, understanding to David himself, when there came the Ziphites, and said to Saul, Behold, is not David hidden with us?" That Saul was persecutor of the holy man David, very well we know: that Saul was bearing the figure of a temporal kingdom, not to life but to death belonging, this also to your Love we remember to have imparted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:7
verses.text: And also that David himself was bearing the figure of Christ, or of the Body of Christ, ye ought both to know and to call to mind, ye that have already learned What then of the Ziphites? There was a certain village, Ziph, whereof the inhabitants were Ziphites, in whose country David had hidden himself, when Saul would find and slay him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:8
verses.text: These Ziphites then, when they had learned this, betrayed him to the king his persecutor, saying, "Behold, is not David hidden with us?" Of no good to them indeed was their betrayal, and to David himself of no harm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:9
verses.text: For their evil disposition was shown: but Saul not even after their betrayal could seize David; but rather in a certain cave in that very country, when into his hands Saul had been given to slay, David spared him, and that which he had in his power he did not But the other was seeking to do that which he had not in  his power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:10
verses.text: Let them that have been Ziphites take heed: let us see those whom to us the Psalm presenteth to be understood by the occasion of those same men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:11
verses.text: If we inquire then by what word is translated Ziphites, we find, "Men flourishing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:12
verses.text: Flourishing then were certain enemies to holy David, flourishing before him hiding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:13
verses.text: We may find them in mankind, if we are willing to understand the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:14
verses.text: Let us find here at first David hiding, and we shall find his adversaries flourishing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:15
verses.text: Observe David hiding: "For ye are dead," saith the Apostle to the members of Christ, "and your life is hid with Christ in God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:16
verses.text: These men, therefore, that are hiding, when shall they be flourishing? "When Christ," he saith, "your life, shall have appeared, then ye also with Him shall appear in glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:17
verses.text: When these men shall be flourishing, then shall be those Ziphites withering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:18
verses.text: For observe to what flower their glory is compared: "All flesh is grass, and the honour of flesh as the flower of grass".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:19
verses.text: What is the end? "The grass hath withered, and the flower hath fallen off".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:20
verses.text: Where then shall be David? See what followeth: "But the Word of the Lord abideth for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:21
verses.text: These men sometimes are observed of the weak sons of light, and their feet totter, when they have seen evil men in felicity to flourish, and they say to themselves, "Of what profit to me is innocence? What doth it advantage me that I serve God, that I keep His commandments, that I oppress no one, from no one plunder anything, hurt no one, that what I can I bestow? behold, all these things I do, and they flourish, I toil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:22
verses.text: But why? Wouldest thou also wish to be a Ziphite? They flourish in the world, wither in judgment, and after withering, into fire everlasting shall be cast: wouldest thou also choose this? Art thou ignorant of what He hath promised thee, who to thee hath come, what in Himself here He displayed? If the flower of the Ziphites were to be desired, would not Himself thy Lord also in this world have flourished? Or indeed was there wanting to Him the power to flourish? Nay but here He chose rather amid the Ziphites to hide, and to say to Pontius Pilate, as if to one being himself also a flower of the Ziphites, and in suspicion about His kingdom, "My kingdom is not of this world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:23
verses.text: Therefore here He was hidden: and all good men are hidden here, because their good is within, it is concealed, in the heart it is, where is faith, where charity, where hope, where their treasure is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:24
verses.text: Do these good things appear in the world? Both these good things are hidden, and the reward of these good things is hidden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:25
verses.text: "O God, in Thy name make me safe, and in Thy virtue judge me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:26
verses.text: Let the Church say this, hiding amid the Ziphites.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:27
verses.text: Let the Christian body say this, keeping secret the good of its morals, expecting in secret the reward of its merits, let it say this: "In Thy virtue judge me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:28
verses.text: Thou hast come, O Christ, humble Thou hast appeared, despised Thou hast been, scourged hast been, crucified hast been, slain hast been; but, on the third day hast risen, on the fortieth day into Heaven hast ascended: Thou sittest at the right hand of the Father, and no one seeth: Thy Spirit thence Thou hast sent, which men that were worthy have received; fulfilled with Thy love, the praise of that very humility of Thine throughout the world and nations they have preached: Thy name I see to excel among mankind, but nevertheless as weak to us hast Thou been preached.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:29
verses.text: For not even did that Teacher of the Gentiles say, that among us he knew anything, "Save Christ Jesus, and Him crucified;" in order that of Him we might choose the reproach, rather than the glory of the flourishing Ziphites.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:30
verses.text: Nevertheless, of Him he saith what? "Although He died of weakness, yet He liveth of the power of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:31
verses.text: He came then that He might die of weakness, He is to come that He may judge in the power of God: but through the weakness of the Cross His name hath been illustrious.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:32
verses.text: Whosoever shall not have believed upon the name made illustrious through weakness, shall stand in awe at the Judge, when He shall have come in power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:33
verses.text: But, lest He that once was weak, when He shall have come strong, with that fan send us to the left hand; may He "save us in His name, and judge us in His virtue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:34
verses.text: For who so rash as to have desired this, as to say to God, for instance "Judge me"? Is it not wont to be said to men for a curse, "God judge thee"? So evidently it is a curse, if He judge thee in His virtue; and shall not have saved thee in His name: but when in name precedent He shall have saved thee, to thy health in virtue consequent He shall judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:35
verses.text: Be thou wit hout care: that judgment shall not to thee be punishment, but dividing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:36
verses.text: For in a certain Psalm  thus is said: "Judge me, O God, and divide my cause from the nation unholy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:37
verses.text: "O God, hearken to my prayer, in Thy ears receive the words of my mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:38
verses.text: To Thee may my prayer attain, driven forth and darted out from the desire of Thy eternal blessings: to Thy ears I send it forth, aid it that it may reach, lest it fall short in the middle of the way, and fainting as it were it fall down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:39
verses.text: But even if there result not to me now the good things which I ask, I am secured nevertheless that hereafter they will come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:40
verses.text: For even in the case of transgressions a certain man is said to have asked of God, and not to have been hearkened to for his good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:41
verses.text: For privations of this world had inspired him to prayer, and being set in temporal tribulations he had wished that temporal tribulations should pass away, and there should return the flower of grass; and he saith, "My God, my God, why hast Thou forsaken me?" The very voice of Christ it is, but for His members' sake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:42
verses.text: "The words," he saith, "of my transgressions I have cried to Thee throughout the day, and Thou hast not hearkened: and by night, and not for the sake of folly to me:" that is, "and by night I have cried, and Thou hast not hearkened; and nevertheless in this very thing that Thou hast not hearkened, it is not for the sake of folly to me that Thou hast not hearkened, but rather for the sake of wisdom that Thou hast not hearkened, that I might perceive what of Thee I ought to ask.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:43
verses.text: For those things I was asking which to my cost perchance I should have received".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:44
verses.text: Thou askest riches, O man; how many have been overset through their riches? Whence knowest thou whether to thee riches may profit? Have not many poor men more safely been in obscurity; having become rich men, so soon as they have begun to blaze forth, they have been a prey to the stronger? How much better they would have lain concealed, how much better they would have been unknown, that have begun to be inquired after not for the sake of what they were, but for the sake of what they had! In these temporal things therefore, brethren, we admonish and exhort you in the Lord, that ye ask not anything as if it were a thing settled, but that which God knoweth to be expedient for you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:45
verses.text: For what is expedient for you, ye know not at all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:46
verses.text: Sometimes that which ye think to be for you is against you, and that which ye think to be against you is for you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:47
verses.text: For sick ye are; do not dictate to the physician the medicines he may choose to set beside you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:48
verses.text: If the teacher of the Gentiles, Paul the Apostle, saith, "For what we should pray for as we ought, we know not," how much more we? Who nevertheless, when he seemed to himself to pray wisely, namely, that from him should be taken away the thorn of the flesh, the angel of Satan, that did buffet him, in order that he might not in the greatness of the revelations be lifted up, heard from the Lord what? Was that done which he wished? Nay, in order to that being done which was expedient, he heard from the Lord, I say, what? "Thrice," he saith, "I besought the Lord that He would take it from me; and He said to me, My Grace sufficeth for thee: for virtue in weakness is made perfect".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:49
verses.text: Salve to the wound I have applied; when I applied it I know, when it should be taken away I know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:50
verses.text: Let not a sick man draw back from the hands of the physician, let him not give advice to the physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:51
verses.text: So it is with all these things temporal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:52
verses.text: There are tribulations; if well thou worshippest God, thou wilt know that He knoweth what is expedient for each man: there are prosperities; take the more heed, lest these same corrupt thy soul, so that it withdraw from Him that hath given these things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:53
verses.text: "For aliens have risen up against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:54
verses.text: What "aliens"? Was not David himself a Jew of the tribe of Judah? But the very place Ziph belonged to the tribe of Judah; it was of the Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:55
verses.text: How then "aliens"? Not in city, not in tribe, not in kindred, but in flowerBut see the Ziphites, see them for a time flourishing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:56
verses.text: With reason "alien" sons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:57
verses.text: Thou amid the Ziphites hiding saidst what? "Blessed the people whereof the Lord is its God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:58
verses.text: Out of this affection this prayer is being sent forth into the ears of the Lord, when it is said, "for aliens have risen up against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:59
verses.text: "And mighty men have sought after my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:60
verses.text: For in a new manner, my brethren, they would destroy the race of holy men, and the race of them that abstain from hoping in this world, all they that have hope in this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:61
verses.text: Certainly commingled they are, certainly together they live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:62
verses.text: Very much to one another are opposed these two sorts: the one of those that place no hope but in things secular, and in temporal felicity, and the other of those that do firmly place their hope in the Lord God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:63
verses.text: And though concordant are these Ziphites, do not much trust to their concord: temptations are wanting; when there shall have come any temptation, so as that a person may be reproved for the flower of the world, I say not to thee he will quarrel with the Bishop, but not even to the Church Herself will he draw near, lest there fall any part of the grass Wherefore have I said these words, brethren? Because now gladly ye all hear in the name of Christ, and according as ye understand, so ye shout out at the word; ye would not indeed shout at it unless ye understood This your understanding ought to be fruitful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:64
verses.text: But whether it is fruitful, temptation doth try; lest suddenly when ye are said to be ours, through temptation ye be found aliens, and it be said, "Aliens have risen up against me, and mighty men have sought my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:65
verses.text: Be not that said which followeth, "They have not set forth God before their face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:66
verses.text: For when will he set God before his face, before whose eyes there is nought but the world? namely, how he may have coin upon coin, how flocks may be increased, how barns may be filled, how it may be said to his soul, "Thou hast many good things, be merry, feast, take thy fill".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:67
verses.text: Doth he set before his face Him, that unto one so boasting and so blooming with the flower of the Ziphites saith, "Fool" (that is, "man not understanding," "man unwise"), "this night shall be taken from thee thy soul; all these things which thou hast prepared, whose shall they be?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:68
verses.text: "For behold, God helpeth me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:69
verses.text: Even themselves know not themselves, amid whom I am hiding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:70
verses.text: But if they too were to set God before their face, they would find in what manner God helpeth me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:71
verses.text: For all holy men are helped by God, but within, where no one seeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:72
verses.text: For in like manner as the conscience of ungodly men is a great punishment, so a great joy is the very conscience of godly men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:73
verses.text: "For our glory this is," saith the Apostle, "the testimony of our conscience".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:74
verses.text: In this within, not in the flower of the Ziphites without, doth glory that man that now saith, "For behold God helpeth me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:75
verses.text: Surely though afar off are to be those things which He promiseth, this day have I a sweet and present help; to-day in my heart's joy I find that without cause certain say, "Who doth show to us good things? For there is signed upon us the light of Thy countenance, O Lord, Thou hast put pleasantness into my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:76
verses.text: Not into my vineyard, not into my flock, not into my cask, not into my table, but "into my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:77
verses.text: "For behold God helpeth me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:78
verses.text: How doth He help thee? "And the Lord is the lifter up of my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:79
verses.text: "Turn away evil things unto mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:80
verses.text: So however green they are, so however they flourish, for the fire they are being reserved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:81
verses.text: "In Thy virtue destroy Thou them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:82
verses.text: Because to wit they flourish now, because to wit they spring up like grass: do not thou be a man unwise and foolish, so that by giving thought to these things thou perish for ever and ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:83
verses.text: For, "Turn Thou away evil things unto mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:84
verses.text: For if thou shalt have place in the body of David Himself, in His virtue He will destroy them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:85
verses.text: These men flourish in the felicity of the world, perish in the virtue of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:86
verses.text: Not in the same manner as they flourish, do they also perish: for they flourish for a time, perish for everlasting: flourish in unreal good things, perish in real torments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:87
verses.text: "In Thy strength destroy," whom in Thy weakness Thou hast endured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:88
verses.text: "Voluntarily I will sacrifice to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:89
verses.text: Who can even understand this good thing of the heart, at another's speaking thereof, unless in himself he hath tasted it? What is, "Voluntarily I will sacrifice to Thee"? For what sacrifice here shall I take, brethren? or what worthily shall I offer to the Lord for His mercy? Victims shall I seek from flock of sheep, ram shall I select, for any bull in the herds shall I look out, frankincense indeed from the land of the Sabaeans shall I bring? What shall I do? What offer; except that whereof He speaketh, "Sacrifice of praise shall honour Me"? Wherefore then "voluntarily"? Because truly I love that which I praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:90
verses.text: I praise God, and in the self-same praise I rejoice: in the praise of Himself I rejoice, at whom being praised, I blush not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:91
verses.text: For He is not praised in the same manner as by those who love the theatrical follies is praised either by a charioteer, or a hunter, or actor of any kind, and by their praisers, other praisers are invited, are exhorted, to shout together: and when all have shouted, ofttimes, if their favourite is overcome, they are all put to the blush.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:92
verses.text: Not so is our God: be He praised with the will, loved with charity: let it be gratuitous (or voluntary) that He is loved and that He is praised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:93
verses.text: What is "gratuitous"? Himself for the sake of Himself, not for the sake of something else.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:94
verses.text: For if thou praisest God in order that He may give thee something else, no longer freely dost thou love God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:95
verses.text: Thou wouldest blush, if thy wife for the sake of riches were to love thee, and perchance if poverty should befall thee, should begin to think of adultery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:96
verses.text: Seeing that therefore thou wouldest be loved by thy partner freely, wilt thou for anything else love God? What reward art thou to receive of God, O covetous man? Not earth for thee, but Himself He keepeth, who made heaven and earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:97
verses.text: "Voluntarily I will sacrifice to Thee:" do it not of necessity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:98
verses.text: For if for the sake of anything else thou praisest God, out of necessity thou praisest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:99
verses.text: These things also which He hath given, because of the Giver are good things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:100
verses.text: For He giveth entirely, He giveth these temporal things: and to certain men to their good, to certain men to their harm, after the height and depth of His judgments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:101
verses.text: "Voluntarily I will sacrifice to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:102
verses.text: Wherefore "voluntarily"? Because gratis.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:103
verses.text: What is gratis? "And I will confess to Thy name, O Lord, for it is a good thing:" for nothing else, but because a "good thing" it is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:104
verses.text: Doth he say, "I will confess to Thy name, O Lord," because Thou givest me fruitful manors, because Thou givest me gold and silver, because Thou givest me extended riches, abundant money, most exalted dignity? Nay.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:105
verses.text: But what? "For it is a good thing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:106
verses.text: Nothing I find better than Thy name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:107
verses.text: "For out of all tribulation Thou hast delivered me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:108
verses.text: For this cause I have perceived how good a thing is Thy name: for if this I were able before tribulations to acknowledge, perchance for me there had been no need of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:109
verses.text: But tribulation hath been applied for admonition, admonition hath redounded to Thy praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:110
verses.text: For I should not have understood where I was, except of my weakness I had been admonished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:111
verses.text: "Out of all tribulations," therefore, "Thou hast delivered me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:112
verses.text: And upon mine enemies mine eye hath looked back:" upon those Ziphites "mine eye hath looked back".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:113
verses.text: Yea, their flower I have passed over in loftiness of heart, unto Thee I have come, and thence I have looked back upon them, and have seen that "All flesh is grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass:" as in a certain place is also said, "I have seen the ungodly man to be exalted and raised up like the cedars of Lebanon: I passed by, and, lo! he was not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:114
verses.text: Wherefore "he was not"? Because thou hast passed by.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:115
verses.text: What is, "because thou hast passed by"? Because not to no purpose hast thou heard "Lift up thy heart;" because not on earth, where thou wouldest have rotted, thou hast remained; because thou hast lifted thy soul to God, and thou hast mounted beyond the cedars of Lebanon, and from that elevation hast observed: and "Lo! he was not;" and thou hast sought him, and there hath not been found place for him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:116
verses.text: No longer is labour before thee; because thou hast entered into the sanctuary of God, and hast understood for the last things So also here thus he concludeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:117
verses.text: "And upon mine enemies mine eye hath looked back".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 55:118
verses.text: This do ye therefore, brethren, with your souls; lift up your hearts, sharpen the edge of your mind, learn truly to love God, learn to despise the present world, learn voluntarily to sacrifice the offerings of praise; to the end that, mounting beyond the flower of the grass, ye may look back upon your enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:1
verses.text: Psalm LV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:2
verses.text: Of this Psalm the title is: "At the end, in hymns, understanding to David himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:3
verses.text: What the "end" is, we will briefly call to your recollection, because ye have known it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:4
verses.text: "For the end of the Law is Christ, for righteousness unto every man believing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:5
verses.text: Be the attention therefore directed unto the End, directed unto Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:6
verses.text: Wherefore is He called the end? Because whatever we do, to Him we refer it, and when to Him we shall have come home, more to ask we shall not have.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:7
verses.text: For there is an end spoken of which doth consume, there is an end spoken of which doth make perfect.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:8
verses.text: In one sense, for instance, we understand it, when we hear, there is ended the food which was in eating; and in another sense we understand it when we hear, there is ended the vesture which was in weaving: in each case we hear, there is ended; but the food so that it no longer is, the vesture so that it is perfected.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:9
verses.text: Our end therefore ought to be our perfection, our perfection Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:10
verses.text: For in Him we are made perfect, because of Himself the Head, the Members are we.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:11
verses.text: And he hath been spoken of as "the End of the Law," because without Him no one doth make perfect the Law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:12
verses.text: When therefore ye hear in the Psalms, "At the end,"—for many Psalms are thus superscribed,—be not your thought upon consuming, but upon consummation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:13
verses.text: "In hymns:" in praises.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:14
verses.text: For whether we are troubled and are straitened, or whether we rejoice and exult, He is to be praised, who both in tribulations doth instruct, and in gladness doth comfort.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:15
verses.text: For the praise of God from the heart and mouth of a Christian man ought not to depart; not that he may be pr aising in prosperity, and speaking evil in adversity; but after the manner that this Psalm doth prescribe, "I will speak good of the Lord in every time, alway the praise of Him is in my mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:16
verses.text: Thou dost rejoice; acknowledge a Father indulging: thou art troubled; acknowledge a Father chastening.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:17
verses.text: Whether He indulge, or whether He chasten, He is instructing one for whom He is preparing an inheritance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:18
verses.text: What then is, "Understanding to David himself"? David indeed was, as we know, a holy prophet, king of Israel, son of Jesse: but because out of his seed there came for our salvation after the flesh the Lord Jesus Christ, often under that name He is figured, and David instead of Christ is in a figure set down, because of the origin of the Flesh of the Same.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:19
verses.text: For after some sort He is Son of David, after some sort He is the Lord of David; Son of David after the flesh, Lord of David after the divinity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:20
verses.text: For if by Him have been made all things, by Him also David himself hath been made, out of whose seed He came to men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:21
verses.text: Moreover, when the Lord had questioned the Jews, whose Son they affirmed Christ to be, they made answer, "David's:" where the Lord chides the Jews, when they said that He was the Son of David He saw that they had stayed at the flesh, and had lost sight of the divinity; and He reproveth them by propounding a question: "How then doth David himself in spirit call Him Lord, 'The Lord hath said unto my Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:22
verses.text: 'If then He in spirit calleth Him Lord, how is He is Son?" A question He propounded; His being Son He denied not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:23
verses.text: Ye have heard "Lord;" say ye how He is his "Son:" ye have heard "Son;" say how He is "Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:24
verses.text: This question the Catholic Faith solveth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:25
verses.text: How "Lord"? Because "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:26
verses.text: How "Son"? Because "The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:27
verses.text: Because then David in a figure is Christ, but Christ, as we have often reminded your Love, is both Head and Body; neither ought we to speak of ourselves as alien from Christ, of whom we are members, nor to count ourselves as if we were any other thing: because "The two shall be in one flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:28
verses.text: "This is a great Sacrament," saith the Apostle, "but I speak in regard of Christ and the Church".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:29
verses.text: Because then whole Christ is "Head and Body;" when we hear, "Understanding to David himself," understand we ourselves also in David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:30
verses.text: Let the members of Christ understand, and Christ in His members understand, and the members of Christ in Christ understand: because Head and Members are one Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:31
verses.text: The Head was in heaven, and was saying, "Why dost thou persecute Me?" We with Him are in heaven through hope, Himself is with us on earth through love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:32
verses.text: Therefore "understanding to David himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:33
verses.text: Be we admonished when we hear, and let the Church understand: for there belongeth to us great diligence to understand in what evil we now are, and from what evil we desire to be delivered, remembering the Prayer of the Lord, where at the e nd we say, "Deliver us from evil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:34
verses.text: Therefore amid many tribulations of this world, this Psalm complaineth somewhat of understanding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:35
verses.text: He lamenteth not with it, who hath not understanding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:36
verses.text: But furthermore, dearly beloved, we ought to remember, that after the image of God we have been made, and that not in any other part than in the understanding itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:37
verses.text: For in many things by beasts we are surpassed: but when a man knoweth himself to have been made after the image of God, therein something in himself he acknowledgeth to be more than hath been given to dumb animals.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:38
verses.text: But on consideration of all those things which a man hath, he findeth himself in this thing peculiarly distinguished from a dumb animal, in that he hath himself an understanding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:39
verses.text: Whence certain men despising in themselves that peculiar and especial thing which from their Maker they had received, the Maker Himself reproveth, saying, "Do not become like horse and mule, in which there is no understanding".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:40
verses.text: "Hear Thou, O God, my entreaty, and despise not my prayer: give heed unto me, and hearken unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:41
verses.text: Of one earnest, anxious, of one set in tribulation, are these words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:42
verses.text: He is praying, suffering many things, from evil yearning to be delivered: it remaineth that we hear in what evil he is, and when he beginneth to speak, let us acknowledge there ourselves to be; in order that the tribulation being shared, we may conjoin prayer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:43
verses.text: "I have been made sad in my exercise, and have been troubled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:44
verses.text: Where made sad, where troubled? "In my exercise," he saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:45
verses.text: Of evil men, whom he suffereth, he hath made mention, and the same suffering of evil men he hath called his "exercise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:46
verses.text: Think ye not that without profit there are evil men in this world, and that no good God maketh of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:47
verses.text: Every evil man either on this account liveth that he may be corrected, or on this account liveth that through him a good man may be exercised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:48
verses.text: O that therefore they that do now exercise us would be converted, and together with us be exercised! Nevertheless, so long as they are such as to exercise, let us not hate them: because in that wherein any one of them is evil, whether unto the end he is to persevere, we know not; and ofttimes when to thyself thou seemest to have been hating an enemy, thou hast been hating a brother, and knowest not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:49
verses.text: The devil and his angels in the holy Scriptures have been manifested to us, that for fire everlasting they have been destined.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:50
verses.text: Of them only must amendment be despaired of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:51
verses.text: Therefore since this rule of Love for thee is fixed, that imitating the Father thou shouldest love an enemy: for, He saith, "love your enemies:" in this precept how wouldest thou be exercised, if thou hadst no enemy to suffer? Thou seest then that he profiteth thee somewhat: and let God sparing evil men profit thee, so that thou show mercy: because perchance thou too, if thou art a good man, out of an evil man hast been made a good man: and if God spared not evil men, not even thou wouldest be found to return thanks.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:52
verses.text: May He therefore spare others, that hath spared thee also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:53
verses.text: For it were not right, when thou hadst passed through, to close up the way of godliness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:54
verses.text: Whence then doth this man pray, set among evil men, with whose enmities he was being exercised? Why saith he, "I have been made sad in my exercise, and have been troubled"? While he is extending his love so as to love enemies, he hath been affected with disgust, being bayed at all around by the enmities of many men, by the frenzy of many and under a sort of human infirmity he hath sunk.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:55
verses.text: He hath seen himself now begin to be pierced through with an evil suggestion of the devil, to bring on hatred against his enemies: wrestling against hatred in order to perfect love herself, in the very fight, and in the wrestling, he hath been troubled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:56
verses.text: For there is his voice in another Psalm, "Mine eye hath been troubled, because of anger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:57
verses.text: And what followeth there? "I have waxen old among all mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:58
verses.text: As if in storm and waves he were beginning to sink, like Peter For he doth trample the waves of this world, that loveth enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:59
verses.text: Christ on the sea was walking fearless, from whose heart there could not by any means be taken away the love of an enemy, who hanging on the Cross did say, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:60
verses.text: Peter too would walk.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:61
verses.text: He as Head, Peter as Body: because, "Upon this rock," He saith, "I will build My Church".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:62
verses.text: He was bidden to walk, and he was walking by the Grace of Him bidding, not by his own strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:63
verses.text: But when he saw the wind mighty, he feared; and then he began to sink, being troubled in his exercise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:64
verses.text: By what mighty wind? "By the voice of the enemy, and by the tribulation of the sinner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:65
verses.text: Therefore, in the same manner as he cried out on the waves, "Lord, I perish, save me,"  a similar voice from this man hath preceded, "Hearken unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:66
verses.text: Wherefore? For what sufferest thou? Of what dost thou groan? "I have been made sad in my exercise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:67
verses.text: To be exercised indeed among evil men Thou hast set me, but too much they have risen up, beyond my powers: calm Thou one troubled, stretch forth a hand to one sinking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:68
verses.text: "For they have brought down upon me iniquity, and in anger they were shadowing me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:69
verses.text: Ye have heard of waves and winds: one as it were humbled they were insulting, and he was praying: on every side against him with the roar of insult they were raging, but he within was calling upon Him whom they did not see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:70
verses.text: But this man being troubled and made sad was praying, his eye being disturbed as it were on account of anger But the anger of a brother if it shall have been inveterate is then hatred.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:71
verses.text: Anger doth trouble the eye, hatred doth quench it: anger is a straw, hatred is a beam.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:72
verses.text: Sometimes thou hatest and chidest an angry man: in thee is hatred, in him whom thou chidest anger: with reason to thee is said, "Cast out first the beam from thine own eye, and so thou shalt see to cast out the straw from thy brother's eye".
