verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:73
verses.text: For that ye may know how much difference there is between anger and hatred: day by day men are angry with their sons, show me them that hate their sons! This man being troubled was praying even when made sad, wrestling against all revilings of all revilers; not in order that he might conquer any one of them by giving back reviling, but that he might not hate any one of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:74
verses.text: Hence he prayeth, hence asketh: "From the voice of the enemy and from the tribulation of the sinner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:75
verses.text: "My heart hath been troubled in me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:76
verses.text: This is the same as elsewhere hath been said, "Mine eye because of anger hath been troubled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:77
verses.text: And if eye hath been troubled, what followeth? "And fear of death hath fallen upon me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:78
verses.text: Our life is love: if life is love, death is hatred.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:79
verses.text: When a man hath begun to fear lest he should hate him that he was loving, it is death he is fearing; and a sharper death, and a more inward death, whereby soul is killed, not body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:80
verses.text: Thou didst mind a man raging against thee; what was he to do, against whom thine own Lord had given thee security, saying, "Fear not them that kill the body"? He by raging killeth body, thou by keeping hatred hast killed soul; and he the body of another, thou thine own soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:81
verses.text: "Fear," therefore, "of death hath fallen upon me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:82
verses.text: "Fearfulness and trembling have come upon me, and darkness hath covered me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:83
verses.text: "And I have said," "He that hateth his brother, is in darkness until now".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:84
verses.text: If love is light, hatred is darkness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:85
verses.text: And what saith to himself one set in that weakness and troubled in that exercise? "Who shall give me wings as to a dove, and I shall fly and shall rest?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:86
verses.text: Either for death he was wishing, or for solitude he was longing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:87
verses.text: So long, he saith, as this is the work with me, as this command is given me, that I should love enemies, the revilings of these men, increasing and shadowing me, do derange mine eye, perturb my sight, penetrate my heart, slay my soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:88
verses.text: I could wish to depart, but weak I am, lest by abiding I should add sins to sins: or at least may I be separated for a little space from mankind, lest my wound suffer from frequent blows, in order that when it hath been made whole it may be brought back to the exercise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:89
verses.text: This is what takes place, brethren, and there ariseth ofttimes in the mind of the servant of God a longing for solitude, for no other reason than because of the multitude of tribulations and scandals, and he saith, "Who shall give me wings?" Doth he find himself without wings, or rather with bound wings? If they are wanting, be they given; if bound, be they loosed; because even he that looseth a bird's wings, either giveth, or giveth back to it its wings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:90
verses.text: For it had not as though its own them, wherewith it could not fly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:91
verses.text: Bound wings make a burden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:92
verses.text: "Who," he saith, "shall give me wings as to a dove, and I shall fly and shall rest?" Shall rest, where? I have said there are two senses here: either, as saith the Apostle, "To be dissolved and to be with Christ, for it is by far the best thing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:93
verses.text: Even he that amended cannot be, is thine, either by the fellowship of the human race, or ofttimes by Church Communion; he is within, what wilt thou do? whither wilt go? whither separate thyself, in order that these things thou mayest not suffer? But go to him, speak, exhort, coax, threaten, reprove.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:94
verses.text: I have done all things, whatever powers I had I have expended and have drained, nothing I see have I prevailed; all my labour hath been spent out, sorrow hath remained.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:95
verses.text: How then shall my heart rest from such men, except I say, "Who shall give me wings?" "As to a dove," however, not as to a raven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:96
verses.text: A dove seeketh a flying away from troubles, but she loseth not love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:97
verses.text: For a dove as a type of love is set forth, and in her the plaint is loved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:98
verses.text: Nothing is so fond of plaints as a dove: day and night she complaineth, as though she were set here where she ought to complain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:99
verses.text: What then saith this lover? Revilings of men to bear I am unable, they roar, with frenzy are carried away, are inflamed with indignation, in anger they shadow me; to do good to them I am unable; O that I might rest somewhere, being separated from them in body, not in love; lest in me there should be troubled love itself: with my words and my speech no good can I do them, by praying for them perchance I shall do good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:100
verses.text: These words men say, but ofttimes they are so bound, that to fly they are not able.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:101
verses.text: For perchance they are not bound with any birdlime, but are bound by duty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:102
verses.text: But if they are bound with care and duty, and to leave it are unable, let them say, "I was wishing to be dissolved and to be with Christ, for it is by far the best thing: to abide in the flesh is necessary because of you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:103
verses.text: A dove bound back by affection, not by cupidity, was not able to fly away because of duty to be fulfilled, not because of little merit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:104
verses.text: Nevertheless a longing in heart must needs be; nor doth any man suffer this longing, but he that hath begun to walk in that narrow way: in order that he may know that there are not wanting to the Church persecutions, even in this time, when a calm is seen in the Church, at least with respect to those persecutions which our Martyrs have suffered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:105
verses.text: But there are not wanting persecutions, because a true saying is this, "All that will godly to live in Christ, shall suffer persecution".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:106
verses.text: "Behold I have gone afar fleeing, and have abode in the desert".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:107
verses.text: In what desert? Wherever thou shalt be, there will gather them together other men, the desert with thee they will seek, will attach themselves to thy life, thou canst not thrust back the society of brethren: there are mingled with thee also evil men; still exercise is thy due portion, "Behold I have gone afar, and have abode in the desert".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:108
verses.text: In what desert? It is perchance in the conscience, whither no man entereth, where no one is with thee, where thou art and God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:109
verses.text: For if in the desert, in any place, what wilt thou do with men gathering themselves together? For thou wilt not be able to be separated from mankind, so long as among men thou livest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:110
verses.text: "I was looking for him that should save me from weakness of mind and tempest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:111
verses.text: Sea there is, tempest there is: nothing for thee remaineth but to cry out, "Lord, I perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:112
verses.text: Let Him stretch forth hand, who doth the waves tread fearlessly, let Him relieve thy dread, let Him confirm in Himself thy security, let Him speak to thee within, and say to thee, "Give heed to Me, what I have borne:" an evil brother perchance thou art suffering, or an enemy without art suffering; which of these have I not suffered? There roared without Jews, within a disciple was betraying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:113
verses.text: There rageth therefore tempest, but He doth save men from weakness of mind, and tempest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:114
verses.text: Perchance thy ship is being troubled, because He in thee is sleeping.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:115
verses.text: The sea was raging, the bark wherein the disciples were sailing was being tossed; but Christ was sleeping: at length it was seen by them that among them was sleeping the Ruler and Creator of winds; they drew near and awoke Christ; He commanded the winds, and there was a great calm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:116
verses.text: With reason then perchance thy heart is troubled, because thou hast forgotten Him on whom thou hast believed: beyond endurance thou art suffering, because it hath not come into thy mind what for thee Christ hath borne.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:117
verses.text: If unto thy mind cometh not Christ, He sleepeth: awake Christ, recall faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:118
verses.text: For then in thee Christ is sleeping, if thou hast forgotten the sufferings of Christ: then in thee Christ is watching, if thou hast remembered the sufferings of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:119
verses.text: But when with full heart thou shalt have considered what He hath suffered, wilt not thou too with equanimity endure? and perchance rejoicing, because thou hast been found in some likeness of the sufferings of thy King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:120
verses.text: When therefore on these things thinking thou hast begun to be comforted and to rejoice, He hath arisen, He hath commanded the winds; therefore there is a great calm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:121
verses.text: "I was looking for Him that should save me from weakness of mind and tempest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:122
verses.text: "Sink, O Lord, and divide the tongues of them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:123
verses.text: He is referring to men troubling him and shadowing him, and he hath wished this thing not of anger, brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:124
verses.text: They that have wickedly lifted up themselves, for them it is expedient that they be sunk.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:125
verses.text: They that have wickedly conspired, it is expedient for them that their tongues should be divided: to good let them consent, and let their tongues agree together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:126
verses.text: But if to one purpose there were a whispering against me, he saith, all mine enemies, let them lose their "one purpose" in evil, divided be the tongues of them, let them not with themselves agree together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:127
verses.text: "Sink, O Lord, and divide the tongues of them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:128
verses.text: Wherefore "sink"? Because themselves they have lifted up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:129
verses.text: Wherefore "divide"? Because for an evil thing they have united.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:130
verses.text: Recollect that tower of proud men made after the deluge: what said the proud men? Lest we perish in a deluge, let us make a lofty tower In pride they were thinking themselves to be fortified, they builded up a lofty tower, and the Lord divided the tongues of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:131
verses.text: Then they began not to understand one another; hence arose the beginning of many tongues.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:132
verses.text: For before, one tongue there was: but one tongue for men agreeing was good, one tongue for humble men was good: but when that gathering together did into a union of pride fall headlong, God spared them; even though He divided the tongues, lest by understanding one another they should make a destructive unity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:133
verses.text: Through proud men, divided were the tongues; through humble Apostles, united were the tongues.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:134
verses.text: Spirit of pride dispersed tongues, Spirit Holy united tongues.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:135
verses.text: For when the Holy Spirit came upon the disciples, with the tongues of all men they spake, by all men they were understood: tongues dispersed, into one were united.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:136
verses.text: Therefore if still they rage and are Gentiles, it is expedient for them divided to have their tongues.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:137
verses.text: They would have one tongue; let them come to the Church; because even among the diversity of tongues of flesh, one is the tongue in faith of heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:138
verses.text: "For I have seen iniquity and contradiction in the city".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:139
verses.text: With reason this man was seeking the desert, for he saw iniquity and contradiction in the city.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:140
verses.text: There is a certain city turbulent: the same it was that was building a tower, the same was confounded and called Babylon, the same through innumerable nations dispersed: thence is gathered the Church into the desert of a good conscience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:141
verses.text: For he saw contradiction in the city.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:142
verses.text: "Christ cometh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:143
verses.text: —"What Christ?" thou contradictest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:144
verses.text: —"Son of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:145
verses.text: —"And hath God a Son?" thou contradictest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:146
verses.text: —"He was born of a virgin, suffered, rose again".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:147
verses.text: —"And whence is it possible for this to be done?" thou contradictest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:148
verses.text: —Give heed at least to the glory of the Cross itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:149
verses.text: Now on the brow of kings that Cross hath been fixed, over which enemies insulted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:150
verses.text: The effect hath proved the virtue It hath subdued the world, not with steel, but with wood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:151
verses.text: The wood of the Cross deserving of insults hath seemed to enemies, and before the wood itself standing they were wagging the head, and saying, "If Son of God He is, let Him come down from the Cross".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:152
verses.text: He was stretching forth His hands to a people unbelieving and contradicting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:153
verses.text: For if just he is that of faith liveth, unjust he is that hath not faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:154
verses.text: By that which here he saith "iniquity," I understand unbelief.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:155
verses.text: The Lord therefore was seeing in the city iniquity and contradiction, and was stretching forth His hands to a people unbelieving and contradicting: and nevertheless waiting for these same, He was saying, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:156
verses.text: Even now indeed there rage the remnant of that city, even now they contradict.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:157
verses.text: From the brows of all men now He is stretching forth hands to the remnant unbelieving and contradicting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:158
verses.text: "Day and night there will compass it upon the walls thereof iniquity, and labour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:159
verses.text: "Upon the walls thereof;" upon the fortifications thereof, holding as it were the heads thereof, the noble men thereof.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:160
verses.text: If that noble man were a Christian, not one would remain a pagan! Oft-times men say, "no one would remain a pagan, if he were a Christian".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:161
verses.text: Ofttimes men say, "If he too were made a Christian, who would remain a pagan?" Because therefore not yet they are made Christians, as if walls they are of that city unbelieving and contradicting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:162
verses.text: How long shall these walls stand? Not always shall they stand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:163
verses.text: The Ark is going around the walls of Jericho: there shall come a time at the seventh going round of the Ark, when all the walls of the city unbelieving and contradicting shall fall Until it come to pass, this man is being troubled in his exercise; and enduring the remains of men contradicting, he would choose wings for flying away, would choose the rest of the desert.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:164
verses.text: Yea let him continue amid men contradicting, let him endure menaces, drink revilings, and look for Him that will save him from weakness of mind and tempest: let him look upon the Head, the pattern for his life, let him be made calm in hope, even if he is troubled in fact.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:165
verses.text: "Day and night there will compass it upon the walls thereof iniquity; and labour in the midst thereof and injustice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:166
verses.text: And for this reason labour is there, because iniquity is there: because injustice is there, therefore also labour is there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:167
verses.text: But let them hear him stretching forth hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:168
verses.text: "Come unto Me, all ye that labour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:169
verses.text: Ye cry, ye contradict, ye revile: He on the contrary, "Come unto Me, all ye that labour," in your pride, and ye shall rest in My humility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:170
verses.text: "Learn of Me," He saith, "for meek I am and humble in heart, and ye shall find rest unto your souls".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:171
verses.text: For whence do they labour, but because they are not meek and humble in heart? God humble was made, let man blush to be proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:172
verses.text: "There hath not failed from the streets thereof usury and deceit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:173
verses.text: Usury and deceit are not hidden at least, because they are evil things, but in public they rage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:174
verses.text: For he that in his house doth any evil thing, however for his evil thing doth blush: "In the streets thereof usury and deceit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:175
verses.text: Money-lending even hath a profession, Money-lending also is called a science; a corporation is spoken of, a corporation as if necessary to the state, and of its profession it payeth revenue; so entirely indeed in the streets is that which should have been hidden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:176
verses.text: There is also another usury worse, when thou forgivest not that which to thee is owed; and the eye is disturbed in that verse of the prayer, "Forgive us our debts—as we too forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:177
verses.text: For what there wilt thou do, when thou art going to pray, and coming to that same verse? An insulting word thou hast heard: thou wouldest exact the punishment of condemnation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:178
verses.text: Do but consent to exact just so much as thou hast given, thou usurer of injuries! With the fist thou hast been smitten, slaying thou seekest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:179
verses.text: Evil usury! How wilt thou go to prayer? If thou shalt have left praying, which way wilt thou come round unto the Lord? Behold thou wilt say: "Our Father which art in heaven, hallowed be Thy Name, Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done, as in heaven so on earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:180
verses.text: Thou wilt say, "Our daily bread give us to-day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:181
verses.text: Thou wilt come to, "Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:182
verses.text: Even in that evil city let there abound these usuries; let them not enter the walls where the breast is smitten! What wilt thou do? because there thou and that verse are in the midst? Petitions for thee hath a heavenly Lawyer composed He that knew what used there to be done, said to thee, "Otherwise thou shalt not obtain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:183
verses.text: "Verily, verily, I say unto you, that if ye shall have forgiven men sins, they shall be forgiven you; but if ye shall not have forgiven sins unto men, neither will your Father forgive you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:184
verses.text: Who saith this? He that knoweth what there is being done, in the place whereat thou art standing to make request.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:185
verses.text: See how Himself hath willed to be thy Advocate; Himself thy Counsellor, Himself the Assessor of the Father, Himself thy Judge hath said, "Otherwise thou shalt not receive".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:186
verses.text: What wilt thou do? Thou wilt not receive, unless thou shalt speak; wilt not receive if falsely thou shalt speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:187
verses.text: Therefore either thou must do and speak, or else what thou askest thou wilt not earn; because they that this do not do, are in the midst of those evil usuries.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:188
verses.text: Be they engaged therein, that yet do idols either adore or desire: do not thou, O people of God, do not thou, O people of Christ, do not thou the Body of Him the Head! Give heed to the bond of thy peace, give heed to the promise of thy life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:189
verses.text: For what doth it profit thee, that thou exactest for injuries which thou hast endured? doth vengeance refresh thee? Therefore, over the evil of another shalt thou rejoice? Thou hast suffered evil; pardon thou; be not ye two.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:190
verses.text: "For if an enemy had upbraided me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:191
verses.text: And indeed above he was "troubled in his exercise" by the voice of the enemy and by the tribulation of the sinner, perhaps being placed in that city, that proud city that was building a tower, which was "sunk," that divided might be the tongues: give heed to his inward groaning because of perils from false brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:192
verses.text: "For if an enemy had upbraided me, I would have undergone it assuredly, and if he that did hate me had over me spoken great words," that is, through pride had on me trampled, did magnify himself above me, did threaten me all in his power: "I would hide myself assuredly from him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:193
verses.text: From him that is abroad, thou wouldest hide thyself where? Amid those that are within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:194
verses.text: But now see whether anything else remaineth, but that thou seek solitude.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:195
verses.text: "But thou," he saith, "man of one mind, my guide and my friend".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:196
verses.text: Perchance sometimes good counsel thou hast given, perchance sometimes thou hast gone before me, and some wholesome advice thou hast given me: in the Church of God together we have been.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:197
verses.text: "But thou,that together with me didst take sweet morsels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:198
verses.text: What are the sweet morsels? Not all they that are present know: but let them not be soured that do know, in order that they may be able to say to them that as yet know not: "Taste ye and see, how sweet is the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:199
verses.text: "In the House of God we have walked with consent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:200
verses.text: Whence then dissension? Thou that wast within, hast become one without.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:201
verses.text: He hath walked with me in the House of God with consent: another house hath he set up against the House of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:202
verses.text: Wherefore hath that been forsaken, wherein we have walked with consent? wherefore hath that been deserted, wherein together we did take sweet morsels?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:203
verses.text: "Let there come death upon them, and let them go down unto Hell living".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:204
verses.text: How hath he cited and hath made us call to mind that first beginning of schism, when in that first people of the Jews certain proud men separated themselves, and would without have sacrificed? A new death upon them came: the earth opened herself, and swallowed them up alive "Let there come," he saith, "death upon them, and let them go down into Hell living".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:205
verses.text: What is "living"? knowing that they are perishing, and yet perishing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:206
verses.text: Hear of living men perishing and being swallowed up in a gulf of the earth, that is, being swallowed up in the voraciousness of earthly desires Thou sayest to a man, What aileth thee, brot her? Brethren we are, one God we invoke, in one Christ we believe, one Gospel we hear, one Psalm we sing, one Amen we respond, one Hallelujah we sound, one Easter we celebrate: why art thou without and I am within? Ofttimes one straitened, and perceiving how true are the charges which are made, saith, May God requite our ancestors! Therefore alive he perisheth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:207
verses.text: In the next place thou continuest and thus givest warning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:208
verses.text: At least let the evil of separation stand alone, why dost thou adjoin thereto that of rebaptism? Acknowledge in me what thou hast; and if thou hatest me, spare thou Christ in me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:209
verses.text: And this evil thing doth frequently and very greatly displease them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:210
verses.text: Because they themselves have the Scriptures in their hands, and know well by daily reading how the Church Catholic through the whole world is so spread, that in a word all contradiction is void; and that there cannot be found any support for their schism they know well: therefore unto the lower places living they go down, because the evil which they do, they know evil to be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:211
verses.text: But the former a fire of divine indignation consumed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:212
verses.text: For being inflamed with desire of strife, from their evil leaders they would not depart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:213
verses.text: There came upon fire a fire, upon the heat of dissension the heat of consuming.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:214
verses.text: "For naughtiness is in their lodgings, in the midst of them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:215
verses.text: "In their lodgings," wherein they tarry and pass away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:216
verses.text: For here they are not alway to be: and nevertheless in defence of a temporal animosity they are fighting so fiercely.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:217
verses.text: "In their lodgings is iniquity; in the midst of them is iniquity:" no part of them is so near the middle of them as their heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:218
verses.text: "Therefore to the Lord I have cried out".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:219
verses.text: The Body of Christ and the oneness of Christ in anguish, in weariness, in uneasiness, in the tribulation of its exercise, that One Man, Oneness in One Body set, when He was wearying His soul in crying out from the ends of the earth; saith, "From the ends of the earth to Thee I have cried out, when My heart was being vexed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:220
verses.text: Himself one, but a oneness that One! and Himself one, not in one place one, but from the ends of the earth is crying as one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:221
verses.text: How from the ends of the earth should there cry one, except there were one? "I to the Lord have cried out".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:222
verses.text: Rightly do thou cry out to the Lord, cry not to Donatus: lest for thee he be instead of the Lord a lord, that under the Lord would not be a fellow-servant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:223
verses.text: "In evening, in morning, at noon-day I will recount and will tell forth, and He shall hearken to my voice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:224
verses.text: Do thou proclaim glad tidings, keep not secret that which thou hast received, "in evening" of things gone by, "in morning" of things to be, at "noonday" of things ever to be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:225
verses.text: Therefore, to that which he saith "in evening" belongeth that which he recounteth: to that which he saith, "in morning," belongeth that which he telleth forth: to that which he saith "at noon-day," belongeth that wherein his voice is hearkened to.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:226
verses.text: For the end is at noon-day; that is to say, whence there is no going down unto setting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:227
verses.text: For at noon-day there is light full high, the splendour of wisdom, the fervour of love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:228
verses.text: "In evening and in morning and at noon-day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:229
verses.text: "In evening," the Lord on the Cross; "in morning," in Resurrection; "at noon-day," in Ascension.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:230
verses.text: I will recount in evening the patience of Him dying, I will tell forth in morning the life of Him rising, I will pray that He hearken at noon-day sitting at the right hand of the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:231
verses.text: He shall hearken to my voice, That intercedeth for us How great is the security of this man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:232
verses.text: How great the consolation, how great the refuge "from weakness of mind and tempest," against evil men, against ungodly men both without and within, and in the case of those that are without though they had been within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:233
verses.text: Therefore, my Brethren, those that in the very congregation of these walls ye see to be rebellious men, proud, seeking their own, lifted up; not having a zeal for God that is chaste, sound, quiet, but ascribing to themselves much; ready for dissension, but not finding opportunity; are the very chaff of the Lord's floor From hence these few men the wind of pride hath dislodged: the whole floor will not fly, save when He at the last shall winnow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:234
verses.text: But what shall we do, save with this man sing, with this man pray, with this man mourn and say securely, "He shall redeem in peace my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:235
verses.text: Against them that love not peace: "in peace He shall redeem my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:236
verses.text: "Because with those that hated peace I was peace-making".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:237
verses.text: "He shall redeem in peace my soul, from those that draw near to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:238
verses.text: For from those that are afar from me, it is an easy case: not so soon doth he deceive me that saith, Come, pray to an idol: he is very far from me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:239
verses.text: Art thou a Christian? A Christian, he saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:240
verses.text: Out of a neighbouring place he is my adversary, he is at hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:241
verses.text: "He shall redeem in peace my soul, from those that draw near to me: for in many things they were with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:242
verses.text: Wherefore have I said, "draw near to me"? Because "in many things they were with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:243
verses.text: In this verse two propositions occur.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:244
verses.text: "In many things they were with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:245
verses.text: Baptism we had both of us, in that they were with me: the Gospel we both read, they were in that with me: the festivals of martyrs we celebrated, they were there with me: Easter's solemnity we attended, they were there with me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:246
verses.text: But not entirely with me: in schism not with me, in heresy not with me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:247
verses.text: In many things with me, in few things not with me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:248
verses.text: But in these few things wherein not with me, there is no profit to them of the many things wherein they were with me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:249
verses.text: For see, brethren, how many things hath recounted the Apostle Paul: one thing, he hath said, if it shall have been wanting, in vain are those things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:250
verses.text: "If with the tongues of men and of angels I shall speak," he saith, "if I have all prophecy, and all faith, and all knowledge; if mountains I shall remove, if I shall bestow all my goods upon the poor, if I shall deliver my body even so that it be burned".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:251
verses.text: How many things he hath enumerated! To all these many things let there be wanting one thing, charity; the former in number are more, the latter in weight is greater.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:252
verses.text: Therefore in all Sacraments they are with me, in one charity not with me: "In many things they were with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:253
verses.text: Again, by a different expression: "For in many things they were with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:254
verses.text: They that themselves have separated from me, with me they were, not in few things, but in many things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:255
verses.text: For throughout the whole world few are the grains, many are the chaffs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:256
verses.text: Therefore he saith what? In chaff with me they were, in wheat with me they were not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:257
verses.text: And the chaff is nearly related to the wheat, from one seed it goeth forth, in one field is rooted, with one rain is nourished, the same reaper it suffereth, the same threshing sustaineth, the same winnowing awaiteth, but not into one barn entereth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:258
verses.text: "God will hear me, and He shall humble them That is before ages".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:259
verses.text: For they rely on some leader or other of theirs that hath begun but yesterday.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:260
verses.text: "He shall humble them That is before ages".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:261
verses.text: For even if with reference to time Christ is of Mary the Virgin, nevertheless before ages: "In the beginning He is the Word and the Word with God, and the Word God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:262
verses.text: "He shall humble them That is before ages.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:263
verses.text: For to them is no changing:" of them I "speak to whom is no changing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:264
verses.text: He knew of some to persevere, and in the perseverance of their own wickedness to die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:265
verses.text: For we see them, and to them is no changing: they that die in that same perverseness, in that same schism, to them is no changing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:266
verses.text: God shall humble them, shall humble them in damnation, because they are exalted in dissension.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:267
verses.text: To them is no changing, because they are not changed for the better, but for the worse: neither while they are here, nor in the resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:268
verses.text: For all we shall rise again, but not all shall be changed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:269
verses.text: Wherefore? Because "'To them is no changing: and they have not feared God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:270
verses.text: "He stretcheth forth His hand in requiting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:271
verses.text: "They have polluted His Testament".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:272
verses.text: Read the testament which they have polluted: "In thy seed shall be blessed all nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:273
verses.text: Thou against these words of the Testator sayest what? The Africa of holy Donatus hath alone deserved this grace, in him hath remained the Church of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:274
verses.text: Say at least the Church of Donatus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:275
verses.text: Wherefore addest thou, of Christ? Of whom it is said, "In thy seed shall be blessed all nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:276
verses.text: After Donatus wilt thou go? Set aside Christ, and then secede.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:277
verses.text: See therefore what followeth: "They have polluted His Testament".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:278
verses.text: What Testament? To Abraham have been spoken the promises, and to his seed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:279
verses.text: The Apostle saith, "Nevertheless, a man's testament confirmed no one maketh void, or super-addeth to: to Abraham have been spoken the promises, and to his seed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:280
verses.text: He saith not, And to seeds, as if in many; but as if in one, And to thy Seed, which is Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:281
verses.text: In this Christ, therefore, what Testament hath been promised? "In thy seed shall be blessed all nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:282
verses.text: Thou that hast given up the unity of all nations, and in a part hast remained, hast polluted His Testament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:283
verses.text: "And His heart hath drawn near".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:284
verses.text: Of whom do we understand it, except of Him, by the anger of whom they have been divided? How "hath his heart drawn near"? In such sort, that we may understand His will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:285
verses.text: For by heretics hath been vindicated the Catholic Church, and by those that think evil have been proved those that think well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:286
verses.text: For many things lay hid in the Scriptures: and when heretics had been cut off, with questions they troubled the Church of God: then those things were opened which lay hid, and the will of God was understood Thence is said in another Psalm, "In order that they might be excluded that have been proved with silver".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:287
verses.text: For let them be excluded, He hath said, let them come forth, let them appear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:288
verses.text: Whence even in silver-working men are called "excluders," that is, pressers out of form from the sort of confusion of the lump.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:289
verses.text: Therefore many men that could understand and expound the Scriptures very excellently, were hidden among the people of God: but they did not declare the solution of difficult questions, when no reviler again urged them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:290
verses.text: For was the Trinity perfectly treated of before the Arians snarled thereat? Was repentance perfectly treated of before the Novatians opposed? So not perfectly of Baptism was it treated, before rebaptizers removed outside contradicted; nor of the very oneness of Christ were the doctrines clearly stated which have been stated, save after that this separation began to press upon the weak: in order that they that knew how to treat of and solve these questions (lest the weak should perish vexed with the questions of the ungodly), by their discourses and disputations should bring out unto open day the dark things of the LawThis obscure sense see in what manner the Apostle bringeth out into light; "It is needful," he saith, "that also heresies there be, in order that men proved may be made manifest among you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:291
verses.text: What is "men proved"? Proved with silver, proved with the word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:292
verses.text: What is "may be made manifest"? May be brought out Wherefore this? Because of heretics.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:293
verses.text: So therefore these also "have been divided because of the anger of His countenance, and His heart hath drawn near".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:294
verses.text: "His discourses have been softened above oil, and themselves are darts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:295
verses.text: For certain things in the Scriptures were seeming hard, while they were obscure; when explained, they have been softened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:296
verses.text: For even the first heresy in the disciples of Christ, as it were from the hardness of His discourse arose.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:297
verses.text: For when He said, "Except a man shall have eaten My flesh and shall have drunk My blood, he shall not have life in himself:" they, not understanding, said to one another, "Hard is this discourse, who can hear it?" Saying that, "Hard is this discourse," they separated from Him: He remained with the others, the twelve.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:298
verses.text: When they had intimated to Him, that by His discourse they had been scandalized, "Will ye also," He saith, "choose to go?" Then Peter: "Thou hast the Word of life eternal: to whom shall we go?" Attend, we beseech you, and ye little ones learn godliness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:299
verses.text: Did Peter by any means at that time understand the secret of that discourse of the Lord? Not yet he understood: but that good were the words which he understood not, godly he believed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:300
verses.text: Therefore if hard is a discourse, and not yet is understood, be it hard to an ungodly man, but to thee be it by godliness softened: for whenever it is solved, it both will become for thee oil, and even unto the bones it will penetrate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:301
verses.text: Furthermore, just as Peter, after their having been scandalized by the hardness, as they thought, of the discourse of the Lord, even then said, "to whom shall we go?" so he hath added, "Cast upon the Lord thy care, and He shall Himself nourish thee up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:302
verses.text: A little one thou art, not yet thou understandest the secret things of words: perchance from thee the bread is hidden, and as yet with milk thou must be fed: be not angry with the breasts: they will make thee fit for the table, for which now little fitted thou art.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:303
verses.text: Behold by the division of heretics many hard things have been softened: His discourses that were hard have been softened above oil, and they are themselves darts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:304
verses.text: They have armed men preaching the Gospel: and the very discourses are aimed at the breast of every one that heareth, by men instant in season and out of season: by those discourses, by those words, as though by arrows, hearts of men unto the love of peace are smitten.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:305
verses.text: Hard they were, and soft they have been made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:306
verses.text: Being softened they have not lost their virtue, but into darts have been converted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:307
verses.text: Upon the Lord cast thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:308
verses.text: Behold thou wilt cast thyself upon the Lord, let no one put himself in the place of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:309
verses.text: "Cast upon the Lord thy care".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:310
verses.text: But to the others what? "But Thou, O God, shall bring them down unto the pit of corruption".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:311
verses.text: The pit of corruption is the darkness of sinking under.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:312
verses.text: When blind leadeth blind, they both fall into a ditch God bringeth them down into the pit of corruption, not because He is the author of their own guilt, but because He is Himself the judge of their iniquities.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:313
verses.text: "For God hath delivered them unto the desires of their heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:314
verses.text: For they have loved darkness, and not light; they have loved blindness, and not seeing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:315
verses.text: For behold the Lord Jesus hath shone out to the whole world, let them sing in unity with the whole world: "For there is not one that can hide himself from the heat of Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:316
verses.text: But they passing over from the whole to a part, from the body to a wound, from life to a limb cut off, shall meet with what, but going into the pit of corruption?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:317
verses.text: "Men of bloods and of deceitfulness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:318
verses.text: Men of bloods, because of slayings he calleth them: and O that they were corporal and not spiritual slayings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:319
verses.text: For blood from the flesh going forth, is seen and shuddered at: who seeth the blood of the heart in a man rebaptized? Those deaths require other eyes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:320
verses.text: Although even about these visible deaths Circumcelliones armed everywhere remain not quiet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:321
verses.text: And if we think of these visible deaths, there are men of bloods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:322
verses.text: Give heed to the armed man, whether he is a man of peace and not of blood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:323
verses.text: If at least a club only he were to carry, well; but he carrieth a sling, carrieth an axe, carrieth stones, carrieth lances; and carrying these weapons, wherever they may they scour, for the blood of innocent men they thirst Therefore even with regard to these visible deaths there are men of bloods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:324
verses.text: But even of them let us say, O that such deaths alone they perpetrated, and souls they slew not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:325
verses.text: These that are men of bloods and of deceit, let them not suppose that we thus wrongly understand men of bloods, of them that kill souls: they themselves of their Maximianists have so understood it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:326
verses.text: For when they condemned them, in the very sentence of their Council they have set down these words: "Swift are the feet of them to shed the blood" (of the proclaimers), "tribulation and calamity are in the ways of them, and the way of peace they have not known".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:327
verses.text: This of the Maximianists they have said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:328
verses.text: But I ask of them, when have the Maximianists shed the body's blood; not because they too would not shed, if there were so great a multitude as could shed, but because of the fear in their minority rather they have suffered somewhat from others, than have themselves at any time done any such thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:329
verses.text: Therefore I question the Donatist and say: In thy Council thou hast set down of the Maximianists, "Swift are the feet of them to shed blood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:330
verses.text: Show me one of whom the Maximianists have hurt so much as a finger! What other thing to me is he to answer, than that which I say? They that have separated themselves from unity, and who slay souls by leading astray, spiritually, not carnally, do shed blood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:331
verses.text: Very well thou hast expounded, but in thy exposition acknowledge their own deeds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:332
verses.text: "Men of bloods and of deceitfulness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:333
verses.text: In guile is deceitfulness, in dissimulation, in seduction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:334
verses.text: What therefore of those very men that have been divided because of the anger of His countenance? They are themselves men of bloods and of deceit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:335
verses.text: But of them he saith what? "They shall not halve their days".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:336
verses.text: What is, "They shall not halve their days"? They shall not make progress as much as they think: within the time which they expect, they shall perish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:337
verses.text: For he is that partridge, whereof hath been said, "In the half of his days they shall leave him, and in his last days he shall be an unwise one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:338
verses.text: They make progress, but for a time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:339
verses.text: For what saith the Apostle? "But evil men and seducers shall make progress for the worse, themselves erring, and other men into error driving".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:340
verses.text: But "a blind man leading a blind man, together into a ditch they fall".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:341
verses.text: Deservedly they fall "into the pit of corruption".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:342
verses.text: What therefore saith he? They shall make progress for the worse: not however for long.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:343
verses.text: For a little before he hath said, "But further they shall not make progress:" that is, "shall not halve their days".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:344
verses.text: Let the Apostle proceed and tell wherefore: "For the madness of them shall be manifest to all men, as also was that of the others".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:345
verses.text: "But I in Thee will hope, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:346
verses.text: But deservedly they shall not halve their days, because in man they have hoped.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:347
verses.text: But I from days temporal have reached unto day eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 56:348
verses.text: Wherefore? Because in Thee I have hoped, O Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:1
verses.text: Psalm LVI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:2
verses.text: Just as when we are going to enter into any house, we look on the title to see whose it is and to whom it belongeth, lest perchance inopportunely we burst into a place whereunto we ought not; and again, in order that we may not through timidity withdraw from that which we ought to enter: as if in a word we were  to read, These estates belong to such an one or to such an one: so on the lintel of this Psalm we have inscribed, "At the end, for the people that from holy men were put afar off, to David himself, at the inscription of the Title, when the Allophyli held him in Gath".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:3
verses.text: Let us therefore take knowledge of the people that from holy men were put afar off at the inscription of the Title.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:4
verses.text: For this doth belong to that David whom now ye know how to understand spiritually.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:5
verses.text: For there is here commended to our notice no other than He of whom hath been said, "The end of the Law is Christ for righteousness to every man believing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:6
verses.text: Therefore when thou hearest "at the end," unto Christ give heed, lest tarrying in the way thou arrive not at the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:7
verses.text: Who are then the people that from holy men were put afar off at the inscription of the Title? Let the Title itself declare to us that people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:8
verses.text: For there was written a certain title at the Passion of the Lord, when the Lord was crucified: there was in that place a Title inscribed in Hebrew, in Greek, and in Latin, "The King of the Jews;" in three tongues as though by three witnesses the Title was confirmed: because "in the mouth of two or three witnesses shall stand every word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:9
verses.text: What therefore meaneth that which to the title itself still belongeth, namely, that "the Allophyli held him in Geth"? Geth was a certain city of the Allophyli, that is, of strangers, to wit, of people afar from holy men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:10
verses.text: All they that refuse Christ for King become strangers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:11
verses.text: Wherefore strangers are they made? Because even that vine, though by Him planted, when it had become sour what heard it? "Wherefore hast thou been turned into sourness, O alien vine?" It hath not been said, My vine: because if Mine, sweet; if sour, not Mine; if not Mine, surely alien.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:12
verses.text: "There held him," then, "Allophyli in Geth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:13
verses.text: We find indeed, brethren, David himself, son of Jesse, king of Israel, to have been in a strange land among the Allophyli, when he was sought by Saul, and was in that city and with the king of that city, but that there he was detained we read not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:14
verses.text: Therefore our David, the Lord Jesus Christ out of the seed of that David, not alone they held, but there hold Him still Allophyli in Geth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:15
verses.text: Of Geth we have said that it is a city.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:16
verses.text: But the interpretation of this name, if asked for, signifieth "press".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:17
verses.text: How therefore here is He held in Geth? Held in a winepress is His Body, that is, His Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:18
verses.text: What is, in a winepress? In pressings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:19
verses.text: But in a winepress fruitful is the pressing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:20
verses.text: A grape on the vine sustaineth no pressing, whole it seemeth, but nothing thence floweth: it is thrown into a winepress, is trodden, is pressed; harm seemeth to be done to the grape, but this harm is not barren; nay, if no harm had been applied, barren it would have remained.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:21
verses.text: Let whatsoever holy men therefore that are suffering pressing from those that have been put afar off from the saints, give heed to this Psalm, let them perceive here themselves, let them speak what here is spoken, that suffer what here is spoken of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:22
verses.text: Private enmities therefore let no one think of, when about to hear the words of this Psalm: "Know ye that for us the wrestling is not against flesh and blood, but against princes and powers, and spiritual things of wickedness," that is, against the devil and his angels; because even when we suffer men that annoy us, he is instigating, he is inflaming, as it were his vessels he is moving.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:23
verses.text: Let us give heed therefore to two enemies, him whom we see, and him whom we see not; man we see, the devil we see not; man let us love, of the devil beware; for man pray, against the devil pray, and let us say to God, "Have pity on me, O Lord, for man hath trodden me down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:24
verses.text: Fear not because man hath trodden thee down: have thou wine, a grape thou hast become in order that thou shouldest be trodden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:25
verses.text: "All day long warring he hath troubled me," every one that hath been put afar off from the saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:26
verses.text: But why should not here be understood even the devil himself? Is it because mention is made of "man"? doth therefore the Gospel err, because it hath said, "A man that is an enemy hath done this"? But by a kind of figure may he also be called a man, and yet not be a man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:27
verses.text: Whether therefore it was him whom he that said these words was beholding, or whether it was the people and each one that was put afar off from holy men, through which kind the devil troubleth the people of God, who cleave to holy men, who cleave to the Holy One, who cleave to the King, at the title of which King being indignant they were as though beaten back, and put afar off: let him say, "Have pity on me, O Lord, for man hath trodden me down:" and let him faint not in this treading down, knowing Him on whom he is calling, and by whose example he hath been made strong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:28
verses.text: The first cluster in the winefat pressed is Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:29
verses.text: When that cluster by passion was pressed out, there flowed that whence "the cup inebriating is how passing beautiful!" Let His Body likewise say, looking upon its Head, "Have pity on me, O Lord, for man hath trodden me down: all day long warring he hath troubled me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:30
verses.text: "All day long," at all times.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:31
verses.text: Let no one say to himself, There have been troubles in our fathers' time, in our time there are not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:32
verses.text: If thou supposest thyself not to have troubles, not yet hast thou begun to be a Christian.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:33
verses.text: And where is the voice of the Apostle, "But even all that will live godly in Christ, persecutions shall suffer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:34
verses.text: If therefore thou sufferest not any persecution for Christ, take heed lest not yet thou hast begun godly to live in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:35
verses.text: But when thou hast begun godly to live in Christ, thou hast entered into the winepress; make ready thyself for pressings: but be not thou dry, lest from the pressing nothing go forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:36
verses.text: "Mine enemies have trodden me down all day long".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:37
verses.text: They that have been put afar off from holy men, these are mine enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:38
verses.text: All day long: already it hath been said, "From the height of the day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:39
verses.text: What meaneth, "from the height of the day"? Perchance it is a high thing to understand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:40
verses.text: And no wonder, because the height of the day it is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:41
verses.text: For perchance they for this reason have been put afar off from holy men, because they were not able to penetrate the height of the day, whereof the Apostles are twelve shining hours.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:42
verses.text: Therefore they that crucified Him, as if man, in the day have erred.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:43
verses.text: But why have they suffered darkness, so that they should be put afar off from holy men? Because on high the day was shining, Him in the height hidden they knew not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:44
verses.text: "For if they had known, never the Lord of Glory would they have crucified".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:45
verses.text: "For many men that war against me, shall fear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:46
verses.text: Shall fear when? When the day shall have passed away, wherein they are high.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:47
verses.text: For for a time high they are, when the time of their height is finished they will fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:48
verses.text: "But I in Thee will hope, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:49
verses.text: He saith not, "But I will not fear:" but, "Many men, that war against me, shall fear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:50
verses.text: When there shall have come that day of Judgment, then "shall mourn for themselves all the tribes of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:51
verses.text: When there shall have appeared the sign of the Son of Man in heaven, then secure shall be all holy men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:52
verses.text: For that thing shall come which they hoped for, which they longed for, the coming whereof they prayed for: but to those men no place for repentance shall remain, because in that time wherein fruitful might have been repentance, their heart they hardened against a warning Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:53
verses.text: Shall they too raise up a wall against a judging God? The godliness of this man do thou indeed acknowledge, and if in that Body thou art, imitate him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:54
verses.text: When he had said, "Many men, that war against me, shall fear:" he did not continue, "But I will not fear;" lest to his own powers ascribing his not fearing, he too should be amid high temporal things, and through pride temporal he should not deserve to come to rest everlasting: rather he hath made thee to perceive whence he shall not fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:55
verses.text: "But I," he saith, "in thee will hope, O Lord:" he hath not spoken of his confidence: but of the cause of his confidence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:56
verses.text: For if I shall not fear, I may also by hardness of heart not fear, for many men by too much pride fear nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:57
verses.text: "In God I will praise my discourses, in God I have hoped: I will not fear what flesh doeth to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:58
verses.text: Wherefore? Because in God I will praise my discourses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:59
verses.text: If in thyself thou praisest thy discourses: I say not that thou art not to fear; it is impossible that thou have not to fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:60
verses.text: For thy discourses either false thou wilt have, and therefore thine own, because false: or if thy discourses shall be true, and thou shalt deem thyself not to have them from God but of thyself to speak; true they will be, but thou wilt be false: but if thou shalt have known that thou canst say nothing true in the wisdom of God, in the faith of the Truth, save that which from Him thou hast received, of whom is said, "For what hast thou which thou hast not received?" Then in God thou art praising thy discourses, in order that in God thou mayest be praised by the discourses of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:61
verses.text: "In God I have hoped, I will not fear what flesh doeth to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:62
verses.text: Wast thou not the same that a little before wast saying, "Have pity on me, O Lord, for man hath trodden me down; all day long warring he hath troubled me"? How therefore here, "I will not fear what flesh doeth to me"? What shall he do to thee? Thou thyself a little before hast said, "Hath trodden me down, hath troubled me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:63
verses.text: Nothing shall he do, when these things he shall do? He hath had regard to the wine which floweth from treading, and hath made answer, Evidently he hath trodden down, evidently hath troubled; but what to me shall he do? A grape I was, wine I shall be: "In God I have hoped, I will not fear what flesh doeth to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:64
verses.text: "All day long my words they abhorred".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:65
verses.text: Thus they are, ye know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:66
verses.text: Speak truth, preach truth, proclaim Christ to the heathen, proclaim the Church to heretics, proclaim to all men salvation: they contradict, they abhor my words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:67
verses.text: But when my words they abhor, whom think ye they abhor, save Him in whom I shall praise my discourses? "All day long my words they abhorred".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:68
verses.text: Let this at least suffice, let them abhor words, no farther let them proceed, censure, reject! Be it far from them! Why should I say this? When words they reject, when words they hate, those words which from the fount of truth flow forth, what would they do to him through whom the very words are spoken? what but that which followeth, "Against me all the counsels of them are for evil?" If the bread itself they hate, how spare they the basket wherein it is ministered? "Against me all the counsels of them are for evil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:69
verses.text: If so even against the Lord Himself, let not the Body disdain that which hath gone before in the Head, to the end that the Body may cleave to the Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:70
verses.text: Despised hath been thy Lord, and wilt thou have thyself be honoured by those men that have been put afar off from holy men? Do not for thyself wish to claim that which in Him hath not gone before.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:71
verses.text: "The disciple is not greater than his Master; the servant is not greater than his Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:72
verses.text: If the Master of the family they have called Beelzebub, how much more them of His household?" Against me all the counsels of them are for evil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:73
verses.text: "They shall sojourn, and shall hide".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:74
verses.text: To sojourn is to be in a strange land.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:75
verses.text: Sojourners is a term used of those then that live in a country not their own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:76
verses.text: Every man in this life is a foreigner: in which life ye see that with flesh we are covered round, through which flesh the heart cannot be seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:77
verses.text: Therefore the Apostle saith, "Do not before the time judge anything, until the Lord come, and He shall enlighten the hidden things of darkness, and shall manifest the thoughts of the heart; and then praise shall be to each one from God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:78
verses.text: Before that this be done, in this sojourning of fleshly life every one carrieth his own heart, and every heart to every other heart is shut.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:79
verses.text: Furthermore, those men of whom the counsels are against this man for evil, "shall sojourn, and shall hide:" because in this foreign abode they are, and carry flesh, they hide guile in heart; whatsoever of evil they think, they hide.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:80
verses.text: Wherefore? Because as yet this life is a foreign one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:81
verses.text: Let them hide; that shall appear which they hide, and they too will not be hidden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:82
verses.text: There is also in this hidden thing another interpretation, which perchance will be more approved of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:83
verses.text: For out of those men that have been put afar off from holy men, there creep in certain false brethren, and they cause worse tribulations to the Body of Christ; because they are not altogether avoided as if entirely aliens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:84
verses.text: Not even those men nevertheless let us fear, brethren: "I will not fear what flesh doeth to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:85
verses.text: Even if they sojourn, even if they go in, even if they feign, even if they hide, flesh they are: do thou in the Lord hope, nothing to thee shall flesh do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:86
verses.text: But he bringeth in tribulation, bringeth in treading down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:87
verses.text: There is added wine, because the grape is pressed: thy tribulation will not be unfruitful: another seeth thee, imitateth thee: because thou also in order that thou mightest learn to bear such a man, to thy Head hast looked up, that first cluster, unto whom there hath come in a man that he might see, hath sojourned, and hath hidden, to wit, the traitor Judas.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:88
verses.text: All men, therefore, that with false heart go in, sojourning and hiding, do not thou fear: the father of these same men, Judas, with thy Lord hath been: and He indeed knew him; although Judas the traitor was sojourning and hiding, nevertheless, the heart of him was open to the Lord of all: knowingly He chose one man, whereby He might give comfort to thee that wouldest not know whom thou shouldest avoid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:89
verses.text: For He might have not chosen Judas, because He knew Judas: for He saith to His disciples, "Have not I chosen you twelve, and one out of you is a devil?" Therefore even a devil was chosen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:90
verses.text: Or if chosen he was not, how is it that He hath chosen twelve, and not rather eleven? Chosen even he is, but for another purpose.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:91
verses.text: Chosen were eleven for the work of probation, chosen one for the work of temptation Whence could He give an example to thee, that wouldest not know what men thou shouldest avoid as evil, of what men thou shouldest beware as false and artificial, sojourning and hiding, except He say to thee, Behold, with Myself I have had one of those very men! There hath gone before an example, I have borne, to suffer I have willed that which I knew, in order that to thee knowing not I might give consolation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:92
verses.text: That which to Me he hath done, the same he will do to thee also: in order that he may be able to do much, in order that he may make much havoc, he will accuse, false charges he will allege.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:93
verses.text: "These same men shall mark my heel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:94
verses.text: For they shall sojourn and hide in such sort, that they may mark where a man slippeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:95
verses.text: Intent they are upon the heel, to see when a slip may chance to be made; in order that they may detain the foot for a fall, or trip up the foot for a stumble; certes that they may find that which they may accuse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:96
verses.text: And what man so walketh, that nowhere he slippeth? For example, how speedily is a slip made even in tongue? For it is written, "Whosoever in tongue stumbleth not, the same is a perfect man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:97
verses.text: What man I pray would dare himself to call or deem perfect? Therefore it must needs be that every one slip in tongue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:98
verses.text: But let them that shall sojourn and shall hide, carp at all words, seeking somewhere to make snares and knotty false accusations, wherein they are themselves entangled before those whom they strive to entangle: in order that they may themselves be taken and perish before that they catch other men in order to destroy them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:99
verses.text: Whatever good thing I have said, whatever true thing I have said, of God I have said it, and from God have said it: whatever other thing perchance I have said, which to have said I ought not, as a man I have said, but under God I have said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:100
verses.text: He that strengtheneth one walking, doth menace one straying, forgive one acknowledging, recalleth the tongue, recalleth him that slipped.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:101
verses.text: Attend thou unto the discourses of him whom thou blamest, whether perchance he may teach thee something to thy health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:102
verses.text: And what, he saith, shall he be able to teach to my health, that hath so slipped in word? This very thing perchance he is teaching thee to thy health, that thou be not a carper at words, but a gatherer of precepts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:103
verses.text: "As my soul hath undergone".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:104
verses.text: I speak of that which I have undergone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:105
verses.text: He was speaking as one experienced: "As my soul hath undergone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:106
verses.text: They shall sojourn and hide".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:107
verses.text: Let my soul undergo all men, men without barking, men within hiding, let it undergo.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:108
verses.text: From without coming, like a river cometh temptation: on the Rock let it find thee, let it strike against, not throw thee down; the house hath been founded upon a Rock Within he is, he shall sojourn and hide: suppose chaff is near thee, let there come in the treading of oxen, let there come in the roller of temptations; thou art cleansed, the other is crushed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:109
verses.text: "For nothing Thou shalt save them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:110
verses.text: He hath taught us even for these very men to pray.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:111
verses.text: However "they shall sojourn and hide," however deceitful they be, however dissemblers and liers in wait they be; do thou pray for them, and do not say, Shall God amend even such a man, so evil, so perverse? Do not despair: give heed to Him whom thou askest, not him for whom thou askest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:112
verses.text: The greatness of the disease seest thou, the might of the Physician seest thou not? "They shall sojourn and hide: as my soul hath undergone".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:113
verses.text: Undergo, pray: and there is done what? "For nothing Thou shalt save them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:114
verses.text: Thou shalt make them safe so as that nothing to Thee it may be, that is, so that no labour to Thee it may be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:115
verses.text: With men they are despaired of, but Thou with a word dost heal; Thou wilt not toil in healing, though we are astounded in looking on.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:116
verses.text: There is another sense in this verse, "For nothing Thou shalt save them:" with not any merits of their going before Thou shalt save them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:117
verses.text: They shall not bring to Thee he-goats, rams, bulls, not gifts and spices shall they bring Thee in Thy temple, not anything of the drink-offering of a good conscience do they pour thereon; all in them is rough, all foul, all to be detested: and though they to Thee bring nothing whereby they may be saved; "For nothing Thou shalt save them," that is, with the free gift of Thy Grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:118
verses.text: "In anger the peoples Thou shalt bring down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:119
verses.text: Thou art angry and dost bring down, dost rage and save, dost terrify and call.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:120
verses.text: Thou fillest with tribulations all things, in order that being set in tribulations men may fly to Thee, lest by pleasures and a wrong security they be seduced.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:121
verses.text: From Thee anger is seen, but that of a father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:122
verses.text: A father is angry with a son, the despiser of his injunctions: being angry with him he boxeth him, striketh, pulleth the ear, draggeth with hand, leadeth to school.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:123
verses.text: How many men have entered, how many men have filled the House of the Lord, in the anger of Him brought down, that is, by tribulations terrified and with faith filled? For to this end tribulation stirreth up; in order to empty the vessel which is full of wickedness, so as that it may be filled with grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:124
verses.text: "O God, my life I have told out to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:125
verses.text: For that I live hath been Thy doing, and for this reason I tell out my life to Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:126
verses.text: But did not God know that which He had given? What is that which thou tellest out to Him? Wilt thou teach God? Far be it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:127
verses.text: Therefore why saith he, "I have told out to Thee"? Is it perchance because it profiteth Thee that I have told out my life? And what doth it profit God? To the advantage of God it doth profit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:128
verses.text: I have told out to God my life, because that life hath been God's doing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:129
verses.text: In like manner as his life Paul the Apostle did tell out, saying, "I that before was a blasphemer and a persecutor and injurious," he shall tell out his life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:130
verses.text: "But mercy I have obtained".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:131
verses.text: He hath told out his life, not for himself, but for Him: because he hath told it out in such sort, that in Him men believe, not for his own advantages, but for the advantages of Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:132
verses.text: "O God, my life I have told out to Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:133
verses.text: Thou hast put my tears in Thy sight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:134
verses.text: Thou hast hearkened to me imploring Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:135
verses.text: "As also in Thy promise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:136
verses.text: Because as Thou hadst promised this thing, so Thou hast done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:137
verses.text: Thou hast said Thou wouldest hearken to one weeping.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:138
verses.text: I have believed, I have wept, I have been hearkened unto; I have found Thee merciful in promising, true in repaying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:139
verses.text: "Turned be mine enemies backward".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:140
verses.text: This thing to these very men is profitable, no ill to these men he is wishing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:141
verses.text: For to go before they are willing, therefore to be amended they are not willing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:142
verses.text: Thou warnest thine enemy to live well, that he amend himself: he scorneth, he rejecteth thy word: "Behold him that adviseth me; behold him from whom I am to hear the commandments whereby I shall live!" To go before thee he willeth, and in going before is not amended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:143
verses.text: He mindeth not that thy words are not thine, he mindeth not that thy life to God thou tellest out, not to thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:144
verses.text: In going before therefore he is not amended: it is a good thing for him that he be turned backward, and follow him whom to go before he willed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:145
