verses.text: The Lord to His disciples was speaking of His Passion that was to be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:146
verses.text: Peter shuddered, and saith, "Far be it, O Lord;" he that a little before had said, "Thou art the Christ, Son of the living God," having confessed God, feared for Him to die, as if but a man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:147
verses.text: But the Lord who so came that He might suffer (for we could not otherwise be saved unless with His blood we were redeemed), a little before had praised the confession of Peter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:148
verses.text: But immediately when the Lord beginneth to speak of His Passion, he feared lest He should perish by death, whereas we ourselves should perish unless He died; and he saith, "Far be it, O Lord, this thing shall not be done".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:149
verses.text: And the Lord, to him to whom a little before He had said, "Blessed thou art, and upon this Rock I will build my Church," saith, "Go back behind, Satan, an offence thou art to Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:150
verses.text: Why therefore "Satan" is he, that a little before was "blessed," and a "Rock"? "For thou savourest not the things which are of God," He saith, "but those things which are of man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:151
verses.text: A little before he savoured the things which are of God: because "not flesh and blood hath revealed to thee, but My Father which is in the Heavens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:152
verses.text: When in God he was praising his discourse, not Satan but Peter, from petra: but when of himself and out of human infirmity, carnal love of man, which would be for an impediment to his own salvation, and that of the rest, Satan he is called.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:153
verses.text: Why? Because to go before the Lord he willed, and earthly counsel to give to the heavenly Leader.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:154
verses.text: "Far be it, O Lord, this thing shall not be done".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:155
verses.text: Thou sayest, "Far be it," and thou sayest, "O Lord:" surely if Lord He is, in power He doeth: if Master He is, He knoweth what He doeth, He knoweth what He teacheth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:156
verses.text: But thou willest to lead thy Leader, teach thy Master, command thy Lord, choose for God: much thou goest before, go back behind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:157
verses.text: Did not this too profit these enemies? "Turned be Mine enemies backward;" but let them not remain backward.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:158
verses.text: For this reason let them be turned backward, lest they go before; but so that they follow, not so that they remain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:159
verses.text: "In whatsoever day I shall have called upon Thee, behold I have known that my God art Thou".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:160
verses.text: A great knowledge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:161
verses.text: He saith not, "I have known that God Thou art:" but, "that my God art Thou".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:162
verses.text: For thine He is, when thee He succoureth: thine He is, when thou to Him art not an alien.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:163
verses.text: Whence is said, "Blessed the people of whom is the Lord the God of the same".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:164
verses.text: Wherefore "of whom is"? For of whom is He not? Of all things indeed God He is: but of those men the God peculiarly He is said to be, that love Him, that hold Him, that possess Him, that worship Him, as though belonging to His own House: the great family of Him are they, redeemed by the great blood of the Only Son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:165
verses.text: How great a thing hath God given to us, that His own we should be, and He should be ours! But in truth foreigners afar have been put from holy men, sons alien they are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:166
verses.text: See what of them is said in another Psalm: "O Lord, deliver me," he saith, "from the hand of alien sons, of whom the mouth hath spoken vanity, and the right hand of them is a right hand of iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:167
verses.text: Let us therefore love God, brethren, purely and chastely.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:168
verses.text: There is not a chaste heart, if God for reward it worshippeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:169
verses.text: How so? Reward of the worship of God shall not we have? We shall have evidently, but it is God Himself whom we worship.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:170
verses.text: Himself for us a reward shall be, because "we shall see Him as He is".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:171
verses.text: Observe that a reward thou shalt obtain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:172
verses.text: I will tell you, brethren: in these human alliances consider a chaste heart, of what sort it is towards God: certainly human alliances are of such sort, that a man doth not love his wife, that loveth her because of her portion: a woman her husband doth not chastely love, that for these reasons loveth him, because something he hath given, or because much he hath given.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:173
verses.text: Both a rich man is a husband, and one that hath become a poor man is a husband.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:174
verses.text: How many men proscribed, by chaste wives have been the more beloved! Proved have been many chaste marriages by the misfortunes of husbands: that the wives might not be supposed to love any other object more than their husband, not only have they not forsaken, but the more have they obeyed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:175
verses.text: If therefore a husband of flesh freely is loved, if chastely he is loved; and a wife of flesh freely is loved, if chastely she is loved; in what manner must God be loved, the true and truth-speaking Husband of the soul, making fruitful unto the offspring of everlasting life, and not suffering us to be barren? Him, therefore, so let us love, as that any other thing besides Himself be not loved: and there takes place in us that which we have spoken of, that which we have sung, because even here the voice is ours: "In whatsoever day I shall have called upon Thee, behold, I have known that my God art Thou".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:176
verses.text: This is to call upon God, freely to call upon Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:177
verses.text: Furthermore, of certain men hath been said what? "Upon the Lord they have not called".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:178
verses.text: The Lord they seemed as it were to call unto themselves and they besought Him about inheritances, about increasing money, about lengthening this life, about the rest of temporal things: and concerning them the Scripture saith what? "Upon the Lord they have not called".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:179
verses.text: Therefore there followeth what? "There they have feared with fear, where there was no fear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:180
verses.text: What is, "where there was no fear"? Lest money should be stolen from them, lest anything in their house should be made less; lastly, lest they should have less of years in this life, than they hoped for themselves: but there have they trembled with fear, where there was no fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:181
verses.text: "In God I will praise the word, in the Lord I will praise the discourse" : "in God I have hoped, I will not fear what man doeth unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:182
verses.text: Now this is the very sense which above hath been repeated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:183
verses.text: "In me, O God, are Thy vows, which I will render of praise to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:184
verses.text: "Vow ye, and render to the Lord your God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:185
verses.text: What vow, what render? Perchance those animals which were offered at the altars aforetime? No such thing offer thou: in thyself is what thou mayest vow and render.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:186
verses.text: From the heart's coffer bring forth the incense of praise; from the store of a good conscience bring forth the sacrifice of faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:187
verses.text: Whatsoever thing thou bringest forth, kindle with love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:188
verses.text: In thyself be the vows, which thou mayest render of praise to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:189
verses.text: Of what praise? For what hath He granted thee? "For Thou hast rescued my soul from death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:190
verses.text: This is that very life which he telleth out to Him: "O God, my life I have told out to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:191
verses.text: For I was what? Dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:192
verses.text: Through myself I was dead: through Thee I am what? Alive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:193
verses.text: Therefore "in me, O God, are Thy vows, which I will render of praise to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:194
verses.text: Behold I love my God: no one doth tear Him from me: that which to Him I may give, no one doth tear from me, because in the heart it is shut up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:195
verses.text: With reason is said with that former confidence, "What should man do unto me?" Let man rage, let him be permitted to rage, be permitted to accomplish that which he attempteth: what is he to take away? Gold, silver, cattle, men servants, maid servants, estates, houses, let him take away all things: doth he by any means take away the vows, which are in me, which I may render of praise to God? The tempter was permitted to tempt a holy man, Job; in one moment he took away all things: whatever of possessions he had had, he carried off: took away inheritance, slew heirs; and this not little by little, but in a crowd, at one blow, at one swoop, so that all things were on a sudden announced: when all was taken away, alone there remained Job, but in him were vows of praise, which he might render to God, in him evidently there were: the coffer of his holy breast the thieving devil had not rifled, full he was of that wherefrom he might sacrifice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:196
verses.text: Hear what he had, hear what he brought forth: "The Lord hath given, the Lord hath taken away; as hath pleased the Lord, so hath been done: be the name of the Lord blessed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:197
verses.text: O riches interior, whither thief doth not draw near! God Himself had given that whereof He was receiving; He had Himself enriched him with that whereof to Him he was offering that which He loved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:198
verses.text: Praise from thee God requireth, thy confession God requireth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:199
verses.text: But from thy field wilt thou give anything? He hath Himself rained in order that thou mayest have.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:200
verses.text: From thy coffer wilt thou give anything? He hath Himself put in that which thou art to give.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:201
verses.text: What wilt thou give, which from Him thou hast not received? "For what hast thou which thou hast not received?" From the heart wilt thou give? He too hath given faith, hope, and charity: this thou must bring forth: this thou must sacrifice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:202
verses.text: But evidently all the other things the enemy is able to take away against thy will; this to take away he is not able, unless thou be willing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:203
verses.text: These things a man will lose even against his will: and wishing to have gold, will lose gold; and wishing to have house, will lose house: faith no one will lose, except him that shall have despised her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:204
verses.text: "Because Thou hast rescued my soul from death, mine eyes from tears, and my feet from slipping: that I may be pleasing before God in the light of the living".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:205
verses.text: With reason he is not pleasing to alien sons, that are put afar off from holy men, because they have not the light of the living, whence they may see that which to God is pleasing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:206
verses.text: "Light of the living," is light of the immortal, light of holy men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:207
verses.text: He that is not in darkness, is pleasing in the light of the living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:208
verses.text: A man is observed, and the things which belong to him; no one knoweth of what sort he is: God seeth of what sort he is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:209
verses.text: Sometimes even the devil himself he escapeth; except he tempt, he findeth not: just as concerning that man of whom just now I have made mention:"Doth Job by any means worship God for nought?" For this was true light, this the light of the living, that gratis he should worship God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:210
verses.text: God saw in the heart of His servant His gratuitous worship.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:211
verses.text: For that heart was pleasing in the sight of the Lord in the light of the living: the devil's sight he escaped, because in darkness he was.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:212
verses.text: God admitted the tempter, not in order that He might Himself know that which He did know, but in order that to us to be known and imitated He might set it forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:213
verses.text: Admitted was the tempter; he took away everything, there remained the man bereft of possessions, bereft of family, bereft of children, full of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:214
verses.text: A wife certainly was left Merciful do ye deem the devil, that he left him a wife? He knew through whom he had deceived Adam.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:215
verses.text: With wound smitten from head even unto feet, whole nevertheless within, he made answer to the woman tempting, out of the light of the living, out of the light of his heart: "thou hast spoken as though one of the unwise women," that is, as though one that hath not the light of the living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:216
verses.text: For the light of the living is wisdom, and the darkness of unwise men is folly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:217
verses.text: Thou hast spoken as though one of the unwise women: my flesh thou seest, the light of my heart thou seest not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:218
verses.text: For she then might more have loved her husband, if the interior beauty she had known, and had beheld the place where he was beautiful before the eyes of God: because in Him were vows which he might render of praise to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:219
verses.text: How entirely the enemy had forborne to invade that patrimony! How whole was that which he was possessing, and that because of which yet more to be possessed he hoped for, being to go on "from virtues unto virtue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:220
verses.text: Therefore, brethren, to this end let all these things serve us, that God gratis we love, in Him hope always, neither man nor devil fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:221
verses.text: Neither the one nor the other doeth anything, except when it is permitted: permitted for no other reason can it be, except because it doth profit us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:222
verses.text: Let us endure evil men, let us be good men: because even we have been evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:223
verses.text: Even as nothing God shall save men, of whom we dare to despair.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:224
verses.text: Therefore of no one let us despair, for all men whom we suffer let us pray, from God let us never depart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:225
verses.text: Our patrimony let Him be, our hope let Him be, our safety let Him be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 57:226
verses.text: He is Himself here a comforter, there a remunerator, everywhere Maker-alive, and of life the Giver, not of another life, but of that whereof hath been said, "I am the Way, and the Truth, and the Life:" in order that both here in the light of faith, and there in the light of sight, as it were in the light of the living, in the sight of the Lord we may be pleasing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:1
verses.text: Psalm LVII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:2
verses.text: We have heard in the Gospel just now, brethren, how loveth us our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, God with the Father, Man with us, out of our own selves, now at the right hand of the Father; ye have heard how much He loveth us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:3
verses.text: Because then this Psalm is singing of the Passion of the Lord, see what is the title that it hath: "at the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:4
verses.text: The end is Christ Why hath He been called end? Not as one that consumeth, but one that consummateth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:5
verses.text: "At the end, corrupt not, for David himself, for the inscription of the title; when he fled from the face of Saul into a cavern".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:6
verses.text: We referring to holy Scripture, do find indeed how holy David, that king of Israel, from whom too the Psalter of David hath received the name thereof, had suffered for persecutor Saul the king of his own people, as many of you know that have either read or have heard the Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:7
verses.text: King David had then for persecutor Saul: and whereas the one was most gentle, the other most ferocious: the one mild, the other envious; the one patient, the other cruel; the one beneficent, the other ungrateful: he endured him with so much mildness, that when he had gotten him into his hands him he touched not, hurt notWhat reference hath this to Christ? If all things which then were being done, were figures of things future, we find there Christ, and by far in the greatest degree.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:8
verses.text: For this, "corrupt not for the inscription of the title," I see not how it belongeth to that David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:9
verses.text: For not any "title" was inscribed over David himself which Saul would "corrupt".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:10
verses.text: But we see in the Passion of the Lord that there had been written a title, "King of the Jews:"  in order that this title might put to the blush these very men, seeing that from their King they withheld not their hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:11
verses.text: For in them Saul was, in Christ David was.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:12
verses.text: For Christ, as saith the Apostolic Gospel, is, as we know, as we confess, of the seed of David after the flesh; for after the Godhead He is above David, above all men, above heaven and earth, above angels, above all things visible and invisible.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:13
verses.text: And because already it had been sung through the Holy Spirit, "Unto the end, corrupt not, for the inscription of the title:" Pilate answered them, "What I have written, I have written:" why do ye suggest to me falsehood? I corrupt not truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:14
verses.text: What therefore is, "When he fled from the face of Saul into a cavern"? Which thing indeed the former David also did: but because in him we find not the inscription of the title, in the latter let us find the flight into the cavern For that cavern wherein David hid himself did figure somewhat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:15
verses.text: But wherefore hid he himself? It was in order that he might be concealed and not be found.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:16
verses.text: What is to be hidden in a cavern? To be hidden in earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:17
verses.text: For he that fleeth into a cavern, with earth is covered so that he may not be seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:18
verses.text: But Jesus did carry earth, flesh which He had received from earth: and in it He concealed Himself, in order that by Jews He might not be discovered as God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:19
verses.text: "For if they had known, never the Lord of glory would they have crucified".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:20
verses.text: Why therefore the Lord of glory found they not? Because in a cavern He had hidden Himself, that is, the flesh's weakness to their eyes He presented, but the Majesty of the Godhead in the body's clothing, as though in a hiding-place of the earth, He hid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:21
verses.text: But wherefore even unto death willed He to be patient? It was in order that He might flee from the face of Saul into a cavern.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:22
verses.text: For a cavern may be understood as a lower part of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:23
verses.text: And certainly, as is manifest and certain to all, His Body in a Tomb was laid, which was cut in a Rock.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:24
verses.text: This Tomb therefore was the Cavern; thither He fled from the face of Saul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:25
verses.text: For so long the Jews did persecute Him, even until He was laid in a cavern.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:26
verses.text: Whence prove we that so long they persecuted Him, until therein He was laid? Even when dead, and, on the Cross hanging, with lance they wounded Him But when shrouded, the funeral celebrated, He was laid in a cavern, no longer had they anything which to the Flesh they might do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:27
verses.text: Rose therefore the Lord again out of that cavern unhurt, uncorrupt, from that place whither He had fled from the face of Saul: concealing Himself from ungodly men, whom Saul prefigured, but showing Himself to His members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:28
verses.text: For the members of Him rising again by His members were handled: for the members of Him, the Apostles, touched Him rising again and believed; and behold nothing profited the persecution of Saul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:29
verses.text: Hear we therefore now the Psalm; because concerning the title thereof enough we have spoken, as far as the Lord hath deigned to give.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:30
verses.text: "Have pity on me, O God, have pity on me, for in Thee hath trusted my Soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:31
verses.text: Christ in the Passion saith, "Have pity on Me, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:32
verses.text: To God, God saith, "Have pity on Me!" He that with the Father hath pity on thee, in thee crieth, "Have pity on Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:33
verses.text: For that part of Him which is crying, "Have pity on Me," is thine: from thee this He received, for the sake of thee, that thou shouldest be delivered, with Flesh He was clothed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:34
verses.text: The flesh itself crieth: "Have pity on Me, O God, have pity on me:" Man himself, soul and flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:35
verses.text: For whole Man did the Word take upon Him, and whole Man the Word became.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:36
verses.text: Let it not therefore be thought that there Soul was not, because the Evangelist thus saith: "The Word was made flesh, and dwelled in us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:37
verses.text: For man is called flesh, as in another place saith the Scripture, "And all flesh shall see the salvation of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:38
verses.text: Shall anywise flesh alone see, and shall Soul not be there?Thou hearest the Master praying, learn thou to pray.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:39
verses.text: For to this end He prayed, in order that He might teach how to pray: because to this end He suffered, in order that He might teach how to suffer; to this end He rose again, in order that He might teach how to hope for rising again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:40
verses.text: "And in the shadow of Thy wings I will hope, until iniquity pass over".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:41
verses.text: This now evidently whole Christ doth say: here is also our voice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:42
verses.text: For not yet hath passed over, still rife is iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:43
verses.text: And in the end our Lord Himself said there should be an abounding of iniquity: "And since iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold; but he that shall have persevered unto the end, the same shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:44
verses.text: But who shall persevere even unto the end, even until iniquity pass over? He that shall have been in the Body of Christ, he that shall have been in the members of Christ, and from the Head shall have learned the patience of persevering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:45
verses.text: Thou passest away, and behold passed are thy temptations; and thou goest into another life whither have gone holy men, if holy thou hast been.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:46
verses.text: Into another life have gone Martyrs; if Martyr thou shalt have been, thou also goest into another life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:47
verses.text: Because "thou" hast passed away hence, hath by any means iniquity therefore passed away? There are born other unrighteous men, as there die some unrighteous men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:48
verses.text: In like manner therefore as some unrighteous men die and others are born: so some just men go, and others are born.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:49
verses.text: Even unto the end of the world neither iniquity will be wanting to oppress, nor righteousness to suffer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:50
verses.text: "I will cry to God most high".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:51
verses.text: If most high He is, how heareth He thee crying? Confidence hath been engendered by experience: "to God," he saith, "who had done good to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:52
verses.text: If before that I was seeking Him, He did good to me, when I cry shall He not hearken to me? For good to us the Lord God hath done in sending to us our Saviour Jesus Christ, that He might die for our offences, and rise again for our justification For what sort of men hath He willed His Son to die? For ungodly men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:53
verses.text: But ungodly men were not seeking God, and have been sought of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:54
verses.text: For He is Most High in such sort, as that not far from Him is our misery and our groaning: because "near is the Lord to them that have bruised the heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:55
verses.text: "God that hath done good to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:56
verses.text: "He hath sent from heaven and hath saved me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:57
verses.text: Now the Man Himself, now the Flesh Itself, now the Son of God after His partaking of ourselves, of Him it is manifest, how He was saved, and hath sent from heaven the Father and hath saved Him, hath sent from heaven, and hath raised Him again: but in order that ye may know, that also the Lord Himself hath raised again Himself; both truths are written in Scripture, both that the Father hath raised Him again, and that Himself Himself hath raised again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:58
verses.text: Hear ye how the Father hath raised Him again: the Apostle saith, "He hath been made," he saith, "obedient unto death, even the death of the Cross: wherefore God also hath exalted Him, and hath given Him a name which is above every name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:59
verses.text: Ye have heard of the Father raising again and exalting the Son; hear ye how that He too Himself His flesh hath raised again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:60
verses.text: Under the figure of a temple He saith to the Jews, "Destroy this Temple, and in three days I will raise it up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:61
verses.text: But the Evangelist hath explained to us what it was that He said: "But this," he saith, "He spake of the Temple of His Body".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:62
verses.text: Now therefore out of the person of one praying, out of the person of a man, out of the person of the flesh, He saith, "He hath saved me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:63
verses.text: He hath given unto reproach those that trampled on me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:64
verses.text: Them that have trampled on Him, that over Him dead have insulted, that Him as though man have crucified, because God they perceived not, them He hath given unto reproach.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:65
verses.text: See ye whether it has not been so done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:66
verses.text: The thing we do not believe as yet to come, but fulfilled we acknowledge it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:67
verses.text: The Jews raged against Christ, they were overbearing against Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:68
verses.text: Where? In the city of Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:69
verses.text: For where they reigned, there they were puffed up, there their necks they lifted up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:70
verses.text: After the Passion of the Lord thence they were rooted out; and they lost the kingdom, wherein Christ for King they would not acknowledge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:71
verses.text: In what manner they have been given unto reproach, see ye: dispersed they have been throughout all nations, nowhere having a settlement, nowhere a sure abode.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:72
verses.text: But for this reason still Jews they are, in order that our books they may carry to their confusion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:73
verses.text: For whenever we wish to show Christ prophesied of, we produce to the heathen these writings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:74
verses.text: And lest perchance men hard of belief should say that we Christians have composed these books, so that together with the Gospel which we have preached we have forged the Prophet, through whom there might seem to be foretold that which we preach: by this we convince them; namely, that all the very writings wherein Christ hath been prophesied are with the Jews, all these very writings the Jews have.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:75
verses.text: We produce documents from enemies, to confound other enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:76
verses.text: In what sort of reproach therefore are the Jews? A document the Jew carrieth, wherefrom a Christian may believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:77
verses.text: Our librarians they have become, just as slaves are wont behind their masters to carry documents, in such sort that these faint in carrying, those profit by reading Unto such a reproach have been given the Jews: and there hath been fulfilled that which so long before hath been foretold, "He hath given unto reproach those that trampled on me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:78
verses.text: But how great a reproach it is, brethren, that this verse they should read, and themselves being blind should look upon their mirror! For in the same manner the Jews appear in the holy Scripture which they carry, as appeareth the face of a blind man in a mirror: by other men it is seen, by himself not seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:79
verses.text: Thou wast inquiring perhaps when he said, "He hath sent from heaven and hath saved me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:80
verses.text: What hath He sent from heaven? Whom hath He sent from heaven? An Angel hath He sent, to save Christ, and through a servant is the Lord saved? For all Angels are creatures serving Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:81
verses.text: For obedience there might have been sent Angels, for service they might have been sent, not for succour: as is written, "Angels ministered unto Him," not like men merciful to one indigent, but like subjects to One Omnipotent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:82
verses.text: What therefore "hath He sent from heaven, and hath saved me"? Now we hear in another verse what from heaven He hath sent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:83
verses.text: "He hath sent from heaven His mercy and His truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:84
verses.text: For what purpose? "And hath drawn out my soul from the midst of the lions' whelps".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:85
verses.text: "Hath sent," he saith, "from heaven His mercy and His truth:" and Christ Himself saith, "I am Truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:86
verses.text: There was sent therefore Truth, that it should draw out my soul hence from the midst of the lions' whelps: there was sent mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:87
verses.text: Christ Himself we find to be both mercy and truth; mercy in suffering with us, and truth in requiting us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:88
verses.text: Who are the lions' whelps? That lesser people, unto evil deceived, unto evil led away by the chiefs of the Jews: so that these are lions, those lions' whelps.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:89
verses.text: All roared, all slew.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:90
verses.text: For we are to hear even here the slaying of these very men, presently in the following verses of this Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:91
verses.text: "And hath drawn out," he saith, "my soul from the midst of the lions' whelps".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:92
verses.text: Why sayest thou, "And hath drawn out my soul"? For what hadst thou suffered, that thy soul should be drawn out? "I have slept troubled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:93
verses.text: Christ hath intimated His death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:94
verses.text: Whence "troubled"? Who troubling? Let us see in what manner he brandeth an evil conscience upon the Jews, wishing to excuse themselves of the slaying of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:95
verses.text: For to this end, as the Gospel speaketh, to the judge they delivered Him, that they might not themselves seem to have killed Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:96
verses.text: Let us question Him, and say, since Thou hast slept troubled, who have persecuted Thee? who have slain Thee? was it perchance Pilate, who to soldiers gave Thee, on the Tree to be hanged, with nails to be pierced? Hear who they were, "Sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:97
verses.text: Of them He speaketh, whom for persecutors He suffered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:98
verses.text: But how did they slay, that steel bare not? They that sword drew not, that made no assault upon Him to slay; whence slew they? "Their teeth are arms and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:99
verses.text: Do not consider the unarmed hands, but the mouth armed: from thence the sword proceeded, wherewith Christ was to be slain: in like manner also as from the mouth of Christ, that wherewith the Jews were to be slain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:100
verses.text: For He hath a sword twice whetted: and rising again He hath smitten them, and hath severed from them those whom He would make His faithful people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:101
verses.text: They an evil sword, He a good sword: they evil arrows, He good arrows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:102
verses.text: For He hath Himself also arrows good, words good, whence He pierceth the faithful heart, in order that He may be loved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:103
verses.text: Therefore of one kind are their arrows, and of another kind their sword.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:104
verses.text: "Sons of men, their teeth are arms and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sabre".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:105
verses.text: Tongue of sons of men is a sharp sabre, and their teeth arms and arrows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:106
verses.text: When therefore did they smite, save when they clamoured, "Crucify, crucify"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:107
verses.text: And what have they done to Thee, O Lord? Let the Prophet here exult! For above, all those verses the Lord was speaking: a Prophet indeed, but in the person of the Lord, because in the Prophet is the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:108
verses.text: "Be exalted," he saith, "above the Heavens, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:109
verses.text: Man on the Cross, and above the Heavens, God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:110
verses.text: Let them continue on the earth raging, Thou in Heaven be judging.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:111
verses.text: Where are they that were raging? where are their teeth, the arms and arrows ? Have not "the stripes of them been made the arrows of infants"? For in another place a Psalm this saith, desiring to prove them vainly to have raged, and vainly unto frenzies to have been driven headlong: for nothing they were able to do to Christ when for the time crucified, and afterwards when He was rising again, and in Heaven was sitting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:112
verses.text: How do infants make to themselves arrows? Of reeds? But what arrows? or what powers? or what bows? or what wound? "Be Thou exalted above the Heavens, O God, and above all the earth Thy glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:113
verses.text: Wherefore exalted above the Heavens, O God? Brethren, God exalted above the Heavens we see not, but we believe: but above all the earth His glory to be not only we believe, but also see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:114
verses.text: But what kind of madness heretics are afflicted with, I pray you observe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:115
verses.text: They being cut off from the bond of the Church of Christ, and to a part holding, the whole losing, will not communicate with the whole earth, where is spread abroad the glory of Christ But we Catholics are in all the earth, because with all the world we communicate, wherever the Glory of Christ is spread abroad For we see that which then was sung, now fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:116
verses.text: There hath been exalted above the Heavens our God, and above all the earth the Glory of the Same.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:117
verses.text: O heretical insanity! That which thou seest not thou believest with me, that which thou seest thou deniest: thou believest with me in Christ exalted above the Heavens, a thing which we see not; and deniest His Glory over all the earth, a thing which we see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:118
verses.text: Let your Love see the Lord speaking to us, and exhorting us by His example: "A trap they have prepared for My feet, and have bowed down My Soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:119
verses.text: They wished to bring It down as if from Heaven, and to the lower places to weigh It down: "They have bowed My Soul: they have digged before My face a pit and themselves have fallen into it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:120
verses.text: Me have they hurt, or themselves? Behold He hath been exalted above the Heavens, God, and behold above all the earth the Glory of the Same: the kingdom of Christ we see, where is the kingdom of the Jews? Since therefore they did that which to have done they ought not, there hath been done in their case that which to have suffered they ought: themselves have dug a ditch, and themselves have fallen into it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:121
verses.text: For their persecuting Christ, to Christ did no hurt, but to themselves did hurt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:122
verses.text: And do not suppose, brethren, that themselves alone hath this befallen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:123
verses.text: Every one that prepareth a pit for his brother, it must needs be that himself fall into it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:124
verses.text: But the patience of good men with preparation of heart accepteth the will of God: and glorieth in tribulations, saying that which followeth: "Prepared is my heart, O God, I will sing and play".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:125
verses.text: What hath he done to me? He hath prepared a pit, my heart is prepared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:126
verses.text: He hath prepared pit to deceive, shall I not prepare heart to suffer? He hath prepared pit to oppress, shall I not prepare heart to endure? Therefore he shall fall into it, but I will sing and play.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:127
verses.text: Hear the heart prepared in an Apostle, because he hath imitated his Lord: "We glory," he saith, "in tribulations: because tribulation worketh patience: patience probation, probation hope, but hope maketh not ashamed: because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, which hath been given to us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:128
verses.text: He was in oppressions, in chains, in prisons, in stripes, in hunger and thirst, in cold and nakedness, in every wasting of toils and pains, and he was saying, "We glory in tribulations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:129
verses.text: Whence, but that prepared was his heart? Therefore he was singing and playing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:130
verses.text: "Rise up, my glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:131
verses.text: He that had fled from the face of Saul into a cavern, saith, "Rise up, my glory:" glorified be Jesus after His Passion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:132
verses.text: "Rise up, psaltery and harp".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:133
verses.text: He calleth upon what to rise? Two organs I see: but Body of Christ one I see, one flesh hath risen again, and two organs have risen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:134
verses.text: The one organ then is the psaltery, the other the harp.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:135
verses.text: Organs  is the word used for all instruments of musicians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:136
verses.text: Not only is that called an organ, which is great, and blown into with bellows; but whatsoever is adapted to playing and is corporeal, whereof for an instrument the player maketh use, is said to be an organ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:137
verses.text: But distinguished from one another are these organsWhat therefore do these two organs figure to us? For Christ the Lord our God is waking up His psaltery and His harp; and He saith, "I will rise up at the dawn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:138
verses.text: I suppose that here ye now perceive the Lord rising.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:139
verses.text: We have read thereof in the Gospel: see the hour of the Resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:140
verses.text: How long through shadows was Christ being sought? He hath shone, be He acknowledged; "at the dawn" He rose again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:141
verses.text: But what is psaltery? what is harp? Through His flesh two kinds of deeds the Lord hath wrought, miracles and sufferings: miracles from above have been, sufferings from below have been.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:142
verses.text: But those miracles which He did were divine; but through Body He did them, through flesh He did them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:143
verses.text: The flesh therefore working things divine, is the psaltery: the flesh suffering things human is the harp.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:144
verses.text: Let the psaltery sound, let the blind be enlightened, let the deaf hear, let the paralytics be braced to strength, the lame walk, the sick rise up, the dead rise again; this is the sound of the Psaltery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:145
verses.text: Let there sound also the harp, let Him hunger, thirst, sleep, be held, scourged, derided, crucified, buried.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:146
verses.text: When therefore thou seest in that Flesh certain things to have sounded from above, certain things from the lower part, one flesh hath risen again, and in one flesh we acknowledge both psaltery and harp.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:147
verses.text: And these two kinds of things done have fulfilled the Gospel, and it is preached in the nations: for both the miracles and the sufferings of the Lord are preached.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:148
verses.text: Therefore there hath risen psaltery and harp in the dawn, and he confesseth to the Lord; and saith what? "I will confess to Thee among the peoples, O Lord, and will play to Thee among the nations: for magnified even unto the Heavens hath been Thy mercy, and even unto the clouds Thy truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:149
verses.text: Heavens above clouds, and clouds below heavens: and nevertheless to this nearest heaven belong clouds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:150
verses.text: But sometimes clouds rest upon the mountains, even so far in the nearest air are they rolled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:151
verses.text: But a Heaven above there is, the habitations of Angels, Thrones, Dominions, Principalities, Powers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:152
verses.text: This therefore may perchance seem to be what should have been said: "Unto the Heavens Thy truth, and even unto the clouds Thy mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:153
verses.text: For in Heaven Angels praise God, seeing the very form of truth, without any darkness of vision, without any admixture of unreality: they see, love, praise, are not wearied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:154
verses.text: There is truth: but here in our own misery surely there is mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:155
verses.text: For to a miserable one must be rendered mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:156
verses.text: For there is no need of mercy above, where is no miserable one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:157
verses.text: I have said this because that it seemeth as though it might have been more fittingly said, "Magnified even unto the Heavens hath been Thy truth, and even unto the clouds Thy mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:158
verses.text: For "clouds" we understand to be preachers of truth, men bearing that flesh in a manner dark, whence God both gleameth in miracles, and thundereth in preceptsGlory to our Lord, and to the Mercy of the Same, and to the Truth of the Same, because neither hath He forsaken by mercy to make us blessed through His Grace, nor defrauded us of truth: because first Truth veiled in flesh came to us and healed through His flesh the interior eye of our heart, in order that hereafter face to  face we may be able to see It Giving therefore to Him thanks, let us say with the same Psalm the last verses, which sometime since too I have said, "Be Thou exalted above the Heavens, O God, and above all the earth Thy glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 58:159
verses.text: For this to Him the Prophet said so many years before; this now we see; this therefore let us also say.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:1
verses.text: Psalm LVIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:2
verses.text: The words which we have sung must be rather hearkened to by us, than proclaimed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:3
verses.text: For to all men as it were in an assemblage of mankind, the Truth crieth, "If truly indeed justice ye speak, judge right things, ye sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:4
verses.text: For to what unjust man is it not an easy thing to speak justice? or what man if questioned about justice, when he hath not a cause, would not easily answer what is just? Inasmuch as the hand of our Maker in our very hearts hath written this truth, "That which to thyself thou wouldest not have done, do not thou to another".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:5
verses.text: Of this truth, even before that the Law was given, no one was suffered to be ignorant, in order that there might be some rule whereby might be judged even those to whom Law had not been given But lest men should complain that something had been wanting for them, there hath been written also in tables that which in their hearts they read not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:6
verses.text: For it was not that they had it not written, but read it they would not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:7
verses.text: There hath been set before their eyes that which in their conscience to see they would be compelled; and as if from without the voice of God were brought to them, to his own inward parts hath man been thus driven, the Scripture saying, "For in the thoughts of the ungodly man there will be questioning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:8
verses.text: Where questioning is, there is law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:9
verses.text: But because men, desiring those things which are without, even from themselves have become exiles, there hath been given also a written law: not because in hearts it had not been written, but because thou wast a deserter from thy heart, thou art seized by Him that is everywhere, and to thyself within art called back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:10
verses.text: Therefore the written law, what crieth it, to those that have deserted the law written in their hearts?  "Return ye transgressors to the heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:11
verses.text: For who hath taught thee, that thou wouldest have no other man draw near thy wife? Who hath taught thee, that thou wouldest not have a theft committed upon thee? Who hath taught thee, that thou wouldest not suffer wrong, and whatever other thing either universally or particularly might be spoken of? For many things there are, of which severally if questioned men with loud voice would answer, that they would not suffer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:12
verses.text: Come, if thou art not willing to suffer these things, art thou by any means the only man? dost thou not live in the fellowship of mankind? He that together with thee hath been made, is thy fellow; and all men have been made after the image of God, unless with earthly coverings they efface that which He hath formed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:13
verses.text: That which therefore to thyself thou wilt not have to be done, do not thou to another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:14
verses.text: For thou judgest that there is evil in that, which to suffer thou art not willing: and this thing thou art constrained to know by an inward law; that in thy very heart is written.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:15
verses.text: Thou wast doing somewhat, and there was a cry raised in thy hands: how art thou constrained to return to thy heart when this thing thou sufferest in the hands of others? Is theft a good thing? No! I ask, is adultery a good thing? All cry, No! Is man-slaying a good thing? All cry, that they abhor it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:16
verses.text: Is coveting the property of a neighbour a good thing? No! is the voice of all men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:17
verses.text: Or if yet thou confessest not, there draweth near one that coveteth thy property: be pleased to answer what thou wilt have.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:18
verses.text: All men therefore, when of these things questioned, cry that these things are not good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:19
verses.text: Again, of doing kindnesses, not only of not hurting, but also of conferring and distributing, any hungry soul is questioned thus: "thou sufferest hunger, another man hath bread, and there is abundance with him beyond sufficiency, he knoweth thee to want, he giveth not: it displeaseth thee when hungering, let it displease thee when full also, when of another's hungering thou shalt have known.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:20
verses.text: A stranger wanting shelter cometh into thy country, he is not taken in: he then crieth that inhuman is that city, at once among barbarians he might have found a home.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:21
verses.text: He feeleth the injustice because he suffereth; thou perchance feelest not, but it is meet that thou imagine thyself also a stranger; and that thou see in what manner he will have displeased thee, who shall not have given that, which thou in thy country wilt not give to a stranger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:22
verses.text: I ask all men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:23
verses.text: True are these things? True.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:24
verses.text: Just are these things? Just.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:25
verses.text: But hear ye the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:26
verses.text: "If truly therefore justice ye speak, judge right things, ye sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:27
verses.text: Be it not a justice of lips, but also of deeds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:28
verses.text: For if thou actest otherwise than thou speakest, good things thou speakest, and ill thou judgest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:29
verses.text: But now to the present case let us come, if ye please.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:30
verses.text: For the voice is that sweet voice, so well known to the ears of the Church, the voice of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the voice of His Body, the voice of the Church toiling, sojourning upon earth, living amid the perils of men speaking evil and of men flattering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:31
verses.text: Thou wilt not fear a threatener, if thou lovest not a flatterer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:32
verses.text: He therefore, of whom this is the voice, hath observed and hath seen, that all men speak justice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:33
verses.text: For what man doth dare not to speak it, lest he be called unjust? When, therefore, as though he were hearing the voices of all men, and were observing the lips of all men, he cried out to them, "If truly indeed justice ye speak,"—if not falsely justice ye speak, if not one thing on lips doth sound, whilst another thing is concealed in hearts,—"judge right things, ye sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:34
verses.text: Hear out of the Gospel His own voice, the very same as is in this Psalm: "Hypocrites," saith the Lord to the Pharisees, "how are ye able good things to speak, when ye are evil men?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:35
verses.text: Either make the tree good, and the fruit thereof good: or make the tree evil, and the fruit thereof evil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:36
verses.text: Why wilt thou whiten thee, wall of mud? I know thy inward parts, I am not deceived by thy covering: I know what thou holdest forth, I know what thou coverest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:37
verses.text: "For there was no need for Him, that any one to Him should bear testimony of man: for He knew Himself what was in man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:38
verses.text: For He knew what was in man, who had made man, and who had been made Man, in order that He might seek man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:39
verses.text: But now ye do what? Why these things to you do I speak? "Because in heart iniquities ye work on earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:40
verses.text: Iniquities perchance in heart alone? Hear what followeth: both their heart hands do follow, and their heart hands do serve, the thing is thought of, and it is done; or else it is not done, not because we would not, but because we could not, Whatever thou willest and canst not, for done God doth count it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:41
verses.text: "For in heart Iniquities ye work on earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:42
verses.text: What next? "Iniquities your hands knit together".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:43
verses.text: What is, "knit together"? From sin, sin, and to sin, sin, because of sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:44
verses.text: What is this? A theft a man hath committed, a sin it is: he hath been seen, he seeketh to slay him by whom he hath been seen: there hath been knit together sin with sin: God hath permitted him in His hidden judgment to slay that man whom he hath willed to slay: he perceiveth that the thing is known, he seeketh to slay a second also; he hath knit together a third sin: while these things he is planning, perchance that he may not be found out, or that he may not be convicted of having done it, he consulteth an astrologer; there is added a fourth sin: the astrologer answereth perchance with some hard and evil responses, he runneth to a soothsayer, that expiation may be made; the soothsayer maketh answer that he is not able to expiate: a magician is sought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:45
verses.text: And who could enumerate those sins which are knit together with sins? "Iniquities your hands do knit together".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:46
verses.text: So long as thou knittest together, thou bindest sin upon sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:47
verses.text: Loose thyself from sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:48
verses.text: But I am not able, thou sayest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:49
verses.text: Cry to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:50
verses.text: "Unhappy man I, who shall deliver me from the body of this death?" For there shall come the Grace of God, so that righteousness shall be thy delight, as much as thou didst delight in iniquity; and thou, a man that out of bonds hast been loosed, shall cry out to God, "Thou hast broken asunder my bonds".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:51
verses.text: "Thou hast broken asunder my bonds," is what else but, "Thou hast remitted my sins"? Hear why chains they are: the Scripture maketh answer, "with the chains of his sins each one is bound fast".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:52
verses.text: Not only bonds, but chains also they are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:53
verses.text: Chains are those which are made by twisting in: that is, because with sins sins thou wast knitting together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:54
verses.text: "Alienated are sinners from the womb, they have gone astray from the belly, they have spoken false things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:55
verses.text: And when iniquity they speak, false things they speak; because deceitful is iniquity: and when justice they speak, false things they speak; because one thing with mouth they profess, another thing in heart they conceal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:56
verses.text: "Alienated are sinners from the womb".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:57
verses.text: What is this? Let us search more diligently: for perhaps he is saying this, because God hath foreknown men that are to be sinners even in the wombs of their mothers For whence when Rebecca was yet pregnant, and in womb was bearing twins, was it said, "Jacob I have loved, but Esau I have hated"? For it was said, "The elder shall serve the younger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:58
verses.text: Hidden at that time was the judgment of God: but yet from the womb, that is, from the very origin, alienated are sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:59
verses.text: Whence alienated? From truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:60
verses.text: Whence alienated? From the blessed country, from the blessed life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:61
verses.text: Perchance alienated they are from the very womb.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:62
verses.text: And what sinners have been alienated from the womb? For what men would have been born, if therein they had not been held? Or what men to-day would be alive to hear these words to no purpose, unless they were born? Perchance therefore sinners have been alienated from a certain womb, wherein that charity was suffering pains, which speaketh through the Apostle, "Of whom again I am in labour, until Christ be formed in you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:63
verses.text: Expect thou therefore; be formed: do not to thyself ascribe a judgment which perchance thou knowest not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:64
verses.text: Carnal thou art as yet, conceived thou hast been: from that very time when thou hast received the name of Christ, by a sort of sacrament thou hast been born in the bowels of a mother.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:65
verses.text: For not only out of bowels a man is born, but also in bowels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:66
verses.text: First he is born in bowels, in order that he may be able to be born of bowels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:67
verses.text: Wherefore it hath been said even to Mary, "For that which is born in thee, is of the Holy Spirit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:68
verses.text: Not yet of Her It had been born, but already in Her It had been born.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:69
verses.text: Therefore there are born within the bowels of the Church certain little ones, and a good thing it is that being formed they should go forth, so that they drop not by miscarriage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:70
verses.text: Let the mother bear thee, not miscarry.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:71
verses.text: If patient thou shalt have been, even until thou be formed, even until in thee there be the sure doctrine of truth, the maternal bowels ought to keep thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:72
verses.text: But if by thy impatience thou shalt have shaken the sides of thy mother, with pain indeed she expelleth thee out, but more to thy loss than to hers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:73
verses.text: For this reason therefore have they gone astray from the belly, because "they have spoken false things"? Or rather have they not for this reason spoken false things, because they have gone astray from the belly? For in the belly of the Church truth abideth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:74
verses.text: Whosoever from this belly of the Church separated shall have been, must needs speak false things: must needs, I say, speak false things; whoso either conceived would not be, or whom when conceived the mother hath expelled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:75
verses.text: Thence heretics exclaim against the Gospel (to speak in preference of those whom expelled we lament).

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:76
verses.text: We repeat to them: behold Christ hath said, "It behoved Christ to suffer, and from the dead to rise again the third day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:77
verses.text: I acknowledge there our Head, I acknowledge there our bridegroom: acknowledge thou also with me the Bride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:78
verses.text: "Indignation to them after the similitude of a serpent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:79
verses.text: A great thing ye are to hear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:80
verses.text: "Indignation to them after the similitude of a serpent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:81
verses.text: As if we had said, What is that which thou hast said? there followeth, "As if of a deaf asp".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:82
verses.text: Whence deaf? "And closing its ears".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:83
verses.text: Therefore deaf, because it closeth its ears.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:84
verses.text: "And closing its ears".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:85
verses.text: "Which will not hearken to the voice of men charming, and of the medicine medicated by the wise man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:86
verses.text: As we have heard, because even men speak who have learned it with such research as they were able, but nevertheless it is a thing which the Spirit of God knoweth much better than any men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:87
verses.text: For it is not to no purpose that of this he hath spoken, but because it may chance that true is even that which we have heard of the asp.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:88
verses.text: When the asp beginneth to be affected by the Marsian charmer, who calleth it forth with certain peculiar incantations, hear what it doeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:89
verses.text: Give heed what is spoken to thee for a simile's sake, what is noted thee for avoidance So therefore here also there hath been given a certain simile derived from the Marsian, who maketh incantation to bring forth the asp from the dark cavern; surely into light he would bring it: but it loving its darkness, wherein coiled up it hideth itself, when it will not choose to come forth, nevertheless refusing to hear those words whereby it feeleth itself to be constrained, is said to press one ear against the ground, and with its tail to stop up the other, and therefore as much as possible escaping those words, it cometh not forth to the charmer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:90
verses.text: To this as being like, the Spirit of God hath spoken of certain persons hearing not the Word of God, and not only not doing, but altogether, that they may not do it, refusing to hear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:91
verses.text: This thing hath been done even in the first times of the faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:92
verses.text: Stephen the Martyr was preaching the Truth, and to minds as though dark, in order to bring them forth into light, was making incantation: when he came to make mention of Christ, whom they would not hear at all, of them the Scripture saith what? of them relateth what? "They shut," he saith, "their ears".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:93
verses.text: But what they did afterwards, the narrative of the passion of Stephen doth publish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:94
verses.text: They were not deaf, but they made themselves deaf.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:95
verses.text: For this thing they did at the point where Christ was named.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:96
verses.text: The indignation of these men was as the indignation of a serpent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:97
verses.text: Why your ears do ye shut? Wait, hear, and if ye shall be able, rage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:98
verses.text: Because they chose not to do aught but rage, they would not hear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:99
verses.text: But if they had heard, perchance they would have ceased to rage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:100
verses.text: The indignation of them was as the indignation of a serpent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:101
verses.text: "God hath broken utterly the teeth of them in their own mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:102
verses.text: Of whom? Of them to whom indignation is as the similitude of a serpent, and of an asp closing up its ears, so that it heareth not the voice of men charming, and of medicine medicated by the wise man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:103
verses.text: The Lord hath done to them what? "Hath broken utterly the teeth of them in their own mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:104
verses.text: It hath been done, this at first hath been done, and now is being done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:105
verses.text: But it would have sufficed, my brethren, that it should have been said, "God hath broken utterly the teeth of them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:106
verses.text: The Pharisees would not hear the Law, would not hear the precepts of truth from Christ, being like to that serpent and asp.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:107
verses.text: For in their past sins they took delight, and present life they would not lose, that is, joys earthly for joys heavenly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:108
verses.text: What is, "in their own mouth"? In such sort, that with their own mouth against themselves they should make declaration: He hath compelled them with their mouth against themselves to give sentence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:109
verses.text: They would have slandered Him, because of the tribute: He said not, "It is lawful to pay tribute," or, "It is not lawful to pay tribute".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:110
verses.text: And He willed to break utterly their teeth, wherewith they were gaping in order to bite; but in their own mouth He would do it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:111
verses.text: If He said, Let there be paid to Caesar tribute, they would have slandered Him, because He had spoken evil to the nation of the Jews, by making it a tributary.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:112
verses.text: For because of sin they were paying tribute, having been humbled, as to them in the Law had been foretold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:113
verses.text: We have Him, say they, a maligner of our nation, if He shall have bidden us to pay tribute: but if He say, Do not pay, we have Him for saying that we should not be under allegiance to Caesar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:114
verses.text: Such a double noose as it were to catch the Lord they laid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:115
verses.text: But to whom had they come? To Him that knew how to break utterly the teeth of them in their own mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:116
verses.text: "Show to Me the coin," He saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:117
verses.text: Why tempt ye Me, ye hypocrites?" Of paying tribute do ye think? To do justice are ye willing? the counsel of justice do ye seek? "If truly justice ye speak, judge right things, ye sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:118
verses.text: But now because in one way ye speak, in another way judge, hypocrites ye are: "Why tempt ye Me, ye hypocrites?" Now I will break utterly your teeth in your mouth: "show to Me the coin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:119
verses.text: And they showed it to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:120
verses.text: And He saith not, it is Caesar's: but asketh Whose it is? in order that their teeth in their own mouth might be utterly broken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:121
verses.text: For on His inquiring, of whom it had the image and inscription, they said, of Caesar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:122
verses.text: Even now the Lord shall break utterly the teeth of them in their own mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:123
verses.text: Now ye have made answer, now have been broken utterly your teeth in your mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:124
verses.text: "Render unto Caesar the things which are of Caesar, and unto God the things which are of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:125
verses.text: Caesar seeketh his image; render it: God seeketh His image; render it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:126
verses.text: Let not Caesar lose from you his coin: let not God lose in you His coin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:127
verses.text: And they found not what they might answer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:128
verses.text: For they had been sent to slander Him: and they went back, saying, that no one to Him could make answer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:129
verses.text: Wherefore? Because broken utterly had been the teeth of them in their own mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:130
verses.text: Of that sort is also the following: "In what power doest Thou these things? I also will ask of you one question, answer me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:131
verses.text: And He asked them of John, whence was the Baptism of John, from heaven, or of men? so that whatever they might answer might tell against themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:132
verses.text: The Lord displeased that Pharisee, who to dinner had bidden Him, because a woman that was a sinner drew near to His feet, and he murmured against Him, saying, "If this man were a prophet, He would know what woman drew near to His feet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:133
verses.text: O thou that art no prophet, whence knowest thou that He knew not what woman drew near to His feet? Because indeed He kept not the purifying of the Jews, which outwardly was as it were kept in the flesh, and was afar from the heart, this thing he suspected of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:134
verses.text: And in order that I may not speak at length on this point, even in his mouth He willed to break utterly the teeth of him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:135
verses.text: For He set forth to him: "A certain usurer had two debtors, one was owing five hundred pence, the other fifty: both had not wherewithal to pay, he forgave both.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:136
verses.text: Which loved him the more?" To this end the one asketh, that the other may answer: to this end he answereth that the teeth of him in his mouth may be broken utterly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:137
verses.text: "The jaw-bones of lions the Lord hath broken utterly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:138
verses.text: Not only of asps.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:139
verses.text: What of asps? Asps treacherously desire to throw in their venom, and scatter it, and hiss.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:140
verses.text: Most openly raged the nations, and roared like lions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:141
verses.text: "Wherefore have raged the nations, and the peoples meditated empty things?" When they were lying in wait for the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:142
verses.text: Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or is it not lawful? Asps they were, serpents they were, broken utterly were the teeth of them in their own mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:143
verses.text: Afterwards they cried out, "Crucify, Crucify".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:144
verses.text: Now is there no tongue of asp, but roar of lion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:145
verses.text: But also "the jaw-bones of lions the Lord hath broken utterly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:146
verses.text: Perchance here there is no need of that which he hath not added, namely, "in the mouth of them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:147
verses.text: For men lying in wait with captious questions, were forced to be conquered with their own answer: but those men that openly were raging, were they by any means to be confuted with questions? Nevertheless, even their jaw-bones were broken utterly: having been crucified, He rose again, ascended into heaven, was glorified as the Christ, is adored by all nations, adored by all kings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:148
verses.text: Let the Jews now rage, if they are able.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:149
verses.text: We have also in the case of heretics this as a warning and precedent, because themselves also we find to be serpents with indignation made deaf, not choosing to hear the "medicine medicated by the wise man:" and in their own mouth the Lord hath broken utterly the teeth of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:150
verses.text: "They shall be despised like water running down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:151
verses.text: Be not terrified, brethren, by certain streams, which are called torrents: with winter waters they are filled up; do not fear: after a little it passeth by, that water runneth down; for a time it roareth, soon it will subside: they cannot hold long.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:152
verses.text: Many heresies now are utterly dead: they have run in their channels as much as they were able, have run down, dried are the channels, scarce of them the memory is found, or that they have been.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:153
verses.text: "They shall be despised like water running down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:154
verses.text: But not they alone; the whole of this age for a time is roaring, and is seeking whom it may drag along.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:155
verses.text: Let all ungodly men, all proud men resounding against the rocks of their pride as it were with waters rushing along and flowing together, not terrify you, winter waters they are, they cannot alway flow: it must needs be that they run down unto their place, unto their end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:156
verses.text: And nevertheless of this torrent of the world the Lord hath drunk.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:157
verses.text: For He hath suffered here, the very torrent He hath drunk, but in the way He hath drunk, but in the passage over: because in way of sinners He hath not stood But of Him saith the Scripture what? "Of the torrent in the way He shall drink, therefore He shall lift up His Head;" that is, for this reason glorified He hath been, because He hath died; for this reason hath risen again, because He hath suffered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:158
verses.text: "Like wax melted they shall be taken away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:159
verses.text: For thou wast about to say, all men are not so made weak, like myself, in order that they may believe: many men do persevere in their evil, and in their malice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:160
verses.text: And of the same fear thou nothing: "Like wax melted they shall be taken away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:161
verses.text: Against thee they shall not stand, they shall not continue: with a sort of fire of their  own lusts they shall perish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:162
verses.text: For there is here a kind of hidden punishment, of it the Psalm is about to speak now, to the end of it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:163
verses.text: There are but a few verses; be attentive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:164
verses.text: There is a certain punishment future, fire of hell, fire everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:165
verses.text: For future punishment hath two kinds: either of the lower places it is, where was burning that rich man, who was wishing for himself a drop of water to be dropped on his tongue off the finger of the poor man, whom before his gate he had spurned, when he saith, "For I am tormented in this flame".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:166
verses.text: And the second is that at the end, whereof they are to hear, that on the left hand are to be set: "Go ye into fire everlasting, that hath been prepared for the devil and his angels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:167
verses.text: Those punishments shall be manifest at that time, when we shall have departed out of this life, or when at the end of the world men shall have come to the resurrection of the dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:168
verses.text: Now therefore is there no punishment, and doth God suffer sins utterly unpunished even unto that day? There is even here a sort of hidden punishment, of the same he is treating now.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:169
verses.text: We see nevertheless sometimes with these punishments just men to be afflicted, and to these punishments unjust men to be strangers: for which reason did totter the feet of him that afterwards rejoicing saith, "How good is the God of Israel to men right in heart! But my own feet have been almost shaken, because I have been jealous in the case of sinners, beholding the peace of sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:170
verses.text: For he had seen the felicity of evil men, and well-pleased he had been to be an evil man, seeing evil men to reign, seeing that it was well with them, that they abounded in plenty of all things temporal, such as he too, being as yet but a babe, was desiring from the Lord: and his feet did totter, even until he saw what at the end is either to be hoped for or to be feared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:171
verses.text: For he saith in the same Psalm, "This thing is a labour before me, until I enter into the sanctuary of God, and understand unto the last things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:172
