verses.text: It is not therefore the punishments of the lower places, not the punishments of that fire everlasting after the resurrection, not those punishments which as yet in this world are common to just men and unjust men, and ofttimes more heavy are those of just men than those of unjust men; but some punishment or other of the present life the Spirit of God would recommend to our notice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:173
verses.text: Give heed, hear ye me about to speak of that which ye know: but a more sweet thing it is when it is declared in a Psalm, which, before it was declared, was deemed obscure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:174
verses.text: For behold I bring forth that which already ye knew: but because these things are brought forth from a place where ye have never yet seen them, it cometh to pass that even known things, as if they were new things, do delight you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:175
verses.text: Hear ye the punishment of ungodly men: "Like wax," he saith, "melted they shall be taken away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:176
verses.text: I have said that through their lusts this thing to them is done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:177
verses.text: Evil lust is like a burning and a fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:178
verses.text: Doth fire consume a garment, and doth not the lust of adultery consume the soul? Of meditated adultery when the Scripture was speaking it saith, "Shall one bind fire in his bosom, and his garments shall he not burn up?" Thou bearest in thy bosom live coals; burned through is thy vest; thou bearest in thought adultery, and whole then is thy soul? But these punishments few men do see: therefore them the Spirit of God doth exceedingly recommend to our notice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:179
verses.text: Hear the Apostle saying, "God hath given them up unto the lusts of their heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:180
verses.text: Behold, the fire from the face of which like wax they are melting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:181
verses.text: For they loose themselves from a certain continence of chastity; therefore even these same men, going unto their lusts, as loose and melting are spoken of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:182
verses.text: Whence melting? whence loose? From the fire of lusts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:183
verses.text: "God hath given them up unto the lusts of their heart, so that they do those things which beseem not, being filled full of all iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:184
verses.text: "There hath fallen upon them fire, and they have not seen the sun".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:185
verses.text: Ye see in what manner he speaketh of a certain punishment of darkening.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:186
verses.text: "Fire hath fallen upon them," fire of pride, a smoky fire, fire of lust, fire of wrath.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:187
verses.text: How great a fire is it? He upon whom it shall have fallen, shall not see the sun.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:188
verses.text: Therefore hath it been said, "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:189
verses.text: Therefore, brethren, fire of evil lust fear ye, if ye will not melt like wax, and to perish from the face of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:190
verses.text: For there falleth upon you that fire, and the sun ye shall not see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:191
verses.text: What sun? Not that which together with thee see both beasts and insects, and good men and evil men: because "He maketh His sun to rise upon good men and evil men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:192
verses.text: But there is another sun, whereof those men are to speak, "And the sun hath not risen to us, passed away are all those things as it were a shadow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:193
verses.text: Therefore we have strayed from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness hath not shone to us, and the sun hath not risen to us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:194
verses.text: "Before that the bramble bringeth forth your thorns: as though living, as though in anger, it shall drink them up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:195
verses.text: What is the bramble? Of prickly plants it is a kind, upon which there are said to be certain of the closest thorns.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:196
verses.text: At first it is a herb; and while it is a herb, soft and fair it is: but thereon there are nevertheless thorns to come forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:197
verses.text: Now therefore sins are pleasant, and as it were they do not prick.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:198
verses.text: A herb is the bramble; even now nevertheless there is a thorn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:199
verses.text: "Before that the bramble bringeth forth thorns:" is before that of miserable delights and pleasures the evident tortures come forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:200
verses.text: Let them question themselves that love any object, and to it cannot attain; let them see if they are not racked with longing: and when they have attained to that which unlawfully they long for, let them mark if they are not racked with fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:201
verses.text: Let them see therefore here their punishments; before that there cometh that resurrection, when in flesh rising again they shall not be changed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:202
verses.text: "For all we shall rise again, but not all we shall be changed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:203
verses.text: For they shall have the corruption of the flesh wherein to be pained, not that wherein to die: otherwise even those pains would be ended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:204
verses.text: Then the thorns of that bramble, that is, all pains and piercings of tortures shall be brought forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:205
verses.text: Such thorns as they shall suffer that are to say, "These are they whom sometimes we had in derision:" thorns of the piercing of repentance, but of one too late and without fruit like the barrenness of thorns.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:206
verses.text: The repentance of this time is pain healing: repentance of that time is pain penal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:207
verses.text: Wouldest thou not suffer those thorns? here be thou pierced with the thorns of repentance; in such sort that thou do that which hath been spoken of, "Turned I have been in sorrow, when the thorn was piercing: my sin I have known, and mine iniquity I have not covered: I have said, I will declare against me my shortcoming to the Lord, and Thou hast remitted the ungodliness of my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:208
verses.text: Now do so, now be pierced through, be there not in thee done that which hath been said of certain execrable men, "They have been cloven asunder, and have not been pierced through".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:209
verses.text: Observe them that have been cloven asunder and have not been pierced through Ye see men cloven asunder, and ye see them not pierced through.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:210
verses.text: Behold beside the Church they are, and it doth not repent them, so as they should return whence they have been cloven asunder.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:211
verses.text: The bramble hereafter shall bring forth their thorns.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:212
verses.text: They will not now have a healing piercing through, they shall have hereafter one penal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:213
verses.text: But even now before that the bramble produceth thorns, there hath fallen upon them fire, that suffereth them not to see the sun, that is, the wrath of God is drinking up them while still living: fire of evil lusts, of empty honours, of pride, of their covetousness: and whatsoever is weighing them down, that they should not know the truth, so that they seem not to be conquered, so that they be not brought into subjection even by truth herself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:214
verses.text: For what is a more glorious thing, brethren, than to be brought in subjection and to be overcome by truth? Let truth overcome thee willing: for even unwilling she shall of herself overcome thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:215
verses.text: As yet the punishments of the lower places have not come, as yet fire everlasting hath not come: let him that is growing in God compare himself now with an ungodly man, a blind heart with an enlightened heart: compare ye two men, one seeing and one not seeing in the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:216
verses.text: And what so great thing is vision of the flesh? Did Tobias by any means have fleshly eyes? His own son had, and he had not; and the way of life a blind man to one seeing did show.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:217
verses.text: Therefore when ye see that punishment, rejoice, because in it ye are not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:218
verses.text: Therefore saith the Scripture, "The just man shall rejoice when he shall have seen vengeance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:219
verses.text: Not that future punishment; for see what followeth: "his hands he shall wash in the blood of the sinner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:220
verses.text: What is this? Let your love attend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:221
verses.text: When man-slayers are smitten, ought anywise innocent men to go thither and wash their hands? But what is, "in the blood of the sinner he shall wash his hands"? When a just man seeth the punishment of a sinner, he groweth himself; and the death of one is the life of another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:222
verses.text: For if spiritually blood runneth from those that within are dead, do thou, seeing such vengeance, wash therein thy hands; for the future more cleanly live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:223
verses.text: And how shall he wash his hands, if a just man he is? For what hath he on his hands to be washed, if just he is? "But the just man of faith shall live".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:224
verses.text: Just men therefore he hath called believers: and from the time that thou hast believed, at once thou beginnest to be called just.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:225
verses.text: For there hath been made a remission of sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:226
verses.text: Even if out of that remaining part of thy life some sins are thine, which cannot but flow in, like water from the sea into the hold; nevertheless, because thou hast believed, when thou shalt have seen him that altogether is turned away from God to be slain in that blindness, there falling upon him that fire so that he see not the sun—then do thou that now through faith seest Christ, in order that thou mayest see in substance (because the just man liveth of faith), observe the ungodly man dying, and purge thyself from sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:227
verses.text: So thou shalt wash in a manner thy hands in the blood of the sinner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:228
verses.text: "And a man shall say, If therefore there is fruit to a just man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:229
verses.text: Behold, before that there cometh that which is promised, before that there is given life everlasting, before that ungodly men are cast forth into fire everlasting, here in this life there is fruit to the just man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:230
verses.text: What fruit? "In hope rejoicing, in tribulation enduring".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:231
verses.text: What fruit to the just man? "We glory in tribulations, knowing that tribulation worketh patience, but patience probation, but probation hope: but hope confoundeth not: because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, that hath been given to us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:232
verses.text: Doth he rejoice that is a drunkard; and doth he not rejoice that is just? In love there is fruit to a just man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:233
verses.text: Miserable the one, even when he maketh himself drunken: blessed the other, even when he hungereth and thirsteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:234
verses.text: The one wine-bibbing doth gorge, the other hope doth feed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:235
verses.text: Let him see therefore the punishment of the other, his own rejoicing, and let him think of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:236
verses.text: He that hath given even now such joy of faith, of hope, of charity, of the truth of His Scriptures, what manner of joy is He making ready against the end? In the way thus He feedeth, in his home how shall He fill him? "And a man shall say, If therefore there is fruit to the just man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:237
verses.text: Let them that see believe, and see, and perceive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:238
verses.text: Rejoice shall the just man when he shall have seen vengeance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:239
verses.text: But if he hath not eyes whence he may see vengeance, he will be made sad, and will not be amended by it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:240
verses.text: But if he seeth it, he seeth what difference there is between the darkened eye of the heart, and the eye enlightened of the heart: between the coolness of chastity and the flame of lust, between the security of hope and the fear there is in crime.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:241
verses.text: When he shall have seen this, let him separate himself, and wash his hands in the blood of the same.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:242
verses.text: Let him profit by the comparison, and say, "Therefore there is fruit to the just man: therefore there is a God judging them in the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:243
verses.text: Not yet in that life, not yet in fire eternal, not yet in the lower places, but here in earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:244
verses.text: If somewhat too prolix we have been, pardon us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:245
verses.text: We exhort you in the name of Christ, to meditate profitably on those things which ye have heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:246
verses.text: Because even to preach the truth is nought, if heart from tongue dissenteth; and to hear the truth nothing profiteth, if a man upon the rock build not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:247
verses.text: He that buildeth upon a Rock, is the same that heareth and doeth: but he that heareth and doeth not, buildeth upon sand: he that neither heareth nor doeth, buildeth nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 59:248
verses.text: Contents   Part  Part.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:1
verses.text: Psalm LIX  The First Part.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:2
verses.text: As the S cripture is wont to set mysteries of the Psalms on the titles, and to deck the brow of a Psalm with the high announcement of a Mystery, in order that we that are about to go in may know (when as it were upon the door-post we have read what within is  doing) either of whom the house is, or who is the owner of that estate: so also in this Psalm there hath been written a title, of a title.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:3
verses.text: For it hath, "At the end, corrupt not for David himself unto the inscription of the title".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:4
verses.text: This is that which I have spoken of, title of Title.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:5
verses.text: For what the inscription of this title is, which to be corrupted he forbiddeth, the Gospel to us doth indicate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:6
verses.text: For when the Lord was being crucified, a title by Pilate was inscribed and set, "King of the Jews," in three tongues, Hebrew, Greek, and Latin: which tongues in the whole world mostly do prevail.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:7
verses.text: Therefore "corrupt not" is most proper and prophetic; since indeed even those Jews made suggestion at that time to Pilate, and said, "Do not write King of the Jews, but write, that Himself said that He was King of the Jews:" for this title, say they, hath established Him King over us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:8
verses.text: And Pilate, "What I have written, I have written".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:9
verses.text: And there was fulfilled, "corrupt not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:10
verses.text: Nor is this the only Psalm which hath an inscription of such sort, that the Title be not corrupted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:11
verses.text: Several Psalms thus are marked on the face, but however in all the Passion of the Lord is foretold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:12
verses.text: Therefore here also let us perceive the Lord's Passion, and let there speak to us Christ, Head and Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:13
verses.text: So always, or nearly always, let us hear the words of Christ from the Psalm, as that we look not only upon that Head, the one mediator between God and man, the Man Christ JesusBut let us think of Christ, Head and whole Body, a sort of entire Man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:14
verses.text: For to us is said, "But ye are the Body of Christ and members," by the Apostle Paul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:15
verses.text: If therefore He is Head, we Body; whole Christ is Head and Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:16
verses.text: For sometimes thou findest words which do not suit the Head, and unless thou shalt have attached them to the Body, thy understanding will waver: again thou findest words which are proper for the Body, and Christ nevertheless is speaking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:17
verses.text: In that place we must have no fear lest a man be mistaken: for quickly he proceedeth to adapt to the Head, that which he seeth is not proper for the Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:18
verses.text: Let us hear, therefore, what followeth: "When Saul sent and guarded his house in order that he might kill him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:19
verses.text: This though not to the Cross of the Lord, yet to the Passion of the Lord doth belong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:20
verses.text: For Crucified was Christ, and dead, and buried.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:21
verses.text: That sepulchre was therefore as it were the house: to guard which the government of the Jews sent, when guards were set to the sepulchre of Christ There is indeed a story in the Scripture of the Reigns, of the occasion when Saul sent to guard the house in order that he might kill DavidBut in like manner as Saul effected not his purpose of slaying David: so this could not the government of the Jews effect, that the testimony of guards sleeping should avail more than that of Apostles watching.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:22
verses.text: For what were the guards instructed to say? We give to you, they say, as much money as ye please; and say ye, that while ye were sleeping there came His disciples, and took Him away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:23
verses.text: Behold what sort of witnesses of falsehood against truth and the Resurrection of Christ, His enemies, through Saul figured, did produce.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:24
verses.text: Enquire, O unbelief, of sleeping witnesses, let them reply to thee of what was done in the tomb.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:25
verses.text: Who, if they were sleeping, whence knew it? If watching, wherefore detained they not the thieves? Let him say therefore what followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:26
verses.text: "Deliver me from mine enemies, my God, and from men rising up upon me, redeem Thou me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:27
verses.text: There hath been done this thing in the flesh of Christ, it is being done in us also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:28
verses.text: For our enemies, to wit the devil and his angels, cease not to rise up upon us every day, and to wish to make sport of our weakness and our frailness, by deceptions, by suggestions, by temptations, and by snares of whatsoever sort to entangle us, while on earth we are still living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:29
verses.text: But let our voice watch unto God, and cry out in the members of Christ, under the Head that is in heaven, "Deliver me from mine enemies, my God, and from men rising up upon me, redeem Thou me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:30
verses.text: "Deliver me from men working iniquity, and from men of bloods, save Thou me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:31
verses.text: They indeed were men of bloods, who slew the Just One, in whom no guilt they found: they were men of bloods, because when the foreigner washed his hands, and would have let go Christ, they cried, "Crucify, Crucify:" they were men of bloods, on whom when there was being charged the crime of the blood of Christ, they made answer, giving it to their posterity to drink, "His blood be upon us and upon our sons".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:32
verses.text: But neither against His Body did men of bloods cease to rise up; for even after the Resurrection and Ascension of Christ, the Church suffered persecutions, and she indeed first that grew out of the Jewish people, of which also our Apostles were.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:33
verses.text: There at first Stephen was stoned, and received that of which he had his name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:34
verses.text: For Stephanus doth signify a crown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:35
verses.text: Lowly stoned but highly crowned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:36
verses.text: Secondly, among the Gentiles rose up kingdoms of Gentiles, before that in them was fulfilled that which had been foretold, "There shall adore Him all the kings of the earth, all nations shall serve Him:" and there roared the fierceness of that kingdom against the witnesses of Christ: there was shed largely and frequently the blood of Martyrs: wherewith when it had been shed, being as it were sown, the field of the Church more productively put forth, and filled the whole world as we now behold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:37
verses.text: From these therefore, men of bloods, is delivered Christ, not only Head, but also Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:38
verses.text: From men of bloods is delivered Christ, both from them that have been, and from them that are, and from them that are to be; there is delivered Christ, both He that hath gone before, and He that is, and He that is to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:39
verses.text: For Christ is the whole Body of Christ; and whatsoever good Christians that now are, and that have been before us, and that after us are to be, are an whole Christ, who is delivered from men of bloods; nor is this voice void, "And from men of bloods save Thou me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:40
verses.text: "For behold they have hunted my soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:41
verses.text: There have rushed upon me strong men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:42
verses.text: We must not however pass on from these strong men: diligently we must trace who are the strong men rising up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:43
verses.text: Strong men, upon whom but upon weak men, upon powerless men, upon men not strong? And praised nevertheless are the weak men, and condemned are the strong men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:44
verses.text: If it would be perceived who are strong men, at first the devil himself the Lord hath called a strong man: "No one," He saith, "is able to go into the house of a strong man, and to carry off his vessels, unless first he shall have bound the strong man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:45
verses.text: He hath bound therefore the strong man with the chains of His dominion: and his vessels He hath carried off, and His own vessels hath made them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:46
verses.text: For all unrighteous men were vessels of the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:47
verses.text: But there are among mankind certain strong men of a blameable and damnable strength, that are confident indeed, but on temporal felicity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:48
verses.text: That man doth not seem to you to have been strong, of whom now from the Gospel hath been read: how his estate brought forth abundance of fruits, and he being troubled, hit upon the design of rebuilding, so that, having pulled down his old barns, he should construct new ones more capacious, and, these having been finished, should say to his soul, "Thou hast many good things, soul, feast, be merry, be filled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:49
verses.text: There are also other men strong, not because of riches, not because of the powers of the body, not because of any temporally pre-eminent power of station, but relying on their righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:50
verses.text: This sort of strong men must be guarded against, feared, repulsed, not imitated: of men relying, I say, not on body, not on means, not on descent, not on honour; for all such things who would not see to be temporal, fleeting, falling, flying? but relying on their own righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:51
verses.text: "Wherefore," say they, doth your Master eat with publicans and sinners? O ye strong men, to whom a Physician is not needful! This strength to soundness belongeth not, but to insanity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:52
verses.text: For even than men frenzied nothing can be stronger, more mighty they are than whole men: but by how much greater their powers are, by so much nearer is their death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:53
verses.text: May God therefore turn away from our imitation these strong men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:54
verses.text: The same are therefore the strong men, that assailed Christ, commending their own justice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:55
verses.text: Hear ye these strong men: when certain men of Jerusalem were speaking, having been sent by them to take Christ, and not daring to take Him (because when he would, then was He taken, that truly was strong): Why therefore, say they, "could ye not take Him?" And they made answer, "No one of men did ever so speak as He".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:56
verses.text: And these strong men, "Hath by any means any one of the Pharisees believed on Him, or any one of the Scribes, but this people knowing not the Law?" They preferred themselves to the sick multitude, that was running to the Physician: whence but because they were themselves strong? and what is worse, by their strength, all the multitude also they brought over unto themselves, and slew the Physician of all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:57
verses.text: What next? "Neither iniquity is mine, nor sin mine, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:58
verses.text: There have rushed on indeed strong men on their own righteousness relying, they have rushed on, but sin in me they have not found.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:59
verses.text: For truly those strong men, that is, as it were righteous men, on what account would they be able to persecute Christ, unless it were as if a sinner? But, however, let them look to it how strong they be, in the raging of fever not in the vigour of soundness: let them look to it how strong they be, and how as though just against an unrighteous man they have raged But, however, "neither iniquity is mine, nor sin mine, O Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:60
verses.text: Without iniquity I did run, and I was guided".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:61
verses.text: Those strong men therefore could not follow me running: therefore a sinner they have deemed me, because my steps they have not seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:62
verses.text: "Without iniquity I did run, and was guided; rise up to meet me, and see".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:63
verses.text: To God is said this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:64
verses.text: But why? If He meet not, is He unable to see? It is just as if thou wast walking in a road, and from afar by some one thou couldest not be recognised, thou wouldest call to him and wouldest say, Meet me, and see how I am walking; for when from afar thou espiest me, my steps thou art not able to see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:65
verses.text: So also unless God were to meet, would He not see how without iniquity he was guided, and how without sin he was running? This interpretation indeed we can also accept, namely, "Rise up to meet me," as if "help me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:66
verses.text: But that which he hath added, "and see," must be understood as, make it to be seen that I run, make it to be seen that I am guided: according to that figure wherein this also hath been said to Abraham, "Now I know that thou fearest God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:67
verses.text: God saith, "Now I know:" whence, but because I have made thee to know? For unknown to himself every one is before the questioning of temptation: just as of himself Peter in his confidence was ignorant, and by denying learned what kind of powers he had, in his very stumbling he perceived that it was falsely he had been confident: he wept, and in weeping he earned profitably to know what he was, and to be what he was not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:68
verses.text: Therefore Abraham when tried, became known to himself: and it was said by God, "Now I know," that is, now I have made thee to know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:69
verses.text: In like manner as glad is the day because it maketh men glad; and sad is bitterness because it maketh sad one tasting thereof: so God's seeing is making to see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:70
verses.text: "Rise up, therefore," he saith, "to meet me, and see".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:71
verses.text: What is, "and see"? And help me, that is, in those men, in order that they may see my course, may follow me; let not that seem to them to be crooked which is straight, let not that seem to them to be curved which keepeth the rule of truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:72
verses.text: Something else I am admonished to say in this place of the loftiness of our Head Himself: for He was made weak even unto death, and He took on Him the weakness of flesh, in order that the chickens of Jerusalem He might gather under His wings, like a hen showing herself weak with her little ones For have we not observed this thing in some bird at some time or other, even in those which build nests before our eyes, as the house-sparrows, as swallows, so to speak, our annual guests, as storks, as various sorts of birds, which before our eyes build nests, and hatch eggs, feed chickens, as the very doves which daily we see; and some bird to become weak with her chickens, have we not known, have we not looked upon, have we not seen? In what way doth a hen experience this weakness? Surely a known fact I am speaking of, which in our sight is daily taking place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:73
verses.text: How her voice groweth hoarse, how her whole body is made languid? The wings droop, the feathers are loosened, and thou seest around the chickens some sick thing, and this is maternal love which is found as weakness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:74
verses.text: Why was it therefore, but for this reason, that the Lord willed to be as a Hen, saying in the Holy Scripture, "Jerusalem, Jerusalem, how often have I willed to gather thy sons, even as a hen her chickens under her wings, and thou hast not been willing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:75
verses.text: But He hath gathered all nations, like as a hen her chickens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:76
verses.text: "And Thou, Lord God of virtues, God of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:77
verses.text: Thou God of Israel, that art thought to be but God of one nation, which worshippeth Thee, when all nations worship idols, Thou God of Israel, "Give heed unto the visiting all nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:78
verses.text: Fulfilled be that prophecy wherein Isaiah in Thy person speaketh to Thy Church, Thy holy City, that barren one of whom many more are the sons of Her forsaken than of her that hath a husband.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:79
verses.text: To Her indeed hath been said, "Rejoice, thou barren, that bearest not," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:80
verses.text: , more than of the Jewish nation which hath a Husband, which hath received the Law, more than of that nation which had a visible king.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:81
verses.text: For thy king is hidden, and more sons to thee there are by a hidden Bridegroom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:82
verses.text: The Prophet addeth, "Enlarge the place of Thy tabernacle, and Thy courts fix thou: there is no cause for thee to spare, extend further thy cords, and strong stakes set thou again and again on the right and on the left".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:83
verses.text: Upon the right keep good men, on the left keep evil men, until there come the fan: occupy nevertheless all nations; bidden to the marriage be good men and evil men, filled be the marriage with guests; it is the office of servants to bid, of the Lord to sever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:84
verses.text: "Cities which had been forsaken Thou shall inhabit:" forsaken of God, forsaken of Prophets, forsaken of Apostles, forsaken of the Gospel, full of demons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:85
verses.text: For Thou shalt prevail; and blush not because abominable Thou hast been.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:86
verses.text: Therefore though there have risen up upon thee strong men, blush not: when against the name of Christ laws were enacted, when ignominy and infamy it was to be a Christian.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:87
verses.text: "Blush not because abominable Thou hast been: for confusion for everlasting Thou shalt forget, of the ignominy of Thy widowhood Thou shall not be mindful".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:88
verses.text: "Have not pity upon all men that work iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:89
verses.text: Here evidently He is terrifying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:90
verses.text: Whom would He not terrify? What man falling back upon his own conscience would not tremble? Which even if to itself it is conscious of godliness, strange if it be not in some sort conscious of iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:91
verses.text: For whosoever doeth sin, also doeth iniquity "For if Thou shalt have marked iniquities, O Lord, what man shall abide it?" And nevertheless a true saying it is, and not said to no purpose, and neither is nor will it be possible to be void, "Have not pity upon all men that work iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:92
verses.text: But He had pity even upon Paul, who at first as Saul wrought iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:93
verses.text: For what good thing did he, whence he might deserve of God? Did he not hate His Saints unto death? did he not bear letters from the chief of the priests, to the end that wheresoever he might find Christians, to punishment he should hurry them? When bent upon this, when thither proceeding, breathing and panting slaughter, as the Scripture testified of him, was he not from Heaven with a mighty voice summoned, thrown down, raised up; blinded, lightened; slain, made alive; destroyed, restored? In return for what merit? Let us say nothing; himself rather let us hear: "I that before have been," he saith, "a blasphemer, and persecutor; and injurious, but mercy I have obtained".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:94
verses.text: Surely "Thou wouldest not have pity upon all men that work iniquity:" this in two ways may be understood: either that in fact not any sins doth God leave unpunished; or that there is a sort of iniquity, on the workers whereof God hath indeed no pity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:95
verses.text: All iniquity, be it little or great, punished must needs be, either by man himself repenting, or by God avenging.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:96
verses.text: For even he that repenteth punisheth himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:97
verses.text: Therefore, brethren, let us punish our own sins, if we seek the mercy of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:98
verses.text: God cannot have mercy on all men working iniquity as if pandering to sins, or not rooting out sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:99
verses.text: In a word, either thou punishest, or He punisheth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:100
verses.text: But let us see now another way in which this sentence may be understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:101
verses.text: There is a certain iniquity, on the worker whereof it cannot be that God have mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:102
verses.text: Ye enquire, perchance, what that is? It is the defending of sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:103
verses.text: When a man defendeth his sins, great iniquity he worketh: that thing he is defending which God hateth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:104
verses.text: And see how perversely, how iniquitously.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:105
verses.text: Whatever of good he hath done, to himself he would have it to be ascribed; whatever of evil, to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:106
verses.text: For in this manner men defend sins in the person of God, which is a worse sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:107
verses.text: Therefore thou defendest thy sin in such sort, that thou layest blame on God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:108
verses.text: So the guilty is excused, so that the Judge may be charged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:109
verses.text: However on men working iniquity God hath no pity at all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:110
verses.text: "Let them be converted at the evening".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:111
verses.text: Of certain men he is speaking that were once workers of iniquity, and once darkness, being converted in the evening.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:112
verses.text: What is, "in the evening"? Afterward.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:113
verses.text: What is "at the evening"? Later.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:114
verses.text: For before, before that they crucified Christ, they ought to have acknowledged their Physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:115
verses.text: Wherefore, when He had been crucified—rising again, into Heaven ascending—after that He sent His Holy Spirit, wherewith were fulfilled they that were in one house, and they began to speak with the tongues of all nations, there feared the crucifiers of Christ; they were pricked through with their consciences, they besought counsel of safety from the Apostles, they heard, "Repent, and be baptized each one of you in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, and your sins shall be remitted unto you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:116
verses.text: After the slaying of Christ, after the shedding of the blood of Christ, remitted are your sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:117
verses.text: "Let these be converted," therefore, they also "at evening".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:118
verses.text: Let them yearn for the grace of God, perceive themselves to be sinners; let those strong men be made weak, those rich men be made poor, those just men acknowledge themselves sinners, those lions be made dogs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:119
verses.text: "Let them be converted at evening, and suffer hunger as dogs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:120
verses.text: And they shall go around the city".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:121
verses.text: What city? That world, which in certain places the Scripture calleth "the city of standing round:" that is, because in all nations everywhere the world had encompassed the one nation of Jews, where such words were being spoken, and it was called "the city of standing round".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:122
verses.text: Around this city shall go those men, now having become hungry dogs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:123
verses.text: In what manner shall they go around? By preaching.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:124
verses.text: Saul out of a wolf was made a dog at evening, that is, being late converted by the crumbs of his Lord, in His grace he ran, and went around the city.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:125
verses.text: "Behold, themselves shall speak in their mouth, and a sword is on the lips of them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:126
verses.text: Here is that sword twice whetted, whereof the Apostle saith, "And the sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:127
verses.text: Wherefore twice whetted? Wherefore, but because smiting out of both Testaments? With this sword were slain those whereof it was said to Peter, "Slay, and eat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:128
verses.text: "And a sword is on the lips of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:129
verses.text: For who hath heard?" They all speak in their mouth, "Who hath heard?" That is, they shall be wroth with men that are slow to believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:130
verses.text: They that a little before were even themselves unwilling to believe, do feel disgust from men not believing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:131
verses.text: And truly, brethren, so it is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:132
verses.text: Thou seest a man slow before he is made a Christian; thou criest to him daily, hardly he is converted: suppose him to be converted, and then he would have all men to be Christians, and wondereth that not yet they are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:133
verses.text: It hath chanced out to him at evening to have been converted: but because he hath been made hungering like a dog, he hath also on his lips a sword; he saith, "Who hath heard?" What is, "Who hath heard?" "Who hath believed our hearing, and to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?" "For who hath heard?" The Jews believe not: they have turned them to the nations, and have preached.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:134
verses.text: The Jews did not believe; and nevertheless through believing Jews the Gospel went around the city, and they said, "For who hath heard?" "And Thou, Lord, shall deride them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:135
verses.text: All nations are to be Christian, and ye say, "Who hath heard?" What is, "shall deride them"? "As nothing Thou shalt esteem all nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:136
verses.text: Nothing for Thee it shall be; because a most easy thing it will be for all nations to believe in Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:137
verses.text: "My strength to Thee I will keep".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:138
verses.text: For those strong men have fallen for this reason; because their strength to Thee they have not kept: that is, they that upon me have risen up and rushed, on themselves have relied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:139
verses.text: But I "my strength to Thee will keep:" because if I withdraw, I fall; if I draw near, stronger I am made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:140
verses.text: For see, brethren, what there is in a human soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:141
verses.text: It hath not of itself light, hath not of itself powers: but all that is fair in a soul, is virtue and wisdom: but it neither is wise for itself, nor strong for itself, nor itself is light to itself, nor itself is virtue to itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:142
verses.text: There is a certain origin and fountain of virtue, there is a certain root of wisdom, there is a certain, so to speak, if this also must be said, region of unchangeable truth: from this the soul withdrawing is made dark, drawing near is made light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:143
verses.text: "Draw near to Him, and be made light:" because by withdrawing ye are made dark.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:144
verses.text: Therefore, "my strength, I will keep to Thee:" not from Thee will I withdraw, not on myself will I rely.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:145
verses.text: "My strength, to Thee I will keep: because, O God, my lifter up Thou art".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:146
verses.text: For where was I, and where am I? Whence hast Thou taken me up? What iniquities of mine hast Thou remitted? Where was I lying? T o what have I been raised up? I ought to have remembered these things: because in another Psalm is said, "For my father and my mother have forsaken me, but the Lord hath taken me unto Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:147
verses.text: "My God, the mercy of Him shall come before me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:148
verses.text: Behold what is, "My strength, to Thee I will keep:" on myself I will in no ways at all rely.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:149
verses.text: For what good thing have I brought, that thou shouldest have mercy on me, and shouldest justify me? What in me hast Thou found, save sins alone? Of Thine there is nothing else but the nature which Thou hast created: the other things are mine own evil things which Thou hast blotted out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:150
verses.text: I have not first risen up to Thee, but to awake me Thou hast come: for "His mercy shall come before me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:151
verses.text: Before that anything of good I shall do, "His mercy shall come before me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:152
verses.text: What answer here shall the unhappy Pelagius make? "My God hath shown to me among mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:153
verses.text: How great mercy He hath put forth concerning me, among mine enemies He hath showed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:154
verses.text: Let one gathered compare himself with men forsaken, and one elect with men rejected: let the vessel of mercy compare itself with the vessels of wrath; and let it see how out of one lump God hath made one vessel unto honour, another unto dishonour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:155
verses.text: "For so God, willing to show wrath, and to manifest His power, hath brought in, in much patience, the vessels of wrath, which have been perfected unto perdition".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:156
verses.text: And wherefore this? "In order that He might make known His riches upon the vessels of mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:157
verses.text: If therefore vessels of wrath He hath brought in, wherein He might make known His riches upon the vessels of mercy, most rightly hath been said, "His mercy shall come before me: My God hath showed to me among mine enemies:" that is however great mercy He hath had concerning me, to me He hath showed it among these men concerning whom He hath not had mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:158
verses.text: For unless the debtor be in suspense, he is less grateful to him by whom the debt hath been forgiven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:159
verses.text: "My God hath showed to me among mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:160
verses.text: But of the enemies themselves what? "Slay them not, lest sometime they forget Thy law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:161
verses.text: He is making request for his enemies, he is fulfilling the commandment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:162
verses.text: Slay not them of whom the sins Thou slayest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:163
verses.text: But what is it to be slain? To forget the law of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:164
verses.text: It is real death, to go into the pit of sin; this indeed may be also understood of the Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:165
verses.text: Why of the Jews, "Slay not them, lest sometime they forget Thy law"? Those very enemies of mine, that have slain me, do not Thou slay.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:166
verses.text: Let the nation of the Jews remain: certes conquered it hath been by the Romans, certes effaced is the city of them, Jews are not admitted into their city, and yet Jews there are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:167
verses.text: For all those provinces by the Romans have been subjugated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:168
verses.text: Who now can distinguish the nations in the Roman empire the one from the other, inasmuch as all have become Romans and all are called Romans? The Jews nevertheless remain with a mark; nor in such sort conquered have they been, as that by the conquerors they have been swallowed up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:169
verses.text: Not without reason is there that Cain, on whom, when he had slain his brother, God set a mark in order that no one should slay him This is the mark which the Jews have: they hold fast by the remnant of their law, they are circumcised, they keep Sabbaths, they sacrifice the Passover; they eat unleavened bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:170
verses.text: These are therefore Jews, they have not been slain, they are necessary to believing nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:171
verses.text: Why so? In order that He may show to us among our enemies His mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:172
verses.text: "My God hath shown to me in mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:173
verses.text: He showeth His mercy to the wild-olive grafted on branches that have been cut off because of pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:174
verses.text: Behold where they lie, that were proud, behold where thou hast been grafted, that didst lie: and be not thou proud, lest thou shouldest deserve to be cut off.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:175
verses.text: "Scatter them abroad in Thy virtue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:176
verses.text: Now this thing hath been done: throughout all nations there have been scattered abroad the Jews, witnesses of their own iniquity and our truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:177
verses.text: They have themselves writings, out of which hath been prophesied Christ, and we hold Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:178
verses.text: And if sometime perchance any heathen man shall have doubted, when we have told him the prophecies of Christ, at the clearness whereof he is amazed, and wondering hath supposed that they were written by ourselves, then out of the copies of the Jews we prove, how this thing so long time before had been foretold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:179
verses.text: See after what sort by means of our enemies we confound other enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:180
verses.text: "Scatter them abroad in Thy virtue:" take away from them "virtue," take away from them their strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:181
verses.text: "And bring them down, my protector, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:182
verses.text: "The transgressions of their mouth, the discourse of their lips: and let them be taken in their pride: and out of cursing and lying shall be declared consummations, in the anger of consummation, and they shall not be".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:183
verses.text: Obscure words these are, and I fear lest they be not well instilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:184
verses.text: The Second Part.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:185
verses.text: For, behold, the Jews are enemies, whom this Psalm seemeth to imply; the law of God they hold, and therefore of them hath been said, "Slay not them, lest sometime they forget Thy law:" in order that the nation of Jews might remain, and by it remaining the number of Christians might increase.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:186
verses.text: Throughout all nations they remain certainly, and Jews they are, nor have they ceased to be what they were: that is, this nation hath not so yielded to Roman institutions, as to have lost the form of Jews; but hath been subjected to the Romans so as that it still retaineth its own laws; which are the laws of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:187
verses.text: But what in their case hath been done? "Ye tithe mint and cummin, and have forsaken the weightier matters of the law, mercy, and judgment, straining a gnat, but swallowing a camel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:188
verses.text: This to them the Lord saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:189
verses.text: And in truth so they are; they hold the law, hold the Prophets; read all things, sing all things: the light of the Prophets therein they see not, which is Christ Jesus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:190
verses.text: Not only Him now they see not, when he is sitting in Heaven: but not even at that time saw they Him, when among them humble He was walking, and they were made guilty by shedding the blood of the Same; but not all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:191
verses.text: This even to-day we commend to the notice of your Love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:192
verses.text: Not all: because many of them were turned to Him whom they slew, and by believing on Him, they obtained pardon even for the shedding of His blood: and they have given an example for men; how they ought not to despair that sin of whatsoever kind would be remitted to them, since even the killing of Christ was remitted to them confessing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:193
verses.text: What in them wilt Thou slay? The Crucify, Crucify, which they cried out, not them that cried out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:194
verses.text: For they willed to blot out, cut off, destroy Christ: but Thou, by raising to life Christ, whom they willed to destroy, dost slay the "transgressions of their mouth, the discourse of their lips".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:195
verses.text: For in that He whom they cried out should be destroyed, liveth, they are taken with dread: and that He whom on earth they despised, in heaven is adored by all nations, they wonder: thus are there slain the transgressions of them, and the discourse of their lips.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:196
verses.text: What is, "let them be taken in their pride"? Because to no purpose have strong men rushed on, and it hath fallen out to them as it were to think themselves to have done somewhat, and they have prevailed against the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:197
verses.text: They were able to crucify a man, weakness might prevail and virtue be slain; and they thought themselves somewhat, as it were strong men, as it were mighty men, as it were prevailing, as it were a lion prepared for prey, as it were fat bulls, as of them in another place he maketh mention: "Fat bulls have beset me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:198
verses.text: But what have they done in the case of Christ? Not life, but death they have slain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:199
verses.text: And what now hath come to pass in those men that have been converted? For it was told to them that He whom they slew rose again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:200
verses.text: They believed Him to have risen again, because they saw that He, being in Heaven, thence sent the Holy Spirit, and filled those that on Him believed; and they found themselves to have condemned nought, and to have done nought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:201
verses.text: Their doing issued in emptiness, the sin remained.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:202
verses.text: Because therefore the doing was made void, but the sin remained upon the doers; they were taken in their pride, they saw themselves under their iniquity It remained therefore for them to confess the sin, and for Him to pardon, that had given Himself up to sinners, and to forgive His death, having been slain by men dead, and making alive men dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:203
verses.text: They were taken therefore in their pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:204
verses.text: "And out of cursing and lying shall be declared consummations, in anger of consummation, and they shall not be".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:205
verses.text: This too with difficulty is understood, to what is joined the "and they shall not be".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:206
verses.text: What shall they not be? Let us therefore examine the context above: when they shall have been taken in their pride, "there shall be declared out of cursing and lying consummations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:207
verses.text: What are consummations? Perfections: for to be consummated, is to be perfected.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:208
verses.text: One thing it is to be consummated, another thing to be consumed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:209
verses.text: For a thing is consummated which is so finished as that it is perfected: a thing is consumed which is so finished that it is not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:210
verses.text: Pride would not suffer a man to be perfected, nothing so much hindereth perfection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:211
verses.text: For let your Love attend a little to what I am saying; and see an evil very pernicious, very much to be guarded against.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:212
verses.text: What sort of evil do ye think it is? How long could I enlarge upon how much evil there is in pride? The devil on that account alone is to be punished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:213
verses.text: Certes he is the chief of all sinners: certes he is the tempter to sin: to him is not ascribed adultery, not wine-bibbing, not fornication, not the robbing of others' goods: by pride alone he fell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:214
verses.text: And since pride's companion is envy, it must needs be that a proud man should envy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:215
verses.text: In a word, all vices in evil-doings are to be feared, pride in well-doings is more to be feared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:216
verses.text: It is no wonder, then, that so humble is the Apostle, as to say, "When I am made weak, then I am strong".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:217
verses.text: For lest he should himself be tempted by this sin, what sort of medicine doth he say was applied to him against swelling by the Physician, who knew what He was healing? "Lest by the greatness," he saith, "of the revelations I should be exalted, there was given to me a thorn of my flesh, the angel of Satan, to buffet me: wherefore thrice the Lord I besought, that it should depart from me: and He said to me, My grace is sufficient for thee, for virtue in weakness is made perfect".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:218
verses.text: See what the consummations are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:219
verses.text: An Apostle, the teacher of Gentiles, father of the faithful through the Gospel, received a thorn of the flesh whereby he might be buffeted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:220
verses.text: Which of us would dare to say this, unless he had not been ashamed to confess this? For if we shall have said that Paul had not suffered this; while to him as it were honour we give, a liar we make him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:221
verses.text: But because truthful he is, and truth he hath spoken; it behoveth us to believe that there was given to him an angel of Satan, lest by the greatness of the revelations he should be exalted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:222
verses.text: Behold how much to be feared is the serpent of pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:223
verses.text: What is, "in the anger of consummation shall be declared consummations"? There is an anger of consummation, and there is an anger of consuming.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:224
verses.text: For every vengeance of God is called anger: sometimes God avengeth, to the end that He may make perfect; sometimes He avengeth, to the end that He may condemn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:225
verses.text: How doth He avenge, to the end that He may make perfect? "He scourgeth every son whom He receiveth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:226
verses.text: How doth He avenge, to the end that He may condemn? When He shall have set ungodly men on the left hand, and shall have said to them, "Go ye into fire everlasting, that hath been prepared for the devil and his angels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:227
verses.text: This is the anger of consuming, not that of consummation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:228
verses.text: But "there shall be declared consummations in the anger of consummation;" it shall be preached by the Apostles, that "where sin hath abounded, grace shall much more abound," and the weakness of man hath belonged to the healing of humility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:229
verses.text: Those men thinking of this, and finding out and confessing their iniquities, "shall not be".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:230
verses.text: "Shall not be" what? In their pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:231
verses.text: "And they shall know how God shall have dominion of Jacob, and of the ends of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:232
verses.text: For before they thought themselves just men, because the Jewish nation had received the Law, because it had kept the commandments of God: it is proved to them that it hath not kept them, since in the very commandments of God Christ it perceived not, because "blindness in part has happened to Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:233
verses.text: Even the Jews themselves see that they ought not to despise the Gentiles, of whom they deemed as of dogs and sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:234
verses.text: For just as alike they have been found in iniquity, so alike they will attain unto salvation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:235
verses.text: "Not only to Jews," saith the Apostle, "but also even to Gentiles".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:236
verses.text: For to this end the Stone which the builders set at nought, hath even been made for the Head of the corner, in order that two in itself It might join: for a corner doth unite two walls.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:237
verses.text: The Jews thought themselves exalted and great: of the Gentiles they thought as weak, as sinners, as the servants of demons, as the worshippers of idols, and yet in both was there iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:238
verses.text: Even the Jews have been proved sinners; because "there is none that doeth good, there is not even so much as one:" they have laid down their pride, and have not envied the salvation of the Gentiles, because they have known their own and their weakness to be alike: and in the Corner Stone being united, they have together worshipped the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:239
verses.text: "They shall be converted at evening" : that is, even if late, that is, after the slaying of our Lord Jesus Christ: "They shall be converted at evening: and hereafter they shall suffer hunger as dogs".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:240
verses.text: But "as dogs," not as sheep or calves: "as dogs," as Gentiles, as sinners; because they too have known their sin that thought themselves righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:241
verses.text: It is a good thing therefore for a sinner to be humbled; and no one is more incurable than he that thinketh himself whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:242
verses.text: "And they shall go around the city".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:243
verses.text: Already we have explained "city;" it is the "city of standing round;" all nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:244
verses.text: "They shall be scattered abroad in order that they may eat" ; that is, in order that they may gain others, in order that into their Body they may change believers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:245
verses.text: "But if they shall not be filled, they shall murmur".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:246
verses.text: Because above also he had spoken of the murmur of them, saying, "For who hath heard?" "And Thou, O Lord," he saith, "shall deride them, sayi ng, Who hath heard?" Wherefore? Because, as nothing Thou shall count all nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:247
verses.text: Let the Psalm be concluded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:248
verses.text: See ye the Corner exulting, now with both walls rejoicing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:249
verses.text: The Jews were proud, humbled they have been; Gentiles were despairing, raised up they have been: let them come to the Corner, there let them meet, there run together, there find the kiss of peace; from different parts let them come, but with differing not come, those of Circumcision, these of uncircumcision.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:250
verses.text: Far apart were the walls, but before that to the Corner they came: but in the Corner let them hold themselves, and now let the whole Church from both walls, say what? "But I will sing of Thy power, and I will exult in the morning of Thy mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:251
verses.text: In the morning when temptations have been overcome, in the morning when the night of this world shall have passed away; in the morning when no longer the lyings in wait of robbers and of the devil and of his angels we dread, in the morning when no longer by the lamp of prophecy we walk, but Himself the Word of God as it were a Sun we c ontemplate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:252
verses.text: "And I will exult in the morning of Thy mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:253
verses.text: With reason in another Psalm is said, "In the morning I will stand by Thee, and I will meditate".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:254
verses.text: With reason also of the Lord Himself the Resurrection was at dawn, that there should be fulfilled that which hath been said in another Psalm, "In the evening shall tarry weeping and in the morning exultation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:255
verses.text: For at even the disciples mourned our Lord Jesus Christ as dead, at dawn at Him rising again they exulted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:256
verses.text: "For Thou hast become my taker up, and my refuge in the day of my tribulation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:257
verses.text: "My Helper, to Thee I will play, because Thou, O God, art my taker up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:258
verses.text: What was I, unless Thou didst succour? How much despaired of was I, unless Thou didst heal? Where was I lying, unless Thou didst come to me? Certes with a huge wound I was endangered, but that wound of mine did call for an Almighty Physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:259
verses.text: To an Almighty Physician nothing is incurable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:260
verses.text: Lastly, thinking of all good things whatsoever we may have, either in nature or in purpose, or in conversion itself, in faith, in hope, in charity, in good morals, in justice, in fear of God; all these to be only by His gifts, he hath thus concluded: "My God is my mercy:" He being filled with the good things of God hath not found what he might call his God, save "his mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 60:261
verses.text: O name, under which no one must despair! If thou say, my salvation, I perceive that He giveth salvation; if thou say, my refuge, I perceive that thou takest refuge in Him; if thou say, my strength, I perceive that He giveth to thee strength: "my mercy," is what? All that I am is of Thy mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:1
verses.text: Psalm LX.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:2
verses.text: David the king was one man, but not one man he figured; sometimes to wit he figured the Church of many men consisting, extended even unto the ends of the earth: but sometimes One Man h e figured, Him he figured that is Mediator of God and men, the Man Christ Jesus In this Psalm therefore, or rather in this Psalm's title, certain victorious actions of David are spoken of:"To the end, in behalf of those men that shall be changed unto the title's inscription, unto teaching for David himself, when he burned up Mesopotamia in Syria, and Syria Sobal, and turned Joab, and smote Edom, in the valley of salt-pits twelve thousand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:3
verses.text: We read of these things in the books of the Reigns, that all those persons whom he hath named, were defeated by David, that is, Mesopotamia in Syria, and Syria Sobal, Joab, Edom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:4
verses.text: These things were done, and just as they were done, so there they have been written, so they are read: let him read that will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:5
verses.text: Nevertheless, as the Prophetic Spirit in the Psalms' titles is wont to depart somewhat from the expression of things done, and to say something which in history is not found, and hence rather to admonish us that titles of this kind have been written not that we may know things done, but that things future may be prefigured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:6
verses.text: But here this thing is inserted for this especial reason, that there it is not written that he burned up Mesopotamia in Syria, and Syria Sobal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:7
verses.text: But now let us begin to examine these things after the significations of things future, and to bring out the dimness of shadows into the light of the word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:8
verses.text: What is "to the end" ye know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:9
verses.text: For "the end of the law is Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:10
verses.text: Those that are changed ye know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:11
verses.text: For who but they that do pass from old life into new?"For ye were sometime darkness, but now light in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:12
verses.text: But they are changed "into the title's inscription,"who into the kingdom of Christ do pass over from the kingdom of the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:13
verses.text: It is well that they are changed unto this title's inscription.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:14
verses.text: But they are changed, as followeth, "unto teaching".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:15
verses.text: He added, "for David himself unto teaching:" that is, are changed not for themselves, but for David himself, and are changed unto teaching.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:16
verses.text: When therefore would Christ have changed us, unless He had done that which He spake of, "Fire I have come to send into the world"? If therefore Christ came to send into the world fire, to wit to its health and profit, we must inquire not how He is to send the world into fire, but how into the world fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:17
verses.text: Inasmuch as therefore He came to send fire into the world, let us inquire what is Mesopotamia which was burned up, what is Syria Sobal? The interpretations therefore of the names let us examine according to the Hebrew language, wherein first this Scripture was written.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:18
verses.text: Mesopotamia  they say is interpreted, "exalted calling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:19
verses.text: Now the whole world by calling hath been exalted, Syria is interpreted "lofty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:20
verses.text: But she which was lofty, burned up hath been and humbled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:21
verses.text: Sobal is interpreted "empty antiquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:22
verses.text: Thanks to Christ that hath burned her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:23
verses.text: Whenever old bushes are burned up, green places succeed; and more speedily and more plentifully, and more fully green, fresh ones spring out, when fire hath gone before them to the burning up of the old.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:24
verses.text: Let not therefore the fire of Christ be feared, hay it consumeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:25
verses.text: "For all flesh is hay, and all the glory of man as flower of hay".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:26
verses.text: He burneth up therefore those things with that fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:27
verses.text: "And turned Joab".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:28
verses.text: Joab is interpreted enemy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:29
verses.text: There was turned an enemy, as thou wilt understand it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:30
verses.text: If turned unto flight, the devil it is: if converted to the faith, a Christian it is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:31
verses.text: How unto flight? From the heart of a Christian: "The Prince of this world," He saith, "now hath been cast out".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:32
verses.text: But how can a Christian turned to the Lord be an enemy turned? Because he hath become a believer that had been an enemy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:33
verses.text: "Smote Edom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:34
verses.text: Edom is interpreted "earthly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:35
verses.text: That earthly one ought to be smitten.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:36
verses.text: For why should one live earthly, that ought to live heavenly? There hath been slain therefore life earthly, let there live life heavenly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:37
verses.text: "For as we have borne the image of the earthly, let us bear also the image of Him that is from Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:38
verses.text: See it slain: "Mortify your members which are upon earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:39
verses.text: But when he had smitten Edom, he smote "twelve thousand in the valley of salt-pits".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:40
verses.text: Twelve thousand is a perfect number, to which perfect number also the number of the twelve Apostles is ascribed: for not to no purpose is it, but because through the whole world was to be sent the Word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:41
verses.text: But the Word of God, which is Christ, is in clouds, that is, in the preachers of truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:42
verses.text: But the world of four parts doth consist.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:43
verses.text: The four parts thereof are exceeding well known to all, and often in the Scriptures they are mentioned: they are the same as the name of the four winds, East, West, North, and South.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:44
verses.text: To all these four parts was sent the Word, so that in the Trinity all might be called.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:45
verses.text: The number twelve four times three do make.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:46
verses.text: With reason therefore twelve thousand  earthly things were smitten, the whole world was smitten: for from the whole world was chosen out the Church, mortified from earthly life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:47
verses.text: Why "in the valley of salt-pits"? A valley is humility: salt-pits signify savour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:48
verses.text: For many men are humbled, but emptily and foolishly, in empty oldness they are humbled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:49
verses.text: One suffereth tribulation for money, suffereth tribulation for temporal honour, suffereth tribulation for the comforts of this life; he is to suffer tribulation and to be humbled: why not for the sake of God? why not for the sake of Christ? why not for the savour of salt? Knowest thou not that to thee hath been said, "Ye are the salt of earth," and, "If the salt shall have been spoiled, for no other thing will it be of use, but to be cast out"? A good thing it is therefore wisely to be humbled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:50
verses.text: Behold now are not heretics being humbled? Have not laws been made even by men to condemn them, against whom divine laws do reign, which even before had condemned them? Behold they are humbled, behold they are put to flight, behold persecution they suffer, but without savour; for folly, for emptiness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:51
verses.text: For now the salt hath been spoiled: therefore it hath been cast out, to be trodden down of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:52
verses.text: We have heard the title of the Psalm, let us hear also the words of the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:53
verses.text: "God, Thou hast driven us back, and hast destroyed us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:54
verses.text: Is that David speaking that smote, that burned up, that defeated, and not they to whom He did these things, that is to say, their being smitten and driven back, that were evil men, and again their being made alive and returning in order that they might be good men? That destruction indeed that David made, strong of hand, our Christ, whose figure that man was bearing; He did those things, He made this destruction with His sword and with His fire: for both He brought into this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:55
verses.text: Both "Fire I am come to send into the world," thou hast in the Gospel: and "A sword I have come to send into the earth," thou hast in the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:56
verses.text: He brought in fire, whereby might be burned up Mesopotamia in Syria, and Syria Sobal: He brought in a sword whereby might be smitten Edom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:57
verses.text: Now again this destruction was made for the sake of "those that are changed unto the title's inscription".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:58
verses.text: Hear we therefore the voice of them: to their health smitten they were, being raised up let them speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:59
verses.text: Let them say, therefore, that are changed into something better, changed unto the title's inscription, changed unto teaching for David himself; let them say, "Thou hast had mercy upon us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:60
verses.text: Thou hast destroyed us, in order that Thou mightest build us; Thou hast destroyed us that were ill builded, hast destroyed empty oldness; in order that there may be a building unto a new man, building to abide for everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:61
verses.text: "Thou hast moved the earth, and hast troubled it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:62
verses.text: How hath the earth been troubled? In the conscience of sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:63
verses.text: Whither go we? Whither flee we, when this sword hath been brandished, "Repent, for near hath drawn the kingdom of Heaven"? "Heal the crushings thereof, for moved it hath been".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:64
verses.text: Unworthy it is to be healed, if moved it hath not been: but thou speakest, preachest, threatenest us with God, of coming judgment holdest not thy peace, of the commandment of God thou warnest, from these things thou abstainest not; and he that heareth, if he feareth not, if he is not moved, is not worthy to be healed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:65
verses.text: Another heareth, is moved, is stung, smiteth the breast, sheddeth tears.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:66
verses.text: The first labour is, that thou shouldest be displeasing to thyself, that sins thou shouldest battle out, that thou shouldest be changed into something better: the second labour, in return for thy having been changed, is to bear the tribulations and temptations of this world, and amid them to hold on even unto the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:67
verses.text: Of these things therefore when he was speaking, while pointing out such things, he addeth what? "Thou hast shown to Thy people hard things" : to Thy people now, made tributary after the victory of David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:68
