verses.text: "Thou hast shown to Thy people hard things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:69
verses.text: Wherein? In persecutions which the Church of Christ hath endured, when so much blood of martyrs was spilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:70
verses.text: "Thou hast given us to drink of the wine of goading".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:71
verses.text: "Of goading" is what? Not of killing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:72
verses.text: For it was not a killing that destroyeth, but a medicine that smarteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:73
verses.text: "Thou hast given us to drink of the wine of goading".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:74
verses.text: Wherefore this? "Thou hast given to men fearing Thee, a sign that they should flee from the face of the bow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:75
verses.text: Through tribulations temporal, he saith, Thou hast signified to Thine own to flee from the wrath of fire everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:76
verses.text: For, saith the Apostle Peter, "Time it is that Judgment begin with the House of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:77
verses.text: And exhorting the Martyrs to endurance, when the world should rage, when slaughters should be made at the hands of persecutors, when far and wide blood of believers should be spilled, when in chains, in prisons, in tortures, many hard things Christians should suffer, in these hard things, I say, lest they should faint, Peter saith to them, "Time it is that Judgment begin with the House of God," etc What therefore is to be in the Judgment? The bow is bended, still in menacing posture it is, not yet in aiming.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:78
verses.text: And see what there is in the bow: is there not an arrow to be shot forward? The string however is stretched back in a contrary direction to that in which it is going to be shot; and the more the stretching thereof hath gone backward, with the greater swiftness it starteth forward.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:79
verses.text: What is it that I have said? The more the Judgment is deferred, with so much the greater swiftness it is to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:80
verses.text: Therefore even for temporal tribulations to God let us render thanks, because He hath given to His people a sign, "that they should flee from the face of the bow:" in order that His faithful ones having been exercised in tribulations temporal, may be worthy to avoid the condemnation of fire everlasting, which is to find out all them that do not believe these things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:81
verses.text: "That Thy beloved may be delivered: save me with Thy right hand, and hearken unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:82
verses.text: With Thy right hand save me, Lord: so save me as that at the right hand I may stand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:83
verses.text: Not any safety temporal I require, in this matter Thy Will be done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:84
verses.text: For a time what is good for us we are utterly ignorant: for "what we should pray for as we ought we know not:" but "save me with Thy right hand," so that even if in this time I suffer sundry tribulations, when the night of all tribulations hath been spent, on the right hand I may be found among the sheep, not on the left hand among the goats "And hearken unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:85
verses.text: Because now I am deserving that which Thou art willing to give; not "with the words of my transgressions" I am crying through the day, so that Thou hearken not, and "in the night so that Thou hearken not," and that not for folly to me," but truly for my warning, by adding savour from the valley of salt-pits, so that in tribulation I may know what to ask: but I ask life everlasting; therefore hearken unto me, because Thy right hand I ask.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:86
verses.text: "God hath spoken in His Holy One".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:87
verses.text: In what Holy One of His? "God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:88
verses.text: In that Holy One, of whom elsewhere ye have heard, "O God, in the Holy One is Thy way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:89
verses.text: "I will rejoice and will divide Sichima.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:90
verses.text: and the valley of tabernacles I will measure out".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:91
verses.text: Sichima is interpreted shoulders.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:92
verses.text: But according to history, Jacob returning from Laban his father-in-law with all his kindred, hid the idols in Sichima which he had from Syria, where for a long time he had dwelled, and at length was coming from thence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:93
verses.text: But tabernacles he made there because of his sheep and herds, and called the place Tabernacles And these I will divide, saith the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:94
verses.text: What is this, "I will divide Sichima"? If to the story where the idols were hidden is the reference, the Gentiles it signifieth; I divide the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:95
verses.text: I divide, is what? "For not in all men is there faith".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:96
verses.text: I divide, is what? Some will believe, others will not believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:97
verses.text: The shoulders are divided, in order that their sins may burthen some men, while others may take up the burden of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:98
verses.text: For godly shoulders He was requiring when He said, "For My yoke is gentle, and My burden is light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:99
verses.text: Another burden oppresseth and loadeth thee, but Christ's burden relieveth thee: another burden hath weight, Christ's burden hath wings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:100
verses.text: For even if thou pull off the wings from a bird, thou dost remove a kind of weight; and the more weight thou hast taken away, the more on earth it will abide.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:101
verses.text: She that thou hast chosen to disburden lieth there: she flieth not, because thou hast taken off a weight: let there be given back the weight, and she flieth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:102
verses.text: Such is Christ's burden; let men carry it, and not be idle: let them not be heeded that will not bear it; let them bear it that will, and they shall find how light it is, how sweet, how pleasant, how ravishing unto Heaven, and from earth how transporting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:103
verses.text: Perchance because of the sheep of Jacob, "the valley of Tabernacles" is to be understood of the nation of the Jews, and the same is divided: for they have passed from thence that have believed, the rest have remained without.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:104
verses.text: "Mine is Galaad".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:105
verses.text: These names are read in the Scriptures of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:106
verses.text: Galaad hath the voice of an interpretation of its own and of a great Mystery: for it is interpreted "the heap of testimony".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:107
verses.text: How great a heap of testimony in the Martyrs? "Mine is Galaad," mine is a heap of testimony, mine are the true Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:108
verses.text: Then meanly esteemed was the Church among men, then reproach on Her a Widow was being thrown, because Christ's She was, because the sign of the Cross on her brow She was wearing: not yet was there honour, censure there was then: when therefore not honour, but censure there was, then was made a heap of witness; and through the heap of witness was the Love of Christ enlarged; and through the enlargement of the Love of Christ, were the Gentiles possessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:109
verses.text: There followeth, "And mine is Manasses;" which is interpreted forgotten.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:110
verses.text: For to Her had been said, "Confusion for everlasting Thou shalt forget, and of the reproach of Thy widowhood Thou shalt not be mindful".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:111
verses.text: There was therefore a confusion of the Church once, which now hath been forgotten: for of Her confusion and of the "reproach" of Her widowhood now She is not mindful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:112
verses.text: For when there was a sort of confusion among men, a heap of witness was made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:113
verses.text: Now no longer doth any even remember that confusion, when it was a reproach to be a Christian, now no one remembereth, now all have forgotten, now "Mine is Manasses, and Ephraim the strength of My head".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:114
verses.text: Ephraim is interpreted fruitfulness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:115
verses.text: Mine, he saith, is fruitfulness, and this fruitfulness is the strength of My Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:116
verses.text: For My Head is Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:117
verses.text: And whence is fruitfulness the strength of Him? Because unless a grain were to fall into the earth, it would not be multiplied, alone it would remain Fall then to earth did Christ in His Passion, and there followed fruit-bearing in the Resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:118
verses.text: He was hanging and was being despised: the grain was within, it had powers to draw after it all things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:119
verses.text: How in a grain do numbers of seeds lie hid, something abject it appeareth to the eyes, but a power turning into itself matter and bringing forth fruit is hidden; so in Christ's Cross virtue was hidden, there appeared weakness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:120
verses.text: O mighty grain! Doubtless weak is He that hangeth, Doubtless before Him that people did wag the head, Doubtless they said, "If Son of God He is, let Him come down from the Cross".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:121
verses.text: Hear the strength of Him: that which is a weak thing of God, is stronger than men With reason so great fruitfulness hath followed: it is mine, saith the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:122
verses.text: "Juda is my king: Moab the pot of my hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:123
verses.text: What Juda? He that is of the tribe of Juda.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:124
verses.text: What Juda, but He to whom Jacob himself said, "Juda, thy brethren shall praise thee"? What therefore should I fear, when Juda my king saith, "Fear not them that kill the body"? "Moab the pot of my hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:125
verses.text: Wherefore "pot"? Because tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:126
verses.text: Wherefore "of my hope"? Because there hath gone before Juda my king.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:127
verses.text: Moab is perceived in the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:128
verses.text: For that nation was born of sin, that nation was born of the daughters of Lot, who lay with their father drunken, abusing a father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:129
verses.text: Better were it to have remained barren, than thus to have become mothers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:130
verses.text: But this was a kind of figure of them that abuse the law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:131
verses.text: For do not heed that law in the Latin language is of the feminine gender: in Greek of the masculine gender it is: but whether it be of the feminine gender in speaking, or of the masculine, the expression maketh no difference to the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:132
verses.text: For law hath rather a masculine force, because it ruleth, is not ruled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:133
verses.text: But moreover, the Apostle Paul saith what? "Good is the law, if any one use it lawfully".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:134
verses.text: But those daughters of Lot unlawfully used their father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:135
verses.text: But in the same manner as good works begin to grow when a man useth well the law: so arise evil works, when a man ill useth the law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:136
verses.text: Furthermore, they ill using their father, that is, ill using the law, engendered the Moabites, by whom are signified evil works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:137
verses.text: Thence the tribulation of the Church, thence the pot boiling up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:138
verses.text: Of this pot in a certain place of prophecy is said, "A pot heated by the North wind".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:139
verses.text: Whence but by the quarters of the devil, who hath said, "I will set my seat at the North"? The chiefest tribulations therefore arise against the Church from none except from those that ill use the law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:140
verses.text: "Into Idumaea I will stretch out my shoe".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:141
verses.text: The Church speaketh, "I will come through even unto Idumaea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:142
verses.text: Let tribulations rage, let the world boil with offences, even unto those very persons that lead an earthly life (for Idumaea is interpreted earthly), even unto those same, "even unto Idumaea, I will stretch out my shoe".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:143
verses.text: Of what thing the shoe except of the Gospel? "How beautiful the feet of them that tell of peace, that tell of good things," and "the feet shod unto the preparation of the Gospel of peace".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:144
verses.text: In these times we see, brethren, how many earthly men do perpetrate frauds for the sake of gain, for frauds perjuries; on account of their fears they consult fortune-tellers, astrologers: all these men are Edomites, earthly; and nevertheless all these men adore Christ, under His own shoe they are; now even unto Idumaea is stretched out His shoe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:145
verses.text: "To Me Allophyli have been made subject".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:146
verses.text: Who are "Allophyli"? Men of other race, not belonging to My race.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:147
verses.text: They "have been made subject," because many men adore Christ, and are not to reign with Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:148
verses.text: "Who will lead Me down into the city of standing round?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:149
verses.text: What is the city of standing round? If ye remember already, I have made mention thereof in another Psalm, wherein hath been said, "And they shall go around the city".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:150
verses.text: For the city of standing round is the compassing around of the Gentiles, which compassing around of the Gentiles in the middle thereof had the one nation of the Jews, worshipping one God: the rest of the compassing around of the Gentiles to idols made supplication, demons they did serve.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:151
verses.text: And mystically it was called the city of standing round; because on all sides the Gentiles had poured themselves around, and had stood around that nation which did worship one God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:152
verses.text: "Who will lead me down even unto Idumaea?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:153
verses.text: "Wilt not Thou, O God, that hast driven us back? And wilt not Thou, O God, march forth in our powers?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:154
verses.text: Wilt not Thou lead us down, that hast driven us back? But wherefore "hast driven us back"? Because Thou hast destroyed us Wherefore hast destroyed us? Because angry Thou hast been, and hast had pity on us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:155
verses.text: Thou therefore wilt lead down, that hast driven back; Thou, O God, that wilt not march forth in our powers, wilt lead down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:156
verses.text: What is, "wilt not march forth in our powers"? The world is to rage, the world is to tread us down, there is to be a heap of witnesses, builded of the spilled blood of martyrs, and the raging heathen are to say, "Where is the God of them?"  Then "Thou wilt not march forth in our powers:" against them Thou wilt not show Thyself, Thou wilt not show Thy power, such as Thou hast shown in David, in Moses, in Joshua the son of Nun, when to their might the Gentiles yielded, and when the slaughter had been ended, and the great laying waste repaired, into the land which Thou promisedst Thou leddest in Thy people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:157
verses.text: This thing then Thou wilt not do, "Thou wilt not march forth in our powers," but within Thou wilt work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:158
verses.text: What is, "wilt not march forth"? Wilt not show Thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:159
verses.text: For indeed when in chains the Martyrs were being led along, when they were being shut up in prison, when they were being led forth to be mocked, when to the beasts they were exposed, when they were being smitten with the sword, when with fire they were being burned, were they not despised as though forsaken, as though without helper? In what manner was God working within? in what manner within was He comforting? in what manner to these men was He making sweet the hope of life everlasting? in what manner was He not forsaking the hearts of them, where the man was dwelling in silence, well if good, ill if evil? Was He then by any means forsaking, because He was not marching forth in the powers of them? By not marching forth in the powers of them, did He not the more lead down the Church even unto Idumaea, lead down the Church even unto the city of standing around? For if the Church chose to war and to use the sword, She would seem to be fighting for life present: but because she was despising life present, therefore there was made a heap of witness for the life that shall be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:160
verses.text: Thou therefore, O God, that wilt not march forth in our powers, "Give to us aid from tribulation, and vain is the safety of man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:161
verses.text: Go now they that salt have not, and desire safety temporal for their friends, which is empty oldness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:162
verses.text: "Give to us aid:" from thence whence Thou wast supposed to forsake, thence succour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:163
verses.text: "In God we will do valour, and Himself to nothing shall bring down our enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:164
verses.text: We will not do valour with the sword, not with horses, not with breastplates, not with shields, not in the mightiness of an army, not abroad.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:165
verses.text: But where? Within, where we are not seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:166
verses.text: Where within? "In God we will do virtue:" and as if abjects, and as if trodden down, men as if of no consideration we shall be, but "Himself to nothing shall bring down our enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:167
verses.text: In a word, this thing hath been done to our enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:168
verses.text: Trodden down have been the Martyrs: by suffering, by enduring, by persevering even unto the end, in God they have done valour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:169
verses.text: Himself also hath done that which followeth: to nothing He hath brought down the enemies of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 61:170
verses.text: Where are now the enemies of the Martyrs, except perchance that now drunken men with their cups do persecute those whom at that time frenzied men did use with stones to persecute?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:1
verses.text: Psalm LXI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:2
verses.text: The title of it doth not detain us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:3
verses.text: For it is "Unto the end, in hymns, to David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:4
verses.text: "In  hymns," to wit in praises.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:5
verses.text: "Unto the end," to wit unto Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:6
verses.text: But the voice in this Psalm (if we are among the members of Him, and in the Body, even as upon His exhortation we have the boldness to trust) we ought to acknowledge to be our own, not that of any foreigner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:7
verses.text: But I have not so called it our own, as if it were of those only that are now in presence; but our own, as being of us that are throughout the whole world, that are from the East even unto the West.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:8
verses.text: And in order that ye may know it thus to be our voice, He speaketh here as if one Man: but He is not One Man; but even as One, the Unity is speaking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:9
verses.text: But in Christ we all are one man: because of this One Man the Head is in Heaven, and the members are yet toiling on earth: and because they are toiling see what He saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:10
verses.text: "Hearken, O God, to my supplication, give heed to my prayer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:11
verses.text: Who saith? He, as if One.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:12
verses.text: See whether one: "From the ends of the earth to Thee I have cried, while my heart was being vexed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:13
verses.text: Now therefore not one: but for this reason one, because Christ is One, of whom all we are the members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:14
verses.text: For what one man crieth from the ends of the earth? There crieth not from the ends of the earth any but that inheritance, of which hath been said to the Son Himself, "Demand of Me, and I will give to Thee the nations for Thine inheritance, and for Thy possession the boundaries of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:15
verses.text: This therefore Christ's possession, this Christ's inheritance, this Christ's Body, this Christ's one Church, this the Unity which we are, is crying from the ends of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:16
verses.text: But wherefore have I cried this thing? "While my heart was being vexed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:17
verses.text: He showeth himself to be throughout all nations in the whole round world, in great glory, but in great tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:18
verses.text: For our life in this sojourning cannot be without temptation: because our advance is made through our temptation, nor does a man become known to himself unless tempted, nor can he be crowned except he shall have conquered, nor can he conquer except he shall have striven, nor can he strive except he shall have experienced an enemy, and temptations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:19
verses.text: This Man therefore is being vexed, that from the ends of the earth is crying, but nevertheless He is not forsaken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:20
verses.text: For ourselves who are His Body He hath willed to prefigure also in that His Body wherein already He hath both died and hath risen again, and into Heaven hath ascended, in order that whither the Head hath gone before, thither the members may be assured that they shall follow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:21
verses.text: Therefore us He did transfer by a figure into Himself, when He willed to be tempted of Satan.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:22
verses.text: But now there was read in the Gospel, how the Lord Jesus Christ in the wilderness was being tempted of the devil Christ entirely was tempted of the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:23
verses.text: For in Christ thou wast being tempted, because Christ of thee had for Himself flesh, of Himself for thee salvation; of thee for Himself death, of Himself for thee life; of thee for Himself revilings, of Himself for thee honours; therefore of thee for Himself temptation, of Himself for thee victory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:24
verses.text: If in Him tempted we have been, in Him we overcome the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:25
verses.text: "On the Rock Thou hast exalted me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:26
verses.text: Now therefore here we perceive who is crying from the ends of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:27
verses.text: Let us call to mind the Gospel: "Upon this Rock I will build My Church".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:28
verses.text: Therefore She crieth from the ends of the earth, whom He hath willed to be builded upon a Rock.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:29
verses.text: But in order that the Church might be builded upon the Rock, who was made the Rock? Hear Paul saying: "But the Rock was Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:30
verses.text: On Him therefore builded we have been.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:31
verses.text: For this reason that Rock whereon we have been builded, first hath been smitten with winds, flood, rain, when Christ of the devil was being tempted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:32
verses.text: Behold on what firmness He hath willed to stablish thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:33
verses.text: With reason our voice is not in vain, but is hearkened unto: for on great hope we have been set: "On the Rock Thou hast exalted me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:34
verses.text: "Thou hast led me down, because Thou hast been made my hope: a tower of strength from the face of the enemy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:35
verses.text: My heart is vexed, saith that Unity from the ends of the earth, and I toil amid temptations and offences: the heathen envy, because they have been conquered; the heretics lie in wait, hidden in the cloak of the Christian name: within in the Church itself the wheat suffereth violence from the chaff: amid all these things when my heart is vexed, I will cry from the ends of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:36
verses.text: But there forsaketh me not the Same that hath exalted me upon the Rock, in order to lead me down even unto Himself, because even if I labour, while the devil through so many places and times and occasions lieth in wait against me, He is to me a tower of strength, to whom when I shall have fled for refuge, not only I shall escape the weapons of the enemy, but even against him securely I shall myself hurl whatever darts I shall please.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:37
verses.text: For Christ Himself is the tower, Himself for us hath been made a tower from the face of the enemy, who is also the Rock whereon hath been builded the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:38
verses.text: Art thou taking heed that thou be not smitten of the devil? Flee to the Tower; never to that tower will the devil's darts follow thee: there thou wilt stand protected and fixed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:39
verses.text: But in what manner shalt thou flee to the Tower? Let not a man, set perchance in temptation, in body seek that Tower, and when he shall not have found it, be wearied, or faint in temptation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:40
verses.text: Before thee is the Tower: call to mind Christ, and go into the Tower.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:41
verses.text: "A sojourner I will be in Thy tabernacle even unto ages".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:42
verses.text: Ye see how he, of whom we have spoken, is he that crieth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:43
verses.text: Which of us is a sojourner even unto ages? For a few days here we live, and we pass away: for sojourners here we are, inhabitants in Heaven we shall be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:44
verses.text: Thou art a sojourner in that place where thou art to hear the voice of the Lord thy God, "Remove".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:45
verses.text: For from that Home everlasting in the Heavens no one will bid thee to remove.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:46
verses.text: Here therefore a sojourner thou art.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:47
verses.text: Whence also is said in another Psalm, "A sojourner I am with Thee and a stranger, as all my fathers were".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:48
verses.text: Here therefore sojourners we are; there the Lord shall give to us mansions everlasting: "Many are," He saith, "the mansions in My Father's house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:49
verses.text: Those mansions not as though to sojourners He will give, but as though to citizens to abide for everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:50
verses.text: Here however, brethren, because for no small time the Church was to be on this earth, but because here shall be the Church even unto the end of the world: therefore here He hath said, "A dweller I will be in Thy tabernacle even unto ages".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:51
verses.text: Well, of a few days thou wouldest choose that the temptations should be: but how would She gather together all Her sons, unless for a long time She were to be here, unless even unto the end She were to be prolonged? Do not envy the rest of mankind that hereafter shall be: do not, because thou hast already passed over, wish to cut down the bridge of mercy: be it here even for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:52
verses.text: And what of temptations, which needs must abound, by how much the more offences come? For Himself saith, "Because iniquity hath abounded, the love of many shall wax cold".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:53
verses.text: But that Church, which crieth from the ends of the earth, is in these circumstances whereof he speaketh in continuation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:54
verses.text: "But he that shall have persevered even unto the end, the same shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:55
verses.text: But whence shalt thou persevere?"I shall be covered up in the veiling of Thy wings".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:56
verses.text: Behold the reason why we are in safety amid so great temptations, until there come the end of the world, and ages everlasting receive us; namely, because we are covered up in the veiling of His Wings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:57
verses.text: There is heat in the world, but there is a great shade under the wings of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:58
verses.text: "For Thou, O God, hast hearkened to my prayer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:59
verses.text: What prayer? That wherewith he beginneth: "Hearken, O God, to my supplication".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:60
verses.text: "Thou hast given inheritance to men fearing Thy name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:61
verses.text: Let us continue therefore in the fear of God's name: the eternal Father deceiveth us not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:62
verses.text: Sons labour, that they may receive the inheritance of their parents, to whom when dead they are to succeed: are we not labouring to receive an inheritance from that Father, to whom not dying we succeed; but together with Him in the very inheritance for everlasting are to live?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:63
verses.text: "Days upon days of the King Thou shalt add to the years of Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:64
verses.text: This is therefore the King of whom we are the members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:65
verses.text: A King Christ is, our Head, our King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:66
verses.text: Thou hast given to Him days upon days; not only those days in that time that hath end, but days upon those days without end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:67
verses.text: "I will dwell," he saith, "in the house of the Lord, for length of days".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:68
verses.text: Wherefore for length of days, but because now is the shortness of days? For everything which hath an end, is short: but of this King are days upon days, so that not only while these days pass away, Christ reigneth in His Church, but the Saints shall reign together with Him in those days which have no end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:69
verses.text: For years of God have been also spoken of: "But Thou art the very Same, and Thy years shall not fail".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:70
verses.text: In the same manner as years, so days, so one day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:71
verses.text: Whatsoever thou wilt thou sayest of eternity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:72
verses.text: Whatever thou wilt thou sayest for this reason, because whatever thou shalt have said, it is too little that thou hast said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:73
verses.text: For thou must needs say somewhat, to the end that there may be something whereby thou mayest meditate on that which cannot be told.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:74
verses.text: "Even unto the day of generation and of generation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:75
verses.text: Of this generation and of the generation that shall be: of this generation which is compared to the moon, because as the moon is new, waxeth, is full, waneth, and vanisheth, so are these mortal generations; and of the generation wherein we are born anew by rising again, and shall abide for everlasting with God, when now no longer we are like the moon, but like that of which saith the Lord, "Then the righteous shall shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:76
verses.text: For the moon by a figure in the Scriptures is put for the mutability of this mortal state.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:77
verses.text: "He shall abide for everlasting in the sight of God" ; according to what, or because of what? "His mercy and truth who shall seek for Him?" He saith also in another place, "All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth, to men seeking His testament and His testimonies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:78
verses.text: Large is the discourse of truth and mercy, but shortness we have promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:79
verses.text: Briefly hear ye what is truth and mercy: because no small thing is that which hath been said, "All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:80
verses.text: Mercy is spoken of, because our merits God regarded not, but His own goodness, in order that He might forgive us all our sins, and might promise life everlasting: but truth is spoken of, because He faileth not to render those things which He hath promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:81
verses.text: Let us acknowledge it here, and let us do it; so that, just as to us God hath shown forth His mercy and His truth, mercy in forgiving our sins, truth in showing forth His promises; so also, I say, let us execute mercy and truth, mercy concerning the weak, concerning the needy, concerning even our enemies; truth in not sinning, and in not adding sin upon sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:82
verses.text: Who is therefore he that doeth this, save one out of those few, of whom is said, "He that shall have continued unto the end, the same shall be saved"? With reason here also "His mercy and truth who shall seek for Him?" Why is there "for Him"? "Who shall seek," would be sufficient.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:83
verses.text: Why hath he added, "for Him," but because many men seek to learn His mercy and truth in His books? And when they have learned, for themselves they live, not for Him; their own things they seek, not the things which are of Jesus Christ: they preach mercy and truth, and do not mercy and truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:84
verses.text: But by preaching it, they know it: for they would not preach it, unless they knew it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:85
verses.text: But he that loveth God and Christ, in preaching the mercy and truth of the Same, doth himself seek her for Him, not for himself: that is, not in order that himself may have by this preaching temporal advantages, but in order that he may do good to His members, that is, His faithful ones, by ministering with truth of that which he knoweth: in order that he that liveth, no longer for himself may live, but for Him that for all men hath died.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:86
verses.text: "So I will play music to Thy name, that I may render my vows from day unto day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:87
verses.text: If thou playest music to the name of God, play not for a time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:88
verses.text: Wilt thou for ever play? wilt thou for everlasting play? Render to Him thy vows from day unto day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:89
verses.text: What is, render to Him thy vows from day unto day? From this day unto that day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 62:90
verses.text: Continue to render vows in this day, until thou come to that day: that is, "He that shall have continued even unto the end, the same shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:1
verses.text: Psalm LXII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:2
verses.text: The title of it is, "Unto the end, in behalf of Idithun, a Psalm to David himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:3
verses.text: I recollect that already to you hath been explained what Idithun is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:4
verses.text: Let us see how far he hath leaped over, and whom he hath "leaped over," and in what place, though he hath leaped over certain men, he is situate, whence as from a kind of spiritual and secure position he may behold what is below.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:5
verses.text: He being set, I say, in a certain fortified place, doth say, "Shall not my soul be subject to God?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:6
verses.text: For he had heard, "He that doth exalt himself shall be humbled; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted:" and fearful lest by leaping over he should be proud, not elated by those things which were below, but humble because of Him that was above; to envious men, as it were threatening to him a fall, who were grieved that he had leaped over, he hath made answer, "Shall not my soul be subject to God?""For from Himself is my salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:7
verses.text: "For Himself is my God and my salvation, my taker up, I shall not be moved more".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:8
verses.text: I know who is above me, I know who stretcheth forth His mercy to men that know Him, I know under the coverings of whose wings I should hope: "I shall not be moved more".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:9
verses.text: Therefore, down from the higher place fortified and protected, he, to whom the Lord hath been made a refuge, he, to whom is God Himself for a fortified place, hath regard to those whom he hath leaped over, and looking down upon them speaketh as though from a lofty tower: for this also hath been said of Him, "A Tower of strength from the face of the enemy:" he giveth heed therefore to them, and saith, "How long do ye lay upon a man?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:10
verses.text: By insulting, by hurling reproaches, by laying wait, by persecuting, ye lay upon a man burthens, ye lay upon a man as much as a man can bear: but in order that a man may bear, under him is He that hath made man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:11
verses.text: If to a man ye look, "slay ye, all of you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:12
verses.text: Behold, lay upon, rage, "slay ye, all of you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:13
verses.text: "As though a wall bowed down, and as a fence smitten against;" lean against, smite against, as if going to throw down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:14
verses.text: And where is, "I shall not be moved more"? But wherefore? "I shall not be moved more".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:15
verses.text: Because Himself is God my Saving One, my taker up, therefore ye men are able to lay burdens upon a man; can ye anywise lay upon God, who protecteth man? "Slay ye, all of you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:16
verses.text: What is that size of body in one man so great as that he may be slain by all? But we ought to perceive our person, the person of the Church, the person of the Body of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:17
verses.text: For one Man with His Head and Body is Jesus Christ, the Saviour of the Body and the Members of the Body: two in one Flesh, and in one voice, and in one passion, and, when iniquity shall have passed over, in one rest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:18
verses.text: The sufferings therefore of Christ are not in Christ alone; nay, there are not any save in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:19
verses.text: For if Christ thou understandest to be Head and Body, the sufferings of Christ are not, save in Christ: but if Christ thou understand of Head alone, the sufferings of Christ are not in Christ alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:20
verses.text: For if the sufferings of Christ are in Christ alone, to wit in the Head alone; whence saith a certain member of Him, Paul the Apostle, "In order that I may supply what are wanting of the oppressions of Christ in my flesh"? If therefore in the members of Christ thou art, whatsoever man thou art that art hearing these words, whosoever thou art that dost hear these words (but however, thou dost hear, if in the members of Christ thou art): whatsoever thing thou sufferest from those that are not in the members of Christ, was wanting to the sufferings of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:21
verses.text: Therefore it is added because it was wanting; thou fillest up the measure, thou causest it not to run over: thou sufferest so much as was to be contributed out of thy sufferings to the whole suffering of Christ, that hath suffered in our Head, and doth suffer in His members, that is, in our own selves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:22
verses.text: Unto this our common republic, as it were each of us according to our measure payeth that which we owe, and according to the powers which we have, as it were a quota of sufferings we contribute.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:23
verses.text: The storehouse of all men's sufferings will not be completely made up, save when the world shall have been ended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:24
verses.text: That whole City therefore is speaking, from the blood of righteous Abel even to the blood of Zacharias Thence also hereafter from the blood of John, through the blood of the Apostles, through the blood of Martyrs, through the blood of the faithful ones of Christ, one City speaketh, one man saith, "How long do ye lay upon a man? Slay ye, all of you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:25
verses.text: Let us see if ye efface, let us see if ye extinguish, let us see if ye remove from the earth the name thereof, let us see if ye peoples do not meditate of empty things, saying, "When shall She die, and when shall perish the name of Her?" "As though She were a wall bowed down, and a fence smitten against," lean ye against Her, smite against Her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:26
verses.text: Hear from above: "My taker up, I shall not be moved more:" for as though a heap of sand I have been smitten against that I might fall, and the Lord hath taken me up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:27
verses.text: "Nevertheless, mine honour they have thought to drive back".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:28
verses.text: Conquered while they slay men yielding, by the blood of the slain multiplying the faithful, yielding to these and no longer being able to kill; "Nevertheless, mine honour they have thought to drive back".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:29
verses.text: Now because a Christian cannot be killed, pains are taken that a Christian should be dishonoured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:30
verses.text: For now by the honour of Christians the hearts of ungodly men are tortured: now that spiritual Joseph, after his selling by his brethren, after his removal from his home into Egypt as though into the Gentiles, after the humiliation of a prison, after the made-up tale of a false witness, after that there had come to pass that which of him was said, "Iron passed through the soul of him:" now he is honoured, now he is not made subject to brethren selling him, but corn he supplieth to them hungering Conquered by his humility and chastity, uncorruptness, temptations, sufferings, now honoured they see him, and his honour they think to check.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:31
verses.text: Is it all against one man, or one man against all; or all against all, or one against one? Meanwhile, when he saith, "ye lay upon a man," it is as it were upon one man: and when he saith, "Slay all ye," it is as if all men were against one man: but nevertheless it is also all against all, because also all are Christians, but in One.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:32
verses.text: But why must those divers errors hostile to Christ be spoken of as all together? Are they also one? Truly them also as one I dare to speak of: because there is one City and one city, one People and one people, King and king.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:33
verses.text: One City and one city is what? Babylon one, Jerusalem one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:34
verses.text: By whatsoever other mystical names besides She is called, yet One City there is and one city; over this the devil is king, over that Christ is King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:35
verses.text: Give heed, brethren, give heed, I entreat you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:36
verses.text: For it delighteth me yet to speak a few words to you of this beloved City.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:37
verses.text: For "most glorious things of Thee have been spoken, City of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:38
verses.text: And, "if I forget Thee, O Jerusalem, let mine own right hand forget me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:39
verses.text: For dear is the one Country, and truly but one Country, the only Country: besides Her whatsoever we have, is a sojourning in a strange land.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:40
verses.text: I will say therefore that which ye may acknowledge, that of which ye may approve: I will call to your minds that which ye know, I will not teach that which ye know not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:41
verses.text: "Not first," saith the Apostle, "that which is spiritual, but that which is natural, afterwards that which is spiritual".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:42
verses.text: Therefore the former city is greater by age, because first was born Cain, and afterwards Abel: but in these the elder shall serve the younger The former greater by age, the latter greater in dignity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:43
verses.text: Wherefore is the former greater by age? Because "not first that which is spiritual, but that which is natural".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:44
verses.text: Wherefore is the latter greater in dignity? Because "the elder shall serve the younger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:45
verses.text: Cain first builded a city, and in that place he builded where no city was.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:46
verses.text: But when Jerusalem was being builded, it was not builded in a place where there was not a city, but there was a city at first which was called Jebus, whence the Jebusites.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:47
verses.text: This having been captured, overcome, made subject, there was builded a new city, as though the old were thrown down; and it was called Jerusalem, vision of peace, City of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:48
verses.text: Each one therefore that is born of Adam, not yet doth belong to Jerusalem: for he beareth with him the offshoot of iniquity, and the punishment of sin, having been consigned to death, and he belongeth in a manner to a sort of old city.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:49
verses.text: But if he is to be in the people of God; his old self will be thrown down, and he will be builded up new.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:50
verses.text: For this reason therefore Cain builded a city where there was not a city.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:51
verses.text: For from mortality and from naughtiness every one setteth out, in order that he may be made good hereafter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:52
verses.text: "For as by the disobedience of one man many were made sinners, so by the obedience of One Man many shall be made just".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:53
verses.text: And all we in Adam do die: and each one of us of Adam was born.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:54
verses.text: Let him pass over to Jerusalem, he shall be thrown down old, and shall be builded new.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:55
verses.text: As though to conquered Jebusites, in order that there may be builded up Jerusalem, is said, "Put ye off the old man, and put on the new".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:56
verses.text: And now to them builded in Jerusalem, and shining by the light of Grace, is said, "Ye have been sometime darkness, but now light in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:57
verses.text: The evil city therefore from the beginning even unto the end doth run on, and the good City by the changing of evil men is builded up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:58
verses.text: And these two cities are meanwhile mingled, at the end to be severed; against each other mutually in conflict, the one for iniquity, the other for the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:59
verses.text: And sometimes this very temporal mingling bringeth it to pass that certain men belonging to the city Babylon, do order matters belonging to Jerusalem, and again certain men belonging to Jerusalem, do order matters belonging to Babylon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:60
verses.text: Something difficult I seem to have propounded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:61
verses.text: Be ye patient, until it be proved by examples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:62
verses.text: "For all things" in the old people, as writeth the Apostle, "in a figure used to befall them: but they have been written for our amendment, upon whom the end of the world hath come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:63
verses.text: Regard therefore that people as also set to intimate an after people; and see then what I say.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:64
verses.text: There were great kings in Jerusalem: it is a known fact, they are enumerated, are named.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:65
verses.text: They all were, I say, wicked citizens of Babylon, and they were ordering matters of Jerusalem: all men from thence to be dissevered at the end, to no one but to the devil do belong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:66
verses.text: Again we find citizens of Jerusalem to have ordered certain matters belonging to Babylon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:67
verses.text: For those three children, Nabuchodonosor, overcome by a miracle, made the ministers of his kingdom, and set them over his Satraps; and so there were ordering the matters of Babylon citizens of Jerusalem Observe now how this is being fulfilled and done in the Church, and in these times.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:68
verses.text: Every earthly commonwealth, sometime assuredly to perish, whereof the kingdom is to pass away, when there shall come that kingdom, whereof we pray, "Thy kingdom come;" and whereof hath been foretold, "And of His kingdom shall be no end:" an earthly commonwealth, I say, hath our citizens conducting the affairs of it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:69
verses.text: For how many faithful, how many good men, are both magistrates in their cities, and are judges, and are generals, and are counts, and are kings? All that are just and good men, having not anything in heart but the most glorious things, which of Thee have been said, City of God And as if they were doing bond-service in the city which is to pass away, even there by the doctors of the Holy City they are bidden to keep faith with those set over them, "whether with the king as supreme, or with governors as though sent by God for the punishment of evil men, but for the praise of good men: " or as servants, that to their masters they should be subject, even Christians to Heathens, and the better should keep faith with the worse, for a time to serve, for everlasting to have dominion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:70
verses.text: For these things do happen until iniquity do pass away Servants are commanded to bear with masters unjust and capricious: the citizens of Babylon are commanded to be endured by the citizens of Jerusalem, showing even more attentions, than if they were citizens of the same Babylon, as though fulfilling the precept, "He that shall have exacted of thee a mile, go with him other twain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:71
verses.text: "I have run in thirst".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:72
verses.text: For they were rendering evil things for good things: for them was I thirsting: mine honour they thought to drive back: I was thirsting to bring them over into my body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:73
verses.text: For in drinking what do we, but send into our members liquor that is without, and suck it into our body? Thus did Moses in that head of the calf The head of the calf is a great sacrament For the head of the calf was the body of ungodly men, in the similitude of a calf eating hay, seeking earthly things: because all flesh is hayAnd what now is more evident, than that into that City Jerusalem, of which the people Israel was a type, by Baptism men were to be made to pass over? Therefore in water it was scattered, in order that for drink it might be given.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:74
verses.text: For this even unto the end this man thirsteth; he runneth and thirsteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:75
verses.text: For many men He drinketh, but never will He be without thirst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:76
verses.text: For thence is, "I thirst, woman, give Me to drink".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:77
verses.text: That Samaritan woman at the well found the Lord thirsting, and by Him thirsting she was filled: she first found Him thirsting, in order that He might drink her believing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:78
verses.text: And when He was on the Cross, "I thirst," He said, although they gave not to Him that for which He was thirsting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:79
verses.text: For for themselves He was thirsting: but they gave vinegar, not new wine, wherewith are filled up the new bottles, but old wine, but old to its loss For old vinegar also is said of the old men, of whom hath been said, "For to them is no changing;" namely, that the Jebusites should be overthrown, and Jerusalem be builded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:80
verses.text: So also the Head of this body even unto the end from the beginning runneth in thirst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:81
verses.text: And as if to Him were being said, Why in thirst? what is wanting to Thee, O Body of Christ, O Church of Christ? in so great honour, in so great exaltation, in so great height also even in this world established, what is wanting to Thee? There is fulfilled that which hath been foretold of thee, "There shall adore Him all kings of the earth, all nations shall serve Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:82
verses.text: They that at Jerusalem's festivals fill up the Churches, at Babylon's festivals fill up the theatres: and for all they serve, honour, obey Her—not only those very persons that bear the Sacraments of Christ, and hate the commandments of Christ, but also they, that bear not even the mere Sacraments, Heathen though they be, Jews though they be,—they honour, praise, proclaim, "but with their mouths they were blessing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:83
verses.text: I heed not the mouth, He knoweth that hath instructed me, "with their heart they were cursing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:84
verses.text: In that place they were cursing, where "mine honour they thought to drive back".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:85
verses.text: What dost Thou, O Idithun, Body of Christ, leaping over them? What dost Thou amid all these things? What wilt Thou? wilt faint? wilt Thou not persevere even unto the end? wilt Thou not hearken, "He that shall have persevered even unto the end, the same shall be saved," though for that iniquity aboundeth, the love of many shall wax cold? And where is it that Thou hast leaped over them? where is it that Thy conversation is in Heaven? But they cleave unto earthly things, as though earthborn they mind the earth, and are earth, the serpent's food What dost thou amid these things?"Nevertheless, to God my soul shall be made subject".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:86
verses.text: And who would endure so great things, either open wars, or secret lyings-in-wait? Who would endure so great things amid open enemies, amid false brethren? Who would endure so great things? Would a man? and if a man would, would a man of himself? I have not so leaped over that I should be lifted up, and fall: "To God my soul shall be made subject: for from Himself is my patience".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:87
verses.text: What patience is there amid so great scandals, except that "if for that which we do not see we hope, through patience we look for it"? There cometh my pain, there will come my rest also; there cometh my tribulation, there will come my cleansing also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:88
verses.text: For doth gold glitter in the furnace of the refiner? In a necklace it will glitter, in an ornament it will glitter: let it suffer however the furnace, in order that being cleansed from dross it may come into light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:89
verses.text: This is the furnace, there is there chaff, there gold, there fire, into this bloweth the refiner: in the furnace burneth the chaff, and the gold is cleansed; the one into ashes is turned, of dross the other is cleansed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:90
verses.text: The furnace is the world, the chaff unrighteous men, the gold just men; the fire tribulation, the refiner God: that which therefore the refiner willeth I do; wherever the Maker setteth me I endure it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:91
verses.text: I am commanded to endure, He knoweth how to cleanse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:92
verses.text: Though there burn the chaff to set me on fire, and as if to consume me; that into ashes is burned, I of dross am cleansed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:93
verses.text: Wherefore? Because "to God my soul shall be made subject: for from Himself is my patience".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:94
verses.text: "For Himself is my God and My Saving One, my Taker up, I will not remove hence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:95
verses.text: Because "Himself is my God," therefore He calleth me: "and my Saving One," therefore He justifieth me: "and my Taker up," therefore He glorifieth me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:96
verses.text: For here I am called and am justified, but there I am glorified; and from thence where I am glorified, "I will not remove".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:97
verses.text: For a sojourner I am with Thee on earth as all my fathers were.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:98
verses.text: Therefore from my lodging I shall remove, from my Heavenly home I shall not remove.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:99
verses.text: "In God is my salvation and my glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:100
verses.text: Saved I shall be in God, glorious I shall be in God: for not only saved, but also glorious, saved, because a just man I have been made out of an ungodly man, by Him justified; but glorious, because not only justified, but also honoured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:101
verses.text: For "those whom He hath predestined, those also He hath called".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:102
verses.text: Calling them, what hath He done here? "Whom He hath called, the same also He hath justified; but whom He hath justified, the same also He hath glorified".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:103
verses.text: Justification therefore to salvation belongeth, glorifying to honour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:104
verses.text: How glorifying to honour belongeth, it is not needful to discuss.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:105
verses.text: How justification belongeth to salvation, let us seek some proof.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:106
verses.text: Behold there cometh to mind out of the Gospel: there were some who to themselves were seeming to be just men, and they were finding fault with the Lord because He admitted to the feast sinners, and with publicans and sinners was eating; to such men therefore priding themselves, strong men of earth very much lifted up, much glorying of their own soundness, such as they counted it, not such as they had, the Lord answered what? "They that are whole need not a Physician, but they that are sick".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:107
verses.text: Whom calleth He whole, whom calleth He sick? He continueth and saith, "I have not come to call just men, but sinners unto repentance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:108
verses.text: He hath called therefore "the whole" just men, not because the Pharisees were so, but because themselves they thought so to be; and for this reason were proud, and grudged sick men a physician, and being more sick than those, they slew the Physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:109
verses.text: He hath called whole, however, righteous men, sick, the sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:110
verses.text: My being justified therefore, saith that man that leapeth over, from Himself I have: my being glorified, from Himself I have: "For God is my salvation and my glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:111
verses.text: "My salvation," so that saved I am: "my glory," so that honoured I am.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:112
verses.text: This thing hereafter: now what? "God of my help, and my hope is in God;" until I attain unto perfect justification and salvation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:113
verses.text: "For by hope we are saved: but hope which is seen, is not hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:114
verses.text: "Hope ye in Him all the council of the people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:115
verses.text: Imitate ye Idithun, leap over your enemies; men fighting against you, stopping up your way, men hating you, leap ye over: "Hope in Him all the council of the people: pour out before Him your hearts:"By imploring, by confessing, by hoping.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:116
verses.text: Do not keep back your hearts within your hearts: "Pour out before Him your hearts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:117
verses.text: That perisheth not which ye pour out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:118
verses.text: For He is my Taker up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:119
verses.text: If He taketh up, why fearest thou to pour out? "Cast upon the Lord thy care, and hope in Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:120
verses.text: What fear ye amid whisperers, slanderers hateful to God, where they are able openly assailing, where they are unable secretly lying in wait, falsely praising, truly at enmity, amid them what fear ye? "God is our Helper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:121
verses.text: Do they anywise equal God? Are they anywise stronger than He? "God is our Helper," be ye without care.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:122
verses.text: "If God is for us, who is against us?" "Pour out before Him your hearts," by leaping over unto Him, by lifting up your souls: "God is our helper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:123
verses.text: "Nevertheless, vain are the sons of men, and liars are the sons of men in the balances, in order that they may deceive, being at one because of vanity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:124
verses.text: Certainly many men there are: behold there is that one man, that one man that was cast forth from the multitude of guests.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:125
verses.text: They conspire, they all seek things temporal, and they that are carnal things carnal, and for the future they hope them, whosoever do hope: even if because of variety of opinions they are in division, nevertheless because of vanity they are at one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:126
verses.text: Divers indeed are errors and of many forms, and the kingdom against itself divided shall not stand: but alike in all is the will vain and lying, belonging to one king, with whom into fire everlasting it is to be thrown headlong—"these men because of vanity are at one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:127
verses.text: And for them see how He thirsteth, see how He runneth in thirst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:128
verses.text: He turneth therefore Himself to them, thirsting for them: "Do not hope in iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:129
verses.text: For my hope is in God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:130
verses.text: Ye that will not draw near and pass over, "do not hope in iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:131
verses.text: For I that have leapt over, my hope is in God; and is there anywise iniquity with God? This thing let us do, that thing let us do, of that thing let us think, thus let us adjust our lyings in wait; "Because of vanity being at one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:132
verses.text: Thou thirstest: they that think of those things against thee are given up by those whom thou drinkest, "Do not hope in vanity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:133
verses.text: Vain is iniquity, nought is iniquity, mighty is nothing save righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:134
verses.text: Truth may be hidden for a time, conquered it cannot be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:135
verses.text: Iniquity may flourish for a time, abide it cannot.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:136
verses.text: "Do not hope upon iniquity: and for robbery be not covetous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:137
verses.text: Thou art not rich, and wilt thou rob? What findest thou? What losest thou? O losing gains! Thou findest money, thou losest righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:138
verses.text: "For robbery be not covetous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:139
verses.text: Therefore, vain sons of men, lying sons of men, neither rob, nor, if there flow riches, set heart upon them: no longer love vanity, and seek lying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:140
verses.text: For "blessed is the man who hath the Lord God for his hope, and who hath not had regard unto vanities, and lying follies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:141
verses.text: Ye would deceive, ye would commit a fraud, what bring ye in order that ye may cheat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:142
verses.text: Deceitful balances.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:143
verses.text: For "lying," he saith, "are the sons of men in the balances," in order that they may cheat by bringing forth deceitful balances.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:144
verses.text: By a false balance ye beguile men looking on: know ye not that one is he that weigheth, Another He that judgeth of the weight? He seeth not, for whom thou weighest, but He seeth that weigheth thee and him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:145
verses.text: Therefore neither fraud nor robbery covet ye any longer, nor on those things which ye have set your hope: I have admonished, have foretold, saith this Idithun.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:146
verses.text: What followeth? "Once hath God spoken, these two things I have heard, that power is of God , and to Thee, O Lord, is mercy, for Thou shalt render to each one after his works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:147
verses.text: "Once hath God spoken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:148
verses.text: What sayest thou, Idithun? If thou that hadst leapt over them art saying, "Once He hath spoken;" I turn to another Scripture and it saith to me, "In many quarters and in many ways formerly God hath spoken to the fathers in the prophets".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:149
verses.text: What is, "Once hath God spoken"? Is He not the God that in the beginning of mankind spake to Adam? Did not the Selfsame speak to Cain, to Noe, to Abraham, to Isaac, to Jacob, to all the Prophets, and to Moses? One man Moses was, and how often to him spake God? Behold even to one man, not once but ofttimes God hath spoken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:150
verses.text: Secondly, He hath spoken to the Son when standing here, "Thou art My beloved Son".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:151
verses.text: God hath spoken to the Apostles, He hath spoken to all the Saints, even though not with voice sounding through the cloud, nevertheless in the heart where He is Himself Teacher What is therefore, "Once hath God spoken"? Much hath that man leapt over in order to arrive at that place, where once God hath spoken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:152
verses.text: Behold briefly I have spoken to your Love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:153
verses.text: Here among men, to men ofttimes, in many ways, in many quarters, through creatures of many forms God hath spoken: by Himself once God hath spoken, because One Word God hath begotten.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:154
verses.text: For it could not be but that God did Himself know that which by the Word He made:  but if that which He made He knew, in Him there was that which was made before it was made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:155
verses.text: For if in Him was not that which was made before it was made, how knew He that which He made? For thou canst not say that God made things He knew not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:156
verses.text: God therefore hath known that which He hath made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:157
verses.text: And how knew He before He made, if there cannot be known any but things made? But by things made there cannot be known any but things previously made, by thee, to wit, who art a man made in a lower place, and set in a lower place: but before that all these things were made, they were known by Him by whom they were made, and that which He knew He made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:158
verses.text: Therefore in that Word by which He made all things, before that they were made, were all things; and after they have been made there are all things; but in one way here, in another there, in one way in their own nature wherein they have been made, in another in the art by which they have been made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:159
verses.text: Who could explain this? We may endeavour: go ye with Idithun, and see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:160
verses.text: For even the Lord saith, "Many things I have to say to you, but ye cannot bear them now".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:161
verses.text: What is therefore, "These two things I have heard"? These two things which to you I am about to say not of myself to you I say, but what things I have heard I say.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:162
verses.text: "Once hath God spoken:" One Word hath He, the Only-begotten God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:163
verses.text: In that Word are all things, because by the Word were made all things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:164
verses.text: One Word hath He, "in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:165
verses.text: One Word He hath, "once hath God spoken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:166
verses.text: "These two things," which to you I am about to say, these I have heard: not of myself I speak, not of myself I say: to this belongeth the "I have heard".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:167
verses.text: But the friend of the Bridegroom standeth and heareth Him, that he may speak the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:168
verses.text: For he heareth Him, lest by speaking a lie, of his own he should speak: lest thou shouldest say, Who art thou that sayest this thing to me? whence dost thou say this to me? I have heard these two things, and I that speak to thee that I have heard these two things, am one who also doth know that once God hath spoken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:169
verses.text: Do not despise a hearer saying to thee certain two things for thee so necessary; him, I say, that by leaping over the whole creation hath attained unto the Only-begotten Word of God, where he hath learned that "once God hath spoken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:170
verses.text: Let him therefore now say certain two things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:171
verses.text: For greatly to us belong these two things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:172
verses.text: "For power is of God, and to Thee, O Lord, is mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:173
verses.text: Are these the two things, power and mercy? These two evidently: perceive ye the power of God, perceive ye the mercy of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:174
verses.text: In these two things are contained nearly all the Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:175
verses.text: Because of these two things are the Prophets, because of these two, the Patriarchs, because of these the Law, because of these Himself our Lord Jesus Christ, because of these the Apostles, because of these all the preaching and spreading of the word of God in the Church, because of these two, because of the power of God, and His mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:176
verses.text: His power fear ye, His mercy love ye.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:177
verses.text: Neither so on His mercy rely, as that His power ye despise: nor so the power fear ye, as that of mercy ye despair.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:178
verses.text: With Him is power, with Him mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:179
verses.text: This man He humbleth, and that man He exalteth: this man He humbleth with power, that man He exalteth in mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:180
verses.text: "For if God, willing to show wrath and to prove His power, hath in much patience borne with the vessels of wrath, which have been perfected unto perdition"—thou hast heard of power: inquire for mercy—"and that He might make known," He saith, "His riches unto the vessels of mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:181
verses.text: It belongeth therefore to His power to condemn unjust men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:182
verses.text: And to Him who would say, What hast thou done? "For thou, O man, who art thou that should make answer to God?" Fear therefore and tremble at His power: but hope for His mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:183
verses.text: The devil is a sort of power; ofttimes however he wisheth to hurt, and is not able, because that power is under power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:184
verses.text: For if the devil could hurt as much as he would; no one of just men would remain, nor could any one of the faithful be on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:185
verses.text: The same through his vessels smiteth against, as it were, a wall bowed down: but he only smiteth against, so far as he receiveth power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:186
verses.text: But in order that the wall may not fall, the Lord will support: for He that giveth power to the tempter, doth Himself to the tempted extend mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:187
verses.text: For according to measure the devil is permitted to tempt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:188
verses.text: And, "Thou wilt give us to drink in tears in a measure".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:189
verses.text: Do not therefore fear the tempter permitted to do somewhat: for thou hast a most merciful Saviour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:190
verses.text: So much he is permitted to tempt as is profitable for thee, that thou mayest be exercised, mayest be proved; in order that by thyself thou mayest be found out, that knowest not thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:191
verses.text: For where, or from whence, ought we to be secure, except by this power and mercy of God? After that Apostolic saying, "Faithful is God, that doth not suffer you to be tempted above that which ye are able".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:192
verses.text: Fear not the enemy: so much he doeth as he hath received power to do, Him fear thou that hath the chief power: Him fear, that doeth as much as He willeth, and that doeth nothing unjustly, and whatever He shall have done, is just.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:193
verses.text: We might suppose something or other to be unjust: inasmuch as God hath done it, believe it to be just.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:194
verses.text: Therefore, thou sayest, if any one slay an innocent man, doeth he justly or unjustly? Unjustly certainly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:195
verses.text: Wherefore doth God permit this?The counsel of God to tell to thee, O man, I am not able: this thing however I say, both that the man hath done unjustly that hath slain an innocent person, and that it would not have been done unless God permitted it: and though the man hath done unjustly, yet God hath not unjustly permitted this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:196
verses.text: Let the reason lie concealed in that person whoever it be, for whose sake thou art moved, whose innocence doth much move thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:197
verses.text: For to thee speedily I might make answer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:198
verses.text: He would not have been slain unless he were guilty: but thou thinkest him innocent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:199
verses.text: I might speedily say this to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:200
verses.text: For thou couldest not examine his heart, sift his deeds, weigh his thoughts, so that thou couldest say to me, unjustly he was slain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:201
verses.text: I might easily therefore make answer: but there is forced upon my view a certain Just One, without dispute just, without doubt just, who had no sin, slain by sinners, betrayed by a sinner; Himself Christ the Lord, of whom we cannot say that He hath any iniquity, for "those things which He robbed not He paid," is made an objection to my answer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:202
verses.text: And why should I speak of Christ? "With thee I am dealing," thou sayest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:203
verses.text: And I with thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:204
verses.text: About Him thou proposest a question, about Him I am solving the question.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:205
verses.text: For therein the counsel of God we know, which except by His own revealing we should not know: so that when thou shalt have found out that counsel of God, whereby He hath permitted His innocent Son to be slain by unjust men, and such a counsel as pleaseth thee, and such a counsel as cannot displease thee, if thou art just, thou mayest believe that in other things also by His counsel God doeth the same, but it escaped thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:206
verses.text: Ah! brethren, need there was of the blood of a just one to blot out the handwriting of sins; need there was of an example of patience, of an example of humility; need there was of the Sign of the Cross to beat down the devil and his angels; need for us there was of the Passion of our Lord; for by the Passion of the Lord redeemed hath been the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:207
