verses.text: How many good things hath the Passion of the Lord done! And yet the Passion of this Just One would not have been, unless unrighteous men had slain the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:208
verses.text: What then? is this good thing which to us hath been granted by the Lord's Passion to be ascribed to the unjust slayers of Christ? Far be it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:209
verses.text: They willed, God permitted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:210
verses.text: They guilty would have been, even if only they had willed it: but God would not have permitted it, unless just it had been.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:211
verses.text: Accordingly, my brethren, both Judas the foul traitor to Christ, and the persecutors of Christ, malignant all, ungodly all, unjust all, are to be condemned all: and nevertheless the Father His own proper Son hath not spared, but for the sake of us all He hath delivered Him up Order if thou art able; distinguish if thou art able (these things): render to God thy vows, which thy lips have uttered: see what the unjust hath here done, what the Just One.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:212
verses.text: The one hath willed, the Other hath permitted: the one unjustly hath willed, the Other justly hath permitted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:213
verses.text: Let unjust will be condemned, just permission be glorified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:214
verses.text: For what evil thing hath befallen Christ, in that Christ hath died? Both evil were they that evil willed to do, and yet nothing of evil did He suffer on whom they did it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:215
verses.text: Slain was mortal flesh, slaying death by death, giving a lesson of patience, sending before an example of Resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:216
verses.text: How great good things of the Just One were wrought by the evil things of the unjust! This is the great mystery of God: that even a good thing which thou doest He hath Himself given it to thee, and by thy evil He doeth good Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:217
verses.text: Do not therefore wonder, God permitteth, and in judgment permitteth: He permitteth, and in measure, number, weight, He permitteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:218
verses.text: With Him is not iniquity: do thou only belong to Him; on Himself thy hope set thou, let Himself be thy Helper, thy Salvation: in Him be there the fortified place, the tower of strength, thy refuge let Himself be, and He will not suffer thee to be tempted above that which thou art able to bear, but will make with the temptation also an escape, that thou mayest be able to support it: so that His suffering thee to bear temptation, be His power; His suffering not any more on thee to be done than thou art able to bear, be His mercy: "for power is of God, and to Thee, O Lord, is mercy, because Thou wilt render to each one after his works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:219
verses.text: That thirst of the Church, would fain drink up that man also whom ye see At the same time also, in order that ye may know how many in the mixed multitude of Christians with their mouth do bless, and in their heart curse, this man having been a Christian and a believer returneth as a penitent, and being terrified by the power of the Lord, turneth him to the mercy of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:220
verses.text: For having been led astray by the enemy when he was a believer, long time he hath been an astrologer, led astray, leading astray, deceived, deceiving, he hath allured, hath beguiled, many lies he hath spoken against God, That hath given to men power of doing that which is good, and of not doing that which is evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:221
verses.text: He used to say, that one's own will did not adultery, but Venus; one's own will did not manslaying, but Mars; and God did not what is just, but Jupiter; and many other blasphemous things, and not light ones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:222
verses.text: From how many Christians do ye think he hath pocketed money? How many from him have bought a lie, to whom we used to say, "Sons of men, how long are ye dull of heart, wherefore love ye vanity, and seek a lie"? Now, as of him must be believed, he hath shuddered at his lie, and being the allurer of many men, he hath perceived at length that by the devil he hath himself been allured, and he turneth to God a penitent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:223
verses.text: We think, brethren, that because of great fear of heart it hath come to pass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:224
verses.text: For what must we say? If out of a heathen an astrologer were converted, great indeed would be the joy: but nevertheless it might appear, that, if he had been converted, he was desiring the clerical office in the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:225
verses.text: A penitent he is, he seeketh not anything save mercy alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:226
verses.text: He must be recommended therefore both to your eyes and hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:227
verses.text: Him whom ye see in hearts love ye, with eyes guard ye.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:228
verses.text: See ye him, mark ye him, and whithersoever he shall have gone his way, to the rest of the brethren that now are not here, point him out: and such diligence is mercy; lest that leader astray drag back his heart and take it by storm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:229
verses.text: Guard ye him, let there not escape you his conversation, his way: in order that by your testimony it may be proved to us that truly to the Lord he hath been turned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:230
verses.text: For report will not be silent about his life, when to you he is thus presented both to be seen and to be pitied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:231
verses.text: Ye know in the Acts of the Apostles how it is written, that many lost men, that is, men of such arts, and followers of naughty doctrines, brought unto the Apostles all their books; and there were burned so many volumes, that it was the writer's task to make a valuation of them, and write down the sum of the price This truly was for the glory of God, in order that even such lost men might not be despaired of by Him that knew how to seek that which had been lost.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:232
verses.text: Therefore this man had been lost, is now sought, found, led hither, he bringeth with him books to be burned, by which he had been to be burned, so that when these have been thrown into the fire, he may himself pass over into a place of refreshment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:233
verses.text: Know ye that he, brethren, once knocked at the Church door before Easter: for before Easter he began to ask of the Church Christ's medicine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:234
verses.text: But because the art wherein he had been practised is of such sort as that it was suspected of lying and deceit, he was put off that he might not tempt; at length however he was admitted, that he might not more dangerously be tempted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:235
verses.text: Pray for him through Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:236
verses.text: Straightway to-day's prayer pour out for him to the Lord our God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:237
verses.text: For we know and are sure, that your prayer effaceth all his impieties.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 63:238
verses.text: The Lord be with you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:1
verses.text: Psalm LXIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:2
verses.text: This psalm hath the title, "For David himself, when he was in the desert of Idumaea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:3
verses.text: By the name of Idumaea is understood this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:4
verses.text: For Idumaea was a certain nation of men going astray, where idols were worshipped.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:5
verses.text: In no good sense is put this Idumaea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:6
verses.text: If not in a good sense it is put, it must be understood that this life, wherein we suffer so great toils, and wherein to so great necessities we are made subject, by the name of Idumaea is signified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:7
verses.text: Even here is a desert where there is much thirst, and ye are to hear the voice of One now thirsting in the desert.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:8
verses.text: But if we acknowledge ourselves as thirsting, we shall acknowledge ourselves as drinking also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:9
verses.text: For he that thirsteth in this world, in the world to come shall be satisfied, according to the Lord's saying, "Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness, for the same shall be satisfied".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:10
verses.text: Therefore in this world we ought not to love fulness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:11
verses.text: Here we must thirst, in another place we shall be filled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:12
verses.text: But now in order that we may not faint in this desert, He sprinkleth upon us the dew of His word, and leaveth us not utterly to dry up, so that there should not be in our case any seeking of us again, but that we may so thirst as that we may drink.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:13
verses.text: But in order that we may drink, with somewhat of His Grace we are sprinkled: nevertheless we thirst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:14
verses.text: And what saith our soul to God?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:15
verses.text: "God, my God, unto Thee from the light I watch".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:16
verses.text: What is to watch? It is, not to sleep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:17
verses.text: What is to sleep? There is a sleep of the soul; there is a sleep of the body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:18
verses.text: Sleep of body we all ought to have: because if sleep of body is not taken, a man fainteth, the body itself fainteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:19
verses.text: For our frail body cannot long sustain a soul watching and on the stretch on active works; if for a long time the soul shall have been intent on active pursuits, the body being frail and earthly holdeth her not, sustaineth her not for ever in activity, and fainteth and falleth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:20
verses.text: Therefore God hath granted sleep to the body, whereby are recruited the members of the body, in order that they may be able to sustain the soul watching.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:21
verses.text: But of this let us take heed, namely, that our soul herself sleep not: for evil is the sleep of the soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:22
verses.text: Good is the sleep of the body, whereby is recruited the health of the body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:23
verses.text: But the sleep of the soul is to forget her God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:24
verses.text: Whatsoever soul shall have forgotten her God, sleepeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:25
verses.text: Therefore the Apostle saith to certain persons that forgot their God, and being as it were in sleep, did act the follies of the worship of idols—the Apostle, I say, saith to certain persons, "Rise, thou that sleepest, and rise up from the dead, and Christ shall enlighten thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:26
verses.text: Was the Apostle waking up one sleeping in body? Nay, but he was waking a soul sleeping, inasmuch as he was waking her, in order that she might be lightened by Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:27
verses.text: Therefore as to these same watchings saith this man, "God, my God, unto Thee from the light I watch".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:28
verses.text: For thou wouldest not watch of thyself, unless there should arise thy Light, to wake thee from sleep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:29
verses.text: For Christ lighteneth souls, and maketh them to watch: but if His light He taketh away, they slumber.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:30
verses.text: For for this cause to Him there is said in another psalm, "Lighten mine eyes, that I may never slumber in death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:31
verses.text: "My soul hath thirsted for Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:32
verses.text: Behold that desert of Idumaea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:33
verses.text: See how here he thirsteth: but see what good thing is here, "Hath thirsted for Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:34
verses.text: For there are they that thirst, but not for God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:35
verses.text: For every one that willeth anything to be granted to him, is in the heat of longing; the longing itself is the thirst of the soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:36
verses.text: And see ye what longings there are in the hearts of men: one longeth for gold, another longeth for silver, another longeth for possessions, another inheritance, another abundance of money, another many herds, another a wife, another honours, another sons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:37
verses.text: Ye see those longings, how they are in the hearts of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:38
verses.text: All men are inflamed with longing, and scarce is found one to say, "My soul hath thirsted for Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:39
verses.text: For men thirst for the world: and perceive not themselves to be in the desert of Idumaea, where their souls ought to thirst for God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:40
verses.text: Wisdom therefore must be thirsted after, righteousness must be thirsted after.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:41
verses.text: With it we shall not be satisfied, with it we shall not be filled, save when this life shall have been ended, and we shall have come to that which God hath promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:42
verses.text: For God hath promised equality with Angels: and now the Angels thirst not as we do, they hunger not as we do; but they have the fulness of truth, of light, of immortal wisdom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:43
verses.text: Therefore blessed they are, and out of so great blessedness, because they are in that City, the Heavenly Jerusalem, afar from whence we now are sojourning in a strange land, they observe us sojourners, and they pity us, and by the command of the Lord they help us, in order that to this common country sometime we may return, and there with them sometime with the Lord's fountain of truth and eternity we may be filled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:44
verses.text: Now therefore let our soul thirst: whence doth our flesh also thirst, and this in many ways? "In many ways for Thee," he saith, "my flesh also".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:45
verses.text: Because to our flesh also is promised Resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:46
verses.text: As to our soul is promised blessedness, so also to our flesh is promised resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:47
verses.text: For if God hath made us that were not, is it a great thing for Him to make again us that were? Therefore let not this seem to you to be incredible, because ye see dead men as it were decaying, and passing into ashes and into dust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:48
verses.text: Or if any dead man be burned, or if dogs tear him in pieces, do ye think that from this he will not rise again? All things which are dismembered, and into a sort of dust do decay, are entire with God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:49
verses.text: For into those elements of the world they pass, whence at first they have come, when we were made: we do not see them; but yet God will bring them forth, He knoweth whence, because even before we were, He created us from whence He knew.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:50
verses.text: Such a resurrection of the flesh therefore to us is promised, as that, although it be the same flesh that now we carry which is to rise again, yet it hath not the corruption which now it hath.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:51
verses.text: For now because of the corruption of frailty, if we eat not, we faint and are hungry; if we drink not, we faint and are thirsty; if long time we watch, we faint and sleep; if long time we sleep, we faint, therefore we watch.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:52
verses.text: Secondly, see how without any standing is our flesh: for infancy passeth away into boyhood, and thou seekest infancy, and infancy is not, for now instead of infancy is boyhood: again this same also passeth into youth, thou seekest boyhood and findest not: the young man becometh a middle-aged man, thou seekest the young man and he is not: the middle-aged man becometh an old man, thou seekest a middle-aged man and findest not: and an old man dieth, thou seekest an old man and findest not: our age therefore standeth not still: everywhere is weariness, everywhere faintness, everywhere corruption.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:53
verses.text: Observing what a hope of resurrection God promiseth to us, in all those our manifold faintings we thirst for that incorruption: and so our flesh manifoldly doth thirst for God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:54
verses.text: Nevertheless, my brethren, the flesh of a good Christian and a believer even in this world for God doth thirst: for if the flesh hath need of bread, if it hath need of water, if it hath need of wine, if it hath need of money, if this flesh hath need of a beast, from God it ought to seek it, not from demons and idols and I know not what powers of this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:55
verses.text: For there are certain who when they suffer hunger in this world, leave God and ask Mercury or ask Jove to give unto them, or her whom they call "Heavenly," or any the like demons: not for God their flesh thirsteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:56
verses.text: But they that thirst for God, everywhere ought to thirst for Him, both soul and flesh: for to the soul also God giveth His bread, that is the Word of Truth: and to the flesh God giveth the things which are necessary, for God hath made both soul and flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:57
verses.text: For the sake of thy flesh thou askest of demons: hath God made the soul, and the demons made the flesh? He that hath made the soul, the Same hath made the flesh also: He that hath made both of them, the Same feedeth both of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:58
verses.text: Let either part of us thirst for God, and after labour manifold let either simply be filled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:59
verses.text: But where thirsteth our soul, and our flesh manifoldly, not for any one but for Thee, O Lord, that is our God? it thirsteth where? "In a land desert, and without way, and without water".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:60
verses.text: Of  this world we have spoken, the same is Idumaea, this is the desert of Idumaea, whence the Psalm hath received its title.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:61
verses.text: "In a land desert".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:62
verses.text: Too little it is to say "desert," where no man dwelleth; it is besides, both "without way, and without water".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:63
verses.text: O that the same desert had even a way: O that into this a man running, even knew where he might thence get forth!Evil is the desert, horrible, and to be feared: and nevertheless God hath pitied us, and hath made for us a way in the desert, Himself our Lord Jesus Christ: and hath made for us a consolation in the desert, in sending to us preachers of His Word: and hath given to us water in the desert, by fulfilling with the Holy Spirit His preachers, in order that there might be created in them a well of water springing up unto life everlasting And, lo! we have here all things, but they are not of the desert.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:64
verses.text: "Thus in a holy thing I have appeared to Thee, that I might see Thy power and Thy glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:65
verses.text: Unless a man first thirst in that desert, that is in the evil wherein he is, he never arriveth at the good, which is God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:66
verses.text: But "I have appeared to Thee," he saith, "in a holy thing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:67
verses.text: Now in a holy thing is there great consolation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:68
verses.text: "I have appeared to Thee," is what? In order that Thou mightest see me: and for this reason Thou hast seen me, in order that I might see Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:69
verses.text: "I have appeared to Thee, that I might see".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:70
verses.text: He hath not said, "I have appeared to Thee, that Thou mightest see:" but, "I have appeared to Thee, that I might see Thy power and Thy glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:71
verses.text: Whence also the Apostle, "But now," he saith, "knowing God, nay, having been known of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:72
verses.text: For first ye have appeared to God, in order that to you God might be able to appear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:73
verses.text: "That I might see Thy power and Thy glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:74
verses.text: In truth in that forsaken place, that is, in that desert, if as though from the desert a man striveth to obtain enough for his sustenance, he will never see the power of the Lord, and the glory of the Lord, but he will remain to die of thirst, and will find neither way, nor consolation, nor water, whereby he may endure in the desert.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:75
verses.text: But when he shall have lifted up himself to God, so as to say to Him out of all his inward parts, "My soul hath thirsted for Thee; how manifoldly for Thee also my flesh!" lest perchance even the things necessary for the flesh of others he ask, and not of God, or else long not for that resurrection of the flesh, which God hath promised to us: when, I say, he shall have lifted up himself, he will have no small consolations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:76
verses.text: But ye have heard but now when the Gospel was being read in what terms He hath notified His Majesty: "I and My Father are One".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:77
verses.text: Behold how great a Majesty and how great an Equality with the Father hath come down to the flesh because of our infirmity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:78
verses.text: Behold how greatly beloved we have been, before that we loved God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:79
verses.text: If before that we loved God, so much by Him we were beloved, as that His Son, Equal with Himself, He made a Man for our sake, what doth He reserve for us now loving Him? Therefore many men think it to be a very small thing that the Son of God hath appeared on earth; because they are not in the Holy One, to them hath not appeared the power of the Same and the glory of the Same: that is, not yet have they a heart made holy, whence they may perceive the eminence of that virtue, and may render thanks to God, nor that to which for their own sakes so great an One came, unto what a nativity, unto what a Passion, they are not able to see, His glory and His power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:80
verses.text: "For better is Thy mercy than lives".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:81
verses.text: Many are the lives of men, but one life God promiseth: and He giveth not this to us as if for our merits but for His mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:82
verses.text: For what is so just a thing as that a sinner should be punished? Though a just thing it be that a sinner should be punished, it hath belonged to the mercy of Him not to punish a sinner but to justify him, and of a sinner to make a just man, and of an ungodly man to make a godly man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:83
verses.text: Therefore "His mercy is better than lives".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:84
verses.text: What lives? Those which for themselves men have chosen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:85
verses.text: One hath chosen for himself a life of business, another a country life, another a life of usury, another a military life; one this, another that.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:86
verses.text: Divers are the lives, but "better is Thy" life "than" our "lives".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:87
verses.text: "My lips shall praise Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:88
verses.text: My lips would not praise Thee, unless before me were to go Thy mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:89
verses.text: By Thy gift Thee I praise, through Thy mercy Thee I praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:90
verses.text: For I should not be able to praise God, unless He gave me to be able to praise Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:91
verses.text: "So I will speak good of Thee in my life, and in Thy name I will lift up my hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:92
verses.text: Now in my life which to me Thou hast given, not in that which I have chosen after the world with the rest among many lives, but that which Thou hast given to me through Thy mercy, that I should praise Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:93
verses.text: "So I will speak good of Thee in my life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:94
verses.text: What is "so"? That to Thy mercy I may ascribe my life wherein Thee I praise, not to my merits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:95
verses.text: "And in Thy name I will lift up my hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:96
verses.text: Lift up therefore hands in prayer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:97
verses.text: Our Lord hath lifted up for us His hands on the Cross, and stretched out were His hands for us, and therefore were His hands stretched out on the Cross, in order that our hands might be stretched out unto good works: because His Cross hath brought us mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:98
verses.text: Behold, He hath lifted up hands, and hath offered for us Himself a Sacrifice to God, and through that Sacrifice have been effaced all our sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:99
verses.text: Let us also lift up our hands to God in prayer: and our hands being lifted up to God shall not be confounded, if they be exercised in good works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:100
verses.text: For what doth he that lifteth up hands? Whence hath it been commanded that with hands lifted up we should pray to God? For the Apostle saith, "Lifting up pure hands without anger and dissension".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:101
verses.text: It is in order that when thou liftest up hands to God, there may come into thy mind thy works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:102
verses.text: For whereas those hands are lifted up that thou mayest obtain that which thou wilt, those same hands thou thinkest in good works to exercise, that they may not blush to be lifted up to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:103
verses.text: "In thy name I will lift up my hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:104
verses.text: Those are our prayers in this Idumaea, in this desert, in the land without water and without way, where for us Christ is the Way,  but not the way of this earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:105
verses.text: Already our fathers are dead, but God liveth: here we could not always have fathers, but there we shall alway have one living Father, when we have our father-land.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:106
verses.text: What sort of country is that? But thou lovest here riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:107
verses.text: God Himself shall be to thee thy riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:108
verses.text: But thou lovest a good fountain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:109
verses.text: What is more passing clear than that wisdom? What more bright? Whatsoever is an object of love here, in place of all thou shalt have Him that hath made all things, "as though with marrow and fatness my soul should be filled: and lips of exultation shall praise Thy name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:110
verses.text: In this desert, in Thy name I will lift up my hands: let my soul be filled as though with marrow and fatness, "and my lips with exultation shall praise Thy name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:111
verses.text: For now is prayer, so long as there is thirst: when thirst shall have passed away, there passeth away praying and there succeedeth praising.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:112
verses.text: "And lips of exultation shall praise Thy name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:113
verses.text: "If I have remembered Thee upon my bed, in the dawnings I did meditate on thee : because Thou hast become my helper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:114
verses.text: His "bed" he calleth his rest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:115
verses.text: When any one is at rest, let him be mindful of God; when any one is at rest, let him not by rest be dissolved, and forget God: if mindful he is of God when he is at rest, in his actions on God he doth meditate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:116
verses.text: For the dawn he hath called actions, because every man at dawn beginneth to do something.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:117
verses.text: What therefore hath he said? If therefore I was not mindful on my bed, in the dawn also I did not meditate on Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:118
verses.text: Can he that thinketh not of God when he is at leisure, in his actions think of God? But he that is mindful of Him when he is at rest, on the Same doth meditate when he is doing, lest in action he should come short.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:119
verses.text: Therefore he hath added what? "Because Thou has become my helper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:120
verses.text: For unless God aid our good works, they cannot be accomplished by us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:121
verses.text: And worthy things we ought to work: that is, as though in the light, since by Christ showing the way we work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:122
verses.text: Whosoever worketh evil things, in the night he worketh, not in the dawn; according to the Apostle, saying, "They that are drunken, in the night are drunken; and they that sleep, in the night do sleep; let us that are of the day, be sober".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:123
verses.text: He exhorteth us that after the day we should walk honestly: "As in the day, honestly let us walk".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:124
verses.text: And again, "Ye," he saith, "are sons of light, and sons of day; we are not of night nor of darkness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:125
verses.text: Who are sons of night, and sons of darkness? They that work all evil things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:126
verses.text: To such a degree they are sons of night, that they fear lest the things which they work should be seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:127
verses.text: No one therefore in the dawn worketh, except him that in Christ worketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:128
verses.text: But he that while at leisure is mindful of Christ, on the Same doth meditate in all his actions, and He is a helper to him in a good work, lest through his weakness he fail.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:129
verses.text: "And in the covering of Thy wings I will exult".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:130
verses.text: I am cheerful in good works, because over me is the covering of Thy wings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:131
verses.text: If thou protect me not, forasmuch as I am a chicken, the kite will seize me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:132
verses.text: For our Lord Himself saith in a certain place to that Jerusalem, a certain city, where He was crucified: "Jerusalem," He saith, "Jerusalem, how often I have willed to gather thy sons, as though a hen her chickens, and thou wouldest not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:133
verses.text: Little ones we are: therefore may God protect us under the shadow of His wings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:134
verses.text: What when we shall have grown greater? A good thing it is for us that even then He should protect us, so that under Him the greater, alway we be chickens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:135
verses.text: For alway He is greater, however much we may have grown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:136
verses.text: Let no one say, let Him protect me while I am a little one: as if sometime he would attain to such magnitude, as should be self-sufficient.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:137
verses.text: Without the protection of God, nought thou art.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:138
verses.text: Alway by Him let us desire to be protected: then alway in Him we shall have power to be great, if alway under Him little we be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:139
verses.text: "And in the covering of Thy wings I will exult".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:140
verses.text: "My soul hath been glued on behind Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:141
verses.text: See ye one longing, see ye one thirsting, see ye how he cleaveth to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:142
verses.text: Let there spring up in you this affection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:143
verses.text: If already it is sprouting, let it be rained upon and grow: let it come to such strength, that ye also may say from the whole heart, "My soul hath been glued on behind Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:144
verses.text: Where is that same glue? The glue itself is love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:145
verses.text: Have thou love, wherewith as with glue thy soul may be glued on behind God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:146
verses.text: Not with God, but behind God; that He may go before, thou mayest follow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:147
verses.text: For he that shall have willed to go before God, by his own counsel would live, and will not follow the commandments of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:148
verses.text: Because of this even Peter was rebuked, when he willed to give counsel to Christ, who was going to suffer for us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:149
verses.text: "Far be it from Thee, O Lord, be Thou merciful to Thyself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:150
verses.text: And the Lord, "Go back behind Me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things which are of God, but the things which are of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:151
verses.text: Wherefore, the things which are of men? Because to go before Me thou desirest, go back behind Me, in order that thou mayest follow me: so that now following Christ he might say, "My soul hath been glued on behind Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:152
verses.text: With reason he addeth, "Me Thy right hand hath taken up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:153
verses.text: This Christ hath said in us: that is in the Man which He was bearing for us, which He was offering for us, He hath said this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:154
verses.text: The Church also said this in Christ, she saith it in her Head: for she too hath suffered here great persecutions, and by her individual members even now she suffereth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:155
verses.text: "But themselves in vain have sought my soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:156
verses.text: They shall go unto the lower places of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:157
verses.text: Earth they were unwilling to lose, when they crucified Christ: into the lower places of the earth they have gone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:158
verses.text: What are the lower places of the earth? Earthly lusts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:159
verses.text: Better it is to walk upon earth, than by lust to go under earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:160
verses.text: For every one that in prejudice of his salvation desireth earthly things, is under the earth: because earth he hath put before him, earth upon himself he hath put, and himself beneath he hath laid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:161
verses.text: They therefore fearing to lose earth, said what of the Lord Jesus Christ, when they saw great multitudes go after Him, forasmuch as He was doing wonderful things? "If we shall have let Him go alive, there will come the Romans, and will take away from us both place and nation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:162
verses.text: They feared to lose earth, and they went under the earth: there befell them even what they feared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:163
verses.text: For they willed to kill Christ, that they might not lose earth; and earth they therefore lost, because Christ they slew.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:164
verses.text: For when Christ had been slain, because the Lord Himself had said to them, "The kingdom shall be taken from you, and shall be given up to a nation doing righteousness:" there followed them great calamities of persecutions: there conquered them Roman emperors, and kings of the nations: they were shut out from that very place where they crucified Christ, and now that place is full of Christian praisers: it hath no Jew, it hath been cleared of the enemies of Christ, it hath been fulfilled with the praisers of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:165
verses.text: Behold, they have lost at the hands of the Romans the place, because Christ they slew, who to this end slew, that they might not lose the place at the hands of the Romans.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:166
verses.text: Therefore, "They shall enter into the lower places of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:167
verses.text: "They shall be delivered unto the hands of the sword".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:168
verses.text: In truth, thus it hath visibly befallen them, they have been taken by storm by enemies breaking in.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:169
verses.text: "Portions of foxes they shall be".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:170
verses.text: Foxes he calleth the kings of the world, that then were when Judaea was conquered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:171
verses.text: Hear in order that ye may know and perceive, that those he calleth foxes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:172
verses.text: Herod the king the Lord Himself hath called a fox.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:173
verses.text: "Go ye," He saith, "and tell that fox".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:174
verses.text: See and observe, my brethren: Christ as King they would not have, and portions of foxes they have been made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:175
verses.text: For when Pilate the deputy governor in Judaea slew Christ at the voices of the Jews, he said to the same Jews, "Your King shall I crucify?" Because He was called King of the Jews, and He was the true King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:176
verses.text: And they rejecting Christ said, "We have no king but Caesar".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:177
verses.text: They rejected a Lamb, chose a fox: deservedly portions of foxes they were made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:178
verses.text: "The King in truth," is so written, because they chose a fox, a King in truth they would not have.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:179
verses.text: "The King in truth:" that is, the true King, to whom the title was inscribed, when He suffered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:180
verses.text: For Pilate set this title inscribed over His Head, "The King of the Jews," in the Hebrew, Greek, and Latin tongues: in order that all they that should pass by might read of the glory of the King, and the infamy of the Jews themselves, who, rejecting the true King, chose the fox Caesar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:181
verses.text: "The King in truth shall rejoice in God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:182
verses.text: They have been made portions of foxes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:183
verses.text: "Stopped up is the mouth of men speaking unjust things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:184
verses.text: No one dareth now openly to speak against Christ, now all men fear Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:185
verses.text: "For stopped up is the mouth of men speaking unjust things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:186
verses.text: When in weakness the Lamb was, even foxes were bold against the Lamb.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 64:187
verses.text: There conquered the Lion of the tribe of Judah, and the foxes were silenced.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:1
verses.text: Psalm LXIV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:2
verses.text: Though chiefly the Lord's Passion is noticed in this Psalm, neither could the Martyrs have been strong, unless they had beheld Him, that first suffered; nor such things would they have endured in suffering, as He did, unless they had hoped for such things in the Resurrection as He had showed of Himself: but your Holiness knoweth that our Head is our Lord Jesus Christ, and that all that cleave unto Him are the members of Him the Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:3
verses.text: And let no one say, that now-a-days in tribulation of passions we are not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:4
verses.text: For alway ye have heard this fact, how in those times the whole Church together as it were was smitten against, but now through individuals she is tried.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:5
verses.text: Bound indeed is the devil, that he may not do as much as he could, that he may not do as much as he would: nevertheless, he is permitted to tempt as much as is expedient to men advancing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:6
verses.text: It is not expedient for us to be without temptations: nor should we beseech God that we be not tempted, but that we be not "led into temptation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:7
verses.text: Say we, therefore, ourselves also: "Hearken, O God, to my prayer, while I am troubled; from fear of the enemy deliver my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:8
verses.text: Enemies have raged against the Martyrs: for what was that voice of Christ's Body praying? For this it was praying, to be delivered from enemies, and that enemies might not have power to slay them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:9
verses.text: Were they not therefore hearkened to, because they were slain; and hath God forsaken His servants of a contrite heart, and despised men hoping in Him? Far be it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:10
verses.text: For "who hath called upon God, and hath been forsaken; who hath hoped in Him, and hath been deserted by Him?" They were hearkened to therefore, and they were slain; and yet from enemies they were delivered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:11
verses.text: Others being afraid gave consent, and lived, and yet the same by enemies were swallowed up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:12
verses.text: The slain were delivered, the living were swallowed up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:13
verses.text: Thence is also that voice of thanksgiving, "Perchance alive they would have swallowed us up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:14
verses.text: Therefore for this prayeth the voice of the Martyrs, "From fear of the enemy deliver Thou my soul:" not so that the enemy may  not slay me, but that I may not fear an enemy slaying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:15
verses.text: For that to be fulfilled in the Psalm the servant prayeth, which but now in the Gospel the Lord was commanding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:16
verses.text: What but now was the Lord commanding? "Fear not them that kill the body, but the soul are not able to kill; but Him rather fear ye, that hath power to kill both body and soul in the hell of fire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:17
verses.text: And He repeated, "Yea, I say unto you, fear Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:18
verses.text: Who are they that kill the body? Enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:19
verses.text: What was the Lord commanding? That they should not be feared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:20
verses.text: Be prayer offered, therefore, that He may grant what He hath commanded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:21
verses.text: "From fear of the enemy deliver my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:22
verses.text: Deliver me from fear of the enemy, and make me submit to the fear of Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:23
verses.text: I would not fear him that killeth the body, but I would fear Him that hath power to kill both body and soul in the hell of fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:24
verses.text: For not from fear would I be free: but from fear of the enemy being free, under fear of the Lord a servant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:25
verses.text: "Thou hast protected me from the gathering together of malignants, and from the multitude of men working iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:26
verses.text: Now upon Himself our Head let us look.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:27
verses.text: Like things many Martyrs have suffered: but nothing doth shine out so brightly as the Head of Martyrs; in Him rather let us behold what they have gone through.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:28
verses.text: Protected He was from the multitude of malignants, God protecting Himself, the Son Himself and the Manhood which He was carrying protecting His flesh: because Son of Man He is, and Son of God He is; Son of God because of the form of God, Son of Man because of the form of a servant: having in His power to lay down His life: and to take it again To Him what could enemies do? They killed body, soul they killed not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:29
verses.text: Observe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:30
verses.text: Too little therefore it were for the Lord to exhort the Martyrs with word, unless He had enforced it by example.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:31
verses.text: Ye know what a gathering together there was of malignant Jews, and what a multitude there was of men working iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:32
verses.text: What iniquity? That wherewith they willed to kill the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:33
verses.text: "So many good works," He saith, "I have shown to you, for which of these will ye to kill Me?" He endured all their infirm, He healed all their sick, He preached the Kingdom of Heaven, He held not His peace at their vices, so that these same should have been displeasing to them, rather than the Physician by whom they were being made whole: for all these His remedies being ungrateful, like men delirious in high fever raving at the physician, they devised the plan of destroying Him that had come to heal them; as though therein they would prove whether He were indeed a man, that could die, or were somewhat above men, and would not suffer Himself to die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:34
verses.text: The word of these same men we perceive in the wisdom of Solomon: "with death most vile," say they, "let us condemn Him; let us question Him, for there will be regard in the discourses of Him; for if truly Son of God He is, let Him deliver Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:35
verses.text: Let us see therefore what was done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:36
verses.text: "For they have whet like a sword their tongues".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:37
verses.text: Which saith another Psalm also, "Sons of men; their teeth are arms and arrows, and their tongue is a sharp sword".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:38
verses.text: Let not the Jews say, we have not killed Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:39
verses.text: For to this end they gave Him to Pilate the judge, in order that they themselves might seem as it were guiltless of His death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:40
verses.text: But if he is guilty because he did it though unwillingly, are they innocent who compelled him to do it? By no means.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:41
verses.text: But he gave sentence against Him, and commanded Him to be crucified: and in a manner himself killed Him; ye also, O ye Jews, killed Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:42
verses.text: Whence did ye kill Him? With the sword of the tongue: for ye did whet your tongues.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:43
verses.text: And when did ye smite, except when ye cried out, "Crucify, Crucify"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:44
verses.text: But on this account we must not pass over that which hath come into mind, lest perchance the reading of the Divine Scriptures should disquiet any one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:45
verses.text: One Evangelist saith that the Lord was crucified at the sixth hour, and another at the third hour: unless we understand it, we are disquieted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:46
verses.text: And when the sixth hour was already beginning, Pilate is said to have sat on the judgment-seat: and in reality when the Lord was lifted up upon the tree, it was the sixth hour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:47
verses.text: But another Evangelist, looking unto the mind of the Jews, how they wished themselves to seem guiltless of the death of the Lord, by his account proveth them guilty, saying, that the Lord was crucified at the third hour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:48
verses.text: But considering all the circumstance of the history, how many things might have been done, when before Pilate the Lord was being accused, in order that He might be crucified; we find that it might have been the third hour, when they cried out, "Crucify, Crucify".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:49
verses.text: Therefore with more truth they killed at the time when they cried out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:50
verses.text: The ministers of the magistrate at the sixth hour crucified, the transgressors of the law at the third hour cried out: that which those did with hands at the sixth hour, these did with tongue at the third hour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:51
verses.text: More guilty are they that with crying out were raging, than they that in obedience were ministering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:52
verses.text: This is the whole of the Jews' sagacity, this is that which they sought as some great matter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:53
verses.text: Let us kill and let us not kill: so let us kill, as that we may not ourselves be judged to have killed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:54
verses.text: "They have bended the bow, a bitter thing, in order that they may shoot in secret One unspotted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:55
verses.text: The bow he calleth lyings in wait.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:56
verses.text: For he that with sword fighteth hand to hand, openly fighteth: he that shooteth an arrow deceiveth, in order to strike.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:57
verses.text: For the arrow smiteth, before it is foreseen to come to wound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:58
verses.text: But whom could the lyings in wait of the human heart escape? Would they escape our Lord Jesus Christ, who had no need that any one should bear witness to Him of man? "For Himself knew what was in man," as the Evangelist testifieth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:59
verses.text: Nevertheless, let us hear them, and look upon them in their doings as if the Lord knew not what they devise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:60
verses.text: The expression he used, "They have bended the bow," is the same as, "in secret:" as if they were deceiving by lyings in wait.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:61
verses.text: For ye know by what artifices they did this, how with money they bribed a disciple that clave to Him, in order that He might be betrayed to them,  how they procured false witnesses; with what lyings in wait and artifices they wrought, "in order that they might shoot in secret One unspotted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:62
verses.text: Great iniquity! Behold from a secret place there cometh an arrow, which striketh One unspotted, who had not even so much of spot as could be pierced with an arrow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:63
verses.text: A Lamb indeed He is unspotted, wholly unspotted, alway unspotted; not one from whom spots have been removed but that hath contracted not any spots.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:64
verses.text: For He hath made many unspotted by forgiving sins, being Himself unspotted by not having sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:65
verses.text: "Suddenly they shall shoot Him, and shall not fear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:66
verses.text: O heart hardened, to wish to kill a Man that did raise the dead! "Suddenly:" that is, insidiously, as if unexpectedly, as if not foreseen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:67
verses.text: For the Lord was like to one knowing not, being among men knowing not what He knew not and what He knew: yea, knowing not that there was nothing that He knew not, and that He knew all things, and to this end had come in order that they might do that which they thought they did by their own power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:68
verses.text: "They have confirmed to themselves malignant discourse".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:69
verses.text: There were done so great miracles, they were not moved, they persisted in the design of the evil discourse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:70
verses.text: He was given up to the judge: the judge trembleth, and they tremble not that have given Him up to the judge: trembleth power, and ferocity trembleth not: he would wash his hands, and they stain their tongues.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:71
verses.text: But wherefore this? "They have confirmed to themselves malignant discourse".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:72
verses.text: How many things did Pilate, how many things that they might be restrained! What said he? what did he? But "they have confirmed to themselves malignant discourse: Crucify, crucify".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:73
verses.text: The repetition is the confirmation of the "malignant discourse".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:74
verses.text: Let us see in what manner "they have confirmed to themselves malignant discourse".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:75
verses.text: "Your King shall I crucify?" They said, "We have no king but Caesar alone".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:76
verses.text: He was offering for King the Son of God: to a man they betook themselves: worthy were they to have the one, and not have the Other.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:77
verses.text: "I find not anything in this Man," saith the judge, "wherefore He is worthy of death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:78
verses.text: And they that "confirmed malignant discourse," said, "His blood be upon us and upon our sons".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:79
verses.text: "They confirmed malignant discourse," not to the Lord, but to "themselves".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:80
verses.text: For how not to themselves when they say, "Upon us and upon our sons"? That which therefore they confirmed, to themselves they confirmed: because the same voice is elsewhere, "They dug before my face a ditch, and fell into it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:81
verses.text: Death killed not the Lord, but He death: but them iniquity killed, because they would not kill iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:82
verses.text: "They told, in order that they might hide traps: they said, Who shall see them?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:83
verses.text: They thought they would escape Him, whom they were killing, that they would escape God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:84
verses.text: Behold, suppose Christ was a man, like the rest of men, and knew not what was being contrived for Him: doth God also know not? O heart of man! wherefore hast thou said to thyself, Who seeth me? when He seeth that hath made thee? "They said, Who shall see them?" God did see, Christ also was seeing: because Christ is also God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:85
verses.text: But wherefore did they think that He saw not? Hear the words following.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:86
verses.text: "They have searched out iniquity, they have failed, searching searchings" : that is, deadly and acute designs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:87
verses.text: Let Him not be betrayed by us, but by His disciple: let Him not be killed by us, but by the judge: let us do all, and let us seem to have done nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:88
verses.text: But what befell them? "They failed searching searchings".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:89
verses.text: Whence? Because he saith, "Who shall see them?" that is, that no one saw  them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:90
verses.text: This they were saying, this among themselves they thought, that no one saw them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:91
verses.text: See what befalleth an evil soul: it departeth from the light of truth, and because itself seeth not God, it thinketh that itself is not seen by God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:92
verses.text: For what followeth? "There shall draw near a man and a deep heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:93
verses.text: They said, Who shall see us? They failed in searching searchings, evil counsels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:94
verses.text: There drew near a man to those same counsels, He suffered Himself to be held as a man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:95
verses.text: For He would not have been held except He were man, or have been seen except He were man, or have been smitten except He were man, or have been crucified or have died except He were man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:96
verses.text: There drew near a man therefore to all those sufferings, which in Him would have been of no avail except He were Man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:97
verses.text: But if He were not Man, there would not have been deliverance for man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:98
verses.text: There hath drawn near a Man "and a deep heart," that is, a secret "heart:" presenting before human faces Man, keeping within God: concealing the "form of God," wherein He is equal with the Father, and presenting the form of a servant, wherein He is less than the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:99
verses.text: For Himself hath spoken of both: but one thing there is which He saith in the form of God, another thing in the form of a servant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:100
verses.text: He hath said in the form of God, "I and the Father are one:" He hath said in the form of a servant, "For the Father is greater than I".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:101
verses.text: Whence in the form of God saith He, "I and the Father are one"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:102
verses.text: "Arrows of infants have been made the strokes of them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:103
verses.text: Where is that savageness? where is that roar of the lion, of the people roaring and saying, "Crucify, Crucify"? Where are the lyings in wait of men bending the bow? Have not "the strokes of them been made the arrows of infants"? Ye know in what manner infants make to themselves arrows of little canes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:104
verses.text: What do they strike, or whence do they strike? What is the hand, or what the weapon? what are the arms, or what the limbs?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:105
verses.text: "And the tongues of them have been made weak upon them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:106
verses.text: Let them whet now their tongues like a sword, let them confirm to themselves malignant discourse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:107
verses.text: Deservedly to themselves they have confirmed it, because "the tongues of them have been made weak upon them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:108
verses.text: Could this be strong against God? "Iniquity," he saith, "hath lied to itself;" "their tongues have been made weak upon them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:109
verses.text: Behold, the Lord hath risen, that was killed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:110
verses.text: What thinkest thou of Him who from the cross came not down, and from the tomb rose again? What therefore did they effect? But even if the Lord had not risen again, what would they have effected, except what the persecutors of the martyrs have also effected? For the Martyrs have not yet risen again, and nevertheless they have effected nothing; of them not yet rising again we are now celebrating the nativities.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:111
verses.text: Where is the madness of their raging? To what did they bring those their searchings, in which searchings they failed, so that even, when the Lord was dead and buried, they set guards at the tomb? For they said to Pilate, "That deceiver;" by this name the Lord Jesus Christ was called, for the comfort of His servants when they are called deceivers; they say therefore to Pilate, "That deceiver said when yet living, After three days I will rise again:" They set for guards soldiers at the sepulchre.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:112
verses.text: At the earth quaking, the Lord rose again: such miracles were done about the sepulchre, that even the very soldiers that had come for guards were made witnesses, if they chose to tell the truth: but the same covetousness which had led captive a disciple, the companion of Christ, led captive also the soldier that was guard of the sepulchre.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:113
verses.text: We give you, they say, money; and say ye, while yourselves were sleeping there came His disciples, and took Him away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:114
verses.text: Sleeping witnesses ye adduce: truly thou thyself hast fallen asleep, that in searching such devices hast failed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:115
verses.text: If they were sleeping, what could they see? if nothing they saw, how are they witnesses? But "they failed in searching searchings:" failed of the light of God, failed in the very completion of their designs: when that which they willed, nowise they were able to complete, surely they failed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:116
verses.text: Wherefore this? Because "there drew near a Man and a deep heart, and God was exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:117
verses.text: "And every man feared".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:118
verses.text: They that feared not, were not even men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:119
verses.text: "Every man feared;" that is, every one using reason to perceive the things which were done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:120
verses.text: Whence they that feared not, must rather be called cattle, rather beasts savage and cruel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:121
verses.text: A lion ramping and roaring is that people as yet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:122
verses.text: But in truth every man feared: that is, they that would believe, that trembled at the judgment to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:123
verses.text: "And every man feared: and they declared the works of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:124
verses.text: "And every man hath feared: and they have declared the works of God, and His doings they have perceived".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:125
verses.text: What is, "His doings they have perceived"? Was it, O Lord Jesus Christ, that Thou wast silent, and like a sheep for a victim wast being led, and didst not open before the shearer Thy mouth, and we thought Thee to be set in smiting and in grief, and knowing how to bear weakness? Was it that Thou wast hiding Thy beauty, O Thou beautiful in form before the sons of men? Was it that Thou didst not seem to have beauty nor grace? Thou didst bear on the Cross men reviling and saying, "If Son of God He is, let Him come down from the Cross".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:126
verses.text: This thing they, that would have had Him come down from the Cross, perceived not: but when He rose again, and being glorified ascended into Heaven, they perceived the works of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:127
verses.text: "The just man shall rejoice in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:128
verses.text: Now the just man is not sad.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:129
verses.text: For sad were the disciples at the Lord's being crucified; overcome with sadness, sorrowing they departed, they thought they had lost hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:130
verses.text: He rose again, even when appearing to them He found them sad.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:131
verses.text: He held the eyes of two men that walked in the way, so that by them he was not known, and He found them groaning and sighing, and He held them until He had expounded the Scriptures, and by the same Scriptures had shown that so it ought to have been done as it was done For He showed in the Scriptures, how after the third day it behoved the Lord to rise again And how on the third day would He have risen again, if from the Cross He had come down?Therefore let us all rejoice in the Lord, let us all after the faith be One Just Man, and let us all in one Body hold One Head, and let us rejoice in the Lord, not in ourselves: because our Good is not ourselves to ourselves, but He that hath made us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:132
verses.text: Himself is our good to make us glad.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:133
verses.text: And let no one rejoice in himself, no one rely on himself, no one despair of himself: let no one rely on any man, whom he ought to bring in to be the partner of his own hope, not the giver of the hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:134
verses.text: Now because the Lord hath risen again, now because He hath ascended into Heaven, now because He hath showed that there is another life, now because it is evident that His counsels, wherein He lay concealed in deep heart, were not empty, because to this end That Blood was shed to be the price of the redeemed; now because all things are evident, because all things have been preached, because all things have been believed, under the whole of heaven, "the just man shall rejoice in the Lord, and shall hope in Him; and all men shall be praised that are right in heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:135
verses.text: God is displeasing to thee, and thou art pleasing to thyself, of perverted and crooked heart thou art: and this is the worse, that the heart of God thou wouldest correct by thy heart, to make Him do what thou wilt have whereas thou oughtest to do what He willeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:136
verses.text: What then? Thou wouldest make crooked the heart of God which alway is right, according to the depravity of thy own heart? How much better to correct thy heart by the rectitude of God? Hath not thy Lord taught thee this, of Whose Passion but now were we speaking? Was He not bearing thy weakness, when He said, "Sad is My soul even unto death"? Was He not figuring thyself in Himself, when He was saying, "Father, if it be possible, let there pass from Me this cup"? For the hearts of the Father and of the Son were not two and different: but in the form of a servant He carried thy heart, that He might teach it by His example.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:137
verses.text: Now behold trouble found out as it were another heart of thine, which willed that there should pass away that which was impending: but God would not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:138
verses.text: God consenteth not to thy heart, do thou consent to the heart of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:139
verses.text: What followeth? If "there shall be praised all men right in heart," there shall be condemned the crooked in heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:140
verses.text: Two things are set before thee now, choose while there is time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:141
verses.text: If of crooked heart thou hast become, there will come that Judgment, there will appear all the reasons on account of which God doeth all these things: and thou that wouldest not in this life correct thy heart by the rectitude of God, and prepare thyself for the right hand, where "there shall be praised all men right in heart," wilt be on the left, where at that time thou shalt hear, "Go ye into fire everlasting, that hath been prepared for the devil and his angels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:142
verses.text: And will there be then t ime to correct the heart? Now therefore correct, brethren, now correct.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:143
verses.text: Who doth hinder? Psalm is chanted, Gospel is read, Reader crieth, Preacher crieth; long-suffering is the Lord; thou sinnest, and He spareth; still thou sinnest, still He spareth, and still thou addest sin to sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:144
verses.text: How long is God long-suffering? Thou wilt find God just also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:145
verses.text: We terrify because we fear; teach us not to fear, and we terrify no more.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:146
verses.text: But better it is that God teach us to fear, than that any man teach us not to fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:147
verses.text: Thou bringest forth grain, barn expect thou; bringest forth thorns, fire expect thou.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:148
verses.text: But not yet hath come either the time of the barn or the time of the fire: now let there be preparation, and there will not be fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 65:149
verses.text: In the name of Christ both we who speak are living, and ye to whom we speak are living: for amending our plan, and changing evil life into a good life, is there no place, is there no time? Can it not, if thou wilt, be done to-day? Can it not, if thou wilt, be now done? What must thou buy in order to do it, what specifics must thou seek? To what Indies must thou sail? What ship prepare? Lo, while I am speaking, change the heart; and there is done what so often and so long while is cried out for, that it be done, and which bringeth forth everlasting punishment if it be not done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:1
verses.text: Psalm LXV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:2
verses.text: The voice of holy prophecy  must be confessed in the very title of this Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:3
verses.text: It is inscribed, "Unto the end, a Psalm of David, a song of Jeremiah and Ezekiel, on account of the people of transmigration when they were beginning to go forth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:4
verses.text: How it fared with our fathers in the time of the transmigration to Babylon, is not known to all, but only to those that diligently study the Holy Scriptures, either by hearing or by reading.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:5
verses.text: For the captive people Israel from the city of Jerusalem was led into slavery unto Babylon But holy Jeremiah prophesied, that after seventy years the people would return out of captivity, and would rebuild the very city Jerusalem, which they had mourned as having been overthrown by enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:6
verses.text: But at that time there were prophets in that captivity of the people dwelling in Babylon, among whom was also the prophet Ezekiel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:7
verses.text: But that people was waiting until there should be fulfilled the space of seventy years, according to the prophecy of Jeremiah It came to pass, when the seventy years had been completed, the temple was restored which had been thrown down: and there returned from captivity a great part of that people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:8
verses.text: But whereas the Apostle saith, "these things in figure happened unto them, but they have been written for our sakes, upon whom the end of the world hath come:" we also ought to know first our captivity, then our deliverance: we ought to know the Babylon wherein we are captives, and the Jerusalem for a return to which we are sighing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:9
verses.text: For these two cities, according to the letter, in reality are two cities.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:10
verses.text: And the former Jerusalem indeed by the Jews is not now inhabited.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:11
verses.text: For after the crucifixion of the Lord vengeance was taken upon them with a great scourge, and being rooted up from that place where, with impious licentiousness being infuriated, they had madly raged against their Physician, they have been dispersed throughout all nations, and that land hath been given to Christians: and there is fulfilled what the Lord had said to them, "Therefore the kingdom shall be taken away from you, and it shall be given to a nation doing justice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:12
verses.text: But when they saw great multitudes then following the Lord, preaching the kingdom of Heaven, and doing wonderful things, the rulers of that city said, "If we shall have let Him go, all men will go after Him, and there shall come the Romans, and shall take from us both place and nation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:13
verses.text: That they might not lose their place, they killed the Lord; and they lost it, even because they killed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:14
verses.text: Therefore that city, being one earthly, did bear the figure of a certain city everlasting in the Heavens: but when that which was signified began more evidently to be preached, the shadow, whereby it was being signified, was thrown down: for this reason in that place now the temple is no more, which had been constructed for the image of the future Body of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:15
verses.text: We have the light, the shadow hath passed away: nevertheless, still in a kind of captivity we are: "So long as we are," he saith, "in the body, we are sojourning afar from the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:16
verses.text: And see ye the names of those two cities, Babylon and Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:17
verses.text: Babylon is interpreted confusion, Jerusalem vision of peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:18
verses.text: Observe now the city of confusion, in order that ye may perceive the vision of peace; that ye may endure that, sigh for this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:19
verses.text: Whereby can those two cities be distinguished? Can we anywise now separate them from each other? They are mingled, and from the very beginning of mankind mingled they run on unto the end of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:20
verses.text: Jerusalem received beginning through Abel, Babylon through Cain: for the buildings of the cities were afterwards erected.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:21
verses.text: That Jerusalem in the land of the Jebusites was builded: for at first it used to be called Jebus, from thence the nation of the Jebusites was expelled, when the people of God was delivered from Egypt, and led into the land of promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:22
verses.text: But Babylon was builded in the most interior regions of Persia, which for a long time raised its head above the rest of nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:23
verses.text: These two cities then at particular times were builded, so that there might be shown a figure of two cities begun of old, and to remain even unto the end in this world, but at the end to be severed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:24
verses.text: Whereby then can we now show them, that are mingled? At that time the Lord shall show, when some He shall set on the right hand, others on the left.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:25
verses.text: Jerusalem on the right hand shall be, Babylon on the left.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:26
verses.text: Two loves make up these two cities: love of God maketh Jerusalem, love of the world maketh Babylon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:27
verses.text: Therefore let each one question himself as to what he loveth: and he shall find of which he is a citizen: and if he shall have found himself to be a citizen of Babylon, let him root out cupidity, implant charity: but if he shall have found himself a citizen of Jerusalem, let him endure captivity, hope for liberty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:28
verses.text: Now therefore let us hear of, brethren, hear of, and sing of, and long for, that city whereof we are citizens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:29
verses.text: And what are the joys which are sung of to us? In what manner in ourselves is formed again the love of our city, which by long sojourning we had forgotten? But our Father hath sent from thence letters to us, God hath supplied to us the Scriptures, by which letters there should be wrought in us a longing for return: because by loving our sojourning, to enemies we had turned our face, and our back to our fatherland.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:30
verses.text: What then is here sung?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:31
verses.text: "For Thee a hymn is meet, O God, in Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:32
verses.text: That fatherland is Sion: Jerusalem is the very same as Sion; and of this name the interpretation ye ought to know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:33
verses.text: As Jerusalem is interpreted vision of peace, so Sion Beholding, that is, vision and contemplation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:34
verses.text: Some great inexplicable sight to us is promised: and this is God Himself that hath builded the city.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:35
verses.text: Beauteous and graceful the city, how much more beauteous a Builder it hath! "For Thee a hymn is meet, O God," he saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:36
verses.text: But where? "In Sion:" in Babylon it is not meet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:37
verses.text: For when a man beginneth to be renewed, already with heart in Jerusalem he singeth, with the Apostle saying, "Our conversation is in the Heavens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:38
verses.text: For "in the flesh though walking," he saith, "not after the flesh we war".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:39
verses.text: Already in longing we are there, already hope into that land, as it were an anchor, we have sent before, lest in this sea being tossed we suffer shipwreck.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:40
verses.text: In like manner therefore as of a ship which is at anchor, we rightly say that already she is come to land, for still she rolleth, but to land in a manner she hath been brought safe in the teeth of winds and in the teeth of storms; so against the temptations of this sojourning, our hope being grounded in that city Jerusalem causeth us not to be carried away upon rocks.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:41
verses.text: He therefore that according to this hope singeth, in that city singeth: let him therefore say, "For Thee a hymn is meet, O God, in Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:42
verses.text: "And to Thee shall there be paid a vow in Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:43
verses.text: Here we vow, and a good thing it is that there we should pay.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:44
verses.text: But who are they that here do vow and pay not? They that persevere not even unto the end in that which they have vowed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:45
verses.text: Whence saith another Psalm, "Vow ye, and pay ye unto the Lord your God:" and, "to Thee shall it be paid in Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:46
