verses.text: For there shall we be whole, that is, entire in the resurrection of just men: there shall be paid our whole vow, not soul alone, but the very flesh also, no longer corruptible, because no longer in Babylon, but now a body heavenly and changed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:47
verses.text: What sort of change is promised? "For we all shall rise again," saith the Apostle, "but we shall not all be changed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:48
verses.text: Where is, O death, thy sting?" For now while there begin in use the first-fruits of the mind, from whence is the longing for Jerusalem, many things of corruptible flesh do contend against us, which will not contend, when death shall have been swallowed up in victory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:49
verses.text: Peace shall conquer, and war shall be ended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:50
verses.text: But when peace shall conquer, that city shall conquer which is called the vision of peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:51
verses.text: On the part of death therefore shall be no contention.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:52
verses.text: Now with how great a death do we contend! For thence are carnal pleasures, which to us even unlawfully do suggest many things: to which we give no consent, but nevertheless in giving no consent we contend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:53
verses.text: "Hearken," he saith, "to my prayer, unto Thee every flesh shall come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:54
verses.text: And we have the Lord saying, that there was given to Him "power over every flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:55
verses.text: That King therefore began even now to appear, when there was being said, "Unto Thee every flesh shall come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:56
verses.text: "To Thee," he saith, "every flesh shall come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:57
verses.text: Wherefore to Him shall "every" flesh come? Because flesh He hath taken to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:58
verses.text: Whither shall there come every flesh? He took the first-fruits thereof out of the womb of the Virgin; and now that the first-fruits have been taken to Him, the rest shall follow, in order that the holocaust may be completed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:59
verses.text: Whence then "every flesh"? Every man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:60
verses.text: And whence every man? Have all been foretold, as going to believe in Christ? Have not many ungodly men been foretold, that shall be condemned also? Do not daily men not believing die in their own unbelief? After what manner therefore do we understand, "Unto Thee every flesh shall come"? By "every flesh" he hath signified, "flesh of every kind:" out of every kind of flesh they shall come to Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:61
verses.text: What is, out of every kind of flesh? Have there come poor men, and have there not come rich men? Have there come humble men, and not come lofty men? Have there come unlearned men, and not come learned men? Have there come men, and not come women? Have there come masters, and not come servants? Have there come old men, and not come young men; or have there come young men, and not come youths; or have there come youths, and not come boys; or have there come boys, and have there not been brought infants? In a word, have there come Jews  (for thence were the Apostles, thence many thousands of men at first betraying, afterwards believing), and have there not come Greeks; or have there come Greeks, and not come Romans; or have there come Romans, and not come Barbarians? And who could number all nations coming to Him, to whom hath been said, "Unto Thee every flesh shall come"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:62
verses.text: "The discourses of unjust men have prevailed over us, and our iniquities Thou shalt propitiate".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:63
verses.text: Every man, in whatsoever place he is born, of that same land or region or city learneth the language, is habituated to the manners and life of that place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:64
verses.text: What should a boy do, born among Heathens, to avoid worshipping a stone, inasmuch as his parents have suggested that worship? from them the first words he hath heard, that error with his milk he hath sucked in; and because they that used to speak were elders, and the boy that was learning to speak was an infant, what could the little one do but follow the authority of elders, and deem that to be good which they recommended? Therefore nations that are converted to Christ afterwards, and taking to heart the impieties of their parents, and saying now what the prophet Jeremias himself said, "Truly a lie our fathers have worshipped, vanity which hath not profited them"—when, I say, they now say this, they renounce the opinions and blasphemies of their unjust parents.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:65
verses.text: There have led us away men teaching evil things, citizens of Babylon they have made us, we have left the Creator, have adored the creature: have left Him by whom we were made, have adored that which we ourselves have made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:66
verses.text: For "the discourses of unjust men have prevailed over us:" but nevertheless they have not crushed us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:67
verses.text: Wherefore? "Our impieties Thou shalt propitiate," is not said except to some priest offering somewhat, whereby impiety may be expiated and propitiated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:68
verses.text: For impiety is then said to be propitiated, when God is made propitious to the impiety.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:69
verses.text: What is it for God to be made propitious to impiety? It is, His becoming forgiving, and giving pardon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:70
verses.text: But in order that God's pardon may be obtained, propitiation is made through some sacrifice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:71
verses.text: There hath come forth therefore, sent from God the Lord, One our Priest; He took upon Him from us that which He might offer to the Lord; we are speaking of those same first-fruits of the flesh from the womb of the Virgin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:72
verses.text: This holocaust He offered to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:73
verses.text: He stretched out His hands on the Cross, in order that He might say, "Let My prayer be directed as incense in Thy sight, and the lifting up of My hands an evening sacrifice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:74
verses.text: As ye know, the Lord about eventide hung on the Cross: and our impieties were propitiated; otherwise they had swallowed up: the discourses of unjust men had prevailed over us; there had led us astray preachers of Jupiter, and of Saturn, and of Mercury: "the discourses of ungodly men had prevailed over us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:75
verses.text: But what wilt Thou do? "Our impieties Thou wilt propitiate".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:76
verses.text: Thou art the priest, Thou the victim; Thou the offerer, Thou the offering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:77
verses.text: "Blessed is he whom Thou hast chosen, and hast taken to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:78
verses.text: Who is he that is chosen by Him and taken to Him? Was any one chosen by our Saviour Jesus Christ, or was Himself after the flesh, because He is man, chosen and taken to Him?Or hath not rather Christ Himself taken to Him some blessed one, and the same whom He hath taken to Him is not spoken of in the plural number but in the singular? For one man He hath taken to Him, because unity He hath taken to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:79
verses.text: Schisms He hath not taken to Him, heresies He hath not taken to Him: a multitude they have made of themselves, there is not one to be taken to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:80
verses.text: But they that abide in the bond of Christ and are the members of Him, make in a manner one man, of whom saith the Apostle, "Until we all arrive at the acknowledging of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the age of the fulness of Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:81
verses.text: Therefore one man is taken to Him, to which the Head is Christ; because "the Head of the man is Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:82
verses.text: The same is that blessed man that "hath not departed in the counsel of ungodly men," and the like things which there are spoken of: the same is He that is taken to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:83
verses.text: He is not without us, in His own members we are, under one Head we are governed, by one Spirit we all live, one fatherland we all long for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:84
verses.text: And to us He will give what? "He shall inhabit," he saith, "in Thy courts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:85
verses.text: Jerusalem, that is, to which they sing that begin to go forth from Babylon: "He shall inhabit in Thy courts: we shall be filled with the good things of Thy House".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:86
verses.text: What are the good things of the House of God? Brethren, let us set before ourselves some rich house, with what numerous good things it is crowded, how abundantly it is furnished, how many vessels there are there of gold and also of silver; how great an establishment of servants, how many horses and animals, in a word, how much the house itself delights us with pictures, marble, ceilings, pillars, recesses, chambers:—all such things are indeed objects of desire, but still they are of the confusion of Babylon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:87
verses.text: Cut off all such longings, O citizen of Jerusalem, cut them off; if thou wilt return, let not captivity delight thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:88
verses.text: But hast thou already begun to go forth? Do not look back, do not loiter on the road.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:89
verses.text: Still there are not wanting foes to recommend thee captivity and sojourning: no longer let there prevail against thee the discourses of ungodly men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:90
verses.text: For the House of God long thou, and for the good things of that House long thou: but do not long for such things as thou art wont to long for either in thy house, or in the house of thy neighbour, or in the house of thy patron.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:91
verses.text: "Thy holy Temple is marvellous in righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:92
verses.text: These are the good things of that House.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:93
verses.text: He hath not said, Thy holy Temple is marvellous in pillars, marvellous in marbles, marvellous in glided ceilings; but is "marvellous in righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:94
verses.text: Without thou hast eyes wherewith thou mayest see marbles, and gold: within is an eye wherewith may be seen the beauty of righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:95
verses.text: If there is no beauty in righteousness, why is a righteous old man loved? What bringeth he in body that may please the eyes? Crooked limbs, brow wrinkled, head blanched with gray hairs, dotage everywhere full of plaints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:96
verses.text: But perchance because thine eyes this decrepit old man pleaseth not, thine ears he pleaseth: with what words? with what song? Even if perchance when a young man he sang well, all with age hath been lost.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:97
verses.text: Doth perchance the sound of his words please thine ears, that can hardly articulate whole words for loss of teeth? Nevertheless, if righteous he is, if another man's goods he coveteth not, if of his own that he possesseth he distributeth to the needy, if he giveth good advice, and soundly judgeth, if he believeth the entire faith, if for his belief in the faith he is ready to expend even those very shattered limbs, for many Martyrs are even old men; why do we love him? What good thing in him do we see with the eyes of the flesh? Not any.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:98
verses.text: There is therefore a kind of beauty in righteousness, which we see with the eye of the heart, and we love, and we kindle with affection: how much men found to love in those same Martyrs, though beasts tare their limbs! Is it possible but that when blood was staining all parts, when with the teeth of monsters their bowels gushed out, the eyes had nothing but objects to shudder at? What was there to be loved, except that in that hideous spectacle of mangled limbs, entire was the beauty of righteousness? These are the good things of the House of God, with these prepare thyself to be satisfied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:99
verses.text: "Blessed they which hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:100
verses.text: "Thy holy Temple is marvellous in righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:101
verses.text: And that same temple, brethren, do not imagine to be aught but yourselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:102
verses.text: Love ye righteousness, and ye are the Temple of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:103
verses.text: "Hearken to us, O God, our Saviour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:104
verses.text: He hath disclosed now Whom he nameth as God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:105
verses.text: The "Saviour" specially is the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:106
verses.text: It hath appeared now more openly of Whom he had said, "Unto Thee every flesh shall come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:107
verses.text: That One Man that is taken unto Him into the Temple of God, is both many and is One.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:108
verses.text: In the person of One he hath said, "Hearken, O God, i-e:, to my hunger:" and because the same One of many is composed, now he saith, "Hearken to us, O God, our Saviour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:109
verses.text: Hear Him now more openly preached: "Hearken to us, O God, our Saviour, the Hope of all the ends of the earth and in the sea afar".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:110
verses.text: Behold wherefore hath been said "Unto Thee every flesh shall come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:111
verses.text: From every quarter they come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:112
verses.text: "Hope of all the ends of the earth," not hope of one corner, not hope of Judaea alone, not hope of Africa alone, not hope of Pannonia, not hope of East or of West: but "Hope of all the ends of the earth, and in the sea afar:" of the very ends of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:113
verses.text: "And in the sea afar:" and because in the sea, therefore afar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:114
verses.text: For the sea by a figure is spoken of this world, with saltness bitter, with storms troubled; where men of perverse and depraved appetites have become like fishes devouring one another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:115
verses.text: Observe the evil sea, bitter sea, with waves violent, observe with what sort of men it is filled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:116
verses.text: Who desireth an inheritance except through the death of another? Who desireth gain except by the loss of another? By the fall of others how many men wish to be exalted? How many, in order that they may buy, desire for other men to sell their goods? How they mutually oppress, and how they that are able do devour! And when one fish hath devoured, the greater the less, itself also is devoured by some greater.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:117
verses.text: Because evil fishes that were taken within the nets they said they would not endure; they themselves have become more evil than they whom they said they could not endure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:118
verses.text: For those nets did take fishes both good and evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:119
verses.text: The Lord saith, "The kingdom of Heaven is like to a sein cast into the sea, which gathereth of every kind, which, when it had been filled, drawing out, and sitting on the shore, they gathered the good into vessels, but the evil they cast out: so it shall be," He saith, "in the consummation of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:120
verses.text: He showeth what is the shore, He showeth what is the end of the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:121
verses.text: "The angels shall go forth, and shall sever the evil from the midst of the just, and shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:122
verses.text: Ha! ye citizens of Jerusalem that are within the nets, and are good fishes; endure the evil, the nets break ye not: together with them ye are in a sea, not together with them will ye be in the vessels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:123
verses.text: For "Hope" He is "of the ends of the earth," Himself is Hope "also in the sea afar".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:124
verses.text: Afar, because also in the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:125
verses.text: "Preparing mountains in His strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:126
verses.text: Not in their strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:127
verses.text: For He hath prepared great preachers, and those same He hath called mountains; humble in themselves, exalted in Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:128
verses.text: "Preparing mountains in His strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:129
verses.text: What saith one of those same mountains? "We ourselves in our own selves have had the answer of death, in order that in ourselves we should not trust, but in God that raiseth the dead".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:130
verses.text: He that in himself doth trust, and in Christ trusteth not, is not of those mountains which He hath prepared in His strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:131
verses.text: "Preparing mountains in His strength: girded about in power".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:132
verses.text: "Power," I understand: "girded about," is what? They that put Christ in the midst, "girded about" they make Him, that is on all sides begirt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:133
verses.text: We all have Him in common, therefore in the midst He is: all we gird Him about that believe in Him: and because our faith is not of our strength, but of His power; therefore girded about He is in His power; not in our own strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:134
verses.text: "That troublest the bottom of the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:135
verses.text: He hath done this: it is seen what He hath done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:136
verses.text: For He hath prepared mountains in His strength, hath sent them to preach: girded about He is by believers in power: and moved is the sea, moved is the world, and it beginneth to persecute His saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:137
verses.text: "Girded about in power: that troublest the bottom of the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:138
verses.text: He hath not said, that troublest the sea; but "the bottom of the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:139
verses.text: The bottom of the sea is the heart of ungodly men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:140
verses.text: For just as from the bottom more thoroughly all things are stirred, and the bottom holdeth firm all things: so whatsoever hath gone forth: by tongue, by hands, by divers powers for the persecution of the Church, from the bottom hath gone forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:141
verses.text: For if there were not the root of iniquity in the heart, all those things would not have gone forth against Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:142
verses.text: The bottom He troubled, perchance in order that the bottom He might also empty: for in the case of cert ain evil men He emptied the sea from the bottom, and made the sea a desert place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:143
verses.text: Another Psalm saith this, "That turneth sea into dry land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:144
verses.text: All ungodly and heathen men that have believed were sea, have been made land; with salt waves at first barren, afterwards with the fruit of righteousness productive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:145
verses.text: "That troublest the bottom of the sea: the sound of its waves who shall endure?" "Who shall endure," is what? What man shall endure the sound of the waves of the sea, the behests of the high powers of the world? But whence are they endured? Because He prepareth mountains in His strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:146
verses.text: In that therefore which he hath said "who shall" endure he saith thus: We ourselves of our own selves should not be able to endure those persecutions, unless He gave strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:147
verses.text: "The nations shall be troubled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:148
verses.text: At first they shall be troubled: but those mountains prepared in the strength of Christ, are they troubled? Troubled is the sea, against the mountains it dasheth: the sea breaketh, unshaken the mountains have remained.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:149
verses.text: "The nations shall be troubled, and all men shall fear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:150
verses.text: Behold now all men fear: they that before have been troubled do now all fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:151
verses.text: The Christians feared not, and now the Christians are feared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:152
verses.text: All that did persecute do now fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:153
verses.text: For He hath overcome that is girded about with power, to Him hath come every flesh in such sort, that the rest by their very minority do now fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:154
verses.text: And all men shall fear, that inhabit the ends of the earth, because of Thy signs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:155
verses.text: For miracles the Apostles wrought, and thence all the ends of the earth have feared and have believed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:156
verses.text: "Outgoings in morning and in evening Thou shalt delight:" that is, Thou makest delightful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:157
verses.text: Already in this life what is there being promised to us? There are outgoings in morning, there are outgoings in the evening.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:158
verses.text: By the morning he signifieth the prosperity of the world, by the evening he signifieth the trouble of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:159
verses.text: At first when he was promising gain, it was morning to thee: but now evening draweth on, sad thou hast become.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:160
verses.text: But He that hath given thee an outgoing in the morning, will give one also in the evening.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:161
verses.text: In the same manner as thou hast contemned the morning of the world by the light of the Lord, so contemn the evening also by the sufferings of the Lord, in saying to thy soul, What more will this man do to me, than my Lord hath suffered for me? May I hold fast justice, not consent to iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:162
verses.text: Let him vent his rage on the flesh, the trap will be broken, and I will fly to my Lord, that saith to me, "Do not fear them that kill the body, but the soul are not able to kill".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:163
verses.text: And for the body itself He hath given security, saying, "A hair of your head shall not perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:164
verses.text: Nobly here he hath set down, "Thou wilt delight outgoings in morning and in evening".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:165
verses.text: For if thou take not delight in the very outgoing, thou wilt not labour to go out thence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:166
verses.text: Thou runnest thy head into the promised gain, if thou art not delighted with the promise of the Saviour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:167
verses.text: And again thou yieldest to one tempting and terrifying, if thou find no delight in Him that suffered before thee, in order that He might make an outgoing for thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:168
verses.text: "Thou hast visited the earth, and hast inebriated it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:169
verses.text: Whence hast inebriated the earth? "Thy cup inebriating how glorious it is!" "Thou hast visited the earth, and hast inebriated it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:170
verses.text: Thou hast sent Thy clouds, they have rained down the preaching of the truth, inebriated is the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:171
verses.text: "Thou hast multiplied to enrich it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:172
verses.text: Whence? "The river of God is filled with water".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:173
verses.text: What is the river of God? The people of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:174
verses.text: The first people was filled with water, wherewith the rest of the earth might be watered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:175
verses.text: Hear Him promising water: "If any man thirst, let him come to Me and drink: he that believeth on Me, rivers of living water from his belly shall flow:" if rivers, one river also; for in respect of unity many are one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:176
verses.text: Many Churches and one Church, many faithful and one Bride of Christ: so many rivers and one river.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:177
verses.text: Many Israelites believed, and were fulfilled with the Holy Spirit; from thence they were scattered abroad through the nations, they began to preach the truth, and from the river of God that was filled with water, was the whole earth watered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:178
verses.text: "Thou hast prepared food for them: because thus is Thy preparing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:179
verses.text: Not because they have deserved of Thee, whom Thou hast forgiven sins: the merits of them were evil, but Thou for Thy mercy's sake, "because thus is Thy preparing," thus "Thou hast prepared food for them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:180
verses.text: "The furrows thereof inebriate Thou".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:181
verses.text: Let there be made therefore at first furrows to be inebriated: let the hardness of our breast be opened with the share of the word of God, "The furrows thereof inebriate Thou: multiply the generations thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:182
verses.text: We see, they believe, and by them believing other men believe, and because of those others believe; and it is not sufficient for one man, that having become himself a believer, he should gain one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:183
verses.text: So is multiplied seed too: a few grains are scattered, and fields spring up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:184
verses.text: "In the drops thereof it shall rejoice, when it shall rise up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:185
verses.text: That is, before it be perchance enlarged to the bulk of a river, "when it shall rise up, in its drops," that is, in those meet for it, "it shall rejoice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:186
verses.text: For upon those that are yet babes, and upon the weak, are dropped some portions of the sacraments, because they cannot receive the fulness of the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:187
verses.text: Hear in what manner he droppeth upon babes, while they are rising up, that is, in their recent rising having small capacities: the Apostle saith, "To you I could not speak as if to spiritual, but as if to carnal, as if to babes in Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:188
verses.text: When he saith, "to babes in Christ," he speaketh of them as already risen up, but not yet meet to receive that plenteous wisdom, whereof he saith, "Wisdom we speak among perfect men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:189
verses.text: Let it rejoice in its drops, while it is rising up and is growing, when strengthened it shall receive wisdom also: in the same manner as an infant is fed with milk, and becometh fit for meat, and nevertheless at first out of that very meat for which it was not fit, for it milk is made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:190
verses.text: "Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of Thy goodness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:191
verses.text: Seed is now sowing, that which is sown is growing, there will be the harvest too.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:192
verses.text: And now over the seed the enemy hath sown tares; and there have risen up evil ones among the good, false Christians, having like leaf, but not like fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:193
verses.text: For those are properly called tares, which spring up in the manner of wheat, for instance darnel, for instance wild oats, and all such as have the first leaf the same.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:194
verses.text: Therefore of the sowing of the tares thus saith the Lord: "There hath come an enemy, and hath sown over them tares;" but what hath he done to the grain? The wheat is not choked by the tares, nay, through endurance of the tares the fruit of the wheat is increased.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:195
verses.text: For the Lord Himself said to certain workmen desiring to root up the tares, "Suffer ye both to grow unto the harvest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:196
verses.text: Conquer the devil, and thou wilt have a crown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:197
verses.text: "Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of Thy goodness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:198
verses.text: Again he maketh reference to the goodness of God, lest any one boast of his own merits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:199
verses.text: "Thy plains shall be filled with abundance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:200
verses.text: "The ends of the desert shall grow fat, and the hills shall be encircled with exultation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:201
verses.text: Plains, hills, ends of the desert, the same are also men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:202
verses.text: Plains, because of the equality: because of equality, I say, from thence just peoples have been called plains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:203
verses.text: Hills, because of lifting up: because God doth lift up in Himself those that humble themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:204
verses.text: Ends of the desert are all nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:205
verses.text: Wherefore ends of the desert? Deserted they were, to them no Prophet had been sent: they were in like case as is a desert where no man passeth by.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:206
verses.text: No word of God was sent to the nations: to the people Israel alone the Prophets preached.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:207
verses.text: We came to the Lord; the wheat believed among that same people of the Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:208
verses.text: For He said at that time to the disciples, "Ye say, far off is the harvest: look back, and see how white are the lands to harvest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:209
verses.text: There hath been therefore a first harvest, there will be a second in the last age.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:210
verses.text: The first harvest was of Jews, because there were sent to them Prophets proclaiming a coming Saviour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:211
verses.text: Therefore the Lord said to His disciples, "See how white are the lands to harvest:"  the lands, to wit, of Judaea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:212
verses.text: "Other men," He saith, "have laboured, and into their labours ye have entered".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:213
verses.text: The Prophets laboured to sow, and ye with the sickle have entered into their labours.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:214
verses.text: There hath been finished therefore the first harvest, and thence, with that very wheat which then was purged, hath been sown the round world; so that there ariseth an other harvest, which at the end is to be reaped.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:215
verses.text: In the second harvest have been sown tares, now here there is labour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:216
verses.text: Just as in that first harvest the Prophets laboured until the Lord came: so in that second harvest the Apostles laboured, and all preachers of the truth labour, even until at the end the Lord send unto the harvest His Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:217
verses.text: Aforetime, I say, a desert there was, "but the ends of the desert shall grow fat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:218
verses.text: Behold where the Prophets had given no sound, the Lord of the Prophets hath been received, "The ends of the desert shall grow fat, and with exultation the hills shall be encircled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:219
verses.text: "Clothed have been the rams of the sheep" : "with exultation" must be understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:220
verses.text: For with what exultation the hills are encircled, with the same are clothed the rams of the sheep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:221
verses.text: Rams are the very same as hills.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:222
verses.text: For hills they are because of more eminent grace; rams, because they are leaders of the flocks.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:223
verses.text: "They shall shout:" thence they shall abound with wheat, because they shall shout.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:224
verses.text: What shall they shout? "For a hymn they shall say".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:225
verses.text: For one thing it is to shout against God, another thing to say a hymn; one thing to shout iniquities, another thing to shout the praises of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 66:226
verses.text: If thou shout in blasphemy, thorns thou hast brought forth: if thou shoutest in a hymn, thou aboundest in wheat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:1
verses.text: Psalm LXVI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:2
verses.text: This Psalm hath on the title the inscription, "For the end, a song of a Psalm of Resurrection".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:3
verses.text: When ye hear "for the end," whenever the Psalms are repeated, understand it "for Christ:" the Apostle saying, "For the end of the law is Christ, for righteousness to every one believing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:4
verses.text: In what manner therefore here Resurrection is sung, ye wilt hear, and whose Resurrection it is, as far as Himself deigneth to give and disclose.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:5
verses.text: For the Resurrection we Christians know already hath come to pass in our Head, and in the members it is to be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:6
verses.text: The Head of the Church is Christ, the members of Christ are the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:7
verses.text: That which hath preceded in the Head, will follow in the Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:8
verses.text: This is our hope; for this we believe, for this we endure and persevere amid so great perverseness of this world, hope comforting us, before that hope becometh reality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:9
verses.text: The Jews did hold the hope of the resurrection of the dead: and they hoped that themselves alone would rise again to a blessed life because of the work of the Law, and because of the justifications of the Scriptures, which the Jews alone had, and the Gentiles had not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:10
verses.text: Crucified was Christ, "blindness in part happened unto Israel, in order that the fulness of the Gentiles might enter in:" as the Apostle saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:11
verses.text: The resurrection of the dead beginneth to be promised  to the Gentiles also that believe in Jesus Christ, that He hath risen again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:12
verses.text: Thence this Psalm is against the presumption and pride of the Jews, for the comfort of the Gentiles that are to be called to the same hope of resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:13
verses.text: Thence he beginneth, "Be joyful in God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:14
verses.text: Who? "Every land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:15
verses.text: Not therefore Judaea alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:16
verses.text: See, brethren, after what sort is set forth the universality of the Church in the whole world spread abroad: and mourn ye not only the Jews, who envied the Gentiles that grace, but still more for heretics wail ye.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:17
verses.text: For if they are to be mourned, that have not been gathered together, how much more they that being gathered together have been divided? "Jubilate in God every land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:18
verses.text: What is "jubilate"? Into the voice of rejoicings break forth if ye cannot into that of words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:19
verses.text: For "jubilation" is not of words, but the sound alone of men rejoicing is uttered, as of a heart labouring and bringing forth into voice the pleasure of a thing imagined which cannot be expressed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:20
verses.text: "Be joyful in God every land:" let no one jubilate in a part: let every land be joyful, let the Catholic Church jubilate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:21
verses.text: The Catholic Church embraceth the whole: whosoever holdeth a part and from the whole is cut off, should howl, not jubilate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:22
verses.text: "But play ye to His name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:23
verses.text: What hath he said? By you "playing" let His name be blessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:24
verses.text: But what it is to "play"? To play is also to take up an instrument which is called a psaltery, and by the striking and action of the hands to accompany voices.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:25
verses.text: If therefore ye jubilate so that God may hear; play also something that men may both see and hear: but not to your own name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:26
verses.text: For if for the sake of yourselves being glorified ye do good works, we make the same reply as He made to certain of such men, "Verily I say unto you, they have received their reward:" and again, "Otherwise no reward ye will have with your Father that is in Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:27
verses.text: Thou wilt say, ought I, then, to hide my works, that I do them not before men? No.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:28
verses.text: But what saith He? "Let your works shine before men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:29
verses.text: In doubt then I shall remain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:30
verses.text: On one side Thou sayest to me, "Take heed that ye do not your righteousness before men:" on the other side Thou sayest to me, "Let your good works shine before men;" what shall I keep? what do? what leave undone? A man can as well serve two masters commanding different things as one commanding different things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:31
verses.text: I command not, saith the Lord, different things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:32
verses.text: The end observe, for the end sing: with what end thou doest it, see thou.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:33
verses.text: If for this reason thou doest it, that thou mayest be glorified, I have forbidden it: but if for this reason, that God may be glorified, I have commanded it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:34
verses.text: Play therefore, not to your own name, but to the name of the Lord your God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:35
verses.text: Play ye, let Him be lauded: live ye well, let Him be glorified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:36
verses.text: For whence have ye that same living well? If for everlasting ye had had it, ye would never have lived ill; if from yourselves ye had had it, ye never would have done otherwise than have lived well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:37
verses.text: "Give glory to His praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:38
verses.text: Our whole attention upon the praise of God he directeth, nothing for us he leaveth whence we should be praised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:39
verses.text: Let us glory thence the more, and rejoice: to Him let us cleave, in Him let us be praised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:40
verses.text: Ye heard when the Apostle was being read, "See ye your calling, brethren, how not many wise after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, but the foolish things of the world God hath chosen to confound the wise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:41
verses.text: But the Lord chose afterwards orators also; but they would have been proud, if He had not first chosen fishermen; He chose rich men; but they would have said that on account of their riches they had been chosen, unless at first He had chosen poor men: He chose Emperors afterwards; but better is it, that when an Emperor hath come to Rome, he should lay aside his crown, and weep at the monument of a fisherman, than that a fisherman should weep at the monument of an Emperor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:42
verses.text: "For the weak things of the world God hath chosen to confound the strong," etcAnd what followeth? The Apostle hath concluded, "That there might not glory before God any flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:43
verses.text: See ye how from us He hath taken away, that He might give glory: hath taken away ours, that He might give His own; hath taken away empty, that He might give full; hath taken away insecure, that He might give solid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:44
verses.text: "Say ye to God, How to be feared are Thy works!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:45
verses.text: Wherefore to be feared and not to be loved? Hear thou another voice of a Psalm: "Serve ye the Lord in fear, and exult unto Him with trembling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:46
verses.text: What meaneth this? Hear the voice of the Apostle: "With fear," he saith, "and trembling, your own salvation work ye out".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:47
verses.text: Wherefore with fear and trembling? He hath subjoined the reason: "for God it is that worketh in you both to will and to work according to good will".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:48
verses.text: If therefore God worketh in thee, by the Grace of God thou workest well, not by thy strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:49
verses.text: Therefore if thou rejoicest, fear also: lest perchance that which was given to a humble man be taken away from a proud one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:50
verses.text: Brethren, if against the Jews of old, cut off from the root of the Patriarchs, we ought not to exalt ourselves, but rather to fear and say to God, "How to be feared are Thy works:" how much less ought we not to exalt ourselves against the fresh wounds of the cutting off! Before there had been cut off Jews, graffed in Gentiles; from the very graft there have been cut off heretics; but neither against them ought we to exalt ourselves; lest perchance he deserve to be cut off, that delighteth to revile them that are cut off.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:51
verses.text: My brethren, a bishop's voice, however unworthy, hath sounded to you: we pray you to beware, whosoever ye are in the Church, do not revile them that are not within; but pray ye rather, that they too may be within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:52
verses.text: For God is able again to graft them in Of the very Jews the Apostle said this, and it was done in their case.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:53
verses.text: The Lord rose again, and many believed: they perceived not when they crucified, nevertheless afterwards they believed in Him, and there was forgiven them so great a transgression.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:54
verses.text: The shedding of the Lord's blood was forgiven the manslayers, not to say, God-slayers: "for if they had known, the Lord of glory they never would have crucified".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:55
verses.text: Now to the manslayers hath been forgiven the shedding of the blood of Him innocent: and that same blood which through madness they shed, through grace they have drunk.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:56
verses.text: O fulness of Gentiles, say thou to God, "How to be feared are Thy works!" and so rejoice thou as that thou mayest fear, be not exalted above the branches cut off.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:57
verses.text: "In the multitude of thy power Thine enemies shall lie to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:58
verses.text: For this purpose he saith, "to Thee thine enemies shall lie," in order that great may be Thy power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:59
verses.text: What is this? With more attention hearken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:60
verses.text: The power of  our Lord Jesus Christ most chiefly appeared in the Resurrection, from whence this Psalm hath received its title.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:61
verses.text: And rising again, He appeared to His disciples He appeared not to His enemies, but to His disciples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:62
verses.text: Crucified He appeared to all men, rising again to believers: so that afterwards also he that would might believe, and to him that should believe, resurrection might be promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:63
verses.text: Many holy men wrought many miracles; no one of them when dead did rise again: because even they that by them were raised to life, were raised to life to die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:64
verses.text: Because therefore the Jews might say, when the Lord did miracles, Moses hath done these things, Elias hath done, Eliseus hath done them: they might for themselves say these words, because those men also did raise to life dead men, and did many miracles: therefore when from Him a sign was demanded, of the peculiar sign making mention which in Himself alone was to be, He saith, "This generation crooked and provoking seeketh a sign, and a sign shall not be given to it, except the sign of Jonas the Prophet: for as Jonas was in the belly of the whale three days and three nights, so shall be also the Son of Man in the heart of the earth three days and three nights".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:65
verses.text: In what way was Jonas in the belly of the whale? Was it not so that afterwards alive he was vomited out? Hell was to the Lord what the whale was to Jonas.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:66
verses.text: This sign peculiar to Himself He mentioned, this is the most mighty sign.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:67
verses.text: It is more mighty to live again after having been dead, than not to have been dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:68
verses.text: The greatness of the power of the Lord as He was made Man, in the virtue of the Resurrection doth appear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:69
verses.text: Observe also the very lie of the false witnesses in the Gospel, and see how it is about Resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:70
verses.text: For when to the Lord had been said, "What sign showest Thou to us, that Thou doest these things?" besides that which He had spoken about Jonah through another similitude of this same thing also He spake, that ye might know this peculiar sign had been especially pointed out: "Destroy this Temple," He saith, "and in three days I will raise it up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:71
verses.text: And they said, "In forty and six years was builded this temple, and wilt Thou in three days raise it up?" And the evangelist explaining what it was, "But this," he saith, "spake Jesus of the Temple of His Body".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:72
verses.text: Behold this His power He said He would show to men in the same thing as that from whence He had given the similitude of a Temple, because of His flesh, which was the Temple of the Divinity hidden within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:73
verses.text: Whence the Jews outwardly saw the Temple, the Deity dwelling within they saw not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:74
verses.text: Out of those words of the Lord false witnesses made up a lie to say against Him, out of those very words wherein He mentioned His future Resurrection, in speaking of the Temple.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:75
verses.text: For false witnesses, when they were asked what they had heard Him say, alleged against Him: "We heard Him saying, I will destroy this Temple, and after three days I will raise it up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:76
verses.text: "After three days I will raise up," they had heard: "I will destroy," they had not heard: but had heard "destroy ye".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:77
verses.text: One word they changed and a few letters, in order to support their false testimony.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:78
verses.text: But for whom changest thou a word, O human vanity, O human weakness? For the Word, the Unchangeable, dost thou change a word? Thou changest thy word, dost thou change God's Word?Wherefore said they that Thou hadst said, "I will destroy;" and said not that which Thou saidest, "destroy ye"? It was, as it were, in order that they might defend themselves from the charge of destroying the Temple without cause.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:79
verses.text: For Christ, because He willed it, died: and nevertheless ye killed Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:80
verses.text: Behold we grant you, O ye liars, Himself destroyed the Temple.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:81
verses.text: For it hath been said by the Apostle, "That loved me, and gave up Himself for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:82
verses.text: It hath been said of the Father, "That His own Son spared not, but gave Him up for us all".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:83
verses.text: By all means be it that Himself destroyed the Temple, Himself destroyed that said, "Power I have to lay down My Soul, and power I have again to take it: no one taketh it from Me, but I Myself lay it down from Me, and again I take it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:84
verses.text: Be it that Himself hath destroyed the Temple in His Grace, in your malice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:85
verses.text: "In the multitude of Thy power thine enemies shall lie to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:86
verses.text: Behold they lie, behold they are believed, behold Thou art oppressed, behold Thou art crucified, behold Thou art insulted, behold head is wagged at Thee, "If Son of God He is, let Him come down from the Cross".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:87
verses.text: Behold when Thou wilt, life Thou layest down, and with lance in the side art pierced, and Sacraments from Thy side flow forth; Thou art taken down from the Tree, wound in linens, laid in the sepulchre, there are set guards lest Thy disciples take Thee away; there cometh the hour of Thy Resurrection, earth is shaken, tombs are cloven, Thou risest again in secret, appearest openly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:88
verses.text: Where then are those liars? Where is the false testimony of evil will? Have not Thine enemies in the multitude of Thy power lied to Thee?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:89
verses.text: Give them also those guards at the Tomb, let them recount what they have seen, let them take money and lie tooThey too were added to the lie of the enemies: increased was the number of liars, that increased might be the reward of believers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:90
verses.text: Therefore they lied, "in the multitude of Thy power" they lied: to confound liars Thou hast appeared to men of truth, and Thou hast appeared to those men of truth whom Thou hast made men of truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:91
verses.text: Let Jews remain in their lies: to Thee, because in the multitude of Thy power they lied, let there be done that which followeth, "Let every land worship Thee, and play to Thee, play to Thy name, O Most Highest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:92
verses.text: A little before, Most Lowly, now Most Highest: Most Lowly in the hands of lying enemies; Most Highest above the head of praising Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:93
verses.text: O ye Gentiles, O most distant nations, leave lying Jews, come confessing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:94
verses.text: "Come ye, and see the works of the Lord: terrible in counsels above the sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:95
verses.text: Son of Man indeed He too hath been called, and verily Son of Man He became: very Son of God in the form of God; very Son of Man in form of a servant: but do not judge of that form by the condition of others alike: "terrible" He is "in counsels above the sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:96
verses.text: Sons of men took counsel to crucify Christ, being crucified He blinded the crucifiers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:97
verses.text: What then have ye done, sons of men, by taking keen counsels against your Lord, in whom was hidden Majesty, and to sight shown weakness? Ye were taking counsels to destroy, He to blind and save; to blind proud men, to save humble men: but to blind those same proud men, to the end that, being blinded they might be humbled, being humbled might confess, having confessed might be enlightened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:98
verses.text: "Terrible in counsels above the sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:99
verses.text: Terrible indeed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:100
verses.text: Behold blindness in part to Israel hath happened: behold the Jews, out of whom was born Christ, are without: behold the Gentiles, that were against Judaea, in Christ are within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:101
verses.text: "Terrible in counsels above the sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:102
verses.text: Wherefore what hath He done by the terror of His counsel? He hath turned the sea into dry land.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:103
verses.text: For this followeth, "That hath turned the sea into dry land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:104
verses.text: A sea was the world, bitter with saltness, troubled with tempest, raging with waves of persecutions, sea it was: truly into dry land the sea hath been turned, now there thirsteth for sweet water the world that with salt water was filled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:105
verses.text: Who hath done this? He "that hath turned the sea into dry land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:106
verses.text: Now the soul of all the Gentiles saith what? "My soul is as it were land without water to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:107
verses.text: "That hath turned the sea into dry land.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:108
verses.text: In the river they shall pass over on foot".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:109
verses.text: Those same persons that have been turned into dry land, though they were before sea, "in the river on foot shall pass over".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:110
verses.text: What is the river? The river is all the mortality of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:111
verses.text: Observe a river: some things come and pass by, other things that are to pass by do succeed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:112
verses.text: Is it not thus with the water of a river, that from earth springeth and floweth? Every one that is born must needs give place to one going to be born: and all this order of things rolling along is a kind of river.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:113
verses.text: Into this river let not the soul greedily throw herself, let her not throw herself, but let her stand still.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:114
verses.text: And how shall she pass over the pleasures of things doomed to perish? Let her believe in Christ, and she will pass over on foot: she passeth over with Him for Leader, on foot she passeth over.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:115
verses.text: "There we will be joyous in Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:116
verses.text: O ye Jews, of your own works boast ye: lay aside the pride of boasting of yourselves, take up the Grace of being joyous in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:117
verses.text: For therein we will be joyous, but not in ourselves: "there we will be joyous in Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:118
verses.text: When shall we joy? When we shall have passed over the river on foot.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:119
verses.text: Life everlasting is promised, resurrection is promised, there our flesh no longer shall be a river: for a river it is now, while it is mortality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:120
verses.text: Observe whether there standeth still any age.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:121
verses.text: Boys desire to grow up; and they know not how by succeeding years the span of their life is lessened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:122
verses.text: For years are not added to but taken from them as they grow: just as the water of a river alway draweth near, but from the source it withdraweth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:123
verses.text: And boys desire to grow up that they may escape the thraldom of elders; behold they grow up, it cometh to pass quickly, they arrive at youth: let them that have emerged from boyhood retain, if they are able, their youth: that too passeth away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:124
verses.text: Old age succeedeth: let even old age be everlasting; with death it is removed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:125
verses.text: Therefore a river there is of flesh that is born.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:126
verses.text: This river of mortality, so that it doth not by reason of concupiscence of things mortal undermine and carry him away, he easily passeth over, that humbly, that is on foot, passeth over, He being leader that first hath passed over, that of the flood in the way even unto death hath drunk, and therefore hath lifted up the head Passing over therefore on foot that river, that is, easily passing over that mortality that glideth along, "there we will be joyous in Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:127
verses.text: But now in what save in Him, or in the hope of Him? For even if we are joyous now, in hope we are joyous; but then in Him we shall be joyous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:128
verses.text: And now in Him, but through hope: "but then face to face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:129
verses.text: "There we will be joyous in Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:130
verses.text: In whom? "In Him that reigneth in His virtue for everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:131
verses.text: For what virtue have we and is it everlasting? If everlasting were our virtue, we should not have slipped, should not have fallen into sin, we should not have deserved penal mortality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:132
verses.text: He, of His good pleasure, took up that whereunto our desert threw us down "That reigneth in His virtue for everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:133
verses.text: Of Him partakers let us be made, in whose virtue we shall be strong, but He in His own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:134
verses.text: We enlightened, He a light enlightening: we, being turned away from Him, are in darkness; turned away from Himself He cannot be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:135
verses.text: With the heat of Him we are warmed; from whence withdrawing we had grown cold, to the Same drawing near again we are warmed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:136
verses.text: Therefore let us speak to Him that He may keep us in His virtue, because "in Him we will be joyous that reigneth in His virtue for everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:137
verses.text: But this thing is not granted to believing Jews alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:138
verses.text: "The eyes of Him do look upon the Gentiles".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:139
verses.text: And what do we? The Jews will murmur; the Jews will say, "what He hath given to us, the same to them also; to us Gospel, to them Gospel; to us the Grace of Resurrection, and to them the Grace of Resurrection; doth it profit us nothing that we have received the Law, and that in the justifications of the Law we have lived, and have kept the commandments of the fathers? Nothing will it avail? The same to them as to us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:140
verses.text: Let them not strive, let them not dispute.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:141
verses.text: "Let not them that are bitter be exalted in their own selves".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:142
verses.text: O flesh miserable and wasting, art thou not sinful? Why crieth out thy tongue? Let the conscience be listened to.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:143
verses.text: "For all men have sinned, and need the glory of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:144
verses.text: Know thyself, human weakness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:145
verses.text: Thou didst receive the Law, in order that a transgressor also of the Law thou mightest be: for thou hast not kept and fulfilled that which thou didst receive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:146
verses.text: There hath come to thee because of the Law, not the justification which the Law enjoineth, but the transgression which thou hast done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:147
verses.text: If therefore there hath abounded sin, why enviest thou Grace more abounding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:148
verses.text: Be not bitter, for "let not them that are bitter be exalted in their own selves".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:149
verses.text: He seemeth in a manner to have uttered a curse in "Let not them that are bitter be exalted;" yea, be they exalted, but not "in themselves".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:150
verses.text: Let them be humbled in themselves, exalted in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:151
verses.text: For, "he that humbleth himself shall be exalted; and he that exalteth himself shall be humbled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:152
verses.text: "Let not them that are bitter be exalted in their own selves".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:153
verses.text: "Bless our God, ye nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:154
verses.text: Behold, there have been driven back they that are bitter, reckoning hath been made with them: some have been converted, some have continued proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:155
verses.text: Let not them terrify you that grudge the Gentiles Gospel Grace: now hath come the Seed of Abraham, in whom are blessed all nations Bless ye Him in whom ye are blessed, "Bless our God, ye nations: and hear ye the voice of His praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:156
verses.text: Praise not yourselves, but praise Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:157
verses.text: What is the voice of His praise? That by His Grace we are whatever of good we are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:158
verses.text: "Who hath set my Soul unto life"  Behold the voice of his praise: "Who hath set my Soul unto life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:159
verses.text: Therefore in death she was: in death she was, in thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:160
verses.text: Thence it is that ye ought not to have been exalted in yourselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:161
verses.text: Therefore in death she was, in thyself: where will it be in life, save in Him that said, "I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life"? Just as to certain believers the Apostle saith, "Ye were sometime darkness, but now light in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:162
verses.text: "And hath not given unto motion my feet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:163
verses.text: He hath set my Soul unto life, He guideth the feet that they stumble not, be not moved and given unto motion; He maketh us to live, He maketh us to persevere even unto the end, in order that for everlasting we may live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:164
verses.text: "For thou hast proved us, O God; Thou hast fired us as silver is fired".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:165
verses.text: Hast not fired us like hay, but like silver: by applying to us fire, Thou hast not turned us into ashes, but Thou hast washed off uncleanness, "Thou hast fired us, as silver is fired".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:166
verses.text: And see in what manner God is wroth against them, whose Soul He hath set unto life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:167
verses.text: "Thou hast led us into a trap:" not that we might be caught and die, but that we might be tried and delivered from it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:168
verses.text: "Thou hast laid tribulations upon our back".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:169
verses.text: For having been to ill purpose lifted up, proud we were: having been to ill purpose lifted up, we were bowed down, in order that being bowed down, we should be lifted up for good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:170
verses.text: "Thou hast laid tribulations on our back:" "Thou hast set men over our heads".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:171
verses.text: All these things the Church hath suffered in sundry and divers persecutions: She hath suffered this in Her individual members, even now doth suffer it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:172
verses.text: For there is not one, that in this life could say that he was exempt from these trials.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:173
verses.text: Therefore there are set even men over our heads: we endure those whom we would not, we suffer for our betters those whom we know to be worse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:174
verses.text: But if sins be wanting, a man is justly superior: but by how much there are more sins, by so much he is inferior.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:175
verses.text: And it is a good thing to consider ourselves to be sinners, and thus endure men set over our heads: in order that we also to God may confess that deservedly we suffer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:176
verses.text: For why dost thou suffer with indignation that which He doeth who is just? "Thou hast laid tribulations upon our back: Thou hast set men over our heads".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:177
verses.text: God seemeth to be wroth, when He doeth these things: fear not, for a Father He is, He is never so wroth as to destroy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:178
verses.text: When ill thou livest, if He spareth, He is more angry.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:179
verses.text: In a word, these tribulations are the rods of Him correcting, lest there be a sentence from Him punishing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:180
verses.text: "We have passed through fire and water".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:181
verses.text: Fire and water are both dangerous in this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:182
verses.text: Certainly water seemeth to extinguish fire, and fire seemeth to dry up water.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:183
verses.text: Thus also these are the trials, wherein aboundeth this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:184
verses.text: Fire burneth, water corrupteth: both must be feared, both the burning of tribulation and the water of corruption.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:185
verses.text: Whenever there is adversity, and anything which is called unhappiness in this world, there is as it were fire: whenever there is prosperity, and the world's plenty floweth about one, there is as it were water.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:186
verses.text: See that fire burn thee not, nor water corrupt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:187
verses.text: Hasten not to the water: through fire pass over to the water, that thou mayest pass over the water also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:188
verses.text: Therefore also in the mystic rites and in catechising and in exorcising, there is first used fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:189
verses.text: For whence ofttimes do the unclean spirits cry out, "I burn," if that is not fire? But after the fire of Exorcism we come to Baptism: so that from fire to water, from water unto refreshment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:190
verses.text: But as in the Sacraments, so it is in the temptations of this world: the straitness of fear draweth near first, in place of fire; afterwards fear being removed, we ought to be afraid lest worldly happiness corrupt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:191
verses.text: But when the fire hath not made thee burst, and when thou hast not sunk in the water, but hast swum out; through discipline thou passest over to rest, and passing over through fire and water, thou art led forth into a place of refreshment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:192
verses.text: For of those things whereof the signs are in the Sacraments, there are the very realities in that perfection of life everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:193
verses.text: But we are not torpid there, but we rest: nor though it be called heat, shall we be hot there, but we shall be fervent in spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:194
verses.text: Observe that same heat in another Psalm: "nor is there any one that hideth himself from the heat thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:195
verses.text: What saith also the Apostle? "In spirit fervent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:196
verses.text: Therefore, "we have gone over through fire and water: and Thou hast led us forth into a cool place".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:197
verses.text: Observe how not only concerning a cool place, but neither of that very fire to be desired he hath been silent: "I will enter into Thy House in holocausts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:198
verses.text: What is a holocaust? A whole sacrifice burned up, but with fire divine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:199
verses.text: For a sacrifice is called a holocaust, when the whole is burned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:200
verses.text: One thing are the parts of sacrifices, another thing a holocaust: when the whole is burned and the whole consumed by fire divine, it is called a holocaust: when a part, a sacrifice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:201
verses.text: Every holocaust indeed is a sacrifice: but not every sacrifice a holocaust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:202
verses.text: Holocausts therefore he is promising, the Body of Christ is speaking, the Unity of Christ is speaking, "I will enter into Thy House in holocausts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:203
verses.text: All that is mine let Thy fire consume, let nothing of mine remain to me, let all be Thine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:204
verses.text: But this shall be in the Resurrection of just men, "when both this corruptible shall be clad in incorruption, and this mortal shall be clad in immortality: then shall come to pass that which hath been written, 'Death is swallowed up in victory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:205
verses.text: '" Victory is, as it were, fire divine: when it swalloweth up our death also, it is a holocaust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:206
verses.text: There remaineth not anything mortal in the flesh, there remaineth not anything culpable in the spirit: the whole of mortal life shall be consumed, in order that in life everlasting it may be consummated, that from death we may be preserved in life These therefore will be the holocausts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:207
verses.text: And what shall there be "in the holocausts"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:208
verses.text: "I will render to Thee my vows, which my lips have distinguished".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:209
verses.text: What is the distinction in vows? This is the distinction, that thyself thou censure, Him thou praise: perceive thyself to be a creature, Him the Creator: thyself darkness, Him the Enlightener, to whom thou shouldest say, "Thou shalt light my lamp, O Lord my God, Thou shalt enlighten my darkness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:210
verses.text: For whenever thou shalt have said, O soul, that from thyself thou hast light, thou wilt not distinguish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:211
verses.text: If thou wilt not distinguish, thou wilt not render distinct vows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:212
verses.text: Render distinct vows, confess thyself changeable, Him unchangeable: confess thyself without Him to be nothing, but Himself without thee to be perfect; thyself to need Him, but Him not to need thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:213
verses.text: Cry to Him, "I have said to the Lord, My God art Thou, for my good things Thou needest not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:214
verses.text: Now though God taketh thee to Him for a holocaust, He groweth not, He is not increased, He is not richer, He becometh not better furnished: whatsoever He maketh of thee for thy sake, is the better for thee, not for Him that maketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:215
verses.text: If thou distinguishest these things, thou renderest the vows to thy God which thy lips have distinguished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:216
verses.text: "And my mouth hath spoken in my tribulation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:217
verses.text: How sweet ofttimes is tribulation, how necessary! In that case what hath the mouth of the same spoken in his tribulation? "Holocausts marrowed I will offer to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:218
verses.text: What is "marrowed"? Within may I keep Thy love, it shall not be on the surface, in my marrow it shall be that I love Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:219
verses.text: For there is nothing more inward than our marrow: the bones are more inward than the flesh, the marrow is more inward than those same bones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:220
verses.text: Whosoever therefore on the surface loveth God, desireth rather to please men, but having some other affection within, he offereth not holocausts of marrow: but into whosesoever marrow He looketh, him He receiveth whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:221
verses.text: "With incense and rams".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:222
verses.text: The rams are the rulers of the Church: the whole Body of Christ is speaking: this is the thing which he offereth to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:223
verses.text: Incense  is what? Prayer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:224
verses.text: "With incense and rams".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:225
verses.text: For especially the rams do pray for the flocks.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:226
verses.text: "I will offer to Thee oxen with he-goats".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:227
verses.text: Oxen we find treading out corn, and the same are offered to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:228
verses.text: The Apostle hath said, that of the preachers of the Gospel must be understood that which hath been written, "Of the ox treading out corn the mouth thou shalt not muzzle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:229
verses.text: Doth God care for oxen?" Therefore great are those rams, great the oxen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:230
verses.text: What of the rest, that perchance are conscious of certain sins, that perchance in the very road have slipped, and, having been wounded, by penitence are being healed? Shall they too continue, and to the holocausts shall they not belong? Let them not fear, he hath added he-goats also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:231
verses.text: "I will offer to Thee oxen with he-goats".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:232
verses.text: By the very yoking are saved the he-goats; of themselves they have no strength, being yoked to bulls they are accepted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:233
verses.text: For they have made friends of the mammon of iniquity, that the same may receive them into everlasting tabernacles Therefore those he-goats shall not be on the left, because they have made to themselves friends of the mammon of iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:234
verses.text: But what he-goats shall be on the left? They to whom shall be said, "I hungred, and ye gave me not to eat:" not they that have redeemed their sins by almsdeeds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:235
verses.text: Come ye, hear, and I will tell, all ye that fear God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:236
verses.text: Let us come, let us hear, what he is going to tell, "Come ye, hear, and I will tell".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:237
verses.text: But to whom, "Come ye, and hear"? "All ye that fear God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:238
verses.text: If God ye fear not, I will not tell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:239
verses.text: It is not possible that it be told to any where the fear of God is not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:240
verses.text: Let the fear of God open the ears, that there may be something to enter in, and a way whereby may enter in that which I am going to tell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:241
verses.text: But what is he going to tell? "How great things He hath done to my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:242
verses.text: Behold, he would tell: but what is he going to tell? Is it perchance how widely the earth is spread, how much the sky is extended, and how many are the stars, and what are the changes of sun and of moon? This creation fulfilleth its course: but they have very curiously sought it out, the Creator thereof have not known This thing hear, this thing receive, "O ye that fear God, how great things He hath done to my soul:" if ye will, to yours also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:243
verses.text: "How great things He hath done to my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:244
verses.text: "To Him with my mouth I have cried".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:245
verses.text: "And this very thing, he saith, hath been done to his soul; that to Him with his mouth he should cry, hath been done, he saith, to his soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:246
verses.text: Behold, brethren, Gentiles we were, even if not in ourselves, in our parents.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:247
verses.text: And what saith the Apostle? "Ye know, when Gentiles ye were, to idols without speech how ye went up, being led".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:248
verses.text: Let the Church now say, "how great things He hath done to my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:249
verses.text: "To Him with my mouth I have cried".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:250
verses.text: I a man to a stone was crying, to a deaf stock I was crying, to idols deaf and dumb I was speaking: now the image of God hath been turned to the Creator thereof.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:251
verses.text: I that was "saying to a stock, My father thou art; and to a stone, Thou hast begotten me:" now say, "Our Father, which art in Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:252
verses.text: "To Him with my mouth I have cried, and I have exalted Him under my tongue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:253
verses.text: See how in secret He would be uncorrupt that offereth marrowed holocausts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:254
verses.text: This do ye, brethren, this imitate, so that ye may say, "Come ye, see how great things He hath done to my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:255
verses.text: For all those things of which he telleth, by His Grace are done in our soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:256
verses.text: See the other things of which he speaketh.
