verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:257
verses.text: "If I have beheld iniquity in my heart, may not the Lord hearken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:258
verses.text: Consider now, brethren, how easily, how daily men blushing for fear of men do censure iniquities; He hath done ill, He hath done basely, a villain the fellow is: this perchance for man's sake he saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:259
verses.text: See whether thou beholdest no iniquity in thy heart, whether perchance that which thou censurest in another, thou art meditating to do, and therefore against him dost exclaim, not because he hath done it, but because he hath been found out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:260
verses.text: Return to thyself, within be to thyself a judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:261
verses.text: Behold in thy hid chamber, in the very inmost recess of the heart, where thou and He that seeth are alone, there let iniquity be displeasing to thee, in order that thou mayest be pleasing to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:262
verses.text: Do not regard it, that is, do not love it, but rather despise it, that is, contemn it, and turn away from it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:263
verses.text: Whatever pleasing thing it hath promised to allure thee to sin; whatever grievous thing it hath threatened, to drive thee on to evil doing; all is nought, all passeth away: it is worthy to be despised, in order that it may be trampled upon; not to be eyed lest it be accepted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:264
verses.text: "Therefore God hath hearkened to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:265
verses.text: Because I have not beheld iniquity in my heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:266
verses.text: "And He hath listened to the voice of my prayer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:267
verses.text: "Blessed be my God, that hath not thrust away my supplication and His mercy from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:268
verses.text: Gather the sense from that place, where he saith, "Come ye, hear, and I will tell you, all ye that fear God, how great things He hath done to my soul:" he hath both said the words which ye have heard, and at the end thus he hath concluded: "Blessed be my God, that hath not thrust away my supplication and His mercy from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:269
verses.text: For thus there arriveth at the Resurrection he that speaketh, where already we also are by hope: yea both it is we ourselves, and this voice is ours.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:270
verses.text: So long therefore as here we are, this let us ask of God, that He thrust not from us our supplication, and His mercy, that is, that we pray continually, and He continually pity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:271
verses.text: For many become feeble in praying, and in the newness of their own conversion pray fervently, afterwards feebly, afterwards coldly, afterwards negligently: as if they have become secure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:272
verses.text: The foe watcheth: thou sleepest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:273
verses.text: The Lord Himself hath given commandment in the Gospel, how "it behoveth men always to pray and not to faint".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:274
verses.text: And he giveth a comparison from that unjust judge, who neither feared God, nor regarded man, whom that widow daily importuned to hear her; and he yielded for weariness, that was not influenced by pity: and the naughty judge saith to himself, "Though neither God I fear, nor men I regard, even because of the weariness which this widow daily putteth upon me, I will hear her cause, and will avenge her".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:275
verses.text: And the Lord saith, "If a naughty judge hath done this, shall not your Father avenge His chosen, that to Him do cry day and night? Yea, I say unto you, He shall make judgment of them speedily".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:276
verses.text: Therefore let us not faint in prayer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:277
verses.text: Though He putteth off what He is going to grant, He putteth it not away: being secure of His promise, let us not faint in praying, and this is by His goodness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:278
verses.text: Therefore he hath said, "Blessed is my God, that hath not thrust away my supplication and His mercy from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 67:279
verses.text: When thou hast seen thy supplication "not thrust away from thee," be secure, that His mercy hath not been thrust away from thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:1
verses.text: Psalm LXVII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:2
verses.text: Your Love remembereth, that in two Psalms, which have been already treated of, we have stirred up our soul to bless the Lord, and with godly chant have said, "Bless thou, O my soul, the Lord ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:3
verses.text: If therefore we have stirred up our soul in those Psalms to bless the Lord, in this Psalm is well said, "May God have pity on us, and bless us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:4
verses.text: Let our soul bless the Lord, and let God bless us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:5
verses.text: When God blesseth us, we grow, and when we bless the Lord, we grow, to us both are profitable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:6
verses.text: He is not increased by our blessing, nor is He lessened by our cursing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:7
verses.text: He that curseth the Lord, is himself lessened: he that blesseth the Lord, is himself increased.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:8
verses.text: First, there is in us the blessing of the Lord, and the consequence is that we also bless the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:9
verses.text: That is the rain, this the fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:10
verses.text: Therefore there is rendered as it were fruit to God the Husbandman, raining upon and tilling us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:11
verses.text: Let us chant these words with no barren devotion, with no empty voice, but with true heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:12
verses.text: For most evidently God the Father hath been called a Husbandman The Apostle saith, "God's husbandry ye are, God's building ye are".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:13
verses.text: In things visible of this world, the vine is not a building, and a building is not a vineyard: but we are the vineyard of the Lord, because He tilleth us for fruit; the building of God we are, since He who tilleth us, dwelleth in us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:14
verses.text: And what saith the same Apostle? "I have planted, Apollos hath watered, but the increase God hath given.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:15
verses.text: Therefore neither he that planteth is anything, nor he that watereth, but He that giveth the increase, even God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:16
verses.text: He it is therefore that giveth the increase.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:17
verses.text: Are those perchance the husbandmen? For a husbandman he is called that planteth, that watereth: but the Apostle hath said, "I have planted, Apollos hath watered".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:18
verses.text: Do we enquire whence himself hath done this? The Apostle maketh answer, "Yet not I, but the Grace of God with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:19
verses.text: Therefore whithersoever thou turn thee, whether through Angels, thou wilt find God thy Husbandman; whether through Prophets, the Same is thy Husbandman; whether through Apostles, the very Same acknowledge to be thy Husbandman.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:20
verses.text: What then of us? Perchance we are the labourers of that Husbandman, and this too with powers imparted by Himself, and by Grace granted by Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:21
verses.text: "Lighten His countenance upon us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:22
verses.text: Thou wast perchance going to enquire, what is "bless us"? In many ways men would have themselves to be blessed of God: one would have himself to be blessed, so that he may have a house full of the necessary things of this life; another desireth himself to be blessed, so that he may obtain soundness of body without flaw; another would have himself to be blessed, if perchance he is sick, so that he may acquire soundness; another longing for sons, and perchance being sorrowful because none are born, would have himself to be blessed so that he may have posterity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:23
verses.text: And who could number the divers wishes of men desiring themselves to be blessed of the Lord God? But which of us would say, that it was no blessing of God, if either husbandry should bring him fruit, or if any man's house should abound in plenty of things temporal, or if the very bodily health be either so maintained that it be not lost, or, if lost, be regained?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:24
verses.text: "Every soul that is blessed is simple," not cleaving to things earthly nor with glued wings grovelling, but beaming with the brightness of virtues, on the twin wings of twin love doth spring into the free air; and seeth how from her is withdrawn that whereon she was treading, not that whereon she was resting, and she saith securely, "The Lord hath given, the Lord hath taken away; as it hath pleased the Lord, so hath been done: be the name of the Lord blessed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:25
verses.text: But let not perchance any weak man say, when shall I be of so great virtue, as was holy Job? The mightiness of the tree thou wonderest at, because but now thou hast been born: this great tree, whereat thou wonderest, under the branches and shade whereof thou coolest thyself, hath been a switch.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:26
verses.text: But dost thou fear lest there be taken away from thee these things, when such thou shalt have become? Observe that they are taken away from evil men also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:27
verses.text: Why therefore dost thou delay conversion? That which thou fearest when good to lose, perchance if evil thou wilt lose still.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:28
verses.text: If being good thou shalt have lost them, there is by thee the Comforter that hath taken them away: the coffer is emptied of gold; the heart is full of faith: without, poor thou art, but within, rich thou art: thy riches with thee thou carriest, which thou wouldest not lose, even if naked from shipwreck thou shouldest escape.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:29
verses.text: Why doth not the loss, that perchance, if evil, thou wilt lose, find thee good; forasmuch as thou seest evil men also suffer loss? But with greater loss they are stricken: empty is the house, more empty the conscience is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:30
verses.text: Whatsoever evil man shall have lost these things, hath nothing to hold by without, hath nothing within whereon he may rest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:31
verses.text: He fleeth when he hath suffered loss from the place where before the eyes of men with the display of riches he used to vaunt himself; now in the eyes of men to vaunt himself he is not able: to himself within he returneth not, because he hath nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:32
verses.text: He hath not imitated the ant, he hath not gathered to himself grains, while it was summer What have I meant by, while it was summer? While he had quietude of life, while he had this world's prosperity, when he had leisure, when happy he was being called by all men, his summer it was.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:33
verses.text: He should have imitated the ant, he should have heard the Word of God, he should have gathered together grains, and he should have stored them within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:34
verses.text: There had come the trial of tribulation, there had come upon him a winter of numbness, tempest of fear, the cold of sorrow, whether it were loss, or any danger to his safety, or any bereavement of his family; or any dishonour and humiliation; it was winter; the ant falleth back upon that which in summer she hath gathered together; and within in her secret store, where no man seeth, she is recruited by her summer toils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:35
verses.text: When for herself she was gathering together these stores in summer, all men saw her: when on these she feedeth in winter, no one seeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:36
verses.text: What is this? See the ant of God, he riseth day by day, he hasteneth to the Church of God, he prayeth, he heareth lection, he chanteth hymn, he digesteth that which he hath heard, with himself he thinketh thereon, he storeth within grains gathered from the threshing-floor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:37
verses.text: They that providently hear those very things which even now are being spoken of, do thus, and by all men are seen to go forth to the Church, go back from Church, to hear sermon, to hear lection, to choose a book, open and read it: all these things are seen, when they are done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:38
verses.text: That ant is treading his path, carrying and storing up in the sight of men seeing him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:39
verses.text: There cometh winter sometime, for to whom cometh it not? There chanceth loss, there chanceth bereavement: other men pity him perchance as being miserable, who know not what the ant hath within to eat, and they say, miserable he whom this hath befallen, or what spirits, dost thou think, hath he whom this hath befallen? how afflicted is he? He measureth by himself, hath compassion according to his own strength; and thus he is deceived: because the measure wherewith he measureth himself, he would apply to him whom he knoweth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:40
verses.text: O sluggard, gather in summer while thou art able; winter will not suffer thee to gather, but to eat that which thou shalt have gathered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:41
verses.text: For how many men so suffer tribulation, that there is no opportunity either to read anything, or to hear anything, and they obtain no admittance, perchance, to those that would comfort them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:42
verses.text: The ant hath remained in her nest, let her see if she hath gathered anything in summer, whereby she may recruit herself in winter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:43
verses.text: There is a double interpretation, both must be given: "lighten," he saith, "Thy face upon us," show to us Thy countenance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:44
verses.text: For God doth not ever light His countenance, as if ever it had been without light: but He lighteth it upon us, so that what was hidden from us, is opened to us, and that which was, but to us was hidden, is unveiled upon us, that is, is lightened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:45
verses.text: Or else surely it is, "Thy image lighten upon us:" so that he said this, in "lighten Thy countenance upon us:" Thou hast imprinted Thy countenance upon us; Thou hast made us after Thine image and Thy likeness, Thou hast made us Thy coin; but Thine image ought not in darkness to remain: send a ray of Thy wisdom, let it dispel our darkness, and let there shine in us Thy image; let us know ourselves to be Thine image, let us hear what hath been said in the Song of Songs, "If Thou shalt not have known Thyself, O Thou fair one among women".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:46
verses.text: For there is said to the Church, "If Thou shalt not have known Thyself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:47
verses.text: What is this? If Thou shalt not have known Thyself to have been made after the image of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:48
verses.text: O Soul of the Church, precious, redeemed with the blood of the Lamb immaculate, observe of how great value Thou art, think what hath been given for Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:49
verses.text: Let us say, therefore, and let us long that He "may lighten His face upon us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:50
verses.text: We wear His face: in like manner as the faces of emperors are spoken of, truly a kind of sacred face is that of God in His own image: but unrighteous men know not in themselves the image of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:51
verses.text: In order that the countenance of God may be lightened upon them, they ought to say what? "Thou shalt light my candle, O Lord my God, Thou shalt light my darkness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:52
verses.text: I am in the darkness of sins, but by the ray of Thy wisdom dispelled be my darkness, may Thy countenance appear; and if perchance through me it appeareth somewhat deformed, by Thee be there reformed that which by Thee hath been formed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:53
verses.text: "That we may know on earth Thy way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:54
verses.text: "On earth," here, in this life, "we may know Thy way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:55
verses.text: What is, "Thy way"? That which leadeth to Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:56
verses.text: May we acknowledge whither we are going, acknowledge where we are as we go; neither in darkness we can do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:57
verses.text: Afar Thou art from men sojourning, a way to us Thou hast presented, through which we must return to Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:58
verses.text: "Let us acknowledge on earth Thy way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:59
verses.text: What is His way wherein we have desired, "That we may know on earth Thy way"? We are going to enquire this ourselves, not of ourselves to learn it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:60
verses.text: We can learn of it from the Gospel: "I am the Way," the Lord saith: Christ hath said, "I am the Way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:61
verses.text: But dost thou fear lest thou stray? He hath added, "And the Truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:62
verses.text: Who strayeth in the Truth? He strayeth that hath departed from the Truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:63
verses.text: The Truth is Christ, the Way is Christ: walk therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:64
verses.text: Dost thou fear lest thou die before thou attain unto Him? "I am the Life: I am," He saith, "the Way and the Truth and the Life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:65
verses.text: As if He were saying, "What fearest thou? Through Me thou walkest, to Me thou walkest, in Me thou restest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:66
verses.text: What therefore meaneth , "We may know on earth Thy Way," but "we may know on earth Thy Christ"? But let the Psalm itself reply: lest ye think that out of other Scriptures there must be adduced testimony, which perchance is here wanting: by repetition he hath shown what signified, "That we may know on earth Thy Way:" and as if thou wast inquiring, "In what earth, what way?" "In all nations Thy Salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:67
verses.text: In what earth, thou art inquiring? Hear: "In all nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:68
verses.text: What way art thou seeking? Hear: "Thy Salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:69
verses.text: Is not perchance Christ his Salvation? And what is that which the old Symeon hath said, that old man, I say, in the Gospel, preserved full of years even unto the infancy of the Word? For that old man took in his hands the Infant Word of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:70
verses.text: Would He that in the womb deigned to be, disdain to be in the hands of an old man? The Same was in the womb of the virgin, as was in the hands of the old man, a weak infant both within the bowels, and in the old man's hand, to give us strength, by whom were made all things; and if all things, even His very mother.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:71
verses.text: He came humble, He came weak, but clothed with a weakness to be changed into strength,  because "though He was crucified of weakness, yet He liveth of the virtue of God," the Apostle saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:72
verses.text: He was then in the hands of an old man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:73
verses.text: And what saith that old man? Rejoicing that now he must be loosed from this world, seeing how in his own hand was held He by whom and in whom his Salvation was upheld; he saith what? "Now Thou lettest go," he saith, "O Lord, Thy servant in peace, for mine eyes have seen Thy Salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:74
verses.text: Therefore, "May God bless us, and have pity on us; may He lighten His countenance upon us, that we may know on earth Thy Way!" In what earth? "In all nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:75
verses.text: What Way? "Thy Salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:76
verses.text: What followeth because the Salvation of God is known in all nations? "Let the peoples confess to Thee, O God" ; "confess to Thee," he saith, "all peoples".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:77
verses.text: There standeth forth a heretic, and he saith, In Africa I have peoples: and another from another quarter, And I in Galatia have peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:78
verses.text: Thou in Africa, he in Galatia: therefore I require one that hath them everywhere.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:79
verses.text: Ye have indeed dared to exult at that voice, when ye heard, "Let the peoples confess to Thee, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:80
verses.text: Hear the following verse, how he speaketh not of a part: "Let there confess to Thee all peoples".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:81
verses.text: Walk ye in the Way together with all nations; walk ye in the Way together with all peoples, O sons of peace, sons of the One Catholic Church, walk ye in the Way, seeing as ye walk.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:82
verses.text: Wayfarers do this to beguile their toil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:83
verses.text: Sing ye in this Way; I implore you by that Same Way, sing ye in this Way: a new song sing ye, let no one there sing old ones: sing ye the love-songs of your fatherland, let no one sing old ones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:84
verses.text: New Way, new wayfarer, new song.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:85
verses.text: Hear thou the Apostle exhorting thee to a new song: "Whatever therefore is in Christ is a new creature; old things have passed away, behold they have been made new".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:86
verses.text: A new song sing ye in the way, which ye have learned "on the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:87
verses.text: In what earth? "In all nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:88
verses.text: Therefore even the new song doth not belong to a part.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:89
verses.text: He that in a part singeth, singeth an old song: whatever he please to sing, he singeth an old song, the old man singeth: divided he is, carnal he is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:90
verses.text: Truly in so far as carnal he is, so far he is old; and in so far as he is spiritual, so far new.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:91
verses.text: See what saith the Apostle: "I could not speak to you as if to spiritual, but as if to carnal".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:92
verses.text: Whence proveth he them carnal? "For while one saith, I am of Paul; but another, I of Apollos: are ye not," he saith, "carnal?" Therefore in the Spirit a new song sing thou in the safe way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:93
verses.text: Just as wayfarers sing, and ofttimes in the night sing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:94
verses.text: Awful round about all things do sound, or rather they sound not around, but are still around; and the more still the more awful; nevertheless, even they that fear robbers do sing How much more safely thou singest in Christ! That way hath no robber, unless thou by forsaking the way fallest in the hands of a robber.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:95
verses.text: Why fear ye to confess, and in your confession to sing a new song together with all the earth; in all the earth, in Catholic peace, dost thou fear to confess to God, lest He condemn thee that hast confessed? If having not confessed thou liest concealed, having confessed thou wilt be condemned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:96
verses.text: Thou fearest to confess, that by not confessing canst not be concealed: thou wilt be condemned if thou hast held thy peace, that mightest have been delivered, by having confessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:97
verses.text: "O God, confess to Thee all peoples".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:98
verses.text: And because this confession leadeth not to punishment, he continueth and saith, "Let the nations rejoice and exult".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:99
verses.text: If robbers after confession made do wail before man, let the faithful after confessing before God rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:100
verses.text: If a man be judge, the torturer and his fear exact from a robber a confession: yea sometimes fear wringeth out confession, pain extorteth it: and he that waileth in tortures, but feareth to be killed if he confess, supporteth tortures as far as he is able: and if he shall have been overcome by pain, he giveth his voice for death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:101
verses.text: Nowise therefore is he joyful; nowise exulting: before he confesseth the claw teareth him; when he hath confessed, the executioner leadeth him along a condemned felon: wretched in every case.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:102
verses.text: But "let the nations rejoice and exult".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:103
verses.text: Whence? Through that same confession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:104
verses.text: Why? Because good He is to whom they confess: He exacteth confession, to the end that He may deliver the humble; He condemneth one not confessing, to the end that He may punish the proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:105
verses.text: Therefore be thou sorrowful before thou confessest; after having confessed exult, now thou wilt be made whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:106
verses.text: Thy conscience had gathered up evil humours, with boil it had swollen, it was torturing thee, it suffered thee not to rest: the Physician applieth the fomentations of words, and sometimes He lanceth it, He applieth the surgeon's knife by the chastisement of tribulation: do thou acknowledge the Physician's hand, confess thou, let every evil humour go forth and flow away in confession: now exult, now rejoice, that which remaineth will be easy to be made whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:107
verses.text: "Let the nations rejoice and exult, for Thou judgest the peoples in equity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:108
verses.text: And that unrighteous men may not fear, he hath added, "and the nations on the earth Thou directest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:109
verses.text: Depraved were the nations and crooked were the nations, perverse were the nations; for the ill desert of their depravity, and crookedness and perverseness, the Judge's coming they feared: there cometh the hand of the same, it is stretched out mercifully to the peoples, they are guided in order that they may walk the straight way; why should they fear the Judge to come, that have first acknowledged Him for a Corrector? To His hand let them give up themselves, Himself guideth the nations on the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:110
verses.text: But guided nations are walking in the Truth, are exulting in Him, are doing good works; and if perchance there cometh in any water (for on sea they are sailing) through the very small holes, through the crevices into the hold, pumping it out by good works, lest by more and more coming it accumulate, and sink the ship, pumping it out daily, fasting, praying, doing almsdeeds, saying with pure heart, "Forgive us our debts, as also we forgive our debtors" —saying such words walk thou secure, and exult in the way, sing in the way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:111
verses.text: Do not fear the Judge: before thou wast a believer, thou didst find a Saviour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:112
verses.text: Thee ungodly He sought out that He might redeem, thee redeemed will He forsake so as to destroy? "And the nations on earth Thou directest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:113
verses.text: He exulteth, rejoiceth, exhorteth, he repeateth those same verses in exhortation "The earth hath given her fruit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:114
verses.text: What fruit? "Let all peoples confess to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:115
verses.text: Earth it was, of thorns it was full; there came the hand of One rooting them up, there came a calling by His majesty and mercy, the earth began to confess; now the earth giveth her fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:116
verses.text: Would she give her fruit unless first she were rained on? Would she give her fruit, unless first the mercy of God had come from above? Let them read to me, thou sayest, how the earth being rained upon gave her fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:117
verses.text: Hear of the Lord raining upon her: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:118
verses.text: He raineth, and that same rain is thunder; it terrifieth: fear thou Him thundering, and receive Him raining.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:119
verses.text: Behold, after that voice of a thundering and raining God, after that voice let us see something out of the Gospel itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:120
verses.text: Behold that harlot of ill fame in the city burst into a strange house into which she had not been invited by the host, but by One invited she had been called; called not with tongue, but by Grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:121
verses.text: The sick woman knew that she had there a place, where she was aware that her Physician was sitting at meat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:122
verses.text: She has gone in, that was a sinner; she dareth not draw near save to the feet: she weepeth at His feet, she washeth with tears, she wipeth with hair, she anointeth with ointment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:123
verses.text: Why wonderest thou? The earth hath given her fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:124
verses.text: This thing, I say, came to pass by the Lord raining there through His own mouth; there came to pass the things whereof we read in the Gospel; and by His raining through His clouds, by the sending of the Apostles and by their preaching the truth, the earth more abundantly hath given her fruit, and that crop now hath filled the round world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:125
verses.text: The fruit of the earth was first in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:126
verses.text: For from thence began the Church: there came there the Holy Spirit, and filled full the holy men gathered together in one place; miracles were done, with the tongues of all men they spake They were filled full of the Spirit of God, the people were converted that were in that place, fearing and receiving the divine shower, by confession they brought forth so much fruit, that all their goods they brought together into a common stock, making distribution to the poor, in order that no one might call anything his own, but all things might be to them in common, and they might have one soul and one heart unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:127
verses.text: For there had been forgiven them the blood which they had shed, it had been forgiven them by the Lord pardoning, in order that now they might even learn to drink that which they had shed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:128
verses.text: Great in that place is the fruit: the earth hath given her fruit, both great fruit, and most excellent fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:129
verses.text: Ought by any means that earth alone to give her fruit? "May there bless us God, our God, may there bless us God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:130
verses.text: Still may He bless us: for blessing in multiplication is wont most chiefly and properly to be perceived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:131
verses.text: Let us prove this in Genesis; see the works of God: God made light, and God made a division between light and darkness: the light He called day, and the darkness He called night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:132
verses.text: It is not said, He blessed the light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:133
verses.text: For the same light returneth and changeth by days and nights.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:134
verses.text: He calleth the sky the firmament between waters and waters: it is not said, He blessed the sky: He severed the sea from the dry land, and named both, the dry land earth, and the gathering together of the waters sea: neither here is it said, God blessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:135
verses.text: How should we will that to us He come? By living well, by doing well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:136
verses.text: Let not things past please us; things present not hold us; let us not "close the ear" as it were with tail, let us not press down the ear on the ground; lest by things past we be kept back from hearing, lest by things present we be entangled and prevented from meditating on things future; let us reach forth unto those things which are before, let us forget things past And that for which now we toil, for which now we groan, for which now we sigh, of which now we speak, which in part, however small soever, we perceive, and to receive are not able, we shall receive, we shall thoroughly enjoy in the resurrection of the just.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:137
verses.text: Our youth shall be renewed as an eagle's, if only our old man we break against the Rock of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:138
verses.text: Whether those things be true, brethren, which are said of the serpent, or those which are said of the eagle, or whether it be rather a tale of men than truth, truth is nevertheless in the Scriptures, and not without reason the Scriptures have spoken of this: let us do whatever it signifieth, and not toil to discover how far that is true.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:139
verses.text: Be thou such an one, as that thy youth may be able to be renewed as an eagle's.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:140
verses.text: And know thou that it cannot be renewed, except thine old man on the Rock shall have been broken off: that is, except by the aid of the Rock, except by the aid of Christ, thou wilt not be able to be renewed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:141
verses.text: Do not thou because of the pleasantness of the past life be deaf to the word of God: do not by things present be so held and entangled, as to say, I have no leisure to read, I have no leisure to hear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:142
verses.text: This is to press down the ear upon the ground.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:143
verses.text: Do thou therefore not be such an one: but be such an one as on the other side thou findest, that is, so that thou forget things past, unto things before reach thyself out, in order that thine old man on the Rock thou mayest break off.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:144
verses.text: And if any comparisons shall have been made for thee, if thou hast found them in the Scriptures, believe: if thou shalt not have found them spoken of except by report, do not very much believe them The thing itself perchance is so, perchance is not so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:145
verses.text: Do thou profit by it, let that comparison avail for thy salvation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:146
verses.text: Thou art unwilling to profit by this comparison, by some other profit, it mattereth not provided thou do it: and, being secure, wait for the Kingdom of God, lest thy prayer quarrel with thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:147
verses.text: For, O Christian man, when thou sayest, Thy Kingdom come, how sayest thou, "Thy kingdom come"? Examine thy heart: see, behold, "Thy kingdom come:" He crieth out to thee, "I come:" dost thou not fear? Often we have told Your Love: both to preach the truth is nothing, if heart from tongue dissent: and to hear the truth is nothing, if fruit follow not hearing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:148
verses.text: From this place exalted as it were we are speaking to you: but how much we are beneath your feet in fear, God knoweth, who is gracious to the humble; for the voices of men praising do not give us so much pleasure as the devotion of men confessing, and the deeds of men now righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 68:149
verses.text: And how we have no pleasure but in your advances, but by those praises how much we are endangered, He knoweth, whom we pray to deliver us from all dangers, and to deign to know and crown us together with you, saved from every trial, in His Kingdom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:1
verses.text: Psalm LXVIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:2
verses.text: Of this Psalm, the title seemeth not to need operose discussion: f or simple and easy it appeareth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:3
verses.text: For thus it standeth: "For the end, for David himself a Psalm of a Song".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:4
verses.text: But in many Psalms already we have reminded you what is "at the end: for the end of the Law is Christ for righteousness to every man believing:" He is the end which maketh perfect, not that which con sumeth or destroyeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:5
verses.text: Nevertheless, if any one endeavoureth to inquire, what meaneth, "a Psalm of a So ng:" why not either "Psalm" or "Song," but both; or what is the difference between Psalm of Song, and Song of Psalm, because even thus of some Psalms the titles are inscribed: he will find perchance something which we leave for men more acute and more at leisure than ourselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:6
verses.text: "Let God rise up, and let His enemies be scattered".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:7
verses.text: Already this hath come to pass, Christ hath risen up, "who is over all things, God blessed for ever," and His enemies have been dispersed through all nations, to wit, the Jews; in that very place, where they practised their enmities, being overthrown in war, and thence through all places dispersed: and now they hate, but fear, and in that very fear they do that which followeth, "And let them that hate Him flee from His face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:8
verses.text: The flight indeed of the mind is fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:9
verses.text: For in carnal flight, whither flee they from the face of Him who everywhere showeth the efficacy  of His presence? "Whither shall I depart," saith he, "from Thy Spirit, and from Thy face whither shall I flee?" With mind, therefore, not with body, they flee; to wit, by being afraid, not by being hidden; and not from that face which they see not, but from that which they are compelled to see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:10
verses.text: For the face of Him hath His presence in His Church been called.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:11
verses.text: "As smoke faileth, let them fail".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:12
verses.text: For they lifted up themselves from the fires of their hatred unto the vapouring of pride, and against Heaven setting their mouth, and shouting, "Crucify, Crucify," Him taken captive they derided, Him hanging they mocked: and being soon conquered by that very Person against whom they swelled victorious, they vanished away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:13
verses.text: "As wax melteth from the face of fire, so let sinners perish from the face of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:14
verses.text: Though perchance in this passage he hath referred to those men, whose hard-heartedness in tears of penitence is dissolved: yet this also may be understood, that he threateneth future judgment; because though in this world like smoke, in lifting up themselves, that is, in priding themselves, they have melted away, there will come to them at the last final damnation, so that from His face they will perish for everlasting, when in His own glory He shall have appeared, like fire, for the punishment of the ungodly, and the light of the righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:15
verses.text: Lastly, there followeth, "And let just men be joyous, and exult in the sight of God, let them delight in gladness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:16
verses.text: For then shall they hear, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive ye the kingdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:17
verses.text: "Let them be joyous," therefore, that have toiled, "and exult in the sight of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:18
verses.text: For there will not be in this exultation, as though it were before men, any empty boasting; but (it will be) in the sight of Him who unerringly looketh into that which He hath granted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:19
verses.text: "Let them delight in gladness:" no longer exulting with trembling, as in this world, so long as "human life is a trial upon earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:20
verses.text: Secondly, he turneth himself to those very persons to whom he hath given so great hope, and to them while here living he speaketh and exhorteth: "Sing ye to God, psalm ye to His name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:21
verses.text: Already on this subject in the exposition of the Title we have before spoken that which seemed meet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:22
verses.text: He singeth to God, that liveth to God: He psalmeth to His name, that worketh unto His Glory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:23
verses.text: In singing thus, in psalming thus, that is, by so living, by so working, "a way make ye to Him," he saith, "that hath ascended above the setting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:24
verses.text: A way make ye to Christ: so that through the beautiful feet of men telling good tidings,  the hearts of men believing many have a way opened to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:25
verses.text: For the Same is He that hath ascended above the "setting:" either because the new life of one turned to Him receiveth Him not, except the old life shall have set by his renouncing this world, or because He ascended above the setting, when by rising again He conquered the downfall of the body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:26
verses.text: "For The Lord is His name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:27
verses.text: Which if they had known, the Lord of glory they never would have crucified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:28
verses.text: "Exult ye in the sight of Him," O ye to whom hath been said, "Sing ye to God, psalm ye to the name of Him, a way make ye to Him that hath ascended above the setting," also "exult in the sight of Him:" as if "sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:29
verses.text: For while ye make a way to Him, while ye prepare a way whereby He may come and possess the nations, ye are to suffer in the sight of men many sorrowful things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:30
verses.text: But not only faint not, but even exult, not in the sight of men, but in the sight of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:31
verses.text: "In hope rejoicing, in tribulation enduring:" "exult ye in the sight of Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:32
verses.text: For they that in the sight of men trouble you, "shall be troubled by the face of Him, the Father of orphans and Judge of widows".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:33
verses.text: For desolate they suppose them to be, from whom ofttimes by the sword of the Word of God both parents from sons, and husbands from wives, are severed: but persons destitute and widowed have the consolation "of the Father of orphans and Judge of widows:" they have the consolation of Him that say to Him, "For my father and my mother have forsaken me, but the Lord hath taken up me:" and they that have hoped in the Lord, continuing in prayers by night and by day: by whose face those men shall be troubled when they shall have seen themselves prevail nothing, for that the whole world hath gone away after Him For out of those orphans and widows, that is, persons destitute of partnership in this world's hope, the Lord for Himself doth build a Temple: whereof in continuation he saith, "The Lord is in His holy place".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:34
verses.text: For what is His place he hath disclosed, when he saith, "God that maketh to dwell men of one mood in a house" : men of one mind, of one sentiment: this is the holy place of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:35
verses.text: For when he had said, "The Lord is in His holy place:" as though we were inquiring in what place, since He is everywhere wholly, and no place of corporal space containeth Him; forthwith he hath subjoined somewhat, that we should not seek Him apart from ourselves, but rather being of one mood dwelling in a house, we should deserve that He also Himself deign to dwell among us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:36
verses.text: This is the holy place of the Lord, the thing that most men seek to have, a place where in prayer they may be hearkened unto.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:37
verses.text: For as in a great house of a man, the Lord thereof doth not abide in every place whatsoever, but in some place doubtless more private and honourable: so God dwelleth not in all men that are in His house (for He dwelleth not in the vessels of dishonour), but His holy place are they whom "He maketh to dwell of one mood," or "of one manner, in a house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:38
verses.text: For what are called τρόποι in Greek, by both modi and mores (moods and manners), in Latin may be interpreted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:39
verses.text: Nor hath the Greek writer, "Who maketh to dwell," but only "maketh to dwell".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:40
verses.text: "The Lord," then, "is in His holy place".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:41
verses.text: But to prove that by His Grace He buildeth to Himself this place, not for the sake of the merits preceding of those persons out of whom He buildeth it, see what followeth: "Who leadeth forth men fettered, in strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:42
verses.text: For He looseth the heavy bonds of sins, wherewith they were fettered so that they could not walk in the way of the commandments: but He leadeth them forth "in strength," which before His Grace they had not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:43
verses.text: "Likewise men provoking that dwell in the tombs:" that is, every way dead, taken up with dead works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:44
verses.text: For these men provoke Him to anger by withstanding justice: for those fettered men perchance would walk, and are not able, and are praying of God that they may be able, and are saying to Him, "From my necessities lead me forth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:45
verses.text: By whom being heard, they give thanks, saying, "Thou hast broken asunder my bonds".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:46
verses.text: But these provoking men that dwell in the tombs, are of that kind, which in another passage the Scripture pointeth out, saying, "From a dead man, as from one that is not, confession perisheth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:47
verses.text: Whence there is this saying, "When a sinner shall have come into the depth of evil things, he despiseth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:48
verses.text: For it is one thing to long for, another thing to fight against righteousness: one thing from evil to desire to be delivered, another thing one's evil doings to defend rather than to confess: both kinds nevertheless the Grace of Christ leadeth forth in strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:49
verses.text: With what strength, but that wherewith against sin even unto blood they are to strive? For out of each kind are made meet persons, whereof to construct His holy place; those being loosened, these being raised to life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:50
verses.text: For even of the woman, whom Satan had bound for eighteen years, by His command He loosed the bonds; and Lazarus' death by His voice He overcame He that hath done these things in bodies, is able to do more marvellous things in characters, and to make men of one mood to dwell in a house: "leading forth men fettered in strength, likewise men provoking that dwell in the tombs".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:51
verses.text: "O God, when Thou wentest forth before Thy people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:52
verses.text: His going forth is perceived, when He appeareth in His works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:53
verses.text: But He appeareth not to all men, but to them that know how to spy out His works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:54
verses.text: For I do not now speak of those works which are conspicuous to all men, Heaven and earth and sea and all things that in them are; but the works whereby He leadeth forth men fettered in strength, likewise men provoking that dwell in the tombs, and maketh them of one manner to dwell in a house.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:55
verses.text: Thus He goeth forth before His people, that is, before those that do perceive this His Grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:56
verses.text: Lastly, there followeth, "When Thou wentest by in the desert, the earth was moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:57
verses.text: A desert were the nations, which knew not God: a desert they were, where by God Himself no law had been given, where no Prophet had dwelled, and foretold the Lord to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:58
verses.text: "When," then, "Thou wentest by in the desert," when Thou wast preached in the nations; "the earth was moved," to the faith earthly men were stirred up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:59
verses.text: But whence was it moved? "For the heavens dropped from the face of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:60
verses.text: Perchance here some one calleth to mind that time, when in the desert God was going over before His people, before the sons of Israel, by day in the pillar of cloud, by night in the brightness of fire; and determineth that thus it is that "the heavens dropped from the face of God," for manna He rained upon His people: that the same thing also is that which followeth, "Mount Sina from the face of the God of Israel," "with voluntary rain severing God to Thine inheritance" , namely, the God that on Mount Sina spake to Moses, when He gave the Law, so that the manna is the voluntary rain, which God severed for His inheritance, that is, for His people; because them alone He so fed, not the other nations also: so that what next he saith, "and it was weakened," is understood of the inheritance being itself weakened; for they murmuring, fastidiously loathed the manna, longing for victuals of flesh, and those things on which they had been accustomed to live in Egypt Lastly, all those men in the desert were stricken down, nor were any of them except two found worthy to go into the land of promise Although even if in the sons of them that inheritance be said to have been perfected, we ought more readily to hold to a spiritual sense.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:61
verses.text: For all those things in a figure did happen to them; until the day should break, and the shadows should be removed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:62
verses.text: May then the Lord open to us that knock; and may the secret things of His mysteries, as far as Himself vouchsafeth, be disclosed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:63
verses.text: For in order that the earth might be moved to the Truth when into the desert of the Gentiles the Gospel was passing, "t he Heavens dropped from the face of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:64
verses.text: These are the Heavens, whereof in another Psalm is sung, "The Heavens are telling forth the glory of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:65
verses.text: So here also, "the Heavens dropped;" but "from the face of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:66
verses.text: For even these very persons have been "saved through faith, and this not of themselves, but God's gift it is, not of works, lest perchance any man should be lifted up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:67
verses.text: For of Himself we are the workmanship," "that maketh men of one mood to dwell in a house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:68
verses.text: But what is that which followeth, "Mount Sina from the face of the God of Israel"? Must there be understood "dropped;" so that what he hath called by the name of Heavens, the same he hath willed to be understood under the name of Mount Sina also; just as we said that those are called mountains, which were called Heavens? Nor in this sense ought it to move us that He saith "mountain," not m ountains, while in that place they were called "Heavens," not Heaven: for in another Psalm also after it had been said, "The Heavens are telling forth the glory of God:" after the manner of Scripture repeating the same sense in different words, subsequently there is said, "And the firmament telleth the works of His hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:69
verses.text: First he said "Heavens," not "Heaven:" and yet afterwards not "firmaments," but "firmament".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:70
verses.text: For God called the firmament Heaven, as in Genesis hath been written.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:71
verses.text: Thus then Heavens and Heaven, mountains and mountain, are not a different thing, but the very same thing: just as Churches many, and the One Church, are not a different thing, but the very same thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:72
verses.text: Why then "Mount Sina, which gendereth unto bondage"? as saith the Apostle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:73
verses.text: Is perchance the Law itself to be understood in Mount Sina, as that which "the Heavens dropped from the face of God," in order that the earth might be moved? And is this the very moving of the earth, when men are troubled, because the Law they cannot fulfil? But if so it is, this is the voluntary rain, whereof in confirmation he saith, "Voluntary rain God severing to Thine inheritance:" because "He hath not done so to any nation, and His judgment He hath not manifested to them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:74
verses.text: God therefore set apart this voluntary rain to His inheritance because He gave the Law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:75
verses.text: And "there was made weak," either the Law, or the inheritance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:76
verses.text: The Law may be understood to have been made weak, because it was not fulfilled; not that of itself it is weak, but because it maketh men weak, by threatening punishment, and not aiding through grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:77
verses.text: For also the very word the Apostle hath used, where he saith, "For that which was impossible of the Law, wherein it was made weak through the flesh:" willing to intimate that through the Spirit it is fulfilled: nevertheless, itself he hath said is made weak, because by weak men it cannot be fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:78
verses.text: But the inheritance, that is, the people, without any doubt is understood to have been made weak by the giving to them of the Law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:79
verses.text: For "the Law came in, that transgression might abound".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:80
verses.text: But that which followeth, "But Thou hast made it perfect," to the Law is thus referred, forasmuch as it is made perfect, that is, is fulfilled after that which the Lord saith in the Gospel, "I have not come to annul the Law, but to fulfil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:81
verses.text: There is in these words yet another sense: which seemeth to me more to approve itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:82
verses.text: For much more in accordance with the context, grace itself is understood to be the voluntary rain, because with no preceding merits of works it is given gratis "For if grace, no longer of works: otherwise grace no longer is grace".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:83
verses.text: "But to humble men He giveth grace".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:84
verses.text: And it was made weak, but Thou hast made it perfect:" because "virtue in weakness is perfected".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:85
verses.text: Some copies indeed, both Latin and Greek, have not "Mount Sina;" but, "from the face of the God of Sina, from the face of the God of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:86
verses.text: That is, "The Heavens dropped from the face of God:" and, as if enquiry were made of what God, "from the face of the God," he saith, "of Sina, from the face of the God of Israel," that is, from the face of the God that gave the Law to the people of Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:87
verses.text: Why then "the Heavens dropped from the face of God," from the face of this God, but because thus was fulfilled that which had been foretold, "Blessing He shall give that hath given the Law"? The Law whereby to terrify a man that relieth on human powers; blessing, whereby He delivereth a man that hopeth in God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:88
verses.text: Thou then, O God, hast made perfect Thine inheritance; because it is made weak in itself, in order that it may be made perfect by Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:89
verses.text: "Thine animals shall dwell therein".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:90
verses.text: "Thine," not their own; to Thee subject, not for themselves free; for Thee needy, not for themselves sufficient.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:91
verses.text: Lastly, he continueth, "Thou hast prepared in Thine own sweetness for the needy, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:92
verses.text: "In Thine own sweetness," not in his meetness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:93
verses.text: For the needy he is, for he hath been made weak, in order that he may be made perfect: he hath acknowledged himself indigent, that he may be replenished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:94
verses.text: This is that sweetness, whereof in another place is said, "The Lord shall give sweetness, and our land shall give her fruit:" in order that a good work may be done not for fear, but for love; not for dread of punishment, but for love of righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:95
verses.text: For this is true and sound freedom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:96
verses.text: But the Lord hath prepared this for one wanting, not for one abounding, whose reproach is that poverty: of which sort in another place is said, "Reproach to these men that abound, and contempt to proud men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:97
verses.text: For those he hath called proud, whom he hath called them that abound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:98
verses.text: "The Lord shall give the Word" : to wit, food for His animals which shall dwell therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:99
verses.text: But what shall these animals work to whom He shall give the word? What but that which followeth? "To them preaching the Gospel in much virtue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:100
verses.text: With what virtue, but with that strength wherein He leadeth forth men fettered? Perchance also here he speaketh of that virtue, wherewith in preaching the Gospel they wrought wondrous signs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:101
verses.text: Who then "shall give the Word to men preaching the Gospel with much virtue"? "The King," he saith, "of the virtues of the Beloved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:102
verses.text: The Father therefore is King of the virtues of the Son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:103
verses.text: For the Beloved, when there is not specified any person that is beloved, by a substitution of name, of the Only Son is understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:104
verses.text: Is not the Son Himself King of His virtues, to wit of the virtues serving Himself? Because with much virtue the King of Virtues shall give the Word to men preaching the Gospel, of Whom it hath been said, "The Lord of Virtues, He is the King of Glory?"  But his not having said King of Virtues, but "King of the Virtues of the beloved," is a most usual expression in the Scriptures, if any one observe: which thing chiefly appeareth in those cases where even the person's own name is already expressed, so that it cannot at all be doubted that it is the same person of whom something is said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:105
verses.text: Of which sort also is that which in the Pentateuch in many passages is found: "And Moses did it, as the Lord commanded Moses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:106
verses.text: He said not that which is usual in our expressions, And Moses did, as the Lord commanded him; but, "Moses did as the Lord commanded Moses," as if one person were the Moses whom He commanded, and another person the Moses who did, whereas it is the very same.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:107
verses.text: In the New Testament such expressions are most difficult to find"The King," therefore, "of the virtues of the Beloved," thus may be understood, as if it were to be said, the King of His virtues, because both King of Virtues is Christ, and the Beloved is the very same Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:108
verses.text: However, this sense hath not so great urgency, as that no other can be accepted: because the Father also may be understood as King of the virtues of His Beloved Son, to whom the Beloved Himself saith, "All Mine are Thine, and Thine Mine".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:109
verses.text: But if perchance it is asked, whether God the Father of the Lord Jesus Christ can be called King also, I know not whether any one would dare to withhold this name from Him in the passage where the Apostle saith, "But to the King of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:110
verses.text: Because even if this be said of the Trinity itself, therein is also God the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:111
verses.text: But if we do not carnally understand, "O God, Thy Judgment to the King give Thou, and Thy justice to the Son of the King:" I know not whether anything else hath been said than, "to Thy Son".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:112
verses.text: King therefore is the Father also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:113
verses.text: Whence that verse of this Psalm, "King of the virtues of the Beloved;" in either way may be understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:114
verses.text: When therefore he had said, "The Lord shall give the Word to men preaching the Gospel with much virtue:" because virtue itself by Him is ruled, and serveth Him by whom it is given; the Lord Himself, he saith, who shall give the Word to men preaching the Gospel with much virtue, is the King of the virtues of the Beloved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:115
verses.text: In the next place there followeth, "Of the Beloved, and of the beauty of the House to divide the spoils".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:116
verses.text: The repetition belongeth to eulogy But whether it be repeated, or whether it be received as spoken once, the word which hath been set down, namely, "Beloved," I suppose that thus must be understood that which followeth, "and of the beauty of a house to divide the spoils;" as if there were said, "Chosen even to divide the spoils of the beauty of a house," that is, Chosen even for dividing the spoils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:117
verses.text: For beautiful Christ hath made His House, that is, the Church, by dividing to Her spoils: in the same manner as the Body is beautiful in the distribution of the members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:118
verses.text: "Spoils" moreover those are called that are stripped off from conquered foes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:119
verses.text: What this is the Gospel adviseth us in the passage where we read, "No one goeth into the house of a strong man to spoil his vessels, unless first he shall have bound the strong man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:120
verses.text: Christ therefore hath bound the devil with spiritual bonds, by overcoming death, and by ascending from Hell above the Heavens: He hath bound him by the Sacrament of His Incarnation, because though finding nothing in Him deserving of death, yet he was permitted to kill: and from him so bound He took away his vessels as though they were spoils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:121
verses.text: For he was working in the sons of disobedience, of whose unbelief he made use to work his own will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:122
verses.text: These vessels the Lord cleansing by the remission of sins, sanctifying these spoils wrested from the foe laid prostrate and bound, these He hath divided to the beauty of His House; making some apostles, some prophets, some pastors and doctors, for the work of the ministry, for the building up of the Body of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:123
verses.text: For as the body is one, and hath many members, and though all the members of the body are many, the body is one: so also is Christ "Are all Apostles? Are all Prophets? Are all Powers? Have all the gifts of healings? Do all speak with tongues? Do all interpret?" "But all these things worketh one and the same Spirit, dividing to each one his own gifts, as He willeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:124
verses.text: And such is the beauty of the house, whereto the spoils are divided, that a lover thereof with this fairness being enkindled, crieth out, "O Lord, I have loved the grace of Thy House".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:125
verses.text: Now in that which followeth, he turneth himself to address the members themselves, whereof the beauty of the House is composed, saying, "If ye sleep in the midst of the lots, wings of a dove silvered, and between the shoulders thereof in the freshness of gold".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:126
verses.text: First, we must here examine the order of the words, in what manner the sentence is ended; which certainly awaiteth, when there is said, "If ye sleep:" secondly, in that which he saith, namely, "wings of dove silvered," whether in the singular number it must be understood as being, "of this wing" thereof, or in the plural as, "these wings".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:127
verses.text: But the singular number the Greek excludeth, where always in the plural we read it written.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:128
verses.text: But still it is uncertain whether it be these wings; or whether, "O ye wings," so as that he may seem to speak to the wings themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:129
verses.text: Whether therefore by the words which have preceded, that sentence be ended, so that the order is, "The Lord shall give the Word to men preaching the Gospel with much virtue, if ye sleep in the midst of the lots, O ye wings of a dove silvered:" or by these which follow, so that the order is, "If ye sleep in the midst of the lots, the wings of a dove silvered with snow shall be whitened in Selmon:" that is, the wings themselves shall be whitened, if ye sleep in the midst "of the lots:" so that he may be understood to say this to them that are divided to the beauty of the House, as it were spoils; that is, if ye sleep in the "midst of the lots," O ye that are divided to the beauty of the House, "through the manifestation of the Spirit unto profit," so that "to one indeed is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:130
verses.text: , if then ye sleep in the midst of the lots, then the wings of a dove silvered with snow shall be whitened in Selmon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:131
verses.text: It may also be thus: "If ye being the wings of a dove silvered, sleep in the midst of the lots, with snow they shall be whitened in Selmon," so as that those men be understood who through grace receive remission of sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:132
verses.text: Whence also of the Church Herself, is said in the Song of Songs, "Who is She that goeth up whitened?" For this promise of God is held out through the Prophet, saying, "If your sins shall have been like scarlet, like snow I will whiten them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:133
verses.text: It may also thus be understood, so that in that which hath been said, "wings of a dove silvered," there be understood, ye shall be, so that this is the sense, O ye that like as it were spoils to the beauty of the house are divided, if ye sleep in the "midst of the lots," wings of a dove silvered ye shall be: that is, into higher places ye shall be lifted up, adhering however to the bond of the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:134
verses.text: For I think no other dove silvered can be better perceived here, than that whereof hath been said, "One is My dove".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:135
verses.text: But silvered She is because with divine sayings she hath been instructed: for the sayings of the Lord in another place are called "silver with fire refined, purged sevenfold".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:136
verses.text: Some great good thing therefore it is, to sleep in the midst of the lots, which some would have to be the Two Testaments, so that to "sleep in the midst of the lots" is to rest on the authority of those Testaments, that is, to acquiesce in the testimony of either Testament: so that whenever anything out of them is produced and proved, all strife is ended in peaceful acquiescence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:137
verses.text: "Between the shoulders," however.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:138
verses.text: This is indeed a part of the body, it is a part about the region of the heart, at the hinder parts however, that is, at the back: which part of that dove silvered he saith is "in the greenness of gold," that is, in the vigour of wisdom, which vigour I think cannot be better understood than by love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:139
verses.text: But why on the back, and not on the breast? Although I wonder in what sense this word is put in another Psalm, where there is said, "Between His shoulders He shall overshadow thee, and under His wings thou shalt hope:" forasmuch as under wings there cannot be overshadowed anything but what shall be under the breast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:140
verses.text: And in Latin, indeed, "between the shoulders," perchance in some degree of both parts may be understood, both before and behind, that we may take shoulders to be the parts which have the head betwixt them; and in Hebrew perchance the word is ambiguous, which may in this manner also be understood: but the word that is in the Greek, μετ€φρενα, signifieth not anything but at the back, which is "between the shoulders".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:141
verses.text: Is there for this reason there the greenness of gold, that is, wisdom and love, because in that place there are in a manner the roots of the wings? or because in that place is carried that light burden? For what are even the wings themselves, but the two commandments of love, whereon hangeth the whole Law and the Prophets? what is that same light burden, but that same love which in these two commandments is fulfilled? For whatever thing is difficult in a commandment, is a light thing to a lover.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:142
verses.text: Nor on any other account is rightly understood the saying, "My burden is light," but because He giveth the Holy Spirit, whereby love is shed abroad in our hearts, in order that in love we may do freely that which he that doeth in fear doeth slavishly; nor is he a lover of what is right, when he would prefer, if so be it were possible, that what is right should not be commanded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:143
verses.text: It may also be required, when it hath not been said, if ye sleep in the lots, but "in the midst of the lots;" what this is, "in the midst of the lots".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:144
verses.text: Which expression indeed, if more exactly it were translated from the Greek, would signify, "in the midst between the lots," which is in no one of the interpreters I have read: therefore I suppose, that what hath been said signifieth much the same, to wit the expression, "in the midst of the lots".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:145
verses.text: Hence therefore what seemeth to me I will explain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:146
verses.text: Ofttimes this word is wont to be used for uniting and pacifying one thing and another, that they may not mutually disagree: as when God is establishing His covenant between Himself and His people, this word the Scripture useth; for instead of that expression which is in Latin between Me and you, the Greek hath, in the midst of Me and you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:147
verses.text: So also of the sign of Circumcision, when God speaketh to Abraham, He saith, "There shall be a testament between Me and thee and all thy seed:" which the Greek hath, in the midst of Me and thee, and the midst of thy seed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:148
verses.text: Also when He was speaking to Noe of the bow in the clouds to establish a sign, this word very often He repeateth: and that which the Latin copies have, between Me and you, or between Me and every living soul, and whatever suchlike expressions there are used, is found in the Greek to be, in the middle of Me and you, which is ‡νὰ μ™σον.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:149
verses.text: David also and Jonathan establish a sign between them, that they may not disagree with a difference of thought: and that which in Latin is expressed, between both, in the middle of both, the Greek hath expressed in the same word, which is ‡νὰ μ™σον.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:150
verses.text: But it was best that in this passage of the Psalms our translators said not, "among the lots," which expression is more suited to the Latin idiom; but, "in the midst of the lots," as though "in the midst between the lots," which rather is the reading in the Greek, and which is wont to be said in the case of those things which ought to have a mutual consent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:151
verses.text: But why in the "lots" the Testaments should be perceived, though this word is Greek, and the Testament is not so named, the reason is, because through a testament is given inheritance, which in Greek is called κληρονομία, and an heir κληρονόμος Now κλῆρος in Greek is the term for lot, and lots according to the promise of God are called those parts of the inheritance which were distributed to the people Whence the tribe of Levi was commanded not to have lot among their brethren, because they were sustained by tithes from them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:152
verses.text: For, I think, they that have been ordained in the grades of the Ecclesiastical Ministry have been called both Clergy and Clerks, because Matthias by lot was chosen, who we read was the first that was ordained by the Apostles Henceforth, because of inheritance which is given by testament, as though by that which is made that which maketh, by the name of "lots" the Testaments themselves are signified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:153
verses.text: Nevertheless, to me here another sense also occurreth, if I mistake not, to be preferred; understanding by cleri the inheritances themselves: so that, whereas the inheritance of the Old Testament, although in a shadow significant of the future, is earthly felicity; but the inheritance of the New Testament is everlasting immortality; to "sleep in the midst of the lots" is not too earnestly now to seek the former, and still patiently to look for the latter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:154
verses.text: And because so well they have slept, on them, as it were on wings now flieth, and with praises is exalted, the Church: to wit, the Dove silvered, in order that by this fame of theirs, posterity having been invited to imitate them, while in like manner the rest also sleep, there may be added wings whereby even unto the end of the world sublimely she may be preached.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:155
verses.text: "While He that is above the heavens distinguisheth kings over Her, with snow they shall be made white in Selmon".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:156
verses.text: While He "above the heavens," He that ascended over all heavens that He might fulfil all things, "while He distinguisheth kings over Her," that is, over that same "Dove silvered".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:157
verses.text: For the Apostle continueth and saith, and "He hath Himself given some for Apostles, and some Prophets, and some Evangelists, and some Pastors and Teachers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:158
verses.text: For what other reason is there to distinguish kings over Her, save for the work of the Ministry, for the edification of the Body of Christ: when she is indeed Herself the Body of Christ? But they are called kings from ruling: and what more than the lusts of the flesh, that sin may not reign in their mortal body to obey the desires thereof, that they yield not their members instruments of iniquity unto sin, but yield themselves to God, as though from the dead living, and their members instruments of righteousness to God? For thus shall the kings be distinguished from foreigners, because they draw not the yoke with unbelievers: secondly, in a peaceful manner being distinguished from one another by their proper gifts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:159
verses.text: For not all are Apostles, or all Prophets, or all Teachers, or all have gifts of healings, or all with tongues do speak, or all interpret "But all these things worketh one and the same Spirit, dividing proper gifts to each one as He willeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:160
verses.text: In giving which Spirit He that is above the Heavens distinguisheth kings over the Dove silvered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:161
verses.text: Of which Holy Spirit, when, sent to His Mother full of grace, the Angel was speaking, to her enquiring in what manner it could come to pass that she was announced as going to bear, seeing she knew not a man:he saith, "The Holy Spirit shall come over upon thee, and the virtue of the Most Highest shall overshadow thee," that is, shall make a shadow for thee, "wherefore that Holy Thing which shall be born of thee, shall be called the Son of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:162
verses.text: That "shadow" again is understood of a defence against the heat of carnal lusts: whence not in carnal concupiscence, but in spiritual belief, the Virgin conceived Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:163
verses.text: But the shadow consisteth of light and body: and further, The "Word" that "was in the beginning," that true Light, in order that a noonday shadow might be made for us; "the Word," I say, "was made Flesh, and dwelled in us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:164
verses.text: But this mountain he calleth the "mountain of God, a mountain fruitful, a mountain full of curds" , or "a mountain fat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:165
