verses.text: But here what else would he call fat but fruitful? For there is also a mountain called by that name, that is to say, Selmon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:166
verses.text: But what mountain ought we to understand by "the mountain of God, a mountain fruitful, a mountain full of curds," but the same Lord Christ? Of whom also another Prophet saith, "There shall be manifest in the last times the mountain of the Lord prepared on the top of the mountains"? He is Himself the "Mountain full of curds," because of the babes to be fed with grace as though it were with milk; a mountain rich to strengthen and enrich them by the excellence of the gifts; for even the milk itself whence curd is made, in a wonderful manner signifieth grace; for it floweth out of the overflowing of the mother's bowels, and of a sweet compassion unto babes freely it is poured forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:167
verses.text: But in the Greek the case is doubtful, whether it be the nominative or the accusative: for in that language mountain is of the neuter gender, not of the masculine: therefore some Latin translators have not translated it, "unto the Mountain of God," but, "the Mountain of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:168
verses.text: But I think, "unto Selmon the Mountain of God," is better, that is, "unto" the Mountain of God which is called Selmon: according to the interpretation which, as we best could, we have explained above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:169
verses.text: Secondly, in the expression, "Mountain of God, Mountain full of curds," Mountain "fruitful," let no one dare from this to compare the Lord Jesus Christ with the rest of the Saints, who are themselves also called mountains of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:170
verses.text: For there were not wanting men to call Him, some John Baptist, some Elias, some Jeremias, or one of the Prophets; He turneth to them and saith, "Why do ye imagine mountains full of curds, a mountain," he saith, "wherein it hath pleased God to dwell therein"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:171
verses.text: "Why do ye imagine?" For as they are a light, because to themselves also hath been said, "Ye are the Light of the world," but something different hath been called "the true Light which enlighteneth every man," so they are mountains; but far different is the Mountain "prepared on the top of the mountains".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:172
verses.text: These mountains therefore in bearing that Mountain are glorious: one of which mountains saith, "but from me far be it to glory, save in the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom to me the world hath been crucified, and I to the world:" so that "he hath glorieth, not in himself, but in the Lord may glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:173
verses.text: "Why" then "do ye imagine mountains full of curds," that "Mountain wherein it hath pleased God to dwell therein"? Not because in other men He dwelleth not, but because in them through Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:174
verses.text: "For in Him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead," not in a shadow, as in the temple made by king Solomon, but "bodily," that is, solidly and truly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:175
verses.text: "For there is One God, and One Mediator of God and men, the Man Christ Jesus," Mountain of mountains, as Saint of saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:176
verses.text: Whence He saith, "I in them and Thou in Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:177
verses.text: "Why then do ye imagine mountains full of curds, the mountain wherein it hath pleased God to dwell in Him?" For those mountains full of curds that Mountain the Lord shall inhabit even unto the end, that something they may be to whom He saith, "for without Me nothing ye are able to do".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:178
verses.text: Thus cometh to pass that also which followeth: "The Chariot of God is of ten thousands manifold:" or "of tens of thousands manifold:" or, "ten times thousand times manifold".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:179
verses.text: For one Greek word, which hath there been used, μυριοπλ€σιον, each Latin interpreter hath rendered as best he could, but in Latin it could not be adequately expressed: for a thousand with the Greeks is called χίλια, but μυρι€δες are a number of tens of thousands: for one μυριὰς are ten thousands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:180
verses.text: Thus a vast number of saints and believers, who by bearing God become in a manner the chariot of God, he hath signified under this name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:181
verses.text: By abiding in and guiding this, He conducteth it, as though it were His Chariot, unto the end, as if unto some appointed place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:182
verses.text: For, "the beginning is Christ; secondly, that are of Christ, at the appearing of Him; then the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:183
verses.text: This is Holy Church: which is that which followeth, "thousands of men rejoicing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:184
verses.text: For in hope they are joyful, until they be conducted unto the end, which now they look for through patience For admirably, when he had said, "Thousands of men rejoicing:" immediately he added, "The Lord is in them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:185
verses.text: That we may not wonder why they rejoice, "The Lord is in them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:186
verses.text: For through many tribulations we must needs enter into the kingdom of God, but, "The Lord is in them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:187
verses.text: Therefore even if they are as it were sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing, though not now in that same end, to which they have not yet come, yet in hope they are rejoicing, and in tribulation patient: for, "The Lord is in them, in Sina in the holy place".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:188
verses.text: In the interpretations of Hebrew names, we find Sina interpreted commandment: and some other interpretations it has, but I think this to be more agreeable to the present passage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:189
verses.text: For giving a reason why those thousands rejoice, whereof the Chariot of God doth consist, "The Lord," he saith, "is in them, in Sins in the holy place:" that is, the Lord is in them, in the commandment; which commandment is holy, as saith the Apostle: "Therefore the law indeed is holy, and the commandment is holy, and just, and good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:190
verses.text: In the next place, turning his address to the Lord Himself, "Thou hast gone up," he saith, "on high, Thou hast led captivity captive, Thou hast received gifts in men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:191
verses.text: Of this the Apostle thus maketh mention, thus expoundeth in speaking of the Lord Christ: "But unto each one of us," he saith, "is given grace after the measure of the giving of Christ: for which cause he saith, He hath gone up on high, He hath led captive captivity, He hath given gifts to men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:192
verses.text: And let it not move us that the Apostle making mention of that same testimony saith not, "Thou hast received gifts in men;" but, "He hath given gifts unto men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:193
verses.text: For he with Apostolic authority hath spoken thus according to the faith that the Son is God with the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:194
verses.text: For in respect of this He hath given gifts to men, sending to them the Holy Spirit, which is the Spirit of the Father and of the Son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:195
verses.text: But forasmuch as the self-same Christ is understood in His Body which is the Church, wherefore also His members are His saints and believers, whence to them is said, "But ye are the Body of Christ, and the members," doubtless He hath Himself also received gifts in men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:196
verses.text: Now Christ hath gone up on high, and sitteth at the right hand of the Father: but unless He were here also on the earth, He would not thence have cried, "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" When the Same saith Himself, "Inasmuch as to one of My least ye have done it, to Me ye have done it:" why do we doubt that He receiveth in His members, the gifts which the members of Him receive?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:197
verses.text: But what is, "Thou hast led captivity captive"? Is it because He hath conquered death, which was holding captive those over whom it reigned? Or hath he called men themselves captivity, who  were being held captive under the devil? Which thing's mystery even the title of that Psalm doth contain, to wit, "when the house was being builded after the captivity:" that is, the Church after the coming in of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:198
verses.text: Calling therefore those very men who were being held captive a captivity, as when "the service" is spoken of there are understood those that serve also, that same captivity he saith by Christ hath been led captive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:199
verses.text: For why should not captivity be happy, if even for a good purpose men may be caught? Whence to Peter hath been said, "From henceforth thou shalt catch men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:200
verses.text: Led captive therefore they are because caught, and caught because subjugated, being sent under that gentle yoke, being delivered from sin whereof they were servants, and being made servants of righteousness whereof they were children.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:201
verses.text: Whence also He is Himself in them, that hath given gifts to men, and hath received gifts in men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:202
verses.text: And thus in that captivity, in that servitude, in that chariot, under that yoke, there are not thousands of men lamenting, but thousands of men rejoicing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:203
verses.text: For the Lord is in them, in Sina, in the holy place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:204
verses.text: But what next doth he adjoin? "For they that believe not to dwell" : or, as some copies have, "For not believing to dwell:" for what else are men not believing, but they that believe not? To whom this hath been said, is not easy to perceive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:205
verses.text: For as though a reason were being given of the above words, when it had been said, "Thou hast led captivity captive, Thou hast received gifts in men:" there hath been added in continuation, "for they that believe not to dwell," that is, not believing that they should dwell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:206
verses.text: What is this? Of whom saith he this? Did that captivity, before it passed into a good captivity, show whence it was an evil captivity? For through not believing they were possessed by the enemy, "that worketh in the sons of unbelief: among whom ye were sometime, while ye were living among them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:207
verses.text: By the gifts therefore of His grace, He that hath received gifts in men, hath led captive that captivity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:208
verses.text: For they believed not that they should dwell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:209
verses.text: For faith hath thence delivered them, in order that now believing they may dwell in the House of God, even they too becoming the House of God, and the Chariot of God, consisting of thousands of men rejoicing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:210
verses.text: Whence he that was singing of these things, in the Spirit foreseeing them, even he too being fulfilled with joy hath burst forth a hymn, saying, "The Lord God is blessed, blessed is the Lord God from day unto day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:211
verses.text: Which some copies have, "by day daily," because the Greeks have it thus, ἡμ™ραν καθ' ἡμ™ραν: which more exactly would be expressed by, "by day daily".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:212
verses.text: Which expression I think signifieth the same as that which hath been said, to wit, "from day unto day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:213
verses.text: For daily this He doeth even unto the end, He leadeth captive captivity, receiving gifts in men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:214
verses.text: And because He leadeth that chariot unto the end, He continueth and saith, "A prosperous journey there shall make for us the God of our healths, our God, the God of making men safe".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:215
verses.text: Highly is grace here commended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:216
verses.text: For who would be safe, unless He Himself should make whole? But that it might not occur to the mind, Why then do we die, if through His grace we have been made safe? immediately he added below, "and the Lord's is the outgoing of death:" as though he were saying, Why are thou indignant, O lot of humanity, that thou hast the outgoing of death? Even thy Lord's outgoing was no other than that of death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:217
verses.text: Rather therefore be comforted than be indignant: for even "the Lord's is the outgoing of death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:218
verses.text: "For by hope we have been saved: but if that which we see not we hope for, through patience we wait for it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:219
verses.text: Patiently therefore even death itself let us suffer, by the example of Him, who though by no sin He was debtor to death, and was the Lord, from whom no one could take away life, but Himself laid it down of Himself, yet had Himself the outgoing of death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:220
verses.text: "Nevertheless, God shall break in pieces the heads of His enemies, the scalp of hair of men walking on in their transgressions" : that is, too much exalting themselves, being too proud in their transgressions: wherein at least they ought to be humble, saying, "O Lord, be Thou merciful to me a sinner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:221
verses.text: But He shall break in pieces their heads: for he that exalteth himself shall be humbled And thus though even of the Lord be the outgoing of death: nevertheless the same Lord, because He was God, and died after the flesh of His own will, not of necessity, "shall break in pieces the heads of His enemies:" not only of those who mocked and crucified Him, and wagged their heads, and said, "If Son of God He is, let Him come down from the Cross;" but also of all men lifting up themselves against His doctrine, and deriding His death as though it were of a man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:222
verses.text: For that very same One of whom hath been said, "Others He saved, Himself He cannot save," is the "God of our healths," and is the "God of saving men:" but for an example of humility and of patience, and to efface the handwriting of our sins, He even willed that the outgoing of death should be His own, that we might not fear that death, but rather this from which He hath delivered us through that.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:223
verses.text: Nevertheless, though mocked and dead, "He shall break in pieces the heads of His enemies," of whom He saith, "Raise Thou me up, and I shall render to them:" whether it be good things for evil things, while to Himself He subdueth the heads of them believing, or whether just things for unjust things, while He punisheth the heads of them proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:224
verses.text: For in either way are shattered and broken the heads of enemies, when from pride they are thrown down, whether by humility being amended, or whether unto the lowest depths of hell being hurled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:225
verses.text: "The Lord hath said, Out of Basan I will be turned" : or, as some copies have, "Out of Basan I will turn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:226
verses.text: For He turneth that we may be safe, of whom above hath been said, "God of our healths, and God of saving men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:227
verses.text: For to Him elsewhere also is said, "O God of virtues, turn Thou us, and show Thy face, and safe we shall be".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:228
verses.text: Also in another place, "Turn us, O God of our healths".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:229
verses.text: But he hath said, "Out of Basan I will turn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:230
verses.text: Basan is interpreted confusion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:231
verses.text: What is then, I will turn out of confusion, but that there is confounded because of his sins, he that is praying of the mercy of God that they may be put away? Thence it is that the Publican dared not even to lift up his eyes to Heaven: so, on considering himself, was he confounded; but he went down justified, because "the Lord hath said, Out of Basan I will turn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:232
verses.text: Basan is also interpreted drought: and rightly the Lord is understood to turn out of drought, that is, out of scarcity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:233
verses.text: For they that think themselves to be in plenty, though they be famished; and full, though they be altogether empty; are not turned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:234
verses.text: "I will turn unto the deep of the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:235
verses.text: If, "I will turn," why, "unto the deep of the sea"? Unto Himself indeed the Lord turneth, when savingly He turneth, and He is not surely Himself the deep of the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:236
verses.text: Doth perchance the Latin expression deceive us, and hath there been put "unto the deep," for a translation of what signifieth "deeply"? For He doth not turn Himself: but He turneth those that in the deep of this world lie sunk down with the weight of sins, in that place where one that is turned saith, "From the depths I have cried to Thee, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:237
verses.text: But if it is not, "I will turn," but, "I will be turned unto the deep of the sea;" our Lord is understood to have said, how by His own mercy He was turned even unto the deep of the sea, to deliver even those that were sinners in most desperate case.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:238
verses.text: Though in one Greek copy I have found, not, "unto the deep," but "in the depths," that is, ἐν βυθοῖς: which strengtheneth the former sense, because even there God turneth to Himself men crying from the depths.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:239
verses.text: And even if He be understood Himself there to be turned, to deliver such sort also, it is not beside the purpose: and so then He turneth, or else to deliver them is so turned, that His foot is stained in blood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:240
verses.text: Which to the Lord Himself the Prophet speaketh: "That Thy foot may be stained in blood" : that is, in order that they themselves who are turned to Thee, or to deliver whom Thou art turned, though in the deep of the sea by the burden of iniquity they may have been sunk, may make so great proficiency by Thy Grace (for where there hath abounded sin, there hath superabounded grace), that they may become Thy foot among Thy members, to preach Thy Gospel, and for Thy name's sake drawing out a long martyrdom, even unto blood they may contend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:241
verses.text: For thus, as I judge, more meetly is perceived His foot stained in blood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:242
verses.text: Lastly, he addeth, "The tongue of Thy dogs out of enemies by Himself," calling those very same that had been about to strive for the faith of the Gospel, even dogs, as though barking for their Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:243
verses.text: Not those dogs, whereof saith the Apostle, "Beware of dogs:" but those that eat of the crumbs which fall from the table of their masters.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:244
verses.text: For having confessed this, the woman of Canaan merited to hear, "O woman, great is thy faith, be it done to thee as thou wilt".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:245
verses.text: Dogs commendable, not abominable; observing fidelity towards their master, and before his house barking against enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:246
verses.text: Not only "of dogs" he hath said, but "of Thy dogs:" nor are their teeth praised, but their tongue is: for it was not indeed to no purpose, not without a great mystery, that Gedeon was bidden to lead those alone, who should lap the water of the river like dogs; and of such sort not more than three hundred among so great a multitude were found.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:247
verses.text: In which number is the sign of the Cross because of the letter T , which in the Greek numeral characters signifieth three hundred.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:248
verses.text: Of such dogs in another Psalm also said, "They shall be turned at even, and hunger they shall suffer as dogs".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:249
verses.text: For even some dogs have been reproved by the Prophet Isaiah, not because they were dogs, but because they knew not how to bark, and loved to sleep In which place indeed he hath shown, that if they had watched and barked for their Lord, they would have been praiseworthy dogs: just as they are praised, of whom is said, "The tongue of Thy dogs".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:250
verses.text: "There have been seen Thy steps, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:251
verses.text: The steps are those wherewith Thou hast come through the world, as though in that chariot Thou wast going to traverse the round world; which chariot of clouds He intimateth to be His holy and faithful ones in the Gospel, where He saith, "From this time ye shall see the Son of Man coming in the clouds".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:252
verses.text: Leaving out that coming wherein He shall be Judge of quick and dead, "From this time," He saith, "ye shall see the Son of Man coming in clouds".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:253
verses.text: These "Thy steps have been seen," that is, have been manifested, by the revealing the grace of the New Testament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:254
verses.text: Whence hath been said, "How beautiful are the feet of them that proclaim peace, that proclaim good things!" For this grace and those steps were lying hid in the Old Testament: but when there came the fulness of time, and it pleased God to reveal His Son, that He might be proclaimed among the Gentiles, "there were seen Thy steps, O God: the steps of my God, of the King who is in the holy place".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:255
verses.text: In what holy place, save in His Temple? "For the Temple of God is holy," he saith, "which ye are".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:256
verses.text: But in order that those steps might be seen, "there went before princes conjoined with men psalming, in the midst of damsels players on timbrels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:257
verses.text: The princes are the Apostles: for they went before, that the peoples might come in multitudes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:258
verses.text: "They went before" proclaiming the New Testament: "conjoined with men psalming," by whose good works that were even visible, as it were with instruments of praise, God was glorified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:259
verses.text: But those same princes are "in the midst of damsels players on timbrels," to wit, in an honourable ministry: for thus in the midst are ministers set over new Churches; for this is "damsels:" with flesh subdued praising God; for this is "players on timbrels," because timbrels are made of skin dried and stretched.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:260
verses.text: Therefore, that no one should take these words in a carnal sense, and by these words should conceive in his mind certain choral bands of wantonness, he continueth and saith, "In the Churches bless ye the Lord" : as though he were saying, wherefore, when ye hear of damsels, players on timbrels, do ye think of wanton pleasures? "In the Churches bless ye the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:261
verses.text: For the Churches are pointed out to you by this mystic intimation: the Churches are the damsels, with new grace decked: the Churches are the players on the timbrels, with chastened flesh being spiritually tuneful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:262
verses.text: "In the Churches," then, "bless ye the Lord God from the wells of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:263
verses.text: For from thence He first chose those whom He made wells.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:264
verses.text: For from thence were chosen the Apostles; and they first heard, "He that shall have drunk of the water that I shall give him, shall never thirst, but there shall be made in him a well of water springing unto life everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:265
verses.text: "There is Benjamin the younger in a trance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:266
verses.text: There is Paul the last of the Apostles, who saith, "For even I am an Israelite, out of the seed of Abraham, out of the tribe of Benjamin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:267
verses.text: But evidently "in a trance," all men being amazed at a miracle so great as that of his calling.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:268
verses.text: For a trance is the mind's going out: which thing sometimes chanceth through fear; but sometimes through some revelation, the mind suffering separation from the corporal senses, in order that that which is to be represented may be represented to the spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:269
verses.text: Whence even thus may be understood that which here hath been written, namely, "in a trance;" for when to that persecutor there had been said from Heaven, "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me:" there being taken from him the light of the eyes of flesh, he made answer to the Lord, whom in spirit he saw, but they that were with him heard the voice of him replying, though seeing no one to whom he was speaking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:270
verses.text: Here also the trance may be understood to be that one of his, whereof he himself speaking, saith, that he knew a man caught up even unto the third Heaven; but whether in the body, or whether out of the body, he knew not: but that he being caught up into Paradise, heard ineffable words, which it was not lawful for a man to speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:271
verses.text: "Princes of Juda the leaders of them, princes of Zabulon, princes of Nephthalim".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:272
verses.text: Since he is indicating the Apostles as princes, wherein is even "Benjamin the younger in a trance," in which words that Paul is indicated no one doubteth; or when under the name of princes there are indicated in the Churches all men excelling and most worthy of imitation: what mean these names of the tribes of Israel?For the names are Hebrew: whereof Juda is said to be interpreted confession, Zabulon habitation of strength, Nephthalim my enlargement.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:273
verses.text: All which words do intimate to us the most proper princes of the Church, worthy of their leadership, worthy of imitation, worthy of honours.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:274
verses.text: For the Martyrs in the Churches hold the highest place, and by the crown of holy worth they do excel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:275
verses.text: But however in martyrdom the first thing is confession, and for this is next put on strength to endure whatsoever shall have chanced; then after all things have been endured, straits being ended, breadth followeth in reward.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:276
verses.text: It may also thus be understood; that whereas the Apostle chiefly commendeth these three things, faith, hope, love; confession is in faith, strength in hope, breadth in love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:277
verses.text: For of faith the substance is, that with the heart men believe unto righteousness, but with the mouth confession be made unto salvation But in sufferings of tribulations the thing itself is sorrowful, but the hope is strong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:278
verses.text: For, "if that which we see not we hope for, through patience we wait for it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:279
verses.text: But breadth the shedding abroad of love in the heart doth give.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:280
verses.text: For "love perfected casteth out fear:" which fear "hath torment," because of the straits of the soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:281
verses.text: "Command, O God, Thy Virtue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:282
verses.text: For one is our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we in Him, of whom we read that He is "the Virtue of God and the Wisdom of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:283
verses.text: But how doth God command His Christ, save while He commendeth Him? For "God commendeth His love in us, in that while yet we were sinners, for us Christ died".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:284
verses.text: "How hath He not also with Him given to us all things?" "Command, O God, Thy Virtue: confirm, O God, that which Thou hast wrought in us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:285
verses.text: Command by teaching, confirm by aiding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:286
verses.text: "From Thy Temple in Jerusalem, to Thee kings shall offer presents".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:287
verses.text: Jerusalem, which is our free mother, because the same also is Thy holy Temple: from that Temple then, "to Thee kings shall offer presents".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:288
verses.text: Whatever kings be understood, whether kings of the earth, or whether those whom "He that is above the heavens distinguisheth over the dove silvered;" "to Thee kings shall offer presents".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:289
verses.text: And what presents are so acceptable as the sacrifices of praise? But there is a noise against this praise, from men bearing the name of Christian, and having diverse opinions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:290
verses.text: Be there done that which followeth, "Rebuke Thou the beasts of the cane".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:291
verses.text: For both beasts they are, since by not understanding they do hurt: and beasts of the cane they are, since the sense of the Scriptures they wrest according to their own misapprehension.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:292
verses.text: For in the cane the Scriptures are as reasonably perceived, as language in tongue, according to the mode of expression whereby the Hebrew or the Greek or the Latin tongue is spoken of, or the like; that is to say, by the efficient cause the thing which is being effected is implied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:293
verses.text: Now it is usual in the Latin language for writing to be called style, because with the stilus it is done: so then cane also, because with a cane it is done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:294
verses.text: The Apostle Peter saith, that "men unlearned and unstable do wrest the Scriptures to their own proper destruction:" these are the beasts of the cane, whereof here is said, "Rebuke Thou the beasts of the cane".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:295
verses.text: Concerning these also is that which followeth, "The congregation of bulls amid the cows of the peoples, in order that there may be excluded they that have been tried with silver".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:296
verses.text: Calling them bulls because of the pride of a stiff and untamed neck: for he is referring to heretics.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:297
verses.text: But by "the cows of the peoples," I think souls easily led astray must be understood, because easily they follow these bulls.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:298
verses.text: For they lead not astray entire peoples, among whom are men grave and stable; whence hath been written, "In a people grave I will praise Thee:" but only the cows which they may have found among those peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:299
verses.text: "For of these are they that steal into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, who are led with divers lusts, alway learning, and at the knowledge of the truth never arriving".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:300
verses.text: For, "may be excluded," hath been said, meaning, may appear, may stand forth: as he saith, "may be made manifest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:301
verses.text: Whence also, in the art of the silversmith, they are called exclusores, who out of the shapelessness of the lump are skilled to mould the form of a vessel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:302
verses.text: For many meanings of the holy Scriptures are concealed, and are known only to a few of singular intelligence, and are never vindicated so suitably and acceptably as when our diligence to make answer to heretics constraineth us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:303
verses.text: For then even they that neglect the pursuits of learning, shaking off their slumber, are stirred up to a diligent hearing, in order that their opponents may be refuted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:304
verses.text: In a word, how many senses of holy Scriptures concerning Christ as God have been vindicated against Photinus, how many concerning Christ as man against Manichaeus, how many concerning the Trinity against Sabellius, how many concerning the Unity of the Trinity against Arians, Eunomians, Macedonians? How many concerning the Catholic Church in the whole world spread abroad, against Donatists, and Luciferians, and others, whoever they be, that with like error dissent from the truth: how many against the rest of heretics, whom to enumerate or mention were too long a task, and for the present work unnecessary?Of whom, as it were bulls, that is, not subject to the peaceful and gentle yoke of discipline, the Apostle maketh mention, in the place where he hath said that such an one must be chosen for the Episcopate as is "able to exhort in sound doctrine and to convince the gainsayers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:305
verses.text: For there are many unruly;" these are bulls with uplifted neck , impatient of plough and yoke: vain-talkers and leaders astray of minds; which minds this Psalm hath intimated under the name of cows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:306
verses.text: "There shall come ambassadors out of Egypt, Ethiopia shall prevent the hands of Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:307
verses.text: Under the name of Egypt or of Ethiopia, he hath signified the faith of all nations, from a part the whole: calling the preachers of reconciliation ambassadors.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:308
verses.text: "For Christ," he saith, "we have an embassy, God as it were exhorting through us: we beseech you for Christ to be reconciled to God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:309
verses.text: Not then of the Israelites alone, whence the Apostles were chosen, but also from the rest of the nations that there should be preachers of Christian peace, in this manner hath been mystically prophesied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:310
verses.text: But by that which he saith, "shall prevent the hands of Him," he saith this, shall prevent the vengeance of Him: to wit, by turning to Him, in order that their sins may be f orgiven, lest by continuing sinners they be punished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:311
verses.text: Which thing also in another Psalm is said, "Let us come before the face of Him in confession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:312
verses.text: As by hands he signifieth vengeance, so by face, revelation and presence, which will be in the Judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:313
verses.text: Because then, by Egypt and Ethiopia he hath signified the nations of the whole world; immediately he hath subjoined, "to God (are) the kingdoms of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:314
verses.text: Not to Sabellius, not to Arius, not to Donatus, not to the rest of the bulls stiff-necked, but "to God (are) the kingdoms of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:315
verses.text: But the greater number of Latin copies, and especially the Greek, have the verses so punctuated, that there is not one verse in these words, "to God the kingdoms of the earth," but, "to God," is at the end of the former verse, and so there is said, "Ethiopia shall come before the hands of her to God," and then there followeth in another verse, "Kingdoms of the earth, sing ye to God, psalm ye to the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:316
verses.text: By which punctuation, doubtless to be preferred by the agreement of many copies, and those deserving of credit, there seemeth to me to be implied faith which precedeth works: because without the merits of good works through faith the ungodly is justified, just as the Apostle said, "To one believing in Him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness:" in order that afterwards faith itself through love may begin to work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:317
verses.text: For those alone are to be called good works, which are done through love of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:318
verses.text: But these faith must needs go before, so that from thence these may begin, not from these this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:319
verses.text: This is faith, whereof to the Church Herself is said in the Song of Songs, "Thou shalt come and shalt pass hence from the beginning of faith".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:320
verses.text: For She hath come like the chariot of God in thousands of men rejoicing, having a prosperous course, and She hath passed over from this world to the Father: in order that there may come to pass in Her that which the Bridegroom Himself saith, who hath passed hence from this world to the Father, "I will that where I am, these also may be with Me:" but from the beginning of faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:321
verses.text: Because then in order that good works may follow, faith doth precede; and there are not any good works, save those which follow faith preceding: nothing else seemeth to have been meant in, "Ethiopia shall come before the hands of her to God," but, Ethiopia shall believe in God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:322
verses.text: For thus she "shall come before the hands of her," that is, the works of her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:323
verses.text: Of whom, except of Ethiopia herself? For this in the Greek is not ambiguous: for the word "of her" there in the feminine gender most clearly hath been put down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:324
verses.text: And thus nothing else hath been said than "Ethiopia shall come before her hands to God," that is, by believing in God she shall come before her works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:325
verses.text: For, "I judge," saith the Apostle, "that a man is justified through faith without the works of the Law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:326
verses.text: Is He God of the Jews only? Is He not also of the Gentiles?" So then Ethiopia, which seemeth to be the utmost limit of the Gentiles, is justified through faith, without the works of the Law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:327
verses.text: For the expression in Greek, χεῖρα αὐτῆς, which most copies have, both of "hand of her" and "her own hand" may be understood: but that which is uncommon in the Greek copies, χειρας αὐτῆς, by both "hands of her" and "her own  hands," in Latin may be expressed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:328
verses.text: Henceforward, as if through prophecy all things had been discoursed of which now we see fulfilled, he exhorteth to the praise of Christ, and next He foretelleth His future Advent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:329
verses.text: "Kingdoms of earth, sing ye to God, psalm ye to the Lord: psalm ye to God, who hath ascended above the Heaven of Heavens to the East".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:330
verses.text: Or, as some copies have it, "who hath ascended above the Heaven of Heaven to the East".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:331
verses.text: In these words he perceiveth not Christ, who believeth not His Resurrection and Ascension.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:332
verses.text: But hath not "to the East," which he hath added, expressed the very spot; since in the quarters of the East is where He rose again, and whence He ascended? Therefore above the Heaven of Heaven He sitteth at the right hand of the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:333
verses.text: This is what the Apostle saith, "the Same is He that hath ascended above all Heavens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:334
verses.text: For what of Heavens doth remain after the Heaven of Heaven? Which also we may call the Heavens of Heavens, just as He hath called the firmament Heaven: which Heaven, however, even as Heavens we read of, in the place where there is written, "and let the waters which are above the Heavens praise the name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:335
verses.text: And forasmuch as from thence He is to come, to judge quick and dead, observe what followeth: "behold, He shall give His voice, the voice of power".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:336
verses.text: He that like a lamb before the shearer of Him was without voice, "behold shall give His voice," and not the voice of weakness, as though to be judged; but "the voice of power," as though going to judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:337
verses.text: For God shall not be hidden, as before, and in the judgment of men not opening His mouth; but "God shall come manifest, our God, and He shall not be silent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:338
verses.text: Why do ye despair, ye unbelieving men? Why do ye mock? What saith the evil servant? "My Lord delayeth to come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:339
verses.text: "Behold, He shall give His voice, the voice of power".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:340
verses.text: "Give ye glory to God, above Israel is the magnificence of Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:341
verses.text: Of whom saith the Apostle, "Upon the Israel of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:342
verses.text: For "not all that are out of Israel, are Israelites:" for there is also an Israel after the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:343
verses.text: Whence he saith, "See ye Israel after the flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:344
verses.text: "For not they that are sons of the flesh, are sons of God, but sons of promise are counted for a seed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:345
verses.text: Therefore at that time when without any intermixture of evil men His people shall be, like a heap purged by the fan, like Israel in whom guile is not, then most pre-eminent "above Israel" shall be "the magnificence" of "Him: and the virtue of Him in the clouds".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:346
verses.text: For not alone He shall come to judgment, but with the elders of His people: to whom He hath promised that they shall sit upon thrones to judge, who even shall judge angels These be the clouds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:347
verses.text: Lastly, lest of anything else the clouds be understood, he hath in continuation added, "Wonderful is God in His saints, the God of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:348
verses.text: For at that time even most truly and most fully there shall be fulfilled the name Israel itself, which is one "seeing God:" for we shall see Him as He is "He Himself shall give virtue and strength to His people, blessed be God:" to His people now frail and weak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:349
verses.text: For "we have this treasure in earthen vessels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:350
verses.text: But then by a most glorious changing even of our bodies, "He Himself shall give virtue and strength to His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:351
verses.text: For this body is sown in weakness, shall rise in virtue He Himself then shall give the virtue which in His own flesh He hath sent before, whereof the Apostle saith, "the power of His Resurrection".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:352
verses.text: But strength w hereby shall be destroyed the enemy death Now then of this long and difficultly understood Psalm we have at length by His own aid made an end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 69:353
verses.text: "Blessed be God, Amen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:1
verses.text: Psalm LXIX.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:2
verses.text: We have been born into this world, and added to the people of God, at that period wherein already the herb from a grain of mustard seed hath spread out its branches; wherein already the leaven, which at first was contemptible, hath leavened three measures, that is, the whole round world repeopled by the three sons of Noe: for from East and West and North and South shall come they that shall sit down with the Patriarchs, while those shall have been driven without, that have been born of their flesh and have not imitated their faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:3
verses.text: Unto his glory then of Christ's Church our eyes we have opened; and that barren one, for whom joy was proclaimed and foretold, because she was to have more sons than she that had the husband, her we have found to be such an one as hath forgotten the reproaches and infamy of her widowhood: and so we may perhaps wonder when we chance to read in any prophecy the words of Christ's humiliation, or our own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:4
verses.text: And it may be, that we are less affected by them; because we have not come at that time when these things were read with zest, in that tribulation abounded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:5
verses.text: But again if we think of the abundance of tribulations, and observe the way wherein we are walking (if indeed we do walk in it), how narrow it is, and how through straits and tribulations it leadeth unto rest everlasting, and how that very thing which in human affairs is called felicity, is more to be feared than misery; since indeed misery ofttimes doth bring out of tribulation a good fruit, but felicity doth corrupt the soul with a perverse security, and giveth place for the Devil the Tempter—when, I say, we shall have judged prudently and rightly, as the salted victim did, that "human life upon earth is trial," and that no one is at all secure, nor ought to be secure, until he be come to that country, whence no one that is a friend goeth forth, into which no one that is an enemy is admitted, even now in the very glory of the Church we acknowledge the voices of our tribulation: and being members of Christ, subject to our Head in the bond of love, and mutually supporting one another, we will say from the Psalms, that which here we have found the Martyrs said, who were before us; that tribulation is common to all men from the beginning even unto the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:6
verses.text: The Title of the Psalm is: "Unto the end, in behalf of those that shall be changed, to David himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:7
verses.text: Now of the change for the better hear thou; for change either is for the worse or for the better.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:8
verses.text: That we have been changed then for the worse, to ourselves let us ascribe: that for the better we  are changed, let us praise God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:9
verses.text: "For those," then, "that shall be changed," this Psalm is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:10
verses.text: But whence hath this change been made but by the Passion of Christ? The very word Pascha in Latin is interpreted passage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:11
verses.text: For Pascha is not a Greek word but a Hebrew.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:12
verses.text: It soundeth indeed in the Greek language like Passion, because π€σχειν signifieth to suffer: but if the Hebrew expression be examined, it pointeth to something else.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:13
verses.text: Pascha doth intimate passage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:14
verses.text: Of which even John the Evangelist hath admonished us, who (just before the Passion when the Lord was coming to the supper wherein He set forth the Sacrament of His Body and Blood) thus speaketh: "But when there had come the hour, wherein Jesus was to pass from this world to the Father".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:15
verses.text: He hath expressed then the "passage" of the Pascha.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:16
verses.text: But unless He passed Himself hence to the Father, who came for our sake, how should we have been able to pass hence, who have not come down for the sake of taking up anything, but have fallen? But He Himself fell not; He but came down, in order that He might raise up him that had fallen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:17
verses.text: The passage therefore both of Him and of us is hence to the Father, from this world to the kingdom of Heaven, from life mortal to life everlasting, from life earthly to life heavenly, from life corruptible to life incorruptible, from intimacy with tribulations to perpetual security.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:18
verses.text: Accordingly, "In behalf of them that shall be changed," the Psalm's title is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:19
verses.text: The cause therefore of our change,  that is, the very Passion of the Lord and our own voice in tribulations in the text of the Psalm let us observe, let us join in knowing, join in groaning, and in hearing, in joint-knowing, joint-groaning, let us be changed, in order that there may be fulfilled in us the Title of the Psalm, "In behalf of them that shall be changed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:20
verses.text: "Save me, O God, for the waters have entered in even unto my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:21
verses.text: That grain is despised now, that seemeth to give forth humble words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:22
verses.text: In the garden it is buried, though the world will admire the greatness of the herb, of which herb the seed was despised by the Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:23
verses.text: For in very deed observe ye the seed of the mustard, minute, dull coloured, altogether despicable, in order that therein may be fulfilled that which hath been said, We have seen Him, and He had neither form nor comeliness But He saith, that waters have come in even unto His soul; because those multitudes, which under the name of waters He hath pointed out, were able so far to prevail as to kill Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:24
verses.text: Whence then doth He so cry out, as though He were suffering something against His will, except because the Head doth prefigure the Members? For He suffered because He willed: but the Martyrs even though they willed not; for to Peter thus He foretold his passion: "When thou shalt be old," He saith, "another shall gird thee, and lead thee whither thou wilt not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:25
verses.text: For though we desire to cleave to Christ, yet we are unwilling to die: and therefore willingly or rather patiently we suffer, because no other passage is given us, through which we may cleave to Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:26
verses.text: For if we could in any other way arrive at Christ, that is, at life everlasting, who would be willing to die? For while explaining our nature, that is, a sort of association of soul and body, and in these two parts a kind of intimacy of gluing and fastening together, the Apostle saith, that "we have a House not made with hands, everlasting in the Heavens:" that is, immortality prepared for us, wherewith we are to be clothed at the end, when we shall have risen from the dead; and he saith, "Wherein we are not willing to be stripped, but to be clothed upon, that the mortal may be swallowed up of life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:27
verses.text: If it might so be, we should so will, he saith, to become immortal, as that now that same immortality might come, and now as we are it should change us, in order that this our mortal body by life should be swallowed up, and the body should not be laid aside through death, so as at the end again to have to be recovered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:28
verses.text: Although then from evil to good things we pass, nevertheless the very passage is somewhat bitter, and hath the gall which the Jews gave to the Lord in the Passion, hath something sharp to be endured, whereby they are shown that gave Him vinegar to drinkFor here both sweet are temporal pleasures, and bitter are temporal tribulations: but who would not drink the cup of tribulation temporal, fearing the fire of hell; and who would not contemn the sweetness of the world, longing for the sweetness of life eternal? From hence that we may be delivered let us cry: lest perchance amidst oppressions we consent to iniquity, and truly irreparably we be swallowed up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:29
verses.text: "Fixed I am in the clay of the deep, and there is no substance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:30
verses.text: What called the clay? Is it those very persons that have persecuted? For out of clay man hath been made But these men by falling from righteousness have become the clay of the deep, and whosoever shall not have consented to them persecuting and desiring to draw him to iniquity, out of his clay doth make gold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:31
verses.text: For the clay of the same shall merit to be converted into a heavenly form, and to be made associate of those of whom saith the Title of the Psalm, "in behalf of them that shall be changed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:32
verses.text: But at the time when these were the clay of the deep, I stuck in them: that is, they held Me, prevailed against Me, killed Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:33
verses.text: "Fixed" then "I am in the clay of the deep, and there is no substance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:34
verses.text: What is this, "there is no substance"? Can it be that clay itself is not a substance? What is then, "fixed I am"? Can it be that Christ hath thus stuck? Or hath He stuck, and was not, as hath been said in the book of Job, "the earth delivered into the hands of the ungodly man"? Was He fixed in body, because it could be held, and suffered even crucifixion? For unless with nails He had been fixed, crucified He had not been.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:35
verses.text: Whence then "there is no substance"? Is that clay not a substance? But we shall understand, if it be possible, what is, "and there is no substance," if first we shall have understood what is a substance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:36
verses.text: For there is substance spoken of even of riches, as we say, he hath substance, and he hath lost substance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:37
verses.text: God is a sort of substance: for that which is no substance, is nothing at all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:38
verses.text: To be a substance then is to be something.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:39
verses.text: Whence also in the Catholic Faith against the poisons of certain heretics thus we are builded up, so that we say, Father and Son and Holy Spirit are of one substance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:40
verses.text: What is, of one substance? For example, if gold is the Father, gold is also the Son, gold also the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:41
verses.text: Whatever the Father is because He is God, the same is the Son, the same the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:42
verses.text: But when He is the Father, this is not what He is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:43
verses.text: For Father He is called not in reference to Himself, but in reference to the Son: but in reference to Himself God He is called.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:44
verses.text: Therefore in that He is God, by the same He is a substance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:45
verses.text: And because of the same substance the Son is, without doubt the Son also is God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:46
verses.text: But yet in that He is Father, because it is not the name of the substance, but is referred to the Son; we do not say that the Son is Father in the same manner as we say the Son is God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:47
verses.text: Thou askest what the Father is; we answer, God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:48
verses.text: Thou askest what is the Father and the Son: we answer, God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:49
verses.text: If questioned of the Father alone, answer thou God: if questioned of both, not Gods, but God, answer thou.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:50
verses.text: We do not reply as in the case of men, when thou inquirest what is father Abraham, we answer a man; the substance of him serveth for answer: thou inquirest what is his son Isaac, we answer, a man; of the same substance are Abraham and Isaac: thou inquirest what is Abraham and Isaac, we answer not man, but men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:51
verses.text: Not so in things divine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:52
verses.text: For so great in this case is the fellowship of substance, that of equality it alloweth, plurality alloweth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:53
verses.text: If then it shall have been said to thee, when thou tellest me that the Son is the same as the Father, in fact the Son also is the Father; answer thou, according to the substance I have told thee that the Son is the same as the Father, not according to that term which is used in reference to something else.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:54
verses.text: For in reference to Himself He is called God, in reference to the Father is called Son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:55
verses.text: And again, the Father in reference to Himself is called God, in reference to the Son He is called Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:56
verses.text: The Father as He is called in reference to the Son, is not the Son: the Son as He is called in reference to the Father, is not the Father: what the Father is called in reference to Himself and the Son in reference to Himself, the same is Father and Son, that is, God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:57
verses.text: What is then, "there is no substance"? After this interpretation of substance, how shall we be able to understand this passage of the Psalm, "Fixed I am in the clay of the deep, and there is no substance"? God made man, He made substance; and O that he had continued in that which God made Him! If man had continued in that which God made him, in him would not have been fixed He whom God begot.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:58
verses.text: But moreover because through iniquity man fell from the substance wherein he was made (for iniquity itself is no substance; for iniquity is not a nature which God formed, but a perverseness which man made); the Son of God came to the clay of the deep, and was fixed; and that was no substance wherein He was fixed, because in the iniquity of them He was fixed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:59
verses.text: "All things by Him were made, and without Him there was made nothing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:60
verses.text: All natures by Him were made, iniquity by Him was not made, because iniquity was not made Those substances by Him were made, which praise Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:61
verses.text: The whole creation praising God is commemorated by the three children in the furnace, and from things earthly to things heavenly, or from things heavenly to things earthly reacheth the hymn of them praising God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:62
verses.text: Not that all these things have sense to praise; but because all things being well meditated upon, do beget praise, and the heart by considering creation is fulfilled to overflowing with a hymn to the Creator.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:63
verses.text: All things do praise God, but only the things which God hath made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:64
verses.text: Do ye observe in that hymn that covetousness praiseth God? There even the serpent praiseth God, covetousness praiseth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:65
verses.text: For all creeping things are there named in the praise of God: there are named all creeping things; but there are not there named any vices.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:66
verses.text: For vices out of ourselves and out of our own will we have: and vices are not a substance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:67
verses.text: In these was fixed the Lord, when He suffered persecution: in the vice of the Jews, not in the substance of men which by Him was made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:68
verses.text: "I have come into the depth of the sea, and the tempest hath made Me to sink down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:69
verses.text: Thanks to the mercy of Him who came into the depth of the sea, and vouchsafed to be swallowed by the sea whale, but was vomited forth the third day He came into the depth of the sea, in which depth we were thrust down, in which depth we had suffered shipwreck: He came thither Himself, and the tempest made Him to sink down: for there He suffered waves, those very men; tempests, the voices of men saying, "Crucify, Crucify".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:70
verses.text: Though Pilate said, I find not any cause in this Man why He should be killed: there prevailed the voices of them, saying, "Crucify, Crucify".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:71
verses.text: The tempest increased, until He was made to sink down that had come into the depth of the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:72
verses.text: And the Lord suffered in the hands of the Jews that which He suffered not when upon the waters He was walking: the which not only He had not suffered Himself, but had not allowed even Peter to suffer it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:73
verses.text: "I have laboured, crying, hoarse have become my jaws".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:74
verses.text: Wher e was this? When was this? Let us question the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:75
verses.text: For the Passion of our Lord in this Psalm we perceive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:76
verses.text: And, indeed, that He suffered we know; that there came in waters even unto His Soul, because peoples prevailed even unto His death, we read, we believe; in the tempest that He was sunk down, because tumult prevailed to His killing, we acknowledge: but that He laboured in crying, and that His jaws were made hoarse, not only we read not, but even on the contrary we read, that He answer ed not to them a word, in order that there might be fulfilled that which in another Psalm hath been said, "I have become as it were a man not hearing, and having not in his mouth reproofs".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:77
verses.text: And that which in Isaiah hath been prophesied, "like a sheep to be sacrificed He was led, and like a lamb before one shearing Him, so He opened not His mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:78
verses.text: If He became like a man not hearing, and having not in His mouth reproofs, how did He labour crying, and how were His jaws made hoarse? Is it that He was even then silent, because He was hoarse with having cried so much in vain? And this indeed we know to have been His voice on the Cross out of a certain Psalm: "O God, My God, why hast Thou forsaken Me?" But how great was that voice, or of how long duration, that in it His jaws should have become hoarse? Long while He cried, "Woe unto you, Scribes and Pharisees:" long while He cried, "Woe unto the world because of offences".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:79
verses.text: And truly hoarse in a manner He cried, and therefore was not understood, when the Jews said, What is this that He saith? "Hard is this saying, who is able to hear it?" We know not what He saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:80
verses.text: He said all these words: but hoarse were His jaws to them that understood not His words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:81
verses.text: "Mine eyes have failed from hoping in My God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:82
verses.text: Far be it that this should be taken of the person of the Head: far be it that His eyes should have failed from hoping in His God: in whom rather there was God reconciling the world to Himself, and Who was the Word made flesh and dwelled in us, so that not only God was in Him, but also He was Himself God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:83
verses.text: Not so then: the eyes of Himself, our Head, failed not from hoping in His God: but the eyes of Him have failed in His Body, that is, in His members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:84
verses.text: This voice is of the members, this voice is of the Body, not of the Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:85
verses.text: How then do we find it in His Body and members?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:86
verses.text: Thus "there have been multiplied above the hairs of My head they that hate Me gratis".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:87
verses.text: How multiplied? So as that they might add to themselves even one out of the twelve "There have been multiplied above the hairs of My head they that hate Me for nought".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:88
verses.text: With the hairs of His head He hath compared His enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:89
verses.text: With reason they were shorn when in the place of Calvary He was crucified Let the members accept this voice, let them learn to be hated gratis.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:90
verses.text: For now, O Christian, if it must needs be that the world hate thee, why do st thou not make it hate thee gratis, in order that in the Body of thy Lord and in this Psalm sent before concerning Him, thou mayest acknowledge thy own voice? How shall it come to pass that the world hate thee gratis? If thou no wise hurtest any one, and art still hated: for this is gratis, without cause.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:91
verses.text: "O God, Thou hast known mine improvidence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:92
verses.text: Again out of the mouth of the Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:93
verses.text: For what improvidence is there in Christ? Is He not Himself the Virtue of God, and the Wisdom of God? Doth He call this His improvidence, whereof the Apostle speaketh, "the foolishness of God is wiser than men"? Mine improvidence, that very thing which in Me they derided that seem to themselves to be wise, Thou hast known why it was done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:94
verses.text: For what was so much like improvidence, as, when He had it in His power with one word to lay low the persecutors, to suffer Himself to be held, scourged, spit upon, buffeted, with thorns to be crowned, to the tree to be nailed? It is like improvidence, it seemeth a foolish thing; but this foolish thing excelleth all wise men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:95
verses.text: Foolish indeed it is: but even when grain falleth into the earth, if no one knoweth the custom of husbandmen, it seemeth foolishImprovidence it appeareth; but hope maketh it not to be improvidence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:96
verses.text: He then spared not Himself: because even the Father spared Him not, but delivered Him up for us all And of the Same, "Who loved me," saith the Apostle, "and delivered up Himself for me:" for except a grain shall have fallen into the land so that it die, fruit, He saith, it will not yield This is the improvidence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:97
verses.text: "And my transgressions from Thee are not concealed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:98
verses.text: It is plain, clear, open, that this must be perceived to be out of the mouth of the Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:99
verses.text: Transgressions none had Christ: He was the bearer of transgressions, but not the committer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:100
verses.text: "Are not concealed:" that is, I have confessed to Thee, all my transgressions, and before my mouth Thou hast seen them in my thought, hast seen the wounds which Thou wast to heal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:101
verses.text: But where? Even in the Body, in the members: in those believers out of whom there was now cleaving to Him that member, who was confessing his sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:102
verses.text: "Let them not blush in Me, that wait for Thee, O Lord, Lord of virtues".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:103
verses.text: Again, the voice of the Head, "Let them not blush in Me:" let it not be said to them, Where is He on whom ye were relying? Let it not be said to them, Where is He that was saying to you, Believe ye in God, and in Me believe? "Let them not blush in Me, that wait for Thee," O Lord, Lord of virtues.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:104
verses.text: Let them not be confounded concerning Me, that seek Thee, O God of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:105
verses.text: This also may be understood of the Body, but only if thou consider the Body of Him not one man: for in truth one man is not the Body of Him, but a small member, but the Body is made up of members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:106
verses.text: Therefore the full Body of Him is the whole Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:107
verses.text: With reason then saith the Church, "Let them not blush in Me, that wait for Thee, O Lord, Lord of virtues".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:108
verses.text: "For because of Thee I have sustained upbraiding, shamelessness hath covered my face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:109
verses.text: No great thing is that which is spoken of in "I have sustained:" but that which is spoken of in "for Thy sake I have sustained," is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:110
verses.text: For if thou sustainest because thou hast sinned; for thine own sake thou sustainest, not for the sake of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:111
verses.text: For to you what glory is there, saith Peter, if sinning ye are punished, and ye bear it? But if thou sustainest because thou hast kept the commandment of God, truly for the sake of God thou sustainest; and thy reward remaineth for everlasting, because for the sake of God thou hast sustained revilings For to this end He first sustained in order that we might learn to sustain"Shamelessness hath covered my face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:112
verses.text: Shamelessness is what? Not to be confused.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:113
verses.text: Lastly, it seemeth to be as it were a fault, when we say, the man is shameless.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:114
verses.text: Great is the shamelessness of the man, that he doth not blush.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:115
verses.text: Therefore shamelessness is a kind of folly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:116
verses.text: A Christian ought to have this shamelessness, when he cometh among men to whom Christ is an offence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:117
verses.text: If he shall have blushed because of Christ, he will be blotted out from the book of the living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:118
verses.text: Thou must needs therefore have shamelessness when Thou art reviled because of Christ; when they say, Worshipper of the Crucified, adorer of Him that died ill, venerator of Him that was slain! here if thou shalt blush thou art a dead man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:119
verses.text: For see the sentence of Him that deceiveth no one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:120
verses.text: "He that shall have been ashamed of Me before men, I will also be ashamed of him before the Angels of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:121
verses.text: Watch therefore thyself whether there be in thee shamelessness; be thou boldfaced, when thou hearest a reproach concerning Christ; yea be boldfaced.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:122
verses.text: Why fearest thou for thy forehead which thou hast armed with the sign of the Cross?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:123
verses.text: "An alien I have become to My brethren, and a stranger to the sons of My mother".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:124
verses.text: To the sons of the Synagogue He became a strangerWhy so? Why did they not acknowledge? Why did they call Him an alien? Why did they dare to say, we know not whence He is? "Because the zeal of Thine House hath eaten Me up:" that is, because I have persecuted in them their own iniquities, because I have not patiently borne those whom I have rebuked, because I have sought Thy glory in Thy House, because I have scourged them that in the Temple dealt unseemly: in which place also there is quoted, "the zeal of Thine House hath eaten Me up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:125
verses.text: Hence an alien, hence a Stranger; hence, we know not whence He is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:126
verses.text: They would have acknowledged whence I am, if they had acknowledged that which Thou hast commanded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:127
verses.text: For if I had found them keeping Thy commandments, the zeal of Thine House would not have eaten Me up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:128
verses.text: "And the reproaches of men reproaching Thee have fallen upon Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:129
verses.text: Of this testimony Paul the Apostle hath also made use (there hath been read but now the very lesson), and saith, "Whatsoever things aforetime have been written, have been written that we might be instructed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:130
verses.text: Why "Thee"? Is the Father reproached, and not Christ Himself? Why have "the reproaches of men reproaching Thee fallen upon Me"? Because, "he that hath known Me, hath known the Father also:" because no one hath reviled Christ without reviling God: because no one honoureth the Father, except he that honoureth the Son also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:131
verses.text: "And I have covered in fasting My Soul, and it became to Me for a reviling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:132
verses.text: His fasting was, when there fell away all they that had believed in Him; because also it was His hunger, that men should believe in Him: because also it was His thirst, when He said to the woman, I thirst, "give Me to drink:" yea for her faith He was thirsting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:133
verses.text: And from the Cross when He was saying, "I thirst," He was seeking the faith of them for whom He had said, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:134
verses.text: But what did those men give to drink to Him thirsty? Vinegar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:135
verses.text: Vinegar is also called old With reason of the old man they gave to drink, because th ey willed not to be new.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:136
verses.text: Why willed they not to become new? Because to the title of this Psalm whereon is written, "For them that shall be changed," they belonged not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:137
verses.text: Therefore, "I have covered in fasting My Soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:138
verses.text: Lastly, He put from Him even the gall which they offered: He chose rather to fast than to accept bitterne ss.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:139
verses.text: For they enter not into His Body that are embittered,  whereof in another place a Psalm saith, "They that are embittered shall not be exalted in themselves".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:140
verses.text: Therefore, "I have covered in fasting My Soul: and it became to Me for a reviling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:141
verses.text: This very thing became to Me for a reviling, that I consented not to them, that is, from them I fasted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:142
verses.text: For he that consenteth not to men seducing to evil, fasteth from them; and through this fasting earneth reviling, so that he is upbraided because he consenteth not to the evil thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:143
verses.text: "And I have set sackcloth my garment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:144
verses.text: Already before we have said something of the sackcloth, from whence there is this, "But I, when they were troubling Me, was covering myself with sackcloth, and was humbling My Soul in fasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:145
verses.text: I have set sackcloth for My garment:" that is, have set against them My flesh, on which to spend their rage, I have concealed My divinity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:146
verses.text: "Sackcloth," because mortal the flesh was: in order that by sin He might condemn sin in the flesh "And I have set sackcloth my garment: and I have been made to them for a parable," that is, for a derision.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:147
verses.text: It is called a parable, whenever a comparison is made concerning some one, when he is evil spoken of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:148
verses.text: "So may this man perish," for example, "as that man did," is a parable: that is, a comparison and likeness in cursing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:149
verses.text: "I have been made to them," then, "for a parable".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:150
verses.text: "Against Me were reviling they that were sitting in the gate".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:151
verses.text: "In the gate" is nothing else but in public.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:152
verses.text: "And against Me they were chanting, they that were drinking wine".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:153
verses.text: Do ye think, brethren, that this hath befallen Christ alone? Daily to Him in His members it happeneth: whenever perchance it is necessary for the servant of God to forbid excess of wine and luxuries in any village or town, where there hath not been heard the Word of God, it is not enough that they sing, nay more even against him they begin to sing, by whom they are forbidden to sing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:154
verses.text: Compare ye now His fasting and their wine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:155
verses.text: "But I with My prayer with Thee, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:156
verses.text: But I was with Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:157
verses.text: But how? With Thee by praying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:158
verses.text: For when thou art evil spoken of, and knowest not what thou mayest do; when at thee are hurled reproaches, and thou findest not any way of rebuking him by whom they are hurled; nothing remaineth for thee but to pray.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:159
verses.text: But remember even for that very man to pray.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:160
verses.text: "But I with my prayer with Thee, O Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:161
verses.text: It is the time of Thy good pleasure, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:162
verses.text: For behold the grain is being buried, there shall spring up fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:163
verses.text: "It is the time of Thy good pleasure, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:164
verses.text: Of this time even the Prophets have spoken, whereof the Apostle maketh mention: "Behold now the time acceptable, behold now the day of salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:165
verses.text: "It is the time of Thy good pleasure, O God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:166
