verses.text: In the multitude of Thy mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:167
verses.text: This is the time of good pleasure, "in the multitude of Thy mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:168
verses.text: For if there were not a multitude of Thy mercy, what should we do for the multitude of our iniquity? "In the multitude of Thy mercy; Hearken to me in the truth of Thy Salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:169
verses.text: Because He hath said, "of Thy mercy," he hath added truth also: for "mercy and truth" are all the ways of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:170
verses.text: Why mercy? In forgiving sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:171
verses.text: Why truth? In fulfilling the promises.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:172
verses.text: "Save Thou Me from the mire, that I may not stick".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:173
verses.text: From that whereof above he had spoken, "Fixed I am in the clay of the deep, and there is no substance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:174
verses.text: Furthermore, since ye have duly received the exposition of that expression, in this place there is nothing further for you to hear particularly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:175
verses.text: From hence he saith that he must be delivered, wherein before he said that he was fixed: "Save Thou Me from the mire, that I may not stick".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:176
verses.text: And he explaineth this himself: "Let Me be rescued from them that hate Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:177
verses.text: They were themselves therefore the clay wherein he had stuck.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:178
verses.text: But the following perchance suggesteth itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:179
verses.text: A little before he had said, Fixed I am; now he saith, Save Thou Me from the mire, that I may not stick:" whereas after the meaning of what was said before he ought to have said, Save Thou Me from the mire where I had stuck, by rescuing Me, not by causing that I stick not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:180
verses.text: Therefore He had stuck in flesh, but had not stuck in spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:181
verses.text: He saith this, because of the infirmity of His members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:182
verses.text: Whenever perchance thou art seized by one that urgeth thee to iniquity, thy body indeed is taken, in regard to the body thou art fixed in the clay of the deep: but so long as thou consentest not, thou hast not stuck; but if thou consentest, thou hast stuck.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:183
verses.text: Let then thy prayer be in that place, in order that as thy body is now held, so thy soul may not be held, so thou mayest be free in bonds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:184
verses.text: "Let not the tempest of waters drown Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:185
verses.text: But already he had been drowned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:186
verses.text: "I have come into the depth of the sea," thou hast said, and "the tempest hath drowned Me," thou hast said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:187
verses.text: It hath drowned after the flesh, let it not drown after the Spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:188
verses.text: They to whom was said, If they shall have persecuted you in one city, flee ye into another; had this said to them, that neither in flesh they should stick, nor in spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:189
verses.text: For we must not desire to stick even in flesh; but as far as we are able we ought to avoid it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:190
verses.text: But if we shall have stuck, and shall have fallen into the hands of sinners: then in body we have stuck, we are fixed in the clay of the deep, it remaineth to entreat for the soul that we stick not, that is, that we consent not, that the tempest of water drown us not, so that we go into the deep of the clay.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:191
verses.text: "Neither let the deep swallow Me, nor the pit close her mouth upon Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:192
verses.text: What is this, brethren? What hath he prayed against? Great is the pit of the depth of human iniquity: every one, if he shall have fallen into it, will fall into the deep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:193
verses.text: But yet if a man being there placed confesseth his sins to his God, the pit will not shut her mouth upon him: as is written in another Psalm, "From the depths I have cried to Thee, O Lord; Lord, hearken unto my voice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:194
verses.text: But if there is done in him that which another passage of Scripture saith, "When a sinner shall have come into the depth of evil things, he will despise," upon him the pit hath shut her mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:195
verses.text: Why hath she shut her mouth? Because she hath shut his mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:196
verses.text: He hath lost confession, really dead he is, and there is fulfilled in him that which elsewhere is spoken of, "From a dead man, as from one that is not, there perisheth confession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:197
verses.text: "Hearken unto me, O Lord, for sweet is Thy mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:198
verses.text: He hath given this as a reason why He ought to be hearkened unto, because sweet is the mercy of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:199
verses.text: To a man set in trouble the mercy of God must needs be sweet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:200
verses.text: Concerning this sweetness of the mercy of God see ye what in another place the Scripture saith: "Like rain in drought, so beautiful is the mercy of God in trouble".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:201
verses.text: That which there he saith to be "beautiful," the same he saith here to be "sweet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:202
verses.text: Not even bread would be sweet, unless hunger had preceded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:203
verses.text: Therefore even when the Lord permitteth or causeth us to be in any trouble, even then He is merciful: for He doth not withdraw nourishment, but stirreth up longing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:204
verses.text: Accordingly what saith he now, "Hearken to me, O Lord, for sweet is Thy mercy"? Now do not Thou defer hearkening, in so great trouble I am, that sweet to me is Thy mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:205
verses.text: For to this end Thou didst defer to succour, in order that to me that wherewith Thou didst succour might be sweet: but now no longer is there cause why Thou must defer; my trouble hath arrived at the appointed measure of distress, let Thy mercy come to do the work of goodness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:206
verses.text: "After the multitude of Thy pities have regard unto me:" not after the multitude of my sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:207
verses.text: "Turn not away Thy face from Thy child".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:208
verses.text: And this is a commending of humility; "from Thy child," that is, "from Thy little one:" because now I have been rid of pride through the discipline of tribulation, "turn not away Thy face from Thy child".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:209
verses.text: This is that beautiful mercy of God, whereof he spake above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:210
verses.text: For in the following verse he explaineth that whereof he spake: "For I am troubled, speedily hearken Thou unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:211
verses.text: What is "speedily"? Now there is no cause why Thou must defer it: I am troubled, my affliction hath gone before; let Thy mercy follow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:212
verses.text: "Give heed to my soul, and redeem her," doth need no exposition: let us see therefore what followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:213
verses.text: "Because of mine enemies deliver me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:214
verses.text: This petition is evidently wonderful, neither briefly to be touched upon, nor hastily to be skipped over; truly wonderful: "Because of mine enemies deliver me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:215
verses.text: What is, "Because of mine enemies deliver me"?I see no reason for this petition, "Because of mine enemies deliver me:" unless we understand it of something else, which when I shall have spoken by the help of the Lord, He shall judge in you, that dwelleth in you There is a kind of secret deliverance of holy men: this for their own sakes is made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:216
verses.text: There is one public and evident: this is made because of their enemies, either for their punishment, or for their deliverance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:217
verses.text: For truly God delivered not the brothers in the book of Maccabees from the fires of the persecutorBut again the Three Children openly were delivered from the furnace of fire; because their body also was rescued, their safety was public.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:218
verses.text: The former were in secret crowned, the latter openly delivered: all however saved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:219
verses.text: There is then a secret deliverance, there is an open deliverance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:220
verses.text: Secret deliverance doth belong to the soul, open deliverance to the body as  well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:221
verses.text: For in secret the soul is delivered, openly the body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:222
verses.text: Again, if so it be, in this Psalm the voice of the Lord let us acknowledge: to the secret deliverance doth belong that whereof he spake above, "Give heed to my soul, and redeem her".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:223
verses.text: There remaineth the body's deliverance: for on His arising and ascending into the Heavens, and sending the Holy Ghost from above, there were converted to His faith they that at His death did rage, and out of enemies they were made friends through His grace, not through their righteousness Therefore he hath continued, "Because of mine enemies deliver me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:224
verses.text: Give heed to my soul," but this in secret: but "because of mine enemies deliver" even my body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:225
verses.text: For mine enemies it will profit nothing if soul alone Thou shalt have delivered; that they have done something, that they have accomplished something, they will believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:226
verses.text: "What profit is there in my blood, while I go down into corruption?" Therefore "give heed to my soul, and redeem her," which Thou alone knowest: secondly also, "because of mine enemies deliver me," that my flesh may not see corruption.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:227
verses.text: "Thou knowest my reproach, and my confusion, and my shame".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:228
verses.text: What is reproach? What is confusion? What shame? Reproach is that which the enemy casteth in the teeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:229
verses.text: Confusion is that which gnaweth the conscience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:230
verses.text: Shame is that which causeth even a noble brow to blush, because of the upbraiding with a pretended crime.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:231
verses.text: There is no crime; or even if there is a crime, it doth not belong to him, against whom it is alleged: but yet the infirmity of the human mind ofttimes is made ashamed even when a pretended crime is alleged; not because it is alleged, but because it is believed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:232
verses.text: All these things are in the Body of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:233
verses.text: For confusion in Him could not be, in whom guilt was not found.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:234
verses.text: There was alleged as a crime against Christians, the very fact that they were Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:235
verses.text: That indeed was glory: the brave gladly received it, and so received it as that they blushed not at all for the Lord's name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:236
verses.text: For fearlessness had covered the face of them, having the effrontery of Paul, saying, "for I blush not because of the Gospel: for the virtue of God it is for salvation to every one believing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:237
verses.text: O Paul, art not thou a venerator of the Crucified? Little it is, he saith, for me not to blush for it: nay, therein alone I glory, wherefore the enemy thinketh me to blush.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:238
verses.text: "But from me far be it to glory, save in the Cross of Jesus Christ, through whom to me the world is crucified, and I to the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:239
verses.text: At such a brow as this then reproach alone could be hurled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:240
verses.text: For neither could there be confusion in a conscience already made whole, nor shame in a brow so free.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:241
verses.text: But when it was being alleged against certain that they had slain Christ, deservedly they were pricked through with evil conscience, and to their health confounded and converted, so that they could say, "Thou hast known my confusion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:242
verses.text: Thou therefore, O Lord, hast known not only my reproach but also my confusion, in certain shame also: who, though in me they believe, publicly blush to confess me before ungodly men, human tongue having more influence with them than promise divine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:243
verses.text: Behold ye therefore them: even such are commended to God, not that so He may leave them, but that by aiding them He may make them perfect.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:244
verses.text: For a certain man believing and wavering hath said, "I believe, O Lord, help Thou mine unbelief".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:245
verses.text: "In Thy sight are all they that trouble Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:246
verses.text: Why I have reproach, Thou knowest; why confusion, Thou knowest; why shame, Thou knowest: therefore deliver Thou me because of mine enemies, because Thou knowest these things of me, they know not; and thus, because they are themselves in Thy sight, not knowing these things, they will not be able to be either confounded or corrected, unless openly Thou shalt have delivered me because of mine enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:247
verses.text: "Reproach my heart hath expected, and misery".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:248
verses.text: What is, "hath expected"? Hath foreseen these things as going to be, hath foretold them as going to be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:249
verses.text: For He came not for any other purpose.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:250
verses.text: If He had been unwilling to die, neither would He have willed to be born: for the sake of resurrection He did both.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:251
verses.text: For there were two particular things known to us among mankind, but one thing unknown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:252
verses.text: For we knew that men were born and died: that they rose again and lived for everlasting we knew not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:253
verses.text: That He might show to us that which we knew not, He took upon Him the two things which we knew.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:254
verses.text: To this end therefore He came.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:255
verses.text: "Reproach my heart hath expected and misery".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:256
verses.text: But the misery of whom? For He expected misery, but rather of the crucifiers, rather of the persecutors, that in them should be misery, in Him mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:257
verses.text: For pitying the misery of them even while hanging on the Cross, He saith, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:258
verses.text: What then did it profit, that I expected? That is, what did it profit that I foretold? What did it profit that I said to this end I had come? I came to fulfil that which I said, "I waited for one that together should be made sorrowful, and there was not; and men comforting, and I found not:" that is, there was none.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:259
verses.text: For that which in the former verse He said, "I waited for one that together should be made sorrowful," the same is in the following verse, "and men comforting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:260
verses.text: But that which in the former verse is, "and there was not;" the same in the following verse is, "and I found not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:261
verses.text: Therefore another sentence is not added, but the former is repeated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:262
verses.text: Which sentence if we reconsider, a question may arise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:263
verses.text: For were His disciples nowise made sorrowful when He was led to the Passion, when on the tree hanged, when dead? So much were they made sorrowful, that Mary Magdalene, who first saw Him, rejoicing told them as they were mourning what she had seen The Gospel speaketh of these things: it is not our presumption, not our suspicion: it is evident that the disciples grieved, it is evident that they mourned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:264
verses.text: Strange women were weeping, when to the Passion He was being led, unto whom turning He saith, "Weep ye, but for yourselves, do not for Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:265
verses.text: Peter certainly loved very much, and without hesitation threw himself to walk on the waves, and at the voice of the Lord he was delivered: and though following Him when led to the Passion, with the boldness of love, yet being troubled, thrice he denied Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:266
verses.text: Whence, except because an evil thing it seemed to him to die? For he was shunning that which he thought an evil thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:267
verses.text: This then even in the Lord he was lamenting, which he was himself shunning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:268
verses.text: On this account even before he had said, "Far be it from Thee, O Lord, merciful be Thou to Thyself: there shall not come to pass this thing:" at which time he merited to hear, "Satan;" after that he had heard, "Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jona".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:269
verses.text: Therefore in that sorrowfulness which the Lord felt because of those for whom He prayed, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do:" no companion He found.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:270
verses.text: "And I waited for one that together should be made sorrowful, and there was not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:271
verses.text: There was not at all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:272
verses.text: "And men comforting, and I found not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:273
verses.text: Who are men comforting? Men profiting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:274
verses.text: For they comfort us, they are the comfort of all preachers of the Truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:275
verses.text: "And they gave for My food gall, and in My thirst they gave Me vinegar to drink".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:276
verses.text: This was done indeed to the letter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:277
verses.text: And the Gospel declareth this to us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:278
verses.text: But we must understand, brethren, that the very fact that I found not comforters, that the very fact that I found not one that together should be made sorrowful, this was My gall, this to Me was bitter, this was vinegar: bitter because of grief, vinegar because of their old man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:279
verses.text: For we read, that to Him indeed gall was offered, as the Gospel speaketh; but for drink, not for food Nevertheless, we must so take and consider that when fulfilled, which here had been before predicted, "They gave for My food gall:" and in that very action, not only in this saying, we ought to seek for a mystery, at secret things to knock, to enter the rent veil of the Temple, to see there a Sacrament, both in what there hath been said and in what there hath been done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:280
verses.text: "They gave," He saith, "for My food gall:" not the thing itself which they gave was food, for it was drink: but "for food they gave it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:281
verses.text: Because already the Lord had taken food, and into it there had been thrown gall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:282
verses.text: But He had taken Himself pleasant food, when He ate the Passover with His disciples: therein He showed the Sacrament of His Body Unto this food so pleasant, so sweet, of the Unity of Christ, of which the Apostle maketh mention, saying, "For one bread, One Body, being many we are;" unto this pleasant food who is there that addeth gall, except the gainsayers of the Gospel, like those persecutors of Christ? For less the Jews sinned in crucifying Him walking on earth, than they that despise Him sitting in Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:283
verses.text: That which then the Jews did, in giving above the food which He had already taken that bitter draught to drink, the same they do that by evil living bring scandal upon the Church: the same do embittered heretics, "But let them not be exalted in their own selves".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:284
verses.text: They give gall after so delectable meat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:285
verses.text: But what doth the Lord? He admitteth them not to His Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:286
verses.text: In this mystery, when they presented gall, the Lord Himself tasted, and would not drink If we did not suffer them, neither at all should we taste: but because it is necessary to suffer them, we must needs taste.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:287
verses.text: But because in the members of Christ such sort cannot be, they can be tasted, received into the Body they cannot be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:288
verses.text: "And they gave for My food gall, and in My thirst they gave Me vinegar to drink".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:289
verses.text: I was thirsting, and vinegar I received: that is, for the faith of them I longed, and I found oldness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:290
verses.text: "Let the table of them be made in their own presence for a trap".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:291
verses.text: Like the trap which for Me they set, in giving Me such a draught, let such a trap be for them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:292
verses.text: Why then, "in their own presence"? "Let the table of them be made for a trap," would have been sufficient.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:293
verses.text: They are such as know their iniquity, and in it most obstinately do persevere: in their own presence there is made a trap for them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:294
verses.text: These are they that, being too destructive, "go down into Hell alive".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:295
verses.text: Lastly, of persecutors what hath been said? Except that the Lord were in us, perchance alive they had swallowed us up What is alive? Consenting to them, and knowing that we ought not to consent to them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:296
verses.text: Therefore in their own presence there is made a trap, and they are not amended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:297
verses.text: Even though in their own presence there is a trap, let them not fall into it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:298
verses.text: Behold they know the trap, and thrust out foot, and bow their necks to be caught.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:299
verses.text: How much better were it to turn away from the trap, to acknowledge sin, to condemn error, to be rid of bitterness, to pass over into the Body of Christ, to seek the Lord's glory! But so much prevaileth presumption of mind, that even in their own presence the trap is, and they fall into it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:300
verses.text: "Let the eyes of them be darkened, that they see not," followeth here: that whereas without benefit they have seen, it may chance to them even not to see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:301
verses.text: "Let the table of them," therefore, "be made in their own presence for a trap".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:302
verses.text: It is not from one wishing, but from one prophesying: not in order that it may come to pass, but because it will come to pass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:303
verses.text: This we have often remarked, and ye ought to remember it: lest that which the prescient mind saith in the Spirit of God, it should seem with ill will to imprecate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:304
verses.text: Let it then be done to them, "both for a requital and for a stumbling-block".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:305
verses.text: And is this by any means unjust? It is just.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:306
verses.text: Why? For it is "for a requital".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:307
verses.text: For not anything would happen to them, which was not owed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:308
verses.text: "For a requital" it is done, "and for a stumbling-block:" for they are themselves a stumbling-block to themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:309
verses.text: "Let the eyes of them be darkened, that they see not, and the back of them alway bow Thou down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:310
verses.text: This is a consequence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:311
verses.text: For they, whose eyes have been darkened that they see not, it followeth, must have their back bowed down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:312
verses.text: How so? Because when they have ceased to take knowledge of things above, they must needs think of things below.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:313
verses.text: He that well heareth, "lift up the heart," a bowed back hath not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:314
verses.text: For with stature erect he looketh for the hope laid up for him in Heaven; most especially if he send before him his treasure, whither his heart followeth But, on the other hand, they perceive not the hope of future life; already being blinded, they think of things below: and this is to have a bowed back: from which disorder the Lord delivered that woman.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:315
verses.text: For Satan hath bound her eighteen years, and her that was bowed down He raised up: and because on the Sabbath He did it, the Jews were scandalized; suitably were they scandalized at her being raised up, themselves being bowed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:316
verses.text: "Pour forth upon them Thine anger, and let the indignation of Thine anger overtake them" , are plain words: but nevertheless, in "overtake them" we perceive them as it were fleeing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:317
verses.text: But whither are they to flee? Into Heaven? Thou art there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:318
verses.text: Into Hell? Thou art present.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:319
verses.text: Their wings they will not take to fly straight: "Let the indignation of Thine anger overtake them," let it not permit them to escape.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:320
verses.text: "Let the habitation of them become forsaken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:321
verses.text: This is now evident.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:322
verses.text: For in the same manner as He hath mentioned not only a secret deliverance of His, saying, "Give heed to My soul, and redeem her;" but also one open after the body, adding, "because of mine enemies deliver me:" so also to these men He foretelleth how there are to be certain secret misfortunes, whereof a little before He was speaking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:323
verses.text: For the blindness of the Jews was secret vengeance: but the open was what? "Let their habitation become forsaken, and in their tabernacles let there not be any one to inhabit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:324
verses.text: There hath come to pass this thing in the very city Jerusalem, wherein they thought themselves mighty in crying against the Son of God, "Crucify, Crucify;" and in prevailing because they were able to kill Him that raised dead men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:325
verses.text: How mighty to themselves, how great, they seemed! There followed afterwards the vengeance of the Lord, stormed was the city, utterly conquered the Jews, slain were I know not how many thousands of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:326
verses.text: No one of the Jews is permitted to come thither now: where they were able to cry against the Lord, there by the Lord they are not permitted to dwell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:327
verses.text: They have lost the place of their fury: and O that even now they would know the place of their rest! What profit to them was Caiaphas in saying, "If we shall have let go this man thus, there will come the Romans, and take away from us both place and kingdom"? Behold, both they did not let Him go alive, and He liveth: and there have come the Romans, and have taken from them both place and kingdom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:328
verses.text: But now we heard, when the Gospel was being read, "Jerusalem, Jerusalem, how often would I have gathered together thy sons, as a hen her chickens under her wings, and thou wouldest not? Behold there is left to you your house forsaken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:329
verses.text: Why so? "For Him whom Thou hast smitten they have themselves persecuted, and upon the pain of my wounds they have added".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:330
verses.text: How then have they sinned if they have persecuted one by God smitten? What sin is ascribed to their mind? Malice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:331
verses.text: For the thing was done in Christ which was to be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:332
verses.text: To suffer indeed He had come, and He punished him through whom He suffered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:333
verses.text: For Judas the traitor was punished, and Christ was crucified: but us He redeemed by His blood, and He punished him in the matter of his price.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:334
verses.text: For he threw down the price of silver, for which by him the Lord had been sold; and he knew not the price wherewith he had himself by the Lord been redeemed This thing was done in the case of Judas.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:335
verses.text: But when we see that there is a sort of measure of requital in all men, and that not any one can be suffered to rage more than he hath received power to do: how have they "added," or what is that smiting of the Lord? Without doubt He is speaking in the person of him from whom He had received a body, from whom He had taken unto Him flesh, that is in the person of mankind, of Adam himself who was smitten with the first death because of his sin Mortal therefore here are men born, as born with their punishment: to this punishment they add, whosoever do persecute men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:336
verses.text: For now here man would not have had to die, unless God had smitten him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:337
verses.text: Why then dost thou, O man, rage more than this? Is it little for a man that some time he is to die? Each one of us therefore beareth his punishment: to this punishment they would add that persecute us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:338
verses.text: This punishment is the smiting of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:339
verses.text: For the Lord smote man with the sentence: "What day ye shall have touched it," He saith, "with death ye shall die".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:340
verses.text: Out of this death He had taken upon Him flesh, and our old man hath been crucified together with Him By the voice of that man He hath said these words, "Him whom Thou hast smitten they have themselves persecuted, and upon the pain of My wounds they have added".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:341
verses.text: Upon what pain of wounds? Upon the pain of sins they have themselves added.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:342
verses.text: For sins He hath called His wounds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:343
verses.text: But do not look to the Head, consider the Body; according to the voice whereof hath been said by the Same in that Psalm, wherein He showed there was His voice, because in the first verse thereof He cried from the Cross, "God, My God, look upon Me, why hast Thou forsaken Me?" There in continuation He saith, "Afar from My safety are the words of Mine offences".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:344
verses.text: "Lay Thou iniquity upon their iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:345
verses.text: What is this? Who would not be afraid? To God is said, "Lay Thou iniquity upon their iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:346
verses.text: Whence shall God lay iniquity? For hath He iniquity to lay? For we know that to be true which hath been spoken through Paul the Apostle, "What then shall we say? Is there anywise iniquity with God? Far be it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:347
verses.text: Whence then, "Lay Thou iniquity upon iniquity"? How must we understand this? May the Lord be with us, that we may speak, and because of your weariness may be able to speak briefly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:348
verses.text: Their iniquity was that they killed a just Man: there was added another, that they crucified the Son of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:349
verses.text: Their raging was as though against a man: but "if they had known, the Lord of Glory they had never crucified".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:350
verses.text: They with their own iniquity willed to kill as it were a man: there was laid iniquity upon their own iniquity, so that the Son of God they should crucify.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:351
verses.text: Who laid this iniquity upon them? He that said, "Perchance they will reverence My Son," Him I will send.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:352
verses.text: For they were wont to kill servants sent to them, to demand rent and profit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:353
verses.text: He sent the Son Himself, in order that Him also they might kill.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:354
verses.text: He laid iniquity upon their own iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:355
verses.text: And these things did God do in wrath, or rather in just requital? For, "May it be done to them," He saith, "for a requital and for a stumbling-block".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:356
verses.text: They had deserved to be so blinded as not to know the Son of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:357
verses.text: And this God did, laying iniquity upon their iniquity; not in wounding, but in not making whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:358
verses.text: For in like manner as thou increasest a fever, increasest a disorder, not by adding disorder, but by not relieving: so because they were of such sort as that they merited not to be healed, in their very naughtiness in a manner they advanced; as it is said, "But evil men and wicked doers advance for the worse:"  and iniquity is laid upon their own iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:359
verses.text: "And let them not enter in Thy righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:360
verses.text: This is a plain thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:361
verses.text: "Let them be blotted out from the book of the living".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:362
verses.text: For had they been some time written therein? Brethren, we must not so take it, as that God writeth any one in the book of life, and blotteth him out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:363
verses.text: If a man said, "What I have written I have written," concerning the title where it had been written, "King of the Jews:" doth God write any one, and blot him out? He foreknoweth, He hath predestined all before the foundation of the world that are to reign with His Son in life everlasting These He hath written down, these same the Book of Life doth contain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:364
verses.text: Lastly, in the Apocalypse, what saith the Spirit of God, when the same Scripture was speaking of the oppressions that should be from Antichrist? "There shall give consent to him all they that have not been written in the book of life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:365
verses.text: So then without doubt they will not consent that have been written.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:366
verses.text: How then are these men blotted out from that book wherein they were never written? This hath been said according to their own hope, because they thought of themselves that they were written.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:367
verses.text: What is, "let them be blotted out from the book of life"? Even to themselves let it be evident, that they were not there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:368
verses.text: By this method of speaking hath been said in another Psalm, "There shall fall from Thy side a thousand, and tens of thousands from on Thy right hand:" that is, many men shall be offended, even out of that number who thought that they would sit with Thee, even out of that number who thought that they would stand at Thy right hand, being severed from the left-hand goats: not that when any one hath there stood, he shall afterwards fall, or when any one with Him hath sat, he shall be cast away; but that many men were to fall into scandal, who already thought themselves to be there, that is, many that thought that they would sit with Thee, many that hoped that they would stand at the right hand, will themselves fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:369
verses.text: So then here also they that hoped as though by the merit of their own righteousness themselves to have been written in the book of God, they to whom is said, "Search the Scriptures, wherein ye think yourselves to have life eternal:" when their condemnation shall have been brought even to their own knowledge, shall be effaced from the book of the living, they shall know themselves not to be there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:370
verses.text: For the verse which followeth, explaineth what hath been said: "And with just men let them not be written".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:371
verses.text: I have said then "Let them be effaced," according to their hope: but according to Thy justice I say what?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:372
verses.text: "Poor and sorrowful I am".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:373
verses.text: Why this? Is it that we may acknowledge that through bitterness of soul this poor One doth speak evil? For He hath spoken of many things to happen to them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:374
verses.text: And as if we were saying to Him, "Why such things?"—"Nay, not so much!" He answereth, "poor and sorrowful I am".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:375
verses.text: They have brought Me to want, unto this sorrow they have set Me down, therefore I say these words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:376
verses.text: It is not, however, the indignation of one cursing, but the prediction of one prophesying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:377
verses.text: For He was intending to recommend to us certain things which hereafter He saith of His poverty and His sorrow, in order that we may learn to be poor and sorrowful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:378
verses.text: For, "Blessed are the poor, for theirs is the kingdom of Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:379
verses.text: And, "Blessed are they that mourn, for they shall be comforted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:380
verses.text: This therefore He doth Himself before now show to us: and so, "poor and sorrowful I am".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:381
verses.text: The whole Body of Him saith this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:382
verses.text: The Body of Christ in this earth is poor and sorrowful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:383
verses.text: But let Christians be rich.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:384
verses.text: Truly if Christians they are, they are poor; in comparison with the riches celestial for which they hope, all their gold they count for sand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:385
verses.text: "And the health of Thy countenance, O God, hath taken Me up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:386
verses.text: Is this poor One anywise forsaken? When dost thou deign to bring near to thy table a poor man in rags? But again, this poor One the health of the countenance of God hath taken up: in His countenance He hath hidden His need.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:387
verses.text: For of Him hath been said, "Thou shalt hide them in the hiding place of Thy countenance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:388
verses.text: But in that countenance what riches there are would ye know? Riches here give thee this advantage, that thou mayest dine on what thou wilt, whenever thou wilt: but those riches, that thou mayest never hunger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:389
verses.text: "The health of Thy countenance, O God, hath taken Me up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:390
verses.text: For what purpose? In order that no longer I may be poor, no longer sorrowful? "I will praise the name of the Lord with a song, I will magnify Him in praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:391
verses.text: Now it hath been said, this poor One praiseth the name of the Lord with a song, he magnifieth Him in praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:392
verses.text: When would He have ventured to sing, unless He had been refreshed from hunger? "I will magnify Him with praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:393
verses.text: O vast riches! What jewels of God's praise hath he brought out of his inward treasures! These are my riches! "The Lord hath given, the Lord hath taken away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:394
verses.text: Then miserable he hath remained? Far be it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:395
verses.text: See the riches: "As it hath pleased the Lord, so hath been done, be the name of the Lord blessed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:396
verses.text: "And it shall please God:" that I shall praise Him, shall please: "above a new calf, bearing horns and hoofs".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:397
verses.text: More grateful to Him shall be the sacrifice of praise than the sacrifice of a calf.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:398
verses.text: "The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:399
verses.text: "Immolate to God the sacrifice of praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:400
verses.text: So then His praise going forth from my mouth shall please God more than a great victim led up to His altar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:401
verses.text: Therefore above this calf my praising shall please Thee, such as hereafter will be, after poverty and sorrow, in the eternal society of Angels, where neither adversary there shall be in battle to be tossed, nor sluggard from earth to be stirred up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:402
verses.text: "Let the needy see and rejoice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:403
verses.text: Let them believe, and in hope be glad.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:404
verses.text: Let them be more needy, in order that they may deserve to be filled: lest while they belch out pride's satiety, there be denied them the bread whereon they may healthily live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:405
verses.text: "Seek the Lord," ye needy, hunger ye and thirst; for He is Himself the living bread that came down from Heaven "Seek ye the Lord, and your soul shall live".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:406
verses.text: Ye seek bread, that your flesh may live: the Lord seek ye, that your soul may live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:407
verses.text: "For the Lord hath hearkened to the poor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:408
verses.text: He hath hearkened to the poor, and He would not have hearkened to the poor, unless they were poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:409
verses.text: Wilt thou be hearkened to? Poor be thou: let sorrow cry out from thee, and not fastidiousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:410
verses.text: "And His fettered ones He hath not despised".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:411
verses.text: Being offended at His servants, He hath put them in fetters: but them crying from the fetters He hath not despised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:412
verses.text: What are these fetters? Mortality, the corruptibleness of the flesh are the fetters wherewith we have been bound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:413
verses.text: And would ye know the weight of these fetters? Of them is said, "The body which is corrupted weigheth down the soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:414
verses.text: Whenever men in the world will to be rich, for these fetters they are seeking rags.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:415
verses.text: But let the rags of the fetters suffice: seek so much as is necessary for keeping off want, but when thou seekest superfluities, thou longest to load thy fetters.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:416
verses.text: In such a prison then let the fetters abide even alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:417
verses.text: "Sufficient for the day be the evil thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:418
verses.text: "Let there praise Him heavens and earth, sea and all things creeping in them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:419
verses.text: The true riches of this poor man are these, to consider the creation, and to praise the Creator.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:420
verses.text: "Let there praise Him heavens and earth, sea and all things creeping therein".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:421
verses.text: And doth this creation alone praise God, when by considering of it God is praised?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:422
verses.text: Hear thou another thing also: "for God shall save Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:423
verses.text: He restoreth His Church, the faithful Gentiles He doth incorporate with His Only-Begotten; He beguileth not them that believe in Him of the reward of His promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:424
verses.text: "For God shall save Sion; and there shall be builded the cities of Juda".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:425
verses.text: These same are the Churches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:426
verses.text: Let no one say, when shall it come to pass that there be builded the cities of Juda? O that thou wouldest acknowledge the Edifice, and be a living stone, that thou mightest enter into Her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:427
verses.text: Even now the cities of Juda are being built.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:428
verses.text: For Juda is interpreted confession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:429
verses.text: By confession of humility there are being builded the cities of Juda: in order that there may remain without the proud, who blush to confess.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:430
verses.text: "For God shall save Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 70:431
verses.text: What Sion? Hear in the following words: "and the seed of His servants shall possess Her, and they that love His name shall dwell therein".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:1
verses.text: Psalm LXX.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:2
verses.text: Thanks to the "Corn of wheat," because He willed to die and to be multiplied: thanks to the only Son of God, our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, who disdained not to undergo our death, in order that He might make us worthy of His life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:3
verses.text: Behold Him that was single until He went hence; as He said in another Psalm, "Single I am until I go hence;" for He was a single corn of wheat in such sort as that He had in Himself a great fruitfulness of increase; in how many corns imitating the Passion of Him we exult, when we celebrate the nativities of the Martyrs! Many therefore members of Him, under one Head our Saviour Himself, being bound together in the bond of love and peace (as ye judge it fit that ye know, for ye have often heard), are one man: and of the same, as of one man, the voice is ofttimes heard, in the Psalms, and thus one crieth as though it were all, because all in one are one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:4
verses.text: There is then in this Psalm the voice of men troubled, and so indeed of Martyrs amid sufferings in peril, but relying on their own Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:5
verses.text: Let us hear them, and speak with them out of sympathy of heart, though it be not with similarity of suffering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:6
verses.text: For they are already crowned, we are still in peril: not that such sort of persecutions do vex us as have vexed them, but worse perchance in the midsts of all kinds of so great scandals.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:7
verses.text: For our own times do more abound in that woe, which the Lord cried: "Woe to the world because of scandals".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:8
verses.text: And, "Because iniquity hath abounded, the love of man shall wax cold".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:9
verses.text: For not even that holy Lot at Sodom suffered corporal persecution from any one, or had it been told him that he should not dwell there: the persecution of him were the evil doings of the Sodomites.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:10
verses.text: Now then that Christ sitteth in Heaven, now that He is glorified, now that necks of kings are made subject to His yoke, and their brows placed beneath His sign, now that not any one remaineth to dare openly to trample upon Christians, still, however, we groan amid instruments and singers, still those enemies of the Martyrs, because with words and steel they have no power, with their own wantonness do persecute them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:11
verses.text: And O that we were sorrowing for Heathens alone: it would be some sort of comfort, to wait for those that not yet have been signed with the Cross of Christ; when they should be signed, and when, by His authority attached, they should cease to be mad.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:12
verses.text: We see besides men wearing on their brow the sign of Him, at the same time on that same brow wearing the shamelessness of wantonness, and on the days and celebrations of the Martyrs not exulting but insulting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:13
verses.text: And amid these things we groan, and this is our persecution, if there is in us the love which saith, "Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is scandalized, and I burn not?" Not any servant of God, then, is without persecution: and that is a true saying which the Apostle saith, "But even all men that will to live godly in Christ, shall suffer persecution".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:14
verses.text: "O God, to my aid make speed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:15
verses.text: For need we have for an everlasting aid in this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:16
verses.text: But when have we not? Now however being in tribulation, let us especially say, "O God, to my aid make speed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:17
verses.text: "Let them be confounded and fear that seek my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:18
verses.text: Christ is speaking: whether Head speak or whether Body speak; He is speaking that hath said, "Why persecutest thou Me?"  He is speaking that hath said, "Inasmuch as ye have done it to one of the least of Mine, to Me ye have done it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:19
verses.text: The voice then of this Man is known to be of the whole man, of Head and of Body: that need not often be mentioned, because  it is known.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:20
verses.text: "Be they confounded," he saith, "and fear that seek my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:21
verses.text: In another Psalm He saith, "I was looking unto the right and saw, and there was not one that would know Me: flight hath perished from Me, and there is not one to seek out My soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:22
verses.text: There of persecutors He saith, that there was not one to seek out His soul: but here, "Let them be confounded and fear that seek My soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:23
verses.text: And where is that which thou hast heard from thy Lord, "Love ye your enemies, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them that persecute you"? Behold thou sufferest persecution, and cursest them from whom thou sufferest: how dost thou imitate the Passions of thy Lord that have gone before, hanging on the cross and saying, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:24
verses.text: To persons saying such things the Martyr replieth and saith, thou hast set before me the Lord, saying, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do:" understand thou my voice also, in order that it may be thine too: for what have I said concerning mine enemies? "Let them be confounded and fear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:25
verses.text: Already such vengeance hath been taken on the enemies of the Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:26
verses.text: That Saul that persecuted Stephen, he was confounded and feared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:27
verses.text: He was breathing out slaughters,  he was seeking some to drag and slay: a voice having been heard from above, "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou Me," he was confounded and laid low, and he was raised up to obedience, that had been inflamed unto persecuting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:28
verses.text: This then the Martyrs desire for their enemies, "Let them be confounded and fear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:29
verses.text: For so long as they are not confounded and fear, they must needs defend their actions: glorious they think themselves, because they hold, because they bind, because they scourge, because they kill, because they dance, because they insult, and because of all these doings they be some time confounded and fear For if they be confounded, they will also be converted: because converted they cannot be, unless they shall have been confounded and shall have feared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:30
verses.text: Let us then wish these things to our enemies, let us wish them without fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:31
verses.text: Behold I have said, and let me have said it with you, may all that still dance and sing and insult the Martyrs "be confounded and fear:" at last within these walls confounded may they beat their breasts!.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:32
verses.text: "Let them be turned away backward and blush that think evil things to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:33
verses.text: At first there was the assault of them persecuting, now there hath remained the malice of them thinking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:34
verses.text: In fact, there are in the Church distinct seasons of persecutions following one another There was made an assault on the Church when kings were persecuting: and because kings had been foretold as to persecute and as to believe, when one had been fulfilled the other was to follow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:35
verses.text: There came to pass also that which was consequent; kings believed, peace was given to the Church, the Church began to be set in the highest place of dignity, even on this earth, even in this life: but there is not wanting the roar of persecutors, they have turned their assaults into thoughts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:36
verses.text: In these thoughts, as in a bottomless pit, the devil hath been bound, he roareth and breaketh not forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:37
verses.text: For it hath been said concerning these times of the Church, "The sinner shall see, and shall be angry".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:38
verses.text: And shall do what? That which he did at first? Drag, bind, smite? He doeth not this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:39
verses.text: What then? "With his teeth he shall gnash, and shall pine away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:40
verses.text: And with these men the Martyr is, as it were, angry, and yet for these men the Martyr prayeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:41
verses.text: For in like manner as he hath wished well to those men concerning whom he hath said, "Let them be confounded and fear that seek my soul:" so also now, "Let them be turned backward, and blush, that think evil things to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:42
verses.text: Wherefore? In order that they may not go before, but follow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:43
verses.text: For he that censureth the Christian religion, and on his own system willeth to live, willeth as it were to go before Christ, as though He indeed had erred and had been weak and infirm, because He either willed to suffer or could suffer in the hands of the Jews; but that he is a clever man for guarding against all these things; in shunning death, even in basely lying to escape death, and slaying his soul that he may live in body, he thinketh himself a man of singular and prudent measures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:44
verses.text: He goeth before in censuring Christ, in a manner he outstrippeth Christ: let him believe in Christ, and follow Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:45
verses.text: For that which had been desired but now for persecutors thinking evil things, the same the Lord Himself said to Peter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:46
verses.text: Now in a certain place Peter willed to go before the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:47
verses.text: A little before, "Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jona, for flesh and blood hath not revealed it to thee, but My Father which is in Heaven:" now in a moment, "Go back behind Me, Satan".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:48
verses.text: What is, "Go back behind Me"? Follow Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:49
verses.text: Thou willest to go before Me, thou willest to give Me counsel, it is better that thou follow My counsel: this is, "go back," go back behind Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:50
verses.text: He is silencing one outstripping, in order that he may go backward; and He is calling him Satan, because he willeth to go before the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:51
verses.text: A little before, "blessed;" now, "Satan".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:52
verses.text: Whence a little before, "blessed"? Because, "to thee," He saith, "flesh and blood hath not revealed it, but My Father which is in Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:53
verses.text: Whence now, "Satan"? Because "thou savourest not," He saith, "the things which are of God, but the things which are of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:54
verses.text: Let us then that would duly celebrate the nativities of the Martyrs, long for the imitation of the Martyrs; let us not wish to go before the Martyrs, and think ourselves to be of better understanding than they, because we shun sufferings in behalf of righteousness and faith which they shunned not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:55
verses.text: Therefore be they that think evil things, and in wantonness feed their hearts, "turned backward and blush".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:56
verses.text: Let them hear from the Apostle afterwards saying, "But what fruit had ye some time in those things at which ye now blush?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:57
verses.text: What followeth? "Let them be turned away forthwith blushing, that say to me, Well, well".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:58
verses.text: Two are the kinds of persecutors, revilers and flatterers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:59
verses.text: The tongue of the flatterer doth more persecute than the hand of the slayer: for this also the Scripture hath called a furnace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:60
verses.text: Truly when the Scripture was speaking of persecution, it said, "Like gold in a furnace it hath proved them" (speaking of Martyrs being slain), "and as the holocaust's victim it hath received them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:61
verses.text: Hear how even the tongue of flatterers is of such sort: "The proving," he saith, "of silver and of gold is fire; but a man is proved by the tongue of men praising him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:62
verses.text: That is fire, this also is fire: out of both thou oughtest to go forth safe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:63
verses.text: The censurer hath broken thee, thou hast been broken in the furnace like an earthen vessel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:64
verses.text: The Word hath moulded thee, and there hath come the trial of tribulation: that which hath been formed, must needs be seasoned; if it hath been well moulded, there hath come the fire to strengthen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:65
verses.text: Whence He said in the Passion, "Dried up like a potsherd hath been My virtue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:66
verses.text: For Passion and the furnace of tribulation had made Him stronger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:67
verses.text: And what cometh to pass when they are all turned back and blush, whether it be they that seek my soul, or they that think evil things to me, or they that with perverse and feigned benevolence with tongue would soften the stroke which they inflict, when they shall have been themselves turned away and confounded; there shall come to pass what? "Let them exult and be joyous in Thee:" not in me, not in this man or in that man; but in whom they have been made light that were darkness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:68
verses.text: "Let them exult and be joyous in Thee, all that seek Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:69
verses.text: One thing it is to seek God, another thing to seek man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:70
verses.text: "Let them be joyous that seek Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:71
verses.text: They shall not be joyous then that seek themselves, whom Thou hast first sought before they sought Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:72
verses.text: Not yet did that sheep seek the Shepherd, it had strayed from the flock, and He went down to it; He sought it, and carried it back upon His shoulders.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:73
verses.text: Will He despise thee, O sheep, seeking Him, who hath first sought thee despising Him and not seeking Him? Now then begin thou to seek Him that first hath sought thee, and hath carried thee back on His shoulders.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:74
verses.text: Do thou that which He speaketh of, "They that are My sheep hear My voice, and follow Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:75
verses.text: If then thou seekest Him that first hath sought thee, and hast become a sheep of His, and thou hearest the voice of thy Shepherd, and followest Him; see what He showeth to thee of Himself, what of His Body, in order that as to Himself thou mayest not err, as to the Church thou mayest not err, that no one may say to thee, that is Christ which is not Christ, or that is the Church which is not the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:76
verses.text: For many men have said that Christ had no flesh, and that Christ hath not risen in His Body: do not thou follow the voices of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:77
verses.text: Hear thou the voice of Himself the Shepherd, that was clothed with flesh, in order that He might seek lost flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:78
verses.text: He hath risen again, and He saith, "Handle ye and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones as ye see Me have".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:79
verses.text: He showeth Himself to thee, the voice of Him follow thou.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:80
verses.text: He showeth also the Church, that no one may deceive thee by the name of Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:81
verses.text: "It behoved," He saith, "Christ to suffer, and to rise again from the dead the third day, and that there should be preached repentance and remission of sins through all nations, beginning with Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:82
verses.text: Thou hast the voice of Thy Shepherd, do not thou follow the voice of strangers: and a thief thou shalt not fear, if thou shalt have followed the voice of the Shepherd.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:83
verses.text: But how shalt thou follow? If thou shalt neither have said to any man, as if it were by his own merit, Well, well: nor shalt have heard the same with joy, so that thy head be not made fat with the oil of a sinner "Let all them exult and be joyous in Thee, that seek Thee; and let them say"—let them say what, that exult? "Be the Lord alway magnified!" Let all them say this, that exult and seek Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:84
verses.text: What? "Be the Lord alway magnified; yea, they that love Thy salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:85
verses.text: Not only, "Be the Lord magnified;" but also, "alway".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:86
verses.text: A sinner thou art, be He magnified in order that He may call; thou confessest, be He magnified in order that He may forgive: now thou livest justly, be He magnified in order that He may direct: thou perseverest even unto the end, be He magnified in order that He may glorify.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:87
verses.text: "Be the Lord," then, "alway magnified; yea, they love His saving health".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:88
verses.text: For from Him they have salvation, not from themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:89
verses.text: The saving health of the Lord our God, is the Saviour our Lord Jesus Christ: whosoever loveth the Saviour, confesseth himself to have been made whole; whosoever confesseth himself to have been made whole, confesseth himself to have been sick.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:90
verses.text: Not their own saving health, as if they could save themselves of themselves: not as it were the saving health of a man, as though by him they could be saved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:91
verses.text: "Do not," he saith, "confide in princes, and in the sons of men, in whom there is no safety".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:92
verses.text: Why so? "Of the Lord is safety, and upon Thy people is Thy blessing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:93
verses.text: Behold, "Be the Lord magnified:" wilt thou never, wilt thou nowhere? In Him was something, in me nothing: but if in Him is whatsoever I am, be He, not I.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:94
verses.text: But thou then what? "But I am needy and poor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:95
verses.text: He is rich, He abounding, He needing nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:96
verses.text: Behold my light, behold whence I am illumined; for I cry, "Thou shalt illumine my candle, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:97
verses.text: What then of thee? "But I am needy and poor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:98
verses.text: I am like an orphan, my soul is like a widow destitute and desolate: help I seek, alway mine infirmity I confess.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:99
verses.text: There have been forgiven me my sins, now I have begun to follow the commandments of God: still, however, I am needy and poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:100
verses.text: Why still needy and poor? Because "I see another law in my members fighting against the law of my mind".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:101
verses.text: Why needy and poor? Because, "blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:102
verses.text: Still I hunger, still I thirst: my fulness hath been put off, not taken away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:103
verses.text: "O God, aid Thou me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:104
verses.text: Most suitably also Lazarus is said to be interpreted, "one aided:" that needy and poor man, that was transported into the bosom of Abraham; and beareth the type of the Church, which ought alway to confess that she hath need of aid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:105
verses.text: This is true, this is godly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:106
verses.text: "I have said to the Lord, My God Thou art".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:107
verses.text: Why? "For my goods Thou needest not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:108
verses.text: He needeth not us, we need Him: therefore He is truly Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:109
verses.text: For thou art not the very true Lord of thy servant: both are men, both needing God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:110
verses.text: But if thou supposest thy servant to need thee, in order that thou mayest give him bread; thou also needest thy servant, in order that he may aid thy labours.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:111
verses.text: Each one of you doth need the other.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:112
verses.text: Therefore neither of you is truly lord, and neither of you truly servant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:113
verses.text: Hear thou the true Lord, of whom thou art the true servant: "I have said to the Lord, My God Thou art".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:114
verses.text: Why art Thou Lord? "Because my goods Thou needest not"? But what of thee? "But I am needy and poor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:115
verses.text: Behold the needy and poor: may God feed, may God alleviate, may God aid: "O God," he saith, "aid Thou me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:116
verses.text: "My helper and deliverer art Thou; O Lord, delay not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:117
verses.text: Thou art the helper and deliverer: I need succour, help Thou; entangled I am, deliver Thou.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:118
verses.text: For no one will deliver from entanglings except Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:119
verses.text: There stand round about us the nooses of divers cares, on this side and on that we are torn as it were with thorns and brambles, we walk a narrow way, perchance we have stuck fast in the brambles: let us say to God, "Thou art my deliverer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:120
verses.text: He that showed us the narrow way, hath taught us to follow it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:121
verses.text: What is, "delay not"? Because many men say, it is a long time till Christ comes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:122
verses.text: What then: because we say, "delay not," will He come before He hath determined to come? What meaneth this prayer, "delay not"? May not Thy coming seem to me to be too long delayed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:123
verses.text: For to thee it seemeth a long time, to God it seemeth not long, to whom a thousand years are one day, or the three hours of a watch But if thou shalt not have had endurance, late for thee it will be: and when to thee it shall be late, thou wilt be diverted from Him, and wilt be like unto those that were wearied in the desert, and hastened to ask of God the pleasant things which He was reserving for them in the Land; and when there were not given on their journey the pleasant things, whereby perchance they would have been corrupted, they murmured against God, and went back in heart unto Egypt:  to that place whence in body they had been severed, in heart they went back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:124
verses.text: Do not thou, then, so, do not so: fear the word of the Lord, saying, "Remember Lot's wife".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:125
verses.text: She too being on the way, but now delivered from the Sodomites, looked back; in the place where she looked back, there she remained: she became a statue of salt, in order to season thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:126
verses.text: For to thee she hath been given for an example, in order that thou mayest have sense, mayest not stop infatuated on the way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:127
verses.text: Observe her stopping and pass on: observe her looking back, and do thou be reaching forth unto the things before, as Paul was What is it, not to look back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:128
verses.text: "Of the things behind forgetful," he saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:129
verses.text: Therefore thou followest, being called to the heavenly reward, whereof hereafter thou wilt glory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 71:130
verses.text: For the same Apostle saith, "There remaineth for me a crown of righteousness, which in that day the Lord, the just Judge, shall render to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:2
verses.text: In all the holy Scriptures the grace of God that delivereth us commendeth itself to us, in order that it may have us commended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:3
verses.text: This is sung of in this Psalm, whereof we have undertaken to speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:4
verses.text: This grace the Apostle commendeth: by this he got to have the Jews for enemies, boasting of the letter of the law and of their own justice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:5
verses.text: This then commending in the lesson which hath been read, he saith thus: "For I am the least of the Apostles, that am not worthy to be called an Apostle, because I persecuted the Church of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:6
verses.text: "But therefore mercy," he saith, "I obtained, because ignorant I did it in unbelief".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:7
verses.text: Then a little afterwards, "Faithful the saying is, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am first".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:8
verses.text: Were there before him not any sinners? What then, was he the first then? Yea, going before all men not in time, but in evil disposition.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:9
verses.text: "But therefore," he saith, "mercy I obtained," in order that in me Christ Jesus might show all long-suffering, for the imitation of those that shall believe in Him unto life eternal: that is, every sinner and unjust man, already despairing of himself, already having the mind of a gladiator, so as to do whatsoever he willeth, because he must needs be condemned, may yet observe the Apostle Paul, to whom so great cruelty and so very evil a disposition was forgiven by God; and by not  despairing of himself may he be turned unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:10
verses.text: This grace God doth commend to us in this Psalm also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:11
verses.text: The title then of this Psalm is, as usual, a title intimating on the threshold what is being done in the house: "To David himself for the sons of Jonadab, and for those that were first led captive".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:12
verses.text: Jonadab (he is commended to us in the prophecy of Jeremiah) was a certain man, who had enjoined his sons not to drink wine, and not to dwell in houses, but in tents.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:13
verses.text: But the commandment of the father the sons kept and observed, and by this earned a blessing from the Lord Now the Lord had not commanded this, but their own father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:14
verses.text: But they so received it as though it were a commandment from the Lord their God; for even though the Lord had not commanded that they should drink no wine and should dwell in tents; yet the Lord had commanded that sons should obey their father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:15
verses.text: In this case alone a son ought not to obey his father, if his father should have commanded anything contrary to the Lord his God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:16
verses.text: For indeed the father ought not to be angry, when God is preferred before him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:17
verses.text: But when a father doth command that which is not contrary to God; he must be heard as God is: because to obey one's father God hath enjoined.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:18
verses.text: God then blessed the sons of Jonadab because of their obedience, and thrust them in the teeth of His disobedient people, reproaching them, because while the sons of Jonadab were obedient to their father, they obeyed not their God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:19
verses.text: But while Jeremiah was treating of these topics, he had this object in regard to the people of Israel, that they should prepare themselves to be led for captivity into Babylon, and should  not hope for any other thing, but that they were to be captives.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:20
verses.text: The title then of this Psalm seemeth from thence to have taken its hue, so that when he had said, "Of the sons of Jonadab;" he added, "and of them that were first led captive:" not that the sons of Jonadab were led captive, but because to them that were to be led captive there were opposed the sons of Jonadab, because they were obedient to their father: in order that they might understand that they had been made captive, because they were not obedient to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:21
verses.text: It is added also that Jonadab is interpreted, "the Lord's spontaneous one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:22
verses.text: What is this, the Lord's spontaneous one? Serving God freely with the will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:23
verses.text: What is, the Lord's spontaneous one? "In me are, O God, Thy vows, which I will render of praise to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:24
verses.text: What is, the Lord's spontaneous one? "Voluntarily I will sacrifice to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:25
verses.text: For if the Apostolic teaching admonisheth a slave to serve a human master, not as though of necessity, but of good will, and by freely serving make himself in heart free; how much more must God be served with whole and full and free will, who seeth thy very will?The first man made us captive, the second man hath delivered us from captivity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:26
verses.text: "For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all shall be made alive".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:27
verses.text: But in Adam they die through the flesh's nativity, in Christ they are delivered through the heart's faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:28
verses.text: It was not in thy power not to be born of Adam: it is in thy power to believe in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:29
verses.text: Howsoever much then thou shalt have willed to belong to the first man, unto captivity thou wilt belong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:30
verses.text: And what is, shalt have willed to belong? or what is, shalt belong? Already thou belongest: cry out, "Who shall deliver me from the body of this death?" Let us hear then this man crying out this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:31
verses.text: "O God, in Thee I have hoped, O Lord, I shall not be confounded for everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:32
verses.text: Already I have been confounded, but not for everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:33
