verses.text: For how is he not confounded, to whom is said, "What fruit had ye in these things wherein ye now blush?" What then shall be done, that we may not be confounded for everlasting? "Draw near unto Him, and be ye enlightened, and your faces shall not blush".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:34
verses.text: Confounded ye are in Adam, withdraw from Adam, draw near unto Christ, and then ye shall not be confounded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:35
verses.text: "In Thee I have hoped, O Lord, I shall not be confounded for everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:36
verses.text: If in myself I am now confounded, in Thee I shall not be confounded for everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:37
verses.text: "In Thine own righteousness deliver me, and save me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:38
verses.text: Not in mine own, but in Thine own: for if in mine own, I shall be one of those whereof he saith, "Being ignorant of God's righteousness, and their own righteousness willing to establish, to the righteousness of God they were not made subject".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:39
verses.text: Therefore, "in Thine own righteousness," not in mine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:40
verses.text: For mine is what? Iniquity hath gone before.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:41
verses.text: And when I shall be righteous, Thine own righteousness it will be: for by righteousness given to me by Thee I shall be righteous; and it shall be so mine, as that it be Thine, that is, given to me by Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:42
verses.text: For I believe on Him that justifieth an ungodly man, so that my faith is counted for righteousness Even so then the righteousness shall be mine, not however as though mine own, not as though by mine own self given to myself: as they thought who through the letter made their boast, and rejected grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:43
verses.text: It is a small thing then that thou acknowledge the good thing which is in thee to be from God, unless also on that account thou exalt not thyself above him that hath not yet, who perchance when he shall have received, will outstrip thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:44
verses.text: For when Saul was a stoner of Stephen, how many were the Christians of whom he was persecutor! Nevertheless, when he was converted, all that had gone before he surpassed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:45
verses.text: Therefore say thou to God that which thou hearest in the Psalm, "In Thee I have hoped, O Lord, I shall not be confounded for everlasting: in Thine own righteousness," not in mine, "deliver me, and save me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:46
verses.text: "Incline unto me Thine ear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:47
verses.text: This also is a confession of humility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:48
verses.text: He that saith, "Incline unto me," is confessing that he is lying like a sick man laid at the feet of the Physician standing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:49
verses.text: Lastly, observe that it is a sick man that is speaking: "Incline unto me Thine ear, and save me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:50
verses.text: "Be Thou unto me for a protecting God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:51
verses.text: Let not the darts of the enemy reach unto me: for I am not able to protect myself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:52
verses.text: And a small thing is "protecting:" he hath added, "and for a walled place, that Thou mayest save me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:53
verses.text: "For a walled place" be Thou to me, be Thou my walled place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:54
verses.text: Behold, God Himself hath become the place of thy fleeing unto, who at first was the fearful object of thy fleeing from.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:55
verses.text: "For a walled place," he saith, be Thou to me, "that Thou mayest save me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:56
verses.text: I shall not be safe except in Thee: except Thou shalt have been my rest, my sickness shall not be able to be made whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:57
verses.text: Lift me from the earth; upon Thee I will lie, in order that I may rise unto a walled place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:58
verses.text: What can be better walled? When unto that place thou shalt have fled for refuge, tell me what adversaries thou wilt dread? Who will lie in wait, and come at thee? A certain man is said from the summit of a mountain to have cried out, when an Emperor was passing by, "I speak not of thee:" the other is said to have looked back and to have said, "Nor I of thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:59
verses.text: He had despised an Emperor with glittering arms, with mighty army.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:60
verses.text: From whence? From a strong place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:61
verses.text: If he was secure on a high spot of earth, how secure art thou on Him by whom heaven and earth were made? I, if for myself I shall have chosen another place, shall not be able to be safe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:62
verses.text: Choose thou indeed, O man, if thou shalt have found one, a place better walled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:63
verses.text: There is not then a place whither to flee from Him, except we flee to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:64
verses.text: If thou wilt escape Him angry, flee to Him appeased.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:65
verses.text: "For my firmament and my refuge Thou art".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:66
verses.text: "My firmament" is what? Through Thee I am firm, and by Thee I am firm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:67
verses.text: "For my firmament and my refuge Thou art:" in order that I may be made firm by Thee, in whatever respects I shall have been made infirm in myself, I will flee for refuge unto Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:68
verses.text: For firm the grace of Christ maketh thee, and immovable against all temptations of the enemy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:69
verses.text: But there is there too human frailness, there is there still the first captivity, there is there too the law in the members fighting against the law of the mind, and willing to lead captive in the law of sin: still the body which is corrupt presseth down the soul Howsoever firm thou be by the grace of God, so long as thou still bearest an earthly vessel, wherein the treasure of God is, something must be dreaded even from that same vessel of clay Therefore "my firmament Thou art," in order that I may be firm in this world against all temptations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:70
verses.text: But if many they are, and they trouble me: "my refuge Thou art".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:71
verses.text: For I will confess mine infirmity, to the end that I may be timid  like a "hare," because I am full of thorns like a "hedgehog".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:72
verses.text: And as in another Psalm is said, "The rock is a refuge for the hedgehogs and the hares:" but the Rock was Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:73
verses.text: "O God, deliver me from the hand of the sinner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:74
verses.text: Generally, sinners, among whom is toiling he that is now to be delivered from captivity: he that now crieth, "Unhappy man I, who shall deliver me from the body of this death? The grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:75
verses.text: Within is a foe, that law in the members; there are without also enemies: unto what cryest thou? Unto Him, to whom hath been cried, "From my secret sins cleanse me, O Lord, and from strange sins spare Thy servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:76
verses.text: But these sinners are of two kinds: there are some that have received Law, there are others that have not received: all the heathen have not received Law, all Jews and Christians have received Law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:77
verses.text: Therefore the general term is sinner; either a transgressor of the Law, if he hath received Law; or only unjust without Law, if he hath not received the Law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:78
verses.text: Of both kinds speaketh the Apostle, and saith, "They that without Law have sinned, without Law shall perish, and they that in the Law have sinned, by the Law shall be judged".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:79
verses.text: But thou that amid both kinds dost groan, say to God that which thou hearest in the Psalm, "My God, deliver me from the hand of the sinner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:80
verses.text: Of what sinner? "From the hand of him that transgresseth the Law, and of the unjust man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:81
verses.text: He that transgresseth the Law is indeed also unjust; for not unjust he is not, that transgresseth the Law: but every one that transgresseth the Law is unjust, not every unjust man doth transgress the Law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:82
verses.text: For, "Where there is not a Law," saith the Apostle, "neither is there transgression".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:83
verses.text: They then that have not received Law, may be called unjust, transgressors they cannot be called.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:84
verses.text: Both are judged after their deservings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:85
verses.text: But I that from captivity will to be delivered through Thy grace, cry to Thee, "Deliver me from the hand of the sinner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:86
verses.text: What is, from the hand of him? From the power of him, that while he is raging, he lead me not unto consenting with him; that while he lieth in wait, he persuade not to iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:87
verses.text: "From the hand of the sinner and of the unjust man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:88
verses.text: Lastly, there followeth the reason why I say this: "for Thou art my patience".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:89
verses.text: Now if He is patience rightly, He is that also which followeth, "O Lord, my hope from my youth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:90
verses.text: My patience, because my hope: or rather my hope, because my patience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:91
verses.text: "Tribulation," saith the Apostle, "worketh patience, patience probation, but probation hope, but hope confoundeth not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:92
verses.text: With reason in Thee I have hoped, O Lord, I shall not be confounded for everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:93
verses.text: "O Lord, my hope from my youth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:94
verses.text: From thy youth is God thy hope? Is He not also from thy boyhood, and from thine infancy? Certainly, saith he.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:95
verses.text: For see what followeth, that thou mayest not think that I have said this, "my hope from my youth," as if God noways profited mine infancy or my boyhood; hear what followeth: "In Thee I have been strengthened from the womb".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:96
verses.text: Hear yet: "From the belly of my mother Thou art my Protector".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:97
verses.text: Why then, "from my youth," except it was the period from which I began to hope in Thee? For before in Thee I was not hoping, though Thou wast my Protector, that didst lead me safe unto the time, when I learned to hope in Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:98
verses.text: But from my youth I began in Thee to hope, from the time when Thou didst arm me against the Devil, so that in the girding of Thy host being armed with Thy faith, love, hope, and the rest of Thy gifts, I waged conflict against Thine invisible enemies, and heard from the Apostle, "There is not for us a wrestling against flesh and blood, but against principalities, and powers," etc There a young man it is that doth fight against these things: but though he be a young man, he falleth, unless He be the hope of Him to whom he crieth, "O Lord, my hope from my youth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:99
verses.text: "In Thee is my singing alway".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:100
verses.text: Is it only from the time when I began to hope in Thee until now? Nay, but "alway".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:101
verses.text: What is, "alway"? Not only in the time of faith, but also in the time of sight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:102
verses.text: For now, "So long as we are in the body we are absent from the Lord: for by faith we walk, not by sight:" there will be a time when we shall see that which being not seen we believe: but when that hath been seen which we believe, we shall rejoice: but when that hath been seen which they believed not, ungodly men shall be confounded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:103
verses.text: Then will come the substance whereof there is now the hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:104
verses.text: But, "Hope which is seen is not hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:105
verses.text: But if that which we see not we hope for, through patience we wait for it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:106
verses.text: Now then thou groanest, now unto a place of refuge thou runnest, in order that thou mayest be saved; now being in infirmity thou entreatest the Physician: what, when thou shalt have received perfect soundness also, what when thou shall have been made "equal to the Angels of God," wilt thou then perchance forget that grace, whereby thou hast been delivered? Far be it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:107
verses.text: "As it were a monster I have become unto many".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:108
verses.text: Here in time of hope, in time of groaning, in time of humiliation, in time of sorrow, in time of infirmity, in time of the voice from the fetters—here then what? "As it were a monster I have become unto many".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:109
verses.text: Why, "As it were a monster"? Why do they insult me that think me a monster? Because I believe that which I see not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:110
verses.text: For they being happy in those things which they see, exult in drink, in wantonness, in chamberings, in covetousness, in riches, in robberies, in secular dignities, in the whitening of a mud wall, in these things they exult: but I walk in a different way, contemning those things which are present, and fearing even the prosperous things of the world, and secure in no other thing but the promises of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:111
verses.text: And they, "Let us eat and drink, for to-morrow we die".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:112
verses.text: What sayest thou? Repeat it: "let us eat," he saith, "and drink".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:113
verses.text: Come now, what hast thou said afterwards? "for to-morrow we die".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:114
verses.text: Thou hast terrified, not led me astray.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:115
verses.text: Certainly by the very thing which thou hast said afterwards, thou hast stricken me with fear to consent with thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:116
verses.text: "For to-morrow we die," thou hast said: and there hath preceded, "Let us eat and drink".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:117
verses.text: For when thou hadst said, "Let us eat and drink;" thou didst add, "for to-morrow we die".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:118
verses.text: Hear the other side from me, "Yea let us fast and pray, 'for to-morrow we die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:119
verses.text: '" I keeping this way, strait and narrow, "as it were a monster have become unto many: but Thou art a strong helper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:120
verses.text: Be Thou with me, O Lord Jesus, to say to me, faint not in the narrow way, I first have gone along it, I am the way itself, I lead, in Myself I lead, unto Myself I lead home.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:121
verses.text: Therefore though "a monster I have become unto many;" nevertheless I will not fear, for "Thou art a strong Helper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:122
verses.text: "Let my mouth be fulfilled with praise, that with hymn I may tell of Thy glory, all the day long Thy magnificence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:123
verses.text: What is "all the day long"? Without intermission.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:124
verses.text: In prosperity, because Thou dost comfort: in adversity, because Thou dost correct: before I was in being, because Thou didst make; when I was in being, because Thou didst give health: when I had sinned, because Thou didst forgive; when I was converted, because Thou didst help; when I had persevered, because Thou didst crown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:125
verses.text: My hope from my youth, "cast me not away in time of old age".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:126
verses.text: What is this time of old age? "When my strength shall fail, forsake Thou not me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:127
verses.text: Here God maketh this answer to thee, yea indeed let thy strength fail, in order that in thee mine may abide: in order that thou mayest say with the Apostle, "When I am made weak, then I am mighty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:128
verses.text: Fear not, that thou be cast away in that weakness, in that old age.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:129
verses.text: But why? Was not thy Lord made weak on the Cross? Did not most mighty men and fat bulls before Him, as though a man of no strength, made captive and oppressed, shake the head and say, "If Son of God He is, let Him come down from the Cross"? Has he deserted because He was made weak, who preferred not to come down from the Cross, lest He should seem not to have displayed power, but to have yielded to them reviling? What did He hanging teach thee, that would not come down, but patience amid men reviling, but that thou shouldest be strong in thy God? Perchance too in His person was said, "As it were a monster I have become unto many, and Thou art a strong Helper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:130
verses.text: In His person according to His weakness, not according to His power; according to that whereby He had transformed us into Himself, not according to that wherein He had Himself come down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:131
verses.text: For He became a monster unto many.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:132
verses.text: And perchance the same was the old age of Him; because on account of its oldness it is not improperly called old age, and the Apostle saith, "Our old man hath been crucified together with Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:133
verses.text: If there was there our old man, old age was there; because old, old age Nevertheless, because a true saying is, "Renewed as an eagle's shall be Thy youth;" He rose Himself the third day, promised a resurrection at the end of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:134
verses.text: Already there hath gone before the Head, the members are to follow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:135
verses.text: Why dost thou fear lest He should forsake thee, lest He cast thee away for the time of old age, when thy strength shall have failed? Yea at that time in thee will be the strength of Him, when thy strength shall have failed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:136
verses.text: Why do I say this? "For mine enemies have spoken against me, and they that were keeping watch for My soul, have taken counsel together : saying, God hath forsaken Him, persecute Him, and seize Him, for there is no one to deliver Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:137
verses.text: This hath been said concerning Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:138
verses.text: For He that with the great power of Divinity, wherein He is equal to the Father, had raised to life dead persons, on a sudden in the hands of enemies became weak, and as if having no power, was seized.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:139
verses.text: When would He have been seized, except they had first said in their heart, "God hath forsaken Him?" Whence there was that voice on the Cross, "My God, My God, why hast Thou forsaken Me?"  So then did God forsake Christ, though "God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself," though Christ was also God, out of the Jews indeed according to the flesh, "Who is over all things, God blessed for ever,"—did God forsake Him? Far be it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:140
verses.text: But in our old man our voice it was, because our old man was crucified together with Him: and of that same our old man He had taken a Body, because Mary was of Adam.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:141
verses.text: Therefore the very thing which they thought, from the Cross He said, "Why hast Thou forsaken Me?" Why do these men think Me left alone to their evil? What is, think Me forsaken in their evil? "For if they had known, the Lord of glory they had never crucified Persecute and seize Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:142
verses.text: More familiarly however, brethren, let us take this of the members of Christ, and acknowledge our own voice in these words: because even He used such words in our person, not in His own power and majesty; but in that which He became for our sakes, not according to that which He was, who hath made us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:143
verses.text: "O Lord, my God, be not far from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:144
verses.text: So it is, and the Lord is not far off at all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:145
verses.text: For, "The Lord is nigh unto them that have bruised the heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:146
verses.text: "My God, unto my help look Thou".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:147
verses.text: "Be they confounded and fail that engage my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:148
verses.text: What hath he desired? "Be they confounded and fail".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:149
verses.text: Why hath he desired it? "That engage my soul"? What is, "That engage my soul"? Engaging as it were unto some quarrel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:150
verses.text: For they are said to be engaged that are challenged to quarrel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:151
verses.text: If then so it is, let us beware of men that engage our soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:152
verses.text: What is, "That engage our soul"? First provoking us to withstand God, in order that in our evil things God may displease us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:153
verses.text: For when art thou right, so that to thee the God of Israel may be good, good to men right in heart? When art thou right? Wilt thou hear? When in that good which thou doest, God is pleasing to thee; but in that evil which thou sufferest, God is not displeasing to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:154
verses.text: See ye what I have said, brethren, and be ye on your guard against men that engage your souls.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:155
verses.text: For all men that deal with you in order to make you be wearied in sorrows and tribulations, have this aim, namely, that God may be displeasing to you in that which ye suffer, and there may go forth from your mouth, "What is this? For what have I done?" Now then hast thou done nothing of evil, and art thou just, He unjust? A sinner I am, thou sayest, I confess, just I call not myself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:156
verses.text: But what, sinner, hast thou by any means done so much evil as he with whom it is well? As much as Gaiuseius? I know the evil doings of him, I know the iniquities of him, from which I, though a sinner, am very far; and yet I see him abounding in all good things, and I am suffering so great evil things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:157
verses.text: I do not then say, O God, "what have I done" to Thee, because I have done nothing at all of evil; but because I have not done so much as to deserve to suffer these things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:158
verses.text: Again, art thou just, He unjust? Wake up, wretched man, thy soul hath been engaged! I have not, he saith, called myself just.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:159
verses.text: What then sayest thou? A sinner I am, but I did not commit so great sins, as to deserve to suffer these things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:160
verses.text: Thou sayest not then to God, just I am, and Thou art unjust: but thou sayest, unjust I am, but Thou art more unjust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:161
verses.text: Behold thy soul hath been engaged, behold now thy soul wageth war.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:162
verses.text: What? Against whom? Thy soul, against God; that which hath been made against Him by whom it was made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:163
verses.text: Even because thou art in being to cry out against Him, thou art ungrateful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:164
verses.text: Return, then, to the confession of thy sickness, and beg the healing hand of the Physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:165
verses.text: Think thou not they are happy who flourish for a time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:166
verses.text: Thou art being chastised, they are being spared: perchance for thee chastised and amended an inheritance is being kept in reserve.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:167
verses.text: Lastly, see what followeth, "Let them put on confusion and shame, that think evil things to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:168
verses.text: "Confusion and shame," confusion because of a bad conscience, shame because of modesty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:169
verses.text: Let this befall them, and they will be good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:170
verses.text: "But I alway in Thee will hope, and will add to all Thy praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:171
verses.text: What is this? "I will add to all Thy praise," ought to move us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:172
verses.text: More perfect wilt thou make the praise of God? Is there anything to be superadded? If already that is all praise, wilt thou add anything? God was praised in all His good deeds, in every creature of His, in the whole establishment of all things, in the government and regulation of ages, in the order of seasons, in the height of Heaven, in the fruitfulness of the regions of earth, in the encircling of the sea, in every excellency of the creature everywhere brought forth, in the sons of men themselves, in the giving of the Law, in delivering His people from the captivity of the Egyptians, and all the rest of His wonderful works: not yet He had been praised for having raised up flesh unto life eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:173
verses.text: Be there then this praise added by the Resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ: in order that here we may perceive His voice above all past praise: thus it is that we rightly understand this also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:174
verses.text: "My mouth shall tell out Thy righteousness" : not mine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:175
verses.text: From thence I will add to all Thy praise: because even that I am righteous, if righteous I am, is Thy righteousness in me, not mine own: for Thou dost justify the ungodly "All the day long Thy salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:176
verses.text: What is, "Thy salvation"? Let no one assume to himself, that he saveth himself, "Of the Lord is Salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:177
verses.text: Not any one by himself saveth himself, "Vain is man's salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:178
verses.text: "All the day long Thy Salvation:" at all times.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:179
verses.text: Something of adversity cometh, preach the Salvation of the Lord: something of prosperity cometh, preach the Salvation of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:180
verses.text: Do not preach in prosperity, and hold thy peace in adversity: otherwise there will not be that which hath been said, "all the day long".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:181
verses.text: For all the day long is day together with its own night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:182
verses.text: Do we when we say, for example, thirty days have gone by, mention the nights also; do we not under the very term days include the nights also? In Genesis what was said? "The evening was made, and the morning was made, one day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:183
verses.text: Therefore a whole day is the day together with its own night: for the night doth serve the day, not the day the night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:184
verses.text: Whatever thou doest in mortal flesh, ought to serve righteousness: whatever thou doest by the commandment of God, be it not done for the sake of the advantage of the flesh, lest day serve night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:185
verses.text: Therefore all the day long speak of the praise of God, to wit, in prosperity and in adversity; in prosperity, as though in the day time; in adversity, as though in the night time: all the day long nevertheless speak of the praise of God, so that thou mayest not have sung to no purpose, "I will bless God at every time, alway the praise of Him is in my mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:186
verses.text: Therefore, he saith, "For I have not known tradings".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:187
verses.text: What are these tradings? Let traders hear and change their life; and if they have been such, be not such; let them not know what they have been, let them forget; lastly, let them not approve, not praise; let them disapprove, condemn, be changed, if trading is a sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:188
verses.text: For on this account, O thou trader, because of a certain eagerness for getting, whenever thou shalt have suffered loss, thou wilt blaspheme; and there will not be in thee that which hath been spoken of, "all the day long Thy praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:189
verses.text: But whenever for the price of the goods which thou art selling, thou not only liest, but even falsely swearest; how in thy mouth all the day long is there the praise of God? While, if thou art a Christian, even out of thy mouth the name of God is being blasphemed, so that men say, see what sort of men are Christians! Therefore if this man for this reason speaketh the praise of God all the day long, because he hath not known tradings; let Christians amend themselves, let them not trade.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:190
verses.text: But a trader saith to me, behold I bring indeed from a distant quarter merchandise unto these places, wherein there are not those things which I have brought, by which means I may gain a living: I ask but as reward for my labour, that I may sell dearer than I have bought: for whence can I live, when it hath been written, "the worker is worthy of his reward"? But he is treating of lying, of false swearing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:191
verses.text: This is the fault of me, not of trading: for I should not, if I would, be unable to do without this fault.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:192
verses.text: I then, the merchant, do not shift mine own fault to trading: but if I lie, it is I that lie, not the trade.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:193
verses.text: For I might say, for so much I bought, but for so much I will sell; if thou pleasest, buy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:194
verses.text: For the buyer hearing this truth would not be offended, and not a whit less all men would resort to me: because they would love truth more than gain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:195
verses.text: Of this then, he saith, admonish me, that I lie not, that I forswear not; not to relinquish business whereby I maintain myself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:196
verses.text: For to what dost thou put me when thou puttest me away from this? Perchance to some craft? I will be a shoemaker, I will make shoes for men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:197
verses.text: Are not they too liars? are not they too false-swearers? Do they not, when they have contracted to make shoes for one man, when they have received money from another man, give up that which they were making, and undertake to make for another, and deceive him for whom they have promised to make speedily? Do they not often say, to-day I am about it, to-day I'll get them done? Secondly, in the very sewing do they not commit as many frauds? These are their doings and these are their sayings: but they are themselves evil, not the calling which they profess.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:198
verses.text: All evil artificers, then, not fearing God, either for gain, or for fear of loss or want, do lie, do forswear themselves; there is no continual praise of God in them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:199
verses.text: How then dost thou withdraw me from trading? Wouldest thou that I be a farmer, and murmur against God thundering, so that, fearing hail, I consult a wizard, in order to learn what to do to protect me against the weather; so that I desire famine for the poor, in order that I may be able to sell what I have kept in store? Unto this dost thou bring me? But good farmers, thou sayest, do not such things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:200
verses.text: Nor do good traders do those things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:201
verses.text: But why, even to have sons is an evil thing, for when their head is in pain, evil and unbelieving mothers seek for impious charms and incantations? These are the sins of men, not of things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:202
verses.text: A trader might thus speak to me—Look then, O Bishop, how thou understand the tradings which thou hast read in the Psalm: lest perchance thou understand not, and yet forbid me trading.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:203
verses.text: Admonish me then how I should live; if well, it shall be well with me: one thing however I know, that if I shall have been evil, it is not trading that maketh me so, but my iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:204
verses.text: Whenever truth is spoken, there is nothing to be said against it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:205
verses.text: Let us inquire then what he hath called tradings, which indeed he that hath not known, all the day long doth praise God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:206
verses.text: Trading even in the Greek language is derived from action, and in the Latin from want of inaction: but whether it be from action or want of inaction, let us examine what it is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:207
verses.text: For they that are active traders, rely as it were upon their own action, they praise their works, they at tain not to the grace of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:208
verses.text: Therefore traders are opposed to that grace which this Psalm doth commend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:209
verses.text: For it doth commend that grace, in order that no one may boast of his own works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:210
verses.text: Because in a certain place is said, "Physicians shall not raise to life," ought men to abandon medicine? But what is this? Under this name are understood proud men, promising salvation to men, whereas "of the Lord is Salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:211
verses.text: With reason the Lord drave from the Temple them to whom He said, "It is written, My House shall be called the House of prayer, but ye have made it a house of trading;" that is, boasting of your works, seeking no inaction, nor hearing the Scripture speaking against your unrest and trading, "be ye still, and see that I am the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:212
verses.text: But there is in some copies, "For I have not known literature".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:213
verses.text: Where some books have "trading," there others "literature:" how they may accord is a hard matter to find out; and yet the discrepancy of interpreters perchance showeth the meaning, introduceth no error.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:214
verses.text: Let us inquire then how to understand literature also, lest we offend grammarians in the same way as we did traders a little before: because a grammarian too may live honourably in his calling, and neither forswear nor lie.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:215
verses.text: Let us examine then the literature which he hath not known, in whose mouth all the day long is the praise of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:216
verses.text: There is a sort of literature of the Jews: for to them let us refer this; there we shall find what hath been said: just as when we were inquiring about traders, on the score of actions and works, we found that to be called detestable trading, which the Apostle hath branded, saying, "For being ignorant of God's righteousness, and willing to establish their own, to the righteousness of God they were not made subject".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:217
verses.text: Just as then we found out the former charge against traders, that is men boasting of action, exalting themselves because of business which admitteth no inaction, unquiet men rather than good workmen; because good workmen are those in whom God worketh; so also we find a sort of literature among the Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:218
verses.text: Moses wrote five books: but in the five porches encircling the pool, sick men were lying, but they could not be healed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:219
verses.text: See how the letter remained, convicting the guilty, not saving the unrighteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:220
verses.text: For in those five porches, a figure of the five books, sick men were given over rather than made whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:221
verses.text: What then in that place did make whole a sick man? The moving of the water.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:222
verses.text: When that pool was moved there went down a sick man, and there was made whole one, one because of unity: whatsoever other man went down unto that same moving was not made whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:223
verses.text: How then was there commended the unity of the Body crying from the ends of the earth? Another man was not healed, except again the pool were moved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:224
verses.text: The moving of the pool then did signify the perturbation of the people of the Jews when the Lord Jesus Christ came.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:225
verses.text: For at the coming of an Angel the water in the pool was perceived to be moved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:226
verses.text: The water then encircled with five porches was the Jewish nation encircled by the Law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:227
verses.text: And in the porches the sick lay, and in the water alone when troubled and moved they were healed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:228
verses.text: The Lord came, troubled was the water; He was crucified, may He come down in order that the sick man may be made whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:229
verses.text: What is, may He come down? May He humble Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:230
verses.text: Therefore whosoever ye be that love the letter without grace, in the porches ye will remain, sick ye will be, lying ill, not growing well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:231
verses.text: For the same figure also it is that Eliseus at first sent a staff by his servant to raise up the dead child.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:232
verses.text: There had died the son of a widow his hostess; it was reported to him, to his servant he gave his staff: go thou, he saith, lay it on the dead child.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:233
verses.text: Did the prophet not know what he was doing? The servant went before, he laid the staff upon the dead, the dead arose not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:234
verses.text: "For if there had been given a law which could have made alive, surely out of the law there had been righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:235
verses.text: The law sent by the servant made not alive: and yet he sent his staff by the servant, who himself afterwards followed, and made alive For when that infant arose not, Eliseus came himself, now bearing the type of the Lord, who had sent before his servant with the staff, as though with the Law: he came to the child that was lying dead, he laid his limbs upon it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:236
verses.text: The one was an infant, the other a grown man: he contracted and shortened in a manner the size of his full growth, in order that he might fit the dead child.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:237
verses.text: The dead then arose, when he being alive adapted himself to the dead: and the Master did that which the staff did not; and grace did that which the letter did not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:238
verses.text: They then that have remained in the staff, glory in the letter; and therefore are not made alive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:239
verses.text: But I will to glory concerning Thy grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:240
verses.text: In that same grace I glorying "literature have not known:" that is, men on the letter relying, and from grace recoiling, with whole heart I have rejected.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:241
verses.text: With reason there followeth, "I will enter into the power of the Lord:" not mine own, but the Lord's.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:242
verses.text: For they gloried in their own power of the letter, therefore grace joined to the letter they knew not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:243
verses.text: But because "the letter killeth, but the Spirit maketh alive:" "I have not known literature, and I will enter into the power of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:244
verses.text: Therefore this verse following doth strengthen and perfect the sense, so as to fix it in the hearts of men, and not suffer any other interpretation to steal in from any quarter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:245
verses.text: "O Lord, I will be mindful of Thy righteousness alone".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:246
verses.text: Ah! "alone".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:247
verses.text: Why hath he added "alone," I ask you? It would suffice to say, "I will be mindful of Thy righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:248
verses.text: "alone," he saith, entirely: there of mine own I think not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:249
verses.text: "For what hast thou which thou hast not received? But if also thou hast received, why dost thou glory as if thou hast not received".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:250
verses.text: Thy righteousness alone doth deliver me, what is mine own alone is nought but sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:251
verses.text: May I not glory then of my own strength, may I not remain in the letter; may I reject "literature," that is, men glorying of the letter, and on their own strength perversely, like men frantic, relying: may I reject such men, may I enter into the power of the Lord, so that when I am weak, then I may be mighty; in order that Thou in me mayest be mighty, for, "I will be mindful of Thy righteousness alone".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:252
verses.text: "O God, Thou hast taught me from my youth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:253
verses.text: What hast thou taught me? That of Thy righteousness alone I ought to be mindful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:254
verses.text: For reviewing my past life, I see what was owing to me, and what I have received instead of that which was owing to me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:255
verses.text: There was owing punishment, there hath been paid grace: there was owing hell, there hath been given life eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:256
verses.text: "O God, Thou hast taught me from my youth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:257
verses.text: From the very beginning of my faith, wherewith Thou hast renewed me, Thou didst teach me that nothing had preceded in me, whence I might say that there was owing to me what Thou hast given.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:258
verses.text: For who is turned to God save from iniquity? Who is redeemed save from captivity? But who can say that unjust was his captivity, when he forsook his Captain and fell off to the deserter? God is for our Captain, the devil a deserter: the Captain gave a commandment, the deserter suggested guile: where were thine ears between precept and deceit? was the devil better than God? Better he that revolted than He that made thee? Thou didst believe what the devil promised, and didst find what God threatened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:259
verses.text: Now then out of captivity being delivered, still however in hope, not yet in substance, walking by faith, not yet by sight, "O God," he saith, "Thou hast taught me from my youth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:260
verses.text: From the time that I have been turned to Thee, renewed by Thee who had been made by Thee, re-created who had been created, re-formed who had been formed: from the time that I have been converted, I have learned that no merits of mine have preceded, but that Thy grace hath come to me gratis, in order that I might be mindful of Thy righteousness alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:261
verses.text: What next after youth? For, "Thou hast taught me," he saith, "from my youth:" what after youth? For in that same first conversion of thine thou didst learn, how before conversion thou wast not just, but iniquity preceded, in order that iniquity being banished, there might succeed love: and having been renewed into a new man, only in hope, not yet in substance, thou didst learn how nothing of thy good had preceded, and by the grace of God thou wast converted to God: now perchance since the time that thou hast been converted wilt thou have anything of thine own, and on thy own strength oughtest thou to rely? Just as men are wont to say, now leave me, it was necessary for thee to show me the way; it is sufficient, I will walk in the way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:262
verses.text: And he that hath shown thee the way, "wilt thou not that I conduct thee to the place?" But thou, if thou art conceited, "let me alone, it is enough, I will walk in the way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:263
verses.text: Thou art left, and through thy weakness again thou wilt lose the way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:264
verses.text: Good were it for thee that He should have conducted thee, who first put thee in the way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:265
verses.text: But unless He too lead thee, again also thou wilt stray: say to Him then, "Conduct me, O Lord, in Thy way, and I will walk in Thy truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:266
verses.text: But thy having entered on the way, is youth, the very renewal and beginning of the faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:267
verses.text: For before thou wast walking through thy own ways a vagabond; straying through woody places, through rough places, torn in all thy limbs, thou wast seeking a home, that is, a sort of settlement of thy spirit, where thou mightest say, it is well; and being in security mightest say it, at rest from every uneasiness, from every trial, in a word from every captivity; and thou didst not find.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:268
verses.text: What shall I say? Came there to thee one to show thee the way? There came to thee the Way itself, and thou wast set therein by no merits of thine preceding, for evidently thou wast straying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:269
verses.text: What, since the time that thou hast set foot therein dost thou now direct thyself? Doth He that hath taught thee the way now leave thee? No, he saith: "Thou hast taught me from my youth; and even until now I will tell forth Thy wonderful works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:270
verses.text: For a wonderful thing is that which still Thou doest; namely, that Thou dost direct me, who in the way hast put me: and these are Thy wonderful works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:271
verses.text: What dost thou think to be the wonderful works of God? What is more wonderful among God's wonderful works, than the raising the dead? But am I by any means dead, thou sayest? Unless dead thou hadst been, there would not have been said to thee, "Rise, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall enlighten thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:272
verses.text: Dead are all unbelievers, all unrighteous men; in body they live, but in heart they are extinct.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:273
verses.text: But he that raiseth a man dead according to the body, doth bring him back to see this light and to breathe this air: but he that raiseth is not himself light and air to him; he beginneth to see, as he saw before.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:274
verses.text: A soul is not so resuscitated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:275
verses.text: For a soul is resuscitated by God; though even a body is resuscitated by God: but God, when He doth resuscitate a body, to the world doth bring it back: when He doth resuscitate a soul, to Himself He bringeth it back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:276
verses.text: If the air of this world be withdrawn, there dieth body: if God be withdrawn, there dieth soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:277
verses.text: When then God doth resuscitate a soul, unless there be with her He that hath resuscitated, she being resuscitated liveth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:278
verses.text: For He doth not resuscitate, and then leave her to live to herself: in the same manner as Lazarus, when he was resuscitated after being four days dead, was resuscitated by the Lord's corporal presence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:279
verses.text: The Lord withdrew from that same city or from that spot, did Lazarus cease to live? Not so is the soul resuscitated: God doth resuscitate her, she dieth if God shall have withdrawn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:280
verses.text: For I will speak boldly, brethren, but yet the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:281
verses.text: Two lives there are, one of the body, another of the soul: as the life of the body is the soul, so the life of the soul is God: in like manner as, if the soul forsake, the body dieth: so the soul dieth, if God forsake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:282
verses.text: This then is His grace, namely, that He resuscitate and be with us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:283
verses.text: Because then He doth resuscitate us from our past death, and doth renew in a manner our life, we say to Him, "O God, Thou hast taught me from my youth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:284
verses.text: But because He doth not withdraw from those whom He resuscitateth, lest when He shall have withdrawn from them they die, we say to Him, "and even until now I will tell forth Thy wonderful works:" because while Thou art with me I live, and of my soul Thou art the life, which will die if she be left to herself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:285
verses.text: Therefore while my life is present, that is, my God, "even until now," what next?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:286
verses.text: "And even unto oldness and old age".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:287
verses.text: These are two terms for old age, and are distinguished by the Greeks.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:288
verses.text: For the gravity succeeding youth hath another name among the Greeks, and after that same gravity the last age coming on hath another name; for πρεσβύτης signifieth grave, and γ™ρων old.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:289
verses.text: But because in the Latin language the distinction of these two terms holdeth not, both words implying old age are inserted, oldness and old age: but ye know them to be two ages.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:290
verses.text: "Thou hast taught me Thy grace from my youth; and even until now;" after my youth, "I will tell forth Thy wonderful works," because Thou art with me in order that I may not die, who hast come in order that I may rise: "and even unto oldness and old age," that is, even unto my last breath, unless with me Thou shalt have been, there will not be any merit of mine; may Thy grace alway remain with me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:291
verses.text: Even one man would say this, thou, he, I; but because this voice is that of a certain great Man, that is, of the Unity itself, for it is the voice of the Church; let us investigate the youth of the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:292
verses.text: When Christ came, He was crucified, dead, rose again, called the Gentiles, they began to be converted, became Martyrs strong in Christ, there was shed faithful blood, there arose a harvest for the Church: this is Her youth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:293
verses.text: But seasons advancing let the Church confess, let Her say, "Even until now I will tell forth Thy wonderful works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:294
verses.text: Not only in youth, when Paul, when Peter, when the first Apostles told: even in advancing age I myself, that is, Thy Unity, Thy members, Thy Body, "will tell forth Thy marvellous works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:295
verses.text: What then? "And even unto oldness and old age," I will tell forth Thy wonderful works: even until the end of the world here shall be the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:296
verses.text: For if She were not to be here even unto the end of the world; to whom did the Lord say, "Behold, I am with you always, even unto the consummation of the world"? Why was it necessary that these things should be spoken in the Scriptures? Because there were to be enemies of the Christian Faith who would say, "for a short time are the Christians, hereafter they shall perish, and there shall come back idols, there shall come back that which was before.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:297
verses.text: How long shall be the Christians?" "Even unto oldness and old age:" that is, even unto the end of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:298
verses.text: When thou, miserable unbeliever, dost expect Christians to pass away, thou art passing away thyself without Christians: and Christians even unto the end of the world shall endure; and as for thee with thine unbelief when thou shalt have ended thy short life, with what face wilt thou come forth to the Judge, whom while thou wast living thou didst blaspheme? Therefore "from my youth, and even until now, and even unto oldness and old age, O Lord, forsake not me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:299
verses.text: It will not be, as mine enemies say, even for a time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:300
verses.text: "Forsake not me, until I tell forth Thine arm to every generation that is yet to come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:301
verses.text: And the Arm of the Lord hath been revealed to whom? The Arm of the Lord is Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:302
verses.text: Do not Thou then forsake me: let not them rejoice that say, "only for a set time the Christians are".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:303
verses.text: May there be persons to tell forth Thine arm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:304
verses.text: To whom? "To every generation that is yet to come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:305
verses.text: If then it be to every generation that is yet to come, it will be even unto the end of the world: for when the world is ended, no longer any generation will come on.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:306
verses.text: "Thy power and Thy righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:307
verses.text: That is, that I may tell forth to every generation that is yet to come, Thine arm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:308
verses.text: And what hath Thine arm effected? This then let me tell forth, that same grace to every generation succeeding: let me say to every man that is to be born, nothing thou art by thyself, on God call thou, thine own are sins, merits are God's: punishment to thee is owing, and when reward shall have come, His own gifts He will crown, not thy merits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:309
verses.text: Let me say to every generation that is to come, out of captivity thou hast come, unto Adam thou didst belong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:310
verses.text: Let me say this to every generation that is to come, that there is no strength of mine, no righteousness of mine; but "Thy strength and Thy righteousness, O God, even unto the most high mighty works which Thou hast made".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:311
verses.text: "Thy power and Thy righteousness," as far as what? even unto flesh and blood? Nay, "even unto the most high mighty works which Thou hast made".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:312
verses.text: For the high places are the heavens, in the high places are the Angels, Thrones, Dominions, Principalities, Powers: to Thee they owe it that they are; to Thee they owe it that they live, to Thee they owe it that righteously they live, to Thee they owe it that blessedly they live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:313
verses.text: "Thy power and Thy righteousness," as far as what? "Even unto the most high mighty works which Thou hast made".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:314
verses.text: Think not that man alone belongeth to the grace of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:315
verses.text: What was Angel before he was made? What is Angel, if He forsake him who hath created? Therefore "Thy power and Thy justice even unto the most high mighty works which Thou hast made".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:316
verses.text: And man exalteth himself: and in order that he may belong to the first captivity, he heareth the serpent suggesting, "Taste, and ye shall be as Gods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:317
verses.text: Men as Gods? "O God, who is like unto Thee?" Not any in the pit, not in Hell, not in earth, not in Heaven, for all things Thou hast made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:318
verses.text: Why doth the work strive with the Maker? "O God, who is like unto Thee?" But as for me, saith miserable Adam, and Adam is every man, while I perversely will to be like unto Thee, behold what I have become, so that from captivity to Thee I cry out: I with whom it was well under a good king, have been made captive under my seducer; and cry out to Thee, because I have fallen from Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:319
verses.text: And whence have I fallen from Thee? While I perversely seek to be like unto Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:320
verses.text: Ill straying, ill presuming, doomed to die by withdrawing from the path of righteousness: behold he breaketh the commandment, he hath shaken off from his neck the yoke of discipline, uplifted with high spirit he hath broken in sunder the reins of guidance: where is he now? Truly captive he crieth, "O Lord, who is like unto Thee?" I perversely willed to be like unto Thee, and I have been made like unto a beast! Under Thy dominion, under Thy commandment, I was indeed like: "But a man in honour set hath not perceived, he hath been compared to beasts without sense, and hath been made like unto them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:321
verses.text: Now out of the likeness of beasts cry though late and say, "O God, who is like unto Thee?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:322
verses.text: "How great troubles hast Thou shown to me, many and evil!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:323
verses.text: Deservedly, proud servant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:324
verses.text: For thou hast willed perversely to be like thy God, who hadst been made after the image of thy Lord Wouldest thou have it to be well with thee, when withdrawing from that good? Truly God saith to thee, if thou withdrawest from Me, and it is well with thee, I am not thy good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:325
verses.text: Again, if He is good, and in the highest degree good, and of Himself to Himself good, and by no foreign good thing good, and is Himself our chief good; by withdrawing from Him, what wilt thou be but evil? Also if He is Himself our blessedness, what will there be to one withdrawing from Him, except misery? Return thou then after misery, and say, "O Lord, who is like unto Thee? How great troubles hast Thou shown to me, many and evil!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:326
verses.text: But this was discipline; admonition, not desertion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:327
verses.text: Lastly, giving thanks, he saith what? "And being turned Thou hast made me alive, and from the bottomless places of the earth again Thou hast brought me back".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:328
verses.text: But when before? What is this "again"? Thou hast fallen from a high place, O man, disobedient slave, O thou proud against thy Lord, thou hast fallen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:329
verses.text: There hast come to pass in thee, "every one that exalteth himself shall be humbled:" may there come to pass in thee, "every one that humbleth himself shall be exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:330
verses.text: Return thou from the deep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:331
verses.text: I return, he saith, I return, I acknowledge; "O God, who is like unto Thee? How great troubles hast Thou shown to me, many and evil! and being turned Thou hast made me alive, and from the bottomless places of the earth again Thou hast brought me back".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:332
verses.text: "We perceive," I hear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:333
verses.text: Thou hast brought us back from the bottomless places of the earth, hast brought us back from the depth and drowning of sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:334
verses.text: But why "aga in"? When had it already been done? Let us go on, if perchance the latter parts of the Psalm itself do not explain to us the thing which here we do not yet perceive, namely, why he hath said "again".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:335
verses.text: Therefore let us hear: "How great troubles Thou hast shown to me, many and evil! And being turned Thou hast made me alive, and from the bottomless places of the earth again Thou hast brought me back".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:336
verses.text: What then? "Thou hast multiplied Thy righteousness, and being turned Thou hast comforted me, and from the bottomless places of the earth again Thou hast brought me back".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:337
verses.text: Behold a second "again"! If we labour to unravel this "again" when written once, who will be able to unravel it when doubled? Now "again" itself is a redoubling, and once more there is written "again".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:338
verses.text: May He be with us from whom is grace, may there be with us the arm also which we are telling forth to every generation that is to come: may He be with us Himself, and as with the key of His Cross open to us the mystery that is locked up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:339
verses.text: For it was not to no purpose that when He was crucified the veil of the temple was rent in the midst, but to show that through His Passion the secret things of all mysteries were opened May He then Himself be with men passing over unto Him, be the veil taken away: may our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ tell us why such a voice of the Prophet hath been sent before, "Thou hast shown to me troubles many and evil: and being turned Thou hast made me alive, and from the bottomless places of the earth again Thou hast brought me back".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:340
verses.text: Behold this is the first "again" which hath been written.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:341
verses.text: Let us see what this is, and we shall see why there is a second "again".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:342
verses.text: Therein Christ died, wherein thou art to die: and therein Christ rose again, wherein thou art to rise again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:343
verses.text: By His example He taught thee what thou shouldest not fear, for what thou shouldest hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:344
verses.text: Thou didst fear death, He died: thou didst despair of rising again, He rose again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:345
verses.text: But thou sayest to me, He rose again, do I by any means rise again? But He rose again in that which for thee He received of thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:346
verses.text: Therefore thy nature in Him hath preceded thee; and that which was taken of thee, hath gone up before thee: therein therefore thou also hast ascended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:347
verses.text: Therefore He ascended first, and we in Him: because that flesh is of the human race.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:348
verses.text: Behold one "again".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:349
verses.text: Hear of its being fulfilled from the Apostle: "If then ye have risen with Christ, the things which are above seek ye, where Christ is sitting on the right hand of God; the things which are above mind ye, not the things which are upon the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:350
verses.text: He then hath gone before: already we also have risen again, but still in hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:351
verses.text: Hear the Apostle Paul saying this same thing: "Even we ourselves groan in ourselves, looking for the adoption, the redemption of our body".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:352
verses.text: What is it then that Christ hath granted to thee? Hear that which followeth: "For by hope we are saved: but hope which is seen is not hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:353
verses.text: For that which a man seeth, why doth he hope for? But if that which we see not we hope for, through patience we wait for it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:354
verses.text: We have been brought back therefore again from the bottomless places in hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:355
verses.text: Why again? Because already Christ had gone before.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:356
verses.text: But because we shall rise again in substance, for now in hope we are living, now after faith we are walking; we have been brought back from the bottomless places of the earth, by believing in Him who before us hath risen again from the bottomless place of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:357
verses.text: Thou hast heard one "again," thou hast heard the other: "again;" one "again" because of Christ going before; and the other, yet however in hope, and a thing which remaineth to be in substance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:358
verses.text: "Thou hast multiplied Thy righteousness," already in me believing, already in those that first have risen again in hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:359
verses.text: "Thou hast multiplied Thy righteousness, and being turned Thou hast comforted me:" and because of the body to rise again at the end, even from the bottomless places of the earth again Thou hast brought me back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:360
verses.text: "For I will confess to Thee in the vessels of a Psalm Thy truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:361
verses.text: The vessels of a Psalm are a Psaltery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:362
verses.text: But what is a Psaltery? An instrument of wood and strings What doth it signify? There is some difference between it and a harp:there seemeth to be signified by the Psaltery the Spirit, by the harp the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:363
verses.text: And because he had spoken of two bringings back of ours from the bottomless places of the earth, one after the Spirit in hope, the other after the bo dy in substance; hear thou of these two: "For I will confess to Thee in the vessels of a Psalm Thy truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:364
verses.text: This after the Spirit: concerning the body what? "I will psalm to Thee on a harp, Holy One of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:365
verses.text: Again hear this because of that same "again" and "again".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:366
verses.text: "My lips shall exult when I shall psalm to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:367
verses.text: Because lips are wont to be spoken of both belonging to the inner and to the outward man, it is uncertain in what sense lips have been used: there followeth therefore, "And my soul which Thou hast redeemed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:368
verses.text: Therefore regarding the inward lips having been saved in hope, brought back from the bottomless places of the earth in faith and love, still however waiting for the redemption of our body, we say what? Already he hath said, "And my soul which Thou hast redeemed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:369
verses.text: But lest thou shouldest think the soul alone redeemed, wherein now thou hast heard one "again," "but still," he saith; why still? "but still my tongue also:" therefore now the tongue of the body: "all day long shall meditate of Thy righteousness" : that is, in eternity without end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:370
verses.text: But when shall this be? Hereafter at the end of the world, at the resurrection of the body and the changing into the Angelic state.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:371
verses.text: Whence is it proved that this is spoken of the end, "but still my tongue also all day long shall meditate of Thy righteousness"? "When they shall have been confounded and shall have blushed, that seek evil things for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:372
verses.text: When shall they be confounded, when shall they blush, save at the end of the world? For in two ways they shall be confounded, either when they shall believe in Christ, or when Christ shall have come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:373
verses.text: For so long as the Church is here, so long as grain groaneth amid chaff, so long as wheat groaneth amid tares, so long as vessels of mercy groan amid vessels of wrath made for dishonour, so long as lily groaneth amid thorns, there will not be wanting enemies to say, "When shall he die, and his name perish?" "Behold there shall come the time when Christians shall be ended and shall be no more: as they began at a set time, so even unto a particular time they shall be".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 72:374
verses.text: But while they are saying these things and without end are dying, and while the Church is continuing preaching the Arm of the Lord to every generation that is to come; there shall come Himself also at last in His glory, there shall rise again all the dead, each with his cause: there shall be severed good men to the right hand, but evil men to the left, and they shall be confounded that did insult, they shall blush that did mock: and so my tongue after resurrection shall meditate of Thy righteousness, all day long of Thy praise, "when they shall have been confounded and shall have blushed, that seek evil things for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:2
verses.text: "For Salomon" indeed this Psalm's title is fore-noted: but things are spoken of therein which could not apply to that Salomon king of Israel after the flesh, according to those things which holy Scripture speaketh concerning him: but they can most pertinently apply to the Lord Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:3
verses.text: Whence it is perceived, that the very word Salomon is used in a figurative sense, so that in him Christ is to be taken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:4
verses.text: For Salomon is interpreted peace-maker: and on this account such a word to Him most truly and excellently doth apply, through Whom, the Mediator, having received remission of sins, we that were enemies are reconciled to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:5
verses.text: For "when we were enemies we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:6
verses.text: The Same is Himself that Peace-maker.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:7
verses.text: Since then we hav e found out the true Salomon, that is, the true Peace-maker: next let us observe what the Psalm doth teach concerning Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:8
verses.text: "O God, Thy judgment to the King give Thou, and Thy justice to the King's Son".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:9
verses.text: The Lord Himself in the Gospel saith, "The Father judgeth not any one, but all judgment He hath given to the Son:" this is then, "O God, Thy judgment to the King give Thou".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:10
verses.text: He that is King is also the Son of the King: because God the Father also is certainly King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:11
verses.text: Thus it hath been written, that the King made a marriage for His Son But after the manner of Scripture the same thing is repeated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:12
verses.text: For that which he hath said in, "Thy judgment;" the same he hath otherwise expressed in, "Thy justice:" and that which he hath said in, "the King," the same he hath otherwise expressed in, "to the King's Son".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:13
verses.text: But these repetitions do much commend the divine sayings, whether the same words, or whether in other words the same sense be repeated: and they are mostly found in the Psalms, and in the kind of discourse whereby the mind's affection is to be awakened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:14
verses.text: Next there followeth, "To judge Thy people in justice, and Thy poor in judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:15
verses.text: For what purpose the royal Father gave to the royal Son His judgment and His justice is sufficiently shown when he saith, "To judge Thy people in justice;" that is, for the purpose of judging Thy people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:16
verses.text: Such an idiom is found in Salomon: "The Proverbs of Salomon, son of David, to know wisdom and discipline:"  that is, the Proverbs of Salomon, for the purpose of knowing wisdom and discipline.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:17
verses.text: So, "Thy judgment give Thou, to judge Thy people:" that is, "Thy judgment" give Thou for the purpose of judging Thy people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:18
verses.text: But that which he saith before in, "Thy people," the same he saith afterwards in, "Thy poor:" and that which he saith before in, "in justice;" the same afterward in, "in judgment:" according to that manner of repetition.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:19
verses.text: Whereby indeed he showeth, that the people of God ought to be poor, that is, not proud, but humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:20
verses.text: For, "blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:21
verses.text: In which poverty even blessed Job was poor even before he had lost those great earthly riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:22
verses.text: Which thing for this reason I thought should be mentioned, because there are certain persons who are more ready to distribute all their goods to the poor, than themselves to become the poor of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:23
verses.text: For they are puffed up with boasting wherein they think their living well should be ascribed to themselves, not to the grace of God: and therefore now they do not even live well, however great the good works which they seem to do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:24
verses.text: But seeing that he hath changed the order of the words (though he had first said, "O God, Thy judgment to the King give Thou, and Thy justice to the King's Son," putting judgment first, then justice), and hath put justice first, then judgment, saying, "To judge Thy people in justice, and Thy poor in judgment:" he doth more clearly show that he hath called judgment justice, proving that there is no difference made by the order in which the word is placed, because it signifieth the same thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:25
verses.text: For it is usual to say "wrong judgment" of that which is unjust: but justice iniquitous or unjust we are not wont to speak of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:26
verses.text: For if wrong and unjust it be; no longer must it be called justice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:27
verses.text: Again, by putting down judgment and repeating it under the name of justice, or by putting down justice and repeating it under the name of judgment, he clearly showeth that he specially nameth that judgment which is wont to be put instead of justice, that is, that which cannot be understood of giving an evil judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:28
verses.text: For in the place where He saith, "Judge not according to persons, but right judgment judge ye;" He showeth that there may be a wrong judgment, when He saith, "right judgment judge ye:" lastly, the one He doth forbid, the other He doth enjoin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:29
verses.text: But when without any addition He speaketh of judgment, He would at once have just judgment to be understood: as is that which He saith, "Ye forsake the weightier matters of the Law, mercy and judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:30
verses.text: That also which Jeremiah saith is, "making his riches not with judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:31
verses.text: He saith not, making his riches by wrong or unjust judgment, or not with judgment right or just, but not with judgment: calling not anything judgment but what is right and just.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:32
verses.text: "Let the mountains bear peace to the people, and the hills justice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:33
verses.text: The mou ntains are the greater, the hills the less.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:34
verses.text: These are without doubt those which another Psalm hath, "little with great".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:35
verses.text: For those mountains did exult like rams, and those hills like lambs of the sheep, at the departure of Israel out of Egypt, that is, at the deliverance of the people of God from this world's servitude.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:36
verses.text: Those then that are eminent in the Church for passing sanctity, are the mountains, who are meet to teach other men also, by so speaking as that they may be faithfully taught, by so living as that they may imitate them to their profit: but the hills are they that follow the excellence of the former by their own obedience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:37
verses.text: Why then "the mountains peace: and the hills justice"? Would there perchance have been no difference, even if it had been said thus, Let the mountains bear justice to the people and the hills peace? For to both justice, and to both peace is necessary: and it may be that under another name justice herself may have been called peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:38
verses.text: For this is true peace, not such as unjust men make among them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:39
verses.text: Or rather with a distinction not to be overlooked must that be understood which he saith, "the mountains peace, and the hills justice"? For men excelling in the Church ought to counsel for peace with watchful care; lest for the sake of their own distinctions by acting proudly they make schisms and dissever the bond of union.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:40
