verses.text: But let the hills so follow them by imitation and obedience, that they prefer Christ to them: lest being led astray by the empty authority of evil mountains (for they seem to excel), they tear themselves away from the Unity of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:41
verses.text: Thus also most pertinently may be understood, "let the mountains bear peace to the people," namely, that we understand the peace to consist in the reconciliation whereby we are reconciled to God: for the mountains receive this for His people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:42
verses.text: "Let the mountains, therefore, receive peace for the people, and the hills justice:" so that in this manner, both being at one, there may come to pass that which hath been written, "justice and peace have kissed one another".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:43
verses.text: But that which other copies have, "let the mountains receive peace for the people, and let the hills:" I think must be understood of all sorts of preaching of Gospel peace, whether those that go before, or those that follow after.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:44
verses.text: But in these copies this followeth, "in justice He shall judge the poor of the people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:45
verses.text: But those copies are more approved of which have that which we have expounded above, "let the mountains bear peace to the people, and the hills justice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:46
verses.text: But some have, "to Thy people;" some have not to "Thy," but only "to the people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:47
verses.text: "He shall judge the poor of the people, and shall save the sons of the poor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:48
verses.text: The poor and the sons of the poor seem to me to be the very same, as the same city is Sion and the daughter of Sion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:49
verses.text: But if it is to be understood with a distinction, the poor we take to be the mountains, but the sons of the poor the hills: for instance, Prophets and Apostles, the poor, but the sons of them, that is, those that profit under their authority, the sons of the poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:50
verses.text: But that which hath been said above, "shall judge;" and afterwards, "shall save;" is as it were a sort of exposition in what manner He shall judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:51
verses.text: For to this end He shall judge, that He may save, that is, may sever from those that are to be destroyed and condemned, those to whom He giveth "salvation ready to be revealed at the" last time For by such men to Him is said, "Destroy not with ungodly men my soul:" and, "Judge Thou me, O God, and sever my cause from the nation unholy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:52
verses.text: We must observe also that he saith not, He shall judge the poor people, but, "the poor of the people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:53
verses.text: For above when he had said, "to judge Thy people in justice and Thy poor in judgment," the same he called the people of God as His poor, that is, only the good and those that belong to the right hand side.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:54
verses.text: But because in this world those for the right and those for the left feed together, who, like lambs and goats at the last are to be put asunder; the whole, as it is mingled together, he hath called by the name of the People.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:55
verses.text: And because even here he putteth judgment in a good sense, that is, for the purpose of saving: therefore he saith, "He shall judge the poor of the people," that is, shall sever for salvation those that are poor among the people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:56
verses.text: "And He shall humble the false-accuser".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:57
verses.text: No false-accuser can be more suitably recognised here than the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:58
verses.text: False accusation is his business.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:59
verses.text: "Doth Job worship God gratis?" But the Lord Jesus doth humble him, by His grace aiding His own, in order that they may worship God gratis, that is, may take delight in the Lord He humbled him also thus; because when in Him the devil, that is, the prince of this world, had found nothing, he slew Him by the false accusations of the Jews, whom the false-accuser made use of as his vessels, working in the sons of unbelief.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:60
verses.text: "And He shall endure to the sun," or, "shall endure with the sun".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:61
verses.text: For thus some of our writers have thought would be more exactly translated that which in the Greek is συμπαραμενεῖ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:62
verses.text: But if in Latin it could have been expressed in one word, it must have been expressed by compermanebit: however, because in Latin the word cannot be expressed, in order that the sense at least might be translated, it hath been expressed by, "He shall endure with the sun".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:63
verses.text: For He shall co-endure to the sun is nothing else but, "He shall endure with the sun".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:64
verses.text: But what great matter is it for Him to endure with the sun, through whom all things were made, and without whom nothing was made, save that this prophecy hath been sent before for the sake of those who think that the religion of the Christian name up to a particular time in this world will live, and afterwards will be no more? "He shall endure" therefore "with the sun," so long as the sun riseth and setteth, that is, so long as these times revolve, there shall not be wanting the Church of God, that is, Christ's body on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:65
verses.text: But that which he addeth, "and before the moon, generations of generations:" he might have expressed by, and before the sun, that is, both with the sun and before the sun: which would have been understood by both with times and before times.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:66
verses.text: That then which goeth before time is eternal: and that is truly to be held eternal which by no time is changed, as, "in the beginning was the Word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:67
verses.text: But by the moon he hath chosen rather to intimate the waxings and wanings of things mortal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:68
verses.text: Lastly, when he had said, "before the moon," wishing in a manner to explain for what purpose he inserted the moon, "generations," he saith, "of generations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:69
verses.text: As though he were saying, before the moon, that is, before the generations of generations which pass away in the departure and succession of things mortal, like the lunar wanings and waxings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:70
verses.text: And thus what is better to be understood by His enduring before the moon, than that He taketh precedence of all mortal things by immortality? Which also as followeth may not impertinently be taken, that whereas now, having humbled the false-accuser, He sitteth at the right hand of the Father, this is to endure with the sun.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:71
verses.text: For the brightness of the eternal glory is understood to be the Son: as though the Sun were the Father, and the Brightness of Him His Son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:72
verses.text: But as these things may be spoken of the invisible Substance of the Creator, not as of that visible creation wherein are bodies celestial, of which bright bodies the sun hath the pre-eminence, from which this similitude hath been drawn: just as they are drawn even from things earthly, to wit, stone, lion, lamb, man having two sons, and the like: therefore having humbled the false-accuser, He endureth with the sun: because having vanquished the devil by the Resurrection, He sitteth at the right hand of the Father, where He dieth no more, and death no longer over Him shall have dominion This too is before the moon, as though the First-born from the dead were going before the Church, which is passing on in the departure and succession of mortals.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:73
verses.text: These are "the generations of generations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:74
verses.text: Or perchance it is because generations are those whereby we are begotten mortally; but generations of generations those whereby we are begotten again immortally.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:75
verses.text: And such is the Church which He went before, in order that He might endure before the moon, being the First-born of the dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:76
verses.text: To be sure, that which is in the Greek γενεας γενεῶν, some have interpreted, not "generations," but, "of a generation of generations:" because γενεας is of ambiguous case in Greek, and whether it be the genitive singular της γενε‚ς, that is, of the generation, or the accusative plural τὰς γενεὰς, that is, the generations, doth not clearly appear, except that deservedly that sense hath been preferred wherein, as though explaining what he had called "the moon," he added in continuation, "generations of generations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:77
verses.text: "And He shall come down like rain into a fleece, and like drops distilling upon the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:78
verses.text: He hath called to our minds and admonished us, that what was done by Gedeon the Judge, in Christ hath its end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:79
verses.text: For he asked a sign of the Lord, that a fleece laid on the floor should alone be rained upon, and the floor should be dry; and again, the fleece alone should be dry, and the floor should be rained upon; and so it came to pass Which thing signified, that, being as it were on a floor in the midst of the whole round world, the dry fleece was the former people Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:80
verses.text: The same Christ therefore Himself came down like rain upon a fleece, when yet the floor was dry: whence also He said, "I am not sent but to the sheep which were lost of the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:81
verses.text: There He chose out a Mother by whom to receive the form of a servant, wherein He was to appear to men: there the disciples, to whom He gave this same injunction, saying, "Into the way of the nations go ye not away, and into the cities of the Samaritans enter ye not: go ye first to the sheep which are lost of the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:82
verses.text: When He saith, go ye first to them, He showeth also that hereafter, when at length the floor was to be rained upon, they would go to other sheep also, which were not of the old people Israel, concerning whom He saith, "I have other sheep which are not of this fold, it behoveth Me to bring in them also, that there may be one flock and one Shepherd".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:83
verses.text: Hence also the Apostle: "for I say," he saith, "that Christ was a minister of the Circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promises of the fathers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:84
verses.text: Thus rain came down upon the fleece, the floor being yet dry.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:85
verses.text: But inasmuch as he continueth, "but that the nations should glorify God for His mercy:" that when the time came on, that should be fulfilled which by the Prophet He saith, "a people whom I have not known hath served Me, in the hearkening of the ear it hath obeyed Me:" we now see, that of the grace of Christ the nation of the Jews hath remained dry, and the whole round world through all nations is being rained upon by clouds full of Christian grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:86
verses.text: For by another word he hath indicated the same rain, saying, "drops distilling:" no longer upon the fleece, but "upon the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:87
verses.text: For what else is rain but drops distilling? But that the above nation under the name of a fleece is signified, I think is either because they were to be stripped of the authority of teaching, just as a sheep is stripped of its skin; or because in a secret place He was hiding that same rain, which He willed not should be preached to uncircumcision, that is, be revealed to uncircumcised nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:88
verses.text: "There shall arise in His days justice and abundance of peace, until the moon be taken away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:89
verses.text: The expression tollatur some have interpreted by "be taken away," but others by "be exalted," translating one Greek word, which is there used, ‡νταναιρεθῇ, just as each of them thought good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:90
verses.text: But they who have said, "be removed," and they who have said, "be taken away," do not so very much differ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:91
verses.text: For by the expression, "be removed," custom doth teach us that there should be rather implied, that a thing is taken away and is no more, than that it is raised to a higher place: but "be taken away" can be understood in no other way at all, than that a thing is destroyed: that is, it is no more: but by "be exalted," only that it is raised to a higher place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:92
verses.text: Which indeed when it is put in a bad sense is wont to signify pride: as is the passage, "In thy wisdom be not exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:93
verses.text: But in a good sense it belongeth to a more exceeding honour, as, for instance, when anything is being raised; as is, "In the nights exalt ye your hands unto holy places, and bless ye the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:94
verses.text: Here then if we have understood the expression, "be removed," what will be, "until the moon be removed," but that it be so dealt with that it be no more? For perchance he willed this also to be perceived, that mortality is to be no longer, "when the last enemy shall be destroyed, death:" so that abundance of peace may be brought down so far as that nothing may withstand the felicity of the blessed from the infirmity of mortality: which will come to pass in that age, of which we have the faithful promise of God through Jesus Christ our Lord, concerning which it is said, "There shall arise in His days justice and abundance of peace:" until, death being utterly overcome and destroyed, all mortality be consumed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:95
verses.text: But if under the term moon, not the mortality of the flesh through which the Church is now passing, but the Church Herself in general hath been signified, which is to endure for everlasting, being delivered from this mortality, thus must be taken the expression, "There shall arise in His days justice and abundance of peace, until the moon be exalted;" as though it were said, There shall arise in His days justice, to conquer the contradiction and rebellion of the flesh, and whereby there may be made a peace so increasing and abundant, until the moon be exalted, that is, until the Church be lifted up, through the glory of the Resurrection to reign with Him, who went before Her in this glory, the first-born of the dead, that He might sit at the right hand of the Father; thus with the sun enduring before the moon, in the place whereunto hereafter was to be exalted the moon also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:96
verses.text: "And He shall be Lord from sea even unto sea, and from the river even unto the ends of the round world" : He to wit concerning whom he had said, "There shall arise in His days justice and abundance of peace, until the moon be exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:97
verses.text: If the Church here is properly signified under the term moon, in continuation he showed how widely that same Church He was going to spread abroad, when He added, "and He shall be Lord from sea even unto sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:98
verses.text: For the land is encircled by a great sea which is called the Ocean: from which there floweth in some small part in the midst of the lands, and maketh those seas known to us, which are frequented by ships.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:99
verses.text: Again, in "from sea even unto sea" He hath said, that from any one end of the earth even unto any other end, He would be Lord, whose name and power in the whole world were to be preached and to prevail exceedingly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:100
verses.text: To which, that there might not be understood in any other manner, "from sea even unto sea:" He immediately added, "and from the river even unto the ends of the round world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:101
verses.text: Therefore that which He saith in "even unto the ends of the round world," the same He had said before in "from sea even unto sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:102
verses.text: But in that which now He saith, "from the river," He hath evidently expressed that He willed Christ to publish at length His power from that place from whence also He began to choose His disciples, to wit from the river Jordan, where upon the Lord, on His baptism, when the Holy Ghost descended, there sounded a voice from Heaven, "This is My beloved Son".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:103
verses.text: From this place then His doctrine and the authority of the heavenly ministry setting out, is enlarged even unto the ends of the round world, when there is preached the Gospel of the kingdom in the whole world, for a testimony unto all nations: and then shall come the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:104
verses.text: "In His presence shall fall down the Ethiopians, and His enemies shall lick the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:105
verses.text: By the Ethiopians, as by a part the whole, He hath signified all nations, selecting that nation to mention especially by name, which is at the ends of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:106
verses.text: By "in His presence shall fall down" hath been signified, shall adore Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:107
verses.text: And because there were to be schisms in divers quarters of the world, which would be jealous of the Church Catholic spread abroad in the whole round world, and again those same schisms dividing themselves into the names of men, and by loving the men under whose authority they had been rent, opposing themselves to the glory of Christ which is throughout all lands; so when He had said, "in His presence shall fall down the Ethiopians," He added, "and His enemies shall lick the earth:" that is, shall love men, so that they shall be jealous of the glory of Christ, to whom hath been said, "Be Thou exalted above the Heavens, O God, and above all the earth Thy glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:108
verses.text: For man earned to hear, "Earth thou art, and unto earth thou shalt go".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:109
verses.text: By licking this earth, that is, being delighted with the vainly talking authority of such men, by loving them, and by counting them for the most pleasing of men, they gainsay the divine sayings, whereby the Catholic Church hath been foretold, not as to be in any particular quarter of the world, as certain schisms are, but in the whole universe by bearing fruit and growing so as to attain even unto the very Ethiopians, to wit, the remotest and foulest of mankind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:110
verses.text: "The kings of Tharsis and the isles shall offer gifts, the kings of the Arabians and of Saba shall lead presents".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:111
verses.text: This no longer requireth an expounder but a thinker; yea it doth thrust itself upon the sight not only of rejoicing believers, but also of groaning unbelievers—except perchance we must inquire why there hath been said, "shall lead presents".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:112
verses.text: For there are wont to be led those things which can walk.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:113
verses.text: For could it by any means have been spoken with reference to the sacrifice of victims? Far be it that such "righteousness" should arise in His days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:114
verses.text: But those gifts which have been foretold as to be led, seem to me to signify men, whom into the fellowship of the Church of Christ the authority of kings doth lead: although even persecuting kings have led gifts, knowing not what they did, in sacrificing the holy Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:115
verses.text: "And there shall adore Him all kings of the earth, all nations shall serve Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:116
verses.text: But while he is explaining the reasons why so great honour is paid Him by kings, and He is served of all nations: "because He hath delivered," he saith, "the needy man from the mighty, and the poor man, to whom was no helper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:117
verses.text: This needy and poor man is the people of men believing in Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:118
verses.text: In this people are also kings adoring Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:119
verses.text: For they do not disdain to be needy and poor, that is, humbly confessing sins, and needing the glory of God and the grace of God, in order that this King, Son of the King, may deliver them from the mighty one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:120
verses.text: For this same mighty one is he who above was called the Slanderer: whom mighty to subdue men to himself, and to hold them bound in captivity, not his virtue did make, but men's sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:121
verses.text: The same is himself also called strong; therefore here mighty also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:122
verses.text: But He that hath humbled the slanderer and hath entered into the house of the strong man to bind him and to spoil his vessels, He "hath delivered the needy and the poor man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:123
verses.text: For this neither the virtue of any one could accomplish, nor any just man, nor any Angel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:124
verses.text: When then there was no helper, by His coming He saved them Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:125
verses.text: But it might occur to one; if because of sins man was held by the devil, have sins pleased Christ, who saved the needy man from the mighty? Far be it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:126
verses.text: But "He it is that shall spare the helpless and poor man" : that is, shall remit sins to the man, humble and not trusting in his own merits, or hoping for salvation because of his own virtue, but needing the grace of his Saviour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:127
verses.text: But when he hath added, "and the souls of the poor He shall save:" he hath recommended to our notice both the aids of grace; both that which is for the remission of sins, when he saith, "He shall spare the poor and needy man;" and that which doth consist in the imparting of righteousness, when he hath added, "and the souls of the poor He shall save".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:128
verses.text: For no one is meet of himself for salvation (which salvation is perfect righteousness), unless God's grace aid: because the fulness of the law is nought but love, which doth not exist in us of ourselves, but is shed abroad in our hearts through the Holy Spirit which hath been given unto us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:129
verses.text: "From usuries and iniquity He shall redeem the souls of them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:130
verses.text: What are these usuries but sins, which are also called debts? But I think they have been called usuries, because more of ill is found in the punishments than hath been committed in the sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:131
verses.text: For, for example's sake, while a man-slayer killeth only the body of a man, but can no wise hurt the soul; of himself both soul and body is destroyed in hell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:132
verses.text: Because of such despisers of present commandment and deriders of future punishment hath been said, "I coming would have exacted with usuries," from these usuries are redeemed the souls of the poor by that blood which hath been shed for the remission of sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:133
verses.text: He shall redeem, I say, from usuries, by remitting sins which owed larger punishments: but He shall redeem from iniquity, by helping them by grace even to do righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:134
verses.text: Therefore the same two things have been repeated which were said above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:135
verses.text: For in that which is above, "He shall spare the helpless and poor man," there is understood "from usuries:" but in that which there he saith, "and the souls of the poor He shall save;" there seemeth to have been implied, "from iniquity:" so that the words "He shall redeem," are understood with both.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:136
verses.text: So when He shall spare the poor and helpless man, and shall save the souls of the poor: thus "from usuries and iniquity He shall redeem the souls of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:137
verses.text: And honourable shall be the name of Him in the presence of them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:138
verses.text: For they give honour to His name for so great benefits, and they respond that "meet and right it is" to render thanks to the Lord their God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:139
verses.text: Or, as some copies have it, "and honourable is the name of them in the presence of Him:" for even if Christians seem despicable to this world, the name of them in the presence of Him is honourable, who to them hath given it, no longer remembering those names in His lips, whereby before they used to be called, when they were bound fast by the superstitions of the Gentiles, or signed with names derived from their own evil deserts, before they were Christians, which name is honourable in the presence of Him, even if it seemeth despicable to enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:140
verses.text: "And He shall live, and there shall be given to Him of the gold of Arabia".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:141
verses.text: There would not have been said, "and He shall live" (for of whom could not this be said, though living for ever so brief a space of time on this earth?) unless that life were being recommended to our notice, wherein He "dieth no more, and death over Him shall have no more dominion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:142
verses.text: And thus, "and He shall live," that was despised in death: for, as another Prophet saith, "there shall be taken away from the earth the life of Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:143
verses.text: But what is, "and there shall be given to Him of the gold  of Arabia"? For the fact that from thence even the former Salomon received gold, in this Psalm hath been in a figure transferred unto another true Salomon, that is, the true Peace-maker.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:144
verses.text: For the former did not have dominion "from the river even unto the ends of the round world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:145
verses.text: Thus then hath been prophesied, that even the wise men of this world in Christ would believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:146
verses.text: But by Arabia we understand the Gentiles; by gold wisdom which doth as much excel among all doctrines as gold among metals.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:147
verses.text: Whence hath been written, "Receive ye prudence as silver, and wisdom as proved gold".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:148
verses.text: "And they shall pray concerning Himself alway".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:149
verses.text: That which the Greek hath, περὶ αὐτοῦ, some have interpreted by "concerning Himself," some "for Himself," or "for Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:150
verses.text: But what is, "concerning Himself," except perchance that for which we pray, saying, "Thy kingdom come"? For Christ's coming shall make present to believers the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:151
verses.text: But how to understand "for Him" is difficult; except that when prayer is made for the Church, for Himself prayer is made, because she is His Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:152
verses.text: For concerning Christ and the Church hath been sent before a great Sacrament, "there shall be two in one flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:153
verses.text: But now that which followeth, "all the day long," that is, in all time, "they shall bless Him," is sufficiently evident.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:154
verses.text: "And there shall be a firmament on the earth, on the tops of the mountains".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:155
verses.text: For, "all the promises of God in Him are Yea," that is, in Him are confirmed: because in Him hath been fulfilled whatever hath been prophesied for our salvation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:156
verses.text: For the tops of the mountains it is meet to understand as the authors of the divine Scriptures, that is, those persons through whom they were supplied: wherein He is indeed Himself the Firmament: for unto Him all things that have been divinely written are ascribed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:157
verses.text: But this He willed should be on earth; because for the sake of those that are upon earth, they were written.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:158
verses.text: Whence He came also Himself upon earth, in order that He might confirm all these things, that is, in Himself might show them to have been fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:159
verses.text: "For it was necessary," He saith, "for all things to be fulfilled which were written in the Law, and the Prophets, and Psalms, concerning Me:" that is, "in the tops of the mountain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:160
verses.text: For so there cometh in the last time the evident Mount of the Lord, prepared on the summit of the mountains: of which here he speaketh, "in the tops of the mountains".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:161
verses.text: "Highly superexalted above Libanus shall be His fruit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:162
verses.text: Libanus we are wont to take as this world's dignity: for Libanus is a mountain bearing tall trees, and the name itself is interpreted whiteness For what marvel, if above every brilliant state of this world there is superexalted the fruit of Christ, of which fruit the lovers have contemned all secular dignities? But if in a good sense we take Libanus, because of the "cedars of Libanus which He hath planted:" what other fruit must be understood, that is being exalted above this Libanus, except that whereof the Apostle speaketh when he is going to speak concerning that love of his, "yet a pre-eminent way to you I show"? For this is put forward even in the first rank of divine gifts, in the place where he saith, "but the fruit of the Spirit is love:" and with this are conjoined the remaining words as consequent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:163
verses.text: "And they shall flourish from the city like hay of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:164
verses.text: Because city is used ambiguously, and there is not annexed of Him, or of God, for there hath not been said, "from the city" of Him, or "from the city" of God, but only "from the city:" in a good sense it is understood, in order that from the city of God, that is, from the Church, they may flourish like grass; but grass bearing fruit, as is that of wheat: for even this is called grass in Holy Scripture; as in Genesis there is a command for the earth to bring forth every tree and every grass, and there is not added every wheat: which without doubt would not have been passed over unless under the name of grass this also were understood; and in many other passages of the Scriptures this is found.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:165
verses.text: But if we must take, "and they shall flourish like the grass of the earth," in the same manner as is said, "all flesh is grass, and the glory of a man like the flower of grass:"  certainly then that city must be understood which doth intimate this world's society: for it was not to no purpose that Cain was the first to build a city Thus the fruit of Christ being exalted above Libanus, that is, above enduring trees and undecaying timbers, because He is the everlasting fruit, all the glory of a man according to the temporal exaltation of the world is compared to grass; for by believers and by men already hoping for life eternal temporal felicity is despised, in order that there may be fulfilled that which hath been written, "all flesh is grass, and all the glory of flesh as the flower of grass: the grass hath dried, the flower hath fallen off, but the word of the Lord doth endure for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:166
verses.text: There is the fruit of Him exalted above Libanus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:167
verses.text: For always flesh hath been grass, and the glory of flesh as the flower of grass: but because it was not clearly proved what felicity ought to have been chosen and preferred, the flower of grass was esteemed for a great matter: not only it was by no means despised, but it was even chiefly sought after.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:168
verses.text: As if therefore at that time He shall have begun to be thus, when there is reproved and despised whatever used to flourish in the world, thus hath been said, "superexalted above Libanus shall be the fruit of Him, and they shall flourish from the city like grass of the earth:" that is, glorified above all things shall be that which is promised for everlasting, and compared to the grass of the earth shall be whatever is counted a great matter in the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:169
verses.text: "Be," therefore, "the name of Him blessed for ever: before the sun endureth the name of Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:170
verses.text: By the sun times are signified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:171
verses.text: Therefore for everlasting endureth the name of Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:172
verses.text: For eternity doth precede times, and is not bounded by time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:173
verses.text: "And there shall be blessed in Him all the tribes of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:174
verses.text: For in Him is fulfilled that which hath been promised to Abraham.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:175
verses.text: "For He saith not, In seeds, as though in many; but as though in one, And to thy Seed, which is Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:176
verses.text: But to Abraham is said, "In thy Seed shall be blessed all the tribes of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:177
verses.text: And not the sons of the flesh but the sons of promise are counted in the Seed "All nations shall magnify Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:178
verses.text: As if in explanation there is repeated that which above hath been said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:179
verses.text: For because they shall be blessed in Him, they shall magnify Him; not of themselves making Him to be great, that of Himself is great, but by praising and confessing Him to be great.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:180
verses.text: For thus we magnify God: thus also we say, "Hallowed be Thy name," which is indeed always holy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:181
verses.text: "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who hath done wonderful things alone".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:182
verses.text: Contemplating all things above spoken of, a hymn bursteth forth; and the Lord God of Israel is blessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:183
verses.text: For that is being fulfilled which hath been spoken to that barren woman, "and He that hath delivered Thee, the God of Israel, shall Himself be called of the whole earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:184
verses.text: "He doeth" Himself "marvellous things alone:" for whosoever do them, He doth Himself work in them, "who doeth wonderful things alone".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:185
verses.text: "And blessed be the name of His glory for everlasting, and for age of age".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:186
verses.text: For what else should the Latin interpreters have said, who could not have said for everlasting, and for everlasting of everlasting? For it soundeth as if one thing were meant in the expression "for everlasting," and another thing in the expression "for age:" but the Greek hath εἰς τὸν αἰωνα, καὶ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος, which perchance more meetly might have been rendered by, "for age, and for age of age:" so that by "for age," might have been understood as long as this age endureth; but "for age of age," that which after the end of this is promised to be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:187
verses.text: "And there shall be fulfilled with the glory of Him every land: so be it, so be it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 73:188
verses.text: Thou hast commanded, O Lord, so it is coming to pass: so it is coming to pass, until that which began with the river, may attain fully even unto the ends of the round world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:2
verses.text: This Psalm hath an inscr iption, that is, a title, "There have failed the hymns of David, the son of Jesse A Psalm of Asaph himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:3
verses.text: So many Psalms we have on the titles whereof is written the name David, nowhere there is added, "son of Jesse," except in this alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:4
verses.text: Which we must believe hath not been done to no purpose, nor capriciously.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:5
verses.text: For everywhere God doth make intimations to us, and to the understanding thereof doth invite the godly study of love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:6
verses.text: What is, "there have failed the hymns of David, the son of Jesse"? Hymns are praises of God accompanied with singing: hymns are songs containing the praise of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:7
verses.text: If there be praise, and it be not of God, it is no hymn: if there be praise, and God's praise, and it be not sung, it is no hymn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:8
verses.text: It must needs then, if it be a hymn, have these three things, both praise, and that of God, and singing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:9
verses.text: What is then, "there have failed the hymns"? There have failed the praises which are sung unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:10
verses.text: He seemeth to tell of a thing painful, and so to speak deplorable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:11
verses.text: For he that singeth praise, not only praiseth, but only praiseth with gladness: he that singeth praise, not only singeth, but also loveth him of whom he singeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:12
verses.text: In praise, there is the speaking forth of one confessing; in singing, the affection of one loving.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:13
verses.text: "There have failed" then "the hymns of David," he saith: and he hath added, "the son of Jesse".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:14
verses.text: For David was king of Israel, son of Jesse, at a certain time of the Old Testament, at which time the New Testament was therein hidden, like fruit in a root.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:15
verses.text: For if thou seek fruit in a root, thou wilt not find, and yet dost thou not find any fruit in the branches, except that which hath gone forth from the root.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:16
verses.text: And in like manner as Christ Himself to be born after the flesh was hidden in the root, that is in the seed of the Patriarchs, and at a certain time must be revealed, as at the fruit appearing, according as it is written, "there hath flourished a shoot from the root of Jesse:" so also the New Testament itself which is in Christ, in those former times was hidden, being known to the Prophets alone, and to the very few godly men, not by the manifestation of things present, but by the revelation of things future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:17
verses.text: For what meaneth it, brethren (to mention but one thing), that Abraham sending his faithful servant to espouse a wife for his only son, maketh him swear to him, and in the oath saith to him, "Put thy hand under my thigh, and swear"?  What was there in the thigh of Abraham, where he put his hand in swearing? What was there there, except that which even then was promised to him, "In thy seed shall be blessed all nations"? Under the name of thigh, flesh is signified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:18
verses.text: From the flesh of Abraham, through Isaac and Jacob, and not to mention many names, through Mary was our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:19
verses.text: But that the root was in the Patriarchs, how shall we show? Let us question Paul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:20
verses.text: The Gentiles now believing in Christ, and desiring as it were to boast over the Jews who crucified Christ; although also from that same people there came another wall, meeting in the corner, that is, in Christ Himself, the wall of uncircumcision, that is, of the Gentiles, coming from a different quarter: when, I say, the nations were lifting up themselves, he doth thus depress them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:21
verses.text: "For if thou," he saith, "being cut out of the natural wild olive, hast been graffed in among them, do not boast against the branches: for if thou boastest, thou dost not bear the root, but the root thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:22
verses.text: Therefore he speaketh of certain branches broken off from the root of the Patriarchs because of unbelief, and the wild olive therein graffed in, that it might be partaker of the fatness of the olive, that is, the Church coming out of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:23
verses.text: And who doth graff the wild olive on the olive? The olive is wont to be graffed on the wild olive; the wild olive on the olive we never saw.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:24
verses.text: For whosoever may have done so will find no berries but those of the wild olive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:25
verses.text: For that which is graffed in, the same groweth, and of that kind the fruit is found.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:26
verses.text: There is not found the fruit of the root but of the graft.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:27
verses.text: The Apostle showing that God did this thing by His Omnipotence, namely, that the wild olive should be graffed into the root of the olive, and should not bear wild berries, but olive—ascribing it to the Omnipotence of God, the Apostle saith this, "If thou hast been cut out of the natural wild olive and against nature hast been graffed into a good  olive, do not boast," he saith, "against the branches".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:28
verses.text: In the time then of the Old Testament, brethren, the promises from our God to that carnal people were earthly and temporal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:29
verses.text: There was promised an earthly kingdom, there was promised that land into which they were also led, after being delivered from Egypt: by Jesus son of Nave they were led into the land of promise, where also earthly Jerusalem was builded, where David reigned: they received the land, after being delivered from Egypt, by passing through the Red Sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:30
verses.text: Such were also those promises, which were not to endure, through which however were figured future promises which were to endure, so that all that course of temporal promises was a figure and a sort of prophecy of things future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:31
verses.text: Accordingly when that kingdom was failing, where reigned David, the son of Jesse, that is, one that was a man, though a Prophet, though holy, because he saw and foresaw Christ to come, of whose seed also after the flesh He was to be born: nevertheless a man, nevertheless not yet Christ, nevertheless not yet our King Son of God, but king David son of Jesse: because then that kingdom was to fail, through the receiving of which kingdom at that time God was praised by carnal men; for this thing alone they esteemed a great matter, namely, that they were delivered temporally from those by whom they were being oppressed, and that they had escaped from persecuting enemies through the Red Sea, and had been led through the desert, and had found country and kingdom: for this alone they praised God, not yet perceiving the thing which God was designing beforehand and promising in these figures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:32
verses.text: In the failing therefore of those things for which the carnal people, over whom reigned that David, was praising God, "there failed the hymns of David," not the Son of God, but the "son of Jesse".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:33
verses.text: Whose voice is the Psalm? "Of Asaph".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:34
verses.text: What is Asaph? As we find in interpretations from the Hebrew language into the Greek, and those again translated to us from the Greek into the Latin, Asaph is interpreted Synagogue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:35
verses.text: It is the voice therefore of the Synagogue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:36
verses.text: But when thou hast heard Synagogue, do not forthwith abhor it, as if it were the murderer of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:37
verses.text: That Synagogue was indeed the murderer of the Lord, no man doubteth it: but remember, that from the Synagogue were the rams whereof we are the sons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:38
verses.text: Whence it is said in a Psalm, "Bring ye to the Lord the sons of rams".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:39
verses.text: What rams are thence? Peter, John, James, Andrew, Bartholomew, and the rest of the Apostles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:40
verses.text: Hence also he too at first Saul, afterwards Paul: that is, at first proud, afterwards humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:41
verses.text: Therefore even Paul came to us from the Synagogue, and Peter and the other Apostles from the Synagogue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:42
verses.text: Therefore when thou hast heard the voice of the Synagogue, do not look to the deserving thereof, but observe the offspring.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:43
verses.text: There is speaking therefore in this Psalm, the Synagogue, after the failing of the hymns of David, the son of Jesse that is, after the failing of things temporal, through which God was wont to be praised by the carnal people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:44
verses.text: But why did these fail, except in order that others might be sought for? That there might be sought for what? Was it things which were not there? No, but things which were there being hidden in figures: not which were not yet there, but which there as it were in a sort were concealed in certain secret things of mysteries.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:45
verses.text: What things? "These," saith the Apostle himself, "were our figures".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:46
verses.text: It was the Synagogue therefore, that is, they that there worshipped God after a godly sort, but yet for the sake of earthly things, for the sake of these present things (for there are ungodly men who seek the blessings of present things from demons: but this people was on this account better than the Gentiles, because although it were blessings present and temporal, yet they sought them from the One God, who is the Creator of all things both spiritual and corporal).

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:47
verses.text: When therefore those godly men after the flesh were observing—that is that Synagogue which was made up of good men, men for the time good, not spiritual men, such as were the Prophets therein, such as were the few that understood the kingdom heavenly, eternal—that Synagogue, I say, observed what things it received from God, and what things God promised to that people, abundance of things earthly, land, peace, earthly felicity: but in all these things were figures, and they not perceiving what was there concealed in things figured, thought that God gave this for a great matter, and had nothing better to give to men loving Him and serving Him: they remarked and saw certain sinners, ungodly, blasphemers, servants of demons, sons of the Devil, living in great naughtiness and pride, yet abounding in such things earthly, temporal, for which sort of things they were serving God themselves: and there sprang up a most evil thought in the heart, which made the feet to totter, and almost slip out of God's way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:48
verses.text: And behold this thought was in the people of the Old Testament: I would it be not in our carnal brethren, when now openly there is being proclaimed the felicity of the New Testament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:49
verses.text: "How good is the God of Israel!" But to whom? "To  men right in heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:50
verses.text: To men perverse what? Perverse He seemeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:51
verses.text: So also in another Psalm He saith: "With a holy man holy Thou shalt be, and with the innocent man innocent Thou shalt be, and with the perverse man perverse Thou shalt be".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:52
verses.text: What is, perverse Thou shalt be with the perverse man? Perverse the perverse man shall think Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:53
verses.text: Not that by any means God is made perverse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:54
verses.text: Far be it: what He is, He is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:55
verses.text: But in like manner as the sun appeareth mild to one having clear, sound, healthy, strong eyes, but against weak eyes doth dart hard spears, so to say; the former looking at it it doth invigorate, the latter it doth torture, though not being itself changed, but the man being changed: so when thou shalt have begun to be perverse, and to thee God shall seem to be perverse, thou art changed, not He.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:56
verses.text: That therefore to thee will be punishment which to good men is joy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:57
verses.text: He calling to mind this thing, saith, "How good is the God of Israel to men right in heart!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:58
verses.text: But what to thee? "But my feet were almost moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:59
verses.text: When were the feet moved, except when the heart was not right? Whence was the heart not right? Hear: "My steps were well nigh overthrown".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:60
verses.text: What he hath meant by "almost," the same he hath meant by "well nigh:" and what he hath meant by "my feet were almost moved," the same he hath meant by "my steps were overthrown".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:61
verses.text: Almost my feet were moved, almost my steps were overthrown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:62
verses.text: Moved were the feet: but whence were the feet moved and the steps overthrown? Moved were the feet to going astray, overthrown were the steps to falling: not entirely, but "almost".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:63
verses.text: But what is this? Already I was going to stray, I had not gone: already I was falling, I had not fallen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:64
verses.text: But why even this? "For I was jealous," he saith, "in the case of sinners, looking on the peace of sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:65
verses.text: I observed sinners, I saw them to have peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:66
verses.text: What peace? Temporal, transient, falling, and earthly: but yet such as I also was desiring of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:67
verses.text: I saw them that served not God to have that which I desired in order that I might serve God: and my feet were moved and my steps were almost overthrown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:68
verses.text: But why sinners have this, he saith briefly: "Because there is no avoidance of their death, and there is a firmament in their scourge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:69
verses.text: Now I have perceived, he saith, why they have peace, and flourish on the earth; because of their death there is no avoidance, because death sure and eternal doth await them, which neither doth avoid them, nor can they avoid it, "because there is no avoidance of their death, and there is a firmament in their scourge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:70
verses.text: And there is a firmament in their scourge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:71
verses.text: For their scourge is not temporal, but firm for everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:72
verses.text: Because of these evil things then which are to be to them eternal, now what? "In the labours of men they are not, and with men they shall not be scourged".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:73
verses.text: Doth not even the devil himself escape scourging with men, for whom nevertheless an eternal punishment is being prepared?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:74
verses.text: Wherefore on this account what do these men, while they are not scourged, while they labour not with men? "Therefore," he saith "there hath holden them pride".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:75
verses.text: Observe these men, proud, undisciplined; observe the bull, devoted for a victim, suffered to stray at liberty; and to damage whatever he may, even up to the day of his slaughter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:76
verses.text: Now it is a good thing, brethren, that we should hear in the very words of a prophet of this bull as it were, whereof I have spoken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:77
verses.text: For thus of him the Scripture doth make mention in another place: he saith that they are, as it were, made ready as for a victim, and that they are spared for an evil liberty "Therefore," he saith, "there hath holden them pride".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:78
verses.text: What is, "there hath holden them pride"? "They have been clothed about with their iniquity and ungodliness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:79
verses.text: He hath not said, covered; but, "clothed about," on all sides covered up with their ungodliness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:80
verses.text: Deservedly miserable, they neither see nor are seen, because they are clothed about; and the inward parts of them are not seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:81
verses.text: For whosoever could behold the inward parts of evil men, that are as it were happy for a time, whosoever could see their torturing consciences, whosoever could examine their souls racked with such mighty perturbations of desires and fears, would see them to be miserable even when they are called happy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:82
verses.text: But because "they are clothed about with their iniquity and ungodliness," they see not; but neither are they seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:83
verses.text: The Spirit knew them, that saith these words concerning them: and we ought to examine such men with the same eye as that wherewith we know that we see, if there is taken from our eyes the covering of ungodliness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:84
verses.text: At first these men are being described.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:85
verses.text: "There shall go forth as if out of fat their iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:86
verses.text: A poor beggar committeth a theft; out of leanness hath gone forth the iniquity: but when a rich man aboundeth in so many things, why doth he plunder the things of others? Of the former the iniquity out of leanness, of the other out of fatness, hath gone forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:87
verses.text: Therefore to the lean man when thou sayest, Why hast thou done this? Humbly afflicted and abject he replieth, Need hath compelled me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:88
verses.text: Why hast thou not feared God? Want was urgent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:89
verses.text: Say to a rich man, Why doest thou these things, and fearest not God?—supposing thee to be great enough to be able to say it—see if he even deigneth to hear; see if even against thyself there will not go forth iniquity out of his fatness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:90
verses.text: For now they declare war with their teachers and reprovers, and become enemies of them that speak the truth, having been long accustomed to be coaxed with the words of flatterers, being of tender ear, of unsound heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:91
verses.text: Who would say to a rich man, Thou hast ill done in robbing other men's goods? Or perchance if any man shall have dared to speak, and he is such a man as he could not withstand, what doth he reply? All that he saith is in contempt of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:92
verses.text: Why? Because he is proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:93
verses.text: Why? Because he is fat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:94
verses.text: Why? Because he is devoted for a victim.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:95
verses.text: "They have passed over unto purpose of heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:96
verses.text: Here within they have passed over.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:97
verses.text: What is, "they have passed over"? They have crossed over the way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:98
verses.text: What is, "they have passed over"? They have exceeded the bounds of mankind, men like the rest they think not themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:99
verses.text: They have passed over, I say, the bounds of mankind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:100
verses.text: When thou sayest to such a man, Thy brother this beggar is; when thou sayest to such a man, Thy brother this poor man is; the same parents ye have had, Adam and Eve: do not heed thy haughtiness, do not heed the vapour unto which thou hast been elevated; although an establishment waiteth about thee, although countless gold and silver, although a marbled house doth contain thee, although fretted ceilings cover thee, thou and the poor man together have for covering that roof of the universe, the sky; but thou art different from the poor man in things not thine own, added to thee from without: thyself see in them, not them in thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:101
verses.text: Observe thyself, how thou art in relation to the poor man; thyself, not that which thou hast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:102
verses.text: For why dost thou despise thy brother? In the bowels of your mothers ye were both naked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:103
verses.text: Forsooth, even when ye shall have departed this life, and these bodies shall have rotted, when the soul hath been breathed forth, let the bones of the rich and poor man be distinguished! I am speaking of the equality of condition, of that very lot of mankind, wherein all men are born: for both here doth a man become rich, and a poor man will not alway be here: and as a rich man doth not come rich, so neither doth he depart rich; the very same is the entrance of both, and like is the departure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:104
verses.text: I add, that perchance ye will change conditions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:105
verses.text: Now everywhere the Gospel is being preached: observe a certain poor man full of sores, who was lying before the gate of a rich man, and was desiring to be filled with crumbs, which used to fall from the table of the rich man; observe also that likeness of thine who was clothed with purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:106
verses.text: It chanced, I say, for that poor man to die, and to be borne by the Angels into the bosom of Abraham: but the other died and was buried; for the other's burial perchance no one cared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:107
verses.text: Brethren, how great was the toil of the poor man! Of how long duration were the luxuries of the rich man! But the condition which they have received in exchange is everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:108
verses.text: Deservedly too late he will say, "Send Lazarus," "let him tell even my brethren;" since to himself there is not granted the fruit of repentance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:109
verses.text: For it is not that repentance is not given, but everlasting will be the repentance, and no salvation after repentance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:110
verses.text: Therefore these men "have passed over unto purpose of heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:111
verses.text: "They have thought and have spoken spitefulness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:112
verses.text: But men do speak spitefulness even with fear: but these men how? "Iniquity on high they have spoken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:113
verses.text: Not only they have spoken iniquity; but even openly, in the hearing of all, proudly; "I will do it;" "I will show you;" "thou shalt know with whom thou hast to do;" "I will not let thee live".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:114
verses.text: Thou mightest have but thought such things, not have given utterance to them! Within the chambers of thought at least the evil desire might have been confined, he might have at least restrained it within his thought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:115
verses.text: Why? Is he perchance lean? "There shall go forth as if out of fatness the iniquity of them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:116
verses.text: "Iniquity on high they have spoken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:117
verses.text: "They have set against Heaven their mouth, and their tongue hath passed over above the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:118
verses.text: For this, "hath passed over above the earth" is, they pass over all earthly things? What is it to pass over all earthly things? He doth not think of himself as a man that can die suddenly, when he is speaking; he doth menace as if he were alway to live: his thought doth transcend earthly frailty, he knoweth not with what sort of vessel he is enwrapped; he knoweth not what hath been written in another place concerning such men: "His spirit shall go forth, and he shall return unto his earth, in that day shall perish all his thoughts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:119
verses.text: But these men not thinking of their last day, speak pride, and unto Heaven they set their mouth, they transcend the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:120
verses.text: If a robber were not to think of his last day, that is, the last day of his trial, when sent to prison, nothing would be more monstrous than he: and yet he might escape.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:121
verses.text: Whither dost thou flee to escape death? Certain will that day be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:122
verses.text: What is the long time which thou hast to live? How much is the long time which hath an end, even if it were a long time? To this there is added that it is nought: and the very thing which is called long time is not a long time, and is uncertain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:123
verses.text: Why doth he not think of this? Because he hath set against Heaven his mouth, and his tongue hath passed over above the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:124
verses.text: "And full days shall be found in them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:125
verses.text: "Therefore there shall return hither My people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:126
verses.text: Now Asaph himself is returning hither.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:127
verses.text: For he saw these things abound to unrighteous men, he saw them abound to proud men: he is returning to God, and is beginning to inquire and discuss.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:128
verses.text: But when? "When full days shall be found in them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:129
verses.text: What is "full days"? "But when there came the fulness of time, God sent His Son".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:130
verses.text: This is the very fulness of time, when He came to teach men that things temporal should be despised, that they should not esteem as a great matter whatever object evil men covet, that they should suffer whatever evil men fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:131
verses.text: He became the way, He recalled us to inward thought, admonished us of what should be sought of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:132
verses.text: And see from what thought reacting upon itself, and in a manner recalling the waves of its impulse, he doth pass over unto choosing true things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:133
verses.text: "And they said, How hath God known, and is there knowledge in the Most High?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:134
verses.text: See through what thought they pass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:135
verses.text: Behold unjust men are happy, God doth not care for things human.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:136
verses.text: Doth He indeed know what we do? See what things are being said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:137
verses.text: We are inquiring, brethren, "How hath God known," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:138
verses.text: (no longer let Christians say it).

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:139
verses.text: For how doth it appear to thee that God knoweth not, and that there is no knowledge in the Most High? He replieth, "Lo! themselves they are sinners, and in the world they have gotten abundant riches".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:140
verses.text: Both sinners they are, and in the world they have gotten abundant riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:141
verses.text: He confessed that he willed not to be a sinner in order that he might have riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:142
verses.text: A carnal soul for things visible and earthly would have sold its justice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:143
verses.text: What sort of justice is that which is retained for the sake of gold, as if gold were a more precious thing than justice herself, or as if when a man denieth the deposit of another man's goods, he to whom he denied them should suffer a greater loss, than he that denieth them to him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:144
verses.text: The former doth lose a garment, the latter fidelity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:145
verses.text: "Lo! they are themselves sinners, and in the world they have gotten abundant riches".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:146
verses.text: On this account therefore God knoweth not, and on this account there is no knowledge in the Most High.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:147
verses.text: "And I said, therefore without cause I have justified my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:148
verses.text: In that I serve God, and have not these things; they serve him not, and they abound in these things: "therefore without cause I have justified my heart, and have washed among the innocent my hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:149
verses.text: This without cause I have done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:150
verses.text: Where is the reward of my good life? Where is the wage of my service? I live well and am in need; and the unjust man doth abound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:151
verses.text: "And I have washed among the innocent my hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:152
verses.text: And I have been scourged all the day long".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:153
verses.text: From me the scourges of God do not impart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:154
verses.text: I serve well, and I am scourged; he serveth not, and is honoured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:155
verses.text: He hath proposed to himself a great question.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:156
verses.text: The soul is disturbed, the soul doth pass over things which are to pass away unto despising things earthly and to desiring things eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:157
verses.text: There is a passage of the soul herself in this thought; where she doth toss in a sort of tempest she will reach the harbour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:158
verses.text: And it is with her as it is with sick persons, who are less violently sick, when recovery is far off: when recovery is at hand they are in higher fever; physicians call it the "critical accession" through which they pass to health: greater fever is there, but leading to health: greater heat, but recovery is at hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:159
verses.text: So also is this man enfevered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:160
verses.text: For these are dangerous words, brethren, offensive, and almost blasphemous, "How hath God known?" This is why I say, "and almost;" He hath not said, God hath not known: he hath not said, there is no knowledge in the Most High: but as if inquiring, hesitating, doubting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:161
verses.text: This is the same as he said a little before, "My steps were almost overthrown".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:162
verses.text: He doth not affirm it, but the very doubt is dangerous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:163
verses.text: Through danger he is passing to health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:164
verses.text: Hear now the health: "Therefore in vain I have justified my heart, and have washed among the innocent my hands: and I have been scourged all the day long, and my chastening was in the morning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:165
verses.text: Chastening is correction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:166
verses.text: He that is being chastened is being corrected.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:167
verses.text: What is, "in the morning"? It is not deferred.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:168
verses.text: That of the ungodly is being deferred, mine is not deferred: the former is too late or is not at all; mine is in the morning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:169
verses.text: "If I said, I shall declare thus; behold, the generation of Thy sons I have reprobated" : that is, I will teach thus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:170
verses.text: How wilt thou teach? that there is no knowledge in the Most High, that God doth not know? Wilt thou propound this opinion, that without cause men live justly who do live justly; that a just man hath lost his service, because God doth more show favour to evil men, or else He doth care for no one? Wilt thou tell this, declare this? He doth restrain himself by an authority repressing him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:171
verses.text: What authority? A man wisheth some time to break out in this sentiment: but he is recalled by the Scriptures directing us alway to live well, saying, that God doth care for things human, that He maketh a distinction between a godly man and an ungodly man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:172
verses.text: Therefore this man also wishing to put forth this sentiment, doth recollect himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:173
verses.text: And what saith he? "I have reprobated the generation of Thy sons".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:174
verses.text: If I shall declare thus, the generation of just men I shall reprobate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:175
verses.text: As also some copies have it, "Behold, the generation of thy sons with which I have been in concert:" that is, with which consisting of Thy sons I have been in concert; that is, with which I have agreed, to which I have been conformed: I have been out of time with all, if so I teach.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:176
verses.text: For he doth sing in concert who giveth the tune together; but he that giveth not the tune together doth not sing in concert.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:177
verses.text: Am I to say something different from that which Abraham said, from that which Isaac said, from that which Jacob said, from that which the Prophets said? For all they said that God doth care for things human, am I to say that He careth not? Is there greater wisdom in me than in them? Greater understanding in me than in them? A most wholesome authority hath called back his thought from ungodliness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:178
verses.text: And what followeth? That he might not reprobate, he did what? "And I undertook to know".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:179
verses.text: May God be with him in order that he may know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:180
verses.text: Meanwhile, brethren, from a great fall he is being withheld, when he doth not presume that he already knoweth, but hath undertaken to know that which he knew not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:181
verses.text: For but now he was willing to appear as if knowing, and to declare that God hath no care of things human.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:182
verses.text: For this hath come to be a most naughty and ungodly doctrine of unrighteous men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:183
verses.text: Know, brethren, that many men dispute and say that God careth not for things human, that by chances all things are ruled, or that our wills have been made subject to the stars, that each one is not dealt with according to his deserts, but by the necessity of his stars,—an evil doctrine, an impious doctrine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:184
verses.text: Unto these thoughts was going that man whose feet were almost moved, and whose steps were all but overthrown, into this error he was going; but because he was not in tune with the generation of the sons of God, he undertook to know, and condemned the knowledge wherein with God's just men he agreed not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:185
verses.text: And what he saith let us hear; how that he undertook to know, and was helped, and learned something, and declared it to us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:186
verses.text: "And I undertook," he saith, "to know".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:187
verses.text: "In this labour is before me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:188
verses.text: Truly a great labour; to know in what manner both God doth care for things human, and it is well with evil men, and good men labour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:189
verses.text: Great is the importance of the question; therefore, "and this labour is before me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:190
verses.text: As it were there is standing in my face a sort of wall, but thou hast the voice of a Psalm, "In my God I shall pass over the wall".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:191
verses.text: And he hath done this; for he saith how long labour is before him; "until I enter into the sanctuary of God, and understand upon the last things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:192
verses.text: A great thing it is, brethren: now for a long time I labour, he saith, and before my face I see a sort of insuperable labour, to know in what manner both God is just, and doth care for things human, and is not unjust because men sinning and doing wicked actions have happiness on this earth; but the godly and men serving God are wasted ofttimes in trials and in labours; a great difficulty it is to know this, but only "until I enter into the Sanctuary of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:193
verses.text: For in the Sanctuary what is presented to thee, in order that thou mayest solve this question? "And I understand," he saith, "upon the last things:" not present things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:194
verses.text: I, he saith, from the Sanctuary of God stretch out mine eye unto the end, I pass over present things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:195
verses.text: All that which is called the human race, all that mass of mortality is to come to the balance, is to come to the scale, thereon will be weighed the works of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:196
verses.text: All things now a cloud doth enfold: but to God are known the merits of each severally.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:197
verses.text: "And I understand," he saith, "upon the last things:" but not of myself; for before me there is labour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:198
verses.text: Whence "may I understand upon the last things"? Let me enter into the Sanctuary of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:199
verses.text: In that place then he understood also the reason why these men now are happy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:200
verses.text: To wit, "because of deceitfulness Thou hast set upon them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:201
verses.text: Because deceitful they are, that is fraudulent; because deceitful they are, they suffer deceits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:202
verses.text: What is this, because fraudulent they are they suffer a fraud? They desire to play a fraud upon mankind in all their naughtinesses, they themselves also suffer a fraud, in choosing earthly good things, and in forsaking the eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:203
verses.text: Therefore, brethren, in their very playing off a fraud they suffer a fraud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:204
verses.text: In that which but now I said, brethren, "What manner of wit hath he who to gain a garment doth lose his fidelity?" hath he whose garment he hath taken suffered a fraud, or he that is smitten with so great a loss? If a garment is more precious than fidelity, the former doth suffer the greater loss: but if incomparably good faith doth surpass the whole world, the latter shall seem to have sustained the loss of a garment; but to the former is said, "What doth it profit a man if he gain the whole world, but suffer the loss of his own soul?" Therefore what hath befallen them? "Because of deceitfulness Thou hast set for them: Thou didst throw them down while they were being exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:205
verses.text: He hath not said, Thou didst throw them down because they were lifted up: not as it were after that they were lifted up Thou didst throw them down; but in their very lifting up they were thrown down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:206
verses.text: For thus to be lifted up is already to fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:207
verses.text: "How have they become a desolation suddenly?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:208
verses.text: He is wondering at them, understanding unto the last things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:209
verses.text: "They have vanished".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:210
verses.text: Truly like smoke, which while it mounteth upward, doth vanish, so they have vanished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:211
verses.text: How doth he say, "They have vanished"? In the manner of one who understandeth the last things: "they have perished because of their iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:212
verses.text: "Like as the dream of one rising up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:213
verses.text: How have they vanished? As vanisheth the dream of one rising up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:214
verses.text: Fancy a man in sleep to have seen himself find treasures; he is a rich man, but only until he awaketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:215
