verses.text: "Like as the dream of one rising up:" so they have vanished, like the dream of one awaking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:216
verses.text: It is sought then and it is not: there is nothing in the hands, nothing in the bed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:217
verses.text: A poor man he went to sleep, a rich man in sleep he became: had he not awoke, he were a rich man: he woke up, he found the care which he had lost while sleeping.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:218
verses.text: And these men shall find the misery which they had prepared for themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:219
verses.text: When they shall have awoke from this life, that thing doth pass away which was grasped as if in sleep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:220
verses.text: "Like as the dream of one rising up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:221
verses.text: And that there might not be said, "What then? a small thing doth their glory seem to thee, a small thing doth their state seem to thee, small things seem to thee inscriptions, images, statues, distinctions, troops of clients?" "O Lord," he saith, "in Thy city their image Thou shalt bring to nothing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:222
verses.text: He hath taken away the pride of rich men, he giveth counsel As if they were saying, We are rich men, thou dost forbid us to be proud, dost prohibit us from boasting of the parade of our riches: what then are we to do with these riches? Is it come to this, that there is nothing which they may do therewith? "Be they rich," he saith, "in good works; let them readily distribute, communicate".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:223
verses.text: And what doth this profit? "Let them treasure unto themselves a good foundation for the future, that they may lay hold of true life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:224
verses.text: Where ought they to lay up treasure for themselves? In that place whereunto he set his eye, when entering into the Sanctuary of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:225
verses.text: Let there shudder all our rich brethren, abounding in money, gold, silver, household, honours, let them shudder at that which but now hath been said, "Thou shalt bring to nothing their image".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:226
verses.text: Are they not worthy to suffer these things, to wit that God bring to nothing their image in His city, because also they have themselves brought to nothing the image of God in their earthly city?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:227
verses.text: "Because my heart was delighted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:228
verses.text: He is saying with what things he is tempted: "because my heart was delighted," he saith, "my reins also were changed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:229
verses.text: When those temporal things delighted me, my reins were changed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:230
verses.text: It may also be understood thus: "because my heart was delighted" in God, "my reins also were changed, that is, my lusts were changed, and I became wholly chaste.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:231
verses.text: "My reins were changed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:232
verses.text: And hear how.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:233
verses.text: "And I was brought unto nothing, and I knew not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:234
verses.text: I, the very man, who now say these things of rich men, once longed for such things: therefore "even I was brought to nothing" when my steps were almost overthrown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:235
verses.text: "And I was brought unto nothing, and I knew not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:236
verses.text: We must not therefore despair even of them, against whom I was saying such things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:237
verses.text: What is, "I knew not"? "As it were a beast I became to Thee, and I am alway with Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:238
verses.text: There is a great difference between this man and others.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:239
verses.text: He became as it were a beast in longing for earthly things, when being brought to nothing he knew not things eternal: but he departed not from his God, because he did not desire these things of demons, of the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:240
verses.text: For this I have already brought to your notice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:241
verses.text: The voice is from the Synagogue, that is, from that people which served not idols.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:242
verses.text: A beast indeed I became, when desiring from my God things earthly: but I never departed from That my God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:243
verses.text: Because then, though having become a beast, I departed not from my God, there followeth, "Thou hast held the hand of my right hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:244
verses.text: He hath not said my right hand, but "the hand of my right hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:245
verses.text: If the hand of the right hand it is, a hand hath a hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:246
verses.text: "The hand Thou hast held of my right hand," in order that Thou mightest conduct me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:247
verses.text: For what hath he put hand? For power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:248
verses.text: For we say that a man hath that in his hand which he hath in his power: just as the devil said to God concerning Job, "Lay to Thine hand, and take away the things which he hath".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:249
verses.text: What is, lay to Thine hand? Put forth power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:250
verses.text: The hand of God he hath called the power of God: as hath been written in another place, "death and life are in the hands of the tongue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:251
verses.text: Hath the tongue hands? But what is, in the hands of the tongue? In the power of the tongue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:252
verses.text: What is, in the power of the tongue? "Out of thy mouth thou shalt be justified, and out of thy mouth thou shalt be condemned".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:253
verses.text: "Thou hast held," therefore, "the hand of my right hand," the power of my right hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:254
verses.text: What was my right hand? That I was alway with Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:255
verses.text: Unto the left I was holding, because I became a beast, that is, because there was an earthly concupiscence in me: but the right was mine, because I was alway with thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:256
verses.text: Of this my right hand Thou hast held the hand, that is, hast directed the power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:257
verses.text: What power? "He gave them power to become sons of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:258
verses.text: He is beginning now to be among the sons of God, belonging to the New Testament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:259
verses.text: See in what manner the hand of his right hand was held.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:260
verses.text: "In Thy will Thou hast conducted me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:261
verses.text: What is, "in thy will"? Not in my merits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:262
verses.text: What is, "in Thy will"? Hear the apostle, who was at first a beast longing for things earthly, and living after the Old Testament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:263
verses.text: He saith what? "I that at first was a blasphemer, and persecutor, and injurious: but mercy I obtained".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:264
verses.text: What is, "in Thy will"? "By the grace of God I am what I am".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:265
verses.text: "And in glory Thou hast taken me up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:266
verses.text: Now to what glory he was taken up, and in what glory, who can explain, who can say? Let us await it, because in the Resurrection it will be, in the last things it will be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:267
verses.text: And he is beginning to think of that same Heavenly felicity, and to reprove himself, because he hath been a beast, and hath longed for things earthly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:268
verses.text: "For what have I in Heaven, and from Thee what have I willed upon earth?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:269
verses.text: By your voice I see that ye have understood He compared with his earthly will the heavenly reward which he is to receive; he saw what was there being reserved for him; and while thinking and burning at the thought of some ineffable thing, which neither eye hath seen, nor ear heard, nor into the heart of man hath ascended, he hath not said, this or that I have in Heaven, but, "what have I in Heaven?" What is that thing which I have in Heaven? What is it? How great is it? Of what sort is it? "And," since that which I have in heaven doth not pass away, "from Thee what have I willed upon earth?"Thou reservest, he saith, for me in Heaven riches immortal, even Thyself, and I have willed from Thee on earth that which even ungodly men have, which even evil men have, which even abandoned men have, money, gold, silver, jewels, households, which even many wicked men have: which even many profligate women have, many profligate men: these things as a great matter I have desired of my God upon earth: though my God reserveth Himself for me in Heaven!.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:270
verses.text: "My heart and my flesh hath failed, O God of my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:271
verses.text: This then for me in Heaven hath been reserved, "God of my heart, and my portion is my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:272
verses.text: What is it, brethren? Let us find out our riches, let mankind choose their parts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:273
verses.text: Let us see men torn with diversity of desires: let some choose war-service, some advocacy, some divers and sundry offices of teaching, some merchandise, some farming, let them take their portions in human affairs: let the people of God cry, "my portion is my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:274
verses.text: Not for a time "my portion;" but "my portion is my God for everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:275
verses.text: Even if I alway have gold, what have I? Even if I did not alway have God, how great a good should I have? To this is added, that He promiseth Himself to me, and He promiseth that I shall have this for everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:276
verses.text: So great a thing I have, and never have it not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:277
verses.text: Great felicity: "my portion is God!" How long? "For everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:278
verses.text: For behold and see after what sort He hath loved him; He hath made his heart chaste: "God of my heart, and my portion is God for everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:279
verses.text: His heart hath become chaste, for nought now God is loved, from Him is not sought any other reward.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:280
verses.text: He that doth seek any other reward from God, and therefore is willing to serve God, more precious doth make that which he willeth to receive, than Him from whom he willeth to receive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:281
verses.text: What then, is there no reward belonging to God? None except Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:282
verses.text: The reward belonging to God, is God Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:283
verses.text: This he loveth, this he esteemeth; if any other thing he shall have loved, the love will not be chaste.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:284
verses.text: Thou art receding from the Fire immortal, thou wilt grow cold, wilt be corrupted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:285
verses.text: Do not recede.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:286
verses.text: Recede not, it will be thy corruption, it will be thy fornication.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:287
verses.text: Now he is returning, now he is repenting, now he is choosing repentance, now he is saying, "my portion is God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:288
verses.text: And after what sort is he delighted with that Same, whom he hath chosen for his portion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:289
verses.text: "Behold, they that put themselves afar from Thee shall perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:290
verses.text: He therefore departed from God, but not far: for "I have become as it were a beast," he saith, and "I am alway with Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:291
verses.text: But they have departed afar, because not only things earthly they have desired, but have sought them from demons and the Devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:292
verses.text: "They that put themselves afar from Thee shall perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:293
verses.text: And what is it, to become afar from God? "Thou hast destroyed every man that committeth fornication away from Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:294
verses.text: To this fornication is opposed chaste love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:295
verses.text: What is chaste love? Now the soul doth love her Bridegroom: what doth she require of Him, from Her Bridegroom whom she loveth? Perchance in like manner as women choose for themselves men either as sons-in-law or as bridegrooms: she perchance chooseth riches, and loveth his gold, and estates, and silver and cattle and horses, and household, and the like.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:296
verses.text: Far be it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:297
verses.text: He doth love Him alone, for nought he doth love Him: because in Him he hath all things, for "by Him were made all things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:298
verses.text: But thou doest what? "But for me to cleave to God is a good thing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:299
verses.text: This is whole good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:300
verses.text: Will ye have more? I grieve at your willing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:301
verses.text: Brethren, what will ye have more? Than to cleave to God nothing is better, when we shall see Him face to face But now what? For yet as a stranger I am speaking: "to cleave," he saith, "to God is a good thing:" but now in my sojourning (for not yet hath come the substance), I have "to put in God my hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:302
verses.text: So long therefore as thou hast not yet cloven, therein put thy hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:303
verses.text: Thou art wavering, cast forward an anchor to the land Not yet dost thou cleave by presence, cleave fast by hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:304
verses.text: "To put in God my hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:305
verses.text: And by doing what here wilt thou put in God thy hope? What will be thy business, but to praise Him whom thou lovest, and to make others to be fellow-lovers of Him with thee? Lo, if thou shouldest love a charioteer, wouldest thou not carry along other men to love him with thee? A lover of a charioteer whithersoever he goeth doth speak of him, in order that as well as he others also may love him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:306
verses.text: For nought are loved abandoned men, and from God is reward required in order that He may be loved? Love thou God for nought, grudge God to no one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:307
verses.text: For what followeth? "In order that I may tell forth all Thy praises in the courts of the daughter of Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:308
verses.text: "In the courts:" for the preaching of God beside the Church is vain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:309
verses.text: A small thing it is to praise God and to tell forth all His praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:310
verses.text: In the courts of the daughter of Sion tell thou forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:311
verses.text: Make for unity, do not divide the people; but draw them un to one, and make them one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:312
verses.text: I have forgotten how long I have been speaking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 74:313
verses.text: Now the Psalm being ended, even judging by this closeness, I suppose I have held a long discourse: but it doth not suffice for your zeal; ye are too impetuous O that with this impetuosity ye would seize upon the kingdom of Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 75:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXIV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 75:2
verses.text: This Psalm's Title is, "Of the Understanding of Asaph".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 75:3
verses.text: Asaph in Latin is translated congregation, in Greek Synagogue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 75:4
verses.text: Let us see what this Synagogue hath understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 75:5
verses.text: But let us understand firstly Synagogue: from thence we shall understand what the Synagogue hath understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 75:6
verses.text: Every congregation is spoken of under the general name of Synagogue: one both of beasts and of men may be called a congregation; but here there is no congregation of beasts when we heard "understanding".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 75:7
verses.text: for this the Psalm's Title doth prescribe, saying, "Of the understanding of Asaph".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 75:8
verses.text: It is therefore a certain understanding congregation whereof we are about to hear the voice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 75:9
verses.text: But since properly Synagogue is said of the congregation of the people of Israel, so that wheresoever we may have heard Synagogue, we are no longer wont to.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:1
verses.text: understand any but the people of the Jews; let us see whether perchance the voice in this Psalm be not of that same people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:2
verses.text: But of what sort of Jews and of what sort of people of Israel? For they are not of the chaff, but perchance of the grain; not of the broken branches, but perchance of those that are strengthened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:3
verses.text: "For not all that are of Israel are Israelites".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:4
verses.text: There are therefore certain Israelites, of whom was he concerning whom was said, "Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom guile is not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:5
verses.text: I do not say in the same manner as we are Israelites, for we also are the seed of Abraham.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:6
verses.text: For to the Gentiles the Apostle was speaking, when he said, "Therefore the seed of Abraham ye are, heirs according to promise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:7
verses.text: According to this therefore all we are Israelites, that follow the footsteps of the faith of our father Abraham.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:8
verses.text: But let us understand here the voice of the Israelites in the same manner as the Apostle saith, "For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:9
verses.text: Here therefore let us understand that whereof the Prophets have spoken, "a remnant shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:10
verses.text: Of the remnant therefore saved let us hear in this place the voice; in order that there may speak that Synagogue which had received the Old Testament, and was intent upon carnal promises; and by this means it came to pass that their feet were shaken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:11
verses.text: For in another Psalm, where too the title hath Asaph, there is said what? "How good is the God of Israel to men right in heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:12
verses.text: But my feet were almost moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:13
verses.text: And as if we were saying, whence were thy feet moved? "Well nigh," he saith, "my steps were overthrown, because I was jealous in the case of sinners, looking on the peace of sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:14
verses.text: For while according to the promises of God belonging to the Old Testament he was looking for earthly felicity, he observed it to abound with ungodly men; that they who worshipped not God were enriched with those things which he was looking for from God: and as though without cause he had served God, his feet tottered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:15
verses.text: But opportunely it hath chanced not by our own but by God's dispensation, that just now we heard out of the Gospel, that "the Law was given by Moses, Grace and Truth came by Jesus Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:16
verses.text: For if we distinguish between the two Testaments, Old and New, there are not the same Sacraments nor the same promises; nevertheless, the same commandments for the most part.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:17
verses.text: When examined they are either all found to be the same, or there are scarce any in the Gospel which have not been spoken by the Prophets.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:18
verses.text: The Commandments are the same, the Sacraments are not the same, the Promises are not the same.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:19
verses.text: Let us see wherefore the commandments are the same; because according to these we ought to serve God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:20
verses.text: The Sacraments are not the same, for some Sacraments there are giving Salvation, others promising a Saviour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:21
verses.text: The Sacraments of the New Testament give Salvation, the Sacraments of the Old Testament did promise a Saviour When therefore thou hast now the things promised, why dost thou seek the things promising, having now the Saviour?God through the New Testament hath taken out of the hands of His sons those things which are like the playthings of boys, in order that He might give something more useful to them growing up, on that account must He be supposed not to have given those former things Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:22
verses.text: He gave both Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:23
verses.text: But the Law itself through Moses was given, Grace and Truth came through Jesus Christ: Grace because there is fulfilled through love that which by the letter was being enjoined, Truth because there is being rendered that which was promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:24
verses.text: This thing therefore this Asaph hath understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:25
verses.text: In a word, all things which to the Jews had been promised have been taken away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:26
verses.text: Where is their kingdom? Where the Temple? Where the Anointing? Where is Priest? Where are now the Prophets among them? From what time there came He that by the Prophets was foretold, in that nation there is now nothing of these things; now she hath lost things earthly, and not yet doth seek things Heavenly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:27
verses.text: Thou shouldest not therefore hold fast things earthly, although God doth bestow them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:28
verses.text: See ye how that in fearing to lose things earthly, the Jews slew the King of Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:29
verses.text: And what was done to them? They lost even those very things earthly: and in the place where they slew Christ, there they were slain: and when, being unwilling to lose the land, they slew the Giver of life, that same land being slain they lost; and at that very time when they slew Him, in order that by that very time they might be admonished of the reason wherefore they suffered these things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:30
verses.text: For when the city of the Jews was overthrown, they were celebrating the Passover, and with many thousands of men the whole nation itself had met together for the celebration of that festival In that place God (through evil men indeed, but yet Himself good; through unjust men, but Himself just and justly) did so take vengeance upon them, that there we re slain many thousands of men, and the city itself was overthrown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:31
verses.text: Of this thing in this Psalm "the understanding of Asaph" doth complain, and in the very plaint the understanding as it were doth distinguish things earthly from things heavenly, doth distinguish the Old Testament from the New Testament: in order that thou mayest see through what things thou art passing, what thou shouldest look for, what to forsake, to what to cleave.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:32
verses.text: Thus then he beginneth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:33
verses.text: "Wherefore hast Thou repelled us, O God, unto the end?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:34
verses.text: "Hast repelled unto the end," in the person of the congregation which is properly called Synagogue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:35
verses.text: "Wherefore hast Thou repelled us, O God, unto the end?" He censureth not, but inquireth "wherefore," for what purpose, because of what hast Thou done this? What hast Thou done? "Thou hast repelled us unto the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:36
verses.text: What is, "unto the end"? Perchance even unto the end of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:37
verses.text: Hast Thou repelled us unto Christ, who is the End to every one believing?  For, "Wherefore hast Thou repelled us, O God, unto the end?" "Thy spirit hath been wroth at the sheep of Thy flock".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:38
verses.text: Wherefore wast Thou wroth at the sheep of Thy flock, but because to things earthly we were cleaving, and the Shepherd we knew not?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:39
verses.text: "Remember Thou Thy congregation, which Thou hast possessed from the beginning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:40
verses.text: Can this by any means be the voice of the Gentiles? Hath He possessed the Gentiles from the beginning? Nay, but He hath possessed the seed of Abraham, the people of Israel even according to the flesh, born of the Patriarchs our fathers: of whom we have become the sons, not by coming out of their flesh, but by imitating their faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:41
verses.text: But those, possessed by God from the beginning, what befell them? "Remember Thy congregation which Thou hast possessed from the beginning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:42
verses.text: Thou hast redeemed the rod of Thine inheritance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:43
verses.text: That same congregation of Thine, being the rod of Thine inheritance, Thou hast redeemed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:44
verses.text: This same congregation he hath called "the rod of the inheritance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:45
verses.text: Let us look back to the first thing that was done, when He willed to possess that same congregation, delivering it from Egypt, what sign He gave to Moses, when Moses said to Him, "What sign shall I give that they may believe me, that Thou hast sent me? And God saith to him, What dost thou bear in thine hand? A rod.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:46
verses.text: Cast it on to the ground," etc What doth it intimate? For this was not done to no purpose.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:47
verses.text: Let us inquire of the writings of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:48
verses.text: To what did the serpent persuade man? To death Therefore death is from the serpent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:49
verses.text: If death is from the serpent, the rod in the serpent is Christ in death Therefore also when by serpents in the desert they were being bitten and being slain, the Lord commanded Moses to exalt a brazen serpent in the desert, and admonish the people that whosoever by a serpent had been bitten, should look thereupon and be made whole Thus also it was done: thus also men, bitten by serpents, were made whole of the venom by looking upon a serpent To be made whole of a serpent is a great Sacrament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:50
verses.text: What is it to be made whole of a serpent by looking upon a serpent? It is to be made whole of death by believing in one dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:51
verses.text: And nevertheless Moses feared and fled What is it that Moses fled from that serpent? What, brethren, save that which we know to have been done in the Gospel? Christ died and the disciples feared, and withdrew from that hope wherein they had beenBut, at that time some thousands of the Jews themselves, the crucifiers of Christ, believed: and because they had been found at hand, they so believed as that they sold all that they had, and the price of their goods before the feet of the Apostles they laid Because then this thing was hidden, and the redemption of the rod of God was to be more conspicuous in the Gentiles: he explaineth of what he saith that which he hath said, "Thou hast redeemed the rod of Thine inheritance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:52
verses.text: This he hath said not of the Gentiles in whom it was evident.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:53
verses.text: But of what? "Mount Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:54
verses.text: Yet even Mount Sion can be otherwise understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:55
verses.text: "That one which Thou hast dwelled in the same".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:56
verses.text: In the place where the People was aforetime, where the Temple was set up, where the Sacrifices were celebrated, where at that time were all those necessary things giving promise of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:57
verses.text: A promise, when the thing promised is bestowed is now become superfluous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:58
verses.text: "Lift up Thine hand upon their pride at the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:59
verses.text: As Thou didst repel us at the end, so "lift up Thine hand upon the pride of them at the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:60
verses.text: The pride of whom? Of those by whom Jerusalem was overthrown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:61
verses.text: But by whom was it, but by the kings of the Gentiles? Well was the hand of Him lifted up upon the pride of them at the end: for they too have now known Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:62
verses.text: "For the end of the Law is Christ for righteousness to every one believing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:63
verses.text: How well doth he wish for them! As if angry he is speaking, and he is seeming to speak evil: and O that there would come to pass the evil which he speaketh: nay now in the name of Christ that it is coming to pass let us rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:64
verses.text: Now they holding the sceptre are being made subject to the Word of the Cross: now is coming to pass that which was foretold, "there shall adore Him all the kings of the earth, all nations shall serve Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:65
verses.text: Now on the brows of kings more precious is the sign of the Cross, than the jewel of a crown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:66
verses.text: "Lift up Thine hand upon the pride of them at the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:67
verses.text: How great things hath the enemy of malice wrought in Thy holy places!" In those which were Thy holy places, that is, in the temple, in the priesthood, in all those sacraments which were at that time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:68
verses.text: In good sooth the enemy at that time wrought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:69
verses.text: For the Gentiles at that time who did this, were worshipping false Gods, were adoring idols, were serving demons: nevertheless they wrought many evil things on the Saints of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:70
verses.text: When could they if they had not been permitted? But when would they have been permitted, unless those holy things, at first promised, were no longer necessary, when He that had promised was Himself holden? Therefore, "how great things hath the enemy of malice wrought in Thy holy places!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:71
verses.text: "And all they have boasted, that hate Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:72
verses.text: Observe the servants of demons, the servants of idols: such as at that time the Gentiles were, when they overthrew the temple and city of God, "and they boasted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:73
verses.text: "In the midst of Thy festival".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:74
verses.text: Remember what I said, that Jerusalem was overthrown at the time when the very festival was being celebrated: at which festival they crucified the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:75
verses.text: Gathered together they raged, gathered together they perished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:76
verses.text: "They have set signs, their own signs, and they have not known".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:77
verses.text: They had signs to place there, their standards, their eagles, their own dragons, the Roman signs; or even their statues which at first in the temple they placed; or perchance "their signs" are the things which they heard from the prophets of their demons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:78
verses.text: "And they have not known".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:79
verses.text: Have not known what? How "thou shouldest have had no power against Me, except it had been given thee from above".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:80
verses.text: They knew not how that not on themselves honour was conferred, to afflict, to take, or overthrow the city, but their ungodliness was made as it were the axe of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:81
verses.text: They were made the instrument of Him enraged, not so as to be the kingdom of Him pacified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:82
verses.text: For God doth that which a man also ofttime doth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:83
verses.text: Sometimes a man in a rage catcheth up a rod lying in the way, perchance any sort of stick, he smiteth therewith his son, and then throweth the stick into the fire and reserveth the inheritance for his son: so sometime God through evil men doth instruct good men, and through the temporal power of them that are to be condemned He worketh the discipline of them that are to be saved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:84
verses.text: For why do you suppose, brethren, that discipline was even thus inflicted upon that nation, in order that it might perish utterly? How many out of this nation did afterwards believe, how many are yet to believe? Some are chaff, others grain; over both however there cometh in the threshing-drag; but under one threshing-drag the one is broken up, the other is purged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:85
verses.text: How great a good hath God bestowed upon us by the evil of Judas the traitor! By the very ferocity of the Jews how great a good was bestowed upon believing Gentiles! Christ was slain in order that there might be on the Cross One for him to look to who had been stung by the serpent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:86
verses.text: Now let us hasten over the verses following after the destruction of Jerusalem, for the reason that they are both evident, and it doth not please me to tarry over the punishment even of enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:87
verses.text: "As if in a forest of trees with axes, they have cut down the doors thereof at once; with mattock and hammer they have thrown Her down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:88
verses.text: That is, conspiring together, with firm determination, "with mattock and hammer" they have thrown Her down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:89
verses.text: "They have burned with fire Thy Sanctuary, they have defiled on the ground the Tabernacle of Thy name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:90
verses.text: "They have said in their heart (the kindred of them is in one)"—Have said what? "Come ye, let us suppress the solemnities of the Lord from the land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:91
verses.text: "Of the Lord," hath been inserted in the person of this man, that is, in the person of Asaph.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:92
verses.text: For they raging would not have called Him the Lord whose temple they were overthrowing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:93
verses.text: "Come ye, let us suppress all the solemnities of the Lord from the land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:94
verses.text: What of Asaph? What understanding hath Asaph in these words? What? Doth he not profit even by the discipline accorded? Is not the mind's crookedness made straight? Overthrown were all things that were at first: nowhere is there priest, nowhere Altar of the Jews, nowhere victim, nowhere Temple.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:95
verses.text: Is there then no other thing to be acknowledged which succeeded this departing? Or indeed would this promissory sign have been taken away, unless there had come that which was being promised? Let us see therefore in this place now the understanding of Asaph, let us see if he profiteth by tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:96
verses.text: Observe what he saith: "Our signs we have not seen, no longer is there prophet, and us He will not know as yet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:97
verses.text: Behold those Jews who say that they are not known as yet, that is, that they are yet in captivity, that not yet they are delivered, do yet expect Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:98
verses.text: Christ will  come, but He will come as Judge; the first time to call, afterwards to sever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:99
verses.text: He will come, because He hath come, and that He will come is evident; but hereafter from above He will come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:100
verses.text: Before thee He was, O Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:101
verses.text: Thou wast bruised because thou didst stumble against Him lying down: that thou mayest not be ground to powder, observe Him coming from above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:102
verses.text: For thus it was foretold by the prophet: "Whoever shall stumble upon that stone shall be bruised, and upon whomsoever it shall have come, it shall grind him to powder".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:103
verses.text: He doth bruise when little, He shall grind to powder when great.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:104
verses.text: Now thy signs thou seest not, now there is no prophet: and thou sayest, "and us He will not know as yet:" because yourselves know not Him as yet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:105
verses.text: "No longer is there a prophet; and us He will not know as yet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:106
verses.text: "How long, O God, shall the enemy revile?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:107
verses.text: Cry out as if forsaken, as if deserted: cry out like a sick man, who hast chosen rather to smite the physician than to be made whole: not as yet doth He know thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:108
verses.text: See what He hath done, who doth not know thee as yet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:109
verses.text: For they to whom there hath been no preaching of Him, shall see; and they that have not heard shall understand: and thou yet criest out, "No longer is there a prophet, and us He will not know as yet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:110
verses.text: Where is thine understanding? "The adversary doth provoke Thy name at the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:111
verses.text: For this purpose the adversary doth provoke Thy name at the end, that being provoked Thou mayest reprove, reproving Thou mayest know them at the end: or certainly, "at the end," in the sense of even unto the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:112
verses.text: "Wherefore dost Thou turn away Thine hand, and Thy right hand from the midst of Thy bosom unto the end?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:113
verses.text: Again, another sign which was given to Moses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:114
verses.text: For in like manner as above from the rod was a sign, so also from the right hand now.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:115
verses.text: For when that thing had been done concerning the rod, God gave a second sign: "thrust," He saith, "thine hand into thy bosom, and he thrust it: draw it forth, and he drew it forth: and it was found white," that is, unclean.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:116
verses.text: For whiteness on the skin is leprosy, not fairness of complexion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:117
verses.text: For the heritage of God itself, that is, His people, being cast out became unclean.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:118
verses.text: But what saith He to him? Draw it back into thy bosom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:119
verses.text: He drew it back, and it was restored to its own colour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:120
verses.text: When doest Thou this, saith this Asaph? How long dost Thou alienate Thy right hand from Thy bosom, so that being without unclean it remaineth? Draw it back, let it return to its colour, let it acknowledge the Saviour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:121
verses.text: "Wherefore dost thou turn away Thine hand, and Thy right hand from the midst of Thy bosom unto the end?" These words he crieth, being blind, not understanding, and God doeth what He doeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:122
verses.text: For wherefore came Christ? "Blindness in part happened unto Israel, in order that the fulness of the Gentiles might enter in, and so all Israel might be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:123
verses.text: Therefore now, O Asaph, acknowledge that which hath gone before, in order that thou mayest at least follow, if thou wast not able to go before.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:124
verses.text: For not in vain came Christ, or in vain was Christ slain, or in vain did the corn fall into the ground; but it fell that it might rise manifold A serpent was lifted up in the desert, in order that it might cure of the poison him that was smitten Observe what was done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:125
verses.text: Do not think it to be a vain thing that He came: lest He find thee evil, when He shall have come a second time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:126
verses.text: Asaph hath understood, because on the Title of the Psalm there is, "understanding of Asaph".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:127
verses.text: And what saith he? "But God, our King before the worlds, hath wrought Salvation in the midst of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:128
verses.text: On the one hand we cry, "No longer is there prophet, and us He will not know as yet:" but on the other hand, "our God, our King, who is before the worlds" (for He is Himself in the beginning of the Word by whom were made the worlds), "hath wrought Salvation in the midst of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:129
verses.text: "God therefore, our King before the worlds," hath done what? "hath wrought Salvation in the midst of the earth:" and I am yet crying as if forsaken!Now the Gentiles are awake, and we are snoring, and as though God hath forsaken us, in dreams we are delirious.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:130
verses.text: "He hath wrought Salvation in the midst of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:131
verses.text: Now therefore, O Asaph, amend thyself according to thy understanding, tell us what sort of Salvation God hath wrought in the midst of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:132
verses.text: When that earthly Salvation of yours was overthrown, what did He do, what did He promise? "Thou didst confirm in Thy virtue the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:133
verses.text: As though the nation of the Jews were as it were dry land severed from the waves, the Gentiles in their bitterness were the sea, and on all sides they washed about that land: behold, "Thou hast confirmed in Thy virtue the sea," and the land remained thirsting for Thy rain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:134
verses.text: "Thou hast confirmed in Thy virtue the sea, Thou hast broken in pieces the heads of dragons in the water".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:135
verses.text: Dragons' heads, that is, demons' pride, wherewith the Gentiles were possessed, Thou hast broken in pieces upon the water: for those persons whom they were possessing, Thou by Baptism hast delivered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:136
verses.text: What more after the heads of dragons? For those dragons have their chief, and he is himself the first great dragon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:137
verses.text: And concerning him what hath He done that hath wrought Salvation in the midst of the earth? Hear: "Thou hast broken the head of the dragon".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:138
verses.text: Of what dragon? We understand by dragons all the demons that war under the devil: what single dragon then, whose head was broken, but the devil himself ought we to understand? What with him hath He done? "Thou hast broken the head of the dragon".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:139
verses.text: That is, the beginning of sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:140
verses.text: That head is the part which received the curse, to wit that the seed of Eve should mark the head of the serpent For the Church was admonished to shun the beginning of sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:141
verses.text: Which is that beginning of sin, like the head of a serpent? The beginning of all sin is pride There hath been broken therefore the head of the dragon, hath been broken pride diabolical.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:142
verses.text: And what with him hath He done, that hath wrought Salvation in the midst of the earth? "Thou hast given him for a morsel to the Ethiopian peoples".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:143
verses.text: What is this? How do I understand the Ethiopian peoples? How but by these all nations? And properly by black men: for Ethiopians are black.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:144
verses.text: They are themselves called to the faith who were black; the very same indeed, so that there is said to them, "for ye were sometime darkness, but now light in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:145
verses.text: Thence was also that calf which the people worshipped, unbelieving, apostate, seeking the gods of the Egyptians, forsaking Him who had delivered them from the slavery of the Egyptians: whence there was enacted that great Sacrament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:146
verses.text: For when Moses was thus wroth with them worshipping and adoring the idol, and, inflamed with zeal for God, was punishing temporally, in order that he might terrify them to shun death everlasting; yet the head itself of the calf he cast into the fire, and ground to powder, destroyed, strawed on the water, and gave to the people to drink: so there was enacted a great Sacrament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:147
verses.text: O anger prophetic, and mind not perturbed but enlightened! He did what? Cast it into the fire, in order that first the form itself may be obliterated; piece by piece grind it down, in order that little by little it may be consumed: cast it into the water, give to the people to drink! What is this but that the worshippers of the devil were become the body of the same? In the same manner as men confessing Christ become the Body of Christ; so that to them is said, "but ye are the Body of Christ and the members".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:148
verses.text: The body of the devil was to be consumed, and that too by Israelites was to be consumed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:149
verses.text: For out of that people were the Apostles, out of that people the first Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:150
verses.text: Thus the devil is being consumed with the loss of his members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:151
verses.text: This was figured also in the serpent of Moses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:152
verses.text: For the magicians did likewise, and casting down their rods they exhibited serpents: but the serpent of Moses swallowed up the rods of all those magicians Let there be perceived therefore even now the body of the devil: this is what is coming to pass, he is being devoured by the Gentiles who have believed, he hath become meat for the Ethiopian peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:153
verses.text: This again, may be perceived in, "Thou hast given him for meat to the Ethiopian peoples," how that now all men bite him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:154
verses.text: What is, bite him? By reproving, blaming, accusing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:155
verses.text: Just as hath been said, by way of prohibition indeed, but yet the idea expressed: "but if ye bite and eat up one another, take heed that ye be not consumed of one another".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:156
verses.text: What is, bite and eat up one another? Ye go to law with one another, ye detract from one another, ye heap revilings upon one another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:157
verses.text: Observe therefore now how that with these bitings the devil is being consumed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:158
verses.text: What man, when angry with his servant, even a heathen, would not say to him, Satan? Behold the devil given for meat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:159
verses.text: This saith Christian, this saith Jew, this saith heathen: him he worshippeth, and with him he curseth!.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:160
verses.text: "Thou hast cleft the fountains and torrents" : in order that they might flow with the stream of wisdom, might flow with the riches of the faith, might water the saltness of the Gentiles, in order that they might convert all unbelievers into the sweetness of the faith by their watering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:161
verses.text: In some men the Word of God becometh a well of water springing up unto life eternal; but others hearing the Word, and not so keeping it as that they live well, yet not keeping silence with tongue, they become torrents.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:162
verses.text: For they are properly called torrents which are not perennial: for sometimes also in a secondary sense torrent is used for river: as hath been said, "with the torrent of Thy pleasures Thou shalt give them to drink".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:163
verses.text: For that torrent shall not ever be dried up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:164
verses.text: But torrents properly are those rivers named, which in summer fail, but with winter rains are flooded and run.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:165
verses.text: Thou seest therefore a man sound in faith, that will persevere even unto the end, that will not forsake God in any trial; for the sake of the truth, not for the sake of falsehood and error, enduring all difficulties.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:166
verses.text: Whence is this man so vigorous, but because the Word hath become in him a well of water springing up unto life eternal? But the other receiveth the Word, he preacheth, he is not silent, he runneth: but summer proveth whether he be fountain or torrent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:167
verses.text: Nevertheless through both be the earth watered, by Him who hath wrought Salvation in the midst of the earth: let the fountains overflow, let the torrents run.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:168
verses.text: "Thou hast dried up the rivers of Etham".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:169
verses.text: What is Etham? For the word is Hebrew.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:170
verses.text: What is Etham interpreted? Strong, stout.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:171
verses.text: Who is this strong and stout one, whose rivers God drieth up? Who but that very dragon? For "no one entereth into the house of a strong man that he may spoil his vessels, unless first he shall have bound fast the strong man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:172
verses.text: This is that strong man on his own virtue relying, and forsaking God: this is that strong man, who saith, "I will set my seat by the north, and I will be like the Most High".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:173
verses.text: Out of that very cup of perverse strength he hath given man to drink.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:174
verses.text: Strong they willed to be, who thought that they would be Gods by means of the forbidden food.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:175
verses.text: Adam became strong, over whom was reproachfully said, "Behold, Adam hath become like one of us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:176
verses.text: As though they were strong, "to the righteousness of God they have not been made subject".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:177
verses.text: Observe ye that a man hath put out of the way his own strength, and remained weak, needy, standing afar off, not daring even to raise his eyes to Heaven; but smiting his breast, and saying, "O Lord, merciful be Thou to me a sinner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:178
verses.text: Now he is weak, now he confesseth his weakness, he is not strong: dry land he is, be he watered with fountains and torrents.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:179
verses.text: They are as yet strong who rely on their own virtue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:180
verses.text: Be their rivers dried up, let there be no advancement in the doctrines of the Gentiles, of wizards, of astrologers, of magic arts: for dried up are the rivers of the strong man: "Thou hast dried up the rivers of Etham".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:181
verses.text: Let there dry up that doctrine; let minds be flooded with the Gospel of truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:182
verses.text: "Thine own is the day and Thine own is the night".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:183
verses.text: Who is ignorant of this, seeing that He hath Himself made all these things; for by the Word were made all things? To that very One Himself who hath wrought Salvation in the midst of the earth, to Him is said, "Thine own is the night".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:184
verses.text: Something here we ought to perceive which belongeth to that very Salvation which He hath wrought in the midst of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:185
verses.text: "Thine own is the day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:186
verses.text: Who are these? The spiritual.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:187
verses.text: "And Thine own is the night".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:188
verses.text: Who are these? The carnal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:189
verses.text: "Thou hast made perfect sun and moon:" the sun, spiritual men, the moon, carnal men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:190
verses.text: As yet carnal he is, may he not be forsaken, and may he too be made perfect.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:191
verses.text: The sun, as it were a wise man: the moon, as it were an unwise man: Thou hast not however forsaken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:192
verses.text: For thus it is written, "A wise man endureth as the sun, but a foolish man as the moon is changed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:193
verses.text: What then? Because the sun endureth, that is, because the wise man endureth as the sun, a foolish man is changed like the moon, is one as yet carnal, as yet unwise, to be forsaken? And where is that which hath been said by the Apostle, "To the wise and unwise a debtor I am"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:194
verses.text: "Thou hast made all the ends of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:195
verses.text: Behold in what manner He hath made the ends of the earth, that hath wrought Salvation in the midst of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:196
verses.text: "Thou hast made all the ends of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:197
verses.text: Summer and spring Thou hast made them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:198
verses.text: Men fervent in the Spirit are the summer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:199
verses.text: Thou, I say, hast made men fervent in the Spirit: Thou hast made also the novices in the Faith, they are the "spring".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:200
verses.text: "Summer and Spring Thou hast made them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:201
verses.text: They shall not glory as if they have not received: "Thou hast made them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:202
verses.text: "Mindful be Thou of this Thy creature".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:203
verses.text: Of what creature of Thine? "The enemy hath reviled the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:204
verses.text: O Asaph, grieve over thine old blindness in understanding: "the enemy hath reviled the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:205
verses.text: It was said to Christ in His own nation, "a sinner is this Man: we know not whence He is:" we know Moses, to him spake God; this Man is a Samaritan "And the unwise people hath provoked Thy name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:206
verses.text: The unwise people Asaph was at that time, but not the understanding of Asaph at that time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:207
verses.text: What is said in the former Psalm? "As it were a beast I have become unto Thee, and I am alway with Thee:" because He went not to the gods and idols of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:208
verses.text: Although he knew not, being like a beast, yet he knew again as a man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:209
verses.text: For he said, "alway I am with Thee, like a beast:" and what afterwards in that place in the same Psalm, where Asaph is? "Thou hast held the hand of my right hand, in Thy will Thou hast conducted me, and with glory Thou hast taken me up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:210
verses.text: In Thy will, not in my righteousness: by Thy gift, not by my work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:211
verses.text: Therefore here also, "the enemy hath reviled the Lord: and the unwise people hath provoked Thy name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:212
verses.text: Have they all then perished? Far be it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:213
verses.text: For even the Apostle Paul through unbelief had been broken, and through faith unto the root he was restored.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:214
verses.text: So evidently "the unwise people provoked Thy name," when it was said, "If Son of God He is let Him come down from the Cross".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:215
verses.text: But what sayest thou, O Asaph, now in understanding? "Deliver not to the beasts a soul confessing to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:216
verses.text: To what beasts, save to those the heads whereof were broken in pieces upon the water? For the same devil is called, beast, lion, and dragon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:217
verses.text: Do not, he saith, give to the Devil and his Angels a soul confessing to Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:218
verses.text: Let the serpent devour, if still I mind things earthly, if for things earthly I long, if still in the promises of the Old Testament, after the revealing of the New, I remain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:219
verses.text: But forasmuch as now I have laid down pride, and my own righteousness I will not acknowledge, but Thy Grace; against me let proud beasts have no power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:220
verses.text: "The souls of Thy poor forget Thou not unto the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:221
verses.text: Rich we were, strong we were: but Thou hast dried up the rivers of Etham: no longer we establish our own righteousness, but we acknowledge Thy Grace; poor we are, hearken to Thy beggars.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:222
verses.text: Now we do not dare to lift our eyes to Heaven, but smiting our breasts we say, "O Lord, be Thou merciful to me a sinner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:223
verses.text: "Have regard unto Thy Testament".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:224
verses.text: Fulfil that which Thou hast promised: the tables we have, for the inheritance we are looking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:225
verses.text: "Have regard unto Thy Testament," not that old one: not for the sake of the land of Canaan I ask, not for the sake of the temporal subduing of enemies, not for the sake of carnal fruitfulness of sons, not for the sake of earthly riches, not for the sake of temporal welfare: "Have regard unto Thy Testament," wherein Thou hast promised the kingdom of Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:226
verses.text: Now I acknowledge Thy Testament: now understanding is Asaph, no beast is Asaph, now he seeth that which was spoken of, "Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, and I will accomplish with the House of Israel and of Juda a new Testament, not after the Testament which I ordered with their Fathers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:227
verses.text: "Have regard unto Thy Testament: for they that have been darkened have been filled of the earth of unrighteous houses:" because they had unrighteous hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:228
verses.text: Our "houses" are our hearts: therein gladly dwell they that are blessed with pure heart "Have regard," therefore, "unto Thy Testament:" and let the remnant be saved: for many men that give heed to earth are darkened, and filled with earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:229
verses.text: For there hath entered into their eyes dust, and it hath blinded them, and they have become dust which the wind sweepeth from the face of the earth "They that have been darkened have been filled of the earth of unrighteous houses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:230
verses.text: For by giving heed to earth they have been darkened, concerning whom there is said in another Psalm, "Let their eyes be blinded, that they see not, and their back ever bow Thou down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:231
verses.text: With earth, then, "they that have been darkened have been filled, with the earth of unrighteous houses:" because they have unrighteous hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:232
verses.text: "Let not the humble man be turned away confounded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:233
verses.text: For them pride hath confounded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:234
verses.text: "The needy and helpless man shall praise Thy name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:235
verses.text: Ye see, brethren, how sweet ought to be poverty: ye see that poor and helpless men belong to God, but "poor in spirit, for of them is the Kingdom of Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:236
verses.text: Who are the poor in spirit? The humble, men trembling at the words of God, confessing their sins, neither on their own merits, nor on their own righteousness relying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:237
verses.text: Who are the poor in spirit? They who when they do anything of good, praise God, when anything of evil, accuse themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:238
verses.text: "Upon whom shall rest My Spirit," saith the Prophet, "but upon the humble man, and peaceful, and trembling at My words?" Now therefore Asaph hath understood, now to the earth he adhereth not, now the earthly promises out of the Old Testament he requireth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:239
verses.text: "Arise, O Lord, judge Thou my cause".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:240
verses.text: Because I am not able to show my God, as if I were following an empty thing, they revile me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:241
verses.text: And not only Heathen, or Jew, or heretic; but sometimes even a Catholic brother doth make a grimace when the promises of God are being preached, when a future resurrection is being foretold And still even he, though already washed with the water of eternal Salvation, bearing the Sacrament of Christ, perchance saith, "and what man hath yet risen again?" And, "I have not heard my father speaking out of the grave, since I buried him!" "God hath given to His servants a law for time, to which let them betake themselves: for what man cometh back from beneath?" And what shall I do with such men? Shall I show them what they see not? I am not able: for not for the sake of them ought God to become visible.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:242
verses.text: I see not, he saith: what am I to believe? Thy soul is seen then, I suppose? Fool, thy body is seen: thy soul who doth see? Since therefore thy body alone is seen, why art thou not buried? He marvelleth that I have said, If body alone is seen, why art thou not buried? And he answereth (for he knoweth as much as this), Because I am alive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:243
verses.text: How know I that thou art alive, of whom I see not the soul? How know I? Thou wilt answer, Because I speak, because I walk, because I work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:244
verses.text: Fool, by the operations of the body I know thee to be living, by the works of creation canst thou not know the Creator? And perchance he that saith, when I shall be dead, afterwards I shall be nothing; hath both learned letters, and hath learned this doctrine from Epicurus, who was a sort of doting philosopher, or rather lover of folly not of wisdom, whom even the philosophers themselves have named the hog: who said that the "chief good" was pleasure of body; this philosopher they have named the hog, wallowing in carnal mire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:245
verses.text: From him perchance this lettered man hath learned to say, I shall not be, after I have died.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:246
verses.text: Dried be the rivers of Etham! Perish those doctrines of the Gentiles, flourish the plantations of Jerusalem! Let them see what they can, in heart believe what they cannot see! Certainly all those things which throughout the world now are seen, when God was working Salvation in the midst of the earth, when those things were being spoken of, they were not then as yet: and behold at that time they were foretold, now they are shown as fulfilled, and still the fool saith in his heart, "there is no God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:247
verses.text: Woe to the perverse hearts: for so will there come to pass the things which remain, as there have come to pass the things which at that time were not, and were being foretold as to come to pass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:248
verses.text: Hath God indeed performed to us all the things which He promised, and concerning the Day of Judgment alone hath He deceived us? Christ was not on the earth; He promised, He hath performed: no virgin had conceived; He promised, He hath performed: the precious Blood had not been shed whereby there should be effaced the handwriting of our death; He promised, He hath performed: not yet had flesh risen again unto life eternal; He promised, He hath performed: not yet had the Gentiles believed; He promised, He hath performed: not yet heretics armed with the name of Christ, against Christ were warring; He foretold, He hath performed: not yet the idols of the Gentiles from the earth had been effaced; He foretold, He hath performed: when all these things He hath foretold and performed, concerning the Day of Judgment alone hath He lied? It will come by all means as these things came; for even these things before they came to pass were future, and as future were first foretold, and afterwards they came to pass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:249
verses.text: It will come, my brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:250
verses.text: Let no one say, it will not come: or, it will come, but far off is that which will come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:251
verses.text: But to thyself it is near at hand to go hence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:252
verses.text: If thou shalt have done that which the devil doth suggest, and shalt have despised that which God hath commanded; there will come the Judgment Day, and thou wilt find that true which God hath threatened, and that false which the devil hath promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:253
verses.text: "Remember Thy reproaches, those which are from the imprudent man all the day long".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:254
verses.text: For still Christ is reviled: nor will there be wanting all the day long, that is, even unto the end of time, the vessels of wrath.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:255
verses.text: Still is it being said, "Vain things the Christians do preach:" still is it being said, "A fond thing is the resurrection of the dead".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:256
verses.text: "Remember Thy reproaches".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:257
verses.text: But what reproaches, save those "which are from the imprudent man all the day long?" Doth a prudent man say this? Nay, for a prudent man is said to be one far-seeing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:258
verses.text: If a prudent man is one far-seeing, by faith he seeth afar: for with eyes scarce that before the feet is seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:259
verses.text: "Forget not the voice of them that implore Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:260
verses.text: While they groan for and expect now that which Thou hast promised from the New Testament, and walk by that same Faith, "do Thou not forget the voice of them imploring Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:261
verses.text: But those still say, "Where is Thy God? Let the pride of them that hate Thee come up always to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:262
verses.text: Do not forget even their pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 76:263
verses.text: Nor doth He forget: no doubt He doth either punish or amend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:2
verses.text: The Title of this Psalm thus speaketh: "At the end, corrupt not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:3
verses.text: What is, "corrupt not?" That which Thou hast promised, perform.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:4
verses.text: But when? "At the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:5
verses.text: To this then let the mind's eye be directed, "unto the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:6
verses.text: Let all the things which have occurred in the way be passed over, in order that we may attain to the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:7
verses.text: Let proud men exult because of present felicity, let them swell with honours, glitter in gold, overflow with domestics, be encircled with the services of clients: these things pass away, they pass away like a shadow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:8
verses.text: When that end shall have come, when all who now hope in the Lord are to rejoice, then to them shall come sorrow without end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:9
verses.text: When the meek shall have received that which the proud deride, then the vapouring of the proud shall be turned into mourning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:10
verses.text: Then shall there be that voice which we know in the Book of Wisdom: for they shall say at that time when they see the glory of the Saints, who, when they were in humiliation, endured them; who, when they were exalted, consented not—at that time then they shall say, "These are they whom sometime we have had in derision".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:11
verses.text: Where they also say, "What hath pride profited us, and the boasting of riches hath bestowed upon us what?" All things have passed away like a shadow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:12
verses.text: Because on things corruptible they relied, their hope shall be corrupted: but our own hope at that time shall be substance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:13
verses.text: For in order that the promise of God may remain whole and sure and certain towards us, we have said out of a heart of faith, "at the end corrupt not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:14
verses.text: Fear not, therefore, lest any mighty man should corrupt the promises of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:15
verses.text: He doth not corrupt, because He is truthful; He hath no one more mighty by whom His promise may be corrupted: let us  be then sure concerning the promises of God; and let us sing now from the place where the Psalm beginneth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:16
verses.text: "We will confess to Thee, O Lord, we will confess to Thee, and will invoke Thy name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:17
verses.text: Do not invoke, before thou confess: confess, and invoke.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:18
verses.text: For Him whom thou art invoking, unto thyself thou callest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:19
verses.text: For what is it to invoke, but unto thyself to call? If He is invoked by thee, that is, if He is called to thee, unto whom doth He draw near? To a proud man He draweth not near.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:20
verses.text: High indeed He is, one lifted up attaineth not unto Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:21
verses.text: In order that we may reach all exalted objects, we raise ourselves, and if we are not able to reach them, we look for some appliances or ladders, in order that being exalted we may reach exalted objects: contrariwise God is both high, and by the lowly He is reached.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:22
verses.text: It is written, "Nigh is the Lord to them that have bruised the heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:23
verses.text: The bruising of the heart is Godliness, humility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:24
verses.text: He that bruiseth himself is angry with himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:25
verses.text: Let him make himself angry in order that he may make Him merciful; let him make himself judge, in order that he may make Him Advocate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:26
verses.text: Therefore God doth come when invoked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:27
verses.text: Unto whom doth He come? To the proud man He cometh not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:28
verses.text: Take heed therefore what ye do: for if He knoweth, He is not unobservant It is better therefore that He be unobservant than known.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:29
verses.text: For what is that same being unobservant, but not knowing? What is, not to know? Not to animadvert.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:30
verses.text: For even as the act of one avenging animadversion is wont to be spoken of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:31
verses.text: Here one praying that He be unobservant: "Turn away Thy face from my sins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:32
verses.text: What then wilt thou do if He shall have turned away His face from thee? A grievous thing it is, and to be feared, lest He forsake thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:33
verses.text: Again, if He turn not away His face, He animadverteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:34
verses.text: God knoweth this thing, God can do this thing, namely, both turn away face from one sinning, and not turn away from one confessing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:35
verses.text: Confess therefore and invoke.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:36
verses.text: For by confessing thou purgest the Temple, into which He may come, when invoked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:37
verses.text: Confess and invoke.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:38
verses.text: May He turn away face from thy sins, not turn away from thee: turn away face from that which thou hast wrought, not turn away from that which He hath Himself wrought For thee, as man, He hath Himself wrought, thy sins thou hast thyself wrought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:39
verses.text: But that there is a strengthening of the sense in repetition, by many passages of the Scriptures we are taught.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:40
verses.text: Thence is that which the Lord saith, "Verily, Verily".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:41
verses.text: Thence in certain Psalms is, "So be it, So be it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:42
verses.text: To signify the thing, one "So be it" would have been sufficient: to signify confirmation, there hath been added another "So be it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:43
verses.text: Countless passages of such sort there are throughout all the Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:44
verses.text: With these it is sufficient that we have commended to your notice a way of speaking which ye may observe in all like cases: now to the substance attend: "We will confess to Thee," he saith, "and we will invoke".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:45
verses.text: I have said why before invocation confession doth precede: because whom thou dost invoke, him thou dost invite.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:46
verses.text: But he willeth not to come when invoked, if thou shalt have been lifted up: lifted up if thou shalt have been, thou wilt not be able to confess.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:47
verses.text: And thou deniest not any things to God that He knoweth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:48
verses.text: Therefore thy confession doth not teach Him, but it purgeth thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:49
verses.text: Hear ye now the words of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:50
verses.text: For these seemed not as it were to be His words, "We will confess to Thee, O God, we will confess to Thee, and will invoke Thy name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:51
verses.text: Now beginneth the discourse in the person of the Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:52
verses.text: But whether Head speaketh or whether members speak, Christ speaketh: He speaketh in the person of the Head, He speaketh in the person of the Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:53
verses.text: But what hath been said? There shall be two in one flesh "This is a great Sacrament:" "I," he saith, "speak in Christ and in the Church".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:54
verses.text: And He Himself in the Gospel, "Therefore no longer two, but one flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:55
verses.text: For in order that ye may know these in a manner to be two persons, and again one by the bond of marriage, as one He speaketh in Isaiah, and saith, "As upon a Bridegroom he hath bound upon me a mitre, and as a Bride he hath clothed me with an ornament".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:56
verses.text: A Bridegroom He hath called Himself in the Head, a Bride in the Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:57
verses.text: He is speaking therefore as One, let us hear Him, and in Him let us also speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:58
verses.text: Let us be the members of Him, in order that this voice may possibly be ours also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:59
verses.text: "I will tell forth," he saith, "all Thy marvellous things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:60
verses.text: Christ is preaching Himself, He is preaching Himself even in His members now existing, in order that He may guide unto Him others, and they may draw near that were not, and may be united with those members of Him, through which members of Him the Gospel hath been preached; and there may be made one Body under one Head, in one Spirit, in one Life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:61
verses.text: And he saith what? "When I shall have received," he saith, "the time, I will judge justices".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:62
verses.text: When shall He judge justices? When He shall have received the time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:63
verses.text: Not yet is the precise time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:64
verses.text: Thanks to His mercy: He first preacheth justices, and then He judgeth justices.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:65
