verses.text: For if He willed to judge before He willed to preach, who would be found that should be delivered: who would meet Him that should be absolved? Now therefore is the time of preaching: "I will tell," he saith, "all Thy marvellous works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:66
verses.text: Hear Him telling, hear Him preaching: for if thou shalt have despised Him, "when I shall have received the time," He saith, "I will judge justices".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:67
verses.text: I forgive, He saith, now sins to one confessing, I will not spare hereafter one despising.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:68
verses.text: He hath received a time as Son of Man; He doth govern times as Son of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:69
verses.text: Hear how as Son of Man He hath received the time of judging.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:70
verses.text: He saith in the Gospel, "He hath given to Him power to execute judgment, because Son of Man He is".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:71
verses.text: According to His nature as Son of God, He hath never received power of judging, because He never lacked the power of judging: according to His nature as Son of Man He hath received a time, as of being born, and of suffering, as of dying, and of rising again, and of ascending, so of coming and of judging.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:72
verses.text: In Him His Body also saith these words, for not without them He will judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:73
verses.text: For He saith in the Gospel, "Ye shall sit upon twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:74
verses.text: Therefore whole Christ saith, that is, Head and Body in the Saints, "when I shall have received the time, I will judge justices".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:75
verses.text: But now what? "The earth hath flowed down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:76
verses.text: If the earth hath flowed down, whence hath it flowed down except by sins? Therefore also they are called delinquencies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:77
verses.text: To delinquish is as it were by a kind of liquidity to slip down from the stability of firmness in virtue and righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:78
verses.text: For it is through desire of lower things that every man sinneth: as he is strengthened by the love of higher things, so he falleth down and as it were melteth away by desire of lower things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:79
verses.text: This flux of things by the sins of man the merciful forgiver observing, being a merciful forgiver of sins, not yet an exactor of punishments, He observeth and saith: The earth herself indeed hath flowed down by them that dwell in her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:80
verses.text: That which followeth is an exposition, not an addition.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:81
verses.text: As though thou wert saying, in what manner hath the earth flowed down? Have the foundations been withdrawn, and hath anything therein been swallowed up in a sort of gulf? What I mean by earth is all they that dwell therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:82
verses.text: I have found, he saith, the earth sinful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:83
verses.text: And I have done what? "I have strengthened the pillars thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:84
verses.text: What are the pillars which He hath strengthened? Pillars He hath called the Apostles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:85
verses.text: So the Apostle Paul concerning his fellow-Apostles saith, "who seemed to be pillars".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:86
verses.text: And what would those pillars have been, except by Him they had been strengthened? For on occasion of a sort of earthquake even these very pillars rocked: at the Passion of the Lord all the Apostles despaired.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:87
verses.text: Therefore those pillars which rocked at the Passion of the Lord, by the Resurrection were strengthened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:88
verses.text: The Beginning of the building hath cried out through the pillars thereof, and in all those pillars the Architect Himself hath cried out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:89
verses.text: For the Apostle Paul was one pillar of them when he said, "Would ye receive a proof of Him that speaketh in me—Christ?" Therefore, "I," he saith, "have strengthened the pillars thereof:" I have risen again, I have shown that death is not to be feared, I have shown to them that fear, that not even the body itself doth perish in the dying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:90
verses.text: There terrified them wounds, there strengthened them scars.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:91
verses.text: The Lord Jesus could have risen again without any scar: for what great matter were it for that power, to restore the frame of the body to such perfect soundness, as that no trace at all of past wound should appear? He had power whence He might make it whole even without scar: but He willed to have that whereby He might strengthen the rocking pillars.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:92
verses.text: We have heard now, brethren, that which day by day is not kept secret: let us hear now what He hath cried through these pillars.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:93
verses.text: He crieth what? "I have said to unjust men, Do not unjustly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:94
verses.text: But already they have done, and they are guilty: already there hath flowed down the earth, and all they that dwell therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:95
verses.text: Pricked to the heart were they that crucified Christ, they acknowledged their sin, they learned something of the Apostle, that they might not despair of the pardon of the Preacher For as Physician He had come, and therefore had not come to the whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:96
verses.text: "For there is no need," He saith, "to the whole of a physician, but to them that are sick.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:97
verses.text: I have not come to call righteous men, but sinners to repentance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:98
verses.text: Therefore, "I have said to unjust men, Do not unjustly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:99
verses.text: They heard not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:100
verses.text: For of old to us it was spoken: we heard not, we fell, were made mortal, were begotten mortal: the earth flowed down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:101
verses.text: Let them hear the Physician even now in order that they may rise, Him that came to the sick man, Him whom they would not hear when whole in order that they might not fall, let them hear when lying down in order that they may rise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:102
verses.text: "I have said to unjust men, Do not unjustly; and to the delinquent, Do not exalt your horn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:103
verses.text: There shall be exalted in you the horn of Christ, if your horn be not exalted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:104
verses.text: Your horn is of iniquity, the horn of Christ is of majesty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:105
verses.text: "Be not therefore lifted up: speak not iniquity against God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:106
verses.text: What saith He in another Psalm? "These things thou hast done," having enumerated certain sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:107
verses.text: "These things thou hast done," He saith, "and was silent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:108
verses.text: What is, "I was silent"? He is never silent with commandment, but meanwhile He is silent with punishment: He is keeping still from vengeance, He doth not pronounce sentence against the condemned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:109
verses.text: But this man saith thus, I have done such and such things, and God hath not taken vengeance; behold I am whole, nought of ill hath befallen me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:110
verses.text: "These things thou hast done, and I was silent: thou hast suspected iniquity, that I shall be like unto thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:111
verses.text: What is, "that I shall be like unto thee"? Because thou art unjust, even Me thou hast deemed unjust; as though an approver of thy misdeeds, and no adversary, no avenger thereof.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:112
verses.text: And what afterwards saith He to thee? "I will convict thee, and will set thee before thine own face"? What is this? Because now by sinning behind thy back thou settest thyself, seest not thyself, examinest not thyself; I will set thee before thyself, and will bring upon thee punishment from thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:113
verses.text: So also here, "Speak not iniquity against God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:114
verses.text: Attend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:115
verses.text: Many men speak this iniquity; but dare not openly, lest as blasphemers they be abhorred by godly men: in their heart they gnaw upon these things, within they feed upon such impious food; it delighteth them to speak against G od, and if they break not out with tongue, in heart they are not silent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:116
verses.text: Whence in another Psalm is said, "The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:117
verses.text: The fool hath said, but he hath feared men: he would not say it where men might hear; and he said it in that pl ace where He might Himself hear concerning whom he said it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:118
verses.text: Therefore here also in this Psalm (dearly beloved attend), whereas that which He said, "Do not speak iniquity against God," this He saw many men do in heart, He hath also added, "for neither from East, nor from West, nor from the deserts of the mountains , for God is Judge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:119
verses.text: Of thine iniquities God is Judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:120
verses.text: If God He is, everywhere He is present.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:121
verses.text: Whither wilt thou take thyself away from the eyes of God, so that in some quarter thou mayest speak that which He may not hear? If from the East God judgeth, withdraw into the West, and say what thou wilt against God: if from the West, go into the East, and there speak: if from the deserts of the mountains He judgeth, go into the midst of the peoples, where thou mayest murmur to thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:122
verses.text: From no place judgeth He that everywhere is secret, everywhere open; whom it is allowed no one to know as He is, and whom no one is permitted not to know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:123
verses.text: Take heed what thou doest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:124
verses.text: Thou art speaking iniquity against God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:125
verses.text: "The Spirit of the Lord hath filled the round world" (another Scripture saith this), "and that which containeth all things hath knowledge of the voice: wherefore he that speaketh unjust things cannot be hid".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:126
verses.text: Do not therefore think God to be in places: He is with thee such an one as thou shalt have been.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:127
verses.text: What is such an one as thou shalt have been? Good, if thou shalt have been good; and evil to thee He will seem, if evil thou shalt have been; but a Helper, if good thou shalt have been; an Avenger, if evil thou shalt have been.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:128
verses.text: There thou hast a Judge in thy secret place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:129
verses.text: Willing to do something of evil, from the public thou retirest into thy house, where no enemy may see; from those places of thine house which are open and before the eyes of men, thou removest thyself into a chamber; thou fearest even in thy chamber some witness from some other quarter, thou retirest into thy heart, there thou meditatest: He is more inward than thy heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:130
verses.text: Whithersoever therefore thou shalt have fled, there He is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:131
verses.text: From thyself whither wilt thou flee? Wilt thou not follow thyself whithersoever thou shalt flee? But since there is One more inward even than thyself, there is no place whither thou mayest flee from God angry, but to God reconciled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:132
verses.text: There is no place at all whither thou mayest flee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:133
verses.text: Wilt thou flee from Him? Flee to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:134
verses.text: What then shall we do now? "Let us come before His face," ἐν ἐξομολογήσει, come before in confession: He shall come gentle whom thou hadst made angry.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:135
verses.text: "Neither from the deserts of the mountains, for God is Judge:" not from the East, not from the West, not from the deserts of the mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:136
verses.text: Wherefore? "For God is Judge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:137
verses.text: If in any place He were, He would not be God: but because God is Judge, not man, do not expect Him out of places.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:138
verses.text: His place thou wilt be, if thou art good, if after having confessed thou shalt have invoked Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:139
verses.text: "One He humbleth, and another He exalteth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:140
verses.text: Whom humbleth, whom exalteth this Judge? Observe these two men in the temple, and ye see whom He humbleth and whom He exalteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:141
verses.text: "They went up into the Temple to pray," He saith, "the one a Pharisee, and the other a Publican.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:142
verses.text: "Verily I say unto you, that Publican went down justified more than that Pharisee: for every one that exalteth himself shall be humbled; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:143
verses.text: Thus hath been explained a verse of this Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:144
verses.text: God the Judge doth what? "One He humbleth, and another He exalteth:" He humbleth the proud, He exalteth the humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:145
verses.text: "For the cup in the hand of the Lord of pure wine is full of mixed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:146
verses.text: Justly so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:147
verses.text: "And He hath poured out of this upon this man; nevertheless, the dreg thereof hath not been emptied; there shall drink all the sinners of earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:148
verses.text: Let us be somewhat recruited; there is here some obscurity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:149
verses.text: The first question that meeteth us is this, "of pure wine it is full of mixed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:150
verses.text: How "of pure," if "of mixed"? But when he saith, "the cup in the hand of the Lord" (to men instructed in the Church of Christ I am speaking), ye ought not indeed to paint in your heart God as it were circumscribed with a human form, lest, though the temples are shut up, ye forge images in your hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:151
verses.text: This cup therefore doth signify something.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:152
verses.text: We will find out this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:153
verses.text: But "in the hand of the Lord," is, in the power of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:154
verses.text: For the hand of God is spoken of for the power of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:155
verses.text: For even in reference to men ofttimes is said, in hand he hath it: that is, in his power he hath it, when he chooseth he doth it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:156
verses.text: "Of pure wine it is full of mixed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:157
verses.text: In continuation he hath himself explained: "He hath inclined," he saith, "from this unto this man; nevertheless the dreg thereof hath not been emptied".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:158
verses.text: Behold how it was full of mixed wine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:159
verses.text: Let it not therefore terrify you that it is both pure and mixed: pure because of the genuineness thereof, mixed because of the dreg.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:160
verses.text: What then in that place is the wine, and what the dreg? And what is, "He hath inclined from this unto this man," in such sort that the dreg thereof was not emptied?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:161
verses.text: Call ye to mind from whence he came to this: "one He humbleth, and another He exalteth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:162
verses.text: That which was figured to us in the Gospel through two men, a Pharisee and a Publican, this let us, taking in a wider sense, understand of two peoples, of Jews and of Gentiles: the people of the Jews that Pharisee was, the people of the Gentiles that Publican.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:163
verses.text: As those by being proud have withdrawn, so these by confessing have drawn near.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:164
verses.text: The cup therefore full of pure wine in the hand of the Lord, as far as the Lord giveth me to understand,the cup of pure wine full of the mixed, seemeth to me to be the Law, which was given to the Jews, and all that Scripture of the Old Testament, as it is called; there are the weights of all manner of sentences.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:165
verses.text: For therein the New Testament lieth concealed, as though in the dreg of corporal Sacraments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:166
verses.text: The circumcision of the flesh is a thing of great mystery, and there is understood from thence the circumcision of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:167
verses.text: The Temple of Jerusalem is a thing of great mystery, and there is understood from it the Body of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:168
verses.text: The land of promise is understood to be the Kingdom of Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:169
verses.text: The sacrifice of victims and of beasts hath a great mystery: but in all those kinds of sacrifices is understood that one Sacrifice and only victim of the Cross, the Lord, instead of all which sacrifices we have one; because even those figured these, that is, with those these were figured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:170
verses.text: That people received the Law, they received commandments just and good What is so just as, thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not speak false testimony, honour thy father and mother, thou shalt not covet the property of thy neighbour, one God thou shalt adore, and Him alone thou shalt serve, all these things belong to the wine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:171
verses.text: But those things carnal have as it were sunk down in order that they might remain with them, and there might be poured forth from thence all the spiritual understanding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:172
verses.text: But "the cup in the hand of the Lord," that is, in the power of the Lord: "of pure wine," that is, of the mere Law: "is full of mixed," that is, is together with the dreg of corporal Sacraments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:173
verses.text: And because the one He humbleth, the proud Jew, and the other He exalteth, the confessing Gentile; "He hath inclined from this unto this," that is, from the Jewish people unto the Gentile people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:174
verses.text: Hath inclined what? The Law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:175
verses.text: There hath distilled from thence a spiritual sense.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:176
verses.text: "Nevertheless, the dreg thereof hath not been emptied," for all the carnal Sacraments have remained with the Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:177
verses.text: "There shall drink all the sinners of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:178
verses.text: Who shall drink? "All the sinners of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:179
verses.text: Who are the sinners of the earth? The Jews were indeed sinners, but proud: again, the Gentiles were sinners, but humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:180
verses.text: All sinners shall drink, but see, who the dreg, who the wine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:181
verses.text: For those by drinking the dreg have come to nought: these by drinking the wine have been justified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:182
verses.text: I would dare to speak of them even as inebriated, and I shall not fear: and O that all ye were thus inebriated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:183
verses.text: Call to mind, "Thy cup inebriating, how passing beautiful!" But why? Do ye think, my brethren, that all those who by confessing Christ even willed to die, were sober? So drunk they were, that they knew not their friends.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:184
verses.text: All their kindred, who strove to divert them from the hope of Heavenly rewards by earthly allurements, were not acknowledged, were not heard by them drunken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:185
verses.text: Were they not drunken, whose heart had been changed? Were they not drunken, whose mind had been alienated from this world? "There shall drink," he saith, "all the sinners of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:186
verses.text: But who shall drink the wine? Sinners shall drink, but in order that they may not remain sinners; in order that they may be justified, in order that they may not be punished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:187
verses.text: "But I," for all  drink, but separately I, that is, Christ with His Body, "for ever will rejoice, I will Psalm to the God of Jacob" : in that promise to be at the end, whereof is said, "corrupt not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:188
verses.text: "And all the horns of sinners I will break, and there shall be exalted the horns of the Just".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:189
verses.text: This is, the one He humbleth, the other He exalteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:190
verses.text: Sinners would not have their horns to be broken, which without doubt will be broken at the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:191
verses.text: Thou wilt not have Him then break them, do thou to-day break them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:192
verses.text: For thou hast heard above, do not despise it: "I have said to unjust men, Do not unjustly, and to the delinquents, Do not exalt the horn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:193
verses.text: When thou hast heard, do not exalt the horn, thou hast despised and hast exalted the horn: thou shalt come to the end, where there shall come to pass, "All the horns of sinners I will break, and there shall be exalted the horns of the Just".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:194
verses.text: The horns of sinners are the dignities of proud men: the horns of the Just are the gifts of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:195
verses.text: For by horns exultations are understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:196
verses.text: Thou hatest on earth earthly exultation, in order that thou mayest have the heavenly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:197
verses.text: Thou lovest the earthly, He doth not admit thee to the Heavenly: and unto confusion will belong thy horn which is broken, just as unto glory it will belong, if thy horn is exalted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:198
verses.text: Now therefore there is time for making choice, then there will not be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:199
verses.text: Thou wilt not say, I will be let go and will make choice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:200
verses.text: For there have preceded the words, "I have said to the unjust".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 77:201
verses.text: If I have not said, make ready an excuse, make ready a defence: but if I have said, seize first upon confession, lest thou come unto damnation; for then confession will be too late, and there will be no defence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXVI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:2
verses.text: The Jews are wont to glory in this Psalm which we have sung, saying, "Known in Judaea is God, in Israel great is the name of Him:" and to revile the Gentiles to whom God is not known, and to say that to themselves alone God is known; seeing that the Prophet saith, "Known in Judaea is God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:3
verses.text: In other places therefore He is unknown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:4
verses.text: But God is known in very deed in Judaea, if they understand what is Judaea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:5
verses.text: For indeed God is not known except in Judaea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:6
verses.text: Behold even we say this, that except a person shall have been in Judaea, known to him God cannot be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:7
verses.text: But what saith the Apostle? He that in secret is a Jew, he that is so in circumcision of the heart, not in letter but in spirit There are therefore Jews in circumcision of the flesh, and there are Jews in circumcision of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:8
verses.text: Many of our holy fathers had both the circumcision of the flesh, for a seal of the faith, and circumcision of the heart, for the faith itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:9
verses.text: From these fathers these men degenerating, who now in the name do glory, and have lost their deeds; from these fathers, I say, degenerating, they have remained Jews in flesh, in heart Heathens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:10
verses.text: For these are Jews, who are out of Abraham, from whom Isaac was born, and out of him Jacob, and out of Jacob the twelve Patriarchs, and out of the twelve Patriarchs the whole people of the Jews But they were generally called Jews for this reason, that Judah was one of the twelve sons of Jacob, a Patriarch among the twelve, and from his stock the Royalty came among the Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:11
verses.text: For all this people after the number of the twelve sons of Jacob, had twelve tribes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:12
verses.text: What we call tribes are as it were distinct houses and congregations of people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:13
verses.text: That people, I say, had twelve tribes, out of which twelve tribes one tribe was Judah, out of which were the kings; and there was another tribe, Levi, out of which were the priests.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:14
verses.text: But because to the priests serving the temple no land was allotted, but it was necessary that among twelve tribes all the Land of promise should be shared: there having been therefore taken out one tribe of higher dignity, the tribe of Levi, which was of the priests, there would have remained eleven, unless by the adoption of the two sons of Joseph the number twelve were completed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:15
verses.text: What this is, observe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:16
verses.text: One of the twelve sons of Jacob was Joseph.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:17
verses.text: This Joseph had two sons, Ephraim and Manasse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:18
verses.text: Jacob, dying, as though by will, received those his grandsons into the number of sons, and said to his son Joseph, "The rest that are born shall be to thee; but these to me, and they shall divide the land with their brethren".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:19
verses.text: As yet there had not been given nor divided the land of promise, but he was speaking in the Spirit, prophesying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:20
verses.text: The two sons therefore of Joseph being added, there were made up nevertheless twelve tribes, since now there are thirteen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:21
verses.text: For instead of one tribe of Joseph, two were added, and there were made thirteen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:22
verses.text: There being taken out then the tribe of Levi, that tribe of priests which did serve the Temple, and lived by the tithes of all the rest unto whom the land was divided, there remain twelve.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:23
verses.text: In these twelve was the tribe of Judah, whence the kings were.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:24
verses.text: For at first from another tribe was given King Saul, and he was rejected as being an evil king; after there was given from the tribe of Judah King David, and out of him from the tribe of Judah were the Kings But Jacob had spoken of this, when he blessed his sons, "there shall not fail a prince out of Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until there come He to whom the promise hath been made".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:25
verses.text: But from the tribe of Judah there came Our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:26
verses.text: For He is, as the Scripture saith, and as ye have but now heard, out of the seed of David born of Mary But as regardeth the Divinity of our Lord Jesus Christ, wherein He is equal with the Father, He is not only before the Jews, but also before Abraham himself; nor only before Abraham, but also before Adam; nor only before Adam, but also before Heaven and earth and before ages: for all things by Himself were made, and without Him there was made nothing Because therefore in prophecy hath been said, "there shall not fail a prince out of Judah," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:27
verses.text: : former times are examined, and we find that the Jews always had their kings of the tribe of Judah, and had no foreign king before that Herod who was king when the Lord was born.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:28
verses.text: Thence began foreign kings, from Herod Before Herod all were of the tribe of Judah, but only until there should come He to whom the promise had been made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:29
verses.text: Therefore when the Lord Himself came, the kingdom of the Jews was overthrown, and removed from the Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:30
verses.text: Now they have no king; because they will not acknowledge the true King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:31
verses.text: See now whether they must be called Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:32
verses.text: Now ye do see that they must not be called Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:33
verses.text: They have themselves with their own voice resigned that name, so that they are not worthy to be called Jews, except only in the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:34
verses.text: When did they sever themselves from the name? They said, "We have no king but Caesar".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:35
verses.text: O ye who are called Jews and are not, if ye have no king but Caesar, there hath failed a Prince of Judah: there hath come then He to whom the promise hath been made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:36
verses.text: They then are more truly Jews, who have been made Christians out of Jews: the rest of the Jews, who in Christ have not believed, have deserved to lose even the very name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:37
verses.text: The true Judaea, then, is the Church of Christ, believing in that King, who hath come out of the tribe of Judah through the Virgin Mary; believing in Him of whom the Apostle was just now speaking, in writing to Timothy, "Be thou mindful that Jesus Christ hath risen from the dead, of the seed of David, after my Gospel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:38
verses.text: For of Judah is David, and out of David is the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:39
verses.text: We believing in Christ do belong to Judah: and we acknowledge Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:40
verses.text: We, that with eyes have not seen, in faith do keep Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:41
verses.text: Let not therefore the Jews revile, who are no longer Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:42
verses.text: They said themselves, "We have no king but Caesar".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:43
verses.text: For better were it for them that their king should be Christ, of the seed of David, of the tribe of Judah.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:44
verses.text: Nevertheless because Christ Himself is of the seed of David after the flesh, but God above all things blessed for ever, He is Himself our King and our God; our King, inasmuch as born of the tribe of Judah, after the flesh, was Christ the Lord, the Saviour; but our God, who is before Judah, and before Heaven and earth, by whom were made all things, both spiritual and corporal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:45
verses.text: For if all things by Himself were made; even Mary herself, out of whom He was born, by Himself was made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:46
verses.text: "Known in Judaea is God, in Israel great is the Name of Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:47
verses.text: Concerning Israel also we ought so to take it as we have concerning Judaea: as they were not the true Jews, so neither was that the true Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:48
verses.text: For what is Israel said to be? One seeing God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:49
verses.text: And how have they seen God, among whom He walked in the flesh; and while they supposed Him to be man, they slew Him?"In Israel great is His Name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:50
verses.text: Wilt thou be Israel? Observe that man concerning whom the Lord saith, "Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom guile is not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:51
verses.text: If a true Israelite is he in whom guile is not, the guileful and lying are not true Israelites.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:52
verses.text: Let them not say then, that with them is God, and great is His name in Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:53
verses.text: Let them prove themselves Israelites, and I grant that "in Israel great is His Name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:54
verses.text: "And there hath been made in peace a place for Him, and His habitation is in Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:55
verses.text: Again, Sion is as it were the country of the Jews; the true Sion is the Church of Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:56
verses.text: But the interpretation of the Hebrew names is thus handed down to us: Judaea is interpreted confession, Israel, one seeing God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:57
verses.text: After Judaea is Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:58
verses.text: Wilt thou see God? First do thou confess, and then in thyself there is made a place for God; because "there hath been made in peace a place for Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:59
verses.text: So long as then thou confessest not thy sins, in a manner thou art quarrelling with God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:60
verses.text: For how art thou not disputing with Him, who art praising that which displeaseth Him? He punisheth a thief, thou dost praise theft: He doth punish a drunken man, thou dost praise drunkenness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:61
verses.text: Thou art disputing with God, thou hast not made for Him a place in thy heart: because in peace is His place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:62
verses.text: And how dost thou begin to have peace with God? Thou beginnest with Him in confession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:63
verses.text: There is a voice of a Psalm, saying, "Begin ye to the Lord in confession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:64
verses.text: What is, "Begin ye to the Lord in confession"? Begin ye to be joined to the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:65
verses.text: In what manner? So that the same thing may displease you as displeaseth Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:66
verses.text: There displeaseth Him thy evil life; if it please thyself, thou art disunited from Him; if it displease thee, through confession to Him thou art united.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:67
verses.text: "There He hath broken the strength of bows, and the shield, and the sword, and the battle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:68
verses.text: Where hath He broken? In that eternal peace, in that perfect peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:69
verses.text: And now, my brethren, they that have rightly believed see that they ought not to rely on themselves: and all the might of their own menaces, and whatsoever is in them whetted for mischief, this they break in pieces; and whatsoever they deem of great virtue wherewith to protect themselves temporally, and the war which they were waging against God by defending their sins, all these things He hath broken there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:70
verses.text: "Thou enlightening marvellously from the eternal mountains".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:71
verses.text: What are the eternal mountains? Those which He hath Himself made eternal; which are the great mountains, the preachers of truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:72
verses.text: Thou dost enlighten, but from the eternal mountains: the great mountains are first to receive Thy light, and from Thy light which the mountains receive, the earth also is clothed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:73
verses.text: But those great mountains the Apostles have received, the Apostles have receiv ed as it were the first streaks of the rising light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:74
verses.text: Wherefore also, in another place, a Psalm saith what? "I have lifted up mine eyes unto the mountains, whence there shall come help to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:75
verses.text: What then, in the mountains is thy hope, and from thence to thee shall there come help? Hast thou stayed at the mountains? Take heed what thou doest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:76
verses.text: There is something above the mountains: above the mountains is He at whom the mountains tremble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:77
verses.text: "I have lifted up," he saith, "mine eyes unto the mountains, whence there shall come help to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:78
verses.text: But what followeth? "My help," he saith, "is from the Lord, who hath made Heaven and earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:79
verses.text: Unto the mountains indeed I have lifted up eyes, because through the mountains to me the Scriptures were displayed: but I have my heart in Him that doth enlighten all mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:80
verses.text: "There have been troubled all the unwise in heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:81
verses.text: How have they been troubled? When the Gospel is preached.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:82
verses.text: And what is life eternal? And who is He that hath risen from the dead? The Athenians wondered, when the Apostle Paul spake of the resurrection of the dead, and thought that he spake but fables But because he said that there was another life which neither eye hath seen, nor ear heard, nor hath it gone up into the heart of man, therefore the unwise in heart were troubled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:83
verses.text: But what hath befallen them? "They have slept their sleep, and all men of riches have found nothing in their hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:84
verses.text: They have loved things present, and have gone to sleep in the midst of things present: and so these very present things have become to them delightful: just as he that seeth in a dream himself to have found treasure, is so long rich as he waketh not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:85
verses.text: The dream hath made him rich, waking hath made him poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:86
verses.text: Sleep perchance hath held him slumbering on the earth, and lying on the hard ground, poor and perchance a beggar; in sleep he hath seen himself to lie on an ivory or golden bed, and on feathers heaped up; so long as he is sleeping, he is sleeping well, waking he hath found himself on the hard ground, whereon sleep had taken him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:87
verses.text: Such men also are these too: they have come into this life, and through temporal desires, they have as it were slumbered here; and them riches, and vain pomps that fly away, have taken, and they have passed away: they have not understood how much of good might be done therewith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:88
verses.text: For if they had known of another life, there they would have laid up unto themselves the treasure which here was doomed to perish: like as Zacchaeus, the chief of the Publicans, saw that good when he received the Lord Jesus in his house, and he saith, "The half of my goods I give to the poor, and if to any man I have done any wrong, fourfold I restore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:89
verses.text: This man was not in the emptiness of men dreaming, but in the faith of men awake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:90
verses.text: "By Thy chiding, O God of Jacob, there have slept all men that have mounted horses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:91
verses.text: Who are they that have mounted horses? They that would not be humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:92
verses.text: To sit on horseback is no sin; but it is a sin to lift up the neck of power against God, and to deem one's self to be in some distinction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:93
verses.text: Because thou art rich, thou hast mounted; God doth chide, and thou sleepest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:94
verses.text: Great is the anger of Him chiding, great the anger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:95
verses.text: Let your Love observe the terrible thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:96
verses.text: Chiding hath noise, the noise is wont to make men wake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:97
verses.text: So great is the force of God chiding, that he said, "By Thy chiding, O God of Jacob, there have slept all men that have mounted horses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:98
verses.text: Behold what a sleep that Pharaoh slept who mounted horses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:99
verses.text: For he was not awake in heart, because against chiding he had his heart hardened For hardness of heart is slumber.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:100
verses.text: I ask you, my brethren, how they sleep, who, while the Gospel is sounding, and the Amen, and the Hallelujah, throughout the whole world, yet will not condemn their old life, and wake up unto a new life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:101
verses.text: There was the Scripture of God in Judaea only, now throughout the whole world it is sung.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:102
verses.text: In that one nation one God who made all things was spoken of, as to be adored and worshipped; now where is He unsaid? Christ hath risen again, though derided on the Cross; that very Cross whereon He was derided, He hath now imprinted on the brows of kings: and men yet sleep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:103
verses.text: "Thou art terrible, and who shall withstand Thee at that time by Thine anger?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:104
verses.text: Now they sleep, and perceive not Thee angry; but for cause that they should sleep, He was angry.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:105
verses.text: Now that which sleeping they perceived not, at the end they shall perceive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:106
verses.text: For there shall appear the Judge of quick and dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:107
verses.text: "And who shall withstand Thee at that time by Thine anger?" For now they speak that which they will, and they dispute against God and say, who are the Christians? or who is Christ? or what fools are they that believe that which they see not, and relinquish the pleasures which they see, and follow the faith of things which are not displayed to their eyes! Ye sleep and snore, ye speak against God, as much as ye are able.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:108
verses.text: "How long shall sinners, O Lord, how long shall sinners glory, they answer and will speak iniquity?" But when doth no one answer and no one speak, except when he turneth himself against himself?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:109
verses.text: "From Heaven Thou hast hurled judgment: the earth hath trembled, and hath rested".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:110
verses.text: She which now doth trouble herself, she which now speaketh, hath to fear at the end and to rest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:111
verses.text: Better had she now rested, that at the end she might have rejoiced.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:112
verses.text: Rested? When? "When God arose unto judgment, that He might save all the meek in heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:113
verses.text: Who are the meek in heart? They that on snorting horses have not mounted, but in their humility have confessed their own sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:114
verses.text: "For the thought of a man shall confess to Thee, and the remnants of the thought shall celebrate solemnities to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:115
verses.text: The first is the thought, the latter are the remnants of the thought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:116
verses.text: What is the first thought? That from whence we begin, that good thought whence thou wilt begin to confess.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:117
verses.text: Confession uniteth us to Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:118
verses.text: But now the confession itself, that is, the first thought, doth produce in us the remnants of the thought: and those very "remnants of thought shall celebrate solemnities to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:119
verses.text: What is the thought which shall confess? That which condemneth the former life, that whereunto that which it was is displeasing, in order that it may be that which it was not, is itself the first thought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:120
verses.text: But because thus thou oughtest to withdraw from sins, with the first thought after having confessed to God, that it may not escape thy memory that thou hast been a sinner; in that thou hast been a sinner, thou dost celebrate solemnities to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:121
verses.text: Furthermore it is to be understood as followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:122
verses.text: The first thought hath confession, and departure from the old life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:123
verses.text: But if thou shalt have forgotten from what sins thou hast been delivered, thou dost not render thanks to the Deliverer, and dost not celebrate solemnities to thy God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:124
verses.text: Behold the first confessing thought of Saul the Apostle, now Paul, who at first was Saul, when he heard a voice from Heaven!He put forth the first thought of obedience: when he heard, "I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest," "O Lord," he saith, "what dost Thou bid me to do?" This is a thought confessing: now he is calling upon the Lord, whom he persecuted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:125
verses.text: In what manner the remnants of the thought shall celebrate solemnities, in the case of Paul ye have heard, when the Apostle himself was being read: "Be thou mindful that Christ Jesus hath risen from the dead, of the seed of David, after my Gospel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:126
verses.text: What is, be thou mindful? Though effaced from thy memory be the thought, whereby at first thou hast confessed: be the remnant of the thought in the memory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:127
verses.text: Even once was Christ sacrificed for us, when we believed; then was thought; but now there are the remnants of thought, when we remember Who hath come to us, and what He hath forgiven us; by means of those very remnants of thought, that is, by means of the memory herself, He is daily so sacrificed for us, as if He were daily renewing us, that hath renewed us by His first grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:128
verses.text: For now the Lord hath renewed us in Baptism, and we have become new men, in hope indeed rejoicing, in order that in tribulation we may be patient: nevertheless, there ought not to escape from our memory that which hath been bestowed upon us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:129
verses.text: And if now thy thought is not what it was,—for the first thought was to depart from sin: but now thou dost not depart, but at that time didst depart,—be there remnants of thought, lest He who hath made whole escape from memory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:130
verses.text: "Vow ye, and pay to the Lord our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:131
verses.text: Let each man vow what he is able, and pay it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:132
verses.text: Do not vow and not pay: but let every man vow, and pay what he can.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:133
verses.text: Be ye not slow to vow: for ye will accomplish the vows by powers not your own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:134
verses.text: Ye will fail, if on yourselves ye rely: but if on Him to whom ye vow ye rely, ye will be safe to pay.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:135
verses.text: "Vow ye, and pay to the Lord our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:136
verses.text: What ought we all in common to vow? To believe in Him, to hope from Him for life eternal, to live godly according to a measure common to all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:137
verses.text: For there is a certain measure common to all men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:138
verses.text: To commit no theft is not a thing enjoined merely upon one devoted to continence, and not enjoined upon the married woman: to commit no adultery is enjoined upon all men: not to love wine-bibbing, whereby the soul is swallowed up, and doth corrupt in herself the Temple of God, is enjoined to all alike: not to be proud, is enjoined to all men alike: not to slay man, not to hate a brother, not to lay a plot to destroy any one, is enjoined to all in common.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:139
verses.text: The whole of this we all ought to vow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:140
verses.text: There are also vows proper for individuals: one voweth to God conjugal chastity, that he will know no other woman besides his wife: so also the woman, that she will know no other man besides her husband.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:141
verses.text: Other men also vow, even though they have used such a marriage, that beyond this they will have no such thing, that they will neither desire nor admit the like: and these men have vowed a greater vow than the former.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:142
verses.text: Others vow even virginity from the beginning of life, that they will even know no such thing as those who having experienced have relinquished: and these men have vowed the greatest vow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:143
verses.text: Others vow that their house shall be a place of entertainment for all the Saints that may come: a great vow they vow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:144
verses.text: Another voweth to relinquish all his goods to be distributed to the poor, and go into a community, into a society of the Saints: a great vow he doth vow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:145
verses.text: "Vow ye, and pay to the Lord our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:146
verses.text: Let each one vow what he shall have willed to vow; let him give heed to this, that he pay what he hath vowed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:147
verses.text: If any man doth look back with regard to what he hath vowed to God, it is an evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:148
verses.text: Some woman or other devoted to continence hath willed to marry: what hath she willed? The same as any virgin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:149
verses.text: What hath she willed? The same as her own mother.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:150
verses.text: Hath she willed any evil thing? Evil certainly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:151
verses.text: Why? Because already she had vowed to the Lord her God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:152
verses.text: For what hath the apostle Paul said concerning such? Though he saith that young widows may marry if they will: nevertheless he saith in a certain passage, "but more blessed she will be, if so she shall have remained, after my judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:153
verses.text: He showeth that she is more blessed, if so she shall have remained; but nevertheless that she is not to be condemned, if she shall have willed to marry.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:154
verses.text: But what saith he concerning certain who have vowed and have not paid? "Having," he saith, "judgment, because the first faith they have made void".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:155
verses.text: What is, "the first faith they have made void"? They have vowed, and have not paid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:156
verses.text: Let no brother therefore, when placed in a monastery, say, I shall depart from the monastery: for neither are they only that are in a monastery to attain unto the kingdom of Heaven, nor do those that are not there not belong unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:157
verses.text: We answer him, but they have not vowed; thou hast vowed, thou hast looked back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:158
verses.text: When the Lord was threatening them with the day of judgment, He saith what? "Remember Lot's wife".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:159
verses.text: To all men He spake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:160
verses.text: For what did Lot's wife? She was delivered from Sodom, and being in the way she looked back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:161
verses.text: In the place where she looked back, there she remained.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:162
verses.text: For she became a statue of salt, in order that by considering her men might be seasoned, might have sense, might not be infatuated, might not look back, lest by giving a bad example they should themselves remain and season others.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:163
verses.text: For even now we are saying this to certain of our brethren, whom perchance we may have seen as it were weak in the good they have purposed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:164
verses.text: And wilt thou be such an one as he was? We put before them certain who have looked back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:165
verses.text: They are savourless  in themselves, but they season others, inasmuch as they are mentioned, in order that fearing their example they may not look back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:166
verses.text: "Vow ye, and pay".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:167
verses.text: For that wife of Lot to all doth belong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:168
verses.text: A married woman hath had the will to commit adultery; from her place whither she had arrived she looked back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:169
verses.text: A widow who had vowed so to remain hath willed to marry, she hath willed the thing which was lawful to her who hath married, but to herself was not lawful, because from her place she hath looked back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:170
verses.text: There is a virgin devoted to continence, already dedicated to God; let her have also the other gifts which truly do adorn virginity itself, and without which that virginity is unclean.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:171
verses.text: For what if she be uncorrupt in body and corrupt in mind? What is it that he hath said? What if no one hath touched the body, but if perchance she be drunken, be proud, be contentious, be talkative? All these things God doth condemn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:172
verses.text: If before she had vowed, she had married, she would not have been condemned: she hath chosen something better, hath overcome that which was lawful for her; she is proud, and doth commit so many things unlawful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:173
verses.text: This I say, it is lawful for her to marry before that she voweth, to be proud is never lawful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:174
verses.text: O thou virgin of God, thou hast willed not to marry, which is lawful: thou dost exalt thyself, which is not lawful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:175
verses.text: Better is a virgin humble, than a married woman humble: but better is a married woman humble, than a virgin proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:176
verses.text: But she that looked back upon marriage is condemned, not because she hath willed to marry; but because she had already gone before, and is become the wife of Lot by looking back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:177
verses.text: Be ye not slow, that are able, whom God doth inspire to seize upon higher callings: for we do not say these things in order that ye may not vow, but in order that ye may vow and may pay.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:178
verses.text: Now because we have treated of these matters , thou perchance wast willing to vow, and now art not willing to vow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:179
verses.text: But observe what the Psalm hath said to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:180
verses.text: It hath not said, "Vow not;" but, "Vow and pay".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:181
verses.text: Because thou hast heard, "pay," wilt thou not vow? Therefore wast thou willing to vow, and not to pay? Nay, do both.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:182
verses.text: One thing is done by thy profession, another thing will be perfected by the aid of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:183
verses.text: Look to Him who doth guide thee, and thou wilt not look back to the place whence He is leading thee forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:184
verses.text: He that guideth thee is walking before thee; the place from whence He is guiding thee is behind thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:185
verses.text: Love Him guiding, and He doth not condemn thee looking back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:186
verses.text: "All they that are in the circuit of Him shall offer gifts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:187
verses.text: Who are in the circuit of Him?Whatever is common to all is in the midst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:188
verses.text: Why is it said to be in the midst? Because it is at the same distance from all, and at the same proximity to all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:189
verses.text: That which is not in the middle, is as it were private.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:190
verses.text: That which is public is set in the middle, in order that all they that come may use the same, may be enlightened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:191
verses.text: Let no one say, it is mine: lest he should be wanting to make his own share of that which is in the midst for all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:192
verses.text: What then is, "All they that are in the circuit of Him shall offer gifts"? All they that understand truth to be common to all, and who do not make it as it were their own by being proud concerning it, they shall offer gifts; because they have humility: but they that make as it were their own that which is common to all, as though it were set in the middle, are endeavouring to lead men astray to a party, these shall not offer gifts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:193
verses.text: "To Him terrible".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:194
verses.text: Let therefore all men fear that are in the circuit of Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:195
verses.text: For therefore they shall fear, and with trembling they shall praise; because they are in the circuit of Him, to the end that all men may attain unto Him, and He may openly meet all, and openly enlighten all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:196
verses.text: This is, to stand in awe with others When thou hast made him as it were thine own, and no longer common, thou art exalted unto pride; though it is written, "Serve ye the Lord in fear, and exult unto Him with trembling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:197
verses.text: Therefore they shall offer gifts, who are in the circuit of Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:198
verses.text: For they are humble who know truth to be common to all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:199
verses.text: To whom shall they offer gifts? "To Him terrible, and to Him that taketh away the spirit of princes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:200
verses.text: For the spirits of princes are proud spirits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:201
verses.text: They then are not His Spirits; for if they know anything, their own they will it to be, not public; but, that which setteth Himself forth as equal toward all men, that setteth Himself in the midst, in order that all men may take as much as they can, whatever they can; not of what is any man's, but of what is God's, and therefore of their own because they have become His.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:202
verses.text: Therefore they must needs be humble: they have lost their own spirit, and they have the Spirit of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:203
verses.text: For if thou shalt have confessed thyself dust, God out of dust doth make man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:204
verses.text: All they that are in the circuit of Him do offer gifts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:205
verses.text: All humble men do confess to Him, and do adore Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:206
verses.text: "To Him terrible they offer gifts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:207
verses.text: Whence to Him terrible exult ye with trembling: "and to Him that taketh away the spirit of princes:" that is, that taketh away the haughtiness of proud men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:208
verses.text: "To Him terrible among the kings of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:209
verses.text: Terrible are the kings of the earth, but He is above all, that doth terrify the kings of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:210
verses.text: Be thou a king of the earth, and God will be to thee terrible.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:211
verses.text: How, wilt thou say, shall I be a king of the earth? Rule the earth, and thou wilt be a king of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:212
verses.text: Do not therefore with desire of empire set before thine eyes exceeding wide provinces, where thou mayest spread abroad thy kingdoms; rule thou the earth which thou bearest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 78:213
verses.text: Hear the Apostle ruling the earth: "I do not so fight as if beating air, but I chasten my body, and bring it into captivity, lest perchance preaching to other men, I myself become a reprobate".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXVII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:2
verses.text: This Psalm's lintel is thus inscribed: "Unto the end, for Idithun, a Psalm to Asaph himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:3
verses.text: What "Unto the end" is, ye know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:4
verses.text: Idithun is interpreted "leaping over those men," Asaph is interpreted "a congregation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:5
verses.text: Here therefore there is speaking "a congregation that leapeth over," in order that it may reach the End, which is Christ Jesus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:6
verses.text: "With my voice," he saith, "to the Lord I have cried".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:7
verses.text: But many men cry unto the Lord for the sake of getting riches and avoiding losses, for the safety of their friends, for the security of their house, for temporal felicity, for secular dignity, lastly, even for mere soundness of body, which is the inheritance of the poor man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:8
verses.text: For such and such like things many men do cry unto the Lord; scarce one for the sake of the Lord Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:9
verses.text: For an easy thing it is for a man to desire anything of the Lord, and not to desire the Lord Himself; as if forsooth that which He giveth could be sweeter than Himself that giveth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:10
verses.text: Whosoever therefore doth cry unto the Lord for the sake of any other thing, is not yet one that leapeth over.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:11
verses.text: He doth indeed hearken to thee at the time when thou dost seek Himself, not when through Himself thou dost seek any other thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:12
verses.text: It hath been said of some men, "They cried, and there was no one to save them; to the Lord, and He hearkened not unto them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:13
verses.text: For why? Because the voice of them was not unto the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:14
verses.text: This the Scripture doth express in another place, where it saith of such men, "On the Lord they have not called".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:15
verses.text: Unto Him they have not ceased to cry, and yet upon the Lord they have not called.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:16
verses.text: What is, upon the Lord they have not called? They have not called the Lord unto themselves: they have not invited the Lord to their heart, they would not have themselves inhabited by the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:17
verses.text: And therefore what hath befallen them? "They have trembled with fear where fear was not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:18
verses.text: They have trembled about the loss of things present, for the reason that they were not full of Him, upon whom they have not called.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:19
verses.text: They have not loved gratis, so that after the loss of temporal things they could say, "As it hath pleased the Lord, so hath been done, be the name of the Lord blessed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:20
verses.text: Therefore this man saith, "My voice is unto the Lord, and He doth hearken unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:21
verses.text: Let him show us how this cometh to pass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:22
verses.text: "In the day of tribulation I have sought out God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:23
verses.text: Who art thou that doest this thing? In the day of thy tribulation take heed what thou seekest out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:24
verses.text: If a jail be the cause of tribulation, thou seekest to get forth from jail: if fever be the cause of tribulation, thou seekest health: if hunger be the cause of tribulation, thou seekest fulness: if losses be the cause of tribulation, thou seekest gain: if expatriation be the cause of tribulation, thou seekest the home of thy flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:25
verses.text: And why should I name all things, or when could I name all things? Dost thou wish to be one leaping over? In the day of thy tribulation seek out God: not through God some other thing, but out of tribulation God, that to this end God may take away tribulation, that thou mayest without anxiety cleave unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:26
verses.text: "In the day of my tribulation, I have sought out God:" not any other thing, but "God I have sought out".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:27
verses.text: And how hast thou sought out? "With my hands in the night before Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:28
verses.text: Tribulation must not be thought to be this or that in particular.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:29
verses.text: For every individual that doth not yet leap over, thinketh that as yet to be no tribulation, unless it be a thing which may have befallen this life of some sad occasion: but this man, that leapeth over, doth count this whole life to be his tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:30
verses.text: For so much doth he love his supernal country, that the earthly pilgrimage is of itself the greatest tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:31
verses.text: For how can this life be otherwise than a tribulation, I pray you? how can that not be a tribulation, the whole whereof hath been called temptation? Thou hast it written in the book of Job, is not human life a temptation upon earth? Hath he said, human life is tempted upon earth? Nay, but life itself is a temptation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:32
verses.text: If therefore temptation, it must surely be a tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:33
verses.text: In this tribulation therefore, that is to say in this life, this man that leapeth over hath sought out God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:34
verses.text: How? "With my hands," he saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:35
verses.text: What is, "with my hands"? With my works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:36
verses.text: For he was not seeking any thing corporeal, so that he might find and handle something which he had lost, so that he might seek with hands coin, gold, silver, vesture, in short everything which can be held in the hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:37
verses.text: Howbeit, even our Lord Jesus Christ Himself willed Himself to be sought after with hands, when to His doubting disciple He showed the scarsWhat then, to us belongeth not the seeking with hands? It belongeth to us, as I have said, to seek with works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:38
verses.text: When so? "In the night".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:39
verses.text: What is, "in the night"? In this age.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:40
verses.text: For it is night until there shine forth day in the glorified advent of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:41
verses.text: For would ye see how it is night? Unless we had here had a lantern, we should have remained in darkness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:42
verses.text: For Peter saith," We too have more sure the prophetic discourse, whereunto ye do well to give heed, as to a lantern shining in a dark place, until day shine, and the day-star arise in your hearts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:43
verses.text: There is therefore to come day after this night, meanwhile in this night a lantern is not lacking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:44
verses.text: And this is perchance what we are now doing: by explaining these passages, we are bringing in a lantern, in order that we may rejoice in this night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:45
verses.text: Which indeed ought alway to be burning in your houses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:46
verses.text: For to such men is said, "The Spirit quench ye not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:47
verses.text: And as though explaining what he was saying, he continueth and saith, "Prophecy despise ye not:" that is, let the lantern alway shine in you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:48
verses.text: And even this light by comparison with a sort of ineffable day is called night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:49
verses.text: For the very life of believers by comparison with the life of unbelievers is day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:50
verses.text: Night and day—day in comparison with unbelievers, night in comparison with the Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:51
verses.text: For the Angels have a day, which we have not yet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:52
verses.text: Already we have one that unbelievers have not: but not yet have believers that which Angels have: but they will have, at the time when they will be equal to the Angels of God, that which hath been promised to them in the Resurrection In this then which is now day and yet night; night in comparison with the future day for which we yearn, day in comparison with the past night which we have renounced: in this night then, I say, let us seek God with our hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:53
verses.text: Let not works cease, let us seek God, be there no idle yearning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:54
verses.text: If we are in the way, let us expend our means in order that we may be able to reach the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:55
verses.text: With hands let us seek God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:56
verses.text: "With my hands in the night before Him, and I have not been deceived".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:57
verses.text: "My soul hath refused to be comforted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:58
verses.text: So great weariness did here possess me, that my soul did close the door against all comfort.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:59
verses.text: Whence such weariness to him? It may be that his vineyard hath been hailed on, or his olive hath yielded no fruit, or the vintage hath been interrupted by rain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:60
verses.text: Whence the weariness to him? Hear this out of another Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:61
verses.text: For therein is the voice of the same: "weariness hath bowed me down, because of sinners forsaking Thy law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:62
verses.text: He saith then that he was overcome with so great weariness because of this sort of evil thing; so as that his soul refused to be comforted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:63
verses.text: Weariness had well nigh swallowed him up, and sorrow had ingulfed him altogether beyond remedy, he refuseth to be comforted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:64
verses.text: What then remained? In the first place, see whence he is comforted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:65
verses.text: Had he not waited for one who might condole with him?"I have been mindful of God, and I have been delighted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:66
verses.text: My hands had not wrought in vain, they had found a great comforter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:67
verses.text: While not being idle, "I have been mindful of God, and I have been delighted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:68
verses.text: God must therefore be praised, of whom this man being mindful, hath been delighted, and hath been comforted in sorrowful case, and refreshed when safety was in a manner despaired of: God must therefore be praised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:69
verses.text: In fine, because he hath been comforted, in continuation he saith, "I have babbled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:70
verses.text: In that same comfort being made mindful of God, I have been delighted, and have "babbled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:71
verses.text: What is, "I have babbled"? I have rejoiced, I have exulted in speaking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:72
verses.text: For babblers they are properly called, that by the common people are named talkative, who at the approach of joy are neither able nor willing to be silent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:73
verses.text: This man hath become such an one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:74
verses.text: And again he saith what? "And my spirit hath fainted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:75
verses.text: With weariness he had pined away; by calling to mind God, he had been delighted, again in babbling he had fainted: what followeth? "All mine enemies have anticipated watches".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:76
verses.text: All mine enemies have kept watch over me; they have exceeded in keeping watch over me; in watching they have been beforehand with me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:77
verses.text: Where do they not lay traps? Have not mine enemies anticipated all watches? For who are these enemies, but they of whom the Apostle saith, "Ye have not wrestling against flesh and blood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:78
verses.text: Against the devil and his angels we are waging hostilities.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:79
verses.text: Rulers of the world he hath called them, because they do themselves rule the lovers of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:80
verses.text: For they do not rule the world, as if they were rulers of heaven and earth: but he is calling sinners the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:81
verses.text: With the devil and his angels there is no concord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:82
verses.text: They do themselves grudge us the kingdom of Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:83
verses.text: They cannot at all be appeased towards us: because "all mine enemies have anticipated watches".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:84
verses.text: They have watched more to deceive than I to guard myself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:85
verses.text: For how can they have done otherwise than anticipate watches, that have set everywhere scandals, everywhere traps? Weariness doth invest the heart, we have to fear lest sorrow swallow us up: in joy to fear lest the spirit faint in babbling: "all mine enemies have anticipated watches".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:86
verses.text: In fine, in the midst of that same babbling, whiles thou art speaking, and art speaking without fear, how much is oft-times found which enemies would lay hold of and censure, whereon they would even found accusation and slander—"he said so, he thought so, he spake so!" What should man do, save that which followeth? "I have been troubled, and I spake not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:87
verses.text: Therefore when he was troubled, lest in his babbling enemies anticipating watches should seek and find slanders, he spake not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:88
verses.text: "I have thought on ancient days".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:89
verses.text: Now he, as if he were one who had been beaten out of doors, hath taken refuge within: he is conversing in the secret place of his own heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:90
verses.text: And let him declare to us what he is doing there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:91
verses.text: It is well with him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:92
verses.text: Observe what things he is thinking of, I pray you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:93
verses.text: He is within, in his own house he is thinking of ancient days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:94
verses.text: No one saith to him, thou hast spoken ill: no one saith to him, thou hast spoken much: no one saith to him, thou hast thought perversely.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:95
verses.text: Thus may it be well with him, may God aid him: let him think of the ancient days, and let him tell us what he hath done in his very inner chamber, whereunto he hath arrived, over what he hath leaped, where he hath abode.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:96
verses.text: "I have thought on ancient days; and of eternal years I have been mindful".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:97
verses.text: What are eternal years? It is a mighty thought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:98
verses.text: See whether this thought requireth anything but great silence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:99
verses.text: Apart from all noise without, from all tumult of things human let him remain quiet within, that would think of those eternal years.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:100
verses.text: Are the years wherein we are eternal, or those wherein our ancestors have been, or those wherein our posterity are to be? Far be it that they should be esteemed eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:101
verses.text: For what part of these years doth remain? Behold we speak and say, "in this year:" and what have we got of this year, save the one day wherein we are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:102
verses.text: For the former days of this year have already gone by, and are not to be had; but the future days have not yet come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:103
