verses.text: In one day we are, and we say, in this year: nay rather say thou, to-day, if thou desirest to speak of anything present.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:104
verses.text: For of the whole year what hast thou got that is present? Whatsoever thereof is past, is no longer; whatsoever thereof is future, is not yet: how then, "this year"? Amend the expression: say, to-day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:105
verses.text: Thou speakest truth, henceforth I will say, "to-day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:106
verses.text: Again observe this too, how to-day the morning hours have already past, the future hours have not yet come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:107
verses.text: This too therefore amend: say, in this hour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:108
verses.text: And of this hour what hast thou got? Some moments thereof have already gone by, those that are future have not yet come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:109
verses.text: Say, in this moment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:110
verses.text: In what moment? While I am uttering syllables, if I shall speak two syllables, the latter doth not sound until the former hath gone by: in a word, in that same one syllable, if it chance to have two letters, the latter letter doth not sound, until the former hath gone by.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:111
verses.text: What then have we got of these years? These years are changeable: the eternal years must be thought on, years that stand, that are not made up of days that come and depart; years whereof in another place the Scripture saith to God, "But Thou art the Self-same, and Thy years shall not fail".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:112
verses.text: On these years this man that leapeth over, not in babbling without, but in silence hath thought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:113
verses.text: "And I have meditated in the night with my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:114
verses.text: No slanderous person seeketh for snares in his words, in his heart he hath meditated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:115
verses.text: "I babbled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:116
verses.text: Behold there is the former babbling.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:117
verses.text: Watch again, that thy spirit faint not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:118
verses.text: I did not, he saith, I did not so babble as if it were abroad: in another way now.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:119
verses.text: How now? "I did babble, and did search out my spirit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:120
verses.text: If he were searching the earth to find veins of gold, no one would say that he was foolish; nay, many men would call him wise, for desiring to come at gold: how great treasures hath a man within, and he diggeth not! This man was examining his spirit, and was speaking with that same his spirit, and in the very speaking he was babbling.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:121
verses.text: He was questioning himself, was examining himself, was judge over himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:122
verses.text: And he continueth; "I did search my spirit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:123
verses.text: He had to fear lest he should stay within his own spirit: for he had babbled without; and because all his enemies had anticipated watches, he found there sorrow, and his spirit fainted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:124
verses.text: He that did babble without, lo, now doth begin to babble within in safety, where being alone in secret, he is thinking on eternal years.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:125
verses.text: And thou hast found what? "God will not repel for everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:126
verses.text: Weariness he had found in this life; in no place a trustworthy, in no place a fearless comfort.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:127
verses.text: Unto whatsoever men he betook himself, in them he found scandal, or feared it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:128
verses.text: In no place therefore was he free from care.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:129
verses.text: An evil thing it was for him to hold his peace, lest perchance he should keep silence from good words; to speak and babble without was painful to him, lest all his enemies, anticipating watches, should seek slanders in his words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:130
verses.text: Being exceedingly straitened in this life, he thought much of another life, where there is not this trial.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:131
verses.text: And when is he to arrive thither? For it cannot but be evident that our suffering here is the anger of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:132
verses.text: This thing is spoken of in Isaiah, "I will not be an avenger unto you for everlasting, nor will I be angry with you at all times".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:133
verses.text: Will this anger of God always abide? This man hath not found this in silence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:134
verses.text: For he saith what? "God will not repel for everlasting, and He will not add any more that it should be well-pleasing to Him still".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:135
verses.text: That is, that it should be well-pleasing to Him still to repel, and He will not add the repelling for everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:136
verses.text: He must needs recall to Himself His servants, He must needs receive fugitives returning to the Lord, He must needs hearken to the voice of them that are in fetters.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:137
verses.text: "Or unto the end will He cut off mercy from generation to generation?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:138
verses.text: "Or will God forget to be merciful?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:139
verses.text: In thee, from thee unto another there is no mercy unless God bestow it on thee: and shall God Himself forget mercy? The stream runneth: shall the spring itself be dried up? "Or shall God forget to be merciful: or shall He keep back in anger His mercies?" That is, shall He be so angry, as that He will not have mercy? He will more easily keep back anger than mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:140
verses.text: "And I said".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:141
verses.text: Now leaping over himself he hath said what? "Now I have begun:" , when I had gone out even from myself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:142
verses.text: Here henceforth there is no danger: for even to remain in myself, was danger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:143
verses.text: "And I said, Now I have begun: this is the changing of the right hand of the Lofty One".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:144
verses.text: Now the Lofty One hath begun to change me: now I have begun something wherein I am secure: now I have entered a certain palace of joys, wherein no enemy is to be feared: now I have begun to be in that region, where all mine enemies do not anticipate watches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:145
verses.text: "Now I have begun: this is the changing of the right hand of the Lofty One".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:146
verses.text: "I have been mindful of the works of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:147
verses.text: Now behold him roaming among the works of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:148
verses.text: For he was babbling without, and being made sorrowful thereby his spirit fainted: he babbled within with his own heart, and with his spirit, and having searched out that same spirit he was mindful of the eternal years, was mindful of the mercy of the Lord, how God will not repel him for everlasting; and he began now fearlessly to rejoice in His works, fearlessly to exult in the same.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:149
verses.text: Let us hear now those very works, and let us too exult.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:150
verses.text: But let even us leap over in our affections, and not rejoice in things temporal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:151
verses.text: For we too have our bed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:152
verses.text: Why do we not enter therein? Why do we not abide in silence? Why do we not search out our spirit? Why do we not think on the eternal years? Why do we not rejoice in the works of God? In such sort now let us hear, and let us take delight in Himself speaking, in order that when we shall have departed hence, we may do that which we used to do while He spake; if only we are making the beginning of Him whereof he spake in, "Now I have begun".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:153
verses.text: To rejoice in the works of God, is to forget even thyself, if thou canst delight in Him alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:154
verses.text: For what is a better thing than He? Dost thou not see that, when thou returnest to thyself, thou returnest to a worse thing? "for I shall be mindful from the beginning of Thy wonderful works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:155
verses.text: "And I will meditate on all Thy works, and on Thy affections I will babble".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:156
verses.text: Behold the third babbling! He babbled without, when he hinted; he babbled in his spirit within, when he advanced: he babbled on the works of God, when he arrived at the place toward which he advanced.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:157
verses.text: "And on Thy affections:" not on any affections.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:158
verses.text: What man doth live without affections? And do ye suppose, brethren, that they who fear God, worship God, love God, have not any affections? Wilt thou indeed suppose and dare to suppose, that painting, the theatre, hunting, hawking, fishing, engage the affections, and the meditation on God doth not engage certain interior affections of its own, while we contemplate the universe, and place before our eyes the spectacle of the natural world, and therein labour to discover the Maker, and find Him nowhere unpleasing, but pleasing above  all things?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:159
verses.text: "O God, Thy way is in the Holy One".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:160
verses.text: He is contemplating now the works of the mercy of God around us, out of these he is babbling, and in these affections he is exulting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:161
verses.text: At first he is beginning from thence, "Thy way is in the Holy One?" What is that way of Thine which is in the Holy One? "I am," He saith, "the Way, the Truth, and the Life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:162
verses.text: Return therefore, ye men, from your affections.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:163
verses.text: "Who is a great God, like our God?" Gentiles have their affections regarding their gods, they adore idols, they have eyes and they see not; ears they have and they hear not; feet they have and they walk not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:164
verses.text: Why dost thou walk to a God that walketh not? I do not, he saith, worship such things, and what dost thou worship? The divinity which is there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:165
verses.text: Thou dost then worship that whereof hath been said elsewhere, "for the Gods of the nations are demons".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:166
verses.text: Thou dost either worship idols, or devils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:167
verses.text: Neither idols, nor devils, he saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:168
verses.text: And what dost thou worship? The stars, sun, moon, those things celestial.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:169
verses.text: How much better Him that hath made both things earthly and things celestial.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:170
verses.text: "Who is a great God like our God?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:171
verses.text: "Thou art the God that doest wonderful things alone".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:172
verses.text: Thou art indeed a great God, doing wonderful things in body, in soul; alone doing them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:173
verses.text: The deaf have heard, the blind have seen, the feeble have recovered, the dead have risen, the paralytic have been strengthened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:174
verses.text: But these miracles were at that time performed on bodies, let us see those wrought on the soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:175
verses.text: Sober are those that were a little before drunken, believers are those that were a little before worshippers of idols: their goods they bestow on the poor that did rob before those of others.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:176
verses.text: "Wonderful things alone".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:177
verses.text: Moses too did them, but not alone: Elias too did them, even Eliseus did them, the Apostles too did them, but no one of them alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:178
verses.text: That they might have power to do them, Thou wast with them: when Thou didst them they were not with Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:179
verses.text: For they were not with Thee when Thou didst them, inasmuch as Thou didst make even these very men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:180
verses.text: How "alone"? Is it perchance the Father, and not the Son? Or the Son, and not the Father? Nay, but Father and Son and Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:181
verses.text: For it is not three Gods but one God that doeth wonderful things alone, and even in this very leaper-over.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:182
verses.text: For even his leaping over and arriving at these things was a miracle of God: when he was babbling within with his own spirit, in order that he might leap over even that same spirit of his, and might delight in the works of God, he then did wonderful things himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:183
verses.text: But God hath done what? "Thou hast made known unto the people Thy power".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:184
verses.text: Thence this congregation of Asaph leaping over; because He hath made known in the peoples His virtue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:185
verses.text: What virtue of His hath He made known in the peoples? "But we preach Christ crucified,Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:186
verses.text: If then the virtue of God is Christ, He hath made known Christ in the peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:187
verses.text: Do we not yet perceive so much as this; and are we so unwise, are we lying so much below, do we so leap over nothing, as that we see not this?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:188
verses.text: "Thou hast redeemed in Thine arm Thy people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:189
verses.text: "With Thine arm," that is, with Thy power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:190
verses.text: "And to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?" "Thou hast redeemed in Thine arm Thy people, the sons of Israel and of Joseph".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:191
verses.text: How as if two peoples, "the sons of Israel and of Joseph"? Are not the sons of Joseph among the sons of Israel?He hath admonished us of some distinction to be made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:192
verses.text: Let us search out our spirit, perchance God hath placed there something—God whom we ought even by night to seek with our hands, in order that we may not be deceived—perchance we shall discover even ourselves in this distinction of "sons of Israel and of Joseph".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:193
verses.text: By Joseph He hath willed another people to be understood, hath willed that the people of the Gentiles be understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:194
verses.text: Why the people of the Gentiles by Joseph? Because Joseph was sold into Egypt by his brethren That Joseph whom the brethren envied, and sold him into Egypt, when sold into Egypt, toiled, was humbled; when made known and exalted, flourished, reigned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:195
verses.text: And by all these things he hath signified what? What but Christ sold by His brethren, banished from His own land, as it were into the Egypt of the Gentiles? There at first humbled, when the Martyrs were suffering persecutions: now exalted, as we see; inasmuch as there hath been fulfilled in Him, "There shall adore Him all kinds of the earth, all nations shall serve Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:196
verses.text: Therefore Joseph is the people of the Gentiles, but Israel the people of the Hebrew nation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:197
verses.text: God hath redeemed His people, "the sons of Israel and of Joseph".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:198
verses.text: By means of what? By means of the corner stone, wherein the two walls have been joined together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:199
verses.text: And he continueth how? "The waters have seen Thee, O God, and they have feared and the abysses have been troubled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:200
verses.text: What are the waters? The peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:201
verses.text: What are these waters hath been asked in the Apocalypse, the answer was, the peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:202
verses.text: There we find most clearly waters put by a figure for peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:203
verses.text: But above he had said, "Thou hast made known in the peoples Thy virtue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:204
verses.text: With reason therefore, "the waters have seen Thee, and they have feared".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:205
verses.text: They have been changed because they have feared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:206
verses.text: What are the abysses? The depths of waters.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:207
verses.text: What man among the peoples is not troubled, when the conscience is smitten? Thou seekest the depth of the sea, what is deeper than human conscience? That is the depth which was troubled, when God redeemed with His arm His people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:208
verses.text: In what manner were the abysses troubled? When all men poured forth their consciences in confession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:209
verses.text: In praises of God, in confessions of sins, in hymns and in songs, in prayers, "There is a multitude of the sound of waters.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:210
verses.text: The clouds have uttered a voice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:211
verses.text: Thence that sound of waters, thence the troubling of the abysses, because "the clouds have uttered a voice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:212
verses.text: What clouds? The preachers of the word of truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:213
verses.text: What clouds? Those concerning which God doth menace a certain vineyard, which instead of grape had brought forth thorns and He saith, "I will command My clouds, that they rain no rain upon it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:214
verses.text: In a word, the Apostles forsaking the Jews, went to the Gentiles: in preaching Christ among all nations, "the clouds have uttered a voice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:215
verses.text: "For Thine arrows have gone through".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:216
verses.text: Those same voices of the clouds He hath again called arrows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:217
verses.text: For the words of the Evangelists were arrows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:218
verses.text: For these things are allegories.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:219
verses.text: For properly neither an arrow is rain, nor rain is an arrow: but yet the word of God is both an arrow because it doth smite; and rain because it doth water.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:220
verses.text: Let no one therefore any longer wonder at the troubling of the abysses, when "Thine arrows have gone through".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:221
verses.text: What is, "have gone through"? They have not stopped in the ears, but they have pierced the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:222
verses.text: "The voice of Thy thunder is in the wheel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:223
verses.text: What is this? How are we to understand it? May the Lord give aid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:224
verses.text: When boys we were wont to imagine, whenever we heard thunderings from Heaven, that carriages were going forth as it were from the stables.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:225
verses.text: For thunder doth make a sort of rolling like carriages.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:226
verses.text: Must we return to these boyish thoughts, in order to understand, "the voice of Thy thunder is in the wheel," as though God hath certain carriages in the clouds, and the passing along of the carriages doth raise that sound? Far be it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:227
verses.text: This is boyish, vain, trifling.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:228
verses.text: What is then, "The voice of Thy thunder is in the wheel"? Thy voice rolleth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:229
verses.text: Not even this do I understand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:230
verses.text: What shall we do? Let us question Idithun himself, to see whether perchance he may himself explain what he hath said: "The voice," he saith, "of Thy thunder is in the wheel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:231
verses.text: I do not understand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:232
verses.text: I will hear what thou sayest: "Thy lightnings have appeared to the round world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:233
verses.text: Say then, I had no understanding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:234
verses.text: The round world is a wheel For the circuit of the round world is with reason called also an "orb:" whence also a small wheel is called an "orbiculus".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:235
verses.text: "The voice of Thy thunder is in the wheel:" Thy "lightnings have appeared to the round world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:236
verses.text: Those clouds in a wheel have gone about the round world, have gone about with thundering and with lightning, they have shaken the abyss, with commandments they have thundered, with miracles they have lightened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:237
verses.text: "Unto every land hath gone forth the sound of them, and unto the ends of the orb the words of them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:238
verses.text: "The land hath been moved and made to tremble:" that is, all men that dwell in the land.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:239
verses.text: But by a figure the land itself is sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:240
verses.text: Why? Because all nations are called by the name of sea, inasmuch as human life is bitter, and exposed to storms and tempests.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:241
verses.text: Moreover if thou observe this, how men devour one another like fishes, how the stronger doth swallow up the weaker—it is then a sea, unto it the Evangelists went.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:242
verses.text: "Thy way is in the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:243
verses.text: But now Thy way was in the Holy One, now "Thy way is in the sea:" because the Holy One Himself is in the sea, and with reason even did walk upon the waters of the sea "Thy way is in the sea," that is, Thy Christ is preached among the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:244
verses.text: "Thy way is in the sea, and Thy paths in many waters," that is, in many peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:245
verses.text: "And Thy footsteps will not be known".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:246
verses.text: He hath touched certain, and wonder were it if it be not those same Jews.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:247
verses.text: Behold now the mercy of Christ hath been so published to the Gentiles, that "Thy way is in the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:248
verses.text: Thy footsteps will not be known".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:249
verses.text: How so, by whom will they not be known, save by those who still say, Christ hath not yet come? Why do they say, Christ hath not yet come? Because they do not yet recognise Him walking on the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:250
verses.text: "Thou hast led home Thy people like sheep in the hand of Moses and of Aaron".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:251
verses.text: Why He hath added this is somewhat difficult to discover.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:252
verses.text: They banished Christ; sick as they were, they would not have Him for their Saviour; but He began to be among the Gentiles, and among all nations, among many peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:253
verses.text: Nevertheless, a remnant of that people hath been saved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:254
verses.text: The ungrateful multitude hath remained without, even the halting breadth of Jacob's thigh For the breadth of the thigh is understood of the multitude of lineage, and among the greater part of the Israelites a certain multitude became vain and foolish, so as not to know the steps of Christ on the waters.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:255
verses.text: "Thou hast led home Thy people like sheep," and they have not known Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 79:256
verses.text: Though Thou hast done such great benefits unto them, hast divided sea, hast made them pass over dry land between waters, hast drowned in the waves pursuing enemies, in the desert hast rained manna for their hunger, leading them home "by the hand of Moses and Aaron:" still they thrust Thee from them, so that in the sea was Thy Way, and Thy steps they knew not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXVIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:2
verses.text: This Psalm doth contain the things which are said to have been done among the old people: but the new and latter people is being admonished, to beware that it be not ungrateful regarding the blessings of God, and provoke His anger against it, whereas it ought to receive His grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:3
verses.text: The Title thereof doth first move and engage our attention.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:4
verses.text: For it is not without reason inscribed, "Understanding of Asaph:" but it is perchance because these words require a reader who doth perceive not the voice which the surface uttereth, but some inward sense.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:5
verses.text: Secondly, when about to narrate and mention all these things, which seem to need a hearer more than an expounder: "I will open," he saith, "in parables my mouth, I will declare propositions from the beginning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:6
verses.text: Who would not herein be awakened out of sleep? Who would dare to hurry over the parables and propositions, reading them as if self-evident, while by their very names they signify that they ought to be sought out with deeper view? For a parable hath on the surface thereof the similitude of something: and though it be a Greek word, it is now used as a Latin word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:7
verses.text: And it is observable, that in parables, those which are called the similitudes of things are compared with things with which we have to do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:8
verses.text: But propositions, which in Greek are called προβήλματα, are questions having something therein which is to be solved by disputation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:9
verses.text: What man then would read parables and propositions cursorily? What man would not attend while hearing these words with watchful mind, in order that by understanding he may come by the fruit thereof?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:10
verses.text: "Hearken ye," He saith, "My people, to My law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:11
verses.text: Whom may we suppose to be here speaking, but God? For it was Himself that gave a law to His people, whom when delivered out of Egypt He gathered together, the which gathering together is properly named a Synagogue, which the word Asaph is interpreted to signify.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:12
verses.text: Hath it then been said, "Understanding of Asaph," in the sense that Asaph himself hath understood; or must it be figuratively understood, in the sense that the same Synagogue, that is, the same people, hath understood, unto whom is said, "Hearken, My people, unto My law"? Why is it then that He is rebuking the same people by the mouth of the Prophet, saying, "But Israel hath not known Me, and My people hath not understood"? But, in fact, there were even in that people they that understood, having the faith which was afterwards revealed, not pertaining to the letter of the law, but the grace of the Spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:13
verses.text: For they cannot have been without the same faith, who were able to foresee and foretell the revelation thereof that should be in Christ, inasmuch as even those old Sacraments were significants of those that should be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:14
verses.text: Had the prophets alone this faith, and not the people too? Nay indeed, but even they that faithfully heard the Prophets, were aided by the same grace in order that they might understand what they heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:15
verses.text: But without doubt the mystery of the Kingdom of Heaven was veiled in the Old Testament, which in the fulness of time should be unveiled in the New "For," saith the Apostle, "they did drink of the Spiritual Rock following them, but the Rock was Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:16
verses.text: In a mystery therefore theirs was the same meat and drink as ours, but in signification the same, not in form; because the same Christ was Himself figured to them in a Rock, manifested to us in the Flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:17
verses.text: "But," he saith, "not in all of them God was well pleased".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:18
verses.text: All indeed ate the same spiritual meat and drank the same spiritual drink, that is to say, signifying something spiritual: but not in all of them was God well pleased.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:19
verses.text: When, he saith, "not in all:" there were evidently there some in whom was God well pleased; and although all the Sacraments were common, grace, which is the virtue of the Sacraments, was not common to all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:20
verses.text: Just as in our times, now that the faith hath been revealed, which then was veiled, to all men that have been baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost, the Laver of regeneration is common; but the very grace whereof these same are the Sacraments, whereby the members of the Body of Christ are to reign together with their Head, is not common to all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:21
verses.text: For even heretics have the same Baptism, and false brethren too, in the communion of the Catholic name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:22
verses.text: Nevertheless, neither then nor now without profit is the voice of him, saying, "Hearken ye, My people, to My law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:23
verses.text: Which expression is remarkable in all the Scriptures, how he saith not, "hearken thou," but, "hearken ye".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:24
verses.text: For of many men a people doth consist: to which many that which followeth is spoken in the plural number.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:25
verses.text: "Incline ye your ear unto the words of My mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:26
verses.text: "Hearken ye," is the same as, "Incline your ear:" and what He saith there, "My law," this He saith here in, "the words of My mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:27
verses.text: For that man doth godly hearken to the law of God, and the words of His mouth, whose ear humility doth incline: not he whose neck pride doth lift up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:28
verses.text: For whatever is poured in is received on the concave surface of humility, is shaken off from the convexity of swelling.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:29
verses.text: Whence in another place, "Incline," he saith, "thine ear, and receive the words of  understanding".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:30
verses.text: We have been therefore sufficiently admonished to receive even this Psalm of this understanding of Asaph, to receive, I say, with inclined ear, that is, with humble piety.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:31
verses.text: And it hath not been spoken of as being of Asaph himself, but to Asaph himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:32
verses.text: Which thing is evident by the Greek article, and is found in certain Latin copies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:33
verses.text: These words therefore are of understanding, that is, of intelligence, which hath been given to Asaph himself: which we had better understand not as to one man, but as to the congregation of the people of God; whence we ought by no means to alienate ourselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:34
verses.text: For although properly we say "Synagogue" of Jews, but "Church" of Christians, because a "Congregation" is wont to be understood as rather of beasts, but a "convocation" as rather of men: yet that too we find called a Church, and it perhaps is more suitable for us to say, "Save us, O Lord, our God, and congregate us from the nations, in order that we may confess to Thy Holy Name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:35
verses.text: Neither ought we to disdain to be, nay we ought to render ineffable thanks, for that we are, the sheep of His hands, which He foresaw when He was saying, "I have other sheep which are not of this fold, them too I must lead in, that there may be one flock and one Shepherd:" that is to say, by joining the faithful people of the Gentiles with the faithful people of the Israelites, concerning whom He had before said, "I have not been sent but to the sheep which have strayed of the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:36
verses.text: For also there shall be congregated before Him all nations, and He shall sever them as a shepherd the sheep from the goats Thus then let us hear that which hath been spoken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:37
verses.text: "Hearken ye, My people, to My law, incline ye your ear unto the words of My mouth:" not as if addressed to Jews, but rather as if addressed to ourselves, or at least as if these words were said as well to ourselves (as to them).

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:38
verses.text: For when the Apostle had said, "But not in all them was God well pleased," thereby showing that there were those too in whom God was well pleased: he hath forthwith added, "For they were overthrown in the desert:" secondly he hath continued, "but these things have been made our figur es".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:39
verses.text: To us therefore more particularly these words have been sung.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:40
verses.text: Whence in this Psalm among other things there hath been said, "That another generation may know, sons who shall be born and shall arise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:41
verses.text: Moreover, if that death by serpents, and that destruction by the destroyer, and the slaying by the sword, were figures, as the Apostle evidently doth declare, inasmuch as it is manifest that all those things did happen: for he saith not, in a figure they were spoken, or, in a figure they were written, but, in a figure, he saith, they happened to them: with how much greater diligence of godliness must those punishments be shunned whereof those were the figures? For beyond a doubt as in good things there is much more of good in that which is signified by the figure, than in the figure itself: so also in evil things very far worse are the things which are signified by the figures, while so great are the evil things which as figures do signify.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:42
verses.text: For as the land of promise, whereunto that people was being led, is nothing in comparison with the Kingdom of Heaven, whereunto the Christian people is being led: so also those punishments which were figures, though they were so severe, are nothing in comparison with the punishments which they signify.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:43
verses.text: But those which the Apostle hath called figures, the same this Psalm, as far as we are able to judge, calleth parables and propositions: not having their end in the fact of their having happened, but in those things whereunto they are referred by a reasonable comparison.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:44
verses.text: Let us therefore hearken unto the law of God—us His people—and let us incline our ear unto the words of His mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:45
verses.text: "I will open," he saith, "in parables My mouth, I will declare propositions from the beginning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:46
verses.text: From what beginning he meaneth, is very evident in the words following.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:47
verses.text: For it is not from the beginning, what time the Heaven and earth were made, nor what time mankind was created in the first man: but what time the congregation that was led out of Egypt; in order that the sense may belong to Asaph, which is interpreted a congregation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:48
verses.text: But O that He that hath said, "I will open in parables My mouth," would also vouchsafe to open our understanding unto them! For if, as He hath opened His mouth in parables, He would in like sort open the parables themselves: and as He declareth "propositions," He would declare in like sort the expositions thereof, we should not be here toiling: but now so hidden and closed are all things, that even if we are able by His aid to arrive at anything, whereon we may feed to our health, still we must eat the bread in the sweat of our face; and pay the penalty of the ancient sentence not with the labour of the body only, but also with that of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:49
verses.text: Let him speak then, and let us hear the parables and propositions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:50
verses.text: "How great things we have heard, and have known them, and our fathers have told them to us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:51
verses.text: The Lord was speaking higher up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:52
verses.text: For of what other person could these words be thought to be, "Hearken ye, O My people, to My law"? Why is it then that now on a sudden a man is speaking, for here we have the words of a man, "our fathers have told them to us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:53
verses.text: Without doubt God, now about to speak by a man's ministry, as the Apostle saith, "Will ye to receive proof of Him that is speaking in me, Christ?" in His own person at first willed the words to be uttered, lest a man speaking His words should be despised as a man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:54
verses.text: For it is thus with the sayings of God which make their way to us through our bodily sense.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:55
verses.text: The Creator moveth the subject creature by an invisible working; not so that the substance is changed into anything corporal and temporal, when by means of corporal and temporal signs, whether belonging to the eyes or to the ears, as far as men are able to receive it, He would make His will to be known.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:56
verses.text: For if an angel is able to use air, mist, cloud, fire, and any other natural substance or corporal species; and man to use face, tongue, hand, pen, letters, or any other significants, for the purpose of intimating the secret things of his own mind: in a word, if, though he is a man, he sendeth human messengers, and he saith to one, "Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to his servant, Do this, and he doeth it;" with how much greater and more effectual power doth God, to whom as Lord all things together are subject, use both the same angel and man, in order that He may declare whatsoever pleaseth Him?For those things were heard in the Old Testament which are known in the New: heard when they were being prophesied, known when they were being fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:57
verses.text: Where a promise is performed, hearing is not deceived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:58
verses.text: "And our fathers," Moses and the Prophets, "have told unto us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:59
verses.text: "They have not been hidden from their sons in another generation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:60
verses.text: This is our generation wherein there hath been given to us regeneration.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:61
verses.text: "Telling forth the praises of the Lord and His powers, and His wonderful works which He hath done".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:62
verses.text: The order of the words is, "and our fathers have told unto us, telling forth the praises of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:63
verses.text: The Lord is praised, in order that He may be loved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:64
verses.text: For what object can be loved more to our health? "And He hath raised up a testimony in Jacob, and hath set a law in Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:65
verses.text: This is the beginning whereof hath been spoken above, "I will declare propositions from the beginning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:66
verses.text: So then the beginning is the Old Testament, the end is the New.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:67
verses.text: For fear doth prevail in the law "But the end of the law is Christ for righteousness to every one believing;" at whose bestowing "love is shed abroad in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, which hath been given to us:" and love made perfect doth cast out fear, inasmuch as now without the Law the righteousness of God hath been made manifest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:68
verses.text: But inasmuch as He hath a testimony by the Law and the Prophets, therefore, "He hath raised up a testimony in Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:69
verses.text: For even that Tabernacle which was set up with a work so remarkable and full of such wondrous meanings, is named the Tabernacle of Testimony, wherein was the veil over the Ark of the Law, like the veil over the face of the Minister of the Law; because in that dispensation there were "parables and propositions".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:70
verses.text: For those things which were being preached and were coining to pass were hidden in veiled meanings, and were not seen in unveiled manifestations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:71
verses.text: But "when thou shalt have passed over unto Christ," saith the Apostle, "the veil shall be taken away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:72
verses.text: For "all the promises of God in Him are yea, Amen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:73
verses.text: Whosoever therefore doth cleave to Christ, hath the whole of the good which even in the letters of the Law he perceiveth not: but whosoever is an alien from Christ, doth neither perceive, nor hath.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:74
verses.text: "He hath set a law in Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:75
verses.text: After his usual custom he is making a repetition.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:76
verses.text: For "He hath raised up a testimony," is the same as, "He hath set a law," and "in Jacob," is the same as "in Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:77
verses.text: For as these are two names of one man, so law and testimony are two names of one thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:78
verses.text: Is there any difference, saith some one, between "hath raised up" and "hath set"? Yea indeed, the same difference as there is between "Jacob" and "Israel:" not because they were two persons, but these same two names were bestowed upon one man for different reasons; Jacob because of supplanting, for that he grasped the foot of his brother at his birth: but Israel because of the vision of God So "raised up" is one thing, "set" is another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:79
verses.text: For, "He hath raised up a testimony," as far as I can judge, hath been said because by it something has been raised up; "For without the Law," saith the Apostle, "sin was dead: but I lived sometime without the Law: but at the coming in of the commandment sin revived".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:80
verses.text: Behold that which hath been raised up by the testimony, which is the Law, so that what was lying hidden might appear, as he saith a little afterwards: "But sin, that it might appear sin, through a good thing hath wrought in me death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:81
verses.text: But "He hath set a law," hath been said, as though it were a yoke upon sinners, whence hath been said, "For upon a just man law hath not been imposed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:82
verses.text: It is a testimony then, so far forth as it doth prove anything; but a law so far forth as it doth command; though it is one and the same thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:83
verses.text: Wherefore just as Christ is a stone, but to believers for the Head of the corner, while to unbelievers a stone of offence and a rock of scandal; so the testimony of the Law to them that use not the Law lawfully, is a testimony whereby sinners are to be convicted as deserving of punishment; but to them that use the same lawfully, is a testimony whereby sinners are shown unto whom they ought to flee in order to be delivered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:84
verses.text: "How great things," he saith, "He hath commanded our fathers, to make the same known to their sons?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:85
verses.text: "That another generation may know, sons who shall be born and shall rise up, and they may tell to their sons".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:86
verses.text: "That they may put their hope in God, and may not forget the works of God, and may seek out His commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:87
verses.text: "That they may not become, like their fathers, a crooked and embittering generation: a generation that hath not guided their heart, and the spirit thereof hath not been trusted with God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:88
verses.text: These words do point out two peoples as it were, the one belonging to the Old Testament, the other to the New: for in that he saith, he hath implied that they received the commandments, "to make them known to their sons," but that they did not know or do them: but they received them themselves, to the end "that another generation might know," what the former knew not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:89
verses.text: "Sons who shall be born and shall arise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:90
verses.text: For they that have been born have not arisen: because they had not their heart above, but rather on the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:91
verses.text: For the arising is with Christ: whence hath been said, "If ye have arisen with Christ, savour ye the things which are above".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:92
verses.text: "And they may tell them," he saith, "to their sons, in order that they may put their hope in God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:93
verses.text: "And may not forget the works of God:" that is to say, in magnifying and vaunting their own works, as though they did them themselves; while "God it is that worketh," in them that work good things, "both to will and to work according to good will".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:94
verses.text: "And may search out His commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:95
verses.text: The commandments which He hath commanded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:96
verses.text: How then should they still search out, whereas they have already learned them, save that by putting their hope in God, they do then search out His commandments, in order that by them, with His aid, they may be fulfilled? And he saith why, by immediately subjoining, "and its spirit hath not been trusted with God," that is, because it had no faith, which doth obtain what the Law doth enjoin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:97
verses.text: For when the spirit of man doth work together with the Spirit of God working, then there is fulfilled that which God hath commanded: and this doth not come to pass, except by believing in Him that doth justify an ungodly man Which faith the generation crooked and embittering had not: and therefore concerning the same hath been said, "The spirit thereof hath not been trusted with God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:98
verses.text: For this hath been said much more exactly to point out the grace of God, which doth work not only remission of sins, but also doth make the spirit of man to work together therewith in the work of good deeds, as though he were saying, his spirit hath not believed in God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:99
verses.text: For to have the spirit trusted with God, is, not to believe that his spirit is able to do righteousness without God, but with God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:100
verses.text: For this is to believe in God: which is surely more than to believe God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:101
verses.text: For ofttimes we must believe even a man, though in him we must not believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:102
verses.text: To believe in God therefore is this, in believing to cleave unto God who worketh good works, in order to work with Him well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:103
verses.text: Lastly, "The sons of Ephrem bending and shooting bows, have been turned back in the day of war".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:104
verses.text: Following after the law of righteousness, unto the law of righteousness they have not attained Why? Because they were not of faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:105
verses.text: For they were that generation whereof the spirit hath not been trusted with God: but they were, so to speak, of works: because they did not, as they bended and shot their bows (which are outward actions, as of the works of the law), so guide their heart also, wherein the just man doth live by faith, which worketh by love; whereby men cleave to God, who worketh in man both to will and work according to good will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:106
verses.text: For what else is bending the bow and shooting, and turning back in the day of war, but heeding and purposing in the day of hearing, and deserting in the day of temptation; flourishing arms, so to speak, beforehand, and at the hour of the action refusing to fight? But whereas he saith, "bending and shooting bows," when it would seem that he ought to have said, bending bows and shooting arrows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:107
verses.text: Some Greek copies to be sure are said to have "bending and shooting with bows," so that without doubt we ought to understand arrows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:108
verses.text: But whereas by the sons of Ephrem he hath willed that there be understood the whole of that embittering generation, it is an expression signifying the whole by a part.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:109
verses.text: And perhaps this part was chosen whereby to signify the whole, because from these men especially some good thing was to have been expected.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:110
verses.text: Although set at the left hand by his father as being the younger, Jacob nevertheless blessed with his right hand, and preferred him before his elder brother with a benediction of hidden meaningFor there was being figured how they were to be last that were first, and first were to be they that were last, through the Saviour's coming, concerning whom hath been said, "He that is coming after me was made before me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:111
verses.text: In like manner righteous Abel was preferred before the elder brother; so to Ismael Isaac; so to Esau, though born before him, his twin brother Jacob; so also Phares himself preceded even in birth his twin brother, who had first thrust a hand out of the womb, and had begun to be born: so David was preferred before his elder brother: and as the reason why all these parables and others like them preceded, not only of words but also of deeds, in like manner to the people of the Jews was preferred the Christian people, for redeeming the which as Abel by Cain, so by the Jews was slain Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:112
verses.text: This thing was prefigured even when Jacob stretching out his hands cross-wise, with his right hand touched Ephrem standing on the left; and set him before Manasse standing on the right, whom he himself touched with the left hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:113
verses.text: But what that is which he saith, "they have been turned back in the day of war," the following words do teach, wherein he hath most clearly explained this: "they have not kept," he saith, "the testament of God, and in His law they would not walk".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:114
verses.text: Behold what is, "they have been turned back in the day of war:" they have not kept the testament of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:115
verses.text: When they were bending and shooting bows, they did also utter the words of most forward promise, saying, "Whatsoever things the Lord our God hath spoken we will do, and we will hear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:116
verses.text: "They have been turned back in the day of war:" because the promise of obedience not hearing but temptation doth prove.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:117
verses.text: But he whose spirit hath been trusted with God, keepeth hold on God, who is faithful, and "doth not suffer him to be tempted above that which he is able; but will make with the temptation a way of escape also," that he may be able to endure, and may not be turned back in the day of war.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:118
verses.text: Therefore these men have been thus branded: "a generation," he saith, "which hath not directed their heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:119
verses.text: It hath not been said, works, but heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:120
verses.text: For when the heart is directed, the works are right; but when the heart is not directed, the works are not right, even though they seem to be right.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:121
verses.text: And how the crooked generation hath not directed the heart, hath sufficiently been shown, when he saith, "and the spirit thereof hath not been trusted with God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:122
verses.text: For God is right: and therefore by cleaving to the right, as to an immutable rule, the heart of a man can be made right, which in itself was crooked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:123
verses.text: "And they forgat His benefits, and the wonderful works of Him which He showed to them; before their fathers the wonderful things which He did".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:124
verses.text: What this is, is not a question to be negligently passed over.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:125
verses.text: Concerning those very fathers he was speaking a little before, that they had been a generation crooked and embittering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:126
verses.text: What fathers, inasmuch as these are the very fathers, whom he would not have posterity to be like? If we shall take them to be those out of whom the others had derived their being, for example, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, by this time they had long since fallen asleep, when God showed wonderful things in Egypt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:127
verses.text: For there followeth, "in the land of Egypt, in the plain of Thanis" : where it is said that God showed to them wonderful things before their fathers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:128
verses.text: Were they perchance present in spirit? For of the same the Lord saith in the Gospel, "for all do live to Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:129
verses.text: Or do we more suitably understand thereby the fathers Moses and Aaron, and the other elders who are related in the same Scripture also to have received the Spirit, of which also Moses received, in order that they might aid him in ruling and bearing the same people? For why should they not have been called fathers? It is not in the same manner as God is the One Father, who doth regenerate with His Spirit those whom He doth make sons for an everlasting inheritance; but it is for the sake of honour, because of their age and kindly carefulness: just as Paul the elder saith, "Not to confound you I am writing these things, but as my dearly beloved sons I am admonishing you:" though he knew of a truth that it had been said by the Lord, "Call ye no man your father on earth, for One is your Father, even God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:130
verses.text: And this was not said in order that this term of human honour should be erased from our usual way of speaking: but lest the grace of God whereby we are regenerated unto eternal life, should be ascribed either to the power or even sanctity of any man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:131
verses.text: Therefore when he said, "I have begotten you;" he first said, "in Christ," and "through the Gospel;" lest that might be thought to be of him, which is of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:132
verses.text: Accordingly, the land of Egypt must be understood for a figure of this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:133
verses.text: "The plain of Thanis" is the smooth surface of lowly commandment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:134
verses.text: For lowly commandment is the interpretation of Thanis.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:135
verses.text: In this world therefore let us receive the commandment of humility, in order that in another world we may merit to receive the exaltation which He hath promised, who for our sake here became lowly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:136
verses.text: For He that "did burst asunder the sea and made them go through, did confine the waters as it were in bottles" , in order that the water might stand up first as if it were shut in, is able by His grace to restrain the flowing and ebbing tides of carnal desires, when we renounce this world, so that all sins having been thoroughly washed away, as if they were enemies, the people of the faithful may be made to pass through by means of the Sacrament of Baptism.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:137
verses.text: He that "led them home in the cloud of the day, and in the whole of the night in the illumination of fire" , is able also spiritually to direct goings if faith crieth to Him, "Direct Thou my goings after Thy word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:138
verses.text: Of Whom in another place is said, "For Himself shall make thy courses right, and shall prolong thy goings in peace" through Jesus Christ our Lord, whose Sacrament in this world, as it were in the day, is manifest in the flesh, as if in a cloud; but in the Judgment it will be manifest like as in a terror by night; for then there will be a great tribulation of the world like as it were fire, and it shall shine for the just and shall burn for the unjust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:139
verses.text: "He that burst asunder the rock in the desert, and gave them water as in a great deep" ; "and brought out water from the rock, and brought down waters like rivers" , is surely able upon thirsty faith to pour the gift of the Holy Spirit (the which gift the performance of that thing did spiritually signify), to pour, I say, from the Spiritual Rock that followed, which is Christ: who did stand and cry, "If any is athirst, let him come to Me:" and, "he that shall have drunk of the water which I shall give, rivers of living water shall flow out of his bosom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:140
verses.text: For this He spake, as is read in the Gospel, to the Spirit, which they were to receive that believed in Him, unto whom like the rod drew near the wood of the Passion, in order that there might flow forth grace for believers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:141
verses.text: And yet, "they," like a generation crooked and embittering, "added yet to sin against Him" : that is, not to believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:142
verses.text: For this is the sin, whereof the Spirit doth convict the world, as the Lord saith, "Of sin indeed because they have not believed on Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:143
verses.text: "And they exasperated the Most High in drought," which other copies have, "in a place without water," which is a more exact translation from the Greek, and doth signify no other thing than drought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:144
verses.text: Was it in that drought of the desert, or rather in their own? For although they had drank of the rock, they had not their bellies but their minds dry, freshening with no fruitfulness of righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:145
verses.text: In that drought they ought the more faithfully to have been suppliant unto God, in order that He who had given fulness unto their jaws, might give also equity to their manners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:146
verses.text: For unto him the faithful soul doth cry, "Let mine eyes see equity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:147
verses.text: "And they tempted God in their hearts, in order that they might seek morsels for their souls".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:148
verses.text: It is one thing to ask in believing, another thing in tempting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:149
verses.text: Lastly there followeth, "And they slandered God, and said, Shall God be able to prepare a table in the desert?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:150
verses.text: "For He smote the rock, and the waters flowed, and torrents gushed forth: will He be able to give bread also, or to prepare a table for His people?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:151
verses.text: Not believing therefore, they sought morsels for their souls.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:152
verses.text: Not so the Apostle James doth enjoin a morsel to be asked for the mind, but doth admonish that it be sought by believers, not by such as tempt and slander God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:153
verses.text: "But if any one of you," he saith, "doth lack wisdom, let him ask of God, who doth give to all men abundantly, and doth not upbraid, and it shall be given to him: but let him ask in faith, nothing wavering".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:154
verses.text: This faith had not that generation which "had not directed their heart, and the spirit thereof had not been trusted with God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:155
verses.text: "Wherefore the Lord heard, and He delayed, and fire was lighted in Jacob, and wrath went up into Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:156
verses.text: He hath explained what he hath called fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:157
verses.text: He hath called anger fire: although in strict propriety fire did also burn up many men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:158
verses.text: What is therefore this that he saith, "The Lord heard, and He delayed"? Did He delay to conduct them into the land of promise, whither they were being led: which might have been done in the space of a few days, but on account of sins they must needs be wasted in the desert, where also they were wasted during forty years? And if this be so, He did then delay the people, not those very persons who tempted and slandered God: for they all perished in the desert, and their children journeyed into the land of promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:159
verses.text: Or did He delay punishment, in order that He might first satisfy unbelieving concupiscence, lest He might be supposed to be angry, because they were asking of Him what He was not able to do? "He heard," then, "and He delayed to avenge:" and after He had done what they supposed He was not able to do, then "anger went up upon Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:160
verses.text: Lastly, when both these things have been briefly touched, afterwards he is evidently following out the order of the narrative.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:161
verses.text: "Because they believed not in God, nor hoped in His saving health".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:162
verses.text: For when he had told why fire was lighted in Jacob, and anger went up upon Israel, that is to say, "because they believed not in God, nor hoped in His saving health:" immediately subjoining the evident blessings for which they were ungrateful, he saith, "and He commanded the clouds above, and opened the doors of Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:163
verses.text: "And He rained upon them manna to eat, and gave them bread of Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:164
verses.text: "Bread of angels man did eat: dainties He sent them in abundance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:165
verses.text: He brought over the South Wind from Heaven, and in His virtue He led in the South West Wind".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:166
verses.text: "And He rained upon them fleshes like dust, and winged fowls like the sand of the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:167
verses.text: "And they fell in the midst of their camp, around their tabernacles".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:168
verses.text: "And they ate and were filled exceedingly; and their desire He brought to them: they were not deprived of their desire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:169
verses.text: Behold why He had delayed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:170
verses.text: But what He had delayed let us hear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:171
verses.text: "Yet the morsel was in their mouths, and the anger of God came down upon them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:172
verses.text: Behold what He had delayed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:173
verses.text: For before "He delayed:" and afterwards, "fire was lighted in Jacob and anger went up upon Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:174
verses.text: He had delayed therefore in order that He might first do what they had believed that He could not do, and then might bring upon them what they deserved to suffer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:175
verses.text: For if they placed their hope in God, not only would their desires of the flesh but also those of the spirit have been fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:176
verses.text: For he that"opened the doors of Heaven, and rained upon them manna to eat," that He might fill the unbelieving, is not without power to give to believers Himself the true Bread from Heaven, which the manna did signify: which is indeed the food of Angels, whom being incorruptible the Word of God doth incorruptibly feed: the which in order that man might eat, He became flesh, and dwelled in us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:177
verses.text: For Himself the Bread by means of the Evangelical clouds is being rained over the whole world, and, the hearts of preachers like heavenly doors, being opened, is being preached not to a murmuring and tempting synagogue, but to a Church believing and putting hope in Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:178
verses.text: He is able also to feed the feeble faith of such as tempt not, but believe, with the signs of words uttered by the flesh and speeding through the air, as though it were fowls: not however with such as come from the north, where cold and mist do prevail, that is to say, eloquence which is pleasing to this world, but by bringing over the South Wind from Heaven; whither, except to the earth? In order that they who are feeble in faith, by hearing things earthly may be nourished up to receive things heavenly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:179
verses.text: But as to unbelievers, being a crooked and embittering generation, as it were, while the morsel was yet in their mouths, "the anger of God went up upon them, and it slew among the most of them" : that is, the most of them, or as some copies have it, "the fat ones of them," which however in the Greek copies which we had, we did not find.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:180
verses.text: But if this be the truer reading, what else must be understood by "the fat ones of them," than men mighty in pride, concerning whom is said, "their iniquity shall come forth as if out of fat"? "And the elect of Israel He fettered".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:181
verses.text: Even there there were elect, with whose faith the generation crooked and embittering was not mixed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:182
verses.text: But they were fettered, so that they might in no sort profit them for whom they desired that they might provide from a fatherly affection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:183
verses.text: For what is conferred by human mercy, on those with whom God is angry? Or rather hath He willed it to be understood, how that even the elect were fettered at the same time with them, in order that they who were diverse both in mind and in life, might endure sufferings with them for an example not only of righteousness, but also of patience? For we have learned that holy men were even led captive with sinners for no other reason; since in the Greek copies we read not ἐνεπόδισεν, which is "fettered;" but συνεπόδισεν, which is rather "fettered together with".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:184
verses.text: But the generation crooked and embittering, "in all these things sinned yet more, and they believed not in His wonderful works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:185
verses.text: "And in their days failed in vanity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:186
verses.text: Though they might, if they had believed, have had days in truth without failing, with Him to whom hath been said, "Thy years shall not fail".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:187
verses.text: Therefore, "their days failed in vanity, and their years with haste".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:188
verses.text: For the whole life of mortal men is hastening, and that which seemeth to be longer is but a vapour of somewhat longer duration.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:189
verses.text: Nevertheless, "when he slew them they sought Him:" not for the sake of eternal life, but fearing to end the vapour too soon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:190
verses.text: There sought Him then, not indeed those whom He had slain, but they that were afraid of being slain according to the example of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:191
verses.text: But the Scripture hath so spoken of them as if they sought God who were slain; because they were one people, and it is spoken as if of one body: "and they returned, and at dawn they came to God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:192
verses.text: "And they remembered that God is their Helper, and the High God is their Redeemer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:193
verses.text: But all this is for the sake of acquiring temporal good things, and for avoiding temporal evil things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:194
verses.text: For they that did seek God for the sake of temporal blessings, sought not God indeed, but things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:195
verses.text: Thus with those God is worshipped with slavish fear, not free love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:196
verses.text: Thus then God is not worshipped, for that thing is worshipped which is loved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:197
verses.text: Whence because God is found to be greater and better than all things, He must be loved more than all things, in order that He may be worshipped.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:198
verses.text: Lastly, here let us see the words following: "And they loved Him," he saith, "in their mouth, and in their tongue they lied unto Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:199
verses.text: "But their heart was not right with Him, and they were not counted faithful in His Testament".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:200
verses.text: One thing on their tongue, another thing in their heart He found, unto whom the secret things of men are naked, and without any impediment He saw what they loved rather.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:201
verses.text: Therefore the heart is right with God, when it doth seek God for the sake of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:202
verses.text: For one thing he desired of the Lord, the same he will require, that he may dwell always in the House of the Lord, and may meditate on the pleasantness of Him Unto Whom saith the heart of the faithful, I will be filled, not with the flesh-pots of the Egyptians, nor with melons and gourds, and garlick and onions, which a generation crooked and embittering did prefer even to bread celestial, nor with visible manna, and those same winged fowls; but, "I will be filled, when Thy glory shall be made manifest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:203
verses.text: For this is the inheritance of the New Testament, wherein they were not counted faithful; whereof however the faith even at that time, when it was veiled, was in the elect, and now, when it hath already been revealed, it is not in many that are called.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:204
verses.text: "For many have been called, but few are elect".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:205
verses.text: Of such sort therefore was the generation crooked and embittering, even when they were seeming to seek God, loving in mouth, and in tongue lying; but in heart not right with God, while they loved rather those things, for the sake of which they required the help of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:206
verses.text: "But He is Himself merciful, and will become propitious to their sins, and He will not destroy them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:207
verses.text: And He will abound to turn away His anger, and He will not kindle all his anger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:208
verses.text: By these words many men promise to themselves impunity for their iniquity from the Divine Mercy, even if they shall have persevered in being such, as that generation is described, "crooked and embittering; which hath not directed their heart, and the spirit thereof hath not been trusted with God:" with whom it is not profitable to agree.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:209
verses.text: For if, to speak in their words, God will perchance not destroy no not even bad men, without doubt He will not destroy good men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:210
verses.text: Why then do we not rather choose that wherein there is no doubt? For they that lie to Him in their tongue, though their heart doth hold some other thing, do think indeed, and will, even God to be a liar, when He doth menace upon such men eternal punishment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:211
verses.text: But whilst they do not deceive Him with their lying, He doth not deceive them with speaking the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:212
verses.text: These words therefore of divine sayings, concerning which the crooked generation doth cajole itself, let it not make crooked like its own heart: for even when it is made crooked, they continue right.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:213
verses.text: For at first they may be understood according to that which is written in the Gospel, "that ye may be like your Father who is in the Heavens, who maketh His sun to rise upon good men and evil men, and raineth upon just men and unjust men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:214
verses.text: For who could not see, how great is the long-suffering of mercy with which He is sparing evil men? But before the Judgment, He spared then that nation in such sort, that He kindled not all His anger, utterly to root it up and bring it to an end: which thing in His words and in the intercession for their sins of His servant Moses doth evidently appear, where God saith, "Let Me blot them out, and make thee into a great nation:" he intercedeth, being more ready to be blotted out for them than that they should be; knowing that he is doing this before One Merciful, who inasmuch as by no means He would blot out him, would even spare them for his sake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:215
verses.text: For let us see how greatly He spared, and doth still spare.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:216
verses.text: In the second place, that we may not seem to do violence to divine words, and lest in the place where there was said, "He will not destroy them," w e should say, "But hereafter He will destroy them:" concerning this very present Psalm let us turn to a very common phrase of the Scripture, whereby this question may be more diligently and more truly solved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:217
verses.text: Speaking of these same persons a little lower down, when He had made mention of the things which the Egyptians because of them had endured, He saith,"And He led them unto the mount of His sanctification, the mount which His right hand won.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:218
verses.text: And He cast out from their face the nations, and by lot distributed to them the land in the cord of distribution".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:219
verses.text: If any one at these words should press a question upon us, and should say, How doth he make mention of all these things as having been bestowed upon them, when the same persons were not led into the land of promise, as were delivered from Egypt, inasmuch as they were dead? What shall we reply but that they were spoken of, because they were the self-same people by means of a succession of sons?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:220
verses.text: "And He remembered that they are flesh, a spirit going and not returning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:221
verses.text: Therefore calling them and pitying them through His grace, He called them back Himself, because of themselves they could not return.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:222
verses.text: For how doth flesh return, "a spirit walking and not turning back," while a weight of evil deserts doth weigh it down unto the lowest and far places of evil, save through the election of grace?For thus also is solved this no unimportant question, how it is written in the Proverbs, when the Scripture was speaking of the way of iniquity, "all they that walk in her shall not return".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:223
verses.text: For it hath been so spoken as if all ungodly men were to be despaired of: but the Scripture did only commend grace; for of himself man is able to walk in that way, but is not able of himself to return, except when called back by grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:224
verses.text: I say then of these crooked and embittering persons, "How often they exasperated Him in the desert, and provoked Him to wrath in the waterless place!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:225
verses.text: "And they turned themselves and tempted God, and exasperated the Holy One of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:226
verses.text: He is repeating that same unbelief of theirs, of which He had made mention above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:227
verses.text: But the reason of the repetition is, in order that there may be mentioned also the plagues which He inflicted on the Egyptians for their sakes: all which things they certainly ought to have remembered, and not to be ungrateful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:228
verses.text: Lastly, there followeth what? "They remembered not His hands, in the day when He redeemed them from the hand of the troubler".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 80:229
