verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:39
verses.text: Conquered, because he willed it; in flesh weak, in majesty strong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:40
verses.text: Having been crucified of weakness, rise Thou in power: "Stir up Thy power, and come Thou, to save us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:41
verses.text: "O God, convert us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:42
verses.text: For averse we have been from Thee, and except Thou convert us, we shall not be converted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:43
verses.text: "And illumine Thy face, and we shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:44
verses.text: Hath He anywise a darkened face? He hath not a darkened face, but He placed before it a cloud of flesh, and as it were a veil of weakness; and when He hung on the tree, He was not thought the Same as He was after to be acknowledged when He was sitting in Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:45
verses.text: For thus it hath come to pass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:46
verses.text: Christ present on the earth, and doing miracles, Asaph knew not; but when He had died, after that He rose again, and ascended into Heaven, he knew Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:47
verses.text: He was pricked to the heart, and he may have spoken also of Him this testimony which now we acknowledge in this Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:48
verses.text: Thou didst cover Thy face, and we were sick: illumine Thou the same, and we shall be whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:49
verses.text: "O Lord God of virtues, how long wilt Thou be angry with the prayer of Thy servant?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:50
verses.text: Now Thy servant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:51
verses.text: Thou wast angry at the prayer of Thy enemy, wilt Thou still be angry with the prayer of Thy servant? Thou hast converted us, we know Thee, and wilt Thou still be angry with the prayer of Thy servant? Thou wilt evidently be angry, in fact, as a father correcting, not as a judge condemning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:52
verses.text: In such manner evidently Thou wilt be angry, because it hath been written, "My son, drawing near unto the service of God, stand thou in righteousness and in fear, and prepare thy soul for temptation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:53
verses.text: Think not that now the wrath of God hath passed away, because thou hast been converted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:54
verses.text: The wrath of God hath passed away from thee, but only so that it condemn not for everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:55
verses.text: But He scourgeth, He spareth not: because He scourgeth every son whom He receiveth If thou refusest to be scourged, why dost thou desire to be received? He scourgeth every son whom He receiveth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:56
verses.text: He who did not spare even His only Son, scourgeth every one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:57
verses.text: But nevertheless, "How long wilt Thou be angry with the prayer of Thy servant?" No longer thine enemy: but, "Thou wilt be angry with the prayer of Thy servant," how long? There followeth: "Thou wilt feed us with the bread of tears, and wilt give us to drink with tears in measure".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:58
verses.text: What is, "in measure"? Hear the Apostle: "Faithful is God, who doth not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able to bear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:59
verses.text: The measure is, according to your powers: the measure is, that thou be instructed, not that thou be crushed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:60
verses.text: "Thou hast set us for a contradiction to our neighbours".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:61
verses.text: Evidently this did come to pass: for out of Asaph were chosen they that should go to the Gentiles and preach Christ, and should have it said to them, "Who is this proclaimer of new demons?" "Thou hast set us for a contradiction to our neighbours".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:62
verses.text: For they were preaching Him who was the subject of the contradiction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:63
verses.text: Whom did they preach? That after He was dead, Christ rose again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:64
verses.text: Who would hear this? Who would know this? It is a new thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:65
verses.text: But signs did follow, and to an incredible thing miracles gave credibility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:66
verses.text: He was contradicted, but the contradictor was conquered, and from being a contradictor was made a believer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:67
verses.text: There, however, was a great flame: there the martyrs fed with the bread of tears, and given to drink in tears, but in measure, not more than they are able to bear; in order that after the measure of tears there should follow a crown of joys.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:68
verses.text: "And our enemies have sneered at us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:69
verses.text: And where are they that sneered? For a long while it was said, Who are they that worship the Dead One, that adore the Crucified? For a long while so it was said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:70
verses.text: Where is the nose of them that sneered? Now do not they that censure flee into caves, that they may not be seen? But ye see what followeth: "O Lord God of virtues, convert us, and show Thy face, and we shall be whole".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:71
verses.text: "A vineyard out of Egypt Thou hast brought over, Thou hast cast out the nations, and hast planted her".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:72
verses.text: It was done, we know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:73
verses.text: How many nations were cast out? Amorites, Cethites, Jebusites, Gergesites, and Evites: after whose expulsion and overthrow, there was led in the people delivered out of Egypt, into the land of promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:74
verses.text: Whence the vineyard was cast out, and where she was planted, we have heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:75
verses.text: Let us see what next was done, how she believed, how much she grew, what ground she covered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:76
verses.text: "A way Thou hast made in the sight of her, and hast planted the roots of her, and she hath filled the land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:77
verses.text: Would she have filled the land, unless a way had been made in the sight of her? What was the way which was made in the sight of her? "I am," He saith, "the Way, the Truth, and the Life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:78
verses.text: With reason she hath filled the land.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:79
verses.text: That hath now been said of this vineyard, which hath been accomplished at the last.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:80
verses.text: But in the mean time what? "She hath covered the mountains with her shadow, and with her branch the cedars of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:81
verses.text: "Thou hast stretched out her boughs even unto the sea, and even unto the river her shoots".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:82
verses.text: This requireth the office of an expositor, that of a reader and pra iser doth not suffice: aid me with attention; for the mention of this vineyard in this Psalm is wont to overcloud with darkness the inattentive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:83
verses.text: But nevertheless the first Jewish nation was this vine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:84
verses.text: But the Jewish nation reigned as far as the sea and as far as the river.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:85
verses.text: As far as the sea; it appeareth in Scripture that the sea was in the vicinity thereof.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:86
verses.text: And as far as the river Jordan.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:87
verses.text: For on the other side of Jordan some part of the Jews was established, but within Jordan was the whole nation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:88
verses.text: Therefore, "even unto the sea and even unto the river," is the kingdom of the Jews, the kingdom of Israel: but not "from sea even unto sea, and from the river even unto the ends of the round world;" this is the future perfection of the vineyard, concerning which in this place he hath foretold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:89
verses.text: When, I say, he had foretold to thee the perfection, he returneth to the beginning, out of which the perfection was made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:90
verses.text: Of the beginning wilt thou hear? "Even unto the river".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:91
verses.text: Of the end wilt thou hear? "He shall have dominion from sea even unto sea:" that is, "she hath filled the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:92
verses.text: Let us look then to the testimony of Asaph, as to what was done to the first vineyard, and what must be expected for the second vineyard, nay to the same vineyard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:93
verses.text: What then, the vineyard before the sight whereof a way was made, that she should fill the earth, at first was where? "Her shadow covered the mountains".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:94
verses.text: Who are the mountains? The Prophets.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:95
verses.text: Why did her shadow cover them? Because darkly they spake the things which were foretold as to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:96
verses.text: Thou hearest from the Prophets, Keep the Sabbath-day, on the eighth day circumcise a child, offer sacrifice of ram, of calf, of he-goat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:97
verses.text: Be not troubled, her shadow doth cover the mountains of God; there will come after the shadow a manifestation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:98
verses.text: "And her shrubs the cedars of God," that is, she hath covered the cedars of God; very lofty, but of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:99
verses.text: For the cedars are types of the proud, that must needs be overthrown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:100
verses.text: The "cedars of Lebanon," the heights of the world, this vineyard did cover in growing, and the mountains of God, all the holy Prophets and Patriarchs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:101
verses.text: Then what? "Wherefore hast Thou thrown down her  enclosure?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:102
verses.text: Now ye see the overthrow of that nation of the Jews: already out of another Psalm ye have heard, "with axe and hammer they have thrown her down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:103
verses.text: When could this have been done, except her enclosure had been thrown down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:104
verses.text: What is her enclosure? Her defence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:105
verses.text: For she bore herself proudly against her planter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:106
verses.text: The servants that were sent to her and demanded a recompense, the husbandmen they scourged, beat, slew: there came also the Only Son, they said, "This is the Heir; come, let us kill Him, and our own the inheritance will be:" they killed Him, and out of the vineyard they cast Him forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:107
verses.text: When cast forth, He did more perfectly possess the place whence He was cast forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:108
verses.text: For thus He threatens her through Isaiah, "I will throw down her enclosure".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:109
verses.text: Wherefore? "For I looked that she should bring forth grapes, but she brought forth thorns".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:110
verses.text: I looked for fruit from thence, and I found sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:111
verses.text: Why then dost thou ask, O Asaph, "Why hast Thou thrown down her enclosure?" For knowest thou not why? I looked that she should do judgment, and she did iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:112
verses.text: Must not her enclosure needs be thrown down? And there came the Gentiles when the enclosure was thrown down, the vineyard was assailed, and the kingdom of the Jews effaced.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:113
verses.text: This at first he is lamenting, but not without hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:114
verses.text: For of directing  the heart he is now speaking, that is, for the "Assyrians," for "men directing," the Psalm is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:115
verses.text: "Wherefore hast Thou thrown down her enclosure: and there pluck off her grapes all men passing along the way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:116
verses.text: What is "men passing along the way?" Men having dominion for a time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:117
verses.text: "There hath laid her waste the boar from the wood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:118
verses.text: In the boar from the wood what do we understand? To the Jews a swine is an abomination, and in a swine they imagine as it were the uncleanness of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:119
verses.text: But by the Gentiles was overthrown the nation of the Jews: but that king who overthrew, was not only an unclean swine, but was also a boar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:120
verses.text: For what is a boar but a savage swine, a furious swine? "A boar from the wood hath laid her waste".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:121
verses.text: "From the wood," from the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:122
verses.text: For she was a vineyard, but the Gentiles were woods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:123
verses.text: But when the Gentiles believed, there was said what? "Then there shall exult all the trees of the woods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:124
verses.text: "The boar from the wood hath laid her waste; and a singular wild beast hath devoured her".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:125
verses.text: "A singular wild beast" is what? The very boar that laid her waste is the singular wild beast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:126
verses.text: Singular, because proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:127
verses.text: For thus saith every proud one, It is I, it is I, and no other.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:128
verses.text: But with what profit is this? "O God of virtues turn Thou nevertheless".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:129
verses.text: Although these things have been done, "Turn Thou nevertheless".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:130
verses.text: "Look from heaven and see, and visit this vineyard".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:131
verses.text: "And perfect Thou her whom Thy right hand hath planted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:132
verses.text: No other plant Thou, but this make Thou perfect.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:133
verses.text: For she is the very seed of Abraham, she is the very seed in whom all nations shall be blessed: there is the root where is borne the graffed wild olive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:134
verses.text: "Perfect Thou this vineyard which Thy right hand hath planted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:135
verses.text: But wherein doth He perfect? "And upon the Son of man, whom Thou hast strengthened to Thyself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:136
verses.text: What can be more evident? Why do ye still expect, that we should still explain to you in discourse, and should we not rather cry out with you in admiration, "Perfect Thou this vineyard which Thy right hand hath planted, and upon the Son of man" perfect her? What Son of man? Him "whom Thou hast strengthened to Thyself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:137
verses.text: A mighty stronghold: build as much as thou art able.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:138
verses.text: "For other foundation no one is able to lay, except that which is laid, which is Christ Jesus".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:139
verses.text: "Things burned with fire, and dug up, by the rebuke of Thy countenance shall perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:140
verses.text: What are the things burned with fire and dug up which shall perish from the rebuke of His countenance? Let us see and perceive what are the things burned with fire and dug up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:141
verses.text: Christ hath rebuked what? Sins: by the rebuke of His countenance sins have perished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:142
verses.text: Why then are sins burned with fire and dug up? Of all sins, two things are the cause in man, desire and fear Think, examine, question your hearts, sift your consciences, see whether there can be sins, except they be either of desire, or of fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:143
verses.text: There is set before thee a reward to induce thee to sin, that is, a thing which delighteth thee; thou doest it, because thou desirest it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:144
verses.text: But perchance thou wilt not be allured by bribes; thou art terrified with menaces, thou doest it because thou fearest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:145
verses.text: A man would bribe thee, for example, to bear false witness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:146
verses.text: Countless cases there are, but I am setting before you the plainer cases, whereby ye may imagine the rest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:147
verses.text: Hast thou hearkened unto God, and hast thou said in thy heart, "What doth it profit a man, if he gain the whole world, but of his own soul suffer loss?" I am not allured by a bribe to lose my soul to gain money.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:148
verses.text: He turneth himself to stir up fear within thee, he who was not able to corrupt thee with a bribe, beginneth to threaten loss, banishment, massacres, perchance, and death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:149
verses.text: Therein now, if desire prevailed not, perchance fear will prevail to make thee sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:150
verses.text: What had evil fear done? It had dug up, as it were.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:151
verses.text: For love doth inflame, fear doth humble: therefore, sins of evil love, with fire were lighted: sins of evil fear were dug up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:152
verses.text: On the one hand, evil fear doth humble, and good love doth light; but in different ways respectively.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:153
verses.text: For even the husbandman interceding for the tree, that it should not be cut down, saith, "I will dig about it, and will apply a basket of dung".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:154
verses.text: The dug trench doth signify the godly humility of one fearing, and the basket of dung the profitable squalid state of one repenting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:155
verses.text: But concerning the fire of good love the Lord saith, "Fire I have come to send into the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:156
verses.text: With which fire may the fervent in spirit burn, and they too that are inflamed with the love of God and their neighbour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:157
verses.text: And thus, as all good works are wrought by good fear and good love, so by evil fear and evil love all sins are committed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:158
verses.text: Therefore, "Things set alight with fire and dug up," to wit, all sins, "by the rebuke of Thy countenance shall perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:159
verses.text: "Let Thy hand be upon the Man of Thy right hand, and upon the Son of Man whom Thou hast strengthened Thyself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:160
verses.text: "And we depart not from Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:161
verses.text: Thou wilt quicken us, and Thy Name we will invoke".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:162
verses.text: Thou shalt be sweet to us, "Thou wilt quicken us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:163
verses.text: For aforetime we did love earth, not Thee: but Thou hast mortified our members which are upon the earth For the Old Testament, having earthly promises, seemeth to exhort that God should not be loved for nought, but that He should be loved because He giveth something on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:164
verses.text: What dost thou love, so as not to love God? Tell me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:165
verses.text: Love, if thou canst, anything which He hath not made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:166
verses.text: Look round upon the whole creation, see whether in any place thou art held with the birdlime of desire, and hindered from loving the Creator, except it be by that very thing which He hath Himself created, whom thou despisest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:167
verses.text: But why dost thou love those things, except because they are beautiful? Can they be as beautiful as He by whom they were made? Thou admirest these things, because thou seest not Him: but through those things which thou admirest, love Him whom thou seest not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:168
verses.text: Examine the creation; if of itself it is, stay therein: but if it is of Him, for no other reason is it prejudicial to a lover, than because it is preferred to the Creator.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:169
verses.text: Why have I said this? With reference to this verse, brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:170
verses.text: Dead, I say, were they that did worship God that it might be well with them after the flesh: "For to be wise after the flesh is death:" and dead are they that do not worship God gratis, that is, because of Himself He is good, not because He giveth such and such good things, which He giveth even to men not good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:171
verses.text: Money wilt thou have of God? Even a robber hath it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:172
verses.text: Wife, abundance of children, soundness of body, the world's dignity, observe how many evil men have.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:173
verses.text: Is this all for the sake of which thou dost worship Him? Thy feet will totter, thou wilt suppose thyself to worship without cause, when thou seest those things to be with them who do not worship Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:174
verses.text: All these things, I say, He giveth even to evil men, Himself alone He reserveth for good men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:175
verses.text: "Thou wilt quicken us;" for dead we were, when to earthly things we did cleave; dead we were, when of the earthly man we did bear the image.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:176
verses.text: "Thou wilt quicken us;" Thou wilt renew us, the life of the inward man Thou wilt give us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:177
verses.text: "And Thy Name we will invoke;" that is, Thee we will love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:178
verses.text: Thou to us wilt be the sweet forgiver of our sins, Thou wilt be the entire reward of the justified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 82:179
verses.text: "O Lord God of virtues, convert us, and show Thy face, and we shall be whole".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXXI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:2
verses.text: For a Tit le this Psalm hath, "Unto the end for the presses, on the fifth of the Sabbath, a Psalm to Asaph himsel f".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:3
verses.text: Into one title many mysteries are heaped together, still so that the lintel of the Psalm indicates the things within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:4
verses.text: As we have to speak of the presses, let no  one expect that we shall speak of a vat, of a press, of olive baskets; because neither the Psalm hath this, and therefore it indicateth the greater mystery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:5
verses.text: No such thing did ye hear in this when it was reading.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:6
verses.text: Therefore take the presses for the mystery of the Church, which is now transacting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:7
verses.text: In the presses we observe three things, pressure, and of the pressure two things, one to be laid up, the other to be thrown away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:8
verses.text: There takes place then in the press a treading, a crushing, a weight: and with these the oil strains out secretly into the vat, the lees run openly down the streets.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:9
verses.text: Look intently on this great spectacle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:10
verses.text: For God ceaseth not to exhibit to us that which we may look upon with great joy, nor is the madness of the Circus to be compared with this spectacle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:11
verses.text: That belongeth to the lees, this to the oil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:12
verses.text: When therefore ye hear the blasphemers babble impudently and say that distresses abound in Christian times; for ye know that they love to say this: and it is an old proverb, yet one that began from Christian times, "God gives no rain; count it to the Christians!" Although it was those of old that said thus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:13
verses.text: But these now say also, "That God sends rain, count it to the Christians! God sends no rain; we sow not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:14
verses.text: God sends rain; we reap not!" And they wilfully make that an occasion of showing pride, which ought to make them more earnest in supplication, choosing rather to blaspheme than to pray.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:15
verses.text: When therefore they talk of such things, when they make such boasts, when they say these things, and say them in defiance, not with fear, but with loftiness, let them not disturb you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:16
verses.text: For suppose that pressures abound; be thou oil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:17
verses.text: Let the lees, black with the darkness of ignorance, be insolent; and let it, as though cast away in the streets, go gibing publicly: but do thou by thyself in thy heart, where He who seeth in secret will requite thee, strain off into the vat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:18
verses.text: To name some one thing about which even they murmur who make them: How great plunderings, they say, are there in our times, how great distresses of the innocent, how great robberies of other men's goods! Thus indeed thou takest notice of the lees, that other men's goods are seized; to the oil thou givest no heed, that to the poor are given even men's own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:19
verses.text: The old time had no such plunderers of other men's goods: but the old time had no such givers of their own goods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:20
verses.text: Wherefore also "on the fifth of the sabbath"? What is this? Let us go back to the first works of God, if perchance we may not there find somewhat in which we may also understand a mystery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:21
verses.text: For the sabbath is the seventh day, on which "God rested from all His works," intimating the great mystery of our future resting from all our works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:22
verses.text: First of the sabbath then is called that first day, which we also call the Lord's day; second of the sabbat h, the second day;and the sabbath itself the seventh day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:23
verses.text: See ye therefore to whom this Psalm speaketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:24
verses.text: For it seems to me that it speaketh to the baptized.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:25
verses.text: For on the fifth day God from the waters created animals: on the fifth day, that is, on the "fifth of the sabbath," God said, "Let the waters bring forth creeping things of living souls".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:26
verses.text: See ye, therefore, ye in whom the waters have already brought forth creeping things of living souls.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:27
verses.text: For ye belong to the presses, and in you, whom the waters have brought forth, one thing is strained out, another is thrown away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:28
verses.text: For there are many that live not worthily of the baptism which they have received.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:29
verses.text: For how many that are baptized have chosen rather to be filling the Circus than this Basilica! How many that are baptized are either making booths in the streets, or complaining that they are not made!  But this Psalm, "For the presses," and "on the fifth of the sabbath," is sung "unto Asaph".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:30
verses.text: Asaph was a certain man called by this name, as Idithun, as Core, as other names that we find in the titles of the Psalms: yet the interpretation of this name intimates the mystery of a hidden truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:31
verses.text: Asaph, in fact, in Latin is interpreted "congregation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:32
verses.text: Therefore, "For the presses, on the fifth of the sabbath," it is sung "unto Asa ph," that is, for a distinguishing pressure, to the baptized, born again of water, the Psalm is sung to the Lord's congregation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:33
verses.text: We have read the title on the lintel, and have understood what it means by these "presses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:34
verses.text: Now if you please let us see the very house of the composition, that is, the interior of the press.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:35
verses.text: Let us enter, look in, rejoice, fear, desire, av oid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:36
verses.text: For all these things ye are to find in this inward house, that is, in the text of the Psalm itself, when we shall have begun to read, and, with the Lord's help, to speak what He grants us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:37
verses.text: Behold yourselves, O Asaph, congregation of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:38
verses.text: "Exult ye unto God our helper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:39
verses.text: Ye who are gathered  together to-day, ye are this day the congregation of the Lord, if indeed unto you the Psalm is sung, "Exult ye unto God our helper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:40
verses.text: Others exult unto the Circus, ye unto God: others exult unto their deceiver, do ye exult unto your helper: others exult unto their god their belly, do ye exult unto your God your helper.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:41
verses.text: "Jubilate unto the God of Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:42
verses.text: Because ye also belong to Jacob: yea, ye are Jacob, the younger people to which the elder is servant "Jubilate unto the God of Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:43
verses.text: Whatsoever ye cannot explain in words, ye do not therefore forbear exulting: what ye shall be able to explain, cry out: what ye cannot, jubilate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:44
verses.text: For from the abundance of joys, he that cannot find words sufficient, useth to break out into jubilating; "Jubilate unto the God of Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:45
verses.text: "Take the Psalm and give the tabret".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:46
verses.text: Both "take," and "give".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:47
verses.text: What is, "take"? what, "give"? "Take the Psalm, and give the tabret".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:48
verses.text: The Apostle Paul saith in a certain place, reproving and grieving, that no one had communicated with him in the matter of giving and receiving.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:49
verses.text: What is, "in the matter of giving and receiving," but that which he hath openly set forth in another place "If we have sowed unto you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we reap your carnal things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:50
verses.text: And it is true that a tabret, which is made of hide, belongs to the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:51
verses.text: The Psalm, therefore, is spiritual, the tabret, carnal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:52
verses.text: Therefore, people of God, congregation of God, "take ye the Psalm, and give the tabret:" take ye spiritual things, and give carnal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:53
verses.text: This also is what at that blessed Martyr's table we exhorted you, that receiving spiritual things ye should give carnal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:54
verses.text: For these which are built for the time, are needful for receiving the bodies either of the living or of the dead, but in time that is passing by.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:55
verses.text: Shall we after God's judgment take up these buildings to Heaven? Yet without these we shall not be able to do at this time the things which belong to the possessing of Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:56
verses.text: If therefore ye are eager in getting spiritual things, be ye devout in expending carnal things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:57
verses.text: "Take the Psalm, and give the tabret:" take our voice, return your hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:58
verses.text: "The pleasant psaltery, with the harp".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:59
verses.text: I remember that we once intimated to your charity the difference of psaltery and harpFor heavenly is the preaching of the word of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:60
verses.text: But if we wait for heavenly things, let us not be sluggish in working at earthly things; because, "the psaltery is pleasant," but, "with the harp".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:61
verses.text: The same is expressed in another way as above, "Take the Psalm, and give the tabret:" here for "Psalm," is put "psaltery," for "tabret," "harp".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:62
verses.text: Of this, however, we are admonished, that to the preaching of God's word we make answer by bodily works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:63
verses.text: "Sound the trumpet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:64
verses.text: This is, Loudly and boldly preach, be not affrighted! as the Prophet says in a certain place, "Cry out, and lift up as with a trumpet thy voice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:65
verses.text: Sound the trumpet in the beginning of the month of the trumpet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:66
verses.text: It was ordered, that in the beginning of the month there should be a sounding of the trumpet: and this even now the Jews do in bodily sort, after the spirit they understand it not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:67
verses.text: For the beginning of the month, is the new moon: the new moon, is the new life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:68
verses.text: What is the new moon? "If any, then, is in Christ, he is a new creature".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:69
verses.text: What is, "sound the trumpet in the beginning of the month of the trumpet"? With all confidence preach ye the new life, fear not the noise of the old life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:70
verses.text: "Because it is a commandment for Israel, and a judgment for the God of Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:71
verses.text: Where a commandment, there judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:72
verses.text: For, "They that have sinned in the Law, by the Law shall be judged".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:73
verses.text: And the very Giver of the commandment, the Lord Christ, the Word made flesh, saith, "For judgment I am come into the world, that they that see not may see, and they that see may be made blind".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:74
verses.text: What is, "That they that see not may see, they that see be made blind," but that the lowly be exalted, the proud thrown down? For not they that see are to be made blind, but those who to themselves seem to see are to be convicted of blindness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:75
verses.text: This is brought about in the mystery of the press, that they who see may not see, and they that see be made blind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:76
verses.text: "A testimony in Joseph He made that".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:77
verses.text: Look you, brethren, what is it? Joseph is interpreted augmentation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:78
verses.text: Ye remember, ye know of Joseph sold into Egypt: Joseph sold into Egypt is Christ passing over to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:79
verses.text: There Joseph after tribulations was exalted, and here Christ, after the suffering of the Martyrs, was glorified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:80
verses.text: Thenceforth to Joseph the Gentiles rather belong, and thenceforth augmentation; because, "Many are the children of her that was desolate, rather than of her that hath the husband".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:81
verses.text: "He made it, till he should go out of the land of Egypt".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:82
verses.text: Observe that also here the "fifth of the sabbath" is signified: when Joseph went out from the land of Egypt, that is, the people multiplied through Joseph, he was caused to pass through the Red Sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:83
verses.text: Therefore then also the waters brought forth creeping things of living souls No other thing was it that there in figure the passage of that people through the sea foreshowed, than the passing of the Faithful through Baptism; the apostle is witness: for "I would not have you ignorant, brethren," he said, "that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea, and were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:84
verses.text: Nothing else then the passing through the sea did signify, but the Sacrament of the baptized; nothing else the pursuing Egyptians, but the multitude of past sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:85
verses.text: Ye see most evident mysteries.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:86
verses.text: The Egyptians press, they urge; so then sins follow close, but no farther than to the water.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:87
verses.text: Why then dost thou fear, who hast not yet come, to come to the Baptism of Christ, to pass through the Red Sea? What is "Red"? Consecrated with the Blood of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:88
verses.text: Why fearest thou to come? The consciousness, perhaps, of some huge offences goads and tortures in thee thy mind, and says to thee that it is so great a thing thou hast committed, that thou mayest despair to have it remitted thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:89
verses.text: Fear lest there remain anything of thy sins, if there lived any one of the Egyptians!  But when thou shalt have passed the Red Sea, when thou shalt have been led forth out of thine offences "with a mighty hand and with a strong arm," thou wilt perceive mysteries that thou knowest not: since Joseph himself too, "when he came out of the land of Egypt, heard a language which he knew not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:90
verses.text: Thou shalt hear a language which thou knowest not: which they that know now hear and recognise, bearing witness and knowing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:91
verses.text: Thou shalt hear where thou oughtest to have thy heart: which just now when I said many understood and answered by acclamation, the rest stood mute, because they have not heard the language which they knew not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:92
verses.text: Let them hasten, then, let them pass over, let them learn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:93
verses.text: "He turned away from burdens his back".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:94
verses.text: Who "turned away from burdens his back," but He that cried, "Come unto Me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden"? In another manner this same thing is signified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:95
verses.text: What the pursuit of the Egyptians did, the same thing do the burdens of sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:96
verses.text: As if thou shouldest say, From what burdens? "His hands in the basket did serve".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:97
verses.text: By the basket are signified servile works; to cleanse, to manure, to carry earth, is done with a basket, such works are servile: because "every one that doeth sin, is the slave of sin;" and "if the Son shall have made you free, then will ye be free indeed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:98
verses.text: Justly also are the rejected things of the world counted as baskets, but even baskets did God fill with morsels; "Twelve baskets" did He fill with morsels; because "He chose the rejected things of this world to confound the things that were mighty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:99
verses.text: But also when with the basket Joseph did serve, he then carried earth, because he did make bricks.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:100
verses.text: "His hands in the basket did serve".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:101
verses.text: "In tribulation thou didst call on Me, and I delivered thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:102
verses.text: Let each Christian conscience recognise itself, if it have devoutly passed the Red Sea, if with faith in believing and observing it hath heard a strange language which it knew not, let it recognise itself as having been heard in its tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:103
verses.text: For that was a great tribulation, to be weighed down with loads of sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:104
verses.text: How does the conscience, lifted from the earth, rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:105
verses.text: Lo, thou art baptized, thy conscience which was yesterday overladen, to-day rejoiceth thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:106
verses.text: Thou hast been heard in tribulation, remember thy tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:107
verses.text: Before thou camest to the water, what anxiety didst thou bear on thee! what fastings didst thou practise! what tribulations didst thou carry in thy heart! what inward, pious, devout prayers! Slain are thine enemies; all thy sins are blotted out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:108
verses.text: In tribulation thou didst call upon Me, and I delivered thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:109
verses.text: "I heard thee in the hidden part of the tempest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:110
verses.text: Not in a tempest of the sea, but in a tempest of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:111
verses.text: "I proved thee in the water of contradiction".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:112
verses.text: Truly, brethren, truly, he that was heard in the hidden part of the tempest ought to be proved in the water of contradiction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:113
verses.text: For when he hath believed, when he hath been baptized, when he hath begun to go in the way of God, when he hath striven to be strained into the vat, and hath drawn himself out from the lees that run in the street, he will have many disturbers, many insulters, many detractors, many discouragers, many that even threaten where they can, that deter, that depress.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:114
verses.text: This is all the "water of contradiction".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:115
verses.text: I suppose there are some here to-day, for instance, I think it likely there are some here whom their friends wished to hurry away to the circus, and to I know not what triflings of this day's festivity: perchance they have brought those persons with them to church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:116
verses.text: But whether they have brought those with them, or whether they have by them not permitted themselves to be led away to the circus, in the "water of contradiction" have they been tried.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:117
verses.text: Do not then be ashamed to proclaim what thou knowest, to defend even among blasphemers what thou hast believed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:118
verses.text: However much the bad that are aliens may rage, O that our own bad people would not help them!  Ye recollect what was said of Christ, that He was thus born for "the fall of many, and the rising again of many, and for a sign to be spoken against".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:119
verses.text: We know, we see: the sign of the Cross has been set up, and it has been spoken against.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:120
verses.text: There has been speaking against the glory of the Cross: but there was a title over the Cross which was not to be corrupted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:121
verses.text: For there is a title in the Psalm, "For the inscription of the title, corrupt thou not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:122
verses.text: It was a sign to be spoken against: for the Jews said, "Make it not, King of the Jews, but make it, that He said I am the King of the Jews".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:123
verses.text: Conquered was the contradiction; it was answered, "What I have written, I have written".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:124
verses.text: All this, from the beginning of the Psalm up to this verse, we have heard of the oil of the press.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:125
verses.text: What remains is rather for grief and warning: for it belongs to the lees of the press, even to the end; perchance also not without a meaning in the interposition of the "Diapsalma".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:126
verses.text: But even this too is profitable to hear, that he who sees himself already of the oil may rejoice; he that is in danger of running among the lees may beware.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:127
verses.text: To both give heed, choose the one, fear the other.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:128
verses.text: "Hear, O My people, and I will speak, and will bear witness unto thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:129
verses.text: For it is not to a strange people, not to a people that belongs not to the press: "Judge ye," He saith, "between Me and My vineyard".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:130
verses.text: "Israel, if thou shalt have heard Me, there shall not be in thee any new god".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:131
verses.text: A "new god" is one made for the time: but our God is not new, but from eternity to eternity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:132
verses.text: And our Christ is new, perchance, as Man, but eternal God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:133
verses.text: For what before the beginning? And truly, "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:134
verses.text: And our Christ Himself is the Word made flesh, that He might dwell in us Far be it, then, that there should be in any one a new god.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:135
verses.text: A new god is either a stone or a phantom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:136
verses.text: He is not, saith one, a stone; I have a silver and a gold one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:137
verses.text: Justly did he choose to name the very costly things, who said, "The idols of the nations are silver and gold".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:138
verses.text: Great are they, because they are of gold and silver; costly they are, shining they are; but yet, "Eyes they have, and see not!" New are these gods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:139
verses.text: What newer than a god out of a workshop? Yea, though those now old ones spiders' webs have covered over, they that are not eternal are new.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:140
verses.text: So much for the Pagans.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:141
verses.text: For if there be error in thee, Thou wilt not worship a strange god.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:142
verses.text: If thou think not of a false god, thou wilt not worship a manufactured god: for "there will not" be in thee any strange god.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:143
verses.text: "For I am".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:144
verses.text: Why wouldest thou adore what is not? "For I am the Lord thy God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:145
verses.text: Because "I am I that Am," and indeed "I Am" He saith, I that Am, over every creature: yet to thee what good have I afforded in time? "Who brought thee out of the land of Egypt".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:146
verses.text: Not to that people alone is it said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:147
verses.text: For we all were brought out of the land of Egypt, we have all passed through the Red Sea; our enemies pursuing us have perished in the water.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:148
verses.text: Let us not be ungrateful to our God; let us not forget God that abideth, and fabricate in ourselves a new god.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:149
verses.text: "I, who led thee out of the land of Egypt," saith God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:150
verses.text: "Open wide thy mouth, and I will fill it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:151
verses.text: Thou sufferest straitness in thyself because of the new god set up in thy heart; break the vain image, cast down from thy conscience the feigned idol: "open wide thy mouth," in confessing, in loving: "and I will fill it," because with me is the fountain of life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:152
verses.text: "And My people obeyed not My voice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:153
verses.text: For He would not speak these things except to His own people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:154
verses.text: For, "we know that whatsoever things the Law saith, it saith to them that are in the Law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:155
verses.text: "And Israel did not listen to Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:156
verses.text: Who? To whom? Israel to Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:157
verses.text: O ungrateful soul! Through Me the soul, by Me the soul called, by Me brought back to hope, by Me washed from sins! "And Israel did not listen to Me!" For they are baptized and pass through the Red Sea: but on the way they murmur, gainsay, complain, are stirred with seditions, ungrateful to Him who delivered them from pursuing enemies, who leads through the dry land, through the desert, yet with food and drink, with light by night and shade by day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:158
verses.text: "And I let them go according to the affections of their heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:159
verses.text: Behold the press: the orifices are open, the lees run.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:160
verses.text: "And I let them go," not according to the healthfulness of My commands; but, according to the affections of their heart: I gave them up to themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:161
verses.text: The Apostle also saith, "God gave them up to the desires of their own hearts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:162
verses.text: "I let them go according to the affection of their heart, they shall go in their own affections".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:163
verses.text: There is what ye shudder at, if at least ye are straining out into the hidden vats of the Lord, if at least ye have conceived a hearty love for His storehouses, there is what ye shudder at.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:164
verses.text: Some stand up for the circus, some for the amphitheatre, some for the booths in the streets some for the theatres, some for this, some for that, some finally for their "new gods;" "they shall go in their own affections".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:165
verses.text: "If My people would have heard Me, if Israel would have walked in My ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:166
verses.text: For perchance that Israel saith, Behold I sin, it is manifest, I go after the affections of my own heart: but what can I do? The devil doth this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:167
verses.text: Demons do this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:168
verses.text: What is the devil? Who are the demons? Certainly thine enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:169
verses.text: "Unto nothing all their enemies I would have brought down; and on them that oppress them I would have sent forth My hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:170
verses.text: But now what have they to do to complain of enemies? Themselves are become the worse enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:171
verses.text: For how? What followeth? Of enemies ye complain, yourselves, what are ye?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:172
verses.text: "The enemies of God have lied unto Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:173
verses.text: Dost thou renounce? I renounce And he returns to what he renounced.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:174
verses.text: In fact, what things dost thou renounce, except bad deeds, diabolical deeds, deeds to be condemned of God, thefts, plunderings, perjuries, manslayings, adulteries, sacrileges, abominable rites, curious arts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:175
verses.text: If therefore all those works "shall not possess the kingdom of God" (yea not the works, but "they that do such things;" for such works there shall be none in the fire: for they shall not, while burning in that fire, be committing theft or adultery; but "they that do such things shall not possess the kingdom of God"); they shall not therefore be on the right hand, with those to whom it shall be said, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive the kingdom:" because, "they that do such things shall not possess the kingdom of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:176
verses.text: If therefore on the right they shall not be, there remaineth not but that they must be on the left.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:177
verses.text: To those on the left what shall He say? "Go ye into eternal fire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:178
verses.text: Because, "their time shall be for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:179
verses.text: Explain to us, then, saith one, how those that build wood, hay, stubble, on the foundation, do not perish, but "are saved, yet so as by fire"? An obscure question indeed that, but as I am able I tell you briefly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:180
verses.text: Brethren, there are men altogether despisers of this world, to whom nothing is pleasant that flows in the course of time, they cling not by love to any earthly works, holy, chaste, continent, just, perchance even selling all their goods and distributing to the poor, or "possessing as though they possessed not, and using this world as though not using it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:181
verses.text: But there are others who cling to things allowed to infirmity with a degree of affection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:182
verses.text: He robs not another of his estate, but so loves his own, that if he loses it he will be disturbed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:183
verses.text: He does not covet another's wife, but so clings to his own, so cohabits with his own, as not therein to keep the measure prescribed in the laws, for the sake of begetting children.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:184
verses.text: He does not take away other men's things, but reclaims his own, and has a law-suit with his brother.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:185
verses.text: For to such it is said, "Now indeed there is altogether a fault among you, because ye have law-suits with each other".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:186
verses.text: But these very suits he orders to be tried in the Church, not to be dragged into court, yet he says they are faults.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:187
verses.text: For a Christian contends for earthly things more than becomes one to whom the kingdom of Heaven is promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:188
verses.text: Not the whole of his heart doth he raise upward, but some part of it he draggeth on the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:189
verses.text: Therefore if thou lovest thy possession, yet dost not for its sake commit violence, dost not for its sake bear false witness, dost not for its sake commit manslaughter, dost not for its sake swear falsely, dost not for its sake deny Christ: in that thou wilt not for its sake do these things, thou hast Christ for a foundation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:190
verses.text: But yet because thou lovest it, and art saddened if thou losest it, upon the foundation thou hast placed, not gold, or silver, or precious stones, but wood, hay, stubble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:191
verses.text: Saved therefore thou wilt be, when that begins to burn which thou hast built, yet so as by fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:192
verses.text: For let no one on this foundation building adulteries, blasphemies, sacrileges, idolatries, perjuries, think he shall be "saved through fire," as though they were the "wood, hay, stubble:" but he that buildeth the love of earthly things on the foundation of the kingdom of Heaven, that is upon Christ, his love of temporal things shall be burned, and himself shall be saved through the right foundation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:193
verses.text: "And He fed them of the fat of wheat, and from the rock with honey He satisfied them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:194
verses.text: In the wilderness from the rock He brought forth water, not honey.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:195
verses.text: "Honey" is wisdom, holding the first place for sweetness among the viands of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:196
verses.text: How many enemies of the Lord, then, that lie unto the Lord, are fed not only of the fat of wheat, but also from the rock with honey, from the wisdom of Christ? How many are delighted with His word, and with the knowledge of His sacraments, with the unfolding of His parables, how many are delighted, how many applaud with clamour! And this honey is not from any chance person, but "from the rock".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:197
verses.text: But "the Rock was Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:198
verses.text: How many, then, are satisfied with that honey, cry out, and say, It is sweet; say, Nothing better, nothing sweeter could be thought or said! and yet the enemies of the  Lord have lied unto Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:199
verses.text: I like not to dwell any more on matters of grief; although the Psalm endeth in terror to this purpose, yet from the end of it, I pray you, let us return to the heading: "Exult unto God our Helper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 83:200
verses.text: Turned unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXXII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:2
verses.text: This Psalm, like others similarly named, was so entitled either from the name of the man who wrote it, or from the explanation of that same name, so as to refer in meaning to the Synagogue, which Asaph signifies; especially as this is intimated in the first verse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:3
verses.text: For it begins, "God stood in the synagogue of gods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:4
verses.text: Far however be it from us to understand by these Gods the gods of the Gentiles, or ido ls, or any creature in heaven or earth except men; for a little after this verse the same Psalm relates and explains what Gods it means in whose synagogue God stood, where it says, "I have said, Ye are gods, and ye are all the children of the Most High: but ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:5
verses.text: In the synagogue of these children of the Most High, of whom the same Most High said by the mouth of Isaiah, "I have begotten sons and brought them up, but they despised Me," stood God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:6
verses.text: By the synagogue we understand the people of Israel, because synagogue is the word properly used of them, although they were also called the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:7
verses.text: Our congregation, on the contrary, the Apostles never called synagogue, but always Ecclesia; whether for the sake of the distinction, or because there is some difference between a congregation whence the synagogue has its name, and a convocation whence the Church is called Ecclesia: for the word congregation (or flocking together) is used of cattle, and particularly of that kind properly called "flocks," whereas convocation (or calling together) is more of reasonable creatures, such as men are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:8
verses.text: I think then that it is clear in what synagogue of gods God stood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:9
verses.text: The next question is, whether we should understand the Father, or the Son, or the Holy Spirit, or the Trinity, "to have stood among the congregation of gods, and in the midst to distinguish the gods;" because Each One is God, and the Trinity itself is One God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:10
verses.text: It is not indeed easy to make this clear, because it cannot be denied that not a bodily but a spiritual presence of God, agreeable to His nature, exists with created things in a wonderful manner, and one which but a few do understand, and that imperfectly: as to God it is said, "If I shall ascend into heaven, Thou art there; if I shall go down into hell, Thou art there also".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:11
verses.text: Hence it is rightly said, that God stands in the congregation of men invisibly, as He fills heaven and earth, which He asserts of Himself by the Prophet's mouth; and He is not only said, but is, in a way, known to stand in those things which He hath created, as far as the human mind can conceive, if man also stand s and hears Him, and rejoices greatly on account of His voice within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:12
verses.text: But I think that the Psalm intimates something that took place at a particular time, by God's standing in the congregation of gods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:13
verses.text: For that standing by which He fills heaven and earth, neither belongs peculiarly to the synagogue, nor varies from time to time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:14
verses.text: "God," therefore, "stood in the congregation of gods;" that is, He who said of Himself, "I am not sent but to the lost sheep of the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:15
verses.text: The cause too is mentioned; "but in the midst, to judge of the gods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:16
verses.text: "How long will ye judge unrighteously, and accept the persons of the ungodly" ; as in another place, "How long are ye heavy in heart?" Until He shall come who is the light of the heart? I have given a law, ye have resisted stubbornly: I sent Prophets, ye treated them unjustly, or slew them, or connived at those who did so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:17
verses.text: But if they are not worthy to be even spoken to, who slew the servants of God that were sent to them, ye who were silent when these things were doing, that is, ye who would imitate as if they were innocent those who then were silent, "how long will ye judge unrighteously, and accept the persons of the ungodly?" If the Heir comes even now, is He to be slain? Was He not willing for your sake to become as it were a child under guardians? Did not He for your sake hunger and thirst like one in need? Did He not cry to you, "Learn of Me, for I am meek and lowly of heart"? Did He not "become poor, when He was rich, that by His poverty we might be made rich"? "Give sentence," therefore, "for the fatherless and the poor man, justify the humble and needy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:18
verses.text: Not them who for their own sake are rich and proud, but Him who for your sake was humble and poor, believe ye to be righteous: proclaim Him righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:19
verses.text: But they will envy Him, and will not at all spare Him, saying, "This is the Heir, come, let us kill Him, and the inheritance shall be ours".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:20
verses.text: "Deliver," then, "the poor man, and save the needy from the hands of the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:21
verses.text: This is said that it might be known, that in that nation where Christ was born and put to death, those persons were not guiltless of so great a crime, who being so numerous, that, as the Gospel says, the Jews feared them, and therefore dared not lay hands on Christ, afterwards consented, and permitted Him to be slain by the malicious and envious Jewish rulers: yet if they had so willed, they would still have been feared, so that the hands of the wicked would never have prevailed against Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:22
verses.text: For of these it is said elsewhere, "Dumb dogs, they know not how to bark".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:23
verses.text: Of them too is that said, "Lo, how the righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:24
verses.text: He perished as far as lay in them who would have Him to perish; for how could He perish by dying, who in that way rather was seeking again what had perished? If then they are justly blamed and deservedly rebuked, who by their dissembling suffered such a wicked deed to be committed; how must they be blamed, or rather not only blamed, but how severely must they be condemned, who did this of design and malice?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:25
verses.text: To all of them, verily, what follows is most fitly suited: "They did not know nor understand, they walk on in darkness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:26
verses.text: "For if even they had known, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory:" and those others, if they had known, would never have consented to ask that Barabbas should be freed, and Christ should be crucified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:27
verses.text: But as the above-mentioned blindness happened in part unto Israel until the fulness of the Gentiles should come in, this blindness of that People having caused the crucifixion of Christ, "all the foundations of the earth shall be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:28
verses.text: So have they been moved, and shall they be moved, until the predestined fulness of the Gentiles shall come in.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:29
verses.text: For at the actual death of the Lord the earth was moved, and the rocks rent And if we understand by the foundations of the earth those who are rich in the abundance of earthly possessions, it was truly foretold that they should be moved, either by wondering that lowliness, poverty, death, should be so loved and honoured in Christ, when it is to their mind great misery; or even in that themselves should love and follow it, and set at nought the vain happiness of this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:30
verses.text: So are all the foundations of the earth moved, while they partly admire, and partly are even altered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:31
verses.text: For as without absurdity we call foundations of heaven those on whom the kingdom of heaven is built up in the persons of saints and faithful; whose first foundation is Christ Himself, born of the Virgin, of whom the Apostle says, "Other foundation can no man lay than that which is laid, which is Christ Jesus;" next the Apostles and Prophets themselves, by whose authority the heavenly place is chosen, that by obeying them we may be builded together with them; whence he says to the Ephesians, "Ye are built upon the foundation of Apostles and Prophets, Christ Jesus Himself being the chief corner stone".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:32
verses.text: But the kingdom of earthly happiness is pride, to oppose which came the lowliness of Christ, rebuking those whom He wished by lowliness to make the children of the Most High, and blaming them: "I said, Ye are gods, ye are all the children of the Most High".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:33
verses.text: "But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:34
verses.text: Whether to those He said this, "I said, Ye are gods," and to those particularly who are unpredestined to eternal life; and to the other, "But ye shall die like men," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:35
verses.text: , "and shall fall like one of the princes," in this way also distinguishing the gods; or whether He blames all together, in order to distinguish the obedient and those who received correction, "I said, Ye are gods, and ye are all the children of the Most High:" that is, to all of you I promised celestial happiness, "but ye," through the infirmity of your flesh, "shall die like men," and through haughtiness of soul, "like one of the princes," that is, the devil, shall not be exalted, but "shall fall".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:36
verses.text: As if He said: Though the days of your life are so few, that ye speedily die like men, this avails not to your correction: but like the devil, whose days are many in this world, because he dies not in the flesh, ye are lifted up so that ye fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:37
verses.text: For by devilish pride it came to pass that the perverse and blind rulers of the Jews envied the glory of Christ: by this will it came to pass, and still does, that the lowliness of Christ crucified unto death is lightly esteemed in the eyes of them who love the excellence of this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:38
verses.text: And therefore that this vice may be cured, in the person of the Prophet himself it is said, "Arise, O God, and judge the earth" ; for the earth swelled high when it crucified Thee: rise from the dead, and judge the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:39
verses.text: "For Thou shalt destroy among all nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:40
verses.text: What, but the earth? that is, destroying those who savour of earthly things, or destroying the feeling itself of earthly lust and pride in believers; or separating those who do not believe, as earth to be trodden under foot and to perish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:41
verses.text: Thus by His members, whose conversation is in heaven, He judges the earth, and destroys it among all nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:42
verses.text: But I must not omit to remark, that some copies have, "for Thou shalt inherit among all nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:43
verses.text: This too may be understood agreeably to the sense, nor does anything prevent both meanings existing at once.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 84:44
verses.text: His inheritance takes place by love, which in that He cultivates by His commands and gracious mercy, He destroys earthly desires.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXXIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:2
verses.text: Of this Psalm the title is, "A song of a Psalm of Asaph".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:3
verses.text: We have already often said what is the interpretation of Asaph, that is, congregation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:4
verses.text: That man, therefore, who was called Asaph, is named in representation of the congregation of God's people in the titles of many Psalms.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:5
verses.text: But in Greek, congregation is called synagogue, which has come to be held for a kind of proper name for the Jewish people, that it should be called The Synagogue; even as the Christian people is more usually called The Church, in that it too is congregated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:6
verses.text: The people of God, then, in this Psalm saith, "O God, who shall be like unto Thee?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:7
verses.text: Which I suppose to be more fitly taken of Christ, because, being made in the likeness of men, He was thought by those by whom He was despised to be comparable to other men: for He was even "reckoned among the unrighteous," but for this purpose, that He might be judged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:8
verses.text: But when He shall come to judge, then shall be done what is here said, "O God, who is like unto Thee?" For if the Psalms did not use to speak to the Lord Christ, that too would not be spoken which not one of the faithful can doubt was spoken unto Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:9
verses.text: "Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever, a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of Thy kingdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:10
verses.text: To him therefore also now it is said, "O God, who shall be like unto Thee?" For unto many Thou didst vouchsafe to be likened in Thy humiliation, even so far as to the robbers that were crucified with Thee: but when in glory Thou shalt come, "who shall be like unto Thee?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:11
verses.text: "For lo Thine enemies have sounded, and they that hate Thee have lifted up the head".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:12
verses.text: He seems to me to signify the last days, when these things that are now repressed by fear are to break forth into free utterance, but quite irrational, so that it should rather be called a "sound," than speech or discourse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:13
verses.text: They will not, therefore, then begin to hate, but "they that hate Thee" will then "lift up the head".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:14
verses.text: And not "heads," but "head;" since they are to come even to that point, that they shall have that head, which "is lifted up above all that is called God, and that is worshipped;" so that in him especially is to be fulfilled, "He that exalteth himself shall be abased;" and when He to whom it is said, "Keep not silence, nor grow mild, O God," shall "slay him with the breath of His mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of His coming".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:15
verses.text: "Upon Thy people they have malignantly taken counsel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:16
verses.text: Or, as other copies have it, "They have cunningly devised counsel, and have devised against Thy saints".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:17
verses.text: In scorn this is said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:18
verses.text: For how should they be able to hurt the nation or people of God, or His saints, who know how to say, "If God be for us, who shall be against us?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:19
verses.text: "They have said, Come, and let us destroy them from a nation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:20
verses.text: He has put the singular number for the plural: as it is said, "Whose is this cattle," even though the question be of a flock, and the meaning "these cattle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:21
verses.text: Lastly, other copies have "from nations," where the translators have rather followed the sense than the word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:22
verses.text: "Come, and let us destroy them from a nation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:23
verses.text: This is that sound whereby they "sounded" rather than spake, since they did vainly make a noise with vain sayings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:24
verses.text: "And let it not be mentioned of the name of Israel any more".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:25
verses.text: This others have expressed more plainly, "and let there not be remembrance of the name of Israel any more".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:26
verses.text: Since, "let it be mentioned of the name" (memoretur nominis), is an unusual phrase in the Latin language; for it is rather customary to say, "let the name be mentioned" (memoretur nomen); but the sense is the same.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:27
verses.text: For he who said, "let it be mentioned of the name," translated the Greek phrase.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:28
verses.text: But Israel must here be understood in fact of the seed of Abraham, to which the Apostle saith, "Therefore ye are the seed of Abraham, according to the promise heirs".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:29
verses.text: Not Israel according to the flesh, of which he saith, "Behold Israel after the flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:30
verses.text: "Since they have imagined with one consent; together against Thee have they disposed a testament" : as though they could be the stronger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:31
verses.text: In fact, "a testament" is a name given in the Scriptures not only to that which is of no avail till the death of the testators, but every covenant and decree they used to call a testament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:32
verses.text: For Laban and Jacob made a testament, which was certainly to have force between the living; and such cases without number are read in the words of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:33
verses.text: Then he begins to make mention of the enemies of Christ, under certain proper names of nations; the interpretation of which names sufficiently indicates what he would have to be understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:34
verses.text: For by such names are most suitably figured the enemies of the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:35
verses.text: "Idumaeans," for instance, are interpreted either "men of blood," or "of earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:36
verses.text: "Ismaelites," are "obedient to themselves," and therefore not to God, but to themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:37
verses.text: "Moab," "from the father;" which in a bad sense has no better explanation, than by considering it so connected with the actual history, that Lot, a father, by the illicit intercourse procured by his daughter, begat him; since it was from that very circumstance he was so named Good, however, was his father, but as "the Law is good if one use it lawfully," not impurely and unlawfully.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:38
verses.text: "Hagarens," proselytes, that is strangers, by which name also are signified, among the enemies of God's people, not those who become citizens, but those who persevere in a foreign and alien mind, and when an opportunity of doing harm occurs, show themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:39
verses.text: "Gebal," "a vain valley," that is, humble in pretence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:40
verses.text: "Amon," "an unquiet people," or "a people of sadness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:41
verses.text: "Amalech," "a people licking;" whence elsewhere it is said, "and his enemies shall lick the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:42
verses.text: The "alien race," though by their very name in Latin, they sufficiently show themselves to be aliens, and for this cause of course enemies, yet in the Hebrew are called "Philistines," which is explained, "falling from drink," as of persons made drunken by worldly luxury.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:43
verses.text: "Tyre" in Hebrew is called Sor; which whether it be interpreted straitness or tribulation, must be taken in the case of these enemies of God's people in that sense, of which the Apostle speaks, "Tribulation and straitness on every soul of man that doeth evil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:44
verses.text: All these are thus enumerated in the Psalms: "The tabernacles of the Edomites, Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagarenes, Gebal, and Amon, and Amalech, and the Philistines with those who inhabit Tyre".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:45
verses.text: And as if to point out the cause why they are enemies of God's people, he adds, "For Assur came with them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:46
verses.text: Now Assur is often used figuratively for the devil, "who works in the children of disobedience," as in his own vessels, that they may assail the people of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:47
