verses.text: "They have holpen the children of Lot," he saith: for all enemies, by the working in them of the devil, their prince, "have holpen the children of Lot," who is explained to mean "one declining".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:48
verses.text: But the apostate angels are well explained as the children of declension, for by declining from truth they swerved to become followers of the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:49
verses.text: These are they of whom the Apostle speaks: "Ye wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities and powers, and the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:50
verses.text: Those invisible enemies are holpen then by unbelieving men, in whom they work in order to assail the people of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:51
verses.text: Now let us see what the prophetic spirit prays may fall upon them, rather foretelling than cursing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:52
verses.text: "Do thou to them," he saith, "as unto Madian and Sisera, as unto Jabin at the brook of Kishon".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:53
verses.text: "They perished at Endor, they became as the dung of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:54
verses.text: All these, the history relates, were subdued and conquered by Israel, which then was the people of God: as was the case also with those whom he next mentions: "Make their princes like Oreb and Zeb, and Zebee and Salmana".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:55
verses.text: The meaning of these names is as follows: Madian is explained a perverted judgment: Sisera, shutting out of joy: Jabin, wise But in these enemies conquered by God's people is to be understood that wise man of whom the Apostle speaketh, "Where is the wise? where is the scribe? where is the disputer of this world?" Oreb is dryness, Zeb, wolf, Zebee, a victim, namely of the wolf; for he too has his victims; Salmana, shadow of commotion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:56
verses.text: All these agree to the evils which the people of God conquer by good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:57
verses.text: Moreover Kishon, the torrent in which they were conquered, is explained, their hardness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:58
verses.text: Endor, where they perished, is explained, the Fountain of generation, but of the carnal generation namely, to which they were given up, and therefore perished, not heeding the regeneration which leadeth unto life, where they shall neither marry nor be given in marriage, for they shall die no more.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:59
verses.text: Rightly then it is said of these: "they became as the dung of the earth," in that nothing was produced of them but fruitfulness of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:60
verses.text: As then all these were in figure conquered by the people of God, as figures, so he prays that those other enemies may be conquered in truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:61
verses.text: "All their princes, who said, Let us take to ourselves the sanctuary of God in possession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:62
verses.text: This is that vain noise, with which, as said above, Thy enemies have made a murmuring.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:63
verses.text: But what must be understood by "the sanctuary of God," except the temple of God? as saith the Apostle: "For the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:64
verses.text: For what else do the enemies aim at, but to take into possession, that is, to make subject to themselves the temple of God, that it may give in to their ungodly wills?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:65
verses.text: But what follows? "My God, make them like unto a wheel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:66
verses.text: This is fitly taken as meaning that they should be constant in nothing that they think; but I think it may also be rightly explained, make them like unto a wheel, because a wheel is lifted up on the part of what is behind, is thrown down on the part of what is in front; and so it happens to all the enemies of the people of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:67
verses.text: For this is not a wish, but a prophecy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:68
verses.text: He adds: "as the stubble in the face of the wind".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:69
verses.text: By face he means presence; for what face hath the wind, which has no bodily features, being only a motion, in that it is a kind of wave of air? But it is put for temptation, by which light and vain hearts are hurried away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:70
verses.text: This levity, by which consent is easily given to what is evil, is followed by severe torment; therefore he proceeds:—  "Like as the fire that burneth up the wood, and as the flame that consumeth the mountains" : "so shalt Thou persecute them with Thy tempest, and in Thy anger shalt disturb them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:71
verses.text: Wood, he saith, for its barrenness, mountains for their loftiness; for such are the enemies of God's people, barren of righteousness, full of pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:72
verses.text: When he says, "fire" and "flame," he means to repeat under another term, the idea of God judging and punishing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:73
verses.text: But in saying, "with Thy tempest," he means, as he goes on to explain, "Thy anger:" and the former expression, "Thou shalt persecute," answers to, "Thou shalt disturb".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:74
verses.text: We must take care, however, to understand, that the anger of God is free from any turbulent emotion; for His anger is an expression for His just method of taking vengeance: as the law might be said to be angry when its ministers are moved to punish by its sanction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:75
verses.text: "Fill their faces with shame, and they shall seek Thy name, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:76
verses.text: Good and desirable is this which he prophesieth for them: and he would not prophesy thus, unless there were even in that company of the enemies of God's people, some men of such kind that this would be granted to them before the last judgment: for now they are mixed together, and this is the body of the enemies, in respect of the envy whereby they rival the people of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:77
verses.text: And now, where they can, they make a noise and lift up their head: but severally, not universally as they will do at the end of the world, when the last judgment is about to fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:78
verses.text: But it is the same body, even in those who out of this number shall believe and pass into another body (for the faces of these are filled with shame, that they may seek the name of the Lord), as well as in those others who persevere unto the end in the same wickedness, who are made as stubble before the wind, and are consumed like a wood and barren mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:79
verses.text: To these he again returns, saying, "They shall blush and be vexed for ever and ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:80
verses.text: For those are not vexed for ever and ever who seek the name of the Lord, but having respect unto the shame of their sins, they are vexed for this purpose, that they may seek the name of the Lord, through which they may be no more vexed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:81
verses.text: Again, he returns to these last, who in the same company of enemies are to be made ashamed for this purpose, that they may not be ashamed for ever: and for this purpose to be destroyed in as far as they are wicked, that being made good they may be found alive for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:82
verses.text: For having said of them, "Let them be ashamed and perish," he instantly adds, "and let them know that Thy name is the Lord, Thou art only the Most Highest in all the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:83
verses.text: Coming to this knowledge, let them be so confounded as to please God: let them so perish, as that they may abide.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:84
verses.text: "Let them know," he says, "that Thy name is the Lord:" as if whoever else are called lords are named so not truly but by falsehood, for they rule but as servants, and compared with the true Lord are not lords; as it is said, I Am that I Am: as if those things which are made are not, compared with Him by whom they are made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:85
verses.text: He adds, "Thou only art the Most Highest in all the earth:" or, as other copies have it, "over all the earth;" as it might be said, in all the heaven, or over all the heaven: but he used the latter word in preference, to depress the pride of earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 85:86
verses.text: For earth ceaseth to be proud, that is, man ceaseth, to whom it was said, "Thou art dust;"  and "why is earth and ashes proud?" when he saith that the Lord is the Most Highest above all the earth, that is, that no man's thoughts avail against those "who are called according to His purpose," and of whom it is said, "If God is for us, who can be against us?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXXIV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:2
verses.text: This Psalm is entitled, "For the winepresses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:3
verses.text: And, as you observed with me, my beloved (for I saw that you attended most closely), nothing is said in its text either of any press, or wine-basket, or vat, or of any of the instruments or the building of a winepress; nothing of this kind did we hear read; so that it is no easy question what is the meaning of this title inscribed upon it, "for the winepresses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:4
verses.text: For certainly, if after the title it mentioned anything about such things as I enumerated, carnal persons might have believed that it was a song concerning those visible wine-presses; but as it has this title, yet says nothing afterwards of those winepresses which we know so well, I cannot doubt that there are other wine-presses, which the Spirit of God intended us to look for and to understand here.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:5
verses.text: Therefore, let us recall to mind what takes place in these visible winepresses, and see how this takes place spiritually in the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:6
verses.text: The grape hangs on the vines, and the olive on its trees.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:7
verses.text: For it is for these two fruits that presses are usually made ready; and as long as they hang on their boughs, they seem to enjoy free air; and neither is the grape wine, nor the olive oil, before they are pressed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:8
verses.text: Thus it is with men whom God predestined before the world to be conformed to the image of His only-begotten Son, who has been first and especially pressed in His Passion, as the great Cluster.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:9
verses.text: Men of this kind, therefore, before they draw near to the service of God, enjoy in the world a kind of delicious liberty, like hanging grapes or olives: but as it is said, "My son, when thou drawest near to the service of God, stand in judgment and fear, and make thy soul ready for temptation:" so each, as he draweth near to the service of God, findeth that he is come to the winepress; he shall undergo tribulation, shall be crushed, shall be pressed, not that he may perish in this world, but that he may flow down into the storehouses of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:10
verses.text: He hath the coverings of carnal desires stripped off from him, like grape-skins: for this hath taken place in him in carnal desires, of which the Apostle speaks, "Put ye off the old man, and put on the new man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:11
verses.text: All this is not done but by pressure: therefore the Churches of God of this time are called winepresses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:12
verses.text: But who are we who are placed in the wine-presses? "Sons of Core".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:13
verses.text: For this follows: "For the winepresses, to the sons of Core".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:14
verses.text: The sons of Core has been explained, sons of the bald: as far as those could explain it to us, who know that language, according to their service due to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:15
verses.text: But being placed under pressure, we are crushed for this purpose, that for our love by which we were borne towards those worldly, secular, temporal, unstable, and perishable things, having suffered in them, in this life, torments, and tribulations of pressures, and abundance of temptations, we may begin to seek that rest which is not of this life, nor of this earth; and the Lord becomes, as is written, "a refuge for the poor man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:16
verses.text: What is, "for the poor man"? For him who is, as it were, destitute, without aid, without help, without anything on which he may rest, in earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:17
verses.text: For to such poor men, God is present.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:18
verses.text: For though men abound in money on earth,they are filled more with fear than with enjoyment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:19
verses.text: For what is so uncertain as a rolling thing? It is not unfitly that money itself is stamped round, because it remains not still.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:20
verses.text: Such men, therefore, though they have something, are yet poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:21
verses.text: But those who have none of this wealth, but only desire it, are counted also among rich men who will be rejected; for God takes account not of power, but of will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:22
verses.text: The poor then are destitute of all this world's substance, for even though it abounds around them, they know how fleeting it is; and crying unto God, having nothing in this world with which they may delight themselves, and be held down, placed in abundant pressures and temptations, as if in winepresses, they flow down, having become oil or wine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:23
verses.text: What are these latter but good desires? For God remains their only object of desire; now they love not earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:24
verses.text: For they love Him who made heaven and earth; they love Him, and are not yet with Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:25
verses.text: Their desire is delayed, in order that it may increase; it increases, in order that it may receive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:26
verses.text: For it is not any little thing that God will give to him who desires, nor does he need to be little exercised to be made fit to receive so great a good: not anything which He hath made will God give, but Himself who made all things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:27
verses.text: Exercise thyself to receive God: that which thou shalt have for ever, desire thou for a long time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:28
verses.text: Wherefore, most beloved, as each can, make vows, and perform to the Lord God what each can: let no one look back, no one delight himself with his former interests, no one turn away from that which is before to that which is behind: let him run until he arrive: for we run not with the feet but with the desire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:29
verses.text: But let no one in this life say that he hath arrived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:30
verses.text: For who can be so perfect as Paul? Yet he saith, "Brethren, I count not myself to have attained".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:31
verses.text: If therefore thou feelest the passions of this world, even when thou art happy, thou understandest now that thou art in the winepress.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:32
verses.text: If therefore the world smile upon thee with happiness, imagine thyself in the winepress, and say, "I found trouble and heaviness, and I did call upon the name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:33
verses.text: He said not, I found trouble, without meaning, of such a kind as was hidden: for some troubles are hidden from some in this world, who think they are happy while they are absent from God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:34
verses.text: "For as long as we are in the body," he saith, "we are absent from the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:35
verses.text: If thou wert absent from thy father, thou wouldest be unhappy: art thou absent from the Lord, and happy? There are then some who think it is well with them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:36
verses.text: But those who understand, that in whatever abundance of wealth and pleasures, though all things obey their beck, though nothing troublesome creep in, nothing adverse terrify, yet that they are in a bad case as long as they are absent from the Lord; with a most keen eye these have found trouble, and grief, and have called on the name of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:37
verses.text: Such is he who sings in this Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:38
verses.text: Who is he? The Body of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:39
verses.text: Who is that? You, if you will: all we, if we will: for Christ's Body is one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:40
verses.text: "How lovely are Thy tabernacles, O Lord of Hosts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:41
verses.text: He was in some tabernacles, that is, in winepresses: but he longed for other tabernacles, where is no pressure: in this he sighed for them, from these, he, as it were, flowed down into them by the channel of longing desire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:42
verses.text: And what follows? "My soul longeth and faileth for the courts of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:43
verses.text: It is not enough that it "longeth and faileth:" for what doth it fail? "For the courts of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:44
verses.text: The grape when pressed hath failed: but for what? So as to be changed into wine, and to flow into the vat, and into the rest of the storeroom, to be kept there in great quiet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:45
verses.text: Here it is longed for, there it is received: here are sighs, there joy: here prayers, there praises: here groans, there rejoicing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:46
verses.text: Those things which I mentioned, let no one while here turn from ashamed: let no one be unwilling to suffer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:47
verses.text: There is danger, lest the grape, while it fears the winepress, should be devoured by birds or by wild beasts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:48
verses.text: Thou hast heard a groan in the winepress, "My soul longeth and faileth for the courts of the Lord:" hear how it holdeth out, rejoicing in hope: "My heart and my flesh have rejoiced in the living God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:49
verses.text: Here they have rejoiced for that cause.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:50
verses.text: Whence cometh rejoicing, but of hope? Wherefore have they rejoiced? "In the living God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:51
verses.text: What has rejoiced in thee? "My heart and my flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:52
verses.text: Why have they rejoiced? "For," saith he, "the sparrow hath found her a house, and the turtle-dove a nest, where she may lay her young".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:53
verses.text: What is this? He had named two things, and he adds two figures of birds which answer to them: he had said that his heart rejoiced and his flesh, and to these two he made the sparrow and turtle-dove to correspond: the heart as the sparrow, the flesh as the dove.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:54
verses.text: The sparrow hath found herself a home: my heart hath found itself a home.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:55
verses.text: She tries her wings in the virtues of this life, in faith, and hope, and charity, by which she may fly unto her home: and when she shall have come thither, she shall remain; and now the complaining voice of the sparrow, which is h ere, shall no longer be there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:56
verses.text: For it is the very complaining sparrow of whom in another Psalm he saith, "Like a sparrow alone on the housetop".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:57
verses.text: From the housetop he flies home.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:58
verses.text: Now let him be on the housetop, treading on his carnal house: he shall have a heavenly house, a perpetual home: that sparrow shall make an end of his complaints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:59
verses.text: But to the dove he hath given young, that is, to the flesh: "the dove hath found a nest, where she may lay her young".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:60
verses.text: The sparrow a home, the dove a nest, and a nest too where she may lay her young.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:61
verses.text: A home is chosen as for ever, a nest is framed for a time: with the heart we think upon God, as if the sparrow flew to her home: with the flesh we do good works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:62
verses.text: For ye see how many good works are done by the flesh of the saints; for by this we work the things we are commanded to work, by which we are helped in this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:63
verses.text: "Break thy bread to the hungry, and bring the poor and roofless into thy house; and if thou see one naked, clothe him:" and other such things which are commanded us we work only through the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:64
verses.text: We speak, brethren, what ye know: how many seem to do good works without the Church? how many even Pagans feed the hungry, clothe the naked, receive the stranger, visit the sick, comfort the prisoner? how many do this? The dove seems, as it were, to bring forth young: but finds not herself a nest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:65
verses.text: How many works may heretics do not in the Church; they place not their young in a nest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:66
verses.text: They shall be trampled on and crushed: they shall not be kept, shall not be guarded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:67
verses.text: In that faith lay thy young: in that nest work thy works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:68
verses.text: For what the nests are, what that nest is, follows at once.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:69
verses.text: Having said, And the dove hath found herself a nest, where she may lay her young; as if thou hadst asked, What nest? "Thy altars, O Lord of Hosts, my King and my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:70
verses.text: What is, "My King and my God?" Thou who rulest me, who hast created me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:71
verses.text: "Blessed are those who dwell in Thy house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:72
verses.text: If thou hast thy own house, thou art poor; if God's, thou art rich.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:73
verses.text: In thy own house thou wilt fear robbers; of the house of God, He is Himself the wall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:74
verses.text: Therefore "blessed are those who dwell in Thy house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:75
verses.text: They possess the heavenly Jerusalem, without constraint, without pressure, without difference and division of boundaries; all have it, and each have all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:76
verses.text: Great are those riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:77
verses.text: Brother crowdeth not brother: there is no want there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:78
verses.text: Next, what will they do there? For among men it is necessity which is the mother of all employments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:79
verses.text: I have already said, in brief, brethren, run in your mind through any occupations, and see if it is not necessity alone which produces them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:80
verses.text: Those very eminent arts which seem so powerful in giving help to others, the art of speaking in their defence or of medicine in healing, for these are the most excellent employments in this life; take away litigants, who is there for the advocate to help? take away wounds and diseases? what is there for the physician to cure? And all those employments of ours which are required and done for our daily life, arise from necessity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:81
verses.text: To plough, to sow, to clear fallow ground, to sail; what is it which produces all these works, but necessity and want? Take away hunger, thirst, nakedness; who has need of all these things?For instance, the injunction, "Break thy bread to the hungry".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:82
verses.text: For whom could you break bread, if there were nobody hungry? "Take in the roofless poor into thy house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:83
verses.text: What stranger is there to take in, where all live in their own country? What sick person to visit, where they enjoy perpetual health? What litigants to reconcile, where there is everlasting peace? What dead to bury, where there is eternal life? None of those honourable actions which are common to all men will then be your employment, nor any of these good works; the young swallows will then fly out of their nest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:84
verses.text: What then? You have said already what we shall have; "Those who dwell in Thy house are blessed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:85
verses.text: Say now what they shall do, for I see not then any need to induce me to action.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:86
verses.text: Even what I am now saying and arguing springs from some need.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:87
verses.text: Will there be any such argument there to teach the ignorant, or remind the forgetful? Or will the Gospel be read in that country where the Word of God Itself shall be contemplated?"They shall be always praising Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:88
verses.text: This shall be our whole duty, an unceasing Hallelujah.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:89
verses.text: Think not, my brethren, that there will be any weariness there: if ye are not able to endure long here in saying this, it is because some want draws you away from that enjoyment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:90
verses.text: If what is not seen gives not so much joy here, if with so much eagerness under the pressure and weakness of the flesh we praise that which we believe, how shall we praise that which we see? "When death shall be swallowed up in victory, when this mortal shall have put on immortality," no one will say, "I have been standing a long time;" no one will say, "I have fasted a long time," "I have watched a long time".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:91
verses.text: For there shall be great endurance, and our immortal bodies shall be sustained in contemplation of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:92
verses.text: And if the word which we now dispense to you keeps your weak flesh standing so long, what will be the effect of that joy? how will it change us? "For we shall be like Him, since we shall see Him as He is".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:93
verses.text: Being made like Him, when shall we ever faint? what shall draw us off? Brethren, we shall never be satiated with the praise of God, with the love of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:94
verses.text: If love could fail, praise could fail.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:95
verses.text: But if love be eternal, as there will there be beauty inexhaustible, fear not lest thou be not able to praise for ever Him whom thou shalt be able to love for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:96
verses.text: For this life let us sigh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:97
verses.text: But how shall we come thither? "Happy is the man whose strength is in Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:98
verses.text: He knew where he was, and that by reason of the frailty of his flesh he could not fly to that state of blessedness: he thought upon his own burden, as it is said elsewhere; "For the corruptible body weighs down the soul, and the earthly house depresses the understanding which has many thoughts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:99
verses.text: The Spirit calls upward, the weight of the flesh calls back again downward: between the double effort to raise and to weigh down, a kind of struggle ensues: this struggle goes toward the pressure of the winepress.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:100
verses.text: Hear how the Apostle describes this same struggle of the winepress, for he was himself afflicted there, there he was pressed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:101
verses.text: "Miserable man that I am: who shall deliver me from the body of this death? The grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:102
verses.text: "For I delight in the Law of God according to the inner man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:103
verses.text: But what shall I do? how shall I fly? how shall I arrive thither? "I see another law in my members," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:104
verses.text: And as in the words of the Apostle, that difficulty and that almost inextricable struggle is alleviated by the addition, "The grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord;" so here, when he sighed in the ardent longing for the house of God, and those praises of God, and when a kind of despair arose at the feeling of the burden of the body and the weight of the flesh, again he awoke to hope, and said , "Blessed is the man whose taking up is in Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:105
verses.text: What then does God supply by His grace to him whom He taketh hold of to lead him on? He goes on to say: "He hath placed steps in his heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:106
verses.text: Where does it place steps? "In his heart, in the valley of weeping".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:107
verses.text: So here thou hast for a winepress the valley of weeping, the very pious tears in tribulation are the new wine of those that love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:108
verses.text: They went forth "weeping," he says, "casting their seed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:109
verses.text: Therefore,  by the grace of God may upward steps be placed in thy heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:110
verses.text: Rise by loving.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:111
verses.text: Hence the Psalm "of degrees" is called.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:112
verses.text: "He hath placed steps of ascent to the place which He hath appointed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:113
verses.text: Now we lament; whence proceed our lamentations, but from that place where the steps of our ascent are placed? Whence comes our lamentation, but from that cause wherefore the Apostle exclaimed that he was a wretched man, because he saw another law in his members, warring against the law in his mind? And whence does this proceed? From the penalty of sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:114
verses.text: And we thought that we could easily be righteous as it were by our own strength, before we received the command; "but when the command came, sin revived; but I died," saith the Apostle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:115
verses.text: For a law was given to men, not such as could save them at once, but it was to show them in what severe sickness they were lying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:116
verses.text: But when sin was made manifest by the law given, sin was but increased, for it is both sin, and against the Law; "Sin," saith he, "taking occasion by the command, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:117
verses.text: What does he mean by "taking occasion by the law"? Having received the command, men tried as by their own strength to obey it; conquered by lust, they became guilty of transgression of this very command also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:118
verses.text: But what saith the Apostle? "Where sin abounded, grace hath much more abounded;" that is, the disease increased, the medicine became of more avail.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:119
verses.text: Accordingly, my brethren, did those five porches of Solomon, in the middle of which the pool lay, heal the sick at all? The sick, says the Evangelist, lay in the five porches In the Gospel we have and read it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:120
verses.text: Those five porches are the law in the five books of Moses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:121
verses.text: For this cause the sick were brought forth from their houses that they might lie in the porches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:122
verses.text: So the law brought the sick men forth, but did not heal them: but by the blessing of God the water was disturbed, as by an Angel descending into it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:123
verses.text: At the sight of the water troubled, the one person who was able, descended and was healed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:124
verses.text: That water surrounded by the five porches, was the people of the Jews shut up in their law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:125
verses.text: The Lord came and disturbed this people, so that He Himself was slain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:126
verses.text: For if the Lord had not troubled the Jews by coming down to them, would He have been crucified? So that the troubled water signified the Passion of the Lord, which arose from His troubling the Jewish people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:127
verses.text: The sick man who believeth in this Passion, like him who descended into the troubled water, is healed thereby.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:128
verses.text: He whom the Law could not heal, that is, while he lay in the porches, is healed by grace, by faith in the Passion of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:129
verses.text: "He shall give blessing," saith he, "who gave the law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:130
verses.text: Grace shall come after the law, grace itself is the blessing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:131
verses.text: And what has that grace and blessing given unto us? "They shall go from virtue to virtue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:132
verses.text: For here by grace many virtues are given.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:133
verses.text: "For to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge according to the same Spirit, to another faith, to another the gift of healing, to another different kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues, to another prophecy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:134
verses.text: Many virtues, but necessary for this life; and from these virtues we go on to "a virtue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:135
verses.text: To what "virtue"? To "Christ the Virtue of God and the Wisdom of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:136
verses.text: He giveth different virtues in this place, who for all the virtues which are necessary and useful in this valley of weeping shall give one virtue, Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:137
verses.text: For in Scripture and in many writers four virtues are described useful for life: prudence, by which we discern between good and evil; justice, by which we give each person his due, "owing no man anything," but loving all men: temperance, by which we restrain lusts; fortitude, by which we bear all troubles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:138
verses.text: These virtues are now by the grace of God given unto us in the valley of weeping: from these virtues we mount unto that other virtue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:139
verses.text: And what will that be, but the virtue of the contemplation of God alone?It follows in that place: "They shall go from virtue to virtue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:140
verses.text: What virtue? That of contemplation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:141
verses.text: What is contemplation? "The God of Gods shall appear in Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:142
verses.text: The God of Gods, Christ of the Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:143
verses.text: When all is finished, that mortality makes necessary, He shall appear to the pure in heart, as He is, "God with God," The Word with the Father, "by which all things were made".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:144
verses.text: And again, from the thought of those joys he returns to his own sighs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:145
verses.text: He sees what has come before in hope, and where he is in reality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:146
verses.text: Therefore returning to the groans proper to this place, he saith, "O Lord God of virtues, hear my prayer: hearken, O God of Jacob" : for Jacob himself also Thou hast made Israel out of Jacob.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:147
verses.text: For God appeared unto him, and he was called Israel,  seeing God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:148
verses.text: Hear me therefore, O God of Jacob, and make me Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:149
verses.text: When shall I become Israel? When the God of Gods shall appear in Sion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:150
verses.text: "Behold, O God our defender.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:151
verses.text: And look on the face of Thy Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:152
verses.text: For when doth God not look upon the face of His Christ? What is this, "Look on the face of Thy Christ"? By the face we are known.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:153
verses.text: What is it then, Look on the face of Thy Christ? Cause Thy Christ to become known to all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:154
verses.text: Look on the face of Thy Christ: let Christ become known to all, that we may be able to go from strength to strength, that grace may abound, since sin hath abounded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:155
verses.text: "For one day in Thy courts is better than a thousand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:156
verses.text: Those courts they were for which he sighed, for which he fainted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:157
verses.text: "My soul longeth and faileth for the courts of the Lord:" one day there is better than a thousand days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:158
verses.text: Men long for thousands of days, and wish to live here long: let them despise these thousands of days, let them long for one day, which has neither rising nor setting: one day, an everlasting day, to which no yesterday yields, which no to-morrow presses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:159
verses.text: Let this one day be longed for by us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:160
verses.text: What have we to do with a thousand days? We go from the thousand days to one day; let us hasten to that one day,  as we go from strength to strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:161
verses.text: "I have chosen to be cast away in the house of the Lord, rather than to dwell in the tents of sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:162
verses.text: For he found the valley of weeping, he found humility by which he might rise: he knoweth that if he would raise himself he shall fall, if he humble himself he shall be exalted: he hath chosen to be cast away, that he may be raised up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:163
verses.text: How many beside this tabernacle of the Lord's winepress, that is beside the Catholic Church, wishing to be lifted up, and loving their honours, refuse to see the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:164
verses.text: If this verse had been in their heart, would they not cast away honours, and run to the valley of weeping, and hence find in their heart the way of ascent, and hence go from virtues to virtue, placing their hope in Christ, not in some man or another? A good word is this, a word to rejoice in, a word to be chosen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:165
verses.text: He himself chose to be cast away in the house of the Lord; but He who invited him to the feast, when he chose a lower place calleth him to a higher one, and saith unto him, "Go up higher".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:166
verses.text: Yet he chose not but to be in the house of the Lord, in any part of it, so that he were not outside the threshold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:167
verses.text: Wherefore did he choose?"Because God loveth mercy and truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:168
verses.text: The Lord loveth mercy, by which He first came to my help: He loveth truth, so as to give to him that believeth what He has promised Hear in the case of the Apostle Paul, His mercy and truth, Paul who was first Saul the persecutor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:169
verses.text: He needed mercy, and he has said that it was shown towards him: "I who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, that in me Christ Jesus might show forth all longsuffering towards those who shall believe in Him unto life eternal".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:170
verses.text: So that, when Paul received pardon of such great crimes, no one should despair of any sins whatever being forgiven him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:171
verses.text: Lo! Thou hast Mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:172
verses.text: Lo, we see that Paul holdeth Him a debtor, having received mercy, demanding truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:173
verses.text: The Lord, he says, shall give back in that day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:174
verses.text: What shall He give thee back, but that which He oweth thee? How oweth He unto thee? What hast thou given Him? "Who hath first given unto Him, and it shall be restored to him again".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:175
verses.text: The Lord Himself hath made Himself a debtor, not by receiving, but by promising: it is not said unto Him, Restore what Thou hast received: but, Restore what Thou hast promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:176
verses.text: He hath shown mercy unto me, he saith, that He might make me innocent: for before I was a blasphemer and injurious: but by His grace I have been made innocent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:177
verses.text: But He who first showed mercy, can He deny His debt? "He loveth mercy and truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:178
verses.text: He will give grace and glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:179
verses.text: What grace, but that of which the same one said: "By the grace of God I am what I am"? What glory, but that of which he said, "There is laid up for me a crown of glory"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:180
verses.text: Therefore "the Lord will not withhold good from those who walk in innocence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:181
verses.text: Why then, O men, are ye unwilling to keep innocence, except in order that ye may have good things?Thou seest wealth in the hands of robbers, of the impious, the wicked, the base; in the hands of scandalous and criminal men thou seest wealth: God giveth them these things on account of their fellowship in the human race, for the abundant overflowing of His goodness: who also "maketh His sun to rise upon the good and the evil, and causeth it to rain upon the righteous and upon the sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:182
verses.text: Giveth He so much to the wicked, and keepeth nothing for thee? He keepeth something: be at ease, He who had mercy on thee when thou wast impious, doth He desert thee when thou hast become pious? He who gave to the sinner the free gift of His Son's death, what keepeth He for the saved through that death? Therefore be at ease.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:183
verses.text: Hold Him a debtor, for thou hast believed in Him promising.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 86:184
verses.text: What then remains for us here, in the winepress, in affliction, in hardship, in our present dangerous life? What remains for us, that we may arrive thither? "O Lord God of virtues, blessed is the man that putteth his hope in Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXXV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:2
verses.text: Its title is, "A Psalm for the end, to the sons of Core".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:3
verses.text: Let us understand no other end than that of which the Apostle speaks: for,  "Christ is the end of the law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:4
verses.text: Therefore when at the head of the title of the Psalm he placed the words, "for the end," he directed our heart to Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:5
verses.text: If we fix our gaze on Him, we shall not stray: for He is Himself the Truth unto which we are eager to arrive, and He Himself the Way by which we run.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:6
verses.text: The Prophet singeth to Him of the future, and useth words as it were of past time: he speaks of things future as if already done, because with God that which is future has already taken place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:7
verses.text: "Lord, Thou hast been favourable unto Thy land" ; as if He had already done so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:8
verses.text: "Thou hast turned away the captivity of Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:9
verses.text: His ancient people of Jacob, the people of Israel, born of Abraham's seed, in the promise to become one day the heir of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:10
verses.text: That was indeed a real people, to whom the Old Testament was given; but in the Old Testament the New was figured: that was the figure, this the truth expressed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:11
verses.text: In that figure, by a kind of foretelling of the future, there was given to that people a certain land of promise, in a region where the people of the Jews abode; where also is the city of Jerusalem, whose name we have all heard of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:12
verses.text: When this people had received possession of this land, they suffered many troubles from their neighbouring enemies who surrounded them: and when they sinned against their God, they were given into captivity, not for destruction, but for discipline; their Father not condemning, but scourging them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:13
verses.text: And after being seized on, they were set free, and many times were both made captives, and set free; and they are now in captivity, and that for a great sin, even because they crucified their Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:14
verses.text: What then are we to unders tand them to mean by the words, "Thou hast turned away the captivity of Jacob"?This Psalm hath prophesied in song.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:15
verses.text: "Thou hast turned away the captivity of Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:16
verses.text: To whom did it speak? To Christ; for it said, "for the end, for the sons of Core:" for He hath turned away the captivity of Jacob.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:17
verses.text: Hear Paul himself confessing: "O wretched man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death?" He asked who it should be, and straightway it occurred to him, "The grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:18
verses.text: Of this grace of God the Prophet speaketh to our Lord Jesus Christ, "Thou hast turned away the captivity of Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:19
verses.text: Attend to the captivity of Jacob, attend, and see that it is this: Thou hast turned away our captivity, not by setting us free from the barbarians, with whom we had not met, but by setting us free from bad works, from our sins, by which Satan held sway over us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:20
verses.text: For if any one has been set free from his sins, the prince of sinners hath not whence he may hold sway over him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:21
verses.text: For how did He turn away the captivity of Jacob? See, how that that setting free is spiritual, see how that it is done inwardly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:22
verses.text: "Thou hast forgiven," he saith, "the iniquity of Thy people: Thou hast covered all their sins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:23
verses.text: Behold how He hath turned away their captivity, in that He hath remitted iniquity: iniquity held them captive; thy iniquity forgiven, thou art freed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:24
verses.text: Confess therefore that thou art in captivity, that thou mayest be worthy to be freed: for he that knoweth not of his enemy, how can he invoke the liberator? "Thou hast covered all their sins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:25
verses.text: What is, "Thou hast covered"? So as not to see them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:26
verses.text: How didst Thou not see them? So as not to take vengeance on them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:27
verses.text: Thou wast unwilling to see our sins: and therefore sawest Thou them not, because Thou wouldest not see them: "Thou hast covered all their sins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:28
verses.text: "Thou hast appeased all Thy anger: Thou hast turned Thyself from Thy wrathful indignation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:29
verses.text: And as these things are said of the future, though the sound of the words is past, it follows: "Turn us, O God of our salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:30
verses.text: That which he had just related as if it were done, how prayeth he that it may be done, except because he wished to show that he had spoken as if of the past in prophecy? But that it was not yet done which he had said was done he showeth by this, that he prayeth that it may be done: "Turn us, O God of our salvation, and turn away Thine anger from us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:31
verses.text: Didst thou not say before: "Thou hast appeased all Thy anger, Thou has turned Thyself from Thy wrathful indignation"? How then now sayest thou, "And turn away Thine anger from us"? The Prophet answereth: These things I speak of as done, because I see them about to be done: but because they are not yet done, I pray that they may come, which I have already seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:32
verses.text: "Be not angry with us for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:33
verses.text: For by the anger of God we are subject to death, and by the anger of God we eat bread on this earth in want, and in the sweat of our face This was Adam's sentence when he sinned: and that Adam was every one of us, for "in Adam all die;" the sentence passed on him hath taken effect after him on us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:34
verses.text: For we were not yet ourselves, but we were in Adam: therefore whatever happened to Adam himself took effect on us also, so that we should die: for we all were in him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:35
verses.text: So far as this the sin of thy father hurts thee not, if thou hast changed thyself, even as it would not hurt thy father if he had changed himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:36
verses.text: But that which our stock hath received unto its subjection to death, it hath derived from Adam.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:37
verses.text: What hath it so derived? That frailty of the flesh, this torture of pains, this house of poverty, this chain of death, and snares of temptations; all these things we carry about in this flesh; and this is the anger of God, because it is the vengeance of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:38
verses.text: But because it was so to be, that we should be regenerated, and by believing should be made new, and all that mortality was to be removed in our resurrection, and the whole man was to be restored in newness; "For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ shall all be made alive;" seeing this the Prophet saith, "Be not angry with us for ever, nor stretch out Thy wrath from one generation to another".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:39
verses.text: The first generation was mortal by Thy wrath: the second generation shall be immortal by Thy mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:40
verses.text: "O God, Thou shalt turn us again, and make us alive".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:41
verses.text: Not as if we ourselves of our own accord, without Thy mercy, turn unto Thee, and then Thou shalt make us alive: but so that not only our being made alive is from Thee, but our very conversion, that we may be made alive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:42
verses.text: "And Thy people shall rejoice in Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:43
verses.text: To their own evil they shall rejoice in themselves: to their own good they shall rejoice in Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:44
verses.text: For when they wished to have joy of themselves, they found in themselves woe: but now because God is all our joy, he that will rejoice securely, let him rejoice in Him who cannot perish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:45
verses.text: For why, my brethren, will ye rejoice in silver? Either thy silver perisheth, or thou: and no one knows which first: yet this is certain, that both shall perish; which first, is uncertain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:46
verses.text: For neither can man remain here always, nor can silver remain here always: so too gold, so garments, so houses, so money, so broad lands, so, lastly, this light itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:47
verses.text: Be not thou willing then to rejoice in these: but rejoice in that light which hath no setting: rejoice in that dawn which no yesterday precedes, which no to-morrow follows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:48
verses.text: What light is that? "I," saith He, "am the Light of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:49
verses.text: He who saith unto thee, "I am the Light of the world," calls thee to Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:50
verses.text: When He calls thee, He converts thee: when He converts thee, He healeth thee: when He hath healed thee, thou shalt see thy Converter, unto whom it is said, "Show us Thy mercy, O Lord, and grant us Thy salvation" : Thy salvation, that is, Thy Christ Happy is he unto whom God showeth His mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:51
verses.text: He it is who cannot indulge in pride, unto whom God showeth His mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:52
verses.text: For by showing him His salvation He persuadeth him that whatever good man has, he hath not but from Him who is all our good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:53
verses.text: And when a man has seen that whatever good he has he hath not from himself, but from his God; he sees that everything which is praised in him is of the mercy of God, not of his own deserving; and seeing this, he is not proud; not being proud, he is not lifted up; not lifting himself up, he falleth not; not falling, he standeth; standing, he clingeth fast; clinging fast, he abideth; abiding, he enjoyeth, and rejoiceth in the Lord his God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:54
verses.text: He who made him shall be unto him a delight: and his delight no one spoileth, no one interrupteth, no one taketh away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:55
verses.text: Therefore, what saith John in his Epistle? "Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:56
verses.text: Who would not rejoice, if suddenly while he was wandering abroad, ignorant of his descent, suffering want, and in a state of misery and toil, it were announced, Thou art the son of a senator: thy father enjoys an ample patrimony on your family estate; I bid thee return to thy father: how would he rejoice, if this were said to him by some one whose promise he could trust? One whom we can trust, an Apostle of Christ, hath come and said to us, Ye have a father, ye have a country, ye have an inheritance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:57
verses.text: Who is that father? "Beloved, we are the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:58
verses.text: Therefore He promised us to show Himself unto us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:59
verses.text: Think, my brethren, what His beauty is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:60
verses.text: All those beautiful things which ye see, which ye love, He made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:61
verses.text: If these are beautiful, what is He Himself? If these are great, how great is He? Therefore from these things which we love here, let us the more long for Him: and despising these things, let us love Him: that by that very love we may by faith purify our hearts, and His vision, when it cometh, may find our heart purified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:62
verses.text: The light which shall be shown unto us ought to find us whole: this is the work of faith now.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:63
verses.text: This is what we have spoken here: "And grant us Thy salvation:" grant us Thy Christ, that we may know Thy Christ, see Thy Christ; not as the Jews saw Him and crucified Him, but as the Angels see Him, and rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:64
verses.text: "I will hearken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:65
verses.text: The Prophet spoke: God spoke within in him, and the world made a noise without.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:66
verses.text: Therefore, retiring for a little from the noise of the world, and turning himself back upon himself, and from himself upon Him whose voice he heard within; sealing up his ears, as it were, against the tumultuous disquietude of this life, and against the soul weighed down by the corruptible body, and against the imagination, that through the earthly tabernacle pressing down, thinketh on many things, he saith, "I will hearken what the Lord God speaketh in me;" and he heard, what? "For He shall speak peace unto His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:67
verses.text: The voice of Christ, then, the voice of God, is peace: it calleth unto peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:68
verses.text: Ho! it saith, whosoever are not yet in peace, love ye peace: for what can ye find better from Me than peace? What is peace? Where there is no war.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:69
verses.text: What is this, where there is no war? Where there is no contradiction, where there is no resistance, nothing to oppose.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:70
verses.text: Consider if we are yet there: consider if there is not now a conflict with the devil, if all the saints and faithful ones wrestle not with the prince of demons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:71
verses.text: And how do they wrestle with him whom they see not? They wrestle with their own desires, by which he suggests unto them sins: and by not consenting to what he suggests, though they are not conquered, yet they fight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:72
verses.text: Therefore there is not yet peace where there is fighting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:73
verses.text: Whatever we provide for our refreshment, there again we find weariness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:74
verses.text: Art thou hungry? one asks thee: thou answerest, I am.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:75
verses.text: He places food before thee for thy refreshment; continue thou to use it, for thou hadst need of it; yet in continuing that which thou needest for refreshment, therein findest thou weariness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:76
verses.text: By long sitting thou wast tired; thou risest and refreshest thyself by walking; continue that relief, and by much walking thou art wearied; again thou wouldest sit down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:77
verses.text: Find me anything by which thou art refreshed, wherein if thou continue thou dost not again become weary.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:78
verses.text: What peace then is that which men have here, opposed by so many troubles, desires, wants, wearinesses? This is no true, no perfect peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:79
verses.text: What will be perfect peace? "This corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:80
verses.text: Persevere in eating much; this itself will kill thee: persevere in fasting much, by this thou wilt die: sit continually, being resolved not to rise up, by this thou wilt die: be always walking so as never to take rest, by this thou wilt die; watch continually, taking no sleep, by this thou wilt die; sleep continually, never watching, thus too thou wilt die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:81
verses.text: When therefore death shall be swallowed up in victory, these things shall no longer be: there will be full and eternal peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:82
verses.text: We shall be in a City, of which, brethren, when I speak I find it hard to leave off, especially when offences wax common.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:83
verses.text: Who would not long for that City whence no friend goeth out, whither no enemy entereth, where is no tempter, no seditious person, no one dividing God's people, no one wearying the Church in the service of the devil; since the prince himself of all such is cast into eternal fire, and with him those who consent unto him, and who have no will to retire from him? There shall be peace made pure in the sons of God, all loving one another, seeing one another full of God, since God shall be all in all We shall have God as our common object of vision, God as our common possession, God as our common peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:84
verses.text: For whatever there is which He now giveth unto us, He Himself shall be unto us instead of His gifts; this will be full and perfect peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:85
verses.text: This He speaketh unto His people: this it was which he would hearken unto who said, "I will hearken what the Lord God will say unto me: for He shall speak peace unto His people, and to His saints, and unto those who turn their hearts unto Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:86
verses.text: Lo, my brethren, do ye wish that unto you should belong that peace which God uttereth? Turn your heart unto Him: not unto me, or unto that one, or unto any man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:87
verses.text: For whatever man would turn unto himself the hearts of men, he falleth with them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:88
verses.text: Which is better, that thou fall with him unto whom thou turnest thyself, or that thou stand with Him with whom thou turnest thyself? Our joy, our peace, our rest, the end of all troubles, is none but God: blessed are "they that turn their hearts unto Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:89
verses.text: "Nevertheless, His salvation is nigh them that fear Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:90
verses.text: There were some even then who feared Him in the Jewish people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:91
verses.text: Everywhere throughout the earth idols were worshipped: devils were feared, not God: in that nation God was feared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:92
verses.text: But why was He feared? In the Old Testament He was feared, lest He should give them up to captivity, lest He should take away their land from them, lest He should destroy their vines with hail, lest He should make their wives barren, lest He should take away their children from them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:93
verses.text: For these carnal promises of God captivated their minds, which as yet were of small growth, and for these things God was feared: but He was near unto them who even for these things feared Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:94
verses.text: The Pagan prayed for land to the devil: the Jew prayed for land to God: it was the same thing which they prayed for, but not the same to whom they prayed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:95
verses.text: The latter, though seeking what the Pagan sought, yet was distinguished from the Pagan; for he sought it of Him who had made all things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:96
verses.text: And God, who was far from the Gentiles, was near unto them: yet He had regard even to those who were afar off, and to those who were near, as the Apostle said: "And He came and preached peace to you who were afar off, and to them that were near".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:97
verses.text: Whom did He mean by those near? The Jews, because they worshipped one God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:98
verses.text: Whom by those who were afar off? The Gentiles, because they had left Him by whom they were made and worshipped things which themselves had made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:99
verses.text: For it is not in space that any one is far from God, but in affections.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:100
verses.text: Thou lovest God, thou art near unto Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:101
verses.text: Thou hatest God, thou art far off.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:102
verses.text: Thou art standing in the same place, both while thou art near and far off.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:103
verses.text: This it was, my brethren, which the Prophet had regard to: although he saw the mercy of God extending over all, yet he saw something especial and peculiar shown toward the Jews, and he saith, "Nevertheless, I will hearken what the Lord God shall say unto me: for He shall speak peace unto His people;" and His people shall be, not Judaea only, but it shall be gathered together out of all nations: "For He shall speak peace unto His Saints, and to those who turn their hearts unto Him," and to all who shall turn their hearts unto Him from the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:104
verses.text: "Nevertheless, His salvation shall be nigh them that fear Him, that glory may dwell in our land:" that is, in that land in which the Prophet was born, greater glory shall dwell, because Christ began to be preached from thence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:105
verses.text: Thence were the Apostles, and thither first they were sent; from thence were the Prophets, there first was the Temple, there sacrifice was made to God, there were the Patriarchs, there He Himself came of the seed of Abraham, there Christ was manifested, there Christ appeared; for from thence was the Virgin Mary who bore Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:106
verses.text: There He walked with His feet, there He worked miracles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:107
verses.text: Thirdly, He ascribed so great honour to that nation, that when a certain Canaanitish woman interrupted Him, praying for the healing of her daughter, He said unto her, "I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:108
verses.text: Seeing this, the Prophet saith, "that glory may dwell in our land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:109
verses.text: "Mercy and truth have met together".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:110
verses.text: "Truth in our land," in a Jewish person, "mercy" in the land of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:111
verses.text: For where was truth? Where the utterances of God were.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:112
verses.text: Where was mercy? On those who had left their God, and turned themselves unto devils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:113
verses.text: Did He look down also upon them? Yea, as if He said, Call those who are fugitives afar off, who have departed far from Me: call them, let them find Me who seek them, since they themselves would not seek Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:114
verses.text: Therefore, "Mercy and truth have met together: righteousness and peace have kissed each other".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:115
verses.text: Do righteousness, and thou shalt have peace; that righteousness and peace may kiss each other.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:116
verses.text: For if thou love not righteousness, thou shalt not have peace; for those two, righteousness and peace, love one another, and kiss one another: that he who hath done righteousness may find peace kissing righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:117
verses.text: They two are friends: thou perhaps willest the one, and not the other: for there is no one who wills not peace: but all will not work righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:118
verses.text: Ask all men, Willest thou peace? With one mouth the whole race of man answers thee, I wish, I desire, I will, I love it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:119
verses.text: Love also righteousness: for these two, righteousness and peace, are friends; they kiss one another: if thou love not the friend of peace, peace itself will not love thee, nor come unto thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:120
verses.text: For what great thing is it to desire peace? Every bad man longeth for peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:121
verses.text: For peace is a good thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:122
verses.text: But do righteousness, for righteousness and peace kiss one another, they quarrel not together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:123
verses.text: "Truth hath sprung out of the earth, and righteousness hath looked down from heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:124
verses.text: "Truth hath sprung out of the earth:" Christ is born of a woman.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:125
verses.text: The Son of God hath come forth of the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:126
verses.text: What is truth? The Son of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:127
verses.text: What is the earth? Flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:128
verses.text: Ask whence Christ was born, and thou seest that "Truth is sprung out of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:129
verses.text: But the Truth which sprang out of the earth was before the earth, and by It the heaven and the earth were made: but in order that righteousness might look down from heaven, that is, in order that men might be justified by Divine grace, Truth was born of the Virgin Mary; that He might be able to offer a sacrifice to justify them, the sacrifice of suffering, the sacrifice of the Cross.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:130
verses.text: And how could He offer a sacrifice for our sins, except He died? How could He die, except He received from us that wherein He might die; that is, unless He received from us mortal flesh, Christ could not have died: because the Word of God dieth not, Godhead dieth not, the Virtue and Wisdom of God doth not die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:131
verses.text: How should He offer a sacrifice, a healing victim, if He died not? How should He die, unless He clothed Himself with flesh? How should He put on flesh, except truth sprang out of the earth?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:132
verses.text: On the same passage we may mention another meaning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:133
verses.text: "Truth is sprung out of the earth:" confession from man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:134
verses.text: For thou, O man, wast a sinner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:135
verses.text: O earth, who when thou hadst sinned didst hear the sentence, "Earth thou art, and unto earth shalt thou return," from thee let truth spring, that righteousness may look down from heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:136
verses.text: How doth truth spring from thee, whilst thou art a sinner, whilst thou art unrighteous? Confess thy sins, and truth shall spring out of thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:137
verses.text: For if whilst thou art unrighteous, thou callest thyself just, how can truth spring out of thee? But if being unrighteous thou dost confess thyself to be so, "truth hath sprung out of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:138
verses.text: What "righteousness hath looked down from heaven"? It is that of God, as though He said: Let us spare this man, for he spareth not himself: let us pardon him, for he himself confesseth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:139
verses.text: He is changed so as to punish his sin: I too will change, so as to set him free.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:140
verses.text: "For the Lord shall give sweetness, and our land shall give her increase".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:141
verses.text: He will give unto thee the sweetness of working righteousness, so that righteousness shall begin to delight thee, whom before unrighteousness delighted: so that thou who at first didst delight in drunkenness, shall rejoice in sobriety: and thou who didst at first rejoice in theft, so as to take from another man what thou hadst not, shalt seek to give to him that hath not that which thou hast: and thou who didst take delight in robbing, shalt delight now in giving: thou whom shows delighted, shalt delight in prayer; thou who didst delight in trifling and lascivious songs, shalt now delight in singing hymns to God; in running to church, thou who at first didst run to the theatre.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:142
verses.text: Whence is that sweetness born to thee, except from this, that "God giveth sweetness"? For, behold, ye see what I mean: behold, I have spoken unto you the word of God, I have sown seed in your devout hearts, finding your souls furrowed, as it were, with the plough of confession: with devout attention ye have received the seed; think now upon the word which ye have heard, like those who break up the clouds, lest the fowls should carry away the seed, that what is sown may be able to spring up there: and unless God rain upon it, what profits it that it is sown? This is what is meant by "our land shall give her increase".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:143
verses.text: May He with His visitations, in leisure, in business, in your house, in your bed, at meal-time, in conversation, in walks, visit your hearts, when we are not by.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:144
verses.text: May the rain of God come and make to sprout what is sown there: and when we are not by, and are resting quietly, or otherwise employed, may God give increase to the seeds which we have sown, that remarking afterwards your improved characters, we too may rejoice for your fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:145
verses.text: "For righteousness shall go before him, and he shall direct his steps in the way" : that righteousness, namely, which consists in confession of sins: for this is truth itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:146
verses.text: For thou oughtest to be righteous towards thyself, and to punish thyself: for this is the beginning of man's righteousness, that thou shouldest punish thyself, who art evil, and God should make thee good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:147
verses.text: Therefore since this is the beginning of man's righteousness, this becomes a way for God, that God may come unto thee: there make for Him a way, in confession of sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:148
verses.text: Therefore John too, when he was baptizing in the water of repentance, and would have men come to him repenting of their former deeds, spoke thus: "Prepare the way of the Lord, make His paths straight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:149
verses.text: Thou didst please thyself in thy sins, O man: let that which thou wast displease thee, that thou mayest be able to become what thou wast not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:150
verses.text: Prepare the way of the Lord: let that righteousness go before, of confession of sins: He will come and visit thee, for now He hath where to place His steps, He hath whereby He may come to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:151
verses.text: Before thou didst confess thy sins, thou hadst shut up the way of God: there was no way by which He might come unto thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 87:152
verses.text: Confess thy past life, and thou openest a way; and Christ shall come unto thee, and "shall place His steps in the way," that He may guide thee with His own footsteps.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXXVIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:2
verses.text: The Title of this eighty-seventh Psalm contains a fresh subject for enquiry: the words occurring here, "for Melech to respond," being nowhere else found.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:3
verses.text: We have already given our opinion on the meaning of the titles Psalmus Cantici and Canticum Psalmi: and the words, "sons of Core," are constantly repeated, and have often been explained: so also "to the end;" but what comes next in this title is peculiar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:4
verses.text: For "Melech" we may translate into Latin "for the chorus," for chorus is the sense of the Hebrew word MelechThe Passion of our Lord is here prophesied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:5
verses.text: Now the Apostle Peter saith, "Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that we should follow His steps;" this is the meaning of "to respond".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:6
verses.text: The Apostle John also saith, "As Christ laid down His life for us, so ought we also to lay down our lives for the brethren;" this also is to respond.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:7
verses.text: But the choir signifies concord, which consists in charity: whoever therefore in imitation of our Lord's Passion gives up his body to be burnt, if he have not charity, does not answer in the choir, and therefore it profiteth him nothing Further, as in Latin the terms Precentor and Succentor are used to denote in music the performer who sings the first part, and him who takes it up; just so in this song of the Passion, Christ going before is followed by the choir of martyrs unto the end of gaining crowns in Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:8
verses.text: This is sung by "the sons of Core," that is, the imitators of Christ's Passion: as Christ was crucified in Calvary, which is the interpretation of the Hebrew word Core.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:9
verses.text: This also is "the understanding of aeman the Israelite:" words occurring at the end of this title.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:10
verses.text: aeman is said to mean, "his brother:" for Christ deigns to make those His brethren, who understand the mystery of His Cross, and not only are not ashamed of it, but faithfully glory in it, not praising themselves for their own merits, but grateful for His grace: so that it may be said to each of them, "Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom there is no guile," just as holy Scripture says of Israel himself, that he was without guile.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:11
verses.text: "O Lord God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:12
verses.text: Let us therefore now hear the voice of Christ singing before us in prophecy, to whom His own choir should respond either in imitation, or in thanksgiving.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:13
verses.text: "O let my prayer enter into Thy presence, incline Thine ear unto my calling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:14
verses.text: For even our Lord prayed, not in the form of God, but in the form of a servant; for in this He also suffered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:15
verses.text: He prayed both in prosperous times, that is, by "day," and in calamity, which I imagine is meant by "night".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:16
verses.text: The entrance of prayer into God's presence is its acceptance: the inclination of His ear is His compassionate listening to it: for God has not such bodily members as we have.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:17
