verses.text: The passage is however, as usual, a repetition.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:18
verses.text: "For my soul is filled with evils, and my life draweth nigh unto hell".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:19
verses.text: Dare we speak of the Soul of Christ as "filled with evils," when the passion had strength as far as it had any, only over the body?The soul therefore may feel pain without the body: but without the soul the body cannot.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:20
verses.text: Why therefore should we not say that the Soul of Christ was full of the evils of humanity, though not of human sins? Another Prophet says of Him, that He grieved for us: and the Evangelist says, "And He took with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and very heavy:" and our Lord Himself saith unto them of Himself, "My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:21
verses.text: The Prophet who composed this Psalm, foreseeing that this would happen, introduces Him saying, "My soul is full of evils, and My life draweth nigh unto hell".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:22
verses.text: For the very same sense is here expressed in other words, as when He said, "My soul is sorrowful, even unto death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:23
verses.text: The words, "My soul is sorrowful," are like these, "My soul is full of evils:" and what follows, "even unto death," like, "my life draweth nigh unto hell".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:24
verses.text: These feelings of human infirmity our Lord took upon Him, as He did the flesh of human infirmity, and the death of human flesh, not by the necessity of His condition, but by the free will of His mercy, that He might transfigure into Himself His own body, which is the Church (the head of which He deigned to be), that is, His members in His holy and faithful disciples: that if amid human temptations any one among them happened to be in sorrow and pain, he might not therefore think that he was separated from His favour: that the body, like the chorus following its leader, might learn from its Head, that these sorrows were not sin, but proofs of human weakness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:25
verses.text: We read of the Apostle Paul, a chief member in this body, and we hear him confessing that his soul was full of such evils, when he says, that he feels "great heaviness and continual sorrow in heart for his brethren according to the flesh, who are Israelites".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:26
verses.text: And if we say that our Lord was sorrowful for them also at the approach of His Passion, in which they would incur the most atrocious guilt, I think we shall not speak amiss.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:27
verses.text: Lastly, the very thing said by our Saviour on  the Cross, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do," is expressed in this Psalm below, "I am counted as one of them that go down into the pit" : by them who knew not what they were doing, when they imagined that He died like other men, subjected to necessity, and overcome by it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:28
verses.text: The word "pit" is used for the depth of woe or of Hell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:29
verses.text: "I have been as a man that hath no help".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:30
verses.text: "Free among the dead".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:31
verses.text: In these words our Lord's Person is most clearly shown: for who else is free among the dead but He who though in the likeness of sinful flesh is alone among sinners without sin?He therefore, "free among the dead," who had it in His power to lay down His life, and again to take it; from whom no one could take it, but He laid it down of His own free will; who could revive His own flesh, as a temple destroyed by them, at His will; who, when all had forsaken Him on the eve of His Passion, remained not alone, because, as He testifies, His Father forsook Him not; was nevertheless by His enemies, for whom He prayed, who knew not what they did, counted "as one who hath no help; like unto them that are wounded, and lie in the grave".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:32
verses.text: But he adds, "Whom thou dost not yet remember:" and in these words there is to be remarked a distinction between Christ and the rest of the dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:33
verses.text: For though He was wounded, and when dead laid in the tomb, yet they who knew not what they were doing, or who He was, regarded Him as like others who had perished from their wounds, and who slept in the tomb, who are as yet out of remembrance of God, that is, whose hour of resurrection has not yet arrived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:34
verses.text: For thus the Scripture speaks of the dead as sleeping, because it wishes them to be regarded as destined to awake, that is, to rise again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:35
verses.text: But He, wounded and asleep in the tomb, awoke on the third day, and became "like a sparrow that sitteth alone on the housetop," that is, on the right hand of His Father in Heaven: and now "dieth no more, death shall no more have dominion over Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:36
verses.text: Hence He differs widely from those whom God hath not yet remembered to cause their resurrection after this manner: for what was to go before in the Head, was kept for the Body in the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:37
verses.text: God is then said to remember, when He does an act: then to forget, when He does it not: for neither can God forget, as He never changes, nor remember, as He can never forget.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:38
verses.text: "I am counted" then, by those who know not what they do, "as a man that hath no help:" while I am "free among the dead," I am held by these men "like unto them that are wounded, and lie in the grave".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:39
verses.text: Yet those very men, who account thus of Me, are further said to be "cut away from Thy hand," that is, when I was made so by them, "they were cut away from Thy hand;" they who believed Me destitute of help, are deprived of the help of Thy hand: for they, as he saith in another Psalm, have digged a pit before me, and are fallen into the midst of it themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:40
verses.text: I prefer this interpretation to that which refers the words, "they are cut away from Thy hand," to those who sleep in the tomb, whom God hath not yet remembered: since the righteous are among the latter, of whom, even though God hath not yet called them to the resurrection, it is said, that their "souls are in the hands of God," that is, that "they dwell under the defence of the Most High; and shall abide under the shadow of the God of Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:41
verses.text: But it is those who are cut away from the hand of God, who believed that Christ was cut off from His hand, and thus accounting Him among the wicked, dared to slay Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:42
verses.text: "They laid Me in the lowest pit" , that is, the deepest pit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:43
verses.text: For so it is in the Greek.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:44
verses.text: But what is the l owest pit, but the deepest woe, than which there is none more deep? Whence in another Psalm it is said, "Thou broughtest me out also of the pit of misery".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:45
verses.text: "In a place of darkness, and in the shadow of death," whiles they knew not what they did, they laid Him there, thus deeming of Him; they knew not Him "whom none of the princes of this world knew".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:46
verses.text: By the "shadow of death," I know not whether the death of the body is to be understood, or that of which it is written, "That they walked in darkness and in the land of the shadow of death, a light is risen on them," because by belief they were brought from out of the darkness and death of sin into light and life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:47
verses.text: Such an one those who knew not what they did thought our Lord, and in their ignorance accounted Him among those whom He came to help, that they might not be such themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:48
verses.text: "Thy indignation lieth hard upon Me" , or, as other copies have it, "Thy anger;" or, as others, "Thy fury:" the Greek word θυμὸς having undergone different interpretations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:49
verses.text: For where the Greek copies have ὀργὴ, no translator hesitated to express it by the Latin ira; but where the word is θυμὸς, most object to rendering it by ira, although many of the authors of the best Latin style, in their translations from Greek philosophy, have thus rendered the word in Latin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:50
verses.text: But I shall not discuss this matter further: only if I also were to suggest another term, I should think "indignation" more tolerable than "fury," this word in Latin not being applied to persons in their senses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:51
verses.text: What then does this mean, "Thy indignation lieth hard upon Me," except the belief of those, who knew not the Lord of Glory? who imagined that the anger of God was not merely roused, but lay hard upon Him, whom they dared to bring to death, and not only death, but that kind, which they regarded as the most execrable of all, namely, the death of the Cross: whence saith the Apostle, "Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the Law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth upon a tree".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:52
verses.text: On this account, wishing to praise His obedience which He carried to the extreme of humility, he says, "He humbled Himself, and became obedient unto death;" and as this seemed little, he added, "even the death of the Cross;" and with the same view as far as I can see, he says in this Psalm, "And all thy suspensions," or, as some translate "waves," others "tossings," "Thou hast brought over Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:53
verses.text: We also find in another Psalm, "All thy suspensions and waves are come in upon Me," or, as some have translated better, "have passed over Me:" for it is διῆλθον in Greek, not εἰσῆλθον: and where both expressions are employed, "waves" and "suspensions," one cannot be used as equivalent to the other.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:54
verses.text: In that passage we explained "suspensions" as threatenings, "waves" as the actual sufferings: both inflicted by God's judgment: but in that place it is said, "All have passed over Me," here, "Thou hast brought all upon Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:55
verses.text: In the other case, that is, although some evils took place, yet, he said, all those which are here mentioned passed over; but in this case, "Thou hast brought them upon Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:56
verses.text: Evils pass over when they do not touch a man, as things which hang over him, or when they do touch him, as waves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:57
verses.text: But when he uses the word "suspensions," he does not say they passed over, but, "Thou hast brought them upon Me," meaning that all which impended had come to pass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:58
verses.text: All things which were predicted of His Passion impended, as long as they remained in the prophecies for future fulfilment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:59
verses.text: "Thou hast put Mine acquaintance far from Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:60
verses.text: If we understand by acquaintance those whom He knew, it will be all men; for whom knew He not? But He calls those acquaintance, to whom He was Himself known, as far as they could know Him at that season: at least so far forth as they knew Him to be innocent, although they considered Him only as a man, not as likewise God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:61
verses.text: Although He might call the righteous whom He approved, acquaintance, as He calls the wicked unknown, to whom He was to say at the end, "I know you not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:62
verses.text: In what follows, "and they have set Me for an abhorrence to themselves;" those whom He called before "acquaintance," may be meant, as even they felt horror at the mode of that death: but it is better referred to those of whom He was speaking above as His persecutors.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:63
verses.text: "I was delivered up, and did not get forth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:64
verses.text: Is this because His disciples were without, while He was being tried within? Or are we to give a deeper meaning to the words, "I cannot get forth" as signifying, "I remained hidden in My secret counsels, I showed not who I was, I did not reveal Myself, was not made manifest"? And so it follows,—  "My eyes became weak from want".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:65
verses.text: For what eyes are we to understand? If the eyes of the flesh in which He suffered, we do not read that His eyes became weak from want, that is, from hunger, in His Passion, as is often the case; as He was betrayed after His Supper, and crucified on the same day: if the inner eyes, how were they weakened from want, in which there was a light that could never fail? But He meant by His eyes those members in the body, of which He was Himself the head, which, as brighter and more eminent and chief above the rest, He loved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:66
verses.text: It was of this body that the Apostle was speaking, when he wrote, taking his metaphor from our own body, "If the whole body were an eye, where were the hearing?" etc What he wished understood by these words, he has expressed more clearly, by adding, "Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:67
verses.text: Wherefore as those eyes, that is, the holy Apostles, to whom not flesh and blood, but the Father which is in Heaven had revealed Him, so that Peter said, "Thou art Christ, the Son of the Living God," when they saw Him betrayed, and suffering such evils, saw Him not such as they wished, as He did not come forth, did not manifest Himself in His virtue and power, but still hidden in His secrecy, endured everything as a man overcome and enfeebled, they became weak for want, as if their food, their Light, had been withdrawn from them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:68
verses.text: He continues, "And I have called upon Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:69
verses.text: This indeed He did most clearly, when upon the Cross.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:70
verses.text: But what follows? "All the day I have stretched forth My hands unto Thee," must be examined how it must be taken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:71
verses.text: For if in this expression we understand the tree of the Cross, how can we reconcile it with the "whole day"? Can He be said to have hung upon the Cross during the whole day, as the night is considered a part of the day? But if day, as opposed to night, was meant by this expression, even of this day, the first and no small portion had passed by at the time of His crucifixion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:72
verses.text: But if we take "day" in the same sense of time (especially as the word is used in the feminine, a gender which is restricted to that sense in Latin, although not so in Greek, as it is always used in the feminine, which I suppose to be the reason for its translation in the same gender in our own version), the knot of the question will be drawn tighter: for how can it mean for the whole space of time, if He did not even for one day stretch forth His hands on the Cross? Further, should we take the whole for a part, as Scripture sometimes uses this expression, I do not remember an instance in which the whole is taken for a part, when the word "whole" is expressly added.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:73
verses.text: For in the passage of the Gospel where the Lord saith, "The Son of Man shall be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth,"  it is no extraordinary licence to take the whole for the part, the expression not being for three "whole" days and three whole nights: since the one intermediate day was a whole one, the other two were parts, the last being part of the first day, the first part of the last.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:74
verses.text: But if the Cross is not meant here, but the prayer, which we find in the Gospel that He poured forth in the form of a servant to God the Father, where He is said to have prayed long before His Passion, and on the eve of His Passion, and also when on the Cross, we do not read anywhere that He did so throughout the whole day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:75
verses.text: Therefore by the stretched-out hands throughout the whole day, we may understand the continuation of good works in which He never ceased from exertion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:76
verses.text: But as His good works profited only the predestined to eternal salvation, and not all men, nor even all those among whom they were done, he adds, "Dost thou show wonders among the dead?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:77
verses.text: If we suppose this relates to those whose flesh life has left, great wonders have been wrought among the dead, inasmuch as some of them have revived: and in our Lord's descent into Hell, and His ascent as the conqueror of death, a great wonder was wrought among the dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:78
verses.text: He refers then in these words, "Dost Thou show wonders among the dead?" to men so dead in heart, that such great works of Christ could not rouse them to the life of faith: for he does not say that wonders are not shown to them because they see them not, but because they do not profit them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:79
verses.text: For, as he says in this passage, "the whole day have I stretched forth My hands to Thee:" because He ever refers all His works to the will of His Father, constantly declaring that He came to fulfil His Father's will: so also, as an unbelieving people saw the same works, another Prophet saith, "I have spread out my hands all day unto a rebellious people, that believes not, but contradicts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:80
verses.text: Those then are dead, to whom wonders have not been shown, not because they saw them not, but since they lived not again through them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:81
verses.text: The following verse, "Shall physicians revive them, and shall they praise Thee?" means, that the dead shall not be revived by such means, that they may praise Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:82
verses.text: In the Hebrew there is said to be a different expression: giants being used where physicians are here: but the Septuagint translators, whose authority is such that they may deservedly be said to have interpreted by the inspiration of the Spirit of God owing to their wonderful agreement, conclude, not by mistake, but taking occasion from the resemblance in sound between the Hebrew words expressing these two senses, that the use of the word is an indication of the sense in which the word giants is meant to be taken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:83
verses.text: For if you suppose the proud meant by giants, of whom the Apostle saith, "Where is the wise? where is the scribe? where is the disputer of this world?"  there is no incongruity in calling them physicians, as if by their own unaided skill they promised the salvation of souls: against whom it is said, "Of the Lord is safety".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:84
verses.text: But if we take the word giant in a good sense, as it is said of our Lord, "He rejoiceth as a giant to run his course;" that is Giant of giants, chief among the greatest and strongest, who in His Church excel in spiritual strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:85
verses.text: Just as He is the Mountain of mountains; as it is written, "And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord's house shall be manifested in the top of the mountains:" and the Saint of saints: there is no absurdity in styling these same great and mighty men physicians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:86
verses.text: Whence saith the Apostle, "if by any means I may provoke to emulation them which are my flesh, and might save some of them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:87
verses.text: But even such physicians, even though they cure not by their own power (as not even of their own do those of the body), yet so far forth as by faithful ministry they assist towards salvation, can cure the living, but not raise the dead: of whom it is said, "Dost Thou show wonders among the dead?" For the grace of God, by which men's minds in a certain manner are brought to live a fresh life, so as to be able to hear the lessons of salvation from any of its ministers whatever, is most hidden and mysterious.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:88
verses.text: This grace is thus spoken of in the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:89
verses.text: "No man can come to Me, except the Father which hath sent Me draw him;"in order to show, that the very faith by which the soul believes, and springs into fresh life from the death of its former affections, is given us by God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:90
verses.text: Whatever exertions, then, the best preachers of the word, and persuaders of the truth through miracles, may make with men, just like great physicians: yet if they are dead, and through Thy grace have not a second life, "Dost Thou show wonders among the dead, or shall physicians raise them? and shall they" whom they raise "praise Thee"? For this confession declares that they live: not, as it is written elsewhere, "Thanksgiving perisheth from the dead, as from one that is not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:91
verses.text: "Shall one show Thy loving-kindness in the grave, or Thy faithfulness in destruction?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:92
verses.text: The word "show" is of course understood as if repeated, Shall any show Thy faithfulness in destruction? Scripture loves to connect loving-kindness and faithfulness, especially in the Psalms.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:93
verses.text: "Destruction" also is a repetition of "the grave," and signifies them who are in the grave, styled above "the dead," in the verse, "Dost thou show wonders among the dead?" for the body is the grave of the dead soul; whence our Lord's words in the Gospel, "Ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but within are full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:94
verses.text: Even so ye outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:95
verses.text: "Shall thy wondrous works be known in the dark, and thy righteousness in the land where all things are forgotten?" , the dark answers to the land of forgetfulness: for the unbelieving are meant by the dark, as the Apostle saith, "For ye were sometimes darkness;" and the land where all things are forgotten, is the man who has forgotten God; for the unbelieving soul can arrive at darkness so intense, "that the fool saith in his heart, There is no God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:96
verses.text: Thus the meaning of the whole passage may thus be drawn out in its connection: "Lord, I have called upon Thee," amid My sufferings; "all day I have stretched forth my hands unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:97
verses.text: I have never ceased to stretch forth My works to glorify Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:98
verses.text: Why then do the wicked rage against Me, unless because "Thou showest not wonders among the dead"? because those wonders move them not to faith, nor can physicians restore them to life that they may praise Thee, because Thy hidden grace works not in them to draw them unto believing: because no man cometh unto Me, but whom Thou hast drawn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:99
verses.text: Shall then "Thy loving-kindness be showed in the grave"? that is, the grave of the dead soul, which lies dead beneath the body's weight: "or Thy faithfulness in destruction"? that is, in such a death as cannot believe or feel any of these things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:100
verses.text: "For how then in the darkness" of this death, that is, in the man who in forgetting Thee has lost the light of his life, "shall Thy wondrous works and Thy righteousness be known".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:101
verses.text: But that those prayers, the blessings of which surpass all words, may be more fervent and more constant, the gift that shall last unto eternity is deferred, while transitory evils are allowed to thicken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:102
verses.text: And so it follows: "Lord, why hast Thou cast off my prayer?" , which may be compared with another Psalm: "My God, My God, look upon me; why hast Thou forsaken me?" The reason is made matter of question, not as if the wisdom of God were blamed as doing so without a cause; and so here.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:103
verses.text: "Lord, why hast Thou cast off my prayer?" But if this cause be attended to carefully, it will be found indicated above; for it is with the view that the prayers of the Saints are, as it were, repelled by the delay of so great a blessing, and by the adversity they encounter in the troubles of life, that the flame, thus fanned, may burst into a brighter blaze.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:104
verses.text: For this purpose he briefly sketches in what follows the troubles of Christ's body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:105
verses.text: For it is not in the Head alone that they took place, since it is said to Saul too, "Why persecutest thou Me?" and Paul himself, as if placed as an elect member in the same body, saith, "That I may fill up that which is behind of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:106
verses.text: "Why then, Lord, hast Thou cast off my soul? why hidest Thou Thy face from me?"  "I am poor, and in toils from my youth up: and when lifted up, I was thrown down, and troubled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:107
verses.text: "Thy wraths went over me: Thy terrors disturbed me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:108
verses.text: "They came round about me all day like water: they compassed me about together".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:109
verses.text: "A friend Thou hast put far from me: and mine acquaintance from my misery".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:110
verses.text: All these evils have taken place, and are happening in the limbs of Christ's body, and God turns away His face from their prayers, by not hearing as to what they wish for, since they know not that the fulfilment of their wishes would not be good for them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:111
verses.text: The Church is "poor," as she hungers and thirsts in her wanderings for that food with which she shall be filled in her own country: she is "in toils from her youth up," as the very Body of Christ saith in another Psalm, "Many a time have they overcome me from my youth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:112
verses.text: And for this reason some of her members are lifted up even in this world, that in them may be the greater lowliness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:113
verses.text: Over that Body, which constitutes the unity of the Saints and the faithful, whose Head is Christ, go the wraths of God: yet abide not: since it is of the unbelieving only that it is written, that "the wrath of God abideth upon him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:114
verses.text: The terrors of God disturb the weakness of the faithful, because all that can happen, even though it actually happen not, it is prudent to fear; and sometimes these terrors so agitate the reflecting soul with the evils impending around, that they seem to flow around us on every side like water, and to encircle us in our fears.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:115
verses.text: And as the Church while on pilgrimage is never free from these evils, happening as they do at one moment in one of her limbs, at another in another, he adds, "all day," signifying the continuation in time, to the end of this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:116
verses.text: Often too, friends and acquaintances, their worldly interests at stake, in their terror forsake the Saints; of which saith the Apostle, "all men forsook me: may it not be laid to their charge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:117
verses.text: But to what purpose is all this, but that early in the morning, that is, after the night of unbelief, the prayers of this holy Body may in the light of faith prevent God, until the coming of that salvation, which we are at present saved by hoping for, not by having, while we await it with patience and faithfulness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 88:118
verses.text: Then the Lord will not repel our prayers, as there will no longer be anything to be sought for, but everything that has been rightly asked, will be obtained: nor will He turn His face away from us, since we shall see Him as He is: nor shall we be poor, because God will be our abundance, all in all: nor shall we suffer, as there will be no more weakness: nor after exaltation shall we meet with humiliation and confusion, as there will be no adversity there: nor bear even the transient wrath of God, as we shall abide in His abiding love: nor will His terrors agitate us, because His promises realized will bless us: nor will our friend and acquaintance, being terrified, be far from us, where there will be no foe to dread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:1
verses.text: Psalm LXXXIX.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:2
verses.text: Understand, beloved, this Psalm, which I am about to explain, by the grace of God, of our hope in the Lord Jesus Christ, and be of good cheer, because He who promised, will fulfil all, as He has fulfilled much: for it is not our own merit, but His mercy, that gives us confidence in Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:3
verses.text: He Himself is mea nt, in my belief, by "the understanding of aethan the Israelite:" which has given this Psalm its title.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:4
verses.text: You see then, who is meant by aethan: but the meaning of the word is "strong".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:5
verses.text: No man in this world is strong, except in the hope of God's promises: for as to our own deservings, we are weak, in His mercy we are strong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:6
verses.text: Weak then in himself, strong in God's mercy, the Psalmist thus begins: "I will sing of Thy mercies, O Lord, for ever: with my mouth will I make known Thy truth unto all generations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:7
verses.text: Let my limbs, he saith, serve the Lord: I speak, but it is of Thine I speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:8
verses.text: "With my mouth will I make known Thy truth:" if I obey not Thee, I am not Thy servant: if I speak on my own part, I am a liar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:9
verses.text: To speak then from Thee, and in my own person, are two things: one mine, one Thine: Truth Thine, language mine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:10
verses.text: Let us hear then what faithfulness he maketh known, what mercies he singeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:11
verses.text: "For Thou hast said, Mercy shall be built up for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:12
verses.text: It is this that I sing: this is Thy truth, for the making known of which my mouth serveth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:13
verses.text: In such wise Thou sayest, I build, as not to destroy: for some Thou destroyest and buildest not; and some whom Thou destroyest Thou dost rebuild.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:14
verses.text: For unless there were some who were destroyed to be rebuilt, Jeremiah would not have written, "See, I have this day set thee to throw down and to build".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:15
verses.text: And indeed all who formerly worshipped images and stones could not be built up in Christ, without being destroyed as to their old error.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:16
verses.text: While, unless some were destroyed not to be built up, it would not be written, "He shall destroy them, and not build them up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:17
verses.text: In what follows, he joins these two words, mercy and faithfulness; "For Thou hast said, Mercy shall be built up for ever: Thy truth shall be established in the Heavens:" in which mercy and truth are repeated, "for all the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth," for truth in the fulfilment of promises could not be shown, unless mercy in the remission of sins preceded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:18
verses.text: Next, as many things were promised in prophecy even to the people of Israel that came according to the flesh from the seed of Abraham, and that people was increased that the promises of God might be fulfilled in it; while yet God did not close the fountain of His goodness even to the Gentiles, whom He had placed under the rule of the Angels, while He reserved the people of Israel as His own portion: the Apostle expressly mentions the Lord's mercy and truth as referring to these two parties.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:19
verses.text: For he calls Christ "a minister of the Circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promises made unto the fathers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:20
verses.text: See how God deceived not; see how He cast not off His people, whom He foreknew.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:21
verses.text: For while the Apostle is treating of the fall of the Jews, to prevent any from believing them so far disowned of God, that no wheat from that floor's fanning could reach the granary, he saith, "God hath not cast away His people, whom He foreknew; for I also am an Israelite".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:22
verses.text: If all that nation are thorns, how am I who speak unto you wheat? So that the truth of God was fulfilled in those Israelites who believed, and one wall from the circumcision is thus brought to meet the corner stone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:23
verses.text: But this stone would not form a corner, unless it received another wall from the Gentiles: so that the former wall relates in a special manner to the truth, the latter to the mercy of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:24
verses.text: "Now I say," says the Apostle, "that Jesus Christ was a minister of the Circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promise made unto the fathers: and that the Gentiles might glorify God for His mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:25
verses.text: Justly then is it added, "Thy truth shalt Thou stablish in the Heavens:" for all those Israelites who were called to be Apostles became as Heavens which declare the glory of God: as it is written by them, "The Heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament showeth His handywork".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:26
verses.text: Since, although they were taken up from hence before the Church filled the whole world, yet as "their words reached to the ends of the world," we are right in supposing this which we have just read, "Thy truth shalt Thou stablish in the Heavens," fulfilled in them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:27
verses.text: "Thou hast said, I have made a covenant with My chosen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:28
verses.text: What covenant, but the new, by which we are renewed to a fresh inheritance, in our longing desire and love of which we sing a new song.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:29
verses.text: "I have made a covenant with My chosen," saith the Psalmist: "I have sworn unto David My servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:30
verses.text: How confidently does he speak, who understands, whose mouth serves truth! I speak without fear; since "Thou hast said".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:31
verses.text: If Thou makest me fearless, because Thou hast said, how much more so dost Thou make me, when Thou hast sworn! For the oath of God is the assurance of a promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:32
verses.text: Man is justly forbidden to swear: lest by the habit of swearing, since a man may be deceived, he fall into perjury.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:33
verses.text: God alone swears securely, because He alone is infallible.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:34
verses.text: Let us see then what God hath sworn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:35
verses.text: "I have sworn," He saith, "to David My servant; thy seed will I establish for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:36
verses.text: But what is the seed of David, but that of Abraham.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:37
verses.text: And what is the seed of Abraham? "And to thy seed," He saith, "which is Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:38
verses.text: But perhaps that Christ, the Head of the Church, the Saviour of the body, is the seed of Abraham, and therefore of David; but we are not Abraham's seed? We are assuredly; as the Apostle saith, "And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:39
verses.text: In this sense, then, let us take the words, brethren, "Thy seed will I stablish for ever," not only of that Flesh of Christ, born of the Virgin Mary, but also of all of us who believe in Christ, for we are limbs of that Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:40
verses.text: This body cannot be deprived of its Head: if the Head is in glory for ever, so are the limbs, so that Christ remains entire for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:41
verses.text: "Thy seed will I stablish for ever: and set up thy throne to generation and generation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:42
verses.text: We suppose he saith, "for ever," because it is "to generation and generation:" since he has said above, with "my mouth will I ever be showing Thy truth to generation and generation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:43
verses.text: What is "to generation and generation"? To every generation: for the word needed not as many repetitions, as the coming and passing away of the several generations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:44
verses.text: The multiplication of generations is signified and set forth to notice by the repetition.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:45
verses.text: Are possibly two generations to be understood, as ye are aware, my beloved brethren, and as I have before explained? for there is now a generation of flesh and blood: there will be a future generation in the resurrection of the dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:46
verses.text: Christ is proclaimed here: He will be proclaimed there: here He is proclaimed, that He may be believed in: there, He will be welcomed, that He may be seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:47
verses.text: "I will set up Thy throne from one generation to another".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:48
verses.text: Christ hath now a throne in us, His throne is set up in us: for unless he sat enthroned within us, He would not rule us: but if we were not ruled by Him, we should be thrown down by ourselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:49
verses.text: He therefore sits within us, reigning over us: He sits also in another generation, which will come from the resurrection of the dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:50
verses.text: Christ will reign for ever over His Saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:51
verses.text: God has promised this; He hath said it: if this is not enough, God hath sworn it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:52
verses.text: As then the promise is certain, not on account of our deservings, but of His pity, no one ought to be afraid in proclaiming that which he cannot doubt of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:53
verses.text: Let that strength then inspire our hearts, whence aethan received his name, "strong in heart:" let us preach the truth of God, the utterance of God, His promises, His oath; and let us, strengthened on every side by these means, glorify God, and by bearing Him along with us, become Heavens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:54
verses.text: "O Lord, the very Heavens shall praise Thy wondrous works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:55
verses.text: The Heavens will not praise their own merits, but Thy wondrous works, O Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:56
verses.text: For in every act of mercy on the lost, of justification of the unrighteous, what do we praise but the wondrous works of God? Thou praisest Him, because the dead have risen: praise Him yet more, because the lost are redeemed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:57
verses.text: What grace, what mercy of God! Thou seest a man yesterday a whirlpool of drunkenness, to-day an ornament of sobriety: a man yesterday the sink of luxury, to-day the beauty of temperance: yesterday a blasphemer of God, to-day His praiser: yesterday the slave of the creature, to-day the worshipper of the Creator.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:58
verses.text: From all these desperate states men are thus converted: let them not look at their own merits: let them become Heavens, and praise the wondrous works of Him by whom they were made Heavens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:59
verses.text: "For who is he among the clouds, who shall be compared unto Thee, Lord!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:60
verses.text: Is this to be the praise of the Heavens, is this to be their rain? What? are the preachers confident, because "none among the clouds shall be compared unto the Lord"? Does it appear to you, brethren, a high ground of praise, that the clouds cannot be compared with their Creator? If it is taken in its literal, not in its mystical meaning, it is not so: what? are the stars that are above the clouds to be compared with the Lord? what? can the Sun, Moon, Angels, Heavens, be even compared with the Lord? Why is it then that he says, as if he meant some high praise, "For who is he among the clouds?" etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:61
verses.text: We understand, my brethren, those clouds, as the Heavens, to be the preachers of truth; Prophets, Apostles, the announcers of the word of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:62
verses.text: If therefore the clouds are the preachers of the truth, let us first enquire why they are clouds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:63
verses.text: For the same men are Heavens and clouds: Heavens from the brightness of the truth, clouds from the hidden things of the flesh: for all clouds are obscure, owing to their mortality: and they come and go.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:64
verses.text: It is on account of these very obscurities of the flesh, that is, of the clouds, that the Apostle saith, "Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come, who will bring to light the hidden things of darkness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:65
verses.text: You see at this moment what a man is saying: but what he has in his heart, you cannot see: what is forced from the cloud, you see, what is kept within the cloud, you see not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:66
verses.text: For whose eyes pierce the cloud? The clouds therefore are the preachers of the truth in the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:67
verses.text: The Creator of all things Himself came in the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:68
verses.text: We are called clouds on account of the flesh, and we are preachers of the truth on account of the showers of the clouds: but our flesh comes in one way, His by another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:69
verses.text: We too are called sons of God, but He is the Son of God in another sense.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:70
verses.text: His cloud comes from a Virgin, He is the Son from eternity, co-eternal with the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:71
verses.text: "Who is he then among the clouds, that shall be compared unto the Lord? and what is he among the sons of God, that shall be like unto the Lord?" Let the Lord Himself say whether He can find one like unto Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:72
verses.text: "Whom do men say that I the Son of Man am?" Because I appear, because I am seen, because I walk among you, and perhaps at present I am become common; say, whom do men say that I the Son of Man am? Surely when they see a son of man, they see a cloud; but say, "Whom do men say that I am?" In answer they gave Him the reports of men; "Some say that Thou art John the Baptist: some Elias, and others Jeremias, or one of the prophets".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:73
verses.text: Many clouds and sons of God are here mentioned: for because they were righteous and holy, as the sons of God, Jeremias, Elias, and John are called also sons of God: in their character of preachers of God, they are styled clouds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:74
verses.text: Ye have said what clouds men imagine Me to be: do ye too say, "Whom say ye that I am?" Peter replying in behalf of all, one for those who were one, answered, "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God;" not like those sons of God who are not made equal to Thee: Thou hast come in the flesh: but not as the clouds, who are not to be compared unto Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:75
verses.text: "God is very greatly to be feared in the counsel of the righteous, and to be had in dread of all them that are round about Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:76
verses.text: God is everywhere; who therefore are round about Him, who is everywhere? For if He has some round about Him, He is represented as finite on every side.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:77
verses.text: Moreover, if it is truly said to God and of God, "of His greatness there is no end;" who remain, who are round about Him, except because He who is everywhere, chose to be born of the flesh on one spot, to dwell among one nation, in one place to be crucified, from one spot to rise again and ascend into Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:78
verses.text: Where He did this, the Gentiles are round about Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:79
verses.text: If He remained where He did these things, He would not be "great, and be had in dread of all them that are round about Him;" but since He preached when there in such a manner as to send preachers of His own name through all nations over the whole world; by working miracles among His servants, He is become "great, and to be had in dread of all them that are round about Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:80
verses.text: "O Lord God of Hosts, who is like unto Thee? Thy truth, most mighty Lord, is on every side".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:81
verses.text: Great is Thy power: Thou hast made Heaven and earth, and all things that in them are: but greater still is thy loving-kindness, which has shown forth Thy truth to all around Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:82
verses.text: For if Thou hadst been preached only on the spot where Thou didst deign to be born, to suffer, to rise again, to ascend; the truth of that promise of God would have been fulfilled, to confirm the promises made unto the fathers: but the promise, "that the Gentiles may glorify God for His mercy," would not have been fulfilled, had not that truth been explained, and diffused to those around Thee from the spot where Thou didst deign to appear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:83
verses.text: On that spot Thou didst thunder out of Thy own cloud: but to scatter rain upon the Gentiles round about, Thou hast sent other clouds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:84
verses.text: Truly in Thy power hast Thou fulfilled what Thou hast said, "Hereafter shall ye see the Son of Man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:85
verses.text: For ye have heard, like men accustomed to the watering of the clouds of God, "Thy truth" then "is in the circuit of Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:86
verses.text: But when without persecutions, when without opposition, since it is said, that "He was born for a sign which shall be spoken against"? Since then that nation, where Thou didst deign to be born, and to dwell, was as a land separated from the waves of the heathen, so that it appeared dry and ready for watering with rain, while the rest of the nations were as a sea in the bitterness of their sterility; what do Thy preachers who scatter Thy truth in circuit of Thee, when the waves of that sea rage furiously? "Thou rulest the power of the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:87
verses.text: For what was the result of the sea raging thus, but the day which we are now keeping holy? It slew Martyrs, scattered seeds of blood, the harvest of the Church sprang up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:88
verses.text: Safely then let the clouds go forth: let them diffuse Thy truth in circuit of Thee, let them not fear the savage waves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:89
verses.text: "Thou rulest the power of the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:90
verses.text: The sea swells, buffets, and roars: but "God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted beyond what ye are able:"  and so, "Thou stillest the waves thereof when they rise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:91
verses.text: Lastly, what hast Thou done in the sea itself, to pacify its rage, and to weaken it? "Thou hast humbled the proud as one that is wounded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:92
verses.text: There is a certain proud serpent in the sea, of which another passage of Scripture speaks, "I will command the serpent, and he shall bite him;" and again, "There is that Leviathan, whom Thou hast made to mock him," whose head He bruises above the water.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:93
verses.text: "Thou," he says, "hast humbled the proud, as one that is wounded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:94
verses.text: Thou hast humbled Thyself, and the proud was humbled: for the proud held the proud ones through pride: but the great One is humbled, and by believing in Him become small.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:95
verses.text: While the little one is nourished by the example of One who from greatness descended to humility, the devil has lost what he held: because the proud held only the proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:96
verses.text: When such an example of humility was displayed before them, men learned to condemn their own pride, and to imitate the humility of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:97
verses.text: Thus also the devil, by losing those whom he had in his power, has even himself been humbled; not chastened, but thrown prostrate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:98
verses.text: "Thou hast humbled the proud like one that is wounded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:99
verses.text: Thou hast been humbled, and hast humbled others: Thou hast been wounded, and hast wounded others: for Thy blood, as it was shed to blot the handwriting of sins,  could not but wound him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:100
verses.text: For what was the ground of his pride, except the bond which he held against us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:101
verses.text: This bond, this handwriting, Thou hast blotted out with Thy blood: him therefore hast Thou wounded, from whom Thou hast rescued so many victims.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:102
verses.text: You must understand the devil wounded, not by the piercing of the flesh, which he has not, but by the bruising of his proud heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:103
verses.text: "Thou hast scattered Thine enemies abroad with Thy mighty arm".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:104
verses.text: "The heavens are thine, the earth also is Thine".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:105
verses.text: From Thee, over Thy earth they rain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:106
verses.text: Thine are the heavens, by whom is preached Thy truth in circuit of Thee; "Thine is the earth," which has received Thy truth in circuit of Thee; and what has resulted from that rain? "Thou hast laid the foundation of the round world, and all that therein is".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:107
verses.text: "Thou hast created the north and the seas".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:108
verses.text: For nothing has any power against Thee, against its Creator.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:109
verses.text: The world indeed may rage through its own malice, and the perversity of its will; does it nevertheless pass over the bound laid down by the Creator, who made all things? Why then do I fear the north wind? Why do I fear the seas? In the north indeed is the devil, who said, "I will sit in the sides of the north; I will be like the Most High;" but Thou hast humbled, as one wounded, the proud one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:110
verses.text: Thus what Thou hast done in them has more force for Thy dominion, than their own will has for their wickedness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:111
verses.text: "Thou hast created the north and the seas".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:112
verses.text: "Thabor and Hermon shall rejoice in Thy name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:113
verses.text: Those mountains are here understood, but they have a meaning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:114
verses.text: "Thabor and Hermon shall rejoice in Thy name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:115
verses.text: Thabor, when interpreted, signifies an approaching light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:116
verses.text: But whence comes the light of which it is said, "Ye are the light of the world," unless from Him concerning whom it is written, "That was the true light, which lighteth every man coming into the world"? The light then which is the light of the world comes from that light which is not kindled from any other source, so that there is no fear lest it be extinguished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:117
verses.text: The light then comes from Him, who is that candle which is not set beneath the bushel, but on a candlestick, Thabor the coming light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:118
verses.text: Hermon means his curse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:119
verses.text: Justly the light comes and is made the curse of him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:120
verses.text: Of whom but the devil, the wounded one, the proud one? Our illumination then is given from Thee; that he is held accursed of us, who kept us in his own error and pride, is from Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:121
verses.text: "Thabor and Hermon, therefore, shall rejoice," not in their own merits, "but in Thy name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:122
verses.text: For they shall say, "Not unto us, Lord, not unto us, but to Thy name give the praise," on account of the raging sea: lest "the heathen say, Where is now their God?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:123
verses.text: "Thou hast a mighty arm".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:124
verses.text: Let no man arrogate anything to himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:125
verses.text: "Thou hast a mighty arm:" by Thee we were created, by Thee we have been defended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:126
verses.text: "Thou hast a mighty arm: strong be Thy hand, and high be Thy right hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:127
verses.text: "Righteousness and judgment are the preparation of Thy seat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:128
verses.text: Thy righteousness and judgment will appear in the end: they are now hidden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:129
verses.text: Of Thy righteousness it is treated in another Psalm, "on the hidden things of the Son".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:130
verses.text: There will then be a manifestation of Thy righteousness and judgment: some will be set on the right, others on the left hand: and the unbelieving will tremble, when they see what now they mock at, and believe not: the righteous will rejoice, when they shall see what they now see not, yet believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:131
verses.text: "Righteousness and judgment are the preparation of Thy seat:" especially in the Day of Judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:132
verses.text: What then now? "mercy and truth go before Thy face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:133
verses.text: I should fear the preparation of Thy seat, Thy justice, and Thy coming judgment, did not mercy and truth go before Thee: why should I at the end fear Thy righteousness, when with Thy mercy going before Thee Thou blottest out my sins, and by showing forth Thy truth fulfillest Thy promises? "Mercy and truth go before Thy face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:134
verses.text: For "all the paths of the Lord are mercy and truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:135
verses.text: In all these things shall we not rejoice? or shall we contain our joy? or shall words suffice for our gladness? or shall the tongue be able to express our rejoicing? If therefore no words suffice, "Blessed is the people, O Lord, that knoweth glad shouting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:136
verses.text: O blessed people! dost thou conceive aright, dost thou understand, glad shouting? For except thou understand glad shouting, thou canst not be blessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:137
verses.text: What do I mean by understanding glad shouting? Whether thou knowest the source of that rejoicing which is beyond words to express.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:138
verses.text: For this joy is not of thyself, since "he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:139
verses.text: Rejoice not then in thy own pride, but in God's grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:140
verses.text: See that that grace is such, that the tongue fails to express its greatness, and then thou understandest glad shouting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:141
verses.text: O Lord, "they shall walk in the light of Thy countenance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:142
verses.text: "They shall rejoice in Thy name all the day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:143
verses.text: That Thabor and Hermon shall rejoice in Thy name: all day shall they rejoice, if they will, in Thy name; but if they will rejoice in their own name, they shall not rejoice all day: for they shall not continue in their joy, when they shall delight in themselves, and fall through pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:144
verses.text: That they may rejoice all day, therefore, "they shall rejoice in Thy name, and in Thy righteousness shall they be exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:145
verses.text: Not in their own, but in Thine: lest they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:146
verses.text: For some are noted by the Apostle, that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge, "being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own," and not rejoicing in Thy light, and thus "not submitting themselves unto the righteousness of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:147
verses.text: And why? because "they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:148
verses.text: But the people who knoweth glad shouting (for the former err from want of knowledge, but blessed is the people not that knoweth not, but that knoweth glad shouting), whence ought it to shout, whence to rejoice, but in Thy name, walking in the light of Thy countenance? And it shall deserve to be exalted, but in Thy righteousness: let every man take away altogether his own righteousness, and be trembled: the righteousness of God shall come, and he shall be exalted, "and in Thy righteousness shall they be exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:149
verses.text: "For Thou art the glory of their strength: and in Thy good pleasure Thou shalt lift up our horns" : because it has seemed good to Thee, not because we are worthy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:150
verses.text: "For of the Lord is our taking up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:151
verses.text: For I was moved like a heap of sand, that I might fall; and I should have fallen, had not the Lord taken me up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:152
verses.text: "For of the Lord is (our) taking up: and of the Holy One of Israel our King".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:153
verses.text: Himself is thy taking up, Himself thy illumination: in His light thou art safe, in His light thou walkest, in His righteousness thou art exalted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:154
verses.text: He took thee up, He guards thy weakness: He gives thee strength of Himself, not of thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:155
verses.text: "Thou spakest sometime in vision unto Thy sons, and saidst".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:156
verses.text: Thou spakest in thy vision.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:157
verses.text: Thou didst reveal this to Thy Prophets.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:158
verses.text: For this reason Thou spakest in vision, that is, in revelation: whence Prophets were called seers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:159
verses.text: They saw something within, which they were to speak without: and secretly they heard what they preached openly Then "Thou spakest in vision unto Thy sons, and saidst, I have laid help upon One that is mighty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:160
verses.text: Ye understand Who is meant by mighty? "I have exalted One chosen out of the people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:161
verses.text: And Who is meant by chosen? One who, ye rejoice, is already exalted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:162
verses.text: "I have found David My servant:" that David from David's seed: "with My holy oil have I anointed Him" : for it is said of Him, "God, even Thy God, hath anointed Thee with the oil of gladness above Thy fellows".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:163
verses.text: "My hand shall hold Him fast, and My arm shall strengthen Him" : because there was a taking up of man; because flesh was assumed in the Virgin's womb, because by Him who in the form of God is coequal with the Father, the form of a servant was taken, and He became obedient unto death, even the death of the Cross.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:164
verses.text: "The enemy shall not be able to do him violence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:165
verses.text: The enemy rages indeed but he shall not be able to do Him violence: he is wont to hurt, but he shall not hurt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:166
verses.text: How then shall he afflict Him? he will exercise Him, but he shall not hurt Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:167
verses.text: There shall be profit in his raging; for those against whom he rages shall be crowned in their conquering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:168
verses.text: For how is he conquered, if he rages not against us? or where is God our helper, if we fight not? The enemy therefore shall do what is in his power; but "he shall not be able to do Him violence: the son of wickedness shall not come nigh to hurt Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:169
verses.text: "I will cut in pieces His enemies before His face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:170
verses.text: They are cut in pieces from their conspiracy, and in that they believe they are cut in pieces; for they believe by degrees; as when the calf's head was ground small, they will come to be the drink of God's people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:171
verses.text: For Moses ground down the calf's head, and sprinkled it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink it All the unbelieving are ground: they believe by degrees; and they are drunk by the people of God, and pass into Christ's body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:172
verses.text: "I will cut in pieces His foes before His face: and put to flight them that hate Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:173
verses.text: "My truth also and My mercy is with Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:174
verses.text: All the paths of the Lord are mercy and truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:175
verses.text: Remember, as much as ye can, how often these two attributes are urged upon us, that we render them back to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:176
verses.text: For as He showed us mercy that He might blot out our sins, and truth in fulfilling His promises; so also we, walking in His path, ought to give back to Him mercy and truth; mercy, in pitying the wretched; truth, in not judging unjustly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:177
verses.text: Let not truth rob you of mercy, nor mercy hinder truth: for if through mercy you shall have judged contrary to truth, or by rigorous truth shall have forgotten mercy, you will not be walking in the path of God, where "mercy and truth meet together".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:178
verses.text: "And in My name shall His horn be exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:179
verses.text: Why should I say more? Ye are Christians, recognise Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:180
verses.text: "I will set His hand also in the sea" : that is, He shall rule over the Gentiles; "and His right hand in the floods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:181
verses.text: Rivers run into the sea: avaricious men roll onwards into the bitterness of this world: yet all these kinds of men will be subject to Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:182
verses.text: "He shall call me, Thou art My Father, and the lifter up of My salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:183
verses.text: "And I will make Him my first-born; higher than the kings of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:184
verses.text: Our Martyrs, whose birthdays we are celebrating, shed their blood on account of these things, which were believed though not yet seen; how much more brave ought we to be, as we see what they believed? For they had not yet seen Christ raised on high among the kings of the earth: as yet princes  were taking counsel together against the Lord and His Anointed: what follows in the same Psalm was not then fulfilled, "Be wise now therefore, O ye kings: be learned, ye that are judges of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:185
verses.text: Now indeed Christ has been exalted among the kings of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:186
verses.text: "My mercy will I keep for Him for ever: and my Testament faithful with Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:187
verses.text: On His account, the Testament is faithful: in Him the Testament is mediated: He is the Sealer, the Mediator of the Testament, the Surety of the Testament, the Witness of the Testament, the Heritage of the Testament, the Coheir of the Testament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:188
verses.text: "His seed will I make to endure world without end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:189
verses.text: Not only for this world, but unto the world without end: whither His seed, which is His heritage, the seed of Abraham, which is Christ, will pass But if ye are Christ's, ye are also Abraham's seed: and if ye are destined His heirs for ever, "He will establish His seed unto world without end: and His throne as the days of Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:190
verses.text: The thrones of earthly kings are as the days of the earth: different are the days of Heaven from those of earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:191
verses.text: The days of Heaven are those years of which it is said, "Thou art the same, and Thy years shall not fail".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:192
verses.text: The days of the earth are soon overtaken by their successors: those which precede are shut out from us: nor do those which succeed remain: but they come that they may go, and are almost gone before they are come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:193
verses.text: Such are the days of earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:194
verses.text: But the days of Heaven, which are also the "One day" of Heaven, and the never failing years, have neither beginning nor end: nor is any day there narrowed between yesterday and to-morrow: no one there expects the future, nor loses the past: but the days of Heaven are always present, where His throne shall be for ever and ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:195
verses.text: This is a strong pledge of the promise of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:196
verses.text: The sons of this David are the children of the Bridegroom; all Christians therefore are called His sons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:197
verses.text: But it is much indeed that God promises, that if Christians, that is, "If his children forsake My law, and walk not in My judgments" ; "if they profane My statutes, and keep not My commandments" ; I will not spurn them, nor will I send them away from Me in perdition: but what will I do? "I will visit their offences with the rod, and their sin with scourges".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:198
verses.text: It is not the mercy of one that calls them only; but also that chastises and scourges them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:199
verses.text: Let therefore thy Father's hand be upon thee, and if thou art a good son, repel not chastening; for "what son is there, to whom his father giveth not chastening?" Let Him chasten him, so long as He takes not from him His mercy: let Him beat him when obstinate, as long as He does not disinherit him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:200
verses.text: If thou hast well understood the promises of thy Father, fear not to be scourged, but to be disinherited: "for whom the Lord loveth He chasteneth: and scourgeth every son whom He receiveth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:201
verses.text: Does the sinful son spurn chastening, when he sees the only Son without sin scourged? "I will visit their offences with the rod".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:202
verses.text: Thus too the Apostle threatens: "What will ye? shall I come unto you with a rod?" Let not pious sons say, if Thou art coming with a rod, come not at all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:203
verses.text: For it is better to be taught with the Father's rod, than to perish in the caresses of the robber.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:204
verses.text: "Nevertheless, My mercy will I not utterly take from Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:205
verses.text: From whom? From that David to whom I gave these promises, whom "I anointed with my holy oil of gladness above His fellows".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:206
verses.text: Do you recognise Him from whom God will not utterly take away His mercy? That no one may anxiously say, since He speaks of Christ as Him from whom He will not take away His mercy, What then will become of the sinner? Did He say anything like this, "I will not take My loving-kindness utterly from them"? "I will visit," He saith, "their offences with the rod, and their sin with scourges".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:207
verses.text: Thou didst expect for thy own security, "I will not utterly take my loving-kindness from" them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:208
verses.text: And indeed this is the reading of some books, but not of the most accurate: though, where they have it, it is a reading by no means inconsistent with the real meaning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:209
verses.text: For how can it be said that He will not utterly take His mercy from Christ? Has the Saviour of the body committed aught of sin either in Heaven or in earth, "who sitteth even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us"? Yet it is from Christ: but from His members, His body which is the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:210
verses.text: For in this sense He speaks of it as a great thing that He will not take away His mercies from Him, supposing us not to recognise the only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father; for there the Man is not counted for His Person, but the One Person is God and Man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:211
verses.text: He therefore does not utterly take His mercies from Him, when He takes not His mercy from His body, His members, in which, even while He was enthroned in Heaven, He was still suffering persecutions on earth; and when He cried from Heaven, "Saul, Saul," not why persecutest thou My servants, nor why persecutest thou My saints, nor My disciples, but, "why persecutest thou Me?" As then, while no one persecuted Him when sitting in Heaven, He cried out, "Why persecutest thou Me?" when the Head recognised its limbs, and His love allowed not the Head to separate Himself from the union of the body: so, when He taketh not away His mercies from Him, it is surely that He taketh it not from us, who are His limbs and body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:212
verses.text: Yet ought we not on that account to sin not without apprehension, and perversely to assure ourselves that we shall not perish, be our actions what they may.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:213
verses.text: For there are certain sins and certain offences, to define and discourse of which it is either impossible for me, or if it were possible, it would be too tedious for the time we have at present.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:214
verses.text: For no man can say that he is without sin; for if he says so, he will lie; "if we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:215
verses.text: Each one therefore is needfully scourged for his own sins; but the mercy of God is not taken away from him, if he be a Christian.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:216
verses.text: Certainly if thou committest such offences as to repel the hand of Him who chasteneth, the rod of Him who scourgeth thee, and art angry at the correction of God, and fliest from thy Father when He chasteneth thee, and wilt not suffer Him to be thy Father, because He spares thee not when thou dost sin; thou hast estranged thyself from thy heritage, He has not thrown thee off; for if thou wouldest abide being scourged, thou wouldest not abide disinherited.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:217
verses.text: "Nor will I do hurt in My truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:218
verses.text: For His mercy in setting free shall not be taken away, lest His truth in taking vengeance do harm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:219
verses.text: "My covenant will I not profane, nor reject the thing that is gone out of my lips".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:220
verses.text: Because his sons sin, I will not on this account be found false: I have promised; I will do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:221
verses.text: Suppose they choose to sin even as past hope, and so fall into sins as to offend their Father's countenance, and deserve to be disinherited; is it not still God Himself, of whom it is said, "From these stones" He "will raise up sons to Abraham"? Therefore I tell you, brethren, many Christians sin venially, many are scourged and so corrected for their sin, chastened, and cured; many turn away altogether, striving with a stiff neck against the discipline of the Father, even wholly refusing God as their Father, though they have the mark of Christ, and so fall into such sins, that it can only be announced against them, "that they who do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:222
verses.text: Nevertheless, Christ shall not be destitute of an inheritance on their account: not for the chaff's sake shall the wheat also perish: nor on account of bad fish shall nothing be cast into the vessels from that net "The Lord knows them that are His".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:223
verses.text: For He who predestined us before we were born, promised undoubtingly: "For whom He did predestinate, them He also called: and whom He called, them He also justified: and whom He justified, them He also glorified".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:224
verses.text: Let desperate sinners sin as far as they choose: let the members of Christ reply, "If God is with us, who shall be against us?" God will not therefore do hurt in His truth, nor will He "profane His Testament".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:225
verses.text: His Testament remains immovable, because in His foreknowledge He predestined His heirs; and "He will not reject the thing that is gone out of His lips".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:226
verses.text: Listen for thy confirmation in hope, for thy security, if thou knowest thyself to be among the members of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:227
verses.text: "I have sworn once by My holiness that I will not lie unto David".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:228
verses.text: Dost thou wait till God swear a second time? How often is He to swear, if in one oath He is false? One oath He made for our life, who sent His Only One to die for us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:229
verses.text: "I have sworn once by My holiness, that I will not lie unto David".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:230
verses.text: "His seed shall endure for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:231
verses.text: His seed endures for ever; because the Lord knows them that are His.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:232
verses.text: "And His seat is like as the sun before me:" "and as the moon perfect for evermore: and the faithful witness in heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:233
verses.text: They are His seat, in whom He sits and reigns.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:234
verses.text: But if His seat, His members also; because even our members are the seat of our head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:235
verses.text: See how all our other members sustain our head: but the head supports nothing above itself, but is itself supported by the rest of our limbs, as if the whole body of a man were the seat of his head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:236
verses.text: His seat, therefore, all in whom God reigns, "shall be like as the sun before Me," He saith: because the righteous in the kingdom of My Father "shall shine like the sun".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:237
verses.text: But the sun is meant in a spiritual, not a bodily sense, as that which shines from Heaven, which He maketh to rise upon the just and unjust Finally, that sun is not before men's eyes only, but even those of cattle and the smallest insects; for which of the vilest animals sees not that sun? What does he say to distinguish the sun meant here? "Like as the sun before Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:238
verses.text: Not before men, before the flesh, before mortal animals, but "before Me, and as the moon".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:239
verses.text: But what moon? one "that is perfect for evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:240
verses.text: For although that moon which we know becomes perfect, the next day she begins to wane, after her orb is full.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:241
verses.text: "He shall be as the moon perfect for evermore," He saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:242
verses.text: His seat shall be made perfect as the moon, but that moon is one which will be perfect for evermore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:243
verses.text: If as the sun, why also as the moon? the Scriptures usually signify by the moon the mortality of this flesh, because of its increasings and decreasings, because of its transitory nature.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 89:244
