verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:84
verses.text: Many such at that period, who had distributed their all to the poor, and already promised themselves a seat beside Christ in judgment of the nations, failed amid their torments under the blazing fire of persecution, as before the demon of the noon-day, and denied Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:85
verses.text: These are they who have fallen "beside" Him: when about to sit with Christ for the judgment of the world, they fell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:86
verses.text: I will now explain who are they who fall on the right hand of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:87
verses.text: And because many have fallen from that hope of being judges, but yet many, many more from that of being on His right hand, the Psalmist thus addresses Christ, "A thousand shall fall beside Thee, and ten thousand at Thy right hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:88
verses.text: And since there shall be many, who regarded not all these things, with whom, as it were with His own limbs, Christ is one, he adds, "But it shall not come nigh Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:89
verses.text: Were these words addressed to the Head alone? Surely not; surely neither (doth it come nigh) to Paul, nor Peter, nor all the Apostles, nor all the Martyrs, who failed not in their torments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:90
verses.text: What then do the words, "it shall not come nigh," mean? Why were they thus tortured? The torture came nigh the flesh, but it did not reach the region of faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:91
verses.text: Their faith then was far beyond the reach of the terrors threatened by their torturers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:92
verses.text: Let them torture, terror will not come nigh; let them torture, but they will mock the torture, putting their trust in Him who conquered before them, that the rest might conquer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:93
verses.text: And who conquer, except they who trust not in themselves?Who will not fear? He who trusts not in himself, but in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:94
verses.text: But those who trust in themselves, although they even hope to judge at the side of Christ, although they hoped they should be at His right hand, as if He said to them, "Come, ye blessed of My Father," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:95
verses.text: ; yet the devil that is at noon overtook them, the raging heat of persecution, terrifying with violence; and many fell from the hope of the seat of judgment, of whom it is said, "A thousand shall fall beside thee;" many too fell from the hope of reward for their duties, of whom it was said, "And ten thousand at thy right hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:96
verses.text: But this downfall and devil that is at noon-day "shall not come nigh thee," that is, the Head and the body; for the Lord knows who are His.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:97
verses.text: "Nevertheless, with thine eyes shalt thou behold, and see the reward of the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:98
verses.text: What is this? Why "nevertheless"? Because the wicked were allowed to tyrannize over Thy servants, and to persecute them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:99
verses.text: Will they then have been allowed to persecute Thy servants with impunity? Not with impunity, for although Thou hast permitted them, and Thine own have thence received a brighter crown, "nevertheless," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:100
verses.text: For the evil which they willed, not the good they unconsciously were the agents of, will be recompensed them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:101
verses.text: All that is wanting is the eye of faith, by which we may see that they are raised for a time only, while they shall mourn for evermore; and to those into whose hands is given temporal power over the servants of God, it shall be said, "Depart into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:102
verses.text: But if every man have but eyes in the sense in which it is said, "With thine eyes shalt thou behold," it is no unimportant thing to look upon the wicked flourishing in this life, and to have an eye to him, to consider what will become of him in the end, if he fail to reform his ways: for those who now would thunder upon others, will afterwards feel the thunderbolt themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:103
verses.text: "For Thou, Lord, art my hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:104
verses.text: He has now come to the power Which rescues him from falling by the "downfall and the devil of the noon-day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:105
verses.text: "For Thou, Lord, art my hope: Thou hast set Thy house of defence very high".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:106
verses.text: What do the words "very high" mean? For many make their house of defence in God a mere refuge from temporal persecution; but the defence of God is on high, and very secret, whither thou mayest fly from the wrath to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:107
verses.text: Within "Thou hast set thine house of defence very high.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:108
verses.text: There shall no evil happen unto Thee: neither shall any plague come nigh Thy dwelling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:109
verses.text: The Holy City is not the Church of this country only, but of the whole world as well: not that of this age only, but from Abel himself down to those who shall to the end be born and believe in Christ, the whole assembly of the Saints, belonging to one city; which city is Christ's body, of which Christ is the Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:110
verses.text: There, too, dwell the Angels, who are our fellow-citizens: we toil, because we are as yet pilgrims: while they within that city are awaiting our arrival.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:111
verses.text: Letters have reached us too from that city, apart from which we are wandering: those letters are the Scriptures, which exhort us to live well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:112
verses.text: Why do I speak of letters only? The King himself descended, and became a path to us in our wanderings: that walking in Him, we may neither stray, nor faint nor fall among robbers, nor be caught in the snares that are set near our path.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:113
verses.text: This character, then, we recognise in the whole Person of Christ, together with the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:114
verses.text: He Himself is our Head, He is God, co-equal with the Father, the Word of God, by whom all things were made: but God to create, Man to renew; God to make, Man to restore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:115
verses.text: Looking upon Him, then, let us hear the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:116
verses.text: Listen, beloved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:117
verses.text: This  is the teaching and doctrine of this school, which may enable you to understand, not this Psalm only, but many, if ye keep in mind this rule.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:118
verses.text: Sometimes a Psalm, and all prophecy as well, in speaking of Christ, praises the Head alone, and sometimes from the Head goes to the Body, that is, the Church, and without apparently changing the Person spoken of: because the Head is not separate from the Body, and both are spoken of as one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:119
verses.text: What then, my brethren, what is said of our Head? "For Thou, Lord, art my hope," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:120
verses.text: Of this we have spoken, "for He hath given His angels charge over Thee, to keep Thee in all Thy ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:121
verses.text: You heard these words but now, when the Gospel was being read; attend therefore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:122
verses.text: Our Lord, after He was baptized, fasted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:123
verses.text: Why was He baptized? That we might not scorn to be baptized.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:124
verses.text: For when John said to our Lord, "Comest Thou to me to be baptized? I ought to be baptized by Thee;" and our Lord replied, "Suffer it to be so now, for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness;" He wished to fulfil all humility, so that He should be washed, who had no defilement.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:125
verses.text: Our Lord, then, was baptized, and after baptism He was tempted; He fasted forty days, a number which has, as I have often mentioned, a deep meaning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:126
verses.text: All things cannot be explained at once, lest needful time be too much taken up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:127
verses.text: After forty days He was an hungred.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:128
verses.text: He could have fasted without ever feeling hunger; but then how could He be tempted? or had He not overcome the tempter, how couldest thou learn to struggle with him? He was hungry; and then the tempter said, "If Thou be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:129
verses.text: Was it a great thing for our Lord Jesus Christ to make bread out of stones, when He satisfied so many thousands with five loaves? He made bread out of nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:130
verses.text: For whence came that quantity of food, which could satisfy so many thousands? The sources of that bread are in the Lord's hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:131
verses.text: This is nothing wonderful; for He Himself made out of five loaves bread enough for so many thousands, who also every day out of a few seeds raises up on earth immense harvests.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:132
verses.text: These are the miracles of our Lord: but from their constant operation they are disregarded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:133
verses.text: What then, my brethren, was it impossible for the Lord to create bread out of stones? He made men even out of stones, in the words of John the Baptist himself, "God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:134
verses.text: Why then did He not so? That he might teach thee how to answer the tempter, so that if thou wast reduced to any straits and the tempter suggested, if thou wast a Christian and belongedst to Christ, would He desert thee now?Listen to our Lord: "Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:135
verses.text: Dost thou think the word of God bread? If the Word of God, through which all things were made, was not bread, He would not say, "I am the bread which came down from heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:136
verses.text: Thou hast therefore learnt to answer the tempter, when pressed with hunger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:137
verses.text: What if he tempt thee in these words: If thou wast a Christian, thou wouldest do miracles, as many Christians have done? Thou, deceived by a wicked suggestion, wouldest tempt the Lord thy God, so as to say to Him, If I am a Christian, and am before Thine eyes, and Thou dost account me at all in the number of Thine own, let me also do something like the many works which Thy Saints have done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:138
verses.text: Thou hast tempted God, as if thou wert not a Christian, unless thou didst this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:139
verses.text: Many who desired such things have fallen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:140
verses.text: For that Simon the sorcerer desired such gifts of the Apostles, when he wished to buy the Holy Spirit for money He loved the power of working miracles, but loved not the imitation of humility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:141
verses.text: What then, if he tempt thee thus, "work miracles"? that thou mayest not tempt God, what shouldest thou answer? What our Lord answered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:142
verses.text: The devil said to Him, "Cast Thyself down; for it is written, He shall give His Angels charge concerning Thee," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:143
verses.text: If Thou shalt cast Thyself down, Angels shall receive Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:144
verses.text: And it might indeed, my brethren, happen, if our Lord had cast Himself down, the attending Angels would receive our Lord's flesh; but what does He say to him? "It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:145
verses.text: Thou thinkest Me a man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:146
verses.text: For the devil came to Him with this view, that he might try whether He were the Son of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:147
verses.text: He saw His Flesh; but His might appeared in His works: the Angels had borne witness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:148
verses.text: He saw that He was mortal, so that he might tempt Him, that by Christ's temptation the Christian might be taught.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:149
verses.text: What then is written? "Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:150
verses.text: Let us not then tempt the Lord, so as to say, If we belong to Thee, let us work a miracle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:151
verses.text: Let us return to the words of the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:152
verses.text: "They shall bear Thee in their hands, lest at any time Thou hurt Thy foot against a stone".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:153
verses.text: Christ was raised up in the hands of Angels, when He was taken up into heaven: not that, if Angels had not sustained Him, He would have fallen: but because they were attending on their King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:154
verses.text: Say not, Those who sustained Him are better than He who was sustained.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:155
verses.text: Are then cattle better than men, because they sustain the weakness of men? And we ought not to speak thus either; for if the cattle withdraw their support, their riders fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:156
verses.text: But how ought we to speak of it? For it is said even of God, "Heaven is My throne".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:157
verses.text: Because then he aven supports Him, and God sits thereon, is therefore heaven the better? Thus also in this Psalm we may understand it of the service of the Angels: it does not pertain to any infirmity in our Lord, but to the honour they pay, and to their service.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:158
verses.text: What the finger of God is, the Gospel explaineth to us; for the finger of God is the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:159
verses.text: How do we prove this? Our Lord, when answering those who accused Him of casting out devils in the name of Beelzebub, saith, "If I cast out devils by the Spirit of God;" and another Evangelist, in relating the same saying, saith, "If I with the finger of God cast out devils".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:160
verses.text: What therefore is in one stated clearly, is darkly expressed in another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:161
verses.text: Thou didst not know what was the finger of God, but another Evangelist explains it by terming it the Spirit of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:162
verses.text: The Law then written by the finger of God was given on the fiftieth day after the slaughter of the lamb, and the Holy Ghost descended on the fiftieth day after the Passion of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:163
verses.text: The Lamb was slain, the Passover was celebrated, the fifty days were completed, and the Law was given.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:164
verses.text: But that Law was to cause fear, not love: but that fear might be changed into love, He who was truly righteous was slain: of whom that lamb whom the Jews were slaying was the type.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:165
verses.text: He arose from the dead: and from the day of our Lord's Passover, as from that of the slaying of the Paschal lamb, fifty days are counted; and the Holy Ghost descended, now in the fulness of love, not in the punishment of fear Why have I said this? For this then our Lord arose, and was glorified, that He might send His Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:166
verses.text: And I said long ago that this was so, because His head is in heaven, His feet on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:167
verses.text: If His head is in heaven, His feet on earth; what means our Lord's feet on earth? Our Lord's saints on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:168
verses.text: Who are our Lord's feet? The Apostles sent throughout the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:169
verses.text: Who are our Lord's feet? All the Evangelists, in whom our Lord travelleth over all nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:170
verses.text: We need not therefore wonder that our Lord was raised up to heaven by the hands of Angels, that His foot might not dash against a stone: lest those who on earth toiled in His body, while they were travelling over the whole world might become guilty of the Law, He took from them fear, and filled them with love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:171
verses.text: Through fear Peter thrice denied Him, for he had not yet received the Holy Ghost: afterwards, when he had received the Holy Spirit, he began to preach with confidence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:172
verses.text: Our Lord so dealt with him, as if He said, thrice thou hast denied Me through fear: thrice confess Me through love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:173
verses.text: With that love and that charity He filled His disciples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:174
verses.text: Why? Because He hath set His house of defence very high: because when glorified He sent the Holy Ghost, He released the faithful from the guilt of the Law, that His feet might not dash against a stone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:175
verses.text: "Thou shalt go upon the asp and the basilisk; the lion and the dragon shalt thou tread under thy feet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:176
verses.text: Ye know who the serpent is, and how the Church treadeth upon him, as she is not conquered, because she is on her guard against his cunning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:177
verses.text: And after what manner he is a lion and a dragon, I believe you know also, beloved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:178
verses.text: The lion openly rages, the dragon lies secretly in covert: the devil hath each of these forces and powers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:179
verses.text: When the Martyrs were being slain, it was the raging lion: when heretics are plotting, it is the dragon creeping beneath us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:180
verses.text: Thou hast conquered the lion; conquer also the dragon: the lion hath not crushed thee, let not the dragon deceive thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:181
verses.text: A few women in the Church have bodily virginity: but the virginity of the heart all the faithful have.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:182
verses.text: In the very matter of faith he feared that the heart's virginity would be corrupted by the devil: and those who have lost it, are uselessly virgins in their bodies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:183
verses.text: What does a woman who is corrupt in heart preserve in her body? Thus a Catholic married woman is before a virgin heretic.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:184
verses.text: For the first is not indeed a virgin in her body, but the second has become married in her heart; and married not unto God as her husband, but unto the dragon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:185
verses.text: But what shall the Church do? The basilisk is the king of serpents, as the devil is the king of wicked spirits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:186
verses.text: These are the words of God to the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:187
verses.text: "Because he hath set his love in me, therefore will I deliver him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:188
verses.text: Not only therefore the Head, which now sits in heaven, because He hath set His house of defence very high, to which no evil shall happen, neither shall any plague come nigh His dwelling; but we also who are toiling on earth, and are still living in temptations, whose steps are feared for, lest they fall into snares, may hear the voice of the Lord our God consoling us, and saying to us, "Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him: I will set him up, because he hath known my name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:189
verses.text: "He shall call upon me, and I will hear him: yea, I am with him in trouble".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:190
verses.text: Fear not when thou art in trouble, as if the Lord were not with thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:191
verses.text: Let faith be with thee, and God is with thee in thy trouble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:192
verses.text: There are waves on the sea, and thou art tossed in thy bark, because Christ sleepeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:193
verses.text: Christ slept in the ship, while the men were perishing If thy faith sleep in thy heart, Christ is as it were sleeping in thy ship: because Christ dwelleth in thee through faith, when thou beginnest to be tossed, awake Christ sleeping: rouse up thy faith, and thou shalt be assured that He deserts thee not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:194
verses.text: But thou thinkest thou art forsaken, because He rescueth thee not when thou thyself dost wish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:195
verses.text: He delivered the Three Children from the fire? Did He, who did this, desert the Maccabees? God forbid! He delivered both of these: the first bodily, that the faithless might be confounded; the last spiritually, that the faithful might imitate them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:196
verses.text: "I will deliver him, and bring him to honour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:197
verses.text: "With length of days will I satisfy him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:198
verses.text: What is length of days? Eternal life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:199
verses.text: Brethren, imagine not that length of days is spoken of in the same sense as days are said to be long in summer, short in winter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:200
verses.text: Hath he such days to give us? That length is one that hath no end, eternal life, that is promised us in long days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:201
verses.text: And truly, since this sufficeth, with reason he saith, "will I satisfy him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:202
verses.text: What is long in time, if it hath an end, satisfieth us not: for that reason it should not be even called long.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:203
verses.text: And if we are covetous, we ought to be covetous of eternal life: long for such a life, as hath no end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:204
verses.text: Lo, a line in which our covetousness may be extended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:205
verses.text: Dost thou wish money without limit? Long for eternal life without limit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:206
verses.text: Dost thou wish that thy possession may have no end? Seek for eternal life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:207
verses.text: "I will show him my salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:208
verses.text: Nor is this, my brethren, to be briefly passed over.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:209
verses.text: "I will show him my salvation:" He means, I will show him Christ Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:210
verses.text: Why? Was He not seen on earth? What great thing hath He to show us? But He did not appear such as we shall see Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:211
verses.text: He appeared in that shape in which those who saw Him crucified Him: behold, those who saw Him, crucified Him: we have not seen Him, yet we have believed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:212
verses.text: They had eyes, have not we? yea, we too have the eyes of the heart: but, as yet we see through faith, not by sight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:213
verses.text: When will it be sight? When shall we, as the Apostle saith, see Him "face to face"? which God promiseth us as the high reward of all our toils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:214
verses.text: Whatever thou toilest in, thou toilest for this purpose, that thou mayest see Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:215
verses.text: Some great thing it is we are to see, since all our reward is seeing; and our Lord Jesus Christ is that very great sight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:216
verses.text: He who appeared humble, will Himself appear great, and will rejoice us, as He is even now seen of His Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:217
verses.text: Let us love and imitate Him: let us run after his ointments, as is said in the Song of Solomon: "Because of the savour of thy good ointments, we will run after thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:218
verses.text: For He came, and gave forth a savour that filled the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:219
verses.text: Whence was that fragrance? From heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:220
verses.text: Follow then towards heaven, if thou do not answer falsely when it is said, "Lift up your hearts," lift up your thoughts, your love, your hope: that it may not rot upon the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 91:221
verses.text: "For wherever thy treasure is, there will be thy heart also".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:1
verses.text: Psalm XCII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:2
verses.text: We are not Christians, except on account of a future life: let no one hope for present blessings, let no one promise himself the happiness of the world, because he is a Christian: but let him use the happiness he hath, as he may, in what manner he may, when he may, as far as he may.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:3
verses.text: When it is present, let him give thanks for the consolation of God: when it is wanting, let him give thanks to the Divine justice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:4
verses.text: Let him always be grateful, never ungrateful: let him be grateful to his Father, who soothes and caresses him: and grateful to his Father when He chasteneth him with the scourge, and teacheth him: for He ever loveth, whether He caress or threaten: and let him say what ye have heard in the Psalm: "It is a good thing to give thanks unto the Lord; and to sing praises unto Thy Name, Thou Most Highest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:5
verses.text: This Psalm is entitled, a Psalm to be sung on the Sabbath day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:6
verses.text: Lo, this day is the Sabbath, which the Jews at this period observe by a kind of bodily rest, languid and luxurious.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:7
verses.text: They abstain from labours, and give themselves up to trifles; and though God ordained the Sabbath, they spend it in actions which God forbids.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:8
verses.text: Our rest is from evil works, theirs from good; for it is better to plough than to dance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:9
verses.text: They abstain from good, but not from trifling, works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:10
verses.text: God proclaims to us a Sabbath.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:11
verses.text: What sort of Sabbath? First consider, where it is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:12
verses.text: It is in the heart, within us; for many are idle with their limbs, while they are disturbed in conscience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:13
verses.text: That very joy in the tranquillity of our hope, is our Sabbath.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:14
verses.text: This is the subject of praise and of song in this Psalm, how a Christian man is in the Sabbath of his own heart, that is, in the quiet, tranquillity, and serenity of his conscience, undisturbed; hence he tells us here, whence men are wont to be disturbed, and he teaches thee to keep Sabbath in thine own heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:15
verses.text: Accuse thyself, and thou receivest indulgence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:16
verses.text: Besides, many do not accuse Satan but their fate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:17
verses.text: My fate led me, saith one when you ask him, why did you do it? why did you sin? he replies, by my evil fate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:18
verses.text: Lest he should say, I did it; he points to God as the source of his sin: with his tongue he blasphemes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:19
verses.text: He saith not this indeed openly as yet, but listen, and see that he saith this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:20
verses.text: You ask of him, what is fate: and he replies, evil stars.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:21
verses.text: You ask, who made, who appointed the stars; he can only answer, God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:22
verses.text: It follows, then, that whether he doth so directly or indirectly, still he accuseth God, and when God punisheth sins, he maketh God the author of his own sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:23
verses.text: It cannot be that God punishes what He hath wrought: He punisheth what thou doest, that He may set free what He hath wrought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:24
verses.text: But sometimes, setting aside everything else, they attack God directly: and when they sin, they say, God willed this; if God had not willed it, I should not have sinned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:25
verses.text: Does He warn thee for this, that not only He may not be listened to,  to keep thee from sin, but even be accused because thou dost sin? What then doth this Psalm teach us? "It is a good thing to confess unto the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:26
verses.text: What is to confess unto the Lord? In both cases: both in thy sins, because thou hast done them; and in thy good works, confess unto the Lord, because He hath done them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:27
verses.text: Then shalt thou "sing unto the Name of God, the Most Highest:" seeking the glory of God, not thine own; His Name, not thine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:28
verses.text: For if thou seekest the Name of God, He also seeketh thy name; but if thou hast neglected the Name of God, He also doth blot out thine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:29
verses.text: "To tell of Thy mercy early in the morning, and of Thy truth in the night season".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:30
verses.text: What is the meaning of this; that the mercy of God is to be told us in the morning, and in the night the truth of God? The morning is, when it is well with us; the night, the sadness of tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:31
verses.text: What then did he say in brief? When thou art prosperous, rejoice in God, for it is His mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:32
verses.text: Now, perhaps thou wouldest say, If I rejoice in God, when I am prosperous, because it is His mercy; what am I to do when I am in sorrow, in tribulation? It is His mercy, when I am prosperous; is it then His cruelty, when I am in adversity? If I praise His mercy when it is well with me, am I then to exclaim against His cruelty when it is ill? No.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:33
verses.text: But when it is well, praise His mercy: when ill, praise His truth: because He scourgeth sins, He is not unjust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:34
verses.text: During the night Daniel confessed the truth of God: he said in his prayer, "We have sinned, and committed iniquity, and have done wickedly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:35
verses.text: O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto Thee: but unto us confusion of face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:36
verses.text: He told of the truth of God during the night-season.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:37
verses.text: What is it to tell of the truth of God in the night-season? Not to accuse God, because thou sufferest aught of evil: but to attribute it to thy sins, His correction: to tell of His loving-kindness early in the morning, and of His truth in the night-season.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:38
verses.text: When thou doest this, thou dost always praise God, always confess to God, and sing unto His Name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:39
verses.text: "Upon a psaltery of ten strings, with a song, and upon the harp".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:40
verses.text: Ye have not heard of the psaltery of ten strings for the first time: it signifies the ten commandments of the Law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:41
verses.text: But we must sing upon that psaltery, and not carry it only.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:42
verses.text: For even the Jews have the Law: but they carry it: they sing not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:43
verses.text: "And upon the harp".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:44
verses.text: This means, in word and deed; "with a song," in word; "upon the harp," in work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:45
verses.text: If thou speakest words alone, thou hast, as it were, the song only, and not the harp: if thou workest, and speakest not, thou hast the harp only.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:46
verses.text: On this account both speak well and do well, if thou wouldest have the song together with the harp.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:47
verses.text: "For Thou, Lord, hast made me glad through Thy works; and I will rejoice in giving praise for the operations of Thy hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:48
verses.text: Ye see what he saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:49
verses.text: Thou hast made me living well, Thou hast formed me: if by chance I do aught of good, I will rejoice in the work of Thy hands: as the Apostle saith, "For we are His workmanship, created unto good works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:50
verses.text: For unless He formed thee to good works, thou wouldest not know any works but evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:51
verses.text: Because thou canst not have truth from thy own self, it remains that thou drink it thence, whence it floweth: as if thou hast gone back from the light, thou art in darkness: as a stone glows not with its own heat, but either from the sun or fire, and if thou withdraw it from the heat, it cools: there it appears, that the heat was not its own; for it became heated either by the sun or by fire: thus thou also, if thou withdraw from God, wilt become cold; if thou approach God, thou wilt warm: as the Apostle saith "fervent in spirit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:52
verses.text: Also what saith he of the light? If thou approach Him, thou wilt be in light; therefore saith the Psalm, "Look upon Him, and be lightened; and your faces shall not be ashamed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:53
verses.text: Because therefore thou canst do no good, unless lightened by the light of God, and warmed by the spirit of God; when thou shalt see thyself working well, confess unto God, and say what the Apostle saith; say unto thyself, that thou be not puffed up, "For what hast thou that thou didst not receive?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:54
verses.text: That wretched man who doeth good, and suffereth evils, seeth him, becometh disturbed, and saith, O God, the wicked, I imagine, please Thee, and Thou hatest the good, and lovest those who work iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:55
verses.text: The Sabbath being now lost in the inner man, and the tranquillity of his heart being shut out, and good thoughts repelled, he now beginneth to imitate him whom he seeth flourishing amid his evil deeds; and turneth himself also to evil works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:56
verses.text: But God is long-suffering, because He is eternal, and he knoweth the day of His own judgment, where He weigheth all things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:57
verses.text: Teaching us this, what saith he? "O Lord, how glorious are Thy works: Thy thoughts are made very deep".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:58
verses.text: Verily, my brethren, there is no sea so deep as these thoughts of God, who maketh the wicked flourish, and the good suffer: nothing so profound, nothing so deep: therein every unbelieving soul is wrecked, in that depth, in that profundity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:59
verses.text: Dost thou wish to cross this depth? Remove not from the wood of Christ's Cross: thou shalt not sink: hold thyself fast to Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:60
verses.text: What do I mean by this, hold fast to Christ? It was for this reason that He chose to suffer on earth Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:61
verses.text: Ye have heard, while the prophet was being read, how He "did not turn away His back from the smiters, and His face from the spittings of men," how "He turned not His cheek from their hands;" wherefore chose He to suffer all these things, but that He might console the suffering? He could have raised His flesh at the last day: but then thou wouldest not have had thy ground of hope, since thou hadst not seen Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:62
verses.text: He deferred not His resurrection, that thou mightest not still be in doubt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:63
verses.text: Suffer then tribulation in the world with the same end as that which thou hast observed in Christ: and let not those who do evil, and flourish in this life, move thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:64
verses.text: "Thy thoughts are very deep".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:65
verses.text: Where is the thought of God? Rejoice not as the fish who is exulting in his bait: the fisherman hath not drawn his hook: the fish hath as yet the hook in his jaws.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:66
verses.text: And what seemeth to thee long, is short; all these things pass over quickly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:67
verses.text: What is the long life of man to the eternity of God? Dost thou wish to be of long-suffering? Consider the eternity of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:68
verses.text: For thou regardest thy few days, and in thy few days thou dost wish all things to be fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:69
verses.text: What things? The condemnation of all the wicked: and the crowning of all the good: dost thou wish these things to be fulfilled in thy days? God fulfilleth them in His own time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:70
verses.text: Why dost thou suffer weariness? He is eternal: He waiteth: He is of long-suffering: but thou sayest, I am not of long-suffering, because I am mortal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:71
verses.text: But thou hast it in thy power to become so: join thy heart to the eternity of God, and with Him thou shalt be eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:72
verses.text: For this reason, after saying, "Thy thoughts are very deep," he at once subjoins: "An unwise man doth not well consider this, and a fool doth not understand it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:73
verses.text: What are the things which an unwise man doth not well consider, and which a fool doth not understand? "When the ungodly are green as the grass".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:74
verses.text: What is, "as the grass"? They flourish when it is winter, but they will wither in the summer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:75
verses.text: Thou observest the flower of the grass? What more quickly passeth by? What is brighter? What is greener? Let not its verdure delight thee, but fear its withering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:76
verses.text: Thou hast heard of the ungodly being green as the grass: hear also of the righteous: "For lo".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:77
verses.text: In the mean while, consider the ungodly; they flourish as the grass; but who are they who understand it not? The foolish and unwise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:78
verses.text: "When the ungodly are green as the grass, and all men look upon the workers of iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:79
verses.text: All who in their heart think not aright of God, look upon the ungodly when they are as green as grass, that is, when they flourish for a time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:80
verses.text: Why do they look upon them? "That they may be destroyed for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:81
verses.text: For they regard their momentary bloom, they imitate them, and wishing to flourish with them for a time, perish for evermore: this is, "That they may be destroyed for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:82
verses.text: "But Thou, Lord, art the Most Highest for evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:83
verses.text: Waiting above in Thy eternity until the season of the wicked be past, and that of the just come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:84
verses.text: "For lo".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:85
verses.text: Listen, brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:86
verses.text: Already he who speaketh (for he speaketh in our person, in the person of Christ's body, for Christ speaketh in His own body, that is, in His Church), hath joined himself unto the eternity of God: as I a little before was saying unto you, God is long-suffering and patient, and alloweth all those evil deeds which He seeth to be done by wicked men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:87
verses.text: Wherefore? because He is eternal, and seeth what He keepeth for them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:88
verses.text: Dost thou also wish to be long-suffering and patient? Join thyself to the eternity of God: together with Him wait for those things which are beneath thee: for when thy heart shall have cleaved unto the Most Highest, all mortal things will be beneath thee: say then what follows, "For lo, thine enemies shall perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:89
verses.text: Those who now flourish, shall afterwards perish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:90
verses.text: Who are the enemies of God? Brethren, perhaps ye think those only enemies of God who blaspheme? They indeed are so, and those wicked men who neither in tongue nor in thought cease to injure God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:91
verses.text: And what do they do to the eternal, most high God? If thou strike with thy fist upon a pillar, thou art hurt: and thinkest thou that where thou strikest God with thy blasphemy, thou art not thyself broken? for thou doest nothing to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:92
verses.text: But the enemies of God are openly blasphemers, and daily they are found hidden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:93
verses.text: Beware of such enmities of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:94
verses.text: For the Scripture revealeth some such secret enemies of God: that because thou knowest them not in thy heart, thou mayest know in God's Scriptures, and beware of being found with them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:95
verses.text: James saith openly in his Epistle, "Know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God?" Thou hast heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:96
verses.text: Dost thou wish not to be an enemy of God? Be not a friend of this world: for if thou art a friend of this world, thou wilt be an enemy of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:97
verses.text: For as a wife cannot be an adulteress, unless she be an enemy to her own husband: so a soul which is an adulteress through its love of worldly things, cannot but be an enemy to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:98
verses.text: It feareth, but loveth not: it feareth punishment but is not delighted with righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:99
verses.text: All lovers of the world, therefore, are enemies of God, all the curious after trifles, all consulters of diviners astrologers, and evil spirits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:100
verses.text: Let them enter, or not enter, Churches: they are enemies of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:101
verses.text: They may flourish for a season like grass, but they will perish, when He beginneth to visit them, and pronounce His sentence upon all flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:102
verses.text: Join thyself to the Scripture of God, and say with this Psalm, "For lo, thine enemies shall perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:103
verses.text: Be not found there, where they shall perish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:104
verses.text: "And all the workers of iniquity shall be destroyed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:105
verses.text: "But mine horn shall be exalted like the horn of an unicorn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:106
verses.text: Why did He say, "like the horn of an unicorn"? Sometimes an unicorn signifies pride, sometimes it means the lifting up of unity; because unity is lifted up, all heresies shall perish with the enemies of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:107
verses.text: And "mine horn shall be exalted like an unicorn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:108
verses.text: When will it be so? "And mine old age shall be in the fatness of mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:109
verses.text: Why did he say, "my old age"? He means, my last days; as our old age is the last season in our lives, so the whole of what the body of Christ at present suffereth in labours, in cares, in watchings, in hunger, in thirst, in stumbling-blocks, in wickednesses, in tribulations, is its youth: its old age, that is, its last days, will be in joy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:110
verses.text: And beware, beloved, that ye think not death meant also, in that he hath spoken of old age: for man groweth old in the flesh for this reason, that he may die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:111
verses.text: The old age of the Church will be white with good works, but it shall not decay through death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:112
verses.text: What the head of the old man is, that our works will be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:113
verses.text: Ye see how the head groweth old, and whiteneth, as fast as old age approacheth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:114
verses.text: Thou sometimes dost seek in the head of one who groweth old duly in his own course a black hair, yet thou findest it not: thus when our life shall have been such, that the blackness of sins may be sought, and none found, that old age is youthful, is green, and ever will be green.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:115
verses.text: Ye have heard of the grass of sinners, hear ye of the old age of the righteous: "My old age shall be in the fathers of mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:116
verses.text: "And Mine eye hath beheld on mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:117
verses.text: Whom doth he call his enemies? All the workers of iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:118
verses.text: Do not observe whether thy friend be wicked: let an occasion come, and then thou provest him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:119
verses.text: Thou beginnest to go contrary to his iniquity, and then thou shalt see that when he was flattering thee, he was thy enemy; but thou hadst not yet knocked, not to raise in his heart what was not there, but that what was there might break out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:120
verses.text: "Mine eye also hath looked upon mine enemies: and mine ear shall hear his desire of the wicked that rise up against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:121
verses.text: When? In my old age.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:122
verses.text: What is, in old age? In the last times.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:123
verses.text: And what shall our ear hear? Standing on the right hand, we shall hear what shall be said to them that are on the left.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:124
verses.text: The grass withereth, the flower of sinners dieth away: what of the righteous? "The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:125
verses.text: The ungodly are green as grass; "The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:126
verses.text: By the palm tree he signifieth height.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:127
verses.text: Possibly he had also this meaning in the palm, that in its extremities it is beautiful: so that thou mayest trace its beginning from the earth, its end in its topmost branches, wherein its whole beauty dwelleth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:128
verses.text: The rough root appeareth in the earth, the beautiful foliage toward the sky.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:129
verses.text: Thy beauty too, then, shall be in the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:130
verses.text: Thy root is fixed fast: but our root is upward.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:131
verses.text: For our root is Christ, who hath ascended into heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:132
verses.text: Humbled, he shall be exalted; "he shall spread abroad like a cedar in Libanus".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:133
verses.text: See what trees he spoke of: the righteous shall flourish like a palm-tree: and shall spread abroad like a cedar in Libanus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:134
verses.text: When the sun hath gone forth, doth the palm-tree wither? Doth the cedar die? But when the sun hath been glowing for some hours, the grass drieth up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:135
verses.text: The judgment, therefore, shall come, that sinners may wither, and the faithful flourish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:136
verses.text: "Such as are planted in the house of the Lord, shall flourish in the courts of the house of our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:137
verses.text: "They shall be yet more increased in fruitful old age, and shall be quiet, that they may show it fo rth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:138
verses.text: Such is the Sabbath, which but a little while ago I commended unto you, whence the Psalm hath its title.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:139
verses.text: "They shall be quiet, that they may show it forth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:140
verses.text: Wherefore are they quiet that show it forth? The grass of sinners moveth them not: the cedar and palm-tree not even in tempests are bent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:141
verses.text: They are therefore quiet, that they may show it forth: and with reason, since at present they must show it forth even unto men who mock at it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:142
verses.text: O wretched men, who are lovers of the world! Those who are planted in the house of the Lord, show it to you: those who praise the Lord with song and lute, in word and deed, show it forth to you, and tell you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:143
verses.text: Be not seduced by the prosperity of the wicked, admire not the flower of grass: admire not those who are happy only for a season, but miserable unto eternity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:144
verses.text: If ye wish to flourish like a palm-tree, and to spread abroad like a cedar in Libanus, and not to wither like grass when the sun is hot; as those who appear to flourish when the sun is absent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:145
verses.text: If then ye wish not to be as grass, but as the palm-tree and the cedar, what will ye show forth? "How true the Lord my strength is: and that there is no unrighteousness in Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:146
verses.text: How is it there is no unrighteousness? A man committeth so great crimes; he is well, he hath sons, a plentiful house, he is full of pride, is exalted by his honours, is revenged on his enemies, and doeth every evil deed; another man, innocent, attending to his own affairs, not robbing another's goods, doing nothing against any one, suffereth in chains, in prison, tosseth and sigheth in poverty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:147
verses.text: How is it that there is no unrighteousness in Him? Be quiet, and thou shalt know: for thou art disturbed, and in thy chamber thou dost darken thy light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:148
verses.text: The eternal God doth wish to shine upon thee: do not then make thee cloudy weather from thy own disturbed mind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:149
verses.text: Be quiet within thyself, and see what I say unto thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:150
verses.text: Because God is eternal, because for the present He spareth the bad, bringing them to repentance: He scourgeth the good, instructing them in the way unto the kingdom of heaven: "There is no unrighteousness in Him:" fear not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:151
verses.text: What, if He leaveth this man unpunished now, because he is doomed to hear, "Depart into everlasting fire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:152
verses.text: But when? when thou shalt be placed at the right hand, then shall it be said to those placed on the left, "Depart into the everlasting fire, which is prepared for the devil and his angels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 92:153
verses.text: Let not therefore those things move thee: Be quiet, keep Sabbath, and show "how true the Lord my strength is: and that there is no unrighteousness in Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:1
verses.text: Psalm XCIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:2
verses.text: It is entitled, "The Song of praise of David himself, on the day before the Sabbath, when the earth was founded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:3
verses.text: Remembering then what God did through all those days, when He made and ordained all things, from the first up to the sixth day (for the seventh He sanctified, because He rested on that day after all the works, which He made very good), we find that He created on the sixth day (which day is here mentioned, in that he saith, "before the Sabbath") all animals on the earth; lastly, He on that very day created man in His own likeness and image.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:4
verses.text: For these days were not without reason ordained in such order, but for that ages also were to run in a like course, before we rest in God But then we rest if we do good works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:5
verses.text: As a type of this, it is written of God, "God rested on the seventh day," when He had made all His works very good For He was not wearied, so as to need rest, nor hath He now left off to work, for our Lord Christ saith openly, "My Father worketh hitherto".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:6
verses.text: For He saith this unto the Jews, who thought carnally of God, and understood not that God worketh in quiet, and always worketh, and is always in quiet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:7
verses.text: We also, then, whom God willed then to figure in Himself, shall have rest after all good works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:8
verses.text: And because these good works are doomed to pass away, that sixth day also, when those very good works are perfected, hath an evening; but in the Sabbath we find no evening, because our rest shall have no end: for evening is put for end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:9
verses.text: As therefore God made man in His own image on the sixth day: thus we find that our Lord Jesus Christ came into the sixth age, that man might be formed anew after the image of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:10
verses.text: For the first period, as the first day, was from Adam until Noah: the second, as the second day, from Noah unto Abraham: the third, as the third day, from Abraham unto David: the fourth, as the fourth day, from David unto the removal to Babylon: the fifth period, as the fifth day, from the removal to Babylon unto the preaching of John.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:11
verses.text: The sixth day beginneth from the preaching of John, and lasteth unto the end: and after the end of the sixth day, we reach our rest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:12
verses.text: The sixth day, therefore, is even now passing And it is now the sixth day, see what the title hath;  "On the day before the Sabbath, when the earth was founded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:13
verses.text: Let us now listen to the Psalm itself: let us enquire of it, how the earth was made, whether perhaps the earth was then made: and we do not read so in Genesis.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:14
verses.text: When, therefore, was the earth founded? when, unless when that which hath been but now read in the Apostle taketh place: "If," he saith, "ye are stedfast, immovable".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:15
verses.text: When all who believe throughout all the earth are stedfast in faith, the earth is founded: then man is made in the image of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:16
verses.text: That sixth day in Genesis signifieth this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:17
verses.text: "The Lord reigneth, He is clothed with beauty; the Lord is clothed with strength, and is girded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:18
verses.text: We see that He hath clothed Himself with two things: beauty and strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:19
verses.text: But why? That He might found the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:20
verses.text: So it followeth, "He hath made the round world so sure, that it cannot be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:21
verses.text: Whence hath He made it so sure? Because He hath clothed Himself in beauty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:22
verses.text: He would not make it so sure, if He put on beauty only, and not strength also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:23
verses.text: Why therefore beauty, why strength? For He hath said both.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:24
verses.text: Ye know, brethren, that when our Lord had come in the flesh, of those to whom He preached the Gospel, He pleased some, and displeased others.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:25
verses.text: For the tongues of the Jews were divided against one another: "Some said, He is a good Man; others said, Nay, but He deceiveth the people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:26
verses.text: Some then spoke well, others detracted from Him, tore Him, bit and insulted Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:27
verses.text: Towards those therefore whom He pleased, "He put on beauty;" towards those whom He displeased, "He put on strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:28
verses.text: Imitate then thy Lord, that thou mayest become His garment: be with beauty towards those whom thy good works please: show thy strength against detractors.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:29
verses.text: Perhaps we should enquire respecting this word also, why he said, "He is girded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:30
verses.text: Girding signifieth work: for every man then girdeth himself, when he is about to work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:31
verses.text: But wherefore did he use the word praecinctus, instead of cinctus? For he saith in another Psalm, "Gird Thee with Thy sword upon Thy thigh, O Thou most mighty: the people shall fall under Thee:" using the word accingere, not cingere, nor praecingere: this word being applied to the act of attaching anything to the side by girding it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:32
verses.text: The sword of the Lord, wherewith He conquered the round world by killing iniquity, is the Spirit of God in the truth of the word of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:33
verses.text: Wherefore is He said to bind His sword around His thigh? In another place, on another Psalm we have spoken in another manner of girding: but nevertheless, since it hath been mentioned, it ought not to be passed over.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:34
verses.text: What is the girding on of the sword around the thigh? He meaneth the flesh by the thigh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:35
verses.text: For the Lord would not otherwise conquer the round world, unless the sword of truth came into the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:36
verses.text: Why therefore is He here said to be girded in front (praecinctus)? He who girdeth himself before, placeth something before himself, wherewith he is girded; whence it is said, He girded Himself before with a towel, and began to wash the disciples' feet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:37
verses.text: Because He was humble when He girded Himself with a towel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:38
verses.text: He washed the feet of His own disciples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:39
verses.text: But all strength is in humility: because all pride is fragile: therefore when He was speaking of strength, he added, "He is girded:" that thou mayest remember how thy God was girded in humility, when He washed His disciples' feet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:40
verses.text: After He had washed their feet, again He sat down; He said unto them, "Ye call me Lord and Master: and ye say well; for so I am.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:41
verses.text: If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; how ought ye also to do to one another's feet?" If therefore strength is in humility, fear not the proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:42
verses.text: The humble are like a rock: the rock seems to lie downwards: but nevertheless it is firm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:43
verses.text: What are the proud? Like smoke: although they are lofty, they vanish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:44
verses.text: We ought therefore to ascribe our Lord's being girded to His humility, according to the mention of the Gospel, that He was girded, that He might wash His disciples' feet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:45
verses.text: " For He hath made the round world sure, which cannot be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:46
verses.text: What then is the round world, "which cannot be moved"? This He would not mention specially, if there were not also a round world that can be moved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:47
verses.text: There is a round world that shall not be moved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:48
verses.text: There is a round world that shall be moved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:49
verses.text: For the good who are stedfast in the faith are the round world: that no man may say, they are only in part of it; while the wicked who abide not in faith, when they have felt any tribulation, are throughout the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:50
verses.text: There is therefore a round world movable: there is a world immovable: of which the Apostle speaketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:51
verses.text: Behold, the round world movable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:52
verses.text: I ask thee, of whom speaketh the Apostle in these words, "Of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus; who concerning the truth have erred, saying that the resurrection is past already: and overthrow the faith of some?" Did these belong to the round world, that shall not be moved? But they were chaff: and as he saith, "they overthrow the faith of some".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:53
verses.text: "Nevertheless, the foundation of God standeth sure; having his seal,"—what seal hath it as its sure foundation?—" The Lord knoweth them that are His".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:54
verses.text: This is the round world that shall not be moved; "The Lord knoweth them that are His".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:55
verses.text: And what seal hath it? "And let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from unrighteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:56
verses.text: Let him depart from unrighteousness: for he cannot depart from the unrighteous, for the chaff is mixed with the wheat until it is fanned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:57
verses.text: "Thy throne is established from thence, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:58
verses.text: What is, "from thence"? From that time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:59
verses.text: As if he said, What is the throne of God? Where doth God sit? In His Saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:60
verses.text: Dost thou wish to be the throne of God? Prepare a place in thy heart where He may sit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:61
verses.text: What is the throne of God, except where God dwelleth? Where doth God dwell, except in His temple? What is His temple? Is it surrounded with walls? Far from it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:62
verses.text: Perhaps this world is His temple, because it is very great, and a thing worthy to contain God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:63
verses.text: It contains not Him by whom it was made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:64
verses.text: And wherein is He contained? In the quiet soul, in the righteous soul: that is it that containeth Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:65
verses.text: He who said, "Before Abraham was, I am:" not before Abraham only, but before Adam: not only before Adam, but before all the angels, before heaven and earth; since all things were made through Him: he added, lest thou, attending to the day of our Lord's nativity, mightest think He commenced from that time, "Thy throne is established, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:66
verses.text: But what God? "Thou art from everlasting:" for which he uses ‡π' αἰῶνος, in the Greek version; that word being sometimes used for an age, sometimes for everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:67
verses.text: Therefore, O Thou who seemest to be born "from thence," Thou art from everlasting! But let not human birth be thought of, but Divine eternity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:68
verses.text: He began then from the time of His birth; He grew: ye have heard the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:69
verses.text: He chose disciples, He replenished them, His disciples began to preach.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:70
verses.text: Perhaps this is what he speaketh of in the following verse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:71
verses.text: "The floods lift up their voices".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:72
verses.text: What are these floods, which have lift up their voices? We heard them not: neither when our Lord was born, did we hear rivers speak, nor when He was baptized, nor when He suffered; we heard not that rivers did speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:73
verses.text: Read the Gospel, ye find not that rivers spoke.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:74
verses.text: It is not enough that they spoke: "They have lift up their voice:" they have not only spoken, but bravely, mightily, in a lofty voice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:75
verses.text: What are those rivers which have spoken?The Spirit itself was a mighty river, whence many rivers were filled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:76
verses.text: Of that river the Psalmist saith in another passage, "The rivers of the flood thereof shall make glad the city of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:77
verses.text: Rivers then were made to flow from the belly of the disciples, when they received the Holy Spirit: themselves were rivers, when they had received that Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:78
verses.text: Whence did those rivers lift their voices? wherefore did they lift them up? Because at first they feared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:79
verses.text: Peter was not yet a river, when at the question of the maid-servant he thrice denied Christ: "I do not know the man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:80
verses.text: Here he lieth through fear: he lifteth not his voice as yet: he is not yet the river.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:81
verses.text: But when they were filled with the Holy Spirit, the Jews sent for them, and enjoined them not to preach at all, nor to teach in the name of Jesus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:82
verses.text: For when the Apostles had been dismissed from the council of the Jews, they came to their own friends, and told them what the priests and elders said unto them: but they on hearing lifted up their voices with one accord unto the Lord, and said, "Lord, it is Thou who hast made heaven and earth, and the sea, and all that in them is;" and the rest which floods lifting up their voices might say, "Wonderful are the hangings of the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:83
verses.text: For when the disciples had lifted up their voices unto Him, many believed, and many received the Holy Spirit, and many rivers instead of few began to lift up their voice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:84
verses.text: Hence there followeth, "from the voices of many waters, wonderful are the hangings of the sea;" that is, the waves of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:85
verses.text: When Christ had begun to be preached by so powerful voices, the sea became enraged, persecutions began to thicken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:86
verses.text: When therefore the rivers had lift up their voice, "from the voices of many waters, wonderful" were "the hangings of the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:87
verses.text: To be hung aloft is to be lifted up; when the sea rages, the waves are hung as from above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:88
verses.text: Let the waves hang over as they choose; let the sea roar as it chooseth; the hangings of the sea indeed are mighty, mighty are the threatenings, mighty the persecutions; but see what followeth: "but yet the Lord, who dwelleth on high, is mightier".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:89
verses.text: Let therefore the sea restrain itself, and sometime become calmed; let peace be granted by Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:90
verses.text: The sea was disturbed, the vessel was tossed; the vessel is the Church: the sea, the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:91
verses.text: The Lord came, He walked over the sea, and calmed the waves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:92
verses.text: How did the Lord walk over the sea? Above the heads of those mighty foaming waves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:93
verses.text: Principalities and kings believed; they were subdued unto Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:94
verses.text: Let us not therefore be frightened; because "the Lord, who dwelleth on high, is mightier".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:95
verses.text: "Thy testimonies, O Lord, are very surely believed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:96
verses.text: The Lord, who dwelleth on high, is mightier than the mighty overhangings of the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:97
verses.text: "Thy testimonies are very surely believed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:98
verses.text: "Thy testimonies," because He had said beforehand, "These things I have spoken unto you, that in Me ye might have peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:99
verses.text: In the world ye shall have tribulation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:100
verses.text: He added, "but be of good cheer, I have overcome the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:101
verses.text: If then He saith, "I have overcome the world," cling unto Him who overcame the world, who overcame the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:102
verses.text: Rejoice in Him, because the Lord, who dwelleth on high, is mightier, and, "Thy testimonies are very surely believed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:103
verses.text: And what is the end of all these? "Holiness becometh Thine house, O Lord!" Thine house, the whole of Thine house, not here and there: but the whole of Thine house, throughout the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:104
verses.text: Why throughout the whole of the round world? "Because He hath set aright the round world, which cannot be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:105
verses.text: The Lord's house will be strong: it will prevail throughout the whole world: many shall fall: but that house standeth; many shall be disturbed, but that house shall not be moved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:106
verses.text: Holiness becometh Thine house, O Lord!" For a short time only? No.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 93:107
verses.text: "Unto length of days".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:1
verses.text: Psalm XCIV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:2
verses.text: As we listened with much attention, while the Psalm was in reading, so let us listen attentively, while the Lord revealeth the mysteries which He hath deigned to obscure in this passage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:3
verses.text: For some mysteries in the Scriptures are shut up for this reason, not that they may be denied, but that they may be opened unto those who knock.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:4
verses.text: If therefore ye knock with affection of piety, and sincere heartfelt love, He, who seeth from what motives ye knock, will open unto you It is known unto all of us (and I wish we may not be among their number), that may murmur against God's long-suffering, and grieve either that impious and wicked men live in this world, or that they have great power; and what is more, that the bad generally have great power against the good, and that the bad often oppress the good; that the wicked exult, while the good suffer; the evil are proud, while the good are humbled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:5
verses.text: Observing such things in the human race (for they abound), impatient and weak minds are perverted, as if they were good in vain; since God averteth, or seemeth to avert, His eyes from the good works of the pious and faithful, and to promote the wicked in those pleasures which they love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:6
verses.text: Weak men, therefore, imagining that they live well in vain, are induced either to imitate the wickedness of those whom they see flourishing: or if either through bodily or mental weakness they are deterred from doing wrong by a fear of the penal laws of the world; not because they love justice, but, to speak more openly, fearing the condemnation of men among men, they refrain indeed from wicked deeds, but refrain not from wicked thoughts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:7
verses.text: And among their wicked thoughts, the chief is the wickedness which leadeth them impiously to imagine that God is neglectful, and regardless of human affairs: and that He either holdeth in equal estimation the good and the wicked: or even, and this is a still more pernicious notion, that He persecuteth the good, and favoureth the wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:8
verses.text: He who thinketh thus, although he doth no harm to any man, doth the greatest to himself, and is impious against himself, and by his wickedness hurteth not God, but slayeth himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:9
verses.text: The Psalm hath this title, th at is, this inscription: "A Psalm of David himself, on the fourth day of the week".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:10
verses.text: This Psalm is about to teach patience in the sufferings of the righteous: it enjoineth patience against the prosperity of the wicked, and buildeth up patience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:11
verses.text: This is the drift of the whole of it, from beginning to end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:12
verses.text: Wherefore then hath it such a title, "on the fourth of the week"? The first of the week is the Lord's day: the second, is the second week-day, which people of the world call the Moon's day: the third, is the third weekday, which they term Mars' day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:13
verses.text: The fourth of the Sabbaths therefore is the fourth week-day, which by Pagans is styled Mercury's day, and also by many Christians; but I would not call it so: and I wish they would change for the better, and cease to do so; for they have a phrase of their own, which they may use.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:14
verses.text: For these terms are not of universal use: many nations have severally different names for them: so that the mode of speech used by the Church better beseemeth the mouth of a Christian Yet if custom hath induced any person to utter that with his tongue which his heart doth disapprove, let him remember, that all those whose names the stars bear were men, and that the stars did not commence their existence in the sky, when those men began theirs, but were there long before; but on account of some mortal services rendered unto mortals, those men in their own times, because they had great power, and were eminent in this life, since they were beloved by men, not on account of eternal life, but of temporal services, received divine honours.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:15
verses.text: For then men of the old world, in being deceived and wishing to deceive, pointed to the stars in heaven, to flatter those who had done them any good service in their affection for this life, saying, that that was the star of such a man, this of another; while the man who had not beheld them before, so as to see that those stars were there before the birth of the man, were deceived into a belief: and thus this vain opinion was conceived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:16
verses.text: This erroneous opinion the devil strengthened, Christ overthrew.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:17
verses.text: According to our mode of speech, then, the fourth of the week is taken for the fourth day from the Lord's day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:18
verses.text: Attend, therefore, beloved, to what this title meaneth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:19
verses.text: Here is a great mystery, and a truly hidden one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:20
verses.text: Let us therefore recall from the holy Scripture in Genesis, what was created on the first day; we find light: what was created on the second day; we find the firmament, which God called heaven: what was created on the third day; we find the form of earth and sea, and their separation, that all the gathering together of the waters was called sea, and all that was dry, the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:21
verses.text: On the fourth day, the Lord made the lights in heaven: "The sun to rule the day: the moon and stars to  govern the night:" this was the work of the fourth  day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:22
verses.text: What then is the reason that the Psalm hath taken its title from the fourth day: the Psalm in which patience is enjoined against the prosperity of the wicked, and the sufferings of the good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:23
verses.text: Thou findest the Apostle Paul speaking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:24
verses.text: "Do all things without murmurings and disputings: that ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world, holding forth the word of life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:25
verses.text: Let us now attend to the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:26
verses.text: "The Lord is the God of vengeance; the God of vengeance hath dealt confidently".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:27
verses.text: Dost thou think that He doth not punish? "The God of vengeance" punisheth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:28
verses.text: What is, "The God of vengeance"? The God of punishments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:29
verses.text: Thou murmurest surely because the bad are not punished: yet do not murmur, lest thou be among those who are punished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:30
verses.text: That man hath committed a theft, and liveth: thou murmurest against God, because he who committed a theft on thee dieth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:31
