verses.text: Therefore, if thou wouldest have another correct his hand, do thou first correct thy tongue: thou wouldest have him correct his heart towards man, correct thy heart towards God; lest perchance, when thou desirest the vengeance of God, if it come, it find thee first.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:32
verses.text: For He will come: He will come, and will judge those who continue in their wickedness, ungrateful for the prolongation of His mercy, for His long-suffering, treasuring up unto themselves wrath against the day of wrath, and revelation of the righteous judgment of God, who will render to every man according to his deeds: because, "The Lord is the God of vengeance," therefore hath He "dealt confidently".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:33
verses.text: Our safety is our Saviour: in Him He would place the hope of all the needy and poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:34
verses.text: And what saith He? "I will deal confidently in Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:35
verses.text: What meaneth this? He will not fear, will not spare the lusts and vices of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:36
verses.text: Truly, as a faithful physician, with the healing knife of preaching in His hand, He hath cut away all our wounded parts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:37
verses.text: Therefore such as He was prophesied and preached beforehand, such was He found.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:38
verses.text: How great things then did He, of whom it is said, "He taught them as one having authority," say unto them? "Woe unto you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites!" What great things did He say unto them, before their face? He feared no one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:39
verses.text: Why? Because He is the God of vengeance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:40
verses.text: For this reason He spared them not in words, that they might remain for Him after to spare them in judgment; because if they were unwilling to accept the healing of His word, they would afterwards incur their Judge's doom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:41
verses.text: Wherefore? Because He hath said, "The Lord is the God of vengeance, the God of vengeance hath dealt confidently;" that is, He hath spared no man in word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:42
verses.text: He who spared not in word when about to suffer, will He spare in judgment when about to judge? He who in His humility feared no man, will He fear any man in His glory? From His dealing thus confidently in time past, imagine how He will deal at the end of time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:43
verses.text: Murmur not then against God, who seemeth to spare the wicked; but be thou good, and perhaps for a season He may not spare thee the rod, that He may in the end spare thee in judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:44
verses.text: And what followed, because He dealt confidently? "Be exalted, Thou Judge of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:45
verses.text: Because they imprisoned Him when humble, thinkest thou they will imprison Him when exalted? Because they judged Him when mortal, will they not be judged by Him when immortal? What then saith He? "Be exalted," Thou, who hast dealt confidently, the confidence of whose word the wicked bore not, but thought they did a glorious deed, when they seized and crucified Thee; they who ought to have seized on Thee with faith, seized Thee with persecution.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:46
verses.text: Thou then who hast among the wicked dealt confidently, and hast feared no man, because Thou hast suffered, "be exalted;" that is, arise again, depart into heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:47
verses.text: Let the Church also bear with long-suffering what the Church's Head hath borne with long-suffering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:48
verses.text: "Be exalted, Thou Judge of the world: and reward the proud after their deserving".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:49
verses.text: He will reward them, brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:50
verses.text: For what is this, "Be exalted, Thou Judge of the world: and reward the proud after their deserving"? This is the prophecy of one who doth predict, not the boldness of one who commandeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:51
verses.text: Not because the Prophet said, "Be exalted, Thou Judge of the world," did Christ obey the Prophet, in arising from the dead, and ascending into heaven; but because Christ was to do this, the Prophet predicted it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:52
verses.text: He seeth Christ abased in the spirit, abased he seeth Him: fearing no man, in speech sparing no man, and he saith, "He hath dealt confidently".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:53
verses.text: He seeth how confidently He hath dealt, he seeth Him arrested, crucified, humbled, he seeth Him rising from the dead, and ascending into heaven, and from thence to come in judgment of those, among whose hands He had suffered every evil: "Be exalted," he saith, "Thou Judge of the world, and reward the proud after their deserving".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:54
verses.text: The proud He will thus reward, not the humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:55
verses.text: Who are the proud? Those to whom it is little to do evil: but they even defend their own sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:56
verses.text: For on some of those who crucified Christ, miracles were afterwards performed, when out of the number of the Jews themselves there were found believers, and the blood of Christ was given unto them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:57
verses.text: Their hands were impious, and red with the blood of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:58
verses.text: He whose blood they had shed, Himself washed them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:59
verses.text: They who had persecuted His mortal body which they had seen, became part of His very body, that is, the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:60
verses.text: They shed their own ransom, that they might drink their own ransom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:61
verses.text: For afterwards more were converted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:62
verses.text: "Lord, how long shall the ungodly, how long shall the ungodly triumph?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:63
verses.text: "They answer, and will speak wickedness, they all will speak that work unrighteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:64
verses.text: What is their saying, but against God, when they say: What profiteth it us that we live thus? What wilt thou reply? Doth God truly regard our deeds? For because they live, they imagine that God knoweth not their actions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:65
verses.text: Behold, what evil happeneth unto them! If the officers knew where they were, they would arrest them; and they therefore avoid the officer's eyes, that they may escape instant apprehension; but no one can escape the eye of God, since He not only seeth within the closet, but within the recesses of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:66
verses.text: Even they themselves believe that nothing can escape God: and because they do evil, and are conscious of what they have done, and see that they live while God knoweth, though they would not live if the officer discovered them; they say unto themselves, These things please God: and, in truth, if they displeased Him, as they displease kings, as they displease judges, as they displease governors, as they displease recorders, yet could we escape the eye of God, as we do escape the eyes of those authorities? Therefore these things please God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:67
verses.text: Some righteous man cometh, and saith, Do not commit iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:68
verses.text: Wherefore? That thou mayest not die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:69
verses.text: Behold, iniquity I have committed: why do I not die? That man wrought righteousness: and he is dead: why is he dead? I have wrought iniquity: why hath not God carried me off? Behold, that man did righteously: and why hath He thus visited him? why suffereth He thus? They answer; this is the meaning of the word "answer:" for they have a reply to make; because they are spared, from the long-suffering of God, they discover an argument for their reply.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:70
verses.text: He spareth them for one reason, they answer for another, because they still live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:71
verses.text: For the Apostle telleth us wherefore He spareth, he expoundeth the grounds of the long-suffering of God: "And thinkest thou this, O man, that judgest them which do such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God? Or despisest thou the riches of His goodness, and forbearance, and long-suffering; not knowing that the long-suffering of God leadeth thee to repentance?" "But thou," that is, he who answereth and saith, If I displeased God, He would not spare me, hear what he worketh for himself; hear the Apostle; "but after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up into thyself wrath against the day of wrath, and revelation of the righteous judgment of God; who will render to every man according to his deeds".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:72
verses.text: He therefore increaseth His long-suffering, thou increasest thine iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:73
verses.text: His treasure will consist in eternal mercy towards those who have not despised His mercy; but thy treasure will be discovered in wrath, and what thou daily layest up by little and little, thou wilt find in the accumulated mass; thou layest up by the grain, but thou wilt find the whole heap.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:74
verses.text: Omit not to watch thy slightest daily sins: rivers are filled from the smallest drops.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:75
verses.text: "They have humbled Thy people, O Lord; and have troubled Thine heritage".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:76
verses.text: "They have murdered the widow, and the fatherless: and slain the proselyte" ; that is, the traveller, the pilgrim: the comer from far, as the Psalmist calleth himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:77
verses.text: Each of these expressions is too clear in meaning to make it worth while to dwell upon them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:78
verses.text: "And they have said, The Lord shall not see" : He observeth not, regardeth not these things: He careth for other matters, He understandeth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:79
verses.text: These are the two assertions of the wicked: one which I have just quoted, "These things hast thou done, and I held my tongue, and thou thoughtest unrighteousness, that I will be like thyself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:80
verses.text: What meaneth, "that I will be like thyself"? Thou thinkest that I see thy deeds, and that they are pleasing unto Me, because I do not punish them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:81
verses.text: There is another assertion of the wicked: because God neither regardeth these things, nor observeth that He may know how I live, God heedeth me not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:82
verses.text: Doth then God make any reckoning of me? or doth He even take account of me? or of men in general? Unhappy man! He cared for thee, that thou mightest exist: doth He not care that thou live well? Such then are the words of these last; "and yet they have said, The Lord shall not see: neither shall the God of Jacob regard it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:83
verses.text: "Take heed now, ye that are unwise among the people: O ye fools, some time understand!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:84
verses.text: He teacheth His people whose feet might slip: any one among them seeth the prosperity of the wicked, himself living well among the Saints of God, that is, among the number of the sons of the Church: he seeth that the wicked flourish, and work iniquity, he envieth, and is led to follow them in their actions; because he seeth that apparently it profiteth him nothing that he liveth well in humility, hoping for his reward here.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:85
verses.text: For if he hopeth for it in future, he loseth it not; because the time is not yet come for him to receive it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:86
verses.text: Thou art working in a vineyard: execute thy task, and thou shalt receive thy pay.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:87
verses.text: Thou wouldest not exact it from thy employer, before thy work was finished, and yet dost thou exact it from God before thou dost work? This patience is part of thy work, and thy pay dependeth upon thy work: thou who dost not choose to be patient, choosest to work less upon the vineyard: since this act of patience belongeth to thy labouring itself, which is to gain thy pay.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:88
verses.text: But if thou art treacherous, take care, lest thou shouldest not only not receive thy pay, but also suffer punishment, because thou hast chosen to be a treacherous labourer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:89
verses.text: When such a labourer beginneth to do ill, he watcheth his employer's eyes, who hired him for his vineyard, that he may loiter when his eye is turned away; but the moment his eyes are turned towards him, he worketh diligently.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:90
verses.text: But God, who hired thee, averteth not His eyes: thou canst not work treacherously: the eyes of thy Master are ever upon thee: seek an opportunity to deceive Him, and loiter if thou canst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:91
verses.text: If then any of you had any such ideas, when ye saw the wicked fl ourishing, and if such thoughts caused your feet to slip in the path of God; to you this Psalm speaketh: but if perchance none of you be such, through you it doth address others, in these words, "Take heed now;" since they had said, "The Lord shall not see: neither shall the God of Jacob regard it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:92
verses.text: "Take heed," it saith, "now, ye that are unwise among the people: and ye fools, some time understand!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:93
verses.text: "He that planted the ear, shall He not hear? or He that made the eye, doth He not consider?"  "or He that instructeth the nations, shall He not reprove?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:94
verses.text: This is what God is at present doing: He is instructing the nations: for this reason he sent His word to man throughout the world: He sent it by Angels, by Patriarchs, by Prophets, by servants, through so many heralds going before the Judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:95
verses.text: He sent also His own Word Himself, He sent His own Son in Person: He sent the servants of His Son, and in these very servants His own Son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:96
verses.text: Throughout the world is everywhere preached the word of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:97
verses.text: Where is it not said unto men, Abandon your former wickedness, and turn yourselves to right paths? He spareth, that ye may correct yourselves: He punished not yesterday, in order that to-day ye may live well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:98
verses.text: He teacheth the heathen, shall He not therefore reprove? will He not hear those whom He teacheth? will He not judge those to whom He hath beforehand sent and sown lessons of warning? If thou wast in a school, wouldest thou receive a task, and not repeat it? When therefore thou receivest it from thy master, thou art being taught: the Master giveth thy task into thy hands, and shall He not exact it from thee when thou comest to repeat it? or when thou hast begun to repeat it, shalt thou not be in fear of stripes? At present then we are receiving our work: afterwards we are placed before the Master, that we may give up to Him all our past tasks, that is, that we may give an account of all those things which are now being bestowed upon us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:99
verses.text: Hear the Apostle's words: "We must all appear before the judgment-seat of Christ," etc "It is He that teacheth man knowledge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:100
verses.text: Doth He not know, who maketh thee to know?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:101
verses.text: "The Lord knoweth the thoughts of man, that they are but vain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:102
verses.text: For although thou knowest not the thoughts of God, that they are righteous; "He knoweth the thoughts of man, that they are but vain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:103
verses.text: Even men have known the thoughts of God: but those to whom He hath become a friend, it is to them He showeth His counsel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:104
verses.text: Do not, brethren, despise yourselves: if ye approach the Lord with faith, ye hear the thoughts of God; these ye are now learning, this is told you, and for this reason ye are taught, why God spareth the wicked in this life, that ye may not murmur against God, who teacheth man knowledge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:105
verses.text: "The Lord knoweth the thoughts of man, that they are but vain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:106
verses.text: Abandon therefore the thoughts of man, which are vain: that ye may take hold on the thoughts of God, which are wise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:107
verses.text: But who is he who taketh hold on the thoughts of God? He who is placed in the firmament of heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:108
verses.text: We have already chanted that Psalm, and have expounded this expression therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:109
verses.text: "Blessed is the man whom Thou chastenest, O Lord: and teachest him from Thy law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:110
verses.text: Behold, thou hast the counsel of God, wherefore He spareth the wicked: the pit is being digged for the sinner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:111
verses.text: Thou wishest to bury him at once: the pit is as yet being dug for him: do not be in haste to bury him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:112
verses.text: What mean the words, "until the pit be digged up for the sinner"? or whom doth He mean by sinner? One man? No.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:113
verses.text: Whom then? The whole race of such that are sinners? No; them that are proud; for he had said before, "Reward the proud after their deserving".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:114
verses.text: For that publican, who would not so much as lift up his eyes to heaven, but "smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner," was a sinner; but since he was not proud, and since God will render a recompense to the proud; the pit is being dug not for him, but for them that are such, until He render a recompense to the proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:115
verses.text: In the words then, "until the pit be digged up for the ungodly," understand the proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:116
verses.text: Who is the proud? He who doth not by confession of his sins do penance, that he may be healed through his humility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:117
verses.text: Who is the proud? He who chooseth to arrogate to himself those few good things which he seemeth to possess, and who doth detract from the mercy of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:118
verses.text: Who is the proud? He who although he doth ascribe unto God his good works, yet insulteth those who do not those good works, and raiseth himself above them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:119
verses.text: This then is the Christian doctrine: no man doeth anything well except by His grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:120
verses.text: A man's bad acts are his own: his good he doth of God's bounty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:121
verses.text: When he hath begun to do well, let not him ascribe it unto himself: when he hath not attributed it to himself, let him give thanks to Him from whom he hath received it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:122
verses.text: But when he doeth well, let him not insult him who doth not as he doth nor exalt himself above him: for the grace of God is not stayed at him, so that it cannot reach another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:123
verses.text: "That Thou mayest give him patience in days of malice: until the pit be digged up for the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:124
verses.text: Have patience therefore every one, if thou art a Christian, in time of malice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:125
verses.text: Days of malice are those in which the ungodly appear to flourish, and the righteous to suffer; but the suffering of the righteous is the rod of the Father, and the prosperity of the ungodly is their own snare.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:126
verses.text: For because God giveth you patience in time of adversity, until the pit be digged up for the ungodly, do not think that the Angels are standing in some place with mattocks, and are digging that great pit which shall be able to contain the whole race of the ungodly; and because ye see that the wicked are many, and say unto yourselves carnally: Truly what pit can contain so great a multitude of the wicked, such a crowd of sinners? where is a pit of such dimensions, as to contain all, dug? when finished? therefore God spareth them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:127
verses.text: This is not so: their very prosperity is the pit of the wicked: for into that shall they fall, as it were into a pitfall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:128
verses.text: Attend, brethren, for it is a great thing to know that prosperity is called a pitfall: "until the pit be digged up for the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:129
verses.text: For God spareth him whom He knoweth to be ungodly and impious, in His own hidden justice: and this very sparing of God, causeth him to be puffed up through his impunity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:130
verses.text: The proud man raiseth himself up against God: God sinket h him: and he sinketh by the very act of raising himself up against God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:131
verses.text: For in another Psalm he thus saith, "Thou hast cast them down, while they were being exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:132
verses.text: He said not, Thou hast cast them down, because they were exalted; or, Thou hast cast them down, after they were exalted; so that the period of their exaltation be one, of their casting down another: but in the very act of their exaltation were they cast down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:133
verses.text: For in proportion as the heart of man is proud, so doth it recede from God; and if it recede from God, it sinketh down into the deep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:134
verses.text: On the other hand, the humble heart bringeth God unto it from heaven, so that He becometh very near unto it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:135
verses.text: Surely God is lofty, God is above all the heavens, He surpasseth all the Angels: how high must these be raised, to reach that exalted One? Do not burst thyself by enlarging thyself; I give thee other advice, lest perchance in enlarging thyself thou burst, through pride: surely God is lofty: do thou humble thyself, and He will descend unto thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:136
verses.text: Do thou rejoice beneath the scourge: because the heritage is kept for thee, "for the Lord will not cast off His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:137
verses.text: He chasteneth for a season, He condemneth not for ever: the others He spareth for a season, and will condemn them for evermore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:138
verses.text: Make thy choice: dost thou wish temporary suffering, or eternal punishment? temporal happiness, or eternal life? What doth God threaten? Eternal punishment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:139
verses.text: What doth He promise? Eternal rest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:140
verses.text: His scourging the good, is temporary: His sparing the wicked, is also temporary.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:141
verses.text: "Neither will He forsake His inheritance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:142
verses.text: "Until righteousness," he saith, "turn again unto judgment, and all they that have it are right in heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:143
verses.text: Listen now, and gain righteousness: for judgment thou canst not yet have.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:144
verses.text: Thou shouldest gain righteousness first; but that very righteousness of thine shall turn unto judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:145
verses.text: The Apostles had righteousness here on earth, and bore with the wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:146
verses.text: But what is said unto them? "Ye shall sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:147
verses.text: Their righteousness therefore shall turn unto judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:148
verses.text: For whoever is righteous in this life, is so for this reason, that he may endure evils with patience: let him suffer patiently the period of suffering, and the day of judging cometh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:149
verses.text: But why do I speak of the servants of God? The Lord Himself, who is the Judge of all living and dead, first chose to be judged, and then to judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:150
verses.text: Those who have righteousness at present, are not yet judges.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:151
verses.text: For the first thing is to have righteousness, and afterwards to judge: He first endureth the wicked, and afterwards judgeth them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:152
verses.text: Let there be righteousness now: afterwards it shall turn again unto judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:153
verses.text: And so long He endureth wicked men, as God doth will, as long as God's Church shall endure them, that she may be taught through their wickedness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:154
verses.text: Nevertheless, God will not cast off His people, "all such as have it are right in heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:155
verses.text: Who are those who are right in heart? Those whose will is the will of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:156
verses.text: He spareth sinners: thou dost wish Him at once to destroy sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:157
verses.text: Thy heart is crooked and thy will perverted, when thy will is one way and the will of God another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:158
verses.text: God wisheth to spare sinners: thou dost not wish sinners spared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:159
verses.text: God is of long-suffering to sinners: thou dost not wish to endure sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:160
verses.text: Wish not to bend the will of God to thy will, but rather correct thy will to His.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:161
verses.text: The will of God is like a rule: behold, suppose, thou hast twisted the rule: whence canst thou be set straight? But the rule itself continueth straight: for it is immutable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:162
verses.text: As long as the rule is straight, thou hast whither to turn thyself, and straighten thy perversity; thou hast a means of correcting what is crooked in thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:163
verses.text: But what do men will? It is not enough that their own will is crooked; they even wish to make the will of God crooked according to their own heart, that God may do what they themselves will, when they ought to do that which God willeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:164
verses.text: "Who will rise up for me against the wicked? or who will take my part against the evil doers?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:165
verses.text: Many persuade us to divers evils: the serpent ceaseth not to whisper to thee to work iniquity: whichever way thou shalt turn, if perchance thou hast done well, thou seekest to live well with some one, and thou hardly findest any one; many wicked men surround thee, for there are few grains of wheat, and much chaff.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:166
verses.text: This floor hath its grains of corn, but as yet they suffer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:167
verses.text: Therefore the whole mass of the wheat, when separated from the chaff, will be great: the grains are few, but when compared with the chaff, still many in themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:168
verses.text: When therefore the wicked cry out on every side, and say, Why livest thou thus? Art thou the only Christian? Why dost thou not do what others also do? Why dost thou not frequent the theatres, as others do? Why dost thou not use charms and amulets? Why dost thou not consult astrologers and soothsayers, even as others do? And thou crossest thyself, and sayest, I am Christian, that thou mayest repel them, whosoever they are; but the enemy presses on, urges his attacks; what is worse, by the example of Christians he choketh Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:169
verses.text: They toil on, in the midst of heat: the Christian soul suffereth tribulation: yet it hath power to conquer: hath it such power of itself? For this reason remark what he saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:170
verses.text: For he answereth, What doth it profit me that I now find charms for myself, and gain a few days? I depart hence from this life, and repair unto my Lord, who shall send me into the flames; because I have preferred a few days to life eternal, He shall send me into hell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:171
verses.text: What hell? That of the eternal judgment of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:172
verses.text: Is it really so (the enemy answereth), unless indeed thou really believest that God careth how men live? And perhaps it is not an acquaintance who speaketh thus to thee in the street, but thy wife at home, or possibly the husband to the faithful and holy wife, her deceiver.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:173
verses.text: If it be the woman to her husband, she is as Eve unto him; if as the husband unto the wife, he is as the devil unto her: either she is herself as Eve unto thee, or thou art a serpent unto her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:174
verses.text: Sometimes the father would incline his thoughts to his son, and findeth him wicked, utterly depraved: he is in a fever of misery, he wavers, he seeketh how to subdue him, he is almost drawn in, and consenteth: but may God be near him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:175
verses.text: "If the Lord," he saith, "had not helped me: within a little my soul had dwelt in hell".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:176
verses.text: I had almost plunged into that pit which is preparing for sinners: that is, my soul had dwelt in hell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:177
verses.text: Because he already began to waver, and nearly to consent, he looked back unto the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:178
verses.text: Suppose, for example's sake, he was insulted to tempt him to iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:179
verses.text: For sometimes the wicked flock together, and insult the good; especially if they are more in number, and if they have taken him alone, as there is often much chaff about one grain of wheat (though there will not be when the heap hath been fanned); he is then taken among many wicked ones, is insulted, and surrounded; they wish to place themselves over him, they torment him and insult him for his very righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:180
verses.text: A great Apostle! say they; Thou hast flown into heaven, as Elias did! Men do these things, so that sometime, when he listeneth to the tongue of men, he is ashamed to be good among the wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:181
verses.text: Let him therefore resist the evil; but not of his own strength, lest he become proud, and when he wishes to escape the proud, himself increase their number.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:182
verses.text: "If I said, My foot hath slipt; Thy mercy, O Lord, held me up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:183
verses.text: See how God loveth confession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:184
verses.text: Thy foot hath slipt, and thou sayest not, my foot hath slipt; but thou sayest thou art firm, when thou art slipping.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:185
verses.text: The moment thou beginnest to slip or waver, confess thou that slip, that thou mayest not bewail thy total fall; that He may help, so that thy soul be not in hell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:186
verses.text: God loveth confession, loveth humility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:187
verses.text: Thou hast slipped, as a man; God helpeth thee, nevertheless: yet say, "My foot hath slipt".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:188
verses.text: Why dost thou slip, and yet sayest, I am firm? "When I said, My foot hath slipt, Thy mercy, O Lord, hath held me up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:189
verses.text: Just as Peter presumed, but not in strength of his own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:190
verses.text: The Lord was seen to walk upon the sea, trampling on the heads of all the proud in this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:191
verses.text: In walking upon the foaming waves, He figured His own course when He trampleth on the heads of the proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:192
verses.text: The Church too doth trample upon them: for Peter is the Church Herself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:193
verses.text: Nevertheless, Peter dared not by himself walk upon the waters; but what said he? "Lord, if it be Thou, bid me come unto Thee on the water".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:194
verses.text: He in His own power, Peter by His order; "bid me," he saith, "come unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:195
verses.text: He answered, "Come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:196
verses.text: For the Church also trampleth on the heads of the proud; but since it is the Church, and hath human weakness, that these words might be fulfilled, "If I said, My foot hath slipt," Peter tottered on the sea, and cried out, "Lord, save me!" and so what is here put, "If I said, My foot hath slipt," is put there, "Lord, I perish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:197
verses.text: And what is here, "Thy mercy, O Lord, hath held me up," is there put, "And immediately Jesus stretched forth His hand, saying, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?" It is wonderful how God proveth men: our very dangers render Him who rescueth us sweeter unto us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:198
verses.text: For see what followeth: because he said, "If I said, My foot hath slipt, Thy mercy, O Lord, hath held me up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:199
verses.text: The Lord hath become especially sweet unto him, in rescuing him from danger; and thus speaking of this very sweetness of the Lord, he exclaimeth and saith, "O Lord, in the multitude of the sorrows that I had in my heart, Thy comforts have refreshed my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:200
verses.text: Many sorrows, but many consolations: bitter wounds, and sweet remedies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:201
verses.text: "Wilt Thou have anything to do with the stool of iniquity, who makest sorrow in learning?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:202
verses.text: He hath said this, No wicked man sitteth with Thee, nor shalt Thou have anything to do with the stool of iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:203
verses.text: And he giveth an account whereof he understandeth this, "For Thou makest sorrow in learning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:204
verses.text: For from this, because Thou hast not spared us, do I understand that Thou hast nothing to do with the stool of iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:205
verses.text: Thou hast this in the Epistle of the Apostle Peter, and for this reason he hath adduced a testimony from the Scripture: "for the time is come," he saith, "that judgment must begin at the house of God;" that is, the time is come for the judgment of those who belong to the house of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:206
verses.text: If sons are scourged, what must the most wicked slaves expect? For which reason he added: "And if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the Gospel of God?" To which he added this testimony: "For if the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and sinner appear?" How then shall the wicked be with Thee, if Thou dost not even spare Thy faithful, in order that Thou mayest exercise and teach them? But as He spareth them not, for this reason, that He may teach them: he saith, "For Thou makest sorrow in learning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:207
verses.text: "Makest," that is, formest: from whence comes the word figulus (from fingo), and a potter's vessel is called fictile: not in the meaning of fiction, a falsehood, but of forming so as to give anything being and some sort of form; as before he said, "He that fabricated (finxit) the eye, shall He not see?"  Is that, "fabricated the eye" a falsehood? Nay, it is understood He fashioned the eye, made the eye.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:208
verses.text: And is He not a potter when He makes men frail, weak, earthly? Hear the Apostle: "We have this treasure in earthen vessels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:209
verses.text: Behold our Lord Himself, how He showeth Himself a potter Because He had made man of clay, He anointed him with clay, for whom He had not made eyes in the womb.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:210
verses.text: And so when he saith, "Hast Thou anything to do," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:211
verses.text: , he saith, out of grief makest learning for us, so that grief itself becomes our instruction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:212
verses.text: How is sorrow our learning? When He scourgeth thee who died for thee, and who doth not promise bliss in this life, and who cannot deceive, and when He giveth not here what thou seekest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:213
verses.text: What will He give? when will He give? how much will He give, who giveth not here, who here teacheth, who maketh sorrow in learning? Thy labour is here, and rest is promised thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:214
verses.text: Thou takest thought that thou hast toil here: but take thought what sort of rest He promiseth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:215
verses.text: Canst thou conceive it? If thou couldest, thou wouldest see that thy toil here is nothing toward an equivalent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:216
verses.text: Attend, brethren; it is for sale What I have is for sale, saith God unto thee, buy it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:217
verses.text: What hath He for sale? I have rest for sale; buy it by  thy toil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:218
verses.text: Attend, that we may be in Christ's name brave Christians: the remainder of the Psalm is but a little, let us not be weary.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:219
verses.text: For how can he be strong in doing, who faileth in hearing? The Lord will help us to expound unto you the remainder.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:220
verses.text: Attend then: God hath, as it were, proclaimed the kingdom of heaven for sale.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:221
verses.text: Thou sayest unto Him, What is its value? The price is toil: if He were to say, its price is gold, it would not suffice to say this only, but thou wouldest seek to know how much gold; for there is a mass of gold, and half an ounce, and a pound, and the like.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:222
verses.text: He said "price," that thou mightest not be at pains to inquire, how long thou shouldest find it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:223
verses.text: The price of the commodity is toil: how much toil is it? Now seek how much thou shouldest toil for it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:224
verses.text: Thou art not as yet told how great that toil is doomed to be, or how much toil is required of thee: God saith this unto thee, I show thee how great that rest will be; do thou judge with what measure of toil it should be bought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:225
verses.text: He promised rest: suffer trouble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:226
verses.text: He threateneth eternal fire; despise temporal pains: and while Christ doth watch, let thy heart be calmed, that thou also mayest reach the harbour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:227
verses.text: For He would not fail to prepare a harbour, who provided a vessel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:228
verses.text: "Hast Thou anything to do with the stool of iniquity, Thou who makest sorrow in learning?" He trieth us with the wicked, and by their persecution He teacheth us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:229
verses.text: By means of the malice of the wicked the good is scourged, through the slave the son is chastened: thus is learning taught by sorrow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:230
verses.text: What God alloweth them power to do, that do wicked men, whom He spareth for a season, do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:231
verses.text: For what followeth? "They will be captious against the soul of the righteous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:232
verses.text: Why will they be captious? Because they can find no true ground of accusation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:233
verses.text: For how were they captious against our Lord? They made up false accusations, because they could not find true ones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:234
verses.text: "And will condemn the innocent blood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:235
verses.text: Why all this taketh place, he will show in the sequel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:236
verses.text: "And the Lord is become my refuge" , he saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:237
verses.text: Thou wouldest not seek such a refuge, if thou wert not in danger: but thou hast therefore been in danger, that thou mightest seek for it: for He teacheth us by sorrow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:238
verses.text: He causeth me tribulation from the malice of the wicked: pricked with that tribulation, I begin to seek a refuge which I had ceased to seek for in that worldly prosperity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:239
verses.text: For who, that is always prosperous, and rejoiceth in present hopes, findeth it easy to remember God? Let the hope of this life give way, and the hope of God advance; that thou mayest say, "And the Lord is become my refuge:" may I sorrow for this end that the Lord may become my refuge! "And my God the help of my hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:240
verses.text: For as yet the Lord is our hope, since as long as we are here, we are in hope, and not in possession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:241
verses.text: But lest we fail in hope, there is near us a provision to encourage us, and to mitigate those very evils which we suffer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:242
verses.text: For it is not said in vain, "God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able: but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it:" who will so put us into that furnace of tribulation, that the vessel may be hardened, but not broken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:243
verses.text: "And the Lord is become my refuge: and my God the help of my hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:244
verses.text: Why then did  He seem to thee to be as it were unjust, in that He spareth the evil? See then how the Psalm i s now set right, and be thou set right together with the Psalm: for, for this reason the Psalm contained thy words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:245
verses.text: Wh at words? "Lord, how long shall the ungodly, how long shall the ungodly triumph?" The Psalm just now used thy words: use therefore thyself the Psalm's words in thy turn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:246
verses.text: "And the Lord shall recompense them according to their works, and after their own malice; the Lord our God shall destroy them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:247
verses.text: The words, "after their own malice," are not said without meaning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:248
verses.text: I am benefited through them: and yet it is said to be their malice, and not their benefits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:249
verses.text: For assuredly He trieth us, scourgeth us, by means of the wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:250
verses.text: To prepare us for what doth He scourge us? Confessedly for the kingdom of heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:251
verses.text: "For He scourgeth every son whom He receiveth; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?" and when God doth this, He is teaching us in order to an eternal heritage: and this learning He often giveth us by means of wicked men, through whom He trieth and perfecteth our love, which He doth will to be extended even to our enemiesThus also they who persecuted the Martyrs, by persecuting them on earth, sent them into heaven: knowingly they caused them the loss of the present life, while unconsciously they were bestowing upon them the gain of a future life: but, nevertheless, unto all who persevered in their wicked hatred of the righteous, will God recompense after their own iniquities, and in their own malice will He destroy them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:252
verses.text: For as the goodness of the righteous is hurtful unto the wicked, so is the iniquity of the wicked beneficial unto the righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:253
verses.text: Let therefore the righteous bear with the ungodly; let the temporal suffering of the righteous bear with the temporal impunity of the wicked; for "the just shall live by faith".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:254
verses.text: For there is no righteousness of man in this life except to live by faith, "which worketh by love".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:255
verses.text: But if he liveth by faith, let him believe both that he will himself inherit rest after his present toil, and that they will suffer eternal torments after their present exultation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:256
verses.text: And if faith worketh by love, let him love his enemies also, and, as far as in him lies, have the will to profit them; for thus he will prevent their injuring him when they have the will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:257
verses.text: And whenever perchance they have received power to hurt and tyrannize; let him lift his heart above, where no man hurteth him, well taught and chastened in the law of God, that he may "have patience given him in the days of adversity, until the pit be digged up for the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:258
verses.text: This I say, brethren, that ye may profit from what ye have heard, and ruminate within yourselves: permit not yourselves to forget, not only by thinking over again upon these subjects, and discoursing upon them, but also by so living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:259
verses.text: For a good life which is led after God's commands, is like a pen, because it is heard writing in our hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 94:260
verses.text: If it were written on wax, it would easily be blotted out: write it in your hearts, in your character, and it shall never be blotted out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:1
verses.text: Psalm XCV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:2
verses.text: I could wish, brethren, that we were rather listening to our father: but even this is a good thing, to obey our father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:3
verses.text: Since therefore he who deigneth to  pray for us, hath ordered us, I will speak unto you, beloved, what from the  present Psalm Jesus Christ our common Lord shall deign to give us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:4
verses.text: Now the title of the Psalm is "David's Song of praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:5
verses.text: The "Song of praise" signifieth both cheerfulness, in that it is a song; and devotion, for it is praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:6
verses.text: For what ought a man to praise more than that which pleaseth him so, that it is impossible that it can displease him? In the praising of God therefore we praise with security.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:7
verses.text: There he who praiseth is safe, where he feareth not lest he be ashamed for the object of his praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:8
verses.text: Let us therefore both praise and sing ; that is, let us praise with cheerfulness and joy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:9
verses.text: But what we are about to praise, this Psalm in the following verses showeth us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:10
verses.text: "O come, let us sing unto the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:11
verses.text: He calleth us to a great banquet of joy, not one of this world, but in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:12
verses.text: For if there were not in this life a wicked joy which is to be distinguished from a righteous joy, it would be enough to say, "Come, let us rejoice;" but he has briefly distinguished it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:13
verses.text: What is it to rejoice aright? To rejoice in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:14
verses.text: Thou shouldest piously joy in the Lord, if thou dost wish safely to trample upon the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:15
verses.text: But what is the word, "Come"? Whence doth He call them to come, with whom he wisheth to rejoice in the Lord; except that, while they are afar, they may by coming draw nearer, by drawing nearer they may approach, and by approaching rejoice? But whence are they afar? Can a man be locally distant from Him who is everywhere?It is not by place, but by being unlike Him, that a man is afar from God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:16
verses.text: What is to be unlike Him? it meaneth, a bad life, bad habits; for if by good habits we approach God, by bad habits we recede from God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:17
verses.text: If therefore by unlikeness we recede from God, by likeness we approach unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:18
verses.text: What likeness? That after which we were created, which by sinning we had corrupted in ourselves, which we have received again through the remission of sins, which is renewed in us in the mind within, that it may be engraved a second time as if on coin, that is, the image of our God upon our soul, and that we may return to His treasures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:19
verses.text: "Let us make a joyful noise unto God, our salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:20
verses.text: Consider, beloved, those who make a joyful noise in any ordinary songs, as in a sort of competition of worldly joy; and ye see them while reciting the written lines bursting forth with a joy, that the tongue sufficeth not to express the measure of; how they shout, indicating by that utterance the feeling of the mind, which cannot in words express what is conceived in the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:21
verses.text: If they then in earthly joy make a joyful noise; might we not do so from heavenly joy, which truly we cannot express in words?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:22
verses.text: "Let us prevent His face by confession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:23
verses.text: Confession hath a double meaning in Scripture.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:24
verses.text: There is a confession of him who praiseth, there is that of him who groaneth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:25
verses.text: The confession of praise pertaineth to the honour of Him who is praised: the confession of groaning to the repentance of him who confesseth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:26
verses.text: For men confess when they praise God: they confess when they accuse themselves; and the tongue hath no more worthy use.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:27
verses.text: Truly, I believe these to be the very vows, of which he speaketh in another Psalm: "I will pay Thee my vows, which I distinguished with my lips".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:28
verses.text: Nothing is more elevated than that distinguishing, nothing is so necessary both to understand and to do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:29
verses.text: How then dost thou distinguish the vows which thou payest unto God? By praising Him, by accusing thyself; because it is His mercy, to forgive us our sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:30
verses.text: For if He chose to deal with us after our deserts, He would find cause only to condemn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:31
verses.text: "O come," he said therefore, that we may at last go back from our sins, and that He may not cast up with us our accounts for the past; but that as it were a new account may be commenced, all the bonds of our debts having been burnt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:32
verses.text: The more therefore thou despairedst of thyself on account of thy iniquities, do thou confess thy sins; for so much greater is the praise of Him who forgiveth, as is the fulness of the penitent's confession more abundant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:33
verses.text: Let us not therefore imagine that we have receded from the song of praise, in understanding here that confession by which we acknowledge our transgressions: this is even a part of the song of praise; for when we confess our sins, we praise the glory of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:34
verses.text: "And make a joyful noise unto Him with Psalms".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:35
verses.text: We have already said what it is "to make a joyful noise:" the word is repeated, that it may be confirmed by the act: the very repetition is an exhortation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:36
verses.text: For we have not forgotten, so as to wish to be again admonished what was said above, that we should make a joyful noise: but usually in passages of strong feeling a well-known word is repeated, not to make it more familiar, but that the very repetition may strengthen the impression made: for it is repeated that we may understand the feeling of the speaker.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:37
verses.text: Hear now: "For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods"  "For the Lord will not cast off His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:38
verses.text: Praise be unto Him, and shouts of joy be unto Him! What people shall He not cast off? we have no right to make our own explanation here: for the Apostle hath prescribed this unto us, he hath explained whereof it is said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:39
verses.text: For this was the Jewish people, the people where were the prophets, the people where were the patriarchs, the people begotten according to the flesh from the seed of Abraham; the people in which all the mysteries which promised our Saviour preceded us; the people among whom was instituted the temple, the anointing, the Priest for a figure, that when all these shadows were past, the Light itself might come; this therefore was the people of God; to it were the prophets sent, in it those who were sent were born; to it were delivered and entrusted the revelations of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:40
verses.text: What then? is the whole of that people condemned? far be it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:41
verses.text: It is called the good olive-tree by the Apostle, for it commenced with the patriarchs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:42
verses.text: This then is the tree itself: though some of its boughs have been broken, yet all have not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:43
verses.text: For if all the boughs were broken, whence is Peter? whence John? whence Thomas? whence Matthew? whence Andrew? whence are all those Apostles? whence that very Apostle Paul who was speaking to us but now, and by his own fruit bearing witness to the good olive? Were not all these of that people? Whence also those five hundred brethren to whom our Lord appeared after His resurrection? Whence were so many thousands at the words of Peter (when the Apostles, filled with the Holy Spirit, spoke with the tongues of all nations) converted with such zeal for the honour of God and their own accusation, that they who first shed the Lord's blood in their rage, learnt how to drink it now that they believed? And all these five thousand were so converted that they sold their own property, and laid the price of it at the Apostles' feet That which one rich man did not do, when he heard from the Lord's mouth, and sorrowfully departed from Him, this so many thousands of those men by whose hands Christ had been crucified, did on a sudden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:44
verses.text: In proportion as the wound was deeper in their own hearts, with the greater eag erness did they seek for a physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:45
verses.text: Since therefore all these were from thence, the Psalm saith of them, "For the Lord will not cast off His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:46
verses.text: What doth the Psalm add? "In His hand are all the corners of the earth" : we recognise the corner stone: the corner stone is Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:47
verses.text: There cannot be a corner, unless it hath united in itself two walls: they come from different sides to one corner, but they are not opposed to each other in the corner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:48
verses.text: The circumcision cometh from one side: the uncircumcision from the other; in Christ both peoples have met together: because He hath become the stone, of which it is written, "The stone which the builders rejected, hath become the head of the corner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:49
verses.text: "For the sea is His and He made it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:50
verses.text: For the sea is this world, but God made also the sea: nor can the waves rage save only so far as to the shore, where He hath marked their bounds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:51
verses.text: There is therefore no temptation, that hath not received its measure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:52
verses.text: "And His hands prepared the dry land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:53
verses.text: Be thou the dry land: thirst for the grace of God: that as a sweet shower it may come upon thee, may find in thee fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:54
verses.text: He alloweth not the waves to cover what He hath sown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:55
verses.text: "And His hands prepared the dry land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:56
verses.text: Hence also therefore let us shout unto the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:57
verses.text: "O come, let us worship, and fall down to Him; and mourn before the Lord our Maker".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:58
verses.text: Perhaps thou art burning with the consciousness of a fault; blot out with tears the flame of thy sin: mourn before the Lord: fearlessly mourn before the Lord, who made thee; for He despiseth not the work of His own hands in thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:59
verses.text: Think not thou canst be restored by thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:60
verses.text: By thyself thou mayest fall off, thou canst not restore thyself: He who made thee restoreth thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:61
verses.text: "Let us mourn before the Lord our Maker:" weep before Him, confess unto Him, prevent His face in confession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:62
verses.text: For who art thou who mournest before Him, and confessest unto Him, but one whom He created? The thing created hath no slight confidence in Him who created it, and that in no indifferent fashion, but according to His own image and likeness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:63
verses.text: "For He is the Lord our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:64
verses.text: But that we may without fear fall down and kneel before Him, what are we? "We are the people of His pasture, and the sheep of His hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:65
verses.text: See how elegantly he hath transposed the order of the words, and as it were not given its own attribute to each word; that we may understand these very same to be the sheep, who are also the people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:66
verses.text: He said not, the sheep of His pasture, and the people of His hand; which might be thought more congruous, since the sheep belong to the pasture; but He said, "the people of His pasture".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:67
verses.text: The people are therefore sheep, since he saith, "the people of His pasture:" the people themselves are sheep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:68
verses.text: He praiseth these sheep also in the Song of Solomon, speaking of some perfect ones as the teeth of His Spouse the Holy Church: "Thy teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn, which come up from the washing; whereof every one beareth twins, and there is none barren".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:69
verses.text: What meaneth, "Thy teeth"? These by whom thou speakest: for the teeth of the Church are those through whom she speaketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:70
verses.text: Of what sort are thy teeth? "Like a flock of sheep that are shorn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:71
verses.text: Why, "that are shorn"? Because they have laid aside the burdens of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:72
verses.text: Were not those sheep, of which I was a little before speaking, shorn, whom the bidding of God had shorn, when He saith, "Go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor; and thou shalt find treasure in heaven: and come and follow Me"? They performed this bidding: shorn they came.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:73
verses.text: And because those who believe in Christ are baptized, what is there said? "which come up from the washing;" that is, come up from the cleansing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:74
verses.text: "Whereof every one beareth twins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:75
verses.text: What twins? Those two commandments, wherefrom hang all the Law and the Prophets.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:76
verses.text: Therefore, "To-day if ye will hear His voice, harden not your hearts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:77
verses.text: O my people, the people of God! God addresses His people: not only the people of His which He shall not cast off, but also all His people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:78
verses.text: For He speaketh in the corner stone to each wall: that is, prophecy speaketh in Christ, both to the people of the Jews, and the people of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:79
verses.text: For some time ye heard His voice through Moses, and hardened your hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:80
verses.text: He then, when you hardened your hearts, spoke through a herald; He now speaketh by Himself, let your hearts soften.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:81
verses.text: He who used to send heralds before Him, hath now deigned to come Himself; He here speaketh by His own mouth, He who used to speak by the mouths of the Prophets.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:82
verses.text: "As in the provocation, and in the day of temptation in the wilderness, where your fathers proved Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:83
verses.text: Let such be no more your fathers: imitate them not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:84
verses.text: They were your fathers, but if ye do not imitate them, they shall not be your fathers: yet as ye were born of them, they were your fathers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:85
verses.text: And if the heathen who came from the ends of the earth, in the words of Jeremias, "The Gentiles shall come unto Thee from the ends of the earth, and shall say, Surely our forefathers have inherited lies, vanity, and things wherein there is no profit:" if the heathen forsook their idols, to come to the God of Israel; ought Israel whom their own God led from Egypt through the Red Sea, wherein He overwhelmed their pursuing foes; whom He led out into the wilderness, fed with manna, never took His rod from correcting them, never deprived them of the blessings of His mercy; ought they to desert their own God, when the heathen have come unto Him? "When your fathers tempted Me, proved Me, and saw My works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:86
verses.text: "Forty years long was I very near unto this generation, and said, It is a people that do always err in their hearts; for they have not known My ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:87
verses.text: The forty years have the same meaning as the word "always".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:88
verses.text: For that number forty indicates the fulness of ages, as if the ages were perfected in this number.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:89
verses.text: Hence our Lord fasted forty days, forty days He was tempted in the desert, and forty days He was with His disciples after His resurrection On the first forty days He showed us temptation, on the latter forty days consolation: since beyond doubt when we are tempted we are consoled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:90
verses.text: For His body, that is, the Church, must needs suffer temptations in this world: but that Comforter, who said, "Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world," is not wanting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:91
verses.text: For this was I with them forty years, to show such a race of men, which alway provoketh Me, even unto the end of the world: because by those forty years He meant to signify the whole of this world's duration.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:92
verses.text: We began with exulting joy: but this Psalm hath ended with great fear: "Unto whom I sware in My wrath, that they should not enter into My rest".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:93
verses.text: It is a great thing for God to speak: how much greater for Him to swear? Thou shouldest fear a man when he sweareth, lest he do somewhat on account of his oath against his will: how much more shouldest thou fear God, when He sweareth, seeing He can swear nought rashly? He chose the act of swearing for a confirmation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:94
verses.text: And by whom doth God swear? By Himself: for He hath no greater by whom to swear By Himself He confirmeth His promises: by Himself He confirmeth His threats.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:95
verses.text: Let no man say in his heart, His promise is true; His threat is false: as His promise is true, so is His threat sure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 95:96
verses.text: Thou oughtest to be equally assured of rest, of happiness, of eternity, of immortality, if thou hast executed His commandments; as of destruction, of the burning of eternal fire, of damnation with the devil, if thou hast despised His commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:1
verses.text: Psalm XCVI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:2
verses.text: My lord and brother Severus still defers the pleasure we shall feel in his discourse, which he oweth us; for he acknowledgeth, that he is held a debtor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:3
verses.text: For all the Churches through which he hath passed, by his tongue the lord hath gladdened: much more therefore ought that Church to be rejoiced, out of which the Lord hath propagated his preaching among the rest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:4
verses.text: But what shall we do, but obey his will? I said, however, brethren, that he deferred, not that he defrauded us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:5
verses.text: Therefore let us keep him as a debtor bound, and release him not until he hath paid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:6
verses.text: Attend therefore, beloved: as far as the Lord alloweth, let us say somewhat of this Psalm, which indeed you already know; for the fresh mention of truth  is sweet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:7
verses.text: Possibly when its title was pronounced, some heard it with wonder.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:8
verses.text: For the Psalm is inscribed: "When the house was being built after the  Captivity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:9
verses.text: This title having been prefixed, ye were perhaps expecting in the text of the Psalm to hear what stones were hewn from the mountains, what masses were drawn to the spot, what foundations were laid, what beams were placed on high, what columns raised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:10
verses.text: Its song is of nothing of this kind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:11
verses.text: It is no such house that is in building; for behold where it is built, not in one spot, not in any particular region.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:12
verses.text: For thus he beginneth:—.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:13
verses.text: "O sing unto the Lord a new song; sing unto the Lord, all the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:14
verses.text: If all the earth singeth a new song, it is thus building while it singeth: the very act of singing is building: but only, if it singeth not the old song.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:15
verses.text: The lust of the flesh singeth the old song: the love of God singeth the new.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:16
verses.text: Hear why it is a new song: the Lord saith, "A new commandment I give unto you, that ye love one another".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:17
verses.text: The whole earth then singeth a new song: there the house of God is built.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:18
verses.text: All the earth is the house of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:19
verses.text: If all the earth is the house of God, he who clingeth not to all the earth, is a ruin, not a house; that old ruin whose shadow that ancient temple represented.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:20
verses.text: For there what was old was destroyed, that what was new might be built up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:21
verses.text: The Apostle bindeth us together into this very structure, and fasteneth us when bound together in that unity, saying, "Forbearing one another in love; endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:22
verses.text: Where there is this unity of Spirit, there is one stone; but one stone formed out of many.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:23
verses.text: How one formed out of many? By forbearing one another in love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:24
verses.text: Therefore the house of the Lord our God is in building; it is this that is being wrought, for this are these words, for this these readings, for this the preaching of the Gospel over the whole world; as yet it is in building.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:25
verses.text: This house hath increased greatly, and filled many nations: nevertheless, it hath not yet prevailed through all nations: by its increase it hath held many, and will prevail over all: and it is gainsaid by those who boast of their being of its household, and who say, it hath already lost ground.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:26
verses.text: It still increaseth, still all those nations which have not yet believed are destined to believe; that no man may say, will that tongue believe? will the barbarians believe? what is the meaning of the Holy Spirit having appeared in the fiery tongues,  except that there is no tongue so hard that it cannot be softened by that fire? For we know that many barbarous nations have already believed in Christ: Christ already possesseth regions where the Roman empire hath never yet reached; what is as yet closed to those who fight with the sword, is not closed to Him who fighteth with wood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:27
verses.text: For "the Lord hath reigned from the wood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:28
verses.text: Who is it who fighteth with wood? Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:29
verses.text: With His cross He hath vanquished kings, and fixed upon their forehead, when vanquished, that very cross; and they glory in it, for in it is their salvation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:30
verses.text: This is the work which is being wrought, thus the house increaseth, thus it is building: and that ye may know, hear the following verses of the Psalm: see them labouring upon, and constructing the house.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:31
verses.text: "O sing unto the Lord all the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:32
verses.text: "Sing unto the Lord, bless His Name: be telling good tidings of His salvation from day to day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:33
verses.text: How doth the building increase? "Be telling," he saith, "good tidings of His salvation from day to day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:34
verses.text: Let it be preached from day to day; from day to day, he saith, let it be built; let My house, saith God, increase.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:35
verses.text: And as if it were said by the workmen, Where dost Thou command it to be built? Where dost Thou will Thy house to increase? Choose for us some level, spacious spot, if Thou wish an ample house built Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:36
verses.text: Where dost Thou bid us be telling good tidings from day to day? He showeth the place: "Declare His honour unto the heathen:" His honour, not yours.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:37
verses.text: O ye builders, "Declare His honour unto the heathen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:38
verses.text: Should ye choose to declare your own honour, ye shall fall: if His, ye shall be built up, while ye are building.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:39
verses.text: Therefore they who choose to declare their own honour, have refused to dwell in that house; and therefore they sing not a new song with all the earth For they do not share it with the whole round world; and hence they are not building in the house, but have erected a whited wall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:40
verses.text: How sternly doth God threaten the whited wall? There are innumerable testimonies of the Prophets, whence He curseth the whited wall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:41
verses.text: What is the whited wall, save hypocrisy, that is, pretence? Without it is bright, within it is dirt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:42
verses.text: A certain person, speaking of this whited wall, said thus: "as, if in a wall which standeth alone, and is not connected with any other walls, you make a door, whoever enters, is out of doors; so in that part which hath refused to sing the new song together with the house, but hath chosen to build a wall, and that a whited one, and not solid, what availeth it that it hath a door?" If thou enterest, thou art found to be without.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:43
verses.text: For because they themselves did not enter by the door, their door also doth not admit them within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:44
verses.text: For the Lord saith, "I am the door: by Me they enter in".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:45
verses.text: "Declare His honour unto the heathen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:46
verses.text: What is, unto the heathen? Perhaps by nations but a few are meant: and that part which hath raised the whited wall hath still somewhat to say: why are not Getulia, Numidia, Mauritania, Byzacium, nations? Provinces are nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:47
verses.text: Let the word of God take the word from hypocrisy, from the whited wall, building up the house over the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:48
verses.text: It is not enough to say, "Declare His honour unto the heathen;" that thou mayest not think any nations excepted, he addeth, "and His wonders unto all people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:49
verses.text: "For the Lord is great, and cannot worthily be praised".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:50
verses.text: What Lord, except Jesus Christ, "is great, and cannot worthily be praised"? Ye know surely that He appeared as a Man: ye know surely that He was conceived in a woman's womb, ye know that He was born from the womb, that He was suckled, that He was carried in arms, circumcised, that a victim was offered for Him, that He grew; lastly, ye know that He was buffeted, spit upon, crowned with thorns, was crucified, died, was pierced with a spear; ye know that He suffered all these things: "He is great, and cannot worthily be praised".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:51
verses.text: Despise not what is little, understand what is great.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:52
verses.text: He became little, because ye were such: let Him be acknowledged great, and in Him ye shall be great.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:53
verses.text: For what can a small tongue say towards the praise of the Great One? By saying, Beyond praise, he hath spoken, and hath given to imagination what it may conceive: as if saying, What I cannot utter, do thou reflect on; and when thou shalt have reflected, it will not be enough.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:54
verses.text: What no man's thought uttereth, doth any man's tongue utter? "The Lord is great, and cannot worthily be praised".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:55
verses.text: Let Him be praised, and preached: His honour declared, and His house built.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:56
verses.text: For the spot where he wished to build the house, is itself woody, where it was said yesterday, "we found it in the wood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:57
verses.text: For he was seeking that very house, when he said, "in the wood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:58
verses.text: And why is that spot woody? Men used to worship images: it is not wonderful that they fed hogs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:59
verses.text: For that son who left his father, and spent his all on harlots, living as a prodigal, used to feed hogs, that is, to worship devils; and by this very superstition of the heathen, all the earth became a wood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:60
verses.text: But he who buildeth a house, rooteth up the wood; and for this reason it was said, "While the house was being built, after the captivity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:61
verses.text: For men were held captive under the devil, and served devils; but they were redeemed from captivity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:62
verses.text: They could sell, but they could not redeem themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:63
verses.text: The Redeemer came, and gave a price; He poured forth His Blood, and bought the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:64
verses.text: Ye ask what He bought? Ye see what He hath given; find out then what He bought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:65
verses.text: The Blood of Christ was the price.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:66
verses.text: What is equal to this? What, but the whole world? What, but all nations? They are very ungrateful for their price, or very proud, who say that the price is so small that it bought the Africans only; or that they are so great, as that it was given for them alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:67
verses.text: Let them not then exult, let them not be proud: He gave what He gave for the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:68
verses.text: He knew what He bought, because He knew at what price He bought it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:69
