verses.text: Thus because we are redeemed, the house is built after the captivity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:70
verses.text: And who are they who held us in captivity? Because they to whom it is said, "Declare His honour," are the clearers of the wood: that they may root out the wood, free the earth from captivity, and build, and raise up, by declaring the greatness of the Lord's house.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:71
verses.text: How is the wood of devils cleared away, unless He who is above them all be preached? All nations then had devils for their gods: those whom they called gods, were devils, as the Apostle more openly saith, "The things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice unto devils, and not to God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:72
verses.text: Since therefore they were in captivity, because they sacrificed to devils, and on that account the whole earth had remained woody; He is declared to be great, and above all worldly praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:73
verses.text: For when he had said, "He is more to be feared than all gods:" he added, "As for all the gods of the heathen, they are devils".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:74
verses.text: Because "all the gods of the heathen are devils".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:75
verses.text: And is this all the praise of Him who cannot worthily be praised, that He is above all the gods of the heathen, which are devils? Wait, and hear what followeth: "It is the Lord that made the heavens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:76
verses.text: Not above all gods only therefore, but above all the heavens which He made, is the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:77
verses.text: If he were to say, "above all gods, for the gods of the heathen are devils," and if the praise of our Lord stopped here, he had said less than we are accustomed to think of Christ; but when he said, "But it is the Lord that made the heavens;" see what difference there is between the heavens and devils: and what between the heavens and Him who made the heavens; behold how exalted is the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:78
verses.text: He said not, But the Lord sitteth above the heavens; for perhaps some one else might be imagined to have made them, upon which He was enthroned: but, "It is the Lord that made the heavens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:79
verses.text: If He made the heavens, He made the Angels also: Himself made the Angels, Himself made the Apostles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:80
verses.text: The devils yielded to the Apostles: but the Apostles themselves were heavens, who bore the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:81
verses.text: O heavens, which He made, declare His honour unto the heathen! Let His house be built throughout the earth, let all the earth sing a new song.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:82
verses.text: "Confession and beauty are before Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:83
verses.text: Dost thou love beauty? Wishest thou to be beautiful? Confess! He said not, beauty and confession, but confession and beauty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:84
verses.text: Thou wast foul; confess, that thou mayest be fair: thou wast a sinner; confess, that thou mayest be righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:85
verses.text: Thou couldest deform thyself: thou canst not make thyself beautiful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:86
verses.text: But of what sort is our Betrothed, who hath loved one deformed, that he might make her fair? How, saith some one, loved He one deformed? "I came not," said He, "to call the righteous, but sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:87
verses.text: Whom callest Thou? sinners, that they may remain sinners? No, saith He.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:88
verses.text: And by what means will they cease to be sinners? "Confession and beauty are before Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:89
verses.text: They honour Him by confession of their sins, they vomit the evils which they had greedily devoured; they return not to their vomit, like the unclean dog; and there will then be confession and beauty: we love beauty; let us first choose confession, that beauty may follow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:90
verses.text: Again, there is one who loveth power and greatness: he wisheth to be great as the Angels are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:91
verses.text: There is a certain greatness in the Angels; and such power, that if the Angels exert it to the full, it cannot be withstood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:92
verses.text: And every man desireth the power of the Angels, but their righteousness every man loveth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:93
verses.text: First love righteousness, and power shall follow thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:94
verses.text: For what followeth here? "Holiness and greatness are in His sanctification".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:95
verses.text: Thou wast before seeking for greatness: first love righteousness: when thou art righteous, thou shall also be great.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:96
verses.text: For if thou preposterously dost wish first to be great, thou fallest before thou canst rise: for thou dost not rise, thou art raised up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:97
verses.text: Thou risest better, if He raise thee who falleth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:98
verses.text: For He who falleth not descendeth unto thee: thou hadst fallen: He descendeth, He hath stretched forth His hand unto thee; thou canst not rise by thy own strength, embrace the hand of Him who descendeth, that thou mayest be raised up by the Strong One.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:99
verses.text: What then? If "confession and beauty are before Him: holiness and greatness in His sanctification".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:100
verses.text: This we declare, when we are building the house; behold, it is already declared unto the heathen; what ought the heathen to do, to whom those who have cleared away the wood have declared the Lord's honour? He now saith to the heathen themselves, "Ascribe unto the Lord, O ye kindreds of the people: ascribe unto the Lord worship and honour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:101
verses.text: Ascribe them not unto yourselves: because they also who have declared it unto you, have not declared their own, but His honour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:102
verses.text: Do ye then "ascribe unto the Lord worship and honour;" and say, "Not unto us, O Lord, not unto us: but unto Thy Name give the praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:103
verses.text: Put not your trust in man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:104
verses.text: If each of you is baptized, let him say: He baptizeth me, of whom the friend of the Bridegroom said, "He baptizeth with the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:105
verses.text: For when ye say this, ye ascribe unto the Lord worship and honour: "Ascribe unto the Lord worship and honour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:106
verses.text: "Ascribe unto the Lord glory unto His Name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:107
verses.text: Not unto the name of man, not unto your own name, but unto His ascribe worship.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:108
verses.text: Confession is a present unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:109
verses.text: O heathen, if ye will enter into His courts, enter not empty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:110
verses.text: "Bring presents".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:111
verses.text: What presents shall we bring with us? The sacrifice of God is a troubled spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, "O God, shalt not Thou despise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:112
verses.text: Enter with an humble heart into the house of God, and thou hast entered with a present.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:113
verses.text: But if thou art proud, thou enterest empty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:114
verses.text: For whence wouldest thou be proud, if thou wert not empty? For if thou wast full, thou wouldest not be puffed up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:115
verses.text: How couldest thou be full? If thou wert to bring a present, which thou shouldest carry to the courts of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:116
verses.text: Let us not retain you much longer: let us run over what remaineth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:117
verses.text: Behold the house increasing: behold the edifice pervade the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:118
verses.text: Rejoice, because ye have entered into the courts; rejoice, because ye are being built into the temple of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:119
verses.text: For those who enter are themselves built up, they themselves are the house of God: He is the inhabitor, for whom the house is built over the whole world, and this "after the captivity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:120
verses.text: "Bring presents, and come into His courts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:121
verses.text: "O worship the Lord in His holy court" : in the Catholic Church; this is His holy court.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:122
verses.text: Let no man say, "Lo, here is Christ, or there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:123
verses.text: For there shall arise false prophets".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:124
verses.text: Say this unto them, "There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:125
verses.text: Ye are calling me to the whited wall; I adore my God in His holy court.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:126
verses.text: "Let the whole earth be moved before His face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:127
verses.text: "Tell it out among the nations, that the Lord reigneth from the wood: and that it is He who hath made the round world so fast that it cannot be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:128
verses.text: What testimonies of the building of the house of God! The clouds of heaven thunder out throughout the world that God's house is being built; and the frogs cry from the marsh, We alone are Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:129
verses.text: What testimonies do I bring forward? That of the Psalter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:130
verses.text: I bring forward what thou singest as one deaf: open thine ears; thou singest this; thou singest with me, and thou agreest not with me; thy tongue soundeth what mine doth, and yet thine heart disagreeth with mine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:131
verses.text: Dost thou not sing this? Behold the testimonies of the whole world: "Let the whole earth be moved before His face:" and dost thou say, that thou art not moved? "Tell it out among the heathen, that the Lord hath reigned from the wood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:132
verses.text: Shall men perchance prevail here, and say they reign by wood, because they reign by means of the clubs of their bandits? Reign by the Cross of Christ, if thou art to reign by wood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:133
verses.text: For this wood of t hine maketh thee wooden: the wood of Christ passeth thee across the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:134
verses.text: Thou hearest the Psalm saying, "He hath set aright the round world, that it cannot be moved;" and thou sayest it hath not only been moved since it was made fast, but hath also decreased.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:135
verses.text: Dost thou speak the truth, and the Psalmist falsehood? Do the false prophets, when they cry out, "Lo, here is Christ, and there,"  speak truth; and doth this Prophet lie? Brethren, against these most open words ye hear in the corners rumours like these; "such an one was a traditor," and, "such an one was a traditor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:136
verses.text: What dost thou say? Are thy words, or the words of God, to be heard? For, "it is He who hath set aright the round world, that it cannot be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:137
verses.text: I show unto thee the round world built: bring thy present, and come into the courts of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:138
verses.text: Thou hast no presents: and on that account thou art not willing to enter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:139
verses.text: What is this? If God were to appoint unto thee a bull, goat, or ram, for a present, thou wouldest find one to bring: He hath appointed a humble heart, and thou wilt not enter; for thou findest not this in thyself, because thou art swollen with pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:140
verses.text: "He hath set aright the round world, that it cannot be moved: and He shall judge the people righteously".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:141
verses.text: Then shall they mourn, who now refuse to love righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:142
verses.text: "Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:143
verses.text: Let the heavens, which declare the glory of God, rejoice; let the heavens rejoice, which the Lord made; let the earth be glad, which the heavens rain upon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:144
verses.text: For the heavens are the preachers, the earth the listeners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:145
verses.text: "Let the sea be stirred up, and the fulness thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:146
verses.text: What sea? The world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:147
verses.text: The sea hath been stirred up, and the fulness thereof: the whole world was roused up against the Church, while it was being extended and built over all the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:148
verses.text: Concerning this stirring up, ye have heard in the Gospel, "They shall deliver you up to councils".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:149
verses.text: "The sea was stirred up: but how should the sea ever conquer Him who made it?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:150
verses.text: "The plains shall be joyful, and all things that are in them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:151
verses.text: All the meek, all the gentle, all the righteous, are the "plains" of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:152
verses.text: "Then shall all the trees of the woods rejoice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:153
verses.text: The trees of the woods are the heathen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:154
verses.text: Why do they rejoice? Because they were cut off from the wild olive, and engraffed into the good olive "Then shall all the trees of the woods rejoice:" because huge cedars and cypresses have been cut down, and undecaying timbers have been bought for the building of the house.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:155
verses.text: They were trees of the woods; but before they were sent to the building: they were trees of the woods, but before they produced the olive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:156
verses.text: "Before the face of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:157
verses.text: For He cometh, for He cometh to judge the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:158
verses.text: He came at first, and will come again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:159
verses.text: He first came in His Church in clouds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:160
verses.text: What are the clouds which bore Him? The Apostles who preached, respecting whom ye have heard, when the Epistle was being read: "We are ambassadors," he saith, "for Christ: we pray you in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:161
verses.text: These are the clouds in whom He cometh, excepting His last Advent, when He will come to judge the quick and the dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:162
verses.text: He came first in the clouds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:163
verses.text: This was His first voice which sounded forth in the Gospel: "From this time shall they see the Son of Man coming in the clouds".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:164
verses.text: What is, "from this time"? Will not the Lord come in later times, when all the tribes of the earth shall mourn? He first came in His own preachers, and filled the whole round world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:165
verses.text: Let us not resist His first coming, that we may not tremble at His second.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:166
verses.text: "But woe to them that are with child, and that give suck in those days!" Ye have heard but now in the Gospel: "Take ye heed, for ye know not at what hour He cometh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:167
verses.text: This is said figuratively.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:168
verses.text: Who are those with child, and who give suck? Those who are with child, are the souls whose hope is in the world: but those who have gained what they hoped for, are meant by "they who give suck".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:169
verses.text: For example: one wisheth to buy a country seat; he is with child, for his object is not gained as yet, the womb swelleth in hope: he buyeth it; he hath brought forth, he now giveth suck to what he hath bought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:170
verses.text: "Woe to them that are with child, and that give suck in those days!" Woe to those who put their hope in the world; woe to them that cling to those things which they brought forth through hope in the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:171
verses.text: What then should the Christian do? He should use, not serve, the world What is this? Those that have as those that have not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:172
verses.text: He who is without carefulness, waiteth without fear for his Lord's coming.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:173
verses.text: For what sort of love is it of Christ, to fear lest He come? Brethren, are we not ashamed? We love Him, and yet we fear lest He come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:174
verses.text: Are we sure that we love Him? or do we love our sins more? Therefore let us hate our sins for their own sake, and love Him who will come to punish our sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:175
verses.text: He will come, whether we like or not: for because He cometh not just now, it is no reason that He will not come at all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:176
verses.text: He will come, and when thou knowest not; and if He shall find thee ready, thy ignorance is no hurt to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:177
verses.text: "Then shall all the trees of the wood rejoice before the Lord; for He cometh:" at His first coming.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:178
verses.text: And what afterwards? "For He cometh to judge the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:179
verses.text: And all the trees of the woods shall rejoice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:180
verses.text: He came first: and later to judge the earth: He shall find those rejoicing who believed in His first coming, "for He cometh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:181
verses.text: "For with righteousness shall He judge the world:" not a part of it, for He bought not a part: He will judge the whole, for it was the whole of which He paid the price.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:182
verses.text: Ye have heard the Gospel, where it saith, that when He cometh, "He shall gather together His elect from the four winds".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:183
verses.text: He gathereth all His elect from the four winds: therefore from the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:184
verses.text: For Adam himself (this I had said before) signifieth in Greek the whole world; for there are four letters, A, D, A, and M.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:185
verses.text: But as the Greeks speak, the four quarters of the world have these initial letters, 'Ανατολὴ, they call the East; Δύσις, the West; ῎Αρκτος, the North; Μεσημβρία, the South: thou hast the word Adam.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:186
verses.text: Adam therefore hath been scattered over the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:187
verses.text: He was in one place, and fell, and as in a manner broken small, he filled the whole world: but the mercy of God gathered together the fragments from every side, and forged them by the fire of love, and made one what was broken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:188
verses.text: That Artist knew how to do this; let no one despair: it is indeed a great thing, but reflect who that Artist was.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:189
verses.text: He who made, restored: He who formed, reformed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:190
verses.text: What are righteousness and truth? He will gather together His elect with Him to the judgment, but the rest He will separate one from another; for He will place some on the right, others on the left hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 96:191
verses.text: But what is more just, what more true, than that they shall not expect mercy from their Judge, who have refused to act mercifully, before their Judge come? But those who chose to act with mercy, with mercy shall be judged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:1
verses.text: Psalm XCVII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:2
verses.text: This Psalm is entitled, "A Psalm of David's, when his land was restored".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:3
verses.text: Let us refer the whole to Christ, if we wish to keep the road of a right understanding: let us not depart from the corner stone, lest our understanding suffer a fall: in Him let that become fixed, which wavered with unstable motion; let that rest upon Him, which before was waving to and fro in uncertainty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:4
verses.text: Whatever doubt a man hath in his mind when he heareth the Scriptures of God, let him not depart from Christ; when Christ hath been revealed to him in the words, let him then be assured that he hath understood; but before he arriveth at the understanding of Christ, let him not presume that he hath understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:5
verses.text: "For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:6
verses.text: What doth this mean, and how are these words understood in Christ, "When his land was restored"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:7
verses.text: The earth restored is the resurrecti on of the flesh; for after His resur rection, all those things which are sung of in the Psalm were done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:8
verses.text: Let us then hear a Psalm full of joy on the restoration of the Earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:9
verses.text: Let the Lord our God excite in us a hope and a pleasure worthy of so great a thing; may He rule our discourse, that it be fit for your hearts, that whatever joy our heart doth feel in such sights, He may bring on to our tongue, and thence conduct it into your ears, then to your heart, thence to your actions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:10
verses.text: "The Lord is King, let the earth be glad: yea, let the multitude of the isles be joyous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:11
verses.text: It is so indeed, because the word of God hath been preached not in the continent alone, but also in those isles which lie in mid sea: even these are full of Christians, full of the servants of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:12
verses.text: For the sea doth not retard Him who made it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:13
verses.text: Where ships can approach, cannot the words of God? The isles are filled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:14
verses.text: But figuratively the isles may be taken for all the Churches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:15
verses.text: Why isles? Because the waves of all temptations roar around them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:16
verses.text: But as an isle may be beaten by the waves which on every side dash around it, yet cannot be broken, and rather itself doth break the advancing waves, than by them is broken: so also the Churches of God, springing up throughout the world, have suffered the persecutions of the ungodly, who roar around them on every side; and behold the isles stand fixed, and at last the sea is calmed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:17
verses.text: "Clouds and darkness are round about Him: righteousness and judgment are the direction of His seat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:18
verses.text: The Lord Himself saith: "For judgment I am come into this world; that they which see not might see, and that they which see might be made blind".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:19
verses.text: They who seem unto themselves to see, who think themselves wise, who think healing not needful for them, that they may be made blind, may not understand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:20
verses.text: And that "they which see not may see;" that they who confess their blindness may obtain to be enlightened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:21
verses.text: Let there be therefore "clouds and darkness round about Him," for those who have not understood Him: for those who confess and humble themselves, "righteousness and judgment are the direction of His seat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:22
verses.text: He called those who believe in Him His seat: for from them hath He made Himself a seat, since in them Wisdom sitteth; for the Son of God is the Wisdom of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:23
verses.text: But we have heard from another passage of Scripture a strong confirmation of this interpretation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:24
verses.text: "The soul of the righteous is the seat of Wisdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:25
verses.text: Because then they who have believed in Him have been made righteous: justified by faith, they have become His own seat: He sitteth in them, judging from them, and guiding them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:26
verses.text: "There shall go a fire before Him, and burn up His enemies on every side".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:27
verses.text: We remember having read in the Gospel, He shall say, "Depart into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:28
verses.text: I do not think it is said of that fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:29
verses.text: Why do I not? Because he speaketh of some fire, which shall go before Him, before He cometh to judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:30
verses.text: For it is said, that the fire goeth before Him, and burneth up His enemies on every side, that is, throughout the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:31
verses.text: That fire will burn after His advent: this, on the contrary, will go before Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:32
verses.text: What fire then is this?Behold, we have understood the fire that goeth before Him, that is to be understood of a kind of temporal punishment of the unbelieving and ungodly: let us understand the fire, if possible, of the salvation of the redeemed also; for thus we had proposed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:33
verses.text: The Lord Himself saith: "I am come to send fire on the earth:" "fire" in the same way as a "sword;" as in another passage He saith, that He was not come to send peace, but a sword, upon earth The sword to divide, the fire to burn: but each salutary: for the sword of His own word hath in salutary wise separated us from evil habits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:34
verses.text: For He brought a sword, and separated every believer either from his father who believed not in Christ, or from his mother in like manner unbelieving: or at least, if we were born of Christian parents, from his ancestors.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:35
verses.text: For no man among us had not either a grandsire, or great grandsire, or some ancestry among the heathen, and in that unbelief which is accursed before God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:36
verses.text: We are separated from that which we were before; but the sword which separateth, but slayeth not, hath cut between us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:37
verses.text: In the same way the fire also: "I am come to send fire upon the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:38
verses.text: Believers in Him were set on fire, they received the flame of love: and for this reason when the Holy Spirit itself had been sent to the Apostles, It thus appeared: "cloven tongues, like as of fire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:39
verses.text: Burning with this fire they set out on their march through the world, to burn and set on fire His enemies on every side.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:40
verses.text: What enemies of His? They who forsaking the God who made them, adored the idols they had made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:41
verses.text: "His lightnings gave shine unto the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:42
verses.text: This is great joy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:43
verses.text: Do we not see? is it not clear? His lightnings have shined unto the whole world: His enemies have been set on fire, and burnt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:44
verses.text: All that gainsaid hath been burnt, and "His lightnings have given shine unto the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:45
verses.text: How have they shone? That the world might at length believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:46
verses.text: Whence were the lightnings? From the clouds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:47
verses.text: What are the clouds of God? The preachers of the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:48
verses.text: But thou seest a cloud, misty and dark in the sky, and it hath I know not what hidden within it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:49
verses.text: If there be lightning from the cloud, a brightness shineth forth: from that which thou didst despise, hath burst forth that which thou mayest dread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:50
verses.text: Our Lord Jesus Christ therefore sent His Apostles, as His preachers, like clouds: they were seen as men, and were despised; as clouds appear, and are despised, until what thou wonderest at gleameth from them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:51
verses.text: For they were in the first place men encumbered with flesh, weak; then, men of low station, unlearned, ignoble: but there was within what could lighten forth; there was in them what could flash abroad.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:52
verses.text: Peter a fisherman approached, prayed, and the dead arose His human form was a cloud, the splendour of the miracle was the lightning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:53
verses.text: So in their words, so in their deeds, when they do things to be wondered at, and utter words to be wondered at, "His lightnings gave shine unto the world; the earth saw it, and was afraid".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:54
verses.text: Is it not true? Doth not the whole Christian world at length exclaim, Amen, afraid at the lightnings which burst forth from those clouds?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:55
verses.text: "The hills melted like wax at the presence of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:56
verses.text: Who are the hills? The proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:57
verses.text: Every high thing raising itself against God, at the deeds of Christ and of the Christians, trembled, yielded, and when I say, what hath been already said, "melted," a better word cannot be found.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:58
verses.text: "The hills melted like wax at the presence of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:59
verses.text: Where is the elevation of powers? where the hardness of the unbelieving? The Lord was a fire unto them, they melted at His presence like wax; so long hard, until that fire was applied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:60
verses.text: Every height hath been levelled; it dareth not now blaspheme Christ: and though the Pagan believeth not in Him, he blasphemeth Him not; though not as yet become a living stone, yet the hard hill hath been subdued.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:61
verses.text: "At the presence of the Lord of the whole earth:" not of the Jews only, but of the Gentiles also, as the Apostle saith; for He is not the God of the Jews alone, but of the Gentiles also He is therefore the Lord of the whole earth, the Lord Jesus Christ born in Judaea, but not born for Judaea alone, because before He was born He created all men; and He who created, also new created, all men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:62
verses.text: "The heavens have declared His righteousness: and all the people have seen His glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:63
verses.text: What heavens have declared? "The heavens declare the glory of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:64
verses.text: Who are the heavens? Those who have become His seat; for as God sitteth in the heavens, so doth He sit in the Apostles, so doth He sit in the preachers of the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:65
verses.text: Even thou, if thou wilt, shalt be a heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:66
verses.text: Dost thou wish to be so? Purge from thy heart the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:67
verses.text: If thou hast not earthly lusts, and hast not in vain uttered the response, that thou hast "lifted up thy heart," thou shalt be a heaven "If ye be risen with Christ," saith the Apostle to believers, "set your affection on things above, not on things of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:68
verses.text: Thou hast begun to set thine affection upon things above, not on things upon earth; hast thou not become a heaven? Thou carriest flesh, and in thy heart thou art already a heaven; for thy conversation will be in heaven Being such, thou also declarest Christ; for who of the faithful declareth not Christ?Therefore the whole Church preacheth Christ, and the heavens declare His righteousness; for all the faithful, whose care it is to gain unto God those who have not yet believed, and who do this from love, are heavens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:69
verses.text: From them God thundereth forth the terror of His judgment; and he who was unbelieving trembleth, and is alarmed, and believeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:70
verses.text: He shows unto men what power Christ had throughout the world, by pleading with them, and leading them to love Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:71
verses.text: For how many this day have led their friends either to some pantomimist, or flute-player? Why, except from their liking him? And do ye love Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:72
verses.text: For He who conquered the world hath exhibited such spectacles, as that no man can say that he findeth in them cause for blame.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:73
verses.text: For each person's favourite in the theatre is often vanquished there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:74
verses.text: But no man is vanquished in Christ: there is no reason for shame.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:75
verses.text: Seize, lead, draw, whom ye may: be without fear, ye are leading unto Him, who displeaseth not those who see Him; and ask ye Him to enlighten them, that they may behold to good account.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:76
verses.text: "Confounded be all they that worship carved images".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:77
verses.text: Hath not this come to pass? Have they not been confounded? Are they not daily confounded? For carved images are images wrought by the hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:78
verses.text: Why are all who worship carved images confounded? Because all people have seen His glory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:79
verses.text: All nations now confess the glory of Christ: let those who worship stones be ashamed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:80
verses.text: Because those stones were dead, we have found a living Stone; indeed those stones never lived, so that they cannot be called even dead; but our Stone is living, and hath ever lived with the Father, and though He died for us, He revived, and liveth now, and death shall no more have dominion over Him This glory of His the nations have acknowledged; they leave the temples, they run to the Churches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:81
verses.text: Do they still seek to worship carved images? Have they not chosen to forsake their idols? They have been forsaken by their idols.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:82
verses.text: "Who glory in their idols".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:83
verses.text: But there is a certain disputer who seemeth unto himself learned, and saith, I do not worship that stone, nor that image which is without sense;I worship not this image but I adore  what I see, and serve him whom I see not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:84
verses.text: Who is that? Some invisible deity, he replieth, who presideth over that image.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:85
verses.text: By giving this account of their images, they seem to themselves able disputants, because they do not worship idols, and yet do worship devils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:86
verses.text: "The things," brethren, saith the Apostle, "which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice unto devils, and not to God; we know that an idol is nothing: and that what the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils, and not to God; and I would not that ye should have fellowship with devils".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:87
verses.text: Let them not therefore excuse themselves on this ground, that they are not devoted to insensate idols; they are rather devoted to devils, which is more dangerous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:88
verses.text: For if they were only worshipping idols, as they would not help them, so they would not hurt them; but if thou worship and serve devils, they themselves will be thy masters.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:89
verses.text: But observe holy men, who are like the Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:90
verses.text: When thou hast found some holy man who serveth God, if thou wish to worship him instead of God, he forbiddeth thee: he will not arrogate to himself the honour due to God, he will not be unto thee as God, but be with thee under God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:91
verses.text: Thus did the holy Apostles Paul and Barnabas.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:92
verses.text: They preached the word of God in Lycaonia.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:93
verses.text: When they had performed wonderful works in Lycaonia, the people of that country brought victims, and wished to sacrifice to them, calling Barnabas Jupiter, and Paul Mercury: they were not pleased.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:94
verses.text: Did they perchance refuse to be sacrificed to, because they abhorred to be compared to devils? No, but because they shuddered at divine honour being paid to men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:95
verses.text: Their own words show this: it is no guess of ours; for the text of the book goeth on to say how they were movedJust then, as good men forbade those who had wished to worship them as gods, and wish rather that God alone be worshipped, God alone be adored, to God alone sacrifice be offered, not to themselves; so also all the holy Angels seek His glory whom they love; endeavour to impel and to excite to the contemplation of Him all whom they love: Him they declare to them, not themselves, since they are angels; and because they are soldiers, they study only how to seek the glory of their Captain; but if they have sought their own glory, they are condemned as usurpers Such were the devil and his angels; he claimed for himself divine honour, and for all his demons; he filled the Pagan temples, and persuaded them to offer images and sacrifices to himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:96
verses.text: Was it not better to worship holy Angels than devils? They answer: we do not worship devils; we worship angels, as ye call them, the powers and the ministers of the great God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:97
verses.text: I wish ye would worship them: ye would easily learn from themselves not to worship them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:98
verses.text: Hear an Angel teaching.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:99
verses.text: He was teaching a disciple of Christ, and showing him many wonders in the Revelation of John: and when some wonderful vision had been shown him, he trembled, and fell down at the Angel's feet; but that Angel, who sought not but the glory of God, said, "See thou do it not; for I am a fellow-servant of thee, and of thy brethren the prophets".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:100
verses.text: What then, my brethren? Let no man say, I fear lest the Angel may be angry with me, if I worship him not as my God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:101
verses.text: He is then angry with thee, when thou hast chosen to worship him: for he is righteous, and loveth God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:102
verses.text: As devils are angry if they are not worshipped, so are Angels angry if they are worshipped instead of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:103
verses.text: But lest the weak and trembling heart perchance say unto itself: If then the demons are incensed because they are not worshipped, I fear to offend them; what can even their chief the devil do unto thee? If he had any power over us no one of us would remain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:104
verses.text: Are not daily so many things said against him by the mouth of Christians, and yet the harvest of Christians increaseth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:105
verses.text: When thou art angry with the most depraved of thy slaves, thou givest him the name, "Satan," Devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:106
verses.text: Perhaps in this thou dost err, since thou sayest it to a man, and thy immoderate anger hurrieth thee to revile the image of God: and yet thou choosest a term thou deeply hatest, to apply to him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:107
verses.text: If he could, would he not revenge himself? But it is not allowed: and he doth so much only as is allowed him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:108
verses.text: For when he wished to tempt Job, he had to ask power to do so: and he could do nothing had he not received power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:109
verses.text: Why then dost thou not fearlessly worship God, without whose will no one hurteth thee, and by whose permission thou art chastened, not overcome? For if it shall have pleased the Lord thy God to permit some man to hurt thee, or some spirit: He will chasten thee, that thou mayest cry unto Him: "Confounded," therefore, "be all they that delight in vain gods: worship Him, all ye His angels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:110
verses.text: Let Pagans learn to worship God: they wish to worship Angels: let them imitate Angels, and worship Him who is worshipped by Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:111
verses.text: "Worship Him, all ye His angels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:112
verses.text: Let that Angel worship who was sent to Cornelius (for worshipping Him he sent Cornelius to Peter), himself Peter's fellow-servant; let him worship Christ, Peter's Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:113
verses.text: "Worship Him, all ye gods!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:114
verses.text: "Sion heard of it, and rejoiced".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:115
verses.text: What did Sion hear? That all His Angels worship Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:116
verses.text: For the Church was not as yet among the Gentiles; in Judaea the Jews had some of them believed, and the very Jews who believed thought that they only belonged to Christ: the Apostles were sent to the Gentiles, Cornelius was preached to; Cornelius believed, was baptized, and they who were with Cornelius were also baptized.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:117
verses.text: But ye know what happened, that they might be baptized: the reader indeed hath not reached this point, but, nevertheless, some recollect; and let those who do not recollect, hear briefly from me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:118
verses.text: The Angel was sent to Cornelius: the Angel sent Cornelius to Peter; Peter came to Cornelius.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:119
verses.text: And because Cornelius and his household were Gentiles, and uncircumcised: lest they might hesitate to give the Gospel to the uncircumcised: before Cornelius and his household were baptized, the Holy Spirit came, and filled them, and they began to speak with tongues.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:120
verses.text: Now the Holy Spirit had not fallen upon any one who had not been baptized: but upon these It fell before baptism.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:121
verses.text: For Peter might hesitate whether he might baptize the uncircumcised: the Holy Spirit came, they began to speak with tongues; the invisible gift was given, and took away all doubt about the visible Sacrament; they were all baptized.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:122
verses.text: What did Sion hear, and rejoice at? That the Gentiles also had received the word of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:123
verses.text: One wall had come, but the corner existed not as yet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:124
verses.text: The name Sion is here peculiarly given to the Church which was in Judaea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:125
verses.text: "Sion heard of it, and rejoiced: and the daughters of Judah were glad".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:126
verses.text: Thus it is written, "The apostles and brethren that were in Judaea heard".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:127
verses.text: See if the daughters of Judaea rejoiced not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:128
verses.text: What did they hear? "That the Gentiles had also received the word of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:129
verses.text: Therefore, "The daughters of Judah rejoiced because of Thy judgments, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:130
verses.text: What is, because of Thy judgments? Because in any nation, and in any people, he that serveth Him is accepted of Him: for He is not the God of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:131
verses.text: See if this be not the reason for the joy of the daughters of Judah.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:132
verses.text: "For Thou, Lord, art most high over all the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:133
verses.text: Not in Judaea alone, but over Jerusalem; not over Sion only, but over all the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:134
verses.text: To this whole earth the judgments of God prevailed, so that it assembled its nations from every quarter: judgments with which they who have cut themselves off have no communion: they neither hear the prophecy, nor see its completion; "For Thou, Lord, art most high over all the earth: Thou art exalted far above all gods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:135
verses.text: What is "far"?  For it is said of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:136
verses.text: What then meaneth "far," except that Thou mayest be acknowledged coequal with the Father? What meaneth, "above all gods"? Who are they? Idols have not life, have not sense: devils have life and sense; but they are evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:137
verses.text: What great thing is it that Christ is exalted above devils? He is exalted above devils: but neither is this very great; the heathen gods indeed are devils, but "He is far above all gods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:138
verses.text: Even men are styled gods: "I have said, Ye are gods: and ye are all the children of the Most Highest:" again it is written, "God standeth in the congregation of princes: He is a Judge among gods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:139
verses.text: Jesus Christ our Lord is exalted above all: not only above idols, not only above devils; but above all righteous men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:140
verses.text: Even this is not enough; above all Angels also: for whence otherwise is this, "Worship Him, all ye gods"? "Thou art far exalted above all gods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:141
verses.text: What then do we all, who have assembled before Him, before Him who is exalted far above all gods? He hath given us a brief commandment, "O ye that love the Lord, see that ye hate the thing which is evil!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:142
verses.text: Christ doth not deserve that with Him thou shouldest love avarice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:143
verses.text: Thou lovest Him: thou shouldest hate what He hateth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:144
verses.text: There is a man who is thine enemy, he is what thou art; ye are the work of one Creator, with the same nature: and yet if thy son were to speak unto thine enemy, and come to his house, and constantly converse with him, thou wouldest be inclined to disinherit him; because he speaketh with thine enemy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:145
verses.text: And how so? Because thou seemest to say justly, Thou art my enemy's friend, and seekest thou aught of my property? Attend then.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:146
verses.text: Thou lovest Christ: avarice is Christ's foe; why speak with her? I say not, speak with her; why dost thou serve her? For Christ commandeth thee to do many things, and thou dost them not; she commandeth thee, and thou dost them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:147
verses.text: Christ commandeth thee to clothe the poor man: and thou dost it not; avarice biddeth thee defraud, and this thou dost in preference.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:148
verses.text: If such be the case, if such thou art, do not very confidently promise thyself Christ's heritage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:149
verses.text: But thou sayest, I love Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:150
verses.text: Hence it appeareth that thou lovest what is good, if thou shalt be found to hate what is evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:151
verses.text: Because then he had said above, "see that ye hate the thing which is evil," lest ye should fear to hate evil, lest he should kill thee, he addeth instantly, "The Lord preserveth the souls of His servants".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:152
verses.text: Hear Him preserving the souls of His servants, and saying, "Fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:153
verses.text: He who hath most power against thee, slayeth the body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:154
verses.text: What hath he done unto thee? What he also did to the Lord thy God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:155
verses.text: Why lovest thou to have what Christ hath, if thou fearest to suffer what Christ did? He came to bear thy life, temporal, weak, subject unto death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:156
verses.text: Surely fear to die, if thou canst avoid dying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:157
verses.text: What thou canst not avoid through thy nature, why dost thou not undergo by faith? Let the adversary who threateneth take away from thee that life, God giveth thee another life: for He gave thee this life also, and without His will even this shall not be taken from thee; but if it be His will that it be taken from thee, He hath a life to give thee in exchange; fear not to be robbed for His sake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:158
verses.text: Art thou unwilling to put off a patched garment? He will give thee a robe of glory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:159
verses.text: What robe dost thou tell me of? "This corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:160
verses.text: This very flesh of thine shall not perish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:161
verses.text: Thine enemy can rage as far as to thy death: he hath not power beyond, either over thy soul, or even over thy flesh; for although he scatter thy flesh about, he hindereth not the resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:162
verses.text: Men were fearful for their life: and what said the Lord unto them? "The very hairs of your head are all numbered".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:163
verses.text: Dost thou, who losest not a single hair, fear the loss of thy life? All things are numbered with God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:164
verses.text: He who created all things, will restore all things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:165
verses.text: They were not, and they were created: they were, and shall they not be restored?"He shall deliver them from the hand of the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:166
verses.text: But perhaps thou wilt say, I lose this light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:167
verses.text: "There is sprung up a light for the righteous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:168
verses.text: What light fearest thou thou mayest lose? fearest thou thou mayest be in darkness? Fear not thou mayest lose light; nay, fear lest while thou art guarding against the loss of this light, thou mayest lose that true light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:169
verses.text: For we see to whom that light is given which thou fearest losing, and with whom it is shared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:170
verses.text: Do the righteous only see this sun, when He maketh it rise over the just and unjust, and raineth upon the just and unjust? Wicked men, robbers, the unchaste, beasts, flies, worms, see that light together with thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:171
verses.text: What sort of light doth He keep for the righteous, who giveth this even to such as these? Deservedly the Martyrs beheld this light in faith; for they who despised this light of the sun, had some light in their eyes, which they longed for, who rejected this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:172
verses.text: Do you imagine that they were really in misery, when they walked in chains? Spacious was the prison to the faithful, light were the chains to the confessors.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:173
verses.text: They who preached Christ amid their torments, had joy in the iron-chair.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:174
verses.text: What light hath sprung up for the righteous? Not that which springeth up for the unrighteous; not that which He causeth to rise over the good and bad.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:175
verses.text: There is a different light which springeth up to the righteous; of which light, that never rose upon themselves, the unrighteous shall in the end say, "Therefore have we erred from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness hath not shined upon us, and the sun of righteousness rose not upon us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:176
verses.text: Behold, by loving this sun they have lain in the darkness of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:177
verses.text: What did it profit them to have seen with their eyes this sun, and not in mind to have seen that light? Tobit was blind, but he used to teach his son the way of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:178
verses.text: Ye know this, that Tobit warned his son, and said to him, "Son, give alms of thy substance; because that alms suffer not to come into darkness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:179
verses.text: Even he who was in darkness spoke thus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:180
verses.text: Dost thou wish to know that light? Be true-hearted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:181
verses.text: What is, be true-hearted? Be not of a crooked heart before God, withstanding His will, and wishing to bend Him unto thee, and not to rule thyself to please Him; and thou wilt feel the joyful gladness which all the true-hearted know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:182
verses.text: "Be glad, ye righteous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:183
verses.text: Perhaps already the faithful hearing the word, "Be glad," are thinking of banquets, preparing cups, waiting for the season of roses; because it is said, "Be glad, ye righteous!" See what followeth, "Be glad in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:184
verses.text: Thou art waiting for the season of spring, that thou mayest be glad: thou hast the Lord for joyful gladness, the Lord is always with thee, He hath no special season; thou hast Him by night, thou hast Him by day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:185
verses.text: Be true-hearted; and thou hast ever joy from Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:186
verses.text: For that joy which is after the fashion of the world, is not true joy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:187
verses.text: Hear the prophet Isaiah: "There is no joy, saith my God, to the wicked".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:188
verses.text: What the wicked call joy is not joy, such as he knew who made no account of their joy: let us believe him, brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:189
verses.text: He was a man, but he knew both kinds of joy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:190
verses.text: He certainly knew the joys of the cup, for he was a man, he knew the joy of the table, he knew the joys of marriage, he knew those joys worldly and luxurious.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:191
verses.text: He who knew them saith with confidence, "There is no joy to the wicked, saith the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:192
verses.text: But it is not man who speaks, it is the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:193
verses.text: But thou sayest, I see not that light which Isaiah saw.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:194
verses.text: Believe, and thou shalt see it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:195
verses.text: For perhaps thou hast not the eye to see it; for it is an eye by which that beauty is discerned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:196
verses.text: For as there is an eye of the flesh, by means of which this light is seen: so there is an eye of the heart, by which that joy is perceived: perhaps that eye is wounded, dimmed, disturbed by passion, by avarice, by indulgence, by senseless lust; thine eye is disturbed: thou canst not see that light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:197
verses.text: Believe, before thou seest: thou shalt be healed, and shalt see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:198
verses.text: "And confess to the remembrance of His holiness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:199
verses.text: Now made glad, now rejoicing in the Lord, confess unto Him; for unless it were His will, ye would not rejoice in Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:200
verses.text: For the Lord Himself saith: "These things I have spoken to you: that in Me ye might have peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:201
verses.text: But in the world ye shall have tribulation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:202
verses.text: If ye are Christians, look for tribulations in this world; look not for more peaceful and better times.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:203
verses.text: Brethren, ye deceive yourselves; what the Gospel doth not promise you, promise not to yourselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:204
verses.text: Ye know what the Gospel saith; we are speaking to Christians; we ought not to disobey the faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:205
verses.text: The Gospel saith this, that in the last times many evils, many stumbling-blocks, many tribulations, much iniquity, shall abound; but he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved "The love," it saith, "of many shall wax cold".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:206
verses.text: Whosoever then hath been stedfastly fervent in spirit, as the Apostle saith, "fervent in spirit," his love shall not wax cold: because "the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost, which is given unto us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:207
verses.text: Let no man therefore promise himself what the Gospel doth not promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:208
verses.text: Behold, happier times will come, and I am doing this, and purchasing this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 97:209
verses.text: It is good for thee to listen to Him who is not deceived, nor hath deceived any man, who promised thee joy not here, but in Himself; and when all here hath passed away, to hope that with Him thou wilt for ever reign; lest when thou dost wish to reign here, thou mayest neither enjoy gladness here, nor find it there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:1
verses.text: Psalm XCVIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:2
verses.text: "O sing unto the Lord a new song".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:3
verses.text: The new man knoweth this, the old man knoweth it not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:4
verses.text: The old man is the old life, and the new man the new life: the old life is derived from Adam, the new life is formed in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:5
verses.text: But in this Psalm, the whole world is enjoined to sing a new song.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:6
verses.text: More openly elsewhere the words are these: "O sing unto the Lord a new song; sing unto the Lord, all the whole earth;"  that they who cut themselves off from the communion of the whole earth, may understand that they cannot sing the new song, because it is sung in the whole, and not in a part of it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:7
verses.text: Attend here also, and see that this is said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:8
verses.text: And when the whole earth is enjoined to sing a new song, it is meant, that peace singeth a new song.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:9
verses.text: "For He hath done marvelous things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:10
verses.text: What marvelous things? Behold, the Gospel was just now being read, and we heard the marvellous things of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:11
verses.text: The only son of his mother, who was a widow, was being carried out dead: the Lord, in compassion, made them stand still; they laid him down, and the Lord said, "Young man, I say unto thee, Arise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:12
verses.text: "The Lord hath done marvellous things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:13
verses.text: What marvellous things? Hear: "His own right hand, and His holy arm, hath healed for Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:14
verses.text: What is the Lord's holy Arm? Our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:15
verses.text: Hear Isaiah: "Who hath believed our report, and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed?" His holy arm then, and His own right hand, is Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:16
verses.text: Our Lord Jesus Christ is therefore the arm of God, and the right hand of God; for this reason is it said, "hath He healed for Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:17
verses.text: It is not said only, "His right hand hath healed the world," but "hath healed for Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:18
verses.text: For many are healed for themselves, not for Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:19
verses.text: Behold how many long for that bodily health, and receive it from Him: they are healed by Him, but not for Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:20
verses.text: How are they healed by Him, and not for Him? When they have received health, they become wanton: they who when sick were chaste, when cured become adulterers: they who when in illness injured no man, on the recovery of their strength attack and crush the innocent: they are healed, but not unto Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:21
verses.text: Who is he who is healed unto Him? He who is healed inwardly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:22
verses.text: Who is he that is healed inwardly? He who trusteth in Him, that when he shall have been healed inwardly, reformed into a new man, afterwards this mortal flesh too, which doth languish for a time, may in the end itself even recover its most perfect health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:23
verses.text: Let us therefore be healed for Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:24
verses.text: But that we may be healed for Him, let us believe in His right hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:25
verses.text: "The Lord hath made known His salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:26
verses.text: This very right hand, this very arm, this very salvation, is our Lord Jesus Christ of whom it is said, "And all flesh shall see the salvation of God;" of whom also that Simeon who embraced the Infant in his arms, spoke, "Lord, now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace; for mine eyes have seen Thy salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:27
verses.text: "The Lord hath made known His salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:28
verses.text: To whom did He make it known? To a part, or to the whole? Not to any part specially.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:29
verses.text: Let no man betray, no man deceive, no man say, "Lo, here is Christ, or there:" the man who saith, Lo, He is here, or there, pointeth to some particular spots.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:30
verses.text: To whom "hath the Lord declared His salvation"? Hear what followeth: "His righteousness hath He openly showed in the sight of the heathen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:31
verses.text: Our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ is the right hand of God, the arm of God, the salvation of God, and the righteousness of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:32
verses.text: "He hath remembered His mercy to Jacob, and His truth unto the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:33
verses.text: What meaneth this, "He hath remembered His mercy and truth"? He hath pitied, so that He promised; because He promised and showed His mercy, truth hath followed: mercy hath gone before promise, promise hath been fulfilled in truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:34
verses.text: "And His truth unto the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:35
verses.text: Who is this Israel? That ye may not perchance think of one nation of the Jews, hear what followeth: "All the ends of the world have seen the salvation of our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:36
verses.text: It is not said, all the earth: but, "all the ends of the world:" as it is said, from one end to the other.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:37
verses.text: Let no man cut this down, let no man scatter it abroad; strong is the unity of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:38
verses.text: He who gave so great a price, hath bought the whole: "All the ends of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:39
verses.text: Because they have seen, then, "Make a joyful noise unto the Lord, all ye lands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:40
verses.text: Ye already know what it is to make a joyful noise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:41
verses.text: Rejoice, and speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:42
verses.text: If ye cannot express your joy, shout ye; let the shout manifest your joy, if your speech cannot: yet let not joy be mute; let not your heart be silent respecting its God, let it not be mute concerning His gifts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:43
verses.text: If thou speakest to thyself, unto thyself art thou healed; if His right hand hath healed thee for Him, speak thou unto Him for whom thou hast been healed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:44
verses.text: "Sing, rejoice, and make melody".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:45
verses.text: "Make melody unto the Lord upon the harp: on the harp and with the voice of a Psalm".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:46
verses.text: Praise Him not with the voice only; take up works, that ye may not only sing, but work also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:47
verses.text: He who singeth and worketh, maketh melody with psaltery and upon the harp.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:48
verses.text: Now see what sort of instruments are next spoken of, in figure: "With ductile trumpets also, and the sound of the pipe of horn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:49
verses.text: What are ductile trumpets, and pipes of horn? Ductile trumpets are of brass: they are drawn out by hammering; if by hammering, by being beaten, ye shall be ductile trumpets, drawn out unto the praise of God, if ye improve when in tribulation: tribulation is hammering, improvement is the being drawn out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:50
verses.text: Job was a ductile trumpet, when suddenly assailed by the heaviest losses, and the death of his sons, become like a ductile trumpet by the beating of so heavy tribulation, he sounded thus: "The Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:51
verses.text: How did he sound? How pleasantly doth his voice sound? This ductile trumpet is still under the hammer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:52
verses.text: We have heard how he was hammered; let us hear how he soundeth: let us, if it please you, hear the sweet sound of this ductile trumpet: "What! shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?" O courageous, O sweet sound! whom will not that sound awake from sleep? whom will not confidence in God awake, to march to battle fearlessly against the devil; not to struggle with his own strength, but His who proveth him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:53
verses.text: For He it is who hammereth: for the hammer could not do so of itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:54
verses.text: See how (I dare so speak, my brethren) even the Apostle was beaten with this very hammer: he saith, "there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan, to buffet me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:55
verses.text: Behold he is under the hammer: let us hear how he speaketh of it: "For this thing," he saith, "I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:56
verses.text: And He said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for My strength is made perfect in weakness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:57
verses.text: I, saith His Maker, wish to make this trumpet perfect; I cannot do so unless I hammer it; in weakness is strength made perfect.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:58
verses.text: Hear now the ductile trumpet itself sounding as it should: "When I am weak, then am I strong".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:59
verses.text: The voice of the pipe of horn, what is it? The horn riseth above the flesh: in rising above the flesh it needs must be solid so as to last, and able to speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:60
verses.text: And whence this? Because it hath surpassed the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:61
verses.text: He who wisheth to be a horn trumpet, let him overcome the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:62
verses.text: What meaneth this, let him overcome the flesh? Let him surpass the desires, let him conquer the lusts of the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:63
verses.text: Hear the horn trumpets.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:64
verses.text: What meaneth this, "Set your affection on things above"? It meaneth, Rise above the flesh, think not of carnal things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:65
verses.text: They were not yet horn trumpets, to whom he now spoke thus: "I could not speak unto you, brethren, as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal, even as unto babes in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:66
verses.text: I have fed you with milk, and not with meat; for hitherto ye were not able to bear it: neither yet now are ye able.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:67
verses.text: For ye are yet carnal".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:68
verses.text: They were not therefore horn trumpets, because they had not risen above the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:69
verses.text: Horn both adhereth to the flesh, and riseth above the flesh; and although it springeth from the flesh, yet it surpasseth it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:70
verses.text: If therefore thou art spiritual, when before thou wast carnal; as yet thou art treading the earth in the flesh, but in spirit thou art rising into heaven; for though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:71
verses.text: Brethren, do not reproach brethren whom the mercy of God hath not yet converted; know that as long as ye do this, ye savour of the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:72
verses.text: That is not a trumpet which pleaseth the ears of God: the trumpet of boastfulness maketh the war fruitless.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:73
verses.text: Let the horn trumpet raise thy courage against the devil; let not the fleshly trumpet raise thy pride against thy brother.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:74
verses.text: "Make a joyful noise in the sight of the Lord the King".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:75
verses.text: While ye are rejoicing, and delighted with the ductile trumpets, and the voice of the horn, what followeth? "Let the sea be stirred up, and the fulness thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:76
verses.text: Brethren, when the Apostles, like ductile trumpets and horns, were preaching the truth, the sea was stirred up, its waves arose, tempests increased, persecutions of the Church took place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:77
verses.text: Whence hath the sea been stirred up? When a joyful noise was made, when Psalms of thanksgiving were being sung before God: the ears of God were pleased, the waves of the sea were raised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:78
verses.text: "Let the sea be stirred up, and the fulness thereof: the round world, and all that dwell therein".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:79
verses.text: Let the sea be stirred up in its persecutions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:80
verses.text: "Let the floods clap their hands together".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:81
verses.text: Let the sea be aroused, and the floods clap their hands together; persecutions arise, and the saints rejoice in God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:82
verses.text: Whence shall the floods clap their hands? What is to clap their hands? To rejoice in works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:83
verses.text: To clap hands, is to rejoice; hands, mean works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:84
verses.text: What floods? Those whom God hath made floods, by giving them that Water, the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:85
verses.text: "If any man thirst," saith He, "let him come unto Me, and drink.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:86
verses.text: He that believeth on Me, out of his bosom shall flow rivers of living water".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:87
verses.text: These rivers clapped their hands, these rivers rejoiced in works, and blessed God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:88
verses.text: "The hills shall be joyful together".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:89
verses.text: "Before the Lord, for He is come; for He is come to judge the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:90
verses.text: "The hills" signify the great.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:91
verses.text: The Lord cometh to judge the earth, and they rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:92
verses.text: But there are hills, who, when the Lord is coming to judge the earth, shall tremble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:93
verses.text: There are therefore good and evil hills; the good hills, are spiritual greatness; the bad hills, are the swelling of pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:94
verses.text: "Let the hills be joyful together before the Lord, for He is come; for He is come to judge the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:95
verses.text: Wherefore shall He come, and how shall He come? "With righteousness shall He judge the world, and the people with equity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:96
verses.text: Let the hills therefore rejoice; for He shall not judge unrighteously.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:97
verses.text: When some man is coming as a judge, to whom the conscience cannot lie open, even innocent men may tremble, if from him they expect a reward for virtue, or fear the penalty of condemnation; when He shall come who cannot be deceived, let the hills rejoice, let them rejoice fearlessly; they shall be enlightened by Him, not condemned; let them rejoice, because the Lord will come to judge the world with equity; and if the righteous hills rejoice, let the unrighteous tremble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:98
verses.text: But behold, He hath not yet come: what need is there they should tremble? Let them mend their ways, and rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:99
verses.text: It is in thy power in what way thou willest to await the coming of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:100
verses.text: For this reason He delayeth to come, that when He cometh He may not condemn thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:101
verses.text: Lo, He hath not yet come: He is in heaven, thou on earth: He delayeth His coming, do not thou delay wisdom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:102
verses.text: His coming is hard to the hard of heart, soft to the pious.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:103
verses.text: See therefore even now what thou art: if hard of heart, thou canst soften; if thou art soft, even now rejoice that He will come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:104
verses.text: For thou art a Christian.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:105
verses.text: Yea, thou sayest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:106
verses.text: I believe that thou prayest, and sayest, "Thy kingdom come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:107
verses.text: Thou desirest Him to come, whose coming thou fearest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 98:108
verses.text: Reform thyself, that thou mayest not pray against thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:1
verses.text: Psalm XCIX.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:2
verses.text: Beloved brethren, it ought already to be known to you, as sons of the Church, and well instructed in the school of Christ through all the books of our ancient fathers, who wrote the words of God and the great things of God, that their wish was to consult for our good, who were to live at this period, believers in Christ; who, at a seasonable time came unto us, the first time, in humility; at the second, destined to come in exaltation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:3
verses.text: For thus it is said in the Psalms: "Truth shall flourish out of the earth: and righteousness hath looked down from heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:4
verses.text: Now, therefore, our whole design is, when we hear a Psalm, a Prophet, or the Law, all of which was written before our Lord Jesus Christ came in the flesh, to see Christ there, to understand Christ there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:5
verses.text: Attend therefore, beloved, to this Psalm, with me, and let us herein seek Christ; certainly He will appear to those who seek Him, who at first appeared to those who sought Him not; and He w ill not desert those who long for Him, who redeemed those who neglected Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:6
verses.text: Behold, the Psalm beginneth concerning Him: of Him it is said:—.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:7
verses.text: "The Lord is King, be the people angry".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:8
verses.text: For our Lord Jesus Christ began to reign, began to be preached, after He arose from the dead and ascended into heaven, after He had filled His disciples with the confidence of the Holy Spirit, that they should not fear death, which He had already killed in Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:9
verses.text: Our Lord Christ began then to be preached, that they who wished for salvation might believe in Him; and the peoples who worshipped idols were angry.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:10
verses.text: They who worshipped what they had made were angry, because He by whom they were made was declared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:11
