verses.text: He announced, in fact, through His disciples, Himself, who wished them to be converted unto Him by whom they were made, and to be turned away from those things which they had made themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:12
verses.text: They were angry with their Lord in behalf of their idols, they who even if they were angry with their slave on their idol's account, were to be condemned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:13
verses.text: For their slave was better than their idol: for God made their slave, the carpenter made their idol.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:14
verses.text: They were so angry in their idol's behalf, that they feared not to be angry with their Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:15
verses.text: But the words, "be they angry," are a prediction, not a command; for in a prophecy it is that this is said, "The Lord is King, be the people angry".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:16
verses.text: Some good resulteth even from the enraged people: let them be angry, and in their anger let the Martyrs be crowned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:17
verses.text: Ye heard when Jeremiah was being read before the reading of the Apostle, if ye listened; ye saw therein the times in which we now live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:18
verses.text: He said, "The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth, let them perish from the earth, and from under the heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:19
verses.text: He said not, The gods that have not made the heavens and earth, let them perish from the heaven and from the earth; because they never were in heaven: but what did he say? "Let them perish from the earth, and from under the heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:20
verses.text: As if, while the word earth was repeated, the repetition of the word heaven were wanting (because they never were in heaven): he repeateth the earth twice, since it is under heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:21
verses.text: "Let them perish from the earth, and from under the heaven," from their temples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:22
verses.text: Consider if this be not now taking place; if in a great measure it hath not already happened: for what, or how much, hath remained? The idols remained rather in the hearts of the pagans, than in the niches of the temples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:23
verses.text: "He who sitteth between the cherubims:" thou dost understand, "He is King: let the earth be stirred up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:24
verses.text: The Cherubim is the seat of God, as the Scripture showeth us, a certain exalted heavenly throne, which we see not; but the Word of God knoweth it, knoweth it as His own seat: and the Word of God and the Spirit of God hath Itself revealed to the servants of God where God sitteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:25
verses.text: Not that God doth sit, as doth man; but thou, if thou dost wish that God sit in thee, if thou wilt be good, shalt be the seat of God; for thus is it written, "The soul of the righteous is the seat of wisdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:26
verses.text: For a throne is in our language called a seat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:27
verses.text: For some, conversant with the Hebrew tongue, have interpreted cherubim in the Latin language (for it is a Hebrew term) by the words, fulness of knowledge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:28
verses.text: Therefore, because God surpasseth all knowledge, He is said to sit above the fulness of knowledge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:29
verses.text: Let there be therefore in thee fulness of knowledge, and even thou shalt be the throne of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:30
verses.text: He knoweth all things: for our hairs are numbered before God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:31
verses.text: But the fulness of knowledge which He willed man to know is different from this; the knowledge which He willed thee to have, pertaineth to the law of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:32
verses.text: And who can, thou mayest perhaps say unto me, perfectly know the Law, so that he may have within himself the fulness of the knowledge of the Law, and be able to be the seat of God? Be not disturbed; it is briefly told thee what thou hast, if thou dost wish to have the fulness of knowledge, and to become the throne of God: for the Apostle saith, "Love is the fulfilling of the Law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:33
verses.text: What followeth then? Thou hast lost the whole of thine excuse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:34
verses.text: Ask thine heart; see whether it hath love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:35
verses.text: If there be love there, there is the fulfilment of the Law there also; already God dwelleth in thee, thou hast become the throne of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:36
verses.text: "Be the people angry;" what can the angry people do against him who hath become the throne of God? Thou givest heed unto them who rage against thee: Who is it that sitteth within thee, thou givest not heed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:37
verses.text: Thou art become a heaven, and fearest thou the earth? For the Scripture saith in another passage, that the Lord our God doth declare, "The heaven is My throne".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:38
verses.text: If therefore even thou by having the fulness of knowledge, and by having love, hast been made the throne of God, thou hast become a heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:39
verses.text: For this heaven which we look up to with these eyes of ours, is not very precious before God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:40
verses.text: Holy souls are the heaven of God; the minds of the Angels, and all the minds of His servants, are the heaven of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:41
verses.text: "The Lord is great in Sion, and high above all people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:42
verses.text: He whom I spoke to thee of as above the Cherubims, is great in Sion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:43
verses.text: Ask thou now, what is Sion? We know Sion to be the city of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:44
verses.text: The city of Jerusalem is called Sion; and is so called according to a certain interpretation, for that Sion signifieth watching, that is, sight and contemplation; for to watch is to look forward to, or gaze upon, or strain the eyes to see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:45
verses.text: Now every soul is a Sion, if it trieth to see that light which is to be seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:46
verses.text: For if it shall have gazed upon a light of its own, it is darkened; if upon His, it is enlightened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:47
verses.text: But, now that it is clear that Sion is the city of God; what is the city of God, but the Holy Church? For men who love one another, and who love their God who dwelleth in them, constitute a city unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:48
verses.text: Because a city is held together by some law; their very law is Love; and that very Love is God: for openly it is written, "God is Love".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:49
verses.text: He therefore who is full of Love, is full of God; and many, full of love, constitute a city full of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:50
verses.text: That city of God is called Sion; the Church therefore is Sion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:51
verses.text: In it God is great.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:52
verses.text: Do ye imagine, brethren, that they whose instruments re-echoed yesterday, are not angry with our fastings? But let us not be angry with them, but let us fast for them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:53
verses.text: For the Lord our God who sitteth in us hath said, He hath Himself commanded us to pray for our enemies, to pray for them that persecute us: and as the Church doth this, the persecutors are almost extinct.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:54
verses.text: The drunken man doth not offend himself, but he offendeth the sober man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:55
verses.text: Show me a man who is at last happy in God, liveth gravely, sigheth for that everlasting peace which God hath promised him; and see that when he hath seen a man dancing to an instrument, he is more grieved for his madness, than for a man who is in a frenzy from a fever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:56
verses.text: If then we know their evils, considering that we also have been freed from those very evils, let us grieve for them; and if we grieve for them, let us pray for them; and that we may be heard, let us fast for them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:57
verses.text: For we do not keep our own fasts in their holidays.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:58
verses.text: Different are the fasts which we celebrate through the days of the approaching Passover, through different seasons which are fixed for us in Christ: but through their holidays we fast for this reason, that when they are rejoicing, we may groan for them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:59
verses.text: For by their joy they excite our grief, and cause us to remember how wretched they are as yet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:60
verses.text: But since we see many freed thence, where we also have been, we ought not to despair even of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:61
verses.text: And if they are still enraged, let us pray; and if still a particle of earth that hath remained behind be stirred up against us, let us continue in lamentation for them, that to them also God may grant understanding, and that with us they may hear those words, in which we are at this moment rejoicing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:62
verses.text: All these very people, over whom Thou art great in Sion, "Let them confess unto Thy Name, which is great".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:63
verses.text: Thy Name was little when they were enraged: it hath become great; let them now confess.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:64
verses.text: In what sense do we say, that the Name of Christ was little, before it was spread abroad to so great an extent? Because His report is meant by His Name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:65
verses.text: His Name was small; already it hath become great.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:66
verses.text: What nation is there that hath not heard of the Name of Christ? Therefore let now the people confess unto Thy Name, which is great, who before were enraged with Thy little Name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:67
verses.text: Wherefore shall they confess? Because it is "wonderful and holy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:68
verses.text: Thy very Name is wonderful and holy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:69
verses.text: He is so preached as crucified, so preached as humbled, so preached as judged, that He may come exalted, that He may come living, that He may come to judge in power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:70
verses.text: He spareth at present the people who blaspheme Him, because "the long-suffering of God leadeth to repentance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:71
verses.text: For He who now spareth, will not always spare: nor will He, who is now being preached that He may be feared, fail to come to judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:72
verses.text: He will come, my brethren, He will come: let us fear Him, and let us live so that we may be found on His right hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:73
verses.text: For He will come, and will judge, so as to place some on the left hand, some on the right And He doth not act in an uncertain manner, so as to err perchance betwixt men, so that he who should be set on the right hand, be set on the left; or that he who ought to stand on the left, by a mistake of God should stand on the right: He cannot err, so as to place the evil where He ought to set the good; nor to place the good, where He should have set the evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:74
verses.text: If He cannot err, we err, if we fear not; but if we have feared in this life, we shall not then have what to fear for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:75
verses.text: "For the King's honour loveth judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:76
verses.text: "Thou hast prepared equity; Thou hast wrought judgment and righteousness in Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:77
verses.text: For we too ought to have judgment, we ought to have righteousness; but He worketh in us judgment and righteousness, who created us in whom He might work them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:78
verses.text: How ought we too to have judgment and righteousness? Thou hast judgment, when thou dost distinguish evil from good: and righteousness when thou followest the good, and turnest aside from the evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:79
verses.text: By distinguishing them, thou hast judgment; by doing, thou hast righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:80
verses.text: "Eschew evil," he saith, "and do good; seek peace, and ensue it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:81
verses.text: Thou shouldest first have judgment, then righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:82
verses.text: What judgment? That thou mayest first judge what is evil, and what is good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:83
verses.text: And what righteousness? That thou mayest shun evil, and do good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:84
verses.text: But this thou wilt not gain from thyself; see what he hath said, "Thou hast wrought judgment and righteousness in Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:85
verses.text: "O magnify the Lord our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:86
verses.text: Magnify Him truly, magnify Him well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:87
verses.text: Let us praise Him, let us magnify Him who hath wrought the very righteousness which we have; who wrought it in us, Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:88
verses.text: For who but He who justified us, wrought righteousness in us? For of Christ it is said, "who justifieth the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:89
verses.text: "And fall down before His footstool: for He is holy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:90
verses.text: What are we to fall down before? His footstool.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:91
verses.text: What is under the feet is called a footstool, in Greek ὑποπόδιον, in Latin Scabellum or Suppedaneum.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:92
verses.text: But consider, brethren, what he commandeth us to fall down before.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:93
verses.text: In another passage of the Scriptures it is said, "The heaven is My throne, and the earth is My footstool".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:94
verses.text: Doth he then bid us worship the earth, since in another passage it is said, that it is God's footstool? How then shall we worship the earth, when the Scripture saith openly, "Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God"? Yet here it saith, "fall down before His footstool:" and, explaining to us what His footstool is, it saith, "The earth is My footstool".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:95
verses.text: I am in doubt; I fear to worship the earth, lest He who made the heaven and  the earth condemn me; again, I fear not to worship the footstool of my Lord, because the Psalm biddeth me, "fall down before His footstool".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:96
verses.text: I ask, what is His footstool? and the Scripture telleth me, "the earth is My footstool".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:97
verses.text: In hesitation I turn unto Christ, since I am herein seeking Himself: and I discover how the earth may be worshipped without impiety, how His footstool may be worshipped without impiety.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:98
verses.text: For He took upon Him earth from earth; because flesh is from earth, and He received flesh from the flesh of Mary.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:99
verses.text: And because He walked here in very flesh, and gave that very flesh to us to eat for our salvation; and no one eateth that flesh, unless he hath first worshipped: we have found out in what sense such a footstool of our Lord's may be worshipped, and not only that we sin not in worshipping it, but that we sin in not worshipping.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:100
verses.text: But doth the flesh give life? Our Lord Himself, when He was speaking in praise of this same earth, said, "It is the Spirit that quickeneth, the flesh profiteth nothing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:101
verses.text: But when our Lord praised it, He was speaking of His own flesh, and He had said, "Except a man eat My flesh, he shall have no life in him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:102
verses.text: Some disciples of His, about seventy, were offended, and said, "This is an hard saying, who can hear it?" And they went back, and walked no more with Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:103
verses.text: It seemed unto them hard that He said, "Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of Man, ye have no life in you:" they received it foolishly, they thought of it carnally, and imagined that the Lord would cut off parts from His body, and give unto them; and they said, "This is a hard saying".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:104
verses.text: It was they who were hard, not the saying; for unless they had been hard, and not meek, they would have said unto themselves, He saith not this without reason, but there must be some latent mystery herein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:105
verses.text: They would have remained with Him, softened, not hard: and would have learnt that from Him which they who remained, when the others departed, learnt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:106
verses.text: For when twelve disciples had remained with Him, on their departure, these remaining followers suggested to Him, as if in grief for the death of the former, that they were offended by His words, and turned back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:107
verses.text: But He instructed them, and saith unto them, "It is the Spirit that quickeneth, but the flesh profiteth nothing; the words that I have spoken unto you, they are spirit, and they are life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:108
verses.text: Understand spiritually what I have said; ye are not to eat this body which ye see; nor to drink that blood which they who will crucify Me shall pour forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:109
verses.text: I have commended unto you a certain mystery; spiritually understood, it will quicken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:110
verses.text: Although it is needful that this be visibly celebrated, yet it must be spiritually understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:111
verses.text: "Moses and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among such as call upon His Name: these called upon the Lord, and He heard them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:112
verses.text: "He spake unto them out of the cloudy pillar".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:113
verses.text: Of Moses it is not there stated that he was a pries t.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:114
verses.text: But if he was not this, what was he? Could he be anything greater than a priest? This Psalm declareth that he also was himself a priest: "Moses and Aaron among His priests".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:115
verses.text: They therefore were the Lord's priests.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:116
verses.text: Samuel is read of later in the Book of Kings: this Samuel is in David's times; for he anointed the holy David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:117
verses.text: Samuel from his infancy grew up in the temple.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:118
verses.text: He mentioneth these: and by these desireth us to understand all the saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:119
verses.text: Yet why hath he here named those? Because we said that we ought here to understand Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:120
verses.text: Attend, holy brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:121
verses.text: He said above, "O magnify the Lord our God: and fall down before His footstool, for He is holy:" praising some one, that is, our Lord Jesus Christ; whose footstool is to be worshipped, because He assumed flesh, in which He was to appear before the human race; and wishing to show unto us that the ancient fathers also had preached of Him, because our Lord Jesus Christ is Himself the True Priest, he mentioned these, because God spake unto them out of the cloudy pillar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:122
verses.text: What meaneth, "out of the cloudy pillar"? He was speaking figuratively.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:123
verses.text: For if He spoke in some cloud, those obscure words predicted some one unknown, yet to be manifest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:124
verses.text: This unknown one is no longer unknown; for He is known by us, our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:125
verses.text: He who first spoke out of the cloudy pillar, hath in Person spoken unto us in His footstool; that is, on earth, when He had assumed the flesh, for which reason we worship His footstool, for He is holy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:126
verses.text: He Himself used to speak out of the cloud, which was not then understood: He hath spoken in His own footstool, and the words of His cloud have been understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:127
verses.text: "They kept His testimonies, and the law that He gave them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:128
verses.text: "Thou heardest them," he saith, "O Lord our God: Thou wast forgiving to them, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:129
verses.text: God is not said to be forgiving toward anything but sins: when He pardoneth sins, then He forgiveth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:130
verses.text: And what had He in them to punish, so that He was forgiving in pardoning them? He was forgiving in pardoning their sins, He was also forgiving in punishing them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:131
verses.text: For what followeth? "And punishedst all their own affections".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:132
verses.text: Even in punishing them Thou wast forgiving toward them: for not in remitting, but also in punishing their sins, hast Thou been forgiving.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:133
verses.text: Consider, my brethren, what he hath taught us here: attend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:134
verses.text: God is angry with him whom, when he sinneth, He scourgeth not: for unto him to whom He is truly forgiving, He not only remitteth sins, that they may not injure him in a future life; but also chasteneth him, that he delight not in continual sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:135
verses.text: Come, my brethren; if we ask how these were punished, the Lord will aid me to tell you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:136
verses.text: Let us consider these three persons, Moses, Aaron, and Samuel: and how they were punished, since he said, "Thou hast punished all their own affections:" meaning those affections of theirs, which the Lord knew in their hearts, which men knew not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:137
verses.text: For they were living in the midst of the people of God, without complaint from man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:138
verses.text: But what do we say? That perhaps the early life of Moses was sinful; for he fled from Egypt, after slaying a man The early life of Aaron also was such as would displease God; for he allowed a maddened and infatuated people to make an idol to worship; and an idol was made for God's people to worship.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:139
verses.text: What sin did Samuel, who was given up when an infant to the temple? He passed all his life amid the holy sacraments of God: from childhood the servant of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:140
verses.text: Nothing was ever said of Samuel, nothing by men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:141
verses.text: Perhaps God knew of somewhat there to chasten; since even what seemeth perfect unto men, unto that Perfection is still imperfect.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:142
verses.text: Artists show many of their works to the unskilful; and when the unskilful have pronounced them perfect, the artists polish them still further, as they know what is still wanting to them, so that men wonder at things they had imagined already perfect having received so much additional polish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:143
verses.text: This happeneth in buildings, and in paintings, and in embroidery, and almost in every species of art.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:144
verses.text: At first they judge it to be already in a manner perfect, so that their eyes desire nothing further: but the judgment of the inexperienced eye is one, and that of the rule of art another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:145
verses.text: Thus also these Saints were living before the eyes of God, as if faultless, as if perfect, as if Angels: but He who punished all their own affections, knew what was wanting in them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:146
verses.text: But He punished them not in anger, but in mercy: He punished them that He might perfect what He had begun, not to condemn what He had cast away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:147
verses.text: God therefore punished all their affections.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:148
verses.text: How did He punish Samuel? where is this punishment?What was said unto Moses was a type, not a punishment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:149
verses.text: What punishment is death to an old man? What punishment was it, not to enter into that land, into which unworthy men entered? But what is said of Aaron? He also died an old man: his sons succeeded him in the priesthood: his son afterwards ruled in the priesthood: how did He punish Aaron also? Samuel also died a holy old man, leaving his sons as his successors I seek for the punishment inflicted upon them, and according to men I find it not: but according to what I know the servants of God suffer every day, they were day by day punished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:150
verses.text: Read ye, and see the punishments, and ye also who are advanced bear the punishments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:151
verses.text: Every day they suffered from the obstinate people, every day they suffered from the ungodly livers; and were compelled to live among those whose lives they daily censured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:152
verses.text: This was their punishment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:153
verses.text: He unto whom it is small hath not advanced far; for the ungodliness of others tormenteth thee in proportion as thou hast departed far from thine own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:154
verses.text: "O magnify the Lord our God!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:155
verses.text: Again we magnify Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:156
verses.text: He who is merciful even when He striketh, how is He to be praised, how is He to be magnified? Canst thou show this unto thy son, and cannot God? For thou art not good when thou dost caress thy son, and evil when thou strikest him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:157
verses.text: Both when thou dost caress him thou art a father, and when thou strikest him, thou art his father: thou dost caress him, that he may not faint; thou strikest him, that he may not perish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:158
verses.text: "O magnify the Lord our God, and worship Him upon His holy hill: for the Lord our God is holy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:159
verses.text: As he said above, "O magnify the Lord our God and fall down before His footstool:" now we have understood what it is to worship His footstool: thus also but now after he had magnified the Lord our God, that no man might magnify Him apart from His hill, he hath also praised His hill.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:160
verses.text: What is His hill? We read elsewhere concerning this hill, that a stone was cut from the hill without hands, and shattered all the kingdoms of the earth, and the stone itself increased.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:161
verses.text: This is the vision of Daniel which I am relating.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:162
verses.text: This stone which was cut from the hill without hands increased, and "became," he saith, "a great mountain, and filled the whole face of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:163
verses.text: Let us worship on that great mountain, if we desire to be heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:164
verses.text: Heretics do not worship on that mountain, because it hath filled the whole earth; they have stuck fast on part of it, and have lost the whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:165
verses.text: If they acknowledge the Catholic Church, they will worship on this hill with us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:166
verses.text: For we already see how that stone that was cut from the mountain without hands hath increased, and how great tracts of earth it hath prevailed over, and unto what nations it hath extended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:167
verses.text: What is the mountain whence the stone was hewn without hands? The Jewish kingdom, in the first place; since they worshipped one God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:168
verses.text: Thence was hewn the stone, our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:169
verses.text: That stone then was born of the mountain without hands: it increased, and by its increase broke all the kingdoms of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:170
verses.text: It hath become a great mountain, and hath filled the whole face of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:171
verses.text: This is the Catholic Church, in whose communion rejoice that ye are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:172
verses.text: But they who are not in her communion, since they worship and praise God apart from this same mountain, are not heard unto eternal life; although they may be heard unto certain temporal things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:173
verses.text: Let them not flatter themselves, because God heareth them in some things: for He heareth Pagans also in some things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:174
verses.text: Do not the Pagans cry unto God, and it raineth? Wherefore? Because He maketh His sun to rise over the good and the bad, and sendeth rain upon the just and the unjust Boast not therefore, Pagan, that when thou criest unto God, God sendeth rain, for He sendeth rain upon the just and the unjust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:175
verses.text: He hath heard thee in temporal things: He heareth thee not in things eternal, unless thou hast worshipped in His holy hill.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 99:176
verses.text: "Worship Him upon His holy hill: for the Lord our God is holy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:1
verses.text: Psalm C.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:2
verses.text: Ye heard the Psalm, brethren, while it was being chanted: it is short, and not obscure: as if I had given you an assurance, that ye should not fear fatigue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:3
verses.text: The title of this Psalm is, "A Psalm of confession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:4
verses.text: The verses are few, but big with great subjects; may the seed bring forth within your hearts, the barn be prepared for the Lord's harvest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:5
verses.text: "Jubilate," therefore, "unto the Lord, all ye lands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:6
verses.text: This Psalm giveth this exhortation to us, that we jubilate unto the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:7
verses.text: Nor doth it, as it were, exhort one particular corner of the earth, or one habitation or congregation of men; but since it is aware that it hath sown blessings on every side, on every side it doth exact jubilance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:8
verses.text: Doth all the earth at this moment hear my voice? And yet the whole earth hath heard this voice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:9
verses.text: All the earth is already jubilant in the Lord; and what is not as yet jubilant, will be so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:10
verses.text: For blessing, extending on every side, when the Church was commencing to spread from Jerusalem throughout all nations, everywhere overturneth ungodliness, and everywhere buildeth up piety: the good are mingled with the wicked throughout all lands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:11
verses.text: Every land is full of the discontented murmurs of the wicked, and of  the jubilance of the good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:12
verses.text: What then is it, "to jubilate"? For the title of the pr esent Psalm especially maketh us give good heed to this word, for it is entitled, "A Psalm of confession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:13
verses.text: What meaneth, to jubilate with confession? It is the sentiment thus expressed in another Psalm: "Blessed is the people that understandeth jubilance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:14
verses.text: Surely that which being understood maketh blessed is something great.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:15
verses.text: May therefore the Lord our God, who maketh men blessed, grant me to understand what to say, and grant you to understand what ye hear: "Blessed is the people that understandeth jubilance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:16
verses.text: Let us therefore run unto this blessing, let us understand jubilance, let us not pour it forth without understanding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:17
verses.text: Of what use is it to be jubilant and obey this Psalm, when it saith, "Jubilate unto the Lord, all ye lands," and not to understand what jubilance is, so that our voice only may be jubilant, our heart not so? For the understanding is the utterance of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:18
verses.text: I am about to say what ye know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:19
verses.text: One who jubilates, uttereth not words, but it is a certain sound of joy without words: for it is the expression of a mind poured forth in joy, expressing, as far as it is able, the affection, but not compassing the feeling.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:20
verses.text: A man rejoicing in his own exultation, after certain words which cannot be uttered or understood, bursteth forth into sounds of exultation without words, so that it seemeth that he indeed doth rejoice with his voice itself, but as if filled with excessive joy cannot express in words the subject of that joy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:21
verses.text: Those who are engaged at work in the fields are most given to jubilate; reapers, or vintagers, or those who gather any of the fruits of the earth, delighted with the abundant produce, and rejoicing in the very richness and exuberance of the soil, sing in exultation; and among the songs which they utter in words, they put in certain cries without words in the exultation of a rejoicing mind; and this is what is meant by jubilating.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:22
verses.text: When then are we jubilant? When we praise that which cannot be uttered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:23
verses.text: For we observe the whole creation, the earth and the sea, and all things that therein are: we observe that each have their sources and causes, the power of production, the order of birth, the limit of duration, the end in decease, that successive ages run on without any confusion, that the stars roll, as it seemeth, from the East to the West, and complete the courses of the years: we see how the months are measured, how the hours extend; and in all these things a certain invisible element, I know not what, but some principle of unity, which is termed spirit or soul, present in all living things, urging them to the pursuit of pleasure and the avoidance of pain, and the preservation of their own safety; that man also hath somewhat in common with the Angels of God; not with cattle, such as life, hearing, sight, and so forth; but somewhat which can understand God, which peculiarly doth belong to the mind, which can distinguish justice and injustice, as the eye discerneth white from black.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:24
verses.text: In all this consideration of creation, which I have run over as I could, let the soul ask itself: Who created all these things? Who made them? Who made among them thyself?I have observed the whole creation, as far as I could.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:25
verses.text: I have observed the bodily creation in heaven and on earth, and the spiritual in myself who am speaking, who animate my limbs, who exert voice, who move the tongue, who pronounce words, and distinguish sensations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:26
verses.text: And when can I comprehend myself in myself? How then can I comprehend what is above myself? Yet the sight of God is promised to the human heart, and a certain operation of purifying the heart is enjoined; this is the counsel of Scripture.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:27
verses.text: Provide the means of seeing what thou lovest, before thou try to see it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:28
verses.text: For unto whom is it not sweet to hear of God and His Name, except to the ungodly, who is far removed, separated from Him?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:29
verses.text: Be therefore like Him in piety, and earnest in meditation: for "the invisible things of Him are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made;" look upon the things that are made, admire them, seek their author.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:30
verses.text: If thou art unlike, thou wilt turn back; if like, thou wilt rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:31
verses.text: And when, being like Him, thou shalt have begun to approach Him, and to feel God, the more love increaseth in thee, since God is love, thou wilt perceive somewhat which thou wast trying to say, and yet couldest not say.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:32
verses.text: Before thou didst feel God, thou didst think that thou couldest express God; thou beginnest to feel Him, and then feelest that what thou dost feel thou canst not express.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:33
verses.text: But when thou hast herein found that what thou dost feel cannot be expressed, wilt thou be mute, wilt thou not praise God? Wilt thou then be silent in the praises of God, and wilt thou not offer up thanksgivings unto Him who hath willed to make Himself known unto thee? Thou didst praise Him when thou wast seeking, wilt thou be silent when thou hast found Him? By no means; thou wilt not be ungrateful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:34
verses.text: Honour is due to Him, reverence is due to Him, great praise is due to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:35
verses.text: Consider thyself, see what thou art: earth and ashes; look who it is hath deserved to see, and What; consider who thou art, What to see, a man to see God! I recognise not the man's deserving, but the mercy of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:36
verses.text: Praise therefore Him who hath mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:37
verses.text: "Serve the Lord with gladness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:38
verses.text: All servitude is full of bitterness: all who are bound to a lot of servitude both are slaves, and discontented.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:39
verses.text: Fear not the servitude of that Lord: there will be no groaning there, no discontent, no indignation; no one seeketh to be sold to another master, since it is a sweet service, because we are all redeemed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:40
verses.text: Great happiness, brethren, it is, to be a slave in that great house, although in bonds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:41
verses.text: Fear not, bound slave, confess unto the Lord: ascribe thy bonds to thine own deservings; confess in thy chains, if thou art desirous they be changed into ornaments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:42
verses.text: At the same time thou art slave, and free; slave, because thou art created such; free, because thou art loved by God, by whom thou wast created: yea, free indeed, because thou lovest Him by whom thou wast made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:43
verses.text: Serve not with discontent; for thy murmurs do not tend to release thee from serving, but to make thee a wicked servant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:44
verses.text: Thou art a slave of the Lord, thou art a freedman of the Lord: seek not so to be emancipated as to depart from the house of Him who frees thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:45
verses.text: I will, therefore, saith he, live separate with a few good men: why should I live in common with crowds? Well: those very few good men, from what crowds have they been strained out? If however these few are all good: it is, nevertheless, a good and praiseworthy design in man, to be with such as have chosen a quiet life; distant from the bustle of the people, from noisy crowds, from the great waves of life, they are as if in harbour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:46
verses.text: Is there therefore here that joy? that jubilant gladness which is promised? Not as yet; but still groans, still the anxiety of temptations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:47
verses.text: For even the harbour hath an entrance somewhere or other; if it had not, no ship could enter it; it must therefore be open on some side: but at times on this open side the wind rusheth in; and where there are no rocks, ships dashed together shatter one another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:48
verses.text: Where then is security, if not even in harbour? And yet it must be confessed, it is true, that persons in harbour are in their degree much better off than when afloat on the main.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:49
verses.text: Let them love one another, as ships in harbour, let them be bound together happily; let them not dash against one another: let absolute equality be preserved there, constancy in love; and when perchance the wind rusheth in from the open side, let there be careful piloting there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:50
verses.text: Now what will one who perchance presideth over such places, nay, who serveth his brethren, in what are called monasteries, tell me? I will be cautious: I will admit no wicked man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:51
verses.text: How wilt thou admit no evil one?Those who are about to enter, do not know themselves; how much less dost thou know them? For many have promised themselves that they were about to fulfil that holy life, which has all things in common, where no man calleth anything his own, who have one soul and one heart in God: they have been put into the furnace, and have cracked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:52
verses.text: How then knowest thou him who is unknown even to himself?Where then is security? Here nowhere; in this life nowhere, except solely in the hope of the promise of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:53
verses.text: But there, when we shall reach thereunto, is complete security, when the gates are shut, and the bars of the gates of Jerusalem made fast; there is truly full jubilance, and great delight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:54
verses.text: Only do not thou feel secure in praising any sort of life: "judge no man blessed before his death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:55
verses.text: By this means men are deceived, so that they either do not undertake, or rashly attempt, a better life; because, when they choose to praise, they praise without mention of the evil that is mixed with the good: and those who choose to blame, do so with so envious and perverse a mind, as to shut their eyes to the good, and exaggerate only the evils which either actually exist there, or are imagined.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:56
verses.text: Thus it happeneth, that when any profession hath been ill, that is, incautiously, praised, if it hath invited men by its own reputation, they who betake themselves thither discover some such as they did not believe to be there; and offended by the wicked recoil from the good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:57
verses.text: Brethren, apply this teaching to your life, and hear in such a manner that ye may live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:58
verses.text: The Church of God, to speak generally, is magnified: Christians, and Christians alone, are called great, the Catholic (Church) is magnified; all love each other; each and all do all they can for one another; they give themselves up to prayers, fastings, hymns; throughout the whole world, with peaceful unanimity God is praised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:59
verses.text: Some one perhaps heareth this, who is ignorant that nothing is said of the wicked who are mingled with them; he cometh, invited by these praises, findeth bad men mixed with them, who were not mentioned to him before he came; he is offended by false Christians, he flieth from true Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:60
verses.text: Again, men who hate and slander them, precipitately blame them: asking, what sort of men are Christians? Who are Christians? Covetous men, usurers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:61
verses.text: Are not the very persons who fill the Churches on holidays the same who during the games and other spectacles fill the theatres and amphitheatres? They are drunken, gluttonous, envious, slanderers of each other.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:62
verses.text: There are such, but not such only.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:63
verses.text: And this slanderer in his blindness saith nothing of the good: and that praiser in his want of caution is silent about the bad.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:64
verses.text: Thus also in that common life of brethren, which exists in a monastery: great and holy men live therein, with daily hymns, prayers, praises of God; their occupation is reading; they labour with their own hands, and by this means support themselves; they seek nothing covetously; whatever is brought in for them by pious brethren, they use with contentedness and charity; no one claimeth as his own what another hath not; all love, all forbear one another mutually.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:65
verses.text: Thou hast praised them; thou hast praised; he who knoweth not what is going on within, who knoweth not how, when the wind entereth, ships even in harbour dash against one another, entereth as if in hope of security, expecting to find no man to forbear; he findeth there evil brethren, who could not have been found evil, if they had not been admitted (and they must be at first tolerated, lest they should perchance reform; nor can they easily be excluded, unless they have first been endured): and becometh himself impatient beyond endurance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:66
verses.text: Who asked me here? I thought that love was here.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:67
verses.text: And irritated by the perversity of some few men, since he hath not persevered in fulfilling his vow, he becometh a deserter of so holy a design, and guilty of a vow he hath never discharged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:68
verses.text: And then, when he hath gone forth himself too, he also becometh a reproacher, and a slanderer; and records those things only (sometimes real), which he asserts that he could not have endured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:69
verses.text: But the real troubles of the wicked ought to be endured for the society of the good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:70
verses.text: The Scripture saith unto him: "Woe unto those that have lost patience".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:71
verses.text: And what is more, he belcheth abroad the evil savour of his indignation, as a means to deter them who are about to enter; because, when he had entered himself, he could not persevere.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:72
verses.text: Of what sort are they? Envious, quarrelsome, men who forbear no man, covetous; saying, He did this there, and he did that there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:73
verses.text: Wicked one, why art thou silent about the good! Thou sayest enough of those whom thou couldest not endure: thou sayest nothing of those who endured thy wickedness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:74
verses.text: "O serve the Lord with gladness" : he addresseth you, whoever ye are who endure all things in love, and rejoice in hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:75
verses.text: "Serve the Lord," not in the bitterness of murmuring, but in the "gladness of love".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:76
verses.text: "Come before His presence with rejoicing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:77
verses.text: It is easy to rejoice outwardly: rejoice before the presence of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:78
verses.text: Let not the tongue be too joyful: let the conscience be joyful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:79
verses.text: "Come before His presence with a song".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:80
verses.text: "Be ye sure that the Lord He is God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:81
verses.text: Who knoweth not that the Lord, He is God? But He speaketh of the Lord, whom men thought not God: "Be ye sure that the Lord He is God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:82
verses.text: Let not that Lord become vile in your sight: ye have crucified Him, scourged Him, spit upon Him, crowned Him with thorns, clothed Him in a dress of infamy, hung Him upon the Cross, pierced Him with nails, wounded Him with a spear, placed guards at His tomb; He is God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:83
verses.text: "It is He that hath made us, and not we ourselves".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:84
verses.text: It is He that hath made us: "and without Him was not anything made that was made".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:85
verses.text: What reason have ye for exultation, what reason have ye for pride? Another made you; the Same who made you, suffereth from you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:86
verses.text: But ye extol yourselves, and glory in yourselves, as if ye were created by yourselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:87
verses.text: It is good for you that He who made you, make you perfect.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:88
verses.text: "We are His people, and the sheep of His pasture".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:89
verses.text: Sheep and one sheep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:90
verses.text: These sheep are one sheep: and how loving a Shepherd we have! He left the ninety and nine, and descended to seek the one, He bringeth it back on His own shoulders ransomed by His own blood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:91
verses.text: That Shepherd dieth without fear for the sheep, who on His resurrection regaineth His sheep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:92
verses.text: "Enter into His gates w ith confession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:93
verses.text: A t the gates is the beginning: begin with confession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:94
verses.text: Thence is the Psalm entitled, "A Psalm of Confession:" there be joyful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:95
verses.text: Confess that ye were not made by yourselves, praise Him by whom ye were made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:96
verses.text: Let thy good come from Him, in departing from whom thou hast caused thine evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:97
verses.text: "Enter into His gates with confession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:98
verses.text: Let the flock enter into the gates: let it not remain outside, a prey for wolves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:99
verses.text: And how is it to enter? "With confession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:100
verses.text: Let the gate, that is, the commencement for thee, be confession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:101
verses.text: Whence it is said in another Psalm, "Begin unto the Lord with confession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:102
verses.text: What he there calleth "Begin," here he calleth "Gates".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:103
verses.text: "Enter into His gates in confession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:104
verses.text: What? And when we have entered, shall we not still confess? Always confess Him: thou hast always what to confess for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:105
verses.text: It is hard in this life for a man to be so far changed, that no cause for censure be discoverable in him: thou must needs blame thyself, lest He who shall condemn blame thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:106
verses.text: Therefore even when thou hast entered His courts, then also confess.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:107
verses.text: When will there be no longer confession of sins? In that rest, in that likeness to the Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:108
verses.text: But consider what I have said: there will there be no confession of sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:109
verses.text: I said not, there will be no confession: for there will be confession of praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:110
verses.text: Thou wilt ever confess, that He is God, thou a creature; that He is thy Protector, thyself protected.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:111
verses.text: In Him thou shalt be as it were hid "Go into His courts with hymns; and confess unto Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:112
verses.text: Confess in the gates; and when ye have entered the courts, confess with hymns.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:113
verses.text: Hymn are praises.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:114
verses.text: Blame thyself, when thou art entering; when thou hast entered, praise Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:115
verses.text: "Open me the gates of righteousness," he saith in another Psalm, "that I may go into them, and confess unto the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:116
verses.text: Did he say, when I have entered, I will no longer confess? Even after his entrance, he will confess.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:117
verses.text: For what sins did our Lord Jesus Christ confess, when He said, "I confess unto Thee, O Father"? He confessed in praising Him, not in accusing Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:118
verses.text: "Speak good of His Name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:119
verses.text: "For the Lord is pleasant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:120
verses.text: Think not that ye faint in praising Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:121
verses.text: Your praise of Him is like food: the more ye praise Him, the more ye acquire strength, and He whom ye praise becometh the more sweet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:122
verses.text: "His mercy is everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:123
verses.text: For He will not cease to be merciful, after He hath freed thee: it belongeth to His mercy to protect thee even unto eternal life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:124
verses.text: "His mercy," therefore, "is to everlasting: and His truth from generation to generation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:125
verses.text: Understand by "from generation to generation," either every generation, or in two generations, the one earthly, the other heavenly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:126
verses.text: Here there is one generation which produceth mortals; another which maketh such as are everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:127
verses.text: His Truth is both here, and there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 100:128
verses.text: Imagine not that His truth is not here, if His truth were not here, he would not say in another Psalm: "Truth is risen out of the earth;" nor would Truth Itself say, Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:1
verses.text: Psalm CI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:2
verses.text: In this Psalm, we ought to seek in the whole body of it what we find in the first verse: "Mercy and judgment will I sing unto Thee, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:3
verses.text: Let no man flatter himself that he will never be punished through God's mercy; for there is judgment also; and let no man who hath been changed for the better dread the Lord's judgment, seeing that mercy goeth before it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:4
verses.text: For when men judge, sometimes overcome by mercy, they act against justice; and mercy, but not justice, seemeth to be in them: while sometimes, when they wish to enforce a rigid judgment, they lose mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:5
verses.text: But God neither loseth the severity of judgment in the bounty of mercy, nor in judging with severity loseth the bounty of mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:6
verses.text: Suppose we distinguish these two, mercy and judgment, by time; for possibly, they are not placed in this order without a meaning, so that he said not "judgment and mercy," but "mercy and judgment:" so that if we distinguish them by succession in time, perhaps we find that the present is the season for mercy, the future for judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:7
verses.text: How is it that the season of mercy cometh first? Consider first how it is with God, that thou also mayest imitate the Father, in so far as He shall permit thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:8
verses.text: "He maketh His sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:9
verses.text: Behold mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:10
verses.text: When thou seest the just and the unjust behold the same sun, enjoy the same light, drink from the same founts, satisfied with the same rain, blessed with the same fruits of the earth, inhale this air in the same way, possess equally the world's goods; think not that God is unjust, who giveth these things equally to the just and the unjust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:11
verses.text: It is the season of mercy, not as yet of judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:12
verses.text: For unless God spared at first through mercy, He would not find those whom He could crown through judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:13
verses.text: There is therefore a season for mercy, when the long-suffering of God calleth sinners to repentance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:14
verses.text: Hear the Apostle distinguishing each season, and do thou also distinguish it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:15
verses.text: "Thinkest thou," he saith, "O man, that judgest them that do such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?" And as if we were to reply, Why do I commit such sins daily, and no evil occurreth unto me? he goeth on to show to him the season of mercy: "Despisest thou the riches of His goodness, and forbearance, and long-suffering?" And he did indeed despise them; but the Apostle hath made him anxious.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:16
verses.text: "Not knowing," he saith, "that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?" Behold the season of mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:17
verses.text: But that he might not think this would last for ever, how did he in the next verse raise his fears? Now hear the season of judgment; thou hast heard the season of mercy, on which account, "mercy and judgment will I sing unto Thee, O Lord:" "But thou," saith the Apostle, "after thy hardness and impenitent heart, treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath, and revelation of the righteous judgment of God, who will render to every man according to his deeds".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:18
verses.text: Lo, "mercy and judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:19
verses.text: But he hath threatened concerning judgment: is therefore the judgment of God to be feared only, and not to be loved? To be feared by the wicked on account of punishment, to be loved by the good on account of the crown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:20
verses.text: Because then the Apostle hath alarmed the wicked in the testimony which I have quoted, hear where he giveth hope concerning judgment to the good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:21
verses.text: He puts forth himself, and shows in himself too the season of mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:22
verses.text: For unless he found a period of mercy, in what condition would judgment find him? A blasphemer, a persecutor, an injurer of others.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:23
verses.text: For he thus speaketh, and praiseth the season of mercy, in which season we are now living: "I who was before," he saith, "a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:24
verses.text: But perhaps he only hath obtained mercy? Hear how he cheereth us: "That in me," he saith, "first, Christ Jesus might show forth all long-suffering, for a pattern to them which should hereafter believe on Him to life everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:25
verses.text: What meaneth, "that He might show forth all long-suffering"? That every sinner and wicked man might see that Paul received pardon, and might not despair of himself? Lo, he hath instanced himself, and thereby cheered others also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:26
verses.text: But did Paul alone deserve this? For I had asserted, that as he raised our fears by the former testimony, so did he encourage us by the latter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:27
verses.text: When he said, "The Lord, the righteous Judge, shall render to me at that day:" he addeth, "and not to me only, but unto all them also that love His appearing" and His kingdom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:28
verses.text: Since therefore, brethren, we have a season of mercy, let us not on that account flatter, or indulge ourselves, saying, God spareth ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:29
verses.text: "I will sing to the harp, and will have understanding, in the spotless way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:30
verses.text: When Thou shalt come unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:31
verses.text: Except in the spotless way, thou canst neither sing to the harp, nor understand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:32
verses.text: If thou dost wish to understand, sing in the spotless way, that is, work with cheerfulness before thy God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:33
verses.text: What is the spotless way? Hear what followeth: "I walked in innocence, in the midst of my house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:34
verses.text: This spotless way beginneth from innocence, and it endeth also in innocence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:35
verses.text: Why seek many words? Be innocent: and thou hast perfected righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:36
verses.text: But who is innocent? He who while he hurteth not another, injureth not himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:37
verses.text: For he who hurteth himself, is not innocent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:38
verses.text: Some one saith: Lo, I have not robbed any one, I have not oppressed any one: I will live happily on my own substance, the fruits of my virtuous toil; I wish to have fine banquets, I wish to spend as much as pleaseth me, to drink with those whom I like as much as I please; whom have I robbed, whom have I oppressed, who hath complained of me? He seemeth innocent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:39
verses.text: But if he corrupt himself, if he overthrow the temple of God within himself, why hope that he will act with mercy toward others, and spare the wretched? Can that man be merciful to others, who unto himself is cruel? The whole of righteousness, therefore, is reduced to the one word, innocence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:40
verses.text: But the lover of iniquity, hateth his own soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:41
verses.text: When he loved iniquity, he fancied he was injuring others.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:42
verses.text: But consider whether he was injuring others: "He who loveth iniquity," he saith, "hateth his own soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:43
verses.text: He therefore who wishes to injure another, first injureth himself; nor doth he walk, since there is no room.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:44
verses.text: For all wickedness suffereth from narrowness: innocence alone is broad enough to walk in.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:45
verses.text: "I walked in the innocence of my heart, in the midst of my house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:46
verses.text: By the middle of his house, he either signifieth the Church herself; for Christ walketh in her: or his own heart; for our inner house is our heart: as he hath explained in the above words, "in the innocence of my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:47
verses.text: What is the innocence of the heart? The middle of his house? Whoever hath a bad house in this, is driven out of doors.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:48
verses.text: For whoever is oppressed within his heart by a bad conscience, just as any man in consequence of the overflow of a waterspout or of smoke goeth out of his house, suffereth not himself to dwell therein; so he who hath not a quiet heart, cannot happily dwell in his heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:49
verses.text: Such men go out of themselves in the bent of their mind, and delight themselves with things without, that affect the body; they seek repose in trifles, in spectacles, in luxuries, in all evils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:50
verses.text: Wherefore do they wish themselves well without? Because it is not well with them within, so that they may rejoice in a good conscience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:51
verses.text: "I set no wicked thing before my eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:52
verses.text: I did love no wicked thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:53
verses.text: And he explaineth this same wicked thing: "I hated them that do unfaithfulness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:54
verses.text: Attend, my brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:55
verses.text: If ye walk with Christ in the midst of His house, that is, if either in your heart ye have a good repose, or in the Church herself proceed on a good journey in the way of godliness; ye ought not to hate those unfaithful only who are without, but whomsoever also ye may have found within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:56
verses.text: Who are the unfaithful? They who hate the law of God; who hear, and do it not, are called unfaithful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:57
verses.text: Hate the doers of unfaithfulness, repel them from thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:58
verses.text: But thou shouldest hate the unfaithful, not men: one man who is unfaithful, hath, ye see, two names, man, and unfaithful: God made him man, he made himself unfaithful; love in him what God made, persecute in him what he made himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:59
verses.text: For when thou shalt have persecuted his unfaithfulness, thou killest the work of man, and freest the work of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:60
verses.text: "I hated the doers of unfaithfulness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:61
verses.text: "The wicked heart hath not cleaved unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:62
verses.text: The heart of a man, who wisheth not anything contrary to any that God wisheth, is called straight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:63
verses.text: If therefore the righteous heart followeth God, the crooked heart resisteth God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:64
verses.text: Suppose something untoward happeneth to him, he crieth out, "God, what have I done unto Thee? What sin have I committed?" He wisheth himself to appear just, God unjust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:65
verses.text: What is so crooked as this? It is not enough that thou art crooked thyself: thou must think thy rule crooked also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:66
verses.text: Reform thyself, and thou findest Him straight, in departing from whom thou hast made thyself crooked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:67
verses.text: He doth justly, thou unjustly; and for this reason thou art perverse, since thou callest man just, and God unjust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:68
verses.text: What man dost thou call just? Thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:69
verses.text: For when thou sayest, "What have I done unto Thee?" thou thinkest thyself just.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:70
verses.text: But let God answer thee: "Thou speakest truth: thou hast done nothing to Me: thou hast done all things unto thyself; for if thou hadst done anything for Me, thou wouldest have done good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:71
verses.text: For whatever is done well, is done unto Me; because it is done according to My commandment; but whatever of evil is done, is done unto thee, not unto Me; for the wicked man doth nothing except for his own sake, since it is not what I command".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:72
verses.text: When ye see such men, brethren, reprove them, convince and correct them: and if ye cannot reprove or correct them, consent not to them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:73
verses.text: "When the wicked man departed from me, I knew him not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:74
verses.text: I approved him not, I praised him not, he pleased me not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:75
verses.text: For we find the word "to know" occasionally used in Scripture, in the sense of "to be pleased".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:76
verses.text: For what is hidden from God, brethren? Doth He know the just, and doth He not know the unjust? What dost thou think of, that He doth not know? I say not, what thinkest thou; but what wilt thou ever think, that He will not have seen beforehand? God knoweth all things, then; and yet in the end, that is in judgment after mercy, He saith of some persons: "I will profess unto them, I never knew you; depart from Me, ye workers of iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:77
verses.text: Was there any one He did not know? But what meaneth, "I never knew you"? I acknowledge you not in My rule.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:78
verses.text: For I know the rule of My righteousness: ye agree not with it, ye have turned aside from it, ye are crooked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:79
verses.text: Therefore He said here also: "When the wicked man departed from Me, I knew him not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:80
verses.text: Therefore, "when the wicked man departed from me," that is, when the wicked man was unlike me, and was unwilling to imitate my paths, was unwilling in his wickedness to live as I had proposed myself for his imitation; "I knew him not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:81
verses.text: What meaneth, "I knew him not"? Not that I was ignorant of him, but that I did not approve him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:82
verses.text: "Whoso privily slandered his neighbour, him I persecuted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:83
verses.text: Behold the righteous persecutor, not of the man, but of the sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:84
verses.text: "With the proud eye, and the insatiable heart, I did not feed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:85
verses.text: What meaneth, "I did not feed with"? I did not eat in common with such.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:86
verses.text: Attend, beloved; since ye are about to hear something wonderful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:87
verses.text: If he did not feed with this man, he did not eat with him; for to feed is to eat; how is it then that we find our Lord Himself eating with the proud? It was not only with those publicans and sinners, for they were humble: for they acknowledged their weakness, and asked for the physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:88
verses.text: We find that He ate with the proud Pharisees themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:89
verses.text: A certain proud man had invited Him: it was the same who was displeased because a sinning woman, one of ill repute in the city, approached the feet of our Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:90
verses.text: That Pharisee was proud: the Lord ate with him; what is it therefore that he saith? "With such an one I did not eat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:91
verses.text: How doth He enjoin unto us what He hath not done Himself? He exhorteth us to imitate Himself: we see that He ate with the proud; how doth He forbid us to eat with the proud? We indeed, brethren, for the sake of reproof, abstain from communion with our brethren, and do not eat with them, that they may be reformed? We rather eat with strangers, with Pagans, than with those who hold with us, if we have seen that they live wickedly, that they may be ashamed, and amend; as the Apostle saith, "And if any man obey not our word by this Epistle, note that man, and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:92
verses.text: Yet count him not as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:93
verses.text: For the sake of healing others we usually do this; but nevertheless we often eat with many strangers and ungodly men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:94
verses.text: The pious heart hath its banquets, the proud heart hath its banquets: for it was on account of the food of the proud heart, that he said, "with an insatiable heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:95
verses.text: How is the proud heart fed? If a man is proud, he is envious: otherwise it cannot be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:96
verses.text: Pride is the mother of enviousness: it cannot but generate it, and ever coexist with it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:97
verses.text: Every proud man is, therefore, envious: if envious, he feedeth on the misfortunes of others.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:98
verses.text: Whence the Apostle saith, "But if ye bite and devour one another, take heed that ye be not consumed of one another".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:99
verses.text: Ye see them, then, eating: eat not with these: fly such banquets: for they cannot satisfy themselves with rejoicing in others' evils, because their hearts are insatiable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:100
verses.text: Beware thou art not caught in their feasts by the devil's noose.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:101
verses.text: Just as birds feed at the trap, or fishes at the hook, they were taken, when they fed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:102
verses.text: The ungodly therefore have their own feasts, the godly also have theirs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:103
verses.text: Hear the feasts of the godly: "Blessed are they who hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:104
verses.text: If therefore the godly eateth the meat of righteousness, and the ungodly of pride; it is no wonder if he is insatiable in heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:105
verses.text: He eateth the meat of iniquity: do not eat the meat of iniquity, and the proud in eye, and the insatiable in heart, eateth not with thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:106
verses.text: And whence wast thou fed? And what pleased thee, when he did not eat with thee? "Mine eyes," he saith, "were upon such as are faithful in the land, that they might sit with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:107
verses.text: That is, that with Me they might be seated In what sense are they "to sit"? "Ye shall sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:108
verses.text: The faithful of the earth judge, for to them it is said, "Know ye not, that we shall judge angels?" "Whoso walketh in a spotless way, he ministered unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:109
verses.text: To "Me," he saith, not to himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:110
verses.text: For many minister the Gospel, but unto themselves; because they seek their own things, not the things of Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:111
verses.text: "The proud man hath not dwelt in the midst of my house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:112
verses.text: Understand this of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:113
verses.text: The proud did not dwell in my heart: no such dwelt in my heart: for he hurried away from me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:114
verses.text: None but the meek and peaceful dwelt in my heart; the proud dwelt not there, for the unrighteous one dwelleth not in the heart of the righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:115
verses.text: Let the righteous be distant from thee, I know not how many miles and stations: ye dwell together, if ye have one heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:116
verses.text: "The proud doer hath not dwelt in the midst of my house: he that speaketh unjust things hath not directed in the sight of my eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:117
verses.text: This is the spotless way, where we understand when the Lord cometh unto us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:118
verses.text: "In the morning I destroyed all the ungodly that were in the land.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:119
verses.text: That I may root out all wicked doers from the city of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:120
verses.text: This is obscure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:121
verses.text: There are then wicked doers in the city of the Lord, and they at present, seemingly, s pared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:122
verses.text: Why so? Because it is the season of mercy: but that of judgment will come; for the Psalm thus began, "Of mercy and judgment will I sing unto Thee, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:123
verses.text: He at present spareth, He will then judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:124
verses.text: But when will He judge? When night shall have passed away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:125
verses.text: For this reason He hath said: "In the morning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:126
verses.text: When the day shall at last have arrived, night having passed by.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:127
verses.text: Why doth He spare them until the dawn? Because it was night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:128
verses.text: What meaneth, it was night? Because it was the season for mercy: He was merciful, while the hearts of men were hidden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:129
verses.text: Thou seest some one living ill; thou endurest him: for thou knowest not of what sort he will prove to be; since it is night; whether he who to-day liveth ill, to-morrow may live well; and whether he who to-day liveth well, to-morrow may be wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:130
verses.text: For it is night, and God endureth all men, since He is of long-suffering: He endureth them, that sinners may be converted unto Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:131
verses.text: But they who shall not have reformed themselves in that season of mercy, shall be slain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:132
verses.text: And wherefore? That they may be scattered abroad  from the city of the Lord, from the fellowship of Jerusalem, from the fellowship of the Saints, from the fellowship of the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:133
verses.text: But when shall they be slain? "At dawn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:134
verses.text: What meaneth, "at dawn"? When night shall have passed away.
