verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:135
verses.text: Wherefore now doth he spare? Because it is the season of mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:136
verses.text: Why doth He not always spare? Because, "Mercy and judgment will I sing unto Thee, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:137
verses.text: Brethren, let no man flatter himself: all the doers of iniquity shall be slain; Christ shall slay them at the dawn, and shall destroy them from His city.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:138
verses.text: But now while it is the time of mercy, let them hear Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 101:139
verses.text: Everywhere He crieth out by the Law, by the Prophets, by the Psalms, by the Epistles, by the Gospels: see that He is not silent; that He spareth; that He granteth mercy; but beware, for the judgment will come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:1
verses.text: Psalm CII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:2
verses.text: Behold, one poor man prayeth, and prayeth not in silence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:3
verses.text: We may therefore hear him, and see who he is: whether it be not perchance He, of whom the Apostle saith, "Though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, that ye through His poverty might be rich".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:4
verses.text: If it is He, then, how is He poor? For in what sense He is rich, who seeth not? What then is richer than He, by whom riches were made, even those which are not true riches? For through Him we have even these riches, ability, memory, character, health of body, the senses, and the conformation of our limbs: for when these are safe, even the poor are rich.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:5
verses.text: Through Him also are those greater riches, faith, piety, justice, charity, chastity, good conduct: for no man hath these, except through Him who justifieth the ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:6
verses.text: Behold, how rich! In one so rich, how are we to recognise these words? "I have eaten ashes as it were bread: and mingled my drink with weeping".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:7
verses.text: Have these so great riches come to this? The former state is a very high one, this is a very lowly one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:8
verses.text: Yet still examine whether this poor man be He; since, "The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:9
verses.text: Reflect also upon these words: "I am Thy servant, and the Son of Thine handmaid".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:10
verses.text: Observe, this handmaid, chaste, a virgin, and a mother: for there He received our poverty, when He was clothed in the form of a servant, emptying Himself; lest thou shouldest dread His riches, and in thy beggarly state shouldest not dare approach Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:11
verses.text: There, I say, He put on the form of a servant, there He was clothed with our poverty; there He made Himself poor, and us rich.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:12
verses.text: We are now drawing near to understand these things of Him: nevertheless we may not as yet rashly pronounce.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:13
verses.text: Let him add poverty then to poverty: let Him transfigure unto Himself our humble body: let Him be our Head, we His limbs, let there be two in one fleshFor He hath deigned to hold even us as His limbs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:14
verses.text: The penitent also are among His limbs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:15
verses.text: For they are not shut out, nor separated from His Church: nor would He make the Church His spouse, unless by words like these: "Repent ye, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:16
verses.text: Let us then hear what the head and the body prayeth, the bridegroom and bride, Christ and the Church, both one Person; but the Word and the flesh are not both one thing; the Father and the Word are both one thing; Christ and the Church are both one Person, one perfect man in the form of His own fulness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:17
verses.text: Let us hear therefore Christ, poor within us and with us, and for our sakes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:18
verses.text: For the title itself indicates the poor one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:19
verses.text: Lastly, remember that I conjectured who that poor one was: let us hear His prayer, and recognise His Person; and mistake not, when thou shalt have heard anything that cannot apply to His Head; it was for this reason that I have prefaced as I have, that whatever thou shalt hear of this description, thou mayest understand as sounding from the weakness of the body, and recognise the voice of the members in the head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:20
verses.text: The title is, "A Prayer of the afflicted, when he was tormented, and poured out his prayer before the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:21
verses.text: It is the same poor one who elsewhere saith: "From the ends of the earth will I call upon Thee, when my heart is in heaviness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:22
verses.text: He is afflicted because He is also Christ; who in the Prophet's words calleth Himself both Bridegroom and Bride: "He hath bound on me the diadem as on a bridegroom, and as a bride hath adorned me with an ornament".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:23
verses.text: He called Himself Bridegroom, He called Himself Bride; wherefore this, unless Bridegroom applieth to the Head, Bride to the body? They are one voice then, because they are one flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:24
verses.text: Let us hear, and recognise ourselves in these words; and if we see that we are without, let us labour to be there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:25
verses.text: "Hear my prayer, O Lord: and let my crying come unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:26
verses.text: "Hear my prayer, O Lord," is the same as, "Let my crying come unto Thee:" the feeling of the suppliant is shown by the repetition.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:27
verses.text: "Turn not Thy face away from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:28
verses.text: When did God turn away His Face from His Son? when did the Father turn away His Face from Christ? But for the sake of the poverty of my members, "Turn not away Thy face from me: whatsoever day I am troubled, incline Thine ear unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:29
verses.text: Thou art in trouble this day, I am in trouble; another is in trouble to-morrow, I am in trouble; after this generation other descendants, who succeed your descendants, are in trouble, I am in trouble; down to the end of the world, whoever are in trouble in My body, I am in trouble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:30
verses.text: Peter prayed, Paul prayed, the rest of the Apostles prayed; the faithful prayed in those times, the faithful prayed in the following times, the faithful prayed in the times of the Martyrs, the faithful pray in our times, the faithful will pray in the times of our descendants.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:31
verses.text: "Right soon:" for I now ask that which Thou art willing to grant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:32
verses.text: I ask not earthly things, as an earthly man; but redeemed at last from my former captivity, I long for the kingdom of heaven; "Hear me right soon:" for it is only to such a longing that Thou hast said, "Even while Thou art speaking, I will say, Here I am".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:33
verses.text: Wherefore dost thou call? in what tribulation? in what want? O poor one, before the gate of God all-rich, in what longing dost thou beg? from what destitution dost thou ask relief? from what want dost thou knock, that it may be opened unto thee?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:34
verses.text: "For my days are consumed away like smoke".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:35
verses.text: O days! if days: for where day is heard of, light is understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:36
verses.text: "My days," my times; wherefore, "like smoke," unless from the puffing up of pride?See smoke, like pride, ascending, swelling, vanishing: deservedly therefore failing, and not stedfast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:37
verses.text: "And my bones are scorched up as it were in an oven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:38
verses.text: Both my bones, and my strength, not without tribulation, not without burning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:39
verses.text: The bones of the body of Christ, the strength of His body, is it anywhere greater than in the Holy Apostles? And yet see that the bones are scorched.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:40
verses.text: "Who is offended, and I burn not?" They are brave, faithful, able interpreters and preachers of the word, living as they speak, speaking as they hear; they are clearly brave, yet all who suffer offences, are an oven to them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:41
verses.text: For there is love there, and more so in the bones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:42
verses.text: The bones are within all the flesh, and support all the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:43
verses.text: But if any man suffer any offence, and endanger his soul; the bone is scorched in proportion as it loveth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:44
verses.text: Look back to Adam, whence the human race sprung.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:45
verses.text: For how but from him was misery propagated? whence but from him is this hereditary poverty? Let him then, who in his own body was at one time in despair, now that he is set in Christ's body, say with hope, "My heart is smitten down, and withered like grass".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:46
verses.text: Deservedly, since all flesh is grass But how did this happen unto thee? "Since I have forgotten to eat my bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:47
verses.text: For God had given His commandment for bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:48
verses.text: For what is the bread of the soul? The serpent suggesting, and the woman transgressing, he touched the forbidden fruit, he forgot the commandment: his heart was smitten as it deserved, and withered like grass, since he forgot to eat his bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:49
verses.text: Having forgotten to eat bread, he drinketh poison: his heart is smitten, and withered like grass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:50
verses.text: Now eat that bread which thou hadst forgotten.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:51
verses.text: But this very Bread hath come, in whose body thou mayest remember the voice of thy forgetfulness, and cry out in thy poverty, so that thou mayest receive riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:52
verses.text: Now eat: for thou art in His body, who saith, "I am the living bread which came down from heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:53
verses.text: Thou hadst forgotten to eat thy bread; but after His crucifixion, "all the ends of the earth shall be reminded, and be converted unto the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:54
verses.text: After forgetfulness, let remembrance come, let bread be eaten from heaven, that we may live; not manna, as they did eat, and died; that bread, of which it is said, "Blessed are they who hunger and thirst after righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:55
verses.text: "For the voice of my groaning, the bones cleave unto my flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:56
verses.text: For many groan, and I also groan; even for this I groan, because they groan for a wrong cause.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:57
verses.text: That man hath lost a piece of money, he groaneth: he hath lost faith, he groaneth not: I weigh the money and the faith, and I find more cause for groaning for him who groaneth not as he ought, or doth not groan at all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:58
verses.text: He committeth fraud, and rejoiceth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:59
verses.text: With what gain, with what loss? He hath gained money, he hath lost righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:60
verses.text: For the latter reason, he who knoweth how to groan, groaneth; he who is near the head, who righteously clingeth to Christ's body, groaneth for this reason.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:61
verses.text: But the carnal do not groan for this reason, and they cause themselves to be groaned for, because they do not groan for this reason; nor can we despise them, whether they groan not at all, or groan for the wrong cause.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:62
verses.text: For we wish to correct them, we wish to amend them, we wish to reform them, and when we cannot, we groan; and when we groan, we are not separated from them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:63
verses.text: "I am become like a pelican in the wilderness, and like an owl among ruined walls".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:64
verses.text: Behold three birds and three places: the pelican, the owl, and the sparrow; and the three places are severally, the wilderness, the ruined walls, and the house-top.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:65
verses.text: The pelican in the wilderness, the owl in the ruined walls, and the sparrow in the house-top.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:66
verses.text: In the first place we must explain, what the pelican signifieth: since it is born in a region which maketh it unknown to us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:67
verses.text: It is born in lonely spots, especially  those of the river Nile in Egypt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:68
verses.text: Whatever kind of bird it is, let us consider what the Psalm intended to say of it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:69
verses.text: "It dwelleth," it saith, "in the w ilderness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:70
verses.text: Why enquire of its form, its limbs, its voice, its habits? As far as the Psalm telleth thee, it is a bird that dwelleth in solitude.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:71
verses.text: The owl is a bird that loveth night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:72
verses.text: Parietinae, or ruins, as we call them, are walls standing without roof, without inhabitants, these are the habitation of the owl.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:73
verses.text: And then as to the house-top and the sparrows, ye are familiar with them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:74
verses.text: I find, therefore, some one of Christ's body, a preacher of the word, sympathizing with the weak, seeking the gains of Christ, mindful of his Lord to come Let us see these three things from the office of His steward.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:75
verses.text: Hath such a man come among those who are not Christians? He is a pelican in the wilderness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:76
verses.text: Hath he come among those who were Christians, and have relapsed? He is an owl in the ruined walls; for he forsaketh not even the darkness of those who dwell in night, he wisheth to gain even these.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:77
verses.text: Hath he come among such as are Christians dwelling in a house, not as if they believed not, or as if they had let go what they had believed, but walking lukewarmly in what they believe? The sparrow crieth unto them, not in the wilderness, because they are Christians; nor in the ruined walls, because they have not relapsed; but because they are within the roof; under the roof rather, because they are under the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:78
verses.text: The sparrow above the flesh crieth out, husheth not up the commandments of God, nor becometh carnal, so that he be subject to the roof.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:79
verses.text: "What ye hear in the ear, that preach ye on the housetops".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:80
verses.text: There are three birds and three places; and one man may represent the three birds, and three men may represent severally the three birds; and the three sorts of places, are three classes of men: yet the wilderness, the ruined walls, and the house-top, are but three classes of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:81
verses.text: Let us not pass over what is said, or even read, of this bird, that is, the pelican; not rashly asserting anything, but yet not passing over what has been left to be read and uttered by those who have written it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:82
verses.text: Do ye so hear, that if it be true, it may agree; if false, it may not hold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:83
verses.text: These birds are said to slay their young with blows of their beaks, and for three days to mourn them when slain by themselves in the nest: after which they say the mother wounds herself deeply, and pours forth her blood over her young, bathed in which they recover life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:84
verses.text: This may be true, it may be false: yet if it be true, see how it agreeth with Him, who gave us life by His blood It agreeth with Him in that the mother's flesh recalleth to life her young with her blood; it agreeth well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:85
verses.text: For He calleth Himself a hen brooding over her youngIf, then, it be so truly, this bird doth closely resemble the flesh of Christ, by whose blood we have been called to life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:86
verses.text: But how may it agree with Christ, that the bird herself slays her own young? Doth not this agree with it? "I will slay, and I will make alive: I will wound, and I will heal".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:87
verses.text: Would the persecutor Saul have died, unless he were wounded from heaven; or would the preacher be raised up, unless by life given him from His blood? But let those who have written on the subject see to this; we ought not to allow our understanding of it  to rest upon doubtful ground Let us rather recognise this bird in the wilderness; as the Psalm expresseth it, "A pelican in the solitude".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:88
verses.text: I suppose that Christ born of a Virgin is here meant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:89
verses.text: He was born in loneliness, because He alone was thus born.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:90
verses.text: After the nativity, we come to His Passion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:91
verses.text: Born in the wilderness, because alone so born; suffering in the darkness of the Jews as it were in night, in their sin, as it were in ruins: what next? "I have watched:" and "am become even as it were a sparrow, that sitteth alone upon the house-top".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:92
verses.text: Thou hadst then slept amid the ruins, and hadst said, "I laid me down, and slept".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:93
verses.text: What meaneth, "I slept"? Because I chose, I slept: I slept for love of night: but, "I rose again," followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:94
verses.text: Therefore "I watched," is here said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:95
verses.text: But after He watched, what did He? He ascended into heaven, He became as a sparrow by flying; that is, by ascending; "alone on the house-top;" that is, in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:96
verses.text: He is therefore as the pelican by birth, as the owl by dying, as the sparrow by ascending again: there in the wilderness, as one alone; here in the ruined walls, as one slain by those who could not stand in the building; and here again watching and flying for our sakes alone on the house-top, He there intercedeth in our behalf For our Head is as the sparrow, His body as the turtle-dove.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:97
verses.text: "For the sparrow hath found her an house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:98
verses.text: What house? In heaven, where He doth mediate for us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:99
verses.text: "And the turtle-dove a nest," the Church of God hath found a nest from the wood of His Cross, where "she may lay her young," her children.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:100
verses.text: "Mine enemies revile me all day, and they that praised me are sworn together against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:101
verses.text: With their mouth they praised, in their heart they were laying snares for me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:102
verses.text: Hear their praise: "Master, we know that Thou art true, and teachest the way of God in truth, neither carest Thou for any man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:103
verses.text: Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar, or not?" And whence this evil repute, except because I came to make sinners my members, that by repentance they may be in my body? Thence is all the calumny, thence the persecution.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:104
verses.text: "Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners? They that be whole need not a physician, but they that be sick".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:105
verses.text: Would that ye were aware of your sickness, that ye might seek a physician; ye would not slay Him, and through your infatuated pride perish in a false health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:106
verses.text: "I have eaten ashes as it were bread: and mingled my drink with weeping".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:107
verses.text: Because He chose to have among His members these kinds of men, that they should be healed and set free, thence is the evil repute.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:108
verses.text: Now at this day what is the character of Pagan calumny against us? what, brethren, do ye conceive they tell us? Ye corrupt discipline, and pervert the morality of the human race.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:109
verses.text: Why dost thou attack us; say why? what have we done? By giving, he replieth, to men room for repentance, by promising impunity for all sins: for this reason men do evil deeds, careless of consequences, because everything is pardoned them, when they are converted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:110
verses.text: And what is to become of thee, miserable man, if there shall be no harbour of impunity? If there is only licence for sinning, and no pardon for sins, where wilt thou be, whither wilt thou go? Surely even for thee did it happen, that that afflicted one ate ashes as it were bread, and mingled His drink with weeping.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:111
verses.text: Doth not such a feast now please thee? But nevertheless, he replieth, men add to their sins under the hope of pardon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:112
verses.text: Nay, but they would add to them if they despaired of pardon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:113
verses.text: Dost thou not observe in what licentious cruelty gladiators live? whence this, except because, as destined for the sword and sacrifice, they choose to sate their lust, before they pour forth their blood?  Wouldest not thou also thus address thyself? I am already a sinner, already an unjust man, one already doomed to damnation, hope of pardon there is none: why should I not do whatever pleaseth me, although it be not lawful? why not fulfil, as far as I can, any longings I may have, if, after these, nothing but torments only be in store? Wouldest thou not thus speak unto thyself, and from this very despair become still worse? Rather than this, then, He who promiseth forgiveness, doth correct thee, saying, "As I live, saith the Lord, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:114
verses.text: For in order that men might not live the worse from despair, He promised a harbour of forgiveness; again, that they might not live the worse from hope of pardon, He made the day of death uncertain: fixing both with the utmost providence, both as a refuge for the returning, and a terror to the loitering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:115
verses.text: Eat ashes as bread, and mingle thy drink with weeping; by means of this banquet thou shalt reach the table of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:116
verses.text: Despair not; pardon hath been promised thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:117
verses.text: Thanks be to God, he saith, because it is promised; I hold fast the promise of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:118
verses.text: Now therefore live well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:119
verses.text: To-morrow, he replieth, I will live well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:120
verses.text: God hath promised the pardon; no one promised thee to-morrow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:121
verses.text: "And that because of thine indignation and wrath: because thou hast taken me up, thou hast cast me down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:122
verses.text: This is thy wrath, O Lord, in Adam: that wrath in which we were all born, which cleaveth unto us by our birth; the wrath froth the stock of iniquity, the wrath from the mass of sin: according to what the Apostle saith, "We also were once the children of wrath, even as others".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:123
verses.text: For He saith not, the wrath of God shall come upon him: but, "abideth upon him:" because that wrath in which he was born is not taken away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:124
verses.text: Man set in honour, is made in the image of God: raised up to this honour, lifted up from the dust, from the earth, he hath received a reasonable soul; by the vivacity of that very reason, he is placed before all beasts, cattle, birds that fly, and fishes For which of these hath reason to understand? Because none of them is created in the image of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:125
verses.text: Therefore, "Because Thou hast taken me up, Thou hast cast me down:" punishment followeth me, because Thou hast given me a free choice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:126
verses.text: For if Thou hadst not given me a free choice, and for this reason didst not make me better than cattle, just condemnation would not follow me when I sinned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:127
verses.text: Thus Thou hast taken me up in giving me freedom of choice, and by Thy judgment Thou hast cast me down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:128
verses.text: "My days have declined like a shadow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:129
verses.text: He had said above, "My days are consumed away like smoke;" and he now saith, "My days have declined like a shadow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:130
verses.text: In this shadow, day must be recognised; in this shadow, light must be discerned; lest afterward it be said in late and fruitless repentance, "What hath pride profited us? or what good hath riches with our vaunting brought us? All those things are passed away like a shadow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:131
verses.text: Say at this season, all things will pass away like a shadow, and thou mayest not pass away like a shadow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:132
verses.text: "My days have declined like a shadow, and I am withered like grass".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:133
verses.text: For he had said above, "my heart is smitten down, and I am withered like grass".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:134
verses.text: But the grass bedewed with the Saviour's blood will flourish afresh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:135
verses.text: "I have withered like grass;" I, that is, man, after that disobedience; this I have suffered from Thy just judgment: but what art Thou?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:136
verses.text: For not because I have fallen, hast Thou grown old: for Thou art strong to set me free, who hast been strong to humble me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:137
verses.text: "But Thou, O Lord, endurest for ever: and Thy remembrance throughout all generations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:138
verses.text: "Thy remembrance," because Thou dost not forget: "throughout all generations," forasmuch as we know the promise of life, both present and future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:139
verses.text: "Thou shalt arise, and have mercy upon Sion: for it is time that Thou have mercy upon her".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:140
verses.text: What time? "But when the fulness of time was come, God sent forth His Son, made of a woman, made under the Law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:141
verses.text: And where is Sion? "To redeem them that were under the Law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:142
verses.text: First then were the Jews: for thence were the Apostles, thence those more than five hundred brethren, thence that later multitude, who had but one heart and one soul toward God Therefore, "the time is come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:143
verses.text: What time? "Behold, now is the accepted time: behold, now is the day of salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:144
verses.text: Who saith this? That Servant of God, that Builder, who said, "Ye are God's building".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:145
verses.text: Here therefore what saith he? "For thy servants take pleasure in her stones".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:146
verses.text: In whose stones? In the stones of Sion? But there are those there that are not stones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:147
verses.text: Not stones of what? What then followeth? "and pity the dust thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:148
verses.text: I understand by the stones of Sion all the Prophets: there was the voice of preaching sent before, thence the ministry of the Gospel assumed, through their preaching Christ became known.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:149
verses.text: Therefore thy servants have taken pleasure in the stones of Sion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:150
verses.text: But those faithless apostates from God, who offended their Creator by their evil deeds, have returned to the earth, whence they were taken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:151
verses.text: They have become dust, they have become ungodly But wait, Lord; bear with us, Lord; be long-suffering, O Lord: let not the wind rush in, and sweep away this dust from the face of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:152
verses.text: Let thy servants come, let them come, let them acknowledge in the stones thy voice, let them pity the dust of Sion, let them be formed in thy image: let the dust say, lest it perish, "Remember that we are but dust".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:153
verses.text: This of Sion: was not that which crucified the Lord, dust? What is worse, it was dust from the ruined walls; altogether dust it was, but nevertheless it was not in vain said of this dust, "Father, forgive them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:154
verses.text: From this very dust there came a wall of so many thousands who believed, and who laid the price of their possessions at the Apostles' feet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:155
verses.text: From that dust then there arose a human nature formed and beautiful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:156
verses.text: Who among the heathen acted thus? How few are there whom we admire for having done thus, compared with the many thousands of these converts? At first suddenly three, afterwards five thousand; all living in unity, all laying the price of their possessions, when they had sold them, at the Apostles' feet, that it might be distributed to each, as each had need, who had one soul and one heart toward God Who made this even of that very dust, but He who created Adam himself out of dust? This then is concerning Sion, but not in Sion only.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:157
verses.text: "The heathen shall fear Thy Name, O Lord; and all the kings of the earth Thy Majesty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:158
verses.text: Now that Thou hast pitied Sion, now that Thy servants have taken pleasure in her stones, by acknowledging the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets; now that they have pitied her dust; so that man is formed, or rather re-formed, in life out of dust; hence preaching hath increased among the heathen: let the heathen fear Thy Name, let another wall approach also from the heathen, let the Corner Stone be recognised, let the two who come from different regions, but who no longer differ in belief, meet in close union.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:159
verses.text: "For the Lord shall build up Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:160
verses.text: This work is going on now.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:161
verses.text: O ye living stones, run to the work of building, not to ruin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:162
verses.text: Sion is in building, beware of the ruined walls: the tower is building, the ark is in building; remember the deluge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:163
verses.text: This work is in progress now; but when Sion is built, what will happen? "And He will appear in His glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:164
verses.text: That He might build up Sion, that He might be a foundation in Sion, He was seen by Sion, but not in His glory: "we have seen Him, and He had no form nor comeliness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:165
verses.text: But truly when He shall have come with His angels to judge, shall they not look then upon Him whom they have pierced? and they shall be put to confusion when too late, who refused confusion in early and healthful repentance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:166
verses.text: "He hath turned Him unto the prayer of the poor destitute, and despised not their desire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:167
verses.text: This is going on now in the building of Sion: the builders of Sion pray, they groan: He is the one poor, because the poor are many; because the thousands among so many nations are one in Him, because He is the unity of the peace of the Church, He is one, He is many: one, through love: many, on account of His extension.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:168
verses.text: Therefore we now pray, we now run: now, if any man hath used to be otherwise, and lived differently, let him eat ashes as it were bread, and mingle his drink with weeping.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:169
verses.text: Now is the time, when Sion is in building: now the stones are entering into the structure: when the building is finished, and the house dedicated, why dost thou run, to ask when too late, to beg in vain, to knock to no purpose, doomed to abide without with the five foolish virgins?  Therefore now run.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:170
verses.text: "Let these things be written for those that come after".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:171
verses.text: When these words were written, they profited not so much those among whom they were written for they were written to prophesy the New Testament, among men who lived according to the Old Testament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:172
verses.text: But God had both given that Old Testament, and had settled in that land of promise His own people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:173
verses.text: But since "Thy remembrance is from generation to generation," belongeth not to the ungodly, but to the righteous; "in our generation" belongeth to the Old Testament; while "in the other generation" belongeth to the New Testament; and since the New Testament announceth this that was prophesied, "Let these things be written for those that come after: and the people which shall be created, shall praise the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:174
verses.text: Not the people which is created, but "the people which shall be created".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:175
verses.text: What is clearer, my brethren? Here is prophesied that creation of which the Apostle saith: "Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature; old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:176
verses.text: "For he hath looked down from His lofty sanctuary".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:177
verses.text: He hath looked down from on high, that He might come unto the humble: from on high He hath become humble, that He might exalt the humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:178
verses.text: "Out of the heaven did the Lord look down upon the earth" : "that He might hear the mournings of such as are in fetters, and deliver the children of such as are put to death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:179
verses.text: We have found it said in another Psalm, "O let the sorrowful sighs of the fettered come before Thee;" and in a passage where the voice of the martyrs was meant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:180
verses.text: Whence are the martyrs in fetters?But God had bound them with these fetters, hard indeed and painful for a season, but endurable on account of His promises, unto whom it is said, "On account of the words of Thy lips, I have kept hard ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:181
verses.text: We must indeed groan in these fetters in order to gain the mercy of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:182
verses.text: These fetters must not be shunned, in order to gain a destructive freedom and the temporal and brief pleasure of this life, to be followed by perpetual bitterness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:183
verses.text: Accordingly Scripture, that we may not refuse the fetters of wisdom, thus addresseth us: "Then shall her fetters be a strong defence for thee, and her chains a robe of glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:184
verses.text: Let the fettered therefore cry out, as long as they are in the chains of the discipline of God, in which the martyrs have been tried: the fetters shall be loosed, and they shall fly away, and these very fetters shall afterwards be turned into an ornament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:185
verses.text: This hath happened with the martyrs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:186
verses.text: For what have the persecutors effected by killing them, except that their fetters were thereby loosed, and turned into crowns?The remission of sins, is the loosing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:187
verses.text: For what would it have profited Lazarus, that he came forth from the tomb, unless it were said to him, "loose him, and let him go"? Himself indeed with His voice aroused him from the tomb, Himself restored his life by crying unto him, Himself overcame the mass of earth that was heaped upon the tomb, and he came forth bound hand and foot: not therefore with his own feet, but by the power of Him who drew him forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:188
verses.text: This taketh place in the heart of the penitent: when thou hearest a man is sorry for his sins, he hath already come again to life; when thou hearest him by confessing  lay bare his conscience, he is already drawn forth from the tomb, but he is not as yet loosed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:189
verses.text: When is he loosed, and by whom is he loosed? "Whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth," He saith, "shall be loosed in Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:190
verses.text: Forgiveness of sins may justly be granted by the Church: but the dead man himself cannot be aroused except by the Lord crying within him; for God doth this within him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:191
verses.text: We speak to your ears: how do we know what may be going on in your hearts? But what is going on within, is not our doing, but His.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:192
verses.text: "That the name of the Lord may be declared in Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:193
verses.text: For at first, when the fettered were appointed unto death, the Church was oppressed: since these tribulations the Name of the Lord has been declared in Sion, with great freedom, in the Church herself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:194
verses.text: For she is Sion: not that one spot, at first proud, afterwards taken captive; but the Sion whose shadow was that Sion, which signifieth a watch-tower; because when placed in the flesh, we see into the things before us, extending ourselves not to the present which is now, but to the future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:195
verses.text: Thus it is a watch-tower: for every watcher gazes far.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:196
verses.text: Places where guards are set, are termed watch-towers: these are set on rocks, on mountains, in trees, that a wider prospect may be commanded from a higher eminence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:197
verses.text: Sion therefore is a watch-tower, the Church is a watch-tower.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:198
verses.text: If therefore the Church be a watch-tower, the Name of the Lord is already declared there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:199
verses.text: Not the Lord's Name only is declared in that Sion, but "His praise," He saith, "in Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:200
verses.text: And how is it declared? "In the nations gathering together in one, and the kingdoms, that they may serve the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:201
verses.text: How is this accomplished, unless by the blood of the slain? How accomplished, but by the groans of the fettered? Those therefore who were in tribulation and humility have been heard; that in our times the Church might be in the great glory which we see her in, so that the very kingdoms which then persecuted her, now serve the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:202
verses.text: "She answered Him in the way of His strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:203
verses.text: The preceding words show, that either "His praise," or "Jerusalem," answered: for it was said, "And His praise in Jerusalem; in the nations gathering together in one, and the kingdoms, that they may serve the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:204
verses.text: Respondit ei".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:205
verses.text: We cannot say, "the kingdoms answered," for he would have said responderunt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:206
verses.text: Respondit ei.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:207
verses.text: We cannot say, "the nations answered," for he would have said, responderunt (in the plural).

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:208
verses.text: Since then it is Respondit ei, in the singular, we look for the singular number above, and find that the words, "His praise," and "Jerusalem," are the only words in which we find it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:209
verses.text: But since it is doubtful, whether it be "His praise," or "Jerusalem," let us expound it each way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:210
verses.text: How did "His praise" answer Him? When they who are called by Him thank Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:211
verses.text: For He calleth, we answer; not by our voice, but by our faith; not by our tongue, but by our life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:212
verses.text: From His elect and holy men, Jerusalem also answereth Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:213
verses.text: For Jerusalem also was called: and the first Jerusalem refused to hear, and it was said unto her, "Behold, thy house shall be left unto the desolate".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:214
verses.text: But that Jerusalem, of whom it was written, "Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear," "She hath answered Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:215
verses.text: What meaneth, "She hath answered Him"? She despiseth Him not when He called.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:216
verses.text: He sent rain, She gave fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:217
verses.text: "She answered Him:" but where? "in the path of His strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:218
verses.text: The Church therefore answered Him not in the way of weakness; because after His resurrection He called the Church from the whole world, no longer weak upon the cross, but strong in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:219
verses.text: For it is not the praise of the Christian faith that they believe that Christ died, but that they believe that He arose from the dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:220
verses.text: Even the Pagan believeth that He died; and maketh this a charge against thee, that thou hast believed in one dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:221
verses.text: What then is thy praise? It is that thou believest that Christ arose from the dead, and that thou dost hope that thou shalt rise from the dead through Christ: this is the praise of faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:222
verses.text: "For if thou shalt confess with thy mouth that Jesus is the Lord, and shalt believe in thy heart that God hath raised Him from the dead, thou shalt be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:223
verses.text: This is the faith of Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:224
verses.text: In this faith then, in which the Church is gathered, "She hath answered Him," She gave Him worship according to His commandments: "in the path of His strength," not in the path of His weakness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:225
verses.text: How she answered Him, ye have already heard above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:226
verses.text: "In the gathering of the nations into one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:227
verses.text: Herein she answered Him, in unity: he who is not in unity, answereth Him not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:228
verses.text: For He is One, the Church is unity: none but unity answereth to Him who is One.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:229
verses.text: Since some were destined to say against her, She hath existed, and no longer doth exist; "Show me," He saith, "the shortness of my days," what is it, that I know not what apostates from me murmur against me? why is it that lost men contend that I have perished? For they surely say this, that I have been, and no longer am: "Show me the shortness of my days".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:230
verses.text: I do not ask from Thee about those everlasting days: they are without end, where I shall be; it is not those I ask of: I ask of temporal days; show unto me my temporal days; "show me the shortness," not the eternity, "of my days".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:231
verses.text: Declare unto me, how long I shall be in this world: on account of those who say, "She hath been," and is no more: on account of those who say, The Scriptures are fulfilled, all nations have believed, but the Church hath become apostate, and hath perished from among all nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:232
verses.text: Seest thou not that there are still nations among whom the Gospel hath not been preached? Since then it is needful that what the Lord spoke shall be fulfilled, declaring unto the Church the shortness of my days, that this Gospel be preached in all nations, and then that the end may come, why is it that thou sayest that the Church hath already perished from among all nations, when the Gospel is being preached for this purpose, that it may be in all nations? Therefore the Church remaineth even unto the end of the world, in all nations; and this is the shortness of Her days, because all that is limited is short; so that She may pass into eternity from this brief existence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:233
verses.text: May heretics be lost, may that which they are be lost, and may they be found, that they may be what they are not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:234
verses.text: Shortness of days will be unto the end of the world: shortness for this reason, because the whole of this season, I say not from this day unto the end of the world, but from Adam down to the end of the world, is a mere drop compared with eternity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:235
verses.text: Let not therefore heretics flatter themselves against me, because I said, "the shortness of my days," as if they would not last down to the end of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:236
verses.text: For what hath he added? "O my God, take me not away in the midst of my days".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:237
verses.text: Deal Thou not with me according as heretics speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:238
verses.text: Lead me on unto the end of the world, not only to the middle of my days; and finish my short days, that Thou mayest afterwards grant unto me eternal days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:239
verses.text: Wherefore then hast thou asked concerning the shortness of thy days? Wherefore? Dost thou wish to hear? "Thy years are in the generation of generations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:240
verses.text: This is why I asked concerning those short days, because although my days should endure unto the end of the world, yet they are short in comparison of Thy days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:241
verses.text: For "Thy years are in the generation of generations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:242
verses.text: Wherefore doth he not say, Thy years are unto worlds of worlds; for thus rather is eternity usually signified in the holy Scriptures; but he saith, "Thy years are in the generation of generations"? But what are thy years? what, but those which do not come, and then pass away? what, but they which come not, so as to cease again? For every day in this season so cometh as to cease again; every hour, every month, every year; nothing of these is stationary; before it hath come, it is to be; after it hath come, it will not be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:243
verses.text: Those everlasting years of thine, therefore, those years that are not changed, "are in the generation of generations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:244
verses.text: There is a "generation of generations;" in that shall thy years be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:245
verses.text: There is one such, and if we acknowledge it aright, we shall be in it, and the years of God shall be in us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:246
verses.text: How shall they be in us? Just as God Himself shall be in us: whence it is said, "That God may be all in all".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:247
verses.text: For the years of God, and God Himself, are not different: but the years of God are the eternity of God: eternity is the very substance of God, which hath nothing changeable; there nothing is past, as if it were no longer: nothing is future, as if it existed not as yet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:248
verses.text: There is nothing there but, Is: there is not there, Was, and Will be; because what was, is now no longer: and what will be, is not as yet: but whatever is there, simply Is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:249
verses.text: Behold this great I Am! What is man's being to this? To this great I Am, what is man, whatever he be? Who can understand that To Be? who can share it? who can pant, aspire, presume that he may be there? Despair not, human frailty! "I am," He saith, "the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:250
verses.text: Thou hast heard what I am in Myself: now hear what I am on thy account.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:251
verses.text: This eternity then hath called us, and the Word burst forth from eternity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:252
verses.text: It is now eternity, it is now the Word, and no longer time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:253
verses.text: From so many generations thou wilt gather together all the holy offspring of all generations, and wilt form one generation thence: "In" this "generation of generations are Thy years," that is, that eternity will be in that generation, which is collected from all generations, and reduced into one; this shall share in Thy eternity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:254
verses.text: Other generations are born for fulfilling their times, out of which this one is regenerated for ever; though changed it shall be endued with life, it shall be fitted to bear Thee, receiving strength from Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:255
verses.text: "Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth: and the Heavens are the work of Thy hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:256
verses.text: God laid the foundation of the earth, we know: the heavens are the works of His hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:257
verses.text: For do not imagine that God doth one thing with His hand, another by His word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:258
verses.text: What He doth by His word, He doth by His hand: for He hath not distinct bodily members, who said, "I Am That I Am".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:259
verses.text: And perhaps His Word is His hand, assuredly His hand is His power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:260
verses.text: For inasmuch as it is said, "Let there be a firmament," and there was a firmament; He is understood to have created it by His Word; but when He said, "Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness;" He seemeth to have created him by His hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:261
verses.text: Hear therefore: "The heavens are the work of Thy hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:262
verses.text: Lo, what He created by His word, He created also by His hands; because He created them through His excellence, through His power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:263
verses.text: Observe rather what He created, and seek not to know in what manner He created them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:264
verses.text: It is much to thee to understand how He created them, since He created thyself so, that thou mayest first be a servant obeying, and afterwards perhaps a friend understanding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:265
verses.text: "They shall perish, but Thou shalt endure".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:266
verses.text: The Apostle Peter saith this openly: "By the word of God the heavens were of old," etc He hath said then that the heavens have already perished by the flood: and we know that the heavens perished as far as the extent of this atmosphere of ours.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:267
verses.text: For the water increased, and filled the whole of that space in which birds fly; thus perished the heavens that are near the earth; those heavens which are meant when we speak of the birds of heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:268
verses.text: But there are heavens of heavens higher than these in the firmament: but whether these also shall perish by fire, or those only which perished also by the flood, is a much harder question among the learned, nor can it easily, especially in a limited space of time, be explained.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:269
verses.text: Let us therefore dismiss or put it off; nevertheless, let us know that these things perish, and that God endureth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:270
verses.text: Perhaps by the heavens we here may understand, without being far-fetched, the righteous themselves, the saints of God, abiding in whom God hath thundered in His commandments, lightened in His miracles, watered the earth with the wisdom of truth, for "The heavens have declared the glory of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:271
verses.text: But shall they perish? Shall they in any sense perish? In what sense? As a garment What is, as a garment? As to the body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:272
verses.text: For the body is the garment of the soul; since our Lord called it a garment, when He said, "Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?" How then doth the garment perish? "Though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:273
verses.text: They then shall perish: but as to the body: "But Thou shalt endure".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:274
verses.text: Such heavens therefore shall  perish; not, however, for ever; they shall perish, that they may be changed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:275
verses.text: Doth not the Psalm say this? Read the following: "They shall all wax old as doth a garment; and as a vesture shalt Thou change them, and they shall be changed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:276
verses.text: Thou hearest of the garment, of the vesture, and dost thou understand anything but the body? We may therefore hope for the change of our bodies also, but from Him who was before us, and abideth after us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:277
verses.text: "But Thou art the same, and Thy years shall not fail".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:278
verses.text: But what are we to those years with these beggarly years? and what are they? Yet we ought not to despair.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:279
verses.text: He had already said in His great and exceeding Wisdom, "I Am That I Am;" and yet He saith to console us, "I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob:" and we are Abraham's seed: even we, although abject, although dust and ashes, trust in Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:280
verses.text: We are servants: but for our sakes our Lord took the garb of a servant: for us who are mortal the Immortal One deigned to die, for our sakes He showed His example of resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:281
verses.text: Let us therefore hope that we may reach these lasting years, in which days are not spent in a revolution of the Sun, but what is abideth even as it is, because it alone truly Is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:282
verses.text: "The children of Thy servants shall dwell there: and their seed shall stand fast for ages" : for the age of ages, the age of eternity, the age that abideth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:283
verses.text: But, "the children," he saith, "of Thy servants:" is it to be feared lest we be the servants of God, and our children, and not ourselves, dwell there? Or if we are the children of the servants, inasmuch as we are the Apostles' children, what are we to say? Can those children rising after have so unhappy a presumption, as to boast in their late succession, and so to venture to say, We shall be there; the Apostles will not be there? May this be far from their piety as children, from their faith as little ones, from their understanding when of age! The Apostles also will be there: rams go before, lambs follow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:284
verses.text: Wherefore then, "the children of Thy servants;" and not in brief, "Thy servants"? Both they are Thy servants, and their children are Thy servants; and the children of these, their grandsons, what are they but Thy servants? Thou wouldest include them all briefly, if Thou shouldest say, Thy servants shall dwell therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:285
verses.text: "The children of Thy servants," are the works of Thy servants; no one shall dwell there, but through his own works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:286
verses.text: What therefore meaneth, Their children shall dwell? Let no man boast that he shall dwell there, if he calleth himself God's servant, and hath not works; for none but children shall dwell there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:287
verses.text: What meaneth therefore, "The children of Thy servants shall dwell there"? Thy servants shall dwell there by their own works, Thy servants shall dwell there through their own children.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:288
verses.text: Be not therefore barren, if thou dost wish to dwell there; send before the children whom thou mayest follow, by sending them before thee, not by burying them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 102:289
verses.text: Let thy children lead thee to the land of promise, the land of the living, not of the dying: whilst thou art living here in this pilgrimage, let them go before thee, let them receive thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:1
verses.text: Psalm CIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:2
verses.text: "Bless the Lord, O my soul! and all that is within me, His holy Name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:3
verses.text: I suppose that he speaketh not of what is within the body; I do not suppose him to mean this, that our lungs and liver, and so forth, are to burst forth into the voice of blessing of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:4
verses.text: There are lungs in our breast indeed, like a kind of bellows, which send forth successive breathings, which breathing forth of the air inhaled is pressed out into voice and sound, when the words are articulated; nor can any utterance sound forth from our mouth, but what the pressed lungs have given vent to; but this is not the meaning here; all this relateth to the ears of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:5
verses.text: God hath ears: the heart also hath a voice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:6
verses.text: A man speaketh to the things within him, that they may bless God, and saith unto them, "all that is within me bless His holy Name!" Dost thou ask the meaning of what is within thee? Thy soul itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:7
verses.text: In saying then, "all that is within me, bless His holy Name," it only repeateth the above, "Bless the Lord, O my soul:" for the word "Bless," is understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:8
verses.text: Cry out with thy voice, if there be a man to hear; hush thy voice, when there is no man to hear thee; there is never wanting one to hear all that is within thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:9
verses.text: Blessing therefore hath already been uttered from our mouth, when we were chanting these very words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:10
verses.text: We sung as much as sufficed for the time, and were then silent: ought our hearts within us to be silent to the blessing of the Lord? Let the sound of our voices bless Him at intervals, alternately, let the voice of our hearts be perpetual.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:11
verses.text: When thou comest to church to recite a hymn, thy voice soundeth forth the praises of God: thou hast sung as far as thou couldest, thou hast left the church; let thy soul sound the praises of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:12
verses.text: Thou art engaged in thy daily work: let thy soul praise God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:13
verses.text: Thou art taking food; see what the Apostle saith: "Whether ye eat or drink, do all to the glory of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:14
verses.text: I venture to say; when thou sleepest, let thy soul praise the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:15
verses.text: Let not thoughts of crime arouse thee, let not the contrivances of thieving arouse thee, let not arranged plans of corrupt dealing arouse thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:16
verses.text: Thy innocence even when thou art sleeping is the voice of thy soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:17
verses.text: "Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all His rewards".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:18
verses.text: But the rewards of the Lord cannot be before thine eyes unless thy sins are before thine eyes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:19
verses.text: Let not delight in past sin be before thine eyes, but let the condemnation of sin be before thine eyes: condemnation from thee, forgiveness from God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:20
verses.text: For thus God rewardeth thee, so that thou mayest say, "How shall I reward the Lord for all His rewards unto me?" This it was that the martyrs considering (whose memory we are this day celebrating), and all the saints who have despised this life, and as ye have heard in the Epistle of St.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:21
verses.text: John, laid down their lives for the brethren, which is the perfection of love, even as our Lord saith: "Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends:" this the holy martyrs, then, considering, despised their lives here, that they might find them there, following our Lord's words when He said, "He that loveth his life, shall lose it; and he that loseth his life for My sake, shall keep it unto life eternal".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:22
verses.text: "Forget not," he saith, "all His rewards:" not awards, but "rewards".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:23
verses.text: For something else was due, and what was not due hath been paid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:24
verses.text: Whence also these words: "What," he asketh, "shall I reward the Lord for all His rewards unto me?" Thou hast rewarded good with evil; He rewardeth evil with good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:25
verses.text: How hast thou, O man, rewarded thy God with evil for good? Thou who hast once been a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious, hast rewarded blasphemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:26
verses.text: For what good things? First, because thou art: but a stone also is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:27
verses.text: Next, because thou livest: but a brute also liveth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:28
verses.text: What reward wilt thou give the Lord, for His having created thee above all the cattle; and above all the fowls of the air, in His image and likeness? Seek not how to reward Him: give back unto Him His own image: He requireth no more; He demandeth His own coin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:29
verses.text: Think thou, soul, of all the rewards of God, in thinking over all thy wicked deeds: for as many as are thy sins, so many are His rewards of good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:30
verses.text: And what present, what offering, what sacrifice, canst thou ever tender unto Him?What wilt thou reward the Lord with? For thou wast reflecting, and couldest not find: "I will receive the cup of salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:31
verses.text: What? hath not the Lord Himself given the cup of salvation? Reward Him from thine own, if thou canst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:32
verses.text: I would say, No, do it not; reward Him not from thine own; God doth not will to be rewarded from thine own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:33
verses.text: If thou rewardest Him from thine own, thou rewardest sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:34
verses.text: For all that thou hast thou hast from Him: sins only thou hast of thine own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:35
verses.text: He doth not wish to be rewarded from thine, He doth will from His own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:36
verses.text: Just as, if thou shouldest bring to a husbandman, from the land which he hath sown, an ear of wheat, thou hast rewarded him from the husbandman's own produce; if thorns, that hast offered him of thine own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:37
verses.text: Reward truth, in truth praise the Lord: if thou shalt choose to reward Him from thine own, thou wilt lie.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:38
verses.text: He who speaketh a lie, speaketh of his own If he who speaketh a lie, speaketh of his own: so he who speaketh truth, speaketh of the Lord's.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:39
verses.text: But what is to receive the cup of salvation, but to imitate the Passion of our Lord?I will receive the cup of Christ, I will drink of our Lord's Passion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:40
verses.text: Beware that thou fail not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:41
verses.text: But, "I will call upon the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:42
verses.text: They then who failed, called not upon the Lord; they presumed in their own strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:43
verses.text: Do thou so return, as remembering that thou art returning what thou hast received.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:44
verses.text: So then let thy soul bless the Lord, as not to forget all His rewards.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:45
verses.text: Hear ye all His rewards.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:46
verses.text: "Who forgiveth all thy sin: who healeth all thine infirmities".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:47
verses.text: Behold His rewards.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:48
verses.text: What, save punishment, was due unto the sinner? What was due to the blasphemer, but the hell of burning fire? He gave not these rewards: that thou mayest not shudder with dread: and without love fear Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:49
verses.text: But thou art a sinner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:50
verses.text: Turn again, and receive these His rewards: He "forgiveth all thy sin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:51
verses.text: Yet even after remission of sins the soul herself is shaken by certain passions; still is she amid the dangers of temptation, still is she pleased with certain suggestions; with some she is not pleased, and sometimes she consenteth unto some of those with which she is pleased: she is taken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:52
verses.text: This is infirmity: but He "healeth all thine infirmities".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:53
verses.text: All thine infirmities shall be healed: fear not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:54
verses.text: They are great, thou wilt say: but the Physician is greater.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:55
verses.text: No infirmity cometh before the Almighty Physician as incurable: only suffer thou thyself to be healed: repel not His hands; He knoweth how to deal with thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:56
verses.text: Be not only pleased when He cherisheth thee, but also bear with Him when He useth the knife: bear the pain of the remedy, reflecting on thy future health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:57
verses.text: Thou dost not endure in uncertainty: He who promised thee health, cannot be deceived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:58
verses.text: The physician is often deceived: and promiseth health in the human body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:59
verses.text: Why is he deceived? Because he is not healing his own creature.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:60
verses.text: God made thy body, God made thy soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:61
verses.text: He knoweth how to restore what He hath made, He knoweth how to fashion again what He hath already fashioned: do thou only be patient beneath the Physician's hands: for He hateth one who rejects His hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:62
verses.text: This doth not happen with the hands of a human physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:63
verses.text: "Who redeemeth thy life from corruption".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:64
verses.text: Behold, "the body which is corrupted, weigheth down the soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:65
verses.text: The soul then hath life in a corruptible body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:66
verses.text: What sort of life? It suffereth burdens, it beareth weights.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:67
verses.text: How great obstacles are there to thinking of God Himself, as it is right that men should think of God, as if interrupting us from the necessity of human corruption? how many influences recall us, how many interrupt, how many withdraw the mind when fixed on high? what a crowd of illusions, what tribes of suggestions? All this in the human heart, as it were, teemeth with the worms of human corruption.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:68
verses.text: We have set forth the greatness of the disease, let us also praise the Physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:69
verses.text: Shall not He then heal thee, who made thee such as to be in health, hadst thou chosen to keep the law of health which thou hadst received?First think of thine own health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:70
verses.text: Sometimes a man is stricken in his own house, on his bed, with a more than usually manifest disorder; although this disorder too, which men dislike to contemplate, be plain; yet each man may be attacked with that sickness for which human physicians are sought, and may gasp with fever in his bed; perhaps he may wish to consider of his domestic affairs, to make some order or disposition relating to his estate or his house; at once he is recalled from such cares by the anxiety of his friends, plainly expressed around him, and he is advised to dismiss these subjects, and first to take thought for his health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:71
verses.text: This then is addressed unto thee, and to all men: if thou art not sick, think of other things: if thy very infirmity prove thee sick, first take heed of thy health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:72
verses.text: Christ is thy health: think therefore of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:73
verses.text: Receive the cup of His saving Health, "who healeth all thine infirmities;" if thou shalt choose, thou shalt gain this Health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:74
verses.text: For thy life hath been redeemed from corruption: rest secure now: the contract of good faith hath been entered upon; no man deceives, no man circumvents, no man oppresses, thy Redeemer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:75
verses.text: He hath here made a barter, He hath already paid the price, He hath poured forth His blood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:76
verses.text: The only Son of God, I say, hath shed His blood for us: O soul, raise thyself, thou art of so great price.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:77
verses.text: "He redeemeth thy life from corruption".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:78
verses.text: "Who crowneth thee with mercy and loving-kindness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:79
verses.text: Thou hadst perhaps begun to be in a manner proud, when thou didst hear the words, "He crowneth thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:80
verses.text: I am then great, I have then wrestled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:81
verses.text: By whose strength? By thine, but supplied by Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:82
verses.text: He crowneth thee, because He is crowning His own gifts, not thy deservings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:83
verses.text: "I laboured more abundantly than they all," said the Apostle; but see what he addeth: "yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:84
verses.text: It is then by His mercy that thou art crowned; in nothing be proud; ever praise the Lord; forget not all His rewards.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:85
verses.text: It is a reward when thou, a sinner and an ungodly man, hast been called, that thou mayest be justified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:86
verses.text: It is a reward, when thou art raised up and guided, that thou mayest not fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:87
verses.text: It is a reward, when strength is given thee, that thou mayest persevere unto the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:88
verses.text: It is a reward, that even that flesh of thine by which thou wast oppressed riseth again and that not even a hair of thy head perisheth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:89
verses.text: It is a reward, that after thy resurrection thou art crowned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:90
verses.text: It is a reward, that thou mayest praise God Himself for evermore without ceasing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:91
verses.text: After the battle, then, I shall be crowned; after the crown, what shall I do? "He who satisfieth thy longing with good things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:92
verses.text: Seek thy own good, O soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:93
verses.text: For one thing is good to one creature, another to another, and all creatures have a certain good of their own, to the completeness and perfection of their nature.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:94
verses.text: There is a difference as to what is essential to each imperfect thing, in order that it may be made perfect; seek for thy own good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:95
verses.text: "There is none good but One, that is, God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:96
verses.text: The highest good is thy good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:97
verses.text: What then is wanting unto him to whom the highest good is good? For there are inferior goods, which are good to different creatures respectively.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:98
verses.text: What, brethren, is good unto the cattle, save to fill the belly, to prevent want, to sleep, to indulge themselves, to exist, to be in health, to propagate? This is good to them: and within certain bounds it hath an allotted measure of good, granted by God, the Creator of all things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:99
verses.text: Dost thou seek such a good as this? God giveth also this: but do not pursue it alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:100
verses.text: Canst thou, a coheir of Christ, rejoice in fellowship with cattle? Raise thy hope to the good of all goods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:101
verses.text: He will be thy good, by whom thou in thy kind hast been made good, and by whom all things in their kind were made good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:102
verses.text: For God made all things very good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:103
verses.text: When shall my longing be satisfied with good things? when, dost thou ask? "Thy youth shall be renewed as the eagle's".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:104
verses.text: Dost thou then ask when thy soul is to be satisfied with good things? When thy youth shall be restored.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:105
verses.text: And he addeth, as an eagle's.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:106
verses.text: Something here lieth hidden; what however is said of the eagle, we will not pass over silently, since it is not foreign to our purpose to understand it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:107
verses.text: Let this only be impressed upon our hearts, that it is not said without cause by the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:108
verses.text: For it hath intimated unto us a sort of resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:109
verses.text: And indeed the youth of the eagle is restored, but not into immortality, for a similitude hath been given, as far as it could be drawn from a thing mortal to signify a thing immortal, not to demonstrate it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:110
verses.text: The eagle is said, after it becometh overpowered with bodily age, to be incapable of taking food from the immoderate length of its beak, which is always increasing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:111
verses.text: For after the upper part of its beak, which forms a crook above the lower part, hath increased from old age to an immoderate length, the length of this increase will not allow of its opening its mouth, so as to form any interval between the lower beak and the crook above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:112
verses.text: For unless there be such an opening, it hath no power of biting like a forceps, by which to shear off what it may put within its jaws.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:113
verses.text: The upper part therefore increasing, and being too far hooked over, it cannot open its mouth, and take any food.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:114
verses.text: This old age doth to it, it is weighed down with the infirmity of age, and becometh too weak from want of power to eat; two causes of infirmity assaulting it, old age, and want.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:115
verses.text: By a natural device, therefore, in order in some measure to restore its youth, the eagle is said to dash and strike against a rock the upper lip of its beak, by the too great increase of which the opening for eating is closed: and by thus rubbing it against the rock, it breaketh off the weight of its old beak, which impeded its taking food.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:116
