verses.text: It cometh to its food, and everything is restored: it will be after its old age like a young eagle; the vigour of all its limbs returneth, the lustre of its plumage, the guidance of its wings, it flieth aloft as before, a sort of resurrection taketh place in it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:117
verses.text: For this is the object of the similitude, like that of the Moon, which after waning and being apparently intercepted, again is renewed, and becometh full; and signifieth to us the resurrection; but when it is full it doth not remain so; again it waneth, that the signification may never cease.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:118
verses.text: Thus also what hath here been said of the eagle: the eagle is not restored unto immortality, but we are unto eternal life; but the similitude is derived from hence, that the rock taketh away from us what hindereth us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:119
verses.text: Presume not therefore on thy strength: the firmness of the rock rubbeth off thy old age: for that Rock was Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:120
verses.text: In Christ our youth shall be restored like that of the eagle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:121
verses.text: "The Lord executeth mercy and judgment for all them that are oppressed with wrong".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:122
verses.text: An adulterous woman is brought forward to be stoned according to the Law, but she is brought before the Lawgiver Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:123
verses.text: Our Lord, at the time she was brought before Him, bending His Head, began writing on the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:124
verses.text: When He bent Himself down upon the earth, He then wrote on the earth: before He bent upon the earth, He wrote not on the earth, but on stone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:125
verses.text: The earth was now something fertile, ready to bring forth from the Lord's letters.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:126
verses.text: On the stone He had written the Law, intimating the hardness of the Jews: He wrote on the earth, signifying the productiveness of Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:127
verses.text: Then they who were leading the adulteress came, like raging waves against a rock: but they were dashed to pieces by His answer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:128
verses.text: For He said to them, "He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:129
verses.text: And again bending His head, He began writing on the ground.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:130
verses.text: And now each man, when he asked his own conscience, came not forward.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:131
verses.text: It was not a weak adulterous woman, but their own adulterate conscience, that drove them back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:132
verses.text: They wished to punish, to judge; they came to the Rock, their judges were overthrown by the Rock.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:133
verses.text: Execute mercy to the wicked, not as being wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:134
verses.text: Do not receive the wicked, in so far forth as he is wicked: that is, do not receive him as if from inclination towards and love for his iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:135
verses.text: For it is forbidden to give unto a sinner, and to receive sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:136
verses.text: Yet how is this, "Give unto every man that asketh of thee"? and this, "if thine enemy hunger, feed him"? This is seemingly contradictory: but it is opened to those who knock in the name of Christ, and will be clear unto those who seek.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:137
verses.text: "Help not a sinner:" and, "give not to the ungodly;" and yet, "give unto every man that asketh of thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:138
verses.text: But it is a sinner who asketh of me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:139
verses.text: Give, not as unto a sinner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:140
verses.text: When dost thou give as unto a sinner? When that which maketh him a sinner, pleaseth thee so that thou givestLet those who give to a man who fights with wild beasts, tell me why they give? Why doth he give to this man? He loveth that in him, in which consists his greatest sin; this he feedeth, this he clotheth in him, wickedness itself, made public by all witnessing it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:141
verses.text: Why doth the man give, who giveth to actors, or to charioteers, or to courtesans? Do not these very persons give to human beings? But it is not the nature of God's work that they attend to, but the iniquity of the human work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:142
verses.text: When therefore thou givest, thou givest to infamy, not to bravery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:143
verses.text: As then he who giveth to the fighter of beasts, giveth not to the man, but to a most infamous profession; for if he were only a man, and not a fighter of beasts, thou wouldest not give; thou honourest him in vice, not nature: so on the other hand, if thou give to the righteous, if thou give to the prophet, if thou give to the disciple of Christ anything of which he is in want, without thinking that he is Christ's disciple, that he is God's minister, that he is God's steward; but art thinking in that case of some temporal advantage, for instance, that when perchance he shall be needful to thy cause, he may be bought for thee, because thou hast given him something; thou hast no more given to the righteous, if thou hast thus given, than he gave to the man, when he gave to the beast-fighter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:144
verses.text: The matter, then, most beloved, is quite open to us, and I conceive, that although it was obscure, it is now clear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:145
verses.text: It was to this that the Lord bound thee, when He said, "He who hath received the righteous man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:146
verses.text: That were enough.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:147
verses.text: But as the righteous may be received with another intention,He saith, "He who receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man:" that is, receiving him in consideration of his righteousness:that is, because he is Christ's disciple, because he is a steward of the Mystery: "Verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:148
verses.text: So understand, he who receiveth a sinner in the name of a sinner shall lose his reward.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:149
verses.text: On this account therefore be merciful without fear, extend love even unto thine enemies: punish those who chance to belong to thy government, restrain them with affection, with charity, in regard to their eternal salvation; lest while thou sparest the flesh, the soul perish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:150
verses.text: Do this: and though thou have to endure many, over whom thou canst not exercise discipline, because thou hast no lawful authority over them; bear their injuries; be without apprehension.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:151
verses.text: He will show mercy unto thee if thou shalt have been merciful: thou shalt be merciful, without the injuries thou sufferest losing their punishment; "To Me belongeth vengeance, I will repay," saith the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:152
verses.text: "He made His ways known unto Moses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:153
verses.text: For the Law was given with this view, that the sick might be convinced of his infirmity, and pray for the physician.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:154
verses.text: This is the hidden way of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:155
verses.text: Thou hadst long ago heard, "Who healeth all thine infirmities".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:156
verses.text: Their infirmities were as yet hidden in the sick; the five books were given to Moses: the pool was surrounded by five porches; he brought forth the sick, that they might lie there, that they might be made known, not that they might be healed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:157
verses.text: The five porches discovered, but healed not, the sick; the pool healed when one descended, and this when it was disturbed: the disturbance of the pool was in our Lord's Passion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:158
verses.text: Since therefore this is a mystery there, he teacheth that the Law was given that sinners might be convinced of their sin, and call upon the Physician in order to receive grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:159
verses.text: Therefore, as I had begun to say, because this is a great mystery in the Law, that it was given with this view, that by the increase of sin, the proud might be humbled, the humbled might confess, the confessing might be healed; these are the hidden ways, which He made known to Moses, through whom He gave the Law, by which sin should abound, that grace might more abound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:160
verses.text: "He hath made known His good pleasure unto the children of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:161
verses.text: To all the children of Israel? To the true children of Israel; yea, to all the children of Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:162
verses.text: For the treacherous, the insidious, the hypocrites, are not children of Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:163
verses.text: And who are the children of Israel? "Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:164
verses.text: "The Lord is full of compassion and mercy: long-suffering, and of great mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:165
verses.text: Why so long-suffering? Why so great in mercy? Men sin and live; sins are added on, life continueth: men blaspheme daily, and "He maketh His sun to rise over the good and the wicked".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:166
verses.text: On all sides He calleth to amendment, on all sides He calleth to repentance, He calleth by the blessings of creation, He calleth by giving time for life, He calleth through the reader, He calleth through the preacher, He calleth through the innermost thought by the rod of correction, He calleth by the mercy of consolation: "He is long-suffering, and of great mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:167
verses.text: But take heed lest by ill using the length of God's mercy, thou treasure up for thyself, as the Apostle saith, wrath in the day of wrath.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:168
verses.text: For some there are who prepare to turn, and yet put it off, and in them crieth out the raven's voice, "Cras! Cras!" The raven which was sent from the ark, never returned God seeketh not procrastination in the raven's voice, but confession in the wailing of the dove.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:169
verses.text: The dove, when sent forth, returned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:170
verses.text: How long, To-morrow! To-morrow!? Look to thy last morrow: since thou knowest not what is thy last morrow, let it suffice that thou hast lived up to this day a sinner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:171
verses.text: Thou hast heard, often thou art wont to hear, thou hast heard to-day also; daily thou hearest, and daily thou amendest not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:172
verses.text: "He will not alway be chiding: neither keepeth He His anger for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:173
verses.text: Since it is in consequence of His anger that we live in the scourges and corruption of mortality: we have this in punishment for the first sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:174
verses.text: Is it not through His anger, my brethren, that "in the sweat of thy face and in toil thou shalt eat bread, and the earth shall bear thorns and thistles unto thee"? This was said to our forefathers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:175
verses.text: Or if our life is different from this; if thou canst, turn unto some pleasure, where thou mayest not feel thorns.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:176
verses.text: Choose what thou hast wished, whether thou art covetous or luxurious; to name these two alone; add a third passion, that of ambition; how great thorns are there in the desire of honours? in the luxury of lusts how great thorns? in the ardour of covetousness how great thorns? What troubles are there in base loves? What terrible anxieties here in this life? I omit hell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:177
verses.text: Beware lest thou even now become a hell unto thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:178
verses.text: The whole of this, my brethren, is the result of His anger: and when thou hast turned thyself unto works of righteousness, thou canst not but toil upon earth; and toil endeth not before life endeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:179
verses.text: We must toil on the way, that we may rejoice in our country.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:180
verses.text: He therefore consoleth by His promises thy toil, thy labours, thy troubles, saying to thee, "He will not alway be chiding".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:181
verses.text: "He hath not dealt with us according to our sins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:182
verses.text: Thanks unto God, because He hath vouchsafed this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:183
verses.text: We have not received what we were deserving of: "He hath not dealt with us according to our sins, nor rewarded us according to our wickednesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:184
verses.text: "For as the height of heaven above the earth, so hath the Lord confirmed His mercy toward them that fear Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:185
verses.text: Observe the heaven: everywhere on every side it covereth the earth, nor is there any part of the earth not covered by the heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:186
verses.text: Men sin beneath heaven: they do all evil deeds beneath the heaven; yet they are covered by the heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:187
verses.text: Thence is light for the eyes, thence air, thence breath, thence rain upon the earth for the sake of its fruits, thence all mercy from heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:188
verses.text: Take away the aid of heaven from the earth: it will fail at once.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:189
verses.text: As then the protection of heaven abideth upon the earth, so doth the Lord's protection abide upon them that fear Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:190
verses.text: Thou fearest God, His protection is above thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:191
verses.text: But perhaps thou art scourged, and conceivest that God hath forsaken thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:192
verses.text: God hath forsaken thee, if the protection of heaven hath forsaken the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:193
verses.text: "Look, how wide the east is from the west; so far hath He set our sins from us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:194
verses.text: They who know the Sacraments know this; nevertheless, I only say what all may hear When sin is remitted, thy sins fall, thy grace riseth; thy sins are as it were on the decline, thy grace which freeth thee on the rise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:195
verses.text: "Truth springeth from the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:196
verses.text: What meaneth this? Thy grace is born, thy sins fall, thou art in a certain manner made new.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:197
verses.text: Thou shouldest look to the rising, and turn away from the setting Turn away from thy sins, turn unto the grace of God; when thy sins fall, thou riseth and profitest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:198
verses.text: One region of the heaven falleth, another riseth: but the region which is now rising will set after twelve hours.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:199
verses.text: Not like this is the grace which riseth unto us: both our sins fall for ever, and grace abideth for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:200
verses.text: "Yea, like as a father pitieth his own children, even so hath the Lord had mercy on them that fear Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:201
verses.text: Let Him be as angry as He shall will, He is our Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:202
verses.text: But He hath scourged us, and afflicted us, and bruised us: He is our Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:203
verses.text: Son, if thou bewailest, wail beneath thy Father; do not so with indignation, do not so with the puffing up of pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:204
verses.text: What thou sufferest, whence thou mournest, it is medicine, not punishment; it is thy chastening, not thy condemnation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:205
verses.text: Do not refuse the scourge, if thou dost not wish to be refused thy heritage: do not think of what punishment thou sufferest in the scourge, but what place thou hast in the Testament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:206
verses.text: "For He knoweth our forming" : that is, our infirmity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:207
verses.text: He knoweth what He hath created, how it hath fallen, how it may be repaired, how it may be adopted, how it may be enriched.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:208
verses.text: Behold, we are made of clay: "The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:209
verses.text: He sent even His own Son, Him who was made the second man, Him who was God before all things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:210
verses.text: For He was second in His coming, first in His returning: He died after many, He arose before all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:211
verses.text: "He knoweth our forming".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:212
verses.text: What forming? Ourselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:213
verses.text: Why sayest thou that He knoweth? Because He hath pitied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:214
verses.text: "Remember that we are but dust".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:215
verses.text: Addressing God Himself, he saith, "Remember," as if God could forget: He perceiveth, He knoweth in such a manner that He cannot forget.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:216
verses.text: But what meaneth, "Remember"? Let thy mercy continue towards us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:217
verses.text: Thou knowest our forming; forget not our forming, lest we forget thy grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:218
verses.text: "Man, his days are but as grass".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:219
verses.text: Let man consider what he is; let not man be proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:220
verses.text: "His days are but as grass".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:221
verses.text: Why is the grass proud, that is now flourishing, and in a very short space dried up? Why is the grass proud that flourisheth only for a brief season, until the sun be hot? It is then good for us that His mercy be upon us, and from grass make gold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:222
verses.text: "For he flourisheth as a flower of the field".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:223
verses.text: The whole splendour of the human race; honour, powers, riches, pride, threats, is the flower of the grass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:224
verses.text: That house flourisheth, and that family is great, that family flourisheth; and how many flourish, and how many years do they live! Many years to thee, are but a short season unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:225
verses.text: God doth not count, as thou dost.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:226
verses.text: Compared with the length and long life of ages, all the flower of any house is as the flower of the field.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:227
verses.text: All the beauty of the year hardly lasteth for the year.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:228
verses.text: Whatever there flourisheth, whatever there is warmed with heat, whatever there is beautiful, lasteth not; nay, it cannot exist for one whole year.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:229
verses.text: In how brief a season do flowers pass away, and these are the beauty of the herbs! This which is so very beautiful, this quickly falleth Inasmuch then as He knoweth as a father our forming, that we are but grass, and can only flourish for a time; He sent unto us His Word, and His Word, which abideth for evermore, He hath made a brother unto the grass which abideth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:230
verses.text: Wonder not that thou shalt be a sharer of His Eternity; He became Himself first a sharer of thy grass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:231
verses.text: Will He who assumed from thee what was lowly, deny unto thee what is exalted in respect of thee?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:232
verses.text: "The wind shall go over on it, it shall not be; and the place thereof shall know it no more".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:233
verses.text: For he is not speaking of grass, but of that for whose sake even the Word became grass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:234
verses.text: For thou art man, and on thy account the Word became man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:235
verses.text: "All flesh is grass:" "and the Word was made flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:236
verses.text: How great then is the hope of the grass, since the Word hath been made flesh? That which abideth for evermore, hath not disdained to assume grass, that the grass might not despair of itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:237
verses.text: In thy reflections therefore on thyself, think of thy low estate, think of thy dust: be not lifted up: if thou art anything better, thou wilt be so by His Grace, thou wilt be so by His mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:238
verses.text: For hear what followeth: "but the mercy of the Lord endureth for ever and ever upon them that fear Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:239
verses.text: Ye who fear not Him, will be grass, and in grass, and in torment with the grass: for the flesh shall arise unto the torment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:240
verses.text: Let those who fear Him rejoice, because His mercy is upon them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:241
verses.text: "And His righteousness upon children's children".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:242
verses.text: He speaketh of reward, "upon children's children".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:243
verses.text: How many servants of God are there who have not children, how much less children's children? But He calleth our works our children; the reward of works, our "children's children".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:244
verses.text: "Even upon such as keep His covenant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:245
verses.text: Let men beware that all may not conceive what is here said to belong to themselves: let them choose, while they have the choice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:246
verses.text: "And keep in memory His commandments to do them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:247
verses.text: Thou wast already disposed to flatter thyself, and perhaps to recite to me the Psalter, which I have not by heart, or from memory to say over the whole Law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:248
verses.text: Clearly thou art better in point of memory than I, better than any righteous man who doth not know the Law word for word: but see that thou keep the commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:249
verses.text: But how shouldest thou keep them? Not by memory, but by life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:250
verses.text: "Such as keep in memory His commandments:" not, to recite them; but, "to do them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:251
verses.text: And now perhaps each man's soul is disturbed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:252
verses.text: Who remembereth all the commandments of God? who remembereth all the writings of God? Lo, I wish not only to hold them in my memory, but also to do them in my works: but who remembereth them all? Fear not: He burdeneth thee not: "on two commandments hang all the Law and the Prophets".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:253
verses.text: "The Lord hath prepared His throne in heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:254
verses.text: Who but Christ hath prepared His throne in heaven? He who descended and ascended, He who died, and rose from the dead, He who lifted up to heaven the manhood He had assumed, hath Himself prepared His throne in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:255
verses.text: The throne is the seat of the Judge: observe therefore ye who hear, that "He hath prepared His throne in heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:256
verses.text: The kingdom is the Lord's, and He shall be the Governor among the people "And His kingdom shall rule over all".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:257
verses.text: "Bless ye the Lord, ye Angels of His, ye that are mighty in strength: ye that fulfil His word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:258
verses.text: By the word of God, then, thou art not righteous, nor faithful, unless when thou dost it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:259
verses.text: "Ye that are mighty in strength, ye that fulfil His commandment, and hearken unto the voice of His words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:260
verses.text: "Bless ye the Lord, all ye His hosts: ye servants of His that do His pleasure".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:261
verses.text: All ye angels, all ye that are mighty in strength: ye that do His word: all ye His hosts, ye servants of His that do His pleasure, do ye, ye bless the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:262
verses.text: For all they who live wickedly, though their tongues be silent, by their lips do curse the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:263
verses.text: What doth it profit if thy tongue singeth a hymn, while thy life breatheth sacrilege? By living ill thou hast set many tongues to blasphemy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:264
verses.text: Thy tongue is given to the hymn, the tongues of those who behold thee, to blasphemy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:265
verses.text: If then thou dost wish to bless the Lord, do His word, do His will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:266
verses.text: "Bless ye the Lord, all ye works of His, in all places of His dominion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:267
verses.text: Therefore in every place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:268
verses.text: Let Him not be blessed where He ruleth not: "in all places of His dominion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:269
verses.text: Let no man perchance say: I cannot praise the Lord in the East, because He hath departed unto the West; or, I cannot praise Him in the West, because He is in the East.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:270
verses.text: "For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor yet from the desert hills.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:271
verses.text: And why? God is the Judge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:272
verses.text: He is everywhere, in such wise that everywhere He may be praised: He is in such wise on every side, that we may be joyful in Him on every side: He is in such wise blessed on every side, that on every side we may live well.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 103:273
verses.text: "In every place of His dominion: bless thou the Lord, O my soul!" The last verse is the same as the first: blessing is at the head of the Psalm, blessing at the end; from blessing we set out, to blessing let us return, in blessing let us reign.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:1
verses.text: Psalm CIV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:2
verses.text: "Bless the Lord, O my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:3
verses.text: Let the soul of us all, made one in Christ, say this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:4
verses.text: "O Lord my God, Thou art magnified exceedingly!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:5
verses.text: Where art Thou magnified? "Confession and beauty Thou hast put on".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:6
verses.text: Confess ye, that ye may be beautified, that He may put you on.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:7
verses.text: "Clothed with light as a garment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:8
verses.text: Clothed with His Church, because she is made "light" in Him, who before was darkness in herself, as the apostle saith: "Ye were sometime darkness, but now light in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:9
verses.text: "Stretching out the heaven like a skin:" either as easily as thou dost a skin, if it be "as easily," so that thou mayest take it after the letter; or let us understand the authority of the Scriptures, spread out over the whole world, under the name of a skin; because mortality is signified in a skin, but all the authority of the Divine Scriptures was dispensed unto us through mortal men, whose fame is still spreading abroad now they are dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:10
verses.text: "Who covereth with waters the upper parts thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:11
verses.text: The upper parts of what? Of Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:12
verses.text: What is Heaven? Figuratively only we said, the Divine Scripture.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:13
verses.text: What are the upper parts of the Divine Scripture? The commandment of love, than which there is none more exalted But wherefore is love compared to waters? Because "the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Spirit who is given unto us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:14
verses.text: Whence is the Spirit Himself water? because "Jesus stood and cried, He that believeth on Me, out of his bosom shall flow rivers of living water".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:15
verses.text: Whence do we prove that it was said of the Spirit? Let the Evangelist himself declare, who followeth it up, and saith, "But this spake He of the Spirit, which they were to receive, who should believe on Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:16
verses.text: "Who walketh above the wings of the winds;" that is, above the virtues of souls.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:17
verses.text: What is the virtue of a soul? Love itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:18
verses.text: But how doth He walk above it? Because the love of God toward us is greater than ours toward God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:19
verses.text: "Who maketh spirits His angels, and flaming fire His ministers" : that is, those who are already spirits, who are spiritual, not carnal, He maketh His Angels, by sending them to preach His gospel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:20
verses.text: "And flaming fire His ministers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:21
verses.text: For unless the minister that preacheth be on fire, he enflameth not him to whom he preacheth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:22
verses.text: "He hath founded the earth upon its firmness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:23
verses.text: He hath founded the Church upon the firmness of the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:24
verses.text: What is the firmness of the Church, but the foundation of the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:25
verses.text: What is the foundation of the Church, but that of which the Apostle saith, "Other foundation can no man lay but that is laid, which is Christ Jesus".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:26
verses.text: And therefore, grounded on such a foundation, what hath she deserved to hear? "It shall not be bowed forever and ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:27
verses.text: "He founded the earth on its firmness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:28
verses.text: That is, He hath founded the Church upon Christ the foundation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:29
verses.text: The Church will totter if the foundation totter; but when shall Christ totter, before whose coming unto us, and taking flesh on Him, "all things were made by Him, and without Him was not anything made;" who holdeth all things by His Majesty, and us by His goodness? Since Christ faileth not, "she shall not be bowed for ever and ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:30
verses.text: Where are they who say that the Church hath perished from the world, when she cannot even be bowed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:31
verses.text: "The deep, like a garment, is its clothing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:32
verses.text: Whose? Is it perchance God's? But he had already said of His clothing, "Clothed with light as with a garment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:33
verses.text: I hear of God clothed in light, and that light, if we will, are we.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:34
verses.text: What is, if we will? if we are no longer darkness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:35
verses.text: Therefore if God is clothed with light, whose clothing, again, is the deep? For an immense mass of waters is called the deep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:36
verses.text: All water, all the moist nature, and the substance everywhere shed abroad through the seas, and rivers, and hidden caves, is all together called by one name, the Deep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:37
verses.text: Therefore we understand the earth, of which he said, "He hath founded the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:38
verses.text: Of it I believe he said, "The deep, like a garment is its clothing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:39
verses.text: For the water is as it were the clothing of the earth, surrounding it and covering it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:40
verses.text: "Above the mountains the waters shall stand:" that is, the clothing of the earth, which is the deep, so increased, that the waters stood even above the mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:41
verses.text: We read of this taking place in the deluge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:42
verses.text: The Prophet minding to foretell future things, not to relate the past, therefore said it, because he would have it understood that the Church should be in a deluge of persecutions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:43
verses.text: For there was a time when the floods of persecutors had covered God's earth, God's Church, and had so covered it, that not even those great ones appeared, who are the mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:44
verses.text: For when they fled everywhere, how did they but cease to appear? And perchance of those waters is that saying, "Save me, O God, for the waters are come in even unto my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:45
verses.text: Especially the waters which make the sea, stormy, unfruitful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:46
verses.text: For whatsoever earth the sea-water may have covered, it will not rather make it fruitful than bring it to barrenness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:47
verses.text: For there were also mountains beneath the waters, because above the mountains waters stoodWhy were the Apostles hidden by flight? Because "above the mountains the waters stood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:48
verses.text: The power of the waters was great, but how long? Hear what followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:49
verses.text: "From Thy rebuke they shall fly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:50
verses.text: And this was done, brethren; from God's rebuke the waters did fly; that is, they went back from pressing on the mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:51
verses.text: Now the mountains themselves stand forth, Peter and Paul: how do they tower! They who before were pressed down by persecutors, now are venerated by emperors.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:52
verses.text: For the waters are fled from the rebuke of God; because "the heart of kings is in the hand of God, He hath bent it whither He would;" He commanded peace to be given by them to the Christians; the authority of the Apostles sprang up and towered high.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:53
verses.text: The waters fled from the rebuke of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:54
verses.text: "From the voice of Thy thunder they shall be afraid".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:55
verses.text: Now who is there that would not be afraid, from the voice of God through the Apostles, the voice of God through the Scriptures, through His clouds? The sea is quieted, the waters have been made afraid, the mountains have been laid bare, the emperor hath given the order.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:56
verses.text: But who would have given the order, unless God had thundered? Because God willed, they commanded, and it was done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:57
verses.text: Therefore let no one of men arrogate anything to himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:58
verses.text: "The mountains ascend, and the plains go down, into the place which Thou hast founded for them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:59
verses.text: He is still speaking of waters.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:60
verses.text: Let us not here understand mountains as of earth; nor plains, as of earth: but waves so great that they may be compared to mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:61
verses.text: The sea did sometime toss, and its waves were as mountains, which could cover those mountains the Apostles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:62
verses.text: But how long do the mountains ascend and the plains go down? They raged, and they are appeased.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:63
verses.text: When they raged they were mountains: now they are appeased they are become plains: for He hath founded a place for them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:64
verses.text: There is a certain channel, as it were a deep place, into which all those lately raging hearts of mortals have retired.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:65
verses.text: They were mountains formerly, now they are plains: yet, my brethren, even a dead calm is sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:66
verses.text: For wherefore are they not now violent? wherefore do they not rage? Wherefore do they not try, if they cannot overthrow our earth, at least to cover it? Wherefore not?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:67
verses.text: Hear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:68
verses.text: "Thou hast set a bound which they shall not pass over, neither shall they turn again to cover the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:69
verses.text: What then, because now the bitterest waves have received a measure, that we must be allowed to preach such things even with freedom; because they have had their due limit assigned, because they cannot pass over the bound that is set, nor shall they return to cover the earth; what is doing in the earth itself? What workings take place therein, now that the sea hath left it bare? Although at its beach slight waves do make their noise, although Pagans still murmur round; the sound of the shores I hear, a deluge I dread not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:70
verses.text: What then; what is doing in the earth? "Who sendeth out springs in the little valleys".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:71
verses.text: "Thou sendest out," he saith, "springs in the little valleys".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:72
verses.text: Ye know what little valleys are, lower places among the lands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:73
verses.text: For to hills and mountains, valleys and little valleys are opposed in contrary shape.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:74
verses.text: Hills and mountains are swellings of the land: but valleys and little valleys, lownesses of the lands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:75
verses.text: Do not despise low places, thence flow springs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:76
verses.text: "Thou sendest out springs in the little valleys".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:77
verses.text: Hear a mountain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:78
verses.text: The Apostle saith, "I laboured more than they all".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:79
verses.text: A certain greatness is brought before us: yet immediately, that the waters may flow, he hath made himself a valley: "Yet not I, but the grace of God with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:80
verses.text: It is no contradiction that they who are mountains be also valleys: for as they are called mountains because of their spiritual greatness, so also valleys because of the humility of their spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:81
verses.text: "Not I," he saith, "but the grace of God with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:82
verses.text: What is, "In the midst between the mountains the waters shall pass through"? We have heard who are the "mountains," the great Preachers of the word, the exalted Angels of God, though still in mortal flesh; lofty not by their own power, but by His grace; but as far as relates to themselves, they are valleys, in their humility they send forth springs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:83
verses.text: "In the midst," he saith, "between the mountains, the waters shall pass through".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:84
verses.text: Let us suppose this said thus, "In the midst between the Apostles shall pass through the preachings of the Word of Truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:85
verses.text: What is, in the midst between the Apostles? What is called in the midst, is common.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:86
verses.text: A common property, from which all alike live, is in the midst, and belongs not to me, but neither belongs it to thee, nor yet to me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:87
verses.text: For if they are not in the midst, they are as it were private, they flow not for public use, and I have mine, and he has his own, it is not in the midst for both me and him to have it; but such is not the preaching of peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:88
verses.text: Therefore, brethren, let what we have said to your Love serve to this purpose, because of the springs: that they may flow from you, be ye valleys, and communicate with all that which ye have from God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:89
verses.text: Let the waters flow in the midst, envy ye no one, drink, be filled, flow forth when ye are filled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:90
verses.text: Everywhere let the common water of God have the glory, not the private falsehoods of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:91
verses.text: For it follows, "All the beasts of the wood shall drink".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:92
verses.text: We do indeed see this also in the visible creation, that the beasts of the wood drink of springs, and of streams that run between the mountains: but now since it hath pleased God to hide His own wisdom in the figures of such things, not to take it away from earnest seekers, but to close it to them that care not, and open it to them that knock; it hath also pleased our Lord God Himself to exhort you by us to this, that in all these things which are said as if of the bodily and visible creation, we may seek something spiritually hidden, in which when found we may rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:93
verses.text: The beasts of the wood, we understand the Gentiles, and Holy Scripture witnesses this in many places.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:94
verses.text: These beasts, then, drink those waters, but passing; not staying, but passing; for all that teaching which in all this time is dispensed passeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:95
verses.text: Unless perchance your love thinketh that in that city to which it is said, "Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem, praise thy God, O Sion; for He hath made strong the bars of thy gates;" when the bars are now strengthened and the city closed, whence, as we said some time since, no friend goeth out, no enemy entereth; that there we shall have a book to read, or speech to be explained as it is now explained to you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:96
verses.text: Therefore is it now treated, that there it may be held fast: therefore is it now divided by syllables, that there it may be contemplated whole and entire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:97
verses.text: The Word of God will not be wanting there: but yet not by letters, not by sounds, not by books, not by a reader, not by an expositor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:98
verses.text: How then? As, "In the beginning was the Word," etc For He did not so come to us as to depart from thence; because He was in this world, and the world was made by Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:99
verses.text: Such a Word are we to contemplate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:100
verses.text: For "the God of gods shall appear in Zion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:101
verses.text: But this when? After our pilgrimage, when the journey is done: if however after our journey is done we be not delivered to the Judge, that the Judge may send us to prison.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:102
verses.text: But if when our journey is ended, as we hope, and wish, and endeavour, we shall have reached our Country, there shall we contemplate What we shall ever praise; nor shall That fail which is present to us, nor we, who enjoy: nor shall he be cloyed that eateth, nor shall that fail which he eateth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:103
verses.text: Great and wonderful shall be that contemplation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:104
verses.text: "The onagers shall take for their thirst".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:105
verses.text: By onagers he meaneth some great beasts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:106
verses.text: For who knoweth not that wild asses are called onagers? He meaneth, therefore, some great untrained ones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:107
verses.text: For the Gentiles had no yoke of the Law: many nations lived after their own customs, ranging in proud boastfulness as in a wilderness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:108
verses.text: And so indeed did all the beasts, but the wild asses are put to signify the greater sort.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:109
verses.text: They too shall drink for their thirst, for for them too the waters flow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:110
verses.text: Thence drinks the hare, thence the wild ass: the hare little, the wild ass great; the hare timid, the wild ass fierce: either sort drinks thence, but each for his thirst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:111
verses.text: So faithfully and gently doth it flow, as at once to satisfy the wild ass, and not to alarm the hare.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:112
verses.text: The sound of Tully's voice rings out, Cicero is read, it is some book, it is a dialogue of his, whether his own, or Plato's, or by whatever such writer: some hear that are unlearned, weak ones of less mind; who dareth to aspire to such a thing? It is a sound of water, and that perchance turbid, but certainly flowing so violently, that a timid animal dare not draw near and  drink.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:113
verses.text: To whom soundeth a Psalm, and he saith, It is too much for me? Behold now what the Psalm soundeth; certainly they are hidden mysteries, yet so it soundeth, that even children are delighted to hear, and the unlearned come to drink, and when filled burst forth in singing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:114
verses.text: Then the Psalm goes on in its text, "Upon them the fowls of the heaven shall inhabit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:115
verses.text: Upon the mountains, then, the fowls of the air shall have their habitation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:116
verses.text: We see these birds dwell upon the mountains, but many of them dwell in plains, many in valleys, many in groves, many in gardens, not all upon mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:117
verses.text: There are some fowls that dwell not save on the mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:118
verses.text: Some spiritual souls doth this name denote.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:119
verses.text: Fowls are spiritual hearts, which enjoy the free air.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:120
verses.text: In the clearness of heaven these birds delight, yet their feeding is on the mountains, there will they dwell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:121
verses.text: Ye know the mountains, they have been already treated of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:122
verses.text: Mountains are Prophets, mountains are Apostles, mountains are all preachers of the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:123
verses.text: But think not that those "fowls of heaven" follow their own authority; see what the Psalm saith: "From the midst of the rocks they shall give their voice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:124
verses.text: Now, if I shall say to you, Believe, for this said Cicero, this said Plato, this said Pythagoras: which of you will not laugh at me? For I shall be a bird that shall send forth my voice not from the rock.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:125
verses.text: What ought each one of you to say to me? what ought he who is thus instructed to say? "If any one shall have preached unto you a gospel other than that ye have received, let him be anathema".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:126
verses.text: What dost thou tell me of Plato, and of Cicero, and of Virgil? Thou hast before thee the rocks of the mountains, from the midst of the rocks give me thy voice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:127
verses.text: Let them be heard, who hear from the rock: let them be heard, because also in those many rocks the One Rock is heard: for "the Rock was Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:128
verses.text: Let them therefore be willingly heard, giving their voice from the midst of the rocks.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:129
verses.text: Nothing is sweeter than such a voice of birds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:130
verses.text: They sound, and the rocks resound: they sound; spiritual men discuss: the rocks resound, testimonies of Scripture give answer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:131
verses.text: Lo! thence the fowls give their voice from the midst of the rocks, for they dwell on the mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:132
verses.text: "Watering the mountains from the higher places".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:133
verses.text: Now if a Gentile uncircumcised man comes to us, about to believe in Christ, we give him baptism, and do not call him back to those works of the Law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:134
verses.text: And if a Jew asks us why we do that, we sound from the rock, we say, This Peter did, this Paul did: from the midst of the rocks we give our voice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:135
verses.text: But that rock, Peter himself, that great mountain, when he prayed and saw that vision, was watered from above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:136
verses.text: "From the fruit of Thy works shall the earth be satisfied".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:137
verses.text: What is, "From the fruit of Thy works"? Let no man glory in his own works: but "he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:138
verses.text: With Thy grace he is satisfied, when he is satisfied: let him not say that grace was given for his own merits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:139
verses.text: If it is called grace, "it is gratuitously given;" if it is returned for works, wages are paid Freely therefore receive, because ungodly thou art justified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:140
verses.text: "Bringing forth grass for the cattle, and green herb for the service of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:141
verses.text: This is true, I perceive; I recognise the creation: the earth doth bring forth grass for the cattle, and green herb for the service of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:142
verses.text: But I perceive the words, "Thou shalt not muzzle the mouth of the ox which treadeth out the corn: Doth God take care for oxen? For our sakes therefore the Scripture saith it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:143
verses.text: How then doth the earth bring forth grass for the cattle? Because "the Lord hath ordained that they which preach the Gospel should live of the Gospel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:144
verses.text: He sent preachers, saying unto them, "Eat such things as are set before you of them: for the labourer is worthy of his hire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:145
verses.text: They give spiritual, they receive carnal things; they give gold, they receive grass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:146
verses.text: "If we have sown unto you spiritual things, is it a great matter if we shall reap your carnal things?" This the Apostle said, a preacher so laborious, so indefatigable, so well tried, that he giveth this very grass to the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:147
verses.text: "Nevertheless," he saith, "we have not used this power".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:148
verses.text: He showeth that it is due to him, yet he received it not; nor hath he condemned those who have received what was due.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:149
verses.text: For those were to be condemned who exact what is not due, not they who accept their recompense: yet he gave up even his own recompense.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:150
verses.text: Thou dost not cease to owe to another, because one hath given up his dues, otherwise thou wilt not be the watered earth which bringeth forth grass for the cattle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:151
verses.text: Thou receivest spiritual things, give carnal things in return: to the soldier they are due, to the soldier thou returnest them; thou art the paymaster of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:152
verses.text: "Who goeth a warfare any time at his own charges? who planteth a vineyard, and eateth not of the fruit thereof? or who feedeth a flock, and eateth not of the milk of the flock? I speak not thus, that it should be so done unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:153
verses.text: There has been such a soldier as gave up his rations of food even to the paymaster: yet let the paymaster pay the rations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:154
verses.text: "That it may bring forth bread out of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:155
verses.text: What bread? Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:156
verses.text: Out of what earth? From Peter, from Paul, from the other stewards of the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:157
verses.text: Hear that it is from the earth: "We have," saith St.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:158
verses.text: Paul, "this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:159
verses.text: He is the bread who descended from heaven, that He might be brought forth out of the earth, when He is preached through the flesh of His servants.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:160
verses.text: The earth bringeth forth grass, that it may bring forth bread from the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:161
verses.text: What earth bringeth forth grass? Pious, holy nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:162
verses.text: That bread may be brought forth out of what earth? The word of God out of the Apostles, out of the stewards of God's Sacraments, who still walk upon the earth, who still carry an earthly body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:163
verses.text: "And wine maketh glad the heart of man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:164
verses.text: Let no man prepare himself for intoxication; nay, let every man prepare him for intoxication.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:165
verses.text: "How excellent is Thy cup which maketh inebriate!" We choose not to say, Let no man be drunk.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:166
verses.text: Be inebriated; yet beware, from what source.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:167
verses.text: If the excellent cup of the Lord doth saturate you, your ebriety shall be seen in your works, it shall be seen in the holy love of righteousness, it shall, lastly, be seen in the estrangement of your mind, but from things earthly to heavenly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:168
verses.text: "To make him a cheerful countenance with oil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:169
verses.text: What is the making the countenance cheerful with oil? The grace of God; a sort of shining for manifestation; as the Apostle saith, "The Spirit is given to every man for manifestation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:170
verses.text: A certain grace which men can clearly see in men, to conciliate holy love, is termed oil, for its divine splendour; and since it appeared most excellent in Christ, the whole world loveth Him; who though while here He was scorned, is now worshipped by every nation: "For the kingdom is the Lord's, and He shall be Governor among the people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:171
verses.text: For such is His grace, that many, who do not believe on Him, praise Him, and declare that they are unwilling to believe on Him, because no man can fulfil what He doth command.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:172
verses.text: They who with reproaches once raged against Him, are hindered by His very praises.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:173
verses.text: Yet by all is He loved, by all is He preached; because He is excellently anointed, therefore He is Christ: for He is called Christ from the Chrism or anointing which He had.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:174
verses.text: Messiah in the Hebrew, Christ in the Greek, Unctus in the Latin: but He anointeth over His whole Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:175
verses.text: All therefore who come, receive grace, that their countenances may be made glad with oil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:176
verses.text: "And bread strengtheneth man's heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:177
verses.text: What is this, brethren? As it were, he hath forced us to understand what bread he was speaking of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:178
verses.text: For while that visible bread strengtheneth the stomach, feedeth the body, there is another bread which strengtheneth the heart, in that it is the bread of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:179
verses.text: There is therefore a wine that truly maketh glad the heart, and knoweth not to do aught else than to gladden the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:180
verses.text: But that thou mayest not imagine that this indeed should be taken of the spiritual wine, but not of that spiritual bread; He hath shown this very point, that it is also spiritual: "and bread," he saith, "strengtheneth man's heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:181
verses.text: So understand it therefore of the bread as thou dost understand it of the wine; hunger inwardly, thirst inwardly: "Blessed are they," saith our Lord, "who hunger and thirst after righteousness; for they shall be filled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:182
verses.text: That bread is righteousness, that wine is righteousness: it is truth, Christ is truth "I am," He said, "the living bread, who came down from heaven;" and, "I am the Vine, and ye are the branches".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:183
verses.text: "The trees of the plain shall be satisfied" : but with this grace, brought forth out of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:184
verses.text: "The trees of the plain," are the lower orders of the nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:185
verses.text: "And the cedars of Libanus which He hath planted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:186
verses.text: The cedars of Libanus, the powerful in the world, shall themselves be filled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:187
verses.text: The bread, and wine, and oil of Christ hath reached senators, nobles, kings; the trees of the plain are filled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:188
verses.text: First the humble are filled; next also the cedars of Libanus, yet those which He hath planted; pious cedars, religious faithful; for such hath He planted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:189
verses.text: For the ungodly also are cedars of Libanus; for, "The Lord shall break the cedars of Libanus".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:190
verses.text: For Libanus is a mountain: there are those trees, even according to the letter most long-lived and most excellent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:191
verses.text: But Libanus is interpreted, as we read in those who have written of these things, a brightness: and this brightness seemeth to belong to this world, which at present shineth and is refulgent with its pomps.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:192
verses.text: There are the cedars of Libanus, which the Lord hath planted; those which the Lord hath planted shall be filled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:193
verses.text: "There shall the sparrows build their nests: their leader is the house of the coot".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:194
verses.text: Where shall the sparrows build? In the cedars of Libanus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:195
verses.text: Who are the sparrows? Sparrows are birds indeed, and fowls of the air, but small fowls are wont to be called sparrows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:196
verses.text: There are therefore some spiritual ones that build in the cedars of Libanus: that is, there are certain servants of God who hear in the Gospel, "Sell all that thou hast, and give to the poor; and thou shalt have treasure in heaven; and come and follow Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:197
verses.text: Let him who hath resigned many things, not be proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:198
verses.text: We know that Peter was a fisherman: what then could he give up, to follow our Lord? Or his brother Andrew, or John and James the sons of Zebedee, themselves also fishermen; and yet what did they say? "Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:199
verses.text: Our Lord said not to him, Thou hast forgotten thy poverty; what hast thou resigned, that thou shouldest receive the whole world? He, my brethren, who resigned not only what he had, but also what he longed to have, resigned much.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:200
verses.text: But although the sparrows will build in the cedars of Libanus, "the house of the coot is their leader".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:201
verses.text: What is the house of the coot? The coot, as we all know, is a water bird, dwelling either among the marshes, or on the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:202
verses.text: It hath rarely or never a home on the shore; but in places in the midst of the waters, and thus usually in rocky islets, surrounded by the waves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:203
verses.text: We therefore understand that the rock is the fit home of the coot, it never dwelleth more securely than on the rock.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:204
verses.text: On what sort of rock? One placed in the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:205
verses.text: And if it is beaten by the waves, yet it breaketh the waves, is not broken by them: this is the excellency of the rock in the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:206
verses.text: How great waves beat on our Lord Jesus Christ? The Jews dashed against Him; they were broken, He remained whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:207
verses.text: And let every one who doth imitate Christ, so dwell in this world, that is, in this sea, where he cannot but feel storms and tempests, that he may yield to no wind, to no wave, but remain whole, while he meets them all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:208
verses.text: The home of the coot, therefore, is both strong and weak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:209
verses.text: The coot hath not a home on lofty spots; nothing is more firm and nothing more humble than that home.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:210
verses.text: Sparrows build indeed in cedars, on account of actual need: but they hold that rock as their leader, which is beaten by the waves, and yet not broken; for they imitate the sufferings of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:211
verses.text: What then followeth? "The loftiest hills are for the stags".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:212
verses.text: The stags are mighty, spiritual, passing in their course over all the thorny places of the thickets and woods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:213
verses.text: "He maketh my feet like harts' feet, and setteth me up on high".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:214
verses.text: Let them hold to the lofty hills, the lofty commandments of God; let them think on sublime subjects, let them hold those which stand forth most in the Scriptures, let them be justified in the highest: for those loftiest hills are for the stags.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:215
verses.text: What of the humble beasts? what of the hare? what of the hedgehog? The hare is a small and weak animal: the hedgehog is also prickly: the one is a timid animal, the other is covered with prickles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:216
verses.text: What do the prickles signify, except sinners? He who sinneth daily, although not great sins, is covered over with the smallest prickles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:217
verses.text: In his timidity he is a hare: in his being covered with the minutest sins, he is a hedgehog: and he cannot hold those lofty and perfect commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:218
verses.text: For "the loftiest hills are for the stags".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:219
verses.text: What then? do these perish? No.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:220
verses.text: For so "is the rock the refuge for the hedgehogs and the hares".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:221
verses.text: For the Lord is a refuge for the poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:222
verses.text: Place that rock upon the land, it is a refuge for hedgehogs, and for hares: place it on the sea, it is the home of the coot.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:223
verses.text: Everywhere the rock is useful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:224
verses.text: Even in the hills it is useful: for the hills without the rock's foundation would fall into the deep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:225
verses.text: "He appointed the Moon for certain seasons".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:226
verses.text: We understand spiritually the Church increasing from the smallest size, and growing old as it were from the mortality of this life; yet so, that it draweth nearer unto the Sun.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:227
verses.text: I speak not of this moon visible to the eye, but of that which is signified by this name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:228
verses.text: While the Church was in the dark, while she as yet appeared not, shone not forth as yet, men were led astray, and it was said, This is the Church, here is Christ; so that "while the Moon was dark, they shot their arrows at the righteous in heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:229
verses.text: How blind is he who now, when the Moon is full, wandereth astray? "He appointed the Moon for certain seasons".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:230
verses.text: For here the Church temporarily is passing away: for this subjection to death will not remain for ever: there will some time be an end of waxing and waning; it is appointed for certain seasons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:231
verses.text: "And the sun knoweth his going down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:232
verses.text: And what sun is this, but that Sun of righteousness, whom the ungodly will lament on the day of judgment never having risen for them; they who will say on that day, "Therefore we wandered from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness shone not on us, and the sun did not arise upon us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:233
verses.text: That sun riseth for him who understandeth Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:234
verses.text: Nor think, brethren, that the sun ought to be worshipped by some men, because the sun doth sometimes in the Scriptures signify Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:235
verses.text: For such is the madness of men; as if we said that a creature should be worshipped, when it is said, the sun is an emblem of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:236
verses.text: Then worship the rock also, for it also is a type of Christ "He was brought as a lamb to the slaughter:" worship the lamb also, since it is a type of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:237
verses.text: "The Lion of the tribe of Judah hath prevailed;" worship the lion also, since it signifieth Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:238
verses.text: Observe how numerous are the types of Christ: all these are Christ in similitude, not in essence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:239
verses.text: What then, when the sun went down, when our Lord suffered? There was a sort of darkness with the Apostles, hope failed, in those to whom He at first seemed great, and the Redeemer of all men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:240
verses.text: How so? "Thou didst make darkness, and it became night; wherein all the beasts of the forest shall move".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:241
verses.text: Here the beasts of the forest are used in different ways: for these things are always understood in varying senses; as our Lord Himself is at one time termed a lion, at another a lamb.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:242
verses.text: What is so different as a lion and a lamb? But what sort of lamb? One that could overcome the wolf, overcome the lion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:243
verses.text: He is the Rock, He the Shepherd, He the Gate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:244
verses.text: The Shepherd entereth by the gate: and He saith, "I am the good Shepherd:" and, "I am the Door of the Sheep".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:245
verses.text: Learn thus to understand, when these things are spoken figuratively; lest perchance when ye have read that the Rock signifieth Christ, ye may understand it to mean Him in every passage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:246
verses.text: In one place it meaneth one thing, another in another, just as we can only understand the meaning of a letter by seeing its position "The lion's whelps roaring after their prey, do seek their meat from God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:247
verses.text: Justly then our Lord, when nigh unto His going down, the very Sun of Righteousness recognising His going down, said to His disciples, as if darkness being about to come, the lion would roam about to seek whom he might devour, that that lion could devour no man, unless with leave: "Simon," said He, "this night Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:248
verses.text: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:249
verses.text: When Peter thrice denied, was he not already between the lion's teeth?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:250
verses.text: "The Sun hath arisen, and they get them away together, and lay them down in their dens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:251
verses.text: More and more as the Sun riseth, so that Christ is recognised by the round world, and glorified therein, do the lion's whelps get them away together; those devils recede from the persecution of the Church, who instigated men to persecute the house of God, by working in the sons of unbelief.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:252
verses.text: Now that none of them dareth persecute the Church, "the Sun hath arisen, and they get them away together".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:253
verses.text: And where are they? "And they lay them down in their dens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:254
verses.text: Their dens are the hearts of the unbelieving.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:255
verses.text: How many carry lions crouching in their hearts? They burst not forth thence, they make no assault upon the pilgrim Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:256
verses.text: Wherefore do they not so? Because the Sun is already risen, and is shining over the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:257
verses.text: What art thou doing, O man of God? thou, O Church of God? what art thou, O body of Christ, whose Head is in Heaven? what art thou doing, O man, His unity? "Man," he saith, "shall go forth to his work".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:258
verses.text: Let therefore this man work good works in the security of the peace of the Church, let him work unto the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:259
verses.text: For sometime there will be a sort of general darkening, and a sort of assault will be made, but in the evening, that is, in the end of the world: but now the Church doth work in peace and tranquillity; for "man shall go forth to his work, and to his labour, unto the evening".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:260
verses.text: "O Lord, how great are made Thy works!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:261
verses.text: Justly great, justly sublime! where were those works made, that are so great? what was that station where God stood, or that seat whereupon He sat, when He did those works? what was the place where He worked thus? whence did those so beautiful works proceed at the first? To take it word for word, every ordained creation, running by ordinance, beautiful by ordinance, rising by ordinance, setting by ordinance, going through all seasons by ordinance, whence hath it proceeded? whence hath the Church herself received her rise, her growth, her perfection? In what manner is she destined to a consummation in immortality? with what heralding is she preached? by what mysteries is she recommended? by what types is she concealed? by what preaching is she revealed? where hath God done these things? I see great works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:262
verses.text: "How great are made Thy works, O Lord!" I ask where He hath made them: I find not the place: but I see what followeth: "In Wisdom hast Thou made them all".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:263
verses.text: All therefore Thou hast made in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:264
verses.text: "The earth is full of Thy creation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:265
verses.text: The earth is full of the creation of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:266
verses.text: And how so? We discern how: for what was not made by the Father through the Son? Whatever walketh and doth crawl on earth, whatever doth swim in the waters, whatever flieth in the air, whatever doth revolve in heaven, how much more then the earth, the whole universe, is the work of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:267
verses.text: But he seems to me to speak here of some new creation, of which the Apostle saith, "If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things have passed away; behold, all things are become new.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:268
verses.text: And all things are of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:269
verses.text: All who believe in Christ, who put off the old man, and put on the new, are a new creature.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:270
verses.text: "The earth is full of Thy works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:271
verses.text: On one spot of the earth He was crucified, in one small spot that seed fell into the earth, and died; but brought forth great fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:272
verses.text: "The earth is full of Thy creation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:273
verses.text: Of what creation of Thine is the earth full? Of all trees and shrubs, of all animals and flocks, and of the whole of the human race; the earth is full of the creation of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:274
verses.text: We see, know, read, recognise, praise, and in these we preach of Him; yet we are not able to praise respecting these things, as fully as our heart doth abound with praise after the beautiful contemplation of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:275
verses.text: But we ought rather to heed that creation, of which the Apostle saith, "If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:276
verses.text: What "old things have passed away"? In the Gentiles, all idolatry; in the Jews themselves, all that servitude unto the Law, all those sacrifices that were harbingers of the present Sacrifice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:277
verses.text: The oldness of man was then abundant; One came to renovate His own work, to melt His silver, to form His coin, and we now see the earth full of Christians believing in God, turning themselves away from their former uncleanness and idolatry, from a past hope to the hope of a new age: and behold it is not yet realized, but is already possessed in hope, and through that very hope we now sing, and say, "The earth is full of Thy creation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:278
verses.text: We do not as yet sing this in our country, nor yet in that rest which is promised, the bars of the gates of Jerusalem not being as yet made fast; but still in our pilgrimage gazing upon the whole of this world, upon men who on every side are running unto the faith, fearing hell, despising death, loving eternal life, scorning the present, and filled with joy at such a spectacle, we say, "The earth is full of Thy creation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:279
verses.text: "So is the great and wide sea also; wherein are things creeping innumerable, both small and great beasts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:280
verses.text: He speaketh of the sea as terrible.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:281
verses.text: Snares creep in this world, and surprise the careless suddenly; for who numbereth the temptations that creep? They creep, but beware, lest they snatch us away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:282
verses.text: Let us keep watch on the Wood; even in the water, even on the waves, we are safe: let not Christ sleep, let not faith sleep; if He hath slept, let Him be awakened; He will command the winds; He will calm the sea; the voyage will be ended, and we shall rejoice in our country.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:283
verses.text: For I see in this terrible sea unbelievers still; for they dwell in barren and bitter waters: but they are both small and great.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:284
verses.text: We know this: many little men of this world are still unbelievers, many great men of this world are so: there are living creatures, both small and great, in this sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:285
verses.text: They hate the Church: the name of Christ is a burden to them: they rage not, because they are not permitted; the cruelty which cannot burst forth in deeds, is shut up within the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:286
verses.text: For all, whether small or great, "creeping things, both small and great," who at present grieve at the temples being shut, the altars overthrown, the images broken, the laws which make it a capital crime to sacrifice to idols; all who mourn on this account, are still in the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:287
verses.text: What then of us? And by what road then are we to journey unto our country? Through this very sea, but on the Wood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:288
