verses.text: Fear not the danger; that wood which holdeth together the world doth bear thee up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:289
verses.text: "There shall go the ships".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:290
verses.text: Lo, ships float upon that which alarmed you, and sink not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:291
verses.text: By ships we understand churches; they go among the storms, among the tempests of temptations, among the waves of the world, among the beasts, both small and great.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:292
verses.text: Christ on the wood of His cross is the Pilot.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:293
verses.text: "There shall go the ships".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:294
verses.text: Let not the ships fear, let them not much mind where they float, but by Whom they are steered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:295
verses.text: "There shall go the ships".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:296
verses.text: What voyage do they find tedious, when they feel that Christ is their Pilot? They will sail safely, let them sail diligently, they will reach their promised haven, they will be led to the land of rest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:297
verses.text: There is also in that sea somewhat which transcends all creatures, great and small.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:298
verses.text: What is this? Let us hear the Psalm: "There is that Leviathan, whom Thou hast formed to make sport of him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:299
verses.text: There are creeping things innumerable, both small and great beasts; there shall the ships go, and shall not fear, not only the creeping things innumerable, and beasts both small and great, but not even the serpent which is there; "whom Thou," he speaketh unto God, "hast made to make sport of him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:300
verses.text: This is a great mystery; and yet I am about to utter what ye already know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:301
verses.text: Ye know that a certain serpent is the enemy of the Church: ye have not seen him with the eyes of the flesh, but ye see him with the eyes of faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:302
verses.text: This serpent then, our ancient enemy, glowing with rage, cunning in his wiles, is in the mighty sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:303
verses.text: "Here is that Leviathan, whom Thou hast formed to make sport of him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:304
verses.text: Do thou now make sport of the serpent: for for this end was this serpent made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:305
verses.text: He falling by his own sin from the sublime realms of the heavens, and made devil instead of angel, received a certain region of his own in this mighty and spacious sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:306
verses.text: What thou thinkest his kingdom, is his prison.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:307
verses.text: For many say: wherefore hath the devil received so great power, that he may rule in this world, and prevaileth so much, can do so much? How much prevaileth he? How much can he do? Unless by permission, he can do nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:308
verses.text: Do thou so act, that he may not be allowed to attack thee; or if he be allowed to tempt thee, he may depart vanquished, and may not gain thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:309
verses.text: For he hath been allowed to tempt some holy men, servants of God: they overcame him, because they departed not from the way, they whose heel he watched, fell not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:310
verses.text: He then, my brethren, who doth wish to watch the serpent's head, and safely to pass this sea; for it must be that this serpent dwelleth here, and, as I had commenced saying, the devil when he fell from heaven received this region; let him watch his head, on the part of the fear of the world, and of the lusts of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:311
verses.text: For it is hence that he suggesteth some object of fear or of desire; he trieth thy love, or thy fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:312
verses.text: If thou fearest hell, and lovest the kingdom of God, thou wilt watch his head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:313
verses.text: "There is no power but of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:314
verses.text: What then fearest thou? Let the dragon be in the waters, let the dragon be in the sea: thou art to pass through it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:315
verses.text: He is made so as to be made sport of, he is ordained to inhabit this place, this region is given him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:316
verses.text: Thou thinkest that this habitation is a great thing for him, because thou knowest not the dwellings of the angels whence he fell: what seemeth to thee his glory, is his damnation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:317
verses.text: What then fearest thou? Perhaps he is about to try thy flesh: it is the scourge of thy Lord, not the power of thy tempter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:318
verses.text: His wish is to injure that salvation which is promised: but he is not allowed: but that he may not be allowed, have Christ for thy Head: repel the serpent's head: consent not unto his suggestion, slip not from thy path.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:319
verses.text: "There is that Leviathan, whom Thou hast made to make sport of him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:320
verses.text: Dost thou wish to see how incapable he is of hurting thee, unless permitted? "These," he saith, "wait all upon Thee, that Thou mayest give them meat in due season".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:321
verses.text: And this serpent wisheth to devour, but he devoureth not whom he wisheth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:322
verses.text: Thou hast heard what the serpent's meat is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:323
verses.text: Thou dost not wish that God give thee to be devoured by the serpent; because not the serpent's food: i-e: forsake not the Word of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:324
verses.text: For where it is said to the serpent, "Dust thou shalt eat," it is said to the transgressor, "Dust thou art, and unto dust thou shalt return".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:325
verses.text: Thou dost not wish to be the serpent's food? be not dust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:326
verses.text: How, thou repliest, shall I not be dust? If thou hast not a taste for earthly things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:327
verses.text: Hear the Apostle, that thou mayest not be dust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:328
verses.text: For the body which thou wearest is earth: but do thou refuse to be earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:329
verses.text: What meaneth this? "Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:330
verses.text: If thou dost not set thy affections on earthly things, thou art not earth: if thou art not earth, thou art not devoured by the serpent, whose appointed food is earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:331
verses.text: The Lord giveth the serpent his food when He will, what He will: but He judgeth rightly, he cannot be deceived, He giveth him not gold for earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:332
verses.text: "When Thou hast given it them, they gather it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:333
verses.text: "When thou openest Thy hand, they shall all be filled with good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:334
verses.text: What is it, O Lord, that Thou openest Thy hand? Christ is Thy hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:335
verses.text: "To whom is the arm of the Lord revealed?" To whom it is revealed, unto him it is opened: for revelation is opening.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:336
verses.text: "When Thou openest Thy hand, they shall all be filled with good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:337
verses.text: When Thou revealest Thy Christ, "they shall all be filled with good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:338
verses.text: But they have not good from themselves; this is oftentimes proved unto them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:339
verses.text: "When Thou hidest Thy face, they are troubled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:340
verses.text: Many filled with good have attributed to themselves what they had, and have wished to boast as in their own righteousnesses, and have said to themselves, I am righteous; I am great: and have become self-complacent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:341
verses.text: Unto these the Apostle speaketh: "What hast thou, that thou didst not receive?" But God, wishing to prove unto man that whatever he hath he hath from Him, so that with good he may gain humility also, sometimes troubleth him; He turneth away His face from him, and he falleth into temptation; and He showeth him that his righteousness, and his walking aright, was only under His government.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:342
verses.text: But wherefore dost Thou do this? wherefore dost Thou hide Thy face, that they may be troubled? "Thou shalt take away their breath, and they shall fail".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:343
verses.text: Their breath was their pride; they boast, they attribute things to themselves, they justify themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:344
verses.text: Hide, therefore, Thy face, that they may be troubled: take away their breath, and let them fail; let them cry unto Thee, "Hear me, O Lord, and that soon, for my spirit waxeth faint: hide not Thy face from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:345
verses.text: "Thou shalt take away their breath, and they shall fail, and shall be turned to their dust".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:346
verses.text: The man who repenteth of his sin discovereth himself, that he had not strength of himself; and doth confess unto God, saying, that he is earth and ashes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:347
verses.text: O proud one, thou art turned to thine own dust, thy breath hath been taken away; no longer dost thou boast thyself, no longer extol thyself, no longer justify thyself; thou seest that thou art made of dust, and when the Lord turneth away His face, thou hast fallen back into thine own dust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:348
verses.text: Pray, therefore, confess thy dust and thy weakness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:349
verses.text: And see what followeth: "Thou shalt send forth Thy Spirit, and they shall be made".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:350
verses.text: Thou shalt take away their spirit, and send forth Thine own: Thou shalt take away their spirit: they shall have no spirit of their own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:351
verses.text: Are they then forsaken? "Blessed are the poor in spirit:" but they are not forsaken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:352
verses.text: They refused to have a spirit of their own: they shall have the Spirit of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:353
verses.text: Such were our Lord's words to the future martyrs: "It is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:354
verses.text: Attribute not your courage to yourselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:355
verses.text: If it is yours, He saith, and not Mine, it is obstinacy, not courage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:356
verses.text: "For we are His workmanship," saith the Apostle, "created unto good works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:357
verses.text: From His Spirit we have received grace, that we may live unto righteousness: for it is He that justifieth the ungodly "Thou shalt take away their spirit, and they shall fail; Thou shalt send forth Thy Spirit, and they shall be made: and Thou shalt renew the face of the earth:" that is, with new men, confessing themselves to have been justified, not righteous of their own power, so that the grace of God is in them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:358
verses.text: What then? When He hath taken away our spirit, we shall be turned again to our dust, beholding to our edification our weakness, that when we receive His Spirit we may be refreshed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:359
verses.text: See what followeth: "Be the glory of the Lord for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:360
verses.text: Not thine, not mine, not his, or his; not for a season, but "for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:361
verses.text: "The Lord shall rejoice in His works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:362
verses.text: Not in thine, as if they were thine: because if thy works are evil, it is through thy iniquity; if good, it is through the grace of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:363
verses.text: "The Lord shall rejoice in His works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:364
verses.text: "Who looketh on the earth, and maketh it tremble; who toucheth the hills, and they shall smoke".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:365
verses.text: O earth, thou wast exulting in thy good, to thyself thou didst ascribe thy fulness and opulence; behold, the Lord looketh on thee, and causeth thee to tremble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:366
verses.text: May He look on thee, and make thee tremble: for the trembling of humility is better than the confidence of pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:367
verses.text: For it is God, he saith, which worketh in you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:368
verses.text: For this reason then with trembling, because God worketh in you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:369
verses.text: Because He gave, because what thou hast cometh not from thee, thou shalt work with fear and trembling, for if thou fearest not Him, He will take away what He gave.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:370
verses.text: Work, therefore, with trembling.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:371
verses.text: Hear another Psalm: "Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice unto Him with trembling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:372
verses.text: If we must rejoice with trembling, God beholdeth us, there cometh an earthquake; when God looketh upon us, let our hearts tremble; then will God rest there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:373
verses.text: Hear Him in another passage: "Upon whom shall My Spirit rest? Even on him that is lowly and quiet, and who trembleth at My Word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:374
verses.text: "Who looketh on the earth, and maketh it tremble; who toucheth the hills, and they shall smoke".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:375
verses.text: The hills were proud, and boastful of themselves, God had not touched them: He toucheth them, and they shall smoke.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:376
verses.text: What meaneth the smoking of the hills? That they pray unto the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:377
verses.text: Behold great hills, proud hills, vast hills, prayed not to God: they wished themselves to be entreated, and entreated not Him who was above them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:378
verses.text: For what powerful, arrogant, proud man is there upon the earth, who deigneth humbly to entreat God? I speak of the ungodly, not of the "cedars of Libanus, which the Lord hath planted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:379
verses.text: Every ungodly man, unhappy soul, knoweth not how to entreat God, while he wisheth himself to be entreated by men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:380
verses.text: He is a hill; it is needful that God touch him, that he may smoke: when he hath begun to smoke, he will offer prayers unto God, as it were the sacrifice of his heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:381
verses.text: He smoketh unto God, he then beateth his breast: he beginneth to weep, for smoke doth elicit tears.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:382
verses.text: "I will sing unto the Lord in my life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:383
verses.text: What will sing? Everything that is willing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:384
verses.text: Let us sing unto the Lord in our life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:385
verses.text: Our life at present is only hope; our life will be eternity hereafter: the life of mortal life, is the hope of an everlasting life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:386
verses.text: "I will praise my God while I have my being".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:387
verses.text: Since I am in Him for ever and ever, while I have my being, I will praise my God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:388
verses.text: Let us not imagine that, when we have commenced praising God in that state, we shall have any other work: our whole life will be for the praises of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:389
verses.text: If we become weary of Him whom we praise, we may also become weary of praising.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:390
verses.text: If He is ever loved, He is ever praised by us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:391
verses.text: "Let my discourse be pleasing to Him: my joy shall be in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:392
verses.text: What is the discourse of man unto God, save the confession of sins? Confess unto God what thou art, and thou hast discoursed with Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:393
verses.text: Discourse unto Him, do good works, and discourse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:394
verses.text: "Wash you, make you clean," saith Isaiah What is it to discourse unto God? Unfold thyself to him who knoweth thee, that He may unfold Himself to thee who knowest not Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:395
verses.text: Behold, it is thy discourse that pleaseth the Lord; the offering of thy humility, the tribulation of thy heart, the holocaust of thy life, this pleaseth God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:396
verses.text: But what is pleasing to thyself? "My joy shall be in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:397
verses.text: This is that discoursing which I meant between God and thyself: show thyself to Him who knoweth thee, and He showeth Himself unto thee who knowest not him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:398
verses.text: Pleasing unto Him is thy confession: sweet unto thee is His grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:399
verses.text: He hath spoken Himself unto thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:400
verses.text: How? By the Word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:401
verses.text: What Word? Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:402
verses.text: "Let the sinners be consumed out of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:403
verses.text: He seemeth angry! O holy soul, which here doth sing and groan! Would that our soul were with that very soul! Would that it were coupled with it, associated, conjoined with it! It shall behold also His loving-kindness when he is angry.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:404
verses.text: For who but he who is filled with charity, understandeth this? Thou tremblest, because he curseth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:405
verses.text: And who doth curse? A saint.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:406
verses.text: Without doubt he is listened to.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:407
verses.text: But it is said unto the saints, "Bless, and curse not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:408
verses.text: What is then the sense of the words, "Let the sinners be consumed out of the earth"? Let them utterly be consumed; let their spirit be taken away, that He may send forth His own Spirit, and they may be restored.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:409
verses.text: "And the ungodly, so that they be no more".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:410
verses.text: In what that they be no more, save as wicked men? Let them therefore be justified, that they may no longer be ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:411
verses.text: The Psalmist saw this, and was filled with joy, and repeateth the first verse of the Psalm: "Bless thou the Lord, O my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:412
verses.text: Let our soul bless the Lord, brethren, since He hath deigned to give unto us both understanding and the power of language, and unto you attention and earnestness in hearing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:413
verses.text: Let each, as he can recall to mind what he hath heard, by mutual conversation stir up the food ye have received, ruminate on what ye have heard, let it not descend in you into the bowels of forgetfulness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:414
verses.text: Let the treasure to be desired rest upon your lips.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 104:415
verses.text: These matters have been sought out and discovered with great labour, with great labour have they been announced and discoursed of; may our toil be fruitful unto you, and may our soul bless the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:1
verses.text: Psalm CV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:2
verses.text: This Psalm is the first of those to which is prefixed the word Allelujah; the meaning of which word, or rather two words, is, Praise the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:3
verses.text: For this reason he beginneth with praises: "O confess unto the Lord, and call upon His Name" ; for this confession is to be understood as praise, just as these words of our Lord, "I confess to Thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:4
verses.text: For after commencing with praise, calling upon God is wont to follow, whereunto he that prayeth doth next add his longings: whence the Lord's Prayer itself hath at the commencement a very brief praise, in these words, "Our Father which art in Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:5
verses.text: The things prayed for, then follow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:6
verses.text: This also followeth, "Tell the people what things He hath done;" or rather, to translate literally from the Greek, as other Latin copies too have it, "Preach the Gospel of His works among the Gentiles".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:7
verses.text: Unto whom is this addressed, save unto the Evangelists in prophecy?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:8
verses.text: "O sing unto Him, and play on instruments unto Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:9
verses.text: Praise Him both by word and deed; for we sing with the voice, while we play with an instrument, that is, with our hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:10
verses.text: "Let your talking be of all His wondrous works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:11
verses.text: Be ye praise in His holy Name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:12
verses.text: These two verses may without any absurdity seem paraphrases of the two words above; so that, "Let your talking be of all His wondrous works," may express the words, "O sing unto Him;" and what followeth, "be ye praised in His holy Name," may be referred to the words, "and play on instruments unto Him;" the former relating to the "good word" wherewith we sing unto Him, in which His wondrous works are told; the latter to the good work, in which sweet music is played unto Him, so that no man may wish to be praised for a good work on the score of his own power to do it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:13
verses.text: For this reason, after saying, "be ye praised," which assuredly they who work well deservedly may, he added, "in His holy Name," since "he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:14
verses.text: This is to be praised in His holy Name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:15
verses.text: Whence we read also in another Psalm: "My soul shall be praised in the Lord: let the meek hear thereof, and be glad;" which here in a sense followeth, "Let the heart of them rejoice that seek the Lord:" for thus the meek are glad, who do not rival with a bitter jealousy those whom they imitate as already workers of good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:16
verses.text: "Seek the Lord, and be strengthened".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:17
verses.text: This is very literally construed from the Greek, though it may seem not a Latin word: whence other copies have, "be ye confirmed;" others, "be ye corroborated".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:18
verses.text: While these words, then, "Come unto Him, and be enlightened," apply to seeing; those in the text relate to doing: "Seek the Lord, and be strengthened".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:19
verses.text: But what meaneth, "Seek His face evermore"? I know indeed that to cling unto God is good for me; but if He is always being sought, when is He found? Did he mean by "evermore," the whole of the life we live here, whence we become conscious that we ought thus to seek, since even when found He is still to be sought? To wit, faith hath already found Him, but hope still seeketh Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:20
verses.text: But love hath both found Him through faith, and seeketh to have Him by sight, where He will then be found so as to satisfy us, and no longer to need our search.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:21
verses.text: For unless faith discovered Him in this life, it would not be said, "Seek the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:22
verses.text: Also, if when discovered by faith, He were not still to be diligently sought, it would not be said, "For if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:23
verses.text: And truly this is the sense of the words, "Seek His face evermore;" meaning that discovery should not terminate that seeking, by which love is testified, but with the increase of love the seeking of the discovered One should increase.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:24
verses.text: "Remember," he saith, "His marvellous works that He hath done, His wonders, and the judgments of His mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:25
verses.text: This passage seemeth like that, "Thou shalt say unto the children of Israel, I Am hath sent me unto you:" an expression which, in ever so small part, scarce a mind taketh in.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:26
verses.text: Then mentioning His own Name, He mercifully mingled in His grace towards men, saying, "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob; this is My Name for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:27
verses.text: By which He would have it to be understood, that they whose God He declared Himself lived with Him for ever, and He said this, which might be understood even by children, that they who by the great powers of love knew how to seek His face for evermore, might according to their capacity comprehend, I Am that I Am.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:28
verses.text: Unto whom is it said, "O ye seed of Abraham His servant, ye children of Jacob, His chosen"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:29
verses.text: He next addeth, "He is the Lord our God: His judgments are in all the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:30
verses.text: Is He the God of the Jews only? God forbid! "He is the Lord our God:" because the Church, where His judgments are preached, is in all the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:31
verses.text: "He hath been alway mindful of His covenant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:32
verses.text: Other copies read, "for evermore;" and this arises from the ambiguity of the Greek.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:33
verses.text: But if we are to understand "alway" of this world and not of eternity, why, when he explaineth what covenant He was mindful of, doth he add, "The word that He made to a thousand generations"? Now this may be understood with a certain limitation; but he afterwards saith, "Even the covenant that He made with Abraham" : "and the oath that He sware unto Isaac; and appointed the same unto Jacob for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting testament".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:34
verses.text: But if in this passage the Old Tes tament is to be understood, on account of the land of Canaan; for thus the language of the Psalm runneth, "saying, Unto thee will I give the land of Canaan: the lot of your inheritance" : how is it to be understood as everlasting, since that earthly inheritance could not be everlasting? And for this reason it is called the Old Testament, because it is abolished by the New.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:35
verses.text: But a thousand generations do not seem to signify anything eternal, since they involve an end; and yet are also too numerous for this very temporal state.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:36
verses.text: For by howsoever few years a generation is limited, such as in Greek is called γεν™α, whereof the shortest period some have fixed is at fifteen years, after which period man hath the power of generation; what then are those "thousand generations," not only from the time of Abraham, when that promise was made him, unto the New Testament, but from Adam himself down to the end of the world? For who would dare to say that this world should last for  years? Hence it seemeth to me that we ought not to understand here the Old Testament, which it said through the prophet was to be cancelled by the New: "Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:37
verses.text: After saying, "He hath been mindful of His covenant unto an age;" which we ought to understand as lasting for evermore, the covenant, namely, of justification and an eternal inheritance, which God hath promised to faith; he addeth, "and the Word that He commanded unto a thousand generations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:38
verses.text: What meaneth "commanded"?The command then was faith, that the righteous should live by faith; and an eternal inheritance is set before this faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:39
verses.text: "A thousand generations," then, are, on account of the perfect number, to be understood for all; that is, as long as generation succeedeth generation, so long is it commanded to us to live by faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:40
verses.text: This the people of God doth observe, the sons of promise who succeed by birth, and depart by death, until every generation be finished; and this is signified by the number thousand; because the solid square of the number ten, ten times ten, and this taken ten times amounts to a thousand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:41
verses.text: "Even the covenant," he saith, "which He made with Abraham: and the oath that He sware unto Isaac; and appointed the same unto Jacob," that is, Jacob himself, "for a law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:42
verses.text: These are the very three patriarchs, whose God He calleth Himself in a special sense, whom the Lord also doth name in the New Testament, where He saith, "Many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:43
verses.text: This is everlasting inheritance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:44
verses.text: He next followeth out the history well known in the truth of the holy Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:45
verses.text: "When they were in small numbers, very few, and they strangers in the land" ; that is, in the land of Canaan.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:46
verses.text: But some copies have the words "very few, and they strangers," in the accusative case, the translator having turned the Greek phrase too literally into Latin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:47
verses.text: If we were to render the whole clause in this way, we must say, "that they were very few, and they strangers;" but the phrase, "while they were," is the meaning of the Greek; and the verb, "to be," takes not an accusative, but a nominative after it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:48
verses.text: "What time as they went from one nation to another, from one kingdom to another people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:49
verses.text: This is a repetition of what he had said, "from one nation to another".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:50
verses.text: "He suffered no man to do them harm: but reproved even kings for their sakes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:51
verses.text: "Touch not," He said, "Mine anointed, and do My prophets no harm".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:52
verses.text: He declareth the words of God chiding or reproving kings, that they might not harm the holy fathers, while they were small in number, very few, and they strangers in the land of Canaan.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:53
verses.text: Although these words be not read in the books of that history, yet they are to be understood as either secretly spoken, as God speaketh in the hearts of men by unseen and true visions, or even as announced through an Angel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:54
verses.text: For both the king of Gerar and the king of the Egyptians were warned from Heaven not to harm Abraham, and another king not to harm Isaac, and others not to harm Jacob; while they were very few, and strangers, before he went over into Egypt to sojourn with his sons: which is understood to be herein mentioned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:55
verses.text: But since it occurred to ask, before they passed over and multiplied in Egypt, how so few in number, and those strangers in a foreign land, could maintain themselves: he next addeth, "He suffered no man to do them wrong," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:56
verses.text: But it may well excite a question, in what sense they were styled (Christs, or) anointed, before there was any unction, from which this title was given to the kingsWhence then were those patriarchs at that time called "anointed"? For that they were prophets, we read concerning Abraham; and certainly, what is manifestly said of him, should be understood of them also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:57
verses.text: Are they styled "christs," because, even though secretly, yet they were already Christians? For although the flesh of Christ came from them, nevertheless Christ came before them; for He thus answered the Jews, "Before Abraham was, I am".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:58
verses.text: But how could they not know Him, or not believe in Him; since they are called prophets for this very reason, because, though somewhat darkly, they announced the Lord beforehand? Whence He saith Himself openly, "Your father Abraham desired to see My day, and he saw it, and was glad".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:59
verses.text: For no man was ever reconciled unto God outside of that faith which is in Christ Jesus, either before His Incarnation, or after: as it is most truly defined by the Apostle: "For there is one God, and one Mediator between God and men, the Man Christ Jesus".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:60
verses.text: He then beginneth to relate how it happened that they went from one nation to another, from one kingdom to another people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:61
verses.text: "He calleth," he saith, "for a famine upon the land: and brake all the staff of bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:62
verses.text: Thus it happened that they went from one nation to another, from one kingdom to another people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:63
verses.text: But the expressions of the holy Scriptures are not to be negligently passed by.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:64
verses.text: "He called," he saith, "for a famine upon the land;" as if famine were some person, or some animated body, or some spirit that would obey Him who called.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:65
verses.text: Under this impression the old Romans consecrated some such deities, as the goddess Fever, and the god Paleness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:66
verses.text: Or meaneth it, as is more credible, He said there should be famine; so that calling be the same thing as mentioning by name; mentioning by name, as speaking; speaking, as commanding? Nor doth the Apostle say,  "He calleth those things which be not, that they may be;" but, "as though they were".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:67
verses.text: For with God that hath already happened which, according to His disposition, is fixed for the future: for of Him it is elsewhere said, "He who made things to come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:68
verses.text: And here when famine happened, then it is said to have been called, that is, that that which had been determined in His secret government, might be realized.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:69
verses.text: Lastly, he at once expounds, how He called for the famine, saying, "He brake all the staff of bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:70
verses.text: "But He had sent a man before them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:71
verses.text: What man? "Even Joseph".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:72
verses.text: How did He send him? "Joseph was sold to be a bond-servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:73
verses.text: When this happened, it was the sin of his brethren, and, nevertheless, God sent Joseph into Egypt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:74
verses.text: We should therefore meditate on this important and necessary subject, how God useth well the evil works of men, as they on the other hand use ill the good works of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:75
verses.text: Next he doth relate the story, mentioning what Joseph suffered in his low estate, and how he was raised on high.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:76
verses.text: "His feet they hurt in the stocks: the iron entered into his soul, until his word came".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:77
verses.text: That Joseph was put in irons, we do not indeed read; but we ought no ways to doubt that it was so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:78
verses.text: For some things might be passed over in that history, which nevertheless would not escape the Holy Spirit, who speaketh in these Psalms.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:79
verses.text: We understand by the iron which entered into his soul, the tribulation of stern necessity; for he did not say body, but "soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:80
verses.text: There is a somewhat similar expression in the Gospel, where Simeon saith unto Mary, "A sword shall pierce through thy own soul also".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:81
verses.text: That is, the Passion of the Lord, which was a fall unto many, and in which the secrets of many hearts were revealed, since their sentiments respecting the Lord were extorted from them, without doubt made His own Mother exceeding sorrowful, heavily struck with human bereavement.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:82
verses.text: Now Joseph was in this tribulation, "until his word came," with which he truly interpreted dreams: whence he was introduced to the king, that unto him also he might foretell what would happen in respect to his dreams But since he said, "Until his words were heard," that we might not altogether so understand "his," that any one might think so great an event was to be ascribed unto man; he at once added, "The word of the Lord inflamed him" ; or, as other copies have it more closely from the Greek, "The word of the Lord fired him," that he also might be reputed amongst those to whom it is said, "Receive ye praise in His holy Name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:83
verses.text: "The king sent and loosed him, the prince of the peoples, and let him go free".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:84
verses.text: The "king" is the same as "the prince of the peoples:" he "loosed" him from his bonds "and let him go free" from his prison.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:85
verses.text: "He made him lord also of his house: and ruler of all his substance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:86
verses.text: "That he might inform his princes like unto himself, and teach his old men wisdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:87
verses.text: The Greek hath, "and teach his elders wisdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:88
verses.text: Which might altogether be rendered to the letter thus; "Might inform his princes like unto himself, and make his elders wise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:89
verses.text: The word translated old men being presbyters or elders, not gerontas, old men: and to teach wisdom being from the Greek to sophize, which cannot be rendered by a single word in Latin, and is from the word sophia, wisdom, different from prudence, which is in Greek phronesis.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:90
verses.text: Yet we do not read this in the high elevation of Joseph, as we read not of fetters in his low estate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:91
verses.text: But how could it happen that so great a man, the worshipper of the One True God, whilst in Egypt, should have been intent upon the nourishing of bodies, and the government of carnal matters only, and have felt no anxiety for souls, and how he could render them better? But those things are written in that history, which, according to the intention of the writer, in whom was the Holy Spirit, were judged sufficient for signifying future events in that narration.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:92
verses.text: "Joseph also came into Egypt, and Jacob was a stranger in the land of Ham".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:93
verses.text: Israel is the same with Jacob, as is Egypt with the land of Ham.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:94
verses.text: Here it is very plainly shown, that the Egyptian race sprang from the seed of Chain, the son of Noah, whose first-born was Canaan.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:95
verses.text: So that in those copies wherein in this passage Canaan is read, we must alter the reading.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:96
verses.text: It is better construed, "was a stranger," than "dwelt," as other copies have it: which would be the same as "was an inhabitant," for it meaneth nothing different; the very same word is used in the Greek passage above, where it is said, "Very few, and they strangers in the land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:97
verses.text: Moreover, the state of an incola or accola doth not signify a native, but a stranger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:98
verses.text: Behold how "they went from one nation to another".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:99
verses.text: What had been briefly proposed, hath been briefly explained in the narration.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:100
verses.text: But from what kingdom they passed over to another people may well be asked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:101
verses.text: For they were not yet reigning in the land of Canaan, because the kingdom of the people of Israel had not yet been established there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:102
verses.text: How then can it be understood, except by anticipation, because the kingdom of their seed was destined there to exist?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:103
verses.text: Next is related what happened in Egypt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:104
verses.text: "And He increased," he saith, "His people exceedingly, and made them stronger than their enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:105
verses.text: Even the whole of this is briefly set forth, in order that the manner in which it took place may be afterwards related.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:106
verses.text: For the people of God was not made stronger than their enemies the Egyptians, at the time when their male offspring were slain, or when they were worn out with making bricks; but when by His powerful hand, by the signs and portents of the Lord their God, they became objects of fear and of honour, until the opposition of the hardened king was overcome, and the Red Sea overwhelmed the persecutor with his army.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:107
verses.text: "And He turned their heart so, that they hated His people, and dealt untruly with His servants".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:108
verses.text: Is it to be in any wise understood or believed, that God turneth man's heart to do sin?For they were not good before they hated His people; but being malignant and ungodly, they were such as would readily envy their prosperous sojourners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:109
verses.text: And so, in that He multiplied His own people, this bountiful act turned the wicked to envy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:110
verses.text: For envy is the hatred of another's prosperity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:111
verses.text: In this sense, therefore, He turned their heart, so that through envy they hated His people, and dealt untruly with His servants.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:112
verses.text: It was not then by making their hearts evil, but by doing good to His people, that He turned their hearts, that were evil of their own accord, to hatred.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:113
verses.text: For He did not pervert a righteous heart, but turned one perverted of its own accord to the hatred of His people, while He was to make a good use of that evil; not by making them evil, but by lavishing blessings upon those, which the wicked might most readily envy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:114
verses.text: The following verses, which are sung in praise of Him when Allelujah is chanted, show how He used this hatred of theirs, both for the trial of His own people, and for the glory of His Name, which is profitable for us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:115
verses.text: "He sent Moses His servant, and Aaron whom He had chosen him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:116
verses.text: "Whom He had chosen," would be sufficient; but there is no difficulty in the addition of "him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:117
verses.text: It is a phrase of Scripture, as, "The land in which they shall dwell in it:" a phrase which the divine pages are full of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:118
verses.text: "He set forth in them the words of His tokens, and of His wonders in the land of Ham".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:119
verses.text: We ought not to understand by "the words of His tokens," words literally, words with which the tokens and wonders were worked, that is, which they uttered, that these tokens and wonders might take place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:120
verses.text: For many were performed without words, either with a rod, or with outstretched hand, or by ashes sent towards heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:121
verses.text: "He sent darkness, and made it dark".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:122
verses.text: This is also written among the plagues with which the Egyptians were smitten.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:123
verses.text: But what followeth, is variously read in different copies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:124
verses.text: For some have, "and they provoked His words;" while others read, "and they provoked not His words;" but the reading first mentioned we have found in most; while, where the negative particle is added, we could hardly discover two copies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:125
verses.text: But perhaps the false reading has abounded owing to the easy sense; for what is easier understood than this, "They provoked His words," that is, by their contumacious rebellions? We have endeavoured to explain the other reading also according to some true sense: and this for the present occurs: "They provoked not His words," that is, in Moses and Aaron; because they most patiently bore with a very stiffnecked people, until all things which God had determined to work by them, were fulfilled in order.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:126
verses.text: "He turned their waters into blood, and slew their fish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:127
verses.text: "He made their land frogs, yea, even in the king's chambers" : as if he were to say, He turned their land into frogs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:128
verses.text: For there was so great a multitude of frogs, that this might well be said by hyperbole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:129
verses.text: "He spake the word, and there came all manner of flies, and lice in all their quarters".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:130
verses.text: If it be asked when He spake, it was in His Word before it took place; and there it was, without time, at what time it should take place: although even then He commanded it to be done, when it was to be done, through Angels, and through his servants Moses and Aaron.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:131
verses.text: He made their rains hail".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:132
verses.text: It is a similar expression to the former, "He made their land frogs;" except that the whole land was not actually turned into frogs, though the whole of the rain may have been turned into hail.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:133
verses.text: "A burning fire in their land:" understand, "He sent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:134
verses.text: "He smote their vines also and fig-trees; and brake every tree of their coasts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:135
verses.text: This was done by the violence of the hail, and by lightnings; whence he spoke of the fire as "burning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:136
verses.text: "He spake the word, and the locust came, and the caterpillar, of which there was no number".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:137
verses.text: The locusts and the caterpillars are one plague: of which the one is the parent, the other the offspring.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:138
verses.text: "And did eat up all the grass in their land, and devoured the fruit of the ground".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:139
verses.text: Even grass is fruit, as Scripture is wont to speak, which calleth even the ripe corn grass; but it wished these two things to harmonize in number with the two which it had spoken of before, that is, the locust and the caterpillar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:140
verses.text: But the whole of this doth belong to the variety of speech, which is a remedy for weariness, not to any difference of senses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:141
verses.text: "He smote every first-born in their land: even the first-fruits of all their strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:142
verses.text: This is the last plague, excepting the death in the Red Sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:143
verses.text: "The first-fruits of all their strength," I imagine to be an expression derived from the first-born of cattle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:144
verses.text: These plagues are ten in number, but they are not all mentioned, nor in the same order in which they are there read to have happened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:145
verses.text: For praise-giving is free from the law which bindeth one who is relating or composing a history.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:146
verses.text: And since the Holy Spirit is the Author and Dictator, through the Prophet, of this praise; by the very same authority with which He guided him who wrote that history, he doth both mention something to have taken place which is not there read, and passeth over what is there read.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:147
verses.text: Now he addeth this also to the praises of God, that He led the Israelites out of Egypt enriched with silver and gold; because even they were then in such a condition, that they could not as yet despise the just and due, though temporal, reward of their toils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:148
verses.text: "He brought them forth also in silver and gold" : this too is a Scripture idiom; for "in silver and gold" is said for the same as if it had been said "with silver and gold: there was not one feeble person among their tribes:" in body, not in mind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:149
verses.text: This also was a great blessing of God, that in this necessity of removal there was no infirm person.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:150
verses.text: "Egypt was glad at their departing: for their fear fell upon them" ; that is, the fear of the Hebrews upon the Egyptians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:151
verses.text: For "their fear" is not that with which the Hebrews feared, but that with which they were feared.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:152
verses.text: Some one will say, how then were the Egyptians unwilling to dismiss them? why did they let them go as if they expected them to return? why did they lend them gold and silver, as to men who were to return, and to repay them, if "Egypt was glad at their departing"? But we must understand, after that final destruction of the Egyptians, and the terrible overthrow of the mighty pursuing army in the Red Sea, that the rest of the Egyptians feared lest the Hebrews should return, and with great ease crush the relics of them: illustrating what he had stated, that He made His people stronger than their enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:153
verses.text: He now proceedeth to the divine blessings which were conferred upon them as they wandered in the desert.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:154
verses.text: "He spread out a cloud to be their covering: and fire to give them light in the night season".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:155
verses.text: This is as clear as it is well known.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:156
verses.text: "They asked, and the quail ca me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:157
verses.text: They did not desire quails, but flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:158
verses.text: But since the quail is flesh, and in this Psalm he speaketh not of the provocation of those who did not please God, but of the faith of the elect, the true seed of Abraham; they are to be understood to have desired that that might come which might crush the murmurs of those who provoked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:159
verses.text: Then in the next line, "And He filled them with the bread of heaven," he has not indeed named manna, but it is obscure to none who hath read those records.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:160
verses.text: "He opened the rock of stone, and the waters flowed out: so that rivers ran in the dry places".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:161
verses.text: This fact too is understood as soon as read.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:162
verses.text: But in all these blessings of His, God doth commend in Abraham the merit of faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:163
verses.text: For the Psalmist goeth on to say, "For why? He remembered His holy promise, which He made to Abraham His servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:164
verses.text: "And He brought forth His people with joy, and His chosen with gladness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:165
verses.text: What he said, "His people," he has repeated in, "His chosen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:166
verses.text: So also what he said, "with joy," he has repeated in, "with gladness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:167
verses.text: "And gave them the lands of the heathen: and they took the labours of the people in possession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:168
verses.text: "The lands of the heathen," and "the labours of the people," are the same; and the words, "He gave," are repeated in these, "they took in possession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:169
verses.text: "That they may keep His statutes, and seek out His law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:170
verses.text: Lastly, since by the seed of Abraham he wished those to be understood here, who were truly the seed of Abraham, such as were not wanting even in that people; as the Apostle Paul clearly showeth, when he saith, "But not in all of them was God well pleased;" for if He was not  pleased with all, surely there were some in whom He was well pleased: since then this Psalm praiseth such men as this, he hath said nothing here of the iniquities and provocations and bitterness of those with whom God was not well pleased.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:171
verses.text: But since not only the justice but also the mercy of Almighty God, t he merciful, was shown even unto the wicked; concerning these attributes the rest of the Psalm pursueth the praises of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:172
verses.text: And yet both sorts were in one people: nor did the latter pollute the good with the contagion of their iniquities.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 105:173
verses.text: For "the Lord knoweth who are His;" and if he cannot separate in this world from wicked men, yet, "let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:1
verses.text: Psalm CVI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:2
verses.text: This Psalm also hath the title Allelujah prefixed to it: and this twice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:3
verses.text: But some say, that one Allelujah belongeth to the end of the former Psalm, the other to the beginning of this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:4
verses.text: And they assert, that all the Psalms bearing this title  have Allelujah at the end, but not all at the beginning; so that they will not allow any Psalm which hath not Allelujah at the end, to have it at the beginning; supposing that what seemeth to belong to the commencement, really belongeth to the end of the former Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:5
verses.text: But until they persuade us by some sure proofs that this is true, we will follow the general custom, which, whenever it findeth Allelujah, attributes it to the same Psalm, at the head of which it is found.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:6
verses.text: For there are very few copies (and I have found this in none of the Greek copies, which I have been able to inspect) which have Allelujah at the end of the CLth Psalm; after which there is no other which belongeth to the same canon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:7
verses.text: But not even this could outweigh custom, although all the copies had it so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:8
verses.text: For it might be that, with some reference to the praise of God, the whole book of Psalms, which is said to consist of five books (for they say that the books severally end where it is written Amen, Amen), might be closed with this last Allelujah, after all that hath been sung; nor, on account of the end of the CLth Psalm, do I see that it is necessary that all the Psalms entitled Allelujah, should have Allelujah at the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:9
verses.text: But when there is a double Allelujah at the head of a Psalm, why as our Lord sometimes once, sometimes twice over, saith Amen, in the same way Allelujah may not sometimes be used once, sometimes twice, I know not: especially, since  as in this CVth, both the Allelujahs are placed after the mark by which the number of the Psalm is described, whereas the one, if it belonged to the end of the former Psalm, ou ght to have been placed before the number; and the Allelujah which belonged to the Psalm of this number, should have been written after the number.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:10
verses.text: But perhaps even in this an ignorant habit hath prevailed, and some reason may be assigned of which we are as yet uninformed, so that the judgment of truth ought rather to be our guide than the prejudice of custom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:11
verses.text: In the mean time, before we are fully instructed in this matter, whenever we find Allelujah written, whether once or twice, after the number  of the Psalm, according to the most usual custom of the Church, we will ascribe it to that Psalm to which the same number is prefixed; confessing that we both believe the mysteries of all the titles in the Psalms, and of the order of the same Psalms, to be important, and that we have not yet been able, as we wish, to penetrate them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:12
verses.text: But I find these two Psalms, the CVth and CVIth so connected, that in one of them, the first, the people of God is praised in the person of the elect, of whom there is no complaint, whom I  imagine to have been there in those with whom God was well pleased; but in the following Psalm those are mentioned among the same pe ople who have provoked God; though the mercy of God was not wanting even to these.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:13
verses.text: This Psalm therefore beginneth like the former; "Confess ye unto the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:14
verses.text: But in that Psalm these words follow: "And call upon His Name:" whereas here, it is as follows, "For He is gracious, and His mercy endureth for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:15
verses.text: Wherefore in this passage a confession of sins may be understood; for after a few verses we read, "We have sinned with our fathers, we have done amiss, and dealt wickedly;" but in the words, "For He is gracious, and His mercy endureth for ever," there is chiefly the praise of God, and in His praise confession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:16
verses.text: Although when any one confesses his sins, he ought to do so with praise of God; nor is a confession of sins a pious one, unless it be without despair, and with calling upon the mercy of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:17
verses.text: It therefore doth contain His praise, whether in words, when it calleth Him gracious and merciful, or in the feeling only, when he believeth this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:18
verses.text: If that mercy be here understood, in respect of which no man can be happy without God; we may render it better, "for ever:" but if it be that mercy which is shown to the wretched, that they may either be consoled in misery, or even freed from it; it is better construed, "to the end of the world," in which there will never be wanting wretched persons to whom that mercy may be shown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:19
verses.text: Unless indeed any man ventured to say, that some mercy of God will not be wanting even to those who shall be condemned with the devil and his angels; not a mercy by which they may be freed from that condemnation, but that it may be in some degree softened for them: and that thus the mercy of God may be styled eternal, as exercised over their eternal misery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:20
verses.text: "Who can express the mighty acts of the Lord?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:21
verses.text: Full of the consideration of the Divine works, while he entreateth His mercy, "Who," he saith, "can express the mighty acts of the Lord, or make all His praises heard?" We must supply what was said above, to make the sense complete here, thus, "Who shall make all His praises heard?" that is, who is sufficient to make all His praises heard? "Shall make" them "heard," he saith; that is, cause that they be heard; showing, that the mighty acts of the Lord and His praises are so to be spoken of, that they may be preached to those who hear them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:22
verses.text: But who can make "all," heard? Is it that as the next words are, "Blessed are they that alway keep judgment, and do righteousness in every time" ; he perhaps meant those praises of His, which are understood as His works in His commandments? "For it is God," saith the Apostle, "who worketh in you," since He worketh in these things in a manner that cannot be spoken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:23
verses.text: "Who will do all His praises heard?" that is, who, when he hath heard them, doth all His praises? which are the works of His commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:24
verses.text: As far as they are done, although all which are heard are not performed, He is to be praised, who "worketh in us both to will and to do of His good pleasure".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:25
verses.text: For this reason, while he might have said, all His commandments, or, all the works of His commandments; he preferred saying, "His praises".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:26
verses.text: But unless there were some difference between judgment and righteousness, we should not read in another Psalm, "Until righteousness turn again unto judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:27
verses.text: The Scripture, indeed, loveth to place these two words together; as, "Righteousness and judgment are the habitation of His seat;" and this, "He shall make thy righteousness as clear as the light, and thy judgment as the noon-day;" where there is apparently a repetition of the same sentiment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:28
verses.text: And perhaps on account of the resemblance of signification one may be put for the other, either judgment for righteousness, or righteousness for judgment: yet, if they be spoken of in their proper sense, I doubt not that there is some difference; viz.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:29
verses.text: that he is said to keep judgment who judgeth rightly, but he to do righteousness who acts righteously.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:30
verses.text: And I think that the verse, "Until righteousness turn again unto judgment," may not absurdly be understood in this sense: that here also those are called blessed, who keep judgment in faith, and do righteousness in deed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:31
verses.text: Next, since God justifieth, that is, maketh men righteous, by healing them from their iniquities, a prayer followeth: "Remember me, O Lord, according to the favour that Thou bearest unto Thy people" : that is, that we may be among those with whom Thou art well pleased; since God is not well pleased with them all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:32
verses.text: "O visit me with Thy salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:33
verses.text: This is the Saviour Himself, in whom sins are forgiven, and souls healed, that they may be able to keep judgment, and do righteousness; and since they who here speak know such men to be blessed, they pray for this themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:34
verses.text: "Visit us," then, "with Thy salvation," that is, with Thy Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:35
verses.text: "To see the felicity of Thy chosen, and to rejoice in the gladness of Thy people" : that is, visit us for this reason with Thy salvation, that we may see the felicity of Thy chosen, and rejoice in the gladness of Thy people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:36
verses.text: For "felicity" some copies read "sweetness;" as in the former passage, "For He is gracious;" where others read, "for He is sweet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:37
verses.text: And it is the same word in the Greek, as is elsewhere read, "The Lord shall show sweetness:" which some have translated "felicity," others "bounty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:38
verses.text: But what meaneth, "Visit us to see the felicity of Thy chosen:" that is, that happiness which Thou givest to Thine elect: except that we may not remain blind, as those unto whom it is said, "But now ye say we see: therefore your sin remaineth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:39
verses.text: For the Lord giveth sight to the blind, not by their own merits, but in the felicity He giveth to His chosen, which is the meaning of "the felicity of Thy chosen:" as, the help of my countenance, is not of myself, but is my God And we speak of our daily bread, as ours, but we add, Give unto us"That Thou mayest be praised with Thine inheritance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:40
verses.text: I wonder this verse hath been so interpreted in many copies, since the Greek phrase is one and the same in these three verses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:41
verses.text: But since this seemeth a doubtful expression, if that sense be true according to which interpreters have preferred, "That Thou mayest be praised," the two preceding verses also must be so understood, because, as I have said, there is one Greek expression in these three verses; so that the whole should be thus understood, "Visit us with Thy salvation, that Thou mayest see the felicity of Thy chosen;" that is, visit us for this purpose, that Thou mayest cause us to be there, and mayest see us there; that "Thou mayest rejoice in the gladness of Thy people," that is, that Thou mayest be said to rejoice, since they rejoice in Thee; that "Thou mayest be praised with Thine inheritance," that is, mayest be praised with it, since it may not be praised save for Thy sake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:42
verses.text: But let us hear what they next confess: "we have sinned with our fathers: we have done amiss, and dealt wickedly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:43
verses.text: What meaneth "with our fathers"?"Our fathers," he saith, "regarded not Thy wonders in Egypt" ; and many other things also, he doth relate of their sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:44
verses.text: Or is, "we have sinned with our fathers," to be understood as meaning, we have sinned like our fathers, that is, by imitating their sins? If it be so, it should be supported by some example of this mode of expression: which did not occur to me when I sought on this occasion an instance of any one saying that he had sinned, or done anything, with another, whom he had imitated by a similar act after a long interval of time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:45
verses.text: What meaneth then, "Our fathers understood not Thy wonders;" save this, they did not know what Thou didst wish to convince them of by these miracles? What indeed, save life eternal, and a good, not temporal, but immutable, which is waited for only through endurance? For this reason they impatiently murmured, and provoked, and they asked to be blessed with present and fugitive blessings, "Neither were they mindful of the greatness of Thy mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:46
verses.text: He reproveth both their understanding and memory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:47
verses.text: Understanding there was need of, that they might meditate unto what eternal blessings God was calling them through these temporal ones; and of memory, that at least they might not forget the temporal wonders which had been wrought, and might faithfully believe, that by the same power which they had already experienced, God would free them from the persecutions of their enemies; whereas they forgot the aid which He had given them in Egypt, by means of such wonders, to crush their enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:48
verses.text: "And they provoked, as they went up to the sea, even to the Red Sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:49
verses.text: We ought especially to notice how the Scripture doth censure the not understanding that which ought to have been understood, and the not remembering that which ought to have been remembered; which men are unwilling to have ascribed to their own fault, for no other reason than that they may pray less, and be less humble unto God, in whose sight they should confess what they are, and might by praying for His aid, become what they are not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:50
verses.text: For it is better to accuse even the sins of ignorance and negligence, that they may be done away with, than to excuse them, so that they remain; and it is better to clear them off by calling upon God, than to clench them by provoking Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:51
verses.text: He addeth, that God acted not according to their unbelief.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:52
verses.text: "Nevertheless," he saith, "He saved them for His Name's sake: that He might make His power to be known" : not on account of any deservings of their own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:53
verses.text: "He rebuked the Red Sea also, and it was dried up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:54
verses.text: We do not read that any voice was sent forth from Heaven to rebuke the sea; but he hath called the Divine Power by which this was effected, a rebuke: unless indeed any one may choose to say, that the sea was secretly rebuked, so that the waters might hear, and yet men could not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:55
verses.text: The power by which God acteth is very abstruse and mysterious, a power which He causeth that even things devoid of sense instantly obey at His will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:56
verses.text: "So He led them through the deeps, as through a wilderness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:57
verses.text: He calleth a multitude of waters the deeps.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:58
verses.text: For some wishing to give the sense of this whole verse, have translated, "So He led them forth amid many waters".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:59
verses.text: What then doth "through the deeps, as through a wilderness," mean, except that that had become as a wilderness from its dryness, where before had been the watery deeps?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:60
verses.text: "And He saved them from the hating ones".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:61
verses.text: Some translators, in order to avoid an expression unusual in Latin, have rendered the word, by a circumlocution, "And He saved them from the hand of those that hated them, and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:62
verses.text: What price was given in this redemption? Is it a prophecy, since this deed was a figure of Baptism, wherein we are redeemed from the hand of the devil at a great price, which price is the Blood of Christ? whence this is more consistently figured forth, not by any sea indiscriminately, but by the Red Sea; since blood hath a red colour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:63
verses.text: "As for those that troubled them, the waters overwhelmed them: there was not one of them left" ; not of all the Egyptians, but of those who pursued the departing Israelites, desirous either of taking or of killing them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:64
verses.text: "Then believed they in His words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:65
verses.text: The expression seemeth barely Latin, for he saith not "believed His word," or "on His words," but "in His words;" yet it is very frequent in Scripture.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:66
verses.text: "And praised praise unto Him;" such an expression as when we say, "This servitude he served," "such a life he lived".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:67
verses.text: He is here alluding to that well-known hymn, commencing, "I will sing unto the Lord, for He hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and the rider hath He thrown into the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:68
verses.text: "They acted hastily: they forgot His works" : other copies read more intelligibly, "They hastened, they forgot His works, and would not abide His counsel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:69
verses.text: For they ought to have thought, that so great works of God towards themselves were not without a purpose, but that they invited them to some endless happiness, which was to be waited for with patience; but they hastened to make themselves happy with temporal things, which give no man true happiness, because they do not quench insatiable longing: for "whosoever," saith our Lord, "shall drink of this water, shall thirst again".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:70
verses.text: Lastly, "And they lusted a lust in the wilderness, and they tempted God in the dry land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:71
verses.text: The "dry land," or land without water, and "desert," are the same: so also are, "they lusted a lust," and, "they tempted God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:72
verses.text: The form of speech is the same as above, "they praised a praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:73
verses.text: "And He gave them their desire, and sent fulness withal into their souls".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:74
verses.text: But He did not thus render them happy: for it was not that fulness of which it is said, "Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:75
verses.text: In this passage he doth not speak of the rational soul, but of the soul as giving animal life to the body; to the substance of which belong meat and drink, according to what is said in the Gospel, "Is not the soul more than meat, and the body than raiment?" as if it belonged to the soul to eat, to the body to be clothed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:76
verses.text: "And they angered Moses in the tents, and Aaron the saint of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:77
verses.text: What angering, or, as some have more literally rendered it, what provocation, he speaketh of, the following words sufficiently show.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:78
verses.text: "The earth opened," he saith, "and swallowed up Dathan, and covered over the congregation of Abiram" : "swallowed up" answereth to "covered over".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:79
verses.text: Both Dathan and Abiram were equally concerned in a most sacrilegious schism.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:80
verses.text: "And the fire was kindled in their company; the flame burnt up the sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:81
verses.text: This word is not in Scripture usually applied to those, who, although they live righteously, and in a praiseworthy manner, are not without sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:82
verses.text: Rather, as there is a difference between those who scorn and scorners, between men who murmur and murmurers, between men who are writing and writers, and so forth; so Scripture is wont to signify by sinners such as are very wicked, and laden with heavy loads of sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:83
verses.text: "And they made a calf in Horeb, and worshipped the graven image".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:84
verses.text: "Thus they changed their glory, in the similitude of a calf that eateth hay".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:85
verses.text: He saith not "into" the likeness, but "in" the likeness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:86
verses.text: It is such a form of speech as where he said "and they believed in His words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:87
verses.text: With great effect in truth he saith not, they changed the glory of God when they did this; as the Apostle also saith, "They changed the glory of the incorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man:" but "their glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:88
verses.text: For God was their glory, if they would abide His counsel, and hasten not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:89
verses.text: "They forgat God who saved them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:90
verses.text: How did He save them? "Who did so great things in Egypt: Wondrous works in the land of Ham, and fearful things in the Red Sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:91
verses.text: The things that are wondrous, are also fearful; for there is no wonder without a certain fear: although these might be called fearful, because they beat down their adversaries, and showed them what they ought to fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:92
verses.text: "So He said, He would have destroyed them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:93
verses.text: Since they forgot Him who saved them, the Worker of wondrous works, and made and worshipped a graven image, by this atrocious and incredible impiety they deserved death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:94
verses.text: "Had not Moses His chosen stood before Him in the breaking".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:95
