verses.text: He doth not say, that he stood in the breaking, as if to break the wrath of God, but in the way of the breaking, meaning the stroke which was to strike them: that is, had he not put himself in the way for them, saying, "Yet now, if Thou wilt forgive their sin;—and if not, blot me, I pray Thee, out of Thy book".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:96
verses.text: Where it is proved how greatly the intercession of the saints in behalf of others prevaileth with God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:97
verses.text: For Moses, fearless in the justice of God, which could not blot him out, implored mercy, that He would not blot out those whom He justly might.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:98
verses.text: Thus he "stood before Him in the breaking, to turn away His wrathful indignation, lest He should destroy them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:99
verses.text: "Yea, they thought scorn of that pleasant land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:100
verses.text: But had they seen it? How then could they scorn that which they had not seen, except as the following words explain, "and believed not in His words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:101
verses.text: Indeed, unless that land which was styled the land that flowed with milk and honey, signified something great, through which, as by a visible token, He was leading those who understood His wondrous works to invisible grace and the kingdom of heaven, they could not be blamed for scorning that land, whose temporal kingdom we also ought to esteem as nothing, that we may love that Jerusalem which is free, the mother of us all, which is in heaven, and truly to be desired.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:102
verses.text: But rather unbelief is here reproved, since they gave no credence to the words of God, who was leading them to great things through small things, and hastening to bless themselves with temporal things, which they carnally savoured of, they "abided not His counsel," as is said above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:103
verses.text: "But murmured in their tents, and hearkened not unto the voice of the Lord" ; who strongly forbade them to murmur.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:104
verses.text: "Then lift He up His hand against them, to overthrow them in the wilderness" ; "to cast out their seed among the nations: and to scatter them in the lands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:105
verses.text: "They were initiated also unto Baalpeor;" that is, were consecrated to the Gentile idol; "and ate the offerings of the dead".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:106
verses.text: "Thus they provoked Him to anger with their own inventions; and destruction was multiplied among them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:107
verses.text: As if He had deferred the lifting up of His hand which was to cast them down in the desert, and to cast out their seed among the nations, and to scatter them in the lands; as the Apostle saith: "And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:108
verses.text: "'Destruction,' therefore, 'was multiplied among them,' when they were heavily punished for their heavy sins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:109
verses.text: "Then stood up Phineas, and appeased Him, and the shaking ceased".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:110
verses.text: He hath related the whole briefly, because he is not here teaching the ignorant, but reminding those who know the history.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:111
verses.text: The word "shaking" here is the same as "breaking" before.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:112
verses.text: For it is one word in the Greek.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:113
verses.text: Lastly, so great was their wickedness, in being consecrated to the idol, and eating the sacrifices of the dead (that is, because the Gentiles sacrificed to dead men as to God), that God would not be otherwise appeased than as Phineas the Priest appeased Him, when he slew a man and a woman together whom he found in adultery If he had done this from hatred towards them, and not from love, while zeal for the house of God devoured him, it would not have been counted unto him for righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:114
verses.text: Christ our Lord indeed, when the New Testament was revealed, chose a milder discipline; but the threat of hell is more severe, and this we do not read of in those threatenings held out by God in His temporal government.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:115
verses.text: "And that was counted unto him for righteousness among all posterities for evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:116
verses.text: God counted this unto His Priest for righteousness, not only as long as posterity shall exist, but "for evermore;" for He who knoweth the heart, knoweth how to weigh with how much love for the people that deed was done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:117
verses.text: "And they angered Him at the waters of strife: so that Moses was vexed for their sakes" ; "because they provoked his spirit, so that he spake doubtfully with his lips".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:118
verses.text: What is spake doubtfully? As if God, who had done so great wonders before, could not cause water to flow from a rock.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:119
verses.text: For he touched the rock with his rod with doubt, and thus distinguished this miracle from the rest, in which he had not doubted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:120
verses.text: He thus offended, thus deserved to hear that he should die, without entering into the land of promise For being disturbed by the murmurs of an unbelieving people, he held not fast that confidence which he ought to have held.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:121
verses.text: Nevertheless, God giveth unto him, as unto His chosen, a good testimony even after his death, so that we may see that this wavering of faith was punished with this penalty only, that he was not allowed to enter that land, whither he was leading the people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:122
verses.text: But they of whose iniquities this Psalm speaketh, when they had entered into that temporal land of promise, "destroyed not the heathen, which the Lord commanded them" ; "but were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:123
verses.text: "Insomuch that they worshipped their idols, which became to them an offence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:124
verses.text: Their not destroying them, but mingling with them, became to them an offence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:125
verses.text: "Yea, they offered their sons and their daughters unto devils" ; "and shed innocent blood, even the blood of their sons and of their daughters, whom they offered unto the idols of Canaan".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:126
verses.text: That history doth not relate tha t they offered their sons and daughters to devils and idols; but neither can that Psalm lie, nor the Prophets, who assert this in many passages of their rebukes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:127
verses.text: But the literature of the Gentiles is not silent respecting this custom of theirs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:128
verses.text: But what is it that followeth? "And the land was slain with bloods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:129
verses.text: We might suppose that this was a mistake of the writer, and that he had written interfecta for infecta, were it not for the goodness of God, who hath willed His Scriptures to be written in many languages; were it not that we see it written as in the text in many Greek  copies which we have inspected; "the land was slain with bloods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:130
verses.text: What meaneth then, "the land was slain," unless this be referred to the men who dwelt in the land, by a metaphorical expression.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:131
verses.text: For they themselves were slaying their own souls when they offered up their sons, and when they shed the blood of infants who were far from consent to this crime: whence it is said, "They shed innocent blood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:132
verses.text: "The land" therefore "was slain with bloods, and defiled by their works" , since they themselves were slain in soul, and defiled by their works; "and they went a whoring after their own inventions".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:133
verses.text: By inventions are meant what the Greeks call ἐπιτηδεύματα: for this word doth occur in the Greek copies both in this and a former passage, where it is said, "They provoked Him to anger with their own inventions;" "inventions" in both instances signifying what they had initiated others in.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:134
verses.text: Let no man therefore suppose inventions to mean what they had of themselves instituted, without any example before them to imitate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:135
verses.text: Whence other translators in the Latin tongue have preferred pursuits, affections, imitations, pleasures, to inventions: and the very same who here write inventions, have elsewhere written pursuits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:136
verses.text: I chose to mention this, lest the word inventions, applied to what they had not invented, but imitated from others, might raise a difficulty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:137
verses.text: "Therefore was the wrath of the Lord kindled against His own people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:138
verses.text: Our translators have been unwilling to use the word anger, for the Greek θυμὸς; though some have used it; while others translate by "indignation" or "mind".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:139
verses.text: Whichever of these terms be adopted, passion doth not affect God; but the power of punishing hath assumed this name metaphorically from custom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:140
verses.text: "Insomuch that He abhorred His own inheritance; and He gave them over into the hand of the heathen: and they that hated them were lords over them" : "and their enemies oppressed them, and they were brought low under their hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:141
verses.text: Since he hath called them the inheritance of God, it is clear that He abhorred them, and gave them over into their enemies' hands, not in order to their perdition, but for their discipline.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:142
verses.text: Lastly, he saith, "Many a time did He deliver them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:143
verses.text: "But they provoked Him with their own counsels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:144
verses.text: This is what he said above, "They did not abide His counsel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:145
verses.text: Now a man's counsel is pernicious to himself, when he seeketh those things which are his own only, not those which are God's In whose inheritance, which inheritance He Himself is to us, when He deigneth His presence for our enjoyment, being with the Saints, we shall suffer no straitening from the society, by our love of anything as our own possession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:146
verses.text: For that most glorious city, when it hath gained the promised inheritance, in which none shall die, none shall be born, will not contain citizens who shall individually rejoice in their own, for "God shall be all in all".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:147
verses.text: And whoever in this pilgrimage faithfully and earnestly doth long for this society, doth accustom himself to prefer common to private interests, by seeking not his own things, but Jesus Christ's: lest, by being wise and vigilant in his own affairs, he provoke God with his own counsel; but, hoping for what he seeth not, let him not hasten to be blessed with things visible; and, patiently waiting for that everlasting happiness which he seeth not, follow His counsel in His promises, whose aid he prayeth for in his prayers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:148
verses.text: Thus he will also become humble in his confessions; so as not to be like those, of whom it is said, "They were brought down in their wickedness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:149
verses.text: Nevertheless, God, full of mercy, forsook them not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:150
verses.text: "And He saw when they were in adversity, when He heard their complaint".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:151
verses.text: "And He thought upon His covenant, and repented, according to the multitude of His mercies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:152
verses.text: He saith, "He repented," because He changed that wherewith He seemed about to destroy them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:153
verses.text: With God indeed all things are arranged and fixed; and when He seemeth to act upon sudden motive, He doth nothing but what He foreknew that He should do from eternity; but in the temporal changes of creation, which He ruleth wonderfully, He, without any temporal change in Himself, is said to do by a sudden act of will what in the ordained causes of events He hath arranged in the unchangeableness of His most secret counsel, according to which He doth everything according to defined seasons, doing the present, and having already done the future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:154
verses.text: And who is capable of comprehending these things? Let us therefore hear the Scripture, speaking high things humbly, giving food for the nourishment of children, and proposing subjects for the research of the older: that everlasting covenant "which He made with Abraham," not the old which is abolished, but the new which is hidden even in the old.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:155
verses.text: "And pitied them," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:156
verses.text: He did that which He had covenanted, but He had foreknown that He would yield this to them when they prayed in their adversity; since even their very prayer, when it was not uttered, but was still to be uttered, undoubtedly was known unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:157
verses.text: So "He gave them unto compassions, in the sight of all that had taken them captive".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:158
verses.text: That they might not be vessels of wrath, but vessels of mercy The compassions unto which He gave them are named in the plural for this reason, I imagine, because each one hath a gift of his own from God, one in one way, another in another Come then, whosoever readest this, and dost recognise the grace of God, by which we are redeemed unto eternal life through our Lord Jesus Christ, by reading in the apostolical writings, and by searching in the Prophets, and seest the Old Testament revealed in the New, the New veiled in the Old; remember the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, where, when He driveth him out of the hearts of the faithful, He saith, "Now is the prince of this world cast out:"  and again of the Apostle, when he saith, "Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of His dear Son".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:159
verses.text: Meditate on these and such like things, examine also the Old Testament, and see what is sung in that Psalm, the title of which is, When the temple was being built after the captivity: for there it is said, "Sing unto the Lord a new song".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:160
verses.text: And, that thou mayest not think it doth refer to the Jewish people only, he saith, "Sing unto the Lord, all the whole earth: sing unto the Lord, and praise His Name: declare," or rather, "give the good news of," or, to transfer the very word used in the Greek, "evangelize day from day, His salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:161
verses.text: Here the Gospel (Evangelium) is mentioned, in which is announced the Day that came from Day, our Lord Christ, the Light from Light, the Son from the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:162
verses.text: This also is the meaning of His salvation: for Christ is the Salvation of God, as we have shown above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:163
verses.text: "Deliver us, O Lord our God, and gather us from among the nations (other copies read, "from the heathen"); that we may give thanks unto Thy holy Name, and make our boast of Thy praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:164
verses.text: Then he hath briefly added this very praise, "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting, and world without end" : by which we understand from everlasting to everlasting; because He shall be praised without end by those of whom it is said, "Blessed are they that dwell in Thy house: they will be alway praising Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:165
verses.text: This is the perfection of the Body of Christ on the third day, when the devils had been cast out, and cures perfected, even unto the immortality of the body itself, the everlasting reign of those who perfectly praise Him, because they perfectly love Him; and perfectly love Him, because they behold Him face to face.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:166
verses.text: For then shall be completed the prayer at the commencement of this Psalm: "Remember us, O Lord, according to the favour that Thou bearest unto Thy people," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:167
verses.text: For from the Gentiles He doth not gather only the lost sheep of the house of Israel, but also those which do not belong to that fold; so that there is one flock, as is said, and one Shepherd.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:168
verses.text: But when the Jews suppose that that prophecy belongeth to their visible kingdom, because they know not how to rejoice in the hope of good things unseen, they are about to rush into the snares of him, of whom the Lord saith, "I am come in My Father's Name, and ye receive Me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:169
verses.text: Of whom the Apostle Paul saith: "that Man of Sin shall be revealed, the son of perdition," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:170
verses.text: And a little after he saith, "Then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the Spirit of His mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of His coming," etcThrough that Apostate, through him who exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped, it seemeth to me, that the carnal people of Israel will suppose that prophecy to be fulfilled, where it is said, "Deliver us, O Lord, and gather us from among the heathen;" that under His guidance, before the eyes of their visible enemies, who had visibly taken them captive, they are to have visible glory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:171
verses.text: Thus they will believe a lie, because they have not received the love of truth, that they might love not carnal, but spiritual blessings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:172
verses.text: For Christ had other sheep that were not of this fold: but the devil and his angels had taken captive all those sheep, both among the Israelites and the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:173
verses.text: The power, therefore, of the devil having been cast out of them, in the sight of the evil spirits who had taken them captive, their cry in this prophecy is, that they may be saved and perfected for evermore: "Deliver us, O Lord our God, and gather us from among the heathen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 106:174
verses.text: Not, as the Jews imagine it, fulfilled through Antichrist, but through our Lord Christ coming in the name of His Father, "Day from day, His salvation;" of whom it is here said, "O visit us in Thy salvation! And let all the people say," the predestined people of the circumcision and of the uncircumcision, a holy race, an adopted people, "So be it! So be it!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:1
verses.text: Psalm CVII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:2
verses.text: This Psalm commendeth unto us the mercies of God, proved in ourselves, and is therefore the sweeter to the experienced.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:3
verses.text: And it is a wonder if it can be pleasing to any one, except to him who has learned in his own case, what he hears in this Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:4
verses.text: Yet was it written not for any one or two, but for the people of God, and set forth that it might know itself therein as in a mirror.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:5
verses.text: Its title needeth not now to be treated, for it is Halleluia, and again Halleluia.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:6
verses.text: Which we have a custom of singing at a certain time in our solemnities, after an old tradition of the Church: nor is it without a sacred meaning that we sing it on particular days Halleluia we sing indeed on certain days, but every day we think it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:7
verses.text: For if in this word is signified the praise of God, though not in the mouth of the flesh, yet surely in the mouth of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:8
verses.text: "His praise shall ever be in my mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:9
verses.text: But that the title hath Halleluia not once only but twice, is not peculiar to this Psalm, but the former also hath it so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:10
verses.text: And as far as appears from its text, that was sung of the people of Israel, but this is sung of the universal Church of God, spread through the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:11
verses.text: Perchance, it not unfitly hath Halleluia twice, because we cry, Abba, Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:12
verses.text: Since Abba is nothing else but Father, yet not without meaning the Apostle said, "in whom we cry, Abba, Father;"  but because one wall indeed coming to the Corner Stone crieth Abba, but the other, from the other side crieth Father; viz.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:13
verses.text: , in that Corner Stone, "who is our Peace, who hath made both one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:14
verses.text: "Confess unto the Lord that He is sweet, because for aye in His mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:15
verses.text: This confess ye that He is sweet: if ye have tasted, confess.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:16
verses.text: But he cannot confess, who hath not chosen to taste, for whence shall he say that that is sweet, which he knoweth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:17
verses.text: But ye if ye have tasted how sweet the Lord is, "Confess ye to the Lord that He is sweet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:18
verses.text: If ye have tasted with eagerness, break forth with confession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:19
verses.text: "For aye is His mercy," that is, for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:20
verses.text: For here "for aye," is so put, since also in some other places of Scripture, for aye, that is, what in Greek is called εἰς αἰῶνα, is understood for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:21
verses.text: For His mercy is not for a time, so as not to be for ever, since for this purpose His present mercy is over men, that they may live with the Angels for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:22
verses.text: "Let them say who are redeemed of the Lord, whom He hath redeemed from the hand of their enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:23
verses.text: Redeemed indeed it seems was also the people of Israel from the land of Egypt, from the hand of slavery, from fruitless labours, from miry works; yet let us see whether those who say these things, are they who were freed by the Lord from Egypt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:24
verses.text: It is not so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:25
verses.text: But who are they? "Those whom He redeemed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:26
verses.text: Still one might take it also of them, as redeemed from the hand of their enemi es, that is, of the Egyptians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:27
verses.text: Let them be expressed exactly who they are, for whom this Psalm would be sung.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:28
verses.text: "He gathered them from the lands;" these might still be the lands of Egypt, for there are many lands even in one province.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:29
verses.text: Let him speak openly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:30
verses.text: "From the east and the west, from the north and the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:31
verses.text: Now then we understand these redeemed, in the whole circle of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:32
verses.text: This people of God, freed from a great and broad Egypt, is led, as through the Red Sea, that in Baptism it may make an end of its enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:33
verses.text: For by the sacrament as it were of the Red Sea, that is by Baptism consecrated with the Blood of Christ, the pursuing Egyptians, the sins, are washed away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:34
verses.text: "But all these things happened to them in a figure, and were written for our admonition, on whom the ends of the ages have come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:35
verses.text: "They wandered in the wilderness, in a dry place, they found not the way of a city to dwell in".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:36
verses.text: We have heard a wretched wandering; what of want? "Hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted in them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:37
verses.text: But wherefore did it faint? for what good? For God is not cruel, but He maketh Himself known, in that it is expedient for us, that He be entreated by us fainting, and that aiding us He be loved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:38
verses.text: And therefore after this wandering, and hunger, and thirst, "And they cried unto the Lord in their trouble, and He delivered them out of their distress".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:39
verses.text: And what did He for them, as they were wandering? "And He led them in the right way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:40
verses.text: They found not the way of a city to dwell in, with hunger and thirst they were vexed and faint, "and He led them into the right way, that they might go into a city to dwell in".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:41
verses.text: How He helped their hunger and thirst, He saith not, but even this expect ye: "Let them confess unto the Lord His mercies, and His wonders towards the children of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:42
verses.text: Tell them, ye that are experienced, to the inexperienced; ye that are already in the way, already directed towards finding the city, already at last free from hunger and thirst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:43
verses.text: "Because He hath satisfied the empty soul, and filled the hungry soul with good things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:44
verses.text: "Them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death, fast bound in beggary and iron".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:45
verses.text: Whence this, but that thou wast attributing things to thyself? that thou wast not owning the grace of God? that thou wast rejecting the counsel of God concerning thee? For see what He addeth: "Because they rebelled against the words of the Lord through pride" , not knowing the righteousness of God, and wishing to establish their own, "and they were bitter against the counsel of the Most High".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:46
verses.text: "And their heart was brought low in labour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:47
verses.text: And now fight against lust; if God cease to aid thou mayest strive, thou canst not conquer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:48
verses.text: And when thou shalt be pressed by thine evil, thy heart will be brought low in labour, so that now with humbled heart thou mayest learn to cry out, "O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?"Freed, thou wilt confess the mercies of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:49
verses.text: "And they cried unto the Lord when they were troubled, and He delivered them out of their distresses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:50
verses.text: They were freed from the second temptation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:51
verses.text: There remains that of weariness and loathing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:52
verses.text: But first see what He did for them when freed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:53
verses.text: "And He led them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and brake their bonds asunder".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:54
verses.text: "Let them confess to the Lord His mercies, and His wonders to the children of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:55
verses.text: Wherefore? what difficulties hath He overcome? "Because He brake the gates of brass, and snapped the bars of iron".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:56
verses.text: "He took them up from the way of their iniquity, for because of their unrighteousnesses they were brought low".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:57
verses.text: Because they gave honour to themselves, not to God, because they were establishing their own righteousness, not knowing the righteousness of God, they were brought low.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:58
verses.text: They found that they were helpless without His aid, who were presuming on their own strength alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:59
verses.text: "Their soul abhorred all manner of meat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:60
verses.text: Now they suffer satiety.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:61
verses.text: They are sick of satiety.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:62
verses.text: They are in danger from satiety.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:63
verses.text: Unless perchance thou thinkest they could be killed with famine, but cannot with satiety.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:64
verses.text: See what followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:65
verses.text: When he had said, "Their soul abhorred all manner of meat," lest thou shouldest think them, as it were, safe of their fulness, and not rather see that they would die of satiety: "And they came near," he saith, "even unto the gates of death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:66
verses.text: What then remaineth? That even when the word of God delighteth thee, thou account it not to thyself; nor for this be puffed up with any sort of arrogance, and having an appetite for food, proudly spurn at those who are in danger from satiety.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:67
verses.text: "And they cried out unto the Lord when they were in trouble, and He delivered them out of their distresses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:68
verses.text: And because it was a sickness not to be pleased, "He sent His Word, and healed them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:69
verses.text: See what evil there is in satiety; see whence He delivers, to whom he crieth that loathes his food.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:70
verses.text: "He sent His Word, and healed them, and snatched them," from whence? not from wandering, not from hunger, not from the difficulty of overcoming sins, but "from their corruption".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:71
verses.text: It is a sort of corruption of the mind to loathe what is sweet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:72
verses.text: Therefore also of this benefit, as of the others before, "Let them confess to the Lord His mercies, and His wonders unto the sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:73
verses.text: "And sacrifice the sacrifice of praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:74
verses.text: For now that He may be praised, the Lord is sweet, "and let them tell out His works with gladness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:75
verses.text: Not with weariness, not with sadness, not with anxiety, not with loathing, but "with gladness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:76
verses.text: "They who go down on the sea in ships, doing their business on the mighty waters" ; that is, amongst many peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:77
verses.text: For that waters are often put for peoples, the Apocalypse of John is witness, when on John's asking what those waters were, it was answered him, they are peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:78
verses.text: They then who do their business on mighty waters, "they have seen the works of the Lord, and His wonders in the deep".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:79
verses.text: For what is deeper than human hearts? hence often break forth winds; storms of sedition, and dissensions, disturb the ship.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:80
verses.text: And what is done in them? God, willing that both they who steer, and they who are conveyed, should cry unto Him, "He spake, and the breath of the storm stood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:81
verses.text: What is, stood? Abode, continued, still disturbeth, long tosseth; rageth, and passeth not away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:82
verses.text: "For He spake, and the breath of the storm stood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:83
verses.text: And what did that breath of the storm? "They go up even to the heavens," in daring; "They go down even into the deeps" , in fearing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:84
verses.text: "Their soul wasted in miseries".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:85
verses.text: "They were disturbed, and moved like a drunken man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:86
verses.text: They who sit at the helm, and they who faithfully love the ship, feel what I say.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:87
verses.text: Certainly, when they speak, when they read, when they interpret, they appear wise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:88
verses.text: Woe for the storm! "and all their wisdom," he saith, "was swallowed up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:89
verses.text: Sometimes all human counsels fail; whichever way one turns himself, the waves roar, the storm rageth, the arms are powerless: where the prow may strike, to what wave the side may be exposed, whither the stricken ship may be allowed to drift, from what rocks she must be kept back lest she be lost, is impossible for her pilots to see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:90
verses.text: And what is left but that which follows? "And they cried out unto the Lord when they were troubled, and He delivered them from their distresses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:91
verses.text: "And He commanded the storm, and it stood unto clear air" , "and the waves of it were still".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:92
verses.text: Hear on this point the voice of a steersman, one that was in peril, was brought low, was freed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:93
verses.text: "I would not," he saith, "have you ignorant, brethren, of our distress, which befell us in Asia, that "we were pressed above strength, and above measure" (I see all his "wisdom swallowed up"), "so that we were weary," he saith, "even of life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:94
verses.text: "And they were glad, because they were still, and He brought them into the haven of their desire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:95
verses.text: "Let His mercies confess unto the Lord, and His wonders towards the sons of men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:96
verses.text: Everywhere, without exception, let not our merits, not our strength, not our wisdom, "confess unto the Lord," but, "His mercies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:97
verses.text: Let Him be loved in every deliverance of ours, who has been invoked in every distress.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:98
verses.text: "And let them exalt Him in the assembly of the people, and praise Him in the seat of the elders".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:99
verses.text: Let them exalt, let them praise, peoples and elders, merchants and pilots.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:100
verses.text: For what hath He done in this assembly? What hath He established? Whence hath He rescued it? What hath He granted it? Even as He resisted the proud, and gave grace to the humble: the proud, that is, the first people of the Jews, arrogant, and extolling itself on its descent from Abraham, and because to that nation "were entrusted the oracles of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:101
verses.text: These things did not avail them unto soundness, but unto pride of heart, rather to swelling than to greatness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:102
verses.text: What then did God, resisting the proud, but giving grace to the humble; cutting off the natural branches for their pride; grafting in the wild olive for its humility?  "He made the rivers a wilderness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:103
verses.text: Waters did run there, prophecies were in course.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:104
verses.text: Seek now a prophet among the Jews; thou findest none.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:105
verses.text: For "He made the outgoings of waters to be thirst".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:106
verses.text: Let them say, "Now there is no prophet more, and He will not know us any more".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:107
verses.text: "A fruitful land to be saltpools".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:108
verses.text: Thou seekest there the faith of Christ, thou findest not: thou seekest a prophet, thou findest not: thou seekest a sacrifice, thou findest not: thou seekest a temple, thou findest none.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:109
verses.text: Wherefore this? "From the wickedness of them that dwell therein".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:110
verses.text: Behold how He resisteth the proud: hear how He giveth grace to the humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:111
verses.text: "He made the wilderness to be a standing water, and the dry ground to be outgoings of waters".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:112
verses.text: "And He caused the hungry to dwell there".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:113
verses.text: Because to Him it was said, "Thou art a Priest for ever, after the order of Melchizedec".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:114
verses.text: For thou seekest a sacrifice among the Jews; thou hast none after the order of Aaron.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:115
verses.text: Thou seekest it after the order of Melchizedec; thou findest it not among them, but through the whole world it is celebrated in the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:116
verses.text: "From the rising of the sun to the setting thereof the name of the Lord is praised".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:117
verses.text: "And they sowed fields, and planted vineyards, and gat fruit of corn" : at which that workman rejoiceth, who saith, "Not because I desire a gift, but I seek fruit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:118
verses.text: "And He blessed them, and they were multiplied exceedingly, and their cattle were not diminished".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:119
verses.text: This standeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:120
verses.text: For "the foundation of God standeth sure; because the Lord knoweth them that are His".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:121
verses.text: They are called "beasts of burden," and "cattle," that walk simply in the Church, yet are useful; not much learned, but full of faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:122
verses.text: Therefore, whether spiritual or carnal, "He blessed them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:123
verses.text: "And they became few, and were vexed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:124
verses.text: Whence this? From athwart? Nay, from within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:125
verses.text: For that they should "become few," "They went out from us, but they were not of us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:126
verses.text: But therefore he speaketh as of these, of whom he spake before, that they may be discerned with understanding; because he speaketh as if of the same, because of the sacraments they have in common.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:127
verses.text: For they belong to the people of God, though not by the virtue, yet surely by the appearance of piety: for concerning them we have heard the Apostle, "In the last times there shall come grievous times, for there shall be men lovers of themselves".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:128
verses.text: The first evil is, "lovers of themselves;" that is, as being pleased with themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:129
verses.text: Would that they were not pleasing to themselves, and were pleasing to God: would that they would cry out in their difficulties, and be freed from their distresses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:130
verses.text: But while they presumed greatly on themselves, "they were made few".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:131
verses.text: It is manifest, brethren: all who separate themselves from unity become few.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:132
verses.text: For they are many; but in unity, while they are not parted from unity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:133
verses.text: For when the multitude of unity hath begun no more to belong to them, in heresy and schism, they are few.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:134
verses.text: "And they were vexed, from distress of miseries and grief".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:135
verses.text: "Contempt was poured on princes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:136
verses.text: For they were rejected by the Church of God, and the more because they wished to be princes, therefore they were despised, and became salt that had lost its savour, cast out abroad, so that it is trodden under foot of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:137
verses.text: "And He led them astray in the pathless place, and not in a way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:138
verses.text: Those above in the way, those directed to a city, and finally led thither, not led astray; but these, where there was no way, led astray.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:139
verses.text: What is, "Led them astray"? God "gave them up to their own hearts' lusts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:140
verses.text: For "led astray" means this, gave them up to themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:141
verses.text: For if thou enquire closely, it is they that lead themselves astray.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:142
verses.text: "And He helped the poor out of beggary".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:143
verses.text: What meaneth this, brethren? Princes are despised, and the poor helped.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:144
verses.text: The proud are cast aside, and the humble provided for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:145
verses.text: "And made him households like sheep".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:146
verses.text: Thou understandest one poor man and one beggar of him concerning whom he said, "He hath helped the poor out of misery:" this poor man is now many households, this poor man is many nations; many Churches are one Church, one nation, one household, one sheep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:147
verses.text: These are great mysteries, great types, how profound, how full of hidden meanings; how sweetly discovered, since long hidden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:148
verses.text: Therefore, "the righteous will consider this, and rejoice: and the mouth of all wickedness shall be stopped".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:149
verses.text: That wickedness that doth prate against unity, and compelleth truth to be made manifest, shall be convicted, and have its mouth stopped.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:150
verses.text: "Who is wise? and he will consider these things; and will understand the mercies of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:151
verses.text: Not his own deservings, not his own strength, not his own power; but "the mercies of the Lord;" who, when he was wandering and in want, led him back to the path, and fed him; who, when he was struggling against the difficulties of his sins, and bound down with the fetters of habit, released and freed him; who, when he loathed the Word of God, and was almost dying with a kind of weariness, restored him by sending him the medicine of His Word; who, when he was endangered among the risks of shipwreck and storm, stilled the sea, and brought him into port; who, finally, placed him in that people, where He giveth grace to the humble; not in that where he resisteth the proud; and hath made him His own, that remaining within he may be multiplied, not that going out he may be minished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:152
verses.text: The righteous see this, and rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 107:153
verses.text: "The mouth," therefore, "of all wickedness shall be stopped".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:1
verses.text: Psalm CVIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:2
verses.text: I have not thought that the CVIIIth Psalm required an exposition; since I have already  expounded it in the LVIIth Psalm, and in the LXth, of the last divisions of which this Psalm consisteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:3
verses.text: For the last part of the LVIIth is the first of this, as far as the verse, "Thy glory is above all the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:4
verses.text: Henceforth to the end, is the last part of the LXth: as the last part of the CXXXVth is the same as that of the CXVth, from the verse, "The images of the heathen are but gold and silver:" as the XIVth and LIIId, with a few alterations in the middle, have everything the same from the beginning to the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:5
verses.text: Whatever slight differences therefore occur in this CVIIIth Psalm, compared with those two, of parts of which it is composed, are easy to understand; just as we find in the LVIIth, "I will sing and give praise; awake, O my glory:" here," I will sing and give praise, with my glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:6
verses.text: Awake, is said there, that he may sing and give praise therewith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:7
verses.text: Also, there, "Thy mercy is great" (or, as some translate, "is lifted up") "unto the heavens;" but here, "Thy mercy is great above the heavens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:8
verses.text: For it is great unto the heavens, that it may be great in the heavens; and this is what he wished to express by "above the heavens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:9
verses.text: Also in the LXth, "I will rejoice, I will divide Shechem:" here "I will be exalted, and will divide Shechem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:10
verses.text: Where is shown what is signified in the division of Shechem, which it was prophesied should happen after the Lord's exaltation, and that this joy doth refer to that exaltation; so that He rejoiceth, because He is exalted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:11
verses.text: Whence he elsewhere saith, "Thou hast turned my heaviness into joy; Thou hast put off my sackcloth and girded me with gladness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:12
verses.text: Also there "Ephraim, the strength of my head:" but here, "Ephraim the taking up of my head".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:13
verses.text: But strength cometh from taking up, that is, He maketh men strong by taking up, causing fruit in us; for the interpretation of Ephraim is, bearing fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:14
verses.text: But "taking up" may be understood of us, when we take up Christ; or of Christ, when He, who is Head of the Church, taketh us up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:15
verses.text: And the words, "them that trouble us," in the former Psalm, are the same with "our enemies," in this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:16
verses.text: We are taught by this Psalm, that those titles which seem to refer to history are most rightly unders tood prophetically, according to the object of the composition of the Psalms.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:17
verses.text: And yet this Psalm is composed of the latter portions of two, whose titles are different.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:18
verses.text: Where it is signified that each concur in a common object, not in the surface of the history, but in the depth of pr ophecy, the objects of both being united in this one, the title of which is, "A Song or Psalm of David:" resembling neither of the former titles, otherwise than in the word David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 108:19
verses.text: Since, "in many places, and in diverse manners," as the Epistle to the Hebrews saith, "God spoke in former times to the fathers through the Prophets;" yet He spoke of Him whom He sent afterwards, that the words of the Prophets might be fulfilled: for "all the promises of God in Him are yea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:1
verses.text: Psalm CIX.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:2
verses.text: Every one who faithfully readeth the Acts of the Apostles, acknowledgeth that this Psalm containeth a prophecy of Christ; for it evidently appeareth that what is here written, "let his days be few, and let another take his office," is prophesied of Judas, the betrayer of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:3
verses.text: For as some things are said which seem peculiarly to apply to the Apostle Peter, and yet are not clear in their meaning, unless when referred to the Church, whom he is acknowledged to have figuratively represented, on account of the primacy which he bore among the Disciples; as it is written, "I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven," and other passages of the like purport: so Judas doth represent those Jews who were enemies of Christ, who both then hated Christ, and now, in their line of succession, this species of wickedness continuing, hate Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:4
verses.text: Of these men, and of this people, not only may what we read more openly discovered in this Psalm be conveniently understood, but also those things which are more expressly stated concerning Judas himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:5
verses.text: The Psalm, then, beginneth thus: "O God, be not silent as to my praise; for the mouth of the ungodly, yea, the mouth of the deceitful is opened upon me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:6
verses.text: Whence it appeareth, both that the blame, which the ungodly and the deceitful is not silent of, is false, and that the praise, which God is not silent of, is true.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:7
verses.text: "For God is true, but every man a liar;" for no man is true, except him in whom God speaketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:8
verses.text: But the highest praise is that of the only-begotten Son of God, in which He is proclaimed even that which He is, the only-begotten Son of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:9
verses.text: But this did not appear, but, when His weakness appeared, lay hid, when the mouth of the ungodly and deceitful was opened upon Him; and for this reason his mouth was opened, because His virtue was concealed: and he saith, "the mouth of the deceitful was opened," because the hatred which was covered by deceit burst out into language.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:10
verses.text: "They have spoken against me with false tongues" : then chiefly when they praised him as a "good Master" with insidious adulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:11
verses.text: Whence it is elsewhere said: "and they that praised me, are sworn together against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:12
verses.text: Next, because they burst into cries, "Crucify Him, crucify Him;" he hath added, "They compassed me about also with words of hatred".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:13
verses.text: They who with a treacherous tongue spoke words seemingly of love, and not of hatred, "against me," since they did this insidiously; afterwards "compassed me about with words" not of false and deceitful love, but of open "hatred, and fought against me without a cause".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:14
verses.text: For as the pious love Christ for nought, so do the wicked hate Him for nought; for as truth is earnestly sought by the best men on its own account, without any advantage, external to itself, in view, so is wickedness sought by the worst men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:15
verses.text: Whence among secular authors it is said of a very bad man, "he was wicked and cruel for no object".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:16
verses.text: "In place," saith he, "of loving me, they detracted from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:17
verses.text: There are six different acts of this class, which may, when mentioned, very easily be borne in mind;  to return good for evil,  not to return evil for evil;  to return good for good,  to return evil for evil;  not to return good for good,  to return evil for good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:18
verses.text: The two first of these belong to the good, and the first of these two is the better; the two last belong to the wicked, and the latter of the two is the worse; the two middle to a sort of middle class of persons, but the first of these borders upon the good, the latter on the bad.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:19
verses.text: We should remark these things in the holy Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:20
verses.text: Our Lord Himself returneth good for evil, who "justifieth the ungodly;" and who, when hanging upon the Cross, said, "Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:21
verses.text: But after he had said, "in place of loving me, they detracted from me;" what doth he add? "But I gave myself unto prayer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:22
verses.text: He said not indeed what he prayed, but what can we better understand than for them themselves? For they were detracting greatly from Him whom they crucified, when they ridiculed Him as if He were a man, whom in their opinion they had conquered; from which Cross He said, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do;" so that while they in the depth of their malignity were rendering evil for good, He in the height of His goodness was rendering good for evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:23
verses.text: The divine words then teach us by our Lord's example, that when we feel others ungrateful to us, not only in that they do not repay us with good, but even return evil for good, we should pray; He indeed for others who were raging against Him, or in sorrow, or endangered in faith; but we for ourselves in the first place, that we may by the mercy and aid of God conquer our own mind, by which we are borne on to the desire of revenge, when any detraction is made from us, either in our presence or our absence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:24
verses.text: He addeth, "Thus have they rewarded me evil for good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:25
verses.text: And as if we asked, what evil? for what good? "And hatred," he saith, "for my good will".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:26
verses.text: This is the sum total of their great guilt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:27
verses.text: For how could the persecutors injure Him who died of His own free-will, and not by compulsion? But this very hatred is the greatest crime of the persecutor, although it be the willing atonement of the sufferer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:28
verses.text: And he hath sufficiently explained the sense of the above words, "In place of loving me," since they owed love not as a general duty only, but in return for His love: in that he hath here added, "for my good will".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:29
verses.text: This love He mentioneth in the Gospel, when He saith, "How often would I have gathered thy children together, and thou wouldest not!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:30
verses.text: He then beginneth to prophesy what they should receive for this very impiety; detailing their lot in such a manner, as if he wished its realization from a desire of revenge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:31
verses.text: Some not understanding this mode of predicting the future, under the appearance of wishing evil, suppose hatred to be returned for hatred, and an evil will for an evil will, since in truth it belongeth to few to distinguish, in what way the punishment of the wicked pleaseth the accuser, who longeth to satiate his enmity; and in how widely different a way it pleaseth the judge, who with a righteous mind punisheth sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:32
verses.text: For the former returneth evil for evil: but the judge when he punisheth doth not return evil for evil, since he returneth justice to the unjust; and what is just, is surely good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:33
verses.text: He therefore punisheth not from delight in another's misery, which is evil for evil: but from love of justice, which is good for evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:34
verses.text: "Set thou an ungodly man to be ruler over him; and let Satan sta nd at his right hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:35
verses.text: Though the complaint had been before concerning many, the Psalm is now speaking of one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:36
verses.text: Since therefore he is here speaking of the traitor Judas, who, according to the Scripture in the Acts of the Apostles, was to be punished with the penalty due to him, what meaneth, "set thou an ungodly man over him," save him whom in the next verse he mentioneth by name, when he saith, "and let Satan stand at his right hand"? He therefore who refused to be subject unto Christ, deserved this, that he should have the devil set over him, that is, that he should be subject unto the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:37
verses.text: For this reason also it is said of those who, preferring the pleasures of this world to God, styled the people blessed who have such and such things, "their right hand is a right hand of iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:38
verses.text: "When sentence is given upon him, let him be condemned, and let his prayer be turned into sin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:39
verses.text: For prayer is not righteous except through Christ, whom he sold in his atrocious sin: but the prayer which is not made through Christ, not only cannot blot out sin, but is itself turned into sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:40
verses.text: But it may be inquired on what occasion Judas could have so prayed, that his prayer was turned into sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:41
verses.text: I suppose that before he betrayed the Lord, while he was thinking of betraying Him; for he could no longer pray through Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:42
verses.text: For after he betrayed Him, and repented of it, if he prayed through Christ, he would ask for pardon; if he asked for pardon, he would have hope; if he had hope, he would hope for mercy; if he hoped for mercy, he would not have hanged himself in despair.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:43
verses.text: "Let his days be few".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:44
verses.text: By "his days," he meant the days of his apostleship, which were few; since before the Passion of our Lord, they were ended by his crime and death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:45
verses.text: And as if it were asked, What then shall become of that most sacred number twelve, within which our Lord willed, not without a meaning, to limit His twelve first Apostles? he at once addeth, "and let another take his office".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:46
verses.text: As much as to say, let both himself be punished according to his desert, and let his number be filled up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:47
verses.text: "Let his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:48
verses.text: After his death, both his children were fatherless, and his wife a widow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:49
verses.text: "Let his children be vagabonds, and be carried away, and beg their bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:50
verses.text: By "vagabonds" he meaneth, uncertain whither to go, destitute of all help.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:51
verses.text: "Let them be driven from their habitations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:52
verses.text: He here explaineth what he had said above, "Let them be carried away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:53
verses.text: How all this happened to his wife and children, the following verses explain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:54
verses.text: "Let the extortioner search out all his substance, and let the strangers spoil his labour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:55
verses.text: "Let there be no man to help him" : that is, to guard his posterity; wherefore followeth, "nor to have compassion on his fatherless children".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:56
verses.text: But as even orphans may, without one to help them, and without a guardian, nevertheless increase amid trouble and want, and preserve their race by descent; he next saith, "Let his posterity be destroyed; and in the next generation let his name be clean put out" : that is, let what hath been generated by him generate no more, and quickly pass away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:57
verses.text: But what is it that he next addeth? "Let the wickedness of his fathers be had in remembrance in the sight of the Lord, and let not the sin of his mother be done away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:58
verses.text: Is it to be understood, that even the sins of his fathers shall be visited upon him? For upon him they are not visited, who hath been changed in Christ, and hath ceased to be the child of the wicked, by not having imitated their conduct.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:59
verses.text: And to these words, "I will visit the sins of the fathers upon the children," is added, "who hate Me;" that is, hate Me as their fathers hated Me: so that as the effect of imitating the good is that even their own sins are blotted out, so the imitation of the wicked causeth men to suffer not their own deservings only, but those also of those whom they have imitated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:60
verses.text: "Let them alway be against the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:61
verses.text: "Against the Lord," meaneth in the Lord's sight: for other translators have rendered this line, "let them be always in the sight of the Lord;" while others have rendered it, "let them be before the Lord alway;" as it is elsewhere said, "Thou hast set our misdeeds in Thy sight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:62
verses.text: By "alway," he meaneth that this great crime should be without pardon, both here, and in a future life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:63
verses.text: "Let the memorial of them perish from off the earth:" that is, of his father and of his mother.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:64
verses.text: By memorial of them, he meaneth, that which is preserved by successive generations: this he prophesied should perish from the earth, because both Judas himself, and his sons, who were the memorial of his father and mother, without any succeeding offspring, as it is said above, were consumed in the short space of one generation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:65
verses.text: "And that, because he remembered not to act mercifully" ; either Judas, or the people itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:66
verses.text: But "remembered not" is better understood of the people: for if they slew Christ, they might well remember the deed in penitence, and act mercifully towards His members, whom they most perseveringly persecuted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:67
verses.text: For this reason he saith, "but persecuted the poor man and the beggar".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:68
verses.text: It may indeed be understood of Judas; for the Lord did not disdain to become poor, when He was rich, that we might be enriched by His poverty But how shall I understand the word "beggar," save perhaps because He said to the Samaritan woman, "Give me to drink," and on the Cross He said, "I thirst".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:69
verses.text: But as to what followeth, I do not see how it can be understood of our Head Himself, that is, the Saviour of His own body, whom Judas persecuted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:70
verses.text: For after saying, "He persecuted the poor man and the beggar:" he addeth, "and to slay," that is, "that he might slay Him," for some have so rendered it, "Him that was pricked at the heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:71
verses.text: This expression is not commonly used except of the stings of past sins in the sorrows of penitence; as it is said of those who, when they had heard the Apostles after our Lord's ascension, were "pricked in heart," even they who had slain the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:72
verses.text: The Psalm then continueth: "His delight was in cursing, and it shall happen to him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:73
verses.text: Although Judas loved cursing, both in stealing from the money bag, and selling and betraying the Lord: nevertheless, that people more openly loved cursing, when they said, "His blood be on us, and on our children".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:74
verses.text: "He loved not blessing, therefore it shall be far from him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:75
verses.text: Such was Judas indeed, since he loved not Christ, in whom is everlasting blessing; but the Jewish people still more decidedly refused blessing, unto whom he who had been enlightened by the Lord said, "Will ye also be His disciples?" "He clothed himself with cursing, like as with a raiment:" either Judas, or that people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:76
verses.text: "And it came into his bowels like water".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:77
verses.text: Both without, then, and within; without, like a garment; within, like water: since he hath come before the judgment-seat of Him "who hath power to destroy both body and soul in hell;" the body without, the soul within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:78
verses.text: "And like oil into his bones".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:79
verses.text: He showeth that he worketh evil with delight, and storeth up cursing for himself, that is, everlasting punishment; for blessing is eternal life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:80
verses.text: For at present evil deeds are his delight, flowing like water into his bowels, like oil into his bones; but it is styled cursing, because God hath appointed torments for such men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:81
verses.text: "Let it be unto him as the cloak which covereth him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:82
verses.text: Since he hath before spoken of the cloak, why doth he repeat it? When he said, "He clothed himself with cursing as with a raiment;" doth the raiment with which he is "covered" differ from that with which he is "clothed"? For every man is clothed with his tunic, covered with his cloak; and what is this, save boasting in iniquity, even in the sight of men? "and as the girdle," he saith, "that he is alway girded withal".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:83
verses.text: Men are girded chiefly that they may be better fit for toil, that they may not be hindered by the folds of their dress.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:84
verses.text: He therefore girdeth himself with curses, who designeth an evil which he hath carefully contrived, not on a sudden impulse, and who learneth in such a manner to do evil, that he is always ready to commit it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:85
verses.text: "This is the work of them that slander me before the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:86
verses.text: He said not, "their reward," but, "their work:" for it is clear that by the clothing, covering, water, oil, and girdle, he was describing the very works by which eternal curses are procured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:87
verses.text: It is not then one Judas, but many, of whom it is said, "This is the work of them that slander me before the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:88
verses.text: Although indeed the plural number might have been put for the singular; even as, when Herod died, it was said by the Angel, "They are dead which sought the young Child's life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:89
verses.text: But who slander Christ more before the Lord, than they who slander the very words of the Lord, by declaring that it is not He whom the Law of the Lord and His Prophets announced beforehand? "And of those that speak evil against my soul:" by denying that He, when He had willed, could have arisen: though He saith, "I have power to lay down My life, and I have power to take it again".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:90
verses.text: "But work Thou with me, O Lord God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:91
verses.text: Some have thought "mercifully" should be understood, some have actually added it; but the best copies have the words thus: "But work Thou with me, O Lord God, for Thy Name's sake".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:92
verses.text: Whence a higher sense should not be passed over, supposing the Son to have thus addressed the Father, "Deal Thou with Me," since the works of the Father and of the Son are the same.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:93
verses.text: Where although we understand mercy,—for these words follow, "for sweet is Thy mercy,"—because he said not, "In me," or, "over me;" or anything of this sort: but, "work Thou with Me;" we rightly understand that the Father and Son together work mercifully towards the vessels of mercy "Work with me," may also be understood to mean, help me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:94
verses.text: We use this expression in our daily language, when we are speaking of anything which is in our favour; "It works with us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:95
verses.text: For the Father aideth the Son, as far as the Deity aideth Man, on account of His having assumed the "form of a servant," to which Man, God, and to which "Form of a servant," the Lord too is Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:96
verses.text: For in the "form of God," the Son needeth not aid, for He is equally all-powerful with the Father, on which account He also is the helper of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:97
verses.text: And because when he had said, "Work Thou with me," he added, "for Thy Name's sake," he hath commended grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:98
verses.text: For without previous deserving works, human nature was raised to such a height, that the whole in one, the Word and Flesh, that is, God and Man, was styled the Only-begotten Son of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:99
verses.text: And this was done that that which had been lost might be sought by Him who had created it, through that which had not been lost; whence the following words, "For Thy mercy is sweet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:100
verses.text: "O deliver me, for I am needy and poor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:101
verses.text: Need and poverty is that weakness, through which He was crucified "And my heart is disturbed within me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:102
verses.text: This alludeth to those words which He spoke when His Passion was drawing near, "My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:103
verses.text: "I go hence like a shadow that declineth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:104
verses.text: By this he signified death itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:105
verses.text: For as night comes of the shadow's declining, so death comes of mortal flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:106
verses.text: "And am driven away as the locusts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:107
verses.text: This I think would be more suitably understood of His members, that is, of His faithful disciples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:108
verses.text: That he might make it much plainer, he preferred writing "locusts" in the plural number: although many may be understood where the singular number is used, as in that passage, "He spake, and the locust came;"  but it would have been more obscure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:109
verses.text: His disciples, then, were driven away, that is, were put to flight by persecutors, either the multitude of whom He wished to be signified by the word locusts, or their passing from one place to another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:110
verses.text: "My knees are weak through fasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:111
verses.text: We read, that our Lord Christ underwent a fast of forty days: but had fasting so great power over Him, that His knees were weakened? Or is this more suitably understood of His members, that is, of His saints? "And my flesh is changed because of the oil;" because of spiritual grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:112
verses.text: Whence Christ was so called from the Greek word, chrisma, which signifies unction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:113
verses.text: But the flesh was changed through the oil, not for the worse, but for the better, that is, rising from the dishonour of death to the glory of immortality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:114
verses.text: His flesh was not yet changed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:115
verses.text: But whether the Holy Spirit be represented by water through the notion of ablution or irrigation, or by oil through that of exultation and the inflaming of charity; It doth not differ from Itself, because Its types are different.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:116
verses.text: For there is a great difference between the lion and the lamb, and yet Christ is represented by both.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:117
verses.text: "I became also a reproach unto them" : through the death of the Cross.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:118
verses.text: "For Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:119
verses.text: "They looked upon Me, and shaked their heads".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:120
verses.text: Because they beheld His crucifixion, without beholding His resurrection: they saw when His knees were weakened, they saw not when His flesh was changed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:121
verses.text: "Help me, O Lord my God: O save me according to Thy mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:122
verses.text: This may be referred to the whole, both to the Head and to the body: to the Head, owing to His having taken the form of a servant; to the body, on account of the servants themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:123
verses.text: For He might even in them have said unto God, "Help Me:" and, "O save Me:" as in them He said unto Paul, "Why persecutest thou Me"?  The following words, "according to Thy mercy," describe grace given gratuitously, not according to the merit of works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:124
verses.text: "And let them know how that this is Thy Hand, and that Thou, Lord, hast made it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:125
verses.text: He said, "Let them know," of those for whom He even prayed while they were raging; for even those who afterwards believed in Him were among the crowd who shook their heads in mockery of Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:126
verses.text: But let those who ascribe unto God the shape of the human body, learn in what sense God hath a hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:127
verses.text: Let us therefore understand, that the Hand of God meaneth Christ: whence it is elsewhere said, "Unto whom is the arm of the Lord revealed?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:128
verses.text: "Though they curse, yet bless Thou".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:129
verses.text: Vain therefore and false is the cursing of the sons of men, that have pleasure in vanity, and seek a lie; but when God blesseth, He doth what He saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:130
verses.text: "Let them be confounded that rise up against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:131
verses.text: For their imagining that they have some power against Me, is the reason that they rise up against Me; but when I shall have been exalted above the heavens, and My glory shall have commenced spreading over the whole earth, they shall be confounded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:132
verses.text: "But Thy servant shall rejoice:" either on the right hand of the Father, or in His members when they rejoice, both in hope among temptations, and after temptations for evermore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:133
verses.text: "Let my slanderers be clothed with shame" : that is, let it shame them to have slandered me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:134
verses.text: But this may also be understood as a blessing, in that they are amended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:135
verses.text: "And let them cover themselves with their own confusion, as with a double cloak;" for diplois is a double cloak; that is, let them be confounded both within and without: both before God and before men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:136
verses.text: "As for me, I will confess greatly unto the Lord with my mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:137
verses.text: Is He said to "praise among the multitude" because He is with His Church here even unto the end of the world; so that we may understand by "among the multitude," that He is honoured by this very multitude? For he is said to be in the midst, unto whom the chief honour is paid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:138
verses.text: But if the heart is, as it were, that which is mid-most of a man, no better construction can be put on this passage than this, I will praise Him in the hearts of many.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:139
verses.text: For Christ dwelleth through faith in our hearts; and therefore he saith, "with my mouth," that is, with the mouth of my body, which is the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:140
verses.text: "For He stood at the right hand of the poor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:141
verses.text: It was said of Judas, "Let Satan stand at his right hand;" since he chose to increase his riches by selling Christ; but here the Lord stood at the right hand of the poor, that the Lord Himself might be the poor man's riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:142
verses.text: "He stood at the right hand of the poor," not to multiply the years of a life that one day must end, nor to increase his stores, nor to render him strong in the strength of the body, or secure for a time; "but," he saith, "to save my soul from the persecutors".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:143
verses.text: Now the soul is rendered safe from the persecutors, if we do not consent to them unto evil; but there is no such consent to them when the Lord standeth at the right hand of the poor, that he may not give way through his very poverty, that is, weakness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 109:144
verses.text: This aid was given to the Body of Christ in the case of all the holy Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:1
verses.text: Psalm CX.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:2
verses.text: This Psalm is one of those promises, surely and openly prophesying our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ; so that we are utterly unable to doubt that Christ is announced in this Psalm, since we are now Christians, and believe the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:3
