verses.text: For when our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ asked of the Jews, whose Son they alleged Christ to be, and they had replied, "the Son of David;" He at once replied to their answer, "How then doth David in spirit call Him Lord, saying, The Lord said unto My Lord?" etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:4
verses.text: "If then,"  He asked, "David in the spirit call Him Lord, how is He his son?" With this verse this Psalm beginneth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:5
verses.text: "The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit Thou on My right hand, until I make Thine enemies Thy footstool".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:6
verses.text: We ought, therefore, thoroughly to consider this question proposed to the Jews by the Lord, in the very commencement of the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:7
verses.text: For if what the.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:8
verses.text: Jews answered be asked of us, whether we confess or deny it; God forbid that we should deny it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:9
verses.text: If it be said to us, Is Christ the Son of David, or not? if we reply, No, we contradict the Gospel for the Gospel of St.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:10
verses.text: Matthew thus beginneth, "The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the Son of David".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:11
verses.text: The Evangelist declareth, that he is writing the book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the Son of David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:12
verses.text: The Jews, then, when questioned by Christ, whose Son they believed Christ to be, rightly answered, the Son of David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:13
verses.text: The Gospel agreeth with their answer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:14
verses.text: Not only the suspicion of the Jews, but the faith of Christians, doth declare this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:15
verses.text: "If then David in the spirit called Him Lord, how is He his son?" The Jews were silent at this question: they found no further reply: yet they did not seek Him as the Lord, for they did not acknowledge Him to be Himself that Son of David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:16
verses.text: But let us, brethren, both believe and declare: for, "with the heart we believe unto righteousness: but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation;" let us believe, I say, and let us declare both the Son of David, and the Lord of David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:17
verses.text: Let us not be ashamed of the Son of David, lest we find the Lord of David angry with us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:18
verses.text: We know that Christ sitteth at the right hand of the Father, since His resurrection from the dead, and ascent into heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:19
verses.text: It is already done: we saw not it, but we have believed it: we have read it in the Scripture, have heard it preached, and hold it by faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:20
verses.text: So that by the very circumstance that Christ was David's Son, He became His Lord also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:21
verses.text: For That which was born of the seed of David was so honoured, that It was also the Lord of David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:22
verses.text: Thou wonderest at this, as if the same did not happen in human affairs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:23
verses.text: For if it should happen, that the son of any private person be made a king, will he not be his father's lord? What is yet more wonderful may happen, not only that the son of a private person, by being made a king, may become his father's lord; but that the son of a layman, by being made a Bishop, may become his father's father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:24
verses.text: So that in this very circumstance, that Christ took upon Him the flesh, that He died in the flesh, that He rose again in the same flesh, that in the same He ascended into Heaven, and sitteth on the right hand of His Father, in this same flesh so honoured, so brightened, so changed into a heavenly garb, He is both David's Son, and David's Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:25
verses.text: Christ, therefore, sitteth at the right hand of God, the Son is on the right hand of the Father, hidden from us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:26
verses.text: Let us believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:27
verses.text: Two things are here said: that God said, "Sit Thou on My right hand;" and added, "until I make Thy enemies Thy footstool;" that is, beneath Thy feet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:28
verses.text: Thou dost not see Christ sitting at the right hand of the Father: yet thou canst see this, how His enemies are made His footstool.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:29
verses.text: While the latter is fulfilled openly, believe the former to be fulfilled secretly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:30
verses.text: What enemies are made His footstool? Those to whom imagining vain things it is said, "Why do the heathen so furiously rage together: and why do the people imagine a vain thing?" etcHe therefore sitteth at the right hand of God, till His enemies be placed beneath His feet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:31
verses.text: This is going on, this is taking place: although it is accomplished by degrees, it is going on without end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:32
verses.text: For though the heathen rage, will they, taking counsel together against Christ, prevent the fulfilment of these words: "I will give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession"?"Their memorial is perished with a cry;" but, "The Lord shall endure for ever:" as another Psalm, but not another Spirit, saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:33
verses.text: And what followeth? "The Lord shall send the rod of Thy power out of Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:34
verses.text: It appeareth, brethren, it most clearly appeareth, that the Prophet is not speaking of that kingdom of Christ, in which He reigneth for ever with His Father, Ruler of the things which are made through Him: for when doth not God the Word reign, who is in the beginning with God? For it is said, "Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honour and glory for ever and ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:35
verses.text: To what eternal King? To one invisible, incorruptible.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:36
verses.text: For in this, that Christ is with the Father, invisible and incorruptible, because He is His Word, and His Power, and His Wisdom, and God with God, through whom all things were made; He is "King eternal;" but, nevertheless, that reign of temporal government, by which, through the mediation of His flesh, He called us into eternity, beginneth with Christians; but of His reign there shall be no end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:37
verses.text: His enemies therefore are made His footstool, while He is sitting on the right hand of His Father, as it is written; this is now going on, this will go on unto the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:38
verses.text: When therefore He hath sent the rod of His power out of Sion: what shall happen? "Be Thou ruler, even in the midst among Thine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:39
verses.text: First, "Be Thou ruler in the midst of Thine enemies:" in the midst of the raging heathen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:40
verses.text: For shall He rule "in the midst of His enemies" at a later season, when the Saints have received their reward, and the ungodly their condemnation? And what wonder if He shall then rule, when the righteous reign with Him for ever, and the ungodly burn with eternal punishments? What wonder, if He shall then? Now "in the midst of Thine enemies," now in this transition of ages, in this propagation and succession of human mortality, now while the torrent of time is gliding by, unto this is the rod of Thy power sent out of Sion, "that Thou mayest be Ruler in the midst of Thine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:41
verses.text: Rule Thou, rule among Pagans, Jews, heretics, false brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:42
verses.text: Rule Thou, rule, O Son of David, Lord of David, rule in the midst of Pagans, Jews, heretics, false brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:43
verses.text: "Be Thou Ruler in the midst of Thine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:44
verses.text: We understand not this verse aright, if we do not see that it is already going on.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:45
verses.text: "With Thee the beginning on the day of Thy power".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:46
verses.text: What is this day of His power, when is there beginning with Him, or what beginning, or in what sense is there beginning with Him, since He is the Beginning?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:47
verses.text: What meaneth, "With Thee is the beginning"? Suppose anything you please as the beginning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:48
verses.text: Of Christ Himself, it would rather have been said, Thou art the Beginning, than, With Thee is the beginning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:49
verses.text: For He answered to those who asked Him, "Who art Thou?" and said, "Even the same that I said unto you, the Beginning;" since His Father also is the Beginning, of whom is the only-begotten Son, in which Beginning was the Word, for the Word was with God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:50
verses.text: What then, if both the Father and the Son are the beginning, are there two beginnings? God forbid! For as the Father is God, and the Son is God, but the Father and the Son are not two Gods, but one God: so is the Father Beginning and the Son Beginning, but the Father and the Son are not two, but one Beginning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:51
verses.text: "With Thee is the beginning".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:52
verses.text: Then it shall appear in what sense the beginning is with Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:53
verses.text: Not that the beginning is not with Thee here also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:54
verses.text: For hast Thou not also said, "Behold, ye shall be scattered, every man to his own, and shall leave Me alone; but I am not alone, because the Father is with Me"? Here therefore also, the beginning is with Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:55
verses.text: For Thou hast said elsewhere also, "But the Father that dwelleth in Me, He doeth His works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:56
verses.text: "With Thee is the beginning:" nor was the Father ever separated from Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:57
verses.text: But when the Beginning shall appear to be with Thee, then shall it be manifest unto all who are made like Thee; since they shall see Thee as Thou art; for Philip saw Thee here, and sought the Father Then therefore shall be seen what now is believed: then shall "the beginning be with Thee" in the sight of the righteous, in the sight of saints; the ungodly being removed, that they may not see the brightness of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:58
verses.text: Explain of what power thou speakest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:59
verses.text: Because here also, as is said, His power is mentioned, when the rod of His power is sent forth out of Sion, that He may be Ruler in the midst of His enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:60
verses.text: Of what power speakest thou, "In the splendour of the saints"? "In the splendour," he saith, "of the saints".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:61
verses.text: He speaketh of that power when the saints shall be in splendour; not when still carrying about their earthly flesh, and groaning in a mortal and corruptible body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:62
verses.text: But this is put off, this will be granted afterwards: what is there now? "From the womb I have begotten Thee, before the morning star".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:63
verses.text: What is here? If God hath a Son, hath He also a womb? Like fleshly bodies, He hath not; for He hath not a bosom either; yet it is said, "He who is in the bosom of the Father, hath declared Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:64
verses.text: But that which is the womb, is the bosom also: both bosom and womb are put for a secret place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:65
verses.text: What meaneth, "from the womb"? From what is secret, from what is hidden; from Myself, from My substance; this is the meaning of "from the womb;" for, "Who shall declare His generation?" Let us then understand the Father saying unto the Son, "From My womb before the morning star have I brought Thee forth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:66
verses.text: What then meaneth, "before the morning star"? The morning star is put for the stars, as if the Scripture signified the whole from a part, and from one conspicuous star all the stars.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:67
verses.text: But how were those stars created? "That they may be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:68
verses.text: This expression also, "before the morning star," is used both figuratively and literally, and was thus fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:69
verses.text: For the Lord was born at night from the womb of the Virgin Mary; the testimony of the shepherds doth assert this, who were "keeping watch over their flock".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:70
verses.text: So David: O Thou, my Lord, who sittest at the right hand of my Lord, whence art Thou my Son, except because, "From the womb before the morning star I have begotten Thee"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:71
verses.text: And unto what art Thou born? "The Lord hath sworn, and will not repent: Thou art a Priest for ever after the order of Melchizedec".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:72
verses.text: For unto this wast Thou born from the womb before the morning star, that Thou mightest be a Priest for ever after the order of Melchizedec.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:73
verses.text: For in that character in which He was born of the Father, God with God, coeternal with Him who begot Him, He is not a Priest; but He is a Priest on account of the flesh which He assumed, on account of the victim which He was to offer for us received from us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:74
verses.text: "The Lord," then, "hath sworn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:75
verses.text: What then meaneth, the Lord hath sworn? Doth the Lord, who forbiddeth men to swear, Himself swear? Or doth He possibly forbid man to swear chiefly on this account, that he may not fall into perjury, and for this reason the Lord may swear, since He cannot be forsworn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:76
verses.text: For man, who, through a habit of swearing, may slip into perjury, is rightly forbidden to swear: for he will be farther from perjury in proportion as he is far from swearing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:77
verses.text: For the man who sweareth, may swear truly or falsely: but he who sweareth not, cannot swear falsely; for he sweareth not at all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:78
verses.text: Why then should not the Lord swear, since the Lord's oath is the seal of the promise? Let Him swear by all means.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:79
verses.text: What then dost thou, when thou swearest? Thou callest God to witness: this is to swear, to call God to witness; and for this reason there must be anxiety, that thou mayest not call God to witness anything false.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:80
verses.text: If therefore thou by an oath dost call God to witness, why then should not God also call Himself to witness with an oath? "I live, saith the Lord," this is the Lord's oath.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:81
verses.text: "The Lord sware," then, that is, confirmed: "He will not repent," He will not change.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:82
verses.text: What? "Thou art a Priest for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:83
verses.text: "For ever," for He will not repent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:84
verses.text: But Priest, in what sense? Will there be those victims, victims offered by the Patriarchs, altars of blood, and tabernacle, and those sacred emblems of the Old Covenant? God forbid! These things are already abolished; the temple being destroyed, that priesthood taken away, their victim and their sacrifice having alike disappeared, not even the Jews have these things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:85
verses.text: They see that the priesthood after the order of Aaron hath already perished, and they do not recognise the Priesthood after the order of Melchizedec.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:86
verses.text: I speak unto believers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:87
verses.text: If catechumens understand not something, let them lay aside sloth, and hasten unto knowledge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:88
verses.text: It is not therefore needful for me to disclose mysteries here:  let the Scriptures intimate to you what is the Priesthood after the order of Melchizedec.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:89
verses.text: "The Lord on Thy right hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:90
verses.text: The Lord had said, "Sit Thou on My right hand;" now the Lord is on His right hand, as if they changed seats.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:91
verses.text: That very Christ, the "Lord on Thy right hand," unto whom Thou hast sworn, and it will not repent Thee: what doth He, Priest for evermore? What doth He, who is at the right hand of God, and intercedeth for us, like a priest entering into the inner places, and into the holy of holies, into the mysteries of heaven, He alone being without sin, and therefore easily purifying from sins He therefore "on Thy right hand shall wound even kings in the day of His wrath".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:92
verses.text: What kings, dost thou ask? Hast thou forgotten? "The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers took counsel together against the Lord, and against His Anointed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:93
verses.text: These kings He wounded by His glory, and by the weight of His Name made kings weak, so that they had not power to effect what they wished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:94
verses.text: For they strove amain to blot out the Christian name from the earth, and could not; for "Whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be broken".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:95
verses.text: Kings therefore fall on this "stone of offence," and are therefore wounded, when they say, Who is Christ? I know not what Jew or what Galilean He may have been, who died, who was slain in such a manner! The stone is before thy feet, lying, so to speak, mean and humble: therefore by scorning thou dost stumble, by stumbling thou fallest, by falling thou art wounded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:96
verses.text: "But on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:97
verses.text: When therefore any one falleth upon it, it lieth as it were low; it then woundeth: but when it shall grind him to powder, then it will come from above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:98
verses.text: See how in these two words, it shall wound him and grind him to powder: he striketh upon it, and it shall come down upon him: are distinguished the two seasons, of the humiliation and the majesty of Christ, of hidden punishment and future judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:99
verses.text: He will not crush, when He cometh, that man whom He doth not wound when He lieth in a contemptible appearance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:100
verses.text: "He shall judge among the heathen: He shall fill up what hath fallen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:101
verses.text: Whoever thou art who art obstinate against Christ, thou hast raised on high a tower that must fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:102
verses.text: It is good that thou shouldest cast thyself down, become humble, throw thyself at the feet of Him who sitteth on the right hand of the Father, that in thee a ruin may be made to be built up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:103
verses.text: For if thou abidest in thy evil height, thou shalt be cast down when thou canst not be built up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:104
verses.text: For of such the Scripture saith in another passage: "Therefore shall He break down, and not build them up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:105
verses.text: Beyond doubt he would not say this of some, unless there were some whom He broke down so as to build them up again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:106
verses.text: And this is going on at this time, while Christ is judging among the heathen in such a manner as to fill up what hath fallen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:107
verses.text: "He shall smite many heads over the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:108
verses.text: Here upon the earth in this life He shall smite many heads.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:109
verses.text: He maketh them humble instead of proud; and I dare to say, my brethren, that it is more profitable to walk here humbly with the head wounded, than with the head erect to fall into the judgment of eternal death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:110
verses.text: He will smite many heads when he causeth them to fall, but He will fill them up and build them up again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:111
verses.text: "He shall drink of the brook in the way, therefore shall he lift up his head".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:112
verses.text: Let us consider Him drinking of the brook in the way: first of all, what is the brook? the onward flow of human mortality: for as a brook is gathered together by the rain, overflows, roars, runs, and by running runs down, that is, finishes its course; so is all this course of mortality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:113
verses.text: Men are born, they live, they die, and when some die others are born, and when they die others are born, they succeed, they flock together, they depart and will not remain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:114
verses.text: What is held fast here? what doth not run? what is not on its way to the abyss as if it was gathered together from rain? For as a river suddenly drawn together from rain from the drops of showers runneth into the sea, and is seen no more, nor was it seen before it was collected from the rain; so this hidden rain is collected together from hidden sources, and floweth on; at death again it travelleth where it is hidden: this intermediate state soundeth and passeth away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:115
verses.text: Of this brook He drinketh, He hath not disdained to drink of this brook; for to drink of this brook was to Him to be born and to die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:116
verses.text: What this brook hath, is birth and death; Christ assumed this, He was born, He died.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 110:117
verses.text: "Therefore hath He lifted up His head;" that is, because He was humble, and "became obedient unto death, even the death of the Cross: therefore God also hath highly exalted Him, and given Him a Name which is above every name; that at the Name of Jesus every knee shall bow, of things in Heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; and that every tongue shall confess that Jesus Christ the Lord is in the glory of God the Father".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:1
verses.text: Psalm CXI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:2
verses.text: The days have come for us to sing AllelujahNow these days come only to pass away, and pass away to come, again, and typify the day which does not come and pass away, because it is neither preceded by yesterday to cause it to come, nor pressed upon by the morrow to cause it to pass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:3
verses.text: For as these days succeed in regular season, with a joyful cheerfulness, the past days of Lent, whereby the misery of this life before the Resurrection of the Lord's body is signified; so that day which after the Resurrection shall be given to the full body of the Lord, that is, to the holy Church, when all the troubles and sorrows of this life have been shut out, shall succeed with perpetual bliss.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:4
verses.text: But this life demandeth from us self-restraint, that although groaning and weighed down with our toil and struggles, and desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven, we may refrain from secular pleasures: and this is signified by the number of forty, which was the period of the fasts of Moses, and Elias, and our Lord Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:5
verses.text: But by the number fifty after our Lord's resurrection, during which season we sing Allelujah, not the term and passing away of a certain season is signified, but that blessed eternity; because the denary added to forty signifieth the reward paid to the faithful who toil in this life, which our Father hath prepared an equal share of for the first and for the last.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:6
verses.text: Let us there fore hear the heart of the people of God full of divine praises.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:7
verses.text: He representeth in this Psalm some one exulting in happy joyfulness, he prefigureth the people whose hearts are overflowing with the love of God, that is, the body of Christ, freed from all evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:8
verses.text: "I will make confession unto Thee, O Lord," he saith, "with my whole heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:9
verses.text: Confession is not always confession of sins, but the praise of God is poured forth in the devotion of confession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:10
verses.text: The former mourneth, the latter rejoiceth: the former showeth the wound to the physician, the latter giveth thanks for health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:11
verses.text: The latter confession signifieth some one, not merely freed from every evil, but even separate from all the ill-disposed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:12
verses.text: And for this reason let us consider the place where he confesseth unto the Lord with all his heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:13
verses.text: "In the counsel," he saith, "of the upright, and in the congregation:" I suppose, of those who shall "sit upon the twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:14
verses.text: For there will be no longer an unjust man among them, the thefts of no Judas are allowed, no Simon Magus is baptized, wishing to buy the Spirit, whilst he designeth to sell it; no coppersmith like Alexander doth many evil deeds, no man covered with sheep's clothing creepeth in with feigned fraternity; such as those among whom the Church must now groan, and such as she must then shut out, when all the righteous shall be gathered together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:15
verses.text: "These are the great works of the Lord, sought out unto all His wills" : through which mercy forsaketh none who confesseth, no man's wickedness is unpunishedLet man choose for himself what he listeth: the works of the Lord are not so constituted, that the creature, having free discretion allowed him, should transcend the will of the Creator, even though he act contrary to His will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:16
verses.text: God willeth not that thou shouldest sin; for He forbiddeth it: yet if thou hast sinned, imagine not that the man hath done what he willed, and that hath happened to God which He willed not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:17
verses.text: For as He would that man would not sin, so would He spare the sinner, that he may return and live; He so willeth finally to punish him who persisteth in his sin, that the rebellious cannot escape the power of justice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:18
verses.text: Thus whatever choice thou hast made, the Almighty will not be at a loss to fulfil His will concerning thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:19
verses.text: "Confession and glorious deeds are His work".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:20
verses.text: What is a more glorious deed than to justify the ungodly? But perhaps the work of man preventeth that glorious work of God, so that when he hath confessed his sins, he deserveth to be justified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:21
verses.text: This is the glorious work of the Lord: for he loveth most, to whom most is forgiven This is the glorious work of the Lord: for "where sin abounded, there did grace much more abound".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:22
verses.text: But perhaps a man would deserve justification from works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:23
verses.text: "Not," saith he, "of works, lest any man boast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:24
verses.text: For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:25
verses.text: For a man worketh not righteousness save he be justified: but by "believing on Him that justifieth the ungodly," he beginneth with faith; that good may not by preceding show what he hath deserved, but by following what he hath received.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:26
verses.text: "He hath made His wonderful works to be remembered" : by abasing this man, exalting that.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:27
verses.text: Reserving unusual miracles for a fit season, that thus human weakness, intent upon novelty, may remember them, although His daily miracles be greater.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:28
verses.text: He created so many trees throughout the whole earth, and no one wondereth: He dried up one with a word, and the hearts of mortals were thunderstruck For that miracle, which hath not through its frequency become common, will cling most firmly to the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:29
verses.text: But of what use were the miracles, save that He might be feared? What too would fear profit, unless "the gracious and merciful Lord" gave "meat unto them that fear Him"? ; meat that doth not spoil, "bread that cometh down from heaven," which He gave to no deservings of ours.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:30
verses.text: For "Christ died for the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:31
verses.text: No one then would give such food, save a gracious and merciful Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:32
verses.text: But if He gave so much to this life, if the sinner who was to be justified received the Word made flesh; what shall he receive when glorified in a future world? For, "He shall ever be mindful of His covenant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:33
verses.text: Nor hath He who hath given a pledge, given the whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:34
verses.text: "He shall show His people the power of His works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:35
verses.text: Let not the holy Israelites, who have left all their possessions and have followed Him, be saddened; let them not be sorrowful and say, "Who then can be saved?" For "it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:36
verses.text: For "with men these things are impossible, but with God all things are possible".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:37
verses.text: "That He may give them the heritage of the heathen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:38
verses.text: For they went to the heathen, and enjoined the rich of this world "not to be high-minded, nor to trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God," to whom that is easy which is difficult for men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:39
verses.text: For thus many were called, thus the heritage of the heathen has been occupied, thus it hath happened, that even many who have not abandoned all their possessions in this life in order to follow Him, have despised even life itself for the sake of confessing His Name; and like camels humbling themselves to bear the burden of troubles, have entered as it were through a needle's eye, through the piercing straits of suffering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:40
verses.text: He hath wrought these effects, unto whom all things are possible.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:41
verses.text: "The works of His hands are verity and judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:42
verses.text: Let verity be held by those who are judged here.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:43
verses.text: Martyrs are here sentenced, and brought to the judgment-seat, that they may judge not only those by whom they have been judged, but even give judgment on angels, against whom was their struggle here, even when they seemed to be judged by men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:44
verses.text: Let not tribulation, distress, famine, nakedness, the sword, separate from Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:45
verses.text: For "all His commandments are true;" He deceiveth not, He giveth us what He promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:46
verses.text: Yet we should not expect here what He promised; we should not hope for it: but "they stand fast for ever and ever, and are done in truth and equity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:47
verses.text: It is equitable and just that we should labour here and repose there; since "He sent redemption unto His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:48
verses.text: But from what are they redeemed, save from the captivity of this pilgrimage? Let not therefore rest be sought, save in the heavenly country.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:49
verses.text: God indeed gave the carnal Israelites an earthly Jerusalem, "which is in bondage with her children:" but this is the Old Covenant, pertaining unto the old man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:50
verses.text: But they who there understood the figure, even then were heirs of the New Covenant; for "Jerusalem which is above is free, which is our everlasting mother in heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:51
verses.text: But that transitory promises were given in that Old Testament is proved by the fact itself: however, "He hath commended His covenant for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:52
verses.text: But what, but the New? Whosoever dost wish to be heir of this, deceive not thyself, and think not of a land flowing with milk and honey, nor of pleasant farms, nor of gardens abounding in fruits and shade: desire not how to gain anything of this sort, such as the eye of covetousness is wont to lust for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:53
verses.text: For since "covetousness is the root of all evils," it must be cut off, that it may be consumed here; not be put off, that it may be satisfied there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:54
verses.text: First escape punishments, avoid hell; before thou longest for a God who promiseth, beware of one who threateneth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:55
verses.text: For "holy and reverend is His Name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:56
verses.text: "The fear of the Lord," therefore, "is the beginning of wisdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:57
verses.text: "Understanding is good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:58
verses.text: Who gainsayeth? But to understand, and not to do, is dangerous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:59
verses.text: It is "good," therefore, "to those that do thereafter".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:60
verses.text: Nor let it lift up the mind unto pride; for, "the praise of Him," the fear of whom is the beginning of wisdom, "endureth for ever:" and this will be the reward, this the end, this the everlasting station and abode.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:61
verses.text: There are found the true commandments, made fast for ever and ever; here is the very heritage of the New Covenant commanded for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:62
verses.text: "One thing," he saith, "I have desired of the Lord, which I will require: even that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 111:63
verses.text: For, "blessed are they that dwell in the house" of the Lord: "they will be alway praising" Him; for "His praise endureth for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:1
verses.text: Psalm CXII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:2
verses.text: I believe, brethren, that ye remarked and committed to memory the title of this Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:3
verses.text: "The conversion," he saith, "of Haggai and Zechariah".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:4
verses.text: These prophets were not as yet in existence, when these verses were sungBut both, the one within a year after the other, began to prophesy that which seemeth to pertain to the restoration of the temple, as was foretold so long before"For the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:5
verses.text: Whoever therefore converteth himself to the work of this building together, and to the hope of a firm and holy edifice, like a living stone from the miserable ruin of this world, understandeth the title of the Psalm, understandeth "the conversion of Haggai and Zechariah".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:6
verses.text: Let him therefore chant the following verses, not so much with the voice of his tongue as of his life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:7
verses.text: For the completion of the building will be that ineffable peace of wisdom, the "beginning" of which is the "fear of the Lord:" let him therefore, whom this conversion buildeth together, begin thence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:8
verses.text: "Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord: he will have great delight in His commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:9
verses.text: God, who alone judgeth both truthfully and mercifully, will see how far he obeyeth His commandments: since "the life of man on earth is a temptation," as holy Job saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:10
verses.text: But "He who judgeth us is the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:11
verses.text: He therefore will see how far each man profiteth in His commandments; yet he who loveth the peace of this building together, shall have great delight in them; nor ought he to despair, since there is "peace on earth for men of good will".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:12
verses.text: Next follows, "His seed shall be mighty upon earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:13
verses.text: The Apostle witnesseth, that the works of mercy are the seed of the future harvest, when he saith, "Let us not be weary in well doing, for in due season we shall reap;" and again, "But this I say, He which soweth sparingly, shall reap also sparingly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:14
verses.text: But what, brethren, is more mighty than that not only Zacchaeus should buy the kingdom of Heaven by the half of his goods, but even the widow for two mites, and that each should possess an equal share there? What is more mighty, than that the same kingdom should be worth treasures to the rich man, and a cup of cold water to the poor?"Glory and riches shall be in his house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:15
verses.text: For his house is his heart; where, with the praise of God, he liveth in greater riches with the hope of eternal life, than with men flattering, in palaces of marble, with splendidly adorned ceilings, with the fear of everlasting death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:16
verses.text: "For his righteousness endureth for ever:" this is his glory, there are his riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:17
verses.text: While the other's purple, and fine linen, and grand banquets, even when present, are passing away; and when they have come to an end, the burning tongue shall cry out, longing for a drop of water from the finger's end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:18
verses.text: "Unto the right-hearted there ariseth up light in the darkness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:19
verses.text: Justly do the godly direct their heart unto their God, justly do they walk with their God, preferring His will to themselves; and having no proud presumption in their own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:20
verses.text: For they remember that they were some time in darkness, but are now light in the Lord "Merciful, pitying, and just is the Lord God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:21
verses.text: It delighteth us that He is "merciful and pitying," but it perhaps terrifieth us that the Lord God is "just".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:22
verses.text: Fear not, despair not at all, happy man, who fearest the Lord, and hast great delight in His commandments; be thou sweet, be merciful and lend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:23
verses.text: For the Lord is just in this manner, that He judgeth without mercy him who hath not shown mercy; but, "Sweet is the man who is merciful and lendeth" : God will not spew him out of His mouth as if he were not sweet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:24
verses.text: "Forgive," He saith, "and ye shall be forgiven; give, and it shall be given unto you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:25
verses.text: Whilst thou forgivest that thou mayest be forgiven, thou art merciful; whilst thou givest that it may be given unto thee, thou lendest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:26
verses.text: For though all be called generally mercy where another is assisted in his distress, yet there is a difference where thou spendest neither money, nor the toil of bodily labour, but by forgiving what each man hath sinned against thee, thou gainest free pardon for thine own sins also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:27
verses.text: He who is unwilling to give to the poor, seeketh riches; listen to what is written, "Thou shalt have treasure in heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:28
verses.text: Thou wilt not then lose honour by forgiving: for it is a very laudable triumph to conquer anger: wilt not grow poor by giving; for a heavenly treasure is a more safe possession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:29
verses.text: The former verse, "Riches and plenteousness shall be in his house," was pregnant with this verse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:30
verses.text: He therefore who doth these things, "shall guide his words with discretion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:31
verses.text: His deeds themselves are the words whereby he shall be defended at the Judgment; which shall not be without mercy unto him, since he hath himself shown mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:32
verses.text: "For he shall never be moved" : he who, called to the right hand, shall hear these words, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:33
verses.text: For no works of theirs, save works of mercy, are there mentioned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:34
verses.text: He therefore shall hear, "Come, ye blessed of My Father;" for, "the generation of the right ones shall be blessed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:35
verses.text: Thus, "the righteous shall be had in everlasting remembrance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:36
verses.text: "He will not be afraid of any evil hearing; for his heart standeth fast and believeth in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:37
verses.text: Such as the words which he will hear addressed to those on the left hand, "Depart into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:38
verses.text: He therefore who seeketh here not his own things, but those of Jesus Christ, most patiently endureth sufferings, waiteth for the promises with faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:39
verses.text: Nor is he broken down by any temptations: "His heart is established, and will not shrink, until he see beyond his enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:40
verses.text: His enemies wished to see good things here, and when invisible blessings were promised them, used to say, "Who will show us any good?" Let our heart therefore be established, and shrink not, until we see beyond our enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:41
verses.text: For they wish to see good things of men in the land of the dying; we trust to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:42
verses.text: But it is a great thing to have the heart established, and not to be moved, while they rejoice who love what they see, and mock at him who hopeth for what he seeth not; "what the Lord hath prepared for them that love Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:43
verses.text: How great is the value of this which is not seen, and it is bought for so much as each man is able to give for it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:44
verses.text: On this account he also "dispersed abroad, and gave to the poor" : he saw not, yet he kept buying; but He was storing up the treasure in heaven, who deigned to hunger and thirst in the poor on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:45
verses.text: It is no wonder then if "his righteousness remaineth for ever:" He who created the ages being his guardian.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:46
verses.text: "His horn," whose humility was scorned by the proud, "shall be exalted with honour".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:47
verses.text: "The ungodly shall see it, and he shall be angered" : this is that late and fruitless repentance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:48
verses.text: For with whom rather than himself is he "angered," when he shall say, "Our pride, what hath it profited us? the boastfulness of our riches, what hath it given us?" seeing the horn of him exalted with honour, who "dispersed abroad, and gave to the poor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:49
verses.text: "He shall gnash with his teeth, and consume away:" for "there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:50
verses.text: For he will no more bring forth leaves and bloom, as would happen if he had repented in season: but he will then repent, when "the desire of the ungodly shall perish," no consolation succeeding.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:51
verses.text: "The desire of the ungodly shall perish," when "all things shall pass away like a shadow," when the flower shall fall down on the withering of the grass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 112:52
verses.text: "But the word of the Lord that endureth for ever," as it is mocked by the vanity of the falsely happy, so will laugh at the perdition of the same when truly miserable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:1
verses.text: Psalm CXIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:2
verses.text: When ye hear sung in the Psalms, "Praise the Lord, ye children" ; imagine not that that exhortation pertaineth not unto you, because having already passed the youth of the body, ye are either blooming in the prime of manhood, or growing gray with the honours of old age: for unto all of you the Apostle saith, "Brethren, be not children in understanding; howbeit, in malice be ye children, but in understanding be men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:3
verses.text: What malice in particular, save pride? For it is pride that, presuming in false greatness, suffereth not man to walk along the narrow path, and to enter by the narrow gate; but the child easily entereth through the narrow entrance; and thus no man, save as a child, entereth into the kingdom of heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:4
verses.text: "Praise the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:5
verses.text: Let Him therefore be alway proclaimed: "Blessed be the Name of the Lord, from this time forth for evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:6
verses.text: Let Him be proclaimed everywhere: "From the rising up of the sun unto the going down of the same, praise ye the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:7
verses.text: If any of the holy children who praise the Name of the Lord were to ask of me and say to me, "for evermore" I understand to mean unto all eternity: but why "from this," and why is not the Name of the Lord blessed before this, and before all ages? I will answer the infant, who asketh not in contumacy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:8
verses.text: Unto you it is said, masters and children, unto you it is said, "Praise the Name of the Lord; blessed be the Name of the Lord:" let the Name of the Lord be blessed, "from this," that is, from the moment ye speak these words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:9
verses.text: For ye begin to praise, but praise ye without end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:10
verses.text: Or, since in this passage he seemeth to signify rather humility than childhood, the contrary of which is the vain and false greatness of pride; and for this reason none but children praise the Lord, since the proud know not how to praise Him; let old age be childlike, and your childhood like old age; that is, that neither may your wisdom be with pride, nor your humility without wisdom, that ye may "praise the Lord from this for evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:11
verses.text: Wherever the Church of Christ is diffused in her childlike saints, "Praise ye the Name of the Lord;" that is, "from the rising up of the sun unto the going down of the same".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:12
verses.text: "The Lord is high above all heathen".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:13
verses.text: The heathen are men: what wonder if the Lord be above all men? They see with their eyes those whom they worship high above themselves to shine in heaven, the sun and moon and stars, creatures which they serve while they neglect the Creator.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:14
verses.text: But not only "is the Lord high above all heathen;" but "His glory" also "is above the heavens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:15
verses.text: The heavens look up unto Him above themselves; and the humble have Him together with them, who do not worship the heavens instead of Him, though placed in the flesh beneath the heavens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:16
verses.text: "Who is like unto the Lord our God, that hath His dwelling so high; and yet beholdeth the humble?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:17
verses.text: Any one would think that He dwelleth in the lofty heavens, whence He may behold the humble things on earth; but "He beholdeth the humble things that are in heaven and earth" : what then is His high dwelling, whence He beholdeth the humble things that are in heaven and earth? Are the humble things He beholdeth His own high dwelling itself? For He thus exalteth the humble, so as not to make them proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:18
verses.text: He therefore both dwelleth in those whom He raiseth high, and maketh them heaven for Himself, that is, His own abode; and by seeing them not proud, but constantly subject to Himself, He beholdeth even in heaven itself these very humble things, in whom raised on high He dwelleth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:19
verses.text: For the Spirit thus speaketh through Isaiah: "Thus saith the Highest that dwelleth on high, that inhabiteth eternity; the Lord Most High, dwelling in the holy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:20
verses.text: He hath expounded what He meant by dwelling on high, by the more full expression, "dwelling in the holy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:21
verses.text: And he hath moved us also to enquire whether the Lord our God beholdeth the same humble things in heaven and in earth: or different humble things in heaven to what He beholdeth on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:22
verses.text: But if the Lord our God beholdeth other humble things in heaven to what He doth on earth; I suppose that He already beholdeth in heaven those whom He hath called, and in whom He dwelleth; while on earth He beholdeth those whom He is now calling, that He may dwell in them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:23
verses.text: For He hath the one with Him musing on heavenly things, the others He is waking, while they yet dream things earthly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:24
verses.text: But since it is difficult to call even those humble, who have not as yet submitted their nec ks in piety to the gracious yoke of Christ, since the divine writings throughout the whole Psalm warn us to understand holy by the word humble; there is also another interpretation, which, Beloved, ye may consider with me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:25
verses.text: I believe that those are now meant by heavens who shall sit upon twelve thrones, and shall judge with the Lord; and under the name of the earth, the rest of the multitude of the blessed, who shall be set on the right hand, that through works of mercy they may be praised and received into everlasting habitations by those whom they have made friends to themselves from the mammon of unrighteousness in this mortal life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:26
verses.text: "He taketh up the destitute out of the dust, and lifteth the poor out of the mire" ; "that He may set Him with the princes, even with the princes of His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:27
verses.text: Let not then the heads of the exalted disdain to be humble, beneath the Lord's right hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:28
verses.text: For though the faithful steward of the Lord's money be placed together with the princes of the people of God, although he be destined to sit on the twelve seats, and even to judge angels; yet he is taken up destitute from the dust, and lifted from out of the mire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:29
verses.text: Was not he possibly lifted up from the mire, who "served divers lusts and pleasures"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:30
verses.text: What then, brethren, if we have already heard of those humble things which are in heaven, lifted up from the mire, that they might be set with the princes of the people; have we by consequence heard nothing of the humble things which the Lord beholdeth on the earth? For those friends who will judge with their Lord are fewer, while those whom they receive into everlasting habitations are more in number.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:31
verses.text: For although the whole of a heap of corn compared with the separate chaff may seem to contain few in number; yet considered by itself, it is abundant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 113:32
verses.text: The Church then speaketh thus in that sense, wherein she seemeth to bear no offspring among those crowds who have not given up all things, that they might follow the Lord, and might sit upon the twelve thrones But how many in the same crowd, who make unto themselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness, shall stand on the right hand through works of mercy? He not only then lifteth up from the mire him whom He is to place with the princes of His people; but also, "Maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children" : He who dwelleth on high, and beholdeth the humble things that are in heaven and earth, the seed of Abraham like the stars of heaven, holiness set on high in heavenly habitations; and like the sand on the sea shore, a merciful and countless multitude gathered together from the harmful waves, and the bitterness of impiety.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:1
verses.text: Psalm CXIV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:2
verses.text: The river Jordan, when they were entering across it into the land of promise, when touched by the feet of the priests who bore the Ark, stood still from above with bridled stream, while it flowed down from below, where it ran on into the sea, until the whole people passed over, the priests standing on the dry ground We know these things, but yet we should not imagine in this Psalm, to which we have now answered by chanting Allelujah, that it is the purpose of the Holy Spirit, that while we call to mind those deeds of the past, we should not consider things like unto them yet to take place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:3
verses.text: For "these things," as the Apostle saith, "happened unto them for ensamples".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:4
verses.text: "When Israel came out of Egypt, and the house of Jacob from among the strange people" , "Judah was His sanctuary, and Israel His dominion" ; "the sea saw that and fled, Jordan was driven back".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:5
verses.text: Think not that past deeds are related unto us, but rather that the future is predicted; since, while those miracles also were going on in that people, things present indeed were happening, but not without an intimation of things future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:6
verses.text: Some things he has related differently to what we have learnt and read there: that he might not truly be thought to be repeating past acts rather than to be prophesying future things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:7
verses.text: For in the first place, we read not that the Jordan was driven back, but that it stood still on the side nearest the source of its streams, while the people were passing through; next, we read not of the mountains and hills skipping: all which he hath added, and repeated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:8
verses.text: For after saying, "The sea saw that, and fled; Jordan was driven back:" he added, "The mountains skipped like rams, and the little hills like young sheep" : and then asketh, "What aileth thee, O thou sea, that thou fleddest: and thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven back?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:9
verses.text: "Ye mountains, that ye skipped like rams; and ye little hills, like young sheep?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:10
verses.text: Let us therefore consider what we are taught here; since both those deeds were typical of us, and these words exhort us to recognise ourselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:11
verses.text: For if we hold with a firm heart the grace of God which hath been given us, we are Israel, the seed of Abraham: unto us the Apostle saith, "Therefore are ye the seed of Abraham".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:12
verses.text: Let therefore no Christian consider himself alien to the name of Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:13
verses.text: For we are joined in the corner stone with those among the Jews who believed, among whom we find the Apostles chief.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:14
verses.text: Hence our Lord in another passage saith, "And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold; them also I must bring, that there may be one fold and one Shepherd".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:15
verses.text: The Christian people then is rather Israel, and the same is preferably the house of Jacob; for Israel and Jacob are the same.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:16
verses.text: But that multitude of Jews, which was deservedly reprobated for its perfidy, for the pleasures of the flesh sold their birthright, so that they belonged not to Jacob, but rather to Esau.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:17
verses.text: For ye know that it was said with this hidden meaning, "That the elder shall serve the younger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:18
verses.text: But Egypt, since it is said to mean affliction, or one who afflicteth, or one who oppresseth, is often used for an emblem of this world; from which we must spiritually withdraw, that we may not be bearing the yoke with unbelievers For thus each one becometh a fit citizen of the heavenly Jerusalem, when he hath first renounced this world; just as that people could not be led into the land of promise, save first they had departed from Egypt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:19
verses.text: But as they did not depart thence, until freed by Divine help; so no man is turned away in heart from this world, unless aided by the gift of the Divine mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:20
verses.text: For what was there once prefigured, the same is fulfilled in every faithful one in the daily travailings of the Church, in this end of the world, in this, as the blessed John writeth, last time Hear the Apostle the teacher of the Gentiles, thus instructing us: "I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; and were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea, and did all eat the same spiritual meat, and did all drink the same spiritual drink; for they drank of that spiritual rock that followed them, and that rock was Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:21
verses.text: But with many of them God was not well pleased, for they were overthrown in the wilderness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:22
verses.text: Now these things were our examples".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:23
verses.text: What more do ye wish, most beloved brethren? For it is surely clear, not from human conjecture, but from the declaration of an Apostle, that is, of God and our Lord: for God spoke in them, and though from clouds of flesh, yet it was God who thundered: surely then it is clear by so great testimony that all these things which were done in figure, are now fulfilled in our salvation; because then the future was predicted, now the past is read, and the present observed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:24
verses.text: Hear what is even more wonderful, that the hidden and veiled mysteries of the ancient books are in some degree revealed by the ancient books.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:25
verses.text: For Micah the prophet speaketh thus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:26
verses.text: "According to the days of thy coming out of Egypt will I show unto him marvellous things, etcIn this Psalm, therefore, although the wonderful spirit of prophecy doth look into the future, yet it seemeth, as it were, to be merely detailing to the past.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:27
verses.text: "Judah," he saith, "was His sanctuary: the sea saw that and fled:" "was," "saw," and "fled," are words of the past tense; and "Jordan was driven back, and the mountains skipped, and the earth trembled," in like manner have a past expression, without, however, any difficulty in understanding by them the future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:28
verses.text: For though it was so long after the departure of that people from Egypt, and so long before these seasons of the Church, that he sang what I have quoted; nevertheless, he witnesseth that he is foretelling the future without any question.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:29
verses.text: "According to the days," he saith, "of thy coming out of the land of Egypt will I show unto him marvellous things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:30
verses.text: "The nations shall see and be confounded".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:31
verses.text: This is what is here said, "The sea saw that, and fled:" for if in this passage, through words of the past tense the future is secretly revealed, as is the case; who would venture to explain the words, "shall see and be confounded," of past events? And a little lower down he alludeth more clearly than light itself to those very enemies of ours, who followed us flying, that they might slay us, that is, our sins, which are overwhelmed and extinguished in Baptism, just as the Egyptians were drowned in the sea, saying, since "He retaineth not His anger for ever, because He is of good will and merciful, He will turn again, He will have compassion upon us, He will drown our iniquities: and Thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:32
verses.text: What is it, most beloved? ye who know yourselves to be Israelites according to Abraham's seed, ye who are of the house of Jacob, heirs according to promise, know that even ye have gone forth from Egypt, since ye have renounced this world; that ye have gone forth from a foreign people, since by the confession of piety, ye have separated yourselves from the blasphemies of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:33
verses.text: For it is not your tongue, but a foreign one, which knoweth not how to praise God, to whom ye sing Allelujah.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:34
verses.text: For "Judah" hath become "His sanctuary" in you; for "he is not a Jew which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh; but he is a Jew which is one inwardly, and by circumcision of the heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:35
verses.text: Examine then your hearts, if faith hath circumcised them, if confession hath cleansed them; in you "Judah" hath become "His sanctuary," in you "Israel" hath become "His dominion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:36
verses.text: For "He gave" unto you "the power to become the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:37
verses.text: But I would not that ye should seek without yourselves, how the Jordan was turned back, I would not ye should augur anything evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:38
verses.text: For the Lord chideth those who have "turned" their "back" unto Him, "and not their face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:39
verses.text: And whoever forsaketh the source of his being, and turneth away from his Creator; as a river into the sea, he glides into the bitter wickedness of this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:40
verses.text: It is therefore good for him that he turn back, and that God whom he had set behind his back, may be before his face as he returneth; and that the sea of this world, which he had set before his face, when he was gliding on towards it, may become behind him; and that he may so forget what is behind him, that he may "reach forward to what is before him;" which is profitable for him when once converted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:41
verses.text: "Tremble, thou earth, at the presence of the Lord, at the presence of the God of Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:42
verses.text: What meaneth, "at the presence of the Lord," save at the presence of Him who said, "Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:43
verses.text: For the earth trembled; but because it had remained slothful, it was made to tremble, so that it might be more firmly fixed at the presence of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:44
verses.text: "Who turned the hard rock into standing waters, and the flint stone into springing wells".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:45
verses.text: For He melted Himself, and what may be called His hardness to water those who believe on Him, that He might in them become "a fountain of water gushing forth unto everlasting life;" because formerly, when He was not known, He seemed hard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:46
verses.text: Hence they who said, "This is an hard saying, who can bear it?" were confounded, and waited not until He should flow and stream upon them when the Scriptures were revealed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 114:47
verses.text: The rock, that hardness, was turned into pools of water, that stone into fountains of waters, when on His resurrection, "He expounded unto them, commencing with Moses and all the prophets, how Christ ought to suffer thus;" and sent the Holy Ghost, of whom He said, "If any man thirst, let him come unto Me, and drink".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:1
verses.text: Psalm CXV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:2
verses.text: "Not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but unto Thy Name give the praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:3
verses.text: For that grace of the water that gushed from the rock ("now that rock was Christ"), was not given on the score of works that had gone before, but of His mercy "that justifieth the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:4
verses.text: For "Christ died for sinners," that men might not seek any glory of their own, but in the Lord's Name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:5
verses.text: "For Thy loving mercy, and for Thy truth's sake".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:6
verses.text: Observe how often these two qualities, loving mercy and truth, are joined together in the holy Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:7
verses.text: For in His loving mercy He called sinners, and in His truth He judgeth those who when called refused to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:8
verses.text: "That the heathen may not say, Where is now their God?" For at the last, His loving mercy and truth will shine forth, when "the sign of the Son of man shall appear in heaven, and then shall all tribes of the earth cry woe;"  nor shall they then say, "Where is their God?" when He is no longer preached unto them to be believed in, but displayed before them to be trembled at.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:9
verses.text: "As for our God, He is in heaven above".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:10
verses.text: Not in heaven, where they see the sun and moon, works of God which they adore, but "in heaven above," which overpasseth all heavenly and earthly bodies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:11
verses.text: Nor is our God in heaven in such a sense, as to dread a fall that should deprive Him of His throne, if heaven were withdrawn from under Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:12
verses.text: "In heaven and earth He hath made whatsoever pleased Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:13
verses.text: Nor doth He stand in need of His own works, as if He had place in them where He might abide; but endureth in His own eternity, wherein He abideth and hath done whatsoever pleased Him, both in heaven and earth; for they did not support Him, as a condition of their being created by Him: since, unless they had been created, they could not have supported Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:14
verses.text: Therefore, in whatsoever He Himself dwelleth, He, so to speak, containeth this as in need of Himself, He is not contained by this as if He needed it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:15
verses.text: Or it may be thus understood: "In heaven and in earth He hath done whatsoever pleased Him," whether among the higher or the lower orders of His people, He hath made His grace His free gift, that no man may boast in the merits of his own works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:16
verses.text: "Their idols," he saith, "are silver and gold, even the work of men's hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:17
verses.text: That is, although we cannot display our God to your carnal eyes, whom ye ought to recognise through his works; yet be not seduced by your vain pretences, because ye can point with the finger to, the objects of your worship.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:18
verses.text: For it were much worthier for you not to have what to point to, than that your hearts' blindness should be displayed in what is exhibited to these eyes by you: for what do ye exhibit, save gold and silver? They have indeed both bronze, and wood, and earthenware idols, and of different materials of this description; but the Holy Spirit preferred mentioning the more precious material, because when every man hath blushed for that which he sets more by, he is much more easily turned away from the worship of meaner objects.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:19
verses.text: For it is said in another passage of Scripture concerning the worshippers of images, "Saying to a stock, Thou art my father; and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:20
verses.text: But lest that man who speaketh thus not to a stone or stock, but to gold and silver, seem wiser to himself; let him look this way, let him turn hitherwards the ear of his heart: "The idols of the Gentiles are gold and silver".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:21
verses.text: Nothing mean and contemptible is here mentioned: and indeed to that mind which is not earth, both gold and silver is earth, but more beautiful and brilliant, more solid and firm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:22
verses.text: Employ not then the hands of men, to create a false Deity out of that metal which a true God hath created; nay, a false man, whom thou mayest worship for a true God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:23
verses.text: "For they have mouths, and speak not: eyes have they, and see not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:24
verses.text: "They have ears, and hear not: noses have they, and smell not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:25
verses.text: "They have hands, and handle not; feet have they, and walk not; neither cry they through their throat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:26
verses.text: Even their artist therefore surpasseth them, since he had the faculty of moulding them by the motion and functions of his limbs: though thou wouldest be ashamed to worship that artist.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:27
verses.text: Even thou surpassest them, though thou hast not made these things, since thou doest what they cannot do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:28
verses.text: Even a beast doth excel them; for unto this it is added, "neither cry they through their throat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:29
verses.text: For after he had said above, "they have mouths, and speak not;" what need was there, after he had enumerated the limbs from head to feet, to repeat what he had said of their crying through their throat; unless, I suppose, because we perceive that what he mentioned of the other members, was common to men and beasts? For they see, and hear, and smell, and walk, and some, apes for instance, handle with hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:30
verses.text: But what he had said of the mouth, is peculiar to men: since beasts do not speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:31
verses.text: But that no one might refer what hath been said to the works of human members alone, and prefer men only to the gods of the heathen; after all this he added these words, "neither cry they through their throat:" which again is common to men and cattle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:32
verses.text: How much better then do mice and serpents, and other animals of like sort, judge of the idols of the heathen, so to speak, for they regard not the human figure in them when they see not the human life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:33
verses.text: For this reason they usually build nests in them, and unless they are deterred by human movements, they seek for themselves no safer habitations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:34
verses.text: A man then moveth himself, that he may frighten away a living beast from his own god; and yet worshippeth that god who cannot move himself, as if he were powerful, from whom he drove away one better than the object of his worship.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:35
verses.text: Even the dead surpasseth a deity who neither liveth nor hath lived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:36
verses.text: But they seem to themselves to have a purer religion, who say, I neither worship an idol, nor a devil; but in the bodily image I behold an emblem of that which I am bound to worship.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:37
verses.text: They presume to reply, that they worship not the bodies themselves, but the deities which preside over the government of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:38
verses.text: One sentence of the Apostle, therefore, testifieth to their punishment and condemnation; "Who," he saith, "have changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:39
verses.text: For in the former part of this sentence he condemned idols; in the latter, the account they give of their idols: for by designating images wrought by an artificer by the names of the works of God's creation, they change the truth of God into a lie; while, by considering these works themselves as deities, and worshipping them as such, they serve the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:40
verses.text: But, it will be said, we also have very many instruments and vessels made of materials or metal of this description for the purpose of celebrating the Sacraments, which being consecrated by these ministrations are called holy, in honour of Him who is thus worshipped for our salvation: and what indeed are these very instruments or vessels, but the work of men's hands? But have they mouth, and yet speak not? have they eyes, and see not? do we pray unto them, because through them we pray to God? This is the chief cause of this insane profanity, that the figure resembling the living person, which induces men to worship it, hath more influence in the minds of these miserable persons, than the evident fact that it is not living, so that it ought to be despised by the living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:41
verses.text: The result that ensueth is that described in the next verse: "They that make them are like unto them, and so are all such as put their trust in them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:42
verses.text: Let them therefore see with open eyes, and worship with shut and dead understandings, idols that neither see nor live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:43
verses.text: "But the house of Israel hath hoped in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:44
verses.text: "For hope that is seen is not hope; for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for? But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:45
verses.text: But that this patience may endure to the end, "He is their helper and defender".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:46
verses.text: Do perhaps spiritual persons (by whom carnal minds are built up in "the spirit of meekness," because they pray as higher for lower minds) already see, and is that already to them reality which to the lower is hope? It is not so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:47
verses.text: For even "the house of Aaron hath hope in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:48
verses.text: Therefore, that they also may stretch forward perseveringly towards those things which are before them, and may run perseveringly, until they may apprehend that for which they are apprehended,  and may know even as they are known, "He is their helper and defender".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:49
verses.text: For both "fear the Lord, and have hoped in the Lord: He is their helper and defender".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:50
verses.text: For we do not by our deservings prevent the mercy of God; but, "The Lord hath been mindful of us, and hath blessed us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:51
verses.text: He hath blessed the house of Israel, He hath blessed the house of Aaron".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:52
verses.text: But in blessing both of these, "He hath blessed all that fear the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:53
verses.text: Dost thou ask, who are meant by both of these? He answereth, "both small and great".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:54
verses.text: That is, the house of Israel with the house of Aaron, those who among that nation believed in Jesus the Saviour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:55
verses.text: For in the character of those who out of that nation believed, it is said, "Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha".
