verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:56
verses.text: Seed, because when it has been scattered over the earth, it multiplied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:57
verses.text: For the great ones, of the house of Aaron, have said, "May the Lord increase you more and more, you and your children".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:58
verses.text: And thus it hath happened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:59
verses.text: For children that have been raised even from the stones have flocked unto Abraham: sheep which were not of this fold, have flocked unto him, that there might be one flock, and one shepherd; the faith of all nations was added, and the number grew, not only of wise priests, but of obedient peoples; the Lord increasing not only their fathers more and more, who in Christ might show the way to the rest who should imitate them, but also their children, who should follow their fathers' pious footsteps.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:60
verses.text: Therefore the Prophet saith unto these great and small, the mountains and the little hills, the rams and the young sheep, what followeth: "Ye are the blessed of the Lord, who made heaven and earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:61
verses.text: As if he should say, Ye are the blessed of the Lord, who made the heaven in the great, earth in the small: not this visible heaven, studded with luminaries which are objects to these eyes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:62
verses.text: For "The heaven of heavens is the Lord's" ; who hath elevated the minds of some saints to such a height, that they became teachable by no man, but by God Himself; in comparison of which heaven, whatever is discerned with carnal eyes is to be called earth; which "He hath given to the children of men;" that when it is contemplated, whether in that region which illumineth above, as that which is called heaven, or in that which is illumined beneath, which is properly called earth (since in comparison with that which is called heaven of heaven, the whole, as we have said, is earth;) the whole therefore of this earth He hath given to the children of men, that by the consideration of it, as far as they can, they may conceive of the Creator, whom with their yet weak hearts they cannot see without that aid to their conception.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:63
verses.text: But nevertheless since they derive the truth and richness of wisdom, not from man nor through man, but through God Himself, they have received little ones who shall be heaven, that they may know that they are heaven of heaven; as yet however earth, unto which they say, "I have planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:64
verses.text: For to those very sons of men whom He made heaven, He who knoweth how to provide for the earth through heaven, hath given earth upon which they work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:65
verses.text: May they therefore abide, heaven and earth, in their God, who made them, and let them live from Him, confessing unto Him, and praising Him; for if they choose to live from themselves, they shall die, as it is written, "From the dead, as though he were not, confession ceaseth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:66
verses.text: But, "The dead praise not Thee, O Lord, neither all they that go down into silence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:67
verses.text: For the Scripture in another passage proclaimeth, "The sinner, when he cometh into the abyss of wickednesses, scorneth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 115:68
verses.text: "But we, who live, will praise the Lord, from this time forth for evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:1
verses.text: Psalm CXVI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:2
verses.text: "I have loved, since the Lord will hear the voice of my prayer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:3
verses.text: Let the soul that is sojourning in absence from the Lord sing thus, let that sheep which had strayed sing thus, let that son who had "died and returned to life," who had "been lost and was found;" let our soul sing thus, brethren, and most beloved sons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:4
verses.text: Let us be taught, and let us abide, and let us sing thus with the Saints: "I have loved: since the Lord will hear the voice of my prayer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:5
verses.text: Is this a reason for having loved, that the Lord will hear the voice of my prayer? and do we not rather love, because He hath heard, or that He may hear? What then meaneth, "I have loved, since the Lord will hear"? Doth he, because hope is wont to inflame love, say that he hath loved, since he hath hoped that God will listen to the voice of his prayer?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:6
verses.text: But whence hath he hoped for this? Since, he saith, "He hath inclined His ear unto me: and in my days I have called upon Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:7
verses.text: I loved, therefore, because He will hear; He will hear, "because He hath inclined His ear unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:8
verses.text: But whence knowest thou, O human soul, that God hath inclined His ear unto thee, except thou sayest, "I have believed"? These three things, therefore, "abide, faith, hope, charity:" because thou hast believed, thou hast hoped; because thou hast hoped, thou hast loved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:9
verses.text: And what are thy days, since thou hast said, "In my days I have called upon Him"? Are they those perchance, in which "the fulness of time came," and "God sent His Son," who had already said, "In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee"?I may rather call my days the days of my misery, the days of my mortality, the days according to Adam, full of toil and sweat, the days accor ding to the ancient corruption.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:10
verses.text: "For I lying, stuck fast in the deep mire," in another Psalm also have cried out, "Behold, Thou hast made my days old;" in these days of mine have I called upon Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:11
verses.text: For my days are different from the days of my Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:12
verses.text: I call those my days, which by my own daring I have made for myself, whereby I have forsaken Him: and, since He reigneth everywhere, and is all-powerful, and holdeth all things, I have deserved prison; that is, I have received the darkness of ignorance, and the bonds of mortality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:13
verses.text: For in these days of mine, "The snares of death compassed me round about, and the pains of hell gat hold upon me" : pains that would not have overtaken me, had I not wandered from Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:14
verses.text: But now they have overtaken me; but I found them not, while I was rejoicing in the prosperity of the world, in which the snares of hell deceive the more.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:15
verses.text: But after "I too found trouble and heaviness, I called upon the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:16
verses.text: For trouble and profitable sorrow I did not feel; trouble, wherein He giveth aid, unto whom it is said, "O be Thou our help in trouble: and vain is the help of man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:17
verses.text: For I thought I might rejoice and exult in the vain help of man; but when I had heard from my Lord, "Blessed are they that mourn, for they shall be comforted:" I did not wait until I should lose those temporal blessings in which I rejoiced, and should then mourn: but I gave heed to that very misery of mine which caused me to rejoice in such things, which I both feared to lose, and yet could not retain; I gave heed to it firmly and courageously, and I saw that I was not only agonized by the adversities of this world, but even bound by its good fortune; and thus "I found the trouble and heaviness" which had escaped me, "and called upon the Name of the Lord; O Lord, I beseech Thee, deliver my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:18
verses.text: Let then the holy people of God say, "I called upon the Name of the Lord:" and let the remainder of the heathen hear, who do not as yet call upon the Name of the Lord; let them hear and seek, that they may discover trouble and heaviness, and may call upon the Name of the Lord, and be saved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:19
verses.text: "Gracious is the Lord, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:20
verses.text: He is gracious, righteous, and merciful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:21
verses.text: Gracious in the first place, because He hath inclined His ear unto me; and I knew not that the ear of God had approached my lips, till I was aroused by those beautiful feet, that I might call upon the Lord's Name: for who hath called upon Him, save he whom He first called? Hence therefore He is in the first place "gracious;" but "righteous," because He scourgeth; and again, "merciful," because He receiveth; for "He scourgeth every son whom He receiveth;" nor ought it to be so bitter to me that He scourgeth, as sweet that He receiveth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:22
verses.text: For how should not "The Lord, who keepeth little ones" , scourge those whom, when of mature age, He seeketh to be heirs; "for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?"  "I was in misery, and He helped me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:23
verses.text: He helped me, because I was in misery; for the pain which the physician causeth by his knife is not penal, but salutary.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:24
verses.text: "Turn again then unto thy rest, O my soul; for the Lord hath done good to thee" : not for thy deservings, or through thy strength; but because the Lord hath done good to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:25
verses.text: "Since," he saith, "He hath delivered my soul from death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:26
verses.text: It is wonderful, most beloved brethren, that, after he had said that his soul should turn unto rest, since the Lord had rewarded him; he added, since "He hath delivered my soul from death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:27
verses.text: Did it turn unto rest, because it was delivered from death? Is not rest more usually said of death? What is the action of him whose life is rest, and death disquietude? Such then ought to be the action of the soul, as may tend to a quiet security, not one that may increase restless toil; since He hath delivered it from death, who, pitying it, said, "Come unto Me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest," etc Meek therefore and humble, following, so to speak, Christ as its path, should the action of the soul be that tendeth towards repose; nevertheless, not slothful and supine; that it may finish its course, as it is written, "In quietness make perfect thy works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:28
verses.text: "Thou hast delivered my soul from death, mine eyes from tears, and my feet from falling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:29
verses.text: Whoever feeleth the chain of this flesh, chanteth these things as fulfilled in hope towards himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:30
verses.text: For it is truly said, "I was in misery, and He delivered me;" but the Apostle saith this also truly, that we are saved by hope And that we are delivered from death, is well said to be already fulfilled, so that we may understand the death of unbelievers, of whom he saith, "Leave the dead to bury their dead".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:31
verses.text: He will then clear our eyes of tears, when He shall save our feet from falling.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:32
verses.text: For there will then be no slipping of our feet as they walk, when there will be no sliding of the weak flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:33
verses.text: But now, however firm our path, which is Christ, be; yet since we place flesh, which we are enjoined to subdue, beneath us; in the very work of chastening and subduing it, it is a great thing not to fall: but not to slip in the flesh, who can attain? "I shall please in the sight of the Lord, in the land of the living".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:34
verses.text: We "labour" indeed now, because we are awaiting "the redemption of our body:" but, "when death shall have been swallowed up in victory, and this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal immortality;" then there will be no weeping, because there will be no falling; and no falling, because no corruption.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:35
verses.text: And therefore we shall then no longer labour to please, but we shall be entirely pleasing in the sight of the Lord, in the land of the living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:36
verses.text: "I believed," saith he, "and therefore did I speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:37
verses.text: But I was sorely brought down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:38
verses.text: For he suffered many tribulations, for the sake of the word which he faithfully held, faithfully preached; and he was sorely brought down; as they feared who loved the praise of men better than that of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:39
verses.text: But what meaneth, "But I"? He should rather say, I believed, and therefore I have spoken, and I was sorely brought down: why did he add, "But I," save because a man may be sorely brought down by those who oppose the truth, the truth itself cannot, which he believeth and speaketh? Whence also the Apostle, when he was speaking of his chain, saith, "the word of God is not bound".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:40
verses.text: So this man also, since there is one person of the holy witnesses, that is, of the Martyrs of God, saith, "I believed, and therefore will I speak".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:41
verses.text: "But I;" not that which I believed, not the word which I have delivered; "but I was sorely brought down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:42
verses.text: "I said in my trance, All men are liars".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:43
verses.text: By trance he meaneth fear, which when persecutors threaten, and when the sufferings of to rture or death impend, human weakness suffereth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:44
verses.text: For this we understand, because in this Psalm the voice of Martyrs is heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:45
verses.text: For trance is used in another sense also, when the mind is not beside itself by fear, but is possessed by some inspiration of revelation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:46
verses.text: "But I said in my haste, All men are liars".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:47
verses.text: In consternation he hath had regard to his infirmity, and hath seen that he ought not to presume on himself; for as far as pertaineth to the man himself, he is a liar, but by the grace of God he is made true; lest yielding to the pressure of his enemies he might not speak what he had believed, but might deny it; even as it happened to Peter, since he had trusted in himself, and was to be taught that we ought not to trust in man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:48
verses.text: And if every one ought not to trust in man, surely not in himself; because he is a man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:49
verses.text: Rightly therefore in his fear did he perceive that every man was a liar; since they also whom no fear robs of their presence of mind, so that they never lie by yielding to the persecutors, are such by the gifts of God, not by their own strength.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:50
verses.text: "What," he asketh, "what reward shall I give unto the Lord, for all the benefits that He hath returned unto me?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:51
verses.text: He saith not, for all the benefits that He hath done unto me but "for all the benefits that He hath returned unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:52
verses.text: What deeds then on the man's part had preceded, that all the benefits of God were not said to be given, but returned? What had preceded, on the man's part, save sins? God therefore repayeth good for evil, whilst unto Him men repay evil for good; for such was the return of those who said, "This is the heir: come, let us kill him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:53
verses.text: But this man seeketh what he may return unto the Lord, and findeth not, save out of those things which the Lord Himself returneth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:54
verses.text: "I will receive," he saith, "the cup of salvation, and call upon the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:55
verses.text: "My vows will I render to the Lord, before all His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:56
verses.text: Who hath given thee the cup of salvation, which when thou takest, and callest upon the Name of the Lord, thou shalt return unto Him a reward for all that He hath returned unto thee? Who, save He who saith, "Are ye able to drink the cup that I shall drink of?" Who hath given unto thee to imitate His sufferings, save He who hath suffered before for thee? And therefore, "Right dear in the sight of the Lord is the death of His Saints".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:57
verses.text: He purchased it by His Blood, which He first shed for the salvation of slaves, that they might not hesitate to shed their blood for the Lord's Name; which, nevertheless, would be profitable for their own interests, not for those of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:58
verses.text: Let therefore the slave purchased at so great a price confess his condition, and say, "Behold, O Lord, how that I am Thy servant: "I am Thy servant, and the son of Thine handmaid".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:59
verses.text: This, therefore, is the son of the heavenly Jerusalem, which is above, the free mother of us all And free indeed from sin she is, but the handmaid of righteousness; to whose sons still pilgrims it is said, "Ye have been called unto liberty;" and again he maketh them servants, when he saith, "but by love serve one another".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:60
verses.text: Let therefore that servant say unto God, Many call themselves martyrs, many Thy servants, because they hold Thy Name in various heresies and errors; but since they are beside Thy Church, they are not the children of Thy handmaid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:61
verses.text: But "I am Thy servant, and the son of Thine handmaid".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:62
verses.text: "Thou hast broken my bonds asunder".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:63
verses.text: "I will offer to Thee the sacrifice of praise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:64
verses.text: For I have not found any deserts of mine, since Thou hast broken my bonds asunder; I therefore owe Thee the sacrifice of praise; because, although I will boast that I am Thy servant, and the son of Thy handmaid, I will glory not in myself, but in Thee, my Lord, who hast broken asunder my bonds, that when I return from my desertion, I may again be bound unto Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:65
verses.text: "I will pay my vows unto the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:66
verses.text: What vows wilt thou pay? What victims hast thou vowed? what burnt-offerings, what holocausts? Dost thou refer to what thou hast said a little before, "I will receive the cup of salvation, and will call upon the Name of the Lord;" and, "I will offer to Thee the sacrifice of thanksgiving"? and indeed whosoever well considereth what he is vowing to the Lord, and what vows he is paying, let him vow himself, let him pay himself as a vow: this is exacted, this is due.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:67
verses.text: On looking at the coin, the Lord saith, "Render unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's, and unto God the things which are God's:" his own image is rendered unto Caesar: let His image be rendered unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:68
verses.text: "In the courts," he saith, "of the Lord's house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:69
verses.text: What is the Lord's house, the same is the Lord's handmaid: and what is God's house, save all His people? It therefore followeth, "In the sight of all His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:70
verses.text: And now he more openly nameth his mother herself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:71
verses.text: For what else is His people, but what followeth, "In the midst of thee, O Jerusalem"? For than that which is returned grateful, if it be returned from peace, and in peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 116:72
verses.text: But they who are not sons of this handmaid, have loved war rather than peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 117:1
verses.text: Psalm CXVII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 117:2
verses.text: "O praise the Lord, all ye heathen: praise Him, all ye nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 117:3
verses.text: These are the courts of the Lord's house, this all His people, this the true Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 117:4
verses.text: Let those rather listen who have refused to be the children of this city, since they have cut themselves off from the communion of all nations "For His merciful kindness is ever more and more towards us: and the truth of the Lord endureth  for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 117:5
verses.text: These are those two things, loving-kindness and truth, which in the CXVth Psalm I admonished you should be committed to memory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 117:6
verses.text: But "the merciful kindness of the Lord is ever more and more towards us," since the furious tongues of hostile nations have yielded to His Name, through which we have been freed: "and the truth of the Lord endureth for ever," whether in those things which He promised to the righteous, or in those which He hath threatened to the ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:1
verses.text: Psalm CXVIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:2
verses.text: We are taught in this Psalm, when we chaunt Allelujah, which meaneth, Praise the Lord, that we should, when we hear the words, "Confess unto the Lord" , praise the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:3
verses.text: The praise of God could not be expressed in fewer words than these, "For He is good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:4
verses.text: I see not what can be more solemn than this brevity, since goodness is so peculiarly the quality of God, that the Son of God Himself when addressed by some one as "Good Master," by one, namely, who beholding His flesh, and comprehending not the fulness of His divine nature, considered Him as man only, replied, "Why callest thou Me good? There is none good but one, that is, God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:5
verses.text: And what is this but to say, If thou wishest to call Me good, recognise Me as God? But since it is addressed, in revelation of things to come, to a people freed from all toil and wandering in pilgrimage, and from all admixture with the wicked, which freedom was given it through the grace of God, who not only doth not evil for evil, but even returneth good for evil; it is most appropriately added, "Because His mercy endureth for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:6
verses.text: "Let Israel now confess that He is good, and that His mercy endureth for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:7
verses.text: "Let the house of Aaron now confess that His mercy endureth for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:8
verses.text: "Yea, let all now that fear the Lord confess that His mercy endureth for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:9
verses.text: Ye remember, I suppose, most beloved, what is the house of Israel, what is the house of Aaron, and that both are those th at fear the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:10
verses.text: For they are "the little and the great," who have already in another Psalm been happily introduced into your hearts: in the number of whom all of us should rejoice that we are joined together, in His grace who is good, and whose mercy endureth for ever; since they were listened to who said, "May the Lord increase you more and more, you and your children;" that the host of the Gentiles might be added to the Israelites who believed in Christ, of the number of whom are the Apostles our fathers, for the exaltation of the perfect and the obedience of the little children; that all of us when made one in Christ, made one flock under one Shepherd, and the body of that Head, like one man, may say, "I called upon the Lord in trouble, and the Lord heard me at large".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:11
verses.text: The narrow straits of our tribulation are limited: but the large way whereby we pass along hath no end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:12
verses.text: "Who shall lay anything to the charge of God's elect?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:13
verses.text: "The Lord is my helper; I will not fear what man doeth unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:14
verses.text: But are men, then, the only enemies that the Church hath? What is a man devoted to flesh and blood, save flesh and blood? But the Apostle saith, "We wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against,"he saith, "spiritual wickedness in high places;" that is, the devil and his angels; that devil whom elsewhere he calleth "the prince of the power of the air".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:15
verses.text: Hear therefore what followeth: "The Lord is my helper: therefore shall I despise mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:16
verses.text: From what class soever my enemies may arise, whether from the number of evil men, or from the number of evil angels; in the Lord's help, unto whom we chant the confession of praise, unto whom we sing Allelujah, they shall be despised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:17
verses.text: But, when my enemies have been brought to contempt, let not my friend present himself unto me as a good man, so as to bid me repose my hope in himself: for "It is better to trust in the Lord, than to put any confidence in man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:18
verses.text: Nor let any one, who may in a certain sense be styled a good angel, be regarded by myself as one in whom I ought to put my trust: for "no one is good, save God alone;"  and when a man or an angel appear to aid us, when they do this of sincere affection, He doth it through them, who made them good after their measure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:19
verses.text: "It is" therefore "better to trust in the Lord, than to put any confidence in princes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:20
verses.text: For angels also are called princes, even as we read in Daniel, "Michael, your prince".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:21
verses.text: "All nations compassed me round about, but in the Name of the Lord have I taken vengeance on them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:22
verses.text: "They kept me in on every side, they kept me in, I say, on every side; but in the Name of the Lord have I taken vengeance on them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:23
verses.text: He signifieth the toils and the victory of the Church; but, as if the question were asked how she could have overcome so great evils, he looketh back to the example, and declareth what she had first suffered in her Head, by adding what followeth, "They kept me in on every side:" and the words, "All nations," are with reason not repeated here, because this was the act of the Jews alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:24
verses.text: There that very religious nation (which is the body of Christ, and in behalf of which was done all that was done in mortal form with immortal power, by that inward divinity, through the outward flesh), suffered from persecutors, of whose race that flesh was assumed and hung upon the cross.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:25
verses.text: "They came about me as bees do a hive, and burned up even as the fire among the thorns: and in the Name of the Lord have I taken vengeance on them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:26
verses.text: Here then the order of the words corresponds with the order of events.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:27
verses.text: For we rightly understand that our Lord Himself, the Head of the Church, was surrounded by persecutors, even as bees surround a hive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:28
verses.text: For the Holy Spirit is speaking with mystic subtlety of what was done by those who knew not what they did.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:29
verses.text: For bees make honey in the hives: while our Lord's persecutors, unconscious as they were, rendered Him sweeter unto us even by His very Passion; so that we may taste and see how sweet is the Lord, "Who died for our sins, and arose for our justification".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:30
verses.text: But what followeth, "and burned up even as the fire among the thorns," is better understood of His Body, that is, of a people spread abroad, whom all nations compassed about, since it was gathered together from all nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:31
verses.text: They consumed this sinful flesh, and the grievous piercings of this mortal life, in the flame of persecution.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:32
verses.text: "Taken vengeance on them:" either because they themselves, that wickedness, which in them persecuted the righteous, having been extinguished, were joined with the people of Christ; or because the rest of them, who have at this time scorned the mercy of Him who calleth them, will at the end feel the truth of Him who judgeth them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:33
verses.text: "I have been driven on like a heap of sand, so that I was falling, but the Lord upheld me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:34
verses.text: For though there were a great multitude of believers, that might be compared to the countless sand, and brought into one communion as into one heap; yet "what is man, save Thou be mindful of Him?" He said not, the multitude of the Gentiles could not surpass the abundance of my host, but, "the Lord," he saith, "hath upheld me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:35
verses.text: The persecution of the Gentiles succeeded not in pushing forward, to its overthrow, the host of the faithful dwelling together in the unity of the faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:36
verses.text: "The Lord is my strength and my praise, and is become my salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:37
verses.text: Who then fall, when they are pushed, save they who choose to be their own strength and their own praise? For no man falleth in the contest, except he whose strength and praise faileth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:38
verses.text: He therefore whose strength and praise is the Lord, falleth no more than the Lord falleth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:39
verses.text: And for this reason He hath become their salvation; not that He hath become anything which He was not before, but because they, when they believed on Him, became what they were not before, and then He began to be salvation unto them when turned towards Him, which He was not to them when turned away from Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:40
verses.text: "The voice of joy and health is in the dwellings of the righteous" ; where they who raged against their bodies thought there was the voice of sorrow and destruction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:41
verses.text: For they did not know the inward joy of the saints in their future hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:42
verses.text: Whence the Apostle also saith, "As sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing;" and again, "And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:43
verses.text: "The right hand of the Lord hath brought mighty things to pass".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:44
verses.text: What mighty things? saith he.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:45
verses.text: "The right hand of the Lord," he saith, "hath exalted me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:46
verses.text: It is a mighty thing to exalt the humble, to deify the mortal, to bring perfection out of infirmity, glory from subjection, victory from suffering, to give help, to raise from trouble; that the true salvation of God might be laid open to the afflicted, and the salvation of men might remain of no avail to the persecutors.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:47
verses.text: These are great things: but what art thou surprised at? hear what he repeateth: "The right hand of the Lord hath brought mighty things to pass".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:48
verses.text: "I shall not die, but live, and declare the works of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:49
verses.text: But they, while they were dealing havoc and death on every side, thought that the Church of Christ was dying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:50
verses.text: Behold, he now declareth the works of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:51
verses.text: Everywhere Christ is the glory of the blessed Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:52
verses.text: By being beaten He conquered those who struck Him; by being patient of torments, the tormentors; by loving, those who raged against Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:53
verses.text: Nevertheless, let him point out to us, why the body of Christ, the holy Church, the people of adoption, suffered such indignities.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:54
verses.text: "The Lord," he saith, "hast chastened and corrected me, but He hath not given me over unto death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:55
verses.text: Let not then the boastful wicked imagine that aught hath been permitted to their power: they would not have that power, were it not given them from above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:56
verses.text: Oft doth the father of a family command his sons to be corrected by the most worthless slaves; though he designeth the heritage for the former, fetters for the latter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:57
verses.text: What is that heritage? Is it of gold, or silver, or jewels, or farms, or pleasant estates? Consider how we enter into it: and learn what it is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:58
verses.text: "Open me," he saith, "the gates of righteousness" (ver ).

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:59
verses.text: Behold, we have heard of the gates.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:60
verses.text: What is within? "That I may," he saith, "go into them, and give thanks unto the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:61
verses.text: This is the confession of praise full of wonder, "even unto the house of God, in the voice of joy and confession of praise, among such as keep holiday:" this is the everlasting bliss of the righteous, whereby they are blessed who dwell in the Lord's house, praising Him for evermore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:62
verses.text: But consider how the gates of righteousness are entered into.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:63
verses.text: "These are the gates of the Lord" he saith, "the righteous shall enter into them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:64
verses.text: At least let no wicked man enter there, that Jerusalem which receiveth not one uncircumcised, where it is said, "Without are dogs".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:65
verses.text: Be it enough, that in my long pilgrimage "I have had my habitation among the tents of Kedar:" I endured even unto the end the intercourse of the wicked, but "these are the gates of the Lord: the righteous shall enter into them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:66
verses.text: "I will confess unto Thee, O Lord, for Thou hast heard me, and art become my salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:67
verses.text: How often is that confession proved to be one of praise, that doth not point out wounds to the physician, but giveth thanks for the health it hath received.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:68
verses.text: But the Physician Himself is the Salvation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:69
verses.text: But who is this whom we speak of? "The Stone which the builders rejected" ; for "It hath become the head Stone of the corner" to "make in Himself of twain one new man, so making peace; and that He might reconcile both unto God in one body;" circumcision, to wit, and uncircumcision.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:70
verses.text: "By the Lord was it made unto it" : that is, it is made into the head stone of the corner by the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:71
verses.text: For although He would not have become this, had He not suffered: yet He became not this through those from whom He suffered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:72
verses.text: For they who were building, refused Him: but in the edifice which the Lord was secretly raising, that was made the head stone of the corner which they rejected.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:73
verses.text: "And it is marvellous in our eyes:" in the eyes of the inner man, in the eyes of those that believe, those that hope, those that love; not in the carnal eyes of those who, through scorning Him as if He were a man, rejected Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:74
verses.text: "This is the day which the Lord hath made".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:75
verses.text: This man remembereth that he had said in former Psalms, "Since He hath inclined His ear unto me, therefore will I call upon Him as long as I live;" making mention of his old days; whence he now saith, "This is the day which the Lord hath made;" that is, wherein He hath given me Salvation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:76
verses.text: This is the day whereof He said, "In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of Salvation have I helped thee;" that is, a day wherein He, the Mediator, hath become the head Stone of the corner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:77
verses.text: "Let us rejoice," therefore, "and be glad in Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:78
verses.text: "Save me now, O Lord: prosper Thou well my way, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:79
verses.text: Because it is the day of Salvation, "save me:" because we, returning from a long pilgrimage, are separated from those who hated peace, with whom we were peaceful, and who, when we spoke to them, made war upon us without a cause; "prosper well our way" as we return, since Thou hast become our Way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:80
verses.text: "Blessed be He that cometh in the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:81
verses.text: Cursed, therefore, is he that cometh in his own name; as He saith in the Gospel: "if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:82
verses.text: "We have blessed you out of the house of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:83
verses.text: I believe that these are the words of the great to the little, of those great ones, to wit, who in spirit commune with God the Word, who is with God, as they may in this life; and yet temper their discourse for the sake of the little ones, so that they may sincerely say what the Apostle saith: "For whether we be beside ourselves, it is to God: or whether we be sober, it is for your cause.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:84
verses.text: For the love of Christ constraineth us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:85
verses.text: They bless the little children from the inner house of the Lord, where that praise faileth not age after age: consider therefore what they proclaim from thence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:86
verses.text: "God is the Lord, who hath showed us light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:87
verses.text: That Lord, who came in the Lord's Name, whom the builders refused, and who became the head Stone of the corner, that "Mediator between God and man, Jesus Christ," is God, He is equal with the Father, He hath showed us light, that we might understand what we believed, and declare it to you who understand it not as yet, but already believe it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:88
verses.text: But that ye also may understand, "Declare a holy day in full assemblies, even unto the horns of the altar;" that is, even unto the inner house of God, from which we have blessed you, where are the high places of the altar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:89
verses.text: "Declare a holy day," not in a slothful manner, but "in full assemblies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:90
verses.text: For this is the voice of joyfulness among those that keep holy day, who walk "in the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even unto the house of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:91
verses.text: For if there be there the spiritual sacrifice, the everlasting sacrifice of praise, both the Priest is everlasting, and the peaceful mind of the righteous an everlasting altar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:92
verses.text: And what shall we sing there, save His praises? What else shall we say there, save, "Thou art my God, and I will confess unto Thee; Thou art my God, and I will praise Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:93
verses.text: I wilt confess unto Thee, for Thou hast heard me, and art become my Salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:94
verses.text: We will not say these things in loud words; but the love that abideth in Him of itself crieth out in these words, and these words are love itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:95
verses.text: Thus as he began with praise, so he endeth: "Conf ess unto the Lord, for He is gracious, and His mercy endureth for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:96
verses.text: With this the Psalm commenceth, with this it endeth; since, as from the commencement which we have left behind, so in the end, whither we are returning, there is not anything that can more profitably please us, than the praise of God, and Allelujah evermore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 118:97
verses.text: Contents   Aleph  Beth  Gimel  Daleth  He  Vav  Zain  Cheth  Teth  Jod  Caph  Lamed  Mem  Nun  Samech  Ain  Pe  Tadze  Koph  Resch  Schin  Tau.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:1
verses.text: Psalm CXIX  Aleph.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:2
verses.text: From its commencement, dearly beloved, doth this great Psalm exhort us unto bliss, which there is no one who desireth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:3
verses.text: And therefore this is the lesson which he teacheth, who saith, "Blessed are those that are undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:4
verses.text: As much as to say, I know what thou wishest, thou art seeking bliss: if then thou wouldest be blessed, be undefiled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:5
verses.text: For the former all desire, the latter fear: yet without it what all wish cannot be attained.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:6
verses.text: But where will any one be undefiled, save in the way? In what way, save in the law of the Lord?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:7
verses.text: Listen now to what he addeth: "Blessed are they that keep His testimonies, and seek Him with their whole heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:8
verses.text: No other class of the blessed seemeth to me to be mentioned in these words, than that which has been already spoken of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:9
verses.text: For to examine into the testimonies of the Lord, and to seek Him with all the heart, this is to be undefiled in the way, this is to walk in the law of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:10
verses.text: He then goeth on to say, "For they who do wickedness, shall not walk in His ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:11
verses.text: And yet we know that the workers of wickedness do search the testimonies of the Lord for this reason, that they prefer being learned to being righteous: we know that others also search the testimonies of the Lord, not because they are already living well, but that they may know how they ought to live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:12
verses.text: Such then do not as yet walk undefiled in the law of the Lord, and for this reason are not as yet blessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:13
verses.text: It is written, and is read, and is true, in this Psalm, that "They who do wickedness, walk not in His ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:14
verses.text: But we must endeavour, with the help of God, "in" whose "hand are both we and our words," that what is rightly said, by not being rightly understood, may not confuse the reader or hearer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:15
verses.text: For we must beware, lest all the Saints, whose words these are, "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us;" may either not be thought to walk in the ways of the Lord, since sin is wickedness, and "they who do wickedness, walk not in His ways;" or, because it is not doubtful that they walk in the ways of the Lord, may be thought to have no sin, which is beyond doubt false.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:16
verses.text: For it is not said merely for the sake of avoiding arrogance and pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:17
verses.text: Otherwise it would not be added, "And the truth is not in us;" but it would be said, Humility is not in us: especially because the following words throw a clearer light on the meaning, and remove all the causes of doubt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:18
verses.text: For when the blessed John had said this, he added, "If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:19
verses.text: What meaneth, "Thou hast charged that we shall keep Thy commandments too much"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:20
verses.text: Is it, "Thou hast charged too much"? or, "to keep too much"? Whichever of these we understand, the sense seems contrary to that memorable and noble sentiment which the Greeks praise in their wise men, and which the Latins agree in praising.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:21
verses.text: "Do nothing too much".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:22
verses.text: But the Latin language sometimes uses the word nimis in such a sense, that we find it in the holy Scripture, and employ it in our discourses, as signifying, very much.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:23
verses.text: In this passage, "Thou hast charged that we keep Thy commandments too much," we simply understand very much, if we understand rightly; and if we say to any very dear friend, I love you too much, we do not wish to be understood to mean more than is fitting, but very much.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:24
verses.text: "O that," he saith, "my ways were made so direct, that I might keep Thy statutes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:25
verses.text: Thou indeed hast charged: O that I could realize what thou hast charged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:26
verses.text: When thou hearest, "O that," recognise the words of one wishing; and having recognised the expression of a wish, lay aside the pride of presumption.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:27
verses.text: For who saith that he desireth what he hath in such a manner in his power, that without need of any help he can do it? Therefore if man desireth what God chargeth, God must be prayed to grant Himself what He enjoineth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:28
verses.text: "So shall I not be confounded, while I have respect unto all Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:29
verses.text: We ought to look upon the commandments of God, whether when they are read, or when they are recalled to memory, as a looking-glass, as the Apostle James saith This man wisheth himself to be such, that he may regard as in a mirror the commandments of God, and may not be confounded; because he chooses not merely to be a hearer of them, but a doer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:30
verses.text: On this account he desireth that his ways may be made direct to keep the statutes of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:31
verses.text: How to be made direct, save by the grace of God? Otherwise he will find in the law of God not a source of rejoicing, but of confusion, if he hath chosen to look into commandments, which he doth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:32
verses.text: "I will confess unto Thee," he saith, "O Lord, in the directing of my heart; in that I shall have learned the judgments of Thy righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:33
verses.text: This is not the confession of sins, but of praise; as He also saith in whom there was no sin, "I will confess unto Thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth;" and as it is written in the Book of Ecclesiasticus, "Thus shalt thou say in confession, of all the works of God, that they are very good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:34
verses.text: "I will confess unto Thee," he saith, "in the directing of my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:35
verses.text: Indeed, if my ways are made straight, I will confess unto Thee, since Thou hast done it, and this is Thy praise, and not mine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:36
verses.text: Next he addeth: "I will keep Thy ordinances".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:37
verses.text: But what is it that followeth? "O forsake me not even exceedingly!" or, as some copies have it, "even too much," instead of, "even exceedingly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:38
verses.text: But since God had left the world to the desert of sins, He would have forsaken it "even exceedingly," if so powerful a cure had not supported it, that is, the grace of God through our Lord Jesus Christ; but now, according to this prayer of the body of Christ, He forsook it not "even exceedingly;" for, "God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto Himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:39
verses.text: Beth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:40
verses.text: "Wherewithal shall a young man correct his way? even by keeping Thy words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:41
verses.text: He questioneth himself, and answereth himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:42
verses.text: "Wherewithal?" So far it is a question: next cometh the answer, "even by keeping Thy words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:43
verses.text: But in this place the keeping of the words of God, must be understood as the obeying His commandments in deed: for they are kept in memory in vain, if they are not kept in life also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:44
verses.text: But what is meant by "young man" here? For he might have said, wherewithal shall any one (homo) correct his way? or, wherewithal shall a man (vir) correct his way? which is usually put by the Scriptures in such a way, that the whole human race is understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:45
verses.text: But in this passage he saith neither any one, nor a man, but, "a young man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:46
verses.text: Is then an old man to be despaired of? or doth an old man correct his way by any other means than by ruling himself after God's word? Or is it perhaps an admonition at what age we ought chiefly to correct our way; according to what is elsewhere written, "My son, gather instruction from thy youth up: so shalt thou find wisdom till thy gray hairs".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:47
verses.text: There is another mode of interpreting it, by recognising in the expression the younger son in the Gospel, who returned to himself, and said, "I will arise and go to my father".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:48
verses.text: Wherewithal did he correct his way, save by ruling himself after the words of God, which he desired as one longing for his father's bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:49
verses.text: "With my whole heart," he saith, "have I sought thee; O repel me not from Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:50
verses.text: Behold, he prayeth that he may be aided to keep the words of God, wherewith he had said that the young man corrected his way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:51
verses.text: For this is the meaning of the words, "O repel me not from Thy commandments:" for what is it to be repelled of God, save not to be aided? For human infirmity is not equal to obeying His righteous and exalted commandments, unless His love doth prevent and aid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:52
verses.text: But those whom He aideth not, these He is justly said to repel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:53
verses.text: "Thy words have I hid within my heart, that I may not sin against Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:54
verses.text: He at once sought the Divine aid, lest the words of God might be hidden without fruit in his heart, unless works of righteousness followed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:55
verses.text: For after saying this, he added, "Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy righteousnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:56
verses.text: "Teach me," he saith, as they learn who do them; not as they who merely remember them, that they may have somewhat to speak of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:57
verses.text: Why then doth he say, "Teach me Thy righteousnesses," save because he wisheth to learn them by deeds, not by speaking or retaining them in his memory? Since then, as it is read in another Psalm, "He shall give blessing, who gave the law;" therefore, "Blessed art Thou, O Lord," he saith, "O teach me Thy righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:58
verses.text: For because I have hidden Thy words in my heart, that I may not sin against Thee, Thou hast given a law; give also the blessing of Thy grace, that by doing right I may learn what Thou by teaching hast commanded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:59
verses.text: "With my lips have I been telling of all the judgments of Thy mouth" ; that is, I have kept silent nothing of Thy judgments, which Thou didst will should become known to me through Thy words, but I have been telling of all of them without exception with my lips.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:60
verses.text: This he seemeth to me to signify, since he saith not, all Thy judgments, but, "all the judgments of Thy mouth;" that is, which Thou hast revealed unto me: that by His mouth we may understand His word, which He hath discovered unto us in many revelations of the Saints, and in the two Testaments; all which judgments the Church ceaseth not to declare at all times with her lips.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:61
verses.text: "I have had as great delight in the way Thy testimonies, as in all manner of riches".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:62
verses.text: We understand that there is no more speedy, no more sure, no shorter, no higher way of the testimonies of God than Christ, "in whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:63
verses.text: Thence he saith that he hath had as great delight in this way, as in all riches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:64
verses.text: Those are the testimonies, by which He deigneth to prove unto us how much He loveth us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:65
verses.text: "I will talk of Thy commandments, and have respect unto Thy ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:66
verses.text: And thus the Church doth exercise herself in the commandments of God, by speaking in the copious disputations of the learned against all the enemies of the Christian and Catholic faith; which are fruitful to those who compose them, if nothing but the ways of the Lord is regarded in them; but "All the ways of the Lord are," as it is written, "mercy and truth;" the fulness of which both is found in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:67
verses.text: Through this sweet exercise is gained also what he subjoineth: "My meditation shall be in Thy statutes, and I will not forget Thy word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:68
verses.text: "My medi tation" shall be therein, that I may not forget them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:69
verses.text: Thus the blessed man in the first Psalm "shall meditate in the law" of the Lord "day and night".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:70
verses.text: Gimel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:71
verses.text: He had said, "Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? Even by keeping Thy words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:72
verses.text: Behold he now more openly asketh aid that he may do this: "Reward," he saith, "Thy servant: let me live, and keep Thy word" It this reward that he asketh, who saith, "Reward Thy servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:73
verses.text: For there are four modes of reward: either evil for evil, as God will reward everlasting fire to the unrighteous; or good for good, as He will reward an everlasting kingdom to the righteous; or good for evil, as Christ by grace justifieth the ungodly; or evil for good, as Judas and the Jews through their wickedness persecuted Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:74
verses.text: Of these four modes of reward, the first two belong to justice, whereby evil is rewarded for evil, good for good; the third to mercy, whereby good is rewarded for evil; the fourth God knoweth not, for to none doth He reward evil for good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:75
verses.text: But that which I have placed third in order, is in the first instance necessary: for unless God rewarded good for evil, there would be none to whom He could reward good for good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:76
verses.text: Nowhere then let human pride raise itself up: God giveth good rewards unto His own gifts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:77
verses.text: "Open Thou mine eyes, and I will consider wondrous things of Thy law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:78
verses.text: What he addeth, "I am a lodger upon earth" : or, as some copies read, "I am a sojourner upon earth, O hide not Thy commandments from me," hath the same meaning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:79
verses.text: Here an important question ariseth respecting the soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:80
verses.text: For the words, I am a sojourner, or lodger, or stranger upon earth, cannot seem to have been said in reference to the body, since the body derives its origin from the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:81
verses.text: But in this most profound question I dare not define anything.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:82
verses.text: For if it might justly have been said in respect of the soul (which God forbid we should suppose derived from the earth), "I am a lodger," or "stranger upon earth;" or in reference to the whole man, since he was at one time an inhabitant of Paradise, where he who spake these words was not; or, what is more free from all controversy, if it be not every man who could say this, but one to whom an everlasting country hath been promised in heaven: this I know, "that the life of man on earth is a temptation;" and that "there is a heavy yoke upon the sons of Adam".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:83
verses.text: But it pleaseth me more to discuss the question in accordance with this construction, that we say we are tenants or strangers upon earth, because we have found our country above, whence we have received a pledge, and where when we have arrived we shall never depart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:84
verses.text: Those whose conversation is in heaven, as far as they abide here conversant, are in truth strangers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:85
verses.text: Let them pray therefore that the commandments of God may not be hidden from them, whereby they may be freed from this temporary sojourn, by loving God, with whom they will be for evermore; and by loving their neighbour, that he may be there where they also themselves will be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:86
verses.text: But what is loved by loving, if love itself be not loved? Whence by consequence that stranger upon earth, after praying that the commandments of God might not be hidden from him, wherein love is enjoined either solely or principally; declareth that he desireth to have a love for love itself, saying, "My soul hath coveted to have a desire alway after Thy judgments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:87
verses.text: This coveting is worthy of praise, not of condemnation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:88
verses.text: But he saith not, "coveteth," only; but, "My soul hath coveted to desire Thy judgments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:89
verses.text: For there is no obstacle to possessing the judgments of God, save that they are not desired, while love hath no warmth toward winning them, though their light is so clear and shining.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:90
verses.text: "Thou hast rebuked the proud: and cursed are they that do err from Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:91
verses.text: For the proud err from the commandments of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:92
verses.text: For it is one thing not to fulfil the commandments of God through infirmity or ignorance; another to err from them through pride; as they have done, who have begotten us in our mortal state unto these evils.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:93
verses.text: But consider now, after saying, "Thou hast rebuked the proud," he saith not, Cursed are they that have erred from Thy commandments; so that only that sin of the first men should come into the mind; but he saith, "Cursed are they that do err".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:94
verses.text: For it was needful that all might be terrified by that example, that they might not err from the divine commandments, and by loving righteousness in all time, recover in the toil of this world, what we lost in the pleasure of Paradise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:95
verses.text: "O turn from me shame and rebuke; for I have sought out Thy testimonies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:96
verses.text: Testimonies are called in Greek μαρτύρια, which word we now use for the Latin word: whence those who on account of their testimony to Christ have been brought low by various sufferings, and have contended unto death for the truth, are not called testes, but by the Greek term Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:97
verses.text: Since then ye hear in this term one more familiar and grateful, let us take these words as if it were said, "O turn from me shame and rebuke; because I have sought out Thy martyrdoms".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:98
verses.text: When the body of Christ speaketh thus, doth it consider it any punishment to hear rebuke and shame from the ungodly and the proud, since it rather reacheth the crown by this means? Why then doth it pray that it should be removed from it as something heavy and insupportable, save because, as I said, it prayeth for its very enemies, to whom it seeth it is destructive, to cast the holy name of Christ as a reproach to Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:99
verses.text: For my enemies, whom Thou enjoinest to be loved by me, who more and more die and are lost, when they despise Thy martyrdoms and accuse them in me, will indeed be recalled to life and be found, if they reverence Thy martyrdoms in me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:100
verses.text: Thus it hath happened: this we see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:101
verses.text: Behold, martyrdom in the name of Christ, both with men and in this world, is not only not a disgrace, but a great ornament: behold, not only in the sight of the Lord, but in the sight of men, "precious is the death of His Saints;" behold, His martyrs are not only not despised, but honoured with great distinctions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:102
verses.text: "Princes also did sit and speak against me: but Thy servant is exercised in Thy statutes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:103
verses.text: Thou who desirest to know what sort of exercise this was, understand what he hath added, "For Thy testimonies are my meditation, and Thy statutes are my counsellors".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:104
verses.text: Remember what I have above instructed you, that testimonies are acts of martyrdom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:105
verses.text: Remember that among the statutes of the Lord there is none more difficult and more worthy of admiration, than that every man should love his enemies Thus then the body of Christ was exercised, so that it meditated on the acts of martyrdom that testified of Him, and loved those from whom, while they rebuked and despised the Church for these very martyrdoms, she suffered persecutions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:106
verses.text: Daleth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:107
verses.text: "My soul cleaveth to the pavement: O quicken Thou me according to Thy word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:108
verses.text: What meaneth, "My soul cleaveth to the pavement, O quicken Thou me according to Thy word"?If we look upon the whole world as one great house, we see that the heavens represent its vaulting, the earth therefore will be its pavement.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:109
verses.text: He wisheth therefore to be rescued from earthly things, and to say with the Apostle, "Our conversation is in heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:110
verses.text: To cling therefore to earthly things is the soul's death; the contrary of which evil, life is prayed for, when he saith, "O quicken Thou me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:111
verses.text: The body itself also, because it is of the earth, is reasonably understood by the word pavement; since, because it is still corruptible and weigheth down the soul, we justly groan while in it, and say unto God, "O quicken Thou me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:112
verses.text: For we shall not be without our bodies when we shall be for evermore with the Lord; but then because they will not be corruptible, nor will they weigh down our souls, if we view it strictly, we shall not cleave unto them, but they rather unto us, and we unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:113
verses.text: For what he was by himself, he confesseth in the following words: "I have acknowledged my ways, and Thou heardest me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:114
verses.text: Some copies indeed read, "Thy ways:" but more, and the best Greek, read "my ways," that is, evil ways.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:115
verses.text: For he seemeth to me to say this; I have confessed my sins, and Thou hast heard me; that is, so that Thou wouldest remit them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:116
verses.text: "O teach me Thy statutes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:117
verses.text: I have acknowledged my ways: Thou hast blotted them out: teach me Thine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:118
verses.text: So teach me, that I may act; not merely that I may know how I ought to act.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:119
verses.text: For as it is said of the Lord, that He knew not sin, and it is understood, that He did no sin; so also he ought truly to be said to know righteousness, who doeth it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:120
verses.text: This is the prayer of one who is improving.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:121
verses.text: Finally he addeth, "Intimate to me the way of Thy righteousness" ; or, as some copies have it, "instruct me;" which is expressed more closely from the Greek, "Make me to understand the way of Thy righteousnesses; so shall I be exercised in Thy wondrous things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:122
verses.text: These higher commandments, which he desireth to understand by edification, he calleth the wondrous things of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:123
verses.text: There are then some righteousnesses of God so wondrous, that human weakness may be believed incapable of fulfilling them by those who have not tried.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:124
verses.text: Whence the Psalmist, struggling and wearied with the difficulty of obeying them, saith, "My soul hath slumbered for very heaviness: O stablish Thou me with Thy word!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:125
verses.text: What meaneth, hath slumbered? save that he hath cooled in the hope which he had entertained of being able to reach them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:126
verses.text: But, he addeth, "Stablish Thou me with Thy word:" that I may not by slumbering fall away from those duties which I feel that I have already attained: stablish Thou me therefore in those words of Thine that I already hold, that I may be able to reach unto others through edification.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:127
verses.text: "Take Thou from me the way of iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:128
verses.text: And since the law of works hath entered in, that sin might abound; he addeth, "And pity me according to Thy law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:129
verses.text: By what law, save by the law of faith? Hear the Apostle: "Where is boasting then? It is excluded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:130
verses.text: By what law? Of works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:131
verses.text: Nay: but by the law of faith".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:132
verses.text: This is the law of faith, whereby we believe and pray that it may be granted us through grace; that we may effect that which we cannot fulfil through ourselves; that we may not, ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to stablish our own, fail to submit ourselves unto the righteousness of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:133
verses.text: But after he had said, "And pity me according to Thy law;" he mentioneth some of those blessings which he hath already obtained, that he may ask others that he hath not yet gained.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:134
verses.text: For he saith, "I have chosen the way of truth: and Thy judgments I have not forgotten".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:135
verses.text: "I have stuck unto Thy testimonies: O Lord, confound me not" : may I persevere in striving toward the point whereunto I am running: may I arrive whither I am running! So then "it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that showeth mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:136
verses.text: He next saith, "I will run the way of Thy commandments, when Thou hast widened my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:137
verses.text: I could not run hadst Thou not widened my heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:138
verses.text: The sense of the words, "I have chosen the way of truth, and Thy judgments I have not forgotten: I have stuck unto Thy testimonies," is clearly explained in this verse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:139
verses.text: For this running is along the way of the commandments of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:140
verses.text: And because he doth allege unto the Lord rather His blessings than his own deservings; as if it were said unto him, How hast thou run that way, by choosing, and by not forgetting the judgments of God, and by sticking to His testimonies? Couldest thou do these things by thyself? I could not, he replieth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:141
verses.text: It is not therefore through my own will, as though it needed no aid of Thine; but because "Thou has widened my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:142
verses.text: The widening of the heart is the delight we take in righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:143
verses.text: This is the gift of God, the effect of which is, that we are not straitened in His commandments through the fear of punishment, but widened through love, and the delight we have in righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:144
verses.text: He.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:145
verses.text: In this great Psalm there cometh next in order that which, with the Lord's help, we must consider and treat of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:146
verses.text: "Set a law for me, O Lord, the way of Thy statutes, and I shall seek it alway".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:147
verses.text: Why doth this man still pray for a law to be laid down for him; which, if it had not been laid down for him, he could not have run the way of God's commandments in the breadth of his heart? But since one speaketh who is growing in grace, and who knoweth that it is God's gift that he profiteth in grace; what else doth he pray, when he prayeth that a law may be laid down for him, save that he may profit more and more? As, if thou holdest a full cup, and givest it to a thirsty man; he both exhausts it by drinking it, and prayeth for it by still longing for it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:148
verses.text: But what meaneth, "Evermore"?Doth "evermore" mean as long as we live here, because we progress in grace so long; but after this life, he who was in a good course of improvement here, is made perfect there? Here the law of God is examined into, as long as we progress in it, both by knowing it and by loving it: but there its fulness abideth for our enjoyment, not for our examination.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:149
verses.text: Thus also is this spoken, "Seek His face evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:150
verses.text: Where, evermore, save here? For we shall not there also seek the face of God, when "we shall see face to face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:151
verses.text: Or if that which is loved without a change of affection is rightly said to be sought after, and our only object is, that it be not lost,  we shall indeed evermore seek the law of God, that is, the truth of God: for in this very Psalm it is said, "And Thy law is the truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:152
verses.text: It is now sought, that it may be held fast; it will then be held fast that it may not be lost.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:153
verses.text: "Give me understanding, and I shall search Thy law, yea, I shall keep it with my whole heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:154
verses.text: For when each man hath searched the law, and searched its deep things, in which its whole meaning doth consist; he ought indeed to love God with all his heart, with all his soul, with all his mind; and his neighbour as himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:155
verses.text: "For on these two commandments hang all the Law and the Prophets".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:156
verses.text: This he seemeth to have promised, when he said, "Yea, I shall keep it with my whole heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:157
verses.text: But since he hath no power to do even this, save he be aided by Him who commandeth him to do what He commandeth, "Make me," he addeth, "to go in the path of Thy commandments, for therein is my desire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:158
verses.text: My desire is powerless, unless Thou Thyself makest me to go where I desire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:159
verses.text: And this is surely the very path, that is, the path of God's commandments, which he had already said that he had run, when his heart was enlarged by the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:160
verses.text: And this he calleth a "path," because "the way is narrow which leadeth unto life;" and since it is narrow, we cannot run therein save with a heart enlarged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:161
verses.text: He next saith, "Incline mine heart unto Thy testimonies, and not to covetousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:162
verses.text: This then he prayeth, that he may profit in the will itselfBut the Apostle saith, "Avarice is a root of all evils".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:163
verses.text: But in the Greek, whence these words have been rendered into our tongue, the word used by the Apostle is not πλεονεξία, which occurs in this passage of the Psalms; but φιλαργυρία, by which is signified "love of money".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:164
verses.text: But the Apostle must be understood to have meant genus by species when he used this word, that is, to have meant avarice universally and generally by love of money, which is truly the root of all evilsIf therefore our heart be not inclined to covetousness, we fear God only for God's sake, so that He is the only reward of our serving Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:165
verses.text: Let us love Him in Himself, let us love Him in ourselves, Him in our neighbours whom we love as ourselves, whether they have Him, or in order that they may have Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:166
verses.text: The next words in the Psalm which we have undertaken to expound are, "O turn away mine eyes, lest they behold vanity: and quicken Thou me in Thy way".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:167
verses.text: Vanity and truth are directly contrary to one another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:168
verses.text: The desires of this world are vanity: but Christ, who freeth us from the world, is truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:169
verses.text: He is the way, too, wherein this man wisheth to be quickened, for He is also the life: "I am the way, the truth, and the life," are His own words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:170
verses.text: He prayeth that those eyes wherewith we consider on what account we do what we do, may be turned away that they behold not vanity; that is, that he may not look to vanity, as his motive, when he doeth anything good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:171
verses.text: In this vanity the first place is held by the love of men's praise, on account of which many great deeds have been wrought by those who are styled great in this world, and who have been much praised in heathen states, seeking glory not with God, but among men, and on account of this living in appearance prudently, courageously, temperately, and righteously; and when they have reached this they have reached their reward: vain men, and vain rewardMoreover, if it be a vain thing to do good works for the sake of men's praises, how much more vain for the sake of getting money, or increasing it, or retaining it, and any other temporal advantage, which cometh unto us from without? Since "all things are vanity: what is man's abundance, with all his toil, wherein he laboureth under the sun?" For our temporal welfare itself finally we ought not to do our good works, but rather for the sake of that everlasting welfare which we hope for, where we may enjoy an unchangeable good, which we shall have from God, nay, what God Himself is unto us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:172
verses.text: For if God's Saints were to do good works for the sake of this temporal welfare, never would the martyrs of Christ achieve a good work of confession in the loss of this same welfare.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:173
verses.text: "O stablish Thy word in Thy servant, that I may fear Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:174
verses.text: And what else is this than, Grant unto me that I may do according to what Thou sayest? For the word of God is not stablished in those who remove it in themselves by acting contrary to it; but it is stablished in those in whom it is immoveable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:175
