verses.text: God therefore stablisheth His word, that they may fear Him, in those unto whom He giveth the spirit of the fear of Him; not that fear of which the Apostle saith, "Ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear;" for "perfect love casteth out" this "fear," but that fear which the Prophet calleth "the spirit of the fear of the Lord;" that fear which "is pure, and endureth for ever;" that fear which feareth to offend Him whom it loveth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:176
verses.text: "Take away my reproach which I have suspected, for Thy judgments are sweet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:177
verses.text: Who is he who suspected his own reproach, and who doth not know his own reproach better than that of his neighbour? For a man may rather suspect another's than his own; since he knoweth not that which he suspecteth; but in each one's own reproach there is not suspicion for him, but knowledge, wherein conscience speaketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:178
verses.text: What then mean the words, "the rebuke which I have suspected"? The meaning of them must be derived from the former verse; since as long as a man doth not turn away his eyes lest they behold vanity, he suspecteth in others what is going on in himself; so that he believeth another to worship God, or do good works, from the same motive as himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:179
verses.text: For men can see what we do, but with a view to what end we act, is hidden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:180
verses.text: "Behold, I have coveted Thy commandments: O quicken Thou me in Thy righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:181
verses.text: Behold, I have coveted to love Thee with all my heart, and with all my soul, and with all my mind, and my neighbour as myself, but, "O quicken Thou me" not in my own, but "in Thy righteousness," that is, fill me with that love which I have longed for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:182
verses.text: Aid me that I may do that which Thou chargest me: Thyself give what Thou dost command.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:183
verses.text: "O quicken Thou me in Thy righteousness:" for in myself I had that which would cause my death: but I find not save in Thee whence I may live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:184
verses.text: Christ is Thy righteousness, "Who of God is made unto us wisdom," etc And in Him I find Thy commandments, which I have coveted, that in Thy righteousness, that is, in Him, Thou mayest quicken me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:185
verses.text: For the Word Himself is God; and "the Word was made flesh," that He Himself also might be my neighbour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:186
verses.text: Vav.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:187
verses.text: "And let Thy loving mercy come also unto us, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:188
verses.text: This sentence seems annexed to the foregoing: for he doth not say, Let it come unto me, but, "And let it come unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:189
verses.text: What then doth he here pray for, save that through His loving mercy who commanded, he may perform the commandments which he hath coveted? For he explaineth in some degree what he meant by adding, "even Thy salvation, according to Thy word:" that is, according to Thy promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:190
verses.text: Whence the Apostle desireth us to be understood as the children of promise: that we may not imagine that what we are is our own work, but refer the whole to the grace of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:191
verses.text: Christ Himself is the Salvation of God, so that the whole body of Christ may say, "By the grace of God I am what I am".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:192
verses.text: "And so shall I make answer," he saith, "to them that reproach me with the word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:193
verses.text: It is doubtful whether it be "reproach me with a word;" or, "I will answer with a word;" but either signifieth Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:194
verses.text: They to whom Christ crucified is a stumbling-block or foolishness, reproach us with Him; ignorant that "the Word was made flesh, and dwelt in us;" the Word which "was in the beginning," and "was with God, and was God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:195
verses.text: But although they may not reproach us with the Word which is unknown unto them, because His Divinity is not known unto those by whom His weakness on the Cross is despised; let us nevertheless make answer of the Word, and let us not be terrified or confounded by their reproaches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:196
verses.text: For "if they had known" the Word, "they would never have crucified the Lord of glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:197
verses.text: Therefore, when the Psalmist had said, "I will make answer unto them that reproach me with the word:" he at once addeth, "For my trust is in Thy words," which meaneth exactly, in Thy promises.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:198
verses.text: "O take not the word of Thy truth away out of my mouth even exceedingly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:199
verses.text: He saith, out of my mouth, because the unity of the body is speaking, among whose members those also are counted who failed at the hour by denying, but by penitence afterwards came again to life, or even, by renewing their confession, received the palm of martyrdom, which they had lost.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:200
verses.text: The word of truth, therefore, was not "even exceedingly," or, as some copies have it, even every way, that is not altogether taken from the mouth of Peter, in whom was the type of the Church; because although he denied for the hour, being disturbed with fear, yet by weeping he was restored, and by confessing was afterwards crowned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:201
verses.text: The whole body of Christ therefore speaketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:202
verses.text: Next followeth, "for I have hoped in Thy judgments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:203
verses.text: Or, as some have more strictly rendered it from the Greek, "I have hoped more;" a word which, although compounded in a somewhat unusual way, yet answers the necessary purpose of conveying the truth in a translation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:204
verses.text: Behold the saints and the humble in heart when they have trusted in Thee, have not failed in persecutions: behold also those who from trusting in themselves have failed, and nevertheless have belonged to the Very Body, have wept when they became known unto themselves, and have found Thy grace a more solid support, because they have lost their own pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:205
verses.text: "So shall I alway keep Thy law" : that is, if Thou wilt not take the word of Thy truth out of my mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:206
verses.text: "Yea, unto age, and age of age:" he showeth what he meant by "alway".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:207
verses.text: For sometimes by "alway" is meant, as long as we live here; but this is not, "unto age, and age of age".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:208
verses.text: For it is better thus translated than as some copies have, "to eternity, and to age of age," since they could not say, and to eternity of eternity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:209
verses.text: That law therefore should be understood, of which the Apostle saith, "Love is the fulfilling of the law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:210
verses.text: For this will be kept by the saints, from whose mouth the word of truth is not taken, that is, by the Church of Christ Herself, not only during this world, that is, until this world is ended; but for another also which is styled, "world without end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:211
verses.text: "And I walked at liberty: for I sought Thy precepts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:212
verses.text: "And I walked at liberty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:213
verses.text: Here the copulative conjunction, "and," is not used as a connecting particle; for he doth not say, and I will walk, as he had said, "and I will keep Thy commandments for ever and ever:" or if this latter verse be in the optative mood, and may I keep Thy law; he doth not add, And may I walk at liberty, as if he had desired and prayed for both of these things; but he saith, "And I walked at liberty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:214
verses.text: If this conjunction were not used here, and if the sentence were introduced free from any such connection with what preceded, "I walked at liberty," the reader would never be induced by anything unusual in the mode of speech to think he should seek for some hidden sense.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:215
verses.text: Doubtless, then, he wished what he hath not said to be understood, that is, that his prayers had been heard; and he then added what he had become: as if he were to say, When I prayed for these things, Thou heardest me, "And I walked at liberty;" and so with the remaining expressions which he hath added to the same purpose.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:216
verses.text: Whence after he had said, "And I walked at liberty," he subjoined the reason, "For I sought out Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:217
verses.text: Some copies have not "commandments" but "testimonies:" but we find "commandments" in most, and especially in the Greek; and who would hesitate rather to believe this tongue, as prior to our own, and that from which these Psalms have been rendered into Latin? If then we wish to know how he sought out these commandments, or how they ought to be sought out, let us consider what our good Master, who both taught and gave them, saith: "Ask, and it shall be given you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:218
verses.text: And a little lower, "If ye then," He saith, "being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in Heaven give good things to them that ask Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:219
verses.text: Where He evidently showeth, that the words He had spoken, seek, ask, knock, belong only to earnestness in asking, that is, in praying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:220
verses.text: Moreover, another Evangelist saith not, He will give good things to them that ask Him; which may be understood in many ways, either as earthly or spiritual blessings; but has excluded other interpretations, and very carefully expressed what our Lord wished us to pray earnestly and instantly for, in these words: "How much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:221
verses.text: "I spoke of Thy testimonies also," he saith, "before kings, and I was not ashamed" : as one who had sought and had received grace to answer those who reproached him with the word, and the promise that the word of truth should not be taken from his mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:222
verses.text: Struggling for this truth even unto death, not even before kings was he ashamed to speak of it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:223
verses.text: For testimonies, whereof he doth avow that he was speaking, are in Greek styled μαρτύρια, a word which we now employ instead of the Latin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:224
verses.text: The name of "Martyrs," unto whom Jesus foretold, that they should confess Him even before kings, is derived hence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:225
verses.text: "And I meditated," he saith, "on Thy commandments, which I have loved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:226
verses.text: "My hands also have I lifted up unto Thy commandments, which I have loved" ; or, as some copies read, "which I have loved exceedingly," or "too much," or "vehemently," as they have chosen to render the Greek word σφόδρα.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:227
verses.text: He then loved the commandments of God because he walked at liberty; that is, through the Holy Spirit, through whom love itself is shed abroad, and enlargeth the hearts of the faithful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:228
verses.text: But he loved, both in thought and in acts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:229
verses.text: With a view to thought, he saith, "And I meditated:" as to action, "My hands also have I lifted up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:230
verses.text: But to both sentences, he hath annexed the words, "which I have loved:" for "the end of the commandment is love out of a pure heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:231
verses.text: The following words, "And my study was in Thy statutes," relate to both.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:232
verses.text: This expression most of the translators have preferred to this, "I rejoiced in," or "I talked of," a version which some have given from the Greek ἠδολ™σχουν.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:233
verses.text: For he who keepeth the commandments of God, which he loveth, both in thought and in works taking delight in them, is exercised with joy, and with a certain abundance of speech, in the judgments of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:234
verses.text: Zain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:235
verses.text: "O remember Thy word unto Thy servant, wherein Thou hast given me hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:236
verses.text: Is forgetfulness incident to God, as it is to man? Why then is it said unto Him, "O remember"? Although in other passages of holy Scripture this very word is used, as, "Why hast Thou forgotten me?" and, "Wherefore forgettest Thou our misery?"These expressions are borrowed from moral discourses on human affections; although God doth these things according to a fixed dispensation, with no failing memory, nor with an understanding obscured, nor with a will changed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:237
verses.text: When therefore it is said unto Him, "O remember," the desire of him who prayeth is displayed, because he asketh for what was promised; God is not admonished, as if the promise had escaped from His mind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:238
verses.text: "O remember," he saith, "Thy word unto Thy servant:" that is, fulfil Thy promise to Thy servant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:239
verses.text: "Wherein Thou hast given me hope:" that is, in Thy Word, since Thou hast promised, Thou hast caused me to hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:240
verses.text: "The same is my comfort in my humiliation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:241
verses.text: Namely, that hope which is given to the humble, as the Scripture saith: "God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:242
verses.text: Whence also our Lord Himself saith with His own lips, "For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:243
verses.text: We well understand here that humiliation also, not whereby each man humbleth himself by confessing his sins, and by not arrogating righteousness to himself; but when each man is humbled by some tribulation or mortification which his prid e deserved; or when he is exercised and proved by endurance; whence a little after this Psalm saith, "Before I was troubled, I went wrong".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:244
verses.text: And the Lord Jesus, when He foretold that this humiliation would be brought upon His disciples by their persecutors, did not leave them without a hope; but gave them one, whereby they might find comfort, in these words: "In your patience shall ye possess your souls;" and declared even of their very bodies, which might be put to death by their enemies, and seemingly be utterly annihilated, that not a hair of their heads should perish This hope was given to Christ's Body, that is, to the Church, that it might be a comfort to Her in her humiliation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:245
verses.text: This hope He gave in the prayer which He taught us, where He enjoined us to say, "Lead us not into temptation:" for He in a manner implicitly promised that He would give to His disciples i n their danger that which He taught them to ask for in their prayers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:246
verses.text: And indeed this Psalm is rather to be understood to speak of this hope: "For Thy word hath quickened me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:247
verses.text: Which they have rendered more closely who have put not "word," but "utterance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:248
verses.text: For the Greek has λόγιον, which is "utterance;" not λόγος, which is "word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:249
verses.text: The next verse is, "The proud dealt exceeding wickedly: yet have I not shrinked from Thy law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:250
verses.text: By the proud he wished to be understood the persecutors of the pious; and he therefore added, "yet have I not shrinked from Thy laws," because the persecution of the proud attempted to force him to do this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:251
verses.text: He saith that they dealt "exceeding wickedly," because they were not only wicked themselves, but even tried to make the godly wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:252
verses.text: In this humiliation, that is, in this tribulation, that hope comforted him which was given in the word of God, who promised aid, that the faith of the Martyrs might not faint; and who by the presence of His Spirit gave strength to them in their toils, that they might escape from the snare of the fowlers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:253
verses.text: "For I was mindful of Thy judgments from the beginning of the world, O Lord, and received comfort" ; or, as other copies have it, "and I was exhorted," that is, received exhortation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:254
verses.text: For either might be rendered for the Greek pareklhqhn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:255
verses.text: "From the beginning of the world," that is, from the birth of the human race, "I was mindful of Thy judgments" upon the vessels of wrath, which are fitted unto perdition: "and I received comfort," since through these also hast Thou shown the riches of Thy glory on the vessels of Thy mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:256
verses.text: "Weariness hath held me; for the ungodly that forsake Thy law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:257
verses.text: "Thy statutes have been my songs in the house of my pilgrimage".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:258
verses.text: This is the low estate, in the house of mortality, of the man who sojourneth away from Paradise and the Jerusalem above, whence one going down to Jericho fell among robbers; but, in consequence of the deed of mercy which was done him by that Samaritan, the statutes of God became his song in the house of his pilgrimage; although he was weary for the ungodly that forsook the law of God, since he was compelled to converse with them for a season in this life, until the floor be threshed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:259
verses.text: But these two verses may be adapted to the two clauses of the preceding verse, respectively.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:260
verses.text: "I have thought upon Thy Name, O Lord, in the night-season, and have kept Thy law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:261
verses.text: Night is that low estate wherein is the trouble of mortality; night is in the proud who deal exceeding wickedly; night is the fear for the ungodly who forsake the law of the Lord; night is, lastly, the house of this pilgrimage, "until the Lord come, and bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts, and then shall every man have praise of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:262
verses.text: In this night, therefore, man ought to remember the Name of the Lord; "So that he who glorieth, may glory in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:263
verses.text: Considering this, he addeth, "This was made unto me, because I sought out Thy righteousnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:264
verses.text: "Thy" righteousnesses, whereby Thou dost justify the ungodly; not mine, which never make me godly, but proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:265
verses.text: For this man was not one of those who, "ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:266
verses.text: Others have better interpreted these righteousnesses, as those whereby men are justified for nought through God's grace, though by themselves they cannot be righteous, "justifications".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:267
verses.text: But what meaneth, "This was made unto me"? What is "This"? It is perhaps the law? as he had said, "and I have kept Thy law;" to which he subjoins, "This was made unto me," meaning, "This was made my law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:268
verses.text: We must therefore enquire first what was thus made unto him, next in what manner, whatever it may have been, was made unto him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:269
verses.text: "This," he saith, "was made unto me:" not "This law," for the Greek, as I have said, refuseth this sense.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:270
verses.text: Perhaps then, "This night:" since the preceding sentence stands thus: "I have thought upon Thy Name, O Lord, in the night-season:" and the next words are, "This was made unto me:" since then it is not the law, it must truly be the night which is thus spoken of.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:271
verses.text: What then meaneth, "I had the night-season: for I have sought out Thy righteousnesses"? Rather light had come unto him than night, since he sought out the righteousnesses of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:272
verses.text: And it is thus rightly understood, "It was made unto me," as if it were said, It became night for my sake, that is, that it might profit me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:273
verses.text: For that low estate of mortality is not absurdly understood as night, where the hearts of mortals are hid to one another, so that from such darkness innumerable and heavy temptations arise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:274
verses.text: Cheth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:275
verses.text: Let us hear what followeth: "I have promised to keep Thy law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:276
verses.text: What meaneth, "My portion, O Lord: I have promised to keep Thy law" ; save because the Lord will be each man's portion then, when he hath kept His law? Consider therefore what he subjoineth: "I entreated Thy face, with my whole heart:" and saying in what manner he prayed: "O be merciful," he saith, "unto me, according to Thy word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:277
verses.text: And as if he had been heard and aided by Him whom he prayed unto, "I thought," he saith, "on mine own ways, and turned away my feet unto Thy testimonies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:278
verses.text: That is, I turned them away from mine own ways, which displeased me, that they might follow Thy testimonies, and there might find a path.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:279
verses.text: For most of the copies have not, "Because I thought," as is read in some; but only, "I thought".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:280
verses.text: But what is here written, "and I turned away my feet:" some read, "Because I thought, Thou also hast turned away my feet:" that this may rather be ascribed to the grace of God, according to the Apostle's words, "For it is God who worketh in us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:281
verses.text: Lastly, when he had received this blessing of grace, he saith, "I was ready, and was not disturbed, that I may keep Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:282
verses.text: Which some have rendered, "to keeping Thy commandments," some "that I should keep," others "to keep," the Greek being τοῦ φυλ€ξασθαι.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:283
verses.text: But in what manner he was ready to keep the divine commandments, he hath added, in these words: "The bands of the ungodly have surrounded me: but I have not forgotten Thy law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:284
verses.text: "The bands of the ungodly" are the hindrances of our enemies, whether spiritual, as the devil and his angels, or carnal, the children of disobedience, in whom the devil worketh For this word peccatorum is not from peccata, "sins;" but from peccatores, "sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:285
verses.text: Therefore when they threaten evils, with which to alarm the righteous, that they may not suffer for the law of God, they, so to speak, entangle them with bands, with a strong and tough cord of their own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:286
verses.text: For "they draw iniquity like a long rope," and thus endeavour to entangle the holy, and sometimes are allowed so to do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:287
verses.text: "At midnight," he saith, "I rise to give thanks unto Thee: because of Thy righteous judgments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:288
verses.text: This very fact, that the bands of the ungodly surround the righteous, is one of the righteous judgments of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:289
verses.text: On which account the Apostle Peter saith, "The time is come when judgment must begin at the house of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:290
verses.text: For he saith this of the persecutions which the Church suffered, when the bands of the ungodly surrounded them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:291
verses.text: I suppose, therefore, that by "midnight" we should understand the heavier seasons of tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:292
verses.text: In which he said, "I arose:" since He did not so afflict him, as to cast him down; but tried him, so that he arose, that is, that through this very tribulation he might advance unto a bolder confession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:293
verses.text: For I imagine that what followeth, "I am a companion of all them that fear Thee, and keep Thy commandments" , doth relate to the Head Himself, as it is in the Epistle which is inscribed to the Hebrews: "Both He that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one: for which cause He is not ashamed to call them brethren".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:294
verses.text: Therefore Jesus Himself speaketh in this prophecy: some things in His Members and in the Unity of His Body, as if in one man diffused over the whole world, and growing up in succession throughout the roll of ages: and some things in Himself our Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:295
verses.text: And on this account, that since He became the companion of His brethren, God of men, the Immortal of the mortal, for this reason the seed fell upon the earth, that by its death it might produce much fruit; he next addeth concerning this very fruit, "The earth, O Lord, is full of Thy mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:296
verses.text: And whence this, save when the ungodly is justified? That we may make progress in the knowledge of this grace, he addeth, "O teach me Thy righteousnesses!"            Teth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:297
verses.text: "Thou hast dealt in sweetness with Thy servant: according unto Thy word;" or rather, "according unto Thine utterance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:298
verses.text: The Greek word χρηστότης hath been variously rendered by our translators by the words "sweetness" and "goodness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:299
verses.text: But since sweetness may exist also in evil, since all unlawful and unclean things afford pleasure, and it may also exist in that carnal pleasure which is permitted; we ought to understand the word "sweetness," which the Greeks termed χρηστότης, of spiritual blessings: for on this account our translators have preferred to term it "goodness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:300
verses.text: I think therefore that nothing else is meant by the words, "Thou hast dealt in sweetness with Thy servant," than this, Thou hast made me feel delight in that which is good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:301
verses.text: For when that which is good delighteth, it is a great gift of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:302
verses.text: But when the good work which the law commandeth is done from a fear of punishment, not from a delight in righteousness, when God is dreaded, not loved; it is the act of a slave, not of a freeman.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:303
verses.text: "O learn me sweetness, and understanding, and knowledge," he saith, "for I have believed Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:304
verses.text: He prayeth these things may be increased and perfected.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:305
verses.text: For they who said, "Lord, increase our faith," had faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:306
verses.text: And as long as we live in this world, these are the words of those who are making progress.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:307
verses.text: But he addeth, "understanding," or, as most copies read, "discipline".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:308
verses.text: Now the word discipline, for which the Greeks use παιδεία, is employed in Scripture, where instruction through tribulation is to be understood: according to the words, "Whom the Lord loveth He disciplineth, and scourgeth every son whom He receiveth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:309
verses.text: In the literature of the Church this is usually called discipline.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:310
verses.text: For this word, παιδεία, is used in the Greek in the Epistle to the Hebrews, where the Latin translator saith, "No discipline for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous," etc He therefore toward whom the Lord dealeth in sweetness, that is, he in whom He mercifully inspires delight in that which is good, ought to pray instantly, that this gift may be so increased unto him, that he may not only despise all other delights in comparison with it, but also that he may endure any amount of sufferings for its sake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:311
verses.text: Thus is discipline healthfully added to sweetness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:312
verses.text: This discipline ought not to be desired, and prayed for, for a small measure of grace and goodness, that is, holy love; but for so great, as may not be extinguished by the weight of the chastening:so much in fact as to enable him to endure with the utmost patience the discipline.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:313
verses.text: In the third place is mentioned knowledge; since, if knowledge in its greatness outstrips the increase of love, it doth not edify, but "puffeth up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:314
verses.text: But in that he saith, not, Give unto me; but, "O learn me;" how is the sweetness taught, if it be not given? Since many know what doth not delight them, and find no sweetness in things of which they have knowledge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:315
verses.text: For sweetness cannot be learnt, unless it please.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:316
verses.text: Also discipline, which signifieth the tribulation which chasteneth, is learnt by receiving; that is, not by hearing, or reading, or thinking, but by feeling.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:317
verses.text: He addeth, "for I have believed Thy commandments," and herein we may justly enquire, why he said not, I obeyed, rather than, I believed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:318
verses.text: For commandments are one thing, promises another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:319
verses.text: We undertake to obey commandments, that we may deserve to receive promises.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:320
verses.text: We therefore believe promises, obey commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:321
verses.text: Teach me therefore sweetness by inspiring charity, teach me discipline by giving patience, teach me knowledge by enlightening my understanding: "for I have believed Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:322
verses.text: I have believed that Thou who art God, and who givest unto man whence Thou mayest cause him to do what Thou commandest, hast commanded these things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:323
verses.text: "Before I was humbled, I went wrong; wherefore I have kept Thy word" ; or, as some have it more closely, "Thy utterance," that is, lest I should be humbled again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:324
verses.text: This is better referred to that humiliation which took place in Adam, in whom the whole human creature, as it were, being corrupted at the root, as it refused to be subject to truth, "was made subject to vanity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:325
verses.text: Which it was profitable to the vessels of mercy to feel, that by throwing down pride, obedience might be loved, and misery perish, never again to return.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:326
verses.text: "Sweet art Thou, O Lord;" or, as many have it, "Sweet art Thou, even Thou, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:327
verses.text: Some also, "Sweet art Thou," or, "Good art Thou:" as we have before treated of this word: "and in Thy sweetness teach me Thy statutes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:328
verses.text: He truly desireth to do the righteousnesses of God, since he desireth to learn them in His sweetness from Him unto whom he hath said, "Sweet art Thou, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:329
verses.text: Next he saith, "The iniquity of the proud hath been multiplied upon me" : of those, that is, whom it profited not that human nature was humbled after it went wrong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:330
verses.text: "But I will search Thy commandments with my whole heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:331
verses.text: Howsoever, he saith, iniquity shall abound, love shall not grow cold in me He, as it were, saith this, who in His sweetness learneth the righteousnesses of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:332
verses.text: For in proportion as the commandments of Him who aideth us are the more sweet, so much the more doth he who loveth Him search after them, that he may perform them when known, and may learn them by doing them; because they are more perfectly understood when they are performed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:333
verses.text: "Their heart is curdled as milk".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:334
verses.text: Whose, save the proud, whose iniquity he hath said hath been multiplied upon him? But he wisheth it to be understood by this word, and in this passage, that their heart hath become hard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:335
verses.text: It is used also in a good sense, and is understood to mean, full of grace: for this word, some have also interpreted "curdled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:336
verses.text: "It is good for me that Thou hast humbled me: that I might learn Thy righteousnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:337
verses.text: He hath said something kindred to this above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:338
verses.text: For by the fruit itself he showeth that it was a good thing for him to be humbled; but in the former passage he hath stated the cause also, in that he had felt beforehand that humiliation which resulted from his punishment, when he went wrong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:339
verses.text: But in these words, "Wherefore have I kept Thy word:" and again in these, "That I might learn Thy righteousnesses:" he seemeth to me to have signified, that to know these is the same thing as to keep them, to keep them the same thing as to know them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:340
verses.text: For Christ knew what He reproved; and yet He reproved sin, though it is said of Him that "He knew not sin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:341
verses.text: He knew therefore by a kind of knowledge, and again He knew not by a kind of ignorance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:342
verses.text: Thus also many learn the righteousnesses of God, and learn them not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:343
verses.text: For they know them in a certain way; and, again do not know them from a kind of ignorance, since they do them not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:344
verses.text: In this sense the Psalmist therefore is to be understood to have said, "That I might learn Thy righteousnesses," meaning that kind of knowledge whereby they are performed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:345
verses.text: But that this is not gained, save through love, wherein he who doeth them hath delight, on which account it is said, "In Thy sweetness teach me Thy righteousnesses:" the following verse showeth, wherein he saith, "The law of Thy mouth is better unto me than thousands of gold and silver" : so that love loveth the law of God more than avarice loveth thousands of gold and silver.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:346
verses.text: Jod.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:347
verses.text: "Thy hands have made me, and fashioned me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:348
verses.text: The hands of God are the power of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:349
verses.text: Or if the plural number moveth them, since it is not said, Thy hand, but, "Thy hands;" let them understand by the hands of God the power and wisdom of God, both of which titles are given to one Christ, who is also understood under the figure, Arm of the Lord Or let them understand by the hands of God, the Son and the Holy Spirit; since the Holy Spirit worketh conjointly with the Father and the Son: whence saith the Apostle, "But all these worketh that one and the self-same Spirit:" he said, "one and the self-same;" lest as many spirits as works might be imagined, not that the Spirit worketh without the Father and the Son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:350
verses.text: It is easy therefore to see how the hands of God are to be understood: provided, at the same time, that He be not denied to do those things through His Word which He doth by His hands: nor be considered not to do those things with His hands, which He doth through His word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:351
verses.text: But is this said in respect of Adam? from whom since all men were propagated, what man, since Adam was made, may not say that he himself also was made by reason of procreation and generation from Adam? Or may it rightly be said, in this sense, "Thy hands have made me, and fashioned me," namely, that every man is born even of his parents not without the work of God, God creating, they generating? Since, if the creative power of God be withdrawn from things, they perish: nor is anything at all, either of the world's elements, or of parents, or of seeds, produced, if God doth not create it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:352
verses.text: The Greek version hath a more concise expression for our, "Give me understanding," συν<> τισον με, expressing "give understanding" by the single word συν<> τισον, which the Latin cannot do; as if one could not say, Heal me; and it were necessary to say, Give me health, as it is here said, "Give me understanding;" or, make me whole, as here it may be said, make me intelligent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:353
verses.text: This indeed an Angel could do: for he said to Daniel, "I am come to give thee understanding;" and this word is in the Greek, as it is here also, συν <> τισαί σε; as if the Latin translator were to render θεραπεῦσαί σε by sanitatem dare tibi.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:354
verses.text: For the Latin interpreter would not make a circumlocution by saying, to give thee understanding, if, as we say from health, "to heal thee," so one could say from intellect, "to intellectuate thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:355
verses.text: But if an Angel could do this, what reason is there that this man should pray that this be done for him by God? Is it because God had commanded the Angel to do it? Just so: for Christ is understood to have given this command to the Angel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:356
verses.text: "That I may learn Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:357
verses.text: Since Thou, saith he, hast formed me, do Thou new form me; that that may be done in Christ's Body, which the Apostle speaks of, "Be transformed by the renewing of your mind".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:358
verses.text: "They that fear Thee," he saith, "will see me, and be glad" : or, as other copies have it, "will be joyful: because I have hoped in Thy word:" that is, in the things which Thou hast promised, that they may be the sons of promise, the seed of Abraham, in whom all nations are blessed Who are they who fear God, and whom will they see and be glad, because he hath put his trust in the word of God? Whether it be the body of Christ, that is, the Church, whose words these are through Christ, or within it, and concerning it, these are as it were the words of Christ concerning Himself; are not they themselves among those who fear God?The same persons, who see the Church and are glad, are the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:359
verses.text: But why said he not, They who fear Thee see me, and are glad: whereas he hath written, "fear Thee," in the present tense; while the verbs "shall see," and shall "be glad," are futures? Is it because in the present state there is fear, as long as "man's life is a temptation upon earth;" but the gladness which he desired to be understood, will be then, when "the righteous shall shine in the kingdom of their Father like the sun".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:360
verses.text: "I know," she saith, "O Lord, that Thy judgments are righteous, and that in Thy truth Thou hast humbled me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:361
verses.text: "O let Thy merciful kindness be my comfort, according to Thy word unto Thy servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:362
verses.text: Mercy and truth are so spoken of in the Divine Word, that, while they are found in many passages, especially in the Psalms, it is also so read in one place, "All the paths of the Lord are mercy and truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:363
verses.text: And here indeed he hath placed truth first, whereby we are humbled unto death, by the judgment of Him whose judgments are righteousness: next mercy, whereby we are renewed unto life, by the promise of Him whose blessing is His grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:364
verses.text: For this reason he saith, "according to Thy Word unto Thy servant:" that is, according to that which Thou hast promised unto Thy servant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:365
verses.text: Whether therefore it be regeneration whereby we are here adopted among the sons of God, or faith and hope and charity, which three are built up in us, although they come from the mercy of God; nevertheless, in this stormy and troublesome life they are the consolations of the miserable, not the joys of the blessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:366
verses.text: But since those things are destined to happen after and through these, he next saith, "O let Thy loving mercies come upon me, and I shall live".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:367
verses.text: For then indeed I shall truly live, when I shall not be able to fear lest I die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:368
verses.text: This is styled life absolutely and without any addition; nor is any life save that which is everlasting and blessed understood, as though it alone were to be called life, compared with which that which we now lead ought rather to be called death than life: according to those words in the Gospel, "If thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:369
verses.text: He then goeth on as follows: "Let the proud be confounded, for they have unrighteously practised iniquity against me: but I will be occupied in Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:370
verses.text: Behold, what he saith, the meditation of the law of God, or rather, his meditation the law of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:371
verses.text: "Let such as fear Thee," he saith, "and have known Thy testimonies, be turned unto me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:372
verses.text: But who is he who saith this? For no mortal will venture to say this, or if he say it, should be listened to.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:373
verses.text: Indeed, it is He who above also hath interposed His own words, saying, "I am a partaker with all them that fear Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:374
verses.text: Because He was made sharer in our mortal state, that we might also become partakers in His Divine Nature, we became sharers in One unto life, He a sharer in many unto death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:375
verses.text: He it is unto whom they that fear God turn, and who know the testimonies of God, so long before predicted of Him through the Prophets, a little before displayed in His presence through miracles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:376
verses.text: "O let my heart," he saith, "be unspotted in Thy righteousnesses, that I be not ashamed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:377
verses.text: He returneth to the words of His body, that is, His holy people, and now prayeth that his heart may be made unspotted, that is, the heart of His members; "in the righteousnesses of God," not in their own strength: for He hath prayed for this, not presumed upon it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:378
verses.text: In the words he hath added, "th at I be not ashamed," there is a resemblance to some of the earlier verses of this Psalm Whereas there, in the words, "O that," he signifieth a wish, he hath here expressed himself in the more open words of one praying: "O let my heart be sound:" so that in neither of these two sentences, each of which is one and the same, there is found the boldness of one who trusteth in his own free will against grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:379
verses.text: While he saith there, "so shall I not be confounded:" he saith here, "that I be not ashamed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:380
verses.text: The heart then of the members and the body of Christ is made unspotted, through the grace of God, by means of the very Head of that Body, that is, through Jesus Christ our Lord, by the "laver of regeneration," wherein all our past sins have been blotted out; through the aid of the Spirit, whereby we lust against the flesh, that we be not overcome in our fight; through the efficacy of the Lord's Prayer, wherein we say, "Forgive us our trespasses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:381
verses.text: Thus regeneration having been given to us, our conflict having been aided, prayer having been poured forth, our heart is made unspotted, so that we be not ashamed            Caph.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:382
verses.text: "My soul hath failed for Thy salvation: and I have hoped because of Thy word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:383
verses.text: It is not every failing that should be supposed to be blameable or deserving punishment: there is also a failing that is laudable or desirable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:384
verses.text: For it is said of a good failing: "My soul hath a desire and failing to enter into the courts of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:385
verses.text: So also here he saith not, faileth away from Thy salvation, but "faileth for Thy salvation," that is, towards Thy salvation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:386
verses.text: This losing ground is therefore good: for it doth indicate a longing after good, not as yet indeed gained, but most eagerly and earnestly desired.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:387
verses.text: But who saith this, save the chosen generation, the royal priesthood, the holy nation, the peculiar people, longing for Christ from the origin of the human race even unto the end of this world, in the persons of those who, each in his own time, have lived, are living, or are to live here?The first seasons of the Church, therefore, had Saints, before the Virgin's delivery, who desired the advent of His Incarnation: but these times, since He hath ascended into heaven, have Saints who desire His manifestation to judge the quick and the dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:388
verses.text: "And I have hoped because of Thy word:" that is, of Thy promise; a hope which causeth us to await with patience that which is not seen by those who believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:389
verses.text: Here also the Greek hath the word ἐπήλπισα, which some of our translators have preferred rendering by, "hoped-more;" since beyond doubt it will be greater than can be described.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:390
verses.text: "Mine eyes," he saith, "have failed for Thy word, saying, O when wilt Thou comfort me?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:391
verses.text: Behold that praiseworthy and blessed failing, in the eyes again, but his inner eyes, not arising from infirmity of mind, but from the strength of his longing for the promise of God: for this he saith, "for Thy word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:392
verses.text: But in what sense can such eyes say, "When wilt Thou comfort me?" save when we pray and groan with such earnestness and ardent expectation? For the tongue, not the eyes, is wont to speak: but in some sense the voice of the eyes is the longing of prayer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:393
verses.text: But in the words, "When wilt Thou comfort me?" he showeth that he endureth as it were delay.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:394
verses.text: Whence is this also, "How long, Lord, wilt Thou punish me?" And this is done either that the happiness may be the sweeter when deferred, or this is the sentiment of those who long, since the space of time, which may be short to Him who cometh to their aid, is tedious to the loving.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:395
verses.text: But God knoweth what He doth and when, for He "hath ordered all things in measure and number and weight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:396
verses.text: But when spiritual desires burn, carnal desires without doubt cool: on this account followeth, "Since I am become like a bottle in the frost, I do not forget Thy righteousnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:397
verses.text: Truly he desireth this mortal flesh to be understood by the bottle, the heavenly blessing by the frost, whereby the lusts of the flesh as it were by the binding of the frost become sluggish; and hence it ariseth that the righteousnesses of God do not slip from the memory, as long as we do not meditate apart from them; since what the Apostle saith is brought to pass: "Make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:398
verses.text: "And I do not forget Thy righteousness:" that is, I forget them not, because I have become such.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:399
verses.text: For the fervour of lust hath cooled, that the memory of love might glow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:400
verses.text: "How many are the days of Thy servant? when wilt Thou be avenged of them that persecute me?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:401
verses.text: In the Apocalypse, these are the words of the Martyrs, and long-suffering is enjoined them until the number of their brethren be fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:402
verses.text: The body of Christ then is asking concerning its days, what they are to be in this world, and that no man might suppose that the Church would cease to exist here before the end of the world came, and that some time would elapse in this world, while the Church was now no more on earth; therefore, when he had enquired concerning the days, he added also respecting the judgment, showing indeed that the Church would exist on earth until the judgment, when vengeance shall fall upon Her persecutors.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:403
verses.text: But if any one wonder why he should ask that question, to which when asked by the disciples, their Master replied, "It is not for you  to know the times and the seasons;" why should we not believe that in this passage of the Psalm it was prophesied that they should ask this very question, and that the words of the Church, which were so long before uttered here, were fulfilled in their question?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:404
verses.text: In what followeth: "The wicked have told me pleasant tales: but not like Thy law, O Lord" : the Latin translators have endeavoured to render the Greek ‡δολεσχίας, which cannot be expressed in one Latin word, so that some have rendered it "delights," and others "fablings," so that we must understand to be meant some kind of compositions, but in discourse of a nature to give pleasure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:405
verses.text: Both secular literature, and the Jewish book entitled Deuterosis, containing besides the canon of divine Scripture thousands of tales, comprise these in their different sects and professions; the vain and wandering loquacity of heretics holds them also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:406
verses.text: All these he wished to be considered as wicked, by whom he saith that ‡δολεσχίαι were related to him, that is, compositions which gave pleasure solely in their style: "But not," he addeth, "as Thy law, O Lord;" because truth, not words, pleases me therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:407
verses.text: Lastly, he addeth, "All Thy commandments are truth: they have persecuted me unjustly; O be Thou my help".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:408
verses.text: And the whole sense dependeth upon the foregoing: "How many are the days of Thy servant: when wilt Thou be avenged of them that persecute me?" For that they may persecute me, they have related to me these pleasant tales; but I have preferred Thy law to them, which on that account hath pleased me more, because all Thy commandments are true; not as in their discourses, where vanity aboundeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:409
verses.text: And for this reason "they have persecuted me falsely," because in me they have persecuted nothing save the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:410
verses.text: Therefore help Thou me, that I may struggle for the truth even unto death; because this is at once Thy commandment, and therefore it is also the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:411
verses.text: When the Church acted thus, She suffered what he hath added, "They had almost made an end of me upon earth" : a great slaughter of martyrs having been made, while they confess and preach the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:412
verses.text: But since it is not in vain said, "O help Thou me;" he addeth, "But I forsook not Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:413
verses.text: And that She might persevere unto the end, "O quicken me," he saith, "after Thy loving mercy: and so shall I keep the testimonies of Thy mouth" ; where the Greek hath Μαρτύρια.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:414
verses.text: This was not to be passed over in silence, on account of that sweetest name of Martyrs, who beyond doubt when so great cruelty of the persecutors was raging, that the Church was almost made an end of upon earth, would never have kept the testimonies of God, unless that had been vouchsafed them which is here spoken of, "O quicken me after Thy loving-kindness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:415
verses.text: For they were quickened, lest by loving life, they should deny the life, and by denying it, should lose it: and thus they who for life refused to forsake the truth, lived by dying for the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:416
verses.text: Lamed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:417
verses.text: The man who speaketh in this Psalm, as if he were tired of human mutability, whence this life is full of temptations, among his tribulations, on account of which he had above said, "The wicked have persecuted me;" and, "They have almost made an end of me upon earth" ; burning with longings for the heavenly Jerusalem; looked up to the realms above, and said, "O Lord, Thy word endureth for ever in heaven;" that is, among Thy Angels who serve everlastingly in Thine armies, without desertion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:418
verses.text: But the next verse, after heaven, pertaineth consequently to earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:419
verses.text: For this is one verse of the eight which relate to thi s letter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:420
verses.text: For eight verses are appended to each of these Hebrew letters, until this long Psalm be ended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:421
verses.text: "Thy truth also remaineth from one generation to the other: Thou hast laid the foundation of the earth, and it abideth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:422
verses.text: Beholding therefore the earth next after heaven with the gaze of a faithful mind, he findeth in it generations which are not in heaven, and saith, "Thy truth remaineth from one generation to the other:" signifying all generations by this expression, from which the Truth of God was never absent in His saints, at one time fewer, at one time more in number, according as the times happened or shall happen to vary; or wishing two particular generations to be understood, one pertaining to the Law and the Prophets, another to the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:423
verses.text: "Day continueth according to Thy ordinance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:424
verses.text: For all these things are day: "and this is the day which the Lord hath made: let us rejoice and be glad in it:" and "let us walk honestly as in the day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:425
verses.text: "For all things serve Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:426
verses.text: He said all things of some: "all" which belong to this day "serve Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:427
verses.text: For the ungodly of whom it is said, "I have compared thy mother unto the night," do not serve Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:428
verses.text: He then looketh back towards the source of this earth's deliverance, which caused it to abide when founded; and addeth, "If my delight had not been in Thy law, I should perchance have perished in my humiliation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:429
verses.text: This is the law of faith, not a vain faith, but that which worketh through love Through this grace is gained, which maketh men courageous in temporal tribulation, that they may not perish in the humiliation of mortality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:430
verses.text: "I will never forget," he saith, "Thy righteousnesses, for with them Thou hast quickened me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:431
verses.text: Behold how it was that he did not perish in his humiliation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:432
verses.text: For, save God quickeneth, what is man, Who can indeed kill, but cannot quicken himself?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:433
verses.text: He next addeth: "I am Thine: O save me, for I have sought Thy righteousnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:434
verses.text: We must not understand lightly the words, "I am Thine".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:435
verses.text: For what is not His? Why then is it that the Psalmist hath commended himself unto God somewhat in a more familiar sense, in these words, "I am Thine: O save me;" save because he wished it to be understood that he had desired to be his own only to his harm, which is the first and the greatest evil of disobedience? and as if he should say, I wished to be my own, and I lost myself: "I am Thine," he saith, "O save me, for I have sought Thy righteousnesses;" not my own inclinations, whereby I was my own, but "Thy righteousnesses," that I might now be Thine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:436
verses.text: "The ungodly," he saith, "have awaited me that they might destroy me; but I have understood Thy testimonies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:437
verses.text: What meaneth, "that they might destroy me"? Did he then fear that he should perish altogether at the death of his body? God forbid! and what meaneth, "have awaited me," save that he should consent with them unto iniquity? For then they would destroy him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:438
verses.text: And he hath said why he hath not perished: "I understood Thy testimonies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:439
verses.text: The Greek word, Μαρτύρια, soundeth more familiarly to the ears of the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:440
verses.text: For though they should slay me not consenting unto them, yet while I confessed Thy testimonies (martyria) I should not perish; but they who, that they might destroy me, were waiting till I should consent unto them, tortured me even when I did confess them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:441
verses.text: Yet he did not leave that which he had understood, looking on it and seeing an end without end, if only he should persevere unto the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:442
verses.text: Lastly, he next saith, "I have seen an end of all consummation: but Thy commandment is exceeding broad".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:443
verses.text: For he had entered into the sanctuary of God, and had understood the end Now "all consummation" appeareth to me in this place to signify, the striving even unto death for the truth, and the endurance of every evil for the true and chief good: the end of which consummation is to excel in the kingdom of Christ, which hath no end; and there to have without death, without pain, and with great honour, life, acquired by the death of this life, and by sorrows and reproaches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:444
verses.text: But in what he hath added, "Thy commandment is exceeding broad;" I understand only love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:445
verses.text: For what would it have profited him, whatever death impended over him, in the midst of whatsoever torment, to confess those testimonies, if love were not in the confessor?Broad therefore is the commandment of charity, that twofold commandment, whereby we are enjoined to love God and our neighbour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:446
verses.text: But what is broader than that, "on" which "hang all the Law and the Prophets"?            Mem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:447
verses.text: We have frequently admonished you, that love was to be understood by that praiseworthy breadth, by means of which, while we do the commandments of God, we feel no straitness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:448
verses.text: On this account also after saying above in this great Psalm, "Thy commandment is exceeding broad:" in the following verse he showeth wherefore it is broad: "what love have I unto Thy law, O Lord!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:449
verses.text: Love is therefore the breadth of the commandment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:450
verses.text: For how can it be that what God commandeth to be loved, be loved, and yet the commandment itself be not loved? For this itself is the law; "in all the day," he saith, "is my study in it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:451
verses.text: Behold how I have loved it, that in the whole day my study is in it; or rather, as the Greek hath it, "all the day long," which more fully expresses the continuance of meditation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:452
verses.text: Now that is to be understood through all time; which is, for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:453
verses.text: By such love lust is driven out: lust, which repeatedly opposeth our performing the commandments of the law, when "the flesh lusteth against the spirit:" against which the spirit lusting, ought so to love the law of God, that it be its study during the whole day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:454
verses.text: And he then addeth: "Thou hast made me to understand Thy commandment above mine enemies; for it is ever with me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:455
verses.text: For "they have indeed a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge," etc But the Psalmist, who understandeth the commandment of God above these his enemies, wishes to be found with the Apostle, "not having" his "own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is of the faith of Christ, which is of God;" not that the Law which his enemies read is not of God, but because they do not understand it, like him who understandeth it above his enemies, by clinging to the Stone upon which they stumbled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:456
verses.text: For "Christ is the end of the law," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:457
verses.text: , "that they may be justified freely through His grace;" not like those who imagine that they obey the law of their own strength, and are therefore, though by God's law, yet still endeavouring to set up their own righteousness; but as the son of promise, who hungering and athirst after it, by seeking, by asking, by knocking, as it were begs it of the Father, that being adopted he may receive it through His only-begotten Son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:458
verses.text: His enemies sought from the same commandment temporal rewards; and therefore it was not unto them for ever, as it was unto this man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:459
verses.text: For they who have translated "for ever" have rendered better than they who have written "for an age," since at the end of time there can be no longer a commandment of the law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:460
verses.text: But what meaneth the following verse, "I have more understanding than my teachers"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:461
verses.text: Who is he who had more understanding than all his teachers? Who, I ask, is he, who dareth to prefer himself in understanding above all the Prophets, who not only by speaking taught with so excellent authority those who lived with them, but also their posterity by writing?What is here said, could not have been spoken in Solomon's person.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:462
verses.text: I recognise plainly Him who had more understanding than His teachers, since when He was a boy of twelve years of age, Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, and was found by His parents after three days' space, "sitting in the temple among the doctors, hearing them and asking them questions".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:463
verses.text: The Son Himself hath said, "As My Father hath taught Me, I speak these things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:464
verses.text: It is very difficult to understand this of the Person of the Word; unless we can comprehend that it is the same thing for the Son to be taught as to be begotten of the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:465
verses.text: "He took upon Himself the form of a servant;" for when He had assumed this form, men of more advanced age might think Him fit to be taught as a boy; but He whom the Father taught, had more understanding than all His teachers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:466
verses.text: "For Thy testimonies," He saith, "are my study".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:467
verses.text: For this reason He had more understanding than all His teachers, because He studied the testimonies of God, which, as concerning Himself, He knew better than they, when He spoke these words: "Ye sent unto John, and he bare witness unto the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:468
verses.text: But I receive not testimony from man," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:469
verses.text: But these teachers may be understood very reasonably to be those aged men, of whom he presently saith, "I am wiser than mine elders".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:470
verses.text: And this seemeth to me to be repeated here thus, that that age of His which is well known to us in the Gospel might be called to our remembrance; the age of boyhood, during which He was sitting among the aged, understanding more than all His teachers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:471
verses.text: For the smaller and the greater in age are wont to be termed younger and elder, although neither of them hath arrived at or approached old age; although if we are concerned to seek in the Gospel the express term, elders, more than whom He understood, we find it when the Scribes and Pharisees said unto Him, "Why do Thy disciples transgression the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:472
verses.text: Behold the transgression of the tradition of the elders is objected to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:473
verses.text: But He who was wiser than His elders, let us hear what answer He made them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:474
verses.text: "Why do ye also, He asked, "transgress the commandment of God by your tradition?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:475
verses.text: But what cometh next, doth not seem to apply to the Head, but to the Body: "I have refrained my feet from every evil way, that I may keep Thy words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:476
verses.text: For that Head of ours, the Saviour of the Body Himself, could not be borne by carnal lust into any evil way, so that it should be needful for Him to refrain His feet, as though they would go thither of their own accord; which we do, when we refrain our evil desires, which He had not, that they may not follow evil ways.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:477
verses.text: For thus we are able to keep the word of God, if we "go not after our evil lusts," so that they attain unto the evils desired; but rather curb them with the spirit which lusteth against the flesh, that they may not drag us away, seduced and overthrown, through evil ways.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:478
verses.text: "I have not shrunk," he saith, "from Thy judgments: for Thou hast laid down a law for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:479
verses.text: He hath stated what made him fear, so that he refrained his feet from every evil way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:480
verses.text: Thou, more inward than my inmost self, Thou hast laid down a law within my heart by Thy Spirit, as it were by Thy fingers, that I might not fear it as a slave without love, but might love it with a chaste fear as a son, and fear it with a chaste love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:481
verses.text: Consider then what followeth: "O how sweet are Thy words unto my throat!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:482
verses.text: Or, as it is more literally rendered from the Greek, "Thy utterances, above honey and the honeycomb unto my mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:483
verses.text: This is that sweetness which the Lord giveth, "So that the earth yield her increase:" that we do good truly in a good spirit, that is, not from the dread of carnal evil, but from the gladness of spiritual good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:484
verses.text: Some copies indeed do not read "honeycomb:" but the majority do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:485
verses.text: Now the open teaching of wisdom is like unto honey; but that is like the comb which is squeezed from the more recondite mysteries, as if from cells of wax, by the mouth of the teacher, as if he were chewing it: but it is sweet to the mouth of the heart, not to the mouth of the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:486
verses.text: But what mean the words, "Through Thy commandments I get understanding"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:487
verses.text: For the expressions, I have understood Thy commandments: and, "I get understanding through Thy commandments;" are different.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:488
verses.text: Something else then he signifieth that he hath understood from the commandments of God: that is, as far as I can see, he saith, that by obeying God's commandments he hath arrived at the comprehension of those things which he had longed to know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:489
verses.text: These then are the words of the spiritual members of Christ, "Through Thy commandments I get understanding".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:490
verses.text: For the body of Christ rightly saith these words in those, to whom, while they keep the commandments, a richer knowledge of wisdom is given on account of this very keeping of the commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:491
verses.text: "Therefore," he addeth, "I hate all evil ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:492
verses.text: For it is needful that the love of righteousness should hate all iniquity: that love, which is so much the stronger, in proportion as the sweetness of a higher wisdom doth inspire it, a wisdom given unto him who obeyeth God, and getteth understanding from His commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:493
verses.text: Nun.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:494
verses.text: "Thy word is a lantern unto my feet, and a light unto my paths".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:495
verses.text: The word "lantern" appears in the word "light;" "my feet" are also repeated in "my paths".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:496
verses.text: What then meaneth "Thy Word"? Is it He who was in the beginning God with God, that is, the Word by whom all things were made? It is not thus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:497
verses.text: For that Word is a light, but is not a lantern.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:498
verses.text: For a lantern is a creature, not a creator; and it is lighted by participation of an unchangeable light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:499
verses.text: For no creature, howsoever rational and intellectual, is lighted by itself, but is lighted by participation of eternal Truth: although sometimes day is spoken of, not meaning the Lord, but that "day which the Lord hath made," and on account of which it is said, "Come unto Him, and be lightened".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:500
verses.text: On account of which participation, inasmuch as the Mediator Himself became Man, He is styled lantern in the Apocalypse But this sense is a solitary one; for it cannot be divinely spoken of any of the saints, nor in any wise lawfully said of any, "The Word was made flesh," save of the "one Mediator between God and men".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:501
verses.text: Since therefore the only-begotten Word, coequal with the Father, is styled a light; and man when enlightened by the Word is also called a light, who is styled also a lantern, as John, as the Apostles; and since no man of these is the Word, and that Word by whom they were enlightened is not a lantern; what is this word, which is thus called a light and a lantern at the same time, save we understand the word which was sent unto the Prophets, or which was preached through the Apostles; not Christ the Word, but the word of Christ, of which it is written, "Faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God"? For the Apostle Peter also, comparing the prophetical word to a lantern, saith, "whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a lantern, that shineth in a dark place".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:502
verses.text: What, therefore, he here saith, "Thy word" is the word which is contained in all the holy Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:503
verses.text: "I have sworn, and am stedfastly purposed to keep Thy righteous judgments" : as one who walked aright in the light of that lantern, and kept to straight paths.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:504
verses.text: For he calleth what he hath determined by a sacrament, an oath; because the mind ought to be so fixed in keeping the righteous judgments of God, that its determination should be in the place of an oath.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:505
verses.text: Now the righteous judgments of God are kept by faith; when, under the righteous judgment of God, neither any good work is believed to be fruitless, nor any sin unpunished; but, because the body of Christ hath suffered many most grievous evils for this faith, he saith, "I was humbled above measure".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:506
verses.text: He doth not say, I have humbled myself, so that we must needs understand that humiliation which is commanded; but he saith, "I was humbled above-measure;" that is, suffered a very heavy persecution, because he swore and was steadfastly purposed to keep the righteous judgments of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:507
verses.text: And, lest in such trouble faith herself might faint he addeth, "Quicken me, O Lord, according to Thy word:" that is, according to Thy promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:508
verses.text: For the word of the promises of God is a lantern to the feet, and a light to the paths.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:509
verses.text: Thus also above, in the humiliation of persecution, he prayed that God would quicken him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:510
verses.text: "Make the freewill offerings of my mouth well pleasing, O Lord" : that is, let them please Thee; do not reject, but approve them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:511
verses.text: By the freewill offerings of the mouth are well understood the sacrifices of praise, offered up in the confession of love, not from the fear of necessity; whence it is said, "a freewill offering will I offer Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:512
verses.text: But what doth he add? "and teach me Thy judgments"? Had he not himself said above, "From Thy judgments I have not swerved"? How could he have done thus, if he knew them not? Moreover, if he knew them, in what sense doth he here say, "and teach me Thy judgments"? Is it as in a former passage, "Thou hast dealt in sweetness with Thy servant:" presently after which we find, "teach me sweetness"? This passage we explained as the words of one who was gaining in grace, and praying that he might receive in addition to what he had received.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:513
verses.text: "My soul is alway in Thy hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:514
verses.text: Some copies read, "in my hand:" but most, "in Thy hand;" and this latter is indeed easy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:515
verses.text: For "the souls of the righteous are in God's hand: in whose hand are both we and our words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:516
verses.text: "And I do not forget Thy law:" as if his memory were aided to remember God's law by the hands of Him in whose hands is his soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:517
verses.text: But how the words, "My soul is in my hands," can be understood, I know not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:518
verses.text: For these are the words of the righteous, not of the ungodly; of one who is returning to the Father, not departing from the FatherIs it perhaps said, "My soul is in my hands," in this sense, as if he offered it to God to be quickened? Whence in another passage it is said, "Unto Thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:519
verses.text: Since here too he had said above, "Quicken Thou me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:520
verses.text: "The ungodly," he saith, "have laid a snare for me: but yet I swerved not from Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:521
