verses.text: Whence this, unless because his soul is in the hands of God, or in his own hands is offered to God to be quickened?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:522
verses.text: "Thy testimonies have I gained in heritage for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:523
verses.text: Some wishing to express in one word what is put in one word in the Greek, have translated it hereditavi.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:524
verses.text: Which although it might be Latin, yet would rather signify one who gave an inheritance than one who received it, hereditavi being like ditavi.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:525
verses.text: Better, therefore, the whole sense is conveyed in two words, whether we say, "I have possessed in heritage," or, "I have gotten in heritage:" not gotten heritage, but "gotten in heritage".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:526
verses.text: If it be asked, what he gained in heritage, he replieth, "Thy testimonies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:527
verses.text: What doth he wish to be understood, save that he might become a witness of God, and confess His testimonies, that is, that he might become a Martyr of God, and might declare His testimonies, as the Martyrs do, was a gift bestowed upon him by the Father, of whom he is heir?But even their wish was prepared by the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:528
verses.text: For this reason he saith he hath gained them in heritage, and this "for ever;" because they have not in them the temporal glory of men who seek vain things, but the eternal glory of those who suffer for a short season, and who reign without end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:529
verses.text: Whence the next words, "Because they are the very joy of my heart:" although the affliction of the body, yet the very joy of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:530
verses.text: He then addeth: "I have applied my heart to fulfil Thy righteousness for ever, for my reward".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:531
verses.text: He who saith, "I have applied my heart," had before said, "Incline my heart unto Thy testimonies:" so that we may understand that it is at once a divine gift, and an act of free will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:532
verses.text: But are we to fulfil the righteousnesses of God for ever? Those works which we perform in regard to the need of our neighbours, cannot be everlasting, any more than their need; but if we do not do them from love, there is no righteousness; if we do them from love, that love is everlasting, and an everlasting reward is in store for it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:533
verses.text: Samech.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:534
verses.text: "I have hated the unrighteous; and Thy law have I loved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:535
verses.text: He saith not, I hate the wicked, and love the righteous; or, I hate iniquity, and love Thy law; but, after saying, "I have hated the unrighteous," he explains why, by adding, "and Thy law have I loved;" to show, that he did not hate human nature in unrighteous men, but their unrighteousness whereby they are foes to the law, which he loveth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:536
verses.text: He next addeth: "Thou art my helper and my taker up" : "my helper," to do good works: "my taker up," to escape evil ones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:537
verses.text: In the next words, "I have hoped more on Thy word," he speaketh as a son of promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:538
verses.text: But what is the meaning of the following verse: "Away from me, ye wicked, and I will search the commandments of my God"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:539
verses.text: For he saith not, I will perform; but, "I will search".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:540
verses.text: In order, therefore, that he may diligently and perfectly learn that law, he bids the wicked depart from him, and even forcibly driveth them away from his company.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:541
verses.text: For the wicked exercise us in the fulfilment of the commandments, but lead us away from searching into them; not only when they persecute, or wish to litigate with us; but even when they court us, and honour us, and yet expect us to occupy ourselves in aiding their own vicious and busy desire, and to bestow our time upon them; or at least harass the weak, and compel them to bring their causes before us: to whom we dare not say, "Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?" For the Apostle instituted ecclesiastical judges of such causes, forbidding Christians to contend in the forumCertainly, on account of those who carry on law suits pertinaciously with one another, and, when they harass the good, scorn our judgments, and cause us to lose the time that should be employed upon things divine; surely, I say, on account of these men we also may exclaim in these words of the Body of Christ, "Away from me, ye wicked! and I will search the commandments of my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:542
verses.text: "O stablish me according to Thy word and I shall live: and let me not be disappointed of my hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:543
verses.text: He who had before said, "Thou art my taker up," prayeth that he may be more and more borne up, and be led unto that, for the sake of which he endureth so many troubles; trusting that he may there live in a truer sense, than in these dreams of human affairs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:544
verses.text: For it is said of the future, "and I shall live," as if we did not live in this dead body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:545
verses.text: While "we await the redemption of our body, we are saved by hope, and hoping for that we see not, we await with patience".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:546
verses.text: But hope disappointeth not, if the love of God be spread abroad in our hearts through the Holy Spirit which is given unto us And, as though it were answered him in silence, Thou dost not wish to be disappointed of thy hope? Cease not to meditate upon My righteousnesses: and, feeling that this meditation is usually hindered by the weaknesses of the soul, "Help me," he saith, "and I shall be safe; yea, I will meditate in Thy righteousnesses always".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:547
verses.text: "Thou hast scorned all," or, as it seems more closely translated from the Greek, "Thou hast brought to nought all them that depart from Thy righteousnesses: for their thought is unrighteous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:548
verses.text: For this reason he exclaimed, "Help Thou me, and I shall be safe; yea, I will meditate in Thy righteousnesses always:" because God bringeth to nought all those who depart from His righteousnesses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:549
verses.text: But why do they depart? Because "their thought is," he saith, "unrighteous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:550
verses.text: They advance in that direction, while they depart from God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:551
verses.text: All deeds, good or bad, proceed from the thoughts: in his thoughts every man is innocent, in his thoughts every man is guilty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:552
verses.text: The next words in the Psalm are, "I have counted," or "thought," or "esteemed, all the ungodly of the earth as transgressors".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:553
verses.text: In the Latin version many different renderings are given of the Greek ἐλογισ€μην; but this passage hath a deep meaning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:554
verses.text: For the following words, "Therefore have I ever loved Thy testimonies:" make it far more profound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:555
verses.text: For the Apostle saith, "The law worketh wrath;" and, explaining these words, he addeth, "For where no law is, there is no transgression:" thereby showing that not all are transgressors.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:556
verses.text: For all have not the law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:557
verses.text: That all have not the law, he declareth more explicitly in another passage, "as many as have sinned without law, shall also perish without law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:558
verses.text: What then meaneth, "I have held all the ungodly of the earth as transgressors"? "As transgressors;" or rather "transgressing," for the Greek saith, παραβαίνοντας, not παραβ€τας.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:559
verses.text: "The law entered that sin might abound".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:560
verses.text: But since all sins are remitted through grace, not only those which are committed without the law, but those also which are committed in the law; he addeth, "But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:561
verses.text: But, indeed, when the Apostle said, "As many as have sinned without law, shall perish without law," he was speaking of that law which God gave to His people Israel through Moses His servant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:562
verses.text: For some even Catholic expositors, from a want of sufficient heedfulness, have pronounced contrary to the truth, that those who have sinned without the law perish; and that those who have sinned in the law, are only judged, and do not perish, as if they should be considered destined to be cleansed by means of transitory punishments, as he of whom it is said, "he himself shall be saved, yet so as by fire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:563
verses.text: The Psalmist also hath subjoined: "Therefore I loved Thy testimonies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:564
verses.text: As if he should say: Since the law, whether given in paradise, or implanted by nature, or promulgated in writing, hath made all the sinners of the earth transgressors; "Therefore I loved Thy testimonies," which are in Thy laws of Thy grace; so that not my but Thy righteousness is in me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:565
verses.text: For the law profiteth unto this end, that it send us forward unto grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:566
verses.text: For not only because it testifieth towards the manifestation of the righteousness of God, which is without the law; but also in this very point that it rendereth men transgressors, so that the letter even slayeth, it driveth us to fly unto the quickening Spirit, through whom the whole of our sins may be blotted out, and the love of righteous deeds be inspired.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:567
verses.text: The grace of God, then, being known, which alone freeth from transgression, which is committed through knowledge of the law, he saith, in prayer, "Fix with nails my flesh in Thy fear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:568
verses.text: For this some Latin interpreters have literally rendered the Greek καθήλωσον, which that language has expressed in one word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:569
verses.text: Some have preferred to render by the word confige, without adding clavis; and while they thus desire to construe one Latin by one Greek word, have failed to express the full meaning of the Greek καθήλωσον, because in confige nails are not mentioned, but καθήλωσον cannot be taken but of nails, nor can "fix with nails" be expressed without using two words in Latin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:570
verses.text: Hath he added, "For I have feared Thy judgments"? What meaneth, "Fix me in Thy fear: for I have feared"? If he had already feared, or if he was now fearing, why did he still pray God to crucify his flesh in His fear? Did he wish so much additional fear imparted to him as would suffice for crucifying his flesh, that is, his carnal lusts and affections; as though he should say, Perfect in me the fear of Thee; for I have feared Thy judgments? But there is here even a higher sense, which must, as far as God alloweth, be derived from searching the recesses of this Scripture: that is, in the chaste fear of Thee, which abideth from age to age, let my carnal desires be quenched; "For I have feared Thy judgments," when the law, which could not give me righteousness, threatened me punishment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:571
verses.text: For the inclination to sin liveth, and it then appeareth in deed, when impunity may be hoped for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:572
verses.text: But when punishment is considered sure to follow, it liveth latently: nevertheless it liveth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:573
verses.text: For it would rather it were lawful to sin, and it grieveth that what the law forbiddeth, is not lawful; because it is not spiritually delighted with the blessing of the law, but carnally feareth the evil which it threateneth But that love, which casteth out this fear, feareth with a chaste fear to sin, although no punishment follow; because it doth not even judge that impunity will follow, since from love of righteousness it considereth the very sin itself a punishment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:574
verses.text: With such a fear the flesh is crucified; since carnal delights, which are forbidden rather than avoided by the letter of the law, are overcome by the delight in spiritual blessings, and also when the victory is perfected are destroyed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:575
verses.text: Ain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:576
verses.text: "I have dealt judgment and righteousness; O give me not over unto mine oppressors".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:577
verses.text: It is not wonderful that he should have dealt judgment and righteousness, since he had above prayed for a chaste fear from God, whereby to fix with nails his flesh, that is, his carnal lusts, which are wont to hinder our judgment from being right.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:578
verses.text: But although in our customary speech judgment is either right or wrong, whence it is said unto men in the Gospel, "Judge not according to the persons, but judge righteous judgment:"  nevertheless in this passage judgment is used as though, if it were not righteous, it ought not to be called judgment; otherwise it would not be enough to say, "I have dealt judgment," but it would be said, I have dealt righteous judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:579
verses.text: Whoso therefore in the chaste fear of God hath his flesh crucified, and corrupted by no carnal allurement, dealeth judgment and the work of righteousness, ought to pray that he may not be given up to his adversaries; that is, that he may not, through his dread of suffering evils, yield unto his adversaries to do evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:580
verses.text: For he receiveth power of endurance, which guardeth him from being overcome with pain, from Him from whom he receiveth the victory over lust, which preventeth his being seduced by pleasure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:581
verses.text: He next saith, "Take off Thy servant to that which is good, that the proud calumniate me not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:582
verses.text: They drive me on, that I may fall into evil; do Thou take me off to that which is good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:583
verses.text: They who rendered these words by the Latin, calumnientur, have followed a Greek expression, not commonly used in Latin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:584
verses.text: Have the words, Let not the proud calumniate me, the same force, as, Let them "not succeed in calumniating me"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:585
verses.text: To prefigure His Cross, Moses by the merciful command of God raised aloft on a pole the image of a serpent in the desert, that the likeness of sinful flesh which must be crucified in Christ might be prefigured By gazing upon this healing Cross, we cast out all the poison of the scandals of the proud: the Cross, which the Psalmist intently looking upon, saith, "My eyes have failed for Thy salvation, and for the words of Thy righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:586
verses.text: For God made Christ Himself "to be sin for us, on account of the likeness of sinful flesh, that we may be made the righteousness of God in Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:587
verses.text: For His utterance of the righteousness of God he therefore saith that his eyes have failed, from gazing ardently and eagerly, while, remembering human infirmity, he longeth for divine grace in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:588
verses.text: In connection with this he goes on to say, "O deal with Thy servant according to Thy loving mercy" ; not according to my righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:589
verses.text: "And teach me," he saith, "Thy righteousnesses;" those beyond doubt, whereby God rendereth men righteous, not they themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:590
verses.text: "I am Thy servant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:591
verses.text: O grant me understanding, that I may know Thy testimonies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:592
verses.text: This petition must never be intermitted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:593
verses.text: For it sufficeth not to have received understanding, and to have learnt the testimonies of God, unless it be evermore received, and evermore in a manner quaffed from the fountain of eternal light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:594
verses.text: For the testimonies of God are the better and the better known, the more understanding a man attaineth to.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:595
verses.text: "It is time," he saith, "for the Lord to lay to His hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:596
verses.text: For this is the reading of most copies: not as some have, "O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:597
verses.text: Now what is this, save the grace which was revealed in Christ at its own time? Of which season the Apostle saith, "But when the fullness of time was come, God sent His Son".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:598
verses.text: But wherefore is it that, seemingly anxious to show the Lord that it was time to lay to His hand, he hath subjoined, "They have scattered Thy law;" as if it were the season for the Lord to act, because the proud scattered His law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:599
verses.text: For what meaneth this? In the wickedness of transgression, they have not guarded its integrity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:600
verses.text: It was needful therefore that the Law should be given to the proud and those presuming in the freedom of their own will, after a transgression of which whosoever were contrite and humbled, might run no longer by the Law, but by faith, to aiding grace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:601
verses.text: When the Law therefore was scattered, it was time that mercy should be sent through the only-begotten Son of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:602
verses.text: "Therefore," he saith, "I love Thy commandments above gold and topaz".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:603
verses.text: Grace hath this object, that the commandments, which could not be fulfilled by fear, may be fulf illed by loveTherefore, they are above gold and topaz stones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:604
verses.text: For this is read in another Psalm also, "Above gold and exceeding precious stones".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:605
verses.text: For topaz is a stone considered very precious.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:606
verses.text: But they not understanding the hidden grace which was in the Old Testament, screened as it were by the veil (this was signified when they were unable to gaze upon the face of Moses), endeavoured to obey the commandments of God for the sake of an earthly and carnal reward, but could not obey them; because they did not love them, but something else.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:607
verses.text: Whence these were not the works of the willing, but rather the burdens of the unwilling.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:608
verses.text: But when the commandments are loved for their own sake "above gold and exceeding precious stones," all earthly reward compared with the commandments themselves is vile; nor are any other goods of man comparable in any respect with those goods whereby man himself is made good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:609
verses.text: "Therefore," he saith, "was I made straight unto all Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:610
verses.text: I was made straight, doubtless, because I loved them; and I clung by love to them, which were straight, that I might also myself become straight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:611
verses.text: Then what he addeth, naturally follows: "and every unrighteous way I utterly abhor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:612
verses.text: For how could it be that he who loved the straight could do aught save abhor an unrighteous way? For as, if he loved gold and precious stones, he would abhor all that might bring loss of such property: thus, since he loved the commandments of God, he abhorred the path of iniquity, as one of the most savage rocks in the sailor's track, whereon he must needs suffer shipwreck of things so precious.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:613
verses.text: That this may not be his lot, he who saileth on the wood of the Cross with the divine commandments as his freight, steereth far from thence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:614
verses.text: Pe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:615
verses.text: "Thy testimonies are wonderful: therefore hath my soul searched them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:616
verses.text: Who counteth, even by their kinds, the testimonies of God? Heaven and earth, His visible and invisible works, declare in some manner the testimony of His goodness and greatness; and the very ordinary and accustomed course of nature, whereby the seasons are rapidly revolved, in all things after their kinds, however temporal and perishable, however held cheap through our constant experience of them, give, if a pious thinker give heed to them, a testimony to the Creator.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:617
verses.text: But which of these is not wonderful, if we measure each not by its habitual presence, but by reason? But if we venture to bring all nature within the comprehensive view of one act of contemplation, doth not that take place in us which the prophet describeth, "I considered Thy works, and trembled"? Yet the Psalmist was not terrified in his wonder at creation, but rather said that this was the reason that he ought to search it, because it was wonderful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:618
verses.text: For after saying, "Thy testimonies are wonderful," he addeth, "therefore hath my soul searched them;" as if he had become more curious from the difficulty of thoroughly searching them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:619
verses.text: For the more abstruse are the causes of anything, the more wonderful it is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:620
verses.text: "When thy word goeth forth," he saith, "it giveth light, and maketh His little ones to understand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:621
verses.text: What is the little one save the humble and weak? Be not proud therefore, presume not in thine own strength, which is nought; and thou wilt understand why a good law was given by a good God, though it cannot give life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:622
verses.text: For it was given for this end, that it might make thee a little one instead of great, that it might show that thou hadst not strength to do the law of thine own power: and that thus, wanting aid and destitute, thou mightest fly unto grace, saying, "Have mercy upon me, O Lord, for I am weak".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:623
verses.text: Let all be little ones, and let all the world be guilty before Thee: because "by the deeds of the Law there shall no flesh be justified" in Thy sight; "for by the Law is the knowledge of sin," etc These are Thy wonderful testimonies, which the soul of this little one hath searched; and hath therefore found, because he became humbled and a little one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:624
verses.text: For who doth Thy commandments as they ought to be done, that is, by "faith which worketh through love," save love itself be shed abroad in his heart through the Holy Spirit?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:625
verses.text: This is confessed by this little one; "I opened my mouth," he saith, "and drew in the spirit: for I longed for Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:626
verses.text: What did he long for, save to obey the divine commandments? But there was no possibility of the weak doing hard things, the little one great things: he opened his mouth, confessing that he could not do them of himself: and drew in power to do them: he opened his mouth, by seeking, asking, knocking: and athirst drank in the good Spirit, which enabled him to do what he could not do by himself, "the commandment holy and just and good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:627
verses.text: Not that they themselves who "are led by the Spirit of God," do nothing; but that they may not do nothing good, they are moved to act by the good Spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:628
verses.text: For so much the more is every man made a good son, in proportion as the good Spirit is given unto Him by the Father in a greater measure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:629
verses.text: He still prayeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:630
verses.text: He hath opened his mouth, and drawn in the Spirit; but he still knocketh in prayer unto the Father, and seeketh: he drinketh, but the more sweet he findeth it, the more eagerly doth he thirst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:631
verses.text: Hear the words of him in his thirst.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:632
verses.text: "O look Thou upon me," he saith, "and be merciful unto me: according to the judgment of those that love Thy Name" : that is, according to the judgment Thou has dealt unto all who love Thy Name; since Thou hast first loved them, to cause them to love Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:633
verses.text: For thus saith the Apostle John, "We love God, because He first loved us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:634
verses.text: See what the Psalmist next most openly saith: "Order my steps after Thy word: and so shall no wickedness have dominion over me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:635
verses.text: Where what else doth he say than this, Make me upright and free according to Thy promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:636
verses.text: But so much the more as the love of God reigneth in every man, so much the less hath wickedness dominion over him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:637
verses.text: What else then doth he seek than that by the gift of God he may love God? For by loving God he loveth himself, so that he may healthily love his neighbour also as himself: on which commandments hang all the Law and the Prophets What then doth he pray, save that God may cause the fulfillment by His help of those commandments which He imposeth by His bidding?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:638
verses.text: But what meaneth this that he saith, "O deliver me from the calumnies of men: so shall I keep Thy commandments"? Did not the holy people of God much the more gloriously keep the commandments among these very calumnies, when they were at their hottest in the midst of tribulations, when they yielded not to their persecutors to commit impieties? But, in truth, the meaning of these words is this: Do Thou, by pouring upon me Thy Spirit, guard me from being overcome by the terrors of human calumny, and from being drawn over to their evil deeds away from Thy commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:639
verses.text: For if Thou hast thus dealt with me, that is, if Thou hast in this manner delivered me by the gift of patience from their calumnies, so that I fear not the false charges they prefer against me; among those very calumnies I will keep Thy commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:640
verses.text: "Show the light of Thy countenance on Thy servant, and teach me thy statutes" : that is, manifest Thy presence, by succouring and aiding me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:641
verses.text: "And teach me Thy righteousnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:642
verses.text: Teach me to work them: as it is more plainly expressed elsewhere, "Teach me to do Thy will".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:643
verses.text: For they who hear, although they retain in their memories what they hear, are by no means to be considered to have learnt, unless they do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:644
verses.text: For it is the word of Truth: "Every man that hath heard and hath learned of the Father, cometh unto Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:645
verses.text: He therefore who obeyeth not in deed, that is, who cometh not, hath not learnt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:646
verses.text: "My eyes have descended streams of waters, because they have not kept Thy law" : that is, my eyes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:647
verses.text: For in some copies there is this reading, "Because I have not kept Thy law, streams of waters" therefore "descended," that is, floods of tears            Tadze.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:648
verses.text: Thus, then, as if giving a reason why he had cause to weep much, and to mourn deeply for his sin, he saith, "Righteous art Thou, O Lord, and true is Thy judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:649
verses.text: "Thou hast commanded Thy testimonies, righteousness, and Thy truth exceedingly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:650
verses.text: This righteousness of God and righteous judgment and truth, is to be feared by every sinner: for thereby all who are condemned are condemned of God; nor is there one who can righteously complain against the righteous God of his own damnation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:651
verses.text: Therefore the tears of the penitent are needful; since if his impenitent heart were condemned, he would be most justly condemned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:652
verses.text: He indeed calleth the testimonies of God righteousness: for He proveth himself righteous by giving righteous commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:653
verses.text: And this is truth also, that God may become known by such testimonies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:654
verses.text: But what is it that followeth: "My zeal hath caused me to pine" ; or, as other copies read, Thy zeal? Others have also, "The zeal of Thy house:" and, "hath eaten me up," instead of, "hath caused me to pine".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:655
verses.text: This, as it seems to me, has been considered as an emendation to be introduced from another Psalm, where it is written, "The zeal of Thy house hath eaten me up:"  a text quoted also, as we know, in the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:656
verses.text: The two words, however, "hath caused me to pine," and "hath eaten me up," are somewhat like.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:657
verses.text: But the words, "my zeal," which most of the copies read, occasion no dispute: for what wonder is it if every man pineth away from his own zeal? The words read in other copies, "Thy zeal," signify a man zealous for God, not for himself: but there is no difficulty in using "my" in the same senseThe Psalmist's jealousy is therefore also to be understood in a good sense: for he addeth the cause, and saith, "Because mine enemies have forgotten Thy words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:658
verses.text: Then considering with himself with what a flame of love he burned for the commandments of God: "Fiery," saith he, "is Thy word exceedingly, and Thy servant hath loved it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:659
verses.text: Justly jealous was he of the impenitent heart in His enemies, who had forgotten God's word; for he endeavoured to bring them unto that which he himself most ardently loved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:660
verses.text: "I am young, and of no reputation; yet do I not forget Thy righteousnesses:" not as my enemies, who "have forgotten Thy words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:661
verses.text: The younger seems to grieve for those older than himself who had forgotten the righteousnesses of God, while he himself had not forgotten.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:662
verses.text: For what meaneth, "I am young, yet do I not forget"? save this, Those older than me have forgotten.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:663
verses.text: For the Greek word is νεώτερος, the same as that used in the words above, "Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way?" This is a comparative, and is therefore well understood in its relation to some one older.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:664
verses.text: Let us therefore here recognize the two nations, who were striving even in Rebecca's womb; when it was said to her, not from works, but of Him that calleth, "The elder shall serve the younger".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:665
verses.text: But the younger saith here that he is of no reputation: for this reason he hath become greater: since "behold, they that were first are last, and they that were last first".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:666
verses.text: It is no wonder that they have forgotten the words of God, who have chosen to set up their own righteousness, ignorant of the righteousness of God; but he, the younger, hath not forgotten, for he hath not wished to have a righteousness of his own, but that of God, of which he now also saith, "Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and Thy law is the truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:667
verses.text: For how is not the law truth, through which came the knowledge of sin, and that which giveth testimony of the righteousness of God? For thus the Apostle saith: "The righteousness of God is manifested, being witnessed by the Law and the Prophets".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:668
verses.text: On account of this law the younger suffered persecution from the elder, so that the younger saith what followeth: "Trouble and hardship have taken hold upon me: yet is my meditation in Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:669
verses.text: Let them rage, let them persecute; as long as the commandments of God be not abandoned, and, after those commandments, let even those who rage be loved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:670
verses.text: "Thy testimonies are righteousness unto everlasting: O grant me understanding, and I shall live".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:671
verses.text: This younger one prayeth for understanding; which if he had not, he would not be "wiser than the aged;" but he prayeth for it in trouble and hardships, that he may thereby understand how contemptible is all that his persecuting enemies can take from him, by whom he saith he hath been despised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:672
verses.text: Therefore he hath said, "and I shall live:" because if trouble and heaviness reached such a pitch, that his life should be terminated by the hands of his persecuting enemies, he will live for ever, who preferreth to temporal things, righteousness which remaineth for evermore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:673
verses.text: This righteousness in trouble and hardship are the Martyria Dei, that is, the testimonies of God, for which Martyrs have been crowned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:674
verses.text: Koph.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:675
verses.text: He who singeth this Psalm, mentioneth such a prayer of his own: "I have called with my whole heart; hear me, O Lord!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:676
verses.text: For to what end his cry profiteth, he addeth: "I will search out Thy righteousnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:677
verses.text: For this purpose then he hath called with his whole heart, and hath longed that this might be given him by the Lord listening unto him, that he may search out His righteousnesses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:678
verses.text: "I have called, save me"  or as some copies, both Greek and Latin, have it, "I have called to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:679
verses.text: But what is, "I have called to Thee," save that by calling I have invoked Thee? But when he had said, "save me;" what did he add? "And I will keep Thy testimonies:" that is, that I may not, through infirmity, deny Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:680
verses.text: For the health of the soul causeth that to be done which it is known to be our duty to do, and thus in striving even to the death of the body, if the extremity of temptation demand this in defence of the truth of the divine testimonies: but where there is not health of the soul, weakness yieldeth, and truth is deserted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:681
verses.text: "I have prevented in midnight," he saith, "and have cried: In Thy words have I trusted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:682
verses.text: If we refer this to each of the faithful, and to the literal character of the act; it oft happeneth that the love of God is awake in that hour of the night, and, the love of prayer strongly urging us, the time of prayer, which is wont to be after the crowing of the cock, is not awaited, but prevented.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:683
verses.text: But if we understand night of the whole of this world's duration; we indeed cry unto God at midnight, and prevent the fulness of time in which He will restore us what He hath promised, as is elsewhere read, "Let us prevent His presence with confession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:684
verses.text: Although if we choose to understand the unripe season of this night, before the fulness of time had come, that is, the ripe season when Christ should be manifested in the flesh; neither was the Church then silent, but preventing this fulness of time, in prophecy cried out, and trusted in the words of God, who was able to do what He promised, that in the seed of Abraham all nations should be blessed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:685
verses.text: The Church saith also what followeth, "Mine eyes have prevented the morning watch, that I might meditate on Thy words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:686
verses.text: Let us suppose the morning to mean the season when "a light arose for them that sat in the shadow of death;" did not the eyes of the Church prevent this morning watch, in those Saints who before were on earth, because they foresaw beforehand that this would come to pass, so that they meditated on the words of God, which then were, and announced these things to be destined in the Law and the Prophets?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:687
verses.text: "Hear my voice, O Lord, according to Thy loving-mercy; and quicken Thou me according to Thy judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:688
verses.text: For first God according to His loving-mercy taketh away punishment from sinners, and will give them life afterwards, when righteous, according to His judgment; for it is not without a meaning that it is said unto Him, "My song shall be of mercy and judgment: unto Thee, O Lord;" in this order of the terms: although the season of mercy itself be not without judgment, whereof the Apostle saith, "If we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged of t he Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:689
verses.text: And the final season of judgment shall not be without mercy, since as the Psalm saith, "He crowneth thee with mercy and loving-kindness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:690
verses.text: But "judgment shall be without mercy," but "unto those" on the left, "who have not dealt mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:691
verses.text: "They draw nigh, that of malice persecute me:" or, as some copies read, "maliciously".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:692
verses.text: Then they that persecute draw nigh, when they go the length of torturing and destroying the flesh: whence the twenty-first Psalm, wherein the Lord's Passion is prophesied, saith, "O go not from me, for trouble is hard at hand;" where those things are spoken of which He suffered when His Passion was not imminent upon Him, but actually realized.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:693
verses.text: "And are far from Thy law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:694
verses.text: The nearer they drew to the persecuting the righteous, so much the farther were they from righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:695
verses.text: But what harm did they do unto those, to whom they drew near by persecution; since the approach of their Lord is nearer unto their souls, by whom they no wise are forsaken?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:696
verses.text: Lastly, it followeth, "Thou art nigh at hand, O Lord, and all Thy ways are truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:697
verses.text: Even in their troubles, it hath been a wonted confession of the saints, to ascribe truth unto God, because they suffer them not undeservedly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:698
verses.text: So did Queen Esther, so did holy Daniel, so did the three men in the furnace, so do other associates in their sanctity confess.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:699
verses.text: But it m ay be asked, in what sense it is here said, "All Thy ways are truth;" since in another Psalm it is read, "All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:700
verses.text: But towards the saints, All the ways of the Lord are at once mercy and truth: since He aideth them even in judgment, and thus mercy is not wanting; and in having mercy upon them, He performeth that which He hath promised, so that truth is not wanting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:701
verses.text: But towards all, both those whom He freeth, and those whom He condemneth, all the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth; because where He doth not show mercy, the truth of His vengeance is displayed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:702
verses.text: For He freeth many who have not deserved, but He condemneth none who hath not deserved it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:703
verses.text: "From the beginning I have known," he saith, "as concerning Thy testimonies, that Thou hast grounded them for ever" What are these testimonies, save those wherein God hath declared that He will give an everlasting kingdom unto His sons? And since He hath declared that He will give this in His only-begotten Son, he said that the testimonies themselves were grounded for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:704
verses.text: For that which God hath promised through them, was everlasting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:705
verses.text: And for this reason the words, "Thou hast grounded them," are rightly thus understood, because they are shown to be true in Christ Whence then did the Psalmist know this in the beginning, save because the Church speaketh, which was not wanting to the earth from the commencement of the human race, the first-fruits whereof was the holy Abel, himself sacrificed in testimony of the future blood of the Mediator that should be shed by a wicked brother? For this also was at the beginning, "They two shall be one flesh:" which great mystery the Apostle Paul expounding, saith, "I speak concerning Christ and the Church".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:706
verses.text: Resch.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:707
verses.text: Let no man, set in Christ's body, imagine these words to be alien from himself, since in truth it is the whole body of Christ placed in this humble state that speaketh: "O consider my humiliation, and deliver me: for I forget not Thy law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:708
verses.text: In this place we cannot understand any law of God so suitably, as that whereby it is immutably determined that "every one that exalteth himself, shall be abased; and every one that humbleth himself; shall be exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:709
verses.text: "Avenge Thou," he saith, "my cause, and deliver me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:710
verses.text: The former sentence is here almost repeated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:711
verses.text: And what is there said, "For I do not forget Thy law," agreeth with what we read here, "Quicken me, according to Thy word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:712
verses.text: For these words are the law of God, which he hath not forgot, so that he hath abased himself, and will therefore be exalted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:713
verses.text: But the words, "Quicken me," pertain to this very exaltation; for the exaltation of the saints is everlasting life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:714
verses.text: "Health," he saith, "is far from the ungodly: for they regard not Thy righteousnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:715
verses.text: This separateth thee, that what they have not done, thou hast done, that is, thou hast regarded the righteousnesses of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:716
verses.text: But "what hast thou that thou hast not received?" Art thou not he who a little before didst say, "I will keep Thy righteousnesses"? Thou therefore hast received from Him, unto whom thou didst call, the power to keep them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:717
verses.text: He therefore doth Himself separate thee from those from whom health is far, because they have not regarded the righteousnesses of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:718
verses.text: This he saw himself also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:719
verses.text: For I should not see it, save I saw it in Him, save I were in Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:720
verses.text: For these are the words of the Body of Christ, whose members we are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:721
verses.text: He saw this, I say, and at once added, "Great are Thy mercies, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:722
verses.text: Even our seeking out Thy righteousnesses, then, cometh of Thy mercies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:723
verses.text: "Quicken me according to Thy judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:724
verses.text: For I know that Thy judgments will not be upon me without Thy mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:725
verses.text: "Many there are that trouble me, and persecute me; yet do I not swerve from Thy testimonies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:726
verses.text: This hath been realized: we know it, we recollect it, we acknowledge it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:727
verses.text: The whole earth has been crimsoned by the blood of Martyrs; heaven is flowery with the crowns of Martyrs, the Churches are adorned with the memorials of Martyrs, seasons distinguished by the birthdays of Martyrs, cures more frequent  by the merits of Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:728
verses.text: Whence this, save because that hath been fulfilled which was prophesied of that Man who hath been spread abroad around the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:729
verses.text: We recognize this, and render thanks to the Lord our God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:730
verses.text: For thou, man, thou hast thyself said in another Psalm, "If the Lord Himself had not been on our side, they would have swallowed us up quick".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:731
verses.text: Behold the reason why thou hast not swerved from His testimonies, and hast won the palm of thy heavenly calling amid the hands of the many who persecuted and troubled thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:732
verses.text: "I have seen," he saith, "the foolish, and I pined" : or, as other copies read, "I have seen them that keep not covenant:" this is the reading of most.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:733
verses.text: But who are they who have not kept covenant, save they who have swerved from the testimonies of God, not bearing the tribulation of their many persecutors? Now this is the covenant, that he who shall have conquered shall be crowned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:734
verses.text: They who, not bearing persecution, have by denial swerved from the testimonies of God, have not kept the covenant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:735
verses.text: These then the Psalmist saw, and pined, for he loved them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:736
verses.text: For that jealousy is good, springing from love, not from envy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:737
verses.text: He addeth in what respect they had failed to keep the covenant, "Because they kept not Thy word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:738
verses.text: For this they denied in their tribulations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:739
verses.text: And he commendeth himself as differing from them, and saith, "Behold, how I have loved Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:740
verses.text: He saith not, I have not denied Thy words or testimonies, as the Martyrs were urged to do, and, when they refused, suffered intolerable torments: but he said this wherein is the fruit of all sufferings; for, "if I give up my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:741
verses.text: The Psalmist, praising this virtue, saith, "Behold, how I have loved Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:742
verses.text: Then he asketh his reward, "O Lord, quicken me, according to Thy mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:743
verses.text: These put me to death, do Thou quicken me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:744
verses.text: But if a reward be asked of mercy, which justice is bound to give; how much greater is that mercy, which enabled him to gain the victory, on account of which the reward was sought for?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:745
verses.text: "The beginning," he saith, "of Thy words is truth; all the judgments of Thy righteousness endure for evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:746
verses.text: From truth, he saith, Thy words do proceed, and they are therefore truthful, and deceive no man, for in them life is announced to the righteous, punishment to the ungodly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:747
verses.text: These are the everlasting judgments of God's righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:748
verses.text: Schin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:749
verses.text: We know what persecutions the body of Christ, that is, the holy Church, suffered from the kings of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:750
verses.text: Let us therefore here also recognise the words of the Church: "Princes have persecuted me without a cause: and my heart hath stood in awe of Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:751
verses.text: For how had the Christians injured the kingdoms of the earth, although their King promised them the kingdom of heaven? How, I ask, had they injured the kingdoms of earth? Did their King forbid His soldiers to pay and to render due service to the kings of the earth? Saith He not to the Jews who were striving to calumniate Him, "Render unto Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and unto God the things that are God's"? Did He not even in His own Person pay tribute from the mouth of a fish? Did not His forerunner, when the soldiers of this kingdom were seeking what they ought to do for their everlasting salvation, instead of replying, Loose your belts, throw away your arms, desert your king, that ye may wage war for the Lord, answer, "Do violence to no man: neither accuse any falsely: and be content with your wages"? Did not one of His soldiers, His most beloved companion, say to his fellow soldiers, the provincials, so to speak, of Christ, "Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers"? Does he not enjoin the Church to pray for even kings themselves? How then have the Christians offended against them? What due have they not rendered? in what have not Christians obeyed the monarchs of earth? The kings of the earth therefore have persecuted the Christians without a cause.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:752
verses.text: They too had their threatening words: I banish, I proscribe, I slay, I torture with claws, I burn with fires, I expose to beasts, I tear the limbs piecemeal But heed what he hath subjoined: "And my heart hath stood in awe of Thy word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:753
verses.text: My heart hath stood in awe of these words, "Fear not them that kill the body," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:754
verses.text: I have scorned man who persecuteth me, and have overcome the devil that would seduce me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:755
verses.text: Then follows, "I am as glad of Thy word as one that findeth great spoils".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:756
verses.text: By the same words he conquered, of which he stood in awe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:757
verses.text: For spoils are stripped from the conquered; as he was overcome and despoiled of whom it is said in the Gospel, "except he first bind the strong man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:758
verses.text: But many spoils were found, when, admiring the endurance of the Martyrs, even the persecutors believed; and they who had plotted to injure our King by the injury of His soldiers, were gained over by Him in addition.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:759
verses.text: Whoever therefore standeth in awe of the words of God, fearing lest he be overcome in the contest, rejoiceth as conqueror in the same words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:760
verses.text: "As for iniquity, I hate and abhor it; but Thy law have I loved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:761
verses.text: That awe, therefore, of His word did not create hatred of those words, but maintained his love unimpaired.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:762
verses.text: For the words of God are no other than the law of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:763
verses.text: Far be it therefore that love perish through fear, where fear is chaste.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:764
verses.text: Thus fathers are at once feared and loved by affectionate sons; thus doth the chaste wife at once fear her husband, lest she be forsaken by him, and loveth him, that she may enjoy his love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:765
verses.text: If then the human father and the human husband desire at once to be feared and loved; much more doth our Father who is in heaven, and that Bridegroom, "beautiful beyond the sons of men," not in the flesh, but in goodness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:766
verses.text: For by whom is the law of God loved, save by those by whom God is loved? And what that is severe hath the father's law to good sons? Let the Father's judgments therefore be praised even in the scourge, if His promises be loved in the reward.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:767
verses.text: Such was, assuredly, the conduct of the Psalmist, who saith, "Seven times a day do I praise Thee, because of Thy righteous judgments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:768
verses.text: The words "seven times a day," signify "evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:769
verses.text: For this number is wont to be a symbol of universality; because after six days of the divine work of creation, a seventh of rest was added; and all times roll on through a revolving cycle of seven days.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:770
verses.text: For no other reason it was said, "a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again:" that is, the just man perisheth not, though brought low in every way, yet not induced to transgress, otherwise he will not be just.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:771
verses.text: For the words, "falleth seven times," are employed to express every kind of tribulation, whereby man is cast down in the sight of men: and the words, "riseth up again," signify that he profiteth from all these tribulations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:772
verses.text: The following sentence in this passage sufficiently illustrates the foregoing words: for it follows, "but the wicked shall fall into mischief".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:773
verses.text: Not to be deprived of strength in any evils, is therefore the falling seven times, and the rising again of the just man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:774
verses.text: Justly hath the Church then praised God seven times in a day for His righteous judgments; because, when it was time that judgment should begin at the house of God, she did not faint in all her tribulations, but was glorified with the crowns of Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:775
verses.text: "Great is the peace," he saith, "that they have who love Thy law: and there is no offence to them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:776
verses.text: Doth this mean that the law itself is not an offence to them that love it, or that there is no offence from any source unto them that love the law? But both senses are rightly understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:777
verses.text: For he who loveth the law of God, honoureth in it even what he doth not understand; and what seemeth to him to sound absurd, he judgeth rather that he doth not understand, and that there is some great meaning hidden: thus the law of God is not an offence to him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:778
verses.text: "I have waited," he saith, "for Thy saving health, O Lord, and have loved Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:779
verses.text: For what would it have profited the righteous of old to have loved the commandments of God, save Christ, who is the saving health of God, had freed them; by the gift of whose Spirit also they were able to love the commandments of God? If therefore they who loved God's commandments, waited for His saving health; how much more necessary was Jesus, that is, the saving Health of God, for the salvation of those that did not love His commandments? This prophecy may suit also the Saints of the period since the revelation of grace, and the preaching of the Gospel, for they that love God's commandments look for Christ, that "when Christ, our life, shall appear, we" may then "appear with Him in glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:780
verses.text: "My soul hath kept Thy testimonies, and I have loved them exceedingly:" or, as some copies read, "hath loved them," understanding, "my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:781
verses.text: The testimonies of God are kept, while they are not denied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:782
verses.text: This is the office of Martyrs, for testimonies are called Martyria in Greek.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:783
verses.text: But since it profiteth nothing, even to be burnt with flames without charity, he addeth, "and I have loved them exceedingly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:784
verses.text: For he who loveth, keepeth them in the Spirit of truth and faithfulness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:785
verses.text: But generally, while the commandments of God are kept, they against whose will they are kept become our foes: then, indeed, His testimonies also must be kept courageously, lest they be denied when the enemy persecuteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:786
verses.text: After the Psalmist, then, had declared that he had done both these things, he ascribeth unto God his having been enabled to do so, by adding, "because all my ways are in Thy sight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:787
verses.text: He saith therefore, "I have kept Thy commandments and Thy testimonies; because all my ways are in Thy sight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:788
verses.text: As much as to say, Hadst Thou turned away Thy face from me, I should have been confounded, nor could I keep Thy commandments and testimonies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:789
verses.text: "I have kept them," then, because "all my ways are in Thy sight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:790
verses.text: With a look favouring and aiding man, he meant it to be understood that God seeth his ways: according to the prayer, "O hide not Thou Thy face from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:791
verses.text: Tau.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:792
verses.text: Let us now hear the words of one praying: since we know who is praying, and we recognise ourselves, if we be not reprobate, among the members of this one praying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:793
verses.text: "Let my prayer come near in Thy sight, O Lord" : for, "The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:794
verses.text: "Give me understanding, according to Thy word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:795
verses.text: He claimeth a promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:796
verses.text: For he saith, "according to Thy word," which is to say, according to Thy promise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:797
verses.text: For the Lord promised this when He said, "I will inform thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:798
verses.text: "Let my request come before Thy presence, O Lord: deliver me, according to Thy word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:799
verses.text: He repeateth what he hath asked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:800
verses.text: For his former words, "Let my prayer come near in Thy presence, O Lord:" are like unto what he saith, "Let my request come before Thy presence, O Lord:" and the words, "Give me understanding according to Thy word," agree with these, "Deliver me according to Thy word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:801
verses.text: For by receiving understanding he is delivered, who of himself through want of understanding is deceived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:802
verses.text: "My lips shall burst forth praise: when Thou hast taught me Thy righteousnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:803
verses.text: We know how God teacheth those who are docile unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:804
verses.text: For every one who hath heard from the Father and hath learned, comes unto Him "who justifieth the ungodly:" so that he may keep the righteousnesses of God not only by retaining them in his memory, but also by doing them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:805
verses.text: Thus doth he who glorieth, glory not in himself, but in the Lord, and burst forth praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:806
verses.text: But as he hath now learned, and praised God his Teacher, he next wisheth to teach.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:807
verses.text: "Yea, my tongue shall declare Thy word: for all Thy commandments are righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:808
verses.text: When he saith that he will declare these things, he becometh a minister of the word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:809
verses.text: For though God teach within, nevertheless "faith cometh from hearing: and how do they hear without a preacher?" For, because "God giveth the increase," is no reason why we need not plant and water.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:810
verses.text: "Let Thy hand be stretched forth (fiat, be made) to save me, for I have chosen Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:811
verses.text: That I might not fear, and that not only might my heart hold fast, but my tongue also utter Thy words: "I have chosen Thy commandments," and have stifled fear with love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:812
verses.text: Let Thy hand therefore be stretched forth, to save me from another's hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:813
verses.text: Thus God saved the Martyrs, when He permitted them not to be slain in their souls: for "vain is the safety of man" in the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:814
verses.text: The words, "Let Thy hand be made," may also be taken to mean Christ the Hand of GodCertainly where we read the following words, "I have longed for Thy salvation, O Lord" : even if all our foes be reluctant, let Christ the Salvation of God occur to us: the righteous men of old confess that they longed for Him, the Church longed for His destined coming from His mother's womb, the Church longeth for His coming at His Father's right hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:815
verses.text: Subjoined to this sentence are the words, "And Thy law is my meditation:" for the Law giveth testimony unto Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:816
verses.text: But in this faith, though the heathen rage furiously, and the people imagine a vain thing: though the flesh be slain while it preacheth Thee: "My soul shall live, and shall praise Thee: and Thy judgments shall help me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:817
verses.text: These are those judgments, which it was time should begin at the house of the Lord But "they will help me," he saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:818
verses.text: And who cannot see how much the blood of the Church hath aided the Church? how great a harvest hath risen in the whole world from that sowing?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:819
verses.text: At last he openeth himself completely, and showeth what person was speaking throughout the whole Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:820
verses.text: "I have gone astray," he saith, "like a sheep that is lost: O seek Thy servant, for I do not forget Thy commandments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:821
verses.text: Let the lost sheep be sought, let the lost sheep be quickened, for whose sake its Shepherd left the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and while seeking it, was torn by Jewish thorns.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:822
verses.text: But it is still being sought, let it still be sought, partly found let it still be sought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 119:823
verses.text: For as to that company, among whom the Psalmist saith, "I do not forget Thy commandments," it hath been found; but through those who choose the commandments of God, gather them together, love them, it is still sought, and by means of the blood of its Shepherd shed and sprinkled abroad, it is found in all nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:1
verses.text: Psalm CXX.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:2
verses.text: The Psalm which we have just heard chanted, and have responded to with our voices, is short, and very profitable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:3
verses.text: Ye will not long toil in hearing, nor will ye toil fruitlessly in working.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:4
verses.text: For it is, according to the title prefixed to it, "A song of degrees".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:5
verses.text: Degrees are either of ascent or of descent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:6
verses.text: But degrees, as they are used in this Psalm, are of ascendingThere are therefore both those who ascend and those who descend on that ladder Who are they that ascend? They who progress towards the understanding of things spiritual.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:7
verses.text: Who are they that descend? They who, although, as far as men may, they enjoy the comprehension of things spiritual: nevertheless, descend unto the infants, to say to them such things as they can receive, so that, after being nourished with milk, they may become fitted and strong enough to take spiritual meat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:8
verses.text: When therefore a man hath commenced thus to order his ascent; to speak more plainly, when a Christian hath begun to think of spiritual amendment, he beginneth to suffer the tongues of adversaries.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:9
verses.text: Whoever hath not yet suffered from them, hath not yet made progress; whoever suffereth them not, doth not even endeavour to improve.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:10
verses.text: Doth he wish to know what we mean? Let him at the same time experience what is reported of us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:11
verses.text: Let him begin to improve, let him begin to wish to ascend, to wish to despise earthly, fragile, temporal objects, to hold worldly happiness for nothing, to think of God alone, not to rejoice in gain, not to pine at losses, to wish even to sell all his substance, and distribute it among the poor, and to follow Christ; let us see how he suffereth the tongues of detractors and of constant opponents, and—a still greater peril—of pretended counsellors, who lead him astray from salvationHe then, who will ascend, first of all prayeth God against these very tongues: for he saith, "When I was in trouble, I called on the Lord; and He heard me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:12
verses.text: Why did He hear him? That He might now place him at the steps of ascent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:13
verses.text: "Deliver my soul, O Lord, from unrighteous lips, and from a deceitful tongue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:14
verses.text: What is a deceitful tongue? A treacherous tongue, one that hath the semblance of counsel, and the bane of real mischief.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:15
verses.text: Such are those who say, And wilt thou do this, that nobody doth? Wilt thou be the only Christian?Some deter by dissuasion, others discourage yet more by their praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:16
verses.text: For since such is the life that hath for some time been diffused over the world, so great is the authority of Christ, that not even a pagan ventureth to blame Christ He who cannot be censured is read.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:17
verses.text: They cannot contradict Christ, they cannot contradict the Gospel, Christ cannot be censured; the deceitful tongue turneth itself to praise as an hindrance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:18
verses.text: If thou praisest, exhort.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:19
verses.text: Why dost thou discourage with thy praise?Thou turnest thyself to another mode of dissuasion, that by false praise thou mayest turn me away from true praise; nay, that by praising Christ thou mayest keep me away from Christ, saying, What is this? Behold these men have done this: thou, perhaps, wilt not be able: thou beginnest to ascend, thou fallest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:20
verses.text: It seemeth to warn thee: it is the serpent, it is the deceitful tongue, it hath poison.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:21
verses.text: Pray against it, if thou wishest to ascend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:22
verses.text: And thy Lord saith unto thee, "What shall be given thee, or what shall be set before thee, against the deceitful tongue?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:23
verses.text: What shall be given thee, that is, as a weapon to oppose to the deceitful tongue, to guard thyself against the deceitful tongue? "Or what shall be set before thee?" He asketh to try thee: for He will answer His own question.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:24
verses.text: For He answers following up his own inquiry, "even sharp arrows of the Mighty One, with coals that desolate, or that lay waste".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:25
verses.text: They that desolate, or that lay waste (for it is variously written in different copies), are the same, because by laying waste, as ye may observe, they easily lead unto desolation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:26
verses.text: What are these coals? First, beloved brethren, understand what are arrows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:27
verses.text: The "sharp arrows of the Mighty One," are the words of GodWhat then are the "coals that lay waste?" It is not enough to plead with words against a deceitful tongue and unrighteous lips: it is not enough to plead with words; we must plead with examples alsoThe word coals, then, is used to express the examples of many sinners converted to the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:28
verses.text: Thou hearest men wonder, and say, I knew that man, how addicted he was to drinking, what a villain, what a lover of the circus, or of the amphitheatre, what a cheat: now how he serveth God, how innocent he hath become! Wonder not; he is a live coal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:29
verses.text: Thou rejoicest that he is alive, whom thou wast mourning as dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:30
verses.text: But when thou praisest the living, if thou knowest how to praise, apply him to the dead, that he may be inflamed; whosoever is still slow to follow God, apply to him the coal which was extinguished, and have the arrow of God's word, and the coal that layeth waste, that thou mayest meet the deceitful tongue and the lying lips.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:31
verses.text: "Alas, that my sojourning is become far off!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:32
verses.text: It hath departed far from Thee: my pilgrimage hath become a far one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:33
verses.text: I have not yet reached that country, where I shall live with no wicked person; I have not yet reached that company of Angels, where I shall not fear offences.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:34
verses.text: But why am I not as yet there? Because sojourning is pilgrimage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:35
verses.text: He is called a sojourner who dwells in a foreign land, not in his own country.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:36
verses.text: And when is it far off? Sometimes, my brethren, when a man goeth abroad, he liveth among better persons, than he would perhaps live with in his own country: but it is not thus, when we go afar from that heavenly Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:37
verses.text: For a man changeth his country, and this foreign sojourn is sometimes good for him; in travelling he findeth faithful friends, whom he could not find in his own country.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:38
verses.text: He had enemies, so that he was driven from his country; and when he travelled, he found what he had not in his country.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:39
verses.text: Such is not that country Jerusalem, where all are good: whoever travelleth away from thence, is among the evil; nor can he depart from the wicked, save when he shall return to the company of Angels, so as to be where he was before he travelled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:40
verses.text: There all are righteous and holy, who enjoy the word of God without reading, without letters: for what is written to us through pages, they perceive there through the Face of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:41
verses.text: What a country! A great country indeed, and wretched are the wanderers from that country.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:42
verses.text: But what he saith, "My pilgrimage hath been made distant," are the words of those, that is, of the Church herself, who toileth on this earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:43
verses.text: It is her voice, which crieth out from the ends of the earth in another Psalm, saying, "From the ends of the earth have I cried unto TheeWhere then doth he groan, and among whom doth he dwell? "I have had my habitation among the tents of Kedar".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:44
verses.text: Since this is a Hebrew word, beyond doubt ye have not understood it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:45
verses.text: What meaneth, "I have had my habitation among the tents of Kedar"? "Kedar," as far as we remember of the interpretation of Hebrew words, signifieth darkness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:46
verses.text: "Kedar" rendered into Latin is called tenebrae.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:47
verses.text: Now ye know that Abraham had two sons, whom indeed the Apostle mentioneth,  and declareth them to have been types of the two covenantsIshmael therefore was in darkness, Isaac in light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:48
verses.text: Whoever here also seek earthly felicity in the Church, from God, shall belong to Ishmael.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:49
verses.text: These are the very persons who gainsay the spiritual ones who are progressing, and detract from them, and have deceitful tongues and unrighteous lips.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:50
verses.text: Against these the Psalmist, when ascending, prayed, and hot coals that lay waste, and swift and sharp arrows of the Mighty One, were given him for his defence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:51
verses.text: For among these he still liveth, until the whole floor be winnowed: he therefore said, "I have dwelt among the tents of Kedar".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:52
verses.text: The tents of Ishmael are called those of Kedar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:53
verses.text: Thus the book of Genesis hath it: thus it hath, that Kedar belongeth unto Ishmael Isaac therefore is with Ishmael: that is, they who belong unto Isaac, live among those who belong unto Ishmael These wish to rise above, those wish to press them downwards: these wish to fly unto God, those endeavour to pluck their wings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:54
verses.text: "My soul hath wandered much".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:55
verses.text: Lest thou shouldest understand bodily wandering, he hath said that the soul wandered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:56
verses.text: The body wandereth in places, the soul wandereth in its affections.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:57
verses.text: If thou love the earth, thou wanderest from God: if thou lovest God, thou risest unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:58
verses.text: Let us be exercised in the love of God, and of our neighbour, that we may return unto charity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:59
verses.text: If we fall towards the earth, we wither and decay.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:60
verses.text: But one descended unto this one who had fallen, in order that he might arise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:61
verses.text: Speaking of the time of his wandering, he said that he wandered in the tents of Kedar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:62
verses.text: Wherefore? Because "my soul hath wandered much".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:63
verses.text: He wandereth there where he ascendeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:64
verses.text: He wandereth not in the body, he riseth not in the body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:65
verses.text: But wherein doth he ascend? "The ascent," he saith, "is in the heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:66
verses.text: "With them that hated peace, I was peaceful".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:67
verses.text: But howsoever ye may hear, most beloved brethren, ye will not be able to prove how truly ye sing, unless ye have begun to do that which ye sing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:68
verses.text: How much soever I say this, in whatsoever ways I may expound it, in whatsoever words I may turn it, it entereth not into the heart of him in whom its operation  is not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:69
verses.text: Begin to act, and see what we speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:70
verses.text: Then tears flow forth at each word, then the Psalm is sung, and the heart doeth what is sung in the PsalmWho are they who hate peace? They who tear asunder unity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:71
verses.text: For had they not hated peace, they would have abode in unity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:72
verses.text: But they separated themselves, forsooth on this account, that they might be righteous, that they might not have the ungodly mixed with them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:73
verses.text: These words are either ours or theirs: decide whose.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:74
verses.text: The Catholic Church saith, Unity must not be lost, the Church of God must not be cut off God will judge afterwards of the wicked and the goodThis we also say: Love ye peace, love ye Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:75
