verses.text: For if they love peace, they love Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:76
verses.text: When therefore we say, Love ye peace, we say this, Love ye Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:77
verses.text: Wherefore? For the Apostle saith of Christ, "He is our peace, who hath made both one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 120:78
verses.text: If Christ is therefore peace, because He hath made both one: why have ye made two of one? How then are ye peace-makers, if, when Christ maketh one of two, ye make two of one? But since we say these things, we are peace-makers with them that hate peace; and yet they who hate peace, when we spake to them, made war on us for nought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:2
verses.text: Let them "lift up their eyes to the hills whence cometh their help".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:3
verses.text: What meaneth, The hills have been lightened? The San of righteousness hath already risen, the Gospel hath been already preached by the Apostles, the Scriptures have been preached, all the mysteries have been laid open, the veil hath been rent, the secret place of the temple hath been revealed: let them now at length lift their eyes up to the hills, whence their help cometh"Of His fulness have all we received," he saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:4
verses.text: Thy help therefore is from Him, of whose fulness the hills received, not from the hills; towards which, nevertheless, save thou lift thine eyes through the Scriptures, thou wilt not approach, so as to be lighted by Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:5
verses.text: Sing therefore what followeth; if thou wish to hear how thou mayest most securely set thy feet on the steps, so that thou mayest not be fatigued in that ascent, nor stumble and fall: pray in these words: "Suffer not my foot to be moved!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:6
verses.text: Whereby are feet moved; whereby was the foot of him who was in Paradise moved? But first consider whereby the feet of him who was among the Angels were moved: who when his feet were moved fell, and from an Angel became a devil: for when his feet were moved he fell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:7
verses.text: Seek whereby he fell: he fell through pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:8
verses.text: Nothing then moveth the feet, save pride: nothing moveth the feet to a fall, save pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:9
verses.text: Charity moveth them to walk and to improve and to ascend; pride moveth them to fallRightly therefore the Psalmist, hearing how he may ascend and may not fall, prayeth unto God that he may profit from the vale of misery, and may not fail in the swelling of pride, in these words, "Suffer not my feet to be moved!" And He replieth unto him, "Let him that keepeth thee not sleep".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:10
verses.text: Attend, my beloved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:11
verses.text: It is as if one thought were expressed in two sentences; the man while ascending and singing "the song of degrees," saith, "Suffer not my foot to be moved:" and it is as if God answered, Thou sayest unto Me, Let not my feet be moved: say also, "Let Him that keepeth thee not sleep," and thy foot shall not be moved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:12
verses.text: Choose for thyself Him, who will neither sleep nor slumber, and thy foot shall not be moved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:13
verses.text: God is never asleep: if thou dost wish to have a keeper who never sleepeth, choose God for thy keeper.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:14
verses.text: "Suffer not my feet to be moved," thou sayest: well, very well: but He also saith unto thee, "Let not him that keepeth thee slumber".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:15
verses.text: Thou perhaps wast about to turn thyself unto men as thy keepers, and to say, whom shall I find who will not sleep? what man will not slumber? whom do I find? whither shall I go? whither shall I return? The Psalmist telleth thee: "He that keepeth Israel, shall neither slumber nor sleep".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:16
verses.text: Dost thou wish to have a keeper who neither slumbereth nor sleepeth? Behold, "He that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep:" for Christ keepeth Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:17
verses.text: Be thou then Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:18
verses.text: What meaneth Israel? It is interpreted, Seeing God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:19
verses.text: And how is God seen? First by faith: afterwards by sight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:20
verses.text: If thou canst not as yet see Him by sight, see Him by faithWho is there, who will neither slumber nor sleep? when thou seekest among men, thou art deceived; thou wilt never find one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:21
verses.text: Trust not then in any man: every man slumbereth, and will sleep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:22
verses.text: When doth he slumber? When he beareth the flesh of weakness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:23
verses.text: When will he sleep? When he is dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:24
verses.text: Trust not then in man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:25
verses.text: A mortal may slumber, he sleepeth in death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:26
verses.text: Seek not a keeper among men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:27
verses.text: And who, thou askest, shall help me, save He who slumbereth not, nor sleepeth? Hear what followeth: "The Lord Himself is thy keeper".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:28
verses.text: It is not therefore man, that slumbereth and sleepeth, but the Lord, that keepeth thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:29
verses.text: How doth He keep thee? "The Lord is thy defence upon the hand of thy right hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:30
verses.text: It seemeth to me to have a hidden sense: otherwise he would have simply said, without qualification, "The Lord will keep thee," without adding, "on thy right hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:31
verses.text: For how? Doth God keep our right hand, and not our left? Did He not create the whole of us? Did not He who made our right hand, make our left hand also? Finally, if it pleased Him to speak of the right hand alone, why said He, "on the hand of thy right hand," and not at once "upon thy right hand"? Why should He say this, unless He were keeping somewhat here hidden for us to arrive at by knocking? For He would either say, "The Lord shall keep thee," and add no more; or if He would add the right hand, "The Lord shall keep thee upon thy right hand;" or at least, as He added "hand," He would say, "The Lord shall keep thee upon thy hand, even thy right hand," not "upon the hand of thy right hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:32
verses.text: I ask you, how ye interpret what is said in the Gospel, "Let not your left hand know what your right hand doeth"? For if ye understand this, ye will discover what is your right hand, and what is your left: at the same time ye will also understand that God made both hands, the left and the right; yet the left ought not to know what the right doeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:33
verses.text: By our left hand is meant all that we have in a temporal way; by our right hand is meant, whatever our Lord promiseth us that is immutable and eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:34
verses.text: But if He who will give everlasting life, Himself also consoleth our present life by these temporal blessings, He hath Himself made our right hand and our left.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:35
verses.text: Let us now come to this verse of the Psalm: "The Lord is thy defence upon the hand of thy right hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:36
verses.text: By hand he meaneth power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:37
verses.text: How do we prove this? Because the power of God also is styled the hand of GodWhereof John saith, "He gave unto them power to become the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:38
verses.text: Whence hast thou received this power? "To them," he saith, "that believe in His Name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:39
verses.text: If then thou believest, this very power is given thee, to be among the sons of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:40
verses.text: But to be among the sons of God, is to belong to the right hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:41
verses.text: Thy faith therefore is the hand of thy right hand: that is, the power that is given thee, to be among the sons of God, is the hand of thy right hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:42
verses.text: "May the Lord shield thee upon the hand of thy right hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:43
verses.text: I have said, and I believe ye have recognised it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:44
verses.text: For had ye not recognised it, and that from the Scriptures, ye would not signify your understanding of it by your voices Since then ye have understood, brethren, consider what followeth; wherefore the Lord shieldeth thee "upon the hand of thy right hand," that is, in thy faith, wherein we have received "power to become the sons of God," and to be on His right hand: wherefore should God shield us? On account of offences.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:45
verses.text: Whence come offences? Offences are to be feared from two quarters, for there are two precepts upon which the whole Law hangeth and the Prophets, the love of God and of our neighbour The Church is loved for the sake of our neighbour, but God for the sake of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:46
verses.text: Of God, is understood the sun figuratively: of the Church, is understood the moon figuratively.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:47
verses.text: Whoever can err, so as to think otherwise of God than he ought, believing not the Father and the Son and the Holy Ghost to be of one Substance, has been deceived by the cunning of heretics, chiefly of the Arians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:48
verses.text: If he hath believed anything less in the Son or in the Holy Spirit than in the Father, he hath suffered an offence in God; he is scorched by the sun.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:49
verses.text: Whoever again believeth that the Church existeth in one province only, and not that she is diffused over the whole world, and whoso believeth them that say, "Lo here," and "Lo there, is Christ," as ye but now heard when the Gospel was being read; since He who gave so great a price, purchased the whole world: he is offended, so to speak, in his neighbour, and is burnt by the moon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:50
verses.text: Whoever therefore erreth in the very Substance of Truth, is burnt by the sun, and is burnt through the day; because he erreth in Wisdom itselfGod therefore hath made one sun, which riseth upon the good and the evil, that sun which the good and the evil see; but that Sun is another one, not created, not born, through whom all things were made; where is the intelligence of the Immutable Truth: of this the ungodly say, "the Sun rose not upon us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:51
verses.text: Whosoever erreth not in Wisdom itself, is not burnt by the sun.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:52
verses.text: Whosoever erreth not in the Church, and in the Lord's Flesh, and in those things which were done for us in time, is not burnt by the moon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:53
verses.text: But every man although he believeth in Christ, erreth either in this or that respect, unless what is here prayed for, "The Lord is thy defence upon the hand of thy right hand," is realized in him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:54
verses.text: He goeth on to say, "So that the sun shall not burn thee by day, nor the moon by night".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:55
verses.text: Thy defence, therefore, is upon the hand of thy right hand for this reason, that the sun may not burn thee by day, nor the moon by night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:56
verses.text: Understand hence, brethren, that it is spoken figuratively.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:57
verses.text: For, in truth, if we think of the visible sun, it burneth by day: doth the moon burn by night? But what is burning? Offence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:58
verses.text: Hear the Apostle's words: "Who is weak, and I am not weak? who is offended, and I burn not?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:59
verses.text: "For the Lord shall preserve thee from all evil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:60
verses.text: From offences in the sun, from offences in the moon, from all evil shall He preserve thee, who is thy defence upon the hand of thy right hand, who will not sleep nor slumber.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:61
verses.text: And for what reason? Because we are amid temptations: "The Lord shall preserve thee from all evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:62
verses.text: The Lord preserve thy soul:" even thy very soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:63
verses.text: "The Lord preserve thy going out and thy coming in, from this time forth for evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:64
verses.text: Not thy body; for the Martyrs were consumed in the body: but "the Lord preserve thy soul;" for the Martyrs yielded not up their souls.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:65
verses.text: The persecutors raged against Crispina, whose birthday we are to-day celebrating; they were raging against a rich and delicate woman: but she was strong, for the Lord was her defence upon the hand of her right hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:66
verses.text: He was her Keeper.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:67
verses.text: Is there any one in Africa, my brethren, who knoweth her not? For she was most illustrious, noble in birth, abounding in wealth: but all these things were in her left hand, beneath her head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:68
verses.text: An enemy advanced to strike her head, and the left hand was presented to him, which was under her head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 121:69
verses.text: Her head was above, the right hand embraced her from above.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:2
verses.text: As impure love inflames the mind, and summons the soul destined to perish to lust for earthly things, and to follow what is perishable, and precipitates it into lowest places, and sinks it into the abyss; so holy love raiseth us to heavenly things, and inflames us to what is eternal, and excites the soul to those things which do not pass away nor die, and from the abyss of hell raiseth it to heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:3
verses.text: Yet all love hath a power of its own, nor can love in the soul of the lover be idle; it must needs draw it on.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:4
verses.text: But dost thou wish to know of what sort love is? See whither it leadeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:5
verses.text: This Psalm is a "Song of degrees;" as we have often said to you, for these degrees are not of descent, but of ascent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:6
verses.text: He therefore longeth to ascend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:7
verses.text: And whither doth he wish to ascend, save into heaven? What meaneth, into heaven? Doth he wish to ascend that he may be with the sun, moon, and stars? Far be it! But there is in heaven the eternal Jerusalem, where are our fellow-citizens, the Angels: we are wanderers on earth from these our fellow-citizens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:8
verses.text: We sigh in our pilgrimage; we shall rejoice in the city.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:9
verses.text: But we find companions in this pilgrimage, who have already seen this city herself; who summon us to run towards her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:10
verses.text: At these he also rejoiceth, who saith, "I rejoiced in them who said unto me, We will go into the house of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:11
verses.text: "Our feet were standing in the courts of Jerusalem" Consider what thou wilt be there; and although thou art as yet on the road, place this before thine eyes, as if thou wert already standing, as if thou wert already rejoicing without ceasing among the Angels; as if that which is written were realized in thee: "Blessed are they that dwell in Thy house; they will be alway praising Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:12
verses.text: "Our feet stood in the courts of Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:13
verses.text: What Jerusalem? This earthly Jerusalem also is wont to be called by the name: though this Jerusalem is but the shadow of that.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:14
verses.text: And what great thing is it to stand in this Jerusalem, since this Jerusalem hath not been able to stand, but hath been turned into a ruin? Doth then the Holy Spirit pronounce this, out of the kindled heart of the loving Psalmist, as a great thing? Is not it that Jerusalem, unto whom the Lord said, "O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the Prophets," etc What great thing then did he desire; to stand among those who slew the Prophets, and stoned them that were sent unto them? God forbid that he should think of that Jerusalem, who so loveth, who so burneth, who so longeth to reach that Jerusalem, "our Mother," of which the Apostle saith, that She is "eternal in the Heavens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:15
verses.text: "Jerusalem that is being built as a city".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:16
verses.text: Brethren, when David was uttering these words, that city had been finished, it was not being built.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:17
verses.text: It is some city he speaketh of, therefore, which is now being built, unto which living stones run in faith, of whom Peter saith, "Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house;" that is, the holy temple of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:18
verses.text: What meaneth, ye are built up as lively stones? Thou livest, if thou believest: but if thou believest, thou art made a temple of God; for the Apostle Paul saith, "The temple of God is holy, which temple are ye".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:19
verses.text: This city is therefore now in building; stones are cut down from the hills by the hands of those who preach truth, they are squared that they may enter into an everlasting structure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:20
verses.text: There are still many stones in the hands of the Builder: let them not fall from His hands, that they may be built perfect into the structure of the temple.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:21
verses.text: This, then, is the "Jerusalem that is being built as a city:" Christ is its foundation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:22
verses.text: The Apostle Paul saith, "Other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Christ Jesus".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:23
verses.text: When a foundation is laid on earth, the walls are built above, and the weight of the walls tends towards the lowest parts, because the foundation is laid at the bottom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:24
verses.text: But if our foundation be in heaven, let us be built towards heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:25
verses.text: Bodies have built the edifice of this basilica, the ample size of which ye see; and since bodies have built it, they placed the foundation lowest: but since we are spiritually built, our foundation is placed at the highest point.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:26
verses.text: Let us therefore run thither, where we may be builtBut what Jerusalem do I speak of? Is it that, he asketh, which ye see standing, raised on the structure of its walls? No; but the "Jerusalem which is being built as a city".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:27
verses.text: Why not, a city, instead of, "as a city;" save because those walls, so built in Jerusalem, were a visible city, as it is by all called a city, literally; but this is being built "as a city," for they who enter it are like living stones; for they are not literally stones? Just as they are called stones, and yet are not so: so the city styled "as a city," is not a city; for he said, "is being built".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:28
verses.text: For by the word building, he meant to be understood the structure, and cohesion of bodies and walls.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:29
verses.text: For a city  is properly understood of the men that inhabit there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:30
verses.text: But in saying "is building," he showed us that he meant a town.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:31
verses.text: And since a spiritual building hath some resemblance to a bodily building, therefore it "is building as a city".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:32
verses.text: But let the following words remove all doubt that we ought not to understand carnally the words, "Whose partaking is in the same".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:33
verses.text: What meaneth, "the same"? What is ever in the same state; not what is now in one state, now in another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:34
verses.text: What then is, "the same," save that which is? What is that which is? That which is everlastingBehold "The Same: I Am that I Am, I AM".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:35
verses.text: Thou canst not understand; it is much to understand, it is much to apprehend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:36
verses.text: Remember what He, whom thou canst not comprehend, became for thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:37
verses.text: Remember the flesh of Christ, towards which thou wast raised when sick, and when left half dead from the wounds of robbers, that thou mightest be brought to the Inn, and there mightest be cured Let us therefore run unto the Lord's house, and reach the city where our feet may stand; the city "that is building as a city: whose partaking is in The Same".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:38
verses.text: That city "which partaketh in the same," partaketh in its stability: justly therefore, since he is made a sharer in its stability, saith he who runneth thither.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:39
verses.text: For all things there stand where nought passeth by.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:40
verses.text: Dost thou too wish to stand there and not to pass by? Run thither.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:41
verses.text: Nobody hath "the same" from himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:42
verses.text: "For thither the tribes went up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:43
verses.text: We were asking whither he ascendeth who hath fallen; for we said, it is the voice of a man who is ascending, of the Church rising.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:44
verses.text: Can we tell whither it ascendeth? whither it goeth? whither it is raised? "Thither," he saith, "the tribes went up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:45
verses.text: Whither? To "partaking in the Same".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:46
verses.text: But what are the tribes? Many know, many know not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:47
verses.text: For if we use the word "curies" in its proper sense, we understand nothing, save the "curies" which exist in each particular city, whence the terms "curiales" and "decuriones," that is, the citizens of a curia or a decuria; and ye know that each city hath such curies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:48
verses.text: But there are, or were at one time, curies of the people in those cities, and one city hath many curies, as Rome hath thirty-five curies of the people These are called tribes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:49
verses.text: The people of Israel had twelve of these, according to the sons of Jacob.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:50
verses.text: There were twelve tribes of the people of Israel: but there were good, and there were bad among them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:51
verses.text: For how evil were those tribes which crucified our Lord! How good those who recognised the Lord! Those tribes then who crucified the Lord, were tribes of the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:52
verses.text: When therefore he here said, "For thither the tribes go up;" that thou mightest not understand all the tribes, he added, "even the tribes of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:53
verses.text: What are the tribes of the Lord? "A testimony unto Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:54
verses.text: Hear, brethren, what this meaneth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:55
verses.text: "A testimony to Israel:" that is, whereby it may be known that it is truly IsraelHe is such in whom there is no guile.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:56
verses.text: And what did the Lord say, when He saw Nathanael? "Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:57
verses.text: If therefore he is a true Israelite, in whom there is no guile, those tribes go up to Jerusalem, in whom there is no guile.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:58
verses.text: Wherefore do they go up? "To confess unto Thy Name, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:59
verses.text: It could not be more nobly expressed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:60
verses.text: As pride presumeth, so doth humility confess.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:61
verses.text: As he is a presumer, who wishes to appear what he is not, so is he a confessor, who does not wish that to be seen which himself is, and loves That which He is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:62
verses.text: To this therefore do Israelites go up, in whom is no guile, because they are truly Israelites, because in them is the testimony of Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:63
verses.text: "For there were seated seats for judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:64
verses.text: This is a wonderful riddle, a wonderful question, if it be not understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:65
verses.text: He calleth those seats, which the Greeks call thrones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:66
verses.text: The Greeks call chairs thrones, as a term of honour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:67
verses.text: Therefore, my brethren, it is not wonderful if even we should sit on seats, or chairs; but that these seats themselves should sit, when shall we be able to understand this? As if some one should say: let stools or chairs sit here.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:68
verses.text: We sit on chairs, we sit on seats, we sit on stools; the seats themselves sit not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:69
verses.text: What then meaneth this, "For there were seated seats for judgment"?If therefore heaven be the seat of God, and the Apostles are heaven; they themselves are become the seat of God, the throne of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:70
verses.text: It is said in another passage: "The soul of the righteous is the throne of wisdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:71
verses.text: A great truth, a great truth, is declared; the throne of wisdom is the soul of the righteous; that is, wisdom sitteth in the soul of the righteous as it were in her chair, in her throne, and thence judgeth whatsoever she judgeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:72
verses.text: There were therefore thrones of wisdom, and therefore the Lord said unto them, "Ye shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:73
verses.text: So they also shall sit upon twelve seats, and they are themselves the seats of God; for of them it is said, "For there were seated seats".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:74
verses.text: Who sat? "Seats".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:75
verses.text: And who are the seats? They of whom it is said, "The soul of the righteous is the seat of wisdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:76
verses.text: Who are the seats? The heavens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:77
verses.text: Who are the heavens? Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:78
verses.text: What is heaven? That of which the Lord saith, "Heaven is My seat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:79
verses.text: The righteous then themselves are the seats; and have seats; and seats shall be seated in that Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:80
verses.text: For what purpose? "For judgment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:81
verses.text: Ye shall sit, He saith, on twelve thrones, O ye thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:82
verses.text: Judging whom? Those who are below on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:83
verses.text: Who will judge? They who have become heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:84
verses.text: But they who shall be judged, will be divided into two bodies: one will be on the right hand, the other on the left.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:85
verses.text: He at once addeth, as unto the seats themselves, "Enquire ye the things that are for the peace of Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:86
verses.text: O ye seats, who now sit unto judgment, and are made the seats of the Lord who judgeth (since they who judge, enquire; they who are judged, are enquired of), "Enquire ye," he saith, "the things that are for the peace of Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:87
verses.text: What will they find by asking? That some have done deeds of charity, that others have not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:88
verses.text: Those whom they shall find to have done deeds of charity, they will summon them unto Jerusalem; for these deeds are "for the peace of Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:89
verses.text: Love is a powerful thing, my brethren, love is a powerful thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:90
verses.text: Do ye wish to see how powerful a thing love is?If charity be destitute of means, so that it cannot find what to bestow upon the poor, let it love: let it give "one cup of cold water;" as much shall be laid to its account, as to Zaccheus who gave half his patrimony to the poor Wherefore this? The one gave so little, the other so much, and shall so much be imputed to the former? Just so much.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:91
verses.text: For though his resources are unequal, his charity is not unequal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:92
verses.text: "And plenteousness," he addeth, "for them that love thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:93
verses.text: He addresses Jerusalem herself, They have plenteousness who love her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:94
verses.text: Plenteousness after want: here they are destitute, there they are affluent; here they are weak, there they are strong; here they want, there they are rich.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:95
verses.text: How have they become rich? Because they gave here what they received from God for a season, and received there what God will afterwards pay back for evermore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:96
verses.text: Here, my brethren, even rich men are poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:97
verses.text: It is a good thing for a rich man to acknowledge himself poor: for if he think himself full, that is mere puffing, not plenteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:98
verses.text: Let him own himself empty, that he may be filled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:99
verses.text: What hath he? Gold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:100
verses.text: What hath he not yet? Everlasting life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:101
verses.text: Let him consider what he hath, and see what he hath not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:102
verses.text: Brethren, of that which he hath, let him give, that he may receive what he hath not; let him purchase out of that which he hath, that which he hath not, "and plenteousness for them that love thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:103
verses.text: "Peace be in thy strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:104
verses.text: O Jerusalem, O city, who art being built as a city, whose partaking is in "The Same:" "Peace be in thy strength:" peace be in thy love; for thy strength is thy love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:105
verses.text: Hear the Song of songs: "Love is strong as death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:106
verses.text: A great saying that, brethren, "Love is strong as death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:107
verses.text: The strength of charity could not be expressed in grander terms than these, "Love is strong as death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:108
verses.text: For who resisteth death, my brethren? Consider, my brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:109
verses.text: Fire, waves, the sword, are resisted: we resist principalities, we resist kings; death cometh alone, who resisteth it? There is nought more powerful than it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:110
verses.text: Charity therefore is compared with its strength, in the words, "Love is strong as death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:111
verses.text: And since this love slayeth what we have been, that we may be what we were not; love createth a sort of death in us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:112
verses.text: This death he had died who said, "The world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world:" this death they had died unto whom he said, "Ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:113
verses.text: Love is strong as death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:114
verses.text: Thus as he was here speaking of charity, he addeth, "For my brethren and companions' sake, I spoke peace of thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:115
verses.text: O Jerusalem, thou city whose partaking is in The Same, I in this life and on this earth, I poor, he saith, I a stranger and groaning, not as yet enjoying to the full thy peace, and preaching thy peace; preach it not for my own sake, as the heretics, who seeking their own glory, say, Peace be with you: and have not the peace which they preach to the people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:116
verses.text: For if they had peace, they would not tear asunder unity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:117
verses.text: "I," he saith, "spoke peace of thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:118
verses.text: But wherefore? "For my brethren and companions' sake:" not for my own honour, not for my own money, not for my life; for, "To me to live is Christ, and to die is gain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:119
verses.text: But, "I spoke peace of thee, for my brethren and companions' sakes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:120
verses.text: For he wished to depart, and to be with Christ: but, since he must preach these things to his companions and his brethren, to abide in the flesh, he addeth, is more needful for you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:121
verses.text: "Because of the house of the Lord my God, I have sought good things for thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:122
verses.text: Not on my own account have sought good things, for then I should not seek for thee, but for myself; and so should I not have them, because I should not seek them for thee; but, "Because of the house of the Lord my God," because of the Church, because of the Saints, because of the pilgrims; because of the poor, that they may go up; because we say to them, we will go into the house of the Lord: because of the house of the Lord my God itself, I have sought good things for Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 122:123
verses.text: These long and needful words gather ye, brethren, eat them, drink them, and grow strong, run, and seize.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:2
verses.text: Let this singer ascend; and let this man sing from the heart of each of you, and let each of you be this man, for when each of you saith this, since ye are all one in Christ, one man saith this; and saith not, "Unto Thee, O Lord, have" we "lift up" our "eyes;" but, "Unto Thee, O Lord, have I lift up mine eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:3
verses.text: Ye ought indeed to imagine that every one of you is speaking; but that One in an especial sense speaketh, who is also spread abroad over the whole world  What maketh the heart of a Christian heavy? Because he is a pilgrim, and longeth for his country.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:4
verses.text: If thy heart be heavy on this score, although thou hast been prosperous in the world, still thou dost groan: and if all things combine to render thee prosperous, and this world smile upon thee on every side, thou nevertheless groanest, because thou seest that thou art set in a pilgrimage; and feelest that thou hast indeed happiness in the eyes of fools, but not as yet after the promise of Christ: this thou seekest with groans, this thou seekest with longings, and by longing ascendest, and while thou ascendest dost sing the Song of Degrees.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:5
verses.text: Where then are the ladders? For we behold so great an interval between heaven and earth, there is so wide a separation, and so great a space of regions between: we wish to climb thither, we see no ladder; do we deceive ourselves, because we sing the Song of Degrees, that is, the Song of ascent? We ascend unto heaven, if we think of God, who hath made ascending steps in the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:6
verses.text: What is to ascend in heart? To advance towards God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:7
verses.text: As every man who faileth, doth not descend, but falleth: so every one who profiteth doth ascend: but if he so profit, as to avoid pride: if he so ascend as not to fall: but if while he profiteth he become proud, in ascending he again falleth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:8
verses.text: But that he may not be proud, what ought he to do? Let him lift up his eyes unto Him who dwelleth in heaven, let him not heed himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:9
verses.text: If, my brethren, we understand by heaven the firmament which we see with our bodily eyes, we shall indeed so err, as to imagine that we cannot ascend thither without ladders, or some scaling machines: but if we ascend spiritually, we ought to understand heaven spiritually: if the ascent be in affection, heaven is in righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:10
verses.text: What is then the heaven of God? All holy souls, all righteous souls.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:11
verses.text: For the Apostles also, although they were on earth in the flesh, were heaven; for the Lord, enthroned in them, traversed the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:12
verses.text: He then dwelleth in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:13
verses.text: How?How long are they the temple according to faith? As long as Christ dwelleth in them through faith; as the Apostle saith, "That Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:14
verses.text: But they are already heaven in whom God already dwelleth visibly, who see Him face to face; all the holy Apostles, all the holy Virtues, Powers, Thrones, Lordships, that heavenly Jerusalem, wanderers from whence we groan, and for which we pray with longing; and there God dwelleth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:15
verses.text: Thither hath the Psalmist lifted up his faith, thither he riseth in affection, with longing hopes: and this very longing causeth the soul to purge off the filth of sins, and to be cleansed from every stain, that itself also may become heaven; because it hath lifted up its eyes unto Him who dwelleth in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:16
verses.text: For if we have determined that that heaven which we see with our bodily eyes is the dwelling of God, the dwelling of God will pass away; for "heaven and earth will pass away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:17
verses.text: Then, before God created heaven and earth, where did He dwell? But some one saith: and before God made the Saints, where did He dwell? God dwelt in Himself, he dwelt with Himself, and God is with Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:18
verses.text: And when He deigneth to dwell in the Saints, the Saints are not the house of God in such wise, as that God should fall when it is withdrawn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:19
verses.text: For we dwell in a house in one way, in another way God dwelleth in the Saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:20
verses.text: Thou dwellest in a house: if it be withdrawn, thou fallest: but God so dwelleth in the Saints, that if He should Himself depart, they fall.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:21
verses.text: What then followeth, since he hath said, "Unto Thee do I lift up mine eyes"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:22
verses.text: How hast thou lifted up thine eyes? "Behold, even as the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters, and as the eyes of a maiden unto the hand of her mistress: even so our eyes wait upon the Lord our God, until He have mercy upon us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:23
verses.text: We are both servants, and a handmaiden: He is both our Master and our Mistress.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:24
verses.text: What do these words mean? What do these similitudes mean? It is not wonderful if we are servants, and He our Master; but it is wonderful if we are a maiden, and He our Mistress.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:25
verses.text: But not even our being a maiden is wonderful; for we are the Church: nor is it wonderful that He is our Mistress; for He is the Power and the Wisdom of GodWhen therefore thou hearest Christ, lift up thine eyes to the hands of thy Master; when thou hearest the Power of God and the Wisdom of God, lift up thine eyes to the hands of thy Mistress; for thou art both servant and handmaiden; servant, for thou art a people; handmaiden, for thou art the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:26
verses.text: But this maiden hath found great dignity with God; she hath been made a wife.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:27
verses.text: But until she come unto those spiritual embraces, where she may without apprehension enjoy Him whom she hath loved, and for whom she hath sighed in this tedious pilgrimage, she is betrothed: and hath received a mighty pledge, the blood of the Spouse for whom she sigheth without fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:28
verses.text: Nor is it said unto her, Do not love; as it is sometimes said to any betrothed virgin, not as yet married: and is justly said, Do not love; when thou hast become a wife, then love: it is rightly said, because it is a precipitate and preposterous thing, and not a chaste desire, to love one whom she knoweth not whether she shall marry.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:29
verses.text: For it may happen that one man may be betrothed to her, and another man marry her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:30
verses.text: But as there is no one else who can be preferred to Christ, let her love without apprehension: and before she is joined unto Him, let her love, and sigh from a distance and from her far pilgrimage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:31
verses.text: "For we have been much filled with contempt".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:32
verses.text: All that will live piously according to Christ, must needs suffer reproof, must needs be despised by those who do not choose to live piously, all whose happiness is earthly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:33
verses.text: They are derided who call that happiness which they cannot see with their eyes, and it is said to them, What believest thou, madman? Dost thou see what thou believest? Hath any one returned from the world below, and reported to thee what is going on there? Behold I see and enjoy what I love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:34
verses.text: Thou art scorned, because thou dost hope for what thou seest not; and he who seemeth to hold what he seeth, scorneth thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:35
verses.text: Consider well if he doth really hold itI have my house, he hath boasted himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:36
verses.text: Thou askest, what house of his own? That which my father left me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:37
verses.text: And whence did he derive this house? My grandfather left it him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:38
verses.text: Go back even to his great grandfather, then to his great grandfather's father, and he can no longer tell their names.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:39
verses.text: Art thou not rather terrified by this thought, that thou seest many have passed through this house, and that none of them hath carried it away with him to his everlasting home? Thy father left it: he passed through it: thus thou also wilt pass by.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:40
verses.text: If therefore thou hast a mere passing stay in thy house, it is an inn for passing guests, not an habitation for permanent abode.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:41
verses.text: Yet since we hope for those things which are to come, and sigh for future happiness, and since it hath not yet appeared what we shall be, although we are already "sons of God;" for "our life is hidden with Christ in God:" "we are utterly despised," by those who seek or enjoy happiness in this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:42
verses.text: "Our soul is filled exceedingly; a reproach to the wealthy, and a contempt to the proud".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:43
verses.text: We were asking who were "the wealthy:" he hath expounded to thee, in that he hath said, "the proud".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:44
verses.text: "Reproach" and "contempt" are the same: and "wealthy" is the same with "proud".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:45
verses.text: It is a repetition of the sentence, "a reproach to the wealthy, and a contempt to the proud".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:46
verses.text: Why are the proud wealthy? Because they wish to be happy here.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:47
verses.text: Why? since they themselves too are miserable, are they wealthy? But perhaps when they are miserable, they do not mock us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:48
verses.text: Listen, my beloved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:49
verses.text: Then perchance they mock when they are happy, when they boast themselves in the pomp of their riches! when they boast themselves in the inflated state of false honours: then they mock us, and seem to say, Behold, it is well with me: I enjoy the good things before me: let those who promise what they cannot show depart from me: what I see, I hold; what I see, I enjoy; may I fare well in this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:50
verses.text: Be thou more secure; for Christ hath risen again, and hath taught thee what He will give in another life: be assured that He giveth it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:51
verses.text: But that man mocketh thee, because he holdeth what he hath.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:52
verses.text: Bear with his mockeries, and thou wilt laugh at his groans: for afterwards there will come a season when these very persons will say, "This was he whom we had sometimes in derision".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:53
verses.text: To this we must add, that sometimes those also who are beneath the scourge of temporal unhappiness, mock usDid not the robber mock, who was crucif ied with our crucified Lord? If therefore they who are not wealthy mock us, why doth the Psalm say, "A reproach to the wealthy"? If we carefully sift the matter, even these (the unfortunate) are wealthy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:54
verses.text: How are they wealthy? Yea; for if they were not wealthy, they would not be proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:55
verses.text: For one man is wealthy in money, and proud on that score: another is wealthy in honours, and is proud on that account: another imagines himself wealthy in righteousness, and hence his pride, which is worse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:56
verses.text: They who seem not to be wealthy in money, seem to themselves to be wealthy in righteousness towards God; and when calamity overtakes them, they justify themselves, accuse God, and say, What wrong have I been guilty of, or, what have I done? Thou repliest: Look back, call to mind thy sins, see if thou hast done nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:57
verses.text: He is somewhat touched in conscience, and returneth to himself, and thinketh of his evil deeds; and when he hath thought of his evil deeds, not even then doth he choose to confess that he deserves his sufferings; but saith, Behold, I have clearly done many things; but I see that many have done worse, and suffer no evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:58
verses.text: He is righteous against God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:59
verses.text: He also therefore is wealthy: he hath his breast puffed out with righteousness; since God seemeth to him to do ill, and he seemeth to himself to suffer unjustly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:60
verses.text: And if thou gavest him a vessel to pilot, he would be shipwrecked with it: yet he wishes to deprive God of the government of this world, and himself to hold the helm of Creation, and to distribute among all men pains and pleasures, punishments and rewards.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:61
verses.text: Miserable soul! yet why do ye wonder? He is wealthy, but wealthy in iniquity, wealthy in malignity; but is more wealthy in iniquity, in proportion as he seemeth to himself to be wealthy in righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:62
verses.text: But a Christian ought not to be wealthy, but ought to acknowledge himself poor; and if he hath riches, he ought to know that they are not true riches, so that he may desire othersAnd what is the wealth of our righteousness? How much soever righteousness there may be in us, it is a sort of dew compared to that fountain: compared to that plenteousness it is as a few drops, which may soften our life, and relax our hard iniquity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:63
verses.text: Let us only desire to be filled with the full fountain of righteousness, let us long to be filled with that abundant richness, of which it is said in the Psalm, "They shall be satisfied with the plenteousness of Thy house: and Thou shalt give them drink out of the torrent of Thy pleasure".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:64
verses.text: But while we are here, let us understand ourselves to be destitute and in want; not only in respect of those riches which are not the true riches, but of salvation itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:65
verses.text: And when we are whole, let us understand that we are weak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:66
verses.text: For as long as this body hungers and thirsts, as long as this body is weary with watching, weary with standing, weary with walking, weary with sitting, weary with eating; whithersoever it turneth itself for a relief from weariness, there it discovereth another source of fatigue: there is therefore no perfect soundness, not even in the body itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:67
verses.text: Those riches are then not riches, but beggary; for the more they abound, the more doth destitution and avarice increaseLet then our whole hunger, our whole thirst, be for true riches, and true health, and true righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:68
verses.text: What are true riches? That heavenly abode in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:69
verses.text: For who is called rich on this earth? When a rich man is praised, what is meant? He is very rich: nothing is wanting to him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:70
verses.text: That surely is the praise of him that praiseth the other: for it is not this, when it is said, He wants nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:71
verses.text: Consider if he really want nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:72
verses.text: If he desires nothing, he wants nothing: but if he still desires more than what he hath, his riches have increased in such wise, that his wants have increased also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 123:73
verses.text: But in that City there will be true riches, because there will be nothing wanting to us there; for we shall not be in need of anything, and there will be true health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXIV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:2
verses.text: Ye already well know, dearest brethren, that a "Song of Degrees," is a song of our ascent: and that this ascent is not effected by the feet of the body, but by the affections of the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:3
verses.text: This we have repeatedly reminded you of: and we need not repeat it too often, that there may be room for saying what hath not yet been said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:4
verses.text: This Psalm, therefore, which ye have now heard sung for you, is inscribed, "A Song of Degrees".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:5
verses.text: This is its title.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:6
verses.text: They sing therefore while ascending: and sometimes as it were one man singeth, sometimes as it were many; because many are one, since Christ is One, and in Christ the members of Christ constitute one with Christ, and the Head of all these members is in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:7
verses.text: But although the body toileth on earth, it is not cut off from its Head; for the Head looketh down from above, and regardeth the body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:8
verses.text: Whether therefore one or many sing; many men are one man, because it is unity; and Christ, as we have said, is One, and all Christians are members of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:9
verses.text: Certain members indeed of that body of which we also are, which can sing in truth, have gone before us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:10
verses.text: And this the holy Martyrs have sung: for they have already escaped, and are with Christ in joy about to receive at last incorruptible bodies, the very same which were at first corruptible, wherein they have suffered pains; of the same there will be made for them ornaments of righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:11
verses.text: Therefore whether they in reality, or we in hope, joining our affections with their crowns, and longing for such a life as we have not here, and shall never gain unless we have longed for it here, let us all sing together, and say, "If the Lord Himself had not been in us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:12
verses.text: "If the Lord Himself had not been in us, now may Israel say" When? "When men rose up against us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:13
verses.text: Marvel not: they have been subdued: for they were men; but the Lord was in us, man was not in us: for men rose up against us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:14
verses.text: Nevertheless men would crush other men, unless in those men who could not be crushed, there were not man, but the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:15
verses.text: For what could men do to you, while ye rejoiced, and sang, and securely held everlasting bliss? what could men do to you when they rose against you, if the Lord had not been on your side? what could they do? "Perchance they had swallowed us up quick".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:16
verses.text: "Swallowed us up:" they would not first have slain us, and so have swallowed us up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:17
verses.text: O inhuman, O cruel men! The Church swalloweth not thus To Peter it was said, "Kill and eat:" not, Swallow quick.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:18
verses.text: Because no man entereth into the body of the Church, save he be slain first What he was dieth, that he may be what he was not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:19
verses.text: Otherwise, he who is not slain, and is not eaten by the Church, may be in the visible number of the people: but he cannot be in the number of the people which is known to God, whereof the Apostle saith, "The Lord knoweth who are His," save he be eaten; and eaten he cannot be, save he first be slain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:20
verses.text: The Pagan cometh, still in him idolatry liveth; he must be grafted among the members of Christ: that he may be engrafted, he must needs be eaten; but he cannot be eaten by the Church, save first he be slain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:21
verses.text: Let him renounce the world, then is he slain; let him believe in God, then is he eatenBut they in whom the Lord is, are slain and die not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:22
verses.text: But they who consent and live, are swallowed quick, when swallowed up they die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:23
verses.text: But they who have suffered, and have not yielded to tribulations, rejoice and say, "If the Lord had not been in us," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:24
verses.text: "When their fury was enraged upon us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:25
verses.text: They are now in anger, they now openly rage: "perchance the water had drowned us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:26
verses.text: By water he meaneth ungodly nations: and we shall see what sort of water in the following verses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:27
verses.text: Whoever had consented unto them, water would have overwhelmed him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:28
verses.text: For he would die by the death of the Egyptians, he would not pass through after the example of the Israelites.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:29
verses.text: For ye know, brethren, that the people of Israel passed through the water, by which the Egyptians were overwhelmed But what sort of water is this? It is a torrent, it flows with violence, but it will pass byHence He, our Head, first drinketh, of whom it is said in the Psalms, "He shall drink of the torrent in the way: therefore shall He lift up His head".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:30
verses.text: For our Head is already exalted, because He drank of the torrent by the way; for our Lord hath suffered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:31
verses.text: If therefore our Head hath been already raised up, why doth the body fear the torrent? Without doubt, because the Head hath been raised, the body also will say hereafter, "Our soul hath passed over the torrent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:32
verses.text: Perhaps our soul hath passed over the water without substance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:33
verses.text: Behold, what sort of water he was speaking of, "The water perchance had overwhelmed us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:34
verses.text: But what meaneth, "without substance"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:35
verses.text: In the first place, what meaneth, "Perchance our soul hath passed over"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:36
verses.text: Understand however the meaning to be this: "Thinkest thou our soul hath passed over?" and why do they say, "Thinkest thou"? Because the greatness of the danger maketh it hardly credible that he hath escaped.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:37
verses.text: They have endured a great death: they have been in great dangers; they have been so much oppressed, that they almost gave consent while alive, and were all but swallowed up alive: now therefore that they have escaped, now that they are secure, but still remember the danger, the great danger, say, "Thinkest thou our soul hath passed over the water without substance?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:38
verses.text: What is the water without substance, save the water of sins without substance? For sins have not substance: they have destitution, not substance; they have want, not substance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:39
verses.text: In that water without substance, the younger son lost the whole of his substanceDost thou wish to see how the water is without substance? Take away with thee to the world below what thou hast acquired: what wilt thou do? Thou hast acquired gold: thou hast lost thy faith: after a few days thou leavest this life; thou canst not take away with thee the gold thou hast acquired by the loss of thy good faith; thy heart, destitute of faith, goeth forth into punishment—thy heart, which if full of faith, would go forth unto a crown.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:40
verses.text: Behold, what thou hast done is nothing: and thou hast offended God for nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:41
verses.text: Men hear that common proverb; and the proverbs of God slumber in them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:42
verses.text: What proverb? "Better in hand than in hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:43
verses.text: Unhappy man, what hast thou in hand? Thou sayest, "Better in hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:44
verses.text: Hold it so as not to lose it, and then say, "Better in hand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:45
verses.text: But if thou holdest it not, why dost thou not hold fast that which thou canst not lose? What then hast thou in hand? Gold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:46
verses.text: Keep it in hand, therefore: if thou hast it in hand, let it not be taken away without thy consent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:47
verses.text: But if through gold also thou art carried where thou wishest not, and if a more powerful robber seeketh thee, because he findeth thee a less powerful robber; if a stronger eagle pursue thee, because thou hast carried off a hare before him: the lesser was thy prey, thou wilt be a prey unto the greater.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:48
verses.text: Men see not these things in human affairs: by so much avarice are they blinded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:49
verses.text: Let them escape the water without substance, and say, "Blessed be the Lord, who hath not given us over for a prey unto their teeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:50
verses.text: For the hunters were following, and had placed a bait in their trap.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:51
verses.text: What bait? The sweetness of this life, so that each man for the sake of the sweetness of this life may thrust his head into iniquity, and be caught in the trap.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:52
verses.text: Not they, in whom the Lord was, they who say, "If the Lord Himself had not been in us;" they have not been taken in the trap.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:53
verses.text: Let the Lord be in thee, and thou wilt not be taken in the trap.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:54
verses.text: "Our soul is escaped, even as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:55
verses.text: Because the Lord was in the soul itself, therefore hath that soul escaped, even as a bird out of the snare of the fowler.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:56
verses.text: Why like a bird? Because it had fallen heedlessly, like a bird; and it could say afterwards, God will forgive me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:57
verses.text: Unstable bird, rather set thy feet firm upon the rock: go not into the trap.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:58
verses.text: Thou wilt be taken, consumed, crushed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:59
verses.text: Let the Lord be in thee, and He will deliver thee from greater threats, from the snare of the fowlers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:60
verses.text: As if thou wert to see a bird about to fall into a snare, thou makest a greater noise that it may fly away from the net; so also, when perhaps some even of the Martyrs were stretching out their neck after the enjoyment of this life, the Lord, who was in them, made the noise of hell, and the bird was delivered from the snare of the fowlers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:61
verses.text: The snare was the sweetness of this life: they were not entangled in the snare, and were slain; by their slaughter the net was broken; no longer did the sweetness of this life remain, that they might again be entangled by it, but it was crushed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:62
verses.text: Was the bird also crushed? Far be it! for it was not in the snare: "The snare is broken, and we are delivered".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:63
verses.text: "Our help standeth in the Name of the Lord, who hath made heaven and earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:64
verses.text: For if this were not our help, the snare would not indeed remain for ever; but when the bird was once taken, it would be crushed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:65
verses.text: For this life will pass away; and they who shall have been taken in by its pleasures, and through these pleasures have offended God, will pass away with this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:66
verses.text: For the snare will be broken; be ye assured of this: all the sweetness of this present life will no longer exist, when the lot assigned to it hath been fulfilled; but we must not be enthralled by it, so that when the net is broken, thou mayest then rejoice and say, "The snare is broken, and we are delivered".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 124:67
verses.text: But lest thou think that thou canst do this of thy own strength, consider whose work thy deliverance is (for if thou art proud, thou fallest into the snare), and say, "Our help standeth in the Name of the Lord, who hath made heaven and earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:2
verses.text: This Psalm, belonging to the number of the Songs of Degrees, teacheth us, while we ascend and raise our minds unto the Lord our God in loving charity and piety, not to fix our gaze upon men who are prosperous in this world, with a happiness that is false and unstable, and altogether seductive; where they cherish nothing save pride, and their heart freezeth up against God, and is made hard against the shower of His grace, so that it beareth not fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:3
verses.text: "They that put their trust in the Lord shall be even as the mount Sion: they shall not be removed for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:4
verses.text: Who are these? "They shall stand fast for ever, who dwell in Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:5
verses.text: If we understand this earthly Jerusalem, all who dwelt therein have been excluded by wars and by the destruction of the city: thou now seekest a Jew in the city of Jerusalem, and findest him not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:6
verses.text: Why then will "they that dwell in Jerusalem not be moved for ever," save because there is another Jerusalem, of which ye are wont to hear much? She is our mother, for whom we sigh and groan in this pilgrimage, that we may return unto her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:7
verses.text: They then who dwell therein "shall never be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:8
verses.text: But they who dwelt in that earthly Jerusalem, have been moved; first in heart, afterwards by exile.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:9
verses.text: When they were moved in heart and fell, then they crucified the King of the heavenly Jerusalem herself; they were already spiritually without, and shut out of doors their very King.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:10
verses.text: For they cast Him out without their city, and crucified Him without He too cast them out of His city, that is, of the everlasting Jerusalem, the Mother of us all, who is in Heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:11
verses.text: What is this Jerusalem? He briefly describes it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:12
verses.text: "The mountains stand around Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:13
verses.text: Is it anything great, that we are in a city surrounded by mountains? Is this the whole of our happiness, that we shall have a city which mountains surround? Do we not know what mountains are? or what are mountains save swellings of the earth? Different then from these are those mountains that we love, lofty mountains, preachers of truth, whether Angels, or Apostles, or Prophets.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:14
verses.text: They stand around Jerusalem; they surround her, and, as it were, form a wall for her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:15
verses.text: Of these lovely and delightful mountains Scripture constantly speaketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:16
verses.text: They are the mountains of whom we sing: "I lifted up mine eyes unto the mountains, from whence my help shall come:" because in this life we have help from the holy Scriptures And through the mountains that receive peace, the little hills received righteousness: for what saith he of the mountains themselves? He said not, they have peace from themselves, or they make peace, or generate peace; but, they receive peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:17
verses.text: The Lord is the source, whence they receive peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:18
verses.text: So therefore lift up thine eyes to the mountains for the sake of peace, that thy help may come from the Lord, who hath made heaven and earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:19
verses.text: Again, the Holy Spirit mentioning these mountains saith this: "Thou dost light them wonderfully from Thy everlasting mountains".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:20
verses.text: He said not, the mountains light them: but, Thou lightest them from Thy everlasting mountains: through those mountains whom Thou hast willed to be everlasting, preaching the Gospel, Thou lighting them, not the mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:21
verses.text: Such then are the "mountains that stand around Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:22
verses.text: And that ye may know what sort of mountains these be that stand around Jerusalem; where Scripture hath mentioned good mountains, very rarely, and hardly, and perhaps never, doth it fail instantly to mention the Lord also, or allude to Him at the same moment, that our hopes rest not in the mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:23
verses.text: Lest thou again shouldest tarry in the mountains, he at once addeth, "Even so the Lord standeth round about His people:" that thy hope might not lie in the mountains, but in Him who lighteth the mountains For when He dwelleth in the mountains, that is, in the Saints, He Himself is round about His people; and He hath Himself walled His people with a spiritual fortification, that it may not be moved for evermore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:24
verses.text: But when Scripture speaketh of evil mountains, it addeth not the Lord unto them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:25
verses.text: Such mountains, we have already told you often, signify certain mighty, but evil, souls.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:26
verses.text: For ye are not to suppose, brethren, that heresies could be produced through any little souls.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:27
verses.text: None save great men have been the authors of heresies; but in proportion as they were mighty, so were they evil, mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:28
verses.text: For they were not such mountains as would receive peace, that the hills might receive righteousness; but they received dissension from their father the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:29
verses.text: There were therefore mountains: beware thou fly not to such mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:30
verses.text: For men will come, and say unto thee, There is a great hero, there is a great man! How great was that Donatus! How great is Maximian! and a certain Photinus, what a great man he was! And Arius too, how illustrious he was! All these I have mentioned are mountains, but mountains that cause shipwreck.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:31
verses.text: But love such mountains, in whom the Lord is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:32
verses.text: Then do those very mountains love thee, if thou hast not placed hope in them See, brethren, what the mountains of God are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:33
verses.text: Thence they are so called in another passage: "Thy righteousness is like the mountains of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:34
verses.text: Not their righteousness, but "Thy righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:35
verses.text: Hear that great mountain the Apostle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:36
verses.text: "That I may be found in Him, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:37
verses.text: But they who have chosen to be mountains through their own righteousness, as certain Jews or Pharisees their rulers, are thus blamed: "Being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, they have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:38
verses.text: But they who have submitted themselves are exalted in such a manner as to be humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:39
verses.text: In that they are great, they are mountains; in that they submit themselves unto God, they are valleys: and in that they have the capacity of piety, they receive the plenteousness of peace, and transmit the copious irrigation to the hills, only beware, at present, what mountains thou lovest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:40
verses.text: If thou wish to be loved by good mountains, place not thy trust even in good mountains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:41
verses.text: For how great a mountain was Paul? where is one like him found? We speak of the greatness of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:42
verses.text: Can any one readily be found of so great grace? Nevertheless, he feared lest that bird should place trust in him: and what doth he say: "Was Paul crucified for you?" But lift up your eyes unto the mountains, whence help may come unto you: for, "I have planted, Apollos hath watered:" but, your help cometh from the Lord, who hath made Heaven and earth; for, "God gave the increase".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:43
verses.text: "The mountains," therefore, "stand around Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:44
verses.text: But as "the mountains stand around Jerusalem, even so standeth the Lord round about His people, from this time forth for evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:45
verses.text: If therefore the mountains stand around Jerusalem, and the Lord standeth round about His people, the Lord bindeth His people into one bond of love and peace, so that they who trust in the Lord, like the mount Sion, may not be moved for evermore: and this is, "from this time forth for evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:46
verses.text: "For the Lord will not leave the rod of the ungodly upon the lot of the righteous, lest the righteous put forth their hands unto wickedness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:47
verses.text: At present indeed the righteous suffer in some measure, and at present the unrighteous sometimes tyrannize over the righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:48
verses.text: In what ways? Sometimes the unrighteous arrive at worldly honours: when they have arrived at them, and have been made either judges or kings; for God doth this for the discipline of His folk, for the discipline of His people; the honour due to their power must needs be shown them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:49
verses.text: For thus hath God ordained His Church, that every power ordained in the world may have honour, and sometimes from those who are better than those in power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:50
verses.text: For the sake of illustration I take one instance; hence calculate the grades of all powers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:51
verses.text: The primary and every day relation of authority between man and man is that between master and slave.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:52
verses.text: Almost all houses have a power of this sort.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:53
verses.text: There are masters, there are also slaves; these are different names, but men and men are equal names And what saith the Apostle, teaching that slaves are subject to their masters? "Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh:" for there is a Master according to the Spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:54
verses.text: He is the true and everlasting Master; but those temporal masters are for a time only.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:55
verses.text: When thou walkest in the way, when thou livest in this life, Christ doth not wish to make thee proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:56
verses.text: It hath been thy lot to become a Christian, and to have a man for thy master: thou wast not made a Christian, that thou mightest disdain to be a servant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:57
verses.text: For when by Christ's command thou servest a man, thou servest not the man, but Him who commanded thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:58
verses.text: He saith this also: "Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:59
verses.text: Behold, he hath not made men free from being servants, but good servants from bad servants.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:60
verses.text: How much do the rich owe to Christ, who orders their house for them! so that if thou hast had an unbelieving servant, suppose Christ convert him, and say not to him, Leave thy master, thou hast now known Him who is thy true Master: he perhaps is ungodly and unjust, thou art now faithful and righteous: it is unworthy that a righteous and faithful man should serve an unjust and unbelieving master.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:61
verses.text: He spoke not thus unto him, but rather, Serve him: and to confirm the servant, added, Serve as I served; I before thee served the unjust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:62
verses.text: If the Lord of heaven and earth, through whom all things were created, served the unworthy, asked mercy for His furious persecutors, and, as it were, showed Himself as their Physician at His Advent (for physicians also, better both in art and health, serve the sick): how much more ought not a man to disdain, with his whole mind, and his whole good will, with his whole love to serve even a bad master! Behold, a better serveth an inferior, but for a season.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:63
verses.text: Understand what I have said of the master and slave, to be true also of powers and kings, of all the exalted stations of this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:64
verses.text: For sometimes they are good powers, and fear God; sometimes they fear not God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:65
verses.text: Julian was an infidel Emperor, an apostate, a wicked man, an idolater; Christian soldiers served an infidel Emperor; when they came to the cause of Christ, they acknowledged Him only who was in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:66
verses.text: If he called upon them at any time to worship idols, to offer incense; they preferred God to him: but whenever he commanded them to deploy into line, to march against this or that nation, they at once obeyed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:67
