verses.text: They distinguished their everlasting from their temporal master; and yet they were, for the sake of their everlasting Master, submissive to their temporal master.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:68
verses.text: But will it be thus always, that the ungodly have power over the righteous? It will not be so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:69
verses.text: The rod of the ungodly is felt for a season upon the lot of the righteous; but it is not left there, it will not be there for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:70
verses.text: A time will come, when Christ, appearing in his glory, shall gather all nations before Him And thou wilt see there many slaves among the sheep, and many masters among the goats; and again many masters among the sheep, many slaves among the goats.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:71
verses.text: For all slaves are not good—do not infer this from the consolation we have given to servants—nor are all masters evil, because we have thus repressed the pride of masters.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:72
verses.text: There are good masters who believe, and there are evil: there are good servants who believe, and there are evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:73
verses.text: But as long as good servants serve evil masters, let them endure for a season.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:74
verses.text: "For God will not leave the rod of the ungodly upon the lot of the righteous".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:75
verses.text: Why will He not? "Lest the righteous put forth their hand unto wickedness:" that the righteous may endure for a season the domination of the ungodly, and may understand that this is not for ever, but may prepare themselves to possess their everlasting heritage.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:76
verses.text: And he therefore addeth, "Do well, O Lord, unto those that are good and true of heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:77
verses.text: They who are right in heart, of whom I was speaking a little before,—they who follow the will of God, not their own will,—reflect upon this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:78
verses.text: But they who wish to follow God, allow Him to go before, and themselves to follow; not themselves to go before, and Him to follow; and in all things they find Him good, whether chastening, or consoling, or exercising, or crowning, or cleansing, or enlightening; as the Apostle saith, "We know that all things work together for good to them that love God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:79
verses.text: Whence the Psalmist at once addeth: "As for such as turn aside, the Lord shall lead them forth unto strangling with the workers of unrighteousness" : that is, those whose deeds they have imitated; because they took delight in their present pleasures, and did not believe in their punishments to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:80
verses.text: What then shall they have, who are righteous in heart, and who turn not back? Let us now come to the heritage itself, brethren, for we are sons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:81
verses.text: What shall we possess? What is our heritage? what is our country: what is it called? Peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:82
verses.text: In this we salute you, this we announce to you, this the mountains receive, and the little hills receive as righteousness Peace is Christ: "for He is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:83
verses.text: Since we are sons, we shall have an inheritance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:84
verses.text: And what shall this inheritance be called, but peace? And consider that they who love not peace are disinherited.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:85
verses.text: Now they who divide unity, love not peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:86
verses.text: Peace is the possession of the pious, the possession of heirs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:87
verses.text: And who are heirs? Sons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:88
verses.text: Since then Christ the Son of God is peace, He therefore came to gather together His own, and to separate them from the wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:89
verses.text: From what wicked men? From those who hate Jerusalem, who hate peace, who wish to tear unity asunder, who believe not peace, who preach a false peace to the people, and have it not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:90
verses.text: To whom answer is made, when they say, "Peace be with you," "And with thy spirit:" but they speak falsely, and they hear falsely.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:91
verses.text: Unto whom do they say, Peace be with you? To those whom they separate from the peace of the whole earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:92
verses.text: And unto whom is it said, "And with thy spirit"? To those who embrace dissensions, and who hate peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:93
verses.text: For if peace were in their spirit, would they not love unity, and leave dissensions? Speaking then false words, they hear false words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:94
verses.text: Let us speak true words, and hear true words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 125:95
verses.text: Let us be Israel, and let us embrace peace; for Jerusalem is a vision of peace, and we are Israel, "and peace is upon Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXVI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:2
verses.text: How man had come into captivity, let us ask the Apostle Paul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:3
verses.text: For he saith: "For we know that the Law is spiritual, but I am carnal, sold under sin".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:4
verses.text: Behold whence we became captives; because we were sold under sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:5
verses.text: Who sold us? We ourselves, who consented to the seducer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:6
verses.text: We could sell ourselves; we could not redeem ourselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:7
verses.text: We sold ourselves by consent of sin, we are redeemed in the faith of righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:8
verses.text: For innocent blood was given for us, that we might be redeemed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:9
verses.text: Whatsoever blood he shed in persecuting the righteous, what kind of blood did he shed? Righteous men's blood, indeed, he shed; they were Prophets, righteous men, our fathers, and Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:10
verses.text: Whose blood he shed, yet all coming of the offspring of sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:11
verses.text: One blood he shed of Him who was not justified, but born righteous: by shedding that blood, he lost those whom he held.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:12
verses.text: For they for whom innocent blood was given were redeemed, and, turned back from their captivity, they sing this Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:13
verses.text: "When the Lord turned back the captivity of Sion, we became as those that are comforted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:14
verses.text: He meant by this to say, we became joyful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:15
verses.text: When? "When the Lord turned back the captivity of Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:16
verses.text: What is Sion? Jerusalem, the same is also the eternal Sion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:17
verses.text: How is Sion eternal, how is Sion captive? In angels eternal, in men captive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:18
verses.text: For not all the citizens of that city are captives, but those who are away from thence, they are captives.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:19
verses.text: Man was a citizen of Jerusalem, but sold under sin he became a pilgrim.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:20
verses.text: Of his progeny was born the human race, and the captivity of Sion filled all lands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:21
verses.text: And how is this captivity of Sion a shadow of that Jerusalem? The shadow of that Sion, which was granted to the Jews, in an image, in a figure, was in captivity in Babylonia, and after seventy years that people turned back to its own cityBut when all time is past, then we return to our country, as after seventy years that people returned from the Babylonish captivity, for Babylon is this world; since Babylon is interpreted "confusion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:22
verses.text: So then this whole life of human affairs is confusion, which belongeth not unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:23
verses.text: In this confusion, in this Babylonish land, Sion is held captive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:24
verses.text: But "the Lord hath turned back the captivity of Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:25
verses.text: "And we became," he saith, "as those that are comforted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:26
verses.text: That is, we rejoiced as receiving consolation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:27
verses.text: Consolation is not save for the unhappy, consolation is not save for them that groan, that mourn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:28
verses.text: Wherefore, "as those that are comforted," except because we are still mourning? We mourn for our present lot, we are comforted in hope: when the present is passed by, of our mourning will come everlasting joy, when there will be no need of consolation, because we shall be wounded with no distress.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:29
verses.text: But wherefore saith he "as" those that are comforted, and saith not comforted? This word "as," is not always put for likeness: when we say "As," it sometimes refers to the actual case, sometimes to likeness: here it is with reference to the actual case.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:30
verses.text: Walk therefore in Christ, and sing rejoicing, sing as one that is comforted; because He went before thee who hath commanded thee to follow Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:31
verses.text: "Then was our mouth filled with joy, and our tongue with exultation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:32
verses.text: That mouth, brethren, which we have in our body, how is it "filled with joy"? It useth not to be "filled," save with meat, or drink, or some such thing put into the mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:33
verses.text: Sometimes our mouth is filled; and it is more that we say to your holiness, when we have our mouth full, we cannot speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:34
verses.text: But we have a mouth within, that is, in the heart, whence whatsoever proceedeth, if it is evil, defileth us, if it is good, cleanseth us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:35
verses.text: For concerning this very mouth ye heard when the Gospel was read.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:36
verses.text: For the Jews reproached the Lord, because His disciples ate with unwashen hands They reproached who had cleanness without; and within were full of stains.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:37
verses.text: They reproached, whose righteousness was only in the eyes of men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:38
verses.text: But the Lord sought our inward cleanness, which if we have, the outside must needs be clean also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:39
verses.text: "Cleanse," He saith, "the inside," and "the outside shall be clean also".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:40
verses.text: But let us return to what was just now read from the Gospel, relating to the verse before us, "Our mouth was filled with joy, and our tongue with delight:" for we are inquiring what mouth and what tongue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:41
verses.text: Listen, beloved brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:42
verses.text: The Lord was scoffed at, because His disciples ate with unwashed hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:43
verses.text: The Lord answered them as was fitting, and said unto the crowds whom He had called unto Him, "Hear ye all, and understand: not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:44
verses.text: What is this? when He said, what goeth into the mouth, He meant only the mouth of the body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:45
verses.text: For meat goeth in, and meats defile not a man; because, "All things are clean to the clean;" and, "every creature of God is good, and none to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:46
verses.text: Guard the mouth of thy heart from evil, and thou wilt be innocent: the tongue of thy body will be innocent, thy hands will be innocent; even thy feet will be innocent, thy eyes, thy ears, will be innocent; all thy members will serve under righteousness, because a righteous commander hath thy heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:47
verses.text: "Then shall they say among the heathen, the Lord hath done great things for them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:48
verses.text: "Yea, the Lord hath done great things for us already, whereof we rejoice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:49
verses.text: Consider, my brethren, if Sion doth not at present say this among the heathen, throughout the whole world; consider if men are not running unto the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:50
verses.text: In the whole world our redemption is received; Amen is answered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:51
verses.text: The dwellers in Jerusalem, therefore, captive, destined to return, pilgrims, sighing for their country, speak thus among the heathen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:52
verses.text: What do they say? "The Lord hath done great things for us, whereof we rejoice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:53
verses.text: Have they done anything for themselves? They have done ill with themselves, for they have sold themselves under sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:54
verses.text: The Redeemer came, and did the good things for them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:55
verses.text: "Turn our captivity, O Lord, as the torrents in the south".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:56
verses.text: Consider, my brethren, what this meaneth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:57
verses.text: As torrents are turned in the south, so turn our captivity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:58
verses.text: In a certain passage Scripture saith, in admonishing us concerning good works, "Thy sins also shall melt away, even as the ice in fair warm weather".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:59
verses.text: Our sins therefore bound us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:60
verses.text: How? As the cold bindeth the water that it run not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:61
verses.text: Bound with the frost of our sins, we have frozen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:62
verses.text: But the south wind is a warm wind: when the south wind blows, the ice melts, and the torrents are filled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:63
verses.text: Now winter streams are called torrents; for filled with sudden rains they run with great force.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:64
verses.text: We had therefore become frozen in captivity; our sins bound us: the south wind the Holy Spirit hath blown: our sins are forgiven us, we are released from the frost of iniquity; as the ice in fair weather, our sins are melted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:65
verses.text: Let us run unto our country, as the torrents in the south.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:66
verses.text: For the next words are, "They that sow in tears, shall reap in joy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:67
verses.text: In this life, which is full of tears, let us sow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:68
verses.text: What shall we sow? Good works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:69
verses.text: Works of mercy are our seeds: of which seeds the Apostle saith, "Let us not be weary in well doing; for in due season we shall reap if we faint not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:70
verses.text: Speaking therefore of almsgiving itself, what saith he? "This I say; he that soweth sparingly, shall reap also sparingly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:71
verses.text: He therefore who soweth plentifully, shall reap plentifully: he who soweth sparingly, shall reap also sparingly: and he that soweth nothing, shall reap nothing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:72
verses.text: Why do ye long for ample estates, where ye may sow plentifully? There is not a wider field on which ye can sow than Christ, who hath willed that we should sow in Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:73
verses.text: Your soil is the Church; sow as much as ye can.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:74
verses.text: But thou hast not enough to do this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:75
verses.text: Hast thou the will?  As what thou hadst would be nothing, if thou hadst not a good will; so do not despond, because thou hast not, if thou hast a good will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:76
verses.text: For what dost thou sow? Mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:77
verses.text: And what wilt thou reap? Peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:78
verses.text: Said the Angels, Peace on earth unto rich men? No, but, "Peace on earth unto men of a good will".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:79
verses.text: Zacchaeus had a strong will, Zacchaeus had great charityDid then that widow who cast her two farthings into the treasury, sow little? Nay, as much as Zacchaeus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:80
verses.text: For she had narrower means, but an equal will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:81
verses.text: She gave her two mites with as good a will as Zacchaeus gave the half of his patrimony.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:82
verses.text: If thou consider what they gave, thou wilt find their gifts different; if thou look to the source, thou wilt find them equal; she gave whatever she had, and he gave what he had.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:83
verses.text: But if they are beggars whose profession is asking alms, in trouble they also have what to bestow upon one another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:84
verses.text: God hath not so forsaken them, but that they have wherein they may be tried by their bestowing of alms.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:85
verses.text: This man cannot walk; he who can walk, lendeth his feet to the lame; he who seeth, lendeth his eyes to the blind; and he who is young and sound, lendeth his strength to the old or the infirm, carrieth him: the one is poor, the other is rich.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:86
verses.text: Sometimes also the rich man is found to be poor, and something is bestowed upon him by the poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:87
verses.text: Somebody cometh to a river, so much the more delicate as he is more rich; he cannot pass over: if he were to pass over with bare limbs, he would catch cold, would be ill, would die: a poor man more active in body cometh up: he carries the rich man over; he giveth alms unto the rich.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:88
verses.text: Think not therefore those only poor, who have not money.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:89
verses.text: Thus love ye, thus be ye affectioned unto one another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:90
verses.text: Attend not solely to yourselves: but to those who are in want around you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:91
verses.text: But because these things take place in this life with troubles and cares, faint not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:92
verses.text: Ye sow in tears, ye shall reap in joy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:93
verses.text: How, my brethren? When the farmer goeth forth with the plough, carrying seed, is not the wind sometimes keen, and doth not the shower sometimes deter him? He looketh to the sky, seeth it lowering, shivers with cold, nevertheless goeth forth, and soweth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:94
verses.text: For he feareth lest while he is observing the foul weather, and awaiting sunshine, the time may pass away, and he may not find anything to reap.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:95
verses.text: Put not off, my brethren; sow in wintry weather, sow good works, even while ye weep; for, "They that sow in tears, shall reap in joy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:96
verses.text: They sow their seed, good will, and good works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:97
verses.text: "They went on their way and wept, casting their seed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:98
verses.text: Why did they weep? Because they were among the miserable, and were themselves miserable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:99
verses.text: It is better, my brethren, that no man should be miserable, than that thou shouldest do alms.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:100
verses.text: Nevertheless, as long as there are objects for its exercise, let us not fail amid those troubles to sow our seed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:101
verses.text: Although we sow in tears, yet shall we reap in joy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:102
verses.text: For in that resurrection of the dead, each man shall receive his own sheaves, that is, the produce of his seed, the crown of joys and of delight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:103
verses.text: Then will there be a joyous triumph, when we shall laugh at death, wherein we groaned before: then shall they say to death, "O death, where is thy strife? O death, where is thy sting?" But why do they now rejoice? Because "they bring their sheaves with them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:104
verses.text: In this Psalm we have chiefly exhorted you to do deeds of alms, because it is thence that we ascend; and ye see that he who ascendeth, singeth the song of steps.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:105
verses.text: Remember: do not love to descend, instead of to ascend, but reflect upon your ascent: because he who descended from Jerusalem to Jericho fell among thievesThe Samaritan as He passed by slighted us not: He healed us, He raised us upon His beast, upon His flesh; He led us to the inn, that is, the Church; He entrusted us to the host, that is, to the Apostle; He gave two pence, whereby we might be healed, the love of God, and the love of our neighbour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 126:106
verses.text: The Apostle spent more; for, though it was allowed unto all the Apostles to receive, as Christ's soldiers, pay from Christ's subjects, that Apostle, nevertheless, toiled with his own hands, and excused the subjects the maintenance owing to him All this hath already happened: if we have descended, and have been wounded; let us ascend, let us sing, and make progress, in order that we may arrive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXVII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:2
verses.text: Among all the Songs entitled the Song of degrees, this Psalm hath a further addition in the title, that it is "Solomon's".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:3
verses.text: For thus it is entitled, "A Song of degrees of Solomon".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:4
verses.text: It hath therefore aroused our attention, and caused us to enquire the reason of this addition, "of Solomon".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:5
verses.text: For it is needless to repeat explanations of the other words, Song of degrees.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:6
verses.text: Solomon was in his time David's son, a great man, through whom many holy precepts and healthful admonitions and divine mysteries have been wrought by the Holy Spirit in the Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:7
verses.text: Solomon himself was a lover of women, and was rejected by God: and this lust was so great a snare unto him, that he was induced by women even to sacrifice to idols, as Scripture witnesseth concerning him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:8
verses.text: But if, by his fall what was delivered through him were blotted out, it would be judged that he had himself delivered these precepts, and not that they were delivered through him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:9
verses.text: The mercy of God, therefore, and His Spirit, excellently wrought that whatever of good was declared through Solomon, might be attributed unto God; and the man's sin, unto the man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:10
verses.text: What marvel that Solomon fell among God's people? Did not Adam fall in Paradise? Did not an angel fall from heaven, and become the devil? We are thereby taught, that no hope must be placed in any among men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:11
verses.text: The name of Solomon is interpreted to mean peacemaker: now Christ is the True Peacemaker, of whom the Apostle saith, "He is our Peace, who hath made both one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:12
verses.text: Since, therefore, He is the true Solomon; for that Solomon was the figure of this Peace maker, when he built the temple; that thou mayest not think he who built the house unto God was the true Solomon, Scripture showing unto thee another Solomon, thus commences this Psalm: "Except the Lord build the house, their labour is but lost that build it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:13
verses.text: The Lord, therefore, buildeth the house, the Lord Jesus Christ buildeth His own house.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:14
verses.text: Many toil in building: but, except He build, "their labour is but lost that build it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:15
verses.text: Who are they who toil in building it? All who preach the word of God in the Church, the ministers of God's mysteries.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:16
verses.text: We are all running, we are all toiling, we are all building now; and before us others have run, toiled, and built: but "except the Lord build, their labour is but lost".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:17
verses.text: Thus the Apostles seeing some fall bewailed these men, in that they had laboured in vain for them We, therefore, speak without, He buildeth within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:18
verses.text: We can observe with what attention ye hear us; He alone who knoweth your thoughts, knoweth what ye think.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:19
verses.text: He Himself buildeth, He Himself admonisheth, He Himself openeth the understanding, He Himself kindleth your understanding unto faith; nevertheless, we also toil like workmen; but, "except the Lord build," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:20
verses.text: But that which is the house of God is also a city.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:21
verses.text: For the house of God is the people of God; for the house of God is the temple of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:22
verses.text: This is Jerusalem: she hath guards: as she hath builders, labouring at her building up, so also hath she guards.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:23
verses.text: To this guardianship these words of the Apostle relate: "I fear, lest by any means your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity which is in Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:24
verses.text: He was guarding the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:25
verses.text: He kept watch, to the utmost of his power, over those over whom he was set.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:26
verses.text: The Bishops also do this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:27
verses.text: For a higher place was for this reason given the Bishops, that they might be themselves the superintendents and as it were the guardians of the people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:28
verses.text: For the Greek word Episcopus, and the vernacular Superintendent, are the same; for the Bishop superintends, in that he looks over.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:29
verses.text: As a higher place is assigned to the vinedresser in the charge of the vineyard, so also to the Bishops a more exalted station is alloted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:30
verses.text: And a perilous account is rendered of this high station, except we stand here with a heart that causeth us to stand beneath your feet in humility, and pray for you, that He who knoweth your minds may be Himself your keeper.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:31
verses.text: Since we can see you both coming in and going out; but we are so unable to see what are the thoughts of your hearts, that we cannot even see what ye do in your houses.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:32
verses.text: How then can we guard you? As men: as far as we are able, as far as we have received power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:33
verses.text: And because we guard you like men, and cannot guard you perfectly, shall ye therefore remain without a keeper? Far be it! For where is He of whom it is said, "Except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:34
verses.text: We are watchful on our guard, but vain in our watchfulness, except He who seeth your thoughts guard you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:35
verses.text: He keepeth guard while ye are awake, He keepeth guard also whilst ye are asleep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:36
verses.text: For He hath once slept on the Cross, and hath risen again; He no longer sleepeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:37
verses.text: Be ye Israel: for "the Keeper of Israel neither sleepeth nor slumbereth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:38
verses.text: Yea, brethren, if we wish to be kept beneath the shadow of God's wings, let us be Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:39
verses.text: For we guard you in our office of stewards; but we wish to be guarded together with you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:40
verses.text: We are as it were shepherds unto you; but beneath that Shepherd we are fellow-sheep with you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:41
verses.text: We are as it were your teachers from this station; but beneath Him, the One Master, we are schoolfellows with you in this school.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:42
verses.text: If we wish to be guarded by Him who was humbled for our sakes, and who was exalted to keep us, let us be humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:43
verses.text: Let no one assume anything unto himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:44
verses.text: No man hath any good, except he hath received it from Him who alone is good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:45
verses.text: But he who chooseth to arrogate wisdom unto himself, is a fool.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:46
verses.text: Let him be humble, that wisdom may come, and may enlighten him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:47
verses.text: But if, before wisdom cometh unto him, he imagine that he is wise; he riseth before light, and walketh in darkness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:48
verses.text: What doth he hear in this Psalm? "It is but lost labour that ye haste to rise up before dawn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:49
verses.text: What meaneth this? If ye arise before light ariseth, ye must needs lose your labour, because ye will be in the dark.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:50
verses.text: Our light, Christ, hath arisen; it is good for thee to rise after Christ, not to rise before Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:51
verses.text: Who rise before Christ? They who choose to prefer themselves to Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:52
verses.text: And who are they who wish to prefer themselves to Christ? They who wish to be exalted here, where He was humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:53
verses.text: Let them, therefore, be humble here, if they wish to be exalted there, where Christ is exalted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:54
verses.text: The Lord recalled the sons of Zebedee to humility, and said unto them, "Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of?" I came to be humble: and are ye wishing to be exalted before Me? The way I go, do ye follow, He saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:55
verses.text: For if ye choose to go this way where I do not go, your labour is lost, in rising before dawn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:56
verses.text: Peter too had risen before the light, when he wished to give the Lord advice, deterring Him from suffering for us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:57
verses.text: But what did our Lord do? He caused him to rise after the Light: "Get thee behind Me, Satan".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:58
verses.text: He was Satan, because he wished to rise before Light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:59
verses.text: "Get thee behind Me:" that I may precede, thou mayest follow: where I go, there thou mayest go; and mayest not wish to lead Me, where thou wouldest go.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:60
verses.text: And as if thou shouldest say, When shall we rise? we are ordered now to sit: when will be our rising? When the Lord's was.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:61
verses.text: Look unto Him, who went before thee: for if thou heedest not Him, "it is lost labour for thee to rise before dawn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:62
verses.text: When was He raised? When He had died.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:63
verses.text: Hope therefore for thine uplifting after thy death: have hope in the resurrection of the dead, because He rose again and ascended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:64
verses.text: But where did He sleep? On the Cross.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:65
verses.text: When He slept on the Cross, He bore a sign, yea, He fulfilled what had been signified in Adam: for when Adam was asleep, a rib was drawn from him and Eve was created; so also while the Lord slept on the Cross, His side was transfixed with a spear, and the Sacraments flowed forth, whence the Church was born.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:66
verses.text: For the Church the Lord's Bride was created from His side, as Eve was created from the side of Adam.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:67
verses.text: But as she was made from his side no otherwise than while sleeping, so the Church was created from His side no otherwise than while dying.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:68
verses.text: If therefore He rose not from the dead  save when He had died, dost thou hope for exaltation save after this life? But that this Psalm might teach thee, in case thou shouldest ask, When shall I rise? perhaps before I have sat down? he addeth, "When He hath given His beloved sleep".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:69
verses.text: God giveth this when His beloved have fallen asleep; then His beloved, that is, Christ's, shall rise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:70
verses.text: For all indeed shall rise, but not as His beloved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:71
verses.text: There is a resurrection of all the dead; but what saith the Apostle? "We shall all rise, but we shall not all be changed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:72
verses.text: They rise unto punishment: we rise as our Lord rose, that we may follow our Head, if we are members of Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:73
verses.text: Hope for such a resurrection; and for the sake of this be a Christian, not for the sake of this world's happiness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:74
verses.text: For if thou wish to be a Christian for the sake of this world's happiness, since He thy Light sought not worldly happiness; thou art wishing to rise before the light; thou must needs continue in darkness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:75
verses.text: Be changed, follow thy Light; rise where  He rose again: first sit down, and thus rise, "when He giveth His beloved sleep".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:76
verses.text: As if thou shouldest ask again, who are the beloved? "Lo, children, the reward of the fruit of the womb, are an heritage of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:77
verses.text: Since he saith, "fruit of the womb," these children have been born in travail.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:78
verses.text: There is a certain woman, in whom what was said unto Eve, "in sorrow shalt thou bring forth children," is shown after a spiritual manner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:79
verses.text: The Church beareth children, the Bride of Christ; and if she beareth them, she travaileth of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:80
verses.text: In figure of her, Eve was called also "the Mother of all living".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:81
verses.text: He who said, "My little children, of whom I travail in birth again, until Christ be formed in you," was amongst the members of her who travaileth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:82
verses.text: But she travailed not in vain, nor brought forth in vain: there will be a holy seed at the resurrection of the dead: the righteous who are at present scattered over the whole world shall abound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:83
verses.text: The Church groaneth for them, the Church travaileth of them; but in that resurrection of the dead, the offspring of the Church shall appear, pain and groaning shall pass away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:84
verses.text: "Like as the arrows in the hand of the mighty one, even so are the children of those that are shot out".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:85
verses.text: Whence hath sprung this heritage, brethren? Whence hath sprung so numerous a heritage? Some have been shot out from the Lord's hand, as arrows, and have gone far, and have filled the whole earth, whence the Saints spring.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:86
verses.text: For this is the heritage whereof it is said, "Desire of Me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:87
verses.text: And how doth this possession extend and increase unto the world's uttermost parts? Because, "like as the arrows in the hand of the mighty one," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:88
verses.text: Arrows are shot forth from the bow, and the stronger the arm which hath sent it forth, the farther flieth the arrow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:89
verses.text: But what is stronger than the darting of the Lord? From His bow He sendeth forth His Apostles: there could not be a spot left where an arrow shot by so strong an arm would not reach; it hath reached unto the uttermost parts of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:90
verses.text: The reason it went no farther was, that there were no more of the human race beyond.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:91
verses.text: For He hath such strength, that even if there were a spot beyond, whither the arrow could fly, He would dart the arrow thither.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:92
verses.text: Such are the children of those who are shot forth as they that are shot forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:93
verses.text: Perhaps the Apostles themselves are styled the sons of those who have been shaken out, the sons of the Prophets.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:94
verses.text: For the Prophets comprised closed and covered mysteries: they were shaken, that they might come forth thence manifestly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:95
verses.text: Except the prophecy involved were sifted with diligence, would the concealed meanings come forth unto us? All these meanings were therefore closed before the Lord's advent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:96
verses.text: The Lord came, and shook out these hidden meanings, and they were made manifest; the Prophets were shaken out, and the Apostles were born.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:97
verses.text: Since then they were born of the Prophets who had been shaken out, the Apostles are sons of those that were shaken out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:98
verses.text: They, placed as the arrows in the hand of the giant, have reached the uttermost parts of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:99
verses.text: The Apostles the sons of the Prophets have been like as the arrows in the hand of a mighty one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:100
verses.text: If He is mighty, He hath shaken them out with a mighty hand; if He hath shaken them out with a mighty hand, they whom He hath shaken forth have arrived even at the uttermost parts of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:101
verses.text: "Blessed is the man who hath filled his desire from them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:102
verses.text: Well, my brethren, who filleth his desire from them? Who loveth not the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:103
verses.text: He who is filled with the desire of the world, hath no room for that to enter which they have preached.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:104
verses.text: Pour forth what thou carriest, and become fit for that which thou hast not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:105
verses.text: That is, thou desirest riches: thou canst not fill thy desire from them: thou desirest honours upon earth, thou desirest those things which God hath given even unto beasts of burden, that is, temporal pleasure, bodily health, and the like; thou wilt not fulfil thy desire from them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:106
verses.text: "He shall not be ashamed, when he speaketh with his enemies in the gate".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:107
verses.text: Brethren, let us speak in the gate, that is, let all know what we speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:108
verses.text: For he who chooseth not to speak in the gate, wisheth what he speaketh to be hidden, and perhaps wisheth it to be hidden for this reason, that it is evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:109
verses.text: If he be confident, let him speak in the gate; as it is said of Wisdom, "She crieth at the gates, at the entry of the city".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:110
verses.text: As long as they hold unto righteousness in innocency, they shall not be ashamed: this is to preach at the gate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:111
verses.text: And who is he who preacheth at the gate? He who preacheth in Christ; because Christ is the gate whereby we enter into that cityThey, therefore, who speak against Christ, are without the gate; because they seek their own honours, not those of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:112
verses.text: But he who preacheth in the gate, seeketh Christ's honour, not his own: and, therefore, he who preacheth in the gate, saith, Trust not in me; for ye will not enter through me, but through the gate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 127:113
verses.text: While they who wish men to trust in themselves, wish them not to enter through the gate: it is no marvel if the gate be closed against them, and if they vainly knock for it to be opened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXVIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:2
verses.text: Felix the Martyr, truly Felix, i-e: "Happy" both in his name and his crown, whose birthday this is, despised the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:3
verses.text: Was he, because he feared the Lord, thence happy, thence blessed, because his wife was as a fruitful vine upon the earth, and his children stood around his table? All these blessings he hath perfectly, but in the Body of Him who is here described; and, because he understood them in this sense, he scorned things present, that he might receive things future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:4
verses.text: Ye are aware, brethren, that he suffered not the death that other martyrs suffered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:5
verses.text: For he confessed, and was set aside for torments; on another day his body was discovered lifeless.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:6
verses.text: They had closed the prison to his body, not to his spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:7
verses.text: The executioners found him gone; when they were preparing to torture, they spent their rage for nought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:8
verses.text: He was lying dead, without sense to them, that he might not be tortured; with sense with God, that he might be crowned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:9
verses.text: Whence was he also happy, brethren, not only in name, but in the reward of everlasting life, if he loved these things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:10
verses.text: "Blessed are all they that fear the Lord, and walk in His ways".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:11
verses.text: He speaketh to many; but since these many are one in Christ, in the next words he speaketh in the singular: "For thou shalt eat the labours of thy fruits".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:12
verses.text: When I speak of Christians in the plural, I understand one in the One Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:13
verses.text: Ye are therefore many, and ye are one; we are many, and we are one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:14
verses.text: How are we many, and yet one? Because we cling unto Him whose members we are; and since our Head is in heaven, that His members may follow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:15
verses.text: Let us therefore so hear this Psalm, as considering it to be spoken of Christ: and all of us who cling unto the Body of Christ, and have been made members of Christ, walk in the ways of the Lord; and let us fear the Lord with a chaste fear, with a fear that abideth for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:16
verses.text: "Thou shalt eat the labours of thy fruits".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:17
verses.text: And ye, O thou, ye many who are One, "Thou shalt eat of the labours of thy fruits".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:18
verses.text: He seemeth to speak perversely to those who understand not: for he should have said, thou shalt eat the fruit of thy labours.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:19
verses.text: For many eat the fruit of their labours.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:20
verses.text: They labour in the vineyard; they eat not the toil itself; but what ariseth from their labour they eat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:21
verses.text: They labour about trees that bear fruit: who would eat labours? But the fruit of these labours, the produce of these trees; it is this that delighteth the husbandman.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:22
verses.text: What meaneth, "Thou shalt eat the labours of thy fruits"? At present we have toils: the fruits will come afterwards.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:23
verses.text: But since their labours themselves are not without joy, on account of the hope whereof we have a little before spoken, "Rejoicing in hope, patient in tribulation;"  at present those very labours delight us, and make us joyful in hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:24
verses.text: If therefore our toil has been what could be eaten, and could also delight us; what will be the fruit of our labour when eaten? "They who went weeping on their way, scattering their seed," did eat their labours; with how much greater pleasure will they eat the fruits of their labours, who "shall come again with joy, bearing their sheaves with them"?"Blessed art thou, and well shall it be with thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:25
verses.text: "Blessed art thou," is of the present: "well shall it be with thee," is of the future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:26
verses.text: When thou eatest the labours of thy fruits, "blessed art thou;" when thou hast reached the fruit of thy labours, "well shall it be with thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:27
verses.text: What hath he said? For if it be well with thee, thou wilt be happy: and if thou wilt be happy, thou wilt also have all well with thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:28
verses.text: But there is a difference between hope and attainment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:29
verses.text: If hope be so sweet, how much sweeter will reality be?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:30
verses.text: Let us now come to the words, "Thy wife" : it is said unto Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:31
verses.text: His wife, therefore, is the Church: His Church, His wife, we ourselves are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:32
verses.text: "As a fruitful vineyard".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:33
verses.text: But in whom is the vineyard fruitful? For we see many barren ones entering those walls; we see that many intemperate, usurious persons, slave dealers, enter these walls, and such as resort to fortune-tellers, go to enchanters and enchantresses when they have a headache.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:34
verses.text: Is this the fruitfulness of the vine? Is this the fecundity of the wife? It is not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:35
verses.text: These are thorns, but the vineyard is not everywhere thorny.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:36
verses.text: It hath a certain fruitfulness, and is a fruitful vine; but in whom? "Upon the sides of thy house".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:37
verses.text: Not all are called the sides of the house.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:38
verses.text: For I ask what are the sides.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:39
verses.text: What shall I say? Are they walls, strong stones, as it were? If he were speaking of this bodily tenement, we should perhaps understand this by sides.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:40
verses.text: We mean by the sides of the house, those who cling unto Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:41
verses.text: "Thy children".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:42
verses.text: The wife and the children are the same.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:43
verses.text: In these carnal marriages and wedlocks, the wife is one, the children other: in the Church, she who is the wife, is the children also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:44
verses.text: For the Apostles belonged to the Church, and were among the members of the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:45
verses.text: They were therefore in His wife, and were His wife according to their own portion which they held in His members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:46
verses.text: Why then is it said concerning them, "When the Bridegroom shall be taken from them, then shall the children of the Bridegroom fast"? She who is the wife, then, is the children also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:47
verses.text: I speak a wonderful thing, my brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:48
verses.text: In the words of the Lord, we find the Church to be both His brethren, and His sisters, and His motherFor Mary was among the sides of His House, and His relatives coming of the kindred of the Virgin Mary, who believed on Him, were among the sides of His House; not in respect of their carnal consanguinity, but inasmuch as they heard the Word of God, and obeyed it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:49
verses.text: He added; "For whosoever shall do the will of My Father which is in heaven, the same is My brother, and sister, and mother".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:50
verses.text: "Brother," perhaps, on account of the male sex whom the Church hath: "sister," on account of the women whom Christ hath here in His members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:51
verses.text: How "mother," save that Christ Himself is in those Christians, whom the Church daily bringeth forth Christians through baptism? In those therefore in whom thou understandest the wife, in them thou understandest the mother, in them the children.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:52
verses.text: Such children ought therefore to be "around" the Lord's "table, like olive-branches".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:53
verses.text: A complete Vine it is, a great bliss: who would now refuse to be there? When thou seest any blasphemer have a wife, children, grandchildren, and thyself perchance without them, envy them not; discern that the promise hath been fulfilled in thee also, but spiritually.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:54
verses.text: If therefore we have, why have we? Because we fear the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:55
verses.text: "Lo, thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:56
verses.text: He is the man, who is also the men; and the men are one man; because many are one, because Christ is One.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:57
verses.text: "The Lord from out of Sion bless thee: and mayest thou see thee good things that are of Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:58
verses.text: Even to the birds was it said, "Be fruitful and multiply".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:59
verses.text: Dost thou wish to hold as a great blessing what was given unto birds? Who can be ignorant, that it was given indeed by the voice of God? But use these goods, if thou receive them; and rather think how thou mayest nourish those who have been born, than that others may be born.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:60
verses.text: For it is not happiness to have children, but to have good ones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:61
verses.text: Labour in the task of nourishing them, if they be born; but if they be not born, give thanks unto God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:62
verses.text: Thy children are infants: thou dost caress the infants: the infants caress thee: do they abide thus? But thou wishest they may grow, thou wishest that their age may increase.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:63
verses.text: But consider that when one age cometh, another dieth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:64
verses.text: When boyhood cometh, infancy dieth; when youth cometh, boyhood dieth: when manhood cometh, youth dieth; when old age cometh, manhood dieth: when death cometh, all age dieth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:65
verses.text: As many successions of ages as thou wishest for, so many deaths of ages dost thou wish for.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:66
verses.text: These things therefore "are" not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:67
verses.text: Finally, are children born unto thee to share life with thee on earth, or rather to shut thee out and to succeed thee? Rejoicest thou in those born to exclude thee? Boys when born speak somewhat like this to their parents: "Now then, begin to think of removing hence, let us too play our parts on the stage".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:68
verses.text: For the whole life of temptation in the human race is a stage play; for it is said, "Every man living is altogether vanity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:69
verses.text: Nevertheless, if we rejoice in children who will succeed us; how much must we rejoice in children with whom we shall remain, and in that Father for whom we are born, who will not die, but that we may evermore live with Him? These are the good things of Jerusalem: for they "are".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:70
verses.text: And how long shall I see the good things of Jerusalem? "All thy life long".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:71
verses.text: If thy life be for ever, thou wilt see the good things of Jerusalem for evermore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:72
verses.text: For, "if in this life only," saith the Apostle, "we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:73
verses.text: For what reason were the Martyrs condemned to beasts? What is that good? Can it be declared? by what means, or what tongue can tell it? or what ears can hear it? That indeed, "Neither ear hath heard, nor hath it entered into man's heart:" only let us love, only let us grow in grace: ye see, then, that battles are not wanting, and that we fight with our lusts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:74
verses.text: We fight outwardly with unbelieving and disobedient men; we fight inwardly with carnal suggestions and perturbations: we everywhere as yet fight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:75
verses.text: What sort of peace then is this? One from Jerusalem, for Jerusalem is interpreted, A vision of Peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:76
verses.text: Thus then "mayest thou see the good things that are of Jerusalem," and that, "all thy life long—and mayest thou see," not only thy children, but, "thy children's children".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:77
verses.text: What meaneth, Thy children? Thy works which thou here dost.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:78
verses.text: Who are thy children's children? The fruits of thy works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:79
verses.text: Thou givest alms: these are thy children: for the sake of thine alms thou receivest everlasting life, these are thy children's children.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 128:80
verses.text: "Mayest thou see thy children's children;" and there shall be "peace upon Israel" , the last words of the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXIX.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:2
verses.text: The Psalm which we have sung is short: but as it is written in the Gospel of Zacchaeus that he was "little of stature," but mighty in works; as it is written of that widow who cast two mites into the treasury, little was the money, but great was her charity; thus also this Psalm, if thou count the words, is short; if thou weigh the sentiments, is great.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:3
verses.text: Let the Spirit of God speak, let It speak to us, let It sing to us; whether we wish or wish not to dance, let It sing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:4
verses.text: For as he who danceth, moveth his limbs to the time; so they who dance according to the commandment of God, in their works obey the sound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:5
verses.text: What therefore saith the Lord in the Gospel to those who refuse to do this? "We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced: we have mourned unto you, and ye have not lamented".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:6
verses.text: Let Him therefore sing; we trust in God's mercy, for there will be those by whom He consoleth us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:7
verses.text: For they who are obstinate, continuing in wickedness, al though they hear the Word of God, by their offences daily disturb the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:8
verses.text: Of such this Psalm speaketh; for thus it beginneth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:9
verses.text: "Many a time have they fought against me from my youth up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:10
verses.text: The Church speaketh of those whom She endureth: and as if it were asked, "Is it now?" The Church is of ancient birth: since saints have been so called, the Church hath been on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:11
verses.text: At one time the Church was in Abel only, and he was fought against by his wicked and lost brother Cain At one time the Church was in Enoch alone: and he was translated from the unrighteous At one time the Church was in the house of Noah alone, and endured all who perished by the flood, and the ark alone swam upon the waves, and escaped to shore At one time the Church was in Abraham alone, and we know what he endured from the wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:12
verses.text: The Church was in his brother's son, Lot, alone, and in his house, in Sodom, and he endured the iniquities and perversities of Sodom, until God freed him from amidst them The Church also began to exist in the people of Israel: She endured Pharaoh and the Egyptians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:13
verses.text: The number of the saints began to be also in the Church, that is, in the people of Israel; Moses and the rest of the saints endured the wicked Jews, the people of Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:14
verses.text: We come unto our Lord Jesus Christ: the Gospel was preached in the PsalmsFor this reason, lest the Church wonder now, or lest any one wonder in the Church, who wisheth to be a good member of the Church, let him hear the Church herself his Mother saying to him, Marvel not at these things, my son: "Many a time have they fought against me from my youth up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:15
verses.text: "Now may Israel say".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:16
verses.text: She now seemeth to be speaking of herself: for she seemed not to have commenced herself, but to have answered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:17
verses.text: But to whom hath she replied? To them that think and say, How great evils do we endure, how great are the scandals that every day thicken, as the wicked enter into the Church, and we have to endure them? But let the Church reply through some, that is, through the voice of the stronger, let her reply to the complaints of the weak, and let the stable confirm the unstable, and the full-grown the infant, and let the Church say, "Many a time have they vexed me from my youth up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:18
verses.text: Let the Church say this: let her not fear it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:19
verses.text: For what is the meaning of this addition, "From my youth up," after the words, "Many a time have they fought against me"? At present the old age of the Church is assailed: but let her not fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:20
verses.text: Hath she then failed to arrive at old age, because they have not ceased to fight against her from her youth up? have they been able to blot her out? Let Israel comfort herself, let the Church console herself with past examples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:21
verses.text: Why have they fought against me? "For they could not prevail against me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:22
verses.text: "Upon my back have sinners built; they have done their iniquity afar off".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:23
verses.text: Why have they fought against me? Because "they could not prevail upon me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:24
verses.text: What is this? They could not build upon me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:25
verses.text: I consented not with them unto sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:26
verses.text: For every wicked man persecuteth the good on this account, because the good man consenteth not with him to evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:27
verses.text: Suppose he do some evil, and the Bishop censure him not, the Bishop is a good man: suppose the Bishop censure him, the Bishop is a bad man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:28
verses.text: Suppose he carry off anything, let the man robbed be silent, he is a good man: let him only speak and rebuke, even though he doth not reclaim his goods, he is everything bad.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:29
verses.text: He is bad then who blameth the robber, and he is good who robbeth!Heed not that such an one speaketh to thee: it is a wicked man through whom It speaketh to thee; but the word of God, that speaketh to thee, is not wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:30
verses.text: Accuse God: accuse Him, if thou canst!.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:31
verses.text: Thou accusest a man of avarice, and he accuseth God on the ground that He made gold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:32
verses.text: Be not covetous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:33
verses.text: And God, thou repliest, should not make gold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:34
verses.text: This now remaineth, because thou canst not restrain thine evil deeds, thou accusest the good works of God: the Creator and Architect of the world displeaseth thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:35
verses.text: He ought not to make the sun either; for many contend concerning the lights of their windows, and drag each other before courts of law.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:36
verses.text: O if we could restrain our vices! for all things are good, because a good God made all things: and His works praise Him, when their goodness is considered by him who hath the spirit of considering them, the spirit of piety and wisdom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:37
verses.text: Lend not money at interest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:38
verses.text: Thou accusest Scripture which saith, "He that hath not given his money upon usury".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:39
verses.text: I wrote not this: it went not forth first from my mouth: hear God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:40
verses.text: He replieth: let not the clergy lend upon usury.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:41
verses.text: Perchance he who speaketh to thee, lendeth not at interest: but if he do so lend, suppose that he doth so lend; doth He who speaketh through him lend at interest? If he doth what he enjoineth thee, and thou dost it not; thou wilt go into the flame, he into the kingdom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:42
verses.text: If he doth not what he enjoineth thee, and equally with thee doth evil deeds, and preaches duties which he doth not; ye will both equally go into the flames.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:43
verses.text: The hay will burn; but "the word of the Lord abideth for evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:44
verses.text: "The righteous Lord shall hew the necks of the sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:45
verses.text: Which of us doth not fix his eyes upon the earth, like the Publican, and say, "Lord, be merciful unto me a sinner"? If therefore all are sinners, and none is found without sin; all must fear the sword that hangs above their neck, because "the righteous Lord shall hew the necks of the sinners".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:46
verses.text: I do not imagine, my brethren, of all sinners; but in the member which He striketh, He marks what sinners He striketh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:47
verses.text: For it is not said, The righteous Lord will hew the hands of the sinners; or their feet; but because proud sinners were meant to be understood, and all proud men carry lofty necks, and not only do evil deeds, but even refuse to acknowledge them to be such, and when they are rebuked, justify themselves:as it is written in Job (he was speaking of an ungodly sinner), "he runneth against God, even upon his neck, upon the thick bosses of his bucklers;" so he here nameth the neck, because it is thus thou exaltest thyself, and dost not fix thine eyes upon the ground, and beat thy breast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:48
verses.text: Thou shouldest cry unto Him, as it is cried in another Psalm, "I said, Lord, be merciful unto me, for I have sinned against Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:49
verses.text: Since thou dost not choose to say this, but justifiest thy deeds against the Word of God; what followeth in Scripture cometh upon thee: the righteous Lord shall hew the necks of sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:50
verses.text: "Let them be confounded and turned backward, as many as have evil will at Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:51
verses.text: They who hate Sion, hate the Church: Sion is the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:52
verses.text: And they who hypocritically enter into the Church, hate the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:53
verses.text: They who refuse to keep the Word of God, hate the Church: "Upon my back have they built:" what will the Church do, save endure the burden even unto the end?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:54
verses.text: But what saith he of them? The next words are, "Let them be even as the grass of the house tops: that withereth before it be plucked up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:55
verses.text: The grass of the house tops is that which groweth on house tops, on a tiled roof: it is seen on high, and hath not a root.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:56
verses.text: How much better would it be if it grew lower, and how much more joyfully would it bloom? As it is, it riseth higher to a quicker withering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:57
verses.text: It hath not yet been plucked up, yet hath it withered: not yet have they received sentence from the judgment of God, and already they have not the sap of bloom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:58
verses.text: Observe their works, and see that they have withered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:59
verses.text: The reapers will come, but they fill not their sheaves from these.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:60
verses.text: For the reapers will come, and will gather the wheat into the barn, and will bind the tares together, and cast them into the fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:61
verses.text: Thus also is the grass of the house tops cleared off, and whatever is plucked from it, is thrown into the fire; because it had withered even before it was plucked up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:62
verses.text: The reaper filleth not his hands thence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:63
verses.text: His next words are, "Whereof the reaper filleth not his hand; neither he that bindeth up the sheaves his bosom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:64
verses.text: And, "the reapers are the angels," the Lord saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:65
verses.text: "So that they who go by say not so much as, The blessing of the Lord be upon you: we have blessed you in the name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:66
verses.text: For ye know, brethren, when men pass by others at work, it is customary to address them, "The blessing of the Lord be upon you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:67
verses.text: And this was especially the custom in the Jewish nation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:68
verses.text: No one passed by and saw any one doing any work in the field, or in the vineyard, or in harvest, or anything of the sort; it was not lawful to pass by without a blessing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:69
verses.text: Who are the passers by? They who have already passed hence to their country through this road, that is, through this life: the Apostles were passers by in this life, the Prophets were passers by.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:70
verses.text: Whom did the Prophets and Apostles bless? Those in whom they saw the root of charity? But those whom they found lifted on high on their house tops, and proud in the bosses of their bucklers, they declared against these what they were doomed to become, but they gave them no blessing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:71
verses.text: Ye therefore who read in the Scriptures, find all those wicked men whom the Church beareth, who are declared cursed, pertain unto Antichrist, pertain unto the devil, pertain to the chaff, pertain to the tares.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 129:72
verses.text: But they who say, None save God sanctifieth, nor is any man good save by the gift of God; they bless in the name of the Lord, not in their own name: because they are the friends of the bridegroom, they refuse to be adulterers of the bride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXX.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:2
verses.text: "Out of the deep have I called unto Thee, O Lord: Lord, hear my voice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:3
verses.text: Jonas cried from the deep; from the whale's belly He was not only beneath the waves, but also in the entrails of the beast; nevertheless, those waves and that body prevented not his prayer from reaching God, and the beast's belly could not contain the voice of his prayer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:4
verses.text: It penetrated all things, it burst through all things, it reached the ears of God: if indeed we ought to say that, bursting through all things, it reached the ears of God, since the ears of God were in the heart of him who prayed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:5
verses.text: For where hath not he God present, whose voice is faithful? Nevertheless, we also ought to understand from what deep we cry unto the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:6
verses.text: For this mortal life is our deep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:7
verses.text: Whoever hath understood himself to be in the deep, crieth out, groaneth, sigheth, until he be delivered from the deep, and come unto Him who sitteth above all the deeps.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:8
verses.text: For they are very deep in the deep, who do not even cry from the deep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:9
verses.text: The Scripture saith, "When the wicked hath reached the depth of evils, he despiseth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:10
verses.text: Now consider, brethren, what sort of deep that is, where God is despised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:11
verses.text: When each man seeth himself overwhelmed with daily sins, pressed down by heaps and weights, so to speak, of iniquities: if it be said unto him, Pray unto God, he laughs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:12
verses.text: In what manner? He first saith, If crimes were displeasing unto God, should I live? If God regarded human affairs, considering the great crimes which I have committed, should I not only live, but be prosperous? For this is wont to happen to those who are far in the deep, and are prosperous in their iniquities: and they are the more plunged in the deep, in proportion as they seem to be more happy; for a deceitful happiness is itself a greater unhappiness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:13
verses.text: "Lord, hear my voice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:14
verses.text: O let Thine ears consider well the voice of my complaint".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:15
verses.text: Whence doth he cry? From the deep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:16
verses.text: Who is it then who crieth? A sinner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:17
verses.text: And with what hope doth he cry? Because He who came to absolve from sins, gave hope even to the sinner down in the deep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:18
verses.text: What therefore followeth after these words: "If Thou, Lord, wilt be extreme to mark what is amiss, O Lord, who may abide it?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:19
verses.text: So, he hath disclosed from what deep he cried out.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:20
verses.text: For he crieth beneath the weights and billows of his iniquities.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:21
verses.text: He said not, I may not abide it: but, "who may abide it?" For he saw that nigh the whole of human life on every side was ever bayed at by its sins, that all consciences were accused by their thoughts, that a clean heart trusting in its own righteousness could not be found.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:22
verses.text: But wherefore is there hope? "For there is propitiation with Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:23
verses.text: And what is this propitiation, except sacrifice? And what is sacrifice, save that which hath been offered for us? The pouring forth of innocent blood blotted out all the sins of the guilty: so great a price paid down redeemed all captives from the hand of the enemy who captured them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:24
verses.text: "With Thee," then, "there is propitiation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:25
verses.text: For if there were not mercy with Thee, if Thou chosest to be Judge only, and didst refuse to be merciful, Thou wouldest mark all our iniquities, and search after them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:26
verses.text: Who could abide this? Who could stand before Thee, and say, I am innocent? Who could stand in Thy judgment? There is therefore one hope: "for the sake of Thy law have I borne Thee, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:27
verses.text: What law? That which made men guilty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:28
verses.text: For a "law, holy, just, and good,"  was given to the Jews; but its effect was to make them guilty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:29
verses.text: A law was not given that could give life, but which might show his sins to the sinner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:30
verses.text: For the sinner had forgotten himself, and saw not himself; the law was given him, that he might see himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:31
verses.text: The law made him guilty, the Lawgiver freed him: for the Lawgiver is the Supreme PowerThere is therefore a law of the mercy of God, a law of the propitiation of God The one was a law of fear, the other is a law of love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:32
verses.text: The law of love giveth forgiveness to sins, blotteth out the past, warneth concerning the future; forsaketh not its companion by the way, becometh a companion to him whom it leadeth on the way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:33
verses.text: But it is needful to agree with the adversary, whilst thou art with him in the way For the Word of God is thine adversary, as long as thou dost not agree with it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:34
verses.text: But thou agreest, when it has begun to be thy delight to do what God's Word commandeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:35
verses.text: Then he who was thine adversary becometh thy friend: so, when the way is finished, there will be none to deliver thee to the Judge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:36
verses.text: Therefore, "For the sake of Thy law I have waited for Thee, O Lord," because thou hast condescended to bring in a law of mercy, to forgive me all my sins, to give me for the future warnings that I may not offend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:37
verses.text: "For the sake," therefore, "of" this "law I have waited for Thee, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:38
verses.text: I have waited until Thou mayest come and free me from all need, for in my very need Thou hast not forsaken the law of mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:39
verses.text: "My soul hath waited for Thy word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:40
verses.text: We therefore trust without fear on the word of Him who cannot deceive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:41
verses.text: "My soul hath trusted in the Lord, from the morning watch even unto night".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:42
verses.text: This morning watch is the end of night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:43
verses.text: We must therefore understand it so that we may not suppose we are to trust in the Lord for one day only.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:44
verses.text: What do you conceive to be the sense, then, brethren? The words mean this: that the Lord, through whom our sins have been remitted, arose from the dead at the morning watch, so that we may hope that what went before in the Lord will take place in us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:45
verses.text: For our sins have been already forgiven: but we have not yet risen again: if we have not risen again, not as yet hath that taken place in us which went before in our Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:46
verses.text: What went before in our Head? Because the flesh of that Head rose again; did the Spirit of that Head die? What had died in Him, rose again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:47
verses.text: Now He arose on the third day; and the Lord as it were thus speaketh to us: What ye have seen in Me, hope for in yourselves; that is, because I have risen from the dead, ye also shall rise again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:48
verses.text: But there are who say, Behold, the Lord hath risen again; but must I hope on that account that I also may rise again? Certainly, on that account: for the Lord rose again in that which He assumed from thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:49
verses.text: For He would not rise again, save He had died; and He could not have died, except He bore the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:50
verses.text: What did the Lord assume from thee? The flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:51
