verses.text: What was He that came Himself? The Word of God, who was before all things, through whom all things were made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:52
verses.text: But that He might receive something from thee, "The Word became flesh, and dwelt among us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:53
verses.text: He received from thee, what He might offer for thee; as the priest receiveth from thee, what he may offer for thee, when thou wishest to appease God for thy sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:54
verses.text: It hath already been done, it hath been done thus.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:55
verses.text: Our Priest received from us what He might offer for us: for He received flesh from us, in the flesh itself He was made a victim, He was made a holocaust, He was made a sacrifice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:56
verses.text: In the Passion He was made a sacrifice; in the Resurrection He renewed that which was slain, and offered it as His first-fruits unto God, and saith unto thee, All that is thine is now consecrated: since such first-fruits have been offered unto God from thee; hope therefore that that will take place in thyself which went before in thy first-fruits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:57
verses.text: Since He then rose with the morning watch, our soul began to hope from hence: and how far? "Even unto night;" until we die; for all our carnal death is as it were sleep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:58
verses.text: And he returns to this, "From the morning watch let Israel hope in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:59
verses.text: Not only "let Israel hope," but "from the morning watch let Israel hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:60
verses.text: Do I then blame the hope of the world, when it is placed in the Lord? No; but there is another hope belonging to Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:61
verses.text: Let not Israel hope for riches as his highest good, not for health of body, not for abundance of earthly things: he will indeed have to suffer tribulation here, if it should be his lot to suffer any troubles for the sake of the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:62
verses.text: "For with the Lord there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:63
verses.text: Admirable! This could not have been better said in its own place, on account of the words, "From the morning watch".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:64
verses.text: Wherefore? Because the Lord rose again from the morning watch; and the body ought to hope for that which went before in the Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:65
verses.text: But, lest this thought should be suggested: The Head might rise again, because It was not weighed down with sins, there was no sin in Him; what shall we do? Shall we hope for such a resurrection, as went before in the Lord, whilst we are weighed down by our sins? But see what followeth: "And He shall redeem Israel from all his sins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:66
verses.text: Though therefore he was weighed down with his sins, the mercy of God is present to him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:67
verses.text: For this reason, He went before without sin, that He may blot out the sins of those that follow Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 130:68
verses.text: Trust not in yourselves, but trust from the morning watch.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXXI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:2
verses.text: In this Psalm, the humility of one that is a servant of God and faithful is commended unto us, by whose voice it is sung; which is the whole body of Christ For we have often warned you, beloved, that it ought not to be received as the voice of one man singing, but of all who are in Christ's Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:3
verses.text: And since all are in His Body, as it were one man speaketh: and he is one who also is many.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:4
verses.text: Now he prayeth in the temple of God, who prayeth in the peace of the Church, in the unity of Christ's Body; which Body of Christ consisteth of many who believe in the whole world: and therefore he who prayeth in the temple, is heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:5
verses.text: For he prayeth in the spirit and in truth, who prayeth in the peace of the Church; not in that temple, wherein was the figure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:6
verses.text: "Lord, my heart is not lifted up".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:7
verses.text: He hath offered a sacrifice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:8
verses.text: Whence do we prove that he hath offered a sacrifice? Because humility of heart is a sacrifice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:9
verses.text: If there is no sacrifice, there is no Priest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:10
verses.text: But if we have a High Priest in Heaven, who intercedeth with the Father for us (for He hath entered into the Holy of Holies, within the veil),we are safe, for we have a Priest; let us offer our sacrifice there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:11
verses.text: Let us consider what sacrifice we ought to offer; for God is not pleased with burnt-offerings, as ye have heard in the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:12
verses.text: But in that place he next showeth what he offereth: "The sacrifice of God is a troubled spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, shalt Thou not despise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:13
verses.text: "Lord, my heart was not lifted up, neither were mine eyes raised on high" ; "I have not exercised myself in great matters, nor in wonderful things which are too high for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:14
verses.text: Let this be more plainly spoken and heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:15
verses.text: I have not been proud: I have not wished to be known among men as for wondrous powers; nor have I sought anything beyond my strength, whereby I might boast myself among the ignorant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:16
verses.text: As that Simon the sorcerer wished to advance into wonders above himself, on that account the power of the Apostles more pleased him, than the righteousness of Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:17
verses.text: What is above my strength, he saith, I have not sought; I have not stretched myself out there, I have not chosen to be magnified there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:18
verses.text: How deeply this self-exaltation in the abundance of graces is to be feared, that no man may pride himself in the gift of God, but may rather preserve humility, and may do what is written: "The greater thou art, the more humble thyself, and thou shalt find favour before the Lord:" how deeply pride in God's gift should be feared, we must again and again impress upon you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:19
verses.text: "If I had not lowly thoughts, but have lifted up my soul, as one taken from his mother's breast, such the reward for my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:20
verses.text: He seemeth as it were to have bound himself by a curse:as though he had been going to say, Let it so happen to me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:21
verses.text: "As one taken away from his mother's breast, may be my soul's reward".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:22
verses.text: Ye know that the Apostle saith to some weak brethren, "I have fed you with milk, and not with meat; for hitherto ye were not able to bear it, neither yet now are ye able".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:23
verses.text: There are weak persons who are not fit for strong meat; they wish to grasp at that which they cannot receive: and if they ever do receive, or seem to themselves to receive what they have not received, they are puffed up thereby, and become proud thereupon; they seem to themselves wise men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:24
verses.text: Now this happeneth to all heretics; who since they were animal and carnal, by defending their depraved opinions, which they could not see to be false, were shut out of the Catholic Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:25
verses.text: Another opinion indeed hath been entertained, and another sense in these words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:26
verses.text: It has been evidently explained, my brethren, where God would have us to be humble, where lofty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:27
verses.text: Humble, in order to provide against pride; lofty, to take in wisdom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:28
verses.text: Feed upon milk, that thou mayest be nourished; be nourished, so that thou mayest grow; grow, so that thou mayest eat bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:29
verses.text: But when thou hast begun to eat bread, thou wilt be weaned, that is, thou wilt no longer have need of milk, but of solid food.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:30
verses.text: This he seemeth to have meant: "If I had not lowly thoughts, but have lifted up my soul:" that is, if I was not an infant in mind, I was in wickedness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:31
verses.text: In this sense, he said before, "Lord, my heart was not lifted up, nor mine eyes raised on high: I do not exercise myself in great matters, nor in wonderful things above me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:32
verses.text: Behold, in wickedness I am an infant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:33
verses.text: But since I am not an infant in understanding, "If I had not lowly thoughts, but have lifted up my soul," may that reward be mine which is given unto the infant that is weaned from his mother, that I may at length be able to eat bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:34
verses.text: This interpretation, also, brethren, displeaseth me not, since it doth not militate against the faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:35
verses.text: Yet I cannot but remark that it is not only said, "As one taken away from milk, such may be my soul's reward;" but with this addition, "As one taken away from milk when upon his mother's breast, such may be my soul's reward".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:36
verses.text: Here there is somewhat that induces me to consider it a curse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:37
verses.text: For it is not an infant, but a grown child that is taken away from milk; he who is weak in his earliest infancy, which is his true infancy, is upon his mother's breast: if perchance he hath been taken away from the milk, he perisheth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:38
verses.text: It is not without a reason then that it is added, "Upon his mother's breast".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:39
verses.text: For all may be weaned by growing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:40
verses.text: He who groweth, and is thus taken away from milk, it is good for him; but hurtful for him who is still upon his mother's breast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:41
verses.text: We must therefore beware, my brethren, and be fearful, lest any one be taken away from milk before his time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:42
verses.text: Let him not therefore wish to lift up his soul, when perchance he is not fit to take meat, but let him fulfil the commandments of humility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:43
verses.text: He hath wherein he may exercise himself: let him believe in Christ, that he may understand Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:44
verses.text: He cannot see the Word, he cannot understand the equality of the Word with the Father, he cannot as yet see the equality of the Holy Spirit with the Father and the Word; let him believe this, and suck it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:45
verses.text: He is safe, because, when he hath grown, he will eat, which he could not do before he grew by sucking: and he hath a point to stretch towards.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:46
verses.text: Seek not out the things that are too hard for thee, and search not the things that are above thy strength; that is, things which thou art not as yet fit to understand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:47
verses.text: And what am I to do? thou repliest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:48
verses.text: Shall I remain thus? "But what things the Lord hath commanded thee, think thereupon always".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:49
verses.text: What hath the Lord commanded thee? Do works of mercy, part not with the peace of the Church, place not thy trust in man, tempt not God by longing for miracles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:50
verses.text: For if ye be not exalted, if ye raise not your heart on high, if ye tread not in great matters that are too high for you, but preserve humility, God will reveal unto you what ye are otherwise minded in But if ye choose to defend this very thing, which ye are otherwise minded about, and with pertinacity assert it, and against the peace of the Church; this curse which he hath described is entailed upon you; when ye are upon your mother's breast, and are removed away from the milk, ye shall die of hunger apart from your mother's breast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:51
verses.text: But if ye continue in Catholic peace, if perchance ye are in anything otherwise minded than ye ought to be, God will reveal it to you, if ye be humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:52
verses.text: Wherefore? Because "God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace unto the humble".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:53
verses.text: This Psalm therefore concludeth to this purpose: "O Israel, trust in the Lord, from this time forth and even unto eternity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:54
verses.text: But the word seculum doth not always mean this world, but sometimes eternity; since eternity is understood in two ways; until eternity, that is, either evermore without end, or until we arrive at eternity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 131:55
verses.text: How then is it to be understood here? Until we arrive at eternity, let us trust in the Lord God; because when we have reached eternity, there will be no longer hope, but the thing itself will be ours.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXXII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:2
verses.text: It was right indeed, most beloved, that we should rather hear our Brother, my colleague, when present before all of us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:3
verses.text: And just now he refused not, but put us off; for he extorted from me that he might now listen to me, on the condition that I also may listen to him, for in charity itself we are all listening unto Him, who is our One Master in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:4
verses.text: Attend therefore to the Psalm, entitled A Song of Degrees; considerably longer than the rest under the same title.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:5
verses.text: Let us not therefore linger, save where necessity shall compel us: that we may, if the Lord permit, explain the whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:6
verses.text: For ye also ought not to hear everything as men untaught; ye ought in some degree to aid us from your past listenings, so that it may not be needful that everything should be declared to you as though new.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:7
verses.text: "Lord, remember David, and all his meekness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:8
verses.text: David according to the truth of history was one man, king of Israel, son of Jesse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:9
verses.text: He was indeed meek, as the Divine Scriptures themselves mark and command him, and so meek that he did not even render evil for evil to his persecutor Saul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:10
verses.text: He preserved towards him so great humility, that he acknowledged him a king, and himself a dog: and answered the king not proudly nor rudely, though he was more powerful in God; but he rather endeavoured to appease him by humility, than to provoke him by pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:11
verses.text: Saul was even given into his power, and this by the Lord God, that he might do to him what he listed: but since he was not commanded to slay him, but had it only placed in his power (now a man is permitted to use his power), he rather turned towards mercy what God gave him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:12
verses.text: The humility of David is therefore commended, the meekness of David is commended; and it is said to God, "Lord, remember David, and all his meekness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:13
verses.text: For what purpose? "How he sware unto the Lord, and vowed a vow unto the Almighty God of Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:14
verses.text: Therefore remember for this, that he may fulfil what he hath promised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:15
verses.text: David himself vowed as though he had it in his power, and he prayeth God to fulfil his vow: there is devotion in the vow, but there is humility in the prayer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:16
verses.text: Let no one presume to think he fulfilled by his own strength what he hath vowed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:17
verses.text: He who exhorteth thee to vow, Himself aideth thee to fulfil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:18
verses.text: Let us therefore see what he vowed, and hence we comprehend how David should be understood in a figure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:19
verses.text: "David" is interpreted, "Strong of hand," for he was a great warrior.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:20
verses.text: Trusting indeed in the Lord his God, he despatched all wars, he laid low all his enemies, God helping him, according to the dispensation of that kingdom; prefiguring nevertheless some One strong of hand to destroy His enemies, the devil and his angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:21
verses.text: These enemies the Church warreth against, and conquereth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:22
verses.text: What then doth he mean, "How he sware," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:23
verses.text: ? Let us see what vow is this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:24
verses.text: We can offer God nothing more pleasing than to swear Now to swear is to promise firmly Consider this vow, that is, with what ardour he vowed what he vowed, with what love, with what longing; nevertheless, he prayeth the Lord to fulfil it in these words, "O Lord, remember David, and all his meekness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:25
verses.text: In this temper he vowed his vow, and there should be a house of God: "I will not come within the tabernacle of mine house, nor climb up into my bed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:26
verses.text: "I will not suffer mine eyes to sleep, nor mine eyelids to slumber".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:27
verses.text: This seemeth not enough; he adds, "Neither the temples of my head to take any rest, until I find out a place for the Lord; an habitation for the God of Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:28
verses.text: Where did he seek a place for the Lord? If he was meek, he sought it in himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:29
verses.text: For how is one a place for the Lord? Hear the Prophet: "Upon whom shall My Spirit rest? Even upon him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at My words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:30
verses.text: Dost thou wish to be a place for the Lord? Be thou poor in spirit, and contrite, and trembling at the word of God, and thou wilt thyself be made what thou seekest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:31
verses.text: For if what thou seekest be not realized in thyself, what doth it profit thee in another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:32
verses.text: How many thousands believed, my brethren, when they laid down the price of their possessions at the Apostles' feet! But what saith Scripture of them? Surely they are become a temple of God; not only each respectively a temple of God, but also all a temple of God together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:33
verses.text: They have therefore become a place for the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:34
verses.text: And that ye may know that one place is made for the Lord in all, Scripture saith, They were of one heart and one soul toward God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:35
verses.text: But many, so as not to make a place for the Lord, seek their own things, love their own things, delight in their own power, are greedy for their private interests.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:36
verses.text: Whereas he who wisheth to make a place for the Lord, should rejoice not in his private, but the common good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:37
verses.text: Let us therefore, brethren, abstain from the possession of private property; or from the love of it, if we may not from its possession; and we make a place for the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:38
verses.text: It is too much for me, saith some one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:39
verses.text: But consider who thou art, who art about to make a place for the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:40
verses.text: If any senator wished to be entertained at your house, I say not senator, the deputy of some great man of this world, and should say, something offends me in thy house; though thou shouldest love it, thou wouldest remove it, nevertheless, lest thou shouldest offend him, whose friendship thou wast courting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:41
verses.text: And what doth man's friendship profit thee?Desire the friendship of Christ without fear: He wishes to be entertained at thy house; make room for Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:42
verses.text: What is, make room for Him? Love not thyself, love Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:43
verses.text: If thou love thyself, thou shuttest the door against Him; if thou love Him, thou openest unto Him: and if thou open and He enter, thou shalt not be lost by loving thyself, but shalt find thyself with Him who loveth thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:44
verses.text: "Lo, we heard of the same at Ephrata".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:45
verses.text: What? A place for the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:46
verses.text: "We heard of it at Ephrata: and found it in the plains of the forests".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:47
verses.text: Did he hear it where he found it? or did he hear it in one place, find it in another? Let us therefore enquire what Ephrata is, where he heard it; let us also enquire what mean the plains of the forests, where he found it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:48
verses.text: Ephrata, a Hebrew word, is rendered in Latin by Speculum, as the translators of Hebrew words in the Scriptures have handed down to us, that we might understand them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:49
verses.text: They have translated from Hebrew into Greek, and from Greek we have versions into Latin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:50
verses.text: For there have been who watched in the Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:51
verses.text: If therefore Ephrata meaneth a mirror, that house which was found in the woodland plains, was heard of in a mirror.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:52
verses.text: A mirror hath an image: all prophecy is an image of things future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:53
verses.text: The future house of God, therefore, was declared in the image of prophecy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:54
verses.text: "We have found it in the plains of the forests".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:55
verses.text: What are the "plains of the forests"? Saltus is not here used in its common sense, as a plot of ground of so many hundred acres; saltus properly signifies a spot as yet untilled and woody.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:56
verses.text: For some copies read, in the plains of the wood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:57
verses.text: What then were the woodland plains, save nations yet untilled? what were they, save regions yet covered with the thorns of idolatry? Thus, though there were thorns of idolatry there, still we find a place for the Lord there, a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:58
verses.text: What was declared in the image to the Jews, was manifested in the faith of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:59
verses.text: "We will go into His tabernacles".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:60
verses.text: Whose? Those of the Lord God of Jacob.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:61
verses.text: They who enter to dwell therein, are the very same who enter that they may be dwelt in.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:62
verses.text: Thou enterest into thy house, that thou mayest dwell therein; into the house of God, that thou mayest be dwelt in.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:63
verses.text: For the Lord is better, and when He hath begun to dwell in thee, He will make thee happy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:64
verses.text: For if thou be not dwelt in by Him, thou wilt be miserable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:65
verses.text: That son who said, "Father, give me the portion of the goods," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:66
verses.text: , wished to be his own master.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:67
verses.text: It was well kept in his father's hands, that it might not be wasted with harlots.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:68
verses.text: He received it, it was given into his own power; going to a far country, he squandered it all with harlots.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:69
verses.text: At length he suffered hunger, he remembered his father; he returned, that he might be satisfied with bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:70
verses.text: Enter therefore, that thou mayest be dwelt in; and mayest be not thine own, so to speak, but His: "We will go into His tabernacles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:71
verses.text: We will worship on the spot where His feet stood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:72
verses.text: Whose feet? The Lord's, or those of the house of the Lord itself? For that is the Lord's house, wherein he saith He ought to be worshipped.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:73
verses.text: Beside His house, the Lord heareth not unto eternal life; for he belongeth to God's house, who hath in charity been built in with living stones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:74
verses.text: But he who hath not charity, falleth; and while he falls, the house stands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:75
verses.text: But if ye incline to understand it of the house itself, where the feet of that house have stood; let thy feet stand in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:76
verses.text: They will then stand, if thou shalt persevere in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:77
verses.text: For what is said of the devil? "He was a murderer from the beginning, and stood not in the truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:78
verses.text: The feet of the devil therefore stood not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:79
verses.text: Also what saith he of the proud? "O let not the foot of pride come against me; and let not the hand of the ungodly cast me down.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:80
verses.text: There are they fallen, all that work wickedness: they are cast down, and were not able to stand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:81
verses.text: That then is the house of God, whose feet stand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:82
verses.text: Whence John rejoicing, saith: what? "He that hath the bride is the bridegroom: but the friend of the bridegroom standeth and heareth him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:83
verses.text: If he stand not, he heareth him not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:84
verses.text: Justly he standeth, because "he rejoiceth on account of the bridegroom's voice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:85
verses.text: Now therefore ye see why they fell, who rejoice because of their own voice That friend of the Bridegroom said, "The same is He which baptizeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:86
verses.text: Some say, We baptize: rejoicing in their own voice, they could not stand; and belong not to that house of which it is said, "where His feet stood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:87
verses.text: "Arise, O Lord, into Thy resting place".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:88
verses.text: He saith unto the Lord sleeping, "Arise".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:89
verses.text: Ye know already who slept, and who rose again.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:90
verses.text: "Thou, and the ark of Thy sanctification:" that is, Arise, that the ark of Thy sanctification, which Thou hast sanctified, may arise also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:91
verses.text: He is our Head; His ark is His Church: He arose first, the Church will arise also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:92
verses.text: The body would not dare to promise itself resurrection, save the Head arose first.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:93
verses.text: The Body of Christ, that was born of Mary, hath been understood by some to be the ark of sanctification; so that the words mean, Arise with Thy Body, that they who believe not may handle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:94
verses.text: "Let Thy priests be clothed with righteousness, and let Thy saints sing with joyfulness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:95
verses.text: When Thou risest from the dead, and goest unto Thy Father, let that royal Priesthood be clothed with faith, since "the righteous liveth by faith;" and, receiving the pledge of the Holy Spirit, let the members rejoice in the hope of resurrection, which went before in the Head: for to them the Apostle saith, "Rejoicing in hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:96
verses.text: "For Thy servant David's sake, turn not away the face of Thine Anointed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:97
verses.text: These words are addressed unto God the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:98
verses.text: "For Thy servant David's sake, turn not away the face of Thine Anointed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:99
verses.text: The Lord was crucified in Judaea; He was crucified by the Jews; harassed by them, He slept.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:100
verses.text: He arose to judge those among whose savage hands He slept: and He saith elsewhere, "Raise Thou Me up again, and I shall reward them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:101
verses.text: He both hath rewarded them, and will reward them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:102
verses.text: The Jews well know themselves how great were their sufferings after the Lord's death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:103
verses.text: They were all expelled from the very city, where they slew Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:104
verses.text: What then? have all perished even from the root of David and from the tribe of Judah? No: for some of that stock believed, and in fact many thousands of men of that stock believed, and this after the Lord's resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:105
verses.text: They raged and crucified Him: and afterwards began to see miracles wrought in the Name of Him Crucified; and they trembled still more that His Name should have so much power, since when in their hands He seemed unable to work any; and pricked at heart, at length believing that there was some hidden divinity in Him whom they had believed like other men, and asking counsel of the Apostles, they were answered, "Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the Name of our Lord Jesus Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:106
verses.text: Since then Christ arose to judge those by whom He had been crucified, and turned away His Presence from the Jews, turning His Presence towards the Gentiles; God is, as it seemeth, besought in behalf of the remnant of Israel; and it is said unto Him, "For Thy servant David's sake, turn not away the presence of Thine Anointed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:107
verses.text: If the chaff be condemned, let the wheat be gathered together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:108
verses.text: May the remnant be saved, as Isaiah saith, "And the remnant hath" clearly "been saved:"  for out of them were the twelve Apostles, out of them more than five hundred brethren, to whom the Lord showed Himself after His Resurrection: out of their number were so many thousands baptized, who laid the price of their possessions at the Apostles' feet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:109
verses.text: Thus then was fulfilled the prayer here made to God: "For Thy servant David's sake, turn not away the presence of Thine Anointed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:110
verses.text: "The Lord hath made a faithful oath unto David, and He shall not repent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:111
verses.text: What meaneth, "hath made an oath"? Hath confirmed a promise through Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:112
verses.text: What meaneth, "He shall not repent"? He will not change.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:113
verses.text: For God suffereth not the pain of repentance, nor is He deceived in any matter, so that He would wish to correct that wherein He hath erred.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:114
verses.text: But as when a man repents of anything, he wisheth to change what he hath done; thus where thou hearest that God repenteth, look for an actual change.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:115
verses.text: God doth it differently from thee, although He calleth it by the name of repentance; for thou dost it, because thou hadst erred; while He doth it, because He avengeth, or freeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:116
verses.text: He changed Saul's kingdom, when He repented, as it is said: and in the very passage where the Scripture saith, "It repented Him;" it is said a little after, "for He is not a man that He should repent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:117
verses.text: When therefore He changeth His works through His immutable counsel, He is said to repent on account of this very change, not of His counsel, but of His work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:118
verses.text: But He promised this so as not to change it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:119
verses.text: Just as this passage also saith: "The Lord sware, and will not repent, Thou art a Priest for ever after the order of Melchizedec;" so also since this was promised so that it should not be changed, because it must needs happen and be permanent; he saith, "The Lord hath made a faithful oath unto David, and He shall not repent; Of the fruit of thy body shall I set upon thy seat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:120
verses.text: He might have said, "of the fruit of thy loins," wherefore did He choose to say, "Of the fruit of thy body"? Had He said that also, it would have been true; but He chose to say with a further meaning, Ex fructu ventris, because Christ was born of a woman without the man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:121
verses.text: What then? "The Lord hath made a faithful oath unto David, and He shall not shrink from it; Of the fruit of thy body shall I set upon thy seat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:122
verses.text: If thy children will keep My covenant and My testimonies that I shall learn them, their children also shall sit upon thy seat for evermore".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:123
verses.text: If thy children keep My covenant, their children also shall sit for evermore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:124
verses.text: The parents establish a desert on behalf of their children.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:125
verses.text: What if his children should keep the covenant, and their children should not keep it? Why is the happiness of the children promised in relation to their parents' deservings? For what saith He, "If thy children will keep My covenant, their children also shall sit for evermore"—He saith not, if thy children keep My covenant, they shall sit upon thy seat; and if their children keep My covenant, they also shall sit upon thy seat: but he saith, "If thy children keep My covenant, their children also shall sit upon thy seat for evermore"—except because He here wished their fruit to be understood by their children? "If thy children," He saith, "will keep My covenant, and if thy children shall keep My testimonies that I shall learn them; their children also shall sit upon thy seat:" that is, this will be their fruit, that they sit upon thy seat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:126
verses.text: For in this life, brethren, do all of us who labour in Christ, all of us who tremble at His words, who in any way endeavour to execute His will, and groan while we pray His help that we may fulfil what He commandeth; do we already sit in those seats of bliss which are promised us? No: but holding His commandments, we hope this will come to pass.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:127
verses.text: This hope is spoken of under the figure of sons; because sons are the hope of man living in this life, sons are his fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:128
verses.text: For this reason also men, when excusing their avarice, allege that they are reserving for their children what they hoard up; and, unwilling to give to the destitute, excuse themselves under the name of piety, because their children are their hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:129
verses.text: For all men who live according to this world, declare it to be their hope, to be fathers of children they may leave behind them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:130
verses.text: Thus then He describes hope generally under the name of children, and saith, "If thy children will keep My covenant and My testimonies that I shall learn them, their children also shall sit upon thy seat for evermore:" that is, they shall have such fruits, that their hope shall not deceive them, that they may come there where they hope to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:131
verses.text: At present therefore they are as fathers, men of hope for the future; but when they have attained what they hope, they are children; because they have brought forth and produced in their works that which they gain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:132
verses.text: And this is preserved unto them for the future, because futurity itself commonly signifieth children.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:133
verses.text: Or if thou understand actual men to be meant by children, the words, "If thy children will keep My covenant and My testimonies that I shall teach them," may mean, "If thy children will keep My covenant and testimonies that I shall teach them, and their children also;" that is, if they too keep My covenant; so that here thou must make a slight pause, and then infer that "they shall sit upon thy seat for evermore;" that is, both thy children and their children, but all if they keep My covenant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:134
verses.text: What then, if they keep it not? Hath the promise of God failed? No: but it is said and promised for this reason, that God foresaw: what, save that they would believe? But that no man should as it were threaten God's promises, and prefer to place in his own power the fulfilment of what God promised: for this reason he saith, "He made an oath:" whereby he showeth that it will without doubt take place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:135
verses.text: How then hath He said here, "If they will keep My covenant"? Glory not in the promises, and leave out thy failing to keep the covenant.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:136
verses.text: Then wilt thou be the son of David, if thou shalt keep the covenant; but if thou dost not keep it, thou wilt not be David's son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:137
verses.text: God promised to the sons of David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:138
verses.text: Say not, I am David's son if thou degenerate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:139
verses.text: If the Jews, who were born of this very stock, say not this (nay, they say it, but they are under a delusion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:140
verses.text: For the Lord saith openly, "If ye were Abraham's children, ye would do the works of Abraham".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:141
verses.text: He thereby denied them to be children, because they did not the works), how do we call ourselves David's children, who are not of his race according to the flesh? It follows then that we are not children, save by imitating his faith, save by worshipping God, as he worshipped.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:142
verses.text: If therefore what thou hopest not through descent, thou wilt not endeavour to obtain by works; how shall the sitting upon David's seat be fulfilled in thee? And if it shall not be fulfilled in thee, thinkest thou that it shall not be fulfilled at all? And how hath He found it in the woodland tracts? and how did His feet stand? Whatsoever then thou mayest be, that house will stand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:143
verses.text: "For the Lord hath chosen Sion to be an habitation for Himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:144
verses.text: Sion is the Church Herself; She is also that Jerusalem unto whose peace we are running, who is in pilgrimage not in the Angels, but in us, who in her better part waiteth for the part that will return; whence letters have come unto us, which are every day read.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:145
verses.text: This city is that very Sion, whom the Lord hath chosen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:146
verses.text: "This shall be My rest for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:147
verses.text: These are the words of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:148
verses.text: "My rest:" I rest there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:149
verses.text: How greatly doth God love us, brethren, since, because we rest, He saith that He also resteth! For He is not sometimes Himself disturbed, nor doth He rest as we do; but He saith that He resteth there, because we shall have rest in Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:150
verses.text: "Here will I dwell: for I have a delight therein".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:151
verses.text: "I will bless her widow with blessings, and will satisfy her poor with bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:152
verses.text: Every soul that is aware that it is bereft of all help, save of God alone, is widowed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:153
verses.text: For how doth the Apostle describe a widow? "She that is a widow indeed and desolate, trusteth in God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:154
verses.text: He was speaking of those whom we all call Widows in the Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:155
verses.text: He saith, "She that liveth in pleasure, is dead while she liveth;" and he numbereth her not among the widows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:156
verses.text: But in describing true widows, what saith he? "She that is a widow indeed and desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:157
verses.text: Here he addeth, "but she that liveth in pleasure, is dead while she liveth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:158
verses.text: What then makes a widow? That she hath no aid from any other source, save from God alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:159
verses.text: They that have husbands, take pride in the protection of their husbands: widows seem desolate, and their aid is a stronger one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:160
verses.text: The whole Church therefore is one widow, whether in men or in women, in married men or married women, in young men or in old, or in virgins: the whole Church is one widow, desolate in this world, if she feel this, if she is aware of her widowhood: for then is help at hand for her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:161
verses.text: Do ye not recognise this widow in the Gospel, my brethren, when the Lord declared "that men ought always to pray and not to faint"? "There was in a city a judge," He said, "which feared not God, neither regarded man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:162
verses.text: And there was a widow in that city; and she came unto him day by day, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:163
verses.text: The widow, by daily importunity, prevailed with him: for the judge said within himself, "Though I fear not God; neither regard man, yet because this woman troubleth me, I will avenge her".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:164
verses.text: If the wicked judge heard the widow, that he might not be molested; heareth not God His Church, whom He exhorteth to pray?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:165
verses.text: Also, "I will satisfy her poor with bread;" what meaneth this, brethren? Let us be poor, and we shall then be satisfied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:166
verses.text: Many who trust in the world, and are proud, are Christians; they worship Christ, but are not satisfied; for they have been satisfied, and abound in their pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:167
verses.text: Of such it is said, "Our soul is filled with the scornful reproof of the wealthy, and with the despitefulness of the proud:" these have abundance, and therefore eat, but are not satisfied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:168
verses.text: And what is said of them in the Psalm? "All such as be fat upon the earth have eaten and worshipped".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:169
verses.text: They worship Christ, they venerate Christ, they pray unto Christ; but they are not satisfied with His wisdom and righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:170
verses.text: Wherefore? Because they are not poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:171
verses.text: For the poor, that is the humble in heart, the more they hunger, the more they eat; and the more empty they are of the world, the more hungry they are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:172
verses.text: He who is full refuseth whatsoever thou wilt give him, because he is full.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:173
verses.text: Give me one who hungereth; give me one of whom it is said, "Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled:" and these will be the p oor of whom he hath just said, "And will satisfy her poor with bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:174
verses.text: For in the very Psalm where it is said, "All such as be fat upon the earth have eaten and worshipped;" this is said of the poor also, and exactly in the same manner as in this Psalm, "The poor shall eat, and be satisfied: they that seek after the Lord shall praise Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:175
verses.text: Where it is said, "All such as be fat upon earth have eaten and worshipped:" it is said, "the poor shall eat, and be satisfied".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:176
verses.text: Why, when the rich are said to have worshipped, are they not said to be satisfied; yet when the poor are mentioned, they are said to be satisfied? And whence are they satisfied? What is the nature, brethren, of this satisfying? God Himself is their bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:177
verses.text: The bread came down upon the earth, that He might become milk unto us; and said to His own, "I am the Living Bread which came down from heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:178
verses.text: Hence these words in the Psalm, "The poor shall eat, and be satisfied".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:179
verses.text: From what source shall they be satisfied? Hear what followeth: "And they that seek after the Lord shall praise Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:180
verses.text: Be ye therefore poor, be ye among the members of that widow, let your help be solely in God alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:181
verses.text: Money is nought; not thence will ye have aid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:182
verses.text: Many have been cast headlong down for money's sake, many have perished on account of money; many for the sake of their riches have been marked out by plunderers; they would have been safe, had they not had what made men hunt for them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:183
verses.text: Many have presumed in their more powerful friends: they in whom they presumed have fallen, and have involved in their ruin those who trusted in them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:184
verses.text: Look back upon the instances to be seen in the human race.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:185
verses.text: Is it anything singular that I am telling you? We speak these things not only from these Scriptures; read them in the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:186
verses.text: Take heed that ye presume not in money, in a friend, in the honour and the boasting of the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:187
verses.text: Take away all these things: but if thou hast them, thank God if thou despisest them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:188
verses.text: But if thou art puffed up by them; think not when thou wilt be the prey of men; already art thou the Devil's prey.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:189
verses.text: But if thou hast not trusted in these things, thou wilt be among the members of that widow, who is the Church, of whom it is said, "I will bless her widow with blessings;" thou wilt also be poor, and one of those of whom it is said, "And will satisfy her poor with bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:190
verses.text: Sometimes, however, and we must not pass over this without mention, thou findest a poor man proud, and a rich man humble: we daily endure such persons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:191
verses.text: Thou hearest a poor man groaning beneath a rich man, and when the more powerful rich man presseth upon him, then thou seest him humble: sometimes not even then, but even then proud; whence thou seest what he would have been, had he any property.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:192
verses.text: God's poor one is therefore poor in spirit, not in his purse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:193
verses.text: Sometimes a man goeth forth having a full house, rich lands, many estates, much gold and silver; he knoweth that he must not trust in these, he humbleth himself before God, he doth good with them; thus his heart is raised unto God, so that he is aware that not only do riches themselves profit him nothing, but that they even impede his feet, save He rule them, and aid them: and he is counted among the poor who are satisfied with bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:194
verses.text: Thou findest another a proud beggar, or not proud only because he hath nothing, nevertheless seeking whereby he may be puffed up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:195
verses.text: God doth not heed the means a man hath, but the wish he hath, and judgeth him according to his wish for temporal blessings, not according to the means which it is not his lot to have.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:196
verses.text: Whence the Apostle saith of the rich, "Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:197
verses.text: What therefore should they do with their riches? He goeth on to say: "That they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:198
verses.text: And see that they are poor in this world: "Laying up in store for themselves," he addeth, "a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on eternal life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:199
verses.text: When they have laid hold of eternal life, then will they be rich; but since they have it not as yet, they should know that they are poor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:200
verses.text: Thus it is that God counteth among His poor all the humble in heart, who are established in that twofold charity, whatever they may have in this world—among His poor, whom He satisfieth with bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:201
verses.text: "I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her saints shall rejoice and sing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:202
verses.text: We are now at the end of the Psalm; attend for a short space, Beloved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:203
verses.text: "I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her saints shall rejoice and sing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:204
verses.text: Who is our salvation, save our Christ? What meaneth, therefore, "I will clothe her priests with salvation"? "As many of you as have been baptized into Christ, have put on Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:205
verses.text: "And her saints shall rejoice and sing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:206
verses.text: Whence shall they rejoice and sing? Because they have been clothed with salvation: not in themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:207
verses.text: For they have become light, but in the Lord; for they were darkness before Therefore he hath added, "There will I raise up the horn of David" : this will be David's height, that trust be put in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:208
verses.text: For horn signifieth height: and what sort of height? Not carnal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:209
verses.text: Therefore, while all the bones are wrapped up in flesh, the horn goeth beyond the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:210
verses.text: Spiritual altitude is a horn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:211
verses.text: But what is spiritual loftiness, save to trust in Christ? not to say, It is my work, I baptize; but, "He it is who baptizeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:212
verses.text: There is the horn of David: and that ye may know that there is the horn of David, heed what followeth: "I have ordained a lantern for mine Anointed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:213
verses.text: What is a lantern? Ye already know the Lord's words concerning John: "He was a burning and a shining light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:214
verses.text: And what saith John? "He it is who baptizeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:215
verses.text: Herein therefore shall the saints rejoice, herein the priests shall rejoice: because all that is good in themselves, is not of themselves, but of Him who hath the power of baptizing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:216
verses.text: Fearlessly therefore doth every one who hath received baptism come unto His temple; because it is not man's, but His who made the horn of David to flourish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:217
verses.text: "Upon Him shall My sanctification flourish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:218
verses.text: Upon whom? Upon Mine Anointed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:219
verses.text: For when He saith, "Mine anointed," it is the voice of the Father, who saith, "I will bless her widow with blessings, and will satisfy her poor with bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:220
verses.text: I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her saints shall rejoice and sing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:221
verses.text: He who saith, "There will I raise up the horn of David," is God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:222
verses.text: He Himself saith, "I have ordained a lantern for Mine Anointed," because Christ is both ours and the Father's: He is our Christ, when He saveth us and ruleth us, as He is also our Lord: He is the Son of the Father, but both our Christ and the Father's.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:223
verses.text: For if He were not the Father's Christ, it would not be said above, "For Thy servant David's sake, turn not Thou away the presence of Thine Anointed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:224
verses.text: "Upon Him shall My sanctification flourish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:225
verses.text: It flourisheth upon Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:226
verses.text: Let none of men assume this to himself, that he himself sanctifieth: otherwise it will not be true, "Upon Him shall My sanctification flourish".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:227
verses.text: The glory of sanctification shall flourish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:228
verses.text: The sanctification of Christ therefore in Christ Himself, is the power of the sanctification of God in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:229
verses.text: In that he saith, "shall flourish," he refers to His glory: for when trees flourish, then are they beautiful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:230
verses.text: Sanctification therefore is in Baptism: thence it flourisheth, and is brightened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 132:231
verses.text: Why hath the world yielded to this beauty? Because it flourisheth in Christ; for, put it in man's power, and how doth it then flourish? since "all flesh in grass, and all the goodliness thereof as the flower of the grass".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXXIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:2
verses.text: This is a short Psalm, but one well known and quoted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:3
verses.text: "Behold, how good and how pleasant is it, that brethren should dwell together in unity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:4
verses.text: So sweet is that sound, that even they who know not the Psalter, sing that verse.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:5
verses.text: For these same words of the Psalter, this sweet sound, that honeyed melody, as well of the mind as of the hymn, did even beget the Monasteries.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:6
verses.text: By this sound were stirred up the brethren who longed to dwell together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:7
verses.text: This verse was their trumpet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:8
verses.text: It sounded through the whole earth, and they who had been divided, were gathered together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:9
verses.text: The summons of God, the summons of the Holy Spirit, the summons of the Prophets, were not heard in Judah, yet were heard through the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:10
verses.text: They were deaf to that sound, amid whom it was sung; they were found with their ears open, of whom it was said, "They shall see him, who were not told of him; they shall understand who heard not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:11
verses.text: Yet, most beloved, if we reflect, the very blessing hath sprung from that wall of circumcision.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:12
verses.text: For have all the Jews perished? and whence were the Apostles, the sons of the Prophets, the sons of the exiles? He speaks as to them who know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:13
verses.text: Whence those five hundred, who saw the Lord after His resurrection, whom the Apostle Paul commemorates? Whence those hundred and twenty, who were together in one place after the resurrection of the Lord, and His ascension into heaven, on whom when gathered into one place the Holy Spirit descended on the day of Pentecost, sent down from heaven, sent, even as He was promised? All were from thence, and they first dwelt together in unity; who sold all they had, and laid the price of their goods at the Apostles' feet, as is read in the Acts of the Apostles And distribution was made to each one as he had need, and none called anything his own, but they had all things common.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:14
verses.text: And what is "together in unity"? They had, he says, one mind and one heart God-wards So they were the first who heard, Behold how good and how pleasant is it, that brethren dwell together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:15
verses.text: They were the first to hear, but heard it not alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:16
verses.text: From the words of this Psalm was taken the name of Monks, that no one may reproach you who are Catholics by reason of the name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:17
verses.text: When you with justice reproach heretics by reason of the Circelliones, that they may be saved by shame, they reproach you on the score of the Monks.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:18
verses.text: Moreover, beloved, there are they who are false Monks, and we know men of this kind; but the pious brotherhood is not annulled, because of them who profess to be what they are not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:19
verses.text: There are false Monks, as there are false men among the Clergy, and among the faithful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:20
verses.text: Since the Psalm says, "Behold, how good and how pleasant is it, that brethren should dwell together in one," why then should we not call Monks so? for Monos is one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:21
verses.text: Not one in any manner, for a man in a crowd is one, but though he can be called one along with others, he cannot be Monos, that is, alone, for Monos means "one alone".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:22
verses.text: They then who thus live together as to make one man, so that they really possess what is written, "one mind and one heart," many bodies, but not many minds; many bodies, but not many hearts; can rightly be called Monos, that is, one alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:23
verses.text: Let the Psalm tell us what they are like.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:24
verses.text: "As the ointment on the head, which descended to the beard, to Aaron's beard, which descended to the fringe of his garment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:25
verses.text: What was Aaron? A priest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:26
verses.text: Who is a priest, except that one Priest, who entered into the Holy of Holies? Who is that priest, save Him, who was at once Victim and Priest? save Him who when he found nothing clean in the world to offer, offered Himself? The ointment is on his head, because Christ is one whole with the Church, but the ointment comes from the head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:27
verses.text: Our Head is Christ crucified and buried; He rose again, and ascended into heaven; and the Holy Spirit came from the head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:28
verses.text: Whither? To the beard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:29
verses.text: The beard signifies the courageous; the beard distinguishes the grown men, the earnest, the active, the vigorous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:30
verses.text: So that when we describe such, we say, he is a bearded man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:31
verses.text: Thus that ointment descended first upon the Apostles, descended upon those who bore the first assaults of the world, and therefore the Holy Spirit descended on them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:32
verses.text: For they who first began to dwell together in unity, suffered persecution, but because the ointment descended to the beard, they suffered, but were not conquered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:33
verses.text: "As the dew of Hermon, which fell upon the hills of Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:34
verses.text: He would have it understood, my brethren, that it is of God's grace that brethren dwell together in unity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:35
verses.text: But ye should know what Hermon is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:36
verses.text: It is a mountain far distant from Jerusalem, that is, from Sion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:37
verses.text: And so it is strange that he says thus: As the dew of Hermon, which fell upon the mountains of Sion, since mount Hermon is far distant from Jerusalem, for it is said to be over Jordan.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:38
verses.text: Let us then seek out some interpretation of Hermon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:39
verses.text: The word is Hebrew, and we learn its meaning from them who know that language.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:40
verses.text: Hermon is said to mean, a light set on a high place.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:41
verses.text: For from Christ comes the dew.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:42
verses.text: No light is set on a high place, save Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:43
verses.text: How is He set on high? First on the cross, afterwards in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:44
verses.text: Set on high on the cross when He was humbled; humbled, but His humiliation could not but be high.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:45
verses.text: The ministry of man grew less and less, as was signified in John; the ministry of God in our Lord Jesus Christ increased, as was shown at their birth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:46
verses.text: The former was born, as the tradition of the Church shows, on the th of June, when the days begin to shorten.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:47
verses.text: The Lord was born on the th of December, when the days begin to lengthen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:48
verses.text: Here John himself confessing, "He must increase, but I must decrease".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:49
verses.text: And the passion of each shows this.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:50
verses.text: The Lord was exalted on the cross; John was diminished by beheading.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:51
verses.text: Thus the light set on high is Christ, whence is the dew of Hermon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:52
verses.text: But if he have the dew of Hermon, which fell on the hill of Sion, he is quiet, peaceable, humble, submissive, pouring forth prayer in place of murmuring.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:53
verses.text: For murmurers are admirably described in a certain passage of the Scriptures, "The heart of a fool is as the wheel of a cart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:54
verses.text: What is the meaning of "the heart of a fool is as the wheel of a cart"? It carries hay, and creaks.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:55
verses.text: The wheel of a cart cannot cease from creaking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:56
verses.text: Thus there are many brethren, who do not dwell together, save in the body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:57
verses.text: But who are they who dwell together? They of whom it is said, "And they had one mind and one heart towards God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:58
verses.text: "Because there the Lord commanded blessing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:59
verses.text: Where did He command it? Among the brethren who dwell together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:60
verses.text: There He enjoined blessing, there they who dwell with one heart bless God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:61
verses.text: For thou blessest not God in division of heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:62
verses.text: Art thou straitened on earth? Depart, have thy habitation in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:63
verses.text: How shall I, a man clothed in flesh, enslaved to the flesh, thou wilt say, have my habitation in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:64
verses.text: First go in heart, whither thou wouldest follow in the body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:65
verses.text: Do not hear, "Lift up your hearts," with a deaf ear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 133:66
verses.text: Keep thy heart lifted up, and no one will straiten thee in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXXIV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:2
verses.text: "Behold, now, bless ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord" , "who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:3
verses.text: Why has he added, "in the courts"? Courts mean the wider spaces of a house.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:4
verses.text: He who stands in the courts is not straitened, is not confined, in some fashion is enlarged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:5
verses.text: Remain in this enlargement, and thou canst love thy enemy, because thou lovest not things in which an enemy could straiten thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:6
verses.text: How canst thou be understood to stand in the courts? Stand in charity, and thou standest in the courts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:7
verses.text: Breadth lies in charity, straitness in hatred.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:8
verses.text: "Lift up your hands by night in the sanctuary, and bless the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:9
verses.text: It is easy to bless by day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:10
verses.text: What is "by day"? In prosperity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:11
verses.text: For night is a sad thing, day a cheerful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:12
verses.text: When it is well with thee, thou dost bless the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:13
verses.text: Thy son was sick, and he is made whole, thou dost bless the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:14
verses.text: Thy son was sick, perchance thou hast sought an astrologer, a soothsayer, perchance a curse against the Lord has come, not from thy tongue, but from thy deeds, from thy deeds and thy life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:15
verses.text: Boast not, because thou blessest with thy tongue, if thou cursest with thy life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:16
verses.text: Wherefore bless ye the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:17
verses.text: When? By night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:18
verses.text: When did Job bless? When it was a sad night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:19
verses.text: All was taken away which he possessed; the children for whom his goods were stored were taken away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:20
verses.text: How sad was his night! Let us however see whether he blesseth not in the night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:21
verses.text: "The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away; it is as the Lord willed; blessed be the name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:22
verses.text: And black was the night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:23
verses.text: "The Lord out of Zion bless thee, who made heaven and earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:24
verses.text: He exhorts many to bless, and Himself blesseth one, because He maketh one out of many, since "it is good and pleasant for brethren to dwell together in one".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:25
verses.text: It is a plural number, brethren, and yet singular, to dwell together in one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:26
verses.text: Let none of you say, It cometh not to me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:27
verses.text: Knowest thou of whom he speaks, "the Lord bless thee out of Zion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:28
verses.text: He blessed one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 134:29
verses.text: Be one, and the blessing cometh to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXXV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:2
verses.text: Ver y pleasant ought it be to us, and we should rejoice because it is pleasant, to which this Psalm exhorteth us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:3
verses.text: For it says, "Praise the name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:4
verses.text: And it forthwith appends the reason, why it is just to praise the name of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:5
verses.text: "Praise the Lord, ye servants".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:6
verses.text: What more just? what more worthy? what more thankful?For if He teaches His own servants who have deserved well of Him, the preachers of His Word, the rulers of His Church, the worshippers of His name, the obeyers of His command, that in their own conscience they should possess the sweetness of their life, lest they be corrupted by the praise or disheartened by the reproach of men; how much the more is He above all, the unchangeable One, who teacheth these things, neither the greater if thou praisest, or the less if thou reproachest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:7
verses.text: For ye will do nothing out of place, by praising your Lord, as servants.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:8
verses.text: And if ye were to be for ever only servants, ye ought to praise the Lord; how much more ought ye servants to praise the Lord, that ye may hereafter gain the privilege of sons?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:9
verses.text: Therefore, "Ye who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God, praise the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:10
verses.text: Be thankful; ye were without, and ye stand within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:11
verses.text: Since then ye stand, is it a small thing for you to think where He should be praised, who raised you when you were cast down, and caused you to stand in His house, to know Him, and to praise Him? Is it a small boon, that we stand in the house of the Lord?If one thinks of this, and is not unthankful, he will utterly despise himself in comparison with the love of his Lord, who hath done so great things for him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:12
verses.text: And since he hath nothing wherewith to repay God for so great benefits, what remains for him but to give Him thanks, not to repay Him? It belongs to the very act of thanksgiving, to "receive the cup of the Lord, and to call upon His name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:13
verses.text: For what can the servant repay the Lord for all that He hath given him?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:14
verses.text: What reason shall I give why you should praise Him? "Because the Lord is good".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:15
verses.text: Briefly in one word is here explained the praise of the Lord our God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:16
verses.text: "The Lord is good;" good, not in the same manner as the things which He here made are good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:17
verses.text: For God made all things very good; not only good, but also very good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:18
verses.text: He made the sky and earth, and all things which are in them good, and He made them very good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:19
verses.text: If He made all these things good, of what sort is He who made them?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:20
verses.text: How far can we speak of His goodness? Who can conceive in his heart, or apprehend how good the Lord is? Let us however return to ourselves, and in us recognise Him, and praise the Maker in His works, because we are not fit to contemplate Him Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:21
verses.text: And in hope that we may be able to contemplate Him, when our heart hath been purified by faith, that hereafter it may rejoice in the Truth; now as He cannot be seen by us, let us look at His works, that we may not live without praising Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:22
verses.text: So I have said, "Praise the Lord, for He is good; sing praises unto His Name, for He is sweet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:23
verses.text: He is Mediator, and thereupon is sweet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:24
verses.text: What is sweeter than angels' food? How can God not be sweet, since man ate angels' food? For men and angels live not on different meat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:25
verses.text: That is truth, that is wisdom, that is the goodness of God, but thou canst not enjoy it in like wise with the angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:26
verses.text: That man might eat angels' food, the Creator of the angels was made man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:27
verses.text: If ye taste, sing praises; if ye have tasted how sweet the Lord is, sing praises; if that which ye have tasted has a good savour, praise it; who is so unthankful to cook or purveyor, as not to return thanks by praising what he tastes, if he be pleased by any food.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:28
verses.text: If we are not silent on such occasions, shall we be silent concerning Him, who has given us all things?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:29
verses.text: "For the Lord hath chosen Jacob to Himself, Israel for His own possession".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:30
verses.text: Let not Jacob therefore extol himself, let him not boast himself, or ascribe it to his own merits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:31
verses.text: He was known before, predestinated before, elected before, not elected for his own merits, but found out, and gifted with life by the grace of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:32
verses.text: So with all the Gentiles; for how did the wild-olive deserve, that it should be grafted in, from the bitterness of its berries, the barrenness of its wildness? It was the wood of the wilderness, not of the Lord's field, and yet He of His mercy grafted the wild-olive into the (true) olive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:33
verses.text: But up to this time the wild-olive was not grafted in.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:34
verses.text: "Because," says he, "I know that the Lord is great, and our God is above all gods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:35
verses.text: If we should say to him, we ask thee, explain to us His greatness; would he not perchance answer us, He whom I see is not so very great, if He be able to be expounded by me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:36
verses.text: Let him then return to His works, and tell us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:37
verses.text: Let him hold in his conscience the greatness of God, which he has seen, which he has committed to our faith, whither he could not lead our eyes, and enumerate some of the things which the Lord hath done here; that unto us, who cannot see His greatness as he can, He may become sweet through the works of His which we can comprehend.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:38
verses.text: "All whatsoever the Lord willed, He made in the heaven, and in the earth, in the sea, and in all its deep places".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:39
verses.text: Who can comprehend these things? Who can enumerate the works of the Lord in the heaven and earth, in the sea, and in all deep places? Yet if we cannot comprehend them all, we should believe and hold them without question, because whatever creature is in heaven, whatever is in earth, whatever is in the sea and in all deep places, has been made by the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:40
verses.text: "Raising the clouds from the ends of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:41
verses.text: We see these works of God in His creation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:42
verses.text: For the clouds come from the ends of the earth to the midst thereof, and rain; thou scannest not whence they arise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:43
verses.text: Hence the prophet signifies this, from "the ends of the earth," whether it be from the bottom, or from the circumference of the ends of the earth, whencesoever He wills He raises the clouds, only from the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:44
verses.text: "He hath made lightnings into rain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:45
verses.text: For lightnings without rain would frighten thee, and bestow nothing on thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:46
verses.text: "He maketh lightnings unto rain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:47
verses.text: It lightens, and thou tremblest; it rains, thou rejoicest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:48
verses.text: "He hath made lightnings unto rain".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:49
verses.text: He who terrified thee, Himself causest that thou shouldest rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:50
verses.text: "Who bringeth the winds out of His treasures," their causes are hidden, thou knowest not whence they come.
