verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:51
verses.text: When the wind blows, thou feelest it; why it blows, or from what treasure of His wisdom it is brought forth, thou knowest not;  yet thou owest to God the worship of faith, for it would not blow unless He had bidden who made it, unless He had brought it forth who created it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:52
verses.text: We see therefore these things in that work of His; we praise, we marvel at, we bless God; let us see what He has done among men for His people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:53
verses.text: "Who smote the first-born of Egypt".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:54
verses.text: But withal those divine doings are told which thou mightest love, those are not told which thou mightest fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:55
verses.text: Attend, and see that also when He is angry, He doeth what He willeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:56
verses.text: "From man even unto beast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:57
verses.text: He sent signs and wonders into the midst of thee, O Egypt!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:58
verses.text: Ye know, ye have read what the hand of the Lord did by Moses in Egypt, to crush and cast down the proud Egyptians, "on Pharaoh and on all his servants".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:59
verses.text: Little did He in Egypt: what did He after His people was led out thence? "Who smote many nations" , who possessed that land, which God willed to give His people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:60
verses.text: "And slew mighty kings, Sehon king of the Amorites,  and Og the king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:61
verses.text: All these things which the Psalm records simply, do we read likewise in others of the Lord's books, and there the hand of the Lord is great.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:62
verses.text: When thou seest what has been done to the wicked, take heed lest it be done to thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:63
verses.text: But when the good man sees what the wicked has suffered, let him cleanse himself from all iniquity, lest he fall into a like punishment, a like chastisement.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:64
verses.text: Then ye have thoroughly understood these things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:65
verses.text: What did God then? He drove out the wicked, "And he gave their land for an inheritance, even an inheritance to Israel His servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:66
verses.text: Then follows the loud cry of His praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:67
verses.text: "Thy Name, O Lord, is for ever and ever" , after all these things which Thou hast done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:68
verses.text: For what do I see that Thou hast done? I behold Thy creation which Thou hast made in heaven, I behold this lower part, where we dwell, and here I see Thy gifts of clouds, and winds, and rain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:69
verses.text: I regard Thy people; Thou leddest them from the house of bondage, and didst signs and wonders upon their enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:70
verses.text: Thou punishedst those who caused them trouble, Thou dravest the wicked from their land, Thou killedst their kings, Thou gavest their land to Thy people: I have seen all these things, and filled with joy have said, "Lord, Thy Name is for ever and ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:71
verses.text: All these things then did God overthrow, in the body at that time, when our fathers were led out of the land of Egypt, in the spirit now.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:72
verses.text: Nor does His Hand cease until the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:73
verses.text: Therefore deem not that these mighty deeds of God were then finished and have ceased.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:74
verses.text: "Thy Name, O Lord," he says, "is for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:75
verses.text: That is, Thy loving-kindness ceaseth not, Thy hand ceaseth not for ever from doing these things, which then Thou didst afore declare in a figure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:76
verses.text: "But they are written for our admonition, on whom the end of the ages is come".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:77
verses.text: One generation and another generation; the generation by which we are made the faithful, and are born again by baptism; the generation by which we shall rise again from the dead, and shall live with the Angels for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:78
verses.text: Thy Memorial, O Lord, is above this generation, and above that; for neither doth He now forget to call us, nor then will He forget to crown us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:79
verses.text: "The Lord hath judged His people, and will be called upon among His servants".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:80
verses.text: Already hath He judged the people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:81
verses.text: Save the final judgment, the people of the Jews is judged.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:82
verses.text: What is "judged"? The just are taken away, the unjust are left.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:83
verses.text: But if I lie, or am thought to lie, because I have said, it is already judged, hear the Lord saying, "I have come for judgment into this world, that they who see not may see, and they who see may be made blind".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:84
verses.text: The proud are made blind, the lowly are enlightened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:85
verses.text: Therefore, "He hath judged His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:86
verses.text: Isaiah spake the judgment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:87
verses.text: "And now, thou house of Jacob, come ye, let us walk in the light of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:88
verses.text: This is a small matter; but what follows? "For He hath put away His people, the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:89
verses.text: The house of Jacob is the house of Israel; for he who is Jacob, the same is Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:90
verses.text: Therefore God had judged His people, by separating the evil and the good; that is to say, "He shall be called upon among His servants".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:91
verses.text: By whom? By the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:92
verses.text: For how vast are the nations who have come in by faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:93
verses.text: How many farms and desert places now come in to us? They come thence no one can tell how numerously; they would believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:94
verses.text: We say to them, What will ye? They answer, To know the glory of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:95
verses.text: Believe, my brethren, that we wonder and rejoice at such a claim of these rustic people.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:96
verses.text: They come I know not whither, roused up by I know not whom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:97
verses.text: How shall I say, I know not by whom? I know indeed by whom, because He says, "No one cometh to Me, save whom the Father draweth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:98
verses.text: They come suddenly from the woods, the desert, the most distant and lofty mountains, to the Church; and many of them, nay, near all hold this language, so that we see of a truth that God teacheth them within The prophecy of Scripture is fulfilled, when it says, "And they shall all be taught of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:99
verses.text: We say to them, What do ye long for? And they answer, To see the glory of God "For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:100
verses.text: They believe, they are sanctified, they will to have clergy ordained for them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:101
verses.text: Is it not fulfilled, "and He will be called upon among His servants"?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:102
verses.text: Lastly, after all that arrangement and dispensation, the Spirit of God turns itself to reproaching and ridiculing those idols, which are now ridiculed by their very worshippers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:103
verses.text: "The idols of the Gentiles are silver and gold".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:104
verses.text: As God made all these things, who made whatever He would in heaven and earth, what can anything that man maketh be, but an object of ridicule, not adoration? Was He perchance about to speak of "the idols of the Gentiles," that we might despise them all? was He about to speak of the idols of the heathen, stones and wood, plaster and pottery? I say not these, they are mean materials.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:105
verses.text: I speak of that which they specially love, that which they specially honour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:106
verses.text: "The idols of the Gentiles are silver and gold, the work of men's hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:107
verses.text: Surely it is gold, surely it is silver: because silver glitters, and gold glitters, have they therefore eyes, or do they see?But as these things are senseless, why make ye men of silver and gold to be gods? See ye not that the gods which ye make see not? "They have a mouth, and will not speak; they have eyes, and will not see" ; "they have ears, and will not hear; neither is there any breath in their mouth" ; "they have nostrils, and will not smell; they have hands, and will not work; they have feet, and will not walk".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:108
verses.text: All these things could the carpenter, the silversmith, the goldsmith make, both eyes, and ears, and nostrils, and mouth, and hands, and feet, but he could give neither sight to the eyes, nor hearing to the ears, nor speech to the mouth, nor smell to the nostrils, nor motion to the hands, or going to the feet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:109
verses.text: And man, thou laughest doubtless at what thou hast made, if thou knowest by whom thou art made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:110
verses.text: But of them who know not, what is said? "All they who make them, and all they who trust in them, are like them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:111
verses.text: And ye believe, brethren, that there is a likeness to these idols expressed not in their flesh, but in their inner man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:112
verses.text: For "they have ears, and hear not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:113
verses.text: God calls to them indeed, "He who hath ears to hear, let him hear".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:114
verses.text: They have eyes, and see not, for they have the eyes of the body, and not the eyes of faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:115
verses.text: Lastly, this prophecy is fulfilled among all the nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:116
verses.text: Is it not fulfilled? Is it not seen, as it is written? And they who remain have eyes, and see not; have nostrils, and smell not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:117
verses.text: They perceive not that savour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:118
verses.text: "We are a good savour of Christ," as the apostle says everywhere.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:119
verses.text: What profiteth it, that they have nostrils, and smell not that so sweet savour of Christ? Truly it is done in them, and truly it is said of them, "All they who make them," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:120
verses.text: But daily do men believe through the miracles of Christ our Lord; daily the eyes of the blind, the ears of the deaf are opened, the nostrils of the senseless are breathed into, the tongues of the dumb are loosed, the hands of the palsied are strengthened, the feet of the lame are guided; sons of Abraham are raised up of these stones, to all of whom be it said, "Bless the Lord, ye house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:121
verses.text: All are sons of Abraham; and if sons of Abraham are raised up from these stones, it is plain that they are rather the house of Israel who belong to the house of Israel, the seed of Abraham, not by the flesh, but by faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:122
verses.text: But even granting that it is said of that house, and the people of Israel is meant, from thence did the Apostles and thousands of the circumcised believe? "Bless the Lord, ye house of Aaron.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:123
verses.text: Bless the Lord, ye house of Levi".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:124
verses.text: Bless the Lord, ye nations, this is, the "house of Israel" generally; bless Him, ye leaders, this is, the "house of Aaron;" bless Him, ye servants, this is, the "house of Levi".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:125
verses.text: What of the other nations? "Ye that fear the Lord, bless the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:126
verses.text: Let us also with one voice say what follows: "Blessed be the Lord out of Zion, who dwelleth in Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:127
verses.text: Out of Zion is Jerusalem too.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:128
verses.text: Zion is "watching," Jerusalem the "vision of peace".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:129
verses.text: In what Jerusalem will He dwell now? In that which has fallen? Nay, but in that which is our mother, which is in the heavens, of which it is said, "The desolate hath more children than she which hath a husband".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:130
verses.text: For now the Lord is from Zion, because we watch when He will come; now as long as we live in hope, we are in Zion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:131
verses.text: When our way is ended, we shall dwell in that city which will never fall, because the Lord dwelleth in her, and keepeth her, which is the vision of peace, the eternal Jerusalem; for the praise of which, my brethren, language sufficeth not; where we shall find no enemy, either within the Church or without the Church, neither in our flesh, nor in our thoughts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 135:132
verses.text: For "death shall be swallowed up in victory," and we shall be free to see God in eternal peace, being made citizens of Jerusalem, the city of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXXVI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:2
verses.text: "Give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endureth for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:3
verses.text: This Psalm contains the praise of God, and all its verses finish in the same way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:4
verses.text: Wherefore although many things are related here in praise of God, yet His mercy is most commended; for without this plain commendation, he, whom the Holy Spirit used to utter this Psalm, would have no verse be ended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:5
verses.text: Although after the judgment, by which at the end of the world the quick and the dead must be judged, the just being sent into life eternal, the unjust into everlasting fire, there will not afterwards be those, whom God will have mercy on, yet rightly may His future mercy be understood to be for ever, which He bestows on His saints and faithful ones, not because they will be miserable for ever, and therefore will need His mercy for ever, but because that very blessedness, which He mercifully bestows on the miserable, that they cease to be miserable, and begin to be happy, will have no end, and therefore "His mercy is for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:6
verses.text: For that we shall be just from being unjust, whole from being unsound, alive from being dead, immortal from being mortal, happy from being wretched, is of His mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:7
verses.text: But this that we shall be, will be for ever, and therefore "His mercy is for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:8
verses.text: Wherefore, "give thanks to the Lord;" that is, praise the Lord by giving thanks, "for He is good:" nor is it any temporal good you will gain from this confession, for, "His mercy endureth for ever;" that is, the benefit which He bestows mercifully upon you, is for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:9
verses.text: Then follows, "Give thanks to the God of gods, for His mercy endureth for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:10
verses.text: "Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for His mercy endureth for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:11
verses.text: We may well enquire, Who are these gods and lords, of whom He who is the true God is God and Lord? And we find written in another Psalm, that even men are called gods The Lord even takes note of this testimony in the Gospel, saying, "Is it not written in your Law, I have said, Ye are gods?"It is not therefore because they are all good, but because "the word of God came to them," that they were called gods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:12
verses.text: For were it because they are all good, He would not thus distinguish between them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:13
verses.text: He saith, "He judgeth between the gods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:14
verses.text: Then follows, "How long do ye judge iniquity!" and the rest, which He says certainly not to all, but to some, because He saith it in distinguishing, and yet He distinguisheth between the gods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:15
verses.text: But it is asked, If men are called gods to whom the word of the Lord came, are the Angels to be called gods, when the greatest reward which is promised to just and holy men is the being equal to Angels? In the Scriptures I know not whether it can, at least easily, be found, that the Angels are openly called gods; but when it had been said of the Lord God, "He is terrible, above all gods," he adds, as by way of exposition why he says this, "for the gods of the heathen are devils," that we might understand what had been expressed in the Hebrew, "the gods of the Gentiles are idols," meaning rather the devils which dwell in the idols For as regards images, which in Greek are called idols, a name we now use in Latin, they have eyes and see not, and all the other things which are said of them, because they are utterly without sense; wherefore they cannot be frightened, for nothing which has no sense can be frightened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:16
verses.text: How then can it be said of the Lord, "He is terrible above all gods, because the gods of the Gentiles are idols," if the devils which may be terrified are not understood to be in these images.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:17
verses.text: Whence also the Apostle says, "We know that an idol is nothing".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:18
verses.text: This refers to its earthy senseless material.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:19
verses.text: But that no one may think, that there is no living and sentient nature, which delights in the Gentile sacrifices, he adds, "But what the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils, and not to God: I would not have you partaken with devils".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:20
verses.text: If therefore we never find in the divine words that the holy Angels are called gods, I think the best reason is, that men may not be induced by the name to pay that ministry and service of religion (which in Greek is called λειτουργία or λατρία) to the holy Angels, which neither would they have paid by man at all, save to that God, who is the God of themselves and men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:21
verses.text: Hence they are much more correctly called Angels, which in Latin is Nuntii, that by the name of their function, not their substance, we may plainly understand that they would have us worship the God, whom they announce.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:22
verses.text: The whole then of that question the Apostle has briefly expounded, when he says, "For though there be who are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, as there are gods many and lords many; yet we have one God the Father, from whom are all, and we in Him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:23
verses.text: Let us therefore "give thanks to the God of gods, and the Lord of lords, for His mercy," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:24
verses.text: "Who alone did wonderful things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:25
verses.text: As at the last part of every verse, it is written, "For His mercy endureth for ever," so we must understand at the beginning of each, though it be not written, "Give thanks".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:26
verses.text: Which indeed in the Greek is very plain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:27
verses.text: It would be so in Latin, if our translators had been able to make use of that expression.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:28
verses.text: Which indeed they could have done in this verse, if they had said, "To Him who doeth wonderful things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:29
verses.text: For where we have, "who did wonderful things," the Greek has τῷ ποιήσαντι, where we must necessarily understand, "give thanks".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:30
verses.text: And I would they had added the pronoun, and said to Him, "who did," or to Him "who doeth," or to Him "who made sure;" because then one might easily understand, "let us give thanks".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:31
verses.text: For now it is so obscurely rendered, that he who either knows not or cares not to examine a Greek manuscript may think, "who made the heavens, who made sure the earth, who made the luminaries, for His mercy endureth for ever," has been so said, because He did these things for this reason, "because His mercy endureth for ever:" whereas they, whom He has freed from misery, belong to His Mercy: but not that we should believe that He makes sky, earth, and luminaries, of His Mercy; since they are marks of His Goodness, who created all things very good For He created all things, that they might have their being; but it is the work of His Mer cy, to cleanse us from our sins, and deliver us from everlasting misery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:32
verses.text: And so the Psalm thus addresses us, "Give thanks unto the God of gods, give thanks unto the Lord of lords".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:33
verses.text: Give thanks to Him, "who alone doeth great wonders;" give thanks to Him, "who by His wisdom made the heavens;" give thanks to Him, "who stretched out the earth above the waters;" give thanks to Him, "who alone made great lights".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:34
verses.text: But why we are to praise, he setteth down at the end of all the verses, "for His mercy endureth for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:35
verses.text: But what meaneth, "who alone doeth great wonders"? Is it because many wonderful things He hath done by means of angels and men? Some wonderful things there are which God doeth alone, and these he enumerates, saying, "who by His wisdom made the heavens" , "who stretched out the earth above the waters" , "who alone made great lights".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:36
verses.text: For this reason did he add "alone" in this verse also, because the other wonders which he is about to tell of, God did by means of man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:37
verses.text: For having said, "who alone made great lights," he goes on to explain what these are, "the sun to rule the day" , "the moon and stars to govern the night" ; then he begins to tell the wonders which He did by means of angels and men: "who smote Egypt with their first-born" , and the rest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:38
verses.text: The whole creation then God manifestly made, not by means of any creature, but "alone;" and of this creation he hath mentioned certain more eminent parts, that they might make us think on the whole; the heavens we can understand, and the earth we see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:39
verses.text: And as there are visible heavens too, by mentioning the lights in them, he has bid us look on the whole body of the heavens as made by Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:40
verses.text: However, whether by what he saith, "who made the heavens in understanding," or, as others have rendered it, "in intelligence," he meant to signify, the heavens we can understand, or that He in His understanding or intelligence, that is, in His wisdom made the heavens (as it is elsewhere written, "in wisdom hast Thou made them all"), implying thereby the only-begotten Word, may be a question.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:41
verses.text: But if it be so, that we are to understand that "God by His wisdom made the heavens," why saith He this only of the heavens, whereas God made all things by the same wisdom? It is that it needed only to be expressed there, so that in the rest it might be understood without being written.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:42
verses.text: How then could it be "alone," if "in understanding" or "in intelligence" means "by His wisdom," that is, by the only-begotten Word? Is it that, inasmuch as the Trinity is not three Gods, but one God, he states that God made these things alone, because He made not creation by means of any creature?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:43
verses.text: But what is, "who laid out the earth above the waters"? For it is a difficult question, because the earth seemeth to be the heavier, so that it should be believed not so much to be borne on the waters, as to bear the waters.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:44
verses.text: And that we may not seem contentiously to maintain our Scriptures against those who think that they have discovered these matters on sure principles, we have a second interpretation to give, that the earth which is inhabited by men, and contains the living creatures of the earth, is "laid out above the waters" because it stands out above the waters which surround it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:45
verses.text: For when we speak of a city on the sea being built "above the waters," it is not meant that the sea is under it in the same way as the waters are under the chambers of caverns, or under ships sailing over them; but it is said to be "above" the sea, because it stands up above the sea below it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:46
verses.text: But if these words further signify something else which more closely concerns us, God "by His wisdom made the heavens," that is, His saints, spiritual men, to whom He has given not only to believe, but also to understand things divine; those who cannot yet attain to this, and only hold their faith firmly, as being beneath the heavens, are figured by the name of earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:47
verses.text: And because they abide with unshaken belief upon the baptism they have received, therefore it is said, "He laid out the earth above the waters".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:48
verses.text: Further, since it is written of our Lord Jesus Christ, that "in Him are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge," and that these two, wisdom and knowledge, differ somewhat from one another is testified by other utterances of Scripture, especially in the words of holy Job, where both are in a manner defined; not unsuitably then do we understand wisdom to consist in the knowledge and love of That which ever is and abideth unchangeable, which is God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:49
verses.text: For where he saith, "piety is wisdom," in Greek is θεοσ™βεια, and to express the whole of this in Latin, we may call it worship of God But to depart from evil, which he calls knowledge, what else is it but to walk cautiously and heedfully "in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation," in the night, as it were, of this world, that each one by keeping himself from iniquity may avoid being confounded with the darkness, distinguished by the light of his proper gift.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:50
verses.text: "Who brought out Israel from the midst of them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:51
verses.text: He brought out also His saints and faithful ones from the midst of the wicked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:52
verses.text: "With a mighty Hand and stretched-out Arm".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:53
verses.text: What more powerful, what more out-stretched, than that of which is said "To whom is the Arm of the Lord revealed?" "Who divided the Red Sea in two parts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:54
verses.text: He divided also in such wise, that the same baptism should be to some unto life, to others unto death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:55
verses.text: "And brought out Israel through the midst of it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:56
verses.text: So too He brings out His renewed people through the laver of regeneration.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:57
verses.text: "And overthrew Pharaoh and his power in the Red Sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:58
verses.text: He quickly destroyeth both the sin of His people and the guilt thereof by baptism.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:59
verses.text: "Who led His people through the wilderness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:60
verses.text: Us too He leadeth through the drought and barrenness of this world, that we perish not therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:61
verses.text: "Who smote great kings" , "and slew famous kings".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:62
verses.text: From us too He smites and slays the deadly powers of the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:63
verses.text: "Sehon king of the Amorites" , an "useless shoot," or "fiery temptation," for so is Sehon interpreted: the king of "them who cause bitterness," for such is the meaning of Amorites.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:64
verses.text: "And Og, the king of Basan".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:65
verses.text: The "heaper-together," such is the meaning of Og, and, king of "confusion," which Basan signifies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:66
verses.text: For what else doth the devil heap together but confusion? "And gave away their land for an heritage" , "even an heritage unto Israel His servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:67
verses.text: For He giveth them, whom once the devil owned, for an heritage to the seed of Abraham, that is, Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:68
verses.text: "Who remembered us in our low estate" , "and redeemed us from our enemies"  by the Blood of His only-begotten Son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:69
verses.text: "Who giveth food to all flesh" , that is, to the whole race of mankind, not Israelites only, but Gentiles too; and of this Food is said, "My Flesh is meat indeed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:70
verses.text: "Give thanks unto the God of Heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:71
verses.text: "Give thanks unto the Lord of lords".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:72
verses.text: For what he here says, "the God of Heaven," I suppose that he meant to express in other words what He had before said, "the God of gods".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:73
verses.text: For what there he subjoined, he has here also repeated.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:74
verses.text: "Give thanks unto the Lord of lords".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:75
verses.text: "But to us there is but one God," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 136:76
verses.text: , "and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by Him;" to whom we confess that "His mercy endureth for ever".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXXVII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:2
verses.text: But to-day we have sung, "By the waters of Babylon we sat down and wept, when we remembered Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:3
verses.text: Observe "the waters of Babylon".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:4
verses.text: "The waters of Babylon" are all things which here are loved, and pass away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:5
verses.text: One man, for example, loveth to practise husbandry, to grow rich thereby, to employ his mind therein, thence to gain pleasure: let him observe the issue, and see that what he hath loved is not a foundation of Jerusalem, but a stream of Babylon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:6
verses.text: Another saith, It is a grand thing to be a soldier: all husbandmen fear those who are soldiers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:7
verses.text: But then other citizens of the holy Jerusalem, understanding their captivity, mark how the natural wishes and the various lusts of men hurry and drag them hither and thither, and drive them into the sea; they see this, and they throw not themselves into the waters of Babylon, but "sit down and weep," either for those who are being carried away by them, or themselves whose deserts have placed them in Babylon, but sitting, that is, humbling themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:8
verses.text: O holy Sion, where all stands firm and nothing flows! Who hath thrown us headlong into this? Why have we left thy Founder and thy society? Behold, placed where all things are flowing and gliding away, scarce one, if he can grasp the tree, shall be snatched from the stream and escape.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:9
verses.text: Humbling ourselves then in our captivity, let us "sit by the waters of Babylon," let us not dare to plunge ourselves in those streams, nor to be proud and lifted up in the evil and sadness of our captivity, but let us sit, and so weep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:10
verses.text: Let us sit "by" the waters, not beneath the waters, of Babylon; such be our humility, that it overwhelm us not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:11
verses.text: Sit "by" the waters, not "in" the waters, not "under" the waters; but yet sit, in humble fashion, talk not as thou wouldest in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:12
verses.text: For many weep with the weeping of Babylon, because they rejoice also with the joy of Babylon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:13
verses.text: When men rejoice at gains and weep at losses, both are of Babylon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:14
verses.text: Thou oughtest to weep, but in the remembrance of Sion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:15
verses.text: If thou weepest in the remembrance of Sion, thou oughtest to weep even when it is well with thee in Babylon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:16
verses.text: "On the willows in the midst thereof we hung up our instruments of music".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:17
verses.text: The citizens of Jerusalem have their "instruments of music," God's Scriptures, God's commands, God's promises, meditation on the life to come; but while they are dwelling "in Babylon," they "hang up their instruments".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:18
verses.text: Willows are unfruitful trees, and here so placed, that no good whatever can be understood of them: elsewhere perhaps there may.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:19
verses.text: Here understand barren trees, growing by the waters of Babylon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:20
verses.text: These trees are watered by the waters of Babylon, and bring forth no fruit; just as there are men greedy, covetous, barren in good works, citizens of Babylon in such wise, that they are even trees of that region; they are fed there by these pleasures of transitory things, as though watered by "the waters of Babylon".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:21
verses.text: Thou seekest fruit of them, and nowhere findest it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:22
verses.text: Therefore by deferring to apply the Scriptures to them, "we hang up our instruments of music upon the willows".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:23
verses.text: For we hold them not worthy to carry our instruments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:24
verses.text: We do not therefore insert our instruments into them and bind them to them, but defer to use them, and so hang them up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:25
verses.text: For the willows are the unfruitful trees of Babylon, fed by temporal pleasures, as by the "waters of Babylon".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:26
verses.text: "For there they that led us captive demanded of us words of songs, and they that led us away, an hymn".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:27
verses.text: They demanded of us words of songs and an hymn, who led us captive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:28
verses.text: We are tempted by the delights of earthly things, and we struggle daily with the suggestions of unlawful pleasures; scarce do we breathe freely even in prayer: we understand that we are captives.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:29
verses.text: But who led us captive? what men? what race? what king? If we are redeemed, we once were captives.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:30
verses.text: Who hath redeemed us? Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:31
verses.text: From whom hath He redeemed us? From the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:32
verses.text: The devil then and his angels led us captive: and they would not lead us, unless we consented.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:33
verses.text: "Those" then "who have led us captive," the devil and his angels, when have they spoken unto us: "Sing us one of the songs of Sion"? What answer we? Babylon beareth thee, Babylon containeth thee, Babylon nourisheth thee, Babylon speaks by thy mouth, thou knowest not to take in save what glitters for the present, thou knowest not how to meditate on things of eternity, thou takest not in what thou askest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:34
verses.text: "How shall we sing the Lord's song in a strange land?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:35
verses.text: Truly, brethren, so it is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:36
verses.text: Begin to wish to preach the truth in such measure as ye know it, and see how needful it is for you to endure such mockers, persecutors of the truth, full of falsehood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:37
verses.text: Reply to them, when they ask of you what they cannot take in, and say in full confidence of your holy song, "How shall we sing the Lord's song in a strange land!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:38
verses.text: But take heed how thou dwellest among them, O people of God, O body of Christ, O high-born band of wanderers (for thy home is not here, but elsewhere), lest when thou lovest them, strivest for their friendship, and fearest to displease such men, Babylon begin to delight thee and thou forget Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:39
verses.text: In fear then of this, see what the Psalmist subjoins, see what follows.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:40
verses.text: "If I forget thee, O Jerusalem" , amid the speeches of those who hold me captive, amid the speeches of treacherous men, amid the speeches of men who ask with ill intent, asking, yet unwilling to learn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:41
verses.text: What then? "If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:42
verses.text: "Let my tongue cleave to my jaws, if I remember not thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:43
verses.text: That is, let me be dumb, he saith, if I remember not thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:44
verses.text: For what word, what sound doth he utter, who uttereth not songs of Sion? That is our tongue, the song of Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:45
verses.text: The song of the love of this world is a strange tongue, a barbarous tongue, which we have learnt in our captivity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:46
verses.text: Dumb then will he be to God, who forgetteth Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:47
verses.text: And it is not enough to remember: for her enemies too remember her, desiring to overthrow her.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:48
verses.text: "What is that city?" say they; "who are the Christians? what sort of men are the Christians? would they were not Christians".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:49
verses.text: Now the captive band hath conquered its capturers; still they murmur, and rage, and desire to slay the holy city that dwells as a stranger among them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:50
verses.text: Not enough then is it to remember: take heed how thou rememberest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:51
verses.text: For some things we remember in hate, some in love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:52
verses.text: And so, when he had said, "If I forget thee, O Jerusalem," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:53
verses.text: , he added at once, "if I prefer not Jerusalem in the height of my joy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:54
verses.text: For there is the height of joy where we enjoy God, where we are safe of united brotherhood, and the union of citizenship.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:55
verses.text: There no tempter shall assail us, no one be able so much as to urge us on to any allurement: there nought will delight us but good: there all want will die, there perfect bliss will dawn on us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:56
verses.text: Then he turneth to God in prayer against the enemies of that city.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:57
verses.text: "Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:58
verses.text: Edom is the same who is also called Esau: for ye heard just now the words of the Apostle read, "Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:59
verses.text: Esau then signifieth all the carnal, Jacob all the spiritual.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:60
verses.text: All carnal persons are enemies to spiritual persons, for all such, desiring present things, persecute those whom they see to long for things eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:61
verses.text: Against these the Psalmist, looking back to Jerusalem, and beseeching God that he may be delivered from captivity, saith—what? "Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:62
verses.text: Deliver us from carnal men, from those who imitate Esau, who are elder brethren, yet enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:63
verses.text: They were first-born, but the last-born have won the pre-eminence, for the lust of the flesh hath cast down the former, the contempt of lust hath lifted up the latter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:64
verses.text: The other live, and envy, and persecute.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:65
verses.text: "In the day of Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:66
verses.text: The day of Jerusalem, wherein it was tried, wherein it was held captive, or the day of Jerusalem's happiness, wherein it is freed, wherein it reaches its goal, wherein it is made partaker of eternity? "Remember," saith he, "O Lord," forget not those "who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:67
verses.text: Remember then, it means, that day wherein they willed to overthrow Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:68
verses.text: For how great persecutions hath the Church suffered! How did the children of Edom, that is, carnal men, servants of the devil and his angels, who worshipped stocks and stones, and followed the lusts of the flesh, how did they say, "Extirpate the Christians, destroy the Christians, let not one remain, overthrow them even to the foundation!" Have not these things been said? And when they were said, the persecutors were rejected, the martyrs crowned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:69
verses.text: Then he turneth himself to her, "O daughter of Babylon, unhappy;" unhappy in thy very exulting, thy presumption, thine enmity; "unhappy daughter of Babylon!".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:70
verses.text: The city is called both Babylon, and daughter of Babylon: just as they speak of "Jerusalem" and "the daughter of Jerusalem," "Sion" and "the daughter of Sion," "the Church" and "the daughter of the Church".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:71
verses.text: As it succeedeth the other, it is called "daughter;" as it is preferred before the other, it is called "mother".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:72
verses.text: There was a former Babylon; did the people remain in it? Because it succeedeth to Babylon, it is called daughter of Babylon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:73
verses.text: O daughter of Babylon, "unhappy" thou!.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:74
verses.text: "Happy shall h e be that repayeth thee, as thou hast served us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:75
verses.text: What repayment meaneth he? Herewith the Psalm closeth, "Happy, that taketh and dasheth thy little ones against the rock".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:76
verses.text: Her he calleth unhappy, but him happy who payeth her as she hath served us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:77
verses.text: Do we ask, what reward? This is the repayment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:78
verses.text: For what hath that Babylon done to us? We have already sung in another Psalm, "The words of the wicked have prevailed against us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:79
verses.text: For when we were born, the confusion of this world found us, and choked us while yet infants with the empty notions of divers errors.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:80
verses.text: The infant that is born destined to be a citizen of Jerusalem, and in God's predestination already a citizen, but meanwhile a prisoner for a time, when learneth he to love ought, save what his parents have whispered into his ears? They teach him and train him in avarice, robbery, daily lying, the worship of divers idols and devils, the unlawful remedies of enchantments and amulets.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:81
verses.text: What shall one yet an infant do, a tender soul, observing what its elders do, save follow that which it seeth them doing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:82
verses.text: Babylon then has persecuted us when little, but God hath given us when grown up knowledge of ourselves, that we should not follow the errors of our parents.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:83
verses.text: How shall they repay her? As she hath served us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:84
verses.text: Let her little ones be choked in turn: yea let her little ones in turn be dashed, and die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:85
verses.text: What are the little ones of Babylon? Evil desires at their birth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:86
verses.text: For there are, who have to fight with inveterate lusts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:87
verses.text: When lust is born, before evil habit giveth it strength against thee, when lust is little, by no means let it gain the strength of evil habit; when it is little, dash it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:88
verses.text: But thou fearest, lest though dashed it die not; "Dash it against the Rock; and that Rock is Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:89
verses.text: Brethren, let not your instruments of music rest in your work: sing one to another songs of Sion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:90
verses.text: Readily have ye heard; the more readily do what ye have heard, if ye wish not to be willows of Babylon fed by its streams, and bringing no fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:91
verses.text: But sigh for the everlasting Jerusalem: whither your hope goeth before, let your life follow; there we shall be with Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:92
verses.text: Christ now is our Head; now He ruleth us from above; in that city He will fold us to Himself; we shall be equal to the Angels of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:93
verses.text: We should not dare to imagine this of ourselves, did not the Truth promise it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:94
verses.text: This then desire, brethren, this day and night think on.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:95
verses.text: Howsoever the world shine happily on you, presume not, parley not willingly with your lusts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:96
verses.text: Is it a grown-up enemy? let it be slain upon the Rock.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:97
verses.text: Is it a little enemy? let it be dashed against the Rock.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:98
verses.text: Slay the grown-up ones on the Rock, and dash the little ones against the Rock.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:99
verses.text: Let the Rock conquer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:100
verses.text: Be built upon the Rock, if ye desire not to be swept away either by the stream, or the winds, or the rain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:101
verses.text: If ye wish to be armed against temptations in this world, let longing for the everlasting Jerusalem grow and be strengthened in your hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 137:102
verses.text: Your captivity will pass away, your happiness will come; the last enemy shall be destroyed, and we shall triumph with our King, without death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXXVIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:2
verses.text: The title of this Psalm is brief and simple, and need not detain us; since we know whose resemblance David wore, and since in him we recognise ourselves also, for we too are members of that Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:3
verses.text: The whole tit le is, "To David himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:4
verses.text: Let us see then, what is to David himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:5
verses.text: The title of the Psalm is wont to tell us what is treated of within it: but in this, since the title informs us not of this, but tells us only to Whom it is chanted, the first verse tells us what is treated of in the whole Psalm, "I will confess to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:6
verses.text: This confession then let us hear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:7
verses.text: But first I remind you, that the term confession in Scripture, when we speak of confession to God, is used in two senses, of sin, and of praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:8
verses.text: But confession of sin all know, confession of praise few attend to.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:9
verses.text: So well known is confession of sin, that, wherever in Scripture we hear the words, "I will confess to Thee, O Lord," or, "we will confess to Thee," forthwith, through habitually understanding in this way, our hands hurry to beating our breast: so entirely are men wont not to understand confession to be of aught, save of sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:10
verses.text: But was then our Lord Jesus Christ Himself too a sinner, who saith in the Gospel, "I confess to Thee, Father, Lord of heaven and earth"? He goeth on to say what He confesseth, that we might understand His confession to be of praise, not of sin, "I confess to Thee, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:11
verses.text: He praised the Father, he praised God, because He despiseth not the humble, but the proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:12
verses.text: And such confession are we now going to hear, of praise of God, of thanksgiving.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:13
verses.text: "With my whole heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:14
verses.text: My whole heart I lay upon the altar of Thy praise, an whole burnt-offering of praise I offer to Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:15
verses.text: "I will confess to Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart: for Thou hast heard the words of my mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:16
verses.text: What mouth, save my heart? For there have we the voice which God heareth, which ear of man knoweth not at all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:17
verses.text: We have then a mouth within, there do we ask, thence do we ask, and if we have prepared a lodging or an house for God, there do we speak, there are we heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:18
verses.text: "For He is not far from every one of us, for in Him we live, and move, and have our being".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:19
verses.text: Nought maketh thee far off from God, save sin only.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:20
verses.text: Cast down the middle wall of sin, and thou art with Him whom thou askest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:21
verses.text: "And before the Angels will I sing unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:22
verses.text: Not before men will I sing, but before the Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:23
verses.text: My song is my joy; but my joy in things below is before men, my joy in things above before the Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:24
verses.text: For the wicked knoweth not the joy of the just: "There is no joy, saith my God, to the wicked".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:25
verses.text: The wicked rejoiceth in his tavern, the martyr in his chain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:26
verses.text: In what did that holy Crispina rejoice, whose festival is kept to-day? She rejoiced when she was being seized, when she was being carried before the judge, when she was being put into prison, when she was being brought forth bound, when she was being lifted up on the scaffold, when she was being heard, when she was being condemned: in all these things she rejoiced; and the wretches thought her wretched, when she was rejoicing before the Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:27
verses.text: "I will worship toward Thy holy Temple".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:28
verses.text: What holy Temple? That where we shall dwell, where we shall worship.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:29
verses.text: For we hasten that we may adore.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:30
verses.text: Our heart is pregnant and cometh to the birth, and seeketh where it may bring forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:31
verses.text: What is the place where God is to be worshipped?"The Temple of God is holy," saith the Apostle, "which Temple ye are".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:32
verses.text: But assuredly, as is manifest, God dwelleth in the Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:33
verses.text: Therefore when our joy, being in spiritual things, not in earthly, taketh up a song to God, to sing before the Angels, that very assembly of Angels is the Temple of God, we worship toward God's Temple.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:34
verses.text: There is a Church below, there is a Church above also; the Church below, in all the faithful; the Church above, in all the Angels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:35
verses.text: But the God of Angels came down to the Church below, and Angels ministered to Him on earth, while He ministered to us; for, "I came not," saith He, "to be ministered unto, but to minister".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:36
verses.text: The Lord of Angels died for man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:37
verses.text: Therefore, "I will worship toward Thy holy Temple;" I mean, not the temple made with hands, but that which Thou hast made for Thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:38
verses.text: "And I will confess to Thy Name in Thy mercy and Thy truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:39
verses.text: These also which Thou hast given to me, do I according to my power give to Thee in return: mercy, in aiding others; truth, in judging.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:40
verses.text: By these God aideth us, by these we win God's favour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:41
verses.text: Rightly, therefore, "All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:42
verses.text: No other ways are there whereby He can come to us, no other whereby we can come to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:43
verses.text: "For Thou hast magnified Thy holy Name over everything".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:44
verses.text: What sort of thanksgiving is this, brethren? He hath magnified His holy Name over Abraham.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:45
verses.text: Of Abraham was born Isaac; over that house God was magnified; then Jacob; God was magnified, who said, "I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:46
verses.text: Then came his twelve sons.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:47
verses.text: The name of the Lord was magnified over Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:48
verses.text: Then came the Virgin Mary.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:49
verses.text: Then Christ our Lord, "dying for our sins, rising again for our justification,"  filling the faithful with His Holy Spirit, sending forth men to proclaim throughout the Gentiles, "Repent ye," etc Behold, "He hath magnified His holy Name above all things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:50
verses.text: "In what day soever I call upon Thee, do Thou quickly hear me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:51
verses.text: Wherefore, "quickly"? Because Thou hast said, "While yet thou art speaking I will say, Lo, here I am".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:52
verses.text: Wherefore, "quickly"? Because now I seek not earthly happiness, I have learnt holy longings from the New Testament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:53
verses.text: I seek not earth, nor earthly abundance, nor temporal health, nor the overthrow of my enemies, nor riches, nor rank: nought of these do I seek: therefore "quickly hear me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:54
verses.text: Since Thou hast taught me what to seek, grant what I seek.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:55
verses.text: Let us see then what he seeketh, with what right he hath said, "quickly hear me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:56
verses.text: For what seekest thou, that thou shouldest quickly be heard? "Thou shalt multiply me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:57
verses.text: In many ways may multiplication be understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:58
verses.text: For men are multiplied in their soul with cares: a man seemeth to be multiplied in soul, in whom vices even are multiplied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:59
verses.text: That is the multiplication of want, not of fulness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:60
verses.text: What then dost thou desire, thou who hast said, "quickly hear me," and hast withdrawn thyself entirely from the body, from every earthly thing, from every earthly desire, so as to say to God, "Thou shalt multiply me in my soul"? Explain yet further what thou desirest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:61
verses.text: Thou shalt multiply me, saith he, in my soul "with virtue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:62
verses.text: "Let all the kings of the earth confess to Thee, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:63
verses.text: So shall it be, and so it is, and that daily; and it is shown that it was not said in vain, save that it was future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:64
verses.text: But neither let them, when they confess to Thee, when they praise Thee, desire earthly things of Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:65
verses.text: For what shall the kings of the earth desire? Have they not already sovereignty? Whatever more a man desire on earth, sovereignty is the highest point of his desire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:66
verses.text: What more can he desire? It must needs be some loftier eminence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:67
verses.text: But perhaps the loftier it is, the more dangerous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:68
verses.text: And therefore the more exalted kings are in earthly eminence, the more ought they to humble themselves before God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:69
verses.text: What do they do? "Because they have heard all the words of Thy mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:70
verses.text: In a certain nation were hidden the Law and the Prophets, "all the words of Thy mouth:" in the Jewish nation alone were "all the words of Thy mouth," the nation which the Apostle praiseth, saying, "What advantage hath the Jew? Much every way; chiefly because that unto them were committed the oracles of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:71
verses.text: These were the words of GodWhat meant Gideon's fleece? It is like the nation of the Jews in the midst of the world, which had the grace of sacraments, not indeed openly manifested, but hidden in a cloud, or in a veil, like the dew in the fleece The time came when the dew was to be manifested in the floor; it was manifested, no longer hidden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:72
verses.text: Christ alone is the sweetness of dew: Him alone thou recognisest not in Scripture, for whom Scripture was written.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:73
verses.text: But yet, "they have heard all the words of thy mouth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:74
verses.text: "And let them sing in the paths of the Lord, that great is the glory of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:75
verses.text: Let all the kings of the earth sing in the paths of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:76
verses.text: In what paths? Those that are spoken of above, "in Thy mercy and Thy truth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:77
verses.text: Let not then the kings of the earth be proud, let them be humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:78
verses.text: Then let them sing in the ways of the Lord, if they be humble: let them love, and they shall sing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:79
verses.text: We know travellers that sing; they sing, and hasten to reach the end of their journey.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:80
verses.text: There are evil songs, such as belong to the old man; to the new man belongeth a new song.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:81
verses.text: Let then the kings of the earth too walk in Thy paths, let them walk and sing in Thy paths.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:82
verses.text: Sing what? that "great is the glory of the Lord," not of kings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:83
verses.text: See how he willed that kings should sing on their way, humbly bearing the Lord, not lifting themselves up against the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:84
verses.text: For if they lift themselves up, what follows? "For the Lord is high, and hath respect unto the lowly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:85
verses.text: Do kings then desire that He have respect unto them? Let them be humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:86
verses.text: What then? if they lift themselves up to pride, can they escape His eyes? Lest perchance, because thou hast heard, "He hath respect unto the lowly," thou choose to be proud, and say in thy soul, God hath respect unto the lowly, He hath not respect unto me, I will do what I will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:87
verses.text: O foolish one! wouldest thou say this, if thou knewest what thou oughtest to love? Behold, even if God willeth not to see thee, dost thou not fear this very thing, that He willeth not to see thee?The lofty then, it seemeth, He hath not respect unto, for it is the lowly He respecteth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:88
verses.text: "The lofty"—what? "He considereth from afar".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:89
verses.text: What then gaineth the proud? To be seen from afar, not to escape being seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:90
verses.text: And think not that thou must needs be safe on that account, for that He seeth less clearly, who seeth thee from afar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:91
verses.text: For thou indeed seest not clearly, what thou seest from afar; God, although He see thee from afar, seeth thee perfectly, yet is He not with thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:92
verses.text: This thou gainest, not that thou art less perfectly seen, but that thou art not with Him by whom thou art seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:93
verses.text: But what doth the lowly gain? "The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:94
verses.text: Let the proud then lift himself up as much as he will, certainly God dwelleth on high, God is in heaven: wishest thou that He come nigh to thee? Humble thyself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:95
verses.text: For the higher will He be above thee, the more thou liftest thyself up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:96
verses.text: "If I walk in the midst of tribulation, Thou shalt revive me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:97
verses.text: True it is: whatsoever tribulation thou art in, confess, call on Him; He freeth thee, He reviveth thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:98
verses.text: Love the other life, and thou shalt see that this life is tribulation, whatever prosperity it shine with, whatever delights it abound and overflow with; since not yet have we that joy most safe and free from all temptation, which God reserveth for us in the end, without doubt it is tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:99
verses.text: Let us understand then what tribulation he meaneth here too, brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:100
verses.text: Not as though he said, "If perchance there shall any tribulation have befallen me, Thou shalt free me therefrom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:101
verses.text: But how saith he? "If I walk," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:102
verses.text: ; that is, otherwise Thou wilt not revive me, unless I walk in the midst of tribulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:103
verses.text: "Thou hast stretched forth Thine hand over the wrath of mine enemies, and Thy right hand hath made me safe".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:104
verses.text: Let mine enemies rage: what can they do? They can take my money, strip, proscribe, banish me; afflict me with grief and tortures; at last, if they be allowed, even kill me: can they do aught more? But over that which mine enemies can do, Thou hast stretched forth Thine hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:105
verses.text: For mine enemies cannot separate me from Thee: but Thou avengest me the more, the more Thou as yet delayest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:106
verses.text: Yet not to make me despair; for it follows, "and Thy right hand hath made me safe".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:107
verses.text: "Thou, Lord, shalt recompense for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:108
verses.text: I recompense not: Thou shalt recompense.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:109
verses.text: Let mine enemies rage their full: Thou shalt recompense what I cannot.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:110
verses.text: "Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves," saith the Apostle, "but rather give place unto wrath; for it is written, Vengeance is Mine, I will repay, saith the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:111
verses.text: There is here another sense not to be neglected, perhaps even to be preferred.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:112
verses.text: "Lord" Christ, "Thou shalt repay for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:113
verses.text: For I, if I repay, have seized; Thou hast paid what Thou hast not seized.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:114
verses.text: Lord, Thou shalt "repay for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:115
verses.text: Behold Him repaying for us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:116
verses.text: They came to Him, who exacted tribute: they used to demand as tribute a didrachma, that is, two drachmas for one man; they came to the Lord to pay tribute; or rather, not to Him, but to His disciples, and they said to them, "Doth not your Master pay tribute?" They came and told Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:117
verses.text: He saith unto Peter, "lest we should offend them, go thou to the sea, and cast an hook, and take up the fish that first cometh up: and when thou hast opened his mouth, thou shalt find a stater:  that take, and give for Me and thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:118
verses.text: The first that riseth from the sea, is the First-begotten from the dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:119
verses.text: In His mouth we find two didrachmas, that is, four drachmas: in His mouth we find the four Gospels.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:120
verses.text: By those four drachmas we are free from the claims of this world, by the four Evangelists we remain no longer debtors; for there the debt of all our sins is paid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:121
verses.text: He then hath repaid for us, thanks to His mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:122
verses.text: He owed nothing: He repaid not for Himself: He repaid for us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:123
verses.text: "Lord, Thy mercy is for everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:124
verses.text: Not for a time only do I desire to be freed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:125
verses.text: "Thy mercy is for everlasting," wherewith Thou hast freed the martyrs, and so hast quickly taken them from this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:126
verses.text: "Despise not Thou the works of Thine own hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:127
verses.text: I say not, Lord, "despise not the works of my hands:" of mine own works I boast not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:128
verses.text: "I sought," indeed, "the Lord with my hands in the night season before Him, and have not been deceived;" but yet I praise not the works of mine own hands; I fear lest, when Thou shalt look into them, Thou find more sins in them than deserts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:129
verses.text: Behold in me Thy Work, not mine: for mine if Thou seest, Thou condemnest; Thine, if Thou seest, Thou crownest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 138:130
verses.text: For whatever good works there be of mine, from Thee are they to me; and so they are more Thine than mine Therefore whether in regard that we are men, or in regard that we have been changed and justified from our iniquity, Lord, "despise not Thou the works of Thine own hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:1
verses.text: Psalm CXXXIX.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:2
verses.text: Our Lord Jesus Christ speaketh in the Prophets, sometimes in His own Name, sometimes in ours, because He maketh Himself one with us; as it is said, "they twain shall be one flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:3
verses.text: Wherefore also the Lord saith in the Gospel, speaking of marriage, "therefore they are no more twain, but one flesh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:4
verses.text: One flesh, because of our mortality He took flesh; not one divinity, for He is the Creator, we the creature.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:5
verses.text: Whatsoever then our Lord speaketh in the person of the Flesh He took upon Him, belongeth both to that Head which hath already ascended into heaven, and to those members which still toil in their earthly wandering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:6
verses.text: Let us hear then our Lord Jesus Christ speaking in prophecy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:7
verses.text: For the Psalms were sung long before the Lord was born of Mary, yet not before He was Lord: for from everlasting He was the Creator of all things, but in time He was born of His creature.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:8
verses.text: Let us believe that Godhead, and, so far as we can, understand Him to be equal to the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:9
verses.text: But that Godhead equal to the Father was made partaker of our mortal nature, not of His own store, but of ours; that we too might be made partakers of His Divine Nature, not of our store, but of His.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:10
verses.text: "Lord, Thou hast tried me, and known me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:11
verses.text: Let the Lord Jesus Christ Himself say this; let Him too say, "Lord," to the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:12
verses.text: For His Father is not His Lord, save because He hath deigned to be born according to the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:13
verses.text: He is Father of the God, Lord of the Man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:14
verses.text: Wouldest thou know to whom He is Father? To the coequal Son.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:15
verses.text: The Apostle saith, "Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:16
verses.text: To this "Form" God is Father, the "Form" equal to Himself, the only-begotten Son, begotten of His Substance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:17
verses.text: But forasmuch as for our sakes, that we might be re-made, and made partakers of His Divine Nature, being renewed unto life eternal, He was made partaker of our mortal nature, what saith the Apostle of Him? He saith, "yet He emptied Himself, and took upon Him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men, and was found in fashion as a man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:18
verses.text: He was in the Form of God, equal to the Father; He took upon Him the form of a servant, so as therein to be less than the Father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:19
verses.text: "Thou hast known My down-sitting and Mine up-rising".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:20
verses.text: What here is "down-sitting," what "up-rising"? He who sitteth, humbleth himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:21
verses.text: The Lord then "sat" in His Passion, "up-rose" in His Resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:22
verses.text: "Thou," he saith, hast known this; that is, Thou hast willed, Thou hast approved; according to Thy will was it done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:23
verses.text: But if thou choosest to take the words of the Head in the person of the Body: man sitteth when he humbleth himself in penitence, he riseth up when his sins are forgiven, and he is lifted up to the hope of everlasting life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:24
verses.text: Lift not up yourselves, unless ye have first been humbled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:25
verses.text: For many wish to rise before they have sat down, they wish to appear righteous, before they have confessed that they are sinners.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:26
verses.text: "Thou hast understood my thoughts from afar; Thou hast tracked out my path and my limit" ; "and all my ways Thou hast seen beforehand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:27
verses.text: What is, "from afar"? While I am yet in my pilgrimage, before I reach that, my true country, Thou hast known my thoughts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:28
verses.text: The younger son went into a far country.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:29
verses.text: After his toil and suffering and tribulation and want, he thought on his father, and desired to return, and said, "I will arise, and go to my father".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:30
verses.text: "I will arise," said he, for before he had sat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:31
verses.text: Here then thou mayest recognise him saying, "Thou hast known my down-sitting and up-rising".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:32
verses.text: I sat, in want; I arose, in longing for Thy Bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:33
verses.text: "Thou hast understood my thoughts from afar".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:34
verses.text: For far indeed had I gone; but where is not He whom I had left? Wherefore the Lord saith in the Gospel, that his father met him as he was coming.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:35
verses.text: Truly; for "he had understood his thoughts from afar".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:36
verses.text: "My path," he saith; what, but a bad path, the path he had walked to leave his father?What is, "my path"? that by which I have gone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:37
verses.text: What is, "my limit"? that whereunto I have reached.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:38
verses.text: "Thou hast tracked out my path and my limit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:39
verses.text: That limit of mine, far distant as it was, was not far from Thine eyes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:40
verses.text: Far had I gone, and yet Thou wast there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:41
verses.text: "And all my ways Thou hast seen beforehand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:42
verses.text: He said not, "hast seen," but, "hast seen beforehand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:43
verses.text: Before I went by them, before I walked in them, Thou didst see them beforehand; and Thou didst permit me in toil to go my own ways, that, if I desired not to toil, I might return into Thy ways.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:44
verses.text: "For there is no deceit in my tongue".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:45
verses.text: What meant he by this? Lo, I confess to Thee, I have walked in my own way, I am become far from Thee, I have departed from Thee, with whom it was well with me, and to my good it was ill with me without Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:46
verses.text: "Behold Thou, Lord, hast known all my last doings, and the ancient ones".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:47
verses.text: Thou hast known my latest doings, when I fed swine; Thou hast known my ancient doings, when I asked of Thee my portion of goods.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:48
verses.text: Ancient doings were the beginnings to me of latest ills: ancient sin, when we fell; latest punishment, when we came into this toilsome and dangerous mortality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:49
verses.text: And would that this may be "latest" to us; it will be, if now we will to return.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:50
verses.text: For there is another "latest" for certain wicked ones, to whom it shall be said, "Go ye into everlasting fire".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:51
verses.text: "Thou hast fashioned me, and hast laid Thine hand upon me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:52
verses.text: "Fashioned me," where? In this mortality; now, to the toils whereunto we all are born.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:53
verses.text: For none is born, but God has fashioned him in his mother's womb; nor is there any creature, whereof God is not the Fashioner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:54
verses.text: But "Thou hast fashioned me" in this toil, "and laid Thine hand upon me," Thine avenging hand, putting down the proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:55
verses.text: For thus healthfully hath He cast down the proud, that He may lift him up humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:56
verses.text: "Thy skill hath displayed itself wonderfully in me: it hath waxed mighty: I shall not be able to attain unto it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:57
verses.text: Listen now and hear somewhat, which is obscure indeed, yet bringeth no small pleasure in the understanding thereon.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:58
verses.text: Moses, the holy servant of God, with whom God spake by a cloud, for, speaking after human fashion, He must needs speak to His servant through some work of His hands which He assumed,longed and desired to see the true appearance of God, and said to God, who was conversing with him, "If now I have found grace in Thy sight, show me Thyself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:59
