verses.text: When this he desired vehemently, and would extort from God in that sort of friendly familiarity, if we may so speak, wherewith God deigned to treat him, that he might see His Glory and His Face, in such wise as we can speak of God's Face, He said unto him, "Thou canst not see My Face; for no one hath seen My Face, and lived;" but I will place thee in a clift of the rock, and will pass by, and will set My hand upon thee; and when I have passed by, thou shalt see My back parts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:60
verses.text: And from these words there ariseth another enigma, that is, an obscure figure of the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:61
verses.text: "When I have passed by," saith God, "thou shalt see My back parts;" as though He hath on one side His face, on another His back.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:62
verses.text: Far be it from us to have any such thoughts of that Majesty! For whoso hath such thoughts of God, what advantageth it him that the temples are closed? He is building an idol in his own heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:63
verses.text: In these words then are mighty mysteries.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:64
verses.text: They who raged against the Lord, whom they saw, now seek counsel how they may be saved; and it is said to them, "Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the Name of Jesus Christ, and your sins shall be forgiven you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:65
verses.text: Behold, they saw the back parts of Him, whose face they could not see.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:66
verses.text: For His Hand was upon their eyes, not for ever, but while He passed by.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:67
verses.text: After He had passed He took away His Hand from their eyes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:68
verses.text: When the hand was taken from their eyes, they say to the disciples, "What shall we do?" At first they are fierce, afterwards loving; at first angry, afterwards fearful; at first hard, then pleasant; at first blind, then enlightened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:69
verses.text: Behold thou findest that the runaway in a far country cannot escape His eyes, from whom he fleeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:70
verses.text: And whither can he go now, whose "limit is tracked out"? Behold, what saith he? "Whither shall I go from Thy Spirit?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:71
verses.text: Who can in the world flee from that Spirit, with whom the world is filled? "And whither shall I flee from Thy Face?" He seeketh a place whither to flee from the wrath of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:72
verses.text: What place will shelter God's runaway? Men who shelter runaways, ask them from whom they have fled; and when they find any one a slave of some master less powerful than themselves, him they shelter as it were without any fear, saying in their hearts, "he hath not a master by whom he can be tracked out".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:73
verses.text: But when they are told of a powerful master, they either shelter not, or they shelter with great fear, because even a powerful man can be deceived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:74
verses.text: Where is God not? Who can deceive God? Whom doth not God see? From whom doth not God demand His runaway? Whither then shall that runaway go from the Face of God? He turneth him hither and thither, as though seeking a spot to flee to.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:75
verses.text: "If I go up," saith he, "to heaven, Thou art there: if I go down to Hades, Thou art present".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:76
verses.text: At length, miserable runaway, thou hast learnt, that by no means canst thou make thyself far from Him, from whom thou hast wished to remove far away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:77
verses.text: Behold, He is everywhere; thou, whither wilt thou go? He hath found counsel, and that inspired by Him, who now deigneth to recall him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:78
verses.text: If by sinning I go down to the depths of wickednesses, and spurn to confess, saying, "Who seeth me" (for "in Hades who shall confess to Thee?") there also Thou art present, to punish.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:79
verses.text: Whither then shall I go that I may flee from Thy presence, that is, not find Thee angry? This plan he found: So will I flee, saith he, from Thy Face, so will I flee from Thy Spirit; from Thy avenging Spirit, Thy avenging Face thus will I flee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:80
verses.text: How? "If I take again my wings right forward, and abide in the utmost parts of the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:81
verses.text: So can I flee from Thy Face.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:82
verses.text: If he will flee to the utmost part of the sea from the Face of God, will not He from whom he fleeth be there?For what are "the utmost parts of the sea," but the end of the world? Thither let us now flee in hope and longing, with the wings of twofold love; let us have no rest, save in "the utmost parts of the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:83
verses.text: For if elsewhere we wish for rest, we shall be hurled headlong into the sea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:84
verses.text: Let us fly even to the ends of the sea, let us bear ourselves aloft on the wings of twofold love; meanwhile let us flee to God in hope, and in faithful hope let us meditate on that "end of the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:85
verses.text: Now listen who may bring us thither.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:86
verses.text: The very same One whose face in wrath we wish to flee from.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:87
verses.text: For what followeth? "Even thither shall Thy hand conduct me, and Thy right hand lead me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:88
verses.text: This let us meditate on, beloved brethren, let this be our hope, this our consolation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:89
verses.text: Let us take again through love the wings we lost through lust.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:90
verses.text: For lust was the lime of our wings, it clashed us down from the freedom of our sky, that is, the free breezes of the Spirit of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:91
verses.text: Thence dashed down we lost our wings, and were, so to speak, imprisoned in the power of the fowler; thence "He" redeemed us with His Blood, whom we fled from to be caught.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:92
verses.text: He maketh us wings of His commandments; we raise them aloft now free from lime.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:93
verses.text: Needs then must we have wings, and needs must He conduct us, for He is our Helper.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:94
verses.text: We have free-will; but even with that free-will what can we do, unless He help us who commandeth us?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:95
verses.text: And considering the length of the way, what said he to himself? "And I said, Peradventure the darkness shall overwhelm me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:96
verses.text: Lo, now I have believed in Christ, now am I wafted aloft on the wings of twofold love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:97
verses.text: Regarding the length of the way, I said to myself, "And the night was light in my delight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:98
verses.text: The night was made to me light, because in the night I despaired of being able to cross so great a sea, to surmount so long a journey, to reach the utmost parts by persevering to the end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:99
verses.text: Thanks to Him who sought me when a runaway, who smote my back with strokes of the scourge, who by calling me recalled me from destruction, who made my night light.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:100
verses.text: For it is night so long as we are passing through this life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:101
verses.text: How was the night made light? Because Christ came down into the night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:102
verses.text: "For darkness shall not be darkened by Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:103
verses.text: Do not thou then darken thy darkness; God darkeneth it not, but enlighteneth it yet more; for to Him is said in another Psalm, "Thou, Lord, shalt light my candle: my God shall enlighten my darkness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:104
verses.text: But who are they who "darken their darkness," which God darkeneth not? Evil men, perverse men; when they sin, verily they are darkness; when they confess not their sins which they have committed but go on to defend them, they "darken their darkness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:105
verses.text: Wherefore now if thou hast sinned thou art in darkness, but by confessing thy darkness thou shalt obtain to have thy darkness lightened; by defending thy darkness, thou shalt "darken thy darkness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:106
verses.text: And where wilt thou escape from double darkness, who wast in difficulty in single darkness?Let us not "darken our darkness" by defending our sins, and "the night shall be light in our delight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:107
verses.text: "And night shall be lightened as the day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:108
verses.text: "Night, as the day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:109
verses.text: "Day" to us is worldly prosperity, night adversity in this world: but, if we learn that it is by the desert of our sins that we suffer adversities, and our Father's scourges are sweet to us, that the Judge's sentence may not be bitter to us, so shall we find the darkness of this night to be, as it were, the light of this night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:110
verses.text: But when Christ our Lord has come, and has dwelt in the soul by faith, and promised other light, and inspired and given patience, and warned a man not to delight in prosperity or to be crushed by adversity, the man, being faithful, begins to treat this world with indifference; not to be lifted up when prosperity befalls him, nor crushed when adversity, but in all things to praise God, not only when he aboundeth, but also when he loseth; not only when he is in health, but also when he is sick"As is His darkness, so is also His light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:111
verses.text: His darkness overwhelms me not, because His light lifts me not up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:112
verses.text: "For Thou, O Lord, hast possessed my reins".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:113
verses.text: The Possessor is within; He occupieth not only the heart, but also the reins; not only the thoughts, but also the delights: He then possesseth that whence I should feel delight at any light in this world: He occupieth my reins: I know not delight, save from the inward light of His Wisdom.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:114
verses.text: What then? Dost thou not delight that thy affairs are very prosperous, times fortunate to thee? dost thou not delight in honour, in riches, in thy family? "I do not," saith he.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:115
verses.text: Wherefore? Because "Thou hast possessed my reins, O Lord; Thou hast taken me up from my mother's womb".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:116
verses.text: While I was in my mother's womb, I did not regard with indifference the darkness of that night and the light of that night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:117
verses.text: Now, having been taken up from the womb of that our mother, we look on them with indifference, and say, "As is His darkness, so is also His light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:118
verses.text: Neither doth earthly prosperity make us happy, nor earthly adversity wretched.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:119
verses.text: We must maintain righteousness, love faith, hope in God, love God, love our neighbours also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:120
verses.text: After these toils we shall have unfailing light, day without setting.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:121
verses.text: Fleeting is all the light and darkness of this night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:122
verses.text: "I will confess to Thee, O Lord, for terribly hast Thou been made wonderful: wondrous are Thy works, and my soul knoweth it right well".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:123
verses.text: Aforetime "Thy knowledge was made wonderful from me, it had waxed great, nor could I attain unto it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:124
verses.text: From me then "it had waxed great".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:125
verses.text: Whence doth "my soul" now "know right well," save because the "night is light in my delight?" save because Thy grace hath come unto me, and enlightened my darkness? save because Thou hast possessed my reins? save because Thou hast taken me up from my mother's womb?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:126
verses.text: "My bone is not hid from Thee, which Thou hast made in secret".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:127
verses.text: "His bone," he saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:128
verses.text: What the people call ossum, is in Latin called os.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:129
verses.text: This is the word in the Greek For we might think the word os is here the one which makes in the plural ora, not os (short), which makes ossa.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:130
verses.text: He saith then, I have a certain bone (ossum) in secret.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:131
verses.text: For this word let us prefer to use; better is it that scholars find fault with us, than that the people understand us not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:132
verses.text: "There is then," saith he, "a certain bone of mine, within, hidden; Thou hast made within a bone for me in secret, yet is it not hidden from Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:133
verses.text: In secret hast Thou made it, but hast Thou therefore hidden it from Thyself? This my bone made by Thee in secret men see not, men know not: Thou knowest, who hast made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:134
verses.text: What "bone" then meaneth he, brethren? Let us seek it, it is "in secret".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:135
verses.text: But because as Christians we are speaking in the Name of the Lord to Christians, now we find what bone is of this kind.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:136
verses.text: It is a sort of inward strength; for strength and fortitude are understood to be in the bones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:137
verses.text: There is then a sort of inward strength of the soul, wherein it is not broken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:138
verses.text: Whatever tortures, whatever tribulations, whatever adversities rage around, that which God hath made strong in secret in us, cannot be broken, yieldeth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:139
verses.text: For by God is made a certain strength of patience, of which is said in another Psalm, "But my soul shall be subjected to God, for of Him is my patience".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:140
verses.text: Wherein dost thou glory? "In tribulations, knowing that tribulation worketh patience".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:141
verses.text: See how that strength is fashioned within in his heart: "because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:142
verses.text: So is fashioned and made strong that hidden bone, that it maketh us even to glory in tribulations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:143
verses.text: But to men we seem wretched, because that which we have within is hidden from them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:144
verses.text: "And my substance is in the lower parts of the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:145
verses.text: Behold, in flesh is my substance, yet have I a bone within, which Thou hast fashioned, such as to cause me never to yield to any persecutions of this lower region, where still my substance is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:146
verses.text: For what great matter is it, if an Angel be brave? This is a great matter, if flesh is brave.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:147
verses.text: And whence is flesh brave, whence is an earthen vessel brave, save because in it is made a bone in secret?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:148
verses.text: "Thine eyes did see Mine imperfect one, and in Thy book shall all be written" , not only the perfect, but also the imperfect.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:149
verses.text: Let not the imperfect fear, only let them advance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:150
verses.text: Nor yet, because I have said, "let them not fear," let them love their imperfection, and remain there, where they are found.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:151
verses.text: Let them advance, as far as in them lieth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:152
verses.text: Daily let them add, daily let them approach; yet let them not fall back from the Body of the Lord: that, compacted in one Body and among these members, they may be counted worthy to have that said of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:153
verses.text: "By day shall they wander, and none among them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:154
verses.text: "The Day" was yet on earth, even our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:155
verses.text: Whence He said, "Walk while ye have the day".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:156
verses.text: But "by day shall" His imperfect ones "wander".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:157
verses.text: They too thought that our Lord Jesus Christ was only man, that He had not within Him the hidden Godhead, that He was not secretly God, but that He was that only which was seen: this they too thought.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:158
verses.text: But what is, "In the day they shall wander"? Shall they perish? Where then is, "In Thy book shall all be written"? When then did they "wander in the day"? When they understood not the Lord set upon earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:159
verses.text: And what followeth? "But to me Thy friends are made very honourable, O God" ; those very ones, who "wandered in the day, and none was in them," became Thy friends, and were made very honourable to me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:160
verses.text: That bone was made in them in secret after the resurrection of the Lord, and they suffered for His Name, at whose death they had been amazed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:161
verses.text: "Mightily strengthened were their chieftainships".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:162
verses.text: They became Apostles, they became leaders of the Church, they became rams leading their flocks, "mightily strengthened".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:163
verses.text: "I will number them, and they shall be multiplied above the sand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:164
verses.text: By means of them, who "wandered in the day," lo! there has been born all this great multitude, which now is like the sand innumerable, save by God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:165
verses.text: For He said, "they shall be multiplied above the sand," and yet He had said, "I will number them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:166
verses.text: The very same who are numbered, "shall be multiplied above the sand".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:167
verses.text: For by Him is the sand numbered, by whom "the very hairs of our head are numbered".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:168
verses.text: "I have risen, and yet am I with Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:169
verses.text: Already have I suffered, saith He, already have I been buried; lo! I have risen, and not yet do they understand that I am with them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:170
verses.text: "Yet am I with Thee," that is, not yet with them, for not yet do they recognise Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:171
verses.text: For thus do we read in the Gospel, that after the resurrection of oar Lord Jesus Christ, when He appeared to them, they did not at once know Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:172
verses.text: There is another meaning also: "I have risen, and yet am I with Thee," as though He would signify this present time, wherein He is as yet hidden at the right hand of the Father, before He is revealed in the brightness, wherein He shall come to judge the quick and the dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:173
verses.text: And then He telleth what meanwhile, during this whole time when He already has risen, and remaineth still with the Father, He suffereth by the intermixture of sinners in His Body, the Church, and by the separation of heretics.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:174
verses.text: "If Thou, O God, shalt slay the sinners (since Thou shalt say in Thy thought, Depart from Me, ye men of blood), they shall receive in vanity their cities" (ver.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:176
verses.text: The words seem to be connected in this order; "If Thou, O God, shall slay the sinners, they shall receive in vanity their cities".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:177
verses.text: Thus are sinners slain, because, "having their understandings darkened, they are alienated from the life of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:178
verses.text: For on account of elation they lose confession, and so they are slain, and in them is fulfilled what Scripture saith, "Confession perisheth from the dead, as from one that is not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:179
verses.text: And so "they receive in vanity their cities," that is, their vain peoples, who follow their vanity; when, puffed up by the name of righteousness, they persuade men to burst the bond of unity, and blindly and ignorantly follow them, as being more righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:180
verses.text: But now the Body of Christ, the Church, saith, Why do the proud speak falsely against me, as though I were stained by other men's sins, and so, by separating themselves, "receive in vanity their cities"? "Have not I hated those who hated Thee, Lord?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:181
verses.text: Why do those who are worse themselves require of me to separate myself in body as well as spirit from the wicked, so as to root up the wheat, together with the tares, before the time of harvest, that before the time of winnowing I lose my power of enduring the chaff; that before all the different sorts of fishes are brought to the end of the world, as to the shore, to be separated, I tear the nets of peace and unity? Are the sacraments which I receive, those of evil men? Do I; by consent, communicate in their life and deeds?But where is, "Love your enemies"? Is it because He said "yours," not "God's"? "Do good to them that hate you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:182
verses.text: He saith not, "who hate God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:183
verses.text: So he followeth the pattern, and saith, "Have not I hated those who hated Thee; Lord?" He saith not, "Who have hated me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:184
verses.text: "And at Thine enemies did I waste away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:185
verses.text: "Thine," he said, not "mine".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:186
verses.text: But those who hate us and are enemies unto us, only because we serve Him, what else do they but hate Him, and are His enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:187
verses.text: Ought we then to love such enemies as these? Or do not they suffer persecution for God's sake, to whom it is said, "Pray for them that persecute you"? Observe then what followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:188
verses.text: "With a perfect hatred did I hate them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:189
verses.text: What is, "with a perfect hatred"? I hated in them their iniquities, I loved Thy creation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:190
verses.text: This it is to hate with a perfect hatred, that neither on account of the vices thou hate the men, nor on account of the men love the vices.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:191
verses.text: For see what he addeth, "They became mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:192
verses.text: Not only as God's enemies, but as his own too doth he now describe them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:193
verses.text: How then will he fulfil in them both his own saying, "Have not I hated those that hated Thee, Lord," and the Lord's command, "Love your enemies"? How will he fulfil this, save with that "perfect hatred," that he hate in them that they are wicked, and love that they are men? For in the time even of the Old Testament, when the carnal people was restrained by visible punishments, how did Moses, the servant of God, who by understanding belonged to the New Testament, how did he hate sinners when he prayed for them, or how did he not hate them when he slew them, save that he "hated them with a perfect hatred"? For with such perfection did he hate the iniquity which he punished, as to love the manhood for which he prayed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:194
verses.text: Since then the Body of Christ is in the end to be severed in body also from the unholy and wicked, but now meanwhile groaneth among them, what doeth the "love of Christ among the daughters, as the lily among thorns"? What are her words? what her conscience? what is the "appearance of the king's daughter within"? Lo, hear what she saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:195
verses.text: "Prove me, O God, and know my heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:196
verses.text: Do Thou, O God, Thou prove me, Thou know; not man, not an heretic, who neither knoweth how to prove, nor can know my heart, whereas Thou provest, and knowest that I consent not to the deeds of the wicked, while they think that I can be defiled by the sins of others; so that, while I in my long wandering do what I mourn in another Psalm, that is, while I "labour for peace among them that hate peace," until I come to that Vision of peace, which is called Jerusalem, "which is the mother of us all," the city "eternal in the heavens;" they, contending, and falsely accusing and separating themselves, may "receive," not, evidently, in eternity, but "in vanity, their cities".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:197
verses.text: Why this? Observe what followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:198
verses.text: "And see," saith he, "if there be any way of wickedness in me, and lead me in the way everlasting".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:199
verses.text: "Search," he saith, "my paths," that is, my counsels and thoughts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:200
verses.text: What else saith he, but "lead me in Christ"? For who is "the way everlasting," save He that is the life everlasting? For everlasting is He who said, "I am the Way, and the Truth, and the Life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:201
verses.text: If then thou findest anything in my way which displeaseth Thine eyes, since my way is mortal, do Thou "lead me in the way everlasting," wherein is no iniquity; for even "if any man sin, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous; and He is the propitiation for our sins;" He is "the Way everlasting" without sin; He is the Life everlasting without punishment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:202
verses.text: These are great mysteries, brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:203
verses.text: How doth the Spirit of God speak with us? how doth it make us delights in this night? What is this, we ask you, brethren, whence are they sweeter, the darker they are? He mixeth us our potion after His love, in certain wondrous ways.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:204
verses.text: He maketh His own sayings wondrous, so that while we were speaking what ye already knew, yet forasmuch as it was dug out of passages which seemed obscure, the knowledge itself seemed to be made new.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 139:205
verses.text: Did ye not know, brethren, that the wicked are to be tolerated in the Church, and schisms not to be made? Did ye not already know, that within those nets which hold both good and bad fishes, we must abide even to the shore, nor must the nets be burst, because on the shore the good shall be separa ted into vessels, and the bad thrown away? Ye know this already; but these verses of this Psalm ye did not understand; that which ye did not understand is explained; that which ye knew has been renewed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:1
verses.text: Psalm CXL.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:2
verses.text: Our Lords have bidden me, brethren, and in them the Lord of all, to bring this Psalm to your understanding, so far as God giveth me to.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:3
verses.text: May He help your prayers, that I may say those things which I ought to say, ye to hear, that to all of us the Word of God may be profitable.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:4
verses.text: For all it doth not profit, for "all have not faith".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:5
verses.text: What this Psalm containeth, I believe that ye perceived when it was being chanted; for therein the Church of Christ, set in the midst of the wicked, complaineth and groaneth, and poureth out prayer to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:6
verses.text: For her voice is in every such prophecy the voice of one in need and want, not yet satisfied, "hungering and thirsting after righteousness," for whom a certain fulness in the end hath been promised, and is reserved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:7
verses.text: "To the end, a Psalm to David himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:8
verses.text: No other end mayest thou look to, than is laid down for thee by the Apostle himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:9
verses.text: For "Christ is the end".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:10
verses.text: He was of the seed of David, not after His Godhead, whereby He is the Creator of David, but after the fle sh; therefore He deigned to be called David in prophecy: look to this "end," for the Psalm is chanted "to David Himself;" hear the voice of His Body; be in His Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:11
verses.text: Let the voice which thou hast heard be thine, and pray, and say what followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:12
verses.text: "Deliver me, O Lord, from the wicked man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:13
verses.text: Not from one only, but from the class; not from the vessels only, but from their prince himself, that is, the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:14
verses.text: Why "from man," if he meaneth from the devil? Because he too is called a man in a figureNow then being made light, not in ourselves, but in the Lord, let us pray not only against darkness, that is, against sinners, whom still the devil possesseth, but also against their prince, the devil himself, who worketh in the children of disobedience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:15
verses.text: "Deliver me from the unrighteous man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:16
verses.text: The same as "from the wicked man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:17
verses.text: For he called him wicked because unrighteous, lest perchance thou shouldest think that any unrighteous man could be a good man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:18
verses.text: For many unrighteous men seem to be harmless; they are not fierce, are not savage, do not persecute nor oppress; yet are they unrighteous, because, following some other habit, they are luxurious, drunkards, given to pleasure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:19
verses.text: Wicked then is every unrighteous man, who must needs be harmful, whether he be gentle or fierce.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:20
verses.text: Whoever falls in his way, whoever is taken by his snares, will find how harmful is that which he thought harmless.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:21
verses.text: For, brethren, even thorns prick not with their roots.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:22
verses.text: Pull up thorns from the ground, handle their roots, and see whether thou feelest pain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:23
verses.text: Yet that in the upgrowth which causeth thee pain, proceeded from that root.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:24
verses.text: Let not then men please you who seem gentle and kind, yet are lovers of carnal pleasure, followers of polluted lusts, let them not please you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:25
verses.text: Though as yet they seem gentle, they are roots of thorns.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:26
verses.text: And so, my brethren, body of Christ, members of Christ groaning among such wicked men, whomsoever ye find hurrying headlong into evil lusts and deadly pleasures, at once chide, at once punish, at once burn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:27
verses.text: Let the root be burnt, and there remaineth not whence the thorn may grow up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:28
verses.text: If ye cannot, be sure that ye will have them as enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:29
verses.text: They may be silent, they may hide their enmity, but they cannot love you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:30
verses.text: But since they cannot love you, and since they who hate you must needs seek your harm, let not your tongue and heart be slow to say to God, "Deliver me, O Lord, from the unrighteous man".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:31
verses.text: "Who have imagined unrighteousnesses in their heart".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:32
verses.text: From them free me, from them let Thy hand be most powerful to deliver me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:33
verses.text: For easy is it to avoid open enmities, easy is it to turn aside from an enemy declared and manifest, while iniquity is in his lips as well as his heart; he is a troublesome enemy, he is secret, he is with difficulty avoided, who beareth good things in his lips, while in his heart he concealeth evil things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:34
verses.text: "All the day long did they make war".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:35
verses.text: What is, "war"? They made for me what I was to fight against all the day.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:36
verses.text: For from thence, from such hearts as these, ariseth all that the Christian fighteth against.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:37
verses.text: Be it sedition, be it schism, be it heresy, be it turbulent opposition, it springeth not save from these imaginings which were concealed, and while they spake good words with their lips, "all the day long did they make war".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:38
verses.text: Ye hear words of peace, yet making war departeth not from their thoughts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:39
verses.text: For the words, "all the day long," signify without intermission, throughout the whole time.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:40
verses.text: "They have sharpened their tongues like serpents".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:41
verses.text: If still thou seekest to make out the man, behold a comparison.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:42
verses.text: In the serpent above all beasts is there cunning and craft to hurt; for therefore does it creep It hath not even feet, so that its footsteps when it cometh may be heard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:43
verses.text: In its progress it draweth itself, as it were, gently along, yet not straightly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:44
verses.text: Thus then do they creep and crawl to hurt, having poison hidden even under a gentle touch.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:45
verses.text: And so it followeth, "the poison of asps is under their lips".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:46
verses.text: Behold, it is "under" their lips, that we may perceive one thing under their lips, another in their lips.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:47
verses.text: "Preserve me, O Lord, from the hand of the sinner, from unrighteous men deliver me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:48
verses.text: Here they wear their real colours, they are known; here we have no need to understand, but to act: we have need to pray, not to ask who they are.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:49
verses.text: But how thou shouldest pray against such men, he explaineth in what followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:50
verses.text: For many pray unskilfully against wicked men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:51
verses.text: "Who have imagined," saith he, "to trip up my steps".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:52
verses.text: Thus far it may be understood carnally.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:53
verses.text: Every one has enemies, who seek to cheat him in trade, to rob him of money, where they are engaged together in business; every one has some neighbour his enemy, who deviseth how to bring mischief upon his family, to injure in some way his property and surely he deviseth this by deceit, by fraud, by devilish devices he endeavoureth to accomplish this: no one can doubt it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:54
verses.text: Yet not for these reasons are they to be guarded against, but lest they lay in wait for thee and draw thee to themselves, that is, separate thee from the Body of Christ, and make thee of their body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:55
verses.text: For as Christ is the Head of the good, so is the devil their head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:56
verses.text: What is, "to trip up my steps"? Not as though thou shouldest be deceived in the business thou hast with him, or he cheat thee in a case which thou hast with him in the law courts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:57
verses.text: He hath "tripped up thy steps," if he have hindered thee in the way of God; so that what thou didst direct aright may stumble, or fall from the way, or fall in the way, or draw back from the way, or stop on the way, or go back to the place from whence it had come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:58
verses.text: Whatsoever hath done this to thee, hath tripped thee up, hath deceived thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:59
verses.text: Against such snares as these pray thou, lest thou lose thy heavenly inheritance, lest thou lose Christ thy Joint-heir, for thou art destined to live for ever with Him, who hath made thee an heir.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:60
verses.text: For thou art made an heir, not by one whom thou art to succeed after his death, but One together with whom thou art to live for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:61
verses.text: "The proud have hidden a trap for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:62
verses.text: He hath briefly described the whole body of the devil, when he saith, "the proud".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:63
verses.text: Hence is it that for the most part they call themselves righteous when they are unrighteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:64
verses.text: Hence is it that nothing is so grievous to them as to confess their sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:65
verses.text: They are men who, being falsely righteous, must needs envy the truly righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:66
verses.text: For none envieth another in that which he wisheth not either to be or to seem.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:67
verses.text: Hence come all allurings and trippings up of others.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:68
verses.text: This the devil first wished, when falling himself he envied man who stood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:69
verses.text: But those "proud ones have hidden a trap for me;" they have sought to trip up my steps.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:70
verses.text: And what have they done? "And have stretched out cords as traps".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:71
verses.text: What cords? The word is well known in holy Scripture, and elsewhere we find what "cords" signify.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:72
verses.text: For "each one is holden with the cords of his sins," saith Scripture.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:73
verses.text: And Esaias saith openly, "Woe to them that draw sin like a long rope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:74
verses.text: And why is it called a "cord"? Because every sinner who persevereth in his sins, addeth sin to sin; and when he ought by accusing his sins to amend, by defending he doubleth what by confession he might have removed, and often seeketh to fortify himself by other sins, on account of the sins he hath already committed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:75
verses.text: But these their sins they "spread" for the righteous, when they persuade them to do the evils which they themselves do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:76
verses.text: Therefore he said, "they spread cords and traps;" that is, by their sins they desired to overthrow me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:77
verses.text: And where did they this? "Beside the paths have they laid a stumbling-block for me:" not in the paths, but, "beside the paths".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:78
verses.text: Thy "paths" are the commandments of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:79
verses.text: They have "laid stumbling-blocks beside the paths;" do not thou withdraw out of the paths, and thou wilt not rush upon stumbling-blocks.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:80
verses.text: Yet will I not that thou shouldest say, "God should prevent them from laying stumbling-blocks beside my paths, and then they would not lay them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:81
verses.text: Nay, rather, God permitted them to "lay stumbling-blocks beside thy paths," that thou shouldest not leave the paths.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:82
verses.text: And what remaineth? what remedy amid such ills, in such temptations, such dangers? "I said unto the Lord, Thou art my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:83
verses.text: Loud is the voice of prayer, it exciteth confidence.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:84
verses.text: Is He not the God of the others? Of whom is not He God, who is the true God? Yet is He specially theirs, who enjoy Him, who serve Him, who willingly submit to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:85
verses.text: For the wicked too, though unwillingly, are subject to Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:86
verses.text: "Hear with Thine ears the voice of my prayer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:87
verses.text: He did not say, "Hear with Thine ears my prayer;" but, as though expressing more plainly the affection of his heart, "the voice of my prayer," the life of my prayer, the soul of my prayer, not that which soundeth in my words, but that which giveth life to my words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:88
verses.text: For all other noises without life may be called sounds, but not words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:89
verses.text: Words belong to those that have souls, to the living.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:90
verses.text: But how many pray to God, yet have neither perception of God, nor right thoughts concerning God! These may have the sound of prayer, the voice they cannot, for there is no life in them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:91
verses.text: This was the voice of the prayer of one who was alive, forasmuch as he understood that God was his God, saw by Whom he was freed, perceived from whom he was freed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:92
verses.text: Commending this to the ears of God, let him say, "Lord, Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:93
verses.text: Thou Lord-Lord, that is, most truly Lord, not like unto the lords-men, not like the lords who buy with money-bags, but the Lord who buyeth with His Blood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:94
verses.text: "Lord, Lord, Thou strength of my health" , that is, who givest strength to my health.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:95
verses.text: What is the meaning of "strength of my health"? He complained of the stumbling-blocks and snares of sinners, of wicked men, vessels of the devil, that barked around him and laid snares around him, of the proud that envy the righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:96
verses.text: But He forthwith added a comfort, "He that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:97
verses.text: This he observed and feared, and, distressed at the abundance of iniquities, turned himself to hope.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:98
verses.text: Verily I shall be saved, if I endure unto the end: but endurance, so as to win salvation, pertaineth unto strength; Thou art "the strength of my salvation;" Thou makest me to endure, that I may attain salvation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:99
verses.text: Toiling then in this warfare, he looked back to the grace of God; and because already he had begun to be heated and parched, he found, as it were, a shade, whereunder to live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:100
verses.text: "Thou hast overshadowed my head in the day of battle:" that is, in the heat, lest I be heated, lest I be parched.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:101
verses.text: "Deliver me not over, O Lord, by my own longing to the sinner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:102
verses.text: Behold to what end Thy overshadowing shall avail for me, that I suffer not heat from myself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:103
verses.text: And what could that "sinner" do to me, rage as he would? For wicked men raged against the martyrs, dragged them away, bound them with chains, shut them up in prisons, slew them with the sword, exposed them to wild beasts, consumed them with fire: all this they did; yet did not God deliver them over to the sinners, because they were not delivered over by their own longing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:104
verses.text: This then pray with all thy might, that God "delivered thee not over by thine own longing to the sinner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:105
verses.text: For thou by thine own longing givest place to the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:106
verses.text: For lo, the devil hath set before thee gain, invited thee to dishonesty; thou canst not have the gain, unless thou commit the dishonesty: the gain is the bait, dishonesty the snare: do thou so look on the bait, that thou see the snare also; for thou canst not obtain the gain, unless thou commit the dishonesty; and if thou commit the dishonesty, thou wilt be caught.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:107
verses.text: Hence is thine head overshadowed in the day of battle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:108
verses.text: For longing causeth heat, but the overshadowing of the Lord tempers longing, that we may be able to bridle that whereby we were being hurried away, that we be not so heated as to be drawn to the snare.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:109
verses.text: "They have thought against me; leave me not, lest perchance they be exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:110
verses.text: Thou hast in another place, "They that oppress me will exult if I be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:111
verses.text: Such are they, because such is the devil also himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:112
verses.text: "The head of their going about, the toil of their own lips shall cover them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:113
verses.text: Me, he saith, the shadow of Thy wings shall cover: for, "Thou hast covered me in the day of battle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:114
verses.text: Them what shall cover? "The head of their going about;" that is, pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:115
verses.text: What is, "their going about"? How they go about and stand not, how they go in the circle of error, where is journeying without end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:116
verses.text: He who goeth in a straight line, beginneth from some point, endeth at some point: he who goeth in a circle, never endeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:117
verses.text: That is the toil of the wicked, which is set forth yet more plainly in another Psalm, "The wicked walk in a circle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:118
verses.text: But "the head of their going about" is pride, for pride is the beginning of every sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:119
verses.text: But whence is pride "the toil of their own lips"? Every proud man is false, and every false man is a liar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:120
verses.text: Men toil in speaking falsehood; for truth they could speak with entire facility.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:121
verses.text: For he toileth, who maketh what he saith: he who wisheth to speak the truth, toileth not, for truth herself speaketh without toil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:122
verses.text: "Coals of fire shall fall upon them upon earth, and Thou shalt cast them down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:123
verses.text: What is, "upon earth"? Here, even in this life, here "coals of fire shall fall upon them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:124
verses.text: What are, "coals of fire"? We know these coals.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:125
verses.text: Are they different from those of which we are about to speak? For these I see avail for punishment, those that I am about to speak of, for salvation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:126
verses.text: For we have spoken of certain coals, when man was seeking aid against a treacherous tongue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:127
verses.text: The examples of the "coals" are added to the wound of the arrows (for I need not fear to say "the wound," when the Spouse herself saith, "I am wounded with love"), and then the hay is consumed, and so they are called "devouring coals".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:128
verses.text: The hay is devoured, but the gold is purified, and the man exchanges death for life, and begins to be himself too a burning coal; such a coal as was the Apostle, "who before was a blasphemer and a persecutor and injurious," a coal black and extinguished; but when he had obtained mercy, he was set on fire from heaven, the voice of Christ set him on fire, all the blackness in him perished, he began to be fervent in spirit, to set others on fire with that wherewith he was set on fire himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:129
verses.text: "A man full of words shall not be guided upon earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:130
verses.text: "A man full of words" loveth lies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:131
verses.text: For what pleasure hath he, save in speaking? He careth not what he speaketh, so long as he speaks.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:132
verses.text: It cannot be that he will be guided.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:133
verses.text: What then ought the servant of God to do, who is kindled with these "coals," and himself made a coal of salvation, what should he do? He should wish rather to hear than to speak; as it is written, "Let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:134
verses.text: And if it may be so, let him desire this, not to be obliged to speak and talk and teach.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:135
verses.text: I can quickly tell you wherein each one may prove himself, not by never speaking, but by requiring a case where it is his duty to speak; let him be glad to be silent, in will, let him speak to teach, when he must.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:136
verses.text: For when must thou needs speak and teach? When thou meetest with one ignorant, when thou meetest with one unlearned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:137
verses.text: If it delight thee always to teach, thou wishest always to have some ignorant one to teach.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:138
verses.text: "Evil shall hunt the unrighteous man to destruction".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:139
verses.text: Evils come, and he standeth not; therefore said he, "they shall hunt him to destruction".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:140
verses.text: For many good men, many righteous men evils have befallen, evils have, as it were, found them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:141
verses.text: Therefore when the evil pursued the good, that is, our martyrs, when they seized them, they "hunted" them, but not "to destruction".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:142
verses.text: For the flesh was pressed down, the spirit was crowned; the spirit was cast out from the body, yet was nought done to the flesh which might hinder it for the future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:143
verses.text: Let the flesh be burned, scourged, mangled; is it therefore withdrawn from its Creator, because it is given into the hands of its persecutor? Will not He who created it from nothing, remake it better than it was?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:144
verses.text: "I know that the Lord will maintain the right of the needy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:145
verses.text: This "needy" one is not "full of words;" for he that is full of words, wisheth to abound, knoweth not to hunger.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:146
verses.text: He is "needy" of whom it is said, "Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:147
verses.text: They groan among the stumbling-blocks of the wicked, they pray to their Head, "to be delivered from the wicked man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:148
verses.text: "And the cause of the poor".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:149
verses.text: These then are they whose cause the Lord will not neglect; although now they suffer hardships, their glory shall appear, when their Head appeareth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:150
verses.text: For to such while placed here it is said, "Ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:151
verses.text: So then we are poor, our life is hid; let us cry to Him that is our Bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:152
verses.text: "But the just shall confess to Thy Name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:153
verses.text: Both when Thou shalt plead their cause, and when Thou shalt maintain their right, they "shall confess to Thy Name;" nought shall they attribute to their own merits, all they shall attribute to nought save to Thy mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:154
verses.text: Therefore see what followeth, see wherewith he concludeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:155
verses.text: "The upright shall dwell with Thy Countenance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:156
verses.text: For ill was it with them in their own countenance; well will it be with them with Thy Countenance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:157
verses.text: For when they loved their own countenance, "In the sweat of their countenance did they eat bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:158
verses.text: Thy Countenance shall come to them with abundance to satisfy them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:159
verses.text: Nought more shall they seek, for nought better have they; no more shall they abandon Thee, nor be abandoned by Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:160
verses.text: For after His Resurrection, what was said of the Lord? "Thou shalt fill me with joy with Thy Countenance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:161
verses.text: Without His Countenance He would not give us joy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 140:162
verses.text: For this do we cleanse our countenance, that we may rejoice in His CountenanceBecause too, "blessed are the poor in heart, for they shall see God;" He gave the Form of Man both to good and evil, the Form of God He preserved for the pure and good, that we may rejoice in Him, and it may be well with us for ever with His Countenance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:1
verses.text: Psalm CXLI.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:2
verses.text: The Psalm which we have just sung is in many parts somewhat obscure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:3
verses.text: When by the help of the Lord what has been said shall begin to be expounded and explained, ye will see that ye are hearing things which ye knew already.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:4
verses.text: But for this cause are they said in manifold ways, that variety of expression may remove all weariness of the truth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:5
verses.text: "Lord, I have cried unto Thee, hear Thou me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:6
verses.text: This we all can say.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:7
verses.text: This not I alone say: whole Christ saith it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:8
verses.text: But it is said rather in the name of the Body: for He too, when He was here and bore our flesh, prayed; and when He prayed, drops of blood streamed down from His whole Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:9
verses.text: So is it written in the Gospel: "Jesus prayed earnestly, and His sweat was as it were great drops of blood".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:10
verses.text: What is this flowing of sweat from His whole Body, but the suffering of martyrs from the whole Church? "Listen unto the voice of my prayer, while I cry unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:11
verses.text: Thou thoughtest the business of crying already finished, when thou saidst, "I have cried unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:12
verses.text: Thou hast cried; yet think not thyself safe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:13
verses.text: If tribulation be finished, crying is finished: but if tribulation remain for the Church, for the Body of Christ, even to the end of the world, let it not only say, "I have cried unto Thee," but also, "Listen unto the voice of my prayer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:14
verses.text: "Let my prayer be set forth in Thy sight as incense, and the lifting up of my hands an evening sacrifice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:15
verses.text: That this is wont to be understood of the Head Himself, every Christian acknowledgeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:16
verses.text: For when the day was now sinking towards evening, the Lord upon the Cross "laid down His life to take it again," did not lose it against His will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:17
verses.text: Still we too are figured there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:18
verses.text: For what of Him hung upon the tree, save what He took of us? And how can it be that the Father should leave and abandon His only begotten Son, especially when He is one God with Him? Yet, fixing our weakness upon the Cross, where, as the Apostle saith, "our old man is crucified with Him," He cried out in the voice of that our "old man," "Why hast Thou forsaken Me?" That then is the "evening sacrifice," the Passion of the Lord, the Cross of the Lord, the offering of a salutary Victim, the whole burnt offering acceptable to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:19
verses.text: That "evening sacrifice" produced, in His Resurrection, a morning offering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:20
verses.text: Prayer then, purely directed from a faithful heart, riseth like incense from a hallowed altar.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:21
verses.text: Nought is more delightful than the odour of the Lord: such odour let all have who believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:22
verses.text: "Set, O Lord, a watch before my mouth, and a door of restraint around my lips".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:23
verses.text: He said not a barrier of restraint, but "a door of restraint".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:24
verses.text: A door is opened as well as shut.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:25
verses.text: If then it be a "door," let it be both opened and shut; opened, to confession of sin; closed, to excusing sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:26
verses.text: So will it be a "door of restraint," not of ruin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:27
verses.text: For what doth this "door of restraint" profit us? What doth Christ pray in the name of His Body? "That Thou turn not aside My heart to wicked words".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:28
verses.text: What is, "My heart"? The heart of My Church; the heart, that is, of My Body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:29
verses.text: But when thine heart hath not been turned aside, O member of Christ, when thy heart hath not been turned aside "to wicked words, to making excuses in sins, with men that work in iniquity," thou shalt also not unite with their elect.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:30
verses.text: For this followeth, "And I will not unite with their elect".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:31
verses.text: Who are "their elect"? Those who justify themselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:32
verses.text: Who are their elect? Those "who trust in themselves that they are righteous, and despise others," as the Pharisee said in the temple, "Lord, I thank Thee that I am not as other men are".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:33
verses.text: Who are their elect? "This Man, if He were a prophet, would know what manner of woman this is that touched His feet".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:34
verses.text: Here thou recognisest the words of that other Pharisee, who invited our Lord to his house; when the woman of that city, who was a sinner, came and approached His Feet.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:35
verses.text: For even this woman herself, "if her heart had turned aside to wicked words," would not have lacked wherewith to defend her sins.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:36
verses.text: Do not women daily, her equals in defilement, but not her equals in confession, harlots, adulteresses, doers of shameful deeds, defend their sins? If they have not been seen, they deny them: if they have been caught and convicted, or have done their deeds openly, they defend them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:37
verses.text: And how easy is their defence, how ready, yet how headlong; how common, yet how blasphemous! "Had God not willed it, I had not done it: God willed it: fortune willed it: fate willed it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:38
verses.text: These are the defences of "the elect" of this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:39
verses.text: But let the members of Christ, the Body of Christ, say, let Christ say in the name of His Body, "Turn not Thou aside, My Heart, to wicked words," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:40
verses.text: , "and I will not unite with their elect".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:41
verses.text: "With men that work wickedness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:42
verses.text: What wickedness? Let me mention some sinful wickedness of theirs.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:43
verses.text: Let me tell you one open sinful wickedness, which they acknowledge.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:44
verses.text: They say, it is better for a man to be an usurer than a husbandman.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:45
verses.text: Thou askest the reason, and they assign one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:46
verses.text: He vexeth the members of Christ, who cleanseth the earth with a furrow: he vexeth the members of Christ, who pulleth grass from the earth: he vexeth the members of Christ, who plucketh an apple from a tree.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:47
verses.text: To avoid committing their imaginary murders in the farm, he committeth real murders in usury.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:48
verses.text: He dealeth no bread to the needy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:49
verses.text: See whether there can be greater unrighteousness than this righteousness He dealeth not bread to the hungry.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:50
verses.text: Thou askest, wherefore? Lest the beggar receive the life which is in the bread, which they call a member of God, the substance of God, and bind it in flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:51
verses.text: What then do ye? why do ye eat? Have ye not flesh? Yes; but we, they say, forasmuch as we are enlightened by faith in Manes, by our prayers and our Psalms, forasmuch as we are elect, we cleanse thereby that bread, and transmit it into the treasure-house of the heavens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:52
verses.text: Such are the elect, that they are not to be saved by God, but saviours of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:53
verses.text: And this is Christ, they say, crucified in the whole universe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:54
verses.text: I received in the Gospel Christ a Saviour, but ye are in your books the saviours of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:55
verses.text: Plainly ye are blasphemers of Christ, and therefore not to be saved by Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:56
verses.text: Therefore lest a crumb be given to the hungry, and in the crumb a member of Christ suffer, is the hungry to die of hunger? False mercy to a crumb causeth true murder of a man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:57
verses.text: But who are their elect? "Turn not thou aside, my heart, to wicked words, and I will not unite with their elect".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:58
verses.text: "The righteous One shall amend me in mercy, and convict me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:59
verses.text: Behold the sinner confessing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:60
verses.text: He desireth to be amended in mercy, rather than praised deceitfully.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:61
verses.text: "Shall convict me," but "in mercy:" shall convict, yet hateth not: yea, shall all the more convict, because He hateth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:62
verses.text: And why doth he therefore give thanks? Because, "rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:63
verses.text: "The righteous One shall amend me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:64
verses.text: Because He persecuteth thee? God forbid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:65
verses.text: He requireth rather amending himself, who amendeth in hate.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:66
verses.text: Wherefore then doth He amend? "In mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:67
verses.text: And shall convict me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:68
verses.text: Wherein? "In mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:69
verses.text: For the oil of a sinner shall not enrich my head".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:70
verses.text: My head shall not grow by flattery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:71
verses.text: Undue praise is flattery: undue praise of a flatterer is "the oil of a sinner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:72
verses.text: Therefore men too, when they have mocked any one with false praise, say, "I have anointed his head".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:73
verses.text: Love then to be "convicted by the righteous One in mercy;" love not to be praised by a sinner in mockery.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:74
verses.text: Have oil in yourselves, and ye shall not seek the "oil of a sinner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:75
verses.text: Thou sayest to me, What am I doing? I am beset with flatterers; they cease not to besiege me; they praise in me what I would not, that praise in me what I hold in little esteem; what I hold dear they blame in me; flatterers, treacherous, deceivers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:76
verses.text: For instance, "Gaiuseius is a great man, great, learned, wise; but why is he a Christian? For great is his learning, great his reading, great his wisdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:77
verses.text: If great is his wisdom, approve of his being a Christian; if great his learning, learnedly hath he chosen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:78
verses.text: In fine, what thou revilest, that pleaseth him whom thou praisest.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:79
verses.text: But what? That praise sweeteneth not: it is "the oil of a sinner".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:80
verses.text: Yet ceaseth he not to speak so.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:81
verses.text: Let him not therewith "fatten thy head;" that is, rejoice not in such things; agree not to such things; consent not to such things; rejoice not in such things; and then, if he have applied to thee the oil of flattery, yet hath thy head remained as it was, it has not been puffed up, it hath not swollen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:82
verses.text: "For still shall My word be well-pleasing to them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:83
verses.text: Wait awhile: now they revile Me, saith Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:84
verses.text: In the early times of the Christians, the Christians were blamed on all sides.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:85
verses.text: Wait as yet; and "My word shall be well-pleasing to them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:86
verses.text: The time shall come when they shall conquer thousands of men, who shall beat their breasts, and say, "Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:87
verses.text: Even now, how many remain who blush to beat their breasts? Let them then blame us: let us bear it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:88
verses.text: Let them blame; let them hate, accuse, detract; "still shall My word be well-pleasing to them;" the time shall come when My word shall please them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:89
verses.text: O wordy defence of iniquity! Verily now whole nations say this, and the thunder of nations beating their breasts ceaseth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:90
verses.text: Rightly do the clouds thunder, wherein now God dwelleth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:91
verses.text: Where is now that wordiness, where that boasting, "I am righteous; nought of ill have I done"? Verily, when thou hast contemplated in Holy Scripture the law of righteousness, how far soever thou hast advanced, thou shalt find thyself a sinner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:92
verses.text: What sort of man am I now speaking of, brethren? I speak of him who worshippeth God alone, who confesseth Christ, who knoweth the Father and the Son and the Holy Ghost to be one God; who committeth not fornication against Him; who worshippeth not devils; who seeketh him not aid from the devil; who holdeth the Catholic Church; whom no one complaineth of as cheating; under whose oppression no weak neighbour groaneth; who assaileth not another's wife; who is content with his own, or even without his own, in such wise as is lawful, and as Apostolical discipline permitteth, with consent of both,  or when she is not yet married.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:93
verses.text: Even he who is such as this, is yet overtaken in such things as I have mentioned.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:94
verses.text: For all these daily sins then what is our hope, save to say with humble heart in the Lord's Prayer, while we defend not our sins, but confess them, "Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors;" and to "have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous," that He may be "the propitiation for our sins"? See what followeth: "their judges have been swallowed up beside the Rock".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:95
verses.text: What is, "swallowed up beside the Rock? That Rock was Christ They have been swallowed up beside the Rock".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:96
verses.text: "Beside," that is, compared, as judges, as mighty, powerful, learned: they are called "their judges," as judging about morals, and laying down their opinions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:97
verses.text: This Aristotle said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:98
verses.text: Set him beside the Rock, and he is swallowed up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:99
verses.text: Who is Aristotle? let him hear, "Christ hath said," and he trembleth among the dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:100
verses.text: This Pythagoras said, that Plato said.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:101
verses.text: Set them beside the Rock, compare their authority to the authority of the Gospel, compare the proud to the Crucified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:102
verses.text: Say we to them "Ye have written your words in the hearts of the proud; He hath planted His Cross in the hearts of kings: finally, He died, and rose again; ye are dead, and I will not ask how ye rise again".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:103
verses.text: So "their judges have been swallowed up beside" that "Rock".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:104
verses.text: So long do their words seem somewhat, till they are compared with the Rock.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:105
verses.text: Therefore if any of them be found to have said what Christ too hath said, we congratulate him, but we follow him not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:106
verses.text: But he came before Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:107
verses.text: If any man speak what is true, is he therefore before the Truth itself? Regard Christ, O man, not when He came to thee, but when He made thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:108
verses.text: The sick man too might say, "But I took to my bed before the physician came to me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:109
verses.text: Why, for that very reason has He come last, because thou first has sickened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:110
verses.text: "They shall hear My Words, for they have prevailed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:111
verses.text: My Words have prevailed over their words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:112
verses.text: They have spoken clever things, I true things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:113
verses.text: To praise one who talketh well is one thing, to praise One who speaketh truth is another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:114
verses.text: "They shall hear My Words, for they have prevailed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:115
verses.text: How have they prevailed? Who of them has been taken offering sacrifice, when such things were forbidden by the law, and has not denied it? Who of them has been taken worshipping an idol, and has not exclaimed, "I did it not," and feared lest he should be convicted? Such servants hath the devil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:116
verses.text: But how have the Words of the Lord prevailed? "Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:117
verses.text: Fear not those who kill the body," etc He gave them fear, He suggested hope, He kindled love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:118
verses.text: "Fear not death," He saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:119
verses.text: Do ye fear death? I die first.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:120
verses.text: Fear ye, lest a hair of your head perish? I first rise again in the flesh uninjured.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:121
verses.text: Rightly have ye heard His Words, for they have prevailed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:122
verses.text: They spake, and were slain; they fell, and yet stood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:123
verses.text: And what was the result of so many deaths of martyrs, save that those words prevailed, and the earth being, so to speak, watered by the blood of Christ's witnesses, the cross of the Church shot up everywhere? How have they "prevailed"? We have said already, when they were preached by men who feared not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:124
verses.text: Feared not what? Neither banishment, nor losses, nor death, nor crucifixion: for it was not death alone that they did not fear; but even crucifixion, a death than which none was thought more accursed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:125
verses.text: It the Lord endured, that His disciples might not only not fear death, but not even that kind of death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:126
verses.text: When then these things are said by men that fear not, they have prevailed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:127
verses.text: What then have all those deaths of the martyrs accomplished? Listen: "As the fatness of the earth is spread over the earth, our bones have been scattered beside the pit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:128
verses.text: "The bones" of the martyrs, that is, the bodies of the witnesses of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:129
verses.text: The martyrs were slain, and they who slew them seemed to prevail.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:130
verses.text: They prevailed by persecution, that the words of Christ might prevail by preaching.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:131
verses.text: And what was the result of the deaths of the saints? What meaneth, "the fatness of the earth is spread over the earth"? We know that everything that is refuse is the fatness of the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:132
verses.text: The things which are, as it were, contemptible to men, enrich the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:133
verses.text: "Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:134
verses.text: As it is contemptible to the world, so is it precious to the husbandman.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:135
verses.text: For he knoweth the use thereof, and its rich juice; he knoweth what he desireth, what he seeketh, whence the fertile crop ariseth; but this world despiseth it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:136
verses.text: Know ye not that "God hath chosen the contemptible things of the world, and those which are not, like as those which are, that the things which are may be brought to nought"? From the dunghill was Peter lifted up, and Paul; when they were put to death, they were despised: now, the earth having been enriched by them, and the cross of the Church springing up, behold, all that is noble and chief in the world, even the emperor himself, cometh to Rome, and whither does he hasten? to the temple of the emperor, or the memorial of the fisherman?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:137
verses.text: "For unto Thee, Lord, are mine eyes; in Thee have I hoped, take not Thou away my life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:138
verses.text: For they were tortured in persecutions, and many failed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:139
verses.text: It occurreth to him that many have failed, many have been in hazard, and as it were in the midst of the tribulation of persecution is sent forth the voice of one praying; "For unto Thee, Lord, are mine eyes:" I care not what they threaten who stand around, "unto Thee, Lord, are mine eyes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:140
verses.text: More do I fix mine eye on Thy promises than on their threats.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:141
verses.text: I know what Thou hast suffered for me, what Thou hast promised me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:142
verses.text: "Keep me from the trap which they have laid for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:143
verses.text: What was the trap? "If thou consentest, I spare thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:144
verses.text: In the trap was set the bait of the present life; if the bird love this bait, it falleth into the trap: but if the bird be able to say, "The day of man have I not desired: Thou knowest:" "He shall pluck his feet out of the net," etc Two things he hath mentioned to be distinguished the one from the other: the trap he said was set by persecutors; the stumbling-blocks came from those who have consented and apostatised: and from both he desires to be guarded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:145
verses.text: On the one side they threaten and rage, on the other consent and fall: I fear lest the one be such, that I fear him; the other such, that I imitate him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:146
verses.text: "This I do to thee, if thou consent not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:147
