verses.text: "Keep me from the trap," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:148
verses.text: "Behold, thy brother hath already consented".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:149
verses.text: "And from the stumbling-blocks," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:150
verses.text: "Sinners shall fall into his nets".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:151
verses.text: Not all sinners, certain sinners, who are so great sinners, as to love this life to such a degree as to prefer it to everlasting life, "shall fall into his trap".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:152
verses.text: But what sayest thou? Shall they that are such, thinkest thou, fall into his nets? what of Thy disciples, O Christ? Behold, when persecution was raging, when they all "left Thee alone, and went every one to his own:" lo! they who were closest to Thee, in Thy trial and persecution, when Thine enemies demanded Thee to be crucified, abandoned Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:153
verses.text: And that bold one, who had promised Thee that he would go with Thee even unto death, heard from the Physician what was being done in him, the sick man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:154
verses.text: For being in a fever, he had said he was whole; but the Lord touched the vein of his heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:155
verses.text: Then came the trial; then came the test; then came the accusation; and now, questioned not by some great power, but by a humble slave, and that a woman, questioned by a handmaid, he yielded; he denied thrice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:156
verses.text: "He wept bitterly," it saith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:157
verses.text: Not yet was he fitted to suffer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:158
verses.text: To him was said, "Thou shalt follow Me afterwards".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:159
verses.text: Hereafter he was to be firm, having been strengthened by the Lord's Resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:160
verses.text: Not yet then was it time that those "bones" should be "scattered beside the pit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:161
verses.text: For see how many failed, even to those who first hung on His mouth; even they failed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:162
verses.text: Wherefore? "I am alone, until I pass over:" for this followeth in the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:163
verses.text: Pascha, as they say who know, and who have explained to us what to read, meaneth "Passover".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:164
verses.text: When then the Lord's Passion was about to come, the Evangelist, as though he would use this very word, saith, "When the hour was come that Jesus should pass over to the Father".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:165
verses.text: We hear then of Pascha in this verse, "I am alone, until I pass over".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:166
verses.text: After Pascha I shall no longer be alone, after passing-over I shall no longer be alone.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:167
verses.text: Many shall imitate Me, many shall follow Me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:168
verses.text: And if afterward they shall follow, what shall be the case now? "I am alone, until I pass over".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:169
verses.text: What is it that the Lord saith in this Psalm, "I am alone, until I pass over"? What is it that we have expounded? If we have understood it, listen to His own words in the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:170
verses.text: "Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone; but if it die, it beareth much fruit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:171
verses.text: Therefore He was alone before He was put to death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:172
verses.text: So far was any from dying for the Name, that is, for confessing the Name of Christ, before that Corn of wheat fell into the ground, that even John, who was slain just before Him, being given by a wicked king to a dancing woman, was not put to death because he confessed Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:173
verses.text: Of course he might have been put to death for this, and that by many.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:174
verses.text: If for another reason he was put to death by one man, how much more might he have been put to death by those very men, who put Christ to death? For John gave testimony to Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:175
verses.text: They who heard Christ, wished to slay Him; the man who gave testimony to Him they slew not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:176
verses.text: He is not slain by the Jews who gave free testimony to Christ, whom the Jews slew; he is slain by Herod, because he said to him, "It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 141:177
verses.text: For his brother had not died without issue For the law of truth, for equity, for righteousness' sake, he did die: therefore is he a saint, therefore a martyr; but yet he died not for that Name whereby we are Christians, wherefore, save that the saying might be fulfilled, "I am alone, until I pass over".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:1
verses.text: Psalm CXLII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:2
verses.text: "With my voice have I cried unto the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:3
verses.text: It were enough to say, "with voice:" not for nothing perhaps has "my" been added.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:4
verses.text: For many cry unto the Lord, not with their own voice, but with the voice of their body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:5
verses.text: Let the "inner man" then, in whom "Christ" hath begun to "dwell by faith," cry unto the Lord, not with the din of his lips, but with the affection of his heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:6
verses.text: God heareth not, where man heareth: unless thou criest with the voice of lungs and side and tongue, man heareth thee not: thy thought is thy cry to the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:7
verses.text: "With my voice have I prayed unto the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:8
verses.text: What he meant by, "I have cried," he explained when he said, "I have prayed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:9
verses.text: For they too who blaspheme, cry unto the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:10
verses.text: In the former part he set down his crying, in the latter he explained what it was.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:11
verses.text: As though it were demanded, With what cry hast thou cried unto the Lord? Unto the Lord, saith he, I have prayed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:12
verses.text: My cry is my prayer, not reviling, not murmuring, not blaspheming.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:13
verses.text: "I will pour out before Him my prayer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:14
verses.text: What is, "before Him"? In His sight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:15
verses.text: What is, in His sight? Where He seeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:16
verses.text: But where doth He not see? For so do we say, 'where He seeth,' as though somewhere He seeth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:17
verses.text: But in this assemblage of bodily substances men too see, animals too see: He seeth where man seeth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:18
verses.text: For thy thoughts no man seeth, but God seeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:19
verses.text: There then pour out thy prayer, where He alone seeth, who rewardeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:20
verses.text: For the Lord Jesus Christ bade thee pray in secret: but if thou knowest what "thy closet" is, and cleansest it, there thou prayest to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:21
verses.text: "But thou," saith He, "when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and shut the door, and pray to thy Father in secret, and He who seeth in secret shall reward thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:22
verses.text: If men are to reward thee, pour out thy prayer before men: if God is to reward thee, pour out thy prayer before Him; and close the door, lest the tempter enter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:23
verses.text: Therefore the Apostle, because it is in our power to shut the door, the door of our hearts, not of our walls, for in it is our "closet,"—because it is in our power to shut this door, saith, "neither give place to the devil".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:24
verses.text: But what is to "shut the door"? This door hath as it were two leaves, desire and fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:25
verses.text: Either thou desireth something earthly, and he enters by this; or thou fearest something earthly, and he enters by that.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:26
verses.text: Close then the door of fear and desire against the devil, open it to Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:27
verses.text: How dost thou open these folding doors to Christ? By desiring the kingdom of heaven, by fearing the fire of hell.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:28
verses.text: By desire of this world the devil entereth, by desire of eternal life Christ entereth; by fear of temporal punishment the devil entereth, by fear of everlasting fire Christ entereth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:29
verses.text: "My tribulation I will proclaim in His sight".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:30
verses.text: There is a repetition, both in the two preceding sentences, and in these which follow: the sentiments are two, but both twice expressed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:31
verses.text: For, "in His sight," is the same as "before Him;" "I will proclaim my tribulation," is the same as, "I will pour out my prayer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:32
verses.text: When doest thou this? Being set in the midst of persecution, he saith, "while my spirit failed from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:33
verses.text: Wherefore hath thy spirit failed, O martyr, set in tribulation? That I may not claim my strength as mine own, that I may know that Another worketh in me the goodness I have.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:34
verses.text: And men perhaps have heard that my spirit hath failed within me, and have despaired of me, and have said, "we have taken him captive, we have overpowered him;" "and Thou hast known my paths".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:35
verses.text: They thought me cast down, Thou didst see me standing upright.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:36
verses.text: They who persecuted me and had seized me, thought my feet entangled, "but their feet were entangled, and they fell, but we are risen, and stand upright".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:37
verses.text: For mine eyes are ever unto the Lord, for He shall pluck my feet out of the net".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:38
verses.text: I have persevered in walking, for "he that shall persevere unto the end, the same shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:39
verses.text: They thought me overpowered, but I continued walking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:40
verses.text: Where did I walk? In paths which they saw not, who thought me prisoner, in the paths of Thy righteousness, in the paths of Thy commandments.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:41
verses.text: For every path is a way, but not every way is a path.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:42
verses.text: Why then are those ways called paths, save because they are narrow? Broad is the way of the wicked, narrow the way of the righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:43
verses.text: That which is "the way" is also "the ways," just as "the Church" is also "the Churches," the "heaven" also the "heavens:" they are spoken of in the plural, they are spoken of also in the singular.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:44
verses.text: On account of the unity of the Church it is one Church; "My dove is one, she is the only one of her mother".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:45
verses.text: On account of the congregation of brethren in various places there are many Churches.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:46
verses.text: "The Churches of Judaea which are in Christ rejoiced," saith Paul, "and they glorified God in me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:47
verses.text: Thus he spake of Churches; and of one Church he thus speaketh, "Give none offence, neither to the Jews, nor to the Gentiles, nor to the Church of God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:48
verses.text: "In this way, wherein I was walking, they hid a trap for me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:49
verses.text: This "way wherein I was walking," is Christ; there have they laid a trap for me, who persecute me in Christ, for Christ's Name's sake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:50
verses.text: There then "have they hid for me a trap".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:51
verses.text: What in me do they hate, what in me do they persecute? That I am a Christian.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:52
verses.text: For the heretics too wish to hide a stumbling-block for us in the Name of Christ, and are themselves deceived.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:53
verses.text: What they think that they put in the way, they put outside the way, for they themselves are outside the way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:54
verses.text: They cannot set a trap where themselves are not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:55
verses.text: The Pagan thinketh to put a stumbling-block in the way, when he saith to me, "Thou worshippest a crucified God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:56
verses.text: He findeth fault with the Cross of Christ, which he understandeth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:57
verses.text: He thinketh that he setteth in Christ, what he setteth near the way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:58
verses.text: I will not depart from Christ, so shall I not fall from the way into the trap.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:59
verses.text: Let him mock at Christ crucified, let me see the Cross of Christ on the foreheads of kings.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:60
verses.text: What he laugheth at, therein am I saved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:61
verses.text: Nought is prouder than a sick man, who laugheth at his own medicine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:62
verses.text: If he laughed not at it, he would take it, and be healed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:63
verses.text: The Cross is the sign of humility, but he through excess of pride acknowledgeth not that whereby may be healed the swelling of his soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:64
verses.text: But if I acknowledge, I am walking in the way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:65
verses.text: So far am I from blushing at the Cross, that in no secret place do I keep the Cross of Christ, but bear it on my forehead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:66
verses.text: Many sacraments we receive, one in one way another in another: some as ye know we receive with the mouth, some we receive over the whole body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:67
verses.text: But because the forehead is the seat of the blush of shame, He who said, "Whosoever shall be ashamed of Me before men, of him will I be ashamed before My Father which is in heaven," set, so to speak, that very ignominy which the Pagans mock at, in the seat of our shame.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:68
verses.text: Thou hearest a man assail a shameless man and say, "He hath no forehead".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:69
verses.text: What is, "He hath no forehead"? He hath no shame.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:70
verses.text: Let me not have a bare forehead, let the Cross of my Lord cover it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:71
verses.text: "I considered upon the right hand, and saw".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:72
verses.text: He considered upon the right hand, and saw: whoso considereth upon the left hand, is blinded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:73
verses.text: What is to consider on the right hand? Where they will be to whom shall be said, "Come, ye blessed of My Father," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:74
verses.text: ,He goeth on to say, "and there was none that knew me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:75
verses.text: For when thou fearest all things, who knoweth what thou regardest, whether thou directest thine eyes to the right hand or to the left? If, in bearing, thou seekest the praise of men, thou hast regarded the left: if, in bearing, thou seekest the promises of God, thou hast regarded the right hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:76
verses.text: Hast thou regarded the right hand, thou shalt see: hast thou regarded the left hand, thou shalt be blinded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:77
verses.text: But even when thou seest on the right hand, there will be none to know thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:78
verses.text: For who comforteth thee save the Lord? "Flight hath perished from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:79
verses.text: He speaketh as though he were hemmed in.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:80
verses.text: Let the persecutors rejoice over him; he is overpowered, he is taken, he is hemmed in, he is conquered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:81
verses.text: "Flight hath perished" from him who fleeth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:82
verses.text: But he who fleeth not, suffereth whatever he can for Christ: that is, he fleeth not in soul.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:83
verses.text: For in body it is lawful to flee; it is allowed, it is permitted; for the Lord saith, "When they persecute you in one city, flee to another".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:84
verses.text: He then who fleeth not in soul, from him "flight hath perished".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:85
verses.text: But it maketh a difference why he fleeth not; whether because he is hemmed in, because he is caught, or because he is brave.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:86
verses.text: For both from him that is caught flight hath perished, and from him that is brave flight hath perished.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:87
verses.text: What flight then is to be avoided? what flight shall we allow to perish from us? That whereof the Lord speaketh in the Gospel, "The Good Shepherd layeth down his life for the sheep.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:88
verses.text: But he that is an hireling, and not the shepherd, when he seeth the wolf coming, fleeth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:89
verses.text: When he seeth the ravager, why fleeth he? "Because he careth not for the sheep".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:90
verses.text: In two ways a man's life is sought, either by his persecutors or by his lovers So then "there is none to seek my life," he said of them; verily they persecute my life, and they seek not my life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:91
verses.text: But if they seek my life, they will find it clinging to Thee: and if they know to seek it, they know also to imitate it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:92
verses.text: "Unto thee have I cried, O Lord: I have said, Thou art my hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:93
verses.text: When I endured, when I was in tribulation, "I said, Thou art my hope".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:94
verses.text: My hope here, therefore I endure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:95
verses.text: But "my portion," not here, but "in the land of the living".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:96
verses.text: God giveth a portion in the land of the living; but not something from Himself without Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:97
verses.text: What will He give to one that loveth Him, save Himself?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:98
verses.text: "Give heed unto my prayer, for much have I been humbled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:99
verses.text: Humbled by persecutors, humbled in confession.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:100
verses.text: He humbleth himself out of the sight of man: he is humbled by enemies in their sight.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:101
verses.text: Therefore is he lifted up by Him both visibly and invisibly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:102
verses.text: Invisibly are the martyrs already lifted up; visibly shall they be lifted up, "when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption" in the resurrection of the dead; when this very part of him, against which alone her persecutors could rage, shall be renewed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:103
verses.text: "Fear not them that kill the body, but cannot kill the soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:104
verses.text: And what perisheth? what kill they?Why then art thou anxious about the rest of thy members, when thou shalt not lose even a hair? "Deliver me from them that persecute me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:105
verses.text: From whom thinkest thou that he prayeth to be delivered? From men who persecuted him? Is it so? are merely men our enemies? We have other enemies, invisible, who persecute us in another way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:106
verses.text: Man persecuteth, that he may slay the body; another persecuteth, that he ensnare the soulThere are then other enemies of ours too, from whom we ought to pray God to deliver us, lest they lead us astray, either by crushing us with troubles of this world, or alluring us by its enticements.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:107
verses.text: Who are these enemies? Let us see whether they are plainly described by any servant of the Lord, by any soldier, now perfected, who hath engaged with them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:108
verses.text: Hear the Apostle saying, "We wrestle not against flesh and blood:" as though he would say, Turn not your hatred against men; think not them your enemies; think not that it is by their hostility you are being bruised; these men whom ye fear are flesh and blood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:109
verses.text: "For they are strengthened over me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:110
verses.text: Who said, "they are strengthened over me"? The Body of Christ crieth out; it is the voice of the Church; the members of Christ cry out, "Much hath the number of sinners increased".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:111
verses.text: "Because iniquity hath abounded, the love of many waxeth cold".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:112
verses.text: "Bring forth my soul out of prison, that it may confess to Thy Name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:113
verses.text: This "prison" has been variously understood by former writers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:114
verses.text: And perh aps it is the prison which is called in the title, "the cave".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:115
verses.text: For the title of this Psalm runneth thus: "Of understanding to David himself, a prayer when he was in the cave".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:116
verses.text: That which is the cave, the same is also the prison.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:117
verses.text: Two things have we set before us to understand, but when we have understood one, both will be understood.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:118
verses.text: A man's deserts make a prison.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:119
verses.text: For in one dwelling place one man finds a house, another a prison.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:120
verses.text: To some then it has seemed that the "cave" and "prison" are this world; and this the Church prayeth, that it may be brought out of prison, that is, from this world, from under the sun, where all is vanity Beyond this world then God promiseth that we shall be in some sort of rest; therefore perhaps do we cry concerning this place, "Bring my soul out of prison".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:121
verses.text: Our soul by faith and hope is in Christ; "Your life is hid with Christ in God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:122
verses.text: But our body is in this prison, in this world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:123
verses.text: But some have said, that this prison and cave is this body, so that this is the meaning of, "Bring my soul out of prison".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:124
verses.text: But this interpretation too is somewhat at fault.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:125
verses.text: For what great thing is it to say, "Bring my soul out of prison," bring my soul out of the body? Do not the souls of robbers and wicked men go forth from the body, and go into worse punishment than here they have endured? What great request then is this, "Bring my soul out of prison," when, sooner or later, it must needs come forth? Perhaps the righteous saith, "Let me die now; bring forth my soul from this prison of the body".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:126
verses.text: If he be too hasty, he hath not love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:127
verses.text: He ought indeed to long for and desire, as the Apostle saith, "having a desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ, which is far better".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:128
verses.text: But where is love? Therefore it followeth, "but to abide in the flesh is needful for you".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:129
verses.text: Let God then lead us forth from the body, when He will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:130
verses.text: Our body too might be said to be a prison, not because that is a prison which God hath made, but because it is under punishment and liable to death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:131
verses.text: For there are two things to be considered in our body, God's workmanship, and the punishment it has deserved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:132
verses.text: Perhaps then he meant by, "Bring my soul out of prison," bring my soul out of corruption.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:133
verses.text: If thus we understand it, it is no blasphemy, the meaning is consistent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:134
verses.text: Lastly, brethren, as I think, he meant this; "Bring my soul out of prison," bring it out of straitness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:135
verses.text: For to one who rejoiceth, even a prison is wide; to one in sorrow, a field is strait.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:136
verses.text: Therefore prayeth he to be brought out of straitness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:137
verses.text: For though in hope he have enlargement, yet in reality at present he is straitened.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:138
verses.text: It is not the body that weigheth down the soul, but the corruptible body.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:139
verses.text: It is not the body then that maketh the prison, but the corruption.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:140
verses.text: "Bring my soul out of prison, that it may give thanks to Thy Name".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:141
verses.text: Now the words which follow seem to come from the Head, our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:142
verses.text: And they are the same as yesterday's last words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:143
verses.text: Yesterday's last words, if ye remember, were, "I am alone, until I pass over".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 142:144
verses.text: And here what are the last words? "The righteous shall sustain me, until thou recompense me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:1
verses.text: Psalm CXLIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:2
verses.text: The title of the Psalm is, "To David himself, when his son was pursuing him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:3
verses.text: We know from the Books of Kings that this happened:but we must recognise here another David, truly "strong in hand," which is the explanation of David, even our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:4
verses.text: For all those events of past time were figures of things to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:5
verses.text: Let us seek then in this Psalm our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, announcing Himself beforehand in His prophecy, and foretelling what should happen at this time by things which were done long ago.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:6
verses.text: For He Himself foretold Himself in the Prophets: for He is the Word of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:7
verses.text: Nor did they say ought of this kind, save when filled with the Word of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:8
verses.text: They announced then Christ, being filled with Christ, they went before Him about to come, and He deserted not them going before.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:9
verses.text: Let then our Lord speak; let Christ with us, whole Christ, speak.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:10
verses.text: "Lord, hear my prayer, receive with Thine ears my entreaty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:11
verses.text: "Hear" and "receive with ears" are the same thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:12
verses.text: It is repetition, it is confirmation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:13
verses.text: "In Thy truth hear me, in Thy righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:14
verses.text: Take it not without emphasis when it is said, "in Thy righteousness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:15
verses.text: For it is a commendation of grace, that none of us think his righteousness his own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:16
verses.text: For this is the righteousness of God, which God hath given thee to possess.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:17
verses.text: For what saith the Apostle of them, who would boast of their own righteousness? Speaking of the Jews, he saith, "they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:18
verses.text: Thou art perverse, because thou imputest what thou hast done ill to God, what well to thyself: thou wilt be right, when thou imputest what thou hast done ill to thyself, what well to God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:19
verses.text: Behold, "in Thy righteousness hear me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:20
verses.text: For when I look upon myself, nought else do I find mine own, save sin.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:21
verses.text: "And enter not into judgment with Thy servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:22
verses.text: Who are willing to enter into judgment with Him, save they who, "being ignorant of the righteousness of God, go about to establish their own?" "Wherefore have we fasted, and Thou hast not seen; wherefore have we afflicted our souls, and Thou takest no knowledge?" As though they would say, "We have done what Thou hast commanded, wherefore dost Thou not render to us what Thou hast promised?" God answereth thee: I will give to thee to receive what I have promised: I have given thee that thou shouldest do that whereby thou mayest receive.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:23
verses.text: Finally, to such proud ones the Prophet speaketh; "Wherefore will ye plead with Me? ye have all transgressed against Me, saith the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:24
verses.text: Why will ye enter into judgment with Me, and recount your own righteousnesses?"For before Thee every one living shall not be justified".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:25
verses.text: "Every one living;" living, that is, here, living in the flesh, living in expectation of death; born a man; deriving his life of man; sprung from Adam, a living Adam; every one thus living may perhaps be justified before himself, but not before Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:26
verses.text: How before himself? By pleasing himself, displeasing Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:27
verses.text: Enter not then into judgment with me, O Lord my God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:28
verses.text: How straight soever I seem to myself, Thou bringest forth a standard from Thy store-house, Thou fittest me to it, and I am found crooked.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:29
verses.text: Well is it said, "with Thy servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:30
verses.text: It is unworthy of Thee to enter into judgment with Thy servant, or even with Thy friendWhat of the Apostles themselves?That ye may perceive it at once, they learnt to pray what we pray: to them was given the pattern of prayer by the heavenly Counsellor.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:31
verses.text: "After this manner," saith He, "pray ye".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:32
verses.text: And having set down certain things first, He laid down this too to be said by the leaders of the sheep, the chief members of the Shepherd and Gatherer of the one flock; even they learnt to say, "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:33
verses.text: They said not, "Thanks be to Thee, who hast forgiven us our debts, as we too forgive our debtors," but, "Forgive, as we forgive".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:34
verses.text: But surely the faithful prayed then, surely the Apostles prayed then, for this Lord's Prayer was given rather to the faithful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:35
verses.text: If those debts only were meant which are forgiven by Baptism, it would befit catechumens rather to say, "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:36
verses.text: Let the Apostles then say, yea let them say, "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:37
verses.text: And when it is said to them, "Wherefore say ye this? what are your debts?" let them answer, "for in Thy sight every one living shall not be justified".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:38
verses.text: "For the enemy hath persecuted my soul: he hath humbled my life on the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:39
verses.text: Here we speak, here our Head speaketh for us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:40
verses.text: Manifestly both the devil persecuted the Soul of Christ and Judas the Soul of his Master: and now too the same devil remaineth to persecute the Body of Christ, and one Judas succeedeth another.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:41
verses.text: There lacketh not then of whom the Body too may say, "For the enemy hath persecuted my soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:42
verses.text: For what doth each one who persecuteth us endeavour save to make us abandon our heavenly hope, and savour of the earth, yield to our persecutor, and love earthly things? "They have laid me in dark places, as the dead of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:43
verses.text: This ye hear more readily from the Head; this ye perceive more readily in the Head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:44
verses.text: For He died indeed for us, yet was He not one of the "dead of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:45
verses.text: For who are the "dead of the world"? And how was not He one of the "dead of the world"? "The dead of the world" are those who have died of their own desert, receiving the reward of iniquity, deriving death from the sin transmissed to them; according as it is said, "For I was conceived in iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:46
verses.text: In dying, saith He, I do the will of My Father, but I am not deserving of death.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:47
verses.text: Nought have I done wherefore I should die, yet is it Mine own doing that I die, that by the death of an innocent One, they may be freed who had wherefore they should die.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:48
verses.text: "They set me in places," as though in Hades, as though in the tomb, as though in His very Passion, "as the dead of the world".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:49
verses.text: "And My Spirit within me," saith He, "suffered weariness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:50
verses.text: Remember, "My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:51
verses.text: Here we see one voice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:52
verses.text: Do we not see plainly the transition from the Head to the members, from the members to the Head?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:53
verses.text: But we too were there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:54
verses.text: He goes to the members.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:55
verses.text: "I have called to mind the days of old".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:56
verses.text: Did He "call to mind the days of old," by whom every day was made? No, but the body speaketh, each one who has been justified by His grace, who dwelleth in Him in love and devout humility, speaketh and saith, "I have meditated upon all Thy works:" plainly because Thou hast made all things good, and nothing would have stood fast, which was not established by Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:57
verses.text: Thy creation is made a spectacle unto me: I have sought in the work the Artificer, in all that is made the Maker.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:58
verses.text: Wherefore this, to what purpose this, save that he might understand, that whatever there was of good in himself was made by Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:59
verses.text: Look back then upon the Framer of thy life, the Author of thy substance, of thy righteousness, and of thy salvation: "meditate upon the works of His hands," for the righteousness too which is in thee, thou wilt find to pertain to His hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:60
verses.text: Hear the Apostle teaching thee this, "not of works," he saith, "lest any should boast".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:61
verses.text: Have we no good works? Plainly we have: but see what follows; "for we are His workmanship," saith he.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:62
verses.text: "We are His workmanship:" perhaps in thus speaking of workmanship, he meant to mention the nature whereby we are men? Evidently not: he was speaking of works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:63
verses.text: But let us not make conjectures; let the text go on, "for we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:64
verses.text: Think not then that thou thyself doest anything, save in so far as thou art evil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:65
verses.text: "Work out your own salvation," saith the Apostle, "with fear and trembling".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:66
verses.text: If we do work out our own salvation, wherefore with fear, wherefore with trembling, when what we work is in our own power? Hear wherefore with fear and trembling: "for it is God that worketh in you both to will and to do, of His good pleasure".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:67
verses.text: Therefore "with fear and trembling," that it may delight our Maker to work in the lowly valley.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:68
verses.text: "I stretched forth," saith he, "my hands to Thee: my soul is as a land without water to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:69
verses.text: Rain upon me, saith he, to bring forth from me good fruit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:70
verses.text: "For the Lord shall give sweetness, that our land may give her fruit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:71
verses.text: "I have stretched forth my hands to Thee; my soul is as a land without water," not to me, but "to Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:72
verses.text: I can thirst for Thee, I cannot water myself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:73
verses.text: "Speedily hear me, Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:74
verses.text: For what need of delay to inflame my thirst, when already I thirst so eagerly? Thou didst delay the rain, that I might drink and imbibe, not reject, Thy inflowing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:75
verses.text: If then Thou didst for this cause delay, now give; for "my spirit hath failed".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:76
verses.text: Let Thy Spirit fill me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:77
verses.text: This is the reason why Thou shouldest speedily hear me.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:78
verses.text: I am now become "poor in spirit," make Thou me "blessed in the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:79
verses.text: For he in whom his own spirit liveth, is proud, is puffed up with his own spirit against God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:80
verses.text: "Turn not Thou away Thy Face from me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:81
verses.text: Thou didst turn it away from me when proud.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:82
verses.text: For once I was full, and in my fulness I was puffed up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:83
verses.text: Once "in my fulness I said, I shall never be moved".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:84
verses.text: "I said in my fulness, I shall not be moved," knowing not Thy Righteousness, and establishing mine own; but "Thou, Lord, in Thy Will hast afforded strength to my beauty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:85
verses.text: "I said in my fulness, I shall not be moved," but from Thee came whatever fulness I had.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:86
verses.text: And to prove to me that it was from Thee, "Thou didst turn away Thy Face from me, and I was troubled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:87
verses.text: After this trouble, where into I was cast, because Thou didst turn away Thy Face, after the weariness of my spirit, after my heart was troubled within me, because Thou didst turn away Thy Face, then became I "like a land without water to Thee: turn not Thou away Thy Face".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:88
verses.text: Thou turnedst it away from me when proud; give it back to me now I am humble.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:89
verses.text: Because, if Thou turn it away, "I shall be like to them that go down into the pit".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:90
verses.text: What is, "that go down into the pit"? When the sinner has come into the depth of sins, he will show contempt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:91
verses.text: They "go down into the pit," who lose even confession; against which is said, "Let not the pit close her mouth over me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:92
verses.text: This depth Scripture calleth mostly "a pit," into which depth when a sinner hath come, "he showeth contempt".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:93
verses.text: What is, "he showeth contempt"? He no longer believeth in Providence, or if he do believe, he thinketh that he has no longer aught to do with it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:94
verses.text: "Make me to hear in the morning Thy mercy, for in Thee have I hoped".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:95
verses.text: Behold, I am in the night, yet "in Thee have I hoped," until the iniquity of the night pass away.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:96
verses.text: "For we have," as Peter saith, "a more sure word of prophecy, whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the daystar arise in your hearts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:97
verses.text: "Morning" then he calleth the time after the end of the world, when we shall see what in this world we believe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:98
verses.text: But what here, until the morning come? For it is not enough to hope for the morning; we must do somewhat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:99
verses.text: Why do somewhat? God is to be sought with the hands in the night.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:100
verses.text: What is, "with the hands"? By good works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:101
verses.text: Since then we must thus hope for the morning, and bear this night, and persevere in this patience until the day dawn, what meanwhile must we do here? lest perchance thou think that thou wilt do aught of thyself, whereby thou mayest earn to be brought to the morning.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:102
verses.text: "Make known to me, O Lord, the way wherein I must walk".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:103
verses.text: Therefore did He kindle the lamp of prophecy, therefore did He send the Lord in the vessel, as it were, of the flesh, who should even say, "My strength is dried up like a potsherd".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:104
verses.text: Walk by prophecy, walk by the lamp of future things predicted, walk by the word of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:105
verses.text: "Deliver me from mine enemies, O Lord, for unto Thee have I fled for refuge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:106
verses.text: I who once fled from Thee, now flee to Thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:107
verses.text: For Adam fled from the Face of God, and hid himself among the trees of Paradise, so that of him was said in the Book of Job, "As a servant that fleeth from his Lord, and findeth a shadow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:108
verses.text: He fled from the Face of his Lord, and found a shadow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:109
verses.text: Woe to him, if he continue in the shade, lest it be said afterward, "All things are passed away like a shadow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:110
verses.text: The rulers of this world, of this darkness, the rulers of the wicked; against these ye wrestle.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:111
verses.text: Great is your conflict, not to see your enemies, and yet to conquer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:112
verses.text: Against the rulers of this world, of this darkness, the devil, that is, and his angels; not the rulers of that world, whereof is said, "the world was made by Him," but that world whereof is said, "the world knew Him not".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:113
verses.text: "For unto Thee have I fled for refuge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:114
verses.text: Whither should I flee? "Whither shall I go from Thy Spirit?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:115
verses.text: "Teach me to do Thy will, for Thou art my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:116
verses.text: Glorious confession! glorious rule! "For Thou," saith he, "art my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:117
verses.text: To another will I hasten to be re-made, if by another I was made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:118
verses.text: Thou art my all, "for Thou art my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:119
verses.text: Shall I seek a father to get an inheritance? "Thou art my God," not only the Giver of mine inheritance, but mine Inheritance itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:120
verses.text: "The Lord is the portion of mine inheritance".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:121
verses.text: Shall I seek a patron, to obtain redemption? "Thou art my God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:122
verses.text: Lastly, having been created, do I desire to be re-created? "Thou art my God," my Creator, who hast created me by Thy Word, and re-created me by Thy Word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:123
verses.text: "Teach Thou me:" for it cannot be that Thou art my God, and yet I am to be mine own master.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:124
verses.text: See how grace is commended to us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:125
verses.text: This hold fast, this drink in, this let none drive out of your hearts, lest ye have "a zeal, of God, but not according to knowledge".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:126
verses.text: Say then this: "Thy good Spirit," not my bad one, "Thy good Spirit shall lead me into the right land".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:127
verses.text: For my bad spirit hath led me into a crooked land.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:128
verses.text: And what have I deserved? What can be reckoned as my good works without Thy aid, through which I might obtain and be worthy to be led by Thy Spirit into the right land?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:129
verses.text: Listen, then, with all your power, to the commendation of Grace, whereby ye are saved without price.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:130
verses.text: "For Thy Name's sake, O Lord, Thou shalt quicken me in Thy righteousness" ; not in mine own: not because I have deserved, but because Thou hast mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:131
verses.text: For were I to show mine own desert, nought should I deserve of Thee, save punishment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:132
verses.text: Thou hast pruned off from me mine own merits; Thou hast grafted in Thine own gifts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:133
verses.text: "Thou shalt bring forth my soul out of tribulation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 143:134
verses.text: "And in thy mercy shalt bring mine enemies to destruction: and thou shalt destroy all them that afflict my soul; for I am Thy servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:1
verses.text: Psalm CXLIV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:2
verses.text: The title of this Psalm is brief in number of words, but heavy in the weight of its mysteries.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:3
verses.text: "To David himself against Goliath".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:4
verses.text: This battle was fought in the time of our fathers, and ye, beloved, remember it with me from Holy Scripture.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:5
verses.text: David put five stones in his scrip, he hurled but one.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:6
verses.text: The five Books were chosen, but unity conquered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:7
verses.text: Then, having smitten and overthrown him, he took the enemy's sword, and with it cut off his head.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:8
verses.text: This our David also did, He overthrew the devil with his own weapons: and when his great ones, whom he had in his power, by means of whom he slew other souls, believe, they turn their tongues against the devil, and so Goliath's head is cut off with his own sword.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:9
verses.text: "Blessed be the Lord my God, who teacheth my hands for battle, my fingers for war".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:10
verses.text: These are our words, if we be the Body of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:11
verses.text: It seems a repetition of sentiment; "our hands for battle," and "our fingers for war," are the same.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:12
verses.text: Or is there some difference between "hands" and "fingers"? Certainly both hands and fingers work.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:13
verses.text: Not then without reason do we take "fingers" as put for "hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:14
verses.text: But still in the "fingers" we recognise the division of operation, yet still a sort of unity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:15
verses.text: Behold that grace! the Apostle saith, To one, this; to another, that; "there are diversities of operations; all these worketh one and the self-same Spirit;" there is the root of unity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:16
verses.text: With these "fingers" then the Body of Christ fighteth, going forth to "war," going forth to "battle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:17
verses.text: By works of Mercy our enemy is conquered, and we could not have works of mercy unless we had charity, and charity we could have none unless we received it by the Holy Ghost; He then "teacheth our hands for battle, and our fingers for war:" to Him rightfully do we say, "My Mercy," from whom we have also that we are merciful: "for he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath showed no mercy".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:18
verses.text: My Mercy and my Refuge, my Upholder and my Deliverer".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:19
verses.text: Much toileth this combatant, having his flesh lusting against his spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:20
verses.text: Keep what thou hast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:21
verses.text: Then shalt thou have in full what thou wishest, when "death shall have been swallowed up in victory;" when this mortal body has been raised, and is changed into the condition of the angels, and rises aloft to a heavenly quality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:22
verses.text: There is life, there are good days, where nought lusteth against the spirit, where it is not said, "Fight," but "Rejoice".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:23
verses.text: But who is he that lusteth for these days? Every man certainly saith, "I do".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:24
verses.text: Hear what followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:25
verses.text: I see that thou art toiling, I see that thou art engaged in battle, and in danger; hear what followeth:"Depart from evil, and do good:" let not the poor first weep under thee, that the poor may rejoice through thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:26
verses.text: For what reward, since now thou art fighting? "Seek peace, and ensue it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:27
verses.text: Learn and say, "My Mercy and my Refuge, mine Upholder and my Deliverer, my Protector:" "mine Upholder," lest I fall; "my Deliverer," lest I stick; "my Protector," lest I be stricken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:28
verses.text: In all these things, in all my toil, in all my battles, in all my difficulties, in Him have I hoped, "who subdueth my people under me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:29
verses.text: Behold, our Head speaketh together with us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:30
verses.text: "Lord, what is man, that Thou hast become known unto him?".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:31
verses.text: All is included in "that Thou hast become known unto him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:32
verses.text: "Or the son of man, that Thou valuest him?" Thou valuest him, that is, Thou makest him of such importance, Thou countest him of such price, Thou knowest under what Thou placest him, over what Thou placest him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:33
verses.text: For valuing is considering the price of a thing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:34
verses.text: How greatly did He value man, who for him shed the blood of His only-begotten Son! For God valueth not man in the same way as one man valueth another: he, when he findeth a slave for sale, giveth a higher price for a horse than for a man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:35
verses.text: Consider how greatly He valued thee, that thou mayest be able to say, "If God be for us, who can be against us?" And how greatly did He value thee, "who spared not His own Son"? "How shall He not also with Him freely give us all things?" He who giveth this food to the combatant, what keepeth He in store for the conqueror?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:36
verses.text: "Man is made like unto vanity: his days pass away like a shadow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:37
verses.text: What vanity? Time, which passeth on, and floweth by.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:38
verses.text: For this "vanity" is said in comparison of the Truth, which ever abideth, and never faileth: for it too is a work of His Hand, in its degree.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:39
verses.text: "For," as it is written, "God filled the earth with His good things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:40
verses.text: What is "His"? That accord with Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:41
verses.text: But all these things, being earthly, fleeting, transitory, if they be compared to that Truth, where it is said, "I Am That I Am," all this which passeth away is called "vanity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:42
verses.text: For through time it vanisheth, like stroke into the air.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:43
verses.text: And why should I say more than that which the Apostle James said, willing to bring down proud men to humility, "What is," saith he, "your life? It is even a vapour, which appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:44
verses.text: Work then, though it be in the night, with thine hands, that is, by good works seek God, before the day come which shall gladden thee, lest the day come which shall sadden thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:45
verses.text: For see how safely thou workest, who art not left by Him whom thou seekest; "that thy Father which seeth in secret may reward thee openly".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:46
verses.text: "Lord, bow Thy heavens, and come down: touch the mountains, and they shall smoke".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:47
verses.text: "Flash Thy lightning, and Thou shalt scatter them; send forth Thine arrows, and Thou shalt confound them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:48
verses.text: "Send forth Thy Hand from above, and deliver me, and draw me out of many waters".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:49
verses.text: The Body of Christ, the humble David, full of grace, relying on God, fighting in this world, calleth for the help of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:50
verses.text: What are "heavens bowed down"? Apostles humbled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:51
verses.text: For those "heavens declare the glory of God;" and of these heavens declaring the glory of God it is presently said, "There is neither speech nor language, but their voices are heard among them," etc When then these heavens sent forth their voices through all lands, and did wonderful things, while the Lord flashed and thundered from them by miracles and commandments, the gods were thought to have come down from heaven to men.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:52
verses.text: For certain of the Gentiles, thinking this, desired even to sacrifice to them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:53
verses.text: But they commended to these the Lord Jesus Christ, humbling themselves, that God might be praised; because "the heavens" were "bowed," that "God" might "come down".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:54
verses.text: "Touch the mountains, and they shall smoke".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:55
verses.text: So long as they are not touched, they seem to themselves great: they are now about to say, "Great art Thou, O Lord:" the mountains also are about to say, "Thou only art the Most Highest over all the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:56
verses.text: But there are some that conspire, that "gather themselves together against the Lord, and against His Christ".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:57
verses.text: They have come together, they have conspired.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:58
verses.text: "Flash forth Thy lightnings, and Thou shalt scatter them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:59
verses.text: Abound with Thy miracles, and their conspiracy shall be broken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:60
verses.text: "Send forth Thine arrows, and Thou shalt confound them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:61
verses.text: Let the unsound be wounded, that, being well wounded, they may be made sound; and let them say, being set now in the Church, in the Body of Christ, let them say with the Church, "I am wounded with Love".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:62
verses.text: "Send forth Thine Hand from on high".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:63
verses.text: What afterward? What in the end? How conquereth the Body of Christ? By heavenly aid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:64
verses.text: "For the Lord Himself shall come with the voice of the Archangel, and with the trump of God shall He descend from heaven," Himself the Saviour of the body, the Hand of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:65
verses.text: What is, "Out of many waters"? From many peoples.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:66
verses.text: What peoples? Aliens, unbelievers, whether assailing us from without, or laying snares within.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:67
verses.text: Take me out of many waters, in which Thou didst discipline me, in which Thou didst roll me, to free me from my filth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:68
verses.text: This is the "water of contradiction".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:69
verses.text: "From the hand of strange children".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:70
verses.text: Hear, brethren, among whom we are, among whom we live, from whom we long to be delivered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:71
verses.text: "Whose mouth hath spoken vanity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:72
verses.text: All of you to-day, if ye had not gathered yourselves together to these divine shows of the word of God, and were not at this hour engaged in them, how great vanities would ye be hearing! "whose mouth hath spoken vanity:" when, in short, would they, speaking vanity, hear you speaking vanity? "And their right hand is a right hand of iniquity".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:73
verses.text: What doest thou among them with thy pastoral scrip with five stones in it? Say it to me in another form: that same law which thou hast signified by five stones, signify in some other way also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:74
verses.text: "I will sing a new song unto Thee, O God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:75
verses.text: "A new song" is of grace; "a new song" is of the new man; "a new song" is of the New Testament.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:76
verses.text: But lest thou shouldest think that grace departeth from the law, whereas rather by grace the law is fulfilled, "upon a psaltery of ten strings will I sing unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:77
verses.text: Upon the law of ten commandments: therein may I sing to Thee; therein may I rejoice to Thee; therein may "I sing to Thee a new song;" for, "Love is the fulfilling of the law".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:78
verses.text: But they who have not love may carry the psaltery, sing they cannot.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:79
verses.text: Contradiction cannot make my psaltery to be silent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:80
verses.text: "Who giveth salvation to kings, who redeemeth David His servant".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:81
verses.text: Ye know who David is; be yourselves David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:82
verses.text: Whence "redeemeth He David His servant"? Whence redeemeth He Christ? Whence redeemeth He the Body of Christ? "From the sword of ill intent deliver me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:83
verses.text: "From the sword" is not sufficient; he addeth, "of ill intent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:84
verses.text: Without doubt there is a sword of good intent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:85
verses.text: What is the sword of good intent? That whereof the Lord saith, "I came not to send peace on earth, but a sword".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:86
verses.text: For He was about to separate believers from unbelievers, sons from parents, and to sever all other ties, while the sword cut off what was diseased, but healed the members of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:87
verses.text: Of good intent then is the sword twice sharpened, powerful with both edges, the Old and New Testaments, with the narration of the past and the promise of the future.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:88
verses.text: That then is the sword of good intent: but the other is of ill intent, wherewith they talk vanity, for that is of good intent, wherewith God speaketh verity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:89
verses.text: For truly "the sons of men have teeth which are spears and arrows, and their tongue is a sharp sword".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:90
verses.text: "From" this "sword deliver me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:91
verses.text: "And take me out of the hand of strange children, whose mouth hath spoken vanity:" just as before.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:92
verses.text: And that which followeth, "their right hand is a right hand of iniquity," the same he had set down before also, when he called them "many waters".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:93
verses.text: For lest thou shouldest think that the "many waters" were good waters, he explained them by the "sword of ill intent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:94
verses.text: "Whose sons are like young vines firmly planted in their youth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:95
verses.text: He wisheth to recount their happiness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:96
verses.text: Observe, ye sons of light, sons of peace: observe, ye sons of the Church, members of Christ; observe whom he calleth "strangers," whom he calleth "strange children," whom he calleth "waters of contradiction," whom he calleth a "sword of ill intent".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:97
verses.text: Observe, I beseech you, for among them ye are in peril, among their tongues ye fight against the desires of your flesh, among their tongues, set in the hand of the devil wherewith he fightethWhat vanity hath their mouth spoken, and how is their right hand a right hand of iniquity? "Their daughters are fitted and adorned after the similitude of a temple".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:98
verses.text: "Their garners are full, bursting out from one store to another: their sheep are fruitful, multiplying in their streets" : "their oxen are fat: their hedge is not broken down, nor their road, nor is their crying in their streets".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:99
verses.text: Is not this then happiness? I ask the sons of the kingdom of heaven, I ask the offspring of everlasting resurrection, I ask the body of Christ, the members of Christ, the temple of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:100
verses.text: Is not this then happiness, to have sons safe, daughters beautiful, garners full, cattle abundant, no downfall, I say not of a wall, but not even of a hedge, no tumult and clamour in the streets, but quiet, peace, abundance, plenty of all things in their houses and in their cities? Is not this then happiness? or ought the righteous to shun it? or findest thou not the house of the righteous too abounding with all these things, full of this happiness? Did not Abraham's house abound with gold, silver, children, servants, cattle? What say we? is not this happiness? Be it so, still it is on the left hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:101
verses.text: What is, on the left hand? Temporal, mortal, bodily.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:102
verses.text: I desire not that thou shun it, but that thou think it not to be on the right hand.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:103
verses.text: For what ought they to have set on the right hand? God, eternity, the years of God which fail not, whereof is said, "and Thy years shall not fail".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:104
verses.text: There should be the right hand, there should be our longing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:105
verses.text: Let us use the left for the time, let us long for the fight for eternity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:106
verses.text: "If riches increase, set not your heart upon them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:107
verses.text: "They have called the people blessed who have these things".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:108
verses.text: O men that speak vanity! They have lost the true right hand, wicked and perverse, they have put on the benefits of God inversely.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:109
verses.text: O wicked ones, O speakers of vanity, O strange children! What was on the left hand, they have set on the right.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 144:110
verses.text: What dost thou, David? What dost thou, Body of Christ? What do ye, members of Christ? What do ye, not strange children, but children of God?What say ye? Say ye with us, "Blessed is the people whose Lord is their God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:1
verses.text: Psalm CXLV.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:2
verses.text: The title is, "Praise, to David himself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:3
verses.text: Praise to Christ Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:4
verses.text: And since He is called David, who came to us of the seed of David, yet He was our King, ruling us, and bringing us into His kingdom, therefore "Praise to David himself" is understood to mean, Praise to Christ Himself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:5
verses.text: Christ according to the flesh is David, because He is the Son of David: but according to His Divine Nature He is the Creator of David, and Lord of David.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:6
verses.text: "I will exalt Thee, my God, my King; and I will bless Thy Name for the age, and age upon age".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:7
verses.text: Ye see that the praise of God is here begun, and this praise is carried on even to the end of the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:8
verses.text: Now then begin to praise, if thou intendest to praise for ever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:9
verses.text: He who will not praise in this transitory "age," will be silent when "age upon age" has come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:10
verses.text: But lest any one should in any otherwise also understand what he saith, "I will praise Thy Name for the age," and should seek another age, wherein to praise, he saith, "Every day will I bless Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:11
verses.text: Praise then and bless the Lord thy God every day, that when single days have passed, and there has come one day without end, thou mayest go from praise to praise, as "from strength to strength".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:12
verses.text: No day shall pass by, wherein I bless Thee not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:13
verses.text: And it is no wonder, if in thy day of joy thou bless the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:14
verses.text: What if perchance some day of sorrow hath dawned on thee, as is natural in the circumstances of our mortal nature, as there is abundance of offences, as temptations are multiplied; what, if something sad befall thee, a man; wilt thou cease to praise God? wilt thou cease to bless thy Creator? If thou cease, thou hast lied in saying, "every day," etc.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:15
verses.text: But if thou cease not, although it seem to thee to be ill with thee in the day of thy sorrow, yet in thy God it shall be well with thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:16
verses.text: "Great is the Lord, and very much to be praised".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:17
verses.text: How much was he about to say? what terms was he about to seek? How vast a conception hath he included in the one word, "very much"? Imagine what thou wilt, for how can that be imagined, which cannot be contained? "He is very much to be praised.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:18
verses.text: And of His Greatness there is no end;" therefore said he "very much:" lest perchance thou begin to wish to praise, and think that thou canst reach the end of His praises, whose Greatness can have no end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:19
verses.text: Think not then that He, whose Greatness has no end, can ever be enough praised by thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:20
verses.text: Is it not then better that as He has no end, so neither should thy praise have end? His Greatness is without end; let thy praise also be without end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:21
verses.text: For how great things besides has His boundless Goodness and illimitable Greatness made, which we do not know! When we lift the gaze of our eyes even to the heaven, and then recall it from sun, moon, and stars to the earth, and there is all this space where our sight can wander; beyond the heavens who can extend the eyesight of his mind, not to say of his flesh? So far then as His works are known to us, let us praise Him through His works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:22
verses.text: "Generation and generation shall praise Thy works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:23
verses.text: Every generation shall praise Thy works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:24
verses.text: For perhaps every generation is meant by "generation and generation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:25
verses.text: Did he perchance mean to imply two generations by that repetition? For we are in this generation sons of God, we shall be in another generation sons of the Resurrection.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:26
verses.text: Scripture hath called us "sons of the Resurrection;" the Resurrection itself it hath called Regeneration.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:27
verses.text: "In the regeneration," it saith, "when the Son of Man shall be seated in His Majesty".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:28
verses.text: So also in another place; "For they shall not marry, nor be given in marriage, for they are the sons of the Resurrection".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:29
verses.text: Therefore "generation and generation shall praise Thy works.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:30
verses.text: And they shall tell out Thine excellence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:31
verses.text: For neither shall they praise Thy works, save in order to "tell out Thine excellence".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:32
verses.text: Boys at school are set to praise, and all such things are set before them to be praised, as God hath wrought: a mortal is set to praise the sun, the sky, the earth; to come to even lesser things, to praise a rose, or a laurel; all these are works of God: they are set, they are undertaken, they are praised: the works are lauded, of the Worker they are silent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:33
verses.text: I desire in the works to praise the Creator: I love not a thankless praiser.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:34
verses.text: Dost thou praise what He hath made, and art silent of Him who made? In that which thou seest, what is it that thou praisest? The form, the usefulness, some virtue, some power in the things.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:35
verses.text: If beauty delight thee, what is more beautiful than the Maker? If usefulness be praised, what more useful than He who made all things? If excellence be praised, what more excellent than He by whom all things were made?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:36
verses.text: "They shall speak of the magnificence of the glory of Thy Holiness, and shall record Thy wondrous deeds".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:37
verses.text: "And the excellence of Thy fearful works shall they speak of: and Thy greatness, they shall relate it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:38
verses.text: "The remembrance of the abundance of Thy sweetness they shall pour forth" : none but Thine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:39
verses.text: See whether this man, meditating on Thy works, hath turned aside from the Worker to the work: see whether he hath sunk from Him who made, to the things which He made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:40
verses.text: Of the things which He hath made, he hath made a step up to Him, not a descent from Him to them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:41
verses.text: For if thou love these more than Him, thou wilt not have Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:42
verses.text: And what profit is it to thee to overflow with the works, if the Worker leave thee? Truly thou shouldest love them; but love Him more, and love them for His sake.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:43
verses.text: For He doth not hold out promises, without holding out threats also: if He held out no promises, there would be no encouragement; if He held out no threats, there would be no correction.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:44
verses.text: They that praise Thee therefore shall "speak" also "of the excellence of Thy terrible deeds;" the excellence of that work of Thy hands which punisheth and administereth discipline, they shall speak of, they shall not be silent: for they shall not proclaim Thine everlasting kingdom, and be silent about Thine everlasting fire.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:45
verses.text: For the praise of God, setting thee in the way, ought to show thee both what thou shouldest love, and what thou shouldest fear; what thou shouldest seek, and what thou shouldest shun; what thou shouldest choose, and what thou shouldest avoid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:46
verses.text: The time of choice is now, the time of receiving will be hereafter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:47
verses.text: Let then the excellence of Thy terrible things be told.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:48
verses.text: Unlimited as it is, though "of Thy greatness there is no end," they shall not be silent about it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:49
verses.text: How shall they recount it, if there is no end of it? They shall recount it when they praise it; and because there is no end of it, so of His praise also there shall be no end.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:50
verses.text: "The remembrance of the abundance of Thy sweetness they shall pour forth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:51
verses.text: O happy feasts! What shall they eat, who thus shall "pour forth"!So eat, that thou mayest pour forth again; so receive, that thou mayest give.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:52
verses.text: Thou eatest, when thou learnest; thou pourest forth again, when thou teachest: thou eatest, when thou hearest; thou pourest forth again, when thou preachest; but that thou pourest forth, which thou hast first eaten.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:53
verses.text: Finally, that most eager feaster John, to whom the very table of the Lord sufficed not, unless he leaned on the Lord's breast, and of his inmost heart drank in divine secrets; what did he pour forth? "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:54
verses.text: How is it that it sufficeth not to say, "Thy remembrance;" or, "the remembrance of Thine abundance"? Because, what availeth it if it be abundant, yet not sweet? So also it is annoying if it be sweet but too little.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:55
verses.text: By "pouring forth" this, His preachers "shall exult in His righteousness" not in their own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:56
verses.text: What then hast Thou done unto us, O Lord, whom we praise, that we should be, that we should praise, that we should "exult in Thy righteousness," that we should "utter forth the remembrance of the abundance of Thy sweetness"? Let us tell it, and, as we tell, let us praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:57
verses.text: "Merciful and pitiful is the Lord; long-suffering, and very merciful".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:58
verses.text: "Sweet is the Lord to all, and His compassions reach into all His works".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:59
verses.text: Were He not such as this, there would be no seeking to recover us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:60
verses.text: Consider thyself: what didst thou deserve, O sinner? Despiser of God, what didst thou deserve? See if aught occur to thee but penalty, if aught occur to thee but punishment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:61
verses.text: Thou seest then what was due to thee, and what He hath given, who gave gratis.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:62
verses.text: There was given pardon to the sinner; there was given the spirit of justification; there was given charity and love, wherein thou mayest do all good works; and beyond this, He will give thee also life everlasting, and fellowship with the angels: all of His mercy.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:63
verses.text: Hear the Scripture: "I will not the death of a sinner, but rather that he should turn, and live".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:64
verses.text: By these words of God, he is brought back to hope; but there is another snare to be feared, lest through this very hope he sin the more.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:65
verses.text: What then didst thou also say, thou who through hope sinnest yet more? "Whensoever I turn, God will forgive me all; I will do whatsoever I will".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:66
verses.text: Say not then, "To-morrow I will turn, to-morrow I will please God; and all to-day's and yesterday's deeds shall be forgiven me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 145:67
