Brethren, let us return their good will (for they do mean it well) with prayers to the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:190
verses.text: They wish us well; but "he that loveth iniquity, hateth his own soul".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:191
verses.text: If he hateth his own soul, how shall he love my soul? Yet with a perverse, and empty, and vain good will, if indeed it may be called good will, they grieve that we lose what they love: let us pray that they lose not what we love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:192
verses.text: Behold of what character that Jerusalem is to be which he exhorteth to praise, or rather foreseeth will praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:193
verses.text: For the praises of that city, when we shall see and love and praise, will not need to be urged on and stirred up by the voice of prophecy; but the Prophets now say this, to drink in as far as while they remain in this flesh they can, the future joys of the blessed, and then giving them forth into our ears, to arouse in us love of that city.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:194
verses.text: Let us burn with longing, let us not be slothful in spirit.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:195
verses.text: "Praise thy God, O Sion".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:196
verses.text: He saith, "He hath made strong the bars of thy gates".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:197
verses.text: The making bars strong is not for open gates, but shut ones, wherefore most manuscripts read, "He hath made strong the bolts of thy gates".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:198
verses.text: Observe, beloved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:199
verses.text: He biddeth Jerusalem when closed in to praise the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:200
verses.text: We praise in unison now, we praise now; but it is amid offences.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:201
verses.text: Many where we wish not, enter in: many though we wish it not, go out: therefore offences are frequent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:202
verses.text: "And because iniquity hath abounded," saith the Truth, "the love of many waxeth cold:" because men come in whom we cannot discern, because men go out whom we cannot retain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:203
verses.text: Wherefore is this? Because not yet is there perfection, not yet is there the bliss that shall be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:204
verses.text: Wherefore is this? Because as yet it is the threshing-floor, not yet the garner.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:205
verses.text: What therefore will be then, save no fear that aught of this kind will happen? He said not only, He hath set, but, "He hath made strong the bars of thy gates".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:206
verses.text: Let none go out, let none come in.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:207
verses.text: Let none go out, we rejoice: let none come in, we fear.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:208
verses.text: Nay, fear not this: when thou hast entered it will be said: only be thou in the number of virgins, who carried their oil with them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:209
verses.text: "He hath blessed thy children within thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:210
verses.text: Who? He "who hath set peace as thy borders".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:211
verses.text: How ye all exult! Love peace, my brethren.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:212
verses.text: Greatly are we delighted, when the love of peace crieth from your hearts.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:213
verses.text: How greatly doth it delight you! I had said nothing: I had explained nothing: I but read the verse, and ye shouted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:214
verses.text: What was it that shouted in you? The love of peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:215
verses.text: children of the kingdom, O citizens of Jerusalem, in Jerusalem is the vision of peace: and all who love peace are blest in her, and they enter in, when the doors are being shut, and the bars made strong.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:216
verses.text: This, which when but named ye so love and esteem, this follow after, this long for: this love in your home, in your business, in your wives, in your sons, in your slaves, in your friends, in your enemies.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:217
verses.text: What ye cried out a while ago at the very mention of peace, ye cried from longing: your cry was from thirst, not from fulness; for there will be perfect righteousness where will be perfect peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:218
verses.text: Now we hunger and thirst after righteousness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:219
verses.text: "They shall be filled".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:220
verses.text: How shall they be filled? When we have arrived at peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:221
verses.text: Therefore when he had said, "Who hath set peace for thy borders," because there is fulness and no want, he added at once, "and filleth thee with the fat of wheat".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:222
verses.text: "Who sendeth forth His Word to the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:223
verses.text: Behold, on earth we toil, weary, fainting, sluggish, cold: when should we be raised up to the fat of wheat that satisfieth, did not He send His Word to the earth, whereby we were weighed down, to the earth, whereby we were hindered from returning? He sent His Word, He deserted us not even in the wilderness, He rained manna from heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:224
verses.text: "Who sendeth forth His Word to the earth;" and to earth His Word came.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:225
verses.text: How? or what is His Word? "Even unto swiftness His Word runneth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:226
verses.text: He said not, "His Word is swift," but, "His Word runneth even unto swiftness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:227
verses.text: Let us understand, my brethren: He could not have chosen a better word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:228
verses.text: He who is hot grows hot by heat, he who is cold grows cold by cold, he who is swift becometh swift by swiftness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:229
verses.text: To what degree then doth it run? "Even to swiftness".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:230
verses.text: Increase as much as you will the swiftness of the Word, and say, It is as swift as this or that, as birds, as the winds, as the Angels; is any of these as great as swiftness itself, "even unto swiftness"? What is swiftness itself, brethren? It is everywhere; it is not in part.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:231
verses.text: This belongeth to the Word of God, not to be in part, to be everywhere by Himself the Word, whereby He is "the Power of God and the Wisdom of God," before He had taken flesh upon Him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:232
verses.text: If we think of God in the Form of God, the Word equal to the Father, this is the Wisdom of God, of which is said, "It reacheth from one end to the other mightily".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:233
verses.text: What mighty speed! "It reacheth from one end to the other mightily".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:234
verses.text: We then are burdened by the sluggishness of this cold body, and the bonds of this earthly and corruptible life; have we no hope of receiving "the Word," which "runneth even unto swiftness"? or hath abandoned us, though by the body we are depressed to the lowest depths? Did not He predestinate us, before we were born in this mortal and sluggish body? He then, who predestinated us, gave snow to the earth, even ourselves.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:235
verses.text: For now let us come to those somewhat obscure verses of the Psalm, let those entanglements begin to be unrolled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:236
verses.text: Behold, we are sluggish on this earth, and are as it were frozen here.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:237
verses.text: And just as happens to the flakes of snow, for they freeze above, then fall down; so as love groweth cold, human nature falleth down to this earth, and involved in a sluggish body becometh like snow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:238
verses.text: But in that snow are predestined sons of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:239
verses.text: For, "He giveth snow like wool".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:240
verses.text: What is "like wool"? It meaneth, of the snow which He hath given, of these, who are as yet slow in spirit and cold, whom He hath predestinated, He is about to make somewhat.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:241
verses.text: For wool is the material of a garment: when we see wool, we look on it as a sort of preparation for a garment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:242
verses.text: Therefore since He hath predestinated these, who at present are cold and creep on earth, and as yet glow not with the spirit of love (for as yet He speaketh of predestination), God hath given these as a sort of wool: He is about to make of them a garment.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:243
verses.text: Rightly did the "raiment" of Christ "shine" on the mountain, "like snow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:244
verses.text: The raiment of Christ did shine like snow, as though of that snow a garment had already been made: of which wool, that is, of the snow which He gave like wool, they being as yet predestined, were sluggish: but wait, see what followeth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:245
verses.text: Since He gave them as wool, a garment is made of them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:246
verses.text: For as the Church is called the Body of Christ, so is the Church also called the garment of Christ: hence cometh that which is said by the Apostle, "that He might present it to Himself a glorious Church, not having spot or wrinkle".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:247
verses.text: Let Him then present unto Himself a glorious Church, not having spot or wrinkle; let Him make Himself a garment of that wool, which He had predestinated in the snow.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:248
verses.text: While men are yet unbelieving, and cold, and sluggish, let Him make a garment of this wool.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:249
verses.text: That it may be washed from spots, let it be cleansed by faith: that it may have no wrinkle, let it be stretched out upon the cross.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:250
verses.text: "He scattereth mist like ashes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:251
verses.text: "He scattereth," saith the Psalmist, "mist like ashes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:252
verses.text: Who? He "who giveth snow like wool".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:253
verses.text: For whom He predestined, He calleth to repentance; for "whom He predestined, them He also called".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:254
verses.text: But "ashes" are connected with repentance.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:255
verses.text: Hear Him calling to repentance, when He upbraided certain cities, saying, "Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works which have been done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they had long ago repented in dust and ashes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:256
verses.text: Therefore, "He scattereth mist like ashes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:257
verses.text: What is, "He scattereth mist like ashes"? When a man is called to learn about God, and it is said to him, "Receive the truth;" he beginneth to wish to receive the Truth, but is not able; he seeth that He is under a sort of darkness, which before he saw not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:258
verses.text: Wander not in the mist, follow in faith.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:259
verses.text: But forasmuch as thou endeavourest to see and art not able, repent of thy sins, for mist is scattered like ashes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:260
verses.text: Repent thee now of having been obstinate against God, repent of having followed thine own evil ways.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:261
verses.text: Thou hast come into this state where it is difficult for thee to see the vision of bliss, and the mist will be healthful to thee, which God scattereth like ashes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:262
verses.text: Thou thyself art as yet a mist, but like ashes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:263
verses.text: For they that are penitent, as yet roll themselves in ashes, my brethren, testifying, as it were, that they are like it, saying unto God, "I am ashes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:264
verses.text: For a certain Scripture saith, "I have despised myself, and wasted away, I have reckoned myself earth and ashes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:265
verses.text: This is the humility of the penitent.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:266
verses.text: When Abraham speaketh to his God, and wisheth the burning of Sodom to be disclosed to him, he saith, "I am but earth and ashes".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:267
verses.text: How hath this humility ever been found in great and holy men!.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:268
verses.text: "Who sendeth His crystal like morsels of bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:269
verses.text: We need not spend our toil again in saying what crystal is.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:270
verses.text: We have already said it, and I do not think that ye, beloved, have forgotten it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:271
verses.text: What is then, "He sendeth His crystal like morsels of bread"? What is "crystal"? It is very hard, it is very tightly congealed; it can not, like snow, be easily melted.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:272
verses.text: Snow, hardened by many years' duration, and by the succession of ages, is called "crystal," and this "He sendeth like morsels of bread".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:273
verses.text: What meaneth this? They were too hard, no longer fit to be compared to snow, but to crystal; but they too are predestinated and called, and some of them even so as to feed others, to be useful to others also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:274
verses.text: And what need is there to enumerate many, whom we happen to know, this one and that one? Every one when he thinks can recall to mind how hardened and obstinate some of those whom he knows have been, how they have struggled against the truth; yet now they preach the truth, they have been made morsels of bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:275
verses.text: Who is that one Bread? "We being many," saith the Apostle, "are one Body in Christ;" he saith also, "we being many are one Bread and one Body".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:276
verses.text: If then the whole Body of Christ is one Bread, the members of Christ are morsels of Bread.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:277
verses.text: Of some that are hard He maketh members of Himself, and useful for feeding others.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:278
verses.text: Behold, the Apostle Paul was a crystal, hard, resisting the truth, crying out against the Gospel, hardening himself, as it were, against the sun.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:279
verses.text: Since then he was crystal, he appeared clear and white, but he was hard and very cold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:280
verses.text: How was he bright and white? "An Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:281
verses.text: Behold the brightness of crystal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:282
verses.text: Now hear the hardness of crystal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:283
verses.text: "As touching zeal, persecuting the Church" of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:284
verses.text: Among the stoners of the holy martyr Stephen, was he, hard, perhaps harder than all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:285
verses.text: "For he kept the raiment of all who were stoning," so that he stoned by the hands of all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:286
verses.text: Thus then we see "the snow, the mist, the crystal:" it is good that He blow and thaw them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:287
verses.text: For if He blow not, if He Himself thaw not the hardness of this ice, "in the face of His cold who shall stand?" He abandoneth a sinner, behold, He calleth him not; behold, He openeth not his perception; behold, He poureth not in grace; let the man thaw himself, if he can, from the ice of folly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:288
verses.text: He cannot.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:289
verses.text: Wherefore can he not? "In the face of His cold who shall stand?" Behold him then growing harder, and saying, "O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?" Behold, I am growing cold, behold, I am growing hard, what heat shall thaw me that I may run? "Who shall deliver me from the body of this death?.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:290
verses.text: In the face of His cold who shall stand?" And who shall free himself, if God abandon him? Who is it that freeth? "The grace of God, through Jesus Christ our Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:291
verses.text: Are we then to despair? God forbid.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:292
verses.text: For it goeth on, "He shall send out His Word, and melt them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:293
verses.text: Let not then the snow despair, nor the mist, nor the crystal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:294
verses.text: For of the snow, as of wool, a garment is being made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:295
verses.text: That mist findeth safety in repentance: for, "whom He predestinated, them He also called".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:296
verses.text: But even though they be the very hardest among the predestinated, though they have been for a long time hardening, and are become crystal, they will not be hard to the mercy of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:297
verses.text: "He shall send out His Word, and melt them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:298
verses.text: What is "melt"? Understand not "melt" in an ill sense: it meaneth, He shall liquefy, He shall thaw them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:299
verses.text: For they are hard through pride.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:300
verses.text: Rightly is pride called also dulness: for whatever is dull, is also cold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:301
verses.text: Despair not even of the crystal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:302
verses.text: Hear a saying of the crystal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:303
verses.text: "Who before was a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:304
verses.text: But wherefore doth God melt the crystal? That the snow despair not of itself.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:305
verses.text: For he saith, "For this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first Jesus Christ might show forth all long-suffering, for a pattern to them that hereafter should believe on Him unto eternal life".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:306
verses.text: God then calleth unto the Gentiles, "Be melted, O crystal; come, ye snows".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:307
verses.text: "His Spirit shall blow, and the waters shall flow".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:308
verses.text: Lo, the "crystal" and the "snows" are melted, they turn into water, "let them that thirst, come and drink".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:309
verses.text: Saul, hard as crystal, persecuted Stephen unto death; Paul, now in the living water, calleth the Gentiles to the Fount.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:310
verses.text: "Announcing His Word unto Jacob, His Righteousnesses and Judgments unto Israel".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:311
verses.text: What "Righteousnesses," what "Judgments"? Because whatever mankind had suffered here before, when it was "snow" and "mist" and "crystal," it suffered for the deserts of its pride and uplifting against God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:312
verses.text: Let us go back to the origin of our fall, and see that most truly is it sung in the Psalm, "Before I was troubled I went wrong".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:313
verses.text: But he who says, "Before I was troubled I went wrong," saith also, "It is good for me that Thou hast humbled me, that I may learn Thy Righteousnesses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:314
verses.text: These righteousnesses Jacob learnt from God, who made him to wrestle with an Angel; under the guise of which Angel, God Himself wrestled with him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:315
verses.text: He held Him, he exerted violence to hold Him, he prevailed to hold Him: He caused Himself to be held, in mercy, not in weakness.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:316
verses.text: Jacob therefore wrestled, and prevailed: he held Him and when he seemed to have conquered Him asked to be blessed of Him How did he understand with Whom he had wrestled, Whom he had held? Wherefore did he wrestle violently, and hold Him? Because "the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:317
verses.text: Wherefore then did he wrestle? Because it is with toil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:318
verses.text: Wherefore do we with difficulty hold, what we so easily lose? Lest, easily getting back what we have lost, we learn to lose that which we hold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:319
verses.text: Let man have toil to hold: he will hold firmly, what he has only held after toil.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:320
verses.text: These His judgments therefore God manifested to Jacob and Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:321
verses.text: "He hath not done so to the whole race".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:322
verses.text: Let none deceive you: it is not announced to any nation, this judgment of God; namely, how the righteous and the unrighteous suffer, how all suffer for their deserts, how the righteous themselves are freed by the grace of God, not in their own merits.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:323
verses.text: This is not announced to the whole race, but only to Jacob, only to Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:324
verses.text: What then do we, if He hath not announced it to the whole race, but only to Jacob, only to Israel? Where will we be? In Jacob.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:325
verses.text: "He hath not manifested His judgments to them".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:326
verses.text: To whom? To all nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:327
verses.text: How then are the "snows" called, when the crystal is melted? How are the nations called, now Paul is justified? How, save to be in Jacob? The wild olive is cut off from its stock, to be grafted into the olive: now they belong to the olive, no longer ought they to be called nations, but one nation in Christ, the nation of Jacob, the nation of IsraelWhat is Israel? "Seeing God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:328
verses.text: Where shall he see God? In peace.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:329
verses.text: What peace? The peace of Jerusalem; for, saith he, "He hath set peace for thy borders".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 147:330
verses.text: There shall we praise: there shall we all be one, in One, unto One: for then, though many, we shall not be scattered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:1
verses.text: Psalm CXLVIII.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:2
verses.text: The subject of our meditation in this present life should be the praises of God; for the everlasting exaltation of our life hereafter will be the praise of God, and none can become fit for the life hereafter, who hath not practised himself for it now.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:3
verses.text: So then now we praise God, but we pray to Him too.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:4
verses.text: Our praise is marked by joy, our prayer by groans.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:5
verses.text: On account of these two seasons, one, that which now is in the temptations and tribulations of this life, the other, that which is to be hereafter in everlasting rest and exultation; we have established also the celebration of two seasons, that before Easter and that after Easter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:6
verses.text: That which is before Easter signifieth tribulation, in which we now are; that which we are now keeping after Easter, signifieth the bliss in which we shall hereafter be.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:7
verses.text: The celebration then which we keep before Easter is what we do now: by that which we keep after Easter we signify what as yet we have not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:8
verses.text: Therefore we employ that time in fastings and prayer, this present time we spend in praises, and relax our fast.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:9
verses.text: This is the Halleluia which we sing, which, as you know, meaneth (in Latin), Praise ye the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:10
verses.text: Therefore that period is before the Lord's Resurrection, this, after His Resurrection: by which time is signified the future hope which as yet we have not: for what we represent after the Lord's Resurrection, we shall have after our own.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:11
verses.text: For in our Head both are figured, both are set forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:12
verses.text: The Baptism of the Lord setteth forth to us this present life of trial, for in it we must toil, be harassed, and, at last, die; but the Resurrection and Glorification of the Lord setteth forth to us the life which we are to have hereafter, when He shall come to recompense due rewards, evil to the evil, good to the good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:13
verses.text: And now indeed all the evil men sing with us, Halleluia; but, if they persevere in their wickedness, they may utter with their lips the song of our life hereafter; but the life itself, which will then be in the reality which now is typified, they cannot obtain, because they would not practise it before it came, and lay hold on what was to come.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:14
verses.text: "Halleluia".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:15
verses.text: "Praise the Lord," thou sayest to thy neighbour, he to thee: when all are exhorting each other, all are doing what they exhort others to do.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:16
verses.text: But praise with your whole selves: that is, let not your tongue and voice alone praise God, but your conscience also, your life, your deeds.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:17
verses.text: For now, when we are gathered together in the Church, we praise: when we go forth each to his own business, we seem to cease to praise God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:18
verses.text: Let a man not cease to live well, and then he ever praiseth God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:19
verses.text: It is impossible for a man's acts to be evil, whose thoughts are good.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:20
verses.text: For acts issue from thought: nor can a man do anything or move his limbs to do aught, unless the bidding of his thought precede: just as in all things which ye see done throughout the provinces, whatsoever the Emperor biddeth goeth forth from the inner part of his palace throughout the whole Roman Empire How great commotion is caused at one bidding by the Emperor as he sits in his palace! He but moveth his lips, when he speaketh: the whole province is moved, when what he speaketh is being executed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:21
verses.text: So in each single man too, the Emperor is within, his seat is in the heart.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:22
verses.text: If he be good and biddeth good things, good things are done: if he be bad and biddeth evil things, evil things are done.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:23
verses.text: When Christ sitteth there, what can He bid, but what is good? When the devil is the occupant, what can he bid, but evil? But God hath willed that it should be in thy choice for whom thou wilt prepare room, for God, or for the devil: when thou hast prepared it, he who is occupant will also rule.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:24
verses.text: Therefore, brethren, attend not only to the sound; when ye praise God, praise with your whole selves: let your voice, your life, your deeds, all sing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:25
verses.text: "Praise ye the Lord from heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:26
verses.text: As though he had found things in heaven holding their peace in the praise of the Lord, he exhorteth them to arise and praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:27
verses.text: Never have things in heaven held their peace in the praises of their Creator, never have things on earth ceased to praise God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:28
verses.text: But it is manifest that there are certain things which have breath to praise God in that disposition wherein God pleaseth them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:29
verses.text: For no one praiseth aught, save what pleaseth him.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:30
verses.text: And there are other things which have not breath of life and understanding to praise God, but yet, because they also are good, and duly arranged in their proper order, and form part of the beauty of the universe, which God created, though they themselves with voice and heart praise not God, yet when they are considered by those who have understanding, God is praised in them; and, as God is praised in them, they themselves too in a manner praise God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:31
verses.text: "Praise ye the Lord from heaven: praise Him in the high places".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:32
verses.text: First he saith, "from heaven," then from earth; for it is God that is praised, who made heaven and earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:33
verses.text: All in heaven is calm and peaceful; there is ever joy, no death, no sickness, no vexation; there the blessed ever praise God; but we are still below: yet, when we think how God is praised there, let us have our heart there, and let us not hear to no purpose, "Lift up your hearts".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:34
verses.text: Let us lift up our heart above, that it become not corrupted on earth: for we take pleasure in what the Angels do there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:35
verses.text: We do it now in hope: hereafter we shall in reality, when we have come thither.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:36
verses.text: "Praise Him" then "in the high places".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:37
verses.text: "Praise Him, all ye angels of His, praise Him, all His powers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:38
verses.text: "Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all ye stars and light".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:39
verses.text: "Praise Him, ye heaven of heavens, and waters that are above the heavens".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:40
verses.text: "Let them praise the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:41
verses.text: When can he unfold all in his enumeration? Yet he hath in a manner touched upon them all summarily, and included all things in heaven praising their Creator.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:42
verses.text: And as though it were said to him, "Why do they praise Him? what hath He conferred on them, that they should praise Him?" he goeth on, "for He spake, and they were made; He commanded, and they were created".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:43
verses.text: No wonder if the works praise the Worker, no wonder if the things that are made praise the Maker, no wonder if creation praise its Creator.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:44
verses.text: In this Christ also is mentioned, though we seem not to have heard His Name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:45
verses.text: By what were they made? By the Word? How doth he show in this Psalm, that all things were made by the Word? "He spake, and they were made; He commanded, and they were created".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:46
verses.text: No one speaketh, no one commandeth, save by word.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:47
verses.text: "He hath established them for the age, and for age upon age".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:48
verses.text: All things in heaven, all things above, all powers and angels, a certain city on high, good, holy, blessed; from whence because we are wanderers, we are wretched; whither because we are to return, we are blessed in hope; whither when we shall have returned, we shall be blessed indeed; "He hath given them a law which shall not pass away".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:49
verses.text: What sort of command, think ye, have things in heaven and the holy angels received? What sort of command hath God given them? What, but that they praise Him? Blessed are they whose business is to praise God! They plough not, they sow not, they grind not, they cook not; for these are works of necessity, and there is no necessity there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:50
verses.text: They steal not, they plunder not, they commit no adultery; for these are works of iniquity, and there is no iniquity there.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:51
verses.text: They break not bread for the hungry, they clothe not the naked, they take not in the stranger, they visit not the sick, they set not at one the contentious, they bury not the dead; for these are works of mercy, and there there is no misery, for mercy to be shown to.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:52
verses.text: O blessed they! Think we that we too shall be like this? Ah! let us sigh, let us groan in sighing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:53
verses.text: And what are we, that we should be there? mortal, outcast, abject, earth and ashes! But He, who hath promised, is almighty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:54
verses.text: Let him then turn himself to things on earth too, since he hath already spoken the praises of things in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:55
verses.text: "Praise ye the Lord from the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:56
verses.text: For wherewith began he before? "Praise ye the Lord from heaven:" and he went through things in heaven: now hear of things on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:57
verses.text: "Dragons and all abysses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:58
verses.text: "Abysses" are depths of water: all the seas, and this atmosphere of clouds, pertain to the "abyss".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:59
verses.text: Where there are clouds, where there are storms, where there is rain, lightning, thunder, hail, snow, and all that God willeth should be done above the earth, by this moist and misty atmosphere, all this he hath mentioned under the name of earth, because it is very changeable and mortal; unless ye think that it raineth from above the stars All these things happen here, close to the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:60
verses.text: Sometimes even men are on the tops of mountains, and see the clouds beneath them, and often it raineth: and all commotions which arise from the disturbance of the atmosphere, those who watch carefully see that they happen here, in this lower part of the universe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:61
verses.text: Thou seest then what kind all these things are, changeable, troublous, fearful, corruptible: yet they have their place, they have their rank, they too in their degree fill up the beauty of the universe, and so they praise the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:62
verses.text: He turns then to them, as though He would exhort them too, or us, that by considering them we may praise the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:63
verses.text: "Dragons" live about the water, come out from caverns, fly through the air; the air is set in motion by them: "dragons" are a huge kind of living creatures, greater there are not upon the earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:64
verses.text: Therefore with them he beginneth, "Dragons and all abysses".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:65
verses.text: There are caves of hidden waters, whence springs and streams come forth: some come forth to flow over the earth, some flow secretly beneath; and all this kind, all this damp nature of waters, together with the sea and this lower air, are called abyss, or "abysses," where dragons live and praise God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:66
verses.text: What? Think we that the dragons form choirs, and praise God? Far from it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:67
verses.text: But do ye, when ye consider the dragons, regard the Maker of the dragon, the Creator of the dragon: then, when ye admire the dragons, and say, "Great is the Lord who made these," then the dragons praise God by your voices.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:68
verses.text: "Fire, hail, snow, ice, wind of storms, which do His word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:69
verses.text: Wherefore added he here, "which do His word"? Many foolish men, unable to contemplate and discern creation, in its several places and rank, performing its movements at the nod and commandment of God think that God doth indeed rule all things above, but things below He despiseth, casteth aside, abandoneth, so that He neither careth for them, nor guideth, nor ruleth them; but that they are ruled by chance, how they can, as they can: and they are influenced by what they say sometimes to one another: e.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:70
verses.text: g.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:71
verses.text: "If it were God that gave rain, would He rain into the sea? What sort of providence," they say, "is this? Getulia is thirsty, and it rains into the sea".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:72
verses.text: They think that they handle the matter cleverly.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:73
verses.text: One should say to them, "Getulia does at all events thirst, thou dost not even thirst".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:74
verses.text: For good were it for thee to say to God, "My soul hath thirsted for Thee".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:75
verses.text: For he that thus argueth is already satisfied; he thinketh himself learned, he is not willing to learn, therefore he thirsteth not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:76
verses.text: For if he thirsted, he would be willing to learn, and he would find that everything happeneth upon earth by God's Providence, and he would wonder at the arrangement of even the limbs of a flea.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:77
verses.text: Attend, beloved.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:78
verses.text: Who hath arranged the limbs of a flea and a gnat, that they should have their proper order, life, motion? Consider one little creature, even the very smallest, whatever thou wilt.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:79
verses.text: If thou considerest the order of its limbs, and the animation of life whereby it moveth; how doth it shun death, love life, seek pleasures, avoid pain, exert divers senses, vigorously use movements suitable to itself! Who gave its sting to the gnat, for it to suck blood with? How narrow is the pipe whereby it sucketh! Who arranged all this? who made all this? Thou art amazed at the smallest things; praise Him that is great.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:80
verses.text: Hold then this, my brethren, let none shake you from your faith or from sound doctrine.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:81
verses.text: He who made the Angel in heaven, the Same also made the worm upon earth: the Angel in heaven to dwell in heaven, the worm upon earth to abide on earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:82
verses.text: He made not the Angel to creep in the mud, nor the worm to move in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:83
verses.text: He hath assigned dwellers to their different abodes; incorruption He assigned to incorruptible abodes, corruptible things to corruptible abodes.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:84
verses.text: Observe the whole, praise the whole.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:85
verses.text: He then who ordered the limbs of the worm, doth He not govern the clouds? And wherefore raineth He into the sea? As though there are not in the sea things which are nourished by rain; as though He made not fishes therein, as though He made not living creatures therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:86
verses.text: Observe how the fishes run to sweet water.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:87
verses.text: And wherefore, saith he, doth He give rain to the fishes, and sometimes giveth not rain to me? That thou mayest consider that thou art in a desert region, and in a pilgrimage of life; that so this present life may grow bitter to thee, that thou mayest long for the life to come: or else that thou mayest be scourged, punished, amended.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:88
verses.text: And how well doth He assign their properties to regions.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:89
verses.text: Behold, since we have spoken of Getulia, He raineth here nearly every year, and giveth corn every year; here the corn cannot be kept, it soon rotteth, because it is given every year; there, because it is given seldom, both much is given, and it can be kept for long.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:90
verses.text: But dost thou perchance think that God there deserteth man, or that they do not there after their own manner of rejoicing both praise and glorify God? Take a Getulian from his country, and set him amid our pleasant trees; he will wish to flee away, and return to his bare Getulia.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:91
verses.text: To all places then, regions, seasons, God hath assigned and arranged what fits them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:92
verses.text: Who could unfold it? Yet they who have eyes see many things therein: when seen, they please; pleasing, they are praised; not they really, but He who made them; thus shall all things praise God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:93
verses.text: It was in thought of this that the spirit of the Prophet added the words, "which do His word".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:94
verses.text: Think not then that these things are moved by chance, which in every motion of theirs obey God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:95
verses.text: Whither God willeth, thither the fire spreads, thither the cloud hurries, whether it carry in it rain, or snow, or hail.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:96
verses.text: And wherefore doth the lightning sometimes strike the mountain, yet strikes not the robber?Perhaps He yet seeketh the robber's conversion, and therefore is the mountain which feareth not smitten, that the man who feareth may be changed.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:97
verses.text: Thou also sometimes, when maintaining discipline, smitest the ground to terrify a child.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:98
verses.text: Sometimes too He smiteth a man, whom He will.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:99
verses.text: But thou sayest to me, Behold, He smiteth the more innocent, and passeth over the more guilty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:100
verses.text: Wonder not; death, whencesoever it come, is good to the good man.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:101
verses.text: And whence dost thou know what punishment is reserved in secret for that more guilty man, if he be unwilling to be converted? Would not they rather be scorched by lightning, to whom it shall be said in the end, "Depart into everlasting fire"? The needful thing is, that thou be guileless.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:102
verses.text: Why so? Is it an evil thing to die by shipwreck, and a good thing to die by fever? Whether he die in this way or in that, ask what sort of man he is who dieth; ask whither he will go after death, not how he is to depart from life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:103
verses.text: Whatever then happeneth here contrary to our wish, thou wilt know that it happeneth not, save by the will of God, by His providence, by His ordering, by His nod, by His laws: and if we understand not why anything is done, let us grant to His providence that it is not done without reason: so shall we not be blasphemers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:104
verses.text: For when we begin to argue concerning the works of God, "why is this?" "why is that?" and, "He ought not to have done this," "He did this ill;" where is the praise of God? Thou hast lost thy Halleluia.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:105
verses.text: Regard all things in such wise as to please God and praise the Creator.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:106
verses.text: For if thou wert to happen to enter the workshop of a smith, thou wouldest not dare to find fault with his bellows, his anvils, his hammers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:107
verses.text: But take an ignorant man, who knows not for what purpose each thing is, and he findeth fault with all.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:108
verses.text: But if he have not the skill of the workman, and have but the reasoning power of a man, what saith he to himself? Not without reason are the bellows placed here: the workman knoweth wherefore, though I know not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:109
verses.text: In the shop he dareth not to find fault with the smith, yet in the universe he dareth to find fault with God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:110
verses.text: Therefore just as "fire, hail, snow, ice, wind of storms, which do His word," so all things in nature, which seem to foolish persons to be made at random, simply "do His word," because they are not made save by His command.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:111
verses.text: Then he mentioneth, that they may praise the Lord, "mountains and hills, fruitful trees and all cedars" : "beasts and all cattle, creeping things, and winged fowls".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:112
verses.text: Then he goeth to men; "kings of the earth and all people, princes and all judges of the earth" : "young men and maidens, old men and young, let them praise the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:113
verses.text: Ended is the praise from heaven, ended is the praise from earth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:114
verses.text: "For His Name only is exalted".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:115
verses.text: Let no man seek to exalt his own name.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:116
verses.text: Wilt thou be exalted? Subject thyself to Him who cannot be humbled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:117
verses.text: "His confession is in earth and heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:118
verses.text: What is "His confession"? Is it the confession wherewith He confesseth? No, but that whereby all things confess Him, all things cry aloud: the beauty of all things is in a manner their voice, whereby they praise God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:119
verses.text: The heaven crieth out to God, "Thou madest me, not I myself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:120
verses.text: Earth crieth out, "Thou createdst me, not I myself".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:121
verses.text: How do they cry out? When thou regardest them, and findest this out, they cry out by thy voice, they cry out by thy regard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:122
verses.text: Regard the heavens, it is beautiful: observe the earth, it is beautiful: both together are very beautiful.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:123
verses.text: He made them, He ruleth them, by His nod they are swayed, He ordereth their seasons, He reneweth their movements, by Himself He reneweth them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:124
verses.text: All these things then praise Him, whether in stillness or in motion, whether from earth below or from heaven above, whether in their old state or in their renewal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:125
verses.text: When thou seest all these things, and rejoicest, and art lifted up to the Maker, and gazest on "His invisible things understood by the things which are made," "His confession is in earth and heaven:" that is, thou confesseth to Him from things on earth, thou confesseth to Him from things in heaven.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:126
verses.text: And since He made all things, and nought is better than He, whatsoever He made is less than He, and whatsoever in these things pleaseth thee, is less than He.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:127
verses.text: Let not then what He hath made so please thee, as to withdraw thee from Him who made: if thou lovest what He made, love much more Him who made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:128
verses.text: If the things which He hath made are beautiful, how much more beautiful is He who made them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:129
verses.text: "And He shall exalt the horn of His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:130
verses.text: Behold what Haggai and Zachariah prophesied.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:131
verses.text: Now the "horn of His people" is humble in afflictions, in tribulations, in temptations, in beating of the breast; when will He "exalt the horn of His people"? When the Lord hath come, and our Sun is risen, not the sun which is seen with the eye, and "riseth upon the good and the evil,"  but That whereof is said, To you that hear God, "the Sun of Righteousness shall rise, and healing in His wings;" and of whom the proud and wicked shall hereafter say, "The light of righteousness hath not shined unto us, and the sun of righteousness rose not upon us".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:132
verses.text: This shall be our summer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:133
verses.text: Now during the winter weather the fruits appear not on the stock; thou observest, so to say, dead trees during the winter.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:134
verses.text: He who cannot see truly, thinketh the vine dead; perhaps there is one near it which is really dead; both are alike during winter; the one is alive, the other is dead, but both the life and death are hidden: summer advanceth; then the life of the one shineth brightly, the death of the other is manifested: the splendour of leaves, the abundance of fruit, cometh forth, the vine is clothed in outward appearance from what it hath in its stock.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:135
verses.text: Therefore, brethren, now we are the same as other men: just as they are born, eat, drink, are clothed, pass their life, so also do the saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:136
verses.text: Sometimes the very truth deceiveth men, and they say, "Lo, he hath begun to be a Christian: hath he lost his headache?" or, "because he is a Christian, what gaineth he from me?" O dead vine, thou observest near thee a vine that is bare indeed in winter, yet not dead.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:137
verses.text: Summer will come, the Lord will come, our Splendour, that was hidden in the stock, and then "He shall exalt the horn of His people," after the captivity wherein we live in this mortal life.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:138
verses.text: "An hymn to all His Saints".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:139
verses.text: Know ye what an hymn is? It is a song with praise of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:140
verses.text: If thou praisest God and singest not, thou utterest no hymn: if thou singest and praisest not God, thou utterest no hymn: if thou praisest aught else, which pertaineth not to the praise of God, although thou singest and praisest, thou utterest no hymn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:141
verses.text: An hymn then containeth these three things, song, and praise, and that of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:142
verses.text: Praise then of God in song is called an hymn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 148:143
verses.text: What then meaneth, "An hymn to all His Saints"? Let His Saints receive an hymn: let His Saints utter an hymn: for this is what they are to receive in the end, an everlasting hymn.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:1
verses.text: Psalm CXLIX.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:2
verses.text: Let  us praise the Lord both in voice, and in understanding, and in good works; and, as this Psalm exhorteth, let us sing unto Him a new song.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:3
verses.text: It beginneth: "Sing ye to the Lord a new song.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:4
verses.text: His praise is in the Church of the Saints".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:5
verses.text: The old man hath an old song, the new man a new song.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:6
verses.text: The Old Testament is an old song, the New Testament a new song.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:7
verses.text: In the Old Testament are temporal and earthly promises.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:8
verses.text: Whoso loveth earthly things singeth an old song: let him that desireth to sing a new song, love the things of eternity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:9
verses.text: Love itself is new and eternal; therefore is it ever new, because it never groweth old.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:10
verses.text: And this song is of peace, this song is of charity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:11
verses.text: Whoso severeth himself from the union of the saints, singeth not a new song; for he hath followed old strife, not new charity.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:12
verses.text: In new charity what is there? Peace, the bond of an holy society, a spiritual union, a building of living stones.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:13
verses.text: Where is this? Not in one place, but throughout the whole world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:14
verses.text: This is said in another Psalm, "Sing unto the Lord, all the earth".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:15
verses.text: From this is understood, that he who singeth not with the whole earth, singeth an old song, whatever words proceed out of his mouth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:16
verses.text: We have already said, brethren, that all the earth singeth a new song.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:17
verses.text: He who singeth not with the whole earth a new song, let him sing what he will, let his tongue sound forth Halleluia, let him utter it all day and all night, my ears are not so much bent to hear the voice of the singer, but I seek the deeds of the doer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:18
verses.text: For I ask, and say, "What is it that thou singest?" He answereth, "Halleluia".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:19
verses.text: What is "Halleluia"? "Praise ye the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:20
verses.text: Come, let us praise the Lord together.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:21
verses.text: If thou praisest the Lord, and I praise the Lord, why are we at variance? Charity praiseth the Lord, discord blasphemeth the Lord".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:22
verses.text: The field of the Lord is the world, not Africa.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:23
verses.text: It is not with the Lord's field, as it is without these fields of ours, where Getulia bears sixty or an hundred fold, Numidia only ten fold: everywhere fruit is borne to Him, both an hundred fold, and sixty fold, and thirty fold: only do thou choose what thou wilt be, if thou thinkest to belong to the Lord's Cross.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:24
verses.text: "The Church" then "of the saints" is the Catholic Church.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:25
verses.text: The Church of the saints is not the Church of heretics.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:26
verses.text: The Church of the saints is that which God first prefigured before it was seen, and then set forth that it might be seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:27
verses.text: The Church of the saints was heretofore in writings, now it is in nations: the Church of the saints was heretofore only read of, now it is both read of and seen.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:28
verses.text: When it was only read of, it was believed; now it is seen, and is spoken against.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:29
verses.text: His praise is in the "children of the kingdom," that is, "the Church of the saints".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:30
verses.text: "Let Israel rejoice in Him who made Him".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:31
verses.text: What is, "Israel"? "Seeing God".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:32
verses.text: He who seeth God, rejoiceth in Him by whom he was made.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:33
verses.text: What is it then, brethren? we have said that we belong to the Church of the saints: do we already see God? and how are we Israel, if we see not? There is one kind of sight belonging to this present time; there will be another belonging to the time hereafter: the sight which now is, is by faith; the sight which is to be will be in reality.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:34
verses.text: If we believe, we see; if we love, we see: see what? God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:35
verses.text: Ask John: "God is love;" let us bless His holy Name, and rejoice in God by rejoicing in love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:36
verses.text: Whoso hath love, why send we him afar to see God? Let him regard his own conscience, and there he seeth God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:37
verses.text: "And let the sons of Sion exult in their King".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:38
verses.text: The sons of the Church are Israel.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:39
verses.text: For Sion indeed was one city, which fell: amid its ruins certain saints dwelt after the flesh: but the true Sion, the true Jerusalem (for Sion and Jerusalem are one), is "eternal in the heavens,"  and is "our mother".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:40
verses.text: She it is that hath given us birth, she is the Church of the saints, she hath nourished us, she, who is in part a pilgrim, in part abiding in the heavens.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:41
verses.text: In the part which abideth in heaven is the bliss of angels, in the part which wandereth in this world is the hope of the righteous.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:42
verses.text: Of the former is said, "Glory to God in the highest;" of the latter, "and on earth peace to men of good will".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:43
verses.text: Let those then who, being in this life, groan, and long for their country, run by love, not by bodily feet; let them seek not ships but wings, let them lay hold on the two wings of love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:44
verses.text: What are the two wings of love? The love of God, and of our neighbour.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:45
verses.text: For now we are pilgrims, we sigh, we groan.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:46
verses.text: There has come to us a letter from our country: we read it to you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:47
verses.text: "And the sons of Sion shall exult in their King".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:48
verses.text: The Son of God, who made us, was made one of us: and He rules us as our King, because He is our Creator, who made us.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:49
verses.text: But He by whom we were made is the same as He by whom we are ruled, and we are Christians because He is Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:50
verses.text: He is called Christ from Chrism, that is, Anointing.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:51
verses.text: Give to the Priest somewhat to offer.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:52
verses.text: What could man find which he could give as a clean victim? What victim? what clean thing can a sinner offer? O unrighteous, O sinful man, whatever thou offerest is unclean, and somewhat that is clean must be offered for thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:53
verses.text: Let then the Priest that is clean offer Himself, and cleanse thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:54
verses.text: This is what Christ did.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:55
verses.text: He found in man nothing clean for Him to offer for man: He offered Himself as a clean Victim.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:56
verses.text: Happy Victim, true Victim, spotless Offering.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:57
verses.text: He offered not then what we gave Him; yea rather, He offered what He took of us, and offered it clean.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:58
verses.text: For of us He took flesh, and this He offered.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:59
verses.text: But where took He it? In the womb of the Virgin Mary, that He might offer it clean for us unclean.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:60
verses.text: He is our King, He is our Priest, in Him let us rejoice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:61
verses.text: "Let them praise His Name in chorus".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:62
verses.text: What meaneth "chorus"? Many know what a "chorus" is: nay, as we are speaking in a town, almost all know.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:63
verses.text: A "chorus" is the union of singers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:64
verses.text: If we sing "in chorus," let us sing in concord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:65
verses.text: If any one's voice is out of harmony in a chorus of singers, it offendeth the ear, and throweth the chorus into confusion.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:66
verses.text: If the voice of one echoing discordantly troubleth the harmony of them who sing, how doth the discord of heresy throw into confusion the harmony of them who praise.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:67
verses.text: The whole world is now the chorus of Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:68
verses.text: The chorus of Christ soundeth harmoniously from east to west "Let them sing a psalm unto Him with timbrel and psaltery".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:69
verses.text: Wherefore taketh he to him the "timbrel and psaltery"? That not the voice alone may praise, but the works too.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:70
verses.text: When timbrel and psaltery are taken, the hands harmonize with the voice.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:71
verses.text: So too do thou, whensoever thou singest "Halleluia," deal forth thy bread to the hungry, clothe the naked, take in the stranger: then doth not only thy voice sound, but thy hand soundeth in harmony with it, for thy deeds agree with thy words.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:72
verses.text: Thou hast taken to thee an instrument, and thy fingers agree with thy tongue.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:73
verses.text: Nor must we keep back the mystical meaning of the "timbrel and psaltery".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:74
verses.text: On the timbrel leather is stretched, on the psaltery gut is stretched; on either instrument the flesh is crucified.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:75
verses.text: How well did he "sing a psalm on timbrel and psaltery," who said, "the world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world"? This psaltery or timbrel He wishes thee to take up, who loveth a new song, who teacheth thee, saying to thee, "Whosoever willeth to be My disciple, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow Me".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:76
verses.text: Let him not set down his psaltery, let him not set down his timbrel, let him stretch himself out on the wood, and be dried from the lust of the flesh.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:77
verses.text: The more the strings are stretched, the more sharply do they sound.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:78
verses.text: The Apostle Paul then, in order that his psaltery might sound sharply, what said he? "Stretching forth unto those things which are before," etc He stretched himself: Christ touched him; and the sweetness of truth sounded.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:79
verses.text: "For the Lord hath dealt kindly among His people".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:80
verses.text: What dealing so kindly, as to die for the ungodly? What dealing so kindly, as with righteous Blood to blot out the handwriting against the sinner? What dealing so kindly, as to say, "I regard not what ye were, be ye now what ye were not"? He dealeth kindly in converting him that was turned away, in aiding him that is fighting, in crowning the conqueror.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:81
verses.text: "And the meek He shall lift up in salvation".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:82
verses.text: For the proud too are lifted up, but not in salvation: the meek are lifted in salvation, the proud in death: that is, the proud lift up themselves, and God humbleth them: the meek humble themselves, and God lifteth them up.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:83
verses.text: "The saints shall exult in glory".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:84
verses.text: I would say somewhat important about the glory of the saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:85
verses.text: For there is no one who loveth not glory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:86
verses.text: But the glory of fools, popular glory as it is called, hath snares to deceive, so that a man, influenced by the praises of vain men, shall be willing to live in such fashion as to be spoken of by men, whosoever they be, in whatsoever way.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:87
verses.text: Hence it is that men, rendered mad, and puffed up with pride, empty within, without swollen, are willing ever to ruin their fortunes by bestowing them on stage-players, actors, men who fight with wild beasts, charioteers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:88
verses.text: What sums they give, what sums they spend! They lavish the powers not only of their patrimony, but of their minds too.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:89
verses.text: They scorn the poor, because the people shouteth not that the poor should be given to, but the people do shout that the fighter with wild beasts be given to.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:90
verses.text: When then no shout is raised to them, they refuse to spend; when madmen shout to them, they are mad too: nay, all are mad, both performer, and spectator, and the giver.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:91
verses.text: This mad glory is blamed by the Lord, is offensive in the eyes of the Almighty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:92
verses.text: Thou choosest to clothe the fighter with wild beasts, who may be beaten, and make thee blush: Christ is never conquered; He hath conquered the devil, He hath conquered for thee, and to thee, and in thee; such a conqueror as this thou choosest not to clothe.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:93
verses.text: Wherefore? Because there is less shouting, less madness about it.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:94
verses.text: They then who delight in such glory, have an empty conscience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:95
verses.text: Just as they drain their chests, to send garments as presents, so do they empty their conscience, so as to have nothing precious therein.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:96
verses.text: But the saints who "exul t in glory," no need is there for us to say how they exult: just hear the verse of the Psalm which followeth: "The saints shall exult in glory, they shall rejoice in their beds:" not in theatres, or amphitheatres, or circuses, or follies, or market places, but "in their chambers".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:97
verses.text: What is, "in their chambers"? In their hearts Hear the Apostle Paul exulting in his closet: "For this is our glory, the testimony of our conscience".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:98
verses.text: On the other hand, there is reason to fear lest any be pleasing to himself, and so seem to be proud, and boast of his conscience.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:99
verses.text: For every one ought to exult with fear, for that wherein he exulteth is God's gift, not his own desert.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:100
verses.text: For there be many that please themselves, and think themselves righteous; and there is another passage which goeth against them, which saith, "Who shall boast that he hath a clean heart, and that he is pure from sin?"  There is then, so to speak, a limit to glorying in our conscience, namely, to know that thy faith is sincere, thy hope sure, thy love without dissimulation.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:101
verses.text: "The exultations of God are in their mouths".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:102
verses.text: In such wise shall they "rejoice in their closets," as not to attribute to themselves that they are good, but praise Him from whom they have what they are, by whom they are called to attain to what they are not, and from whom they hope for perfection, to whom they give thanks, because He hath begun.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:103
verses.text: "And swords sharpened on both sides in their hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:104
verses.text: This sort of weapon contains a great mystical meaning, in that it is sharp on both sides.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:105
verses.text: By "swords sharpened on both sides," we understand the Word of the Lord: it is one sword, but therefore are they called many, because there are many mouths and many tongues of the saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:106
verses.text: How is it two edged? It speaks of things temporal, it speaks also of things eternal.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:107
verses.text: In both cases it proveth what it saith, and him whom it strikes, it severeth from the world.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:108
verses.text: Is not this the sword whereof the Lord said, "I am not come to send peace upon earth, but a sword"? Observe how He came to divide, how He came to sever.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:109
verses.text: He divideth the saints, He divideth the ungodly, He severeth from thee that which hindereth thee.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:110
verses.text: The son willeth to serve God, the father willeth not: the sword cometh, the Word of God cometh, and severeth the son from the father.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:111
verses.text: Wherefore then is it in their hands, not in their tongues? "And swords," it saith, "sharpened on both sides in their hands".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:112
verses.text: By "in their hands," he meaneth in power.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:113
verses.text: They received then the word of God in power, to speak where they would, to whom they would, neither to fear power, nor to despise poverty.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:114
verses.text: For they had in their hands a sword; where they would they brandished it, handled it, smote with it: and all this was in the power of the preachers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:115
verses.text: For if the Word be not in their hands, why is it written, "The Word of the Lord was put in the hand of the Prophet Haggai"? Surely, brethren, God set not His Word in His fingers.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:116
verses.text: What is meant by, "was put in his hand"? It was put into his power to preach the Word of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:117
verses.text: Lastly, we can understand these "hands" in another way also.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:118
verses.text: For they who spake had the word of God in their tongues, they who wrote, in their hands.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:119
verses.text: Now, brethren, ye see the saints armed: observe the slaughter, observe their glorious battles.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:120
verses.text: For if there be a commander, there must be soldiers; if soldiers, an enemy; if a warfare, a victory.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:121
verses.text: What have these done who had in their hands swords sharpened on both sides? "To do vengeance on the nations".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:122
verses.text: See whether vengeance have not been done on the nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:123
verses.text: Daily is it done: we do it ourselves by speaking.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:124
verses.text: Observe how the nations of Babylon are slain.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:125
verses.text: She is repaid twofold: for so is it written of her, "repay her double for what she hath done".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:126
verses.text: How is she repaid double? The saints wage war, they draw their "swords twice sharpened;" thence come defeats, slaughters, severances: how is she repaid double? When she had power to persecute the Christians, she slew the flesh indeed, but she crushed not God: now she is repaid double, for the Pagans are extinguished and the idols are broken.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:127
verses.text: And lest thou shouldest think that men are really smitten with the sword, blood really shed, wounds made in the flesh, he goeth on and explaineth, "upbraidings among the peoples".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:128
verses.text: What is "upbraidings"? Reproof.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:129
verses.text: Let the "sword twice sharpened" go forth from you, delay not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:130
verses.text: Say to thy friend, if yet thou hast one left to whom to say it, "What kind of man art thou, who hast abandoned Him by whom thou wast made, and worshippest what He made? Better is the Workman, than that which He worketh".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:131
verses.text: When he beginneth to blush, when he beginneth to feel compunction, thou hast made a wound with thy sword, it hath reached the heart, he is about to die, that he may live.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:132
verses.text: "That they may bind their kings in fetters, and their nobles in bonds of iron".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:133
verses.text: "To execute upon them the judgment written".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:134
verses.text: The kings of the Gentiles are to be bound in fetters, "and their nobles in fetters," and that "of iron".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:135
verses.text: For these verses which we are beginning to explain are obscure.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:136
verses.text: For for this purpose God willed to set down some of His verses obscurely, not that anything new should be dug out of them, but that what was already well known, might be made new by being obscurely set forth.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:137
verses.text: We know that kings have been made Christians; we know that the nobles of the Gentiles have been made Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:138
verses.text: They are being made so at this day; they have been, they shall be; the "swords twice sharpened" are not idle in the hands of the saints.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:139
verses.text: How then do we understand their being bound in fetters and chains of iron? Ye know, beloved and learned brethren (learned I call you, for ye have been nourished in the Church, and are accustomed to hear God's Word read), that "God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the strong, and the foolish things of the world hath God chosen to confound the wise, and things which are not, just as things which are, that the things which are may be brought to nought".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:140
verses.text: It is said by the Lord, "If thou wilt be perfect, go sell all that thou hast, and give to the poor, and come, follow Me, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:141
verses.text: Many of the nobles did this, but they ceased to be nobles of the Gentiles, they chose rather to be poor in this world, noble in Christ.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:142
verses.text: But many retain their former nobility, retain their royal powers, and yet are Christians.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:143
verses.text: These are, as it were, "in fetters and in bonds of iron".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:144
verses.text: How so? they received fetters, to keep them from going to things unlawful, the "fetters of wisdom," the fetters of the Word of God.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:145
verses.text: Wherefore then are they bonds of iron and not bonds of gold? They are iron so long as they fear: let them love, and they shall be golden.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:146
verses.text: Observe, beloved, what I say.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:147
verses.text: Ye have heard just now the Apostle John, "There is no fear in love, but perfect love casteth out fear, because fear hath torment".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:148
verses.text: This is the bond of iron.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:149
verses.text: And yet unless a man begin through fear to worship God, he will not attain to love.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:150
verses.text: "The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:151
verses.text: The beginning then is bonds of iron, the end a collar of gold.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:152
verses.text: For it is said of wisdom, "a collar of gold around thy neck".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:153
verses.text: There cometh to us a man powerful in this world, his wife offendeth him, and perhaps he hath desired another man's wife who is more beautiful, or another woman who is richer, he wisheth to put away the one he hath, yet he doeth it not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:154
verses.text: He heareth the words of the servant of God, he heareth the Prophet, he heareth the Apostle, and he doeth it not; he is told by one in whose hands is a "sword twice sharpened," "Thou shalt not do it: it is not lawful for thee: God alloweth thee not to put away thy wife, "save for the cause of fornication".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:155
verses.text: He heareth this, he feareth, and doeth it not.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:156
verses.text: Listen, young men; the bonds are of iron, seek not to set your feet within them; if ye do, ye shall be bound more tightly with fetters.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:157
verses.text: Such fetters the hands of the Bishop make strong for you.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:158
verses.text: Do not men who are thus fettered fly to the Church, and are here loosed? Men do fly hither, desiring to be rid of their wives: here they are more tightly bound: no man looseth these fetters.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:159
verses.text: "What God joined together, let not man put asunder".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:160
verses.text: But these bonds are hard.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:161
verses.text: Who but knows it? This hardness the Apostles grieved at, and said, "If this be the case with a wife, it is not good to marry".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:162
verses.text: If the bonds be of iron, it is not good to set our feet within them.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:163
verses.text: And the Lord said, "All men cannot receive this saying, but let him that can receive it, receive it".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:164
verses.text: "Art thou bound unto a wife? seek not to be freed," for thou art bound with bonds of iron.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:165
verses.text: "Art thou free from a wife, seek not a wife;" bind not thyself with bonds of iron.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:166
verses.text: "To do in them the judgment that is written".

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:167
verses.text: This is the judgment which the saints do throughout all nations.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:168
verses.text: Wherefore "written"? Because these things were before written, and now are fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustin: Psalms 149:169
